We only stayed for a stop over (2 nights) but the room was fine for us. The room was clean and spacious and the apartment interior looked like it had been remodeled. Zach is a "hands off" host but has the most ingenious ways of getting keys (he uses a lock box). I wish more hosts would do that as it would eliminate the stress of getting there at the assigned him. The apartment is located in Flushing, enough away from Manhattan craziness but close to the subways. It is a working class, multi-cultural neighborhood but a lot like where I live in San Francisco so it was fine with me. Didn't have a lot of time to check it out though. I would have liked to if I had the time.

Usually when something looks too good to be true it is. This Air bnb was the exception to that rule. It was an absolute steal for the property and location compared to price. The host/hostess  were kind and accommodating beyond words. The home was clean and organized. The neighborhood all though busy at times we felt extremely safe and every person we encountered walking to and from train was respectful and curious. There is honestly not 1 single negative thing I can say about my stay. It really felt like home 2,000 miles away from my home. Would recommend for any one looking to visit New York.

Apartment was in a great location, super close to several subway stations and Battery Park. The apartment itself was clean, and Lucas was super welcoming. He made enough coffee for everyone each morning and was always friendly without being overbearing. Our flight got cancelled the night before checkout — resulting in some major stress — and Lucas made us brownies because he felt bad that he couldn’t help more. Great guy and great place to stay.

The apartment has a great location, subway is just a few blocks away. Many restaurants around and very quiet neighborhood. The room design is nice, but on the downside the fact that there is no lock on the door was weird, we hesitated on shopping because we were afraid that someone would walk into the room ( we did noticed someone walked into the room, nothing was taken but still). Also the weekend was party mode for the rest of the tenants, which was kind of hard to rest. The description mentions that there is room with terrace, but we were clearly stated that we were only allowed in our room and by the lift not the stairs, which was disappointing, because we at least wanted a good glass of wine with a great view in the terrace.

This was our first Airbnb experience and it was excellent. The room was spacious, comfortable and clean. And it was very quiet. We especially loved the rainfall shower head! The location near museums, shopping and restaurants was perfect as well. One minus was that there was no cable TV. Normally this wouldn't matter, except that our stay coincided with the Olympics and we wanted to watch. The biggest drawback was that we could not lock our room when departing. This made us a little uncomfortable but thankfully nothing was stolen. We were able to lock ourselves in at night, though. Very important! We would definitely stay here again! Our room was just as advertised.

Wish we could've met Alexis, but her home was amazing. Located on a quiet block within walking distance of several great restaurants and small drug and grocery stores. Though not a completely quiet environment, we rested well at Alexis's home in this quiet neighborhood. Would absolutely stay again if we were looking for a place in the UES.

This room is exactly as advertised. Check-in was a breeze.  Alexis and Mara were extremely responsive when I had questions. The room is sparkling clean, quiet and spacious. A perfect location for visiting museums and enjoying the beautiful neighborhoods of the Upper East Side. As others have commented, the room does not have an individual lock, but I never felt unsafe or insecure. It is a family home but I had complete privacy.

We loved staying here.  The neighborhood has lots of great restaurants and is very close to the beautiful campus of City College.  We walked everywhere at all times of the day and evening and never felt unsafe.  Anatha and her husband are very sweet and welcoming.

The room was just as described, modern and clean. Unfortunately the door to the room does not lock leaving our valuables accessible to anyone in the building. We were told no one else was staying on our floor therefore our belongings would be safe however just minutes later a young gentleman entered the room across the hall! Although we were instructed on how to use the light and shade switches we ere not instructed on the two TV remotes leaving us unable to watch tv at all during our stay. So much for the advo re Netflix. Arlinda couldn't get the TV to work either and was curt with us. Also the advo says check out is noon but Arlinda told us 11 making us rush when we were delayed due to a non working electrical outlet in the bathroom with the only mirror to use when blow drying our hair. I felt she was rude to us when we discussed our dissatisfaction with non operating TV and non locking door! How dare we complain.

Everything was exactly as it was described.  Gagandeep and his wife, Samira, were more than willing to help with anything and were easily reached whenever we had a question or concern.  They were warm and inviting.    We used this listing as our residence with our four month old for three weeks while our own apartment only a few blocks away was being renovated.  Despite being an extremely stressful time for us, we were grateful to have a warm, comfortable place to call home.  The kitchen allowed us to cook dinners and prepare breakfast and lunch and the washer/dryer allowed us to keep up with the baby's laundry.  When our renovation went a day late, Gagandeep made a point to check in on us and allowed us to move out as we needed on our last day showing real flexibility and genuine concern.  If we had to do it again, we would book it in a heartbeat.  We plan to recommend this place to anyone looking to stay in our neighborhood (which we love and recommend itself for great restaurants, nearness to Prospect Park and accessibility to Manhattan) in the future.

I recommend this spacious, clean, bright room. The photos conform to reality. The bedding is very comfortable. Alexis was a great help with the late arrival time following my flight being 6 hours late. The possibility of being able to leave your suitcases until the end of the day is a real plus. The area is very pleasant, just a 5-minute walk from the metro. If I were to come back to New York I would not hesitate to come back to Alexis.

I had such a lovely stay with Sarah and highly recommend her place. Right from the beginning I felt welcome, at ease and safe in the gorgeous quiet area. I stayed for a full month as I studied a busy and stressful course. Sarah was very helpful with any NY questions, local area information and nice little chats whenever we had the time.   Zissou is the lovely dog Sarah owns I also got to live with. He is a real character and always had a warm welcome for me on my return. The location is great, nice and quiet, bargain shops around the corner,  the A train is across the road, express train, midtown in 30mins and the local park overlooked the Hudson River. Also, the big double bed is a dream to sleep in!  Sarah and Zissou made my stay in NY so enjoyable and I will definitely be back again to stay.

Gagandeep made my stay!  He was able to be flexible with my check-in hour which was a great stress-reliever for me.  His place is as described but I found the master bedroom more beautiful and I definitely loved his big bathtub.  It was helpful to take the New York chill off after a long day of sight-seeing.  The flat was quiet, clean and warm. The location is perfect....two metro stations a short walk away!!!!  The neighborhood is trendy with plenty of amazing coffee shops, restaurants and wine bars.

-In the last night, something really terrible happened! We were feeling a gas smell and we went up stairs to check the oven and so, but everything was turned off, so we opened the door for a while, the smell was apparently gone, then we went downstairs to sleep. In the next day, we woke up very early in the morning, around 5am and the gas smell was reaaally strong! We couldn’t even breath properly, we had bought things to cook for our breakfast on the previous day, but we couldn’t cook anything, we were really worried about any possible explosion due to the gas leak, other than this we couldn’t stay in the home for any longer (it was dangerous and unhealthy). We closed our suitcases and left the home as soon as possible, it was a really bad time and in the airport one of us was feeling really sick and the other one had strong headache (we found out it could be related to the gas leak). Our American simcard stopped working so we contacted Victoria when in the airport (we got some wifi), when we told her what had happened she didn’t look any worried (it felt like it is something usual, because if you learn your home has a gas leak you try to check it as soon as possible, because it may explode, isn’t it?), but instead she said “I’ll ask the landlord to check it”….a few hours later, when we were already out of New York (she thought we were still in the home), she was still texting us, telling that the landlord would just go there if we were out of the home (gosh, why didn’t the landlord just run to check what was going on? What if it wasn’t our last days and if we couldn’t just move on? We could have welcomed the landlord, we really didn’t understand it). In the end she didn’t give us any explanation about what happened and we could have gotten serious problems or even did for we smelled that much gas during the whole night! Other than the last day “surprise” we faced a few other things during our staying: -The home was full of her things everywhere, in the fridge (she left us a really small space and we were 3 people staying there for 8 days, so almost every day we had to return to the Market to buy something else cause if we had bought everything at once it wouldn’t fit in the fridge), the desk in the room was taken by clothes and necklaces and the bathroom as well was full of her shampoos, creams and other stuff, which were not available for us and which were also not leaving space for us to leave our things (so after each bath we had to put everything back to our suitcases). -The room is downstairs, but who needs the place to be dark to sleep can’t sleep well. There is a...

I ended up staying at Lillybeth and Crystal's place on very short notice, due to an unforeseen situation at another Airbnb apartment I booked.  The hosts were quick to respond to my request, and made the transition to the new home quick, easy, and stress free.  Lillybeth and Crystal's studio is perfect for all types of travelers coming into NYC for any length of stay.  The bed was very comfortable, and there was plenty of space to spread out and feel at home.  While the listing states it is a private room, it truly felt like a separate apartment, so that was a very nice bonus.  Having a private bathroom made all the difference, as I was up early each day for work, so not having to compete for time in the bathroom made getting ready each day stress free.  I will definitely look to reserve Lillybeth and Crystal's place next time I am in NYC.  Thanks again for being a great host!

Wonderful place. The place is clean and very comfortable and suits well for people who want to be bit further away from the chaos of the city centre. Our host was very helpful and helped us many times during our stay!   Even though the location in Harlem might look sketchy, I found the area to be quite safe as it is gentrified area.

We had a lovely stay at this airbnb for two nights in July 2019. We found the room very clean and tidy and it had everything you could need including a mini fridge, large TV, and a range of kitchen equipment. We also appreciated the small touches such as the coffee maker and grounds, candles, and reed diffuser. The photos of this place really don’t do it justice nor capture the smaller details. The only note to consider would be the location of this airbnb. Although the room felt safe, the neighborhood is quite far from central and tourist areas, and felt we a little unsafe walking around the streets at night.

Lillybeth & Crystals place was a 10/10. They were great at communication, the place was clean and exactly as pictured, and they went above and beyond with the amenities. The neighborhood was safe, we were out some nights past 1am and never felt unsafe. The check in and check out process was very easy, as well as finding the train nearby. This is the perfect place to stay if you plan to run around Manhattan and sight see. I will recommend this to anyone visiting NY.

Alberto is a great host and was so understanding and accommodating when we ran into a very long delay in checking in due to circumstances over which we had no control. He kept in constant communication with us throughout reassuring us so we wouldn’t stress out which I appreciated so much. The room we had was very nice and his place is a very short walk from the subway. Alberto gave us great recommendations on nice places to eat in the area which we took advantage of after checking out. I would highly recommend Alberto as a host and a stay at his place!

Great and affordable place for our girls trip to NYC! We never felt unsafe or worried, and it’s a nine minute walk to the nearest subway station. If you’re looking to be in the heart of the city then this isn’t for you. If you’re looking for an affordable, and cozy place to lay your head after a long day in the city - look no further

Lillian was responsive prior to check in, however once checked in, she was unresponsive. This may sound silly, but when we checked in, there was only 1/4-1/5 of the toilet paper roll left and no extra toilet papers. We messaged the host however she did not respond. Going out to buy toilet paper is not a big deal, but part of the Airbnb fees include house keeping and it was unpleasant to run out prior to any of the nearby stores being open. We aren’t sure who lives downstairs but we often heard them talking and their baby. The wall outlet also randomly started to zap and burn so we had to unplugged it on our last day. Host was aware that we inquired about a later check out time prior to the trip but said there was someone else checking in after so we couldn’t which is totally fine and understandable. But after being unresponsive about the toilet paper issue, she messaged us 4-5minutes before our scheduled check out time that we could stay longer.
It is in the attic and the stairs to get to the attic is pretty scary but it's clean

I had a wonderful stay for 8 nights at this beautiful west village apartment. It was so enjoyable to come home to a home, rather than a hotel. The apartment is beautifully and tastefully decorated, quiet and comfortable. Although the West Village is a bustling area, the street that this apartment is located on is wonderfully quiet and I always got a great nights sleep.   Kim was an absolutely outstanding host, staying in close contact before my stay, and providing amazing tips as to places to see, visit and eat in the area. The apartment was extremely clean and tidy when I arrived, and Kim made plenty of room for me to hang and store my clothes while I was there. She really went out of her way to ensure that I enjoyed my first trip to New York, and even bought me her favorite coffee to enjoy!  I chose the West Village because I'm a bit of a foodie, and I'm really glad I did. I didn't have to wander more than a few blocks to find some of the best food that I've ever eaten.  I did more exploring of New York than anticipated, so luckily the apartment was extremely well located, with only a short walk to the 1, A, B, C, D, F, M trains. This meant I never needed to catch a cab, and was always able to get to and from the apartment with ease, which turned out to be incredibly important.  Don’t let the lack of a laundry scare you off; there is a wash and fold one street down that took great care of my clothes, and had them washed, dried and back in my hands within a day. I used the time I saved to explore the city, and I’m glad I did.  I would stay here again without hesitation!

The accommodation is well located (12 minutes walk from the metro), consistent with the description and photos and Cara is very responsive by message. However, we deplored the bad smells of the sheets and towels which made us doubt the hygiene, and the quality of the bedding which is below minimum standards (sofa bed which squeaks enormously and whose mattress is at the end of its life). Additionally, we chose Airbnb to be able to cook, but we didn't feel welcome in the kitchen because it was cluttered with dirty dishes and there was no room in the fridge to store our groceries. Finally, despite having indicated to Cara our check out which respected the time of the announcement (11 a.m.), the cleaning lady came to clean 1 hour before our departure and we had to hurry to pack our bags and vacate the room. However Cara allowed us to leave our suitcases in the apartment while waiting for our flight (in the evening).

AFI Apartments is the perfect place for long-term stays.  The apartment has many amenities, as advertised,  and is located w/n proximity to 2 subway lines, and a great variety of food places, drug and convenience stores.  The place is sparkling clean and equipped with cable tv, ac, and modern appliances and dishes.

This is a great find! Patricio is a SUPER responsive host who is hospitality driven and it really shows during your stay. The apartment is exactly what you'd expect in NY based on the listing. Everything was clean and tidy, and I had everything I needed.   I was looking for somewhere that would be a roughly 30-45 minute commute to mid-town. Across all of the boroughs, the best value stays are usually about that far and if you don't mind the commute you can save a TON in exchange for a little time. Find some food/drinks near one of your stops along the way if you don't want to ride the whole thing at once! The subway station is roughly 2 blocks away and you have access to the 1 and A trainlines. I had no trouble late-night or weekends getting home. For a seasoned traveler the neighborhood isn't that bad at night and I felt fairly safe walking home. If you're new to big cities it might feel a little sketchy but just walk with purpose and confidence and you'll be fine! Most airbnb's will feel the same on the outside wherever you go in the city anywhere near this pricepoint.  There's a bodega close by if you need something from the store, but the food in a walkable distance is pretty basic. Luckily it's a short commute to any highly rated restaurant/coffee shop/bar! A great time to check out what upper Manhattan has to offer.

Patricio was amazing. He made our stay stress free. He was very commutative and made us feel welcome. His place was clean and wonderful. This location was close to the subways and in a good neighborhood. Would recommend to anyone. Looking forward to staying with him again. Totally recommend!

This stay was a disaster. Please save yourself the hell I had to go through during this stay. The second I opened the door of the apartment I felt heat. The apartment was so hot, it was 90 degrees. Their's one mini AC unit in the kitchen I turned it on immediately, The AC noise was so loud I had a headache after 10 mins. Even with the one AC unit on at 60 degrees and windows open the temperature wouldn't drop below 80(I knew the temperature from the AC remote). The apartment has zero modern ventilation, no thermostat to control the temperature, there are 2 radiators( one in the bedroom and one in the living room) and 3 radiator long pipes on the walls in the bedroom,living room and kitchen. The radiators and pipes were all emitting high amounts of heat so I called the landlord Antonio to turn off the radiator and pipes because it was super hot in the room, I was sweating and had trouble breathing. Antonio said there was no way to turn off the pipes because it would shut off for the whole building and the maintenance was only able to shut off the radiator (not the pipe) in the room, the other radiator had a broken  part and needed fixing. When he told me he couldn't turn off the heat I immediately said I want a refund so I could check into a hotel. Antonio refused to give a refund for the stay, wouldn't allow me to cancel, he tried offering a different apartment in the building but it was just as hot, the entire building was a melting pot. This company appears to be false advertising(especially air conditioning the little AC unit in the kitchen was basically useless) and what's worse is they're putting people in dangerous environments, If it had been someone with underlying conditions it could be much worse so airbnb should definitely investigate this company. The living room was the hotest and the wifi only worked in the living so it was hell, I was miserable I couldn't enjoy anything even eating my food, I started getting nose bleeds. To add to all of it the kitchen floor had no padding it almost fell like the wood would break at any moment it felt hollow and was super squeaky. The shower water had barely any water pressure, the curtains are literally made of paper and everything in the apartment is made out've cheap wood and masqueraded to make it look better. Communication was horrible, Antonio wouldn't respond to texts or calls so my only resort was to contact airbnb get a refund and leave. This is the first I've dealt with airbnb customer service and to be honest they weren't great they kept throwing my case around from one agent to the next,  I had to call like 15 times, some agents were nice some weren't as much but they failed to see the urgency of the situation that they were keeping me in an unlivable situation, they kept me waiting for 2 days until finally one very nice agent addressed my issue refunded me and I left to a hotel, I just didn't have the luxury of booking a hotel stay while also paying for the airbnb I'm just visiting NY for a couple months and I don't live on a NY salary so I was forced to stay until I was issued a refund. I really hope you come across this comment before booking and avoid this terrible experience.

Unforgettable stay. As soon as we returned, we felt at home. The accommodation corresponds perfectly to the description and even better. Everything is perfect for exploring New York.  On our late arrival (11 p.m.), we found accommodation that was clean, functional, welcoming and warm.  The stocked refrigerator allowed us to refresh ourselves and prepare hearty breakfasts for the following days. (Granola, bagels, jam, butter, orange juice, milk...) The rooms are spacious, tastefully decorated and well arranged. The bathroom is functional. The room overlooking the garden is equipped with a very large bed which allowed us to easily regain strength after long days of walking in the Big Apple. The icing on the cake: the garden. Small, quiet haven of peace, with a large tree and squirrels who regularly come to visit us. Ideal for taking a breather and finding calm after the tumult of New York!  The accommodation is located a 10-minute walk from an express subway station, which allows you to be in the heart of Manhattan in 20-25 minutes.  Less than 5 minutes away, there is a beautiful little grocery store (on the corner of the street), a Haitian restaurant and a restaurant with very wide opening hours which offers competitive breakfasts and where you can eat very well at lunchtime and in the evening with great value for money. If you move further away you can find a larger supermarket. The neighborhood is pleasant and lively. No feeling of insecurity. We found it pleasant at each crossing to see the “real” life of a Brooklyn neighborhood.  Finally, we appreciated the availability of our host, his good advice (welcome book, guides, good addresses) and his little touches which made our stay even more pleasant.  Thank you for this week at home!

Irene's place was amazing. Very clean, very stylish! She had thorough (not to mention entertaining!) recommendations for the nearby restaurants and other locations. I would love to stay here again in the future. Definitely a steal, too!

I would stay here every time I went to Brooklyn if I could. Our hosts were a pleasure to communicate with. There was no stress of our trip to Brooklyn because Irene, informed us about our check in process it was peaceful and painless. The apartment is beautiful along with a very zen back yard. I loved staying here and had an amazing time being back in Brooklyn.

Cara duplex on the upper Eastside is a gem. I am so happy that I got to stay there during my New York City vacation. She is a great host I and will definitely stay again on my next trip. Don’t think twice go ahead and book it. Don’t let the sofa bed scare you. It was extremely comfortable.
Beautifully updated and furnished. Very clean. Nice private backyard to enjoy in the shade. Owner provides useful and accurate information on the area.
The apartment was as described, clean, and easy to navigate. The surrounding area was run down and seemed sketchy at times, worse than we expected from the description. Overall, it was a nice stay.

This Airbnb unit is probably a better fit for the younger generation than it was for me and my wife (we are in our 60s).  One issue for us was the two steep flights of stairs - this is not an elevator unit - leading to the rental.  Fortunately, David helped us to move our luggage up, but we did need to get everything down on our own.  My wife and I believe that a younger generation would appreciate the Apple TV and the availability of video games.  David did spend some time (15 minutes, perhaps) trying to orient us to this world of technology, but in the end, we were more interested in watching the news.  This was tricky as the very limited live TV seemed to be antenna based reception, which was sketchy.    We wished there had been blankets - at least one - provided, as there was one day that was chilly.  When we realized there was no heat (mid afternoon) we called David.  He told us he would call the landlord.  We also reported this to Airbnb, which may also have contacted David, because he called back to tell us that he had contacted a neighbor in the building, who said the heat was beginning to come up.  We were fortunate to have family nearby.  They loaned us a blanket.  David also said he would reimburse us if we wanted to buy a blanket, but by that time, we were uncertain where to make such a purchase since it was Saturday evening, and the neighborhood had no clearly identifiable stores to buy bedding.    We also had an arrangement to meet David at 4 p.m, on the day of our arrival.  We called him several times, and went to the building three times and rang the doorbell.  On the final attempt, David did see my wife, but since he did not know her, he did not respond to the doorbell.  We called Airbnb, who also tried calling David, but with no success.  At about 5 p.m., David called us from a different number than the one he had given us.  He said he thought he had given us the number he was calling from.  However, neither we nor Airbnb had this number.  My wife and I believe that younger, more techno-savvy people would very much enjoy this unit. There are, however, obstacles for techno-phobes such as my wife and myself.

I will start by saying that if u want to throw a party here, find another place. The apt. Is on a tilt so if i threw a party o would have been afraid of the floor cracking or falling in. The apartment looks much better in person and is ideal if u are looking for a comfortable a quiet getaway. Everything except for the oven (which was under repair) was a available to me for my stay. I would highly recommend staying here.

Well, this was my first time renting a room at Airbnb, I was afraid but my host Helen and Jimmy were very nice  and reliable. My fiancé and I had car trouble on the road which made us arrive at Helen's place at 11:30pm and Helen was in touch with us the whole time, making sure we were okay; when we got to her place her husband Jimmy was waiting for us( very nice guy). He went out of his way to print something out for us that we forgot about. I highly recommend them, their place is nice and clean. It's across from the park which you walk through to get to Arthur Ashe Stadium; very pleasant walk.

This is not the room I stayed in.....initially the host did not want to give me the wifi password. I told him I would not stayed there without a wifi connection. After the 1st night, the wifi died. It was restored by the 2nd night. I got mysterious itchy bites on my arm every night and I don't recall seeing any mosquitos. I never opened any windows. Possibly the early stages of a New York bed bug infestation. The bed only came with a bottom sheet and a "communal" comforter with the matching pillows. I don't think the comforter or the pillows were fresh for me. Sleeping like this feels like homeless. No top sheet with a "communal" comforter. No towels or bath mat were provided. They were promised but never arrived. The AC unit was weak and dusty and the room was not particularly clean. Dirt was visible on the ledges. There was hair in the bath, not mine. Yes, a roll of toilet paper was provided.

I was visiting with three female colleagues for a trade show in Manhattan. I know this neighborhood well and so the location was perfect especially once we discovered that the Javits Center now has a 7 train station. This apartment has a train station very close by which made it very convenient but we also used a lot of cabs (we were carrying a lot of stuff for work). The apartment is huge and great for our needs with tons of terraces that we even used for our private workout sessions. Great great food in the area including cafes. Be aware there are a lot of steps and staircases which we didn't mind but just a heads up. The apartment is situated over three levels and there are 2 staircases to climb to get to the first level. Great for our workout :). The concierge for the owner was very communicative for our check in process leading up to our arrival and each room had a private a/c unit which made it great for each of us to adjust to our own needs. I would totally stay here again and appreciate the clear, honest, open communication of this apartment and their host admits a sea of scammers and not so honest hosts. Thank you!!!

The apartment is perfect. It is larger than it appears in the photos and in addition to being beautiful, it is comfortable and very well equipped.  Mark is kind, as well as funny if you have a drink with him and talk for a while, and he is always willing to help you.  The neighborhood is quiet and pleasant. We didn't have any problems and I don't think there's anything unsafe about it, contrary to what the Airbnb page says, (unpredictably unsafe). We entered and left the house day and night, we returned on the subway after twelve at night, and we never had a feeling of risk.  In short, if I had to return to NY, I would return to Mark's apartment without hesitation.

I stayed with Leah and Aaron for a little over a month while I found an apartment of my own and I cannot stress more what a wonderful experience it was staying with them.  The apartment is spacious and beautiful and cozy with a nice laid back and homey vibe.  I really enjoyed my time living with Leah and Aaron, both of whom I can now call my friends!

John was a really nice and caring host. We had a good communication before and during our stay. He told us the easiest way to get there and let us keep our luggage in the appartment during our last day. As our flight went late that was very helpfull. We could even get changed and got a tasty snack before we left.  The appartment was small but really nice. John thought about many things to make it handy. There was enough space for everything.  The area was really nice with many places to eat and to go out. (Try the ice cream at "the little gay ice cream". Loved it!!! The waiting line is worth it.) Never felt unsafe at any day or night time. I would definetly stay there again!

Room was good for the price, perfect for a single or couple travelers. John was a bit gruff early in communication, but he apologized due to a bad day. He was gracious showing me the quirks of the place once I got there.  Shower is handheld in the tub, so just be aware of that. Your room connects to john's but he always maintained my privacy. Good location in the city near the lower east side, though there were a good number of transients hanging out outside of the building but never felt unsafe. Overall would stay there again.

Kristen was a lovely host. She was always ready to give me nice tips about the city and to show the best spots. The little dog Lexington is the joy of the place. Greets you at the door and not unusually join you in your time inside the apartment. Talking about the place, it couldn't be better located. Steps from MoMA, close to Central Park and between 5th and 6th Ave. Always clean and with access to the kitchen.  I loved the time a expended there.  Thanks Kristen! Say hello to Lexington for me.  Rob!

I cannot say enough great things about Mark’s place! My words cannot express what a delight Mark and his home were throughout our first visit to NYC. I traveled with my husband and two teenage daughters (14 and 18 yrs young). The home is a classic brownstone with plenty of space for us. We commuted into Manhattan via the subway, which was about a 10 minute walk through the neighborhood. The A train took you just about anywhere you needed to go. We regularly returned from our explorations pretty late and had no issues or felt unsafe walking back to Mark’s place. We also enjoyed the local corner market that was open 24hrs and were reasonably priced. There are several great restaurants (Peaches and Saraghina) that are a few minutes away, along with a cool local hangout, Lunatico. The WiFi connection was great and the locals were friendly. To top it off, Mark was a tremendous host. He was easy to communicate with and he checked on us, without being intrusive. You can tell that he genuinely cares about his guests enjoyment in his home and neighborhood. Stop searching for a place and book Mark’s brownstone. You’ll be glad you did!

Do not stay in this apartment.   Julia was a terrible host, and she was impossible to contact during our stay. Her apartment was not as advertised, and there was no AC or functioning WiFi. There was a thermostat on the wall,  and it was completely broken. When we finally heard from Julia about our concerns (with only 1 day left in our 4 day visit), she was completely useless.  She suggested that we look under her coats and luggage in the back of her closet to find the old window AC unit and "install it" ourselves. She also claimed that the WiFi was working perfectly, but that there was nothing she could do since she was out of the country. We tried re-setting the WiFi, and the issues remained. Since it was over 80 degrees during our visit, the lack of AC made the apartment sweltering hot; however, we're not above opening the windows to create air flow.   Opening the windows created one more problem: the fire station. There were fire trucks coming and going with incredibly loud sirens throughout the day and night. This and the lack of AC made it nearly impossible to sleep. I have never been less rested in my entire life, and the apartment was ultimately an unpleasant place to be.   I spent the majority of my visit trying to stay out of Julia's apartment, and the time that I was forced to spend there was not comfortable. If you enjoy a host who doesn't respond to e-mails and doesn't leave check-in instructions, then by all means: this is the place for you!   If you want to stay in an apartment that matches the advertisement and has AC/WiFi, then I highly suggest you find another AirBNB. This experience was terrible! I'm sad that the end of my NYC vacation was ruined by this AirBNB experience, because Williamsburg is such a great place otherwise.

"I feel like a Princess".... these words just came out of my mouth after I had entered the beautiful appartment on Van Buren St and was greeted by Eric and Justin. Because I was not only greeted! In the freezer there was coffee and pizzas, in the fridge breakfast, juice and water. From the sofa I could just sit and relax, watch my favourite movies and let the jetlag settle. My stay with Eric and Justin was brilliant, I felt so welcome and well cared for. Such hospitality, such friendliness. The appartment is a really awesome place for a very reasonable price, and if you like me don't mind to spend some time in the public transportation system, it is definitely worth choosing.  The area may at first seem a bit scary, but during my 9 days there, I never felt unsafe and was greeted in a friendly manner by people living there. I will always give my best recommendations Van Buren St and its wonderful hosts.

Very large bedroom and bathroom for New York! The bed was very comfortable, the room has its own private entrance and it feels like you have your own place, which is really nice. Parking on the street is no problem. I never felt unsafe traveling to Brooklyn and Manhattan and this area made no exception, even for a woman alone. Excellent location just next to the L line, perfect to go in and out the city at any time of day/night. I haven't met Oliver, though we had contact through emails and he was very nice. It's the perfect place to stay near the city without having to pay a fortune. Thanks Oliver:))

Eric was fantastic! Always very easy to get in touch with, and even supplied us with great information on how to get to the apartment from the airport, and info for the area! And there was breakfast stuff in the fridge when we got there which was so nice! The apartment itself was perfect. Enormous for 2 people, comfortable, clean, beautiful. Less than 10 mite walk to the subway station, less than 10 mins subway to Williamsburg and about 30 mins to places in manhattan. Really easy. And to be honest, it was only a $20 cab ride from Lower manhattan anyway which was perfect! The only thing, which all the other reviewers have said, is that the area is a bit rougher around the edges than the rest of Brooklyn and manhattan. We sometimes felt a bit uneasy, particularly at night, but I don't think that was very fair as we never had a single problem! I think we were uneasy as everyone we spoke to warned us that the area was unsafe, so keep that in mind if you're uneasy in that situation. If not, Eric and his place were absolutely great! Thank you!

What can i say about my stay in jhon's place? One word...Fantastic.. Jhon and Gabriel are really amazing host. They made me feel like part of their family the very moment i stepped into their apartment. They really keep their place nice, clean and tidy. During my stay, i almost couldn't wake up early in the morning, because the bed is too comfy and smell good too; do i have to mention more..sweet dreams every night. Jhon and Gabriel really care about my short time trip in new york. They will make sure where i need to go, best and nice bars to go to enjoy my wonderful night life...it's in new york, the city never sleeps!!! Their place is closed to the subway, about 5 minutes walk. it is also surrounded by many restaurants. Their place is also situated in a nice and safe neighborhood. I always come home late at night alone and i don't feel unsafe at all. Seriously, if you want to stay like a new yorker, you've gotta stay in jhon's place. No regret... This was my first ever trip to my dream place, new york. Because of jhon and gabriel, I had a wonderful and unforgettable trip of my life time and i'm gonna miss them for sure.

Jhon and Gabriel were fantastic. Everything was easy to handle, good communication, and stress free. They were very friendly and helpful during our trip to NYC (my first time there - so a lot to learn!) and patient while doing so. We were given plenty of privacy which allowed for a more relaxed trip. The metro, a supermarket and deli were all extremely close, affordable and convenient - allowing us to use the kitchen quite often to save some money. Thanks guys! If we are in the area again we would definitely enjoy staying at your place!

A welcoming trip to NYC/Brooklyn that would not have been the same without the charm and comfort that we experienced in Eric's apt in Bed Stuy. Friendly and accommodating, (and a steal for the price!) Eric was a perfect host.  A little hiccup with the water pipes in the dead of winter put no damper on our trip as Eric was on it right away- and the apartment had everything we needed and more. Easy to get to Manhattan and the jewels that Brooklyn has to offer. We would've stayed longer if we could, and hope to come back soon and stay again! Cannot thank you both enough- Warmly, Natalie and Mike

We are delighted with our stay at Jhon's place. He and his friend gave us the warmest welcome... they spoiled us and gave us excellent advice. The apartment is very clean and we felt at home. Metro station 6 is 1 minute from the apartment and the neighborhood is lively and safe. We will come back to them without hesitation and recommend them to our loved ones.

Joao was a gracious host and his place was a great steal for NYC. Close access to subway to get to Manhattan in 20 minutes or buses to go directly to Brooklyn. Bed was huge and very comfortable. It wasn't too cold surprisingly in winter, but the heat worked very well so it's definitely a good spot for the winter!

Overall we had a really nice stay. Jhon was really friendly and attentive. He made us a delicious breakfast twice during our stay. The only slightly negative points were that firstly we felt that the neighbours from the adjacent building could look inside the bathroom. Secondly we thought that the neighbourhood was slightly unsafe at night, which required us to take a taxi in the evnings. Overall we had a really nice stay though and lived Jhon‘s hospitality.

My dream of discovering NYC has come true... and Michael's apartment was a big part of it. 15 minutes by metro from Times Square (door to door), on the 2nd floor in a pretty, quiet street. Very comfortable and spacious apartment (we were 2 adults and 3 teenagers), well-equipped kitchen and good bedding, with a nice decor as a bonus! The rooms are on the garden side with the singing of birds when you wake up (no shutters). It was nice to come back and curl up in this bright accommodation after long days of walking through Manhattan. Metro, shops, Starbucks and a few restaurants within a 200m radius. No feeling of insecurity in the neighborhood and very appreciable calm at night. We chose peace and space rather than the center of Manhattan and will keep this address in mind for next time. Thanks again to Michael for his welcome, his gospel research and gluten free addresses and the responses to the numerous emails preparing for our trip..

On a quiet street in Brooklyn, we were made very welcome by Eric and Justin. We found a spacious, clean apartment with everything we needed to be rested and well settled as soon as we arrived after a long flight. The best, the fridge with some foodstuffs and the welcome little one on the slate! Really the best! 10 minutes from the metro, NETFLIX available with some films in French, so if in the future we travel to NYC again, this is where we will return.

Christine is a very gracious host and the rooms are wonderful and exactly as pictured. The beds are comfortable and this is is surely the pleasantest bathroom in Brooklyn. South Slope is a great neighborhood, too: quiet and shady with everything you might need in walking distance + easy subway access. I would be happy to stay in Christine's home again.

My wife and I spent six nights in the apartment. It was really nice and we had a great time during our visit.   The apartment matched the description and our expectations. The bedroom was spacious, the living room and bathroom was really nice and the kitchen was well equipped. Eric and Justin had put some breakfast-stuff in the fridge together with som emergency food in the freezer. That was something unexpected which really made us feel welcome.  The apartment was nicely furnished and decorated. It was clean and had everything we needed.  The surroundings was quite nice. A little bit rough around the edges (Eric's description), but we never felt unsafe. A few minutes walk to the subway which takes you downtown or uptown Manhattan without having to change train. Grocery stores and restaurants for breakfast, lunch or dinner nearby.  Eric and Justin were really great hosts and they made sure we felt welcome. We got quick responses from Eric when we e-mailed.   We can recommend this place for exploring NY. Great place and great hosts!

The host confirmed the reservation and was supposed to provide the code for key lock 3 days prior to check-in. When that didn’t happen I tried contacted him (DM, called, contacted customer service and they tried multiple times over the next 24 hours) but he never responded. I ended up in a middle of NYC with two suitcases and no place to stay, while I also have work meetings to attend and show to organize. It’s been a nightmare to find another place on such short notice and really irresponsible. I recommend you find another place to stay as this could be a scam. Although AirBnb refunded me in full, nobody compensated me for staying in a more expensive and less convenient location because that’s the only thing I could find in less than a day notice. Horrible experience.

Ephraim was a wonderful host. You can tell he is kind and gracious through and through - I can't stress how important that is when u share a space with someone. I would recommend this place to anyone. It's not fancy. In fact, it's just as you see it in the description - but it's certainly good for the price. Thank you Ephraim for everything

First of all I cannot thank Jefry enough for his trust because it was actually not me that stayed at his place but a friend who needed accomodation at very short notice and didn't have an Airbnb account. Jefry responded to my request immediately and communication with him was just great! He also proved flexible when arrival times changed unexpectedly, which was very much appreciated :) Thanks so much! My friend was very happy staying at his place, which is in a great location, and told me to especially stress here that Jefry is a wonderful host, a really great person, always available and very very helpful.  If I should ever plan a trip to Manhattan myself I will most definitely contact Jefry! Thank you so much again for all your  help Jefry and for making my friend's stay in your cozy home such a wonderful experience!

We arrived in NYC more than 7 hours late due to our flight, and yet it was with a smile that Jennifer welcomed us. While it's cold outside, the door opens into a cute little apartment, very cozy and warm. We quickly took advantage of the comfortable bedding. To visit Manhattan, the apartment is ideally located because it is very close to 2 subway stations. The neighborhood is pleasant and you can walk there at any time without any problem. Moreover, Jennifer presents her good addresses near the apartment. The latter is well equipped, we lacked nothing. Finally Jennifer is very accommodating with logistics, keys, luggage... We recommend this address.

We had an amazing experience !!!The apartment was perfect  for our family and the neighbourhood  was great,lots of useful shops and subway close by, makes it a perfect destination to experience New York.Jennifer was great with providing us with a stress free arrival and always available if needed.We would most definitely recommend this apartment and would love to come back in the future!!!!

Jennifer is a charming hostess who was very patient in waiting for our arrival given the delay of our flight. The accommodation is a little far from JFK, but in a very quiet area from which it is very easy to access the center of Manhattan by the nearby subway. Additionally, the proximity to Central Park in good weather is another plus. Everything was ready when we arrived: bedding, towels, soaps, etc. Attention to detail: electrical conversion plugs for US sockets. A place to recommend for discovering Manhattan.

The house is very nice, and has a very comfortable bed. At the same time, it has a kitchen with all the accessories one needs to cook. As for the bathroom, it has a good shower since the water comes out very well. Regarding the neighborhood, it is very quiet... during the day it is very pleasant to go for a walk there and at night, although there are not many people on the streets, I have not felt unsafe. It has a deli on the corner open 24 hours and several restaurants near the house. In addition, 2 blocks from the apartment, there are two subway stations through which several lines pass and there are also bus stops that make it very easy to get to the central points of Manhattan. Without a doubt, I recommend Jennifer's house because in addition to being very complete and welcoming, she was always making sure that everything was fine. It is the first time I have rented through this page, and it was a great experience!!

Vance's place was a great value. She was very pleasant, the space was clean and safe, and you can't beat the location. We were able to park on street on the same block for free (No parking Mon and Thurs from 11:30-1:00), and we could get anywhere in the city easily.  The other comments that mention the space being small and her apartment being unlocked are true, but a) every space in NYC is small and this was by no means specifically small, and b) the building's front door locks. At no point did I feel unsafe. The neighborhood is not sketchy whatsoever and I felt comfortable walking there day or night.  Vance had towels ready for us, a closet to store our stuff in, a plug strip near the bed, and everything we needed to rest our heads at night. If you're looking for a place to hang out and lounge around I might suggest looking elsewhere, but you really cannot beat this spot for a place to sleep when you're out and about all day.

Booked because of great reviews, which are well deserved. Great location, terrific value, a guide to local restaurants and amenities provided, and a host that communicates and is highly responsive. Can’t stress enough how great the neighborhood is and how accessible to subway and other transportation, and how wonderful it was to have such a super host.

Kyla is such a great host!! My sister and I spent our Thanksgiving in NYC and lived in her apartment for 3 nights. One night, we came back late. It was dark outside. We were scared walking back on the street. I texted her asked whether she can pick us at exit of subway. She said yes without hesitation! We appreciated that a lot! And her apartment is a lovely place to live.

Jennifer's apartment is great for visiting NY, a few steps from several subway lines and everything you could need (restaurants, stores...) It can be a little noisy at night but otherwise everything was perfect. Jennifer is an available host who was attentive and allowed us to leave our luggage until it was time to leave because we had a late flight.

Close to two subway stations that service Times Square and downtown locations (walk from stations is a little sketchy in the dark, but never really felt at risk; just be vigilant). Adequate grocery store nearby. Accommodations are comfortable and spacious for 2 people. Comfortable bed. Stocked kitchen cooking and serving utensils. Great shower temperature and water pressure. We felt safe and secure inside. Everything you could want/need for a vacation to NYC.

It is a very convenient area.  The whole area is a bit strong regarding the issue of marijuana, in all the streets in Nostrand and throughout everyone is smoking marijuana. and three houses towards Nostrand Avenue, every night a group of 3 or similar people get together to smoke crack. However, they do not mess with anyone nor are they dangerous. I arrived on that side on 3 occasions and I did not feel in danger. although it is a somewhat strong neighborhood. I never felt in danger. It is a strategic and very central location. I recommend it for the site no matter the rest. It is very close to everything. It is an area with many mice. although they say that in NY there are mice everywhere. I think I saw them all there.

Viveca was a great host for the 2 nights she stayed with us, we had the entire loft for 7 days. The apartment has everything you need with a private closed off space for yourself. 50 metres from the subway line. At night the walk from the subway can be a little scary, although we didn't have any problems and neither had Viveca - mainly cause it was deserted.  It's a great location for getting to Manhattan - you can get to Union Square in around 15 minutes.

My stay at Santina's was superb. I needed a comfortable, low-stress environment to live in while I completed a 2 week rotation at NYPH Cornell, and I got just that from her. She was very accommodating, offered me full use of her home, and responded promptly to any requests. She even rushed about to accommodate my last minute request to move in a couple nights early. Air conditioning was spot on during the muggy weather. I would recommend this experience to my friends.

I felt at home at Santina's place.  She seemed like a wonderful person to get to know, and Whiskers (the cat) was friendly and affectionate as well.  Her place was in a safe neighborhood close to many restaurants and grocery/drug stores.  I especially appreciated being within walking distance of two subway lines.  (I traveled by subway/train the entire time I was in NYC.)  Another perk: she lives on the first floor, so you don't have to lug your stuff up flights of stairs as I've heard you may have to do in other places in the city.  I'd definitely stay with her again if I were in the area. ^_^

We had a great stay! It is pretty close to the subway, so it's easy to go to Manhattan. The neighborhood does get dark and might feel a bit threatening / unsafe to walk at times. You can take a bus that stops half a block from the appartment though. Would recommend.

I stayed at Santina's for 11 days while in NY for a training, and couldn't have asked for a more relaxing, peaceful place. Santina was very hospitable and kind without being intrusive.The location  was great, check in with lock box easy and Santina always replied very quickly. The apartment needs a bit of TLC, but everything was in working order and for the price, it's  a steal. Especially if having a quiet space is important for you, I would highly recommend it.

I was a little afraid about the location in Harlem when I arrived at first. But it was safe enough to walk around at night. I can get access to Manhattan easily by my car or subway. Marie was so kind that we could   stay comfortably and enjoy Newyork. Thank you again.

We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in Harlem.   Having all the equipment for the baby on hand made the trip so much less stressful.    We also enjoyed experiencing what life as a real New Yorker feels like living in a residential district.  It was a joy to come home to the apartment in the evenings and get out of the chaos of the city.  Transport into and out of NYC is very good from here - we found the M2 bus at the end of the road a lifesaver as having a buggy on the underground was difficult with a lack of lifts and lots of steps.  The apartment is very well equipped and has everything that you could possibly need - we even did a little bit of washing whilst there of baby clothes and dried them.  Having the mezzanine floor meant we weren't all on top of each other and the additional bathroom also helped having 4 adults and 1 infant staying in the apartment. All in all a very memorable second trip to NYC.   Personal highlight going to the gospel church and being treated to a rendition of a song by a star who was currently on a Broadway show.
Good value and spacious accommodations, neighborhood up and coming but still a little sketchy at night for those traveling alone

This was probably the worst AirBnB that I have ever stayed in. First and foremost the description entirely off about the location. The location is not set in a fantastic neighborhood, rather the neighborhood is dirty and insanely smelly. You walk out and you smell nothing but trash. There are homeless people sleeping on the sidewalk and a few took the liberty to poop on our front door. Not only that but this neighborhood is certainly not the kind to bring a family around as my housemates and I were constantly afraid to leave the apartment after 11pm. Secondly coming into the house the fridge had mold, so getting ice was rather unhygienic and quite difficult. Halfway through the summer we realized that the wifi was being shared amongst two apartments, so even though it was the “fastest” wifi, it only properly worked in the upstairs apartment. When asked to fix it she brought in repair men and yes! The wifi was fixed for the upstairs apartment, downstairs still had terrible reception. It was to the point that we decided to just leave it and travel to our office amidst the pandemic. Lastly the rats in the 2nd floor, we were absolutely terrified that they would make their way downstairs. Thankfully we managed to buy a few bottles of raid and spray possible areas that could cause these rats to come up.   All in all, this experience was probably one of the worst. From false descriptions to poor hosting and horrible hygienic practices.

I stayed at the Aletia's place for 1 week and in general I am very happy with my choice - good price, great location and friendly host. My room had a lock with key which was one of my requirements to feel safe. The subway is literally 10 steps from the apartment building and it was absolutely not scary to come back home even at 2am for a girl on her own. It is about 20 minutes to get to the Times Square from Aletia's place which I think very close for NYC. Thank you Aletia for making my visit so great :) I felt real NY atmosphere.

The apartment is conveniently located just a 5 minute walk from the 1 train which will take you all the way to the South Ferry. It was so easy and effortless to travel from Lupi's apartment. As a single female, I never felt threatened or scared coming back "home" late at night, although I didn't return later than midnight. The bedroom was clean with a very comfortable bed and 2 mirrors and enough hanging space and hangers. The bathroom was also clean with good shower pressure and nice warm water to warm up after a day out in a very cold NYC. There were other travelers in the house, but everyone was respectful and kept the areas clean. I also never waited to use the bathroom, which is shared with the other tenants. Overall a great and comfortable stay, with all the basics one might need for a 4 night stay. Thank you Lupi!

This place was amazing! Lupi was so responsive and so nice! The space was just like the pictures and so clean! As a young adult, I never felt scared or unsafe in the room or the apartment or the neighborhood outside! It was amazing! Highly recommend!!

Aletia hosted a great room, on the upper west side of Manhattan. The room was clean- hardwood floors swept and surfaces wiped down. She's got great insight on creating a "home" for the traveling, and really goes out of her way to create just that. I felt very welcome, and enjoyed our conversations!  The place is right on top of the Subway route 1, so its pretty simple to get anywhere downtown with ease. The area surrounding has enough going on where I never felt unsafe while traveling. Plus for the price of staying- hard to beat!
Just an incredibly warm and comforting experience. With kids and dogs things can be very stressful, David and Janet’s House was a welcoming refuge.

This place is great! Subway is right at the corner of the street and takes you directly to Times Square. The area is ok, the building looks great, both on the inside and on the outside.  This was my first Airbnb experience and i was a bit afraid but everything was perfect.  Aletia is a great host, very helpful and a quick responder to all of our questions.  If i come again to New York i will want to stay at her place so i would definitly  recommend her! ❤️

We stayed two nights December 30th & 31st 2012. There is a serious problem will the shower.  The water temperature fluctuates suddenly from scalding hot to ice cold. The problem is with the old plumbing in the building and with the mixer valves in the shower.  We both were scalded more than once while taking a shower. This issue is not acceptable and is especially dangerous for unsuspecting children.  We do not recommend that apt for anyone until the shower problem is resolved.  We would not have booked it had we known in advance that the shower did not work. We both wanted to leave the next morning, but we couldn’t find anything available or affordable for New Year’s Eve.  The location is good for the subway, parking is easy and free, the bed is comfortable. The lobby of the building is run down and dirty. Nataliya is a friendly host but she should have been upfront about the shower (before booking).

We were delighted with Gabriela's apartment for our one week stay in Brooklyn. The place is clean and spacious, and very comfortable for two people. There's a cute garden in the back, and the morning light into the bedroom is gorgeous. The neighborhood is charming and felt very safe. It's primarily residential, but nearby Williamsburg has several great bars and restaurants worth a visit. There is a bit of a walk to the metro station, but I suspect visiting NYC, you're going to get quickly accustomed to at least a small walk anywhere. Once to the train, it's a quick, easy ride into the city. I'd definitely recommend this home to any friend visiting New York.

Unfortunately this accommodation left much to be desired.   Our experience was nothing but unfortunate from start to finish. Upon check in we noticed pockets of dust and dirt throughout the property, hairs on towels and sheets, the beautiful drapes in the pictures were ripped down the middle, as well as stains and grease in the kitchen. In the following days, we discovered mould in the coffee pot, and worse of all a USED condom down the side the bed. Upon this discovery, we left the accommodation.   Communication was slow with co-host Monique, sometimes waiting hours for responses. Another clean was offered but the problems weren’t resolved.   When I eventually spoke directly with the host Tracey, she was very apologetic, which we appreciated, and assured us this had never happened before.   With that being said, this issue took 3 days out of our 8 day trip in Brooklyn causing unnecessary stress and incurring much greater costs to us to stay in another accommodation last minute.

To begin with, the area where it is located is not very good, although it is true that it is close to a station, the place seems a little dangerous and good in the case of the host, the truth is that at all times the atmosphere felt heavy, considering that this was my first experience with Airbnb, I consider it to be the last

Traveling with my Fiancé... Looked for a last minute Airbnb in Nyc. Found a steal with Evelyn. Prime location in the west village Easy coordinating keys. The reason it was available and a steal is the possibility of no hot water. The heater had broken. Evelyn was totally transparent about this. We belong to an upscale gym that has location all over the city so it wasn't an issue for us. There was one slight issue prior to our arrival the workers had been in the apartment and had left a slight mess. But Evelyn was quick to react and had a cleaning service come everyday as a consolation. Very kind of her. I believe she was on vacation herself somewhere so this was quite amazing she steeped up as she did. Definitely would stay again. The apartment is a studio... Low ceilings. But very charming.

TERRIBLE. UNPLEASANT. CONFUSING. (mood swings?)  I don't usually leave a review like this but man, my stay at Christopher's apartment was the only negative thing during my week in NYC.  This was my first but probably my last time staying at a shared studio/apartment. Trying to stay objective here, but what bothered me the most was his attitude. Yes, on the first day he was welcoming, still, I can recognize his tone was not fully friendly.  He is arrogant, without saying it, it makes you feel like he's doing you a favor. Hey, this is after a service, where both parties agree to give/receive service.  Well by the second night he was bothered if I ask a question. I was never in the apartment. I'd leave early, really early, and come back late. So I really don't know what bothered him.  Anyways, just a word for those checking this place out. Spend a little more and avoid this place.   Other people already said it in the reviews, apparently, I was not careful enough to read them all, but among the things, you can expect on top of the obvious, shady neighborhood,  inexact address, an apartment that hasn't been properly clean in a while, to say a few.  Christopher made me feel unwelcomed starting on the second night, was very rude when I  asked basic questions,  and was always in the house, so there was never a chance to try to rest and not feel unwelcomed.  P.S Christopher, when you reply to this review, just don't try to defend yourself with the basic things that a decent Airbnb host does. That's a given and is the least one can expect. The main problem, in my opinion, is your attitude, plain and simple.  Yes, you had times where it appeared like you were a decent host but others when you were unbearable.  Anyway, I am glad this is over and I am back home.

Evelyn’s apartment isn’t the most fancy, but the location is fantastic. If you’re okay with a tiny place, that’s old and cozy and you just need somewhere to sleep, you’ll be fine. I really can’t stress how great the location was though! Got to meet Evelyn and she was really cool too!

Jen's apartment is really your home away from home. Likewise the apartment, the room is very spacious and very clean. The bed is extremely comfy and noises during the night are not intense, so you can have a good night's sleep. The AC works well and cools you down from a hot day in the city. The bathroom is very nice too. Jen further gives you some space in the fridge, which is definitely great to store some groceries. In general, the apartment is located in a very safe neighborhood, I never felt unsafe when I walked home late. It's also not far away from supermarkets, restaurants, Chinatown, cinema and many interesting places. A bus stops just in front of the house, the metro is around 10min walk from the house. Your host Jen is extremely helpful and gives useful tips on a variety of topics. So I'd say this place is definitely worth a visit and I couldn't have had a better stay.  Highly recommend it.

Wiebke is very patient and kind. She left me a greeting card with an informative direction upon my arrival. Staying in her place was a wonderful and unforgettable experience. This spacious and lovely apartment has a perfect location. You get to walk around and see the most vibrant part of New York City. The apartment itself has everything you need. I really enjoyed sitting by the window with some music and breeze. The two cats Mata and Jomo are absolutely adorable although they tried to steal my food sometimes. They made this trip very healing and unique. This apartment will be my first choice when I return to the city.

Autumn was very helpful and always very quick in responding our questions&needs. The room was quite comfortable with its own bathroom. Although there is no sink in it, the one at the next door was almost always available so no worries. Although at the beginning I was suspicious about the location, we liked the neighbourhood. Its safe and vibrant. We liked especially the old residential buildings on the way to the subway station along the Washington ave. Overall, this was our first airbnb experience and it was definitely encouraging for our future trips.

The apartment is lovely, strategically placed and full of grace and atmosphere — a soulful haven in a lively neighborhood . On the other hand, the whole communication process has been difficult and stressful, though we believe Barry himself is not responsible for the letdown, and things will surely improve. Overall, we absolutely recommend host and place.

I had a pleasant stay in Autumn’s Airbnb. She provided clear check in/out instructions. The rococo room is as listed; the full bed and pillows are extremely comfortable, everything was spotless clean, there were plenty of towels, toilet paper, toiletries (shampoo, conditioner and body wash) and mirrors. Though it was really hot and there is no way to control the heating, I used the AC window unit to cool the room down. I used both the room bathroom (it doesn’t have a sink) and the shared bathroom that is right outside the room. There was minimal noise from the other neighbors.  I found the location to be very convenient. The building is located in a quiet street, half a block away from a busy avenue where there are tons of options to get food and drinks. It did not feel unsafe to walk around, even at night. The G line subway is around 10 mins away (walking); it usually takes 40-45 mins to get to Manhattan.  I’m overall satisfied with and recommend Autumn’s airbnb.

Overall, I can't give Marianne a good review. To be fair the house is clean with good access to public transportation. I appreciated the free coffee in the morning. It might be good in the short-term. However, I never  felt welcome. Guests are generally treated as an inconvenience. The unspoken rule is that guests should stay in their rooms as much as possible. They aren't tolerated in the living and barely in the kitchen. Although it says full access to kitchen, guests are discouraged from using it. Most likely she won't make room for you in her packed, full-size family fridge either. She charges $10 per load of laundry which is higher than any laundromat around. Additionally, since Marianne doesn't have a bedroom herself and sleeps on the couch, she stores all her clothes in her guests' rooms, meaning that every time she wants to change her clothing, she will come in your room when you arent there. Opening a drawer full of her personal items can be rather awkward as a friend of mine observed. Personally, I left early. After I handwashed three dresses in the sink and hung them in the bathroom and adjusted the aircon, Marianne's son thought it was appropriate to yell at me at 1140 pm at night for these offenses when I had work the next day. That's when I realized the situation was toxic and left. Before leaving, I chatted with the other tenants about how we didn't like living there and bonded over it. It was a stressful situation, but I couldn't ask for better hosts that the ones I am currently staying through AirBnB. They cooked us breakfast before we had to meet with Marianne's son to convince him to give us back the money we were owed. The contrast couldn't be higher.  Overall, only stay here short term and only if you can't find anything else. Also, if you pay for a guest to stay with you, don't give money in advance. You deserve to have wonderful, welcoming people to be your hosts, like the ones I have now.

It was wonderful staying in Luis's apartment! He kindly left towels and extra sheets and blankets for us and had everything we could possibly need while staying the weekend. The place was very clean, nice and warm and incredibly convenient to the subway. Luis was also very flexible in meeting us, which makes for a stress-free and comfortable stay! I would definitely recommend a stay here. Thanks so much!

Me and my best friend stayed there for a month, we had the best time in New York. Luis was really helpful and a great host. Apartment looks exactly as the pictures. The bed takes most of the floor space in the room but it is really comfortable. Overall the apartment was really clean which is really important.   Apartment was really close to shops, subways stations, cafes, bars etc. It was a really safe neighborhood, as two girls, we were never afraid of coming home late.   Couldn't ask for a better place to stay! I can easily recommend Luis' place to anyone looking for a comfortable stay in NYC. Thank you Luis :)

Art and Ed are lovely, they really know how to make guests feel welcome. The apartment is so close to the Highline (a real highlight and retreat from the pace of the City), which makes the location wonderful. The room is very comfortable, the bathroom total luxury, and the rest if the apartment is gorgeous too. The hosts' living space is upstairs which gives them, as well as guests, plenty of privacy.   Everything was wonderful regarding communication and checking in/out, all easy and stress-free. The breakfast was a welcome touch too! Perfect for a slower paced start to the busy NYC days.  My stay couldn't have been better and I was really glad to be able to sit down with Art on my last morning and have a great chat. I'd definitely visit again. No hesitation!

If you want to be centrally located in manhattan - If you want to stay with people who are truly interested in you having a fulfilling and low stress vacation - you really should consider Art and Ed's place in the heart of Chelsea.  It is right on the Chelsea HighLine, which is a terrific addition to a city that doesn't even need more reasons to visit!  Art and Ed could not have been more helpful to us.  It is like having a concierge in-house. If we had a question, we had a human version of Google to check in with!  Also - if cleanliness is important to you - this location will make you so happy!  It also feels great to not worry about your personal belongings as you do in hotels.  If you have not tried this sort of housing in NYC, Art and Ed's place is a perfect start.

Our family (mom, dad, 4-year-old, and 10-month-old) recently stayed in David's apartment for a month while repairs and renovations were done on our place, which is nearby. David was an extremely gracious host. He was kind and laid-back during our stressful relocation process, which really helped alleviate some of our stress. And the apartment was great. It's right across from an entrance to the park--I took the kids for long walks on the nature trails, and we loved opening our curtains every morning and seeing the green meadow and the fall leaves. Now that we're back in our home, we've stayed in touch with David, whom we're glad to have as a neighbor!

We stayed at Greer's place for a week and had a really nice time. The room is spacious, the beds are very comfortable. The appartment looks nice and clean. It is also within easy reach of the A line subway, which makes it easy to go wherever you want to go. Inwood is a nice area, it has some nice places to get a coffee or something to eat. The area is peaceful and we never felt unsafe. Greer is very friendly, she makes you feel welcome in her appartment and can help you find your way around. We definitely recommend staying at her place!

I booked Alison's place last minute due to a flight cancellation out of Laguardia.  At 5pm, American airlines told me I wasn't going to make it out that night, but 6:30pm, I was comfortably sitting in Alison's apartment.  The space is absolutely GORGEOUS, so wonderful in fact I was sad I only could stay one night!! Very clean, bright, spacious, excellent laundry machines, smells great and everything is labelled and laid out clearly for guest use.    Alison's place turned what could've been a very stressful experience into a phenomenal and calming bonus night in Brooklyn!  I highly recommend and can't wait to book again for a long term stay.

Had a wonderful experience staying at Alison's sweet Brooklyn apartment! She was great at communication and made my stay very easy and stress free. Will most definitely be staying at her apartment again the next time I spend a weekend in Brooklyn. Thanks again, Alison!

We were three females under 30 travelling together and I would like to emphasise we felt very unsafe when coming home later at night( i.e 10-12pm), with an incident on the sidewalk outside of the closest subway station, my friend was forcefully shoved, adding to our nervousness. We put this down to being travellers until we had 2 taxi drivers and 2 Brooklyn locals (on the subway) express concern as to the area we were staying. Whilst  Alison and her husband were very friendly and responsive and the apartment clean and tidy, I would not recommend you stay there.

I'm giving this a 3-star rating--because with a few "upgrades" this could be a superior experience. This is a spacious and bright garden-level apartment with lots of original details -- and there is a lot to like. But, overall, it needs a bit of "spit and polish."  - A fully-equipped kitchen if you want to reheat or prep a meal. Downside: no dish soap so we couldn't wash our own dishes :--(  Maybe it was there but I couldn't locate it.  - Coffeemaker AND french press! Downside: if you need coffee first thing like I do, you better stop and buy some beans before you check in-- there's a great coffee shop on Fulton where you can buy them.  - Washer & Dryer! We were here for 6 nights so it was great to wash clothes.  - No washcloths, but plenty of extra pillows, blankets, etc. We didn't need, but nice to have them there. No washcloths, though.  - TV. There isn't cable so you can't catch the news (would have been nice as the Brussels attacks had just happened) but there is a DVD player and Alison was kind enough to bring newly released movies.  - Cool vintage clawfoot bathtub.  Perfect for a leisurely bath (or shower). Downside: The tub and sink weren't as clean as I'd like. After running the NYC Half-Marathon, I wanted a bath and had to scour the build-up off the bottom of the tub. Bathroom sink needed a little love, too. And a sink-stopper would be great (I couldn't find it, perhaps it was there) for face washing.  Downside: there were little used bars of soap in the bathroom and leftover toiletries (i.e. facial toner).  - If you need it, bring a magnifying make-up mirror -- as the mirror in the bathroom is small and for us "older" gals, it's hard to see what you're doing.  - Nice notebook with all info about neighborhood. Best shops / restaurants are to the right on Fulton.

We very much enjoyed our stay at Alison and Dane's. Communications were clear and prompt right from the start.  The apartment is exactly as pictured and is very clean. The bed was quite comfortable, although it didn't look like it would be!  The neighborhood is up-and-coming, with lots of nice little restaurants in the area. We walked everywhere and even coming home late did not feel unsafe. the place is in easy walking distance to a lot of other great neighborhoods and to Prospect Park. There are several City Bike kiosks in the area, but please take the time to read and understand their use policy.
