Greer hosted us warm way with refreshments after a long trip. She had everything planned for our stay: water bottles, umbrellas, adapters, hairdryer, pen... And we gave advice to our movements. Room had many storage drawers, and beds were comfortable. The room was fortunately very well air-conditioned. Greer is a nice person and interesting, we were able to share our experiences and points of view sometimes in french. It was a pleasure to meet her! Her cats are adorable (I am afraid of cats in normal time). Her apartment is located 30-40 minutes from Time Square, the area is calm, many amenities (supermarkets), we have not been frightened to cross it the night. The Park is awesome, the street is nice, we feel well. We hope to come back one day! Thank you Greer. Sabrina, Fabien and Lilian.

We had a very pleasant stay at Greer's and she (and her cat) made us feel very welcome.  Greer is extremely well prepared in hosting tourists from clear guidelines of house rules, to tips about navigating around the otherwise could-be-confusing city.  After her briefing we felt completely at ease travelling around NYC.  Her instructions that guide us to her place from the airport was extremely clear as well.  The neighbourhood is also good and not too scary to go back even after a late night.  Overall it was an enjoyable stay and the cat was a delightful company :)

Suzanne and her boyfriend are nice and good hosts. The room corresponds to the description and the photo. The house or apartment is a bit older. This is precisely why the apartment has a cool flair.   Many Puerto Ricans, Cubans, Mexicans and people with South American roots live in this neighborhood. For us Germans it seemed a bit unsafe at the beginning. Over the course of the week, it turned out to be one of the coolest areas in Brooklyn. There are many dining and shopping options. The metro is close by and the people are super nice!

This is my second time being hosted by Suzanne.  She's such a nice person and always willing to make sure you're comfortable and taken care of.  She cares about her guests and goes out of her way to make sure you have a stress free experience.  It's a great place to stay,

The apartment looks exactly like in the pictures. It is a comfortable place with enough space for four people. Great to come back and chill here after a tiring day in town. The kitchen is well equipped and has everything you need to cook a meal. The neighborhood is great and full of Harlem history. You should not be worried about this location as it is safe, clean and comfortable. If you want to explore Harlem, this is your place to be. There are several stores within walking distance. Martin is a helpful host and communicates quickly. Even during our stay he responded immediately to any questions we had and helped us spontaneously wherever necessary. He is flexible with check in and check out time. The express subway lines got us to and from mid- and downtown easily. It takes only 10-15 minutes to lower Manhattan. Even getting back late night was no problem. We never felt unsafe walking from the subway station to the apartment. I would definitely recommend staying at Martin's place. Book it!

This was our first time using AirBnB and we could not have picked a better place. The apartment has literally everything you could ever need. Including a book full of places nearby and menus to restaurants. The apartment is very spacious and very comfortable. There’s even a washer and dryer for convenience and they provide detergent. We were scared that we would not be as comfortable here as a hotel because we didn’t know how private it would be, however it is way better than a hotel. It felt like we lived in our own apartment in Brooklyn. Bed sheets were very clean! She provides shampoos, conditioner, soaps, towels, literally everything you have in your own house.  Easy walk to two subways. And lots of convenient stores, grocery, liquor, and even a family dollar within walking distance. Sooooo glad we found Allison’s place! Highly recommend!-

A much darker appartment than on the pictures. Its situated in the half- basement/grund floor.   The backyard was unpleasant and could not be used in september. The appartment is I believe not so good for people with asthma because of bad ventilation. The entrance really need to be renovated. Maybe other people find it charming and bohemian chick - in that case the place is nice enough.
My stay was once again great. Martin and his amazing housekeeper were incredibly accommodating with my early arrival and departure times, which made the experience stress-free.

I stayed here to shelter-in-place while working for NYC’s COVID-19 response. This was honestly the perfect place to do my work as it was so quiet and cozy. The backyard space and general cute vibe of the apartment helped tons with the work stress. Despite the pandemic, there were still essential places  open that were very close by such as a pharmacy and grocery store (and a bakery that I bought a cake from to treat myself). The kitchen was fully equipped with what I needed to cook meals for myself, and I was pleasantly surprised by how nice the giant tub was. Thank you for bringing me comfort and peace in these chaotic times.

Excellent location - close to train to get you anywhere really- is really what I can't stress more on! My husband and I stayed here with a 1 year old and we absolutely loved it! Alison provided a high chair for us and baby slept with us (which was okay even though he usually sleeps in a crib). Honestly was able to visit the Nature and Manhattan children museums, central park by train easily with stroller or carrier. We walked to prospect zoo and Brooklyn children museum (~20 - 30 minutes). Took train to Brooklyn bridge - visited a ton of restaurants and lots of good picks by the house. Very close grocery stores for baby items we needed for our son. We did have to reach out on the kitchen light but it wasn't a big deal. The light would sometimes not turn on - Allison was very responsive though. Lastly, the white noise machine came super handy for us and I absolutely loved the open kitchen to use for a crawling baby :)

Spoiler alert: It wasn't a good experience.  The good things first, the location was really good, its close to the metro and a close to a good variety of shops. Also is at a walking distance of Prospect Park, the Brooklyn Botanical Garden, Brooklyn Library, the Brooklyn Museum among others. Also the flat was clean and free from unpleasant odors. The bed where generous in size and comfy.  The Bab things now, it seems that the hostess became vegan recently and tries to impose that to others, to an uncomfortable level.  Noises, if you spend 8 hours walking, when you got to the flat you want to rest, but not here, you have to withstand people singing in the hallways until 4AM in the morning or later. Shower, if you feel like 'washing' yourself with pressure washer, this is your place, the pressure of the water so high and so focused in a tiny spot that might hurt. If I rent a complete flat is to have comforts accordingly, like use real dishes and cutlery, well, not here, the hostess as an after thought forbid me to use that. There's more but I think that I told more than enough to keep you away from this place.

I had a really great stay at Giorgia and Bens place in Williamsburg. Right on the L train stop at Lorimer St, this apartment is a perfect launching place into Manhattan, as well as the great food joints in Brooklyn.  Giorgia was away when I stayed there, but Ben made me feel very at home and was a really good guy to meet. He even lent me his old phone after my phone was stolen in Cuba!!!!  You have a really comfy bed in your own room, and plenty of towels and soap etc. Its a nice basement apartment that is surprisingly quiet from street noise. And the bathroom, along with the whole apartment, is clean and tidy.  Plus a big TV!!  So all in all it's a great place in a great location. I can't recommend this apartment enough.

As a first timer to airbnb and to New York my partner and I could not have asked for a better experience! Literally a minute walk to the L train and surrounded by nice bars and great/affordable reatausrants. We never felt unsafe and although Ben and Giorgia were not there when we arrived they were readily available to help with any questions we had. We had plenty New York books and maps in our room which was a really nice touch and eeb though it was really hot out the AC in the room was great! The place was really clean and pictures are exactly what you get. I would definitely recommend to anyone looking for a neat place and location to stay while in New York.

Giorgia & Ben were nice and the appartment cosy ! You can go out in the garden wich is nice in NYC! You have less than 1 mn by feet from the subway station (L). It´s a hipster's neighbourhood with a lot of bars! Giorgia & Ben had to leave for 2 days and left us the appartment, they made us feel like home. And the dog is not dangerous, he's sweet!

Staying at giorgia's & bens' place made our holiday even better! Even though they werent there when we arrived, this was The warnest welcome ever with a personal video and a personal note On The table. Their dog 'Sky' is just fantastic, he gas stolen our hearts! If you are Looking for something different and you want to feel home, I would Definitely recommend you to stay over at Giorgia & ben. Guys, thnx for The places you've told us to go to, good luck with everything!!   Cheers Thomas & Jill

I had quite a bad experience staying at Hannah's apartment.  The three primary issues are:  1) Mold and gross conditions in the bathroom. The shower has a leaking hole above it that has evidently been growing for months and most probably has mold. This is unsanitary. No guest should have been allowed to stay here with this condition, as it may be unsafe; I was concerned for my health. Additionally, the shower curtain was also covered in mold when I moved in. When I communicated about this, Hannah was responsive in getting a new one. This can of course be fixed, but Hannah will need to take the time to do so prior to having further guests stay.  2) Disruptive and intrusive train noise. The train passed by approximately 100 feet from the main bedroom window, and goes by every 20-30 minutes. I saw this described in a previous review, so I asked Hannah about it prior to booking the apartment – she assured me that she doesn't even notice it and that it wouldn't be an issue. Lo and behold, I did not sleep the first 3 nights, which really messed me up for that week. Fortunately, by closing the bedroom door and sleeping in the interior bedroom with earplugs, I was able to sleep. But this means that I had no sunlight. And the train continued to pass through all day every day, which you can hear and feel throughout the apartment. I have no doubt that after months of staying there, you might become accustomed to it, but for a temporary stay, this was very disruptive to me. It was disingenuous to assure me that this was not an issue, and future guests should be aware that unless you can tune out loud train sounds every 20-30 minutes day and night, you may have difficulty at this apartment.  3) The kitchen utensils were in an unacceptable state for cooking. I paid extra to have Hannah set up, included a pot and pan in poor condition whose teflon was coming off and got into my food. I stopped cooking after a few days.  When I reported these issues, Hannah said she hadn't heard about these issues from previous guests. The problem with this way of thinking is that relying strictly on what previous guests have said, is insufficient; instead, what is necessary is for a host to spend time in the apartment and consider it deeply from a guest's perspective. If this had been done, the gaping hole in the shower that is leaking intermittently (and highly likely moldy), as well as the moldy shower curtain, and the disruptive train, and the unusable kitchen cooking utensils, would have been evident and addressed prior to my stay. A host who is providing a professional experience must experience the apartment from the guest's perspective and be vigilant about issues rooted in their own personal, direct experience.   For the most part Hannah is a responsive and clear communicator. She means well, and I could tell she wanted for me to have a positive experience, but unfortunately this was not the case. I moved out early and asked for a refund for my unused days, a request that she did not respond to until the day of check-out, 5 days later. I would have moved out even earlier but, given everything going on in life, between COVID-19, my work situation, and the logistics of moving my numerous possessions around, I did not have the time or energy to coordinate other accommodations and instead just hoped that my health won't suffer from the possible mold and that I would get enough sleep.

I strongly recommend to stay away from this place unless you have a very low rate, you travel without kids, you don’t need to sleep and the only thing you care about is having a roof on top of your head, no matter the condition of the flat.  We were supposed to stay 10 days for the holidays but had to move to an hotel after the first night because of the insalubrious condition of the flat and the noise that made sleep absolutely impossible, especially for the kids. Hannah refused any refund as she estimated it was our responsibility to check the flat before - her behavior (and especially the one of the male friend she brought with her to pick up the keys on day 2) became agressive when I refused to write on the Air bnb app that it was entirely my  fault if I don’t like the flat. I really hated feeling that unsafe because of an holiday rental and want to forget this experience as soon as possible.  Yet, I want to help others not being ripped off by an host and have their NYC experience being ruined by the disappointment of the place they stay at.  So here are some additional information. You will see similar evaluations in some comments, look in details, I was mislead by the positive reviews (difficult to believe these are real ones…) and oversaw the ones expressing what I experienced.  Location: - very convenient to get to Manhattan - 30 feet from an open metro station and path: impossible to sleep even with ear plugs in the first bedroom, potentially possible in the other room with ear plug but kids woke up every 30min all night… - it is like sleeping in a metro station  Flat: - very poor state: paint falling and missing in some places, bathroom and kitchen looks unhealthy - not settled to welcome guests. Untidily put, full of host stuff, no place for guest clothes, bath products, etc… Hannah did free one shelf in the fridge when I asked her… so nice  - as an example, one used disposable mask was even hanging in the entry… - despite what is written in the description, Hannah isn’t comfortable with guest cooking in the kitchen which she « clarified » 3 hours before we were supposed to arrive (I asked the question one month before when I was still on time to cancel the reservation…)  I know that theoretically, this flat can be rented but make sure you read all the comments, don’t be mislead with the overall rating which doesn’t reflect the very poor level of the flat
Not knowing the area, I felt a bit unsafe and arriving after dark didn’t help. All in all it turned out to be a good stay.

Anja was a great host, we would have checked in with her again at any time. We were in New York for a week in total and whenever we had questions, she always helped us with tips etc. She's hardly at home during the day, so we usually had the apartment to ourselves, but it wasn't at all unpleasant when she was in the apartment with us at the same time, on the contrary.  The apartment is in a great location and made a very neat impression on us. Gladly again at any time.

My stay with Raymond and Heather was the epitome of AirBnB experiences!  They are by far the nicest, friendliest and most welcoming hosts one could ask for.  It's no surprise their ratings are so high, and I am happy to give five stars to these superstars!  Heather is an absolute doll, and Raymond is by far one of the funniest people I have ever met.  Like tears rolling down my face, I can't breathe kind of funny.  An absolute joy and one of the greatest surprises of my vacation!  As for the room, it was very cozy and though it appears out in the open I never once felt like I didn't have privacy.  The bed is comfortable and the space is relaxing.  The location is not far from the subway and it's not too far to head into Manhattan. I didn't feel like I was out in the boonies at all. I explored a lot of Brooklyn on this trip so it was actually a perfect location for me.  I came home late often and never felt unsafe walking alone from the subway to the apartment.  Heather and Raymond are so awesome, I wish I could clone them and have every travel experience be as great as it was with them.  They are the best of the best and I feel so lucky to have met them and spent some time getting to know them.  They are awesome!  Thank you for making my vacation so much fun.  You guys are the best!!

A good option for budget traveller if you are just looking for a shelter and a place to have a shower. The area is like industrial area, many trucks passing through. Nothing to see and crap restaurants. Feeling unsafe and scary if coming back after midnight. Not really recommend for single female traveller. Other than that, far from centre, takes an hour to get to 42th street. No lift in the building, so you expect to carry your own luggage to climb to 4th floor. The place is dusty and the toilet smells. But the price is cheap, you pay what you get, fair enough. Having said that, the host is nice and welcoming.

I stayed here for 3 nights and had a chance to meet both Ray and Heather. I only spoke with Ray very briefly so I didn't really get a chance to get to know him and I did speak with Heather, who is very social and friendly. The apartment is small, but the living room had more than enough room to suit me. I was rarely in the apartment anyways so all I really needed was a place to crash and a place to shower. The apartment is about 5 blocks from the closest subway station so expect some walking. There are a ton of restaurants nearby and some shops. Even though the neighborhood doesn't look the most inviting, I never felt there was any sense of danger walking around at night. You do have to walk up 4 flights of stairs to get to their apartment and the walls can be a bit thin, so you can hear the neighbors and some outside noise, but it never kept me up or anything. Ray and Heather made sure to contact me the day before and day of the trip to make sure I got in just fine and seemed genuinely looking to be as helpful as possible. They also let me check in the morning right when I arrived in NY so I didn't have to wait till the afternoon, which was great. This place is a good value stay as NY can be expensive and also not too far away to a lot of great things in either Brooklyn or Manhattan.

Raymond and Heather were super welcoming Hosts! Very friendly :) I can't stress it enough how warm and welcoming they are!!   I was busy over my stay with many wedding events, so I didn't have much time to stay in the apartment - but it was great for what I was looking for: a safe place I could come back for some sleep, a shower, and a clean change of clothes to tackle the city with ;)  ALSO - it was 2 blocks from the F line (Metro) which was absolutely KEY for me!!

Thank you so much for your hospitality these past 10 days. This was my first Air BnB experience and it was a good one. Everyone else's comments helped me choose your place and they were accurate! Even though you both had crazy schedules leading into Christmas the little time I did spend with you enhanced my New York experience! You are both chilled out, friendly, positive, respectful souls. Your apartment is tidy, comfortable, makes a great base and the price was right. Although the bed is in your living room it is a private space and its a large room. I liked Ray's fish tank keeping me company! It was handy having unlimited wifi to map out my adventures and stay connected. The apartment is an easy 5 minute walk to the subway even with luggage, and as a single female I never felt unsafe even when returning late at night. The train lines that leave from the nearby subway are good lines to be on for tourists, you're not too far from the major sites. The Gowanus neighbourhood is dotted with great independent restaurants and shops. There's a coal pizza place and a gourmet pie place worth sampling. I especially liked the pretty shopping strip of 7th Avenue, Park Slope and the brownstone houses around there. Prospect Park (similar to Central Park) is walking distance and is a nice escape. I really liked the Wholefoods supermarket which is walking distance, so many options and a cafeteria space upstairs. I enjoyed being in a living, breathing Brooklyn neighbourhood and seeing how the locals lived. I can see the area turning 'hipster cool', it's beginning to happen already. Thanks again for everything. Especially to Heather for scoring me some Broadway tickets - an unexpected bonus!
Anja's place was great! The neighborhood was a little scary for two girls to go in and out at night time but was worth it since the restraunts around were all very tasty.

Anja was a wonderful host and the place was a great spot to come back to after exploring the city all day. The apartment is close to then B and D subway lines which get you close to all the major tourist attractions quite easily. There are also some great cafes and bars around!   Only downside was the homeless people outside the apartment building that made us feel slightly uncomfortable. But that’s the reality of a big city these days!
It's a pretty good place to stay! John gave us a lot great advices about nyc. However, there are some creepy ornaments on the wall which scared me at first lol. Overall, it’s a nice piece to stay!

Damian is very kind, available, and attentive, even if I did not have the opportunity to meet him, he constantly kept up to date. In addition, he is flexible, we had a late flight, he allowed us to stay in the apartment, until the time we wanted. The apartment is consistent with the photos, clean and very well located (3 metro stations 8 minutes walk). In addition, the neighborhood is lively, restaurants, shops, bars....No complaints, everything was perfect.

Raymond and Heather are wonderful hosts; they made my quick trip a lot less stressful than I was expecting with their helpful tips and lovely home. I was offered great food suggestions (was not disappointed!) and had an amazing time, would recommend them for anyone staying in the Brooklyn area!

Overall an unpleasant experience. I almost believed that the landlord was a kind and easygoing person as he acted very welcoming and friendly in the beginning. However, he was unkind and short-tempered when there was issue occurred. During my stay, there were two internet outages. The second one occurred when I was doing important work stuffs on my laptop. So I sent the landlord a message asking him to communicate with the internet provider to fix it. He talked with them and got back to me that the problem would be fixed in six hours. Six hours later the internet still was not fixed, he called me and was basically “Demanding” me to talk with the internet provider by myself and fix the problem on my own because he was busy and wanted to stay out of this. He kept saying that “ You have to be flexible on this” when the issue remained unresolved which sounds really disrespectful and irresponsible. Yes, it was not his fault that we had two 6-hours long internet outages when I need internet for working, but as a landlord, it was his responsibility to fix this problem. His attitude was surprisingly irritable and disrespectful. This was unfortunate because his sister Maryanne was such a nice lady and I had good time meeting her when she came visit. Otherwise about the place: 1. Bedroom windows are facing a major street so very noisy.  2. Cluttering in the pantry shelf and in the bathroom closet. Need to dig out a corner for my toothpaste and face washer.  3. The landlord came out of bathroom twice with upper body naked when he knew I was outside, which were really unpleasant.

Monica was a great host, she contacted me one day prior to my arrival to make sure I would be able to enter the apt. The room was clean and as described, and everything was prepared when I arrived. The apt itself and the bathroom were also neat and tidy. She had a folder ready with the Wifi key (very important ;)) and some tips on what to see and where to eat in the neighborhood.  The location of the apt is also great, just two minutes from the "Prospect Park" metro station. In general I felt pretty safe in the neighborhood and wasn't afraid coming back to the apt even late at night.  One of the downsides was the noisy road facing the room. Also, there was a large fridge in the room, which started humming intermittently at night.  Earplugs solved this problem for me, though ;)

Our family of 8 stayed here for four nights. Delightful experience. Subway stop two blocks away. Easy access to Manhattan. Grocery, fresh produce, spirits, bakery and drug store all within two to three blocks. Ari and his father made us feel most welcome. The apartment offered a washer/dryer for my husband to do his laundry, a kitchen for my son the chef to prepare us lovely meals, and a large table for all to gather each evening to share their tales of the day. Perfect retreat from the hustle of the city. Highly recommend.

The place is exactly as described in the advertisement. The stay was impeccable, the services were optimal and the space was excellent. The subway station is very close, around the corner, and takes you to downtown Manhattan in 20 minutes. The area is a little busy, but I didn't feel it was dangerous. There are lively but respectful people in the neighborhood. Although we didn't talk much, Patricia was always attentive to our stay and answered our questions quickly. We were satisfied and highly recommend the stay.

The apartment and neighborhood both were as noted in the pictures....clean, neat, and safe. We brought our own towels, paper towels, disinfectant spray, detergent, etc but did not need to because Ari had EVERYTHING readily available and in abundance.   The most important thing for our family was neighborhood safety and we felt the safety from day one. The subway station was about 2 blocks away; we would get back home really late but would find numerous people still out walking and no one bothered us or made us feel unsafe.  Rite Aid was literally right behind the apartment and an awesome Caribbean restaurant, Jemz, was 2 blocks away. There were also other food places nearby.   Ari was extremely detailed and helpful when needed. We would definitely return to this location. We felt right at home for the week we were there.

Monica's place was great. Very clean, spacious by New York standards, and in a great location - convenient to coffee, drug/convenience stores, the subway, and of course Prospect Park. The street was a little bit loud at night, but I don't know of any place in NYC where the streets are actually *quiet* on a Saturday night, so no big deal :) Monica provides a helpful guide in the room with her own opinions on local places to get food & drink, and places to see.

As a group of three, we recently stayed at Bob's apartment over an 11 day visit to NYC.  Don't let it's location scare you off, while it may be further north of the 'main' Manhattan district, it is absolutely no hassle with the apartment located right on the blue subway line.  We were absolutely thrilled on arrival, finding the apartment to be much bigger than we expected (even has a second bathroom!), in addition to a very modern, very lovely open living/kitchen/dining area that could comfortably seat six people.  Despite the fact we did not meet Bob in person, he was a very accommodating host, and prompt with answering any questions we had.  Upon visiting NYC again, would definitely consider Bob's apartment as a choice of accommodation again!

The room was pretty nice! 2bedrooms were large, the kitchen was well equipped, especially the livingroom was special with a lot of sunshine and comfortable large sofa.  Bob was kind enough to advise me how to live in this area. He paid attention to my comfortable life in Washington heights.  There are a lot of Hispanic people in Washington heights, but I think it is not so dangerous. 20 minutes by subway-express to the central of Manhattan.  You can spend a comfortable NY life here!

It was a good stay. The district is safe, the appartment is very nice, bright and full equipped. The garden should even be more attractive with a little more maintenance. But it was not a problem. Bob had been very reactive when we needed help or informations. We recommend this place.  Bon séjour chez Bob, qui a été très réactif lorsque nous avons fait appel à lui. L'appartement est vraiment agréable, spacieux, bien équipé, clair et propre. Le petit jardin est sympa, même si un peu laissé à l'abandon. Le quartier est tranquille, aucun sentiment d'insécurité, et bien relié au centre de Manhattan.  A 5 mn du métro, calme. Excellent endroit pour séjourner à deux ou quatre.

My girlfriend and I had such a great time in New York and some of our favorite moments were here at Sekiya’s place! The decor alone is inspiring and the accommodations were so comfortable. Super close to the metro, local coffee shops, and mini markets/convenience stores. Great location for exploring the Brooklyn area! She also had super quick communication for any questions we had! Traveling can be so stressful, so the ease of having a comfortable& easily accessible  place to stay was so worth it and we’ll appreciated .

The space is definitely an “oasis” the building was pretty sketchy outside of the apartment. While it was super conveniently located close to the trains, it’s not a great place to stay if you are travelling for work. The neighbours like their loud music throughout the night and are very heavy footed. So sleep is sparse without ear plugs.
Very cute place, love how modern it is & it’s conveniently right next to a bar called Night Shade

Carla and Ken’s lovely garden apartment was the perfect place for my long-term stay! Carla and Ken are amazing hosts — friendly, kind, and always available. In the midst of this pandemic, they are covid-conscious and compliant, and our communication prior to my arrival made me feel safe and secure that everyone was taking precautions. The apartment itself is sparkling clean and is more than spacious enough for two people to live AND work comfortably. On top of that, it’s fully-stocked with everything you might need for an extended stay in the city: a full kitchen with pots, pans, knives, and all the accoutrements; umbrellas and reusable shopping bags; laundry basket and laundry bag; really nice toiletries, soaps and lotions; towels and linens that lasted our entire stay. You name it, Carla and Ken have provided it! The North Park Slope neighborhood is vibrant and alive with outdoor dining, drinking, and shopping. The apartment is just minutes away from 5th Avenue and its many restaurants and shops, a huge grocery store, laundry facilities, a drug store and pharmacy, and just a 15 minute walk to Prospect Park. In short, my stay here was fantastic and I would not hesitate to stay here again. In fact, I look forward to coming back! Thank you so much, Carla and Ken!

Pros:  The inside of the apartment is very nice and clean, just like the pictures. Plenty of room for 2 people and their stuff. Nice little kitchen space and decent size shower. Nice decor and comfy bed. Would be a lovely little space if it weren't for the cons.  Host responded quickly and was willing to accommodate a late check-in, which I really did appreciate (although this was hands down the oddest airbnb check-in I've ever experienced.)  Cons:  I was not familiar with Queens, and so felt like I was completely blindsided by the kind of place we ended up in. Pictures did not give a clue since you only see the inside, and not the entrance or street it's on...  The description and reviews imply a safe and friendly neighborhood, HOWEVER, this Airbnb was tucked upstairs from a club, the entrance hidden behind a utility door on the main street, between the night club and a shop. When our Uber drive dropped us off, I thought we were at the wrong place, because there is no address on the unmarked metal door. The host should really post a picture of the entrance door from the street level (Liberty Ave) so that people from out of town know what they're getting into. FYI Saturday night had drunks passed out next to the door and insanely loud thumping music from the area all night. Was not friendly or safe for an airbnb-er from out of town... The unbelievably loud music kept us up until 2am both nights. Really bummed at the cost I spent on this, wish I had just paid the little more for a real hotel nearby.  TLDR: Inside was cute, but neighborhood and entrance to airbnb was super sketchy and loud music from drivers-by (seems common in the neighborhood) kept us up both nights.

Then I walked up the long four flights to enter the unit, and the keys didn’t work at all, so I had to enter the unit through another entrance, after finally getting another set of keys the next day, which was also upsetting!!😡😡 once I got into the unit, I noticed I had to walk through another persons room before I could enter the bedroom, which was also a bad sign, not knowing if there was another client in the unit. Later on that same night, my wife goes to the bathroom then she hears a voice that scared the CRAP out of her as she ran back to our bedroom in fear of her life, locking the door behind her!!!😡😡 So, we had to walk through and share this persons room/space in order to get to the restroom which is totally unacceptable!!!😡😡😡 Then, after finally getting to use the restroom, we noticed the shower had TON’s OF MOLD ALL OVER THE BATHROOM, and my wife has health issues so I was very concerned!! The shower was soooo filthy with mold and tiles needing replaced, it was disgusting!!!😳😳😡😡 I had to place a plastic bag on the floor in order to take a shower, which I only took one, it was so nasty!!!😡😡 Even after communicating with the HOST, she still didn’t want to refund my funds to help me in this sad situation!!!😡😡🥲🥲😞😞 My vacation was totally ruined!!! Now I must go get a Covid test ASAP, because of the client that was in the unit unknowingly!!😡😡😡 The bedroom floor was filthy/dirty and she had the balls to ask everyone to take their shoes off before entering the unit, which is crazy!!! This is a horrible place to rent/stay ever and I travel ALL around the world and I’ve never been treated this way!!! Sad!!!!😡😡😡😡😳😳🥲🥲🤔👎🏽👎🏽👎🏽👎🏽👎🏽👎🏽😞

My boyfriend and I stayed at Christian’s place for the weekend and it could not have been any better. The check in process was seamless and space... amazing. So cozy and made us feel right at home. Christian even left me fresh cookies for my birthday (how sweet!) Just can’t stress enough how much we enjoyed our stay. Definitely planning on coming back whenever we’re in Brooklyn again!
Amazing, Renee is accommodating and the room is a steal I swear.

First thing is first, Kerreu is one of the kindest souls I have met. She is an absolute angel and made me and my families first experience staying at an AirBnb very easygoing and stress free. When we arrived at the home, we weren’t sure what to expect. She greeted us and helped us bring in our luggage. So many wonderful little touches and  unexpected goodies were waiting for us. The house looked and smelled spotless! It was very comfortable for all 5 of us to sleep. The location of the home was very close to the airport (Uber was only $20 for up to 6 people.) The location was also a 3 minute walk to the bus stop which was about a 20 minute ride until you arrived at the subway station. All the touristy spots are mostly in Manhattan- which was only about an hour commute total from the home. Everyone in the neighborhood was very friendly and helpful. Tons of good eats in the area, and all in walking distance. A wonderful place to stay!

We stayed at Vanessa and David’s place as a family of 5 adults over the Christmas and New Year period.   The Apartment was everything we needed. It is furnished to a high standard and the kitchen was well kitted out. The beds were comfortable and the apartment was lovely and warm. The shower was powerful and warm and there were plenty of towels. There were also some really nice thoughtful touches for guests. The apartment was decorated beautifully for Christmas.   We found the location to be a little further out from Manhattan than anticipated, but there is good access to the subway (about a 5 minute walk) and regular trains. The road that the apartment is on is nice, but some of the surrounding area was a little sketchy, but certainly an up and coming area.   Vanessa was a great host, she was very attentive and responded quickly to any queries.   An overall great stay.

Heidi & Rob were SO welcoming! Ms. Heidi greeted me at the door. Rob was such a gentleman an assisted me with my luggage & setting up the washing machine so I could do my laundry. They are so amazing to talk to & shared their tea stash with me! (Lol) The room had a lock & key. My privacy was respected. You will encounter other guest & bathroom is shared. Neighborhood safe.   Final Verdict: Overall......GREAT COMFORTABLE STAY! If you need an Airbnb & don't mind sharing a restroom. GET THIS ONE! Thank you both so much for being such fabulous human beings! So happy to have met you. Many blessings to you & you your family.

This is my best airbnb stay ever. Heidi and Rob are the best host and they make sure you get every help you need and treat you like a family. I have no words to describe the hospitality but in the end you would not want to leave this place 😍.

I had a really great time at her place!She always replied me very quickly, treated me like a family.This place is close by the station,  the main street is always busy and so safe even at the midnight.I spent a month there, so glad to have met Heidi and her boyfriend,Rob.Thanks for everything.

Hey fellow travelers! :) I'll try to be brief. You can expect friendly and experienced hosts, a comfy and elegantly decorated home and bedroom (with mini-fridge, AC, Fan,  and more). To all my cooks, you will find a beautiful modern kitchen with top quality appliances (rice cooker, toaster, oven, stove, blender, an expresso machine -that's classy). Rob & Heidi's home is located in a prime location, Ridgewood, at the border between Brooklyn and Queens. The Airbnb is a 10 mins walking distance to many well-stocked and reasonably priced supermarkets,  banks (Chase and TD Bank), major pharmacy chains, and the subway. I enjoyed my stay and don't regret booking with Heidi and Rob, they are legit Super-hosts☺️
Great Host in both Heidi & Rob. Communication was great. Place was clean, quiet. The area has a lot of options to choose from. Definitely a place to consider for your stay
This is truly a hidden gem.  Heidi and Rob are amazing hosts and their home is perfect for a getaway to New York.  I will definitely be coming back again :-)

Sonia place is beautiful, what you see in the picture is what you get..It's nice and cosy beautiful house.I like will book it again definitely..I recommend anyone who wants something nice and cosy and quiet with private parking if you driving..Me I was driving so it worked out good for me because I didn't have stress to look for parking.

The hot water CONTINUOUSLY went cold. I had to get compensated that’s how much the issue had come about. The WiFi Continuously went out. The host did not answer the phone not one time I called. She only communicated through text which is very lousy. The neighbors were drunk & banged on our door harassing me and my guest. I wouldn’t recommend this Bungalow at all. You will surely be annoyed by the hot water turning cold so quickly. & that’s no shade at all. Just saying my experience.

Not going to lie, we were a bit nervous when we first arrived as the neighborhood seemed a bit “sketchy” but once we settled in, we realized it was a great neighborhood!  Our host was fantastic from beginning (alerting us to a parking space!) to end (offering to change burnt out lightbulbs and bring towels at 10 pm!)  We loved eating at the Bungalow Bar and Rockaway Roasters. street parking was a bit challenging to locate.

Great location! I didnt meet Diana, but she responded to the few texts I had pretty quickly throughout my stay. Check in and out was painless, the neighbors were friendly in the few interactions I had with them, and it was a lovely time overall.   I wasnt feeling too great during one of my days, so it was incredible to have the private backyard space. There is overhead covering to protect you during the rain and just enough of a large gap to get a breeze and sunlight (and a bit of rain, but a reasonable amount that allows you to still grill and hangout in the backyard-PERFECT). Privacy is a big deal for me, so I was worried when I had to walk through what seemed to be other people's property to get to the bungalow, but the space is at the very end, so no one will go through your yard during your stay. It was nice hearing the neighborhood kid playing with their dad outside while I hung out in the yard.   There were snacks left in a basket for me upon arrival which was great. Couch was super comfy and reclined! Beds werent the best, but I have an incredibly mushy mattress at home myself. The bathroom was nice and had good water pressure in the shower too. Everything was clean when I got there, clean towels in a basket, soap, shampoo, everything I needed except toothpaste I think (which I bring while traveling anyway).   The area is a 5-10 minute walk to either coast of the island. I had such a stress-free time and hope I can schedule in another stay before swimming season is over!

Great little apartment located on a quiet street. Don’t let the fact that it’s in the Bronx scare you away from this nice place. Sonia has taken great care in decorating the place nicely and it is just an eight minute walk from a subway stop that brings you right into Manhattan in about 40 minutes. We stayed for a girls weekend (two moms and three teenage girls). It was a little tight for our larger group, but the apartment would be perfect for a couple getaway. It was very clean and the quiet neighborhood was a nice break after a long day in Manhattan. Would absolutely stay here again. Sonia is a great hostess! The off street parking was a HUGE plus too!

Edmund's place was exactly as described and exceeded our needs/expectations. It was quiet and very close to public transit, drug stores, delis, restaurants, etc. There was plenty of space for the four of us. He even had nice touches like toothbrushes, toothpaste, and soap/shampoo. The kitchen is fully stocked with kitchen needs and even had some bottled water and coffee/tea. We would stay here again. Thanks for a great experience! Highly recommended.

Close to subway, easy to get into the city. Place as described, appreciated the water provided. Easy to get in and out of building without disturbing hosts. Other reviews critiquing this place only do so because this is a non-gentrified community. I traveled alone and never felt unsafe during my stay.

Place was clean, had everything I needed. It’s more spacious than it looks in the photos! Everything that I used worked perfectly so I can’t have any complaints. Check-in was quick and easy. Location is very close to a subway station serving the 3 and 4 lines, so it’s very convenient to get around to Manhattan and elsewhere. Location itself was nice, never once felt unsafe there even when walking late at night. Would definitely consider staying here again if I come back to New York, as I can’t think of any complaints to make!

A bit of a noisy location without any decent cafes or coffee shops nearby. Some homeless on streets and a little rough. Also, it’s the last stop on the 4 line so a bit farther from downtown NYC.  Overall okay value though.  The place itself was spacious, clean, and everything worked as expected.  I’m not sure I’ll stay again.

Asil was a great host. The place is very neat and close to everything. The neighborhood is very special close to everything and accesible from everywhere even 4 blocks from times square but if your not familiarized with ny or It’s your first time could be a little scary at night until you get used to and realize that is safe and nothing happens even is there is Sole guy sleeping at the stairs. A mean is not the fancy zone in ny but it is very affordable clean and very Well located to move around. Is Just like every big city. The place has everything you May need but excepto May be day light but hey, you are supposed to be out as much as you can. You can get by walking to Rockefeller center, Times Square, Empire State, grand central and all the midtown attractions. For the rest of the city you are 5 blocks away from penn station so you can get anywhere by subway or even train which by the way is the faster and better way to get from jfk airport to manhattan. All that been said you get a great deal: an affordable and clean place near everything. Plus the host has a great ear plugs collection if you are sensitive to any noises. The building is actually quiet. You may only need it if you turn on the ac.
Excellent location, the place was clean, and the checkin and Asil's communication was excellent. There are some sketchy guys sitting on the stoop though, and no central air. But the value is there.

Great stay close to the airport! We didn’t feel unsafe at all in the neighborhood and that was a big area of concern for us as we were unsure of what area to stay in. The place was clean and the bed was very comfortable. It’s a great place for the price.

Everything was good with Asil condo, I guess for New York prices he’s Place is sure good value for money. The only downside was the homeless people that sit on the steps, they are harmless,. The upside is close to to Penn station, Central Park and Broadway.

Would 100% recommend this host.  Best deal I have seen this far!   You are close to shops, restaurants, theaters, etc.   I noted some prior comments mentioned there being a lot of homeless people and a lot of trash outside.  That, however, is part of the New York experience.

First off, great location! Only a few blocks from time square and so the location is hard to beat for sure!! There are a lot of homeless on the street but you will find that that is the case for most streets in NYC! I would like to say that the bed was horribly uncomfortable and the pillows were so thin. Upgrading the mattress and pillows would make a world of difference for the stay. Just being honest because after full days of walking miles around the city, a comfy bed is needed! All in all the stay was pleasant and communication was great!
It says it’s an entire place but it’s a basement in a home other then hearing the foot steps and noises being creepy it was a nice clean basement to stay for a day

This is a great find, I have to say I'm conflicted in giving it a great review, only because I want to come back and stay again and I'm afraid that it'll be booked out. There are great personal touches, a comfortable bed and a lovely shower. It is a really great AirBnB.

The house was really clean, I heard a lot about the neighborhood is dangerous but it was OK, 2 minutes to the supermarket and 7 to the subway. We have seen the host twice during our visit. I recommend it!

Communication with the host was good, and Erika was quickly responsive when I contacted her regarding her notification that the address listed on AirBnb was not the actual address of the rental unit. After renting this unit, I realize there were limited reviews on its area. Currently the area has many boarded up businesses and store fronts in the blocks surrounding it. If unfamiliar with New York or the area, it may feel unsafe. While the Myrtle subway stop is a 10 minute walk, there are few nearby open businesses to quickly, easily walk to from the rental unit. The coffee shop mentioned in past reviews is closed down. While I know the area is changing, this immediate area isn't 'trendy' yet as stated in the description. You will have to rely heavily on subways to reach cafes/restaurants from this unit. The Williamsburg Bridge (mentioned as "near" in the description) is actually a 2.5 mile (1 hour walk) from the unit, the Bushwick Collective area is 1 mile (20 minute walk) from the unit, and the Dumbo area is 3 miles (1 hour walk).

Nothing to say about the apartment. Everything is thought out with labels. Very nice apartment. No bad surprises. Nothing to say about the apartment. Everything is thought out with labels. Very nice apartment. No unpleasant surprises. Thank you very much.

Unfortunately I’m conflicted over this review as this couple were both quite lovely and hospitable but I do need to be honest and share our experience. We rented the master bedroom and the main bed was pretty comfortable plus there is a pull out with a single mattress. Unfortunately my daughter was very uncomfortable as the wires can be felt. Which made it an uncomfortable sleep for 2 nights. Our biggest issue was the strong odour coming from the bathroom. It’s noticeable in the bathroom, the hallway and the bedroom. Not sure if it’s a cleanliness issue or sewage issue but nonetheless, it was unpleasant. I brought my own blanket and pillow for my daughter and we noticed when we got home that they both smelled. We paid 120$ per night and stayed two nights and unfortunately we wouldn’t stay there again.

As someone who uses Airbnb frequently, I hope that my review can be helpful to those traveling to Brooklyn.   First of all, I’m actually a local. I live about 5 stops away on the L train. I used this space for a small gathering of women where we met for some virtual networking and education. We didn’t sleep in this space but we spent all day here for 3 days in a row.   The pros: Josh was very responsive. He was polite, professional and when I had questions about anything, he quickly gave me thorough answers. I appreciated him as a host overall.  The location is pretty great. It’s just on the border of where the nice part of Williamsburg ends and across the street from the M and J trains which is convenient. It’s also a reasonable (and nice) walk from the L stop on Lorimer.  The space itself is spacious and had decent light at all times of day. The beds looked very nice and the host had basics, toiletries, linens, kitchen essentials all readily available. There were even some beers in the fridge. The bedroom decor was also ok but a bit cluttered.  The check out procedures were super easy with barely anything to do - which was cool because a lot of hosts expect you to do half the housekeeping before you leave. We did clean up, washed dishes and left linens and trash ready to go, but we didn’t have to - which was nice.   And now to the cons: The decor. The description says authentic artist loft. No. Not in any way would I consider that accurate. There were leftover Christmas junk decorations, dead plants, pots of dirt, broken furniture and burnt out lightbulbs. Lots of junk (not antique, kitch, cute or fun, there is a difference) furniture cluttering the space. There was not a single piece of actual art.  The place was also quite dusty and dirty. Really needed a good cleaning and decluttering.  The entry to the building is typical for a nyc loft apt (not pretty) but the hallways to enter the apartment itself made me question if I was the next victim in a horror flick.  I checked the rooftop also , super excited as a New Yorker to have “access to a rooftop deck” as the listing implied but the stairs leading up were definitely scary, rickety and the roof itself was NOT stable, was covered in pallets as flooring and had no usable seating area. It was dangerous. I didn’t even attempt to walk across. This should NOT be in the listing as an amenity.  It was not usable.  Also, you should know that there is no television. I was surprised to find not one television in the entire place.   Overall, I was disappointed that I spent what I did for what I got.  Yes, you can sleep 4 large beds worth of people (whatever that means for you) but I think this listing was overpriced for what is actually offered.
Cool location, awesome apartment - and Josh gives A1 communication for a stress-free stay. Thank you!

Davica and her mom made me feel welcomed, allowing  me to stow my luggage following my early morning flight and providing a much welcomed cup of tea and time to rest in the common area downstairs. Check- in was easy and stress free. Both Davica and her mom were attentive to my needs and made my time with them comfortable.   The neighbourhood was quiet with basic shops  and a variety of food places / stores within walking of the house.  If you want night time entertainment you will have to travel outside the area to where these are in the Brooklyn area.  The subway is very easy to access making it very easy to get to Manhattan when you have to use public transportation.  If you want somewhere quiet, clean and affordable to stay then this is the place for you. :)  E. S. H.

Ben was a great host, and his place is a steal. I stayed at his apartment in LES/Chinatown for a month while I searched for apartments after moving to NYC, and this is the perfect spot for anyone in a similar situation. I was able to walk to work (in FiDi), and to other fun areas of the city (Little Italy, East Village, etc), but there is also subway access close by. Though Ben was very busy during my stay, he still made a big effort to get to know me and make sure I had everything I needed. The apartment gets cleaned weekly which is a plus, and it's air conditioned, which makes a huge difference during the summer. Highly recommend staying here.

AVOID AT ALL COST! This place was absolutely filthy even after checking in and complaining to the host. It took fours hours for the cleaning lady to come and clean yet no proper cleaning tools were provided for her to complete the cleaning. Also, all the towels, bed sheets, blanket were left wet inside the host’s broken dryer. I spend my entire stay on the sofa next to heater because the host refused to help. Be aware this host is a scammer because she is telling Airbnb that she provided me with sheets and blankets. Also, the TV only works when her internet works which is very rare. Also, do not be fooled by the photos there is no dining table. Make sure to clean the pots and pans before using. No utensils were adequately clean. Keep in mind the host will not refund you for any inconveniences. I have photos if anyone wants proof.

Worst AirBnB experience ever. The location of where AirBnB sent after booking was different than the location that host sent. She said she would update that with AirBnB, so I didn’t think of anything. The room was on 5th floor without an elevator in a building that smelled really bad, and so far these are not the worst of it. We were greeted by a cute dog which was not mentioned. More importantly, early reviews mentioned the apartment was run by nice girls, but there are other people in the apartment as well. She was helpful in checkin early, keeping luggage before checkin, fast communications, but the place was so shady and the room was along with apartment was dirty. There were bed bugs that I realized after leaving. The room’s window had an AC unit that did not allow window to close, so I did not sleep all night with noise of 1st street all night long. The worst part was, as I was going to the shared bathroom in the morning, a naked man was coming out of it. It was early and dark, but was obvious. I left right after instead of staying another night and reported to AirBnB. Worst stay of my life.

The place was very clean. it was relatively quiet for newyork. the room is in shade so it doesn't get hot too soon. The bed is fine, 7/10 comfortable. the shower had great pressure. we had slow Internet and a clicking AC on the first night. Upon informing Patricio he fixed both immediately and after that it was perfect. the neighbourhood is great. lots of families, many Dominicans and other central American backgrounds. always music and good food and nice people. old but charming buildings. the  metro 1  is very close. I loved our stay at Patricio's. I would recommendand or go myself again.

Great space, very clean and neat. Has the essentials for a great NYC experience. Apartment has all the basic necessities, no tv in the place, but who needs a tv in NYC? You are right in middle of all the action! Times Square, Hudson Harbor, Central Park, the Highline, and metro subway connections to any of the five burrows all a short walk away. We had an amazing trip and will definitely be back! Oh yeah the price is a steal for the amount of space and location in NYC.

Apartment not suitable for 5 people although 4 beds including 1 double bed. No storage apart from 1 small wardrobe in the bedroom. Air conditioning too noisy and just curtains on the windows. Unfriendly place when you return late at night, homeless people at the door of the building. The only plus, next to the main metro station, bus, close to Time Square.

There is black mold growing everywhere. The host does not speak English at all, the keys don’t work, we had to get refunded after a few days because the mold made us sick. Beware of this place. There’s no way this guy is a “super host” with only 4 sketchy reviews. Very disappointed in Airbnb
Location isn't very nice but the apartment and Marc is very cool. The location isn't dangerous but as a foreigner, it was weird. The place us clean and Marc is a nice guy.
It was nice accomodation for this price. I apprichiate full stocked kitchen and bathroom. The area seems little bit dangerous but everything was OK.

What an absolute steal! Check in was effortless and the room we rented was huge! We did have to use an air mattress for our 3rd guest but towels and sheets were provided and clean. The space has a full kitchen and a coffee maker, a living room and a beautiful backyard space with a grill and tea lights! It made for a perfect evening with friends and Chantal was even kind enough to bring down more chairs for our Wine night enjoying the beautiful weather!! The backyard space was well worth the stay just on its own :)   There was only a few minor setbacks as the stay was pretty much perfect. We didn’t have the opportunity to use the living room as it was rented as another bedroom - but we ended up just using the back patio with extraordinary weather. The entire Apt also only has one bathroom for 3 rooms of guests but it didn’t really make for many issues as the other guests were very kind and we all made it work! There wasn’t any large grocery stores directly nearby and the Apt is a 10 min walk from the subway — but we were able to get what we needed and the D train is LIGHTNING FAST into the city! 30 min or less! We also were given a great discount for 4 or more days so Chantal was incredibly accommodating as a host and I would definitely recommend!! We hope to rent it again soon!!

Host was very responsive. The actual apartment was very nice however I wish I had gotten a better description on the location. I have never been to Brooklyn before but I was definitely slightly shocked by the type of people who lived in the area. Felt unsafe walking my dog,

We were planning a weekend in NY my husband and I to have my mother in law discover the city for the first time. Harlem was not our first neighbourhood choice but we found David’s place and didn’t regret it! Price-quality ratio exceeded our expectations! Although the building was a bit vintage (but it gave us a cool New Yorker experience), the apartment was impeccable! Clean, cozy and very functional. David was fast to respond and very accommodating, which definitely contributed to make our trip pleasant! Our challenge was time as we wanted to see and visit as much as possible, so the smooth and easy check-in and check-out helped to make our stay stress-free and enjoyable. I left a note in his guestbook (which by the way is a lovely idea to make the place more personable), maybe you’ll read it ;)  I would recommend David’s place anytime!

We spent two nights at David’s place. It was very easy with check in. David gives you the entrance lock codes and you can arrive anytime after the check-in time. We found that place wasn’t cleaned, the floor in our room was dirty and the main floor washroom had a lot of hair in the bathroom. Also we were very disappointed with the neighbourhood. We had an inconvenience with the subway line which was closed during all our staying and we had to use a bus to get to another subway line. It took 30 minutes on a bus plus 40 minutes to downtown on a subway. The neighbourhood looks unsafe, especially in a evening time. I guess the price of David’s place is quite reasonable for NYC but you should be expecting what you get for this money.

I’m baffled that this air bnb has so many high star ratings. I arrived at the air bnb and stayed for less than 5 minutes before leaving. This place was so bad I stayed at the airport for 5 hours until security opened. Key things I did not notice in the pictures originally because I was so distracted by the good reviews - there are bug spray containers mounted throughout the house and right next to the bed indicating that there’s a bug problem, the door to the bedroom has vent slits making it so someone can stand in the living room and watch you in the bedroom, there was some sort of motion activated red light mounted to the bottom of the TV that blinks with motion (camera?- it is not the remote reader light as the TV was off and there was another cord tracked to it), and lastly although there were many locks on the inside of the bedroom door, the window did not lock and was on the ground level floor. The whole house also had a strong odor. I did not expect much from the Airbnb, just a quick place to sleep before my flight, but everything felt so sketchy and unsafe it wasn’t even worth it.

Spotless, spacious apartment. Great location in terms of convenience (C train is just a block away) but a little sketchy with the substance abuse treatment center across the street and visibly strung out folks on the corner coupled with the many locks on the door that are a little difficult to lock and must be relocked upon entry.
Apartment was great and check in was super easy and stress-free.

First of all Annie is a great host who reacts and responds very quickly. The check in was very easy, as Well as check out. The bathroom is very Well equipped and TV offers a lot of different channels. Unfortunately, I must agree with other comments about how you can hear everything the neighbors upstairs are doing. The bed is indeed very big but personally the mattress was too hard for us. Overall place didn’t seem fully cleaned before our arrival beside the toilet and bedroom. It’s worth to mention that AC is only in the bedroom and it’s tough to cool down the whole place during summer. When it comes to the location, we were concerned that it’d be too far but honestly daily it took us ~40 minutes to get to Manhattan main attractions and after couple rides we got used to it, so the distance was not a problem at all. However,  neighborhood itself made us feel unsafe, especially on the weekends when we had to walk from Crescent St. Overall OK stay.
This was my first Air BNB experience and it was a bit scary not knowing what I was getting into but this place was amazing and was perfect for me and my family. I would definitely book again.

Nice two-story place that captures the feel of living in an older NY apt. Reasonably close to subway to get anywhere easily, parking is also straightforward if you have a car. Huge kitchen/dining area, comfy couch and cool skylight all add to the charm.  Fast internet for those trying to work too. If you're a light sleeper, we suggest earplugs. Also be mindful of the stairs to get in & inside as they can be a bit steep with low overhangs. Area is a bit rough but we never felt unsafe during the times we walked around. Wonderful, attentive and very communicative hosts here, responding within minutes to my messages. Thanks so much Myrtle!!
Sharon's place was neat and comfortable. Its proximity to JFK airport was exactly as stated and it made my journey stress free.

The neighborhood may be a bit sketchy as the Uber driver stayed with me to access the unit at 11 pm.  Thus, I would recommend coming in during the day time, if you can.  Also the house is on the corner and there are three entry doors with the same address number, so make sure to use the correct door.  I left around 6 am so didn’t really explore the unit or the area but overall had a restful night, in spite of the six hour jet lag, and a refreshing shower with good water pressure.   Overall I would recommend Sharon’s place if staying overnight for a quick jaunt to JFK.

My partner and I stayed at Sharon's place during a 16 hour layover at JFK. It was a great way to relax in a peaceful and comfortable space between long flights and airport stress. The house is very clean and it's clear Sharon puts a lot of thought and effort into her home. It's a short ride from the airport and Sharon was flexible about our late arrival. I wish we had had time to explore the neighborhood and some of the Carribean and west African restaurants nearby!
Great hotel the location is a bit creepy but the hotel speaks for itself

Room looked like it did in photos, I wish they had a mini fridge or microwave. Maybe they did outside of the room but I don’t think so. No good window scenery, Wifi was fast, room was clean, towels, shampoo, conditioner, heating and cooling system, hot water. Some reviewers said the area was creepy and it kinda was at night but that’s not the hotels fault and it wasn’t a problem. Comfy stay overall!

I would like to share my experience so that you have a clear understanding of what you’re getting yourself into when booking this place for your vacation or family gathering. If you are OK with someone, this being the host, constantly looking at their cameras to monitor what the guests are doing then you should be OK booking this place. The host monitors her cameras and she  is very particular about who comes in to her property. my son lives two blocks away from there in a very small apartment , as all apartments are in New York City. we have not seen our son for two years because of Covid we finally get to see him we fly three hours to go see him we think it’s OK for him to come over for pizza after he perform on Broadway and the host gives us a call and basically says he needs to get out that no one other than the people that are on the reservation are allowed in her house. She repeated that she has rules and that they need to be follow no one other than the people on the reservation are allowed in the house   so if you’re planning to visit family and have them come over to visit with you don’t reserve this place because you will not be allowed to have people come over. If you are not OK with sketchy areas dark neighborhoods trash and dirtiness outside then don’t book this place because it’s very sketchy it’s dark scary at night and there’s trash everywhere including rats. The inside of the place is old there’s stairs to the second floor that are very noisy they almost feel as they’re going to fall apart as you go up the stairs very scary for little kids which we had little kids with us. The TV in the room do not work just there for display there’s no place for you to put your clothes we had to put ours on the floor because closets are preoccupied with clutter. The bathroom door does not lock I had to tell everyone to knock before going in because the bathroom did not lock. If you go in the winter time or when it’s cold we prepare to be told that the temperature is already set at what it needs to be per New York City guidance regardless if you and  the rest of the guests are cold.  Be prepare to be asked to leave the place simply because you had someone come over we were in a city that we do not know a neighborhood that is not the safest not the cleanest, we were asked to leave because my son came over for pizza. We had to look for a hotel we still had another night left we were not credit any money back instead the host wanted to charge us $500 more for breaking the rules and allowing my son to come in for a slice of pizza. It is inhuman to ask a family with children to get out of home simply because they had an extra person come over for pizza a person that you love that you have not seen for two years and you flew three hours to go see.  it does not make sense it’s unkind and unhuman especially when you have children that are scared wondering what’s going on why do we have to pack and go, it was raining and cold we had to walk and try to figure out what we were going to do. We had to see if there was a hotel that had rooms available, on call for. If you wish to experience all of this, go book this Place. The other thing we noticed is the towels that were given to us to use in the bathroom were all different colors they look old nothing special about those towels I feel that if you’re going to book your place for people to enjoy you should at least have decent same color towels. Also there was no trash cans other than in the kitchen it would be nice to have a trashcan in the bathroom.Last but not least if you wish to rent your place out for people to come and enjoy the city or family you should probably allow the families to enjoy your place and not be watching them over a camera and Not dictating who can and cannot come visit. We were simply having pizza after my son’s performance. We were relax and tired simply together just talking at the table we were not listening to music we were not having a party we were simply just gather as family talking and enjoying celebrating we were reunited with some good New York pizza.  I share this so that you have a true picture of our experience never again. I have rented many before and have never experienced what I experience this time in New York.  To have The heart to kick a family out is unbelievable no compromise no working things out. The host called that evening to say you have an extra person that is not on your reservation why are they there they need to leave the place and you explain to the host that is your son who came over to celebrate his performance and enjoy pizza with you and still they do not have the heart to say don’t worry about it it’s OK enjoy your son instead they tell you he needs to leave and then the next morning you get a phone call from Airbnb asking you to leave the place , thank you for reading my review.

Decent place to stay for a small group. Neighborhood is not very clean, but OK for The Bronx. Did not feel unsafe. Amenities are ok and provided. Myrtle was an hour late upon arrival, which is annoying after about 12h of travelling.

There is a lot to like about this place. In terms of space, you get a lot for you money here. (We only had three guests--not sure you'd really want more than 4-5.) Myrtle is great with communication.  The location is convenient to LG and the Yankees. We had a few challenges. Apparently, previous guests had damaged the kitchen floor substantially, and that was still a problem. Those guests also destroyed a fire alarm. With Myrtle's permission, we removed it from the ceiling because it was beeping. Also, some of the surfaces were sticky, frankly. Check in is tricky because they need to see who you are--I guess they have problems with scammers. :(  The neighborhood is pretty working  class, but there were nice places to eat close by. We would stay again--good value for the price.

Washroom drainage was not working properly. So this place has only one washroom. Stairs are very dangerous to climb. I will not recommend this. Host communication was not clear at all. She keeps on asking for more without any notification. This is consider as fraud. I will not revisit this place. I will not recommend this place.

Really cute place. I like the whole pineapple theme. The location is great but not so great at the same time. Its right next to penn station and isnt too far from port authority etheir which is nice if you out of state....but the location its self wasn't all too pleasant since there were alot of unpleasant people outside. I wanted to go to the store and my boyfriend didnt think it would be safe to go so late (becauseof the people outside). Even though it was 2 blocks away. Other then that the hotel itself is awesome!
Very lovely room. Nice view of the city. Amazing front desk help with checking and settling in. A lot of homeless around the area and tough parking situations.

This is literally the worst hotel i’ve ever stayed in, first off it’s located on a block full of homeless and drug addicts right outside the door that eyeball the guest coming out, I felt very unsafe every time i came in and out. second there is a lady that sits in the lobby who watches every guest you bring in and out to make sure you bring no more than 2 people in a room. Also all guest you bring have to be id and security checked. The room is literally the size of a closet, and they charge you so many hidden fees not listed on airbnb. DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!

The room and place it’s self was very nice, looked just like the pictures and was actually very nice. The outside of the hotel was very sketchy though, as soon as you walked out there was lots of people crowding us. It was not a nice area and I did not feel safe.
It's really pretty, but rooms are very small. Doesn't make sense..also alot of activity in the area like homeless ppl
Place was small & outside was a bit filled with homeless people but other then that it was really clean & cute little rooms

Just don’t stay here. They trick you with fees and there are way too many homeless people just outside the hotel. Front desk guy was sketchy. I called the hotel to resolve a dispute and they told me to call Airbnb. I call Airbnb and they said it’s the hotel I need to resolve this with. What a waste of time I’ll never get back.  **I wouldn’t be surprised if they take down my honest, accurate review since it doesn’t help their agenda.**

This is a scam. Pictures lie, no towels, flies everywhere, very rude host, unclear check in instructions. We didn’t even spend a night there. This experience made us re-consider ever getting another Airbnb in NY. I’ll just provide one example: we came back to the place at 12:40am, quietly went to our (not so clean or cute, but rather disgusting room that separated us from the hosts by sliding doors through which lights were coming through) room on a Saturday night. We went to bed.  As we were falling asleep, the host goes to the kitchen (which was right next to our room), and starts washing pots and pans very loudly (it felt purposeful). After about 10 minutes, I peak into the kitchen and politely ask, “Do you mind keeping it down, we’re trying to sleep?” I wasn’t expecting the response that I got. She said: “I’m washing the dishes, when do you want me to wash my own dishes. This is my house and I can’t be quiet because I have to wash the dishes” (we didn’t use her dishes at all, left the place as soon as we could and only were there to sleep because of how dirty it was). After her response and her behavior, we left. This was at 1 am! Anyway, please don’t be fooled by the pictures or reviews. The worst Airbnb experience we have ever had.
Good place, sparkling clean. The area is a little sketchy and the room very small but its nice inside and worth the price. Hosts are helpful

Front desk associate was rude and unprofessional. He was more concerned with flirting with a female and flexin his front desk pull and left us standing in the rain for 7 minutes while he and said female flirted. He said “I can’t let you in you need your key card lol” she’s like “ nah let me in lol” hehe haha and he was dead looking us in our face during his little weak game play. He accused us of allegedly smoking when we burned sage bc it’s a full moon. He revoked our licenses to be there without giving us the benefit of doubt, so we left. But I would never ever return, and ya need to fix the crackhead problems outside Because that makes anyone feel unsafe. And the pictures are misleading, no robes in the rooms, no husky dog on the bed.

Philipps space was amazing. Communication was over the top. Check was smooth, the lock attacked to the tree is kinda cool. There are great restaurants right outside, don’t have to go far. This place two doors to the left had a great duck meal. Overall, great experience. Will 1000% be back when I’m in NYC. Thanks Philipp!

The staff were friendly, but we would not stay here again. The price is similar to a hotel but without the amenities.  We had issues with check-in, the card reader on our door, and the TV remote. Our room very small - the bed is essentially against the wall on one side. The shower door had a broken seal and allowed water to pool on the floor.   The location is great - just blocks from Penn Station - but on a sketchy and rather empty street.

The stay was fine, the issue was that the price for the hotel, once the cleaning fee was added was too high particularly for the size of the room and location. Reception was on the second floor, rooms on the third and fourth floors with no elevator.  The rooms were clean however the moment you enter the hotel you are hit by an overpowering, unpleasant smell. This was also present in the rooms but you could air it out.

Please be extremely cautious when reserving here. I am only going to report what happened to me, and what I observed, but I can safely say that this is the worst hotel experience I have ever had, and that it could have jeopardized my physical and mental safety.   I was in NYC for one day only to get a cardiac test. My heart acted up during the test, and I had to go to the ER to rule out a heart attack.  When I was released, it was around 7:30 pm and I needed a place to stay. I reserved the Sohotel through an instant booking. Their check in time is very late, between 9 to 11 pm. I arrived around 9:30. When I got there, I was initially told that they couldn’t find my reservation in the system and that there were no available rooms. They asked me to wait while they looked into this. They claimed it was a mistake due to the reservations clerk (who I never saw), and that it was not an instant booking (AirBnB later confirmed that it was an instant booking).  Then I hear them on the phone attempting to relocate other guests who had reserved through Expedia and Priceline. I personally saw someone else get turned away. The woman told him he would get a call, but I have no way of knowing if that happened. Finally the woman said I could have a room, so they could not honor my reservation because my room was taken. So they upcharged me $50 for a different room. They also made me pay a $250 security deposit (which definitely wasn’t listed on AirBnB).
