I heard a lot of bad things about bed-stuy, but i didnt feel unsafe(even walking home with my girlfriend around 10-11pm). Kitchen, toilet and bathroom were very new and very clean. The room is small, but we did not spend much time there. There is nice common area in case you want to sit somewhere else then your bed. Armando's Pizza is good place to get some food fast. All in all, we would come again. Thanks.

The accommodation is well placed, clean, quiet   I think that's stealing, more than 200$ a night, just for a queen size bed, a bathroom with a tiny shower, no A/C (it was colder in the hallway than the bedroom),  my wife and I slept badly because of the heat.  Rbnb was created to help people not to do business, there are hotels around that are much cheaper with the same or better services.  Very disappointed

Sarah and Kaptan, thank you for the wonderful 4-week stay at your apt in NYC (Alphabet City)! You have been great hosts! Thanks for being always friendly, fun and accommodating. It was amazing! The spacious apartment is located in a quiet and save neighborhood away from the daily NYC stress. However, you'll have multiple great restaurants, bars and pubs next around the corner. The highlight of the apt is the porch and the backyard which invite you to relax and recharge at home. Next train stop is in 10min walking distance. It was the perfect location! I will definitely come back!

Kaptan was an incredible host!!  Although we never met, he was very friendly, personable and prompt with communication. the location was excellent!!  my only reservation was the lack of sleep to be had while sharing the apartment. I didn't realize going into booking that it was a 4 bedroom 2 story apartment. I was awakened every morning by 6 am by the other guests moving or/ cleaning up/ putting away things in the kitchen. It felt like I was staying in a dorm. anytime I walked out of the bathroom/shower, I was always surrounded by at least 4 people. it made for a somewhat stressful stay- which has nothing to do with the host. moving forward I know to ask more specific questions with bookings if it's not mentioned :)

This was a great crash pad if that is what you need. There is no kitchen (there is a microwave and a kettle). The location was pretty easy. Check-in was a breeze and Francis was immediately accessible and responsive.  The building's ammenties are pretty impressive- gym, co-working space, social area.  The apartment itself is pretty basic.  There is a washer/dryer but it is locked up and not accessible. The shower is pretty retro.  Because the apartment is on the ground floor you must choose between privacy and natural light.  You can open the sun shade, but then everyone can see in.  Again, if you need a crash pad in Hells Kitchen this is a perfect spot.
Adeyemi made my stay stress free and wonderful. The place was clean upon arrival, air conditioning was always on, and the shared bathroom was always clean.

Unfortunately my stay at this b & b was very difficult and uncomfortable. I had a lot of difficulties with coexistence, I was not welcomed in a hospitable manner. On the day of my arrival I had come very tired from my trip and hoped to rest quietly and instead the continued noises of people in the street and especially the rudeness of a living person who in the middle of the night knocked on my door waking up and asking me ( without giving me any welcome or showing the slightest courtesy) asked me who I was and who did not know about my arrival. The night I slept in this tiny, very noisy room, there were always screams and high volume music from the street. I did not receive any indication of the structure, did not know how to have breakfast, did not come out of the shower, did not give me the password for the wi fi. A really unpleasant atmosphere.

One of my most wonderful air bnb experiences ever!! . The space is exceptionally clean and comfortable and Cyrina is one of the most beautiful spirits I've ever met . it's a short walk to the train with a drug store near by and is very secure ...

Good stay overall, however small inconveniences, such as the room poorly insulated from the cold, dirty gas stove, dirty sponge, few cutlery, dirty carpet. The cleaning staff (a man) is not very welcoming or even unpleasant, the host remains available despite everything and the price remains affordable.

Our time at Adeyemi's apartment was very satisfactory, we had some problems at check in, but once resolved we had a great stay, clean apartment, good sized room, only the dishwasher didn't work, when we had any doubts they were always resolved, the apartment is close to two subway stations that take us to all regions in Manhattan in an average of 40-50 minutes, we didn't feel scared anywhere near the region. I recommend hosting Adeyemi.

Thanks a lot to airbnb and Banty for very pleasant time which I spent in NY. A person who first time is coming to NY can be afraid of situation with transport. Be calm, only not that sometimes especially on weekend there can be repairing works you should change a lot of bases and lines for getting your way. But the place, where is Banty's apartment is very nice, it is very easy to find, only  5 min walk and you already near the metro. Please note that transport in NY is expensive. The room is small, but it composed so accurately that even sometimes I could not understand where Banty find so many place. You have everything inside of your room: TV, fridge, lamp, hairdryer, cooler, heater, the big very nice and soft bad, when you can lost yourself, and even dumbbells. Banty clean everything all day. Of course somebody could say that the bathroom is small and old, but the smell of clearance is everywhere. Banty left for gests everything which is important: tea, coffee, chocolate, water and fruits. She is so good person. I have not met yet such a heart housekeeper. So, have a nice holidays with Banty.

This place was a steal! The location was central to all the fun to be had in Park Slope and very accessible by the subway. Fourth kindly welcomed us, even though we arrived very late on Day 1. I would definitely stay here again!

The apartment is anything but cozy. A bed tossed on the floor, no TV, horrible internet service and an unpleasant bathroom are just a few of the reasons that I would never stay at this Air bnb again.  The only thing going for this place is the great location.

Very clean and welcoming space in a fantastic location. I was most grateful for the fact that there is a separate entrance; it made coming and going at my preferred hours stress-free. There is lots to do in the neighborhood and the L train and M train are in easy walking distance if you need to commute into the city. Banty was very kind and responsive. The space is a great value for the price.

I booked this air bnb because my mom was coming to visit and we didn’t have the room in our apt to put her up. Nick received my mom when she arrived and helped her with her bags and to get checked in and settled. When I asked my mom about her stay she said the following: “Upon arriving, I immediately felt secure and welcomed, not only by the family but also their pet!  At numerous times I was given input as to local travel and helpful answers to several questions. Location was excellent - within short walking distance to bus lines and the subway.  And several times I was out late and also up early but never felt unsafe because the area is very well lit. I plan on using this address in the future!  Also, the room and bathroom were very clean. And the bed was most comfortable.  And there was an ease of communication with the family that made me feel totally at ease in a home where I had never before been!”  Good feelings all around. Thanks Nick!

Nick and Sapir are wonderful people with a comfortable, quiet room to share. Nick helped me a lot with subway directions, and Sapir kindly offered me some tea when I got it. Bunk is very friendly, and even though I'm sometimes a little afraid of dogs, he was so sweet and never made me nervous. It was convenient having the 24/7 bodega around the corner too.  I would stay with them again in a heartbeat.

Nick and Sapir were the best Airbnb hosts we have ever had. Both were extremely welcoming and accommodating! We felt right at home the second we entered their space. They gave us the perfect eating recommendations along with fun places to check out and explore. Their apartment itself is adorable and impeccably clean and inviting. It is super easy to get to Manhattan and Williamsburg from their place and their neighborhood is really cute and walk able! This listing is SUCH a steal and I couldn't recommend it more. Nick and Sapir are wonderful people and we felt so lucky to have found them. It was a hard goodbye and next time we are in New York you can bet we will be staying here :)

Nick and Sapir were excellent hosts.  Their place was super clean; the bathroom and kitchen were also in perfect condition.  If you like to cook, they have a fully stocked kitchen that they take immaculate care of.  It was a stressful time for me as I was moving apartments, but Nick helped me carry all of my boxes.  They even had coffee ready when I was headed to work in the morning!  They are an adorable couple; both very pleasant, resourceful, and warm-hearted.  I felt welcome in their beautiful home - it was more like staying with friends than strangers.    If you’re looking for a place in Brooklyn, definitely consider staying here.

Maria was a wonderful host, quickly replied to any messages and let us leave our luggage at the place for few more hours after checking out.  The room was very clean, cosy and warm for NY November weather. Everything needed was there and we felt really comfortable.  The Bushwick area of NY was somewhat sketchy in the evenings, however it's great for thrift shopping, interesting cafes and bars. Good subway connections to move to other districts.

Stayed at Marias place 02/09 to 2/12 and I definitely recommend this place. Area was a bit sketchy when I got there but the people are very nice and it's about a 6-8 minute walk to the train station. A lot of stores and restaurants within a few minutes from the apartment. My room was nice and clean, I spent a lot of time out and exploring but it was a great place and space to sleep and get ready in.
Very clean, well organized, esthetically pleasing...makes for a stress free stay.

We had a very nice stay in Kyle‘s Studio. The room kitchen and bathroom were very clean and comfortable. The hallway had a slightly unpleasant smell, but not the studio itself. Also Kyle was very responsive. The building was very quiet, but if someone speaks, you can hear it through the wall (probably typical for NY). Would definitely come again!!!

Perfect place for a woman traveling solo, particularly if you plan to be out all day and are mainly looking for a place to rest. Great neighborhood with tons of coffee shops/restaurants, super convenient location, minutes away from subway.  Never felt unsafe at any point. Laura was incredibly sweet and helpful!

The location of Ainslie and John’s townhouse was wonderfully situated in a quiet and safe area where easy access to Prospect Park and public transportation was convenient. Ainslie helped us set up a sofa bed, which was much appreciated. To our dismay, my souvenir chocolate gifts that were kept in their refrigerator were opened and consumed by their family member.  We understood that it may have been a miscommunication and accepted John's offer for a monetary compensation. However, during the conversation it was unfortunate that we had to deal with unpleasant arguments from that family member. We thank Ainslie for her professional hospitality and John’s quick willingness to resolve the negative incident.

We had a great experience in New York and the apartment is so nice and clean. Zaza was also so nice providing us with towels and also the check in was easy (you just take the key from downstairs so we didn’t wait). But we must say something:   1.- The neighbourhood is not very safe (at least during the night, the streets are so dark and they look a bit dangerous, even we took some ubers from the metro till the house). Indeed, the metro is not 10 minutes far away from the metro, but 15-20 (and I walk fast!).   2.- The apartment is nice, luminous and quiet but the room has inflatable mattresses. For one-two days is okay, but not for one week. I think that should be said that in the announcement, because it is not clear in the pictures.  3.- In the rules of the house it is written that you can cook at the appartment but if you cook Zaza is a bit strict in that sense. For example, you can just use one pan and it is a disaster (it should be changed). Indeed, if you put something in the fridge you have to ask her.  Furthermore, the night before our departure she took off our things from the fridge and we didn't understand why if we had still one more day.   4.- The worst thing (at least for me) is that the day of our departure she didn’t let us leave the luggage at the appartment. Our flight was at 11 pm and the check in is at 10 am. She said that she had other guests, but I never saw that because in the flat there is a lot of space to put the luggage for a few hours. It is new york, what do you do with your luggage for almost 12 hours?
Very accommodating (despite our last minute request) and excellently located. Made our stay stress free and convenient.

THIS IS NOT A 1 BEDROOM APARTMENT. THIS IS A ROOM IN AN APARTMENT. This listing is an apartment were one room is rented out, Zaza stays in one room and it seemed like there was another person around as well. The bathroom is shared. The bathroom is small and Zaza said only use soap labeled "AIR BNB" but there was no soap available with that label. The bathroom was disgusting. I had to clean it just to sit on it and do number 2, when going number , I squatted. There were little black hairs all over the shower walls, sink, toilet and floors. Only took one shower and when I saw the hairs in the shower, got out immediately and never got another there. If comparing to a hotel bathroom it would of been comparable to a 2 star hotel bathroom. When I got there, Zaza looked like she was about to go to bed. She handed me the keys to the front door and explained that the bathroom was shared. Her and another women spoke for a little bit in the living room, then she went to her room. I only spoke with her one other time during my stay about a restaurant. The living room looked disheveled and unwelcoming. Zaza said we could use the living room but we were to not sleep there. When we arrived her friend was laying on it watching TV and it felt like that was there space and we weren't welcomed. The kitchen is shared as well. I was not made aware before hand that the fridge would also be shared. Zaza stated that if we had any items to put in fridge, to make her aware, so that she could make room. There was barely any room to be made. It looked as if she had recently went grocery shopping; it was packed. We had to leave food in the car that ended up melting or going bad. The fridge was filthy and looked like it had never been cleaned out. That made us uncomfortable with leaving items there anyway. If you plan on cooking there, DONT. The kitchen was filthy. In the mornings when I woke up there were signs of cooking or drinking the night before; dishes left on the counter and in the sink. Never once were we told that we were allowed to use the stove and it also felt unwelcoming, too. The bedroom walls looked like they were props for a horror movie. They were so filthy and caked with gunk we didn't even want to put our stuff against the walls or touch them. We had two sleeping pillows, one on each bed. Both were flattened, old and dingy. So were the blankets.  Thankfully, we had brought our own blankets and pillows to use. We didn't even use hers; but to lay on top of. I wish we would not have even layed on top of hers, one person from our party got a rash. We pulled the blankets off of the mattresses to see what they looked like, they were unfathomable. They looked like someone had been massacred on them. So many spots and blotches. When comparing to a hotel, the kitchen would have been a 1 star motel. The bedroom would have been 1 star motel, as well. I asked Zaza for a steak house because that's one of the things I went to NYC for. I let her know I was going to "Keens". She suggested and persuaded me to goto "Mastros". DONT GO TO "MASTROS". We spent $300 for food that wasn't better than our city's outback restaurant. When Zaza later asked what I thought about the restaurant, I expressed this to her. She then told me that "you don't go to 'mastros' for the steak you go for the scallops." -_- Why tell someone to go to a steakhouse were the scallops are the only item that's good and not specify this. If your going to NYC for something particular do your own research, don't just necessarily take Zaza's suggestion. THE LISTING SAIDS FREE PARKING BUT THERE IS A CATCH. She lives right in front of a school so Monday-Friday your not allowed to park from 7-mid afternoon. So Friday morning we had to make sure that we moved our vehicle by 7am to avoid a ticket. Also, there is hardly parking around the neighborhood for free, be prepared to pay for parking. If going on a weekend and the school days are not an issue, know that the parking is kind of like an alley way. There is not much space, you will probably not get parking unless you leave the vehicle there and take the subway, like we did. It's not the safest-feeling neighborhood but it doesn't feel like the most dangerous either. Zaza said she did not drive so was not able to offer any parking info for NYC. If you are not going to park your car and take the subway or walk everywhere, be prepared to pay a nice amount for parking in NYC. All in all I will return to NYC, because it is my favorite city, as of yet. But, I will never stay at this place or any other Air BNB that Zaza host's nor would I offer this to my dog.

I recommend this accommodation, especially because it is not very expensive and the service is irreproachable. Concerning the location, the main tourist places of Manhattan are a bit far (20-30 minutes by car) but this is compensated by the more interesting price. The district of spanish harlem was quiet and we don't feel in danger being tourists. I recommend
This place is a steal for the price ! Beverly is a great host and I enjoyed my stay. Will definitely be back if I’m in New York again.

The price is a steal, the place is super clean and spotless. Bev the host is a very nice lady indeed. I feel safe on her place. I travel for work  and love to stay again on her place. Thank you Beverly God bless you always🙏

I really appreciate the  stay in your home.  It was a beautiful home and very clean.  Very very clean!!   However, as a woman traveling alone I would like to have known that there was a man staying in the basement that I might encounter and I would be home alone with that person through the night.  From your post, it says I would only be sharing the space with you, which made me comfortable and the reason why I chose your Airbnb.  To be honest, I was scared the entire night and only slept 2 hrs.  You might want to let people know. Other than that it was a perfect location.  Great room!  And Beverly was nice.

Sheilas place was conveniently located next to JFK. Check-in was a breeze and instructions were clearly presented.   The neighborhood is a little loud at night but that didn’t bother us.   We also liked that the LIRR was a 5min drive away and that it stops right at Penn station in the heart of NYC and Atlantic station in Brooklyn.   Neighborhoods might seem a little sketchy to some but we felt totally safe and comfortable. Would highly recommend for convenience to everything alone.   Sheila is always a great communicator that responds to any inquiry very quickly.

Sam’s place is literally in the hot part of Williamsburg. I stayed here for around a month to work remotely and found it to be very cozy. The place is steps away from the L. Sam was also very accommodating. Overall, this place was a steal.   These aspects didn’t bother me, but I think the wall borders the stairwell so you could occasionally hear footsteps. This is probably typical of anywhere else in NYC, so if you’re a light sleeper I would just bring earplugs. Overall, if I’m in the city I would stay here again!

Sam and her beautiful loft space couldn't have been more perfect for my work/apartment hunting trip. The space is a lot bigger than the pictures show; I wasn't needing a lot of space, but it was really nice to have such high ceilings and sunlight flooding in. The bed was very comfortable, and Sam made sure I was not needing for anything at all. Everything was very clean and tidy, and Sam always had fruit and coffee nearby. The area in which Sam's space is located was perfect for hopping into the city, as the L train was a 3 minute walk away. I came home at every late hour possible and never once felt unsafe in the neighborhood. I had several coffee places to choose from, so I was able to switch up my work environment every day.  I was just looking for an economic place to stay, I didn't care too much for the amenities because I knew I wouldn't be home very much, but Sam's place made it feel as though I booked for a luxury trip to the city, it was such a wonderful and pleasant surprise.  Sam was a truly generous, gracious host, and I look forward to booking with her in the future!

Carla's home was by far the best Airbnb location I have visited--and she is the kindest and most exceptional host!  Carla and her husband made me feel like a welcome friend in their impeccable home; I felt embraced.  The room itself is ideal: elegantly decorated, spacious and quiet, with every conceivable need anticipated.  They have provided a desk, with a desk lamp, a very comfortable desk chair, window AC, a TV with Netflix and Hulu, fruits, healthy snacks, and even a coffee maker and an electric kettle.    The twin bed is supremely comfortable; indeed comfier than my own bed at home. The linens are white and pristine, so it was like sleeping in a cloud--the most restorative night's sleep I have enjoyed in any Airbnb.  The bedroom is also immediately to the right of the front door, and right next to the bedroom, so both are conveniently independent of the rest of the home.  Carla even installed a baby gate at the end of the hall to prevent her sweet dog Ella from visiting her guests.  (I would have welcomed such visits, but it was yet another considerate gesture from Carla toward her guests.)    Every detail of the accommodations was exquisite, from the fine linens, down to the soft sanitary paper in the bathroom.  The bedroom and the bathroom were absolutely spotless and well supplied with everything an overnight guest might need--even a selection of towels in several sizes.  In the morning, Carla left a plate with fresh croissant to complement the coffee and fruits already in the room.  She also texted to make sure I was safe when I arrived a bit later than expected the second night.  Her building is in a lively diverse neighborhood, a mere 3-4 blocks from the #1 train, and surrounded by fantastic Dominican cafeterias, a large grocery store (C-Town) and a drug store (Duane Reade).  Carla and her husband are warm, lovely hosts who will chat if you feel like it and will respect your privacy if you prefer to rest quietly in the peaceful sanctuary you will find in their guest room after a busy day in the city.  I cannot say enough about how delightful it was to meet such splendid hosts and to spend two calm nights in their heavenly home.

Carla and Kalel's place was a steal. It was in an ideal location for my purposes (close to the university I was visiting), had good amenities and a clean bathroom/bedroom, and was in a generally safe neighborhood. All for an affordable price. The best part of my stay was how considerate Carla and Kalel were. My flight was delayed nearly 6 hours and I arrived to the apartment early in the morning (around 2 am) and Carla woke up and gave me some nuts and fruits when she heard that I hadn't had a chance to eat dinner. In addition, there were water bottles provided along with towels laid out on my bed.   The only real downside is the walk up the stairs, particularly if you have a lot of luggage. It's 5 flights of stairs - but I guess you could see this as a chance to workout.  If you need to be close to Morningside Heights, Harlem, or Upper Manhattan, this apartment listing is a great value.

Honestly such a steal of a place, as long as you don’t mind the 6 flights of stairs. They were such nice, accommodating hosts. Fortunately one of them was home when I was leaving and they helped me down with my luggage. Will definitely be coming back and staying here again. 10/10

We spent two months at Elan’s place in Queens. It is a wonderful apartment!  The neighborhood:  The studio is on a quiet residential street; it  is at the back of the building, so you hear no street noise at all.  The subway is only 1.5 blocks away, yet there is no appreciable subway noise and a very quick ride into Manhattan.  We had no concerns about safety, even with going out late in the evening.  Several grocery stores, bakeries, and wonderful restaurants are within 3-4 blocks of the apartment.   The studio:  The studio is spacious with a very comfortable queen bed by the large west-facing windows; I stayed here with an adult daughter and we never felt cramped.   It is bright and sunny and tastefully decorated.  There’s a tree outside the window, and you’ll see the occasional squirrel or cat down below. Above the opposing rooftops you can see some of the Long Island City high-rises in the distance.   There  is a sectional couch large enough for two people to sleep on, with plenty of open floor space between the bed and couch (the TV can be viewed from both).  The kitchen feels like a separate room and is very well equipped with the usual appliances, equipment, microwave, and a small table.  The coffee table in front of the couches is also height adjustable and can be used for dining.  The bathroom is nicely outfitted, has another window, and is small—room enough for one person to get ready. There is plenty of storage, including a pantry, large closet, and a large bureau.  There is even a robo-vacuum!  Self check-in was simple, and the apartment was spotless when we moved in.  The host:  Elan was very responsive to any questions we had. We would stay here again in a heartbeat.

My partner and I originally chose this spot to save some money while in NY, but we realized that it's extremely far away from everything we wanted to see in Brooklyn and Manhattan. At nighttime (because we were afraid to use the subway at night) we ended up Ubering back from Manhattan and it was so expensive that it would have been more worth it to stay closer to the more popular areas; we ended up spending just as much money because of the Ubers and spent a lot of time on the subway when we rode it during the day (this bnb is at the very final stop of the L train).   The Airbnb had all the necessities to survive which was incredible and appreciated. However, there isn't a ton of sunlight coming into the space and the interior design could use a more intentional touch. If you're not planning to spend much time in the home, this won't matter to you, but my partner and I were working from home during the day and I can't exactly say that the ambiance was preferable or homey/comfortable.   The noise upstairs was probably the most problematic part of the experience. You can hear everything going on upstairs and sometimes it feels like someone is trying to get into the house.   The host was also not the most responsive. He was helpful upon our arrival, but after that, he wasn't extremely communicative.  Other than that, if you're planning to visit near Canarsie or Coney Island, etc., this is a perfect location and if you're not super picky about ambiance, then this is a sweet spot. It's incredibly roomy which we appreciated and has EVERYTHING you need to get by. The neighborhood seems friendly and relaxed, as well.

Petra's place is a studio apartment that has its own entrance. Its felt like home when we stayed. Husband and wife were very accomodating and they felt like my parents and they treated us very nicely.  There was no stress and it was easy to move arround with taxi.  This is where you want to spend your timeout or holiday.

Petra and Tony were one of the best hosts I’ve ever had. They were super attentive, kind and accommodating to us.  We booked this place the day before because we ended up staying in New York an extra day and man did I wish we had stayed at Petra’s place the whole time! They were incredible hosts. I can’t stress that enough. We were supposed to be a party of 4 but the rest of the family had their room cancel at the last minute, and they still accommodated us, even bringing us extra towels and other amenities that went above and beyond (bananas for breakfast, a brand new coffee maker for us at the last minute, etc!)  The room is even better than pictured, and Petra and Tony kept it very clean and inviting. They were always available if we needed anything and were very fun and friendly, even just for our one night stay.  I would definitely recommend Petra and Tony’s room and them as hosts to anyone.   Only thing you may want to consider is there is not a subway station that is ‘super close’ to this part of Brooklyn, but Petra made sure to send us in the right direction through the bus system that got us where we needed to go in no time. The bus stop that got us to the subway was only a block away.   All in all, it was a great stay and we will definitely be visiting them again the next time we stay in Brooklyn!

Denise is the perfect host. She is a warm and friendly person. She was very helpful and so nice to talk to. Denise and her family really made me feel at home.  My room was spacious and clean and had all the comfort that I needed. I really loved the neighborhood, very colorful and lively. I never felt unsafe, even when I came home late at night. The subway was nearby and I could walk to prospect park.

My stay at Farrel's place was excellent! Much cleaner and safer than my last experience living in the Bronx. He's very laid back and easy to communicate with. The check-in process was much simpler than expected. House is very nicely furnished and clean. Never felt unsafe living there and felt fortunate I got to play with his two adorable little doggies as well.

Mauro’s place was clean and spacious. It was conveniently located near a subway station but was in a rougher area of Brooklyn. During the day was fine but at night it felt a little bit sketchy & unsafe. We had a nice stay at the apartment & the balcony was nice too. The vent system in our room wasn’t great because when the door was closed it would get very cold. Mauro had a good response time with our questions, but at the end of our stay tried to charge us for an extra towel usage (which he never mentioned anywhere previously) and we had to dispute the charge so that wasn’t ideal. but overall not bad

Staying at Farrel's place was a pleasant experience! Most of our friends told us we shouldn't book a place in Bronx cause its dangerous and/or far away! Well it wasn't! We didn't feel unsafe, although we were coming back home at night, riding the subway, walking the streets etc. The price for this home was far cheaper than everything we could find in Manhattan and it took about 20 min, by train, to get downtown. Farrel was a great host! He made as feel like home, always with a smile, a great sense of humour and he has there to be found if we needed anything! The house is comfortable, stylish, clean and the bed mattress was really nice (always a plus)! Finally the best part was the company we had! Farrel most of the day isn't home, but the other two hosts the little ShihTzus, Banksy and Tobie, were there and they were adorable. They would keep us company and in return they only needed to be cuddled and we'll surely gonna miss these two sleepyheads!!! All in all we had a great stay and we hope to get back soon, cause we surely are going miss all three of our hosts!!

This was by far my worst experience on Airbnb. First, there are cockroaches in the bathroom. Second, the window is broken so it doesn’t properly seal, the portable charger is really dirty and makes a really bad smell when you turn it on. So good luck on staying warm, I had back pain after my two nights because of having to sleep with all my clothes on. I even requested to change rooms (there’s a second room that looked empty and clean) but got denied despite giving the reasons above. Third, the dog kept barking all night too. Cesar has a big dog and it was impossible to sleep with the noise. Lastly, coming the NYC from abroad I didn’t have internet access, so I was at the mercy of the Airbnb host to provide the wifi password. Unfortunately, he didn’t leave any information for me and I had to walk around the apartment looking for the router in case the wifi password was written on it’s back. Fortunately the second clean room had a paper with the wifi information. All in all, I can’t believe this is listen on Airbnb. This is an unsafe environment for anyone, mentally and physically speaking. Stay away.

Marvis and Nigel are wonderful hosts!  They were very quick to answer any of our questions before arrival and very flexible with our delayed arrival due to our flight delay.  The room was exactly as stated online.  The big pros are: Marvis and Nigel, great location (safe and well lit area, easy access to subway, a bit north, but can get to theater district in 25-30 min), privacy, and the great price.  The cons were:  bed is plenty large for two people (my 18 yr old daughter and I stayed here), but it is more of a futon mattress, so after four nights it was pretty uncomfortable.  Also, they are on the 4th floor (as advertised!), which felt like a long way up after a full day exploring the city.  Also, sharing one bathroom was a bit tricky.  The 4 nights we stayed we had a few times when we were getting up and ready to take a shower, but the bathroom was in use.  Possibly we could have planned better and requested the bathroom at a certain time in the am, but we were being spontaneous and did not always know what time we'd want it.  This was not a big problem, though, as (I am guessing) Marvis and Nigel were thinking of us and it was never a long delay (maybe 5-10 min).  For a shorter, less expensive way to stay in and explore NYC this home is great choice!  I would much rather have a kind, friendly, helpful host in a safe location and a little less comfortable bed rather than an irritable and hard to deal with host in a sketchy part of the city and a dream bed!

Pros: Great hospitality and communication. He responds right away and is flexible with your stay. Plenty of closet space and the room is spacious. The location is not bad especially since it's right next to Yankee Stadium and plenty of restaurants.  Cons: There were some roaches during my first night. As soon as I told the host, he took care of it right away and I never saw any after that. Ceiling and walls are a bit sketchy, but I rarely looked at them. Could use a coffee maker. There is some noise from neighbors outside, but that is out of the host's control.  Overall: It's 5 stars based on it's value. Host is great and you'll sleep just fine at night.

Brandon's place was amazing for location and transit. There's a train station 10 minute walk away that will take you right into times square and there are great food places near the station. Brandon's apartment is clean cozy, has very friendly neighbours and an AMAZING view. The only hassle we had during our stay was that parking was difficult to find at times and because there is street cleaning we had to wake up at 8 to move our car to a new parking space. We felt safe walking around the neighbourhood and there are so mmany people walking there families and dogs you never feel unsafe. I would recommend this place to anyone travelling to New York for leisure and tourism.

**Amazing experience!!**    There was amazing communication from the host. That’s important to me so I’m not left confused when visiting a new place. I really felt safe in the area. I hear all these scary horror stories about New York and Brooklyn, but it was totally fine.   The room was perfect. It had everything we needed to enjoy ourselves. The bed was very comfy! The room felt very clean too.   Public transportation was nearby so getting into Manhattan by subway was totally doable. We chose to drive all around Brooklyn, Queens, and then Manhattan the next day and it was great.   You won’t regret staying here!

Go there with your eyes closed. Yes, the neighborhood is the opposite of what you expect.... Yes, some people will say that it is a "special" neighborhood BUT it's true, I lived there with my 18 and 14 year old sons for a week, returning to Petra and Tony's house at any time without any fear because in the neighborhood there is respect without any measure among us❤️
Simple and practical apartment for 1 night before the return flight. Petra is adorable, always ready to help.

This place is good location & could be worth it. However, all guests must know this is a 4 floor walk up. If you have suitcases & over 30 good luck!!! The stairway was extremely dirty & v. unpleasant to walk up. A simple clean up such as sweeping would of made a big difference. Within the apt. my biggest disappointment was the host had a young kid come to clean, he had no idea how to clean a bathroom which I had to do myself. During my stay the toilet got clogged up due to "kid cleaner" hired by host, throwing hair & papertowel in bowl. Then I of the 7 guests did a disgusting mess in toilet making it unpleasant for everyone. The host needs to be more hands on, during my ck. in she was away in Fl. then came for 2days & again left for Turkey for a month according to her. My advice to this host is if you are not staying on property while guests are coming & going, you need to hire a professional cleaner so your guests can have a clean stay.

Easy access to city and very close to Chinatown, budget friendly but there is nothing besides location.  Linens, towels and beds were old and stained (nothing like the pictures).  The place was clean aside from the sheets and towels which were not pleasant to use or sleep on.  The neighbour is also a little run down and sketchy.  Host was responsive. The room is also very small with no dresser or desk to put your stuff or gather yourself on.

The place was very clean. The keys were not where they were supposed to be and we were a bit put off by the woman we eventually got them from (didn't introduce herself or ask our names). The neighborhood wasn't great (decent amount of homeless people/shopping carts) and we ended up leaving and not staying the night. I did not get to check out the roof views. I suspect they are lovely. Jerome was nice over our messages. We would not go back.

The location of this place was awesome. Easily accessible to ALL public transportation, local restaurants, and attractions. We understood that the apartment wasn't updated, however we were disappointed with the accommodations. There was only one roll of toilet paper, the paper towel rack in the kitchen had about 10 sheets left, there was little to no dish soap to wash our dishes, there was no hand soap in the restroom to wash hands (we used someone’s left over body wash) and lastly the front door to the building was left unlocked/unsecured all night which we thought was kind of sketchy. I would recommend in the future making sure the small details are kept in mind; making sure there’s soap, towels, toilet paper, instructions on operating the projector, local restaurant recommendations/attractions, etc.

Jeremiah has a great place that sure feels like home away from home. However, it was uncomfortably warm in the apartment and there were no towels for me to dry with after a shower. Overall, the place is very clean and well-kept, I just wish my experience was what I hoped it to be. The rooftop is awesome with a great view of the NYC skyline, but beware to anyone who is afraid of climbing a vertical ladder! I would recommend this place but give warning to making sure everything you need is available before it’s too late to request any help.

Jeremiah’s place was great! Easy check in, awesome rooftop, a bit scary to climb up but thrilling lol. Responded well allowed me to check out a lil bit later then than the the time. Overall nice spot will recommend. Thanks

Nothing is as pictured. The rooftop was the biggest disappointment, its what i looked forward to but you have to go up via a very unsafe ladder (im 6months pregnant). The bedroom was super dull & very uncomfortable. There is NO COUCH as pictured.  The views out the windows were disturbing. There was an open bag of ice in the freezer (unsanitary). Host claims free parking but almost towed my car. He also is very hard to reach via phone. Overall i did not like the space but had no choice.

I was bummed there were no couches but the bean bags are a nice touch and comfy. The projector is a cool feature to bring in the style of the house. Awesome privacy and the roof top is dope, but the ladder is scary to go up and down. Overall the place was very clean and spacious, perfect spot if you just need a place to stay and lounge while you make your moves in NY. Can’t wait to book again!   Side note: coming off the highway I didn’t expect to see the projects but where is the air bnb is located is nice and residential
Stress-free / convenient / as described / great location / roof access a real bonus! Thank you - we'll be coming back. Briony x

Perfect little place to sleep between outings or relax all day.  Big TV, comfortable bed and pillows, AWESOME water pressure (I'm back home and suffering from shower envy as I type), quiet block as NYC goes, building was clean, lots of necessities that past tenants have left behind (hangers!!), great blackout shade.  Hillary responded to the couple of questions we had within minutes.   The neighborhood was great too. Lots of great restaurants and bars, barber shops, 24-hour pharmacies, and banks within a two-block radius.  One block to the subway.  We really don't have anything negative to say about the whole package.  We just hope it's available when we finalize our next trip.

This little place is terrific for a couple.  Location is outstanding, with the subway nearby, and tons of great restaurants within just a few blocks.  Drug store and Starbucks is close, too.  The apartment is in great shape and well kept.  Hillary is very helpful and a great host!  Would definitely stay here again!
Hillary was great, quick replies, easy pick-up of keys, no cancelation, no stress. I'd like to come back if I have the chance!

I can’t say enough about how great the location is. You’re a block away from the E train (which is one of the three direct lines connecting the JFK Airport’s AirTrain), making cheap transportation to and from the airport a breeze. You’re also a block or less away from great restaurants and cheap street vendors. The apartment wasn’t exactly what I expected when I booked because of out dated photos. However, my husband and I didn’t mind as it was mostly furniture changes. The foam pillows and firm mattress were the best I’ve ever slept on at an Airbnb. The full window pull down shade was also a much needed bed time accessory with the summer’s 5AM sunrise. Overall, a great and enlightening experience! Staying here definitely gave us a glimpse into what it would be like to live in the area.

This place is a great Midtown find, close to many restaurants and shops. A drug store, the subway, a post office, and amazing bagels are all within just a few minutes of the flat. And it even has a lift! Small yet efficient, this studio is outfitted with a comfortable bed, a spacious closet, and chest of drawers big enough to warrant unpacking your bags. Good water pressure and not too much neighborly noise. Definitely worth the price.

I was too busy to take advantage of all the amenities this host offers, but much enjoyed what I had time for.  I was a bit worried about the Murphy bed, but it was terrific - NOTHING like a sofa bed, which is what I feared.  Very very comfortable, as good as the best bed I've ever slept in.  All the linens seemed to be 100% cotton, and it felt very relaxing and luxurious.  Grace cooks a lot and offered me some of her home-made eggnog.  She also whipped up some "Golden Milk" that makes palatable turmeric, a powerful anti-inflammatory that's great for arthritis.  Her place is very close to the neighborhood's Saturday Farmer's Market which featured wonderful specialty foods such as duck bacon and fresh cider. It's also right around the corner from one of the neighborhood's best cafes, Indian Road, and so close to Inwood Hill Park and Fort Tryon and The Cloisters.  I also enjoyed the consistent aesthetic of her apartment and how she made the most of its space.  Meticulously clean and a wonderful refuge from the city and the stressful events that caused me to need to be there.  When I arrived it was after 10 p.m.  I was offered dinner and provided with fruit and salad, per my preferences.  It was unexpected and very very nice to be treated so hospitably and have my individual personal needs met.  I needed to be in this area, so this location was perfect for me.  It is just one block from huge Inwood Hill Park, which along with playgrounds and tennis courts, has trails that lead up to heights overlooking the Hudson.  It's a wonderful neighborhood with lots of community feeling.  (I did not have a car.)  It's a short walk from the 207th St. subway station on the A train line.

We stayed for five nights at Emily's place in Brooklyn and it was perfect. We enjoyed morning coffee in the beautiful back garden and slept well on a comfy bed after a day of exploring the city. Emily was very welcoming and a great hostess. All logistics about the stay (key pick up, etc.) were very clearly communicated, so no travel related stress whatsoever. The location is perfect: close to the subway, but on a very quiet street. We loved our stay and hope to return next time we visit.

Janina and her husband Cecil were great hosts and made our stay amazing. Cleanliness was top-notch and the location was also very helpful. The room was a bit smaller than we thought (from the pictures) and the bathroom is a little away from the room and closer to the other 2 rooms; hence, we were always afraid that we might be disturbing other people at night. Other than that, it was great! Definitely, recommend it.

Our Host Was very nurturing to me & my wife. She was having major spine surgery at the time and under a lot of stress.     The apartment and room were exactly as stated in the description.    The neighborhood was close to the hospital and very safe.

I stayed with Kim for more than three months and had a really hard time. Most of the time the kitchen was really dirty, many times I had no possibility to use it. Kim is a really loud roommate, sometimes she sings and listen to music loud. Other times she comes home in the middle of the night, really loud, and starts to talk to the cat or the persons she brought home. And she often has friends over, most of the times they came after 11 p.m. and stayed until 3 or 4 a.m., what was really annoying. I always had to text her or talk to her, if they could be more quiet. Sometimes it worked, many times not. A few comments below she wrote something about a "zero noise tolerance after ten p.m.", that sounds to me like a bad joke. She and her friends were loud after midnight, the whole week. Not even from Monday to Thursday she tried to respect her own rules. Even in my final-exam week I asked her at 1 am if she and her friend could be more quiet - they did not.  The Bathroom was really dirty as well, sometimes the cat peed and shitted into the bathroom. The dirt of Kim and her friends was there for weeks, I don't know how "often" she cleaned the room while my 14 weeks stay.  After one discussion about the circumstances in the kitchen and the bathroom she wanted me to move out. She ignored me for a few days and texted me that she wants me to move out. I knocked on her door a few times and than she said "I'm sleeping!". It is not possible to discuss with her. For staying in the apartment she wanted more money from me, I was so afraid of being in New York without an apartment that I started thinking about it. It was the second time she asked me for more money, without informing Airbnb about it.  I also know, that she was in my room without asking me for permission. She took something out of my closet. I don't know how often she went into my room, but that is not ok.  In front of the building are sitting a few young guys, while summer I appreciate the fact, that they took care who walks into the house. But while autumn the guys started to smoke inside (in front of the doors to the apartments) and downstairs in the garbage room. All in all is the apartment really sweet and Harlem is a nice place to stay, but I can not recommend to stay with Kim. She does not respect her guests and is really moody.

This was my first Airbnb and it exceeded my expectations. Grace was an excellent host from the moment I selected her place.  The room, bathroom and kitchen was extremely clean and organized. Considering how old the building is, the plumbing / water pressure was as if i was in a new home (just perfect). There's an air conditioning unit in the bedroom and i used it one night and it cooled the room quickly. The location was easy to find and just a 30 min subway ride into the heart of NY.  There's a neighborhood park and a track and field just down the street for those that want to run / workout.  Grace was easy to communicate with and made me feel at home once i arrived. I never once felt unsafe or uncomfortable in the home and in the neighborhood. It truly was a great experience and i will def stay here again should i return.

Our first experience with AirBnB and we loved Larah's appartment! and we absolutly reccomend it .   The appartment is exactly like the pictures and description in Airbnb, it was very clean and well equipped with all you may need. In addition, because it is a familiar building you feel like your are at your own home and neighborhood. The building is located in a residencial street that is nice, quiet and secure. You don't feel dangerous in the area at all during daytime or at  night.   The location is perfect, you can arrive in 5 min. walking from 125st subway station, in which  there are four subway lines (two are express trains ), from which you can arrive, between 10- 15 min to the center of Manhattan, also it takes a 20 min nice walk to Central Park. Two blocks away from the apartment you can find a supermarket and nice little restaurants.    We did`t have much interaction with our host (because we were out the whole day lol), but every time we met, they were very friendly and always helping us with our needs, logistics with Lara and her family was very flexible and easy :) .    We are planning to go back to NY in a sooner future and for sure we will talk to Larah  to book her apartment again. 100% recommended.

It was very nice apartment and host. The room was tidy and stylish as expected. Check in and Check out were very smooth. Host was very kind.  I warried about the area,harlem, because I heard that harlem was a little dangerous from guidebook but it was  not anything dangerous. (I went back the apartment from downtown by subway at about 11:00 pm.)  I enjoyed NYC stay a lot thanks to the aparment and host.

Clean, conveniently located apartment.  Great access to the subway, with a supermarket, drug store and restaurants within walking distance. Our hosts were friendly and helpful - even printing out our sports tickets for us! Couldn't recommend this apartment more highly.

A fabulous apartment, good value for money. Close to the subway and also a walkable distance from Central Park. Spotlessly clean, and very roomy. Initially I was a bit nervous about the area- it is Harlem! But I actually didn't feel unsafe at all whilst there. A great laundry in the basement too, which is so essential when traveling.

Wonderful true b&b experience. Grace clearly takes great pride in her property and has attention to detail beyond any host I’ve previously experienced. Artful touches, soothing lighting, exquisitely comfortable bed, chocolates. Absolutely immaculate bathroom! Wonderfully quiet location and an easy pleasing walk to the A train past an expansive park. It was much like staying in a high end boutique hotel, just with a shared bathroom. This is the type of Airbnb experience the hotels are afraid of. No one will ever bake you an apple pie at the Hilton. 5 stars, hurrah!!

I loved this place!!  Grace has created such a lovely, peaceful and organized space in my beloved hectic New York City!   I had a lot to accomplish in my business, and it could have been a very stressful venture.  Yet Grace’s place was a heavenly oasis to come “home” to!  I slept so well there.  The bed is comfortable, the A/C rapidly cools in the summer heat, the bed lamps make for cozy reading, and there is even a white noise machine with your choice of sounds for perfect sleep.  Grace is a host who genuinely cares about you enjoying your trip, and this greatly aided in keeping all the stress of my day at bay.  Examples of her hosting:  Once during my trip, I injured myself (pulled a muscle at work), and Grace drew me an Epsom Salt bath that successfully relaxed my sore and irritated body.  She is also an AMAZING cook, and loves to surprise her guests with treats she has made.  Grace is very aware of her Guests comfort level, and gives plenty of personal space to them.  However, she is also receptive to friendship should you offer it to her.  She is very clear of the organizational rules and boundaries of her place, which all result in a much more pleasant stay for all.    Grace deserves a standing ovation for some of her hosting innovations, and I highly recommend learning from her methods.    In summary:  I very much enjoyed my stay at her place, and I believe my business ventures were even more successful due to her care and attention to the comfort of her place and her guests.

NEGATIVE Feedback.   I did not expect to experience this situation  from an Airbnb listing whose slogan is : “It’s trust that makes it work “ . After a few days , I started feeling very uncomfortable at the host’s apartment. The host showed a very anxious behavior related to  - what she called suspicious behavior of her upstairs neighbor. Actions like peeking through  the hole of the door, unplugging electrical wires etc etc  became daily. I suggested she had the situation investigated, for her own sake and as a safety concern for her paying guests. She didn’t do so, but confronted me instead. Not  feeling safe in her place anymore , I decided to leave a week earlier and asked  –by principle and for the money too - for a partial refund, which I received thru Airbnb. The cleanliness of the room is very questionable too – there is a lack of freshness in the whole apartment and I had to open my window all the time because of a bad odor. The carpet was very old and certainly has not been deep cleaned or received a bacterial treatment for a long time. Maybe this is what caused me coughing so much .The apartment is described as a “2 bedroom” at the website which attracted me , but in reality the host sleeps in a corner of the living room , separated by a foldable screen – which is not very pleasant either….

Sandy's place is lovely. It is just as it looks in the pictures. The neighborhood is also in a great part of town with a lot of places to eat, Lincoln Center down the street, and Central Park a short walk away. I never felt unsafe there or in the apartment itself. There is also a grocery store just a block away and its close to a subway station. Sandy is also the type of host that wants to make sure her guests are having a good experience. She is very quick to contact you back with any needs or questions you have. Highly recommend!

We never met James, but did not experience any hiccups with moving in and out of the place. Apartment is clean and nice, located on quiet street. 10-12 minutes walk to stations (we had small kids with us) and access to most of city with just one line.  Place is big, as advertised, and we did not have issues in finding space for 6 adults and 4 kids. Area around stations is a bit shady, but we never felt any danger or inconvinience. Small bar (Hoghead) 1 minute walk from place was also good addition. On the cons - I had to buy my shampoo myself, since I could not find any in the apartment, and realised it should have been provided with the place only after checking out. Kitchen was big and well equipped, but dont expect to have much seating space if you are party bigger than 6 people. Shower and bathtub are on the second floor, so if you have elderly or disabled persons with you, it might be a challenge to climb quite steep steps to take shower.

Duplex accommodation as described.  We were a group of 9 (5 children and 4 adults). Metro station nearby (line 1) allowing easy access to the center of NY (despite a certain travel time...) We did not meet James, collected the keys in a key box and left them in the accommodation when checking out. Sheets and towels provided We did not feel unsafe in the neighborhood. Few restaurants nearby but an establishment that we appreciated (excellent value for money). Well-stocked supermarket nearby and with very late opening hours: very practical!

The apartment was nice and spacious and is accurate as shown in pictures. James was nice and communicative and recommended us places around the neighborhood. We had a good time overall except for a few issues and concerns.  - We found the neighborhood a bit shady which we weren't aware of and went thru some racist comments too. - Since James lives in the same building, he was able to come into the apartment when we weren't around to clean up and throw the garbage. It was nice of him to help but we felt like it was an invasion of privacy for coming in and throwing what was left out while we were away. - Towards the end of our trip, we had some issues with the keys and our conversation with James was not pleasant. To be honest, he was frustrated and we felt that the conversation could have gone a lot better than if did. He came off a little rude and abrupt but later apologized and we got everything sorted out.

I loved my experience and stay at Dragan's lovely home. I was a little hesitant because I have always hear scary stories about staying at someone's elses home. But Dragan was accommodating and always a text away.   The pictures are depict exactly what you have. The rooms were big, furniture are good as new, bathroom is cleaner than ever. It was so nice of him to have toiletries and everyday necessities. I also loved how he recycles and separates trash from recyclables. Coming from bay area, it always nice to see someone practice a green life style  The kitchen was equipped with pots and pans if you would like to cook. There is a coffee maker if you are a javaholic and even flu medication if you catch a cold. Everything you need and more!  I didn't realize how close this is from Manhattan. The subway is literary 50 steps away. You can take either the R or the M to get to the city. The home is also located on a big street so if you need a to catch a cab, it will not be an issue. I flew from La Guardia so it was about a 10 minute cab ride (approximately 12 bucks with tip).   Queens is a great place to stay if you want to be away from the touristy area but a couple trains stops away from the big city. Perfect for travelers like me. I would definitely recommend anyone to Dragan's home. He is such a kind host with two lovely dogs. I could not have asked for a better stay. Thank Dragan!

Very good and quiet neighbourhood and Dragan is a nice and helpful host. My best recommendation. Ian and family P.S. at the time we stayed there the subway was under maintains, so the last direct line to Queens was around 9:30pm from Manhattan, a little stressful some evenings.

Wendy has a nice little garden apartment on a lovely Brooklyn street. Staying in Wendy's nice little garden apartment comes, unfortunately, with Wendy as your host- or, I should say- your invisible overseer. Based on my recent 4 night stay, it seems that Wendy would very much like you to pay handsomely to stay in her apartment- and then not stay there, if at all possible. Wendy has many house rules which she will gladly let you know you're breaking with an instant phone call, regardless of the time. Strangely, Wendy calls from a remote location in a different state, so one gets the feeling there are hidden cameras in Wendy's nice little garden apartment. The overall effect can only be described as creepy... and very unwelcoming. Wendy also neglected to provide soap, a working coffee maker and a wireless password until it was asked for. Also, a key to the backdoor, leading to a lockout situation on a freezing cold morning. Wendy's apartment also lacked any of the personal "niceties" that make airbnb a unique traveling experience; a note, a bottle of wine, a list of local restaurants, shops, etc. Wendy does this for a living, apparently, and she knows how keep her expenses low. In fairness, the apartment is in a great neighborhood and the place was clean. But if you're expecting to walk into a space with a welcoming feel and a friendly vibe, lower your expectations. And whatever you do, don't walk or talk while you're in Wendy's nice little garden apartment; that's a breech of the house rules. And remember- Wendy is watching you....

Staying at Eric's place was a good decision! It made our trip to NYC much more confortable, mainly because of the apartment location, just 1 small block away from the 103th Subway Station, which gives you easy acess to most city areas. Besides that, the place had everything we needed for a stress-free stay, from bed sheets to kitchen tools, we found it as clean as one would expect, and maybe the most relevant detail was the host; we had a very inconvenient check-in/check-ou schedule, but Eric was very understanding and made the best he could to help us with this.  I would surely recommend to a friend staying at Eric's Apartment!

Alex and Toby's apartment is a great place to stay if you're wanting to experience New York City.  We stayed there for 3 months (January-March) with our dog Oscar.  We loved that it was a couple of blocks away from Washington Square Park and close to so many amazing, affordable restaurants (Mamoun's, Old Tbilisi, John's Pizza, and La Lanterna were some of our favorites). Alex was very accommodating in meeting us at the apartment when we arrived, providing a list of accommodations we may need during our stay,  and replying to any questions/concerns (our internet went out once).   The apartment itself has a lot of character and has everything you need for a short or extended stay.  The biggest drawback is by far the noise.  It's on a very busy street, and it can be noisy until 3 or 4am.  The white noise machines definitely help, and we eventually got used to it.  The advantage of living on a busy street however is that you never know what you'll encounter.  For instance one night we returned to the apartment to find Robert Deniro shooting a movie in front of our place.  Not only did we get to watch the filming, but because we lived there, we got to be extras!  Also because the street and neighborhood are so active, we never felt unsafe walking the dog at night or venturing out alone. The close proximity to the subway also made exploring other parts of the city very easy.  We'll definitely look back with fond memories of our time spent at this apartment in Greenwich Village.

A great find for sure...Brian was so clear with directions via email.  He sent me step by step directions on the location of his door with visuals, the location of where to pick up my keys, since he had to work when I arrived.  Then step by step instructions on how to key into his building, his apartment door.  The location is easy to find and easy to access.  Just as he described it on the site.  No surprises and perfect for my visit.  The apartment was perfect.  When I arrived, he has pages of instructions on house rules, how to handle the heat, the tv and the kitchen waiting for you in the bedroom.  Brian covers it all.  Emergency contacts and list of special sites, eateries and all.  Brian’s apartment is a simple walk from Time Square and the subway.  Of course, Hell’s Kitchen is the best place to stay when you visit the city.  Can’t go wrong and you can’t go wrong with Brian as a host.  He is available by text and emails and truly opens his apartment to his guest.  The bedroom as big enough for me and would be for two.  There is a window for light, but not much of a view.  But that is not important.  There is great storage.  Dresser, cupboards and a closet with hangers.  There is also space for your luggage, which is nice.  The rest of the apartment is nicely decorated and gives you space to relax to read or watch TV.    Brian helped me out when I thought I lost my phone and needed access the web.  He happened to show up while I was in the apartment and let me use his phone to find my phone, which was with friend in their car.  I found it and got it, thanks to Brian taking the time.  There are so many local stores, coffee shops, drug stores, and restaurants within minutes from this location.  He mentioned a bar located downstairs, and you can hear the music, but it really just becomes white noise and I slept like a baby.  It is what it is, an apartment in Hell’s Kitchen...no frills, but perfect to visit the city.  A great deal and great host.    Thank you Brian.

great apartment very well located, we feel very comfortable there, which allowed us to come back during the day. convenient for going to Times Square, Central Park, TOR, Empire without taking the metro each time. In terms of noise, it's NY....the exterior wind tunnel is very unpleasant at night, you should know that but it doesn't prevent you from sleeping....

Eric was great when checking us in, he gave us a tour of the apartment and a short tour of the block to point us in the direction of markets, food, central park, and the subway. I thought this was great! The apartment itself looks exactly like the photos, very clean. It is on the small side, but it worked great for my husband and I. The kitchen was stocked with utensils and cookware, which was great when we wanted to prepare our own food or reheat leftovers. It is pretty quiet at night but the New York city sounds start early on in the morning. The subway (Line 6) was about 1.5 blocks away and was very convenient. We took it often. The area is in East Harlem and there were some sketchy characters walking around at night but we never felt unsafe. There are markets and soooooo many fast food places within a block away. The only thing I wish was that there were more restaurants and things to do nearby at night that didn't require a subway ride to enjoy. We very much enjoyed our stay. Thank you Eric!

I had a really wonderful time in Igor and Gita's place. I was studying in New York and so booked to stay there for roughly 3 weeks. It was an extremely warm and welcoming environment that I felt very at home in - the perfect retreat from the sometimes overwhelming nature of New York! The flat is perfectly located for access to Manhattan - either a very short walk to the subway or, as I often chose to do, a beautiful wander across Prospect Park, which is essentially on the doorstep. There are several good supermarkets/laundrettes etc. roughly 2-3 minutes walk from the flat, and I never felt unsafe in the area on the nights that I was returning late.  Igor knows a lot about music (Jazz in particular) and was incredibly generous with his knowledge and experience of the music scene in Brooklyn/Manhattan. The flat is a treasure trove of books on art/music/film/etc. and it was sometimes difficult to tear myself away from the place. Certainly if you're interested in the arts and culture you'll feel very at home here.  I will 100% check first to see if this place is available the next time I am in New York (soon I hope). Compared to other Airbnb places I've stayed this felt like a real gem.

We had a wonderful six night stay in Thomas's apartment!! There isn't enough room allotted to share how perfect the location was for us - we will never stay anywhere but West Village when we return! The most amazing food, coffee/tea shops, and subways are all RIGHT there. (Definitely don't miss out on Mary's Fish Camp directly below you). Thomas was so easy to work with and accommodating - he made the experience stress free & fun! Thank you so much, Thomas!! We loved your apartment & our time in the city.

Eric’s place was the perfect location for our week long stay in New York. The place was close to the subway, bakeries, and Central Park! Eric was a great host and took the time to explain where the local shops were which I greatly appreciated. The apartment is tucked away towards the back of the building so expect very quiet evenings/nights in NY. I felt very safe in this locations as well. I have stayed in NY several times and Eric’s place is my absolute favorite. The location was hands down the best part. Need snacks? Seven-11 is around the corner. Need great local coffee? Bakery on Third has great coffee and pastries! Need some food? The Ideal Basket has all you need. There is also another grocery store called Fine and Fare around the block. Need cheap transportation to your favorite NY attractions? The subway entrance to the 4 and 6 train is less than a three minute walk! Eric’s place is the perfect place to stay at especially for first time visitors to the city. While the apartment is small, it has everything you need for a great stay in NY. Don’t let the 350 square foot scare you. You will have a full kitchen and table, with a great sofa mattress in the living room and an awesome size restroom. Out of all the apartments I have stayed at in NY Eric’s place had the most to offer to make you comfortable. I highly recommend booking your stay at Eric’s place! We will definitely stay here again on our next trip to NY.

The subway is about 10 minutes walk from the house, alternatively there is a bus very close. The quarter is full of restaurants and shops.  We  were very disappointed for the poor cleaning of the house: we  found an apartment dirty and messy. The bathroom in particularly was very untidy and dirty. In a room you could smell the dog (of the owner) and on the bed (the cover) we found animal hair. We love cats and dogs, but it doesn't mean that we accept this kind of things. I loved the apartment, but it was absolutely dirty....As I already wrote in my previous private comment, i love dogs and cats, and I allow my dog on my bed....but when I have guests, I change the covers ! There was a terrible , unpleasant  smell in my room.... The shower courtin is black because humidity...... and I do not imagine to find used razors or similar in the shower of a rented apartment... The freezer was full of old food, passed out...  I would love hear other comments...it is impossible nobody noticed what I am speaking about....

Daniel responded to our booking very quickly. Afterwards, all communication was done through his Mum, Nancy. She was quick to respond to our text messages and very helpful and accommodating. We never actually met Daniel, but Nancy was lovely.  The apartment is in a great location, a few minutes walk from the subway with 2 lines going to Manhattan (M & R). There is a laundromat, convenience store and Chinese takeaway place around the corner, and with cafes and restaurants just a short walk away. We never felt unsafe in the neighbourhood.  The apartment and bedroom were very clean, Nancy provided us with bath and face towels, and we had full access to the bathroom and kitchen.  Our one complaint was that the internet was choppy and unreliable which was a bit of a hassle.  Otherwise, we loved our stay in NYC. It was a lovely apartment, great location, close to everywhere we wanted to go, and Nancy was very accommodating. Would strongly recommend!

I have really enjoyed my stay at Daniel's place in Astoria. If you need to go to Manhattan but you don't necessarily want to stay in the city area, Astoria is the place to be. It is very close to Steinway St station, which will take you to the city in 30m or less. There are supermarkets, a dollar tree, a drug store, cafes and places to eat within walking distance. You get to lock your room before you leave the apartment which is nice too. There is no elevator so you need to bring your luggage up the stairs to the 3rd floor. Overall I had a very great time here, and Nancy was very nice as well.

We stayed in Olivia and Bob’s beautiful Nolita apartment for a long weekend while visiting New York. It was in every aspect superb: the apartment itself is spacious and well-appointed, it has an excellent roof terrace, and it is ideally located in a fun and friendly neighbourhood (the proximity to the New Museum was a particular treat!)  Olivia and Bob were excellent hosts, providing plenty of information about the apartment and the local area. It was clear that they cared about us having a good time and had put much thought into equipping their apartment to be a great place to say.   In a town full of small, overpriced hotel rooms I cannot stress enough what a delight it was to stay here.
The photos are real, the place is clean. The area looks a little unsafe. The last day the apartment had a bad smell in the main bedroom, internet a little slow

We were overall disappointed with our stay at Simme’s house. The area was ok and perfectly safe (there are some great coffee shops - albeit it’s a bit suburban) but the house itself is not comfortable. The couch is purely decorative and not at all comfortable. The bed is old and creaky, the sheets don’t fit properly and are synthetic, and the air conditioner is so loud it kept us awake at night. However, the worst part was that Simme let herself in one day unannounced and surprised my husband who was sick and trying to get some rest. She was impolite and seemed suspicious of us which is absurd. Coming in unannounced with no warning is totally unacceptable. She didn’t even ring the bell. When we left, she opened the door, scowled at us and then shut the door again. I would not recommend you stay here as it’s just not worth it. It’s uncomfortable, the host is unfriendly and obtrusive, and the area is ok but there are better places in Brooklyn.

This was my first AirBnB experience so naturally I was a bit apprehensive, especially given our late arrival time. However, even though Casper was unable to meet us to hand over the keys, his instructions were clear and he responded to my questions quickly. We picked up the keys and found the apartment with no problems.   We were very pleased with the apartment, it is exactly as Casper describes and has a cool living area and kitchen. As others have said, it is in a great place, close to the L subway and just a short walk into the East Village and all it has to offer. We were able to easily explore most of Manhattan using the apartment as a base. Again Casper responded quickly to all my questions and concerns and was always ready to offer assistance. His suggestion I use the Yelp app was an excellent one - using the WiFi in the apartment and Yelp helped us pick restaurants and bars to visit.   Checking-out was as painless as checking-in. Overall our AirBnB experience was excellent and Casper is a great host. We did all of our communication through AirBnB and nothing went wrong. All of this for much less than a hotel would have cost. I hope my next AirBnB holiday goes as well as this one did.   Rob H.

Davids Apartement is a very individual und unique place.  We loved the surroundings and the area. (The Café in the same house was a great breakfast place !!)  The Apartment was very clean and David responded very quick, that was super easy.  He made our stay very convenient and stress-free which I really appreciated. I would recommend Davids Place to all travellers, who wants so live in a hip area in a cosy apartment with enough space.

Casper was very kind and good host. Without any problem. Apartment and room was good, but little bit smaller as it is in pictures, so little bit less space for personal stuff in room. Everything was clean and tidy.  Casper was not at home by our arrive. The keys gave us his friend just one block away from apartment. Also we needed once Casper's help with some administration, he do not had any problem with that. So thank you. Casper is really nice and kind person.  About location. We was little bit, but really just a little bit sad. First half of street from 2nd Ave is nice, clean, there is a park front of street. But second half, where starts the entry to building was more dirty, homeless people there, trash on street, sidewalk. On 1st Ave corner smelled too much pees from homeless people. This was really not pleasantly. Also there is a Hospital right front of building so ambulance cars siren hooting almost every time. No elevator in building. No possibility to let the window open in room. But although this, it was fine. This was just a few small problems. Nothing important.  Subway is a block away, there is much restaurants from 2nd Ave above, markets, street food, fruits stands etc. So the location is good. If you want just sleep in apartment, go ahead. It is really ideal for that :)

We enjoyed the time in Deborah's place. It was very quiet which was a surprise. It was located within walking distance to subway connection train L, down the other way to Houston St. to iconic Katz's.  We are two sisters in our 60's & 70's & never felt unsafe even when walking from the subway after enjoying an evening at the theater.  Downside--the washing machine was not working which we weren't told about prior to our visit.  Also the front gate lock is tricky beyond belief.

Perfect spot!  Ideally located in the East Village close to everything (subway, restaurants, coffee shops, parks and more).  David's place reminded me very much of my own so I felt at home.  I am a big coffee drinker so having a coffee maker avaliable in the apartment as well as a great coffee shop downstairs was ideal.  I don't think I would stay anywhere else on my future trips to the city.  Clean, perfectly set up, comfy and fun.  All the house information took the guesswork and stress out of the visit.
Casper’s place is a real steal and in a great location. He is accommodating and posted description is accurate. Casper is also super helpful!

So, NYC can be stressful, especially in a crowd on Times Square in the rain; however coming back to a safe and peaceful place was enormously comforting. Liam and Ed were wonderful hosts.
