The location is phenomenal for hanging out in the neighborhood with everything that is has to offer (it’s just 3 blocks away from Prospect Park!!) and it’s also easy to get to Manhattan as the F line is a couple of blocks away.   The apartment itself is very well decorated and thoughtfully organized. Rezi and family are very welcoming and made sure that we were well stocked with coffee and cleaning products. We are a family of 3 spending a week in NYC and we have plenty of space to relax and recharge.   Highly recommended.

Just like the title of this place says this is really a peaceful corner in the lively Harlem.  You have everything just right there: Supermarket, convenience store, pharmacy, laundry, restaurants, bank, coffee shop and more. There are two subway stations less than half mile away, there are also couple of bus stops just outside the building. I felt  safe in the neighborhood, I stayed there 10 days and used to walk back from the subway station to the apartment around 2 or 3 am and never felt unsafe. Taela is a great host, she lets you enjoy your staying and gives answer to any question you might have, she won't ever bother you at all.  I really recommend Taela's place. If I am back in New York I'll make sure to comeback to this peaceful place in Harlem.
Very nice host. Accommodating and patient. Cute apartment. Area is a touch sketchy.

First time in NY after many years, felt very unsafe in the room around 2am someone was attempting to enter the room with my daughter & I. Finally They stopped after me yelling, I laid in the bed and couldn’t sleep after that. I got up dressed and left in a hurry the next morning.

This stay was absolutely horrible and unsafe. Run by the hosts sons, upon arrival, one son opened the door and screamed that they didn’t know a tenant was coming to stay. The building reeked of cigarette smoke as well. Both sons were creepy. Stared at you when you opened a door and watched until you were back in your room. The door does not lock from the outside. VERY UNSAFE. Anytime when leaving your room, the whole building had access to your personal belongings. My room was entered upon twice without my presence. The worse of it, was that someone peed in my toilet and didn’t flush while I was gone for the day. Upon messaging the host, she was very rude. Said I was making false allegations and obviously forgot to flush the toilet (i never flush nor do I fold my tp that way) said she doesn’t run a club and she refused to give my refund despite leaving the premises with all belongings within five hours of check in. The mail door to the street is supposed to be shut and need to be unlocked by a key. Two of the three times I entered the building. The door was wide open to the street along with your personal door not shutting. The whole world has access to your room. A horrible horrible place to stay and should be taken off the air bnb site due to safety problems. Never stay here.   Side note: there is a mini fridge in the room with a small freezer but the freezer is unusable. Tenants of this building had hello fresh meat stored in there obviously as extra space for their personal freezer

Jeaneth is an excellent host. She responds quickly and provides periodic useful information.  The property is immaculate and beautifully decorated. She even provided a welcome basket full of goodies. The home was very quiet with no unpleasant noises from the family upstairs or the neighbors.  I can't say enough wonderful things about the home and my stay there. I highly recommend this property and I plan to stay there whenever I'm in the NY area.

Place was great, quiet for the most part, just a few times you can hear people yelling outside or the typical city noises. It was just what I needed, a clean place to sleep and shower and nothing more. The area can seem a bit shady but never had an issue with anyone. Would definitely recommend to anyone looking for the same basic needs.

The kitchen needs air conditioning, we were never able to use it, it is suffocating to take a single step in there. The neighborhood is very dangerous, for three nights we heard gunshots in the street, we couldn't get out of the fear we felt.

Overall good space for a big group, area seemed a little sketchy at first but we were able to walk to and from the subway station at night without any issues. Subway station a couple blocks away with most trips to the city taking about 45 minutes. Water, mints, and other items were provided. Only two showers, and one is in the master bedroom. Overall pretty good and fits a lot of people comfortably.

Genevieve’s listing is exactly as described.  My stay went very smoothly.  I was running late and having a lockbox is such a stress reliever.  Upon arriving, I was greeted with special doggie treats for my corgi back home. So thoughtful.  My room was in the back of the apartment, 2nd level, and very quiet. The bed and pillows were very comfy.  I stayed during COVID, so no interaction with the host or any other guest(s).  Checkout was at 10:00, but Genevieve was gracious enough to offer me a later one! Thanks again... Great neighborhood too! I drove a vehicle there. Not sure on subway info.  I definitely recommend Genevieve’s place!

Room is big and has a desk which is super nice! There is lots of street noise and honking... I sleep well in general and even I woke up too early from it. There are blackout curtains which are quite nice for blocking out ALL the light. Room comes with a space heater and a rack to hang clothes on, both of which were much appreciated. Mattress was super comfy :) The door locks to the room which I didn't happen to use but appreciated none the less.  Host has AWESOME communication and met me in person for check-in which was great.  Apartment was a little stressful to stay in because it feels a bit like a hostel... I think there are 3 bedrooms that are all rented on airbnb and then the host sleeps in the living room.
A little sketchy. Very small space.
Host is very nice. Really quick responses. Place is very tidy. It's 7 minutes walk to the subway and then 30min to Manhattan. Neighborhood very safe (dont be scared when back from Broadway show).

Agustin is a great host. Everything was good. Communication is perfect. Roomate are friendly and quiet. The area might be a bit sketchy at late night. But I was walking after 7-9 pm and I was fine. But later at night , ladies, just use Uber. Public Transportation is convenient. I can recommend this place.

Austine’s place is fantastic! It’s clean, modern, in a great neighborhood and very well kept. He’s there to help, the amenities are awesome-the shower is AMAZING!   Very easy to walk to the metro (<10 min) and very accessible (flat). If you come home at night, it’s safer than other places, of course be on the lookout, but didn’t feel wary or sketchy at all. Residential/family neighborhood:)   Will definitely be back, it was a wonderful place with a super nice host.

Alicia was wonderful. The place was incredibly clean. She is a very kind host, and does whatever she can for her guests. I had to come late after my luggage was lost and she had no issue. I had to make the trip last minute due to some things going on at the room I usually rent. She took no issue with when you come and go. I had a peaceful visit! For anyone concerned about the dog - the dog comes to visit with family once in awhile. She does not have a dog or any pet in the house otherwise. The dog was clean, did not bother anyone and left with family. I felt no threat or danger. She and her family occasionally played some music - of which I enjoyed hearing. It was a nice experience! I’m Indian Mongolian and European mix heritage, and staying there was a pleasant local foray into other cultures. She even shared some treats with me. If she forgot to mention any house rules, she was very nice about it. Her communication skills are top notch. I have absolutely nothing nasty to say about this lady or my time here.

Jenifer was a wonderful host! She kept a very tidy place, was quick to respond, and even had some baked goods in the kitchen for you! The bed was pretty comfy and the shower was hot and had amazing pressure.   If you’re not from a city, you might be put off by the neighborhood the house is in. I didn’t feel unsafe, but I am from a city and currently live in one. As for my friend, she was a little weary when walking to and from the subway.   The neighbors to the left of the house could be overheard fighting in the morning, but hey it’s New York!   I did enjoy my stay and would stay again! Jenifer was sweet and so helpful!

This is what happens when people think that "great location" all they need so rent out an apartment. Well, maybe that works in Manhattan  So, list of things I encountered for 7-days living  There were things that host can control:  1. Dirty room upon arrival (hairs on a sheet, dust, dirty mirror). Not clear communication from the cleaner. Also, found two small cockroaches in the bath floor two days in a row. But that's really center of hell's kitchen, so I guess they can climb walls and be everywhere. Bath have mold on a ceiling but I guess this part is unaviodable in a 4th floor out of 4 2. Noise. Room windows face 9th avenue. There is A LOT of going on in there: crazy homeless people fighting and screaming, firefighter trucks with their soundtrack, ambulances, pricks who think their car horn will make traffic dissapear if they press it long enough. All of that. They can't fix that, but you can fix one-glass-window with a curtain - that isolates like 30% of that sound level. There was no night when I was waken up less than 2 times. Yeah, changing or muting windows with some noise-blocking is expensive but ut's really base level of comfort, just be able to sleep  Also I experienced some things that host have little to control over:  3. Bath clog = 2 days without shower. Not their fault I guess. Buiding is old really 4. 3 days with little to no access to Wi-fi. Not their fault also, but there was no plan B, like second provider or portable router. They just contacted provider, provider said it's ok. It was broken again. Rinse, repeat for 3 days  So, the apartment itself is okay, it's just needs to me managed better. Or maybe I won unluckiest bingo of all times.   So, if location is all you need, then yeah. This is as good as location in Manhattan can be, book it but be ready at least for old building features

Lots of black mold!!  Do not stay here!! Avoid at all costs!! The pictures are incredibly deceiving. It looks clean, but those photos are heavily edited. The space is very SKETCHY (rotting wood, gaps in between doors) and not clean. There was BLACK MOLD SPROUTING literally all over the ceiling of shower room and toilet room. There was a large, translucent bucket hanging over the toilet that had an insane amount of mold growing. i had to book another airbnb as soon as i saw it because i was not about to sacrifice my health.  HORRIBLE COMMUNICATION: they did not provide me with any kind of details prior to my trip. MINIMUM OF THREE HOURS RESPONSE TIME. Had to call one of FOUR CONTACTS to get the address and for her to tell me “I’m not in charge of anything, so I don’t know.” They didn’t even tell me about giving the former guest a late checkout (and thereby PUSHED CHECK IN TIME BY FOUR HOURS). They made me pay for a locker at a restaurant to store my luggage. Had I known, I would’ve booked a later flight!  this is on a WALKUP. the tiles of the VERY STEEP STAIRS are literally falling off. i almost fell down a couple times while hauling my 50lb bag up there.   LIMITED PRIVACY. this isn’t their fault — it’s new york. the walls are thin and you can hear literally everything.

The pictures look more elegant. The room and the premises are really so-so and in a very old creepy building. There is no attached bathroom. That being said, share the bathroom and toilet with 4/5 other rooms. The window also had an opening and all the cold air would come in. Overall it’s an okay place to stay.

This is a really nice place to stay in Hell’s Kitchen, I really loved the experience Because I was able to do everything by walking, and as I like to explore the city, it was the perfect place for me !  The only thing is that the room stays in the 4th floor, so if you have a big luggage and are traveling alone it could be a little stressful. If I come back to nyc I would definitely stay there again!

The apartment was comfortable and clean. It was very close to the train which made it easy to get around as we did not have a car. If you're not familiar with the neighborhood you may find it a little scary, but the people were nice and there were small stores and restaurants close by that made everything accessible for us.

The place itself was very neat, clean and comfortable which was greatly appreciated.  My only negative was the air conditioning.  Only two of the bedrooms are air conditioned and two are not.  If floor fans were provided in in the other two bedrooms I think that would be sufficient.  The neighborhood is sketchy - so be prepared for that.  You will hear loud things going on outside at night so be prepared for that.  The check-in and out process was easy.  Andrew was available to communicate with and answer questions.  We had a power issue during our stay (not the host's fault) and he did all that he could to help us through it.  Very close to the subway and our vehicle survived the free on-street parking on both Lincoln and Lefferts St.  All in all, I would stay here again.

Place is clean, has everything you need for a short stay. Area is kind sketchy, specially across the street with a questionable residential building and people standing outside talking loudly until 4am . Jelena lives upstairs with her family that can be very noisy when home. If you like to sleep until 10am it will be a challenge.
Listing not well advertised, felt unsafe with a shared door in the apartment

Amazing place with lovely decoration! I stayed for 9 days with my friend and felt like at home! Great amenities.   Takeshi is very kind and caring, very easy to communicate with! He would also check in once in a while to see how we were doing via Airbnb app.   Although the location is great as it is walking distance to Soho and East Village, sometimes heard loud disruptive noises at night while sleeping. The neighborhood seemed a bit sketchy at night.

Apartment was absolutely beautiful, and extra touches to everything made it a wonderful stay (especially during rona times when everything is closed). More than worth the price point imo. Would air bnb here again. But street this air bnb was on was a little shady. Vape shop just outside had some unsavory characters loitering right outside of apartment entrance which is a door covered in graffiti. Random guy literally screaming on the street outside at 5 AM woke us up every day of our stay (but that’s the city for you). Otherwise absolutely beautiful apartment. Just one street over and it feels way safer and it is really close to everything! Overall worth it.

On the positive side: The bedroom is ok & clean, the foam mattress and pillows where comfortable, the shared kitchen space is available for the basics, and the location is convenient for Time's Square & Broadway shows.  On the negative: The bathroom ceiling has lots of mildew, the 4 flights of stairs to the apartment are scary, it's not romantic, and it was a little loud from outside noise.  Bottom line: If you just want a basic room on a budget this is ok, but it will not impress your date!
very good! not handicap accessible just fyi very dangerous stairs to get in. a very good value stay that was clean and quick to get in and out in the city

NOTE THIS IS A SHARED LISTING AND YOU MAY HAVE ROOMMATES.  I am upset. The hosts did not clarify with my partner and I before we moved in. They failed to inform us that there was anyone in apartment with us leaving us feeling very unsafe! They did not make the shared living situation clear in the face of a global pandemic--unacceptable!  We should have been notified that there was a second room in the space, that it would be booked, and by how many people--and if we had known this, we would NOT have stayed here as I informed the hosts upon booking that we were trying to avoid exposure from others, yet, despite this, they failed to communicate the nature of the listing. Very disappointing. This ended up costing us over $245 for just one night because of cancellation fees rather than stay change fees that should've been accommodated considering the unclear communication. There were also bugs biting us all night. We are leaving this listing feeling scammed and deceived.

The room was good for a quick visit and if you don't plan on spending much time in the room. Only "negative"  things I would say about my stay is that the bathroom and shower are across the hall and in separate rooms. Also, the buildings front door is the kind you have to really shut, I'm mentioning this because I woke out the hall to start my second day of the trip and there was a homeless person sleeping in the middle of the walkway. The sign on the front door reads something like "Shut door all the way, has been left open many times." So be aware of that. Lastly, the room is VERY loud due to the ac unit or whatever it is sticking outside of the window so a lot of the honking and yelling is CLEARLY heard. You won't get much sleep but the price was good and I wasn't spending much time in their anyways besides sleeping and taking breaks from the busy streets. Regarding the rooftop access, I did not even attempt to go up there because the weather was so bad so I don't have anything to say about that.

Wouldn’t recommend, like to anyone. Doors didn’t lock and we felt pretty unsafe, bathroom had a disgusting vomit like substance on the floor, bathroom was detached and down a hallway. Only good part was the proximity to Patsys Italian Restaurant.

Overall, not a bad place to stay. Great location, and based on cost, not a bad value. However, the journey up the stairs is not for the faint of heart, and isn't the safest, but can understand the stairs needing work isn't their fault. If I had another issue it would be that the lock to the bedroom door is broken and can feel a bit unsafe. Other than those things, wouldn't mind staying there again because it's a good bang for your buck.

It’s a scary abandoned building. You feel like the building is going to collapse any moment. The bedroom lock wasn’t working properly. I was scared all night. The shared bathroom was all the across the building. The bedroom was cold because of the window crack.

THE ROOM DOOR DOESN’T lock. You can just push the door open. Very small room with a bed. Not clean. Stuff sticks to your feet after getting out of the shower. Gum on the wall. Pillow cases and sheets don’t fit. Random stuff in boxes through the place. Overall not clean.  Menacing and very creepy writing on the wall in the bedroom.  Bathroom is across the hall in another unit.   Not self check in, needed to coordinate with a 3rd person.  There’s a giant Tv mounted that isn’t plugged in,  doesn’t work and extension cords running all over the ground.  However, it’s in a great location!

Dirty accommodation (dusty room with lots of hair, stains on the walls, dirty bathroom and toilet depending on the guests present, little cleaning), Stairs to go up to the 4th floor very dangerous because the steps are moving, Extremely noisy because there is a big light at the window blocked with a few pieces of plastic, Very soft mattress therefore significant back pain, Broken bedroom door with an opening above 5cm and I think a little bump in the shoulder would be enough to open it I even had cold water and difficulty getting water in the accommodation the first days The only positive point is the location 5 minutes walk from Times Square I strongly advise against this accommodation and this host who has several accommodations given the state of this room
the area isnt the best. a little sketchy walking around theres a lot of trash outside and such but the airbnb itself was nice, smelled good was clean and comfortable. the host was really nice

If you’re staying by yourself or you have one person go ahead and book this place it’s very clean very private and you’ll have a good time 🥰 The host answered right away if you ever have any questions don’t be afraid to contact her at all very very dope place to stay and I’ll be back

The location of this place can't be beat for the cost, and our room was great - a nice comfortable bed, and a huge closet!  We didn't get to meet Belkis during our stay but she left very detailed instructions and her friend welcomed us and was a fantastic resource.  While the apartment building itself is a little odd (perhaps not originally built for residential use?) the street is mostly lined with lovely brownstones. We were late checking in and Belkis worked with us, which we really appreciated, especially since she wasn't even in town and these were last-minute changes. Overall, this was a perfect fit for our needs, and I cannot stress enough how fanastic the location is for accessing the subway, good food and drink, and excellent coffee.

The room is really clean and nice. I enjoyed a lot my stay there.  It’s just 4 minutes away from the train station that takes you to the touristic places.  if you are by yourself at night the walk from the train station to the AIRBNB can be a little scary, but since it is a short walk it’s totally fine.  I recommend this place. Great value!

I am shocked and still confused at how negative my experience with Joyce turned out. The credit card I used to originally book the place had changed account numbers so when AirBNB tried to charge me for the second payment I got a bounce back notification at 9PM on a Friday night. I was driving and thought OK I'll fix that in the morning. At 2AM I get a call from an AirBNB mediator saying Joyce was canceling her contract with me and that I needed to be out within 24 hours. The mediator reported she said it was because of issues that she supposedly addressed with me that were never resolved (which never happened) and that I had an issue with paying. When I called her in the morning (as requested by the mediator) she told me that she actually wanted the place for her friend and after begging said she was willing to let me stay "a few days longer." When all this is going on I am away that weekend to visit my grandfather who is in hospice on his death bed. I then had to scramble and spend all of Saturday to find a place last second near NYC in the summer just so I wouldn't become homeless. Although I spent some time with my grandfather, when I left Sunday night to go pack and move places he died within an hour of me leaving. Instead of being with my family, I had to take care of a problem created by Joyce. On top of it all, I had to move into a hostel in a space shared between 10 men in New Jersey rather than a private room because that was the only thing available last minute within the same price range without doubling or tripling my cost. Aside from this, the kitchen was never usable to cook in, she and her son would regularly yell at each other at 2AM on work nights, and her son Donovan was always screaming homophobic slurs while playing video games. I would have never written about these other issues if my experience did not turn out so bad, but I now feel obligated to. I can never forgive Joyce for the position she put me in and I would recommend for anyone to not trust staying with her.

My best friend and I loved our experience with Belkis! It was our first time in NYC and she just made the experience that much more amazing with her suggestions/recommendations. The place was a steal considering we stayed during the NYE weekend and I would definitely recommend  her to anyone looking for a friendly and helpful host!

Amal has a beautiful home in South Harlem, pretty close to transit and grocery stores and the high ceilings made the space feel really big. She was also able to accommodate some special requests for us with check-in and check-out which was much appreciated.   Unfortunately, we had some issues with cleanliness. The sheets were spotted with a lot of stains. The kitchen had some nice new appliances, but the utensils and cups were all dirty/dusty and had to be washed before use (but even the dishwasher sponge was pretty dirty).   The sofa bed was pretty tough to sleep on. We ended up pulling the topper from the old sofabed in the bedroom to lay on top of the new one to make it a bit better.   The heating was a little finicky or perhaps we just didn't know how to use the thermostat properly. Not sure what was happening but the first few nights, the bedroom was sweltering and the rest of the unit was cold, and then the last few nights it somehow fixed itself.   WiFi was VERY spotty. I suspect a restart in the router would help.   Otherwise, it was pretty good - having laundry in the unit was very helpful, we definitely took advantage of that. It was also a surprisingly quiet; noise wasn't an issue, and neither was safety.

Brandon's place was clean, well decorated, and full of useful amenities. This place would be good for a single traveler or a couple, either in town for business or for fun.  The immediate neighborhood is walkable, full of restaurants and bars, and even a grocery store. The stairs to the apartment would be a challenge for someone with mobility issues, but otherwise this spot is a steal!

Amal was very accommodating when we had to reduce our booked stay a few weeks before our arrival even though we passed the deadline. She was gracious throughout.    The place was nice , and roomy for Manhattan.  There is  ten minute access to two subway lines.  One to Lower Manhattan’s west side and one to lower Manhattan’s east side.  The walk from the  east side subway line  stop, Lex and 116th gets  a bit sketchy after 11 pm so I would recommend taking the west side line after 11 pm, Malcom X and 116th if that bothers you.    I would rent the place again.  There is a very nice coffee shop a few blocks from the house on Malcom X blvd  Restaurants and supermarkets and big pharmacy chains are close and best of all the top of Central Park is a ten minute walk
Kevin's apartment is exactly how it appears in the photos. The location is amazing and he was very helpful with checking in and out which made our stay stress-free. Thanks again!
Kevin is a great host! I was running around to meetings and definitely needed a stress free stay which it was! I would definitely book with Kevin again.

The neighborhood was maybe a little shady, but the gated community was so safe and secure feeling that you'd never notice. The apartment is beautiful, and great for the price, and perfectly located to take the subway into the city. My boyfriend and I loved staying here!

We had an outstanding time staying in The Carson family home! We couldn’t have asked for a better place to stay and celebrate the holidays with our immediate and extended families in NY.  From the spacious rooms and family friendly setup to the easy to use sound systems and appliances, this home was a dream come true! We also loved learning about the rich history of the house and the neighborhood through the lovely coffee table book.  Thank you Jonathan and Cynthia for offering us a comfortable, stress free and enjoyable home away from home. Our trip was unforgettable. We’d jump at the opportunity to stay again!

This was my first Airbnb experience, and I have to say-- it could not have been with a nicer, more accommodating host! We were flying in from Alaska, getting in earlier than official check-in time, and Sabia most graciously offered that we should check in when we could get there. You don't know how much stress this alleviated, especially after having traveled for several days already! And so we did, and the gated community home was exactly as described. We got lost a little bit when looking for the place, but everyone around was so dang nice helping us find the place, it was really a non-issue. Get your butt to Harlem! Experience some of the history; the people; the food! It was an easy walk to the train station that further opened our horizons completely. We went everywhere and ate all of the things! Would highly recommend!

We stayed at Stephen's townhouse during the Covid-19 pandemic, and I could not have hoped for a more generous and thoughtful host. This has been a very stressful time, but we found such a wonderful respite in Greenwich Village. I grew up not far from here, and staying in the townhouse brought back so many great memories. This townhouse has been lovingly updated throughout, and has every modern convenience including a washer and dryer! You cannot beat hospitality like this, and I would stay here again in a heartbeat. Thank you so much Stephen!

For our first Airbnb experience... This was amazing! Our experience started as we entered New York with John calling us and giving directions not only to the apartment but to the apartment parking space. He stayed on the phone until we were in the building.  The apartment was exactly as described if not better. John was so easy to deal with and so willing to help in every way he could. If we had any questions about anything, for example; how to get somewhere, where something was located in the apartment, even what the best pizza delivery was. In every instance he answered our texts within minutes. You could tell it mattered that we felt at home to him.   The beds were very comfortable and the rooms were roomy. It was very clean and beautiful.  He even had little toiletries on the bathroom sink.    We were literally one block to the bus station which took us six blocks to the subway. There is grocery stores, drug stores, liquor store and restaurants all within walking distance.   The apartment building was a security building and everyone we came across was very friendly and warm. We could do our own laundry in the laundry room in the basement.  We even had our own parking space behind the building in a secure area. The neighborhood was really nice too.  If we had questions about how to get somewhere we could ask anyone and  the neighbors were more than happy to help.   We would definitely recommend this apartment to any family and anyone looking to experience ny in a nice neighborhood as a New Yorket. John even text us after we were home several times to make sure that we got home safe and that we were happy with our experience. We are so grateful we choose this location!

We really enjoyed our stay at Jeffery and Anna Rita's place. The apartment was very nice and clean, and our hosts always made sure we had everything we needed.   There is a bit of a commute getting into Manhattan but the ferry ride is really nice (and free) and you get a good view of the Statue of Liberty. We sometimes felt a little bit unsafe walking home at nighttime, but other than that we had a great stay!

Thank you for accomodating our request for the earlier check-in. We really enjoyed staying at the place for a week. Initially we were afraid that the travel to the places of interest would be long and boring but the ferry rides and bus rides were a great way to see NYC better. Would be back when we come back to NYC next.

The transport connections through the SIR were very good for getting to Manhattan and we never felt unsafe or uncomfortable for a second.  The apartment was as described and clean! But above all, the top cuisine is worth mentioning!  Jeffrey replied quickly!  We would definitely come back, especially because of the great price-performance ratio:)

The airbnb is ideally located for a stay in NYC, with quick access to the metro as there are several lines nearby. Harlem is certainly not completely relaxed, but we didn't have any problems. The apartment is nicely furnished and equipped. Clothes have to stay in the suitcase because all the cupboards are full of the landlord's things. For us the only downside was the small, crowded and stuffy bedroom. You can't ventilate and the air conditioning is very loud. A bit uncomfortable at 30 degrees!  Jorge and his partner are very friendly and attentive!

The apartment is very well located in relation to the metro, in a quiet building and with shops nearby. There is a church right next door to go to to hear a magnificent gospel mass, we quickly integrated into this neighborhood. We happened to return late and we never felt in danger. The apartment is comfortable and Jorge leaves everything at our disposal. Thank you so much.

Apartment ideally located because close to all metro amenities, supermarket, gospel etc. Owner rather available because he was kind enough to wait for us very late at night for a key handover (Following a delayed flight)

This place was ok. Flatbush is apprx 45 - 60 mins away from the city. The surrounding may be a little dangerous at night. There are numerous methods of transit to Manhattan. Its one bed in a living room with a couch. The hosts were very nice and helpful.

Ray's place was charming and in a great location. Harlem sounds scary but actually it was pretty nice and welcoming. As long as you are not walking around with a map and expensive electronics at 4am then I would say you are pretty safe. Like any big city, don't be stupid, be aware of your surroundings. The apartment was comfortable and pretty quiet. Once the AC is on you hear nothing and I am a light sleeper. I slept fine. We had a little leak from some AC but Ray sorted it out quickly. The apartment has everything you need. Even umbrellas! The living room has no overhead lights, the lights are on the walls and there are a couple lamps so it can be a little dark. It was fine for me but a little dark for my mother. I wish we could have used the backyard, but it rained every day except for the day we left! If you have good weather, I implore you to sit outside and relax in the great space outdoors.   Had a great time in NY!

Good location: interesting neighborhood with many shops and places to eat; There are several metro lines nearby, a seven-minute walk away; safely. Pros: the patio, the hot water in the shower and the artificial light (it is a basement but has many lamps). We were able to leave our suitcases until we took the taxi to the airport. Cons: excessively noisy bed, slightly uncomfortable sofa, the Wi-Fi connection is not good and the TV cuts out a lot.  We had a pleasant stay, but some details could be improved.

The place is located at the prime location area in Manhattan Beach, NY. Very convenient to travellers with electronic front main door entrance, next door market, and a bus stop just in front of the building makes this place an ideal location for everyone. To be fair though, there are 2 key issues that bothered me the most, number 1 is in regards to the heating pipe in the bathroom (health risk) and the address location needs to be very clear which is an easy fix. If those key issues been addressed, the location alone is a steal. Happy hunting you guys.

The apartment has everything you need and is very clean, although we had to kill 3 cockroaches, that was very unpleasant. The shower could be improved, very little water comes out. AND ATTENTION! The door has no number or bell!!  I wasted a lot of time driving around in the car. The neighborhood is very nice, it is a few blocks from the beach.

Ray and his wife were perfect hosts. They were sympathetic about our early flight and heavy luggage and were very accommodating in allowing us to check in early and easily. They were quick to respond and very helpful with whatever we needed. The location was surprisingly clean and quiet. Our group did not feel unsafe at all walking home late at night, post 2 am. The kitchen, microwave, washer, dryer and all the appliances made being in NYC much more convenient. I would totally recommend and I plan on using this home again on my next trip!

Gary has a lovely place and he made sure we had everything we needed. The Audioengine speakers were a nice touch. He was very responsive and the location is convenient to the subway and its quiet at night. It's walkable to 7th ave where there are a lot more restaurant options. Only con I'd point out is during the summer time, there are some bugs and mosquitos near the private entrance door so just make sure you close the door quickly (not a huge deal if you are not afraid of mosquitos). Would recommend staying here if you are looking for a nice getaway but don't want to pay for double the price to stay in manhattan.

Gary provides a lot of little amenities that make your stay convenient. There is a keurig and pods for coffee, an electric pot for making hot water for tea and tea bags, a toaster oven and microwave and utinsels, sugar, sweeters,  cups and access to a frig. There was even fresh creamer in the frig down the hall. The room is plenty big. The bed was comfortable. There was a fan in the bathroom because it can get kind of steamy in there. It's the little things that make Garys place pleasant. One thing I did note, because you are lower level, below the ground level, it's kind of musty smelling but nothing too unpleasant. If odors bother you, you might want to consider bringing airfreshner. Bathroom showed signs of a previous tenant, and that perhaps it wasn't thoroughly cleaned before I arrived, but there were fresh towels and plenty of shampoo, conditioner and body wash. That was my only issue. I'm pretty neurotic for clean bathrooms.

If you want to stay in Red Hook, which in my opinion is the best part of Brooklyn, then Steve’s place is in the heart of it all!  Steve is so thoughtful and a great communicator-the check in process was completely stress-free. He helped me with my luggage, gave me a thorough tour and was just so welcoming!  His apartment is very clean and he clearly cares about the health and safety of his guests during these times. Thank you so much, Steve! A perfect stay in a perfect location!

Ok for starters... Johnathan was a great communicator!!! He answered right away every time!!   So let me start by saying this is not a bad review because honestly I had a whole apartment for a whole month for $1300 ... that’s a steal!!! It was bug/rodent free!  Laundry in the building and it was quiet for the most part except the upstairs neighbors .. they must have kids or something..  Cons...This place doesn’t have a TV however because I’m moving I had my smart TV and used that... the internet worked fine! The apartment is old so chipping paint and old carpet. The bed was horrible .. I’m sure for younger people it’s fine .. but I’m 40 and the springs were in places that they shouldn’t have been .. I would play a game sometimes on how long I can lay in one spot to se if I can trick myself into falling asleep. The kitchen I did not use except to heat food in the microwave (I had to slam it shut cause otherwise it will pop back open) .. the blinds were severely broken that the surrounding building can see inside. I had to run the water in the bathroom because of the water giving rust in the beginning... I did spend only like 50% of my time there because I really looked for a bed to get some real sleep some nights ... oh and if you are a driver forget about finding parking after 4-5pm you will circle the block for 30+ min.  I feel bad cause Johnathan was thoughtful and told me it was old...  he also allowed  me to completely check out a day later because of a family emergency and also let me come back to get clothes I left in the closet by accident...  This place was close to work and my family .. so it worked for what I paid for..

I stayed two nights in Kim's apartment with my girlfriend. Kim is a great host! Room was clean and with everything we needed, a little hot but I guess it's common due to the period. Area can seem a little scary at first but actually it is quite nice and comfortable to subway and buses, served with many restaurants and supermarket/pharmacy. The city itself is great! Really enjoyed our time in NYC. Recommend Kim's place!

We had a comfortable stay at Kim's.  She was friendly and all our basic needs were met. I appreciated the hotel-like coffee and tea station she had set up in our room, as well as the fresh towels she provided for us.  The only downside was that the front hallway had a strong smell of old cigarette smoke, which was unpleasant.  It didn't bleed into the bedroom that much, but someone with a sensitivity to such smells should be cautious before staying here.

First time in New York, I landed in this apartment thinking that it would suit me for 1 month but I was wrong.  UNLIVABLE, DIRTY, NO SECURITY!!! I really don’t recommend it!!  Water leak problem, which is getting worse day by day, Blocked bathroom, hissing heating, front door secured with a tissue, dressing room filled with broken furniture, Apparently dangerous for anyone.  I will even ask Airbnb to remove this apartment

Franklin and Chiemi made me feel instantly at home. They are very friendly and responsive. The apartment is quiet, spacious and super convenient to public transportation. A little "neighborhood guide" with restaurant recommendations and directions to the grocery store/pharmacy was on the night stand when I came in.  Natsu and Mochi are well-behaved fur babies. But Baby Oliver steals the show!!

Excellent Host and on providing  information. If you are tight on budget and need to make sure you leave your budget to get to see the city, then this is a good option. It is an space just to go to sleep, Subway is around 10 minutes walking. Walking at night around the neighborhood was a little sketchy, wouldn't recommend for someone alone.  There is a close by supermarket which is great for healthy food and snacks.  Keep in mind New York space is tighter and most buildings are a little old.

We had a great stay in Harlem. Kim was a very good host and the room was nice! We walked a lot, and also used the metro a lot. Perfect because you can use two stations. We really liked Harlem and never felt unsafe or something like that. The building is really Nice and the people helpfull. The room itself was clean and so was the bathroom. Thanks again!
We had an amazing time! Kim helped to make our first time in NY easy and stress-free. She is very kind and helpful. Definitely worth your stay!!

The positive: the A train line takes you to Manhattan in 25 minutes and is approximately 3 or 4 blocks away, on that side mobility is very good, the apartment is nice and has all the necessary things for the stay, your roommate was very attentive to our arrival and collaborated with us in everything we asked, the neighborhood is old and a lot of Latin people live, it is quiet, we arrived late several nights and we never felt afraid. The negative: the entrance to the apartment is not through the main entrance shown in the photo but through a small side door that takes you to an unwelcoming passage, the building is quite old and not very pretty, the apartment has no ventilation and had a quite bad smell (I understand that all apartments in NY have that smell, I'm not sure), however they placed a fan in the living room and in the bedroom that fixed that a bit, as for the beds there were two large ones but one of them had a rod that went through the bed and no It allowed me to sleep well because the mattress sank, but since I am skinny I settled in that piece and I had no problem but it is not comfortable at all, the bathroom was dirty, the trash can was full and had the smell of urine, the toilet was so dirty that I didn't want to use it and along with the smell of the apartment it was quite annoying. In conclusion, it is a good option in terms of price and even more so that one is not there all the time, the location is very far from Manhattan but with the subway one arrives in good time and the owner collaborated with all the doubts that I always had.

Jeff and Alex were wonderful hosts, and did their best to make my daughter and I feel at home. Jeff was super responsive with questions I had about transportation (the train line we initally intended to take from Penn Station had significant delay issues on the Friday afternoon we arrived, but we were able to get on an alternate line with Jeff’s help), and was happy to offer us suggestions for places to eat nearby after our long travel day. Their cats April and Franklin were delights (especially the kitten, Franklin, who loved to play with us) and my daughter really appreciated their company.  The guest’s bedroom is large and the two beds are both comfortable. There’s a round table and chairs in the bedroom to eat at or play games, and temperature can be controlled both by a fan and an air conditioner unit (which wasn’t an issue for us as the weather was mild during our visit). The kitchen and common living area is small (the galley kitchen really couldn’t fit more than one person at a time), but we appreciated having our own bar fridge to store food in. The bathroom has been remodeled at some point and the shower is quite large and has two rainfall showerheads, which was a very nice start to the day. Appreciated all of the extra towels and the heated towel bars.  Jeff’s appartment is on the ground level, but at no time did we feel unsafe, as there are at least two secured doors between the street and every entrance to the suite. My daughter and I had come to New York to see Paul Simon’s farewell concert in Queens (incredible!), and when we also wanted to check out a Broadway musical, Alex was happy to provide recommendations on the best shows to see in town. We appreciated our North Manhattan location’s proximity to Central Park and all of the museums and cultural institutions nearby. The neighbourhood is strongly Latino (I heard more Spanish spoken than English), and it was fun to walk the streets surrounding our place with its strong sense of community (we encountered birthday and anniversary parties spread out on the sidewalks and in the parks we went through).  We had an incredible time during our short stay in New York, and will definitely come back!

Perfect for 1-2 guests.  Little tight for 4, but you can't beat the location.  Very quiet, ground level for easy access.  Room is on opposite side of condo for privacy.  Neighborhood has everything you could want or need.  Close to amazing Dominican food and coffee, grocery, drug store etc.  Subway stations for 1 and A really are both 5 min walk.  Great communication from Jeff.  Franklin the cat was a bonus, super playful and lovey.

Pete’s place was absolutely perfect! We had only been to NYC once in 2015, and have never stayed in a rented bedroom before so I was a little nervous. I mean, a rented room in NYC, sounds crazy! Well let me tell you, it wasn’t!  It turned out I was worried for nothing, and it was the best decision I could have made.   He was quick to accept the booking, and reached out to hear a little more about our plans so he could get recommendations together. Our arrival ended up being a little earlier than excepted, but Pete said no problem and worked it out to meet us on arrival.   Upon arrival, the place is spotlessly clean, and the room is spacious (by NYC standards). We had plenty of room for our luggage and a mirror for me to use while getting ready. The bed is super comfortable. The room has its own AC unit which was AMAZING. We could keep our room as warm or cool as we wished! AC is a luxury in NYC, and pete’s place has it. We loved the little touches of the lights in the jar for a night light, and the books available to read.  He provided amenities  such as an espresso machine (try the green!), towels, iron and ironing table, and he set out water bottles for our use. Also, he provides umbrellas if needed (lifesaver!)   The shared bathroom was never a problem for us. We always needed it at different times so we never ran into trouble. The bathroom itself is spotless, and the hot water gets super hot! (Definitely a plus).   Throughout our stay Pete gave us many recommendations for restaurants, things to do, things not to do, and just general tips.  He always responded quickly, and was open to anything else we might need.   Aside from the gracious host, and spotless comfortable place, it’s also beautifully located just a couple blocks from Union Square! From Union square you can catch a subway train to anywhere in the city. In those blocks are countless restaurants, dessert holes, pubs, wine bars, stores, etc. The whole area around Pete’s place feels super safe. I walked around alone several times (I’m a small woman) and I never felt unsafe.  Overall, I would absolutely stay with Pete again. This was the best Airbnb experience we’ve ever had. If you are looking for a clean, safe, and comfortable place that’s close to everything East Village has to offer... this is it!

Awesome place! Pete was super flexible with our checkin which was a huge stress reliever! The place was in a GREAT (safe) location and was clean, comfortable and cozy...all the things you want in a vacation! When I come back to New York I will be booking this room!!

A quirky, ramshackle old house, very close to the subway.  Comfy bed in a small room, though the window overlooks a major road and could use a curtain that keeps the sunlight out.  It's a very creaky building, which really needs its upgrade completing, as certain areas seemed a little unsafe. I didn't mind, but, if you are a worrier, this may not be the property for you.  I didn't meet Daniel, though he was clear and friendly in his communication.

The space offered by JaTarra is very clean, comfortable, spacious, well organized and above all safe. It's a residential neighborhood and a great way to see how New Yorkers live as it's not a touristy place. There is public transport nearby but to the subway stations we have to walk a few blocks. Nothing impossible. JaTarra was super helpful in helping me arrive and leave when she made her schedule flexible. I felt really good knowing that she doesn't like drugs in the place and cares about recycling disposables and saving energy and water. I loved it and recommend it 100%!

Location was good, did not feel unsafe walking to and from the bus. Easy access to transportation. Space was clean and pleasant. JaTarra was prompt in communication. Overall an easy and pleasant stay.

Sebastian is very welcoming, before our arrival he answered our questions quickly, he sent us our route from the airport. Besides, Sebastian came to pick us up from the metro station at 2 a.m. (our flight was late). Perfect for a short stay in Manhattan and 2 steps from the 116th street subway station!

Bright, modern and super comfortable, this is a great spot to explore Manhattan. I stayed here for 3 months and found the location convenient for getting around--the subway is mere blocks away and grocery stores, banks, gyms, and drug stores are extremely close. There's a very good restaurant, Peque, just 2 blocks away, that features live music.  It became my favorite neighborhood place for dinner and drinks.

A place for the traveler that needs a place to crash after a full day in the city. Street parking makes it difficult if you drive every day, but if you're riding public transportation this is close to access. A very diverse Brooklyn neighborhood (which on isn't?). I never felt unsafe, but it may not be for the feint of heart. Bodegas on every corner! The bed was quite comfortable and a floor fan provided the perfect white noise to drown out city noise.  A good value considering you're in NYC.

We decided to spend New Year's in NY and started using Airbnb for the first time, Katherine's apartment is more comfortable and spacious than what can be seen in the photos. Their cats are calm and friendly, the white one a little shy and the gray one very intelligent. The room has everything you need. When we arrived the host was not at home but she left all the instructions to follow and a person to greet us and give us the keys. We were delighted with the neighborhood, there are many bars, cafes and restaurants in the area, East Village is very safe, at least we walked until late at night and felt safe. The subway stations are very close to wherever you want to go, it's just a matter of walking a couple of blocks. On our penultimate day we met Katherine, a very hospitable and pleasant person. Without a doubt a great experience and we highly recommend the place. From the room you can see the Empire. We will definitely return to NY My friend and I decided to spend new year in New York and we picked Airbnb for the first time, Katherine’s apartment is so comfortable and bigger than it looks in the pictures, her cats are nice and friendly, the white one is shy and the gray one is smart and always goes around. The room has everything that you'll need, when we arrived the host wasn't there but she left all the indications and the keys with a friend there welcomed us. We loved the neighborhood there are so many bars and restaurants around, east village is so safe, we walked until late and never felt danger, the metro stations are close. In the last days we met Katherine and she is so nice and polite. It was a great experience, we recommend this place, pretty sure we will return to NY.

Sebastian was a great host and was very easy to get a hold of from the day we booked the stay until we left. The neighborhood looks kind of sketchy but well worth the price you pay. It is very close to public transit and Lyft rides into the city are not too expensive. All linens were clean and ready for use and Sebastian explained everything when we got there and let us know about the area upon arrival. He also had toiletries for us to use although we had our own but was appreciated. Overall great stay!

Sebastian was a great host ! I went there with my friend (we were two girls) and there was nothing to worry about ! He helped us and showed us how the subway worked when we arrived, there is a subway station 2 streets away from Sebastian's so it was pretty easy ! The entry of the building was a little dirty but Sebastian's apartment was very very clean and tidy ! And it smelled good. He always made sure we had everything to make us feel comfortable. We were a bit scared about the area at first but people were actually very friendly and we didn't have any problem with anyone ! And when there's sun, there's music in the street and it's a great atmosphere. We highly recommend Sebastian's apartment ! Thank you again Sebastian for being an amazing host, we will definitely come back to you if we go to again to New York.
Accommodation close to the metro, not even 2 min. Very well decorated, not very noisy. The neighborhood is not dangerous.
very good host, comfortable house, everything to feel comfortable, good restaurants in the Latin Quarter, it looks more dangerous than it really is, access to the metro is close and fast.

Be prepared to walk far to get to anything cool or nice if you stay here. The subway to take you to Manhattan is a 10 min walk which isn’t bad. The area is not very nice though- you don’t want to hang out there or eat at any of the restaurants. The grocery store nearby has some essentials but is super over priced. We didn’t feel unsafe but everything was a little sketchy looking.

I cannot say enough good things. This stay was perfect. Sebastian is a wonderful host. The room was clean and quiet and just what I needed for my solo trip. He provided me with a lot of information prior to me getting there. He met me at the door to get me settled in. The apartment was clean and quiet. The neighborhood is also wonderful. I never felt unsafe once as a woman traveling alone and right by the 6 train station. I will be staying here anytime I’m back in the city.

Virginias place is great! 5 min walk to the subway and a corner store right across the street with a late night taco stand! She did her best to make me feel right at home. The location is safe. I walked from the subway to the apartment at 4AM and did not feel scared or creeped out and was a lone female. I will definitely be back! Thank you!

As the pictures, bright and welcoming place. Shai was also a wonderful host, considering our plane was late and he was very flexible for the check-in. Very clean appartment, nice neighbourhood (good restaurants around :) ).  Comme sur les photos, un appartement lumineux et accueillant ! Shai fut en outre un excellent hôte, sachant que notre vol fut retardé et qu'il fut flexible sur l'heure d'arrivée. Un endroit très propre et un voisinage sympathique (de bons restaurants aux alentours :) ).  Igual que en las fotografías, un apartamento luminoso y acogedor. Shai fue un excelente anfitrión, sabiendo que nuestro avión llegaba con retraso, fue muy flexible sobre la hora de llegada. Un apartamento muy limpio, barrio agradable (buenos restaurantes cercanos :) ).

Im always considering the reviews where i will gonna stay in my trip. And this place catched my eyes. The number one i love about it is because the profit that they are getting here are for all the homeless in manhattan.  Alex is very nice. He is very responsive and very helpful. Even through my inquiries he's helping me a lot even im not yet sure if i will gonna take the room or not. And upon my arrival, he asked me where i wanna stay and where i will be more comfortable. He's the best ever! The room is very small. it is really only for one but i really love it. You have your own privacy. It is a shared bathroom but always clean. There's a complimentary breakfast meal but available 24 hours. If i dont wanna eat outside i can survived for that meals and save a lot of money! I supposed to help them also in distributing foods but indidnt get chance because i have a short time only. And he said it is totally fine. My stay in their pods is already a big help for them. It melts my heart! I swear to God we tried our best to be part of that goodwill but we didnt make it. They are very flexible about the check out also and if they need the room, you can leave your luggage in their office so you can still go around NYc and you can still use their bathroom if you wanna take a shower. My most favorite thing about this also is the location. 10 mins walk only from the empire state building. Very near also in times square. The train and bus station is just around the corner. Its the best location to enjoy New York City! I told to myself and my friend that i will gonna come back in this place again. I prefer to stay here than in any other place!  PS! It is noisy at night and in the morning but for me i dont care.

1. Location is great. Consider UES rather than Midtown. It's not sketchy and I feel safe walking at midnight. Restaurants are within 1-7 block. And I can go to Central Park during lunch break. Easy subway access. It's almost the same as living at Midtown in terms of travel time.  2. Apartment condition is great. I especially like the balcony. In April I was lucky enough to see the Sakura blossom right in front of the window. It's so beautiful and make you happy. Wifi is good enough for video calls..The sheets and blanket really need to be upgraded. They don't feel nice. Minor things: The TV resolution could be a little bit better. The sofa is a bit narrow. AC didn't work and there's no way to adjust the heat. I felt so so hot during the first 2 nights. But later I think the building management team finally lowered the heat. You need a lot of coins to do laundry. And the dryer doesn't work perfectly. I need 2 cycles to get it done.   3. Communication could be better. They require you to move to emails. But they are not super responsive there either. But they are legitimate for sure. So be patient and you can call if you have urgent questions.
Excellent service, clean room and facilities. Fantastic overall and a steal given the price.

The Chelsea Interfaith Retreat provides everything a single traveler needs including a bed, secure storage for your belongings, bathroom, kitchen, and shared living space with other guests. The sleeping spaces are small but with a shelf above the bed and storage space beneath, I didn't feel too camped with my luggage. I would not recommend this for light sleepers, as the rooms dont have a formal ceiling, more of a lattice structure at the top, and as a result, you can hear others sleeping or coming in late. There are designated quiet hours to lessen any disturbances, but I occasionally woke up and I'm a hard sleeper. Everyone I interacted with was pleasant and kind, and it was a very rewarding experience to feed the homeless with them on a cold Wednesday morning. I would stay here again if travelling alone, and think I had excellent expectations set by the quality of other reviews when selecting this place.

The place was bigger than I expected based on the reviews. The bed is a little small, but perfect for my height. The free breakfast was nice, but I didn't take advantage of it enough because I preferred eating out. Great location. Close to many subway stations and area didn't feel unsafe. I was out of my room the entire day so the cramped spaces didn't affect me. Great place to stay for cheap in Chelsea.

Our stay at Tracy’s place was amazing.  Her appartment is located only two streets away form Central Park which is the best if you like to go running or even go for a nice walk.  Everything is near this place : food, supplies, subway stations that will get you downtown directly ; all of these ensure you have the best experience of NYC you could ever have. Her cat was a bit scared of us at first when we arrived, but really quite get along with us only after a few days.  Tracy has been very explicit with indications, explanations, and has been always available by phone whenever we had a question.  We highly recommend that you book a stay at Tracy’s place if you have the opportunity !

Talk about cozy. I have nothing but great things to say- you get your own tiny box with warm lighting, surrounded by paintings and books on spirituality. There is fresh fruit and other foods available at all times which saved me in the mornings on my way out. The hosts were very helpful, welcoming and sweet. I appreciated the community aspect in that there were multiple people running it throughout my stay. In a bustling city like NY it was peaceful and relaxing to come back and sleep in a quiet space. Any noise from others reminded me of living with my family growing up so it was nostalgic in a way. The showers weren't amazing (bring sandals) but this place offers all that you need and even had me reevaluating what I perceive to be necessary when I travel. This was my first stay at an AirBnB and I'm hooked. Why spend money on a hotel when you can stay at a place that works toward the betterment of mankind? Feeding homeless and uniting religions? I'm all for it. Next time I'm in the area I hope to volunteer with them!

You cannot have a more personable host combined with the convenience in location. 2 blocks from Penn Station and plenty of great food/business at the front door.   I'd shy away from crashing for taller folks as the bedroom/bed is fairly compact but it's nothing I will complain about myself. after all, I was there for the vegetarian environment/experience and I can easily get behind the mission of helping feed the homeless, which is their first priority with the funds accrued. Thanks again, Alex. We could use more like you and I appreciate your leadership.

For NYC, this was one of the few affordable options available during the holiday season but it was a bit tighter and more crowded than I expected (I needed a place to crash while teaching a workshop), even though it is clear this is hostel, not a hotel or private home.   I realized the room space would be small, but sound from neighbors was a bit challenging (these are tiny locked door pod-rooms with an open wood trellis "ceiling" and one shared 3 stall 2 shower bathroom for a large number of people)---although others were largely respectful and polite.  I was near the common area, which was very sweetly decorated, but lights on from the lamps and traffic of people coming by woke me up several times and the room got incredibly warm.  While I was happy fresh fruit was abundant for breakfast, the package of bagels I opened was moldy.  I do like that some of the money is donated for feeding the homeless, and the ashram vibe was fine.

This apartment is in a fantastic location. As a base it was great but I had been expecting a more obvious sofa bed with bedding which I could have used and in the end we just had to share the bed which was fine in our circumstances but had we been more people it would not have worked out! The check out arrangements weren’t ideal either and added a bit of unnecessary stress at the end of the holiday. But overall we had a good stay.

If you're looking for a peaceful place with lovely energy this place is great. However, do not expect a good night's sleep unless you are a very heavy sleeper. It really is a bed in a dorm with your own lock and visual privacy. The "rooms" (bed cubicles) have no ceiling so you can hear everything. There is access to fruit, toast, tea and coffee, which is lovely. I don't think it's worth what they charge. However, your money goes to support their good work feeding homeless people, so there's that. And it is in a great location.

I was incredibly excited to stay here for my vacation. It was pretty centrally located to the sites I wanted to see and just a short walk from Penn Station, which seemed a huge plus for my arrival. Unfortunately, I fell and broke my ankle shortly after arriving at Penn Station. I messaged the hosts that I was going to be arriving much later than expected and they replied promptly that someone was in the office 24-hours. The place is charming, well air conditioned (my stay was for mid-summer), and they observe quiet hours at night, which are all pluses. I will stress, however, the location is not handicap accessible. It is located on the second floor and there’s a large step up into the bathroom. I only was able to stay one night, but the hosts kindly helped me get my luggage to my room and then back into a cab the next morning. I truly wish I could’ve stayed as long as I planned. The cabins are small, yes, but there’s enough room still to change and sleep (even with crutches in the way). There’s a common area to relax in and fresh fruit and tea is always available. The bathroom was well cleaned. It is definitely a place I will recommend to anyone I know traveling to NYC and one day, hopefully, I can return to complete my full stay.

This was my 1st hostel stay,  I was very surprised at how clean and how peaceful this retreat was.  I am a big guy 6'3", 280 pounds an I fit perfectly in these pods.  I could lay comfortably in the bed and slept great through the night. Alex was a great host!  The bathrooms were clean and had everything that you would need and the water was hot. One suggestion please bring a sleep mask and ear plugs (there was a pair of ear plugs on my bed when I checked in!)  because the ceiling is lattice which you will hear any noises in the room.  There is a lock on the door so you and your possessions are secure. I felt safe but I am 6' 3, 280 pounds. The place was heated and the water in the showers was hot. So all in all a great experience. And it felt good know that the profits from your stay goes to help feed the homeless.

Andre was an amazing host! He was able to accommodate my earlier check-in with no issues at all. Space is just the right size for a relaxing and cozy stay. The only thing missing is a stove but don't let that scare you, there is a rice cooker available.   Things that made the stay so pleasant • AC cools entire apartment no problem with remote • Balcony is so relaxing with an outdoor fridge and patio set •  Alexa was a fun addition for my six-year-old to play music she enjoys. • Netflix and a number of movie and show platforms available • Andre also provided water bottles that covered my entire stay, it was a thoughtful touch • Communication was very easy and Andre went above and beyond in making sure we were good • Many kitchen appliances and utensils were provided  Thank you again Andre! It was a very delightful stay for what I needed. I definitely will be back in the future! :)

Nice people. A little scary if you’re a single woman. I recommend bringing a friend and an eye mask. They provide ear plugs, which help, due to the very close proximity of the individual, but private, bunks. Nice community space! Very chill! S

What a lovely humble space in the Chelsea that is close to so0o many things! You get a little private room which is better than a dorm hostel & is SUPER affordable for this prime location!! I also enjoyed the 24/7 snack bar they have. Be aware, it is VERY QUIET & everyone is very respectful of this especially after 8:30pm, so understand that. Also it is charitable organization that uses alot of what they make to serve free food to the homeless at a nearby park so0o  I would deff advise to choose to stay here to make your trip a bit more wholesome! I would love loveee to stay here again for a bit longer, hopefully soon when this pandemic starts weaning down. Enjoy your stay here!
The rules are too strict, and it felt a bit unsafe

This place is the closest thing to living in a homeless shelter. Because the place offers free oranges and apples, prepare for flies buzzing and biting you while you try to sleep. You will hear and smell random people’s farts.

Sheila was very helpful and ultra responsive. Windsor Terrace has an easygoing vibe, the train access was great, there's a good bagel spot you can walk to, and my kids and I never felt even slightly unsafe.  The bedrooms stayed nice and warm despite single-digit temps, and check-in and check-out were a breeze.

The apartment and location were good but I wouldn’t recommend this place because of the hosts. The toilet lever was broken and the water was running and the hosts took 12 days to make this simple and essential repair. Even worse, they knew we had an infant in the apartment but came to the apartment twice without a mask despite our requests. We felt unsafe and disrespected.

Let me just say......I very rarely write reviews but you need to know that this is a great apartment. I’ve just got back to the UK.  Location. 10/10. Less than 10 minute walk to subway. A choice of 2 stations and one is the E line that takes to to/from JFK.  Quiet block considering that it is a central location. We walked to Grand Central in about 20 minutes.  Cleanliness. I’ll mark it down by half a point due to lipstick marked glasses nd dirty coffee cups. No big deal, but others might find it rather unpleasant. Other than that it was IMMACULATE.  The bed is super comfy. Better than my bed at home that has a £2000 memory foam mattress on it ! Superb.  Check in. A slight issue when Maria thought we were 2 days early but all was good in the end. Didn’t meet Evan or Maria. Collected the keys from the doorman at their apartment block next door. He was a bit stern but no problem. He allowed us to store our cases in a small storeroom.  Good shower. Point of note. This is a studio apartment. The bed is in the lounge. You also have a sofa and a small table with chairs and a coffee table.  Small kitchenette but we only used the coffee maker and put some milk in fridge. You couldn’t really make a meal there as it’s quite small but who goes to New York to cook ??!!?? There are about 18 steps from the street to the apartment front door so if you’re elderly or have bid heavy suitcases you might struggle.  We had a great time in New York. This was a fantastic apartment that met all our needs.

We loved The Healing  Place! Valerie's home is beautiful and it was a welcomed refuge while we were moving our daughter to NYC.  The location is very quiet, which I didn't think was possible in the heart of Brooklyn.  Valerie was an excellent host. She gave us enough information to be helpful, but wasn't over involved. She said she has only been an Airbnb host for a few months, but she acted like a real pro.  She even had an air mattress for our daughter to use since her apartment wasn't ready yet.  This was our first experience using Airbnb and I'm afraid Valerie spoiled us!

Compact and bijou apartment, located on a quiet street within a safe neighbourhood. Great eateries located within walking distance and all the key landmarks easily accessible. The hosts were clear communicators making the overall booking stress-free. Highly recommended for couples or small families.

Three of us stayed at Evan and Maria for a week, aiming for sightseeing of NYC.  Apartment is in very safe and quiet location, comfortable and very clean.  Everything is according to the description and photos. 24/7 grocery store just behind the corner. Two metro stations are in distance of 8 minutes walk. Thanks to very good location, use of subway is not necessary,  bit longer walk and you reach Empire State, Chrysler, Times Square, 5th Ave, Grand Central etc. We have encountered a problem with bed linen at the beginning, but it was solved immediately. Owners were very helpful through all of our stay, responding instantly, solving our problems with great care. A lot of amenities are available in the apartment,  useful things in kitchen and bathroom. Be aware that there is no view from the windows, just wall,  shady, but it gives very quiet nights and comfortable sleep, perfect after whole day of visiting busy city. I recommend  Evan and Maria as hosts.

At the first impression, I was a little bit scared about the neighborhood but in reality it was ok! We walked around the block late in the night and nothing happened  to us ! The place is close to the train and the commodities are all at 2 minutes walking. Jamie's garden was so peaceful and we loved to take our breakfast in !  Thanks ! :)

Read the other reviews before booking. I would say this is more of a closet than a cubical with one twin bed, maybe 2 feet of space to the sides and a side table. While there is space under the bed, it’s a tight squeeze with luggage. This is an interfaith place so there’s a lot of touches of Jesus and Buddhism. There is no ceiling and it’s just a plethora of fake walls to make rooms. While decent area for a tourist, tons of homeless people in the area

Had to check out an hour after cause the room was tiny and I heard all the neighbors and felt completely unsafe. I’m 6’3 and hardly ever feel nervous about sketchy spots but this was another level. Don’t stay here!!!

The location is perfect for me because I want to go to Madison Square Garden. It’s also not far from Train Station, Port Authority and the Time Square. It looks a bit scary at night but honestly that’s the same for everything in NYC. Not a place for you to stay because it’s definitely not as comfortable or convenient as other places, just for resting at night and leave early in the morning to travel.

The cabin is modest, with just enough room for a single bed and a hallway. Suitcases can be left under the bed and clothes on the shelves. The cabins have no roof and you can hear the noises from the other cabins (snoring, cell phones, alarms...) And also the smell. In the room you can find sheets, towels and earplugs. The upper floor is male and the lower floor is mixed. Women can stay on the men's floor when there are no rooms downstairs, but they must use the downstairs bathroom, which is an uncomfortable circumstance, although the hosts will warn you about this. There is fruit available, and bread, infusions, yogurts, cereals, peanut butter, jam, milk, cocoa and something else available to guests at any time of the day in addition to a fountain that dispenses hot and cold water and a refrigerator. The staff is friendly and the accommodation is clean and although it has the aforementioned inconveniences, it is very well located. The host offers a $15 discount if you collaborate in the vegetarian breakfast service program for homeless people.

Kristina was an amazing host and made it so easy for us . being our first time using Airbnb it was stress free easy to find in a great location , the bed was so comfy , the place was always tidy and the wifi was really good too . I'd recommend Kristina to anyone !

I returned just like I said I would and it felt just like home! Valerie is the most amazing host. Her beautiful and peaceful energy has made the “The Healing Place” my escape from real life stress. Everything you need to just relax. Each morning and evening I sat in the yard that is fully furnished with a blossoming garden and grill!   I love the place so much I tried to convince Valerie to rent it to me lol!

Yiin is very nice and the room is true to the description and clean, however the rest of the apartment was really dirty and the smell was very unpleasant.  We didn't meet Yiin directly, we were with 2 of his roommates.

My stay at Nicolas's place was perfect!  If Airbnb had an award for best hosts, these guys would totes get it.  Firstly, the apartment is even more lovely in real life than the photos! Its spacious, well appointed, and spotlessly clean!  Nicolas and his roommates are awesome, super friendly and fun and were so helpful and accommodating.  They were all very communicative and made the whole process easy & stress free.  The neighborhood is very quaint and quiet.  There are some good restaurants/bars and a bodega at the end of the block.  Its two blocks to the A/C utica ave stop, which gets you to midtown in about 30 minutes, but its not so close that you hear the train while in the apartment.  I enjoyed my stay so much that Im extending it through the end of June in his roommates room while she is in France!  Seriously can't say enough good things about these folks!

This is a great location close to the subway entrance and to everything you would want to see in Manhattan! The place is clean and the host is kind. There are 5 flights of stairs to climb to get to the room but that is mentioned on the posting and is as expected. The location is in a safe area and close to a couple drug stores and several places to eat.
Place was so nice and cozy. Lots of stores near but area is a little sketchy. There is a train a few blocks down which was convenient. Kelly was super nice and responded quickly.

The home has convenient access to the subway and local shops. The surrounding neighborhood is a little “grungy,” but I never felt unsafe at any time. The quarters were cute and tidy. Kelly was very helpful and responsive. I would stay here again.

Although the building is old, the apartment  is very clean as pictured. The host couple are nice and responsive. Communication was easy. The location is convenient as far as access to subway and bus lines are concerned.  The place is quite small, there are two of us and I didn't like hanging out in the place for long as it feels a bit tight. South exposure so a lot of sunlight -- I imagine it would be warm in the winter but it can be hot in the summer, so one needs to keep the shade down and AC on all day. AC is a bit noisy, and because it is close to bed (practically touches the bed) so you will feel the vibration while sleeping which is a little annoying. We stayed for 12 days and I was a little surprised that there was no change of linens or towels. The hosts explained that this was the airBNB policy ( what a strange policy ) so I didn't ask for more towels. ( they do have laundry downstairs but I didn't want to bother with that. ) but such policy does seem weird and not so reasonable.
