To be fair, after explaining the policy the host did offer to come over and wash the linen for us ( which was nice of them) but I didn't want to impose it on them so we declined. Overall an ok experience, but I have stayed in NYC often and given the small space, and east 100th street location, I feel there are other places that are probably better value for money.

Overall, staying at Ben's houseboat was a great experience! I do think it's worth mentioning that I suspect that the description of the boat in the listing is slightly out of date, in that the boat is currently dry docked and there is no longer a bathroom on the boat. The marina bathrooms were close by and well maintained, but it was somewhat annoying to have to go out to them if you need to use the bathroom at night.   On the plus side, Ben was incredibly responsive via text, the boat was beautiful and comfortable (the hammocks!), and it was a lovely way to spend a long weekend in the Rockaways.

I can only recommend Mey for your trip to New York. The apartment is really great, clean and well located. Mey is very caring, and very responsive when you have something to ask her. She is also accommodating because we have to leave the apartment at 11 a.m., we asked her if we can leave later because our flight was in the evening which was not a problem. Go there with your eyes closed, you won’t be disappointed 😉

Poor communication on the part of the hosts meant for a very stressful and unpleasant stay. Finding an Airbnb to accommodate 14 people in Manhattan is no easy feat. This listing is one of few able to host a large group, and as such as cornered the market - the value was reasonable, though the location being so north in West Harlem means transportation to main attractions and popular neighbourhoods for travellers added up in both time and money. The unit itself was very well appointed, clean, spacious and as advertised with a lovely outdoor space. With the keypad locks check-in is seamless and easy for multiple people to access the unit without having to worry about a key being lost or shared in the group. I unfortunately would not recommend this particular Airbnb based on the communication of the hosts. As a host myself, I understand the importance of communication and how to ensure guests have a seamless and easy experience. I did not have this experience staying with Jane and May which may the trip stressful for me, and more stressful than needed as I was managing 13 other people. I requested a late checkout and after some back and forth the hosts agreed that it would be possible. We were very grateful! During that conversation they requested that a contractor gain access to the unit on the 2nd day of our stay to review some upcoming work being planned in the backyard. The time proposed was when we would be out of the unit -naturally I said this was no problem whatsoever. Unfortunately both of those arrangements were amended multiple times. And I was receiving multiple text messages each day of our trip with various changes to the agreed schedule. We were then asked to have the contractor access the unit once to review the work to be done, and then again on the 3rd day of our stay to start the work - arriving earlier than we would be awake. I indicate this would be problematic and unfair to those staying in the unit who paid a significant amount to be there. After more back and forth we agreed he would come, an hour later to ensure the guests were awake. So the girls woke up earlier than planned and got ready anticipating his arrival. Then at the exact time he was to be arriving we were notified that he would no longer be coming. Additionally the late checkout was confirmed for 3pm. Then at 11pm at night the night before we were leaving I was notified we would only be allowed to access 1 of the units for late checkout. Not what had been outlined when the late checkout was approved - and at this time we were already out for the evening and not in a position to begin packing and planning for an earlier checkout than was agreed to. The cleaning lady arrived at 11am waking up some of the guests as she...

Mey is a nice person and her apartment is lovely,cozy and convenient. We communicate really well about cleaning schedule and changes of checking in/out time. Although the appearance of an unexpected cockroach brings some unpleasant, Mey solved the problem at the first time and showed her apologise. I am satisfied with this apartment all in all.

I work in East Harlem and Mey’s place was a perfect location to get to my school on East 106th Street. The apartment faces the back so it is quiet and serene. The large picture window has a shade and from the bed you can see the beautiful fall colors of the trees in the backyard. I appreciated Mey’s quick response and ease accessing the apartment. An easy walk to Central Park and the reservoir. Try Frenchy Coffee just around the corner on Lex and 102 for the best and freshest Croissants in NYC that are light and flaky.  I also tried Au Jus that is literally a few steps away on Lex which has amazing slow cooked meats at every price point. The sautéed Kale and portobello mushrooms are excellent. I cannot wait to return to Mey’s spot.

This apartment is very clean, the furniture is new and the heating is perfect for the winter. There is a laundromat right next door, so it's totally fine to stay there even if it doesn't have a washing machine inside. Disavantages: there is no sunlight at any time of the day. The building is not really well kept; there's dirt all over the floors and people leave the door open for strangers all the time, which might make you feel unsafe given that the apartment is in the ground floor and right next to the door. I wouldn't say it's a safe part of the neighborhood to go out by yourself at night, too. Overall, though, it's a good apartment and well equipped, with a reasonable price for the region. I stayed for 4 months and I don't regret it, it had everything I needed.

157th/broadway station was very convenient and apartment itself was great. The street at times was a little scary. The outside noise/neighbors affected sleep the 1st night. We used the seamless app a few times to have food delivered, that was nice. There is not an abundance of restaurants in walking distance but the deli stores came in handy. I wish I would have remembered the reviews saying there would not be washcloths. I probably will stay in a hotel next time but it was nice to see how a New Yorker lives. Communication was great with owners, friendly and helpful.

Nice place exactly like on the picture. Ivana and Tami gave me a welcome feeling although I didn't meet them when I arrived. But I must also mention that I had a huge delay with my flight. They were all flexible and cool about that.  Good thing is that you can enter the building with a code. So you can come and go as you please.  If you have a big suitcase (like I did) take into account that you will have to cary it 4 stairs up. Also the room will be filles as soon as you open your suitcase. Fortunately there is a large closset.   There are no curtains in the room, which made me feel a little uncomfortable while getting dressed;)  The street where the appartment is in, came across as sketchy. I did not feel okay to walk around there alone during the evening. During the day I got a lot of attention of men on the street.  (That kind of attention you don't want to have as a girl and really I had normal clothes on lol). I felt so uncomfortable outside the appartment that I decided not to stay for the night. But this is my personal experience, maybe I am a whimp;)  Good part of the neighbourhood is that the metro to Manhattan and Williamsburg is verry close by (5 min walk). Also there is a really nice bistro place around the corner with a good lunch menu and a verry sweet Argentinian owner.   All over the appartment is a nice place. Tami and Ivana are nice and easy going girls. If I would have been a guy and not feel so uncomfortable outside in the street I would have definitely stayed.

This was a our most unpleasant Air BNB experience ever. The first thing you should know is that the apartment is dangerous. It has incorrectly installed Mortise lock on the apartment door. These locks, when engaged at the faceplate (the part on the side of the door), are supposed to lock the outside doorknob. This one however locks the inside doorknob as well. And since the lock can only be engaged/disengaged from the faceplate, once its locked and closed, you are out of luck if you are inside the apartment, which is what happened to us. Fortunately May's employee Sofia was in the building and was able to open the door from the outside with a key, but this could be very dangerous if there is a fire or other emergency situation where you need to leave quickly. May and Sofia insisted this was a safety feature but were unable to explain how locking their guests in the apartment would keep them safe. (Also, it seemed a bit unnecessary as there are two deadbolts on the door as well). To make matters worse, in my exchanges with May about the issue, she accused me of leaving my toddler in the apartment alone. The last thing I need on my vacation is someone judging my parenting, so this is really what knocked a few stars of my review. Sofia did find a temporary fix by taping over the faceplate so that the lock could not be engaged accidentally but I'm alarmed that they are unconcerned about how dangerous this is. Beyond that unpleasant experience, here are our pros and cons: PROS -Close to subway -Nice apartment--everything was clean and nicely decorated CONS -Terrace is badly misrepresented on the listing. When we arrived, it was flooded from raining and I had to ask Sofia to come back and get rid of the water. Then we saw how poorly maintained it was. The tiles are disintegrating (probably from constant flooding), the plants are dead, and the strings lights don't work. It rained again later in the week and we had to get Sofia to come back to get rid of the water again. -The kitchen is poorly stocked. We had to ask for additional silverware, it was missing some basics like a toaster, and there were no place mats or cloth napkins (which I usually see in my air bnbs). Sofia did drop off more silverware and the place mats and napkins but it was an additional interaction that should have been unnecessary. -There were not enough chairs for a group. Our first night, someone had to eat dinner standing up. We were six people, and this place is supposed to accommodate at least that. (There are only 4 chairs on the terrace.) -The location is pretty far from most of the tourist spots so be prepared for long subway trips (45-hour) to get downtown. -The volume of interaction I had to have with May and Sofia was just too much. While they...

I stayed in this apartment 1 month. Thank you Corporate Housing!  Details:  1) It was easy to check in. I had to take keys near central train station in agency’s office.  2) Building is totally clean. I’m afraid of cockroaches, so I was happy that there were NO insects at all.  3) Neighborhood is great.  4) In apartment’s description I found notice that during my stay agency can show my apartments to other people who want to rent, but nobody disturbed me.  5) There were a lot of towels and clean sheets.  6) I found tea kettle, it’s great because I like hot tea.  7) 2 rooms, 2 sofa-bed  in first room and queen bed in bedroom.  Unfortunately, there was renovation of next building and every morning last week from 7 AM was very hard to sleep... But it’s not fault of agency. And there is a window right above your head when you sleep in bedroom, so it’s windy, I had to buy a small heater. Anyway, I will stay with Corporate Housing again.

Ivana and Tami's place is really tidy and clean. The bed is big and super comfy and you have an air con/heater that you can use as you like.  The location is great for getting to Manhattan and other neighbourhoods in NYC and it feels quite safe - we came back late a few times and we didn't feel in danger. Ivana and Tami are really kind and friendly and super easy going. They kept telling us to make it our home for the duration of our stay. They were very generous as well. They were chatty but also respected our space. They also left out guide books and answered all of our questions. I would definitely stay there again.
We had an under average experience overall, confusing check-out times, unsafe neighbourhood and communication issues made the whole experience disappointing. There is room for improvements.

Unfortunately, my experience in Tami and Ivana's apartment was very stressful and disappointing. The night I arrived, I was surprised to find a leak next to my bed, which dripped all night and made it difficult to sleep. The bathroom ventilation did not work, the mattress had stains (and no mattress cover) and the couch advertised in the common area was gone. At first, I overlooked all this and chose to stay to avoid logistical challenges. However, as I was leaving for a short trip with my partner a few days later, Tami told us that the management company would come to "spray the whole building preventively" because the downstairs apartment had an infestation. We offered to put our things in bags to protect them, but Tami declined and offered to do it herself when the bags arrived. On our way back, we asked Tami for information about the nature of the pesticide that was used. We did not receive a response and chose to spend the night in a hotel preventively. The next day, we arrived to discover (i) some of our belongings, including shoes, covered in pesticide, and (ii) that the host's story ("the whole building had to be sprayed preventively, by law, twice") did not match the account of the neighbor (they were not sprayed and had heard of no infestation anywhere in the building).  We were also concerned for our health, since we felt the pesticides in our throats and we still didn't have a response about what chemicals were used. All windows were closed and there was a layer of residue on the floor. We decided to leave the building, replace/disinfect all our belongings and request a full refund.  At first, the hosts offered to refund us and asked for my Venmo account. When I asked for the refund through AirBnB instead, they refused and AirBnB had to override them to issue the refund. I assume (and hope) this was an anomalous event, given that most of their reviews are favorable. My feeling, however, is that they systematically misled us.

This place was a beautiful home and May was an amazing host to us.  The apartment is exactly as pictured, and extremally spacious for NYC.  The location to the 1 and C lines are great.  Only 20-30 min train ride to downtown Manhattan.  Highline Park and Hudson Parks within a few blocks for walking pets.  The smell of weed and dog poop on the streets were a little tough and there are sidewalk parties with loud music, but in this area of town, that is all common and expected.  People in the neighborhood were nice and no one bothered you.  I stayed for 3 months and had no issues with security or felt unsafe.  May has a very beautiful home and updated décor.  The balcony was a nice touch as well.  Loved going out on the cooler nights and drinking hot cocoa with my puppy and husband on the balcony.  Over all, May went above and beyond to make sure our stay was comfortable.  I will rent any of her places again anytime I come to NYC.

We stayed at Paulettes place for three nights and it had everything we needed. Unfortunately we never really had time to enjoy the patio since we were away most of the time, but it sure looked like a nice spot to have morning coffee! Small bottles of shampoo and soap and fresh towels were there for us. The neighbourhood may seem a bit sketchy after dark, but it is probably fine. Thank you for letting us stay!

Nathan was a perfect host. Great communication for a long-term stay (30 days). Reception and check-in were a breeze and Nathan made sure that our stay was comfortable and stress-free.  Recommend Nathan next time we stay in New York.

Tracey's place is exactly as pictured! It is very cute and cozy. We loved the water and snack basket she left for us. Also, she left a very detailed book on where to eat, etc. I would definitely stay there again if it were in a different location. Tracey was very easy to communicate with and made everything so easy! The location for us felt a little unsafe at times. The street itself is safe. We were two girls traveling alone, so that might be why. Definitely use the Rockaway subway station if using the metro. We had an unfortunate experience getting of the metro at the Atlantic station and would definitely not recommend others making the same mistake. But, once again, if you are more familiar with your surroundings than we were, this may not be a consideration. We definitely enjoyed the room itself!!
Beautiful, modern, clean & comfortable 3rd floor apt on quiet residential street with shade trees & one of NYC's best Italian restaurants at end of block, plus great shower & living space.

Tracy was a great host during my week-long stay in New York. The living space was clean and inviting, and she provided some snacks and water bottles that were much appreciated during my first days in the city.  The subway station is a short walk from Tracy's home. The neighborhood looks a little sketchy at night, but I think it's a safe area to walk through and explore at any time of day. There's a school with a basketball court right across the street, lots of families in the area, and all the people we spoke with in the restaurants nearby were friendly.  While the main street can get noisy during the day and night (that's New York for you), Tracy's home is far enough away from most traffic so the noise won't keep you awake.  If you want an authentic New York experience at a great price, I'd recommend staying at Tracy's.

Space is very accurate to the listing. If you bring a car, parking can be a bit stressful as you have to move your car to the alternate side, multiple times a week, based off of street sweeping schedule. Space heaters were provided which made the space all the more cozy. Public transportation was also very accessible. Overall a successful trip.

We didn't spend too much time in the house as we were out exploring day and night. But for 4 people we fit in nicely. We arrived late at night and the neighborhood looked a little sketchy, but when we had a chance to look around in the morning it was a pleasant area. Many thanks to Yahaira

This apartment should not be on Airbnb. The beds are so creaky no-one could sleep at night. The windows don't lock so it feels incredibly unsafe. There was construction right by building but we weren't informed, there are also dangerous stairs (4 stories) leading to the apartment. We lasted less than 12 hours, were made to pay ridiculous cash fees for cleaning (on top of what is demanded in the listing) and for late check in.

I wanted to write about everything in details,but I'll be short ,as I think that there wouldn't be enough space,and it will take everyone much time to read. I read the previous comments and I actually don't understand anyone.But keep in mind,I have stayed here mostly for 2 months and know every vice.  The area is not safe,very dirty,although the subway is close,you can hear it and it is not very frequent. Actually,you text Tina but in fact you live with her father(who will be half naked)who wIll disturb you every 5 minutes when he doesn't like something,he will eavesdrop your conversations(as he did in my case and then asked to turn the phone off to talk with me) he will complain about everything that you do and don't,he will always mention what is included in price and what's not,and every day he will say what to do in the way HE only likes it to be done.  ( Tina lied,because she said that he would live near the house,but as you can see,he would actually live with you,from time to time there would be even her children and her brother). Overall,I didn't like the house at all,it was dirty and uncomfortable to live in,I saw bugs in the bathroom and in the kitchen,there were not enough cooking supplies and facilities.Be aware that your food in the fridge or shelves may be eaten.What's more,that "old unconscious father"(politely saying) will not allow you to use even that minimum amount of facilities in the house,sometimes even water,and don't forget to minimize your usage of electricity,of course. As you can understand,I haven't mentioned even the half of disadvantages.Am so disappointed,I had an unpleasant experience living there which caused health problems,because I was constantly nervous.It was the worst house I have ever stayed in.  I WOULD NEVER RECOMMEND THIS PLACE TO ANYBODY!!!

Gregory's house is so stylish, classy, fresh, beautiful and pleasant. I almost did not want to leave the house!:) Gregory himself is so easy to talk to you. He makes you feel that he is a friend. I will definitely ask to stay in his home again if I need a place to stay. This place is such a steal. I recommend it to everyone.

Host Sen was very communicative, helpful, always responding quickly to us which was the best thing during the stay. However, there're few things I'd like to share for the people who want to stay here for a long term.  First, I feel the photos are very misleading. We were specifically told that the room we stayed at was what's in the listing. However, our windows were facing completely opposite direction than in the photos, unless they were photoshopped. I picked this place because it showed plenty sunlight. But in reality, there's another building right next to it, so barely any light coms in the apt. During 14 days, it always felt gloomy like it was raining or cloudy outside even when sun is bright out (you can never tell what's the weather's like today unless you stick out your head to the window).  Place is very clean, as I don't think any life can endure the strong smell and toxins of the beach material he uses to clean. We checked in right after cleaning so had to open the window all day long. The smell may go away with air freshener, but that doesn't change the fact that it contains chemicals that are probably toxic and hazardous for both environment and people.  Also, just that the building has never properly renovated, there're many unusual rules to follow. I think it should be advised in advance in the listing. And I'm not talking about the things like making sure to lock the doors behind you, or no smoking inside, etc.  1. All the light switches need to be pulled carefully in a certain way so that they don't fall on your head. There was one light looking like it's going to fall and we were scared to walk below it. 2. You keep the water running for 5 minutes until you get hot water, which in reality, it takes more than that at times. There are so much water wasted every single day and it was not even so cold outside yet. I hate to do this while a billion people are suffering from global water shortage. On the other hand, some people are selfish caring for saving their bucks. I really hope people stop being greedy and be aware that the water problems will lead to next global crisis. 3. You CAN'T use two electronic devices at the same time together. That is, using any of these two devices together will blow the fuse in the entire unit-- toaster, hair dryer, microwave, portable heater, rice cooker, etc. In other words, if you wants to use the microwave, you shout to the room to turn off the heater. If you want to use the hair dryer, you shout out to let the people know so they don't use anything else.

The apt. was exactly as described. Very roomy. Freshly cleaned. Staff was very responsive.   As we were informed when booking, the property is prewar  (1930s) and has not been updated and it is four flights up.  Certainly no unpleasant surprises and it served our purposes well.

Let's start with the apartment's location The access to bus and Subway is good, and you can find a couple of good grocery stores in less than five minutes walk. The apartment building itself has a laundry facility, but if you want to have a wash and fold service there's a laundromat just next door.  The apartment is in a relatively new building. The building is well-maintained.  I know Harlem might not be the most immediate option for those who have never been to NYC. But we never feel unsafe walking around in Gregory's neighborhood in particular, and this side of Harlem. You just need to be as mindful as you need to be when navigating at nights in a big city.    Now the apartment itself. Yes, when we check in it's very clean (including the bathroom) and everything works. We can say Gregory's is the cleanest in our more than five years of using Airbnb. The bed is also the most comfortable.  Yes, the apartment is not huge but it's not cluttered and is enough for a couple.  Last but not least, Gregory is very helpful. He communicates clearly and responds quickly. He takes time to explain to us on how to enjoy Harlem for first-time visitors.  We visit NYC often and if possible, we really want to stay at this place again.

My two kids (20 and 15) and I stayed at Michael’s place from July 14-19. We found the accommodations comfortable, super clean, and stylish, located up two flights of stairs on the 3rd level of an old 1860’s building and tavern. The weather was quite warm while we were in New York City, but two air conditioning units kept the place plenty cool enough. Upon our arrival we found more than enough clean towels and linens, in addition to toilet paper, soap, shampoo, and conditioner. There’s also a LOT of storage space to unpack your clothing, including nightstands and dressers with several drawers, and a large armoire for hanging items. Walking to Times Square took about 10-15 minutes, as did getting to the nearest subway. We never felt unsafe walking to and from Michael’s place, even very late at night. There’s a deli/small grocery store just around the corner that stays open 24/7. And while there are a ton of eateries within easy walking distance, do be sure to eat at least once at the Landmark Tavern downstairs.  Very delicious food(!), and I noticed they even have a children’s menu. Michael was always very gracious in our communications and was quick to get back to me with any questions I had. Our time in NYC went way too fast, and I’m hoping to return to see more in the next few years. I’d stay here again in a heartbeat!!

cute place. fun to stay in a house boat. the neighbors are all fishermen so that is fun. Location is pretty close to the beach, which is great, but the neighborhood right around you is a little sketchy. BUT the marina is a gated community so you don't feel at all in danger inside the marina.   All and all it is a super cool place! unique and worth the experience.  I would recommend it for the adventurous, just remember it is more like camping (nice camping) than a hotel. We love camping.   Things to be aware of, not negatives, just important to be aware of: - near JFK, (which is why we picked this spot) but noisy often. BUT it is super peaceful with tons of little fish jumping between jets taking off.  - cold shower in the boat, but warm showers in the community area on the dock. The community bathrooms are well taken care of.  - the charm of the boat is that it is pieced together from scraps and cool collections.  This is also a negative because sometimes you get jabbed by an awkward piece of plywood holding the AC on the couch. OR you can get slivers or rub up against a nail on reclaimed wood.   - the ceilings are short. I am only 6 ft but I found myself hitting my head on fishing polls and stuff.

Ben is a very responsive and an easy going host. The James Franco has a lot of character and is definitely a unique stay! If his rules scare you then this stays probably not for you. My stay was during the 4th of July which the boat had a perfect view of fireworks from all over.

WARNING DO NOT BOOK WITH BUDDY!!!  HE IS A LIAR AND A THIEF! HE NEVER RESPONDED, TOLD US WHERE TO GO OR GAVE US A KEY! I REPEAT DO NOT BOOK WITH THIS SORRY EXCUSE FOR A HUMAN BEING UNLESS YOU WISH TO BE ROBBED!
it was good long walks to subway and Manhattan. and the area next to the subway atation was sketchy like 100% at night but overall a good experience. no one got mugged 😂

I booked this place very last minute for my parents- who were in town for my wedding- as the previous airbnb I booked for them turned out to be a health hazard. As such, I did not see Buddy's place myself, however I trust my parents who are neat-freaks. They really loved Buddy's place, and found it clean, cozy and spacious. Buddy was so kind and accommodating throughout their entire stay and made this otherwise stressful hiccup easier to manage. Thank you Buddy!

Due to an unfortunate death in our family we were looking to book something in Da Bronx, NY since that’s where the funeral was being held. Our family did not want to be spilt apart and it was hard finding something big enough in a short amount of time. Fortunately, my sister went on Airbnb and found this beautiful house in Da Bronx and by the looks of the pictures seem like a decent choice even with pricing. Only problem is there were other people looking to rent as well, so I emailed the host about my situation and thank god he gave us the opportunity to stay at his house. It was a true blessing especially since it was a perfect location and meant we didn’t have to be split up. The host provided all the details i needed and keep great communication prior to arriving. Once we arrived, we were amazed on how beautiful and well kept the place was. The pictures did justice and it was even better in person. The few days we stayed was a pleasure and had enough room for all of us. This was definately better than being at a hotel and I definitely want to come back here. This is my first Airbnb and honestly the host set the bar high so when I use this service again I only hope anything more or I might be unhappy lol. God definitely made a rough situation better due to finding this place that eliminated unnecessary stress. You will not be disappointed because I am beyond happy and satisfied!!!

Such a fun and unique getaway! It’s not a luxurious beach resort, don’t stay here if you are afraid to get a little dirty and salty! Ben is not nearby but was super available and communicative via text if we had any questions or issues. It was a really special and memorable experience; we had a great time and would love to stay at the James Franco again.

Ben welcome us aboard his boat.  Even though a very short stay, it became a huge part on our book of cherished memories. We’ve discovered another aspect of Far Rockaway’s personality. It’s a falling in love with the air over and over again experience.  We can’t stress enough the dedication you’ll find from Ben during your stay.  The boat has its gentle roughness , a very cosy charm. Your mind will embark into an imagination life boat trip. Thank you Ben.

My weekend stay on the James Franco was wonderful. Don't let the intense rules scare you away -- they really aren't that bad in reality. Check-in was a breeze with fully detailed instructions. I highly recommend sunset drinks on the top deck! As some reviews have mentioned, the downstairs bathroom does not have a door. Honestly, skip that toilet. Use the bathhouse toilets mostly, and if you have to pee overnight, use the one on the top deck. It's easier and your butt and bladder will thank you.  The bed is super comfy, and pro tip: if you use the fan, wedge folded up paper or a napkin under the front and it will level the blades out and it won't rattle. Between the fan and open windows, I never needed at AC.  You are right by JFK so you do hear the planes at night, they seem to go right over the marina around 12-1am. It's fine. Loud but not bad, but I also live near LGA so I'm used to it. It's cool to watch them take of and land during the day.  The beach is just a short, straight walk, maybe 10 mins. Enjoy!

I was freelancing from home during my stay and had a great experience. Grant was a fantastic host and kept to himself. The place is in an awesome location on the 1 line, I never felt unsafe as a young woman. The room itself is sunny, clean, and a good size. The kitchen was great to cook in (although no microwave), and there was always enough room in the fridge for my own food. The bathroom was clean and the hot water good. It can get pretty noisy because it is NYC, and just a loud neighborhood in general, but it didn't bother me at all. I did have to use a sleeping mask because the room was so bright and the curtains didn't do much, but that wasn't a problem either. Grant even split an AC with me to make my experience more comfortable since I was working from home and the summer was so brutal, which was really nice of him.

I thoroughly enjoyed staying at Athena's place while in New York!  She called me a few days before to give me instructions on how to access her building, which has very wonderful doormen.  I was in town settling my daughter for college and her apartment is right down the street from her dorm.  She was fabulous with not only me, but with my daughter as well who came up a few times to meet me before leaving for the day.    The neighborhood is safe and I never felt unsafe even walking home late at night.  She did everything to make me feel comfortable.  The cats were not an issue as I don't mind pets and they were very friendly and quiet.  Very clean and comfortable bedroom with a hall doorway so I virtually had a private area.  The bathroom is shared, but it was never an issue.  Athena sleeps out in the living room with a screen so as to give some privacy.  She does smoke, which is different for me, but was willing to not smoke in front of me and only in the bathroom if that is what I desired.  She has air purifiers and I could not smell it in the bedroom AT ALL.  I was only there to sleep, so it was not an issue for me.   Athena provides a nice space in the closet to hang up and store folded clothes and shoes.  She also provided me with bagels and juice! She is a wonderful and fun host! She told me some fun places to stop and see when I told her where I was headed for the day.  It was a pleasure staying in her apartment and getting to know her! I highly recommend staying with her if you are ever in the NYC area! She is a fun and gracious host and person!  She exudes the true New York spirit and is a true New Yorker! Loved staying with her!
Homey feel with a great view of the skyline. Don’t be afraid to ask for anything during the stay!

This place was a steal for its location alone! Phil was very accommodating, he let me amend my trip a few weeks before arrival, which was much appreciated. The space was cozy, the bed comfy and it was really quiet at night. There is a/c, which you can individually control. The apartment is typical for NY, small and in an old building, but it worked really well for me. I loved my stay & would definitely be back!

If you need an affordable place in Manhattan to sleep and shower and are ok with climbing stairs and ladders, search no more! Phil was a wonderful host, doing everything he can to make my stay pleasant. I saved so much time staying in East Village (as opposed to Queens, where I usually stay). As a solo female traveller, I never felt unsafe. I would absolutely stay here again. Thanks, Phil!
Neighborhood can be shady at times!

Very easy to get to the subway - great value! Cuban bakery around corner - 5 Estrellas is the name I think- amazing coffee and baked goods! Do need to get to the grocery store to stock up so don't get in too late. All the delivery restaurants said 45 mins to deliver but I think actually was a little sooner. We have 4 kids and 4 adults. 2 of the kids shared a bed and the other 2 used the bunk bed. Make sure your littles are used to the bunk beds. It caused a little drama the first couple of nights- he was afraid to get down from the top bunk.

She is a good host and will communicate with you but it was not communicated to me that she had children to pick up and I was coming from another state with nowhere else to place my bags and her sister who only speaks Spanish had to let me in which was a little struggle. Granted I can speak some Spanish myself it was a little bit stressful otherwise the apartment is clean and in a decent location.

This was a horrible experience. AirBB was super responsive and helpful.  This unit is not as advertised.  First it was dirty and with stains all over the walls. Second there was no heat except for one small space heater that barely worked. Third, there is a washer in the unit and when we opened the door rancid water, like backed up sewage, came poring out and we had to scramble to throw towels down to dry it up while gagging. Then we had to use Clorox spray and our own mop and cleaning supplies to try and fix the smell.  This was after we had already cleaned the apartment because it seemed so filthy.  The host did nothing to help. Before the rancid water we were extremely disappointed but that incident made me feel unsafe from a health perspective and the smell was still there despite us cleaning up. Thank God Air BB helped us find a great place and refunded our money.

Lorena provides much more than she advertises. A fridge, towels, shampoo, toothbrush and more are all provided and available for use. The room is large and comfortable and Lorena is quick to answer any questions you may have. The neighborhood can be a little noisy but it’s not dangerous and comes with good access to midtown Manhatten.

We really loved the stay! At the time we booked (for the NYC Marathon), this was one of the best rates we found, and the apartment was in a FANTASTIC neighborhood, very quiet, and the apartment looked out onto the back yards, so was itself very quiet.  The apartment was super clean, cute, and while not huge, was a good size for NYC (and much less claustrophobic than typical hotel rooms).  The building entrance isn't fancy or particular promising, but it's certainly fine, and more importantly, the apartment is nice, and we really enjoyed our stay.   Incredibly convenient in terms of being < 5 minutes to Central Park, to the subway station, restaurants, and groceries/drug stores.  We would absolutely return!

We had a wonderful stay at Aqlesia with our baby.  The apartment is very functional and well decorated, although it appeared larger in the photos. The 2 bathrooms are practical and the small bathtub is perfect for a child. The terrace is incredible with a superb view, particularly over Manhattan, although we couldn't really enjoy it because it was winter. A summer stay at Aqlesia must be great!  Aqlesia was super responsive and very accommodating. We were able to leave our luggage on the last day and collect it early in the evening for our flight, which allowed us to enjoy the last day! The only small points of improvement: - There was their stuff everywhere, except for 3 small shoe drawers that we used. As a result, most of our belongings remained in our suitcases and we didn't really feel at home. - the pillows are very high and hurt the neck. I had to use a decorative cushion

This stay was during my birthday weekend and J & JR made it very stress free and easy. I enjoyed the stay and the bed is super comfy & safe location!!! Secured building and near many wonderful places to eat!! J & JR are very warm, welcoming & personable!! Thank you again for accommodating me when I needed to check out a bit later. I am grateful!

My husband and I wanted to gift a trip to New York to our 17 years old daughter. Manhattan options were too expensive for the small spaces they offered. So, although I was a little scared of the voices about Bronx area, I decided to give it a try. The neighborhood was tranquil and none of us felt in danger walking any time of the day around the streets. The subway is only few blocks away and takes you everywhere. The apartment was clean, quiet and has everything we needed for our short stay. The communication with the host was excellent and they accommodate us kindly with an earlier check in after a long red eye flight. If you are a fancy client that want luxury accommodation, then this is not the place for you. But if you are normal people with normal necessities, a budget and need a place for few days, then I definitely recommend this place.

The room is emasculate and clean, location is very close to LaGuardia however if you are using public transportation into Manahattan or any or the other boroughs outside of queens will be a chore. Also smokers beware. I was woken up at 4 am by noise coming from upstairs where the host and his family live. Instead of complaining about it I went outside to smoke a joint. When I came back into the home I was greeted by the host and asked to leave bc I was “caught” smoking. The host lied on other guest in the house saying to me he recieved complaints about smoking. When I asked the other guest about it, I was told by that guest he didn’t know what I was talking about bc he’s never met the host and was only staying there one night. When I asked the host about lying on other guest he then said his neighbors have cameras and had me on camera. I then asked the host to show me the video or photo bc I had never smoked in or around his home precious to that morning. I was treated like I was commuting a crime even though it’s is legal to smoke marijuana in NYS and NYC as well as no longer a crime on the federal level here in the United States.   The host claimed he would reimburse me for the days stay but I only received a $25 refund.   Needless to say I was forced to report this incident to Air bnb and they are going to give me a full refund. If you smoke cigarettes, a pipe, cigar, vape or majuana and the host “catches” you doing it outside on the sidewalk near his home at 4 am after he has woken you up with noise from his home, he is going to ask you to leave. Smokers beware.

The heating system makes extremely loud banging noises throughout the night….the radiators spit hot water from them and the windows needs sealing to prove t this NYC cold air from blowing through all night   Russell you need to supply better linens for all the rooms as well as essentials for the bathroom, toilet paper, bath towels, washcloths, and the tub needs to be fixed the stopper constantly gets in the way of the water draining so that makes the person have to bend over and hold it until all the waters out.   it seemed as if this was a newly opened Airbnb, but there was a lot of touchups that needs to be done before allowing the public to use it those sound at night, or extremely loud and very scary, especially for a person that is not from New York City   overall, Russell was very friendly accommodating and quick to respond. He allowed us to check in a hour or so early because it was extremely cold so I think some for that but I didn’t know it was OK for the day and a half that we stayed.

Sonali rented her apartment illegally on air bnb and put us in unsafe, uncomfortable and not honest conditions. The place was not up to cleanliness standards and she kept asking to come in and out of the apartment. It was a very uncomfortable and a very poor air bnb experience. She said it was her first time renting her apartment but based on the experience it should be her last considering that the apartment can not even be rented in the building.

Up until Check-in Our communication with Lina had been great and then someone called Esteban (supposedly Lina's son) took over communication. They gave us great details of how to checkin and when I asked if we could have their mobile number incase of any issues as there were flight delays and cancellations there was no response. From the moment the message was sent around 2pm EST about how to check in up until today almost a whole week after leaving we have not heard anything from the hosts. During our stay we experienced a multitude of isses - upon arrival there was an awful funky smell so we had to air the apartment and buy scented candles, there was also a cockroach on the kitchen floor that appeared a couple of hours later and the wifi details we were provided were incorrect. All was flagged with the hosts however (no response.) To make matters worse the building is terribly soundproofed and is incredibly noisy which I realised was not mentioned by the host/hosts at all in the airbnb listing/description despite the fact that they owe that to the gusts they host. There was construction in the building happening all week so we were woken at 7:30am every morning which is not the biggest issue had we been told beforehand but because all the other apartments and neighbours were also so loud it meant that through the night we barely slept and then to be awake from 7:30 when you've only managed 3-5 hours sleep was very problematic. The toilet also became clogged/blocked..... again this was raised with the host but no response so we had to escalate the situation quickly with Airbnb who also tried getting in touch with the hosts - even with warnings but they were unsuccessful and instead compensated us for the stress.

When my family and I arrived at the unit, we did not have the necessary check in info sent to us and we had to wait outside until we were able to make contact with the host which was not ideal considering the neighborhood. From there things were confusing, and one of the contact persons (there seem to be two and they're not coordinated) allowed us to leave our bags on our last day for a few hours after check in so that we didn't have to lug them around the city which was helpful, but later I received a text from one host telling me to move them which was confusing after my request had been granted.   As for the place and it's location: my family and I were in search of an affordable resting place in a decent area from which we could explore the city. The place was by no means high quality, and we struggled to track down simple things like bowls, sheets and garbage bags. We have stayed in a lot of Airbnbs and I've never had to put pillow cases and sheets on a bed. From dirt on the kitchen floors to dust and an old coke bottle beneath the main bed, to dirt and dust in every corner, the apartment just didn't feel clean at all. I didn't get the feeling that the place had been deeply cleaned at all, if ever.  The neighborhood itself was another disappointment. I've stayed in Brooklyn many times but never in an area with quite so much trash on the streets and people smoking weed in literally every doorway, including inside the building which I could smell through the vents. The whole area felt filthy. when I say there was trash everywhere, I mean everywhere. The location was purported to be in a good location, but there was a lot more of a sketchy vibe than I would have liked, which presents a serious challenge if you want to find food or groceries or walk to public transportation at night. The closest subway stop isn't exactly close either, and as I mentioned, walking this distance in this type of neighborhood feels unsafe. When you do walk to where the restaurants and subway stop are, there are very few decent food options and because of how filthy the neighborhood is, none feel particularly enticing. I tried to walk to a Dunkin Donuts one morning with my 11 year old and the entire area felt bad. Finally, after our stay I received a request from the host for $100 to repair a cleaning supply cabinet in the kitchen that neither myself or my family had anything to do with, or even aware of. It just contributed to the overall feeling at this place of feeling scammed and that the hosts haven't sorted out how to properly communicate with guests or run an Airbnb. I do not recommend this place and I would book someplace else.

The apartment was laid out a bit awkward but given the size was suitable for our needs. The door between the two bedrooms doesn't close.  There is a privacy curtain, but that doesn't help with the sound. There is a door that could be closed but you would have to move the bed to be able to close it.   We walked to the subway and traveled to Times Square without any issues. We had our dog and I walked him in the morning and evening (after dark) and never felt unsafe.   We were able to find a parking spot very close to the apartment. There is a school across the street and parking seems to be restricted during school days.   The host sent us detailed instructions for how to get into the apartment. She also left a little gift for us, which was very sweet.  We would definitely stay here again.

Good location for proximity to the UN and other related offices. The room was clean and well equipped for a business stay. The only negative feedback, which is not related to Evan or the room itself, is that the corner of the property felt a bit unsafe at night. This could be due to crowds from UNGA events, not sure if it is always the case.

Beautiful modern studio, just like the pictures, don’t be afraid to ask how to turn off the lights and the shower, as was a little complicated to figure out. Host was very responsive and friendly. Great value and location!

Didn’t match the photos, wasn’t particularly comfortable, amenities were bare minimum, was very expensive. Sink area was so crowded we couldn’t wash our faces without smacking our heads on the medicine cabinet. Paper thin walls. Signs throughout the building that Airbnbs are not allowed. Confronted by neighbors about this on our way out. The whole thing felt shady. We left a day early. We were really uncomfortable about the whole thing. The one positive I will say is that Edwin was somewhat responsive, though I didn’t feel satisfied by the responses. When I pointed out the apartment was different than the listing, he said there was a disclaimer on the listing about the layout of furniture maybe being different. He said things would need to be replaced as needed. We felt that was different than providing an entirely different space. And the listing was new, so it was unclear why things would need to be replaced. No response to our request about a partial refund for leaving early.

Very nice place! The hosts very nice and accommodating. The location seems a little sketchy at first but all the people around were nice. The upstairs residents are very noisy but it is bearable. The tub is fun and relaxing and the bed was very comfy! The walk to the subway was quick and easy, there were many restaurants close. Overall recommend!

We had a wonderful time with my friend for the following reasons : - The appartment was very clean and pretty. A little bit of noise but I feel like it’s New York’s and it did not disturb us.  - The room was really nice, spacious, the bed was very comfy. - The bathroom was very clean. - The neighbordhood was close to Manhattan (within 30min you could go anywhere in transport) and we didn’t felt unsafe as 2 girls. - Claire was very flexible, she answered really fast and was precise for the arrival. Also, she was really nice to talk to and helped us. - All this considering that the place is affordable.   Again thank you Claire for sharing your place ! We wish you the best.

Young’s place seemed pretty good on the Airbnb app and the photos did represent the size and layout of the place well. Young was not at the property during our stay. When we arrived we discovered cameras in all the living areas and hallways. We were unaware that there would be cameras and found their presence disturbing. The sheets were satin and made you sweat at night and the pillows were old and hard. The mattress was ok. The bathroom door didn’t shut or lock properly. I recommend taking a door wedge to make sure no one walks in on you as it seemed like each of the rooms is rented out separately. The neighbourhood is a little sketchy. Each night we were woken by people shouting in the street. There was, however, a cute little coffee shop very close by that makes the best coffee I’ve ever had in America! It’s called PABADE CAFE AND BAKERY at 135 E 110th St. Definitely go there and try their flat white.

Young was one of the best hosts we have ever had. He communicated amazingly and was proactive about information. He even let us store our bags in the apartment after check-out which saved us so much stress. Just be mindful you will have to pay for parking most likely if you stay here and have a car!

Young made our one night stay in NYC very comfortable and stress-free. Given that our trip was so short, our goal was to stay out in the city for as long as possible, so our main concern was having to carry our luggage everywhere. Young was super helpful in allowing us to store our luggage before check-in and after check-out. We were also greeted to a clean, well kept room when we got back to the room at night, and had no issues with the amenities provided. I recommend this room and Young as a host to anyone visiting NYC.

This is a very spacious apartment in an amazing location close to hudson yards and the high line. 3 bedrooms each with two beds each, couch/tv area and large kitchen with two big tables. Hosts very responsive to questions.  Beds were comfortable, plenty of hot water. What you need to know though is that it is a 3rd floor walkup with steep cement stairs in case that is an issue for anyone in your group. The outside also looks a little sketchy but felt perfectly safe.  I would describe it as sparse. We each had a towel but there were maybe 2 hand towels and 3 washcloths. plenty of shampoo /conditioner but no soap in the shower.  in terms of noise, the tenant below was having a loud party until about 2 or 3 am. Louder in front bedroom but quieter in the back.  Overall it worked out great for our group of 6 girls there for a weekend

George's property was great from beginning to end. I liked that we had the whole entire home to ourselves. The location was great. The neighborhood/area did not seem sketchy at all. Nothing much was at walking distance but everything you need was about 20 minutes away or less. The house itself was really nice inside I would say pretty modern and we were provided with everything we needed to make our stay comfortable. It's really nice that there's a washer and dryer. On top of that George was really responsive to any concerns we had and solved an issue we had upon arrival at the property. Would definitely book with George at this property again.

Where to begin.  I’ll start with the fact that this host violated Air BnB’s safety and privacy policies so grievously while I was there that they decided my safety was at risk and moved me to a hotel for 3 nights free of charge and refunded me for part of my stay. They also removed his listings from their platform. That’s how serious they considered his behavior.  The host entered my room without my consent when I wasn’t home on at least 2 occasions that I know of. He also repeatedly let himself into the apartment that I was sharing with other guests without consent or permission. After the 2 guests I was sharing the unit with moved out and I was alone he would let himself in and out of the unit, at will, day and night. Sometimes he would just use the toilet and leave. Other times he would conduct his personal business on speakerphone outside my door. Sometimes he would sleep the entire night there in the spare room even though he had a fully furnished apartment downstairs with all of his clothes, food and toiletries. I cannot stress enough that he did not live in the unit. His residence was elsewhere in the building. I even came home one night at 1 am after helping a friend with her new restaurant to find him in the apartment cleaning with all the lights on. Again, a place he didn’t even reside in or have permission to be in. He stayed in the apartment until 2:30 am making noise. The noise continued the next morning at 7:30 am. He moved in a phone charger, a coat and a couple of t shirts and claimed that he now “lived there” and would be using the place as he pleased. He also has a strict policy against house guests that’s posted on the refrigerator but low and behold he was hosting a guest in the unit at 8:30 am. Again, hosting a guest at a residence that he doesn’t even live at with a paying guest inside. His father owns the building and because of that the host feels he owns it too and that all the units in the building are his residences to come and go as he pleases. He behavior was so erratic and worrisome that I had to eventually call Air Bnb for help and they moved me to safety. I fear for the next person that stays in his building because at his core he doesn’t understand that what he’s doing is wrong. He had little to no sense of boundaries or personal privacy. He views his paying guests as flatmates or boarders of his he is free to pedantically inspect, bully and lord over. Dude, I am not your housemate or your friend. I am a paying guest. I hung 5 t shirts and a pair of jeans in an empty room to dry after washing and he accused me of using “his bedroom” to dry my wash (again, he lives downstairs). Another example of his delusional sense of ownership and boundaries when it comes to his guests and where he legally resides.  On top of all of that the place was filthy and without heat. Dirty, threadbare towels greeted me upon my arrival. A shower curtain caked with mold. Hair and debris all over the floor and rug. I asked for blankets because the unit had no heat and he brought up filthy, dust ball ridden “blankets” in a trash bag from the basement to try and put on the bed. The blankets had to be at least 30 years old and complete worthless. I suspect they were actually rugs because they did little to nothing to heat the bed. I took the least filthy one because I was tired is sleeping in a coat. Also the deadbolt was disabled when I arrived. I now know it’s so he can let himself into the unit at will. Also no screens on many of the windows so when we let fresh air in we were also letting in flies and mosquitoes. And no covering on the bathroom window so people in adjacent lofts and see inside.  No cleaning or cleaning service for over 3 weeks. Dirty oven and stove top. Poor communication before the booking as well. I shared a coffee with my host early in my stay as I often do being a traveler. Perhaps he took that as a weakness. I’ll never know but I fear it’s how he decides just how far he can push boundaries with his guests.  I had been stranded abroad from my home of Brooklyn since the pandemic began. I was so excited to come home and experience my city again after all this time. This experience tainted that homecoming and robbed me of something I had looked so forward to. Again, I fear for the lone traveler on a budget who stays in these units should he ever be allowed back on the platform. He advertises them as “shared units” but it’s a rouse. It’s used as a disclaimer to invade the privacy of his guests whenever he decides to claim residency at one of his many rooms and units. He’ll come and go as he pleases and enter your bedroom without permission. My worry now is that he’ll start doing it when guests are inside that bedroom. After all, in his mind he “lives there.”

Felt unsafe in the location. We are a family of 4 from London. We are well traveled including to NYC several times, but having booked 4 nights we checked out after 1 night as didn’t feel safe. Interior of the apartment is very nice , clean and exactly as it looks in the photos. Rohit was a very helpful and responsive owner. But exterior of the apartment was disappointing- the house sits between the derelict house next door with windows and doors all boarded up, and a fried chicken outlet, with lots of litter. Taxi drivers were surprised that tourists were staying there and warned us to be careful in the area, especially at night. I would recommend to show some external photos of the building on airbnb so people can make an informed choice.

Great place to stay, very clean and comfortable, enough room for 7 people. The kitchen is well equipped and the bathrooms were clean. The check-in was a little bit difficult as the entrance is between some stores, but Carupano quickly help us with instructions. The neighborhood might look a little bit dangerous at 1st sight but is pretty calm, something good was that it’s near to restaurants, pharmacies and groceries. A big advantage that it’s near to 2 subway stations (5min walk) that takes to Manhattan. Carupano was a great host, very nice and good communication.

it is a room in a shared accommodation with two other people and not a studio.  the next room leave the television on all night and play loud music.  the 1st day the heating was too low, the 2nd day the heating did not work but the husband in Basma brought us a portable heater.  there was a cockroach in the room. the neighborhood is dangerous. we were verbally harassed near the metro.  it's far from the city center.  the roommates speak out loud.

Honestly this place was fine easy check in the only thing was there was no heater for you to turn on so u had to keep yourself warm and your would occasionally hear someone talking outside your door and the neighborhood a little shady but I guess that’s Brooklyn in general anyway it’s was a great stay for the price and I would definitely book again.

Following a flight cancellation we had to find emergency accommodation. Our path took us to Brooklyn to David's and we don't regret it. Serious, available and top accommodation. You can go there with your eyes closed. I recommend.

It’s rare to never that I say I wouldn’t stay at an Airbnb again. The place itself was fine for us, convenient enough location in Bed Stuy, close to A and C train and longer walk to G train, there’s a noticeable smell from people smoking cigarettes and weed in the apartment. The pull out couch was broken and there  weren’t enough sheets and towels for all of us even though the host was informed of how many people would be staying. None of this was a big deal though, the bigger issue was communication with the host was just much more stressful than it needed to be. He kept trying to get more money out of us for things, after we’d already paid, which i haven’t experienced at an Airbnb before, and there are extra charges for every little thing, inflexible check in and out, wanted more money, I thought he might charge us $20 to take a shower if he could.

Mischa was very helpful, with great communication. She made our stay stress free by providing us with all of the information we needed about her place. The location was amazing, with beautiful views of the NYC skyline. And close to many great bars and restaurants. Would highly recommend.

A TOTAL DUMPSTER FIRE! A key was not available upon my arrival.   ***STAIRS STAIRS STAIRS*** The stairs to the apartment building are unsafe and difficult to navigate with overnight bags. The stairs are warped and rails non-existent.   ***DIRTY*** Common areas were unkempt and the bathroom was dirty!!   ***NO HOT WATER*** Upon a late check-in, I learn there is no hot water for showers. The host communicates that hot water should return to the apartment, but alas that was not the case. By early morning, I checked into a hotel.   ***BEWARE*** The photos on this listing are nice but the experience is quite the alternative!
The Airbnb was very clean and perfect for our ladies weekend. Rohit was very responsive when we needed extra linens. Very nice person. We had a wonderful stress free weekend.

Our stay was just great. Pascale was such a great host and person. The tiny house is like a little oasis to relax from the stressful city and is connected very well via bus and train. We could not have asked for more. It was just great.

Pros:  This apartment is exactly what’s listed. What you see is what you get. Nice spacious bedrooms, decent sized bathroom for 1. Kitchen and living shared area.   Cons: Just so you know before you book this apartment, it’s located in one of the worst/dangerous neighborhoods in Brooklyn. Especially in the summer. If you’re an out of towner, this is not where you want to be caught at walking around exploring the neighborhood lol.   The neighbors are terrible. Everyday I was there they had their door wide open cooking (burning) food and playing loud Spanish music. The floors are very noisy as well so walking around the apartment just makes you feel like everyone in the building can hear you. The beds are also uncomfortable and still have plastic on the mattress. Idk what was going on with the shades but you can’t lower/raise them. Not many toiletries also. One of the toilet rolls in the dispenser had a weird coffee colored stain on it.     That’s really it but if you asked me if I’d stay again, I would just based on the price and the fact that I’m familiar with neighborhood and now the situation on the walk in/stay.

This is a GREAT spot. It is a large, comfortable, yet quaint studio apartment. The host actually met us at check-in, giving us a tour of the apartment, and answering any questions.  The doorman was extremely helpful during our stay and the tenants of the building were warm and friendly.  It is conveniently located near the subway, large drug store, Whole Foods and good neighborhood restaurants. Try "The Palace" for breakfast.  If healthy food is a preference there are several eateries close by as well. There is actually a Bloomingdale's about three blocks away.  Its a mile from Central Park and about two miles from Times Square and the theatres.  We plan to return to NYC in May and hopefully rebook  Oded's Airbnb.

I’m so glad I found this listing! The property was immaculate and cleanliness 5 star! Andreas the host was fantastic, so great communicating everything felt easy and stress free! I’d highly recommend this property and will be looking to visit again.

I took a chance because it was a new listing, but the place looked just like the pictures! The apartment is in a safe residential neighborhood, a few blocks from the subway station. I personally really enjoyed the access to different streaming subscriptions. Thank you Jason for such an enjoyable stay! For the price, it was a steal.

Iustin’s place was exactly as advertised: clean, spacious and within walking distance to public transit (for straightforward trips into Manhattan via the subway)…with a private parking space on the driveway behind gates! That saved so much time and offered peace of mind since street parking looked a bit tough around the surrounding streets. Honestly, what more could you ask for, especially in NYC?   Iustin was extremely responsive even late at night, and answered all questions promptly and in a friendly manner. His flexibility with check-in and check-out was truly appreciated, and made our weekend trip stress-free. Thanks again Iustin - we hope to stay at your Airbnb again soon!

Our stay was ok in the end, although the apartment was way more run down than anticipated. The beds were comfortable, which was good. But all in all, it was surprising to hear it was recently renovated, because it seems like it could use another face lift. The couch was broken and the tub was dirty, not to mention it was totally freezing due to the a/c on full blast. And as much as the b/w artsy look was alluring, it ended up being a bit stressful. We did, however, appreciate Michael's prompt communication throughout our stay. We had just hoped it would be nicer.

These are some tradeoffs you need to consider before booking this place. This is a typical NYC apartment. It was small as expected but well designed to sleep 4 with 2 bedrooms.  You need to walk up two flights of stairs. The co-host was kind enough to meet and carry our bag up to the apartment. Jamie the host is A+ on communication; prompt and courteous. The location is fantastic. There is a Trader Joes within a minute, a Starbucks across the street and you can walk to transit station in about 7 minutes. The apartment was clean. You are not going to spend much time in the apartment anyway. Sleeping is pretty much the only thing and here is where things got real bad.  The building controls heating/cooling and you have no control on it. The apartment was super warm through the nights. We barely got any sleep all four nights. You can open the windows in one bedroom but that brings a new set of problems: Lot of street noise and one room gets super cold. The other bedroom has a wall on its side, so no use opening the window. There are also a lot of clanking noises going through the night every few minutes and that made sleep almost impossible.  Those familiar with such apartments might not see these as surprises, but if you are not too familiar with old NYC apartments, these surely come across as unpleasant surprises. Should have been disclosed in the listing in my view. There are some small issues like the shower knobs get super hot, almost untouchable and the oven knobs in the kitchen need fixing, but these weren't deal breakers; every apartment will have some small issues. For me, this was a bad experience, but if you are not so sensitive to temperature or noises and can sleep through,  this apartment has a lot going for it. The location is great and the hosts are good people.

A number of pro's and con's to this Airbnb space:-  PRO's Easy check-in Laundy Options Comfy bed Plenty of hot water Good shower pressure  CON's A lot of noise from neighbours / other apartments Communal areas / hallways in poor state of repair and cleanliness Gaps in shower tiles (not a problem for us but can imagine that will be a problem for the owner in the future) General upkeep of decor and apartment needs attention Apartment temperature is very very warm and cooling unit noisy so cannot leave on all the time / at night The photos of the apartment are somewhat skewed as the available space is much smaller The reception area can be busy with luggage and children.  Local Area NYC seems to be full of construction and this local area is the same. Scaffolding outside the building made it difficult to see initially. Also a lot of homelessness and people asking for money which is sad but constant. Finally and this is a personal issue is the constant smell of drug use in the whole city

the place was under construction. no one was living in the entire premise. and there were orders to vacate the building posted everywhere. the host didn't inform us about this. so no matter how good the location and the place was from inside, it was really unsafe!

Alwyn’s place is a steal for the price. It’s comfortable, homey, beautiful and she’s is so communicative and friendly!! We stayed for one night and the six of us had absolutely everything we could have ever needed. If I ever need to be back in that part of Brooklyn I wouldn’t hesitate to consider this apartment!

Alwyn is such a great host and I appreciate her compassion and support she gave me during this difficult time and situation. It was our second stay and very convenient and close to my extended family that resides there. I visited for a funeral and everything ( funeral home, church, repass reception) was under 10 minutes away which alleviated the stress of being on time to wherever we went. It worked out well considering that it was such short notice and sudden.

My family and I (there were four of us) had a great week-long stay in James & Shannon’s place. It’s a small unit but we expected that (it’s NY!) so we weren’t disappointed. The pictures accurately depict what you can expect. While it sleeps six, I think it’d be difficult to have six people in the main living/dining area at one time. That said, if you’re spending most of your time out and about, or if you’re a close bunch, it works just fine.   The location is about a five minute walk to the subway so it was easy to get around (15 mins to Midtown) There are also plenty of great places to eat directly in the neighborhood. We both walked the neighborhood and rode the subway multiple times and never felt unsafe.   If you’re planning to cook in the unit, just know that there are very basic cooking provisions (cookware/cooking utensils) and there was no seasoning, oil, etc. Most people don’t come to NY and cook - plus there’s limited storage space - so I understand this. I just thought this mention might be helpful to someone else so they know what they should plan to pick up. I did ask if it was possible to be provided a blender and the hosts had one shipped to the unit - which I really appreciated!   The hosts are great communicators and checked in on us more than once.   All and all, I would recommend the unit and would happily stay here again! 😊

✅Cons-  1) The town can be quite sketchy in the night for a solo female traveler. I was fine to walk around but there are many garbages outside and it is the outskirts of Brooklyn  2) The front yard seems like it needs some maintenance as it was full of leaves, trashes. I didn’t recognize the place at first 😅 as it was quite different from the photo   3) Bathroom can be more cleaner as it had some stains/spots and also there are many random flying insects which I assume happening out of plants?   ✅ Pros-  1) Jiyouns place is exactly like the photo. Spacious room with a living room full of plants and you feel Cozy inside.   2) Room is spacious and clean. There is a big table in both in my room and also living room which allowed me to work remotely and this was one of the most important part for me - finding a space in New York with a reasonable price and working/sleeping   3) House is full of plants and if you are plants lover this would be perfect

We had a great stay here. Perfect accommodation for exploring Manhattan. You can walk to the Staten Island Ferry and have a great way to start your day by driving past the Statue of Liberty.  Great communication, everything is fine 👌😊

The room is just as in the pictures, everything was just as we expected. Area is kind of sketchy at night but overall close to main tourist attractions of NYC. Main issue is that there were rats in the apartment, they made noises at night and ate from our food. If the host is able to take care of the rat problem, I would recommend this place for the price.
It was really clean and nice! the only thing was the neighborhood that was a little more sketchy for our liking but over all a GREAT appartement and we all loved it!

Clean, large, pleasant and well-equipped apartment. A small downside on the heating in the very noisy rooms and a very poorly soundproofed apartment with the exterior (railway). No danger felt in this area of ​​Harlem (traveling alone with the 2 girls). Very good choice and good value for money.
Great suite and communicative hostess - the only thing that’d drag my opinion of the place down is the sketchy neighborhood.

I needed a place to stay last minute in Brooklyn, and this was a great value. The place was clean and the surrounding neighborhood was nice. Jovon did a nice job being communicative and the place was perfect for my needs.   The check-in says 4-6pm, but it was 5 pm for me b/c he was at work. It was a minor inconvenience for me and I suspect if I had booked earlier then he would have been able to plan better to be there closer to 4 pm. If you're looking for a place in Brooklyn with not too much fanfare, but well-kept, clean, and a helpful/accomodating host - I can't recommend enough.

Natalie's space is exactly like the photos, maybe even a little better (as it doesn't have a photo of the 3 bedrooms). Everything was great, the apartment is cute and being in NYC and feeling like a “local” was an incredible experience. The only point that disappointed me was that the television control was not there and as we stayed for 5 nights it was very unpleasant not being able to turn on the only TV in the room. I informed Natalie and she promptly responded, but unfortunately she was unable to resolve it. The little bar below the building is pleasant and inviting for a good glass of wine, there are many options of bars and restaurants around. And in fact you will be less than a 10-minute walk to Times Square. Access to the metro and buses is also very easy and is close to the apartment. The kitchen utensils are well equipped and we were able to use everything easily (there were just no bowls). Other than that, I would describe the apartment as a perfect experience, thank you Natalie.

Kadisha’s place was located within a 14 story public housing unit.  Constant NYPD and ambulance sirens.    Unsafe child cooking practices, animal(s) not taken out frequent enough to potty, so they went to potty inside on the floor.   Someone entered the home and taken items late at night.     Too much  to list.  Would not recommend this listing.  Airbnb refunded my money and helped me find another home and location.

This was a comfortable stay. It actually looked even better in person. The host was very responsive and helpful as well as leaving some snacks and beverages in the fridge. The only setback was the bathroom, it wasn’t very spacious but it was still nice and comfortable as well. The building was a little creepy but the people were nice and helpful. Overall it was a nice place to return to and I definitely would book again for my next trip.

The Gramercy was great! Great location; only about a mile to Time Square, mile and a half to Central Park, less than a mile to Empire State, etc. I never felt unsafe while staying here which was a huge worry of mine being in a huge city. Kristina and the host were extremely helpful, super quick with responses (even late at night), and offered up suggestions when needed. The only reason I put 4 stars is due to the sheets having a few stains, the duvet not having a cover, and the shower not having a curtain causing water to get everywhere when in use (there was a drain on the bathroom floor though, so it did dry fast). All in all, this was a great experience, a safe place, increíble location, all for a great price! Cant beat it!

It was not the room I rented, however, even though it was far away it was convenient because it is in front of the subway, the neighborhood seems dangerous but since it is in front of the subway I had no problems

Where do I begin? Akio was such a great host. Super quick responses! Any questions I had were answered within minutes. Check-in was really smooth and stress free. The apartment itself was very, very spacious- especially for a Brooklyn apartment! Two large bedrooms and very clean. 4 guests were able to fit comfortably. The location is also ideal being right at Flatbush Junction near trains and so many options for food. This one was a steal and I would happily stay here again. Thanks Akio!

BE VERY CAREFUL BOOKING THIS PLACE: Tish refused to refund me after my flight from Miami was cancelled because of the hurricane . Then after getting another ticket because I decided I wasn’t going to just lose my $500 for a place I wasn’t even staying. When I finally got to New York Tish refused to book us in claiming she had a check in time between 3- 5 pm. After calling customer care I was advised that Tish had edited the check in time so she could cancel our trip without a refund and nowhere to stay after I travelled from Florida.  I was refunded after customer care did an investigation and confirmed she did edit the check in time SHE IS A THIEF AND DISHONEST PERSON.
