Life in Brooklyn in definitely less expensive than in Manhattan. It is also less touristy place that allows you to feel like a true New Yorker. Actually there was nothing to complain about. I'm very happy to have chosen Olivier's Luminous Room.

Vik was very responsive and check in was a breeze. This apt is really nice, and cozy. Like a real home, not a rental. I live in the area and had to rent a space while undergoing construction, and I'm afraid I've been a bit spoiled by the terrace (now even more gorgeous than the pictures with beautiful plants!), washer/dryer, and amazing shower. We had a great time here and highly recommend this space.

We loved loved loved Mona's apartment! 3 Cs for her!  Cosy! Clean! Convenient! - metro's just right the corner which brings you to Times Square under 30mins!! There's a supermarket opposite as well!   Although we had an unpleasant experience with a yellow cab driver on the way to Mona's place, she made it up quickly with flowers and sweet little treats upon our arrival! It was a kind gesture! Mona was always in contact with us to make sure we are all ok in this big city. Couldn't be more thankful for her! Would love to stay at her apartment again if we ever get the chance. Thank you!

Mona's place is great for a trip to NYC! I stayed there with my mom for her birthday, and we found it cozy and clean, and VERY close to the subway (which was so helpful!)  This is neither a positive nor a negative, but potentially relevant! The apartment is quite small, and there were a number of scented products that left the place with a quite noticeable (but not unpleasant) scent. If you are scent sensitive, that would perhaps be useful to know! We found that opening a window and moving a few of the scented products to a closed room (which Mona was very understanding of) addressed it.  Mona herself was so lovely--really gracious and available, and very helpful when I had a bit of a boneheaded moment trying to open the door to the apartment. Would highly recommend staying here!

We (family of four – two teenage boys) had such a great holiday in NY and were very happy with Mike & Kelly’s apartment. It is located in East Williamsburg, so the area is not as super-hipster-cute as the streets around Bedford Ave. However, cute cafés and restaurants are only a few blocks away. More importantly (for us,) the subway is less that 5 minutes away and will take you into the heart of Manhattan in no time. The apartment is small, but cozy and well equipped. Comfy beds, good shower, good internet. Also, it was stocked-up with paper towels, toilet paper and high-quality soap, which I thought was a nice touch. Unfortunately, the weather was too cold for us to use the patio, but we enjoyed the light chains. As mentioned by other guests, the place is a bit worn, but it shouldn’t scare future guests off. Mike & Kelly’s place is great value for money and we will definitely recommend.

We were 4 of us in Kelly's apartment and we filled up very homely and well. The bedrooms are spacious with plenty of storage space and the bed were comfortable. The kitchen is well-equipped with coffee machine, tea maker, toaster, etc. The bathroom is small but sufficient, good shower and clean. Too bad that there is no heating in the bathroom and was partly very cold . The heating can also rob you of sleep when it heats up the water. The location was ok for us, quiet street, close to the subway and bus station. I can recommend the apartment to anyone who need some peace and quiet from the busy live in Manhattan and likes it simple and cosy.

Very pleasant apartment, very clean and perfectly consistent with the photos in the description. Rooms overlooking gardens (very quiet). We did not see Vineth but the communication by email was excellent and the handing over of instructions went very well. Surprising neighborhood, very mixed with a mix of streets with charming houses while other spaces are a little "ramshackle"... No feeling of insecurity, communication with Manhattan is very good thanks to lines A and C (allow 10 minutes max. walk from the station. Frequent subways) In the end, a very pleasant stay for our little family.

Ruby’s house is full of character—plants, books, and charming touches of an older house like stained glass and wood floors.  We had 2 adults and 6 teenagers and basically took over the house! She was a gracious hostess and made sure we had what we needed. We found a a great family owned Mexican food restaurant around the corner.   Don’t be afraid of the Bronx!  Great opportunity to get out of Manhattan.   I hope to return.
Rubí excellent service, very nice lady, the bad thing is the area and there are too many plants in the house and there are animals around the plants, the area is not pretty and it looks dangerous

The place was great, really clean , exactly as pictured. It's a short walk to Prospect Park and the subway station to Manhattan . Eleanor was really responsive and reached out to me to let me know I could cancel with out penalty when we had the hurricane scare.

Sugeiry was an excellent host! My friend and I stayed at her apartment for 5 nights and had a great time. She welcomed us when we got there, provided us with helpful maps to public transportation, and gave us excellent suggestions for dinner. She even did some grocery shopping for us so we had snacks, food for breakfast, and even a celebratory bottle of wine (she didn't even know it was my birthday)!  The apartment itself is absolutely adorable! It was very spacious, clean, cozy, extremely well decorated, and even stocked with travel size toiletries. Although she did not have cable tv, we were able to watch so many movies and shows with her apple tv, which was so incredibly cool! Although in Harlem, we did not feel unsafe at all. The security station was just down the street and she has a 24hr doorman with two security doors at the entrance. Her apartment is less than a 10 minuet walk to most train stations and the bus stops are even closer, which made getting around all of New York very easy! She was so respectful of our privacy the entire time we were there and frequently checked in on us to make sure everything was going well and that we were having fun.  We highly recommend staying at Sue's apartment for your visit!

David was a great host, responsive, and accommodating. The place was as described and the pictures are exact. The place was cleaned and bedrooms was roomier then it looks in the pictures. All the amenities were there for use and fresh big towels too. The bed was comfortable. The neighborhood was quiet with an occasional air traffic noise. Yes, the metro is close by about 10 minute depending on how fast you walk and we use the metro every day. We didn't have any problem walking the neighborhood at around 2am. The guide book was helpful to get to know the neighborhood and getting around. I would highly recommend this place. Thanks for making our vacation memorable and stress free.

In my group of travelers, safety, cleanliness, and accessibility to public transportation were the top important things to us. David's place definitely passed all 3 of these points with flying colors. There were multiple nights where we took the subway home passed 11:30pm and had no issues getting from the subway exit to our place. I never once felt unsafe at any time of day and this was incredibly important to me as we were a group of all women. We were welcomed into a very warm and clean home with everything we needed. I slept on the couch pullout bed and let me tell you, this was THE most comfortable couch pullout bed I have ever slept on! I was pleasantly surprised. We're from Southern California so we were wondering how it would be walking to subway entrances or bus stops from the home and that was a breeze as well! Depending on where you were headed, bus stops and subways entrances were all under a 10 min walk, some 5 minutes. David also very kindly accommodated our request for a late checkout as our flight wasn't until later afternoon and we wanted to do one last trip out to Manhattan before our flight. Overall, we are very happy with our stay at David's and would highly recommend to any traveler :)

David is very welcoming and even though he was not there when we arrived, all his instructions were very clear and precise so that we arrived smoothly. We had a wonderful 3 weeks in this apartment which was excellently located and close to our family who we wanted to see and who also lives in Queens. There are all kinds of advantages to living at David's: the nearby laundromat offers to wash your laundry for cheap and they are charming ($15 for two large bags of laundry, to be collected at any time, 24/7!), the variety of cuisines and restaurants in the area: the Mexican restaurant La Flor (also charming and yum!), a small organic café at Lucid Cafe, the delicious pizzas from Gino's Pizza, close to the 61st station (I left a leaflet, I think), delivered to your home free of charge for orders over $10, groceries at the Asian supermarket (but not just Asian food) on Roosevelt avenue at the end of 57th street and another one further up towards the 52nd metro station, very well stocked (reasonable prices for these places and some organic products!), an organic store further down, at the corner of 61st (more expensive); not far from the Italian, a Japanese restaurant... We found that we were missing a pair of scissors, something to peel cucumbers and presto, David immediately provided us with what we needed. It might be good to update the binder with advice about the neighborhood. Everything is there but we get a little lost because the documents, which are widely consulted, are dated and the information has sometimes aged! But these are details and I highly recommend David, his house and his neighborhood really close to Manhattan and Central Park with amazing subway connections. Note that at the station near David's (61st/Woodside) there is also the express: from there, it takes you very quickly to the 42nd/Grand Central Station. In just half an hour, door to door and without stress, we were close to all the major museums and sites (from the "Museum Mile" on 5th Avenue). In addition, we are very close to two amazing museums in Queens: The Museum of the Moving Image (cinema and its history - very popular with children) and The MoMa PS1 (ultra-contemporary art). I recommend in passing the "diner" at the foot of Court Square station, where you get off to go to this extension of the MoMa (a real "diner" dating from 1947: the period decoration has been preserved - very pretty and very good)... Our daughters (15 and 17) really enjoyed living there - even if they had to share the room; one of them, who opted for the sofa as a single bed (so as not to sleep two people in the double bed), found it very comfortable. We were also able to have a friend come to visit us from Philadelphia and she slept very well on the sofa bed in the living room with her daughter. Thanks to David for allowing us to invite him. We unfortunately broke a glass and lost one of the duplicate keys the very morning of departure (soooo sorry... still looking for them and I'll send them to you as soon as I find them) but David was very understanding and told us not to worry about it. SO: DON'T HESITATE and go and stay in Queens at David's.  Well, We hope to come back to your place...-

Great space for a couple with or without a kid. However, bedroom faces west so can be quite bright if trying to put a baby to sleep before sun goes down (found this out the hard way!)  Location is great and close to the F and A/C trains. Easy walk to Brooklyn bridge park. However is also 2 blocks from housing project towers (in the other direction) that can feel a little unsafe in the evening.   Sharam was a great host and was very responsive to questions etc before arrival.

Reliable and relatively convenient; very close to the places you probably want to hang out in and nice neighborhood charm. A haul to the A and C trains, but close to the G.   Heads up to parents looking for a place with two bedrooms: they do not allow children under 10 and made an exception for me, but it was a stressful realizing that just a few days before our stay!

We spent five nights in Tameisha studio and it was great stay : exactly as the announce, the studio is new, clean and cosy. It's a really small place but confortable. Don't be afraid to walk for the subway, but good neighborhood. And lovely person! Thank you so much.

Todd's place was everything I needed for the two weeks I was in NYC.  He was incredibly kind and generous -- he offered me espresso when I landed from my red-eye and was an overall great guy to get to know during my stay.  The place was so lovely!!  It was clean and bright, had great AC (thank god!), warm and inviting style, with a super comfy bed and spacious area to relax in.  The garden terrace is incredible!  I always felt safe and respected, an important quality for me as a woman traveling alone.  The guide he created for keys, access and other basic apartment info was through and really easy to navigate, which made arrival and departure so simple and stress free.  It is so close to some of the best restaurants in williamsburg, mccarren park, and just a couple blocks from the subway, making the location excellent for anyone traveling for work or fun.  Highest recommendations!

This spot was perfect for me traveling alone.  I just needed a "home base" while traveling, and Tameisha's studio was just what I needed.  It was about a 10 min walk to the J or the L trains, and from there I could use the subway system to get anywhere I wanted to go.  There are grocery stores, coffee shops, and bars within walking distance too.  The neighborhood is quiet for NY standards. There was a bit of confusion in check in and check out, but nothing stressful.  I would definitely stay here again.

The apartment is quite good, clean and with everything you need for a long stay. The beds are quite soft and uncomfortable.  The bad thing, the location. At night it is a somewhat dangerous neighborhood and you don't feel very safe on its streets.

This was the best place ever. Julia and her husband were warm charming, very flexible and nice.  Let me not forget there prince of a son(7 months) who let us know all the house rules. Very sweet baby. The place was very very clean with a secured entrance.  Now the surroundings have so many hidden treasures from the upscale restaurants/bars to the ability to get around with ease due to the bus(2 min. walk), trains(2 min. walk), ubers and cabs.  Transportation was never a problem even getting to and from LaGuardia Airport (M60).  The area is buzzing with so much energy. We where surrounded by the heart of Harlem which is very diverse and what New York is all about.  Central Park(116th or was it 110th no matter is a very nice walk down Lenox) is also close for those of you that want to exercise...trust me you will eat ....so do your body good and get it in.  We came in at 2 am and had no problems in this area. In fact we never felt unsafe.  Our Host knew a great deal about fun things to do around Harlem and beyond.  This place is perfect for couples wanting a quiet yet fun time.  It was a just right fit for two people.  Forget staying in midtown downtown or the village...Harlem by far is a  diamond... where people should stay. Harlem has change and leads NYC in diverse, land marks and great food at a price that will not kill your wallet. (Brooklyn to me is 2nd) Riverside Park( best place to start this ride/run or walk is at 145th street and riverside ...its on the West side of things) which is a great bike ride/walk... it runs along the Hudson which has the best scenery(is that spelled right) by far and get this there is a bar there to. From brunch on Saturday/Sunday ...to pizza for lunch(Custom Fuel Pizza the best...a must try 123 and 7th).  There are tons of great mom and pa's eateries that will have you wishing for more. And the bars...WHAT!!! who knew!. ...why pay crazy money when you can do it near your  Bright Garden ever so private apartment. Start High (Uptown) and you will not regret you trip to NYC. Julia your the best. Finding Pearls is what NYC is all about and staying at the place is high on my list of them.  I cant wait to use this home away from home again.  Thanks for everything Julia, Husband and son(he is the real boss).

Me and my friends were in town to visit NYC and booked this place for the same night. She responded quickly without being on the instant filter list.   There was free parking on the street which was nice. The accommodation was nice and she had extra blankets and pillows in case anyone required it. Overall it was a steal deal with cheap accommodation and free parking.

Orhun's place was perfect; the location is great and the flat is really spacious, tidy, and with a brilliant view! I never felt unsafe walking around the neighbourhood at any hour of the day or night, and there is a huge choice of shops and restaurants in the area.  His housemates made me feel really welcome and always had time to help me with anything I needed or just to chat, I felt settled straight away. They were also super friendly and could always recommend a new place to go or a favourite restaurant. It is a sixth floor walkup, but you really do get used to it and it's a nice workout... I would recommend Orhun's place to anyone, I had a great time!

This place is close to JFK. That is the advantage. The place looks a little scary as lots of people on the road and playing music late into the night. The room is cleaned well with all amenities. Closer to restaurants etc. There is no air conditioner but you have an air cooler. The basement would have been a storage place earlier. Good for a short stay - a day or two. The host is very good in communicating. Responded to all messages quickly. Had a pack of water bottles and snacks.

The apartment was clean and nicely decorated. We didn't use the 2 bikes because we took the subway, which was a good 5-minute walk away. All the usual sights from Cental Park downwards are easily accessible by metro. We found the location to be very good for exploring Manhattan for the price.  We always felt safe and had nice conversations with the residents. So don't be afraid of Harlem.

This apartment is wonderful! Extremely comfortable bed and well-equipped kitchen/bathroom. Even though it's a basement apartment, there's lots of natural light, and it on a surprisingly quiet street.   I stayed here because I was interviewing at Columbia University, and I found this to be a perfect spot for someone who wanted a quiet place to de-stress that was also centrally located.

My son and I stayed at Julia place for 4 nights. Julia responded to my questions very quickly. The apartment was nicely appointed, clean and quite comfortable. The bed was super comfy. The bathroom was roomy and equipped with a washer & dryer which was a huge bonus, especially in NYC. There were plenty of clean towels as well as shampoo and body wash. The roman shade on the one window kept the apt. dark which was nice for sleeping in. The AC could be adjusted and kept the apt. at a very comfortable temp. even though it was close to 90 outside. The street was quiet and about a 10 min walk to the 2/3 trains. Plenty of stores nearby including Starbucks on 125th St and Whole Foods.   Pizza at Babbalucci was absolutely delicious.  Make sure to give It a try you won’t regret it.   Heavy rain one night resulted in the area by the entrance gate to have muddy puddles. Maybe some planks would be nice to keep shoes clean and dry.   Thank you Julia for a wonderful stay.

This building is undergoing renovations and the security door is not in place. Front door has been attempted to be broken in and only a suspect deadbolt protects you. Door is almost in pieces. Area is not the best and lack of security is unacceptable.

the place itself is so lovely - comfy bed, very clean, fully functional kitchen. however, if you’re a lone female traveler, know that, even though the apartment is safe (gate, locked door), the surrounding neighborhood is a bit scary at night. just keep your wits about you!! had a great stay :)!

Great property. Very clean. Great host. A little scary location in not to great area of the town. Good deal for someone like us on a budget. Numerous covered parking lots. 5 mins to closest train station. Overall great experience.

Julia’s place is great. The location is perfect and it’s a cute little studio. There was everything you need in the kitchen and check in/out was seamless. I booked Julia’s place the day of after my other Airbnb ghosted me at check in. Julia was extremely responsive and really turned around a very very stressful situation. Definitely recommend!!

This Airbnb is located on a beautiful street. The neighborhood is a little sketchy, but we never felt unsafe. It’s close to the subway, which took us quickly to many locations we wanted to visit. Overall, we loved Julia’s place and had a nice stay.  The only downside we experienced was loud neighbors over us. They were fighting the first night (after midnight), and then we heard them walking back and forth at all hours. Luckily, it never kept us from sleeping.

+ Wifi quality was great! + An apartment was well equipped with all necessary items such as trash bags, toilette paper, shampoo, detergents even pads (although knives were missing) + There were both washing machine and dryer, detergent included! + Really good comms with the rest of the city, subway is really close  - Think twice before choosing Harlem as your base. Once we came upon a shooting scene around 5 minutes after it happened (on 125st). Nothing bad happened to us though during the stay and we didn't directly experience anything bad, you just need to be cautious of uour surroundings. - Keep in mind the trashbins are just outside the window and homeless people keep coming to these bins looking for cans. It is quite uncomfortable when you are for example chilling on the bed and have a stranger 1 meter away behind your window. - The apartment is a little bit below ground level with only one window so there’s almost no light coming inside. Little even for NY standards. - There is no ventilation so cooking is a real struggle. Once you fry something the whole studio smells like this (including your clothes).

kathisha was very welcoming. the place felt comfy; plus pets allowed in bldg, balcony, laundry in building,  and parking in lot assigned which you can view from the balcony.  the area in general is nice; close to many shopping stores and accessible to transit. Had no issues feeling unsafe traveling solo.  the place overall look just like pics and fits the description provided.

After 39 hours of traveling from South East Asia back to the states my husband and I were just so eager to get to hot shower and settle in.  Check in was fairly easy. Although there was no welcome from Kishorie, she sent us the check in information quickly.  We came in about 11 pm and washed one outfit a piece so that we'd have clean clothes to change into, took showers and left to meet up with some friends for the night. We returned to Kishorie's place about 6:45 am and went straight to sleep.  There's a door to the left immediately when you walk in and around 10:30 am we heard a knock at the door to the left which leads to the inside of Kishorie's main home as this is a basement. We looked at other confused and Kishorie called my name so I went to answer the door.  Before I can even reach the door to open it Kishorie had unlocked and opened it from the other side and accused us of doing laundry since 7am. She was extremely confrontational and rude when speaking to us which is disgusting behavior. There was no way we were doing laundry since 7, we were fast asleep! The fact that she was able to open the door just stripped us of the feeling of privacy.  We felt as though we needed to lock our luggage as there was no safe available and after her confrontation we weren't sure if she'd walk in and inspect our things while we were gone. The neighborhood is a bit sketchy, we did not feel safe walking around at night so we took lyft to and from our destinations. To address the space it was fine for what we needed.  There were slight stains on the towels and it's a very tiny space so if you're 5'9 or taller this might be a little tight for you.  We never even recieved a thank you from her in the slightest bit.  I would not recommend this to any of my friends or family nor would I consider this rental again.  Kishorie can really benefit from some hospitality lessons.

We were made to feel very welcome with a gift of fruit and water upon arrival. Our hosts were very responsive when we encountered a problem with the shower curtain, resolving the issue the same day we reported it. The photos accurately reflect the apartment. The neighborhood is a little "rough" but we never felt unsafe. The mattresses were quite worn and not very comfortable. The apartment is rather dark but it is very clean and practical - nothing luxurious but everything works. The corner grocery store is very helpful as it has many products which are organic and gluten-free, which we needed. The subway is convenient, about 10 minutes away by walking. Our rating of 4 stars represents a "3" for the apartment itself and a "5" for the customer service.

The house is exactly as described in the advertisement, clean and in perfect condition.  Additionally, it is equipped with everything you need to have a good stay, including generous amounts of things like soap, dish detergent, shampoo, trash bags, and others.  It is close to the subway station, and it takes just a few minutes to get to Manhattan.  The neighborhood is not very nice, but I didn't find it unsafe.  Nice detail with fruits and bottles of water when you arrive.  Near the house there is a “deli” and organic super market with very good quality products, and another large super market with everything you need.

The accommodation conforms to the photos. The neighborhood is lively and picturesque and very safe. 10 minutes from the subway and 20 minutes from lower Manhattan. Very well equipped accommodation (the kitchen with a mini market around the corner). We did not have the pleasure of meeting Owen but contact is very easy (is very responsive to emails and responds to requests). He kindly allowed us to leave our luggage because our flight was only 10 p.m. Small downside: the apartment is at street level and therefore moderately bright in the living room and the small bedroom. The second bright bedroom with an XXL bed!) That said, we are there mainly to sleep. Little advice when you return later at night you have to take line A (which takes over from line C) and stops at the Franklin stop.  We recommend this address to our friends

What a great host! Clean,tidy apartment and very comfortable. Andy was very helpful for my time at the apartment,made me feel welcome and at home. He is quite conversant with the area and was great help at suggestions of how to get by,things to do and in general very helpful! I'd definitely recommend this property for anyone,young or old,whether on business or holiday. The property is right in the heart of the financial district,yet cozy and quiet. I had my own living area and spacious room. For New York apartments this is definitely a steal in that regard! In general I had a great experience,hope you get to enjoy this gem. Will definitely be back!

The apartment was simply perfect compared to our expectations. Large, clean, on a quiet street to rest after a busy day in Manhattan while being 20 minutes by subway, and our host Owen answered us very quickly to every question we had. He even allowed us to leave our suitcases on the day of our departure to enjoy a last day of visiting even though our flight was only in the evening. The quality of this accommodation contributed perfectly to the wonder of our stay. Thanks Owen.

The place was exactly what was expected from the photos and description. The subway station is really close by and had a lot of breakfast places and cafes nearby for that little bite before heading to the city. Everything was perfect!! The host was also super helpful and responded very quickly!   PS: Don't be alarmed by the small bathroom!! That is normal size for places in New York City, you did not get scammed!!

Hearing the location 'Harlem' might awake the image 'unsafe'. It might be so some decades ago.  The circumstances seem to me that for the middle class. BMW and Jagua on the roadside.  The location is just north ending from the Central Park of New York. 30-40 minutes to/from downtown by two subway lines and buses.  Very clean, comfortable and quiet rooms. Erin and Erol are friendly.  I shall stay here on next visit to this city.

Loved my stay. The apartment is very cute and I found it was peaceful to come back home to it over the course of a month. Safe, snug, cozy feeling inside. The pictures show it well, but the place is roomier than what I was able to work out from the photos. The bathroom is full bath. The bed is really comfortable, the bedding good quality. The kitchen has this great floor to ceiling window that you can kind of stand inside of to have a morning coffee and watch the neighborhood. It's also stocked with what you'll need to cook and dine. The brownstone building itself is a corner building, older and slightly creaky, well lit inside and well managed. It snowed a few times when I was there and the surrounding sidewalk was always prepped and shoveled.   It was very important to me to feel like I could rely on the host. The booking process was seamless with her and reaching her upon arrival was stress free. I was greeted by her and someone who took my luggage up the stairs. She's very nice!  As for the neighborhood, it's a definite yes. Too much to say about it but I'll just let you know that the Greene Ave Market is open 24 hrs most nights. It's two blocks straight down and you'll pass it if you're coming in from the subway.

Misleading (you only get the 2nd floor and a hot attic with ineffective air conditioner) Unkempt unclean unwelcoming unsafe (kitchen window frame falls out)  Overall, this is more like a hostel for undiscriminating youth who don't mind a slum-like poorly maintained "home" in an otherwise nice neighborhood.

If I had a choice to stay on Manhattan or Brooklyn I would choose Brooklyn all the way. This cosy apartment, as described in the ad, is nestled in Williamsburg and probably easier to get to and from Manhattan than staying in Manhattan itself. Close to great cafes and even an Aussie style cafe.. (If you're from Australia you'll understand how much we value barista  coffee!) One easy quick train ride to the centre of NY makes for a less stressful subway experience for the novice.  The bathroom was newly renovated however was a little tricky to negotiate due to the size as it is a combined toilet/shower but I'm sure an addition of a small shelf will help to have a place to rest clothes while drying off or changing.  Nicole was fantastic in providing info and communication was excellent. The provision of a map on the coffee table was also saviour.  This is a great apartment with a homely feel with plenty of wardrobe and drawer space.  hurry up and book as it is good value for $. Remember there is more to NY than Manhattan -Brooklyn is the best!

Definitely a super host, she always kept in touch to check if everything was ok during my stay. The room is simple and spacious to organize yourself.  The only negative thing was the neighborhood, I was a bit scared of walking around there by myself, specially at night. Besides that, was all good!

There`s  no much to say! except that everything was really much more than we expected to be! and we made the best choice ever!..me and my girlfriend had an incredible time at Marjorie`s House...Her Husband Paul it`s very kind and respectfull, he helped us a lot since the first day..we will be back to their house as soon as we can.. The House it`s really clean, cosy and nice...the neighborhood its really nice as well, and there`s no danger..it`s like two blocks from the subway so its very accesible..we´ll loved to stay there again!

If you go to new york its a good place to stay. She realy try to make you confortable. But the house is unsafe for babys. The bed is too high and there is 2 staircase to reach the location, so if you go with stroller is a litle bit dificult.

We stayed for a few days at Helen's house and it has pros and cons, therefore I will NOT recommend this place (later you will understand).  Positive: The place is clean, tidy and located in a very bohemian (but quiet) neighborhood close to the metro.  The water pressure is good as is the breakfast offered (very complete), a set of keys is provided to be able to enter at any time deemed convenient.   Negative: Little privacy: The room has a curtain as a door, and Helen is home all the time, plus the apartment only has one bathroom (which Helen also occupies) which is INSIDE the room.  Helen's Temperament: This point was the most complex for us, as it made us feel uncomfortable most of the time.  We had a problem with Helen on the first day that was our fault and we apologized for it (she lost the doctor an hour waiting for us), which caused her to bang on the doors and have a very unpleasant attitude that was exacerbated by the fact that she doesn't speak Spanish and we don't speak English, therefore we couldn't communicate fluently (we spoke via email).  Sometimes he is in a very good mood and is a charming person (when that happened he sent us some e-mails indicating that he was at our disposal for tourist information), but when he was in a bad mood he threw all the positives to the ground, since he knocked on the door, answered in the worst way and did not have a good disposition).  In Summary: The place is good, but the bad attitude of the host spoiled everything good. Personally, I constantly felt uncomfortable and because of the above I did not do some things such as occupying his kitchen to prepare some food. I think he didn't like us from the first conflict, constantly causing a bad disposition.  The most pleasant days were when she went out for 3 days for a family activity and we were alone in the apartment.   Rodrigo Ibanez

The best part about Helen's place is the location. You are around the corner from the subway and in a lively neighbourhood near Russ and Daughters, Katz, and other bars/nightlife. While her place is quite small, for lower Manhattan it is honesty a steal. She is extremely knowledgable and can give you tons of great suggestions for how to best use your time in New York. Parking on her street is also free if you're crazy enough to be driving to Manhattan.

A unique experience for visiting New York! An apartment located in Brooklyn, not too far from the subway (10-15 min walk) to visit the heart of New York. An incredible view indeed, an atypical small building. We have the impression of discovering the “real” life of New Yorkers a little better by moving away a little. Concerning our host (who does not actually live there) we will not have seen him. Very simple check in check out with keybox. We would have liked some touches like water or soft drinks in the fridge, a guest book. We had asked before booking if it was possible to keep our luggage (late return flight on the day of departure), we ultimately had to deal with a specialized service (city co pilot, excellent!)

We stayed at Marjorie's for 1 week, and we loved the room and the bathroom. The cleanliness was really impressive and we felt at home quickly.  The bed is very comfortable and the shower magnificent!   We haven't visited this area, but don't be fooled by appearances, we were never afraid even when returning late at night.

Contact with Marjorie prior to the trip was quick and informative.   On arrival we were welcomed by Paul and handed the 3 keys for entry to the building and the room, all of which seemed safe and secure. You have your own entrance.  The room was clean and well equipped with coffee, milk, water and biscuits provided along with a microwave, coffee maker and fridge.   The bathroom was fitted to a very high standard and included a hairdryer and electric socket.   The bed was extremely comfortable.   Although NYC has lots to do it may have been nice for a small television or radio or docking station to help unwind after a busy day.  That said the wifi is very good if you have an ipad or other device to watch things on. This is not a deal breaker. The room was superb.   The area had mixed reviews prior to our visit however local cafes,  restaurants and bakery made us feel welcome, good quality food and reasonable prices for NYC.   We travelled around the area on both the bus and subway, a couple of times arriving back quite late (11pm/12am). As two women travelling we never felt unsafe.    The area is still in the city and there is a bit of street noise but we had brought earplugs as one of the party is a light sleeper.   Although it is geographically a good bit from downtown it is very accessible via subway and the station is just around the corner.   All round very enjoyable stay, very warm and comfortable apartment. We hope to be back!   Thanks to Paul and Marjorie!

Devon and Eric are a lovely, warm, talented couple who made our stay more than just comfortable. The bed was great, the location convenient.  From the Upper West Side you can easily get to all parts of Manhattan by subway who his close by.  There are lots of places to eat in the neighborhood as well as a small grocery store on the corner, a drug store a block away, and lots of other shops along Columbus Avenue and W 72nd St.  Oh, and as an extra plus, Eric has an awesome coffee-cappuccino-expresso maker which he generously shared with is!  Thank you both for sharing your home with us.

The apartment had some good points and some not so good points.  First, the good stuff. Devon was nice and helpful when I needed her to be. The location of the apartment was perfect for my needs.  Its on the UWS and close to all public transport and Central Park. The room was large and I was able to keep many things there and still have space to walk around.  The not so good points include the fact that there are three flights of pretty steep stairs; one from the street to the main floor, one set down to the apartment main door and another down to the basement room Devon rents.  It was OK for me but it should be explained carefully.  Its difficult moving luggage in and out of there.  The basement room has no windows  or proper ventilation and gets very stuffy even in Spring weather.  The hosts should think about putting a fan to circulate the air a bit.  My biggest complaint about the stay was the fact that the room was pretty dirty.  The bed sheets were clean but the floors needed scrubbing.  The bathroom was full of someone else's bathroom trash when I moved in and the bathroom was littered with empty plastic bottles of hand soap and lotion, seriously empty bottles.  The bathroom rug was pretty filthy.  Devon doesn't seem to put much care or energy into being a airbnb host and one gets the feeling that on has  slipped into the role of a college roomate, with nasty stuff in the frig and no one who cares to keep the place even slightly cleaned or organized.  Its an OK way to live if you're not collecting a nice daily fee as a hostess.  I didn't see anyone there most of the time so it was difficult to ask for things like a bar of soap or toilet paper.  I just bought my own and it was fine.  I did not however feel like I wanted to clean the place up, even though I was seriously  tempted to do so.  The room could be a nice little rental space if there was just more care put into making it sanitary and a bit more pleasant for guests.  They just need to care more.  Their own upstairs space was equally unpleasant.  You just need to care more when you're collecting money from others for use of the space.

**Renter beware**  Positive: Host is great at communication check in and questions. She is always friendly and kind. The locate of the apt. is great. Right off the park and near transit.  Negative: The last morning of our stay we saw two cockroaches, that was extremely jarring. I was able to kill one.   When you walk into the apartment there is a notable smell of urine. The entire apartment smell like urine all the time. The pee pad at the top of the stairs can be an unpleasant sight and smell. There are also pee pads in the hosts bedrooms on the first floor. We tried using room freshener but it was not enough to clear the smell. I also noticed the pee pad does not get changed daily. We changed it because it was 2 days old with urine.   The toilet downstairs was broken when we arrived. She stated she would call the super. That evening when the toilet still wasn't fixed, I fixed it myself. I was looking to clean our bathroom, downstairs, and I was not able to locate any cleaning products in the apartment, not a single disinfecting wipe or toilet cleaner. We have also had to purchase hand soap for the bathroom.  The area rugs, both upstairs, downstairs and bathroom, are covered in dog hair. There is a ball of dog hair right next to the bed downstair, that cannot missed from a distance. There is no vacuum cleaner, I could locate, or I would have run it.  The host requests that we rate the apartment as "clean" in our review because other guests have been commenting on the cleanliness of the apt in their recent reviews. That made me uncomfortable. The apartment is not cluttered and things are in place, however I would not feel comfortable stating that it is clean.   I provided the same feedback to the host, prior to posting my review, and she did not respond.

Louise was godsend. I brought my family and my dog from VA only to find out the airbnb host that I booked with was a scammer and canceled my booking as soon as i arrived. Frantically, airbnb helped me find a place for us to stay and Louise's luckily available. I was so glad to see that she welcomed dogs! The apartment was a block away from the central park so it made walking my dog very convenient. Apartment was clean and spacious as indicated. Subway station was also very nearby for us to conveniently catch a ride  to the time square.   Thanks again Louise!

The location of the brownstone apartment is really unbeatable.  You are right next to the subway station and only a block from Central Park.  Great restaurants and bars are minutes by walking.  Louise is a very nice host and good to talk to.  The bed was comfy and room spacious.  We did not use the kitchen.    This was our first time staying in an Airbnb while the owner was home.  It was fine and presented no awkward moments LOL.   We did have to pretend to be out of town family/friends as there has been some controversy regarding Airbnb.  One night when we got home there was a nasty note in the hall about the police evicting sublet guest!  Nothing ever came of it but I am afraid it will only get worse.

All emotions detached, Helen was a great host. She introduced us to local tourist attractions, daytime, nighttime activities all while being considerate of our price range. However, as informative as she was, she was also very passive aggressive in the way she talked. On the first day, I made a mistake to leave my shoes in the hallway, and this was met with a lot of aggression rather than a simple reminder. To make matters worse, the water bottle (filled with water) which she had kindly offered to us, had heavy heavy lipstick smudged all over (my gf was not wearing any); it was not a stain. It was clearly unwashed or even rinsed slightly. It was not only disgusting (as we have already taken many sips before noticing), but also dangerous during the epidemic and we could have been infected with more than just COVID-19. She did try to make it up with coffee the next morning. But this is not a mistake she could have fixed with coffee, or money, or anything as it is our health on the line. Considering you have been a long-term host to an Airbnb, it is important that you clean the most basic amenities; you don’t have to sterilize, but at least rinse. On our end, we have caused some trouble for Helen by accidentally splattering some of my gf’s purple shampoo on her shower curtains. Of course, we are very apologetic for that. All in all, she can improve her attitude and her basic hygiene.
The place is great. Typical NYC living, right in the heart of the E Village. Super clean and Helen’s communication made everything simple and stress free!  Exactly as described in the ad.

We stayed at Marjorie's for 6 nights and had a great time in New York. Since we were initially overwhelmed by the various public transport systems that intertwine, we drove in the wrong direction. We communicated that our check was delayed and it wasn't a problem at all. The key was left with a piece of paper and we found everything we needed. The houses in the neighborhood offer every look: from completely renovated to completely run down, everything is there. The people on the street are very friendly and totally helpful. Whenever we stood on the side of the road with our city map, someone came and said: you look lost, May I help you? Even as darkness fell, we never felt unsafe in East Harlem.  All the best

Will definitely come again!  +single apartment with own shower +comfortable bed +nice bathroom +coffee machine, microwave, refrigerator +own entrance +everything you need is available -no TV - Good location for getting everywhere by bike, but a little dangerous after sunset and in the morning. Harlem.
The accommodation is great for an overnight stay with 2 people. Bright and super clean, with everything you need. We never felt unsafe in the area, a subway station is less than 5 minutes away.

We had a lovely experience. The place was very nice and comfortable. The entrance was secure. The apartment was quite a ways from the end of the subway and we had to figure out the bus schedule at the last minute. After a full day of traveling, it was more stressful than it needed to be because of her lack of communication.  After our arrival and settling in, she was more responsive and checked in on us often.  We had a great place to stay. The only thing I could recommend would be for Sandra to be more quick to respond and to give more information in advance about traveling and check in/check out.  I admit these things may be common knowledge that I was unaware of, however I did feel more nervous and stressed out than I feel I should have.

I’ve had a very disturbing experience staying at this place for one reason - the host got home on Saturday night( I’ve only stayed 2 nights there) after a party with his friends and we’re loud and drinking and he was cutting some boxes open and whatnot… I was scared and super uncomfortable- I didn’t know what to expect being me as a small girl and a few man in the apartment drinking. I’ve texted the host that I couldn’t sleep and he apologized and said “ we are leaving now” - now was in the next 45 min. I couldn’t sleep even after they were gone. Thanks God nothing bad happened, but as a hole I’ll be more selective with hosts now. Other than that he seemed like a good guy, but if you are hosting somebody, please be respectful, as you ask of renters .

Great private room and bathroom with a private entrance. We were very pleased with this find and would definitely recommend it.   The hosts were responsive and accommodating in letting us drop our bags off early and being flexible with check in time.   Location was close to a subway, which was handy, but we did feel it was a bit of a sketchy area at night so we chose to Uber when coming back late and had no problems at all!

It is a great accommodation considering quality-price. It is two blocks from the subway (6 min), has restaurants and food stores nearby. The neighborhood seems dangerous but there is a lot of police surveillance and although on several occasions I returned to sleep late at night I did not have any problems. Marjorie is very supportive at all times and allows luggage to be stored after checkout. Highly recommended

It was very nice for us to live with Marjorie. Here you get a different view of life outside of Manhattan. We never felt unsafe at any time. Great neighborhood, great restaurants. Very noisy and sometimes loud, you should be aware of this. But it didn't bother us too much, except when going to the toilet. They would book again. Thank you!

The apartment is perfect, it has everything you need, plus the service is incredible, they are very friendly and have details such as providing coffee, water, and clean face masks. The only disadvantage is its location, I went alone with my friend and getting to and leaving the area was horrible, it is a very ugly area for 2 women alone, it looks very dangerous and dirty, I do not recommend it if you go alone.

Marjorie and Paul are very nice host, prompt communication, they also agreed to keep our luggage past check-out time. Convenient location to Central Park and metro line. Very nice designer room, looked pretty new. Extremely clean. The room if fully equipped with fridge, microwave oven, coffee machine and A/C unit. Some defaults: unsafe neighborhood for a single woman; not a lot of traffic in the street, but the people are loud, and the room faces the street at mezzanine level. The fridge and the A/C are very loud. The mattress is not the most comfortable.

It’s the perfect place to get a taste of the “real” NYC vibe and if you want to get off the beaten track. Located in East Harlem (also known as Spanish Harlem or El Barrio) you will be able to immerse yourself in a multicultural atmosphere. Certainly, certain scenes can be scary or heartbreaking (drugs, homeless, etc.) but nothing that you can't see in Europe. Very well connected to access all the emblematic places (line 6 2 steps away). The north gate of Central Park is a 20-minute walk away.  The apartment is made up of a large bedroom with its bathroom (very large). There is a fridge and a coffee maker as well as a microwave. The bed is very comfortable. The only downside is the noise from the street (earplugs required) and the noisy air conditioning. As for us, we slept very, very well. For those coming to the USA for the first time, there are no blinds. Daylight is present from early morning.

George and Diana were welcoming, communicative, and very friendly. They were flexible with our check in and check out times. They ensured that we had every possible item we would need, even a beer and wine in the fridge! The apartment was charming, perfectly spaced, comfortable and roomy for two, but will easily accommodate three). It was clean, nicely decorated, with a vintage feel. It allowed me to really feel as though I lived in Queens for a week. The building seems small, and the neighbors that I met were friendly and welcoming. The first floor bedroom window faces the street, so there was a tiny bit of honking and foot traffic noise.  However, that is to be expected in NYC and the bed was so comfortable that restful sleep happened. It was warm when we went, but not too hot. The two air conditioners kept the place cool for us. The home is perfectly placed, a short walk to the subway and lots of food and drink nearby. It's a very safe and quiet neighborhood, we never felt intimidated or afraid. George and Diana were ready with helpful suggestions for the neighborhood and overall travel tips.  We found so much enjoyment in exploring, drinking coffee and eating delicious things, including baklava (Gulluoglu), shark (Bahari Estiatorio), bagels (Brooklyn Bagel), pastries (Leli's Bakery), and tons of espresso (Kinship Coffee)!  It took us about 15-20 minutes to get to the Central Park area, so the apartment isn't too far away from Manhattan. We opted to Uber from Penn station to the apartment and paid about 25 dollars.  All in all, we loved our time here, and would definitely stay again and again and again.

If you are looking for a place to stay in NYC, there isn't a better find. We moved as a young couple to New York City for grad school, and were nervous because we had never visited before. Rachel and Karlton's place exceeded any and all expectations we could have had.   The unit is located close to major transportation that makes it easy to get anywhere in the city and near the M60 bus that connects directly with the LaGuardia Airport. We were able to easily access lower Manhattan/Times Square, both the West and East Sides of Manhattan (due to the proximity to multiple subway lines), Columbia University, the Bronx, and essentially anywhere else we wanted to go. Being just minutes from so many public transportation options made getting around the city so fun and accessible, and made commuting for school/work a breeze!   In addition to the fantastic transportation, the unit is also near plenty of major stores, restaurants, activities, and historical sites. Not only can you pop into the local grocery store as soon as you turn the street corner, but there is a Whole Foods right down the street and plenty of local fruit/vegetable vendors. There are so many incredible restaurants close by, and plenty more that are just a short bus/subway ride away. Our personal favorites were Lenox Coffee (the best coffee around!) and UpTown Veg (a vegan soul food restaurant that is out of this world!). Despite being so close to the hustle and bustle, the unit is surprisingly quiet and serene.   The beautiful row of brownstones where the unit is located is absolutely gorgeous. The unit itself is pushed back off the street, providing both privacy and quiet. We always felt safe living here, as Rachel and Karlton have exceptional safety protocols. There are some stairs to get down to the unit, which are somewhat steep. We did not have any problem with this, but just something to note, although there is a railing along the wall for support. The private backyard is a wonderful retreat from the fast-pace of the city, and is the perfect place to enjoy a cup of coffee or do some work or reading. This is just one of the incredible amenities that makes this unit unique.   When it comes to the inside of the apartment, there isn't anything more you could ask for. The unit has amenities that you will not find anywhere else in the city, including a washer and dryer, dishwasher, full-sized fridge, full-sized oven, a full shower/bathtub and an amazing heating/cooling system. We looked at so many places that didn't even have one of these, let alone all of them! This made living so much easier and hassle-free.   Despite being a studio, this unit still feels spacious and comfortable. Rachel and Karlton have done a perfect job of decorating the unit to feel like home. Although the unit is completely open, it still feels as though there are different areas of the house. The living/dining area has the couch/table/tv, then there is a desk perfect for working, then the bedroom space, and finally the bathroom. This made the unit very livable and comfortable. Additionally, there is a small area where the piano used to be that Rachel and Karlton have outfitted with some cute chairs perfect for reading, however this also was a perfect space to lay out my yoga mat and do some yoga! Definitely an unexpected perk that I loved having!   Overall, everything in the house was as described. There was ample storage space in the kitchen and closet, and the dressers provided plenty of extra space without feeling overcrowded. There was plenty of space to cook, relax and work, and this was more than we could have asked for! Everything was clean and in great shape. We have absolutely loved living here and couldn't have imagined a more perfect place to be.   Last but certainly not least, Rachel and Karlton were superb hosts. They were welcoming when we arrived, offering suggestions and recommendations. Check-in was extremely easy and the least stressful part of our trip getting there. Whenever we needed something or had a question, they responded within the hour and were quick to help in any way they could. They are both darling people who are friendly and ready to help, but never overbearing and have great boundaries. They were both . wonderful hosts and we couldn't have asked for a better experience!   All we can say is that if you are looking for a New York stay, especially a long-term one, this is sure to be your best option. After 4 months in the unit, we were sad to be leaving and would recommend this to anyone looking for a great unit in New York City. This unit has everything you could possible need, and Rachel and Karlton are both lovely and responsive hosts. We are so grateful to have lived here and to experience Harlem - the time we spent here has been truly unforgettable in the best way!

We didn't meet Katherine, but she returned texts within minutes.  The room was nice, lots of light, and a clean homey feel to the apt.  Lots of hot water for the morning shower!  She left a note telling us about some good restaurants in the area.  Also said to check out the rooftop, which has a little table and chairs.  It was kind of cool to sit and have coffee in the morning.  We got in late after her roomie, who was soooo quiet in the morning, that she managed to leave without waking us.  Also really easy to get to from the 1 train.  No stress about checking in or out at all.  If you want a place that feels like your cousin's place, I'd stay at Katherine's.  The neighborhood is a delight - very friendly people.  We had an excellent breakfast twice at Lenny's.  Inexpensive and they have both inside and outside tables.  Folks stopped and said "hi," both times.  Only a 3 block walk to Central Park.  10 min walk to the Bellacort where they do free Shakespeare in the park.

The apartment was as-listed, amenity-wise, although a few less decorations than the pictures showed, but nothing bad!  I absolutely loved the neighborhood, and it never felt unsafe no matter when I walked back home. Lots of bus lines that you definitely should take advantage of.  Madison was a great host, and very responsive to any question we had!

We spent a week in New York at Alex's apartment and couldn't have asked for a better place. Excellent location in the UES, close to 2 different metro lines and only a 10min walk to Central park!  The apartment itself was very clean and looks just like the pictures. Other "nice to haves" for convenience include a laundry room on the floor at very reasonable rates as well as a T-Mobile just downstairs for overseas travellers needing a US sim card. There's also a guy in a food truck 1 block away who sells really decent bagels and coffee for $3 all in, which in New York is practically a steal...  Alex was a fantastic host, he's very easy going and was always available to help us with any questions we had. He would also check in from time to time just to make sure we were okay.  Would definitely stay here again and highly recommend it to anyone planning to visit NYC.

The Hamilton Guest room was just as advertised. The pics is 100% accurate and exactly what i needed for my 7 night stay. From the day i made the reservation up until the time i checked out Hugo the host was in contact with me giving very clear directions from JFK to the apartment and any other news relating to the guest room.  The apartment is simple but clean and has all the basics you will require. The wifi is excellent and there is also a TV in the room.  On arrival I was welcomed by Hugos mother and brother Corey. As a family they are a very welcoming and warm trio. They were all helpful and kind throughout my stay.   The area in general was very safe. I came and left at all hours of the day and not once did i feel unsafe or threatened in anyway. The apartment is a 5 min walk from the subway.  I would definitely recommend this apartment to any solo traveller.

The place was great. Clean and exactly as advertised. The host was very friendly, extremely helpful and laid-back. Overall I had a very good time and would probably stay there again.  Although I didn't have any bad experience, the neighborhood looks a bit sketchy at night.

Pervaiz was a very responsive host and always responds promptly to messages and inquiries. The apartment is exactly as pictured and is very nice. Central AC was on point! It was in the 90s the whole weekend we were there. The area is interesting because it's undergoing a lot of gentrification (like many parts of Brooklyn) and has a completely different feel during the day vs. the night but not dangerous in our experience. Great place to stay if you want to explore Brooklyn (we spent most of our weekend in Williamsburg) - though you're going to have to Uber/cab there and just minutes to the Kingston-Throop stop if you want to go into the city, though we ended up waiting a while for the trains.
The welcome was super friendly But very dangerous area!!! I was attacked in the street and I had to change location!!!

My stay at Hugo's place was way better than any hotel stay. First, this is a close-knit family who really care a lot about their guests' well-being, and they are truly generous warm-hearted people. Hugo is excellent at communicating over emails, and responsive to any needs you might have. The room itself had a very nice Caribbean feel to it, not your typical NYC place. Hugo's mom, Margarita, is usually there and she is a remarkable lady. She has very interesting stories to tell, and I spent hours chatting with her about the city, natural medicine and making soap! For anyone visiting NYC and interested beyond the touristy stuff, this is a great way of getting to know real New Yorkers and get a glimpse of their everyday lives. Especially this place would be great for experienced travelers who know New York well enough, quite a few major bus routes stop right next to the place, and the subway 1 train is a short walk. I also felt no problems returning here late at night, this is a very safe neighborhood, even if it seems a bit sketchy. If you've been to NYC a few times before and know the basics well enough, this place is a hidden gem so close to the busier parts of the city.

I have huge appreciation to the host Hugo and his wonderful mom！！！This is the best ever airbnb experience for me！  The price is great, location is very convenience, 5min to subway no.1, and still  a lot of restaurant down the street. The neighborhood is very safe, who says harlem is unsafe.   the room is in the basement, however, the host always put the AC on even when you are away.so the air is still OK. Room is pretty cozy, also has a TV, so you won't feel bored at all.  The most important thing is host is extremely kind, Hugo's mom is a fantastic person, helped me with a lot problems！  In a word, This experience is extremely awesome！  If I'll come back to NYC, it's no doubt, This place will be My first choice. I just feel like home here！

This place was great! Our host was away on a trip, however we were still greeted by someone familiar with the place, who was welcoming and there if we needed anything. The actual space was more than I was expecting! It was great to have our own apartment that we felt we could truly relax in. Parking on the street was easy to find, and we left my car for a few days with no issues. The neighborhood is a mix of residential and commercial space, with a very easy walk to the subway. I never felt unsafe.

We loved it here! Our family spent six days in Julias apartment. It was located a few blocks from the 5/6 and 2/3 subway stop. We used the latter stop most frequent, taking us downtown in about 15 min. Did not feel unsafe in this neighbourhood and it was fairly quiet with the bedrooms facing the garden.   First of all, Julia served us homemade MUFFINS the first morning. Service you will never get in any hotel! Fresh flowers and clean apartment. Hair dryer, clothing iron, shampoo, conditioner, shower gel, body scrub at your use. Julia was always available for questions.  She also let us leave our luggage in the apartment after check out since our plane left in the evening- very nice!   Will gladly recommend this place to anyone! We would happily visit Julia again next time we visit beautiful New York.

We spent a week in Julia's apartment, 3 adults and 2 kids. The apartment is very comfortable and clean. For the fifth guest twin and double aerobeds were available. Julia was providing all necesary information in due time prior to the arrival and check out. From and to JFK we used public transportation (AirTrain to Jamaica station and E train and 2-3 express red trains via Time square to 125th street, 2hrs transfer time). The apartment is about 5-7 min in walking distance from the metro station. (There is also the green train in short distance but I do not suggest to use it only if needed due to unpleasant atmosphere next to that particular station. On the contrary, this green line connects you very easily with the museum mile.)   We felt absolutely secure around the location of the apartment. Supermarket called Pioneer is is 8-10 min walking distance. There are very nice restaurants close by, red rooster and sylvia's, streetbird a bit further. If you go to west you will see even more very nice streets with young people, shops, restaurants.  Julia and her husband were accessible in case of questions and requests of help. Wifi and cable tv channels were available. Both sleeping rooms were equipped with AC. The only thing that needs to be refreshed is the bath tub.   In sum, we were very happy in the apartment, we liked this part of the city very much, the arrangments were very well prepared by the hosts for us. I would certainly recommend this apartment for families up to 5 people.   Julia, thanks for making our stay very comfortable in your apartment!

Keys where left in box so no need to see host but available by phone if needed. Apartment was warm and clean, beds comfy. When bathroom is renovated soon will be great but this didn't affect stay. Location is good, not far to subway stations and never felt unsafe.

This large, very quiet, clean and well-equipped apartment in Harlem is located 8 minutes from the subway and 5 minutes from restaurants such as "Red Rooster" and "Sylvia's". It takes 35 minutes by subway to go to the southern tip of Manhattan (at One World Trade Center). Certainly the metro at the end of the day can seem a little too much, but what a satisfaction to find yourself in peace after the hustle and bustle of the day (people, sounds of horns, fire and police sirens).  We feel at home in this large cozy nest and what's more Julia is an adorable interlocutor, very responsive and ready to be of service.  We had a flight at 9 p.m. and Julia very kindly allowed us to leave our suitcases which allowed us to enjoy another good day visiting New York. I highly recommend this rental.

I stayed at Hugo's with a friend of mine we booked both rooms in the apartment. The first thing I need to say is his mother is an absolutely beautiful soul, she is very kind and extremely hospitable. We did not get a chance to get to know Hugo, but he was very cooperative.  However, there was no mention of the apartmen being under the ground, which was kind of surprising to us especially since odors very easily accumulated.  Also, my friend and I did not normally get up early but there were always people in the house from the early morning and it was very difficult for us to sleep in due to the noise. Privacy was not always there due to the construction of the bathroom, if I woke up late I had to greet people in my jammies. And the fact that the bathroom was going to be under construction during our stay should've been stated to us because it was not always convenient.  However, I do need to stress that we did enjoy our stay relatively due to hugo's mother margarita and his friend manny who gave us a pamphlet of all the places to visit in Harlem. They also made us coffee and told us where to go out to eat and such.  Thank you Hugo!

We had 3 wonderful days in N.Y . The place was ok because the price was cheap but there were a few things that were unpleasant . Two of the beds were very hard , a bit of music at night but not too loud and the distance from New York can be considered far . (45’ at least from Times Square ) and the neighborhood is ok but not really beautiful .  But as I said it was cheap for N.Y so we’ll say that overall it was ok.

This is definitely a great location if you are traveling here for the Kings Theater, which is why we came. It is right down the road. A couple notes for travelers coming to this airbnb: 1) The shower is tiny, I am 5’10 and I had to squat for the water to hit my head so definitely not ideal for tall people. 2) The stairs and beds are extremely loud and squeaky. 3) If you are uncomfortable with people staying in the same house as you, DO NOT stay here. This is on the 3rd floor of their house. Alex was great at communicating with anything we needed. The location seemed fine and safe, however it is Brooklyn New York so there were homeless people in a lot of areas. Overall it was worth it for us for the value and cheap prices, as well as the location to Kings Theater.

My family of three stayed here in late July 2018. I don't think we could have done much  much better in Bed-Stuy than this lovely two-bedroom walk-up. Located on a quiet, shady neighborhood street opposite a school, families/groups of up to four should find this a clean, bright, relaxing apartment. Beds are cozy and comfortable. TVs in living room and both bedrooms. WiFi is available, too. Kitchen is a bit small (this is NYC) but it features a large refrigerator and four-burner gas stove and oven. This is not your parents' Bed-Stuy. The area is undergoing huge changes. You'll see hipsters on bikes going by old school barber shops. On one intersection you'll dodge a BMW, at the next you'll find a block party. There's a great selection of economical restaurants. Along with residents you'll encounter other AirBnB-ers from all over the world. The apartment is about an 8-block walk from the Kingston-Throop subway stop at Fulton Street. It is about a 10-15 minute subway ride to downtown Manhattan. A little longer for mid-town. Uber fare can be $25-$40 from Manhattan, depending on time of day and where you're coming from. From LaGuardia Airport on Saturday afternoon, Uber was $40. We did not take taxis. There's a small grocery store around the corner, as well as a few corner markets between Monroe Street and Fulton Street.  There's also a large grocery store on Fulton Street, if you really want to stock up.  Staying here brought back a lot of memories of my childhood in Brooklyn. Linda's "Oasis" offers a great taste of New York few visitors see at a great value.

Nice neighborhood, 15 minutes from the metro. The accommodation is large and the bedding is good, but these are the only qualities of this accommodation. We had to live with at least one mouse, a very unpleasant smell in the kitchen and the hallway. There is no pressure in the shower and the water is difficult to control. Namely, the windows do not open.

The house was like the pictures. It was clean overall but make sure you check the sheets to ensure that they all have been washed. Mines were sprayed with febreeze and had strains of hair in the bed. The host was very nice when we first arrived Because she allowed me to leave my luggage because her unit wasn’t ready and I had asked to check in early. But when we returned she was very unpleasant especially when I asked her for the keys out the lockbox that she just put back n there as I walked up. But couldn’t open the lockbox because my phone had die and she was aware of that because I told her. She had other guest above us and they were very loud. Left the outside doors wide open.

'Bohemian chic' calls Jenny her Airbnb rent out. And, that it is exactly the right term. You got the all upper floor of an end-19-century townhouse for yourself with a very spacious bedroom in the front (smaller bedroom is attached) and a spacious living in the back with an open kitchen. In the middle, between bathroom and living, you will find the bathroom. So, in fact, it is a complete apartment for yourself on a thirty-minute subway ride from Manhattan.  A very light apartment in which you could easily live a complete Brooklyn life. The Bohemian part is the very authentic neighborhood, not being dominated by tourists nor yuppies and the fact that you will have a shower in a bathtub with a bath curtain (still good, warm, and clean) and that furniture is gathered together, which is in itself also its charm. So for this price, an you are not afraid of Bohemian life, a very good place. Apart from that is Jenny very nice, supportive and communicative, a thru host. Ter info voor Nederlanders, een buitengewoon gaaf appartement, waarbij je het gevoel hebt een volledig appartement in de Pijp te huren, maar net wat ruimer en lichter, en dan twintig/dertig jaar geleden toen de Pijp nog de volkse Pijp was.

Jenny is a very pleasant hostess, accessible if necessary. The apartment is very well located between 2 metro stations on line G and close to multiple bus stops. We were 30 to 40 minutes from Manhattan by subway and 10 minutes from Downtown Brooklyn by bus. the apartment is very bright and well equipped. All it needs is a microwave and that would be perfect. Please note that the small bedroom is only accessible through the large bedroom. Jenny is very accommodating with schedules, we were able to drop off our bags the day before we arrived as we were going to Washington and didn't want to be too busy and at the end of our stay we were able to stay in the apartment until 5pm as our flight was in the evening. We ultimately had a very pleasant stay (13 days in total).

Went with my boyfriend and we really enjoyed the home. It's a beautiful home. The only problem is we thought we had the place to ourselves and at one point when we were in the bedroom we heard someone in the hallway and then we heard someone spitting and gargling in the bathroom. I would've showered there but as soon as that happened I decided to just wait until I got home to shower because I was afraid someone besides my boyfriend would come to use it. Besides that it was fine.

I enjoyed the cleanliness of the house and the privacy. The location to LGA was ideal. I think that Asad is a great host. He was very communicative and helpful. It is a shared house where other guests can stay besides yourself. I did not appreciate other guests banging on doors and walls at 2:45am and cooking food at 3am. I know that he cannot control this, but this is why my rating is so low for the stay. If you are a light sleeper or startle easily like myself, I would recommend talking with the other guests or Asad to prevent late-night scares. I unfortunately did not have the opportunity to meet the other guests before I went to bed, so this was a huge issue for me. But I was looking for a convenient place near LGA, and Asad provided that for me.

My group booked both of Linda's apartments - Oasis and Oasis 2 - for 5 nights in Sep. We were very happy overall with both places, which are very similar in design and directly below each other. They're good value for money. Both have one full bedroom with a large queen bed and a smaller bedroom with a single bed. The kitchens are small but fully equipped - we cooked a few breakfasts here and it was easily managed with the pots and pans and utensils provided. Each unit has one bathroom, which is spacious and fully functional. The  apartments give one a good feel for the Bed-Stuy neighborhood in Brooklyn. Plenty of good bars, restaurants, and grocery stores near by, including one newish convenience store right on the corner. The Subway is a 10-13 min walk and we used that to get into and back from from Manhattan daily. Lots of people on the street during the day and evenings too, so it felt safe and we walked back from the Subway most nights between 7-9 pm without feeling unsafe (I'm from Oakland and wouldn't do this in my neighborhood there).  On the whole, I'd highly recommend both apartments and especially for anyone visiting NYC on a budget.

This is a good option if you’re planning to come a NYC with a low budget😂 It’s cheap and great to stay for the price.   There are some points that could be better. For example there are only 1 complete bathroom for 4 rooms so you need to wait your turn even if you just want to brush your teeth.   The location it’s ok, the house is near to a bus station (9 min walking) but it’s Queens so it’s a little scary at night.   I think it’s a good option if you want to stay for a couple of days.   Assad’s house has coffee and cereal free and you can cook in the kitchen. Thanks for that 🤩

Karen's apartment was a great place to stay for our New York visit. The apparent was just as described and very clean. There were a lot of house rules, and we were always a little afraid that we broke some of them, and the internet was more off than on, apart from that we enjoyed our stay very much.  We really liked the neighborhood, and with Karen's maps and suggestions to where we could go for groceries and food, it was no problem to find the good spots in a neighborhood that we probably would not have visited if we were not staying there. We felt really safe in the neighborhood.

Karen's apartment is cute and clean. The self check-in process was easy and convenient. Unfortunately I had two issues with the apartment.   The first and smaller issue was the AC. It is very small and can only comfortably cool the bedroom with the door closed when the temperature is not very hot outside. During my stay the temperature was over 90°F, so the AC was not strong enough to make the bedroom comfortably cool and the rest of the apartment was extremely hot.   The second and larger issue was the WiFi. The WiFi was broken for over 3 days. I wanted to cancel the rest of my 2-week reservation because the WiFi was still not fixed, but when I asked for a cancellation and refund, Karen refused because she was going to get an ethernet cable, which would not solve the problem for most of my electronics. I called AirBnB and they cancelled my reservation for me and issued a refund, but the whole situation was stressful and unfortunate.

I was worried getting there too late from the airport but the bus stop was close enough that I didn't feel dangerous walking after 10pm. I had to wait for the bus at the airport so I recommend to take a Lyft if you have $12 to spare. I stayed in room 4 which looks down the backyard. It got a lot of Sun coming in in the morning, I liked it.
Conforms to the description, an unpleasant smell of paint due to a renovation, but otherwise perfect!

The accommodation was clean and had everything one would need. We didn’t care for the neighbourhood and felt unsafe when venturing out. We were booked to stay 4 nights but ended up leaving after the first night. I was unable to sleep due to the air conditioner noise which also blew directly onto the bed (and in the heat of summer it was stifling without it). We also had a major issue with the fact that you could not flush toilet paper down the toilet. Karen said this was in her original listing, I still haven’t found where that is mentioned so perhaps this could be made clearer for future guests who may feel the same way we did about this.
