These issues were not something that could be resolved during our stay which is why we chose to leave. Karen was very understanding about this and promptly issued a refund for the nights we did not stay and also offered to help us find alternate accommodation. All in all, this wasn’t the place for us but I thank Karen for her hospitality and understanding.

Everything was clean and we were met at the door by the host's father who was very welcoming. Much smaller than the photos made it appear and in a sketchy neighborhood. Also the host did not mention anywhere in the listing that we couldn't flush toilet paper down the toilet, instead we had to put it in the trash, which was really unsanitary and disguising.

Angelo was extremely responsive when it came to answering any of my queries during my stay. The apartment is as described however I felt like the neighborhood was a little sketchy so I refrained from traversing Brooklyn during the evening. He is very accommodating with kitchen dishes and toiletries. The television came in handy too. Overall I had a great stay and would recommend this Airbnb to anyone that would like to stay in New York!

Loved the location of this airbnb, very walkable part of NY. The place was pretty clean, but one of the beds had some hair on it that wasn't mine, which makes me suspect that it wasn't washed well? Nevertheless, Greg and his family were very nice and helpful. Overall, a nice stay.

Donalda’s place was cute! It was very clean and a good fit for two people.  It was very quiet. The only thing I wish it had was curtains because it got very bright in the morning and since I am a light sleeper it would wake me up early.   It was about a five minute walk to the Nostrand station.   I liked that we could take the A train directly to the city.  The host always replied pretty quickly and I appreciated that they held our luggage on the last day since we had a late flight.   It was my first time in New York and Brooklyn so I admit I am not familiar with the area, but it felt a bit sketchy, particularly at night.  A few people we met during the trip said the Bed-Stuy area was recently gentrified. Some suggested we take Lyft/Uber instead of  the subway if it was late at night.

Let´s start off by saying that we enjoyed our stay and the hosts were very friendly. De room itself is very clean and the location is decent. We didn´t get the chance to speak to carlos in person, but he was very helpful when we spoke to him via online chat. Carlos´s wife helped us settle in. She was very friendly.   However, there are a few reasons why I can´t give five stars:  - In their driveway you will find a car fully stickerd with anti-biden and anti democratic stickers. This car belongs to the host. In my opinion, this is unacceptable. Since you want to be welcoming to everyone and not make people feel unsafe because of their political preference.  - The bathroom had it´s problems. The knob that you use to turn on the shower had mold growing inside of it and the shower curtain was hanging on a railing that had rust all over it. The bathroom itself was not always clean, even though we used it at various times during the day.  - During our stay and after our stay we were asked a lot of times to leave a 5 star review. They were quick to judge the people that didn´t leave a 5 star review. I also recieved multiple phone calls days on my dutch telephone number days after we arrived back at our home in the Netherlands. I don´t appriciate the pressure that was given to leave a 5 star review.  - The last point is the fact that even though the location is okay, it is not worthy of 5 stars. The neigbourhood isn´t trendy or particularly nice. The house is close to a metro station, but it´s still a long way to Manhatten or Brooklyn.  Ofcour we also have to take the price into consideration. This is why the rating is still high.

Mary’s apartment is the ideal Brooklyn apt: ideal location in a welcoming neighborhood, close to the best restaurants, and close to numerous subway lines! Mary is a wonderful host very helpful and communicative for checking in and out. I would say her apt is a steal and highly recommend it for everyone traveling to NYC!

Milana is a great host. Her place is great!  Everything is high quality, microwave heats up fast,  air conditioners worked well,  out door roof top patio is very nice with 360 view, I was afraid of height still enjoyed.  Bathroom is very modern and clean.  Pretty much everything was clean and nice.  Location is close to grocery stores and restaurants.  3 blocks away from subway station and close to the beach!  Then about an extra 20 minutes walk on the board walk to Coney Island.  Thank you, I would love to come back and stay longer.

My family enjoyed our stay at Angela's spacious and conveniently located home near Flushing's K-town.  Having a private parking space, a small playground nearby at the school, and the restaurants/shop made our stay comfortable and stress-free.  The area seemed safe and was relatively quiet.

I can highly recommend this place!  The apartment is a 2mins walk to the Subway. 20mins to Times Square by Subway. There is a Supermarket 2 blocks away with everything you need.  The room was very nice and looks exactly like in the pictures. It’s also a quiet building.  The check in was smooth and quick. All of the roommates that I met were very friendly and helpful. Everything was on point and well prepared.  Dee & Mattia were very nice and helpful. I felt very welcomed and save at their place.  I can also recommend the area. As a woman I can say I wasn’t afraid at all to walk home alone in the evening/night.   So if you don’t mind a 20min ride by Subway to the City then you should check out their place :-) Even the train ride is very funny sometimes 😉

The good. Check in was easy. Free street parking was available within a 2-minute walk after a short search. Subway station is about 10-minute walk away. There are window AC units, contrary to what the listing says. The bad.  While the place was mostly clean, dishes in the kitchen had a layer of aged grease on them. The light switch in the bathroom had some suspicious brown substance on it. Furniture items were broken or defaced. Only one towel per guest was provided. No towel or paper towels in the kitchen. The $75 cleaning fee felt outrageous for what we saw. The neighbourhood felt very unsafe and neglected. There was garbage everywhere in the street (check the street view pictures on a map site), and weeds instead of lawns. Most windows have grills for burglary protection. Houses appear run down. There is no racial diversity. Later I looked up the crime level, and this neighbourhood really stands out in a bad way.

Great location not far from a lot of things in the city. There are 3 doors that you have to unlock before getting to the actual apartment door, which made me feel safe (not that it’s unsafe but we are talking NYC here). Would definitely stay again.

Еverything is generally quite good, quite clean and comfortable, but the mattress is very hard. and if you are as afraid of insects as I am, then this is not your option, there are a lot of spiders and bugs (one got out of the sink when I was brushing my teeth, I almost died). plus very audible when walking on top.

If you are looking for somewhere reasonably priced and in a quiet area, this is a phenomenal place without a doubt.  Some friends pre-judged El Barrio saying that it could be dangerous but on the contrary, we found quite nice and hard-working people.  And the best thing is Jamel's hospitality, our flight was delayed and we arrived in the wee hours of the morning and we had no problem getting home and finding it. Furthermore, he made sure that everything was fine throughout the stay, he even bought us some sweets and some bottles of wine in the middle of the stay that he left for us right at the entrance. I have booked many Airbnbs and have never found anyone as helpful and attentive as Jamel and his family.

This place is perfect for me. The kitchen is inclusive, and it's all you'll need to make decent meals during your time there. The whole place is very clean and doesn't have the sort of "creepy" feel you might expect of a basement. The A/C is a lifesaver. It's also easy to access and totally private. Great place, overall.

Jamel is a really kind and nice host! The place was so clean and tidy, and whatever concerns and problems we had, he solved them for us very fast. The location is good enough for the price, the metro station being 20 mins walking distance away. Other than that, the neighborhood didn’t seem really scary, as some would think - we still used Uber to go home from the church ave metro station during the night. All in all, it was a really nice experience and Jamel is a host we would recommend anytime. Thank you again!!

Do not rent this air bnb, the host is very disrespectful and inconsiderate of guests. The pictures do not resemble the actuality of the place. false advertisement. As well as unsafe environment. The heater does not work and the Host did not accommodate or be considerate of safety hazards for guests. Instead, cares more about getting paid and money. Very horrible experience.

Jack and his place is truly wonderful. His team is AMAZING. The staff is beyond helpful and make having an event at 38 parlor so easy and stress free. Had it not been for them, hosting a party there would have been much more difficult and a totally different experience. Thanks to them I got to enjoy my night and my guest cannot stop talking about the wonderful time we all had. Highly recommend 38 parlor. I would rent this place every weekend if I could!

Overall, John’s place was fine - location in Bushwick is a 6 minute walk to the JZ trains and there are enough stores nearby. The actual room is crowded with stuff but organized. While John seems like a pleasant dude, the experience could’ve been more seamless.   My main issues are with check-in and the roommate situation. Upon arriving, the trip details page had the wrong check-in keycode so I couldn’t access the keys to get into the building. After a long journey there, it was a very stressful experience. John responded but several hours later.   Secondly, there are 3 roommates (which aren’t mentioned in the listing). For a few nights, the roommates either had a guest sleep in the living room or brought over 1 - 10 guests at once to hang out at night.   Lastly, the room faces the street and so expect to be woken up often by the roar of the train. Definitely bring ear plugs!!

The flat has many advantages as disavantages. It is located very close to the metro which goes directly to Manhattan, the flat is spacious as well as the room, where there is a very comfortable bed. Kitchen is well equipped with quality furniture as It Is the bathroom.    If you have a ligh sleep, resting will be difficult as the metro is not underground and runs very close to the building, the sourranding neighbourhood is a bit unpleasant and it will take you at least 15 min walking to get in the nice area of Williamsburg. Be aware hosts do not appreciate if you leave your door (even just slightly) open when going back and forth from the toilet (which is private but outside the room) and they might even close it for you. Also, notice that if you need to leave the luggages a few extra hours you will be charged 30 dollars for a "late check out". However, if within this time you need ten minutes to change a t-shirt before travelling you might be asked to leave. So, definitely it was a great occasion for an affordable accommodation in NYC, but as we did not feel very welcomed in the flat, we will not choose it a second time.

Dana is very friendly and welcoming! Her place is a very nice size and very nice and clean. The area seemed to be good. There are food places, stores, and even a flea market within walking distance. I never felt unsafe in this area. The train is about a two minute walk from Dana’s place. This was my first time doing an AirBnB and it was a great experience.

What a steal. Simple, but beautiful large room with lovely natural sunlight very close to the Halsey subway stop. Lakisha was quick to respond and so sweet. It’s a room with other rooms that I believe are rented out sometimes but I didn’t see anyone during my three night stay. You won’t be disappointed!

My boyfriend and I had a fabulous time exploring NYC using Agus' apartment as our home base. We spent long days exploring, so unfortunately did not have the chance to meet Agus. However, she was always quick to respond to any questions or concerns that we had.   Agus' apartment is lovely and clean. The building feels very safe and secure. Unfortunately, we found the neighbourhood to be quite sketchy. The walk from the subway is thankfully quite short, but I would not have been comfortable walking alone. Because I was travelling with my boyfriend (who is not small), it was fine. This apartment is not located in the hip area of Williamsburg.   Our room was clean and spacious. The kitchen appeared to be clean and well supplied; however, we did not eat there (too much good food to try in NYC)! The bathroom was also very clean and we were happy it was private.   The apartment can be quite noisy and Agus did have friends visit one night (which is of course understandable), but they were quite noisy well into the night, so I do recommend bringing earplugs.   Checking in and checking out were very easy. She charges $30 to leave luggage beyond the 10am check out which seems excessive to me.   Overall, a nice, clean, modern apartment close to Manhatten, but in a dodgy neighbourhood.

After spending time looking for the best Airbnb in south slope, I found Mike’s listing, which is not only an amazing steal, but is perfectly located (on a quiet street close to all the restaurants and bars on 5th and 7th), sizable (you can really stretch out in this apartment), and clean. I’m going to plan future trips to Brooklyn around this listing’s availability.

Our family of five stayed at La Couronne for five weeks in 2021 at the tail end of the Covid crisis in NYC. We needed a temporary apartment while we waited to close on our new home in Brooklyn. I can't express how thankful I am to have had such a perfect space and gracious hosts during a relatively stressful time for our family. Daphne and Jonathan did not bat any eye when I told them we had three kids ages 4, 2 and 4 months. We were welcomed with open arms. A stylish and sturdy space with all that our family could have needed -- plenty of space for play, lounging, cooking/eating and sleeping ("sleep" being relative with three babies!). We were totally comfortable. It felt like being on vacation in our home town. The place was as clean as can be (and I'm picky).  We enjoyed experiencing a new part of Brooklyn -- good BBQ and nice bakery just around the corner. Great supermarket a 5 minute walk. Major subway lines just a few blocks away. Easy walk to playgrounds and Prospect Park, as well as to stylish Franklin Ave and Bed Stuy. Highly recommended! Thank you Daphne and Jonathan!
Helen was a wonderful and respectful host of the space rented from her, responses are quick and she will help you with anything so don't be afraid to ask! Will definitely return.

Hugh Suites sound impressive but it didn’t impress us in many ways, here’s why: We stayed here from the 1st - 3rd & 24th - 29th August. The ceilings are too low. My 6’2” husband had to walk with his head down. To my knowledge he hit his head three times. There’s a supporting beam from the lounge through the bedroom which makes it even lower. We booked in February, a disclaimer regarding the low ceiling was sent to us on August 1st, the day we were checking in. We didn’t see the disclaimer regarding the low ceiling until we arrived at the airport after 18 hours of travel from Europe. Nice surprise, what were we meant to do. Entrance is at the rear and below the hosts’ residence. It’s a garage compound and where refuse bins are kept by nearby residents so not at all private. Steps leading to the basement, was a scruffy piece of mat outside the rear door of the hosts and overhanging at face level as walking down the steps. The steps are uneven and one of them broken which can be potentially very dangerous. There’s a security light but it switches off very quickly so be extra careful when dark. Windows are tiny, almost at ground level since it’s a basement. Overlooked by neighbours and anyone walking by so we couldn’t leave them open as not private. It was stuffy, uncomfortable & felt like a prison. No welcome pack provided to tie us over until the next morning before we could purchase our own stuff. We found just two tiny( 8oz ) bottles of water in the fridge and some organic tea bags, several salt, pepper and sauce sachets in a tray on the worktop left over by past guests, I guess. After such a long journey it would have been so nice to have a small welcome pack even if we had to pay for it. This was just too poor. Never stayed anywhere before and received such poor service. We like Airbnb because it’s meant to have a bit of a personal touch but not here. Before our second visit I messaged our host if she could provide us with the above but messaged me back to say it wasn’t possible. Didn’t notice on the first stay but on our second stay the place was not thoroughly cleaned. Walls, skirting are badly marked, window seal dirty, however, we were charged for two lots of cleaning. Travelling to the city by public transport is approximately 3.5 hour return journey which can be rather tiring. Our checking was done by Ramon. On our first visit I met the hostess as we were leaving. What impressed us Since we had problems with our luggage, we were delayed leaving the airport and the hostess communicated with us frequently. The taxi service provided by Ramon, the hosts’ representative. JFK airport is only 10 minutes away by taxi. The shower is very powerful. Excellent WiFi. The hostess lent...

Nice spacious “mini” apartment space with private entrance.  There is plenty of room to stretch out for 2-3 guest.  The ceilings are very low, as this is a basement apartment.  The doorway to get inside is a very narrow space that includes about 4 steps down.  It was a struggle with bags and I’m 5’4.   Also, there was an ant 🐜 problem.  There is a pipe next to the bed that have tiny ant like bugs, if the cover flops over they crawl into bed with you.  They also attacked the futon 😩Wish I could attach pictures.......  Also, only contact the host on her phone.  Inbox messages through Air BNB are not answered.

Good place on the inside and the family was nice but unfortunately the neighbourhood was pretty rough and had multiple people asking me for money when I went for groceries/people selling drugs in the open/a fight broke out in front of the local deli while I was picking up sandwich meats and milk....all of this led to me staying inside most of the time unless I was driving far away from the house to meet friends.

Great place to stay with your significant other! Quiet neighborhood with great local restaurants and bars near by. 10 min walk in either direction to the nearest subway station. Easy check in instructions and great recommendations from Peter. Definitely stop by Fazio's for some of the best pizza we had during our stay, it's only a block away! Don't let the pull out sofa bed scare you away, it was very comfortable! Somehow Peter knew I'd forget my toothbrush and was so happy to receive a goody bag filled with toiletries! Will stay again for a Brooklyn getaway!

This place is nothing as described they was dirty dishes in the cabinet the inside of the microwave had food stuck to the sides and top from the past 4 guest the towels they leave for you are the cheap white one with the blue stripe down the middle hotels you for cleaning they was a chunk missin out of the wood kitchen floor they say they provide WiFi but the box is not in the unit so It buffered and loaded all night there is 10 diffierent loud ass noises that you hear all night and it’s not a apartment it’s the basement of they house they literally spy on you they walked down the basement stair and basically sat there and listened so creepy I definitely don’t recommend anyone staying here it’s so uncomfortable to be honest I feel like they have cameras down there

The whole experience was awesome. Peter was incredibly responsive and always available. He even arranged parking for us, which is challenging in the area!  The apartment was super clean and everything was cozy.  The photos posted on the profile are very accurate. The location is about a 10min walk from the subway and there are loads of cute bars and restaurants in the area.  The only "challenge" we faced was there is no AC (like several places in NY we discovered) and we happened to go during a ridiculous heat wave (mid 90's)! It was not smoldering but warm. There was a large fan provided by Peter that helped.  Outside of that, everything was perfect!!! I would definitely stay there again when in the city. It really was a steal for the price!

Vincente’s place is just a hop from Grand Central, located on busy 34th street. There are lots of options for food and public transportation. You are a block from the Empire State Building! And, if you are going to Times Square it’s an easy walk.   The apartment is small, but clean. Don’t be scared when you enter an old building. There is a 2 flight walk up, for those of you with knee issues. No elevator. You will have a private room with a double bed and large window. The bathroom is shared with the home occupants. They have an air circulation tower in the room that helps with air flow and noise. Ample closet space.   Vincente was kind enough to meet us early, so we could drop off our bags. And, he let us also have some extra time after checkout to hold the bags as well. Much more enjoyable in the city without lugging your stuff around.   It was a great location for us. It is a safe area of the city and well lit. This is a very good choice if you want something simple and in Central Manhattan.   Thanks!

The entrance to the accommodation is not very reassuring but the accommodation is clean. Having a person living in the kitchen is unpleasant! Place to avoid if you want silence (among other things at night) but place to recommend if you want to be in the center of Manhatten at a price that is not too unaffordable...

I'm sure we were the first guests  to use the sleeper sofa, which my daughter said was comfortable.  But on the first night we discovered there was no obvious bedding.  I hunted down new sheets in package, and we pulled the plastic off the new mattress.  I shared pillows from my bed, which were plentiful, but I had no extra blankets to share.  She made do with the little couch throw and an extra sheet.  It was warm so she was ok.  The bath towels were thin, and I had 5-6 long black hairs on me after I showered. I don't have long black hair and I hope they had been clean?!  The extra 2 towels hadn't been washed (new from store), it appeared.  The place was obviously newly renovated and appointed, and I think we were just there at an off time.  It seemed pretty nice, new, and overall clean (maybe some extra dusting and sweeping would have been good).  Fairly quiet (upstairs neighbor dropped something around 7:30 am both mornings that sounded like a large chair).  Diverse neighborhood, friendly people.  Sketchy at night!  Don't walk to market or subway! TV's were nice, New with lots of stations.  I'm suggesting a few hooks in bathroom for towels and robe, and a shelf for toiletries would be convenient.

My husband and I had a very pleasant experience staying at this property. Peter is a very gracious host, accommodating and considerate, even offering to pick us up from the subway station. He even left a bottle of wine for our enjoyment! Easy check in, the place was sparkling clean, had enough sunlight reach through the windows, and offered available streaming services on our lazy mornings lying in bed. excellent location in a quiet and picturesque neighborhood away from the hustle and bustle of the city, but only 10-13 minute walk to subway station, so super convenient to get into the city and other boroughs of NYC. Only recommendation is to change out the bed to either a larger size or have a sofa bed available for more than 1 guest. the pull out twin bed was a bit uncomfortable and unsafe because it could slip and slide when you are trying to get in and out of bed. Other than that, everything else was excellent. I would highly recommend staying here!

The apartment is very clean, with independent entrance, is comfortable, large, and with all the necessary amenities for us who spent 14 days staying. Peter is an excellent host, very attentive, available, discreet and concerned with our well being throughout our stay and of course, left us super at ease.  The location is a few blocks from the subway to Manhattan and is very convenient and easy to use. At neighborhood there are markets, pharmacies, Best Buy, Amazon Locker, Michaels, laundromats, restaurants and other services that are worth to be visited.  The city, is super charming and beautiful, and safe. We left early for Manhattan and returned at 9 or 10 PM with shopping bags and cameras and at no time we did feel unsafe.  when we get back to NY, we'll would like to stay be back at the  Peter apartment. We were really grateful for a reception, for the care, attention and especially for the concern for our well-being throughout the period.

DONT STAY HERE FOR EVEN 20 MINUTES!!!!!!! This underground basement is full of health and safety voilations!!! The place is very tiny and the cealing is very low enough for bump your head a few times! There's wholes in the floor big enough for your heel to get to get stuck in. Its FREEZING in the basement we had to put the oven on for heat like we were in the projects. There are 2 pots the size of a Chinese foodcontainer and no utensils. No real towels....they have stolen gym towels and put them in the bnb who knows if they are clean? I could go on.....dont stay here if you have some place else to go please go and not to mention the host Hugh is a liar!!!

Peter’s place was lovely — cozy, well-appointed, easy to access, and exactly as described. I didn’t need much, but when I did have a question, Peter responded quickly and courteously. Check in and out were easy and stress-free. Peter is a great host and his place is perfectly located in a great spot in Astoria. I would stay here again in a heartbeat!

Leland was a great host. The place is ideal for a visit of NYC on a budget. Sleeping wasn't too comfortable, but nothing too bad. Neighborhood might feel a little unwelcoming at night, but I guess that is just what NYC is, we were regurarly returning at 11 pm or later and we never felt unsafe.

Cannot stress how convenient everything was, Location was great, easy check in and out, the tv selection was great. I flew in late and Leland was understanding and approachable. Can’t recommend this space enough.

The location and place was as described. The location was walkable to the subway, neighborhood was beautiful and room was clean. The problem we had was that we couldn’t sleep. The first night of our arrival the heat was very high, and we were afraid of opening the windows as NYC is famous for mice/rats. The room was not as hot the next day so it was better. But both beds were VERY uncomfortable. The full size bed mattress is uneven and twin mattress felt like a sinkhole. The three of us had a hard time sleeping. The low star rating (no pleasure in giving it) is because we needed place to sleep and paid over $400 per night as it was new year’s eve timeframe. So when you ended up being super tired during your day because of lack of sleep and paid prime price… it ends being not worthy.  I will not be staying here again.

I am never a person who leaves a bad review. But staying at Lakisha’s place was absolutely a nightmare.  There is a long pipeline goes through the bedroom that constantly makes very loud buzzing noise (every 5-10 mins) through out the day. I barely got any sleep. When I communicate with the host about this issue, she was extremely rude. First she told me the pipeline company cannot come in time to fix this issue (I booked 9 nights with the host), which I understand. When I express my disappointment very polity, saying while I understand the situation, but my stay was unpleasant. She became annoy d and asked me “what not to understand”. Also asked me to move out if I found the noise so disturbing.  With her extremely rude attitude, also the noise in the room, I end up having to find a hotel to stay for five night. ALSO ALERT.  This place has very loud neighbors. Location is not that safe.

This Airbnb experience was the worst thing I’ve ever encountered. I booked here since I came to play in the Us Open and it was close to the site, I had no clue it would turn out to be so stressful and uncomfortable for me . The house rules the hosts sends through makes you feel as though you are walking on eggshells everyday .Even before check in I called host to introduce myself and ask a question , I was basically yelled at on the phone by her saying she wants to speak over messages . I messaged her a few days later to let her know the air conditioning in the room was loud and no air was coming out , hoping she  could tell me how to fix it, she proceeded to send me a string of disrespectful messages accusing me of lying about it . I told her I would send her a video of the sound it was making and was told it is illegal to send that , and the sound the ac was making was probably in my head. I’ve been with air bnb for years and had amazing experiences, even kept great friendships with my hosts after departure. Very confused how after the great reviews my host had that I was treated as a low class liar when I was the one getting no sleep before my matches. Definitely would not ever stay here again or recommend this house to anyone.
excellent host and clean the place only that surroundings are a little dangerous but from there on out everything very well
It was a great place. Location was nice and was right next to the subway, plus the neighborhood wasn’t shady. The apartment was clean and beautiful and I would definitely recommend staying here.

I stayed at Ibrahim’s place with my 18 y.o. son. Ibrahim accepted our request very quickly even it was late night and last call.  His place was beyond our expectations: cozy, very tidy and smells nice. The bed was super comfortable to sleep in. Warm blanket and towels were provided. Freezer and microwave in a room is super comfortable. Ibrahim explained us the best way to get to the sightseeings. The district was normal for us, we didn’t see anything scary around. I definitely recommend Ibrahim place to stay. If there would be an opportunity to return back to NYC, I’d for sure stay at his place again!
Good accommodation, dangerous area

Joy is an incredible host. Very open to communication and willing to accommodate. The place is honestly a steal considering the private room and amenities that came with. Simply put, I would have no problems suggesting it to any friends or family.

This is a very special and wonderful stay. The location is incredible (so close to the BQ) and I spent every morning exploring Prospect Park. There are wonderful grocery stores, laundromats, coffee shops, and restaurants all around. The area is so nice and fairly priced that I’m deciding to move to a place not far away.   Rasha is a fantastic host. She is kind, communicative, honest, and caring. Her apartment comes fully stocked with everything you’d need. It also has an amazing vibe: cozy, boho, artist, traveler vibes. It is very easy to feel at home here.  As a single, young woman, I felt very safe here. There are usually clusters of men on the street who might talk to you as you walk by, but it is never hostile and I never felt unsafe. The neighborhood is a community of families where everyone knows and takes care of each other.  The building is older, so be prepared for a few things to break here and there. However, the super fixed them the day of and at no extra charge. And Rasha was extremely prompt and hands-on during these moments.  Overall, I can’t recommend Rasha’s place enough. I’d stay here again in a heartbeat!

I had a fantastic stay at Ervita's. Not only was she extremely accommodating to a check in time that wound up being over an hour later than we had projected (due to subway delays), but she also offered good navigation tips for the rest of our stay in the city. Super clean apartment, never felt unsafe in the neighborhood. Would definitely recommend to anyone!
Well stocked and roomy apartment.  Far too much cleaning "spray" odor.  Some dangerous blocks in the neighborhood.  "Close" to subway.

The apartment was REALLY good; in some ways, it exceeded expectations. The bed is a massive King-sized memory foam mattress. The living room is spacious. The bathroom is the right size. The fridge is huge. I hosted my girlfriend and myself here and used the entire kitchen suite to cook. This showed me one glaring problem with the kitchen setup: using the gas burner stove-tops to cook will leave a heavy gas smell. The window helps a little bit, but the stove fan doesn't work enough to suck up that gas. The location isn't too bad, but it might be a bit much for travelers new to the NYC area (especially Harlem). The east side of Harlem isn't far enough to be out of mind, but since the apartment is literally across the street from a school, it's hard to feel too uneasy. The host was a pleasure talking to, great communication, easy to talk to, which was a great help. Overall, I would give it 5 stars if it weren't for the area being a challenge to navigate around and nearby other sketchier areas.

Rasha's place is cute, has a nice homey vibe, close to the train station (to have easy access to manhattan) and right next to prospect park! You also have to try "Ix" the Guatemalan restaurant nearby and the stew there! It's delicious. Wifi was an issue when we first got there, but Rasha quickly accommodated a new service and now it is up and running smoothly! It was a deal breaker for me since I work fully remote, so I appreciated the quick turnaround and how well the wifi worked after :). My partner mentioned it was better than his wifi at home! haha  Rasha is a very kind and accommodating host so I enjoyed communicating with her through my month-long stay. And the neighbors who I communicated with at times are very kind too:).  The only thing I would mention is that though I loved the coziness with wonderful home touches in this studio - I got scared of bumping into things and accidentally knocking them over. And... I definitely knocked a lamp over by accident!!:( (Side-note: Rasha and I worked it out and I paid for it:) I appreciated her grace through the process).  Overall, I would recommend this place to guests. Thank you Rasha!

This apartment is in a great area within walking distance to nice coffee shops, restaurants and the subway stops. It’s simple to get where you want to go. Houman had great suggestions of where to eat and shop that we took advantage of. He responded quickly to any questions we had. We recommend it if you want to be out and active in Brooklyn.  The apartment is well maintained. Understand that this is Houman’s place of residence so you need to be comfortable in that space. We liked seeing his personal style. He had a lot of cool books to look through and has a lot of barware for making cocktails if you choose.  Be aware that the apartment is on the first floor and the windows face the street so you may hear people talking outside.  We would recommend this apartment. There’s a security door for the building so we never felt unsafe.  The bathroom and shower are small so if you’re accustomed to larger bathrooms keep that in mind. This is the first time we stayed in Brooklyn in an older apartment so we would guess it’s normal for the area. The shower did have good water pressure and plenty of hot water.  We really enjoyed our stay!

Place just like the photos.Pierrer lives right above, so he is easy to be there to give a quick response for any problem that may arise. The area of ​​the apartment is correct and has services nearby. The nearest metro station 125 str. Something insecure.

Clean, cozy and very quiet apartment where you feel good after long hours of wandering around New York. Pierre is a very kind host, considerate and very involved in making your stay as pleasant as possible. Small downside about the area, keep in mind that you are in the heart of Harlem, which may not suit everyone, personally it bothered me (feeling of insecurity) but less so my husband. The line is 5 minutes away on foot, a big plus for going straight out and about, unfortunately misery and poverty are also very present in front of the metro train. To conclude a nice meeting: Pierre and a really good apartment
Great hospitality from Pierre!!!! Super nice and clean. Location is kinda sketchy at night but it makes you feel like a local.

Very affordable place to stay.  Don't let the area scare you, as long as you know what you're doing and aren't being silly it's no problem staying in harlem. 5 minute walk from the subway which will pretty much take you anywhere.

Everything was great. I expected the area to be a lil dangerous but between the house and the metro station is a Police Department so you will see a police car at every corner at any hour. The place is just amazing and so confortable. Amber is great and she responds so quickly anytime you need her. She even helped me with some suggestiona where to go and what to do in the city.

The bed was comfortable and there was adequate bedding and towels.  There is a pocket door that will close off the sleeping area but essentially this is like a large studio. All the appliances were new and worked well.  This second floor walk-up is so sparce and clean it feels a bit thoughtless and soulless, sort of like students crash there:  a tall mirror and a picture both sitting on the floor, leaning up against the wall, a single comfortable couch but nowhere to store your clothes except in a tiny cabinet or by tossing them on the floor in the large bedroom closet, a single bedside table and lamp. There is a pretty view of the park and soccer field out the two, tall windows. The neighborhood is a little sketchy but we had no major problems and enjoyed the Target store nearby.  There is an OK  local deli and a small restaurant on the block but count on 30 to 40 minutes to get to midtown after a short walk and several transfers; so get ready to take the bus. The Internet was fast enough so we did not miss having a TV.  The kitchen has a fridge, drip coffee maker, salt and pepper and a few spices, utensils, two frying pans, Melmac dishes, some glasses, a roll of paper towels and a small table with two chairs.  We found a hair dryer in a drawer.  The shower is so terrific that you never want to get out!  The owners are friendly and responsive.  All in all this is an OK place to sleep, have breakfast and leave.

Ok so i stayed here for 5 days. Previous reviews are 100% accurate. Scott was very communicative. My only gripe was i wish he was more flexible on early check ins/late check outs but he was not flexible at all. Everything inside was good, just not the cheap ikea bed with the wood slates at the bottom. I used to live in the area so i was familiar, but for someone who is not from here it can be a lil sketchy, as its close to the projects on 1st ave and it is in a highly concentrated area of lower income folks(although that is changing quite quickly). The apartment itself is really clean and well maintained. Wish the price was lower though and not as high as $170+ a night considering the area. Also you are required to take the trash out at the end of your stay. I dont think thats fair because i paid a cleaning fee. I shouldnt be responsible for throwing out trash because at a hotel i wouldnt be responsible for that either. The cleaning crew would be, especially when you charge hotel prices, with NO ELEVATOR. All in all because of those reasons i rate this place a 3.8/5. Overally I'd stay here again if i want to experience "the barrio"

Agnes is a wonderful hostess – so friendly, very communicative and helpful, just as described in other reviews.  Check-In instructions were clear and easy.  We rented for over two weeks while our son was in Allen Hospital, a 7 min walk away. Agnes’ apartment was extremely convenient as we could easily travel back and forth to hospital without an Uber.   Apartment is just as expected from reviews & photos.  Super clean, nice-sized bedrooms with large closet each and fresh white sheets & duvets on each bed.  Large open kitchen with breakfast table & seating area.  Kitchen amenities included tea, coffee and coffee pot, nice large fridge and island for food prep. Large remodeled bathroom has plenty of nice thick, clean white towels and soaps, toothbrushes, hair dryer, etc.  Just like a hotel!  They even offered to let us use their washer & dryer, when needed.  The Marble Hill location is great!  Convenient to both the train and Subway to downtown.  Neighborhood is quiet in the evening and safe.  Also, walking distance to grocery stores, nice cafes, Target, post office, drug stores…you name it!  We will stay here again the next time we are in NYC.  Highly recommend!

Staying in this apartment was much better than we thought. It looks exactly like the pictures. We were late for check in, but it was no problem. Also it was really great, that we could leave our baggage in the apartment till we left.  Before we got here, we were a little bit concerned if it could be dangerous, but the neighborhood was really good.  We really recommend this one!

The apartment it self was fine, would have need slightly more cleaning but ok. 2nd bed room has very tiny beds and no air conditioning in the bedroom when our first night was pretty warm. Master bed room is great and we could enjoy the outside terrace which is honestly very nice. Rashida did send one message and then never replied my message / question. We didn’t have check in information / confirmation just 3 hours prior to landing in New York which was a bit scary and we didn’t feel very welcomed. Neighborhood is okay, indeed safe but a lot of abandoned houses which makes it not super cheerful. Very close from the subway.
Very nice place, it is not in the best of areas but not once did we feel unsafe. Jose was very responsive and helpful when we had any questions. Would recommend to anyone staying in the Bronx.

Okay place . You are getting what you pay for . I would suggest avoiding the subway and taking alternative transportation. Neighborhood is a bit sketchy as it is an urban area. Apartment does have the basics you could need . Walls are very thin and the neighborhood does get pretty noisy especially with a school right across the street. I would suggest not walking outside after 7pm . Last night here  was a complete scare with a shooting down two blocks from us !

While Klara's home (once inside) is lovely, the approach was not. The hallways are unfinished (concrete) and apartments are not labeled. The exterior door into the apartments was wide open (anyone could come in). The area was sketchy and unsafe to be walking at night. Only half block from the train, it was also very noisy. We were very disappointed in this airbnb.

My fiancée and I another couple went for a fun weekend stay to Manhattan. We had expected to stay in a quaint and cozy pad near Central Park to get access to all the activities going on this great city. I must say we ended up being very disappointed in this place.  Firstly, the place is in east Harlem which is a very rough area to be staying in. When you walk around this area you don’t feel safe. There were even people doing drugs in front of the premises.  Second, the accuracy of the description was way off. Here we were two couples and yes the place has five beds but my fiancée and I had to sleep together in a very small kids bed. Sure very cozy but not what we were expecting.  It appears that the place isn’t being kept up or cleaned enough. Large black flies flying around, garbage under the bed, no bathroom toiletries or enough towels. It needs better housekeeping.  Also the host was delayed a bit in her responses which made our trip planning a bit more stressful.  In general, this place is overrated for the price and the owner needs to reset expectations about what  audience they are trying to capture. We don’t recommend staying here if you are visiting NYC.

The inside of the apartment is just as expected. I didnt like the building itself which isn’t her fault. The building is undergoing reservations so it looks very messy right now. The elevator seemed a little suspicious as I was not sure if it was going to get stuck. I didn’t like the neighborhood, there were people up and out until 3 AM blasting music. The neighbors just stared at us and made us feel very uncomfortable (again not the hosts fault).  Other than that, the apartment was just as expected. The pictures are very accurate.

Tamer is a great host. He accommodated every need or question me or my friends had. The apartment was beautiful, well kept together and clean. It snowed the second day we were at the apartment and his staff made sure to clear the snow and salt the property for our safety. The apartment is an ABSOLUTE steal for the price, and the area in Brooklyn is close to everything. I would definitely suggest this apartment to anyone who wants to stay in the Brooklyn area for a great price with a very accommodating/reliable host as well as his staff. Thank you for the great New Years Eve Weekend!

Privacy, peace, close to stores, air conditioning, and a fully stocked kitchen. A home away from home! Agnes was a great host and showed us around the house on the first day and made us feel very welcomed! There’s lots of great local stores around, and is close to the 1 train. There were so many board games provided, we enjoyed playing as much as we can! My nephew really enjoyed the hammock too! Just a couple insider tips: there are stairs outside the house and inside, they require a bit of patience because they can get a bit tricky because of the sizing of them. There’s also no AC in the living room but there’s a nice ceiling fan, which helped lots. We found the house to be a bit scary at times, but it added character to it. We definitely enjoyed our time there and wish we stayed longer. Thank you so much Anges, for allowing us in your home!

BEWARE.  SECURITY ISSUE!! There is a secret under-the-stairwell passageway between the host unit and the guest unit with no lock on the guest side. There is just a handwritten sign taped up to the cabinet door saying that it is "not an entrance". The host's husband actually used this passageway to enter the guest unit shortly after my arrival even though there is a regular outside door at the top of the stairs. He was there to check on me to make sure everything was okay. That's customary, but popping through a creepy unlocked secret passageway is definitely not customary.  I was totally unnerved and left immediately afterwards to find another rental. Agnes pointed out that there is a bolt lock on their side for "their security". Swell.  That's not much comfort if you can't also lock it from the guest side.  The unit itself is cute and well furnished, and it was in a good location.  If it wasn't for the security issue with the secret passageway, I'm sure I would have enjoyed my stay.  I'm hoping the host corrects this security issue by installing a bolt lock on the guest side and not using this passageway when a guest is in the unit. That would solve everything.

This place is a total scam. I had a TERRIBLE experience. if I could give zero stars I would. Let me start off by saying not all the pictures are accurate. The view of central park out the window is completely fake. Next, there is absolutely no building staff to let you in or leave your luggage with... unless building staff means neighbor down the hall that you have to figure out how to get ahold of. The entire lobby is "under construction", but based off other reviews months ago, nothing is being constructed. Lastly and most importantly this host is not even allowed to have air bnb! I came home one night to a note on the door saying maintenance was going to be coming from 8-4 for two days during my stay. I reached out to the host and she explained not to answer the door because she is not allowed to host air bnb and that her husband would come stay with my stuff while they came. Yes because I rented and paid for an apartment because I did not plan on being in it... Not to mention sure, I would love a stranger to sit with my belongings all day. Great!  I ended up leaving after one night because of this mess. The best part the host will not acknowledge my well deserved refund. Why host air bnb if you know you are not allowed to? Total scam do not waste your time or money. You are better off pitching a tent in Central Park.

Klara's apartment is beautiful, clean, and very spacious for NYC. There is a large TV that was easy to use, a big kitchen to cook in, and a spacious common area. There was even shampoo, lotion, sunscreen, etc. provided for use. The pictures of the unit were completely accurate, which can't be said for many other apartments on Airbnb. The location is great in terms of being close to the subway, Central Park, the Met, etc.   The main negative part about it in my opinion is the building itself, which is not at all nice. Not only is it under construction (and both of the main doors downstairs are thus left unlocked at all times, which doesn't seem very safe, especially in a potentially sketchy neighborhood where there were groups of men hanging out outside the building late at night), but it also smells very badly and just feels gross in the main area/elevator/stairwell. The entrance is also on the basement level. Clearly the building itself is not kept up well (it didn't actually even seem like construction was even happening while we were there/it doesn't sound like there's been much progress made on this over time, based on other reviews), but of course there is nothing Klara could do about this. If this is important to you though, this may not be the place for you. The unit itself is great, though, and was perfect for my needs! The elevator was also working.   The only other potentially negative experience is getting access to the unit. I had to connect with a neighbor who had a key. She was easy to reach and nice, so it worked out fine, but a lock box would probably be ideal, in case the neighbor isn't there. I also think the neighbor has her own key, which has the potential to be a little scary (though again, she seemed very nice and never once bothered us).   Overall, we had a great time, despite the sketchy building area. Once we were in the actual apartment itself we felt like we were in a completely different, very nice building, and it was also very quiet inside. I definitely recommend this apartment overall!

I had never been to NYC prior to this trip; this air bnb was a steal for how gorgeous, clean and efficiently run it is. Tamer accommodated my group when we needed to drop off our bags before check in, and let us keep our bags there until our flight on the day of check out. He also helped us figure out the very high end alarm system. Beyond that, the space is brand new and classy/comfortable.  The location was perfect for Brooklyn, but via Uber a little farther from Manhattan (to be expected) but nothing too crazy!   Will absolutely return and recommend to my friends and family!! Loved it.

I saw a note in the hall saying the gas was shut off in September. We Booked Nov 1. We were never told there would be No working stove or Heat or hot water. Knowing the entire building would be using hot plates and space heaters did not make us feel safe. (Major Fire Hazard) The bathroom mirror was disgusting. The vent in the kitchen was caked with dust.  The fridge was dirty and had rotting salads in it. The hand soap was so watered down it was unusable. There was a bar of soap in the shower that had hair and something else in it. I have pictures. Because there was no gas there was no hot water.   We were there because my husband needed heart surgery at Mt Sinai. He needed to be clean and use special wipes after a warm shower, on surgery day.  This made our life 10 times more stressful than it had to be. We didn't stay. The Quote in the bedroom that read "I'm not really a bitch I just play one in your life" should have been a clue. He sent a refund but not all we paid. He told me to contact Airbnb for the rest. Again...more stress I didn't need.  The Elevator was a plus.

This super clean apartment in the middle of Brooklyn has everything you need for a NYC trip. Arriving late in the evening was no problem. We immediately felt comfortable. It's about 20 minutes by subway to Manhattan plus a short walk. There were four of us in the apartment and had a comfortable time thanks to the 2 bathrooms :) The location is also safe, we never felt unsafe, even though the apartment is in the middle of Brooklyn. We would definitely book it again! Thanks for everything, Tamer!

Very nice stay! The apartment looks exacly like the pictures. Very comfy and stylish. The neighborhood is a bit sketchy but we didn't feel unsafe not for a moment, and we were traveling with a 12 year old. It's our first Airbnb experience and we are pleased. The host is very communicative and nice. Entering the place was very easy. The subway is a 5 minute walk and it takes you streight to Manhattan. Good experience.
Great place, not so beautiful zone but it looks safe a bit scary at night specially on the street we’re the subway it’s located.

Mory’s place is an excellent spot to stay in if you’re traveling to NYC and want comfort and proximity to the best places in New York. First off the apartment is just as advertised. It’s clean and the neighbors are quiet and friendly.  The neighborhood is a little hidden but it’s well lit at night and easy to access. The elevator ride might look sketchy but trust me it’s all appearance.   Mory really put in effort on making his guests comfortable. He’s communicative, polite, and tries to make the experience one worth remembering. If I’m ever back in NY I’ll definitely try to see if his place is available again.

Jerry – who goes by Wayne – was a great host, prompt with communication, even meeting us to help carry bags upstairs, and explaining everything about his living space. He picked up on a passing comment and bought us some egg bagels for breakfast! His apartment was tastefully decorated and neat and clean.  Be advised that this is a New York apartment in an older building. I.e. the kitchen and bathroom spaces are small, you will hear street noise at random hours, and parking can be challenging, though we were able to find  free street parking within a couple blocks. (Street cleaning signs required that we move our vehicle twice during three days here.)   One thing to note: the toilet seating area is very cramped and was a little unpleasant even to us who are smaller people, because the installation of the toilet was at a strange angle. Also, be sure Wayne explains the trick for flushing successfully! He will also likely explain how the apartment door key can be a little tricky to use.  Entertainment options were great,  including streaming of various video services with surround sound audio in his living room. Window air conditioners were quiet and in every room. Fully stocked kitchen accessories were available. Extra towels and wash cloths were available for the shower.   Location was excellent for us: a couple short blocks from Prospect Park and, in another direction, from the MTA Q line Church Av subway station with easy service to downtown Brooklyn and Manhattan one way, or else to Coney Island the other way.

The place was just as described. It was located pretty close to the subway, which made it easier to get anywhere. Jerry is super nice, he left tons of goodies for us, we felt very welcomed. He was very responsive. He was staying close from the place so it was easy for him to come by if we needed anything. He came by on the second day while we were gone and stayed in the house waiting for his mail, so we wouldn’t have to stress about it. Super nice guy. I would stay there again! :)

The place was top-notch. All clean, everything was there and was great. Everything was nearby (groceries, food), Subway 10 min walk (125th) but the area isn't that great. East Harlem is shady. Our girlfriends didn't felt safe but it has nothing to do with the airbnb-place. Just look out after 8/9pm or when it's dark. Take an Uber if you don't feel safe. We mostly took the subway and it was fine.  I would still recommend this place! Thank you!
Good location. Dont be afraid of the area. It looks sketchybut it's safe.

The unit was very clean and as spacious as it looks in the listing.   Communication was quick and easy before and during out stay.  Four of us stayed in this unit and were very comfortable.  We used a 7 day unlimited MetroCard to get around NYC.  The nearest subway station was about a 5 block walk.  While the neighborhood was likely safe enough, we tried to arrive at our apartment before dark as the walk to and from the subway station passed by some sketchy parts of Harlem and we were traveling with two teenage girls.  Had it just been my husband and I we would have been less apprehensive about being out after dark.  We were probably too cautious but better safe than sorry.   I really enjoyed the balcony and spent a lot of time there in the mornings and evenings drinking my coffee and tea.  (P.S. I made good use of the electric kettle to make my tea.  A pleasant bonus surprise in the kitchen.)
Great space, area's a bit sketchy but overall fantastic

Excellent Amazing host!! Thank you Myles. You da man You da man 100% on all categories. Myles far exceeded our expectations and earns 5 out of 5 stars. Wish I could give him more!  Enough space for four people with two twin beds and a queen bed. Sheets, pillows towels were provided. The beds were comfortable. during this cold week I am happy to say the apt was always warm.  There was a very nice living room space with free Wi-Fi, a fancy sectional couch with a smart tv.   The shower and kitchen were modern. Kitchen was open and had plenty of room to store groceries. The grocery store, drug store and laundromat really are around the corner. Pots pans, plates cups and folks are provided. We got lucky my cousin is a great cook and Myles is a great host. Yupppp the counter tops are a gorgeous granite. The ad was very accurate about the listing. Close to the subway and shopping and buses. The apartment was clean and fully furnished beautiful. It was very easy to check in. Myles did me a big favor and helped me pick up some relatives at the airport. He is very easy to reach and always willing to help. Great value. He should charge more.   I was very nervous since I never rental a BnB but with host like Myles I am a fan. He made me and my family feel like we were at home and was only a text away if we needed anything. I hope all hosts are like Myles. Fantastico!!! I am telling all my friends to rent from Myles and posted his card on my Facebook and Instagram. Very highly recommend you stay with Myles.

Myles is the best host, he is a wonderful person who cares about going the extra mile for his guests.  He was so kind to pick us up from and to the airport and even brought us refreshments!  Every day he asked us if everything was okay and if we needed help with something, he makes sure you feel at home and is always accessible and willing to help.  The apartment is very nice, recently renovated, very comfortable, nice bathroom, good beds, large TV with cable and wifi, new and fully equipped kitchen.  To enter the apartment you use a code and this way you don't run the risk of ever losing the key or you can separate into groups and arrive at different times.  The neighborhood is quiet and safe, nice houses around, we arrived between 12pm and 3am every day and we never felt in danger.  The subway station is 3 blocks away, the trains run all night and easily connect with the rest of Brooklyn and Manhattan.  There are many shops, supermarkets and restaurants near the metro, many of which are open 24 hours so you can always get what you need.    I recommend Myles and his apartment 100% and I would definitely stay with him again on my next visit to NY.

It has been our first visit to New York and we are happy that we chose to stay at Myles’s fabulous apartments. Myles made us truly welcome and the apartments are beautiful, comfortable, clean, with every detail thought to make your stay stress-free. We have found all appliances and amenities exactly as they are listed on Airbnb and Myles have been in touch weeks before our arrival to provide useful information about the apartment, local area and best sightseeings to visit while in town. Prior our  arrival Myles sent us all necessary details (key code and wifi password) and he was so welcoming. The place is indeed a home away from home. It’s felt like you are visiting your best cousin in New York who is always there for you, ready to help and provide any info you need 🙂 The apartments are located 3-4min walk from subway (underground). The area is very safe, we have been returning most days quite late (at around midnight) and we always felt safe. There are plenty of shops, cafes, banks and huge  Target department store in short walking distance. Myles is very kind, respectful and simply great person. We would 110% recommend Myles’ apartments to book for your visit to New York!

As soon as we booked, Myles quickly wrote to us to establish contact. Even before our arrival, he made himself available and sent us useful information to prepare our stay. When we arrived in New York he came to pick us up and was very patient despite the delay of our flight...I had never seen that. The first contact was immediately friendly and good-natured. Myles took advantage of the trip to show us around the neighborhood and get to know us. The apartment is modern, well equipped, very clean and well located. Myles had even taken the trouble to do some shopping for us so that we didn't miss anything the first few days. The area is safe, quiet with all amenities nearby (store, restaurant, metro 2 minutes walk). During our stay Myles was available and discreet. The height of happiness, he accompanied us to the airport on the day of our departure. In a word Magnificent, the best Air BnB host we have ever had. Thank you Myles and I hope to see you soon.
great place to get away from stress
The apartment is very cozy, small, it does not have many appliances for cooking for long stays. The location is good, however the neighborhood is a bit dangerous.

Nice apartment, as advertised. A little far away from the action and a little pricey. Everything went smoothly though, subway is near. Neighborhood seems alright, nothing to be afraid of really. Quiet street.

The apartment fully conforms to the description given on the site (the photos speak volumes). Sheena is a very responsive, welcoming and serious host. She answered - always very quickly - to all my logistical questions (arrival from the airport, nearest public transport, etc.) and was very understanding, particularly with regard to our luggage on the day of departure. The apartment has two bedrooms (1 single and one double) - including a double bedroom - and it is possible to sleep in the convertible sofa in the living room. Everything is very comfortable. There can be a little noise in the street in the morning in particular; drivers do not hesitate to honk their horns at all hours! The rooms are also very bright, especially in sunny weather; this may bother some people... It will undoubtedly be improved soon. Note that you are 45 minutes by public transit from Times Square, no change. No feeling of insecurity in the neighborhood. You are 10 minutes walk from the station (RER type). In short: a great welcome and a perfect base when you're on vacation in NYC! My children (two teenagers) and I loved it! Congratulations to Sheena!

We stayed there 10 days with my brother to visit New York. We did not have any problem to enter the unit. Having no windows was great to sleep, and the AC was also really useful as it can get pretty warm and humid in NYC in summer.   It was said in the description that there was some beach material (Umbrella, Blanket, Tuba) but nothing was found when we decided to go to the Rockaway beach. It was also said in the description that the breakfast was included, but there was nothing. Fortunately, the kitchen was well equipped so we had the possibility to cook our own meals.   The apartment was really clean when we arrived but we started to observe more and more cockroaches in the unit. I hope none was brought back to my own apartment. One night we even found a rat in the living room while watching the TV. It tried to hide and we never saw it again. We do not know how it managed to enter.   The wifi worked correctly and the TV as well. As we stayed 10 days, the lady that was doing the cleaning offered to change our pillows, bed sheets and towels, thanks to her. She also gave us more toilet paper as only one toilet paper roll was present in the restroom. (for a 10 days stay ...).  To conclude on our stay, the quality-price ratio was ok in spite of the insect pests (But hey, it is NYC ...). We would not have had enough money to stay anywhere else at this time of the year otherwise. I would also recommend to take the subway at the Shepard Ave station instead of the Euclid station as it is a bit unsafe near the Euclid station even though the Express train can be taken only at Euclid.

Sheena's place is FABULOUS. From the woodsy decor, to the starbucks freshly ground coffee, to the comfortable beds, to the quaint garden area with a waterfall and fire pit; every detail was thoughtful and generous. We would DEFINITELY stay here again when visiting NYC.  As far as the neighborhood, we walked from the apartment to the subway station in about 15 minutes and never felt unsafe.  If you're thinking about booking this place, go for it! You won't be disappointed.

Very nice art-filled cozy apartment with personality in a quiet yet hip neighborhood in Greenpoint, Brooklyn.  Great place to stay if you want to escape from the noise and stress of Manhattan or your day job.  Short walk to Greenpoint subway and all the restaurants and shops there.  Short trip to Manhattan or even walk to Williamsburg.  Really nice stay and plenty of freedom with the place.  I'd definitely stay here again.

The place was wonderful! it was very spacious with a large garden that was lovely to relax after a stressful day in the city. i can recommend the place for anyone looking for a quiet and clean place to stay in the area.

Some might say it's the real deal - a grand, traditional brownstone apartment in Brooklyn. We very much enjoyed our stay here. The flat was spacious, well-equipped and spotlessly clean. There was plenty of space for our family of 5 as one of the bedrooms has a 2 double beds and lots of storage space. Adina was our host who was extremly efficient and helpful. She even went to the trouble of buying us a DVD player whilst we were there as the apartment didn't have one. The neighbourhood is what could be described as up and coming. It has pockets of gentrification but still is very much a regular, vibrant area which we enjoyed. As we have young children we weren't often out late at night but I'd say there are probably safer areas (but definitely many that would be more dangerous!) It's close to the speedy subway express subway line A. We went to Manhatten most days but did visit the excellent Children's Museum, Prospect Park etc in Brooklyn. Can recommend a special doughnut bakery called Dough....

I was with Barbara for two nights. It was very nice. The house really feels like home. By the time I was there, Barbara worked a lot. So I did not get to meet her much. But she did prepared everything we need and it works out fine. Being on 1st floor means a lot to big suitcases too :) ... The area looks different from inside the city but nothing seems to be dangerous. There is McDonald 24hrs with wifi right across the station, I used it as a meeting point because sometimes we went to different places :) Thank you Barbara and I would recommend this place to stay for NY visit :)

Barbara was very kind.  We got stuck outside one day and she came to unlock the door for us.  It's located in Harlem so by metro it's about 20 minutes from Times Square.  I didn't like the neighborhood but I'm used to neighborhoods that are a little more disadvantaged so... It's not Manhattan but it's not a ghetto either.  I never felt in danger,

Barb was very accommodating in letting us check in early. Though Barb was very accommodating her apartment was not well kept.  -The floors were clearly dirty, uneven, and damaged.  -There were dust balls and dirt everywhere.  -The tub is damaged and needs to be re-glazed.  -The shower water smells like hydrogen peroxide but we think that's a New York issue just beware.  -There are no full sets of dishes or pots.  -The dresser drawers do not have bottoms.  -The heat does not reach the basement. -Cold air seeps through the basement windows. -There was no hand soap. -We were left with a sole roll of paper towels with 5 paper towels left on it with no additional paper towel rolls. -There is a random door downstairs that is duck taped shut with a towel stuffed at the foot of the door.  -The stair case is steep and slippery. -The bed downstairs is not on a bed frame it sits directly on the floor.  -The pull outs beds are basically covered spring boards.  -Both pull out couches cannot be pulled out simultaneously without causing a fire hazard.  -There are random screws hanging from the pipe on the ceiling in the basement at a 6'4" clearance (dangerous). -The mini fridges are dirty.  -The lamp downstairs does not have a shade.  -There is no iron. -There are odd amounts of industrial sized laundry detergent stacked in the living room. -There are only two washcloths. -There are supposedly clean but unfolded sheets in the linen closet. -There is only one ply toilet paper.  -There was dirty laundry in the hamper.  -BUT the 99¢ tea lights do offer a nice ambiance (lol). -There are NY trinkets everywhere and the oddest collection of books I've ever seen.  -Natural light does not exist here, but that's an NY thing.  -The "curtains" are fabric pieces taped to the window.  -There was hot chocolate and teas with a broken pot on the stove left for us to use to boil water.  -The grouting is a filthy disgrace. -The light switch and outlet covers are barely screwed on and cracked, some are even missing large chunks of the cover. -The furniture is wobbly or broken.   This is no ones home away from home. This is a halfway house in a safe neighborhood. This is my worst Air BnB experience and I've used hem across the globe. This just felt like a spare property that was dusted off for extra money. It's simply not worth the savings. Not at all. I want more than my cleaning fee back. I wanted to stay somewhere else.

Judy’s spacious lovely apartment was great for visiting our daughter in Brooklyn. Great location with access to everything we needed. Check in was very low stress. We would definitely consider staying here for future visits.

She is phenomena should take you around New York like you live here like don’t do the bike ride with her oh you really will enjoy are you ready ready we’re ready to act like a New Yorker then because those bike routes that she was like you are worth it really every moment I promise to you but it’s scary but I did not get hit like three times almost but it’s OK I’m still alive, the queen of New York Barbara five stars all the way around I can’t believe that woman she is phenomena I will totally be back trust and believe that. Now the 3rd would like to thank you.   3rd She was very nice and was a great tour guide she showed us a lot of great things in a short period of time and showed us all the best places to eat and how not to spend a lot of money on food when you can buy the same thing for cheaper uptown, takes you all around on the bike and gives you the real New York experience she has all the movie and show apps setup for you already and the bed is good just when you take a shower put it on cold instead of hot it’s backwards but she was a great host.

We spent 5 nights in Lori's apartment, with our 3 children aged 12 to 17. Ideally located and served by a multitude of metro lines (3 different stations nearby, one of which is 10 steps away), the apartment is pleasant, spacious, well equipped, very clean, in a small typical building. The convertible sofa bed is very comfortable. Only downside: the noise from the street, lots of horns and loud voices late at night and early in the morning in this rather lively neighborhood. This is the only downside to this apartment, but personally it won't stop me from returning because we all loved this rental. Lori is very cool and flexible, we arrived at 10 p.m., and were able to leave our luggage in the apartment until 2 p.m. on the day of departure. A quick word about the neighborhood: delicious brunch around the corner at Oxford Kitchen, very nice cafes on the way to Greene Park, Pathmark (superstore) 5 minutes away open 24 hours a day, no insecurity. For basketball fans, the Barclays Center is two minutes away!  In short, it's what we call a good plan!

This was our first time using AirBNB and I had the usual apprehension about the state of the apartment, meeting the owner and whether this was, in fact a good idea as I am quite fussy when it comes to cleanliness. I need not have worried! The apartment was small but newly refurbished, had quality furnishings and was spotlessly clean!  Meeting Izi was also a relief as he was friendly, experienced and professional and always contactable in case of any issues. Izi owns the building that is at the end stages of a complete restoration, and has created comfortable and safe spaces to retreat to after spending most days exploring this great city.  The apartment is fully self-contained and is equipped with everything you may need.  The washer and dryer in the basement were also very useful as we stayed for a month. The area is fantastic! A typical street with many heritage brownstone buildings just like in the movies.  We walked in the neighbourhood very late at night and never felt unsafe. There are many excellent restaurants, local supermarket (Gristedes) and great coffee shop (Joe) around the corner. Thank you Izi for making our first New York experience even better than I had expected! We will be back in New York later this year and I hope that you will still have an apartment available because as the word gets out, you are sure to be fully booked!

Apartment ideally located for visiting New York. There you will find all the main lines for most of what is to visit, particularly in Manhattan (including a metro station 50m away). Shops are also just a stone's throw away and a shopping center at the end of the street closes at midnight with even more metro lines. Downtown Brooklyn is a 15-minute walk away and the bridge is a 30-minute walk away. The apartment is ideal for a couple with 2 children for example. The bedrooms and living room are air-conditioned. Lorrie (the host) is super accommodating both on arrival and departure and the exchanges are pleasant. We were able to leave our suitcases there until the last moment for an evening flight and therefore fully enjoy our last day.
Very well located accommodation Close to metro stations and stores But Not very clean Unpleasant encounter with a cockroach

This was my first stay at an airbnb so expectations were moderate. Linda's place was decent. The place has character and history and is pretty clean. I would recommend the floors be repaired or touched up as there are a lot of spacing, nails sticking up from the ground and also very loud and squeaky. Live plants should probably be replaced with fake plants just for ease of maintenance.   Linda and her assistant were really nice but I confirmed with Linda the checkin process four days prior to arriving, which she stated her assistant would meet me at the location at 2pm. Not only did her assistant not show up, I also could not get a hold of anyone for 30 minutes which was quite disappointing (and scary since this was my first experience for airbnb). After I checked out I received a call from Linda 2 days later mistaking me for the current tenant. Not a big deal but some help on organization is recommended.

This was my first Airbnb experience and I am sorry to say probably the last.  I rented Scooter's apartment for a full month, paid well over 5000$ and got in return tons of grief.  It started a few days before my flight, Scooter got in trouble with his co op management for subletting his place and in a private text message asked me to cancel the Airbnb reservation and strike a private deal with him. When I refused he became increasingly unpleasant. At this point I tried to find via Airbnb another place to suit my needs but couldn't . This was not just a vacation I had important meetings set up  When I arrived, I was stunned.  The nice fully equipped kitchen Scooter advertized: the oven does not work at all & a small toaster oven was put in as replacement. The sink tap had to be opened in a certain angle only and if you miss the angle by an inch a powerful shpritz of water shot from the wall near the fridge right into your face.  The old air conditions, both in living room and bed room, have no remote control. I had to climb on sofas to reach them to turn on or off and in the bed room I even had to pull the plug out & the electric outlet had no cover.          The pillows Scooter left for me were so smelly there was no way I could put my head on them so  tired as I was after a very long flight, I went to Macys and bought a new pillow.  One thin summer blanket was all I could use.  A second somewhat warmer white blanket had large nasty dirt spots of something brown on it and for me was unusable.   The living room had no light at all other than a very faint lamp in one corner. In the evenings I was sitting in total darkness. I made this reservation about 2 months in advance and Scooter didn't bother to fix anything in the apartment not even replace a light bulb that was burnt out in the kitchen. He came to pick up his tuxedo and I showed him the problems. He promised to bring me on the following Sunday a clean warmer blanket and some lamps to light the living room so I can write (I had a dead line & could not write or even read in the dark). He never showed up. Since every contact with Scooter was nerve racking for me I decided to swallow all this and not contact him again in order to salvage what I could from this very expensive trip & for me a traumatic encounter with Scooter.    When the fierce storm hit NYC it turned really cold & I had no warm blanket and no idea how to heat the place up.  I became sick of course I got a nasty cold & cough that lingered on even back at home.
