I had a wonderful time with Gloria and her little dog Rascal immediately stole his way into my heart. The room is quite small as you can see in the pictures, but has everything you need. You can also stay in the kitchen or the large living room at any time if you want. You can also use all kitchen appliances including the refrigerator, which can make an expensive stay in NYC a little cheaper. Gloria is very nice without being pushy, which I really appreciated. The journey to one of the nearest metro stations takes 15-20 minutes, but can also be done by bus. Several bus stations are just a 1-2 minute walk away. Overall, I can recommend everyone to stay at Gloria's. The price-performance ratio was great and I had a great time!

This apartment requires a lot of upkeep. The additional fees charged for the apartment aren’t really being invested back into the apartment for up keep or cleanliness. The wooden floors pictured on Airbnb look beautiful, but in person are very very noisy, unsafe to walk on barefooted and are raised in certain areas. The curtains of the apartment in the living room/living area and bedroom are stained. The bathroom was not cleaned. There were stains present around the tub and in the tub. There were stains on the bathroom mirror frame and stains present in different areas throughout the apartment. There was food from the previous Airbnb renters/tenants still present in the refrigerator and were not discarded. There was also food left in the freezer. The neighborhood was very noisy until 3 am. You can hear everything. There were a lot of drunken people outside of the apartment speaking loudly, shouting and screaming towards the apartment. The neighborhood did not feel safe and not recommended for families with small children. It wasn’t the low key, quiet, picturesque neighborhood one would think would be Greenwich Village. The hallway entrance to the apartment is musty and old, and also requires upkeep. Part of the hallway floor is slightly sunken. The pictures make the apartment look modern but it’s not. I think the listing is overpriced and unfair. Left after one night. Had to book a hotel for the remainder of our stay somewhere else. Me and my siblings would not stay another night. We got no sleep and stayed sitting on the stained living room couch the whole night until we could leave. For the price charged the apartment should have better upkeep, flooring should be checked for damage under and as to why the flooring makes so much noise and is raised in certain areas.

This is a difficult review for me to make because I really did love the apartment itself. It’s really beautiful and old world feeling. The bed was great. However, I would not recommend renting this place. There is some sort of drug hand off site happening on the block and there were junkies literally smoking crack and shooting up in front of my face nearly everyday. One overdosed and passed out and we had to call the emt. If you have children or will be bothered by this DO NOT rent this place. Linda did not respond personally and when I told the other owner he said ‘oh that’s surprising, I’ll call the authorities myself next time.’ It was pretty appalling that neither of them seemed to think this was an issue. There were also two mice spotted and a roach in the bathroom. Also hot water is scarce. My advice is that the beauty of the apartment is not worth it.

It's a good place if you just need a place to sleep. It's a little out of the way to come back to in the afternoon to take a break from the city. We never felt unsafe but the culture of the city is different than what one may be used to. This is not to deter you from staying at Kate's place. It is very close to the J train and easy to navigate transfers to other trains to visit common tourist sites.

The apartment was very cute and clean, and having my own bathroom was really nice! Overall a really great place to stay, although I will say as a warning that the area is a little scary at night when you’re by yourself.
Everything was sooo Nice! I was afraid to rent on airbnb since it was my first time but it was perfect. Will never rent hotels no more

The apartment is clean, spacious, bright and quiet in a very quiet and safe area, I have never been afraid to walk alone in this area! The kitchen is huge, with all the necessary fields for cooking: utensils, microwave, coffee maker, toaster .... The beds were comfortable and clean, the space of the cabinets more than enough. there is the typical outdoor space with stairs. George was an exceptional host who met  every our  request. There is even free Wi Fi Links to Manhattan are comfortable, with a subway to 200mt, 400mt to another line, and 600m with another. You arrive in Time Square in 10-15 minutes, no more! There are also bus connections to the city center. The supermarket is very close and fully stocked. The nearby restaurants are great. Certainly when I get back to New York I will ask George to have the apartment.

I really enjoyed staying with Terri and her husband. It was my first experience with AirBNB and it was a really good one. I went to the city everyday and the subway is very close, a ten minute walk. The neighborhood is very friendly, I never felt unsafe and I got to the house sometimes pretty late (alone). The food around there is very nice (I went to the diner around the corner and of course some Chinese places). Also there is a supermarket nearby, which I really enjoyed.   The house itself is very clean. My room was very nice and tidy, very spacious for one person but two can easily stay there as well. There is an closet with drawers for your clothes and personal items, a stool, a verrry nice bed and Terri also left some brochures about New York City, very thoughtful. Also there is a television, with channels I really liked (as a citizen of the Netherlands, where we need to wait about a year for the good series to be on our channels). The bathroom is really nice as well. I liked the huge shower and the toilet and sink are fine as well. It was very clean and tidy. You get towels, so that was nice.   I didn't use their kitchen that much, but Terri invited me to eat there. That was very lovely of her. Because Terri's family lives in a room on the other side of their house we didn't run into each other that often. That is nice for your privacy, but if you want to see them you can find them easily. Also the communication is great. If you need anything you can contact Terri and she will help you out.   I really recommend Terri's place to stay if you are visiting New York City. I liked it very much and I would definitely stay there again if I would go to NYC again.

Its really a good place. I like the room and it is exactly what she described in the description. very neat and clean. Good part is , this is my first airbnb stay but it was very comfortable. She communicated everything very clearly well before which helps me  not to scare much. Definitely for my next trip, i will happily go to her place and will recommend my friends too.

Spacious and very bright apartment (not directly overlooked) on the 3rd and last floor without elevator. Note the room, very large and the vast American-style kitchen. However, a few points to improve: (brief) cleaning of the floors, bathroom door not being able to close completely and small minor water leak from the toilet.  We really appreciated the calm of the street (trees) and the neighborhood during our stay.  Halfway between 2 metro lines (B & C and 2 & 3), the 116th St stations are less than 10 minutes walk from the apartment. We also liked the walking distance to 125th St (Apollo Theater etc...).  We did not meet George Michael Weathers but his friendly assistant when we arrived and departed. Despite a last minute unforeseen event (canceled flight on the way out forcing us to shorten our stay by one night), there was no difficulty linked to this delay on the part of George M W. We discovered and really liked Harlem We recommend this apartment.

George's place was very comfortable and very well situated in south Harlem - an easy walk to train and bus stations. The apartment was really quiet and had lots of natural light and was well equipped with amenities to make the stay really easy and stress-free. Would definitely recommend staying!

I was really excited for this place, I have never stayed overnight in New York and after reading the reviews I had really high expectations. The first thing I would say is that the pictures do not really represent the apartment. They are edited a lot for lighting, it looks nice and bright but is in reality dim and a lot darker than what it really looks like online.  I noticed several people say that they loved the decor but in my opinion it was very dated, non cohesive and odd...I guess would be the right word.  Also, the parking was a nightmare. I was told I would not have an issue parking and that is absolutely not the case. Beware if you stay here with a car, you might need to park several blocks away and walk with your suitcase and it is up 6 flights of stairs so I had to leave my suitcase in the car and just take my backpack.  It was kind of a sketchy area and I was worried about the car all night with my suitcase in the trunk but it ended up being okay thankfully. I liked that it had a full kitchen but it wasn't really stocked well with dishes/silverware, there were a lot of random items in the drawers and food other people had left. It was just a menagerie of stuff collected from previous guests. Also there was a TV but not connected to anything, even cable. Overall I would not stay in this place again and I would not recommend it but if you don't have a car and have light luggage, it might not be as bad for you. When we had something come up and needed to leave early we could not get a refund for the last night we didn't stay which was disappointing. It was our most expensive airbnb on this trip and also the one we were most disappointed with.
Everything was as described in the Airbnb ad, easy and stress free check-in. Only stayed a night but it was great!

Ahmed was a gracious, attentive host. He gladly accommodated our late check in and early check out. He checked in periodically and encouraged us to use his metro card which I appreciated, since, it was a lot more convenient and a better way to get to know the city. Ahmed’s apartment was adorable, modernly decorated with lots of culture, the bed was very comfortable and a sparkling clean and roomy bathroom. His neighborhood was quiet and safe. Not once did I feel scared or uncomfortable walking around his neighborhood late at night. Close to all shorts of delicious foods and markets, short walk to the station along with a short ride to Manhattan. This was my first airbnb experience and I am very impressed. Thanks Ahmed!!

My wife and I stayed at Ahmed’s place for a few days over New Year’s and really enjoyed our stay. It is a great little neighborhood with some good food right nearby.   We were attending concerts in midtown Manhattan and the N train that goes right through there is only about 2 blocks from Ahmed’s apartment and is really convenient.   It’s quiet and away from the bustle while still being very easy to get to the busier parts of the city if you want to. It’s also very affordable.  Ahmed’s communication was quick and responsive which made for a stress free trip.   The space was clean and comfortable and we have no complaints about anything really. Overall a great stay!

Antony is the most respectful and friendly host. He greatly helped me with the many basic questions I had about living in this city for the first time. Great atmosphere in the apartment and all the privacy you need. The room has a good size for NYC standards and feels comfortable. Only issue is if your noise sensitive you should bring earplugs as the window goes to the street.  Nice area with grocery, laundry, gym etc all in close walking distance. Many restaurants and good vibe as it’s very close to Columbia University. I never felt unsafe walking around alone at night (displaying  the usual amount of caution).

marta’s very responsive and a great host! the apartment is very artsy n cute n close to a lot of public transport - a total steal for nyc :) its in a safe neighbourhood as well which is great for solo traveller - cant recommend this place enough!

Marta’s place was lovely, and the location is amazing. It is so close (literally right around the corner) to Atlantic Terminal which will take you anywhere in the city. If you’re traveling during the summer, it is important to note that NYC can be very warm; you are provided with a fan and shady open windows which helps a ton, but it is still warm inside. Marta’s place is beautiful, open, and calm in such a busy city. Such a great value!

My daughter and I stayed at Trevor’s apartment August 5 to 13. The apartment is on the ground floor of a three-story rowhouse. You descend half a flight of stairs and enter through a door that takes you from the exterior into a small interior hallway. I loved it! RESERVATION/COMMUNICATION: Grade A. Trevor was very effective at communication. He answered my e-mails and text messages very promptly. When we arrived he met us at the property on time and showed us around. Trevor was forthright in answering my questions and made me feel comfortable dealing with him. Checking in and out were easy. PRIVACY/HOSTING: Grade A. The entrance and the unit itself are very private. For being in the middle of Brooklyn the apartment was surprisingly quiet. I couldn’t tell most of the time that anyone else lived in the house. Trevor was there when we needed him but not intrusive. SUPPLIES: Grade A. The apartment had everything we needed. It was well stocked with cutlery, plates, glassware, cookware, towels, linens, etc. The coffee and condiments were a nice touch. REPRESENTATION: Grade A-. The apartment was as it was represented in the advertisement and photos. However, Trevor told me the sofa made into a bed. The sofa is way too hard and bumpy to sleep on. AMENITIES: Grade A. The amazing thing about the apartment was the private yard in the back. It has a wooden privacy fence and a patio with chairs. Where else in NYC can you find an apartment with a private yard and patio? The apartment has a cozy, homey feel. That having been said, I had two minor complaints: (1) the shower curtain needs a curtain liner; and (2) the faucet for the kitchen sink needs to be fixed. NEIGHBORHOOD/LOCATION: Grade B. The immediately surrounding neighborhood is pretty quiet and feels safe, but there are areas surrounding it that don’t feel safe. TRANSPORTATION TIPS/SUGGESTIONS: The closest subway station is the J train station at Myrtle Ave. However, that station is about a 9-block walk, and frankly if you’re walking at night you travel through some areas that feel unsafe. Here are my suggestions: 1. If using the J train, exit at Flushing Ave. Next to the station is Woodhull Hospital (corner of Broadway & Marcus Garvey Blvd.). In front of the hospital, take the B15 bus to Quincy St. Total amount of walking: 2 blocks. To get to the J train from Trevor’s, catch the B15 bus northbound on Lewis Ave. at Quincy and get off on Broadway at Flushing Ave. 2. Another option is to take the B or Q train (better than the J if headed to midtown Manhattan or Queens; going outbound those trains take you to Coney Island). To get to that station, take the B52 bus westbound on Gates Ave. (the street just south of Quincy) at Marcus Garvey Blvd. Exit the bus at the corner of Fulton & Flatbush Ave. Right around the corner is the DeKalb Ave. metro...

The unit was very spacious and clean, and Trevor was a very helpful host! He was always available to answer questions and was always very polite. The unit has a full kitchen with plenty of utensils and cookware if you need it. The only drawback for us was the location. The train station was just under a mile away, and certain parts of the trek were a bit sketchy late at night. It is worth noting that we did not have any unsavory encounters on our daily walks to and from the station. Overall, it was a great stay!

The apartment was clean and nice but we would not recommend it. It is at least 20 minutes from any train station and you have to walk through areas which seem unsafe. But what we really didn't like about the apartment was that it was impossible to cook anything. There's a fire alarm right in the kitchen and it will start ringing like crazy just toasting bagels! Maybe there was a way to turn it off but we stayed 7 nights and never met Trevor or anybody else.  If you are looking for a cheap apartment, you may like Trevor's but keep in mind you can only microwave or eat cold food.

We really liked the apartment ! It was big enough (we were with 4 adults) and clean and in a very convenient area for visiting NY: the subway was close. Also  a good connection to La Guardia with bus M60.  Just round the corner were nice places to eat and a good supermarket . We never felt unsafe, although I must say that the latest we came back was 8:00 pm. Diane and Craig were very nice people and did everything to make us feel comfortable. We would certainly recomment this apartment to our friends !

Our stay behind the red door II was very pleasant. The apartment is as advertised, nice and clean. From my experience, it is probably significantly better than a lot of hotel rooms. Diane and Craig were friendly hosts. The neighborhood, as  stated in other reviews, is also nice. We did not feel unwelcome, unsafe or encounter any hostile behavior.   We would gladly stay there again :)

When planning my NYC trip, I considered a couple of neighborhoods: Harlem, Williamsburg, SoHo. I honestly never considered Astoria, but Emily & Lou made me so glad I did.  They are super chill, super helpful, and their apartment is super clean.  TRANSPORTATION: I commuted into Manhattan every day, and Lou courteously advised me on the best way to get wherever I was going. The N train turned out to be proximal to everywhere I needed I go- Queens was much more convenient to lower Manhattan than I expected.  NEIGHBORHOOD: Their neighborhood is full of late night bodegas & cafes, should you happen to need to something. And being Queens, dining & shopping there is much more affordable than in Manhattan.   After dark every night, I walked home from the train station, and I never ever felt unsafe.   ACCOMMODATIONS: As explained in their listing, you will be sleeping on an air bed in their living room. The air bed is a bit squeaky, but completely comfortable. Emily & Lou are very courteous & tried to afford me privacy while I was there, so even though the room is not private it felt like it was.   This was my first AirBnB experience and it was definitely worth repeating. Thanks Emily & Lou!

We had a short time in NYC and Lou made it super easy and stress free for us. He offered to pick up our bags from Manhattan for a super small fee which allowed us to walk around and explore, and he even dropped us by some great restaurants. He also gave us a ride to the airport for a super fair price. He kindly offered both of these rides which made our lives super easy! The room was great- a very comfortable new air mattress, warm blankets, and a comfortable, clean, and welcoming atmosphere.  Lou himself us a really awesome guy- friendly and kind. He was easy to talk to but also gave us plenty of space.  Overall one of the best airbnb experiences we've had, highly recommend staying with Lou!

First thing: Lou is an absolutely amazing host, and I can see why he’s listed as a “superhost”, he gets all the stars.  I’ve used AirBnB quite a few times. But it’s always been the whole home, as I generally rent them with friends. I’ve never just rented out a room, and I’ve also never rented out a shared space. But for this trip I wasn’t traveling with anyone, and while I do have friends in the area I was mostly going to be flying solo. So I decided to give this a shot and I’m so glad I did! Pros: *Very close to LGA, between 2-3 miles. A cheap uber drive or if you’re light on luggage there’s an express bus that drops you off only a few blocks from his place.  *Transit abounds. Lots of buses, and a few train lines within less than a mile that will zip you right to manhattan if that’s where you want to go.  *Any type of food you can imagine is basically within arms length. Grocery stores, pharmacies, you name it, it’s close *Safe – I was often by myself walking around and never once felt unsafe. While it’s very near some very busy streets, the immediate area is a quiet residential one. *Clean – it was as clean and neat as any hotel I’ve stayed in. No insects/bugs. Everything was shiny and well taken care of. *Price – can’t be beat. Seriously – the price is so low that you might be thinking there’s a “catch”, but there’s not.    Lou was extremely friendly, helpful, accommodating, and very, very respectful of your space. While you are sleeping on a (very comfortable!) air mattress in the living room it never really feels like it. He’s very quiet and mostly was either away from the apartment or in his room. But when he was around he was a great person to chat with, and always ready to offer to make food, coffee, etc.   Cons: None??? Seriously I have no complaints/issues.   I would gladly stay here again, and will probably try to schedule my vacation so that I would be able to stay here again, because when you’ve struck gold once why tempt fate?

We stayed in the Red Door apartment for almost five weeks and really enjoyed our stay. The apartment is very roomy for a central Harlem apartment and it was an asset to have so much room. The bed was huge and super comfortable and the linen and pillows were of a high quality. The kitchen had all we needed to cook almost every night. There is a smaller room that can accommodate one person and that is handy if you are travelling with a child or a third adult. The apartment was on the top floor of three and you have to navigate a narrow staircase. Staying in Harlem is an experience on many levels. It can be noisy at times and sirens continuously wail. That said we never felt unsafe and freely walked the streets. For a different New York experience,​ the Red Door and hosts Diane and Craig would be hard to beat.

Diane is an amazing host and the apartment is lovely! I didn’t feel completely safe in the neighborhood (I’m a 24 year old white girl), because I had a few bad experiences with the homeless people the first two weeks of my stay. That gave me some anxiety and that’s why I shortened my stay. I think in general though, it’s a safe area. I was sad to leave, because I really liked the apartment!

[Warning] First of all, I would like to thank Tammy about the warm welcome and availability she was amazing. However Eni's flat was quite disappointing: no sheets, no towels and no curtains which leave you with people being able to see you from the street (and it's a studio so you cannot hide), sun and noise waking you up early the morning, dangerous wet floor after shower and unable to dry the dishes. The bed was... terrifying, still don't know how it's still up but every time you move the wood cracks from everywhere. It's really difficult to climb up and pretty dangerous to go down the ladder. It was so hot in the flat we could hardly sleep, waking up sweating af even with the fan on. Price is way too high for the quality as I am still wondering what was the $100 cleaning fees I paid for. And finally we saw a big roach that I managed to make leave the building. Yummy!

Eni's place looks lovely in the photos, and that's why it was so sad to arrive in a flat that just felt a little rough around the edges. Despite paying a lot for cleaning, I was still met with sticky drawers, crockery and floor, as well as a dead cockroach next to the fridge and human hairs (head and otherwise) next to the bed.   The bed itself is not suitable for anyone who doesn't fancy a treacherous climb. While the fact that you have to bring the sheets yourself IS stated clearly in the description, it doesn't take away from the fact that this is as almost as annoying as actually trying to put them on the mattress when balancing in the air with no barriers to stop you from falling off on either side (this also made me worry about my phone/neck during the night).   The plastic sheet on the bed was an added touch of sadness, as was the fact that you can't read in bed, for to get to the light switch you have to make that dangerous journey back down the steps again. It's perhaps better that there were no sheets though, considering the soiled air of the (broken) sofa and the brownish hue of the fabric shelves in the wardrobe. A bathroom mat wouldn't go amiss however, particularly on such a slippy floor, and it is difficult to dry plates with nowhere to put them and no tea-towel. Neither would a curtain; although the window had some 'misting' on them, it was still completely possible to be seen from outside. This leaves one with the tricky decision of where to change clothes- in a slippy bathroom or in full-view of the neighbors? This also brings about the problem of sleeping while illuminated by the green neon light of the neighboring church. While I'm happy to know they have prayer meetings every Thursday, my own prayers to be able to get to sleep were left unanswered.  I understand this apartment is in a big dirty city, that this is often the Airbnb experience, but this apartment deserves a bit more love and a bit more attention, and this traveler deserves her cleaning bill back.

Just spent 9 days in NYC and used this as our lodging for the entire trip. This place is very nice and was clean. The master bed was the most comfortable bed I've ever slept on. The linens on the bed and towels were very good quality. Pete's dad met us on our arrival and provided the keys. He then gave us a tour of the place and pointed out some necessary information. There are 2 subway stops about .5 miles away. One being the L train. It will take you to Manhatten in about half hour. The neighborhood is "interesting" and I suspect you get an idea of how true New Yorkers live. We walked to the subway at various times and never felt threatened. It was nice to have a washer/dryer for a quick refresh of some laundry. The master bedroom has a nice bathroom with a large shower. The main bathroom is nicely equipped also and it has a bath tub. The air conditioner works very well and we never heard a noise from the streets or neighbors. It is also very nice to have a direct access elevator that takes you right into the apartment. The pictures represent the apartment very well. This was an easy exchange and we enjoyed ourselves while there.

Chandle is a kind and hospitable host. He has great recommendations if you're in need of it. The apartment is always clean and well-managed. The bathroom is rather tiny, but the living space is roomy and you're surrounded by incredible art. The neighborhood of Sunset Park is wonderful. There's a lot of great local eats and the streets are full of families. I have never felt unsafe in this part of the city.  A bit of a heads up for summer travelers: be very, very mindful that there is no working A/C in the bedroom. There's a fan but heat rises, so the whole apartment gets very warm at night in the summer time. Chandle does his best to keep a breeze flowing through the apartment in the day, but opening windows at night invites occasional street noise and flying insects.

What a fantastic location with a 5 minute walk away from so many iconic landmarks and restaurants!   Andrew was very attentive and would respond to any query swiftly. Although he was not in town during my stay, we used Keycafe at a local restaurant and the check-in, check-out process was very convenient and stress free.   The apartment is completely like the photos. It was spotlessly clean and the shower had great hot water. The bed was very comfortable. We had been staying in hotels prior to this stay and honestly the bedding was on the same comfort level! The apartment was on the third floor. This for me was great as it minimised the street noise (which was only noticeable on the weekends and Andrew's white noise generator completely dissolved), but with a third floor apartment came three flights of stairs. Again, for me, this was not an issue at all.   There was no cable but there was Netflix and Hulu.   Make sure you head to Joe's pizza which is literally 5 minutes away and see if you can spot Leo or Bradley Cooper, and definitely check out Bantam Bagels for a very quick on-the-go  breakfast which isn't even a hundred steps away! Also Ramen-ya which again is a minute away - best ramen I've ever had. Washington Square park is like a 7 minute walk and the apartment is situated 5 minutes between two subway stations, meaning you have a very direct access to most of the city. We went everywhere from Brooklyn, Times Sq, Bryant Park, Upper West Side etc on a direct line which was SO convenient.   Thank you Andrew for a great stay!

Trevor's flat is really great, just like on the photos. Fast internet, TV, comfortable bed, nice bathroom and a small, nice terrace. The neighborhood has its special character. You can feel the real newyorkcity and not the touristic or chic part, however it feels quite dangerous especially during the night. The metro is 15 blocks away which is 15 minutes walk. (10 min during the night as you speed up...). There is a bus in 2 minutes which is a bit slower but definitely better than the metro. Good experience.

Andrew has got to be the best host through Air BnB. We got to NY a day prior to finding Andrew and could not stay in our original air BnB (no AC contrary to the listing, unsafe location etc.) and as a last minute fix Air BnB placed us here. Honestly, I wish we got to enjoy the property for that one extra day. Great location and great amenities, if you want to have the full experience of New York this is the spot to be in. The place was also incredibly stylish. Would 10/10 recommend and revisit!

Superb and Quiet Apartment in New York it exists!!! ;) I was a little afraid to be so high up in Manhattan to visit but the subway 100m away is an express.  The decoration is great, the neighborhood is great, everything was perfect, we will be happy to return. Lindsay paid little attention to us, perfect communication and is very responsive. I LOVED it Thank you!

I really enjoyed my stay with Seth.  He was very welcoming and I felt like I was hanging out at a friend's place.  Speaking of the apartment, it's about a 4 min walk from the L train and there are lots of restaurants, bars, grocery and drug stores around - and yet it's still a quiet building.  I'll be back the next time I'm in NY!

I'd never imagine my trip to New York without Sarah and her family.  As a first year University Student in Canada, I have always dreamed of traveling alone and visiting my dream city NYC. I had no idea what the trip would be like -- not going to lie, I am a bit of scared. I am extremely lucky to find Sarah's family on Airbnb -- the price is perfect for a student like me, the neighbourhood is quiet and peaceful, the location is very close (5min walk) to the subway station with many stores open till late night and breakfast restaurants around. The room is very tidy, spacious and bright. I felt like living at home -- Sarah and her husband didn't treat me like a guest/stranger but more like a family member -- they always gave me useful advice, asked about my day and gave me as much help as I needed. I still remembered one day I woke up to their daughter playing the piano (a very beautiful song) and Sarah and I ended up talking about our passion about music for half an hour. At that moment I just wanted to tell her how much I appreciated their host, and how glad I was meeting this family in this lively city. My experience with Sarah's family was definitely one of the top things that made my trip. Miss Melodie and Sophie! Miss NYC! I will be back soon!

The room was perfect, just as advertised! It was clean, big enough for one person and I could always use the kitchen and bathroom whenever I wanted to. Sarah and her family were really nice and welcoming, and I could always go to them if I had questions about anything. Sarah was really interested in me and gave me a lot of tips about things to do in the city.  The neighborhood was mostly hispanic, but the people I met were all very friendly and welcoming as well. I, as a 20-year old girl alone, have never felt unsafe while I was out and coming back to the room. I would definitely book this room again if I was coming back to New York alone!

Sarah's place is located in a safe neighborhood-- I never felt in danger as a solo female traveler.  She is extremely close to a train line that you can take all the way into downtown Manhattan-- I used it every day and it worked out fine.  Sarah and her family are so kind and made sure I had everything I needed.  If I'm in NYC on my own again, I will absolutely come back!

Sarah and her family are friendly, easy-going, helpful and maintain an exceptionally clean and stress-free environment. At no point did I feel I was vying for time in the bathroom or kitchen. Sarah has a serve yourself freely breakfast policy with a well-stocked fridge and cupboards.  The very pleasant guest room is well-equipped--enough drawers and hangers, a writing desk and a fan for the window with an unobstructed view south.  An extra kicker of having a fan is it helps neutralize outdoor sound when the workday begins as the subway passes nearby, and, hey, it's NYC.  I have no reservations in highly recommending this accommodation.

This was our highlight of our east coast trip! I have stayed a few times in NYC before and never had the pleasure of such a beautiful apartment. You get a whole apartment just for yourself! In NYC!  The apartment is exactly as beautiful as pictured and was easy to access for us. Ok - it is a bit far from the subway (16-20min walk), especially when you have lots of luggage it can be a workout - but we are used to walking, so it was no problem for us. The area is Brooklyn - it might seem scary at first but all the people we had a chat with were lovely and helping. We went through the area by night and nothing happened - I guess something can happen anywhere. We loved the charming area. The communication with the host was easy, quick and friendly. Thank you Trevor for the great stay - we really had a wonderful time in NYC. Would def book this again!

The area is somewhat sketchy    The pictures of the outside do not represent what the actual environment is    The sheet on the bed had a yellow stain on it     The refrigerator still had food from the prior tenant open food in it

Staying at Trevor’s place was the perfect way to end our USA trip. The metro stations are all 10-15min walk and take you everywhere in NYC you need to go. There are loads of shops and restaurants around. And the place is just as seen in the picture and as described. Pretty, comfy, clean and with all the amenities you need for a vacation stay. My partner and I were a bit scared coming here after reading all the comments regarding the neighborhood but at the end we did not feel unsafe walking from the metro at night or during the day. There was one incident, though, on Halloween, when we were arriving home late in the night and there was a large group of youngsters fighting each-other just on the corner of the street, hitting literally everyone who came on their path (although it seemed like it was two groups fighting each-other). That was the one and only time we felt unsafe, and we are used to all safe/unsafe neighborhood. The place is still worth to visit and rent, it is a great price for a great location. If you do feel a bit unsafe I suggest either taking an Uber (pool or X) from the metro station to the apartment and/or using Utica metro station (we found it was the best and the safest - A and C trains run there).

Livia is one of the best people I've had the pleasure to stay with. she is warm, hospitable, and very generous. Livia invited me to hang out with her and her friends for an evening when I would be just hanging out at this house. This is only one of many examples of how nice of a person and wonderful host she is. What's more, Livia is a fantastic cook and makes amazing breakfasts. When I come back to NY I will plan well ahead so I can be sure to rent her room again. Don' take your chances with someone who looks a sketchy. Go with Livia and you will have a first rate NY experience. Yeah Livia!

Beautiful place to stay. Clean and spacious. Livia was a wonderful host, very helpful with directions and great company.  Train is close by. My cab driver did not know the neighborhood and didn't have a GPS. Unfortunately I used Google maps which made for some stress in finding the place. I suggest using a GPS and maybe clarifying your route of choice with Livia before you come. Had I done this, it would have alleviated the stress. All other aspects of my stay were superb. Thanks, Livia!

Cannot recommend Livia's place more!! I needed a place to stay while looking for a permanent rental and a quiet comfortable space where I could work from home during the day and finish my masters thesis at night. Livia's place was absolutely exactly what I needed for all of my needs during a very stressful time. The room is Huge and the rest of the apartment is beautiful and spotless!! Book her place with confidence! Even though I found I great place to move into in Brooklyn, I was actually a little sad to go! A++ communication and hosting. The bed was heavenly, the electric fireplace was heavenly, the room was decorated beautifully and smelled amazing!

Julio's guest house was spectacular and full of charm! Dont let the Bronx "danger" myth keep you from this gem, everyone in the area was so friendly and diverse. It is barely a block away from the subway and walking distance to the Yankee stadium. I truly recommend it!

My husband and I recently stayed with Madison for 23 nights, and it was wonderful.  When we arrived Madison showed us how to use the coded door. We loved having a code rather than actual keys to worry about when we left the house. Madison has addressed the previous review mentioning not having a light to see - a sensor light has been put in and there was no trouble seeing.  The place was really clean and had everything we needed. She had left us a bowl of snacks and there was various toiletries and soap in the bathroom. There was basic cooking necessities in the kitchen - saucepans and pots, oils, salt and sugar. Madison was always available and willing to help us with anything we needed, and checked up on us via email every so often.  It is located on a busy street, so there is some noise in the kitchen, but as the bedroom is located at the back there was barely any street noise you could hear from there, only the occasional siren.  The place itself is a very good location. We really wanted to see it all, so most nights we didn't get back until 2am, and never had any problems walking around Bushwick. We always felt safe and the streets are well lit. Sure there was homeless people asking for change, but there was not many and it's the same all over New York.  Five minutes walk from the J train which takes you into Manhattan down to battery park, or to Jamaica station which links you to the AirTrain and to the Long Island Rail Road which we used to travel out to Montauk. It's also about fifteen minutes from the L train which takes you up through Brooklyn and to the East Village and Midtown.  Just around the corner is a supermarket, a laundromat and a chemist, which was convenient for grabbing supplies after getting off the train, especially with the chemist (rite aid) open 24 hours.  We would highly recommend Madison's apartment to anyone who wants a clean, cheap and spacious location from which to see all of New York State.

Alan was a fantastic host and his apartment is amazing!  From our first message exchange Alan was prompt and helpful with information about the apartment and answered our queries quickly. Alan kindly agreed to put up his Christmas Tree for us, which really was above and beyond host requirements but helped to make our Christmas stay in New York even more festive and enjoyable.  The apartment is even more spacious than the photographs show and is fully equipped with everything you might need. The fridge was ready stocked with all the essentials and even a bottle of fizz to welcome us. The lovely open plan layout is great, and the large comfy sofa is just what you need to chill out on after a long day sightseeing. Great shower too and comfy beds.  We absolutely loved the location, it was so much nicer to be in the East Village rather than the more touristy areas. We found brilliant bars, cafes and restaurants all very close by and Alan left us a list of his favourites which was very helpful. We would definitely recommend the Lucien French Bistro just a couple of blocks away, both the service and the food were superb! We had a wonderful time in New York and the experience was greatly enhanced by staying in Alan's spacious apartment, it felt like a home from home and Alan was a great host, we would not hesitate to book again in future.  Sarah, Shaun, Nikki & Rob

Fantastic experience.  What you see is what you get-- the place is pretty small, but it's cozy and clean.  Close to a number of different metro stops and lots shops and places to eat.  The neighborhood seems really nice, I certainly never felt unsafe walking back at night.  For much less than what a pretty bad hotel would've cost, we got to stay right in the city and have a nice homey apartment to come back to every day.  I would highly recommend staying here, and will probably check it out again if I'm ever taking a similar trip.

We are former NYers who were looking for a private, affordable space where we could visit friends and Madison's apt was wonderful. Clean, cozy, and beautifully decorated like the Brooklyn apartment we always wanted but never put enough time into decorating. Plus Madison owns the building so it's not like other NYC air bnbs where hosts are shady and ask guests to hide from other residents. Loved this place and will definitely stay again on other trips home!

I totally recommend Madison's accommodation, who welcomed us warmly and gave us good advice (transport, restaurants, etc.). The apartment, very cute, is well equipped for cooking in particular. The keyless entry system is great (no stress of losing keys!)

This place is such a steal. Great price for a great location. Madison is a super helpful host, and she put together a great little binder with any information you'd need. The bed is super comfy and the apartment is bigger than I expected!

From the moment I stepped foot in this place, I felt at home. I stayed for 5 months and the entire journey exceeded my expectations.   First, the house is gorgeous. It’s  filled with funky artwork and plants. The kitchen is great and there’s a huge table to sit and have your meal. There are many spots to hang out - it’s very spacious.  My room was a good size, with a very comfortable bed, drawers for my clothes and air conditioning. There are 2 tidy bathrooms.   Location wise, it was really easy to get around. I went into Manhattan for Uni everyday and it was a breeze! I walked around a lot and never felt unsafe once. And when I needed a delicious coffee, Routine was just a 8 minute walk.   Lastly and most importantly, the people who live there make the experience priceless. Gary, the host, is extremely kind and caring and a pleasure to live with.  If you don’t book this place, you’re missing out on something very special!

Pro: It was a very homey apartment. There was plenty of body wash, conditioner, soap, towels, etc. for us to use. I felt comfortable right away. It was like living at home. The apartment was also clean and organized. AC and the fan were great. The keyless door was also very convenient.  Cons: The wifi connection isn't so great, my phone disconnected a few times. It took some time to watch videos on my laptop. I couldn't use the TV cause there was no HDMI cable. The toilet handle was very sensitive, so I had some issues with that. The location isn't the best. It was a bit sketchy area especially at night, but that's almost every where in NYC. It took us about 30-40 minutes to get to places on the train. Despite the cons, I recommend this place to anyone looking for a place in NYC. Just do some researches if you want to travel far or stay around Brooklyn.

The location and accommodations were perfect. I especially enjoyed the spa like bathroom with waterfall shower and body jets. Perfect for washing the stress away. The location was close enough to walk to all the fun and activity while keeping that neighborhood feel of the block. I would definitely stay there again.

the price and location were great for my purposes the issue was the main host was out of town and the co-host kept trespassing and violating my privacy. I caught him twice in the space without my permission and don't know how many other times he has been in the space my permission. One of those times he called me from inside my space upset about something I did, then photographed my belongings and sent pictures to the main host. When I spoke to the main host and notified her of his behavior not 5 minutes after our conversation he came back down into my space no mask without permission and began to argue with me when I told him he needs to call or text me first and have a mask before he enters the space. At that point I was done and asked to cancel my reservation and be refunded for the rest of my stay and promise I wouldn't write a review(I thought she understood how inappropriately things were being run in her absence and was trying to do the right thing). She agreed but later asked me to do a walk-through with the psycho dude to check for damages, but at that point I was as already gone. When she suggested I do a walk-through with someone who has already over-stepped and violated me in so many ways I felt it my duty to write this review. Did she have an  inability to comprehend the danger of this guy's behavior or was she sleaze just like him I don't know. If best case scenario something was not reaching her brain helping her to realize how dangerous a situation she was putting me in she would definitely put someone else in that situation.

We enjoyed our stay with Seth. He was super accommodating and made sure we had all we needed. Quiet yet amazing location with every amenity within a few blocks including drug store, well-known restaurants, and subway line. Manhattan places are all expensive, but the location of his place totally makes it worth it. We would stay again!

What a pleasant surprise!  This was my first air bnb stay. I can only hope that my future air bnb experiences can be as nice as this one.  A wonderfully spacious and comfortable apartment. Timothy and Phillip are gracious host. I was in NYC for a work project, which in itself was very stressful.  It was so nice to come "home" to such a comfortable and relaxing apartment. I had to work on both the east and west sides of Manhattan, and the 2/3 trains were a quick walk, and the 4/5/6 relatively close as well. Pioneer grocery store a few blocks away was great - had everything I needed (I cook a lot and their kitchen had everything). There is a bed bath & beyond, TJ Maxx, marshalls, and a bunch of other stores really close on Lenox and 125th. Whole Foods opening up this summer!

Seth was absolutely great! He was super accommodating for my crazy travel schedule while I was staying in NYC and made the stay much less stressful. Also, bonus for the summer travelers, the A/C in the bedroom was on full blast, which was great since I arrived to NYC in super humid 80* weather! :)

The apartment was a steal in a great location. Mary was very helpful in the days leading up to our arrival. Everything went very smoothly. The next time I plan on visiting New York, the first thing I will do is check the availability of this quiet and clean sanctuary on the upper east side. Thanks, Mary!!!
Clean place, comfy bed, and not far from the subway; what more could you want when taking in a few days in NYC?   Mary was responsive and the keys came days before via UPS.  Easy and stress-free.

I chose AirBnb because I heard about it from my son's girlfriend.  I have spoken with a few friends who also use AirBnb when traveling.  This was my very first experience.    I was thankful that I found an apartment which was in the exact area where I wanted to stay.  The apartment had a good feel to it.  I liked that when I first walked in and took my first breath of air, there was no unpleasant smell, like in some hotel rooms.  I was thankful that the bed was very comfortable.  Did I have any problems?  There were a few minor issues that needed attention, which I reported to Mary.  Also, there are only a few inches between the toilet seat and the sink’s countertop and cabinet, so that was a tight squeeze for my hips.  I would have preferred to have queen-sized sheets on the bed (to go along with the provided extra blankets) instead of the 2 duvets that were slightly smaller than the bed, but my overall experience there was great.  The apartment and appliances were in good shape.  Her neighbors were quiet.  It is a nice neighborhood.  I would recommend her apartment to others.  Thank you Mary!

Mary’s apartment is lovely—stylish, efficiently designed and in a great neighborhood. It is conveniently located, a block and a half from the subway, and close to lots of restaurants, as well as grocery and drug stores. Communication was excellent, whether from Mary via messages (since she was out of town) or her friend who was available to address any question we had, and did so promptly. We had a wonderful stay and would love to stay there again.

The apartment is located in a nice Upper East Side area and is only a couple of blocks from the nearest subway station (and that subway station, unlike most others in NYC, is new and is air-conditioned) and within an easy walk of grocery stores, drug stores, restaurants, and more.  Make sure you are capable of bringing your luggage up and down several flights of stairs to/from the apartment, which is on the 4th floor -- and the stairwell is not air-conditioned, so I was a sweaty mess by the time I got to the apartment.  For some reason the address provided by Airbnb when I first paid for my reservation is not correct (one street north of the actual address), and I was given the correct address in an email from Mary two days before check-in.  The apartment is quiet (on the back side of the building), a huge plus for me!  The bed was comfortable and the TV in the bedroom had many channels to choose from.  The apartment was clean and, while not large, is not too cramped for one or two people.  The bathroom is small but clean and there's enough room on and around the sink for your toiletries.  The shower worked fine and had good water pressure.  It was easy to get the keys for the building and apartment at a 7-11 store very close to the apt building, and the building is very secure -- front door, then a second door (both lock automatically as soon as they close), and a second key is needed to enter the apartment.  It was warm and a big muggy while I was in New York, so the A/C unit in the bedroom (the only one in the place) kept me comfortable while sleeping.  It's a small unit that did not cool the rest of the apartment that much (aside from the bedroom), so I suggest that you close the bedroom door while sleeping to better cool the bedroom.

We were very well received despite the lateness of our flight. Jeffrey showed us around the neighborhood that same evening with his car, which allowed us to scout out the places before our trip.  The apartment matches the photos, everything is functional and well equipped  The bathroom is on the landing and is located on the 3rd floor. In addition, cold drinks awaited us! Alex the neighbor is very nice We did not enjoy the surrounding restaurants The very close metro allows easy access to Manathan and the neighborhood is very quiet and secure  If we return to NY we will return to Jeffrey's without problem

Had a great stay. If I need a short stay in NYC, I’d easily rent here again. Place was beautifully and thoughtfully decorated by Seth and was clean. AC unit in room. I was here on a stressful work trip and the room was great to come back to to unwind. Location allowed me to walk to places I needed to get to and the L train close by. He’s quick to respond and if you want recommendations -  just ask. Definitely recommend.

Elon's place is great! The apartment itself is probably the cleanest I've seen in Brooklyn! Also very spacious for BK- especially the bathroom! He has everything you would need, including netflix, a washer/dryer, a French press - all the good stuff. Also important- the building has an elevator- and not the old scary kind either. Right next door is a cute little restaurant/bar, and across the street from that is a cool little bar that stays open later. The apt gets tons of light, really a rarity in NY, so you might want to bring a sleep mask if you're not an early riser. I would TOTALLY recommend his place and definitely would go back.  Elon was super flexible when I had some schedule changes and was a gracious host. Thanks so much Elon!

Room and building were as advertised; no surprises. No frills, but an affordable, clean, comfortable room. Natasha is a very friendly and helpful host, and was very accommodating even though my arrival into Brooklyn was delayed by several hours. The room was a little chilly (I was there in early March of an especially cold winter), but a small space heater was provided which was able to heat the room after a while. Other than that, very comfortable and quiet. The neighbourhood is fine; just a typical working-class residential area in Brooklyn. I never felt unsafe, and the local shop owners were all very helpful. All in all, a great value; would definitely repeat. Thanks Natasha!

Natasha was so sweet and extremely hospitable - whenever I had a question or needed help with anything, she was there right away, and she also provided breakfast foods in the kitchen. The neighborhood was great, I never felt unsafe, and all the basics like groceries and the subway (2, 5, Q, B lines) were a short walking distance. Kind of a long ride if you're going into midtown (45min) but not a big deal, just bring a magazine.The house was a bit on the older side and the locks on all the doors were really stiff which was made getting in/out a bit of a nuisance, but Natasha is doing some repairs next month so hopefully this won't be a problem soon. There were other guests staying in two other rooms but this wasn't a problem for me since  I was out most of the time. All in all an amazing deal, especially if you're going to be out all day and just need a place to crash at night.. I'd stay here again.
Nice clean, fully stocked, and quiet apartment for an absolute steal. We enjoyed our stay, and took the opportunity to visit a bunch of amazing restaurants around the apartment. Thank you again!

This AirBnb is an 11/10 and a total steal. Out of the handful I have stayed in across Europe and the US, Lucien's apartment really stands out. Gorgeous artwork fills the entire space, floor to ceiling and wall to wall. Each piece is so interesting and unique, and it's lovely that the proceeds are put towards such a great cause (supporting local creatives). Lucien offered quite a warm welcome to his place, which is extremely well-located in a beautiful, quieter area of Brooklyn right near the subway. Very well-stocked kitchen and tastefully furnished. Thank you for an excellent stay!!

Linda is a good host. Her house is clean and tidy. She is nice and allowed us to make the last minute change to best fit to our itinerary. However, her home is a little bit far away from the metro station(abt 20 mins) walk n 45mins ride to Manhattan. And the bathroom has no knob. The door was opened by the wind when in used, which scare us.

Could not recommend to stay here enough. What an absolute dream. We loved the style of the Airbnb and also really loved the neighbourhood. So many restaurants, supermarkets, drug stores etc. we felt really safe here which was important to us. The apartment stayed nice and cool with the aircon unit. 10/10 would stay here again

Our stay with Linda and her family was more than we had hoped for.  Her husband knows NYC like the back of his hand. During the first few days of our trip NYC was overwhelming with transit etc. But Linda and her husband helped us have a remarkable worry free tour of the areas we wanted to go with a list of the subway stops we needed to take. I loved the distance their home was from where we wanted  to go because you could see everything worth seeing from the subway heading to wherever you go. We also enjoyed nights loving on their cats after getting home stuffed with pizza and pasta we ate in Little Italy. Linda and her husbands kids were adorable as well. There is a lot of love hope honesty and integrity in their home. We were scared to death about our trip...it was my daughter and my first time driving a long distance alone. Not to mention fear of driving in the city that is rumored to have thee most aggressive drivers which is very true. Linda made us feel at ease about getting there, and finding free parking near their place and bing boom bang it was unrealistically easy. Seriously! The neighborhood is very safe, clean, and colorful as well. I cannot wait to someday visit again soon with my whole family.    Thanks again guys we had a ball.

Excellent stay.  We were looking for a private room near a specific spot in Greenpoint, Brooklyn (a mostly-quiet, safe area with a lot of young families) and this filled the bill admirably.  Summer was a charming host, but we were left mostly in privacy, as we preferred.  Though she lived downstairs from us in a basement apt., things were eerily quiet, to the point that we didn't know if she was at home when we came in.  Never any shared-bathroom/kitchen conflicts or gridlock, even in the morning.  Everything was scarily clean and neat, and well arranged.  I liked the individual high-intensity bedside reading lamps, focused so as not to disturb one's partner, and the bed had a nice firm mattress.  Our bedroom opened out to a cool, shady back yard with some nice flowers (Summer's work), stately trees (probably not her work), and comfy Adirondack-ish chairs.  Though it's not shown in her pictures, Summer has a full-size fridge and there was ample room inside to store our OJ, milk, etc.  She also confesses to being the only non-coffee-drinker "within a 100-mile radius," so if you need coffee to wake up, bring your own coffee and maker, or take a short stroll to one of the nearby coffee shops.  Tea, OTOH, is available in profusion in her cabinet.  There's also a pretty-well-stocked Met Food mini-supermarket right across the street, as is large, shady, kid-swarming Monsignor McGolrick Park.  Highly recommended!

The apartment is beautiful and Yoki is an extremely hospitable host. It snowed the day we were supposed to leave and Yoki left us a message offering the apartment for another day in case our travel arrangements were effected.  This apartment is less than a block from a major metro station making is a great base for exploring the whole city. While not in the best neighborhood, we never felt unsafe walking around, even when we were getting back late at night.  Also worth noting: The apartment is outfitted with enough cooking equipment to make basic meals which we really enjoyed.

Yoki was very friendly. She took care of our arrival very well and even during our stay she was available to questions both through emails and by person.  The apartment is nice, clean and confortable. We only had a scary moment when the first night we saw a light in the kitchen, and it was Yoki. That's because the bathroom and the kitchen are shared with her, but we didn't know it. Concerning the neighborhood, well it is Brooklyn. Very characteristic and typical, a complete different world from Manhattan. We did not have any trouble and all went well, looking like a nice spot next to the Fulton.

Very fast responses  from Yoki, easy check-in, and clean apartment. The neighborhood was a little run down, and we had a run-in with a homeless person trying to convince us to stay at the apartment, but Yoki was quick to step in and take care of things for us. The close location to the subway and direct access to manhattan made it a good choice for those visiting the city on a budget.

This was our first visit to NYC and it was great! The apartment was very clean, cozy, and had everything we needed (iron, microwave, toaster, etc.) Suzanne gives very clear, easy directions and great recommendations for things to do. I was able to call and text her no problem. The apartment was not too far from the subway and bus stops. Given it was our first time to NYC, we didn't know the area well and found it to be just a little sketchy at night, but you can expect that with city living. We took the subway everywhere and had a great time, I would recommend this apartment! (Sam's Famous pizza nearby was really good)

Everything about this rental was as promised or better! Suzanne was prompt and thorough with her communication and all the instructions were acurate. The flat itself was beautiful and comfortable. Great big windows and a cozy bed. The neighborhood was not glamorous, but I never felt unsafe, even walking back after midnight. The 6 train is a five minute walk away  so all we needed was a Merto card and the island was ours! There is even a Target/Costco shopping center 2 blocks over. I would definitely recommend this listing and thanks to Suzanne for a wonderful weekend.

Great apartment in a decent location! We booked it last minute and it was absolutely perfect. Easy contact and instructions, not far from the metro. Can't say the area is amazing but it's close to so many good things. Never felt unsafe but I would just advise pretty general caution, as anyone should in a big city. But it was great!

Dan has a well kept and appointed, stylish apartment, in a professionally-managed building, that is located in a great and vibrant Hell's Kitchen neighborhood.  This location is very convenient to Times Square, deliciously diverse restaurants and cafes, smart shops, and the waterfront.  Dan is a fantastic and generous host, offering the practical touches needed for stress-free travel, answers to all your standard questions, and personal insights into what can make for a special and unique visit to NYC.  Highly recommended!

Dan was an EXCELLENT host.  Very attentive, made sure we felt at home and quick to respond if we needed anything. The location was perfect! So close to Times Square and restaurants.  The space was comfortable, clean, modern, easy to find and most importantly never felt unsafe.   I was travelling with my mother for her birthday and she thought we couldn't have found a better option.  I would recommend Dan's place to any type of traveler.   New York was a wonderful city and I hope to be back again one day!   Thanks again Dan!   -Merrilee and Carol Victoria, BC  Canada

It doesn’t say in the listing there’s no elevator and you have to walk up five flights of stairs with your luggage to get to the apartment. This makes for an unpleasant experience.   It doesn’t say that a dog is sprawled everywhere on your bed when you walk in. I don't mind dogs and knew one would be present but the last thing you want when you walk in exhausted at night is someone else's large dog lying on your bed blocking you. We had to wait half an hour for him to finally move. We would have just picked up and left at that moment if we weren't so tired. Please be courteous and keep the dog in your bedroom with you next time you have a guest.   No curtains on large bedroom window so street light floods into bedroom.   He complains about being spread too thin because he’s constantly going upstate to get free food from the grocery chain he likes to get handouts from which covers his grocery costs. Meanwhile he’s making thousands from his rental and still complains to us about the cost of washing our bedsheets. If you’re going to run a business and earn thousands per month renting room don’t complain about the cost of detergent, especially after you charged extra $10 per person. Don’t complain about bedsheets to a paying customer. That's like a restaurant complaining about having to clean your tablecloth.   We don’t need to hear that as paying guests. That is poor hospitality.   We agreed to a price and I took screenshot. I paid that price. He claimed he misunderstood the currency. I had to pay more in cash to him. He then gave me a hard time about cleaning sheets and saying we got deal, even though we paid exactly what he asked including additional $55 over two nights which more than covers sheet cleaning.   He was always getting into our business and asking personal questions. Made us feel uncomfortable.   It felt like a college slum. Located in a co-op. In a sketchy part of town. Yet he repeatedly stated he was giving us a deal. He repeated this so often I went online. Quickly found listing at Hilton for the same price and night and took screenshot.   Worst part is he didn't want to pay for a cleaner upon checkout so insisted we get out of room before agreed upon 11am checkout time posted on his listing.  Then he complained his car was double parked and he made us clean the apartment because he couldn't stay to do it. He had 'very important guests' from competing rental website coming.   We really felt like slaves to this man. We left the place impeccably clean. Yet when I phoned to tell him this the final straw was when he said we were 'taking advantage' and got a great deal. This does not meet the test of reason and is false. He took advantage of our family. This was a miserable experience.

Dan gets 5 stars from us in every category!  This was my brother and my first trip to NYC.  Prior to traveling, Dan sent suggestions for things to do, places to eat, places to shop, and other helpful tips about traveling in NYC.  This was priceless to us, because we knew very little about the city!  His apartment was beautiful, clean, and stylish.  It has a fantastic location near everything you’ll want to do in NYC.  Dan met us to “check-in” and showed us the details of the apartment.  He also checked in with us throughout the trip to make certain all was ok.  We can’t say enough positive  things about this trip!  It was amazing and stress free because of all the help we had from Dan. He gets an A+ for communication too!  We highly suggest booking with him if you’re ever in NYC and need a great place to stay.  We’ll definitely tell all our friends about his rental.  Thanks Dan, for letting us use your apartment and for being the perfect host!

I had a great stay at Jessica's place. I was met with a clean room, adorable space, and a welcome package filled with water, tea, towels, and hair dryer. So cute!   Apartment was quiet, got great light (very hard to find) and was charmingly colorful.  The subway is very close and the neighborhood is calm and friendly. I never felt that it was unsafe walking home late at night.   Jessica was very kind and accommodating. She is very friendly and easy to get along with. Thanks, Jess!

Aleksandra and Alex made me feel very welcome in their lovely, peaceful, clean and tidy home. I thought of it as my oasis from the bustling city while working on a project for 2 weeks. I can't think of a thing that they could do better... it was already the BEST. Everything was as shown. The room was comfortable, nice desk, and the big screen tv was a real treat. Awesome bathtub for a soak after a stressful day! Well appointed kitchen and great local grocery and little health food shop nearby. The L train is VERY convenient (3 blocks) and a very quick trip into the heart of the city. I should not oversell because I definitely will make this my first choice place to stay on my next trips and will need to book early : )
Everything was great, just what we'd hoped for. The apartment is extremely clean, comfortable, and spacious, and Nigel is friendly and welcoming. Close to a subway stop, supermarket, drug store, etc.

Alex and his wife Aleksandra were wonderful hosts. From the moment we arrived until our return (even an extra day due to my flight being canceled), they took incredible care of us. They have always been available, accommodating and caring. During the entire stay, Alex did a lot for us to make us feel good and safe in NYC. As for the room and the apartment, the bedding is very comfortable, the ceilings are very high (which gives a feeling of volume), the kitchen is very pretty and well equipped, the bathroom very clean (just like the rest of the apartment). The location of the apartment is of course very good since the L line connects Manhattan to the apartment in 20 minutes. Alex's advice on places to see and restaurants should be followed. Looking forward to seeing Aleksandra and Alex again, and thank you again for everything!

I was appalled on arriving at the apartment.  It was not how it had been represented on Airbnb.  The photos looked as though it was sparkling clean whereas it barely passed the “surface clean” test. I went out the first day to buy cleaning materials before I was prepared to use anything. In the room I was in I tried to open the window and the whole window just came off.  The shade on the window was broken and half mast couldn’t go up or down. All windows were filthy so that you could barely see out of them. In the pictures on line there is a large flat screen TV on the all. Well don’t be mislead it doesn’t work. The place is tiny.  I would have left immediately had I not prepaid $350/night for 21 days $7350AUD and could see no way of recovering any compensation.  Despite the money I couldn’t stand it and left a week early.

My sister and I loved staying here! The apartment is very spacious and recently renovated so it looks amazing. The kitchen has everything you need with Alex and Shalia stocking it with a few basics. The neighbourhood is a little shabby, especially compared to the home we stayed in. We were told by some people in Manhattan that the neighbour of Bed-Stuy used to be very dangerous and just to be careful walking around at night. Walking from the subway after dark was a little daunting but we remained safe. We did catch a cab a few times from Manhattan as it was very late. Overall, it was a positive experience with Alex and Shalia being very helpful, even going out of their way to let us store our luggage at Shalia's work the day we were to fly out. They were great hosts.

She is friendly but she don't like gust to stay at home, I said its late I'm lazy to go out and that kinda creep her out abit, also my friend just went here company me for abit. She seems shock when she saw there is someone else. I mean it was my fault that I did told her before hand, but this scared me. But she will give you a text if you didn't go home and wonder if you are safe. I break the policy by bring food to the room which I didn't read the policy obviously, so this just bring a awkward situation and atmosphere. So if you planing staying at home more often this might not be the place to stay. But the bed is extremely clean and professional so is the towel seems new , neat clean as well :)

The stay at Alex and Shaila's was great. The apartment has plenty of space. It's also spotless and well decorated (I noticed something new everyday). We used street parking with no problems finding a spot. If your looking to stay in Brooklyn this is the place I'd suggest.   The neighborhood is family oriented with a great block party mural on the street. There are several restaurants around but if your looking to go to the park slope or Williamsburg area, I suggest a cab. The subways are not too far away, if you prefer to take them.   Lastly, I was concerned about bed-stuy's crime in the past. I'd say those days are behind it. Some areas still have problems but they are far from the apartment and nothing out of the ordinary for a large city. Use your head, and everything will be fine.

Elise was an excellent host, and her apartment was ENORMOUS and the perfect spot for a summer Brooklyn weekend. The back patio is delightful, and I spent a morning doing some yoga in the shade and eating breakfast watching the birds. The bed is extremely comfortable, the couch is perfect for napping, the internet fast, the kitchen very well appointed, and the building perfectly silent. Thank you to Elise for sharing her wonderful home with us - we would come back in a heartbeat!

My partner and I had a wonderful, no stress weekend at Elise's beautiful apartment. Though we didn't have a chance to meet, Elise found a convenient way to get us the keys and provided helpful instructions for our stay. The space is clean, interesting, convenient to public transit, and larger than most in the city. Great host, great stay.

Alex was a good host. He made sure we were well settled in from the start and provided us with a small guide of his favourite places around Bed-Stuy (restos, bars, cafes, etc.). The place was exactly as described and as pictured. Very nice place, modern stove that was awesome to cook with, and comfortable bed after long days of roaming around NYC. My boyfriend and I were traveling to Manhattan and within Brooklyn, and public transit was not a problem. We also never felt in danger coming back at night. You will definitely hear their toddler running around and playing on the above floor but it was not a big issue for us. Also, the kitchen equipment was of very good quality, but not high in number (for example, only the necessary pots were available, which was  sufficient for us). Overall, we were very happy with our stay.

Mouldy food in the fridge. Dishwasher full of dirty dishes. Come home to Sheila in the apartment on our second day and was obviously not expecting us home, she was flustered and said there was a bad smell in the cupboard before we had arrived she was trying to get rid of. It clearly states that if they needed to access the basement which the door is in the apartment we were in they would give plenty of notice but we hadn't got anything except to our surprise when we walked in the door everything was open and she was roaming around. It was a massive invasion of privacy.  We had our stuff everywhere obviously just getting off a long flight and wanting to get straight out. I had a few packages which I had told them well in advance that they would be arriving and to hold onto them. One was open when I recieved them, even though it clearly had my name on it and they had been expecting them.  Alex is up at crazy hours doing dishes and walking around which sounds like an elephant clashing plates right next to your ears. The noise travels and is super loud. To be woken up at between 12 and 3am every night was becoming a joke. We kindly went up to ask to keep it down as the kitchen is obviously right above the bedroom he was super rude and tried telling us no one was up. But then the next day said he was up at that time. They obviously have no idea how loud it really is. And to be disturbed every single night. Who is up at 1am clashing dishes around honestly. Then you can never sleep in and make up for the broken sleep as the child is up screaming running and thudding so loud at 7am   Day 5 Alex come down as someone was knocking on out door apparently to check the electricals  No warning just entered and barged straight through the door and I had just gotten out of the shower. Again massive invasion of privacy! Our last night we thought we would get a proper rest for once before our flight, to my surprise wheelie bins were being dragged and rubbish bags going through it was so loud I thought there was a homeless person rummaging through the trash, nope just Alex at 1230 in the morning making more noise right out our window.  I think it was becoming entertainment for him haha such a joke I have honestly never experienced anything like this and if I had read a review that explained how noisy it was from above and that you can literally hear word for word the conversations had I would have passed straight past the ad.

Our 3 weeks stay with Christa and Zach in New York was a great experience. They are very supportive and welcome you warmly so you can feel yourself at home. The room is clean and brightly lit, with comfy bed, closet and dresser. We had everything we might need and guys always asked whether anything else is required to make our stay better. The only concern we had was temperature control since we came in the middle of July heat wave to NYC and there was not enough air circulation however this issue has been fixed straight away the first time we mentioned that by adding stronger fan.  The house is 5 minutes walk from the subway and even late you can easily reach it from Manhattan by 2 various trains so we never had an issue coming back. There are also grocery stores couple of blocks from the house, as well as drug store which is very handy.  Thank you Christa and Zach, you made our stay perfect!

Thanks Caitlin for such amazing gracious hospitality.You made my first stay in NY stress free and I felt completely looked after by this lovely woman.Caitlin has a gorgeous apartment in a really nice area .Not once have I felt unsafe actually quite the opposite, with people going out of their way to help.Having Central Park so close is just such a bonus and easy walk to a lot of art galleries/museums .Straight forward location for accessing all areas by a short walk to subway...and the bed is OUTSTANDING..ten outta ten Ms Caitlin

Jo’s home was a comfortable and convenient stay with he being a very welcoming and helpful host. However, the pet dog kept on the upper floor was untamed and very prone to attack at any moment upon entering. Great place, great host, but not the most comfortable regarding safety and pet management.

Wasn’t what I was expecting but I think I’ve come to realize for New York it’s what to expect for the price point.   There was a pool of water in the bathroom  from another guest. Joe quickly tended to it and cleaned up.  Was a bit of mould in the corner of the room I was staying in, but Joe did allow me to move beds.  Good spot to rest your head. I don’t think you’d want to spend too long in there!   Can’t complain. Was safe and could leave my stuff unattended in there without fear of it being stolen.

Unsanitary and unsafe, nothing like photos in ad.  Sign in bathroom that guest is not to flush used toilet paper down toilet! Feces and urine stained t.p. is to go in a waste bin inside the unit!?!Completely against all health and sanitation codes. Filthy and shabby, cluttered entry.  Kitchen sink dirty with molded sponge. Beds not memory foam as advertised. Wet towels left in room and hanging in closet. Shower in kitchen area and half hidden by fridge! Loose chickens and a rooster roaming on property. Back entry/stairwell up to yard a death trap with hose and trash in the way. Filthy chicken coop, wood piles, garbage, in yard. Solvent smells coming through the one window in the unit.
