I had some difficulty communicating with Kevin in advance of arrival and then got locked out after coming back from dinner at night - both which were pretty stressful. Overall, this wasn't the smoothest or most comfortable arrangement, but Kevin's generosity (he offered me rides from the station and to the airport) and good-naturedness helped to make up for it. He does need to be there to let you in, so be clear about when you will arrive, and he will do his best to take good care of you!

The room is great, and Diana is wonderful! Th location seems a little bit dangerous, but it turns out that actually it is fine. Diana will also tell you lots of tips for living in the area and they are really helpful!

Gary was a very responsive host who I was able to reach easily. Checkin went smoothly.  The location of the apartment is great, it is next to a pharmacy, police station, and two train stops.  Unfortunately the common areas apartment was very messy upon move in. The kitchen trash was piling up and had overflowed from the trash can and was smelling. Furthermore, the bathroom trash was overflowing, there was no toilet paper, and bacteria stains were present on the shower curtain.  The private room was clean, had a well made (although slightly uncomfortable bed), and treats. It was enough space for two people. There is no available closet to hang clothes but a three-drawer dresser is available. A desk and some door hangers are also present.  Apartment was well insulated and there was minimal noise and cold coming from the outside.  The other rooms in the apartment are owned by other people and one of the rooms was rented out to guests by another tenant/landlord. We had issues with these other guests which could not be resolved because they were not being hosted by Gary. These ranged from noise complaints to cluttering the common space. Unfortunately the apartment is shared by multiple people, so if issues with other tenants arise, Gary has no say over them or rules for the common areas.  One of the room mates as in charge of checkout and cleaning after we had left. This was never communicated to Eli’s and she was quite rude as she insisted we checkout at 9 am (15 hours before the listed checkout).   For the space, the apartment is a decent value. But, I would not stay here again due to cleanliness issues and the fact that other tenants are not being hosted by Gary. It created for a very messy, unpleasant, and univiting environment. The location is good though.

I was at us Open and the location is comfortable for visiting every day. I liked the district more. Kabak and his family are very helpful, kind and always trying to help. They have a big dog and I was always afraid of him :) They open the door at any time whenever I come. Metro is very close and there are a number of Russian speaking stores what I liked too.

We stayed at Jing's apartment for a whole month in Harlem. The property is a little expensive for its location - we found the area really sketchy, lots of crazy people screaming at passers-by daily - thankfully we never came back too late, as it probably is more dangerous then. If we knew NY better we would have booked another part of town. Jing was a lovely host however - great communication, and had some great tips. The apartment wasn't cleaned properly when we arrived as her cleaner cancelled last minute - not her fault - but we did have to clean it ourselves (remove hair from the shower plug, clean the rug which had dirty paper plates hidden under it), and there were about three days the wifi didn't work (again, not Jing's fault, maybe it's just the area's connection). It's small and cosy so be prepared for New York sized apartments, and I would say only book if you're not worried about sketchy neighborhoods - on our first day we saw three separate fights happen on Lenox Ave! Yikes! We love Jing though, we just wish she was the owner of another apartment. She's so accommodating and sweet and even gets each guest slippers, and ensures everything is stocked nicely (we had plenty of soap/towels/washing liquid etc for the whole month). Thank you Jing :)

I overall enjoyed staying at Jings apartment. The house is located really close to the subway station, so you are there in no time if you are out exploring the city. No long walking around the neighbourhood. The neighborhood itself is ok, its more residential and has lots of churches in the same street. The occasional homeless person around the hospital, but I felt relatively safe. In the house itself there are lots of younger people (from who I met) and it is overall relatively quiet.  The apartment itslef has everything you need, especially if you stay a little longer.  You can cook, sleep, and wash (in the basement, but its clean and nobody steals it). The only thing is that it was not cleaned properly when I arrived, but Jing had someone come and clean it, thankfully. The appliances in the place are functional, but relatively old. If you do not mind that, the place is perfect. It is ideal for an individual staying longer. And the communication works well, Jing responds super fast and is always helpful.

Matt made sure to send me all of the details before I arrived in Brooklyn. Directions for grabbing the apartment keys and the convenience of its location made our arrival smooth and stress free. The apartment was very clean with towels and soaps provided. This place is definitely worth the price and I would definitely stay here again!

- Very clean accommodation with all amenities (4-burner gas stove, oven, microwave oven, dishes, refrigerator, bathtub, numerous cupboards) - perfect for a couple, - 15 minutes from the metro on foot (station: Myrtle Avenue line M or J), - Many convenience stores nearby, - No blackout curtains on the windows, - Owner not visible (collection of the apartment key in a lock-box) but enough available by phone or text message, - TV: box with replay or pay-per-view shows (no live channels), - No possibility of storing luggage for the last day (if flight at the end of the day).

The apartment was very clean and nicely designed. We really enjoyed our stay. It's also quiet in the evening. Although we didn't get to meet Jeremy, he was responsive whenever I messaged him. Also, he had great suggestions for restaurants. The subway station might seem a little sketchy, so we usually took the uber home in the evening.

A place that is really close to JFK. Just about 10 minutes drive. The thing that mattered to me the most was free street side parking and easy commute. There were no tolls nothing to be worried about whatsoever gave me a big relief. I guess each of us would be anxious about different things and to me it was the stress of the long travel followed by finding the location. There were a bit of issues in google maps showing the exact location, it was kind of going around in circles, but kevin was on the phone all the time to guide me.   Other than this, the rooms were as described, very apt for a nights stay but then for those who are really jet lagged and wanting to get a quick nap, this would be ideal provided you dont get a noisy neighbor in the other room as even the slightest ruffle of a plastic bag can be heard !!

I love that Kevin's place is close to the airport and so eliminated the need for undue stress about arriving on time. It is a little space, not luxurious, but was adequately heated for the terrible weather., and adequate for short stays. Kevin got out of his bed to meet the cab since we were a bit lost. A Caribbean girl, I arrived without any cold weather clothes and Kevin loaned me his hat and jacket. I would be happy to stay for an overnighter again.

This is a great space in a great neighborhood! The apartment is cozy and has everything you need for a comfortable stay. The music at night is not at all intrusive and is barely audible during the day time. All in all this place is a steal and I would definitely consider booking again on another trip up.

I was torn on giving this place a bad review because I know running an Airbnb is hard, but after seeing the host attack the last person that gave a measured, reasonable negative review I don't feel bad. This place has bad vibes and fundamentally it comes down to poor hospitality. The space and host really make it feel like it's incumbent on you to please them and not the other way around. We never received a check in text at any point to ask if everything was okay. The only unprompted text was one accusing us of smoking inside as we were quietly eating dinner. The curtains are transparent and the host walks by them all the time, and I know it's been brought up in past reviews. There was half a roll of toilet paper here. The art is creepy, we were given the wrong wifi password, but really, seeing the host call a guest a Karen just set it all up for failure. Like dude, you're a white person that owns an Airbnb in a gentrifying neighborhood. How are guests supposed to feel welcome when you attack people who are unsatisfied. Some people just aren't cut out for hospitality, and this is one of them. We're in a similarly priced Airbnb in the same area now, and are much happier.

Great appartment, very clean an easy to find. Shelly was a great host, very accommodating. She let us drop our bags off early, and gave us some great tips for food and activities in the area. The neighborhood is a little questionable but at no point did I feel unsafe. The loft that you stay in has nice privacy.

Definitely worth the price. The hosts were friendly, easy going and down to earth. They let me ck in a couple hrs early and leave my bags while I went to the museum after check out. It was a straight shot to the subway lines, but about a a 7 block walk, however, I enjoyed getting my steps in. There's a little bar on the corner that has really good fried chicken and 2 dollar shots on Tuesday's. The rooftop view was amazing. I got up early to catch the sunrise and even saw a sunset too. Malachi was a great conversationalist and I learned a thing or too during our talks over tea & coffee. The only gripe I have was that the wifi would not work consistently or for very long, (the host tried to fix it several times, but it kept shutting off, so I decided to forget it), there was an unpleasant odor in the kitchen area, gnats and a few ants that I spent more time than I'd like to have trying to kill. Also, the linens had hair on them and the floors were a little dusty in the room, so I kept on socks. Other than that, I'd return again, as it was a well kept beautiful space for the most part

The place that Shelley owns is absolutely beautiful! The rooftop really adds to the place and for the price, it is quite the steal. Shelley was also very accommodating when I asked if a friend of mine could stay over one night. Sometimes it can get loud though since the room has no doors, but it is easily solved with earplugs!
Avon is wonderful! He is a super attentive host and sets the area up wonderfully for guests. He was incredibly helpful and accommodating. He made the stress of planning a trip very easy!

Shelley and Malachi are fantastic hosts and this listing is a steal! The apartment is in a fantastic location within Brooklyn with easy access to the trains you want. I didn’t find a whole lot of good eats or attractions in the immediate area outside of the bare essentials but it’s simple enough to hop a train to where the city life is. Keep in mind that if you’re visiting on a weekend there might be some hard partiers and your rooftop access is shared with the adjacent unit. If that sounds like your thing, more power to ya! Thanks again to the hosts, I’d definitely pick this spot again!!
Nice room in Brooklyn Very comfortable and with a good view Shelley very friendly and helpful Good option in the area although the neighborhood feels a little unsafe

First time in New York for me. Enjoyed our private room and bath along with a rooftop patio. Location was close to the subways which is where we did all our traveling to the city. Neighborhood was a little sketchy late at night but we had zero problems.

Shelleys place is OK. The area is not up n coming in any way. The description was very deceiving to us. It is also pretty far from everything - even getting to Willamsburg, Brooklyn or Downtown Brooklyn was WORK so imagine getting to the city. We just found the location description very deceiving as that direct street was not up n coming in any manor. We literally saw kids robbing someones chain off of them at our train stop (Utica). The room and bathroom were not clean and didn't seem to be cleaned from the previous guest.  For such a late check-in, I expected the place to be in a lot better shape. The best part of the place was the access to the rooftop. I honestly wouldn't recommend this apartment... especially to single girls. We should of done our own research on the area rather than trusting the description, so maybe that's on us. Other than that - thank you for letting us stay at your place, Shelley!

My boyfriend and I really enjoyed our time at this stay! Quick recap of our time there: Check-in was very seamless although a bit sketchy at first because the walk to the stay is behind the addressed house and was poorly lit; the key was inside a lockbox like it typically is with stays nowadays. The room was quaint and spacious with a full kitchen and small fridge. Bathroom was a good size although the shower was small. Host equipped the stay with essentials like garbage bags, cleaning supplies and bathroom supplies (soap and lotion), which was very appreciated. He even packed the kitchen with a few of our favorite snacks! AC/Heat control through a remote control was also appreciated. We recommend this stay, as we would enjoy staying here again.

wasn't able to stay here with my wife and baby since we pulled up to the listing and witnessed a hit and run. The person got out of the vehicle and harassed us since we saw it happen. Was totally unsafe to stay there in fears of being attacked by this person and our vehicle vandalized. So we had to leave and get a hotel else where.

Great stay for a few days in the city. The host was super responsive and helpful with any questions we had. The only concern was walking to the place in the dark from the subway station as it was a little sketchy but overall a good stay for a few days!

We arrived in New York City and the owner of the original apartment we rented through AirBnB on the island of Manhattan didn’t respond.  Paul’s place was suggested to us, and we were thankful to not be homeless in the snow!    The apartment is large and very warm and comfortable.  Guests will enjoy lounging in the living room and the luxurious bathroom.    We were planning on staying in the city, so the commute on the ferry was exhausting due to our expectations.  When staying here and going to the city, do make plans to go and stay for the day, it’s not a timely endeavor to go back and forth.   Upon arrival with luggage, wait for the bus at the ferry terminal!  Or choose another route other than straight up Hamilton Avenue.  That hill is for real.  There are other paths that spread the altitude climb over a greater distance at a more subtle slope.    Paul was very quick to respond.  The apartment was wonderful.  The beds were very comfortable.   The bus stop is literally on the corner of the property and an easy five minute ride to and from the ferry station, and the ferry is an 8-10 minute walk away.   Allow generally 1-1.5 hours to get from the apartment to any destinations in the city.

Do not rent here, it looks nice but it isn’t. I stayed here for 30 nights and left three nights early! It’s right across the street from a high school, daily fights outside your door. Cops everywhere. At night you will have drug dealers outside your window talking about all the girls they have slept with and the guns they have. Cars racing and subwoofers booming all night on the street. You may have to park on the street, and the owner rents out the driveway to people, one of whom drives a beat up car that sideswiped my rental. The tenant downstairs plays rap music every night until 2am and you can feel the bass on your pillow. The owner tried to make a side deal with me to bypass Airbnb and when I denied he turned mean towards me. Very bad place to stay. Avoid. SO SHADY!!!

This home was exactly as described!    The rooms were spacious enough to fit all of us. We were 2 families of four traveling together, and we didn’t feel cramped at all. There enough room in the closet, not only to hang our clothes, but to comfortably put our luggage away.   Amy was a wonderful host offering tips on where to eat, how to find the train etc. She was quick to respond to any of our questions. Plus she had amenities like a fully stocked kitchen, shampoo, conditioner, soap, new toothbrushes, a hair dryer, and a washer/dryer machine. While the washer does not hold a lot of clothes it gets the job done and at least we didn’t have to come home with a suitcase full of dirty clothes.   The neighborhood is quite and we never felt unsafe in the area.   Most importantly, everything was clean!  Spotless!  We couldn’t have asked for a better place.   The only con for us, was the distance to and from the city. The Q train was about a 7 min walk, not bad.  However, it took anywhere from 35min to an hour to get to and from the city, depending on the time of day. If you are riding during a busy time and the train is full, you may have to stand the whole way home (we did one day). Still, the apartment was totally worth it! You wouldn’t be able to get a space this size, for the same price in the city.   We would most definitely be happy to stay here again anytime!
Extremely clean, and a truly great location. Sharon and David were responsive, accommodating, and made the entire stay stress-free. I hope to visit their space again on future trips!

Unclean. Unsafe. Uncomfortable.  Honestly, I think my conversation with Kevin on WhatsApp covers what you should be prepared for:  Me, Day 2: “Good morning, Kevin. Just wanted to touch on a few points after my first 24 hours here and second night at your place: 1. When does the daily water supply get replenished? 2. How often are the common areas cleaned? I traveled to NY with my husband and our two young children. Ms. Sheila’s place is very nice. She put a lot of extra thought into making it comfy yet stylish. The pullout sofa for the kids was extra soft and they loved the fuzzy blankets. She even had children’s books to entertain them. The decorations throughout the apartment were very nice but not too much so I wasn’t afraid my kids would damage anything. The bedroom is really large for NY and the bed was super cozy. It wouldn’t be fair not to mention hearing cars on the highway but if you are a deep sleeper or accustomed to city sounds you will be just fine. The bathroom shower is awesome. The kitchen has everything you need. Having a place to prepare meals was great. I also appreciated seeing condiments and other “I failed to pack” items in the apartment. It’s a super quiet neighborhood, very easy to get to and a convenient location. We will definitely stay here again. Thank you Ms. Sheila!

Shay’s place was absolutely perfect. After traveling overseas with our kids for three weeks we were really dreading spending one more night near the airport before our red-eye flight home in the morning. Shay’s place made everything ok! A quick 6 min taxi ride from JFK and we were at her spotless, comfy and very well-appointed place. Communication before, during and after our stay was excellent, quick, and super friendly. Check in and check out were a breeze. The sleeper sofa was comfy, but the bed in the bedroom with its fresh soft bedding was possibly the most comfortable bed I’ve ever slept in! Thank you so much, Ms. Shelia, for turning what could have been a stressful night into a lovely experience. We’ll be back for our next flight!
Sheila is such a great host! She was answering my questions immediately and the place is so neat and clean! The next morning we casually walked to the car without any stress to JFK!!

Sha’s place had that homey feeling, it was welcoming clean and comfortable, it smelled Amazing everything was organized just as if I was at my own home. She so detailed with everything I didn’t need nothing extra because everything was right there for me, in the direction and instruction she provided even the cold bottles of water ;-) she checked on us (thru message) just to make sure we were okay and our stay was as comfortable as can be, If I had any questions she was so fast with her response, her communication made me comfortable, She asked us to let her know when we arrived so she could make sure we were okay with the access to the home we arrived extremely late I was afraid to message her so late but I did what I was asked I couldn’t believe she was on point and ready to respond when needed Thank you for that!  never been to NewYork and not be able to find parking right in front of where I was staying it was so convenient made me feel lucky every time I pulled up lol. Thank you for being a great host, I look forward to booking with Sha’s place in the future.

He is unprofessional and, I believe that His actions were disrespectful. He charged  $44 but only refunded $36. He is a scammer so be careful someone like this don't deserve to serve people like you and me. I have reported and have his apartment looked into. Him waiting  at the last minute to cancel was unforgivable. But you see “karma is a bitch” so just wait your turn! I pray none of your family get in this situation of being stranded on the roadside!!! PLEASE DON'T USED THIS AIRBNB THE OWNER IS “VERBALLY ABUSIVE” AND WILL CANCEL AT THE LAST MINUTE SO HE CAN  TAKE PART OF YOUR MONEY.

I booked Kian's place as I needed somewhere to stay when visiting family. I found the check-in to be easy, and the space extremely clean and homey. Kian even had bottled water and juices for me in the refrigerator! My 5 nights were completely stress free. The private room was immaculate, with queen sized bed, new sheets/pillows and cable TV, plenty of closet space. Large living room as well. Chris, the other resident, was friendly. The street is quiet, apartment across from a grade school and park. I plan to book Kian's space again when I return to Brooklyn. Thanks Kian!

The owner is a major control freak who will constantly message/call you about your status.   Times Kevin has imposed on me throughout this reservation: #1 - Upon reservation request, he told me I need a working phone so that he could call me when I was on the way.  I told him I needed to catch a JFK flight but he assumed I was landing #2 - Upon him confirming my reservation, he backtracks and says that I need to send him a real picture for him to accept my reservation. I promptly uploaded a picture of myself to my airBnB profile #3 - When I'm on the way to his place I call him to update him. He tells me he will send me pictures as directions. It is largely a pointless call, where he asks me my name and rejects my telling him to call me by my English name. I suspect he's just trying to size his guests up #4 - When I'm at his place I look through his pictures (which is him just pointing on the street and is largely unhelpful). When I'm unable to get in I call him for directions. I detail to him about my troubles and instead of letting me know the directions step by step he keeps repeating the same question and starts getting angry through the phone. #5 - Eventually we figure it out and I get in. At this point, I am exhausted and stressed. He then starts listing off all of the house rules and the "necessary" information and tells me "not to hang up".   I was patient throughout all this and got through it, but this was not a pleasant experience at all. Talk about not being smart -- how about providing us with a map and listing out the directions on the AirBnB page? Not only would that require less work on the host but it would be much more convenient for the tenants.  The tiny room isn't much to speak of either. The entrance opens up to a creepy stairway to a dingy basement where the rooms are located. The blanket is so small that it covers a fraction of the bed. The bathroom is shared and dirty. I would not want to use the shower if it depended on my life. He leaves a bottle of water and a couple of granola bars as "accommodation". There's wifi and a heater at least..  This is less of an accommodation, more of a real-life horror movie experience

We loved our stay in Queens!  Pros: It was very clean! We appreciated the sweet touches like juice for our kids and a spare high chair. It was the perfect space for us- 2 adults and 2 toddlers. We fit two pack and plays in the bedroom and had no trouble setting up the monitor. We had a bed in which to sleep in the living room so we didn’t wake the kids. The bedroom was nice and dark so it didn’t wake the toddlers. Street parking wasn’t hard at all. Great communication!  Cons- you can hear every movement from upstairs, especially when the kids played near the door to the basement. This was stressful during nap time and bedtime for our 1.5 year olds.  The bedroom has only one plug and even though we brought a power strip, we had to buy an adapter because the plug wouldn’t take strips with three prongs. We had trouble figuring out the keypad- but that was probably just us!  Overall a great trip and the noise probably wouldn’t bother people without young children!

The self-check in guide is easy to follow along and convenient to have, especially since we arrived late on a Friday night. Windows were open when we arrived, so a couple of bugs came in (no biggie - just make sure to close them!) The place itself is a bit bare, but clean and within walking distance to coffee shops/restaurants. As mentioned in the description, you will hear steps from above or outside considering the location, but this did not bother us. Serena and Justin were easy to communicate with and always responded quickly - don't be afraid to ask if you need anything. They were very accommodating!

The explanations for arrival are not difficult but I couldn't find the door. They scolded me for "loitering" in the neighbor's alley when I was trying to find the door, I had a bad signal and they didn't answer my phone. A boy opened the door and showed me the refrigerator, the bathroom and my room. I didn't get any key to lock my room or the code for the front door. At 1am a person came in who was making a lot of noise, the same as at 7am. I didn't feel welcome in the place at all. Nothing unpleasant happened to me but whoever took me in the Uber told me to be careful in that neighborhood because it is an area with high rates of vandalism. A good detail is that they leave you a half-liter bottle of water and two skacks for breakfast.  I wouldn't go back, but good luck if you go.
Ok apartment, neighborhood looks scary but during our stay we had no problems

Hosts were very friendly and the apartment was cute and small. The location was great- very close to the beach and boardwalk and also close to the subway station. It’s right next to a grocery store so very convenient. The neighborhood was a little sketchy at nighttime but well lit when we were walking home!
Edwin was nice and explained everything clearly. The main issue was a bed sheet that had suspicious stains on it. There was no other blanket in the house so we split!

Reggie was very kind and helpful in helping us collect the keys to the apartment, although we would have liked him to be there when we arrived, which would have saved us from having to look for the keys in a neighboring business, which did not give us the right ones... We were, however, very disappointed by the cleanliness of the accommodation, the sheets and towels were not changed and dirty, the trash cans were half full and the bath was clogged, so it made the shower very unpleasant to take. I wouldn't go back there.

Ed was a great host. Super quick to respond and patient.  My girlfriend and I enjoyed our stay but moved out to be in a different part of the city.  The area is rustic and rundown and seems unsafe, but Ed is respected  in the neighbourhood and the house is safe.
Didn’t end up staying cause I felt the neighborhood was unsafe nothing to do with the place or host.

+The apartment is very nice, comfortable, light and spacious. Everything that you need is there.  +The host is very friendly, responds immediately. +Very close to the train +Very close to the ocean. There is even a sea view from the apartment.   -Bad neighbourhood, looks and feels very unsafe outside -There were loud sounds from the radiator that we couldn't sleep (we stayed in winter) -The neighbours from the closest building had a party at night that was very loud. We had to call the police.

Great stay in Coney Island close to the subway, beach, Luna Park, restaurants and food stores. Exceptionally comfortable bed. Communication and check-in  with Ed and Isabel was easy and stress-free. Apartment was clean with no weird smells. Excellent smart tv and good lighting. Highly recommend.

Our stay here was perfect. As a host, Joan was incredibly accommodating. We received a little welcome basket upon arrival with snacks, we were provided with essentials such as hair products and lotion etc, and there was even a pair of slippers to keep us warm during the super cold weather. One time we were unsure of which subway line to take and Joan printed out directions for us which was so sweet.   The room was comfortable and spacious. The bed was the perfect size for the two of us, so we would definitely recommend this room to couples or a single person.   In terms of the location, there was a nearby station that allowed us to get to Manhattan pretty easily. As two people who have never used subways in New York, it wasn’t hard to figure out. The streets are safe - we never felt afraid walking around and we often came back from the city around midnight.   So overall it was a great stay and everything was just right. Thank you so much Joan and Petra :)

Anna's place in a comfy studio. The location is great in the heart of East Village - lots of good restaurants, nightlife, and easy to get anywhere with public transit.   There's no microwave, so you'll need to be comfortable using the stove or oven to heat food.   There's also an old-school radiator for heating, which is very common in nyc, but also very noisy at night. I'm a heavy sleeper and it constantly woke me up but it was fine after I got some ear plugs.  The internet was fast and reliable.   It feels homey, I suspect Anna or another resident lives here full time when it's not rented out.  I stayed for a month and had a great time, would stay again.

I would like to start by saying Anelcia's place is exactly as described. It's in a great place - felt like a family neighborhood. It was amazingly clean! We were in town to clean out the home of a family member who had recently passed away, & after dealing with old, dusty things all day it was so refreshing to come back to a cozy & clean place. Anelcia left shampoos/soaps in the shower & water bottles in the kitchen - nice little extra touches!  Unfortunately there was one issue that still bothers me 2 weeks later, however. I've put off writing my review in hopes I'd feel differently, but I still feel a little bitter. Anelcia made it very clear ahead-of-time that guests are not to use the backyard or smoke. That was perfectly fine with me, as I had no interest in being outside in the cold wind (and if I did, we would've gone walking on sidewalks anyway) and my husband and I are not even smokers! In fact, I can't stand cigarette smoke!! When we arrived the first day, I flipped a light switch in the bedroom and it didn't do anything, so we found another switch that worked. At 10:30 pm that night, we were in bed and Anelcia sent me with a somewhat snippy message strongly "reminding" me that there is no smoking and guests aren't to use the backyard. She then ended it with, "turn off the back light." For several minutes I was very confused until I remembered that we had flipped that switch and it must have been for a backyard light. I had no idea! I explained to her that we must have accidentally flipped it and left it on but we hadn't been outside or smoked, and I then asked if she thought we were for some reason, since her message implied so. She told me, "well, Lisa, in fact my neighbor thought you must be smoking in the backyard..." I was floored. It was very accusatory and implied that, because the backyard light was on, we must have been back there and of course must be smoking. It made me feel very awkward that apparently the neighbor was watching & tattling and Anelcia just assumed it must be so. It was all a little much and it made me feel defensive when we hadn't done anything wrong!  The following night I jokingly sang the old song, "Smoking in the Boys' Room" to my husband, replacing the lyrics with "Smoking in the Backyard." Fifteen minutes later a giant blast of music started up from outside, like a rock band, and the singing was clear as day - "There is no smoking in the backyard...!" My husband and I absolutely froze & stared at each other. It was sooooooo creepy!!! We started whispering because it seriously felt like Anelcia had just overheard me joking around with that song. It made me incredibly uncomfortable. Given how quiet the apartment/neighborhood had been until just that moment, and the words we heard, it was too much to be a coincidence. My husband and I discussed trying to find a different place to stay, as we felt an invasion of our privacy at this point.  I've never, ever had an issue with any airbnb we've rented and I have no idea what we did to rub Anelcia the wrong way (other than accidentally leaving the backyard light on!!) but it left a bad taste in our mouths and we wouldn't not stay there again because of it. It's a shame, because it's a great little home and we felt safe until it felt like we were being spied on. Considering I had agreed through airbnb not to smoke or use the backyard, and considering electricity for a single backyard lightbulb would cost a few extra cents, Anelcia should have trusted us and let it go.  Bottom line - if you stay at Anelcia's cozy apartment, whatever you do, do NOT turn on the backyard light. She will definitely assume you are breaking all of the apartment rules if you do so.

The location of Paige's apartment is insanely great. You're near a number of trains and bus routes, great bars are right down the street, and it's a relatively short walk to the water. At no point did I feel like it took forever to get anywhere or that my pal and I were unsafe. In regards to the apartment, Paige's space is small but cozy. There was a time when we thought we were going to have an extra guest for only one night and when I brought that up with Paige, she was wonderfully hospitable. All in all, a good stay.

I traveled to New York to see some friends. Chris is a great host with efficient communication and check in was very easy. The apartment is bigger than I was expecting, it has high ceilings and is very bright. I think for the price this place is a steal. It is close to bars, restaurants, the metro, shops, and the river. The neighborhood is quiet as is the building. However, I was playing music while taking a shower and the neighbor came to ask if I could not make noise in the bathroom because the emergency exit door seems to open into his apartment. This wasn't an issue and he was very nice. All in all I would definitely (and probably will) stay here again because it is easy, clean, great value, and the host is magnificent.

1st trip to NYC was a success! I have never used Airbnb before and Di made my experience very easy for someone not accustomed to the big city. She touched base with me the day before I was scheduled to arrive and we were in constant contact for the duration of my stay (and quick to respond). Her place is very quiet and clean and I had 0 issues with her neighbors. She lives in a very nice neighborhood and I never felt that I was in any danger. Her place is within walking distance of several nice diners/restaurants which are definitely worth checking out. I highly recommend this listing and will try to use her in future visits to the city!

Stars for cute place with great location over Palma’s amazing restaurant. Arrival instructions were a problem as they were sent months ago and were never received. This caused stress! For $300 night we were a little surprised there was no coffee, except for a couple teaspoons of instant. Disappointed, especially since there was such an amazing restaurant below.

This home is perfect for someone who needs a place to stay that is quiet and relaxing. It has a comfortable stress free feel to it that makes you feel at home. Great appliances and nice decor.  And there’s only 3 words or 3 letters to describe Cat, at that’s OMG, i don’t think anyone can meet a more polite woman than her.

The apartment was just as described, and the location very convenient: close to both the subway and the LIRR at their Nostrand Ave. stops, which makes it a short trip to Manhattan and also easy to reach from the JFK airport. Before traveling we were afraid that it would be cold in New York, but the heating in the apartment works very well and we even had to turn it down a bit! Oh, and it was very pleasant to sink down in the comfy armchairs in the evenings after spending the day walking.  Last but not least, John was very kind and gave us very good advice to find our way around. It was a pleasure to meet him.

Cat is an amazing host!  I stayed at her place for a couple days after a stressful work trip.  She was on top of every message / communication, and couldn’t have been nicer or more helpful.  Having a great host like Cat makes all the difference when choosing where to stay, and I feel like she went above and beyond to provide concierge-level service.

If you are looking for "location" this is definitely a great option. If you are looking for comfort, this is a roomy apartment, and having 1 1/2 bathrooms is very convenient. However, there are a couple of things we found to be very unpleasant.... the sofa in the living room is in very bad condition, some of the wires on the back rest are exposed.... the chairs in the dining area could use cushions and one of them is falling apart.  If you are looking for cleanliness, the apartment was pretty clean, but the towels could smell better and be a better quality.  We only had light breakfasts and we did not cook so we are not sure how the kitchen appliances work.  If safety is important to you...there are no smoke detectors in the apartment...this really needs to be corrected.  The apartment is in the basement, this makes it darker than usual....yes there are windows in the living room and bedroom but   there is no direct light coming in.  We needed a second set of towels and a lighter weight blanket and the host responded quickly to our needs without any issues.

This place is so cute you won't even believe it!  Kathleen was in communication with us to make our arrival easy and she was there to greet us and show us everything we needed to know about her beautiful place.  I joked with her about putting chocolate chips in her famous banana bread and she made us a loaf with them in it - it was AHHH-mazing!  I would go back for another loaf of that alone :)  Travelling with our sweet dog Tula is very important to all of us (no family member left behind!) and she made Tula feel very welcomed as well (dog bowls for food and water, doggy bed with a blanket for her!) and gave her some attention when we arrived too.  She is a wonderful human being and we won't stay anywhere else when we are in that area anymore!  If anyone is going to Jersey - it's a hop skip and a jump from there.  We went to a comedy show in New Brunswick at the Stress Factory and it was so simple from the Sweet Pea Cottage to get there.  I highly recommend this beautiful little place and the sweet hostess!

The quietest city apartment I’ve ever been in! This is a basement apartment but still gets decent light. It is SO quiet and peaceful!! Cat was extremely helpful, kind and very responsive. It should be noted that the checkin process was more cumbersome than other Airbnb’s I’ve used as the key is not very close to the apartment building. This may be something that happens in many city airbnbs but I found it stressful. There is also poor phone service in the apartment and you have to use Wi-Fi calling which was choppy.

The host was excellent and helped us with all that was needed. Although she had family health issues, she still made time for us.   Trains and buses just minutes away. Just make sure to prepare yourselves for the very cold outdoors. Wear the right clothings as it could get very nasty.    One word of advise. Avoid small grocers such as the one in the coner just seconds away from the apartment as they will rob you alive. They do not give you an itemized bill. They just give you a random price to pay as they will know you are foreign.   You buy a few things today and they charge you one price. You buy the very same things the next day, and they will charge you differently. When you ask for the itemised bill, they start talking to each other with their own language. Insulting me for all I know. Other then that, I recommend the apartment and the host.

I spent a week with my two teenage children and it turned out very well, excellent quality/price ratio. Nice apartment for 3/4 people 15 minutes walk from the subway that takes you to the center of Manhattan in 30/40 minutes. Old but clean, well maintained and well decorated. Equipped with wifi, iron, hairdryer, TV, microwave...Michelle very nice and attentive. The neighborhood is humble but not unsafe at any time. To return!!

Charming little country cottage in SI, NYC!  Kathleen is a great hostess and she provided plush towels, a generous selection of coffee and tea and all the little things I needed for a stress-free stay. The cottage is tucked away in the garden, much like it's shown in the pictures. Walking distance to stores and transit. Safe area. I would definitely stay there again!

Nice, small apartment with New York charm. The apartment was as pictured, but showed slight signs of wear in the bathroom and is quite noisy. Michelle always responded quickly and also agreed to store the bags after checkout.  The subway can be reached in 10 minutes with direct access to Manhattan and JFK Airport.  There are shopping opportunities in the area. Bed-Stuy is certainly not a posh neighborhood, but there's no need to be afraid.   All in all, a successful holiday in a good alternative to an expensive hotel!
There is a mouse in the room, which scared me last night and I hardly slept.一只老鼠半夜在屋里蹦跶得欢，受到惊吓。其他还行吧。

GREAT location, especially from LaGuardia, and an easy ride to JFK too. It's a short walk to a grocery store, and even closer to markets, 24-hour drug store and everything from sushi, Greek, Mexican, etc.  The subway (R was our mainstay, but E & F too) is RIGHT there and a short ride can get you to Battery Park, Central Park, or... This is a quiet location, far enough off a bus-served, commercial thorofare, but close enough to get to the city, even a full on grocery store is walking distance. The neighborhood has a diverse mix of restaurants that we really miss from our days of living on Chicago's north side.  The unit itself has been updated, it's roomy and clean and well appointed with a comfty couch, entertainment options, nice dining table (we had 4-1/2 for meals) with power readily available. For those traveling from other countries, several power strips, and outlets, have USB sockets. The kitchen is well stocked with glasses, pans & plates. While we enjoyed the dining options, it's nice having breakfast in during a long weekend where Grandma & Grandpa are babysitting, before heading out to the zoo, or walking over to the park.  The downside to the unit is that it only has 1 bathroom, but we did not spend that much time in the bathroom that it turned out to be a problem. We spent more time planning our Zoo trips (Queens Zoo, Bronx Zoo, Staten Island Zoo, & The Central Park Zoo).

Great little place to stay - so quaint and unique. Kathleen was so sweet - making sure she greeted my husband and I and gave us some background about the cottage.  Baked some delicious banana bread and macadamia cookies.  We slept on her Murphy bed and it was so comfortable! Kathleen was a pleasure to rent from -  not intrusive but made it known that she was available if anything was needed.  As for location, this area of Staten Island is very convenient to public transportation and if driving here - lots of parking is available. Don't have to worry about crime but like any city you should lock doors.  It's sort of mid-island so commute to Manhattan or to New Jersey is easy enough.  Definitely will be coming back again!

The room is as advertised, a little narrow but correct. The apartment is really 20 minutes from Times Square, my only problem was not knowing which exit to take from the metro... (20 minutes to find the street...after an 8 hour flight, and 1h30 of transport at 8:30 p.m., not easy) Aurélien had to come and help me get the key, super nice, welcoming and interesting ;)) I will come back ;))
Natasha was gracious and very flexible and helpful.  Her energy was easy and chill as she said! She made being there and coming and going very stress free.

This cozy and beautiful studio Bed-Stuy apartment is located in the heart of everything that makes Brooklyn fabulous: gorgeous old brownstones, block parties that all the neighbors attend, amazing music playing, big shade trees, and an overall upbeat atmosphere in a safe and chill family neighborhood packed with fantastic little eateries and coffeeshops.   With its high ceilings, dramatic crown molding, big fireplace (I don't think it works but it's a stunning feature), and inlaid wood floors, the apartment will no doubt see caring restoration one day but even without is stunning.   The apt is more spacious than I anticipated and nicely equipped with everything to make my stay comfy. One standout feature: the queen bed is amazingly comfortable.   Jamal was very communicative and gracious. I had a problem getting into the apartment when I arrived; Jamal took responsibility for this and I have no doubt that future guests will have no issue in this regard.    Jamal's place is around the corner from my daughter's home in Brooklyn and I will be visiting as often as I'm able; Jamal's place will be my first choice of places to stay.   Jane

If you don’t want to take the subway after the game and rather get back to your room ASAP, choose this spot. It’s right across the street from the stadium. It’s a normal place to sleep, big enough for 4-5 people and perfect location. Amílcar was quick to respond and gave us our space. He also has the cutest little kitty that will steal your heart. Fyi, to save energy the AC to the room wasn’t on when we arrived but once we turned it on it cooled very quickly. Highly recommend!!

Jamal has provided his guests with a relaxing getaway. The room is inviting, warm and nicely furnished with just what a traveler needs to unwind after a busy day. Well maintained, clean and comfortable. The whole process of checking in, communication and being in a safe environment made the experience stress free. Easy access to public transportation, shops, restaurants and walkability. We will be looking forward to another stay when we come back to Brooklyn.

Very pleasant stay in Jamal's apartment. Very clear arrival instructions. Access to the Nostrand Avenue metro station can give you a feeling of insecurity, but the adjacent streets are much less so with a welcoming neighborhood and a very pleasant neighborhood. The apartment itself is very well equipped and perfect for a stay in New York, including to get to Manhattan which is a few minutes away by subway with the A express line. All while enjoying the calm of Brooklyn.

We would repeat again! We had a pleasant stay, the apartment was exactly as described in the advertisement, it was clean, tidy, a very quiet area to rest. Night and nothing dangerous. It has many bars, 24-hour supermarkets and the subway just a 7-minute walk away and takes you directly to Times Square 🙂 (it is line 1, the best of all from our point of view since you don't have to make transfers to go downtown) it takes about 30 minutes to get to the center of Manhattan but you get away from the hustle and bustle of the city as well as from paying very high prices. 100% advisable!!

DO NOT BOOK THIS AIR AND B IF YOU ARE AFRAID OF ICE PEOPLE THAT UNSELFISHLY SHARE THEIR SAFE AND WELL MAINTAINED HOME THAT IS EXACTLY AS ADVERTISED WITH A PLEASANT SURPRISE OF ULTIMATE COMFORT AND PRIVACY THAT DOESNT FEEL STANDOFFISH.  SPACIOUS CLEAN HEAVILY STOCKED KITCHEN AND BED THAT WILL ALOW YOU TO FEEL THE LOVE FROM THE FAMILY ABOVE YOU. ONE OF THE BEST AND IT FELT SO SINCERE FROM HELLO TO GOODBYE

With all due respect, our stay was mediocre at best.  When our group of 4 adult women (2 over 60 of age) arrived there were only thin sheets on the bed, old towels and pillows. Julio's accommodation is correct and economical. It is located near a metro station to get to Manhattan in about 30 minutes. Communication with Julio was not easy. One person kindly waited for us until midnight. However it was incorrect to ask for 25 dollars in cash without a receipt especially when arriving late from a flight from Europe. Finally it would be welcome to provide towels. The apartment is quiet. The kitchen deserves a little more attention. Overall good value for money for New York.

Bathroom is upstairs which is pretty annoying. Other than that it is a wonderful place to stay. Super comfy beds, a ton of pillows and fancy room. Location can’t get better. In the middle of Bushwick (I see people saying that it’s unsafe, it’s called NYC. This is how Brooklyn looks like :) if you want a super safe space with no people at night go to small town). Location location location (which is awesome). Host was very nice and accommodating.

We thought, we could not be more amazed than what we expected from the photos of the apartment - how much we were wrong. Jeff is the best host which you can imagine. Trust me, there is no better. He will take care of you as good as your own mother and help you even with the smallest things. Neighbourhood might feel unsafe for the first time, but even when I came back at midnight, there was no problem at all and you can see how quiet it is. Close to metro and a few really good restaurants nearby.

Geoffrey accommodations made for a first stress free trip to NewYork. He was very responsive and always checked in to make sure we had everything we needed.  His place was clean, quiet , comfortable, and accessible enough to all the major attractions of the city but also secluded enough to enjoy a quiet evening. He provided local expertise and personal touches to the space to make it feel like home. Would definitely stay here again!

The place was very clean and comfortable. They provide many amenities and the private entrance is also a plus. It’s really a steal for anyone looking to stay near queens or visit Manhattan. And not to mention the hosts are super nice and respond quickly!

Best stay ever😆😆😆😁 The cleanest apartment I’ve stayed in U.S. And the host is a really friendly and nice person! Bus is super convenient, the neighborhood has good food, everything u could expected!! Good place. Perfect location, just two blocks away from the amusement parks, the boardwalk, and the beach. Really cheap too. You can't beat the price. We'll definitely stay here again if we ever come back. Almost don't even want to write this review because I don't want someone else to steal my slot when I come back.
The apartment is comfortable, in a somewhat reliable area, at dusk it is quite dangerous

We booked this apartment for 5 nights.  We stayed for the first night only.  The neighborhood was filthy and not safe.  The apartment building was old and dreary inside. The apartment we stayed in was on the third floor.   The stairwell was dirty and smelly.  The apartment does not have central AC.  The weather that day was very warm and humid.  The only air we had:  the ceiling fan and open windows.  When Edwin showed us around the apartment, the bathroom smelled of urine.  Realizing that we were unhappy, Edwin offered to reimburse me.    Shortly thereafter I emailed Edwin that I would take him up on his offer to reimburse me.  I expected to be reimbursed for 4 out of the 5 nights, however, after we secured other accommodations thru Airbnb we found out that the reimbursement was less than half of what we expected.   Our one—and thankfully ONLY--night at Edwin’s turned out to be sleepless because of the noise coming from the street and, for my sister, a very uncomfortable sofa bed.  I think the sofa was alive; I’m not sure.  I was afraid I’d wake up during the night and find that my sister had been swallowed up!  LOL!
Clean clean clean my 2 nd time staying there .and wont be my last .its like a steal for the price. The place is really great

If you are deciding whether to pick this home for your next destination, I can 100% vouch that this is the best Airbnb experience I have ever had. From the process of booking to the last day in New York, Geoffrey was so helpful and attentive to my boyfriend and I. Always quick to reply, Geoffrey makes you feel like a home away from home. We were welcomed to his hospitality and his adorable dog Champ and left with no regrets, just wonderful memories to share for a lifetime. Finding a secure, clean as well as cozy place relieved so much stress from us during our trip. The amenities were great quality and the area is 3 min away from a train station. Geoffrey was always available to direct us on how to get to places or just friendly chat. Thank you Goeffrey for making our trip to New York an unforgettable one. We can't wait to see you and Champ again when we return to New York!
Super nice host and wonderful demeanor. Wasn’t afraid to answer all the questions I had and had open communication

While searching for the accomodation, my and my girlfriend were kind of afraid that we will not choose the right one - now I am 100% sure that we have chosen the best possible option! The Apartment is in calm location just a couple metres from metro station (take an “A” train and step out on “80”st. Apartment was one of the cleanest place I have ever visited, the equipment of the Apartment is amazing as well and you can find here everything you will need during your stay and most likely even more. Photos are 100% accurate.   The second part is the host itself - Jeff is great person! He made our stay even more comfortable with all the information he provided us with. Nothing was a problem and Jeff kindly answered all our questions and provided us with advices what to see and visit.   I am sure that in case we will return to New York, we will try to return to Jeffs place.

Geoffrey was an excellent host. From the beginning he gave us all the clear instructions, he received us with great kindness, he guided us to move in the city, he gave us his help when we needed it. It is located near the subway that goes directly to Manhattan, the area is quiet and even though it is lonely it is not dangerous. The house is just like the photos, very impeccable, tidy and the perfect space to stay. We would definitely stay there again.

The apartment was solid, and Ed was a wonderful host- attentive, thoughtful and responsive. We ended up staying in his second apt in the building, so another guest could extend her stay, which was totally fine by us bc the second was almost identical and we were just looking for a quiet weekend visit. Ed was communicative and flexible thru that. The apt had a lived-in feel, but was clean. We just got door dash and takeout and used minimal dishes — what we did use was functional and clean.  Our stay was early March so it was cold and (heads up) the building pipes were pretty loud. Gave us a scare the first time. It’s a great location in summer being to close to the beach!  When we arrived (round 10pm) there was no street parking, so Ed gave us his parking spot. On our last day, he was kind enough to let us stay into the evening despite the morning check out time, as we stalled before an evening flight at JFK. Would def stay here again.

The apartment we were in was not ready for guests. I think Ed is working on it. The shower was fixed on 2x4 and the trimming was not complete in the bathroom. The fact that the ocean is across the street and the subway for NY is near the apartment is definitely the positive side of this place. The private parking is a nightmare!  Once your car is parked, which is not an easy thing to achieve,  you can't have access to it unless you give the host a 2 hour notice. You must be aware that the neighbourhood is uncertain. There are lots of people on drugs in the streets.

I urge anybody travelling to New York to consider staying in Nicholas’ apartment. My family and I stayed here for 11 nights over Christmas and New Years and could not have been happier with the experience. The apartment is perfectly located in Astoria Queens and only a step away from a huge variety of shops, laundromats, supermarkets, and restaurants (including some of the best bagels in NYC). The Astoria-Ditmars train stop is only a few blocks away - it is a 15-20 minute ride into Times Square and being the last stop on the N and W lines there is always a train at the station. I highly recommend this location as an alternative to staying in Manhattan and promise you won’t be disappointed with your choice. The area is quiet but also busy at most hours of the day meaning there is never a need to feel unsafe, even when arriving back home in the early hours of the morning.   Nicholas’ apartment is exactly as described. It is tidy and well-equipped. It has everything you need to cook at home which is a god send for weary travellers on a long holiday. Nicholas himself was a pleasure to meet. Though we did not have a lot of contact he was flexible with early check-in and met us at the apartment to welcome us and give us a quick tour, he was also kind enough to stock the apartment with a few groceries to help us settle in. Nicholas was always available via text if needed and messaged us midway through our stay to make sure everything was going smoothly. The apartment was also great value for money for 3 people trying to find accomodation in New York over the holidays on short notice.   Again I would highly recommend a stay at Nicholas’ place.

I rate my two-week stay at Michael’s Brooklyn apartment 5 stars.  From the start of my interest in Michael’s apartment, he was quick in his responses to my inquiries/questions.  And because of Michael’s attention to details, the access to his apartment was stress-free and the everything related to his rental, including the building, neighborhood and New York was provided with emails and printouts located on the refrigerator.    About the rental, Michael's newly-constructed building was clean with an elevator, and his modern apartment was extremely clean, quiet and well-appointed...top-tier amenities, high ceilings, and beautiful wood floors.  I particularly loved the bed’s mattress, pillows and linens…so comfortable.  With regard to getting into Manhattan, Michael’s Brooklyn apartment was 5 blocks away from the G Train; travel a few train stops and you can transfer to the A, C or F Trains to continue into the city…easy and convenient.  I think it obvious that I loved my stay at Michael’s Airbnb;  I highly recommend renting from him.  Thanks again Michael!  Peace and blessings, Deionna

Mckenzie and the kids are great. Is the perfect place to stay with a child. The room is relatively small but cozy and you're only there to sleep anyway. It's only a 5 minute walk from the subway to the apartment. From Brooklyn to Manhattan very good subway connections in 40 minutes. The environment felt very safe, even at night we were never afraid of walking home and not in the subway either. If you would like any information McKenzie is very helpful, just ask. We had a very great time.

Great location, in a stylish high rise. Providing impeccable views of the city. Nice sized one bedroom apartment. Great comfy bed, stellar kitchen, and modern bathroom. Not far from grocery, subway, or a drug store. Just note there is no tv. But highly recommended.

The house is exactly as the pictures, clean, new and comfortable as it looks. Ted was very nice and welcoming, he was waiting for us on the check in day, and help us with the bags (more like he carried them by himself), and also on the  check out day. The house is located in Brooklyn (half an hour from Manhattan), the area at first may seems shady  (manly if is your first time in NY), but me and my friend, two girls, didn't any problems. The house is a renovated basement, but it has a lot of light and is very quiet, since it gives you access to the backyard, you can hear the birds and everything, very pleasant. The only two this that may affect choosing this airbnb is the soft mattress and poor pressure in the shower, but definitely it didn't affected my stay!

Location was close to the Ralph train station (maybe a 5 minute walk away), which was great.  The place was also very clean, which was much appreciated. Since we visited when it started snowing in NYC, we were worried about the suite getting a little too cold at night, but the place remained very cozy. We also liked that the front door required unlocking four separate locks to enter (not because the neighborhood is particularly unsafe or anything, but just as a general precaution).

The hosts kept in contact with myself before our trip, day of, and the night prior to our departure.  The apartment is very cute, comfy sofa, gigantic tv with Netflix, great water pressure in the shower with excellent temperature.  The neighborhood seemed at first rather sketchy but it wasn't.  It is very quiet at nighttime and we, two females, didn't have any issues walking around the neighborhood to the local cafe or the subway station.  There is a convenient store on either corner of the street and both of the owners are very nice.  Getting to the subway station is a breeze, the C train local runs throughout the day very frequently and the A train local runs late night/early morning.  From this station you can get to basically anywhere going uptown and also to Queens.  Also, a bonus it does have its own private entry and private back patio.

I have to stay here the first day arrived, I was impressed with the hospitality and effort to help me most comfortable and friendly between her and her husband. While staying here, both of whom helped me throughout.  For trips into town, it seemed like a railway line to enter,and the neighborhood is not scary walk away.

OMG where do I start? Kristin was most gracious, informative, professional and helpful. She made sure I was at once comfortable and knew not only my surroundings but also with her AMAZING kitchen provided with every possible tool one can imagine. The room is comfortable and light, and the bed heavenly. Additionally, there is quite a bit of room not to lie store and hang clothes, plus a work desk facing a beautiful tree. The shower is something I wanted to steal away, with full flowing jets and very spacious. Lastly the neighborhood: this trip spoiled it for me because I will never be able to lodge in any other part of NYC. Greenwich/West Village (she is on the border of both I think) is the best! ton of coffee shops, restaurants and parks. Clothing stores (second hand too), and minutes from the river. I also found a great yoga place five minutes from her house and the main shopping thoroughfares (Avenue of the Americas, 5th Avenue) are 5-10 minutes away max.
Experience was fantastic. The apartment is great and the neighborhood is wonderful. Was clean, easy to get the key, easy to check out and just 100% stress free.

Kate made the stay great! We had good communication prior to my check in. I arrived late getting into NYC but it was not a problem for Kate when I arrived. Her place is a 10 minute ride from Penn station. When I arrived Kate made me fell like I was staying with family even making recommendations for local things to do. Her place had all that I needed. Its in a very walkable area of midtown, drug store, market and diner nearby. It was a short walk to the subway. cabs were very easy to get and it was not a far walk to 5th ave shopping. I believe that someone mentioned the apt is on the second floor but it is the third floor. All in all it met all of my needs and expectations.

I stayed at Bensife's place for 5 days. It was a great experience. Besinfe was a very good host, always cleaning and taking care of his place.   For those who are not used to the vibrant and diverse community in Harlem, theighborhood might seem  intimidating, but for the 5 days I stayed there, I never felt unsafe at any moment even though, at times, I was coming from town very late.   The place is close to a lot of stores and restaurants. You even have a dry cleaner close to the apartment.

Many thanks to Jay! My experience here was wonderful. Quite, clean home and friendly host.  Would definitely stay here again.  The community is vibrant and as a solo female traveler, I never felt unsafe. Public transportation is very quickly accessible with subway stations scattered nearby. Lots to do in the area as well. Would highly recommend!

This apartment is incredibly located in close proximity to many cool lower east side neighborhoods and easy access to many different subway lines. The location was by far the best selling point for me. We never felt unsafe walking around this neighbourhood. The apartment was clean and the air conditioner worked great especially as NYC was HOT during our trip. The kitchenette has all the basics you need and the bathroom is well sized and clean. We packed light and are able and healthy. My only caution is, if you are not, the apartment is a good workout climbing five flights of stairs and not the best choice for everybody in terms of accessibility. It was not a problem for us. Chris was extremely prompt in communicating with us. They were flexible with the check-in and check-out as we needed and as they could accommodate. If stars align I will absolutely return to this Airbnb in future visits.

This was honestly the worst Airbnb experience I’ve ever had. When I arrived to NY I called Jay (Besinfe) because i still didn’t have any instructions on how to access his home. Once I was in front of his apartment door, he told me to look down, and there was the key to his apartment laying on the hallway floor. He told me to leave the key there for his other guests that were arriving later. We were to share the key by leaving it on the floor outside of the apartment throughout the stay. I told him that this made me feel unsafe. I didn’t like the fact that anyone could just walk into the apartment at anytime. He argued with me and tried to justify how this was ok as if I didn’t have the right to feel worried about this situation. The apartment was located in a Harlem and honestly didn’t look the safest outside. He basically told me since I didn’t feel safe than I shouldn’t stay at his place. At this point, I’m already in NY with no where else to go. Him and my significant other speak and we agree to go have a key duplicated. Jay said he would reimburse for the key. Although I was unhappy, I just decided to move on with my day (which was delayed due to traveling to get a key made) since I was only going to be there for the weekend. My boyfriend and I finally go out and have an amazing time. I almost forgot about my experience until we came back and got ready for bed. Once my boyfriend and I got in bed together, it collapsed. We couldn’t do anything but laugh. I looked around. The wall next to the bed was extremely dirty. The knob and lock to the bedroom were hanging off. I honestly couldn’t believe this was happening. My boyfriend managed to get the bed back together and once we woke up the next morning, I went to slide out of the bed and it collapsed again! We could NOT stay another night in this horrible place. I was disgusted! We called Airbnb and thank God they took excellent care of us! We found another place to stay and went on to enjoy the rest of our weekend. Jay tried to call me and threaten me advising me that he had a sensor in the place and could tell how long we were in there. He became argumentative with me all over again. I told him I was done speaking with him and would only talk to Airbnb moving forward. I didn’t want to stay in that dirty sketchy apartment another minute! And if he can afford sensors, he should probably invest in another bed. I actually read some of his older reviews and found out that the bed  collapsed on another guest. I’m not sure where the cleaning fee is going because it was dirty in there. Because I should say something positive, I’ll say the bathroom was clean. Overall I would not suggest staying here unless you’re ok with an argumentative host who does not provide good hospitality.

To start off with we were given the wrong room. The pictures did not match our room but overall was a clean environment. He offers a flat rate to keep luggage after checkout which is pretty nice. The first day we left for a few hours and when we came back noticed he had gone into the room and unplugged my charger where my Apple Watch was charging which makes me makes me suspicious. Our second night we were awaken at 3 am by the repeated ringing of the doorbell. This went on for about an hour before it was answered. The night before checkout he took our keys “Incase he didn’t see us in the morning” which prevented us from going out. Overall it was a clean place but I guess I was expecting a bit more hospitality. It was an experience to say the least.

Besinfe is the perfect host. Upon arrival we received phone calls making sure we were getting to the Stay safely, and if we had any questions or concerns. Host was able to communicate promptly with efficiency as to where we should park without pay, and anything else we needed to know. When arrived we were greeted with great feelings of comfort and hospitality. The location of the Stay is perfect; we had easy access to the subway taking us all throughout Manhattan as pleased. We felt completely safe walking back through the night and had no problems with feeling unsafe/uncomfortable. The large apartment itself was just as good if not better in person. The inside was renovated with modern interior design and really gave off the "New York" Vibe. On top of that, the sanitation, and neatness of the living space was nothing short of immaculate. Besinfe is a compassionate host and genuinely cares about his guests. He makes it his mission to make his home feel as though it is yours, with success. If you are planning to stay anywhere near manhattan, Besinfe provides the best home and amenities in the area.

Right when I landed in NY I learned I booked at a scam location. Long story short I found this location and I am glad it didn’t work out with any other air bnb. Great location and close to the 1 train to head to downtown. Fredrick was very welcoming and always checked to make sure his guests were comfortable. I stayed for 3 months for a internship and became good friends with Fredrick. Definitely rebooking at this location when I am back in NY.

Julie is a wonderful kind person, friendly host and helped me a lot (literary a lot) in any situation. The place locate very comfortable and safety. I walked around late night or very early morning from subway station where is 3 block away, but I never feel dangerous. My Room is clean and cosy for enjoying my stay in New York City. When I come back again to NYC, I'll definitely ask appointment her place. THANKS, Julie!

The accommodation was very good, the description of the apartment is the same as in the advertisement, everything was very clean and comfortable, very suitable for 4 or 5 people. The master bedroom is a little noisy at night, I suggest modifying the acoustic insulation of it. To get to the most touristic places in Manhattan, the subway is very close and taking the express line takes only 15 minutes to get everywhere. The neighborhood is quiet and offers security even late at night. We did not observe any activity that seemed dangerous or that worried us. I highly recommend the department.

We were a party of three from Germany and stayed in Theresas apartment for six nights to visit NY for the first time. Theresa was very nice and the apartment was very clean and had just everything we needed. Especially the amount of towels, the city guide and HD television have to be positively mentioned here. The subway was very closeby and it was super easy to get everywhere.   The neighbourhood was ok. There are certainly more tourist-friendly areas to stay, but the longer we stayed the more safe we felt. It was just the first night (Saturday I have to add) that there was a physical fight between two loudly cursing groups in front of our window that scared us a little.
Theresa the host is amazing you will have any issues if anything she is very helpful. The location it’s self is slightly rough and can be dangerous on a night.

Staying at alfredo was a nightmare, the room is tiny and full of toys, bed sheets smell like a pee , no AC  it was 32‘C degrees in NY is woke up every day drowing in my sweat with the sun hitting my face and his kids screaming from 7am with no respect to the sleeping guest No elevator and he was just staring while i was suffering to bring up my luggage , very tiny stairs and the building smells like fried chicken , There’s no privacy no key for the room and alfredo comes without informing me in the room and criticize the way i organize my stuff  The host took my key and locked me out at 3 am in that dangerous place with no taxies around so i had to take a hotel Its not worth the price at all looks like a storage room with bad lighting and no space to put my luggage, it felt like i was homeless  The only good thing I’ve heard from him is do you need an umbrella other than that is just unfriendly comments
Antonio was a great host! It was amazing how he drove us to the airport in the morning for such a reasonable price. That made our trip so stress-free. :)

Alfredo is very kind and does his best to make his guests feel welcome.  The apartment is clean and tastefully furnished. The room and apartment are quite small but perfectly adequate for a short stay. The location, less than five minutes walk from Central Park, is excellent. There is quite a bit of outside noise in the apartment (traffic and voices from the street) but I suspect that is unavoidable in New York.  I felt safe walking home, even late at night. I was happy to have stayed in this apartment.

Alex's flat is absolutely lovely. It looks just as pretty, if not prettier than in the photos. It's extremely clean, comfortable and cosy with all the amenities you could possibly need. The location is one thing that my friend and i struggled with a little only because we weren't aware of how far it was to Williamsburg which was my only prior experience with brooklyn (my fault...) It can feel a bit shady at times but we grew more and more comfortable with it each day that passed. I would definitely recommend this listing to other guests

Clean place, room was small but perfect for one night of good sleep.  I wish I had known that the room doesn't have a window though.  The hood is pretty sketchy though, and loud (loud BBQs at night) and I had to wake up at 9am to move my car.

Nat was an excellent host.  She was incredibly responsive and helpful with my questions prior to booking and was there to answer any questions during the trip.  The check-in/key process could not have been any easier and was completely stress-free (we were travelling cross-country with our 2 year old and 4 year old, so having that be so easy when everyone was hungry, tired and out of their element was greatly appreciated).  The apartment is exactly as captured in the photographs.  The water pressure in the shower was great and there was plenty of hot water. The bedrooms are generously sized (especially for NYC) and there was plenty of room for our large suitcases.  We never felt cramped.  The building itself is very quiet - you rarely heard the other tenants. The back bedroom is super quiet.  The front bedroom is over a street, so there was some external street noise, but it was never that late, that loud, or disruptive.  Its a residential neighborhood and a single-lane, one-way street so, by NYC standards, it is quiet as you can get.  The location is amazing - plenty of great bars, restaurants within a few blocks.    We enjoyed our trip and would highly recommend the apartment, the location, and Nat.

The place was really nice. surprisingly quiet for being just 1.5 blocks from time square. It was really easy to find and the neighborhood is quiet lovely.   The room was spic and span (they had a lovely lady who cleans the place daily and after each guest)  The facilities are excellent for a family type occupation as well as single occupants.  We had a comfortable stay because of its location, cleanliness and safety features AND that we were allowed to leave our luggage in the common area till our check in time and after our checkout time due to our flight time.  there are so many good things to say about the place I'm afraid i may bore you.

Disgusting. The house is just for airbnb; the host doesn't live on the premises. Which is against NYC renting/housing laws. The bedroom isn't up to NYC codes--the window faces the living room! By NYC codes, a bedroom isn't a legal bedroom unless it has a window that opens out to the outdoors. The pillow smelt of hair grease and was flatter than a pancake. The sheets were dirty. I had to use a paper towel to dry my face. The host was unresponsive. I was also told that the air conditioning in the living room would also work in my bedroom--another lie. Extremely unsafe neighborhood. Neighbors were blasting music and letting their kids run around on the street after midnight. The only saving grace was that there was toilet paper in the bathroom.

This place is such a steal! Check-in is super easy. Clean space. Clean bathroom. Close to public transportation (B26 is the closest but there are also A train, B52 and B46). A little far from Manhattan, but the price even it out.

This is a great place for the single traveler looking for a place to lay your head. Clean sheets, easy check in/out, and the location was the best part of my stay.   The only issues I had with my stay is that the water temperature was too low, I felt like I was taking a cold shower, and brushed my teeth with cold water, which also had an unpleasant smell to it.   Safe neighborhood, I would recommend to a short stay traveler.

It’s hard to imagine a better location. Nat is a communicative and helpful host, but on our visit the apartment had a collection of maintenance problems. The ceiling lights turned on and off by themselves (it turns out because the wrong bulbs were overheating and the safety switch turned them off).
