The toilet wouldn’t stop flushing. 3 wall switches wouldn’t work. All things with easy solutions that would’ve made the apartment nicer. I’m sure these things will be fixed by the time of your visit.  Something that won’t be fixed…The hot water is sketchy. Just part of a cheap NY apt.   But at the end of the day all these things are forgotten because New York is New York and this apartment is right in the center of a transportation and food Mecca.

My first time staying in an  Airbnb in New York. (And my first time in New York in about 20+ years.) Since I’ve never stayed in a NYC apartment, I really couldn’t compare this property to similar properties—but, I was very happy with it. My college daughter has seen other apartments in The City and said Nat’s place was excellent. We have no complaints and would stay there again. A final note or two: The parking can be tricky to find and the noise can creep up at times. But I expected it.

David and Maria were excellent hosts! I stayed with them for a month while working at a nearby hospital. They made my stay comfortable and stress-free. Their home is in a safer neighborhood in the Bronx and the room that they have prepared was above and beyond what I expected. During my stay with their family, we became friends and I can't wait until I can return to NY and see them again.

Great stay especially if you are coming in to Montefiore to work for a couple of weeks for medical or dental rotations. I didn't feel unsafe my whole time there, the family was really nice and very accommodating.

This rental in Brooklyn is exceptional. We were very warmly welcomed by a family friend. The house is as beautiful as in the photos with a great terrace especially on the 1st floor. This neighborhood of Brooklyn is very safe and quiet (numerous grocery stores, small restaurants) and allows you to reach Manhattan very easily (about 5 minutes walk from Franklin station for the C and S lines and 20 minutes from the city), ideally located between Prospect Park and Williamsburg. The equipment and decoration of the house are perfect. Mike and Aurélie trusted us by leaving many products in the fridge. And they were also very relaxed about our departure times (night flight) for the airport, saving us the hassle of luggage and allowing us a final walk to the Brooklyn Botanic Garden in the afternoon. There is even a Citybike station near the house. Like us, you will love the charm of Bed-sty's houses and their inhabitants, that's for sure. Another big thank you to Mike and Aurélie. We can't wait to come back soon!

Everything was great! Coming from Seattle it was a bit of a culture shock at first but I was surprised how nice everyone was! The neighborhood looked a bit scary at first but we had zero trouble and we came home fairly late on pretty much every night we were there! Would definitely stay again!

This is the 1st time I ever stayed with Airbnb, and Frances made the experience absolutely pleasant and unforgettable! The room is well lit and nicely furnished. The bed is very comfortable, much better than hotel beds. Apart from everything you need, she would surprise you with a bottle of wine (oops, spoiler). The fridge is full of water, yogurt, orange juice, bread, PB&J. There're even Mac & Cheese and instant noodles for snack attack. The best part is: all of them are FREE!   Frances is such a wonderful host, she'd text you in the morning and ask you whether you want pancake, egg, and coffee/chocolate for breakfast. For the 3 nights I stayed there, I felt as if I was home, warm and welcomed in this chilly New York weather. She even gave me a ride early in the morning when I locked my rental car in a parking garage.   Overall, this is a great place to stay, Five Star experience.

The location is perfect, very central, great access to public transport and not far from Central Park. The area is quite safe, I often walked home on my own in the middle of the night and never felt in danger. There are plenty of restaurant and things to do within walking distance. Marg is very concerned about her guests, always ready to give advice and open to show you around or do something together.

Marg's a wonderful host! I enjoyed staying at her place; it was cozy and my room was just the right amount of space for me. Her place is so close to many restaurants and just a 10 minute walk to Times Square. The subway is just minutes from her place so it was much easier to get around. Marg was very helpful with planning my days in the city. She's knowledgeable about everything. Don't be afraid to ask for help especially where to eat, what to see, and how to get around NY! I really felt like I had been staying in NYC for more than the 5 days since I felt so at home at Marg's. She does have a cat, so I suggest that if you're a lover of cats, choose this place! I would definitely stay with Marg again because we connected so well and she is a pleasure to talk to.

Marg is a very kind and passionate person. If you didn't decide your schedule yet, she is willing to help you to solve the problem. She told me a lot of information such as how to book the ticket of Vessel, how to take the subway to JFK, which lobster store is better. She has an adorable cat. Sometimes you can touch him or play with him. The location is really close to Times Square by walking a few minutes. No matter taking the subway, shopping, eating or celebrating New Year Eve, everything is convenient. My personality is a little bit shy. Every night I went home, Marg asked me how's going? where did I go? what did I eat? In the beginning, I dare not talk too much. A few days later, I started to share more with her. The last night before I left, I went home early and ate dinner with her nearby the house. After we finished, we went home and chatted for more than one hour. We shared some stories about ourselves. She told me that don't be afraid of making mistakes about learning languages, don't care too much about others' ridicule, and hope me that making some friends with native speakers. I appreciate that she took care of me in those nine days. If someone also wanna experience the feeling of living nearby Times Square, here is your best choice!!!  Marg是一位非常友善和熱情的奶奶，她很願意幫你規畫行程，她告訴我很多資訊，像是如何訂Vessel的票、如何搭地鐵去甘迺迪機場、哪間店的龍蝦更好吃...等。她有一隻很可愛的橘白色公貓，偶爾可以摸摸他，跟他玩耍一下。住宿地點距離時代廣場走路只要幾分鐘，不管搭地鐵、購物、吃飯、跨年都很便利。我的個性比較害羞，每晚回家房東都會問我過得如何? 去了哪裡? 吃了什麼? 一開始都不太敢講話，到後來跟房東漸漸熟絡才比較敢分享。離開前最後一晚，我提早回家跟房東去附近吃晚餐，吃完後回家聊了超過一小時，互相分享一些彼此的生命故事，她告訴我學語言不要怕犯錯，不要太在乎別人的嘲諷，並希望我往後在大學的日子裡能夠早日交到美國當地的朋友。很謝謝她那9天的照顧，如果有人也想體驗住在時代廣場附近的感覺，請務必選擇這裡!!!

Beautiful room and perfect location. Myrta was so prompt and responsive in all communications, and gave great suggestions for places to check out in the neighborhood. She is a very kind host. Check in was so easy and low-stress. The apartment is absolutely beautiful. This is wonderful place to stay in Brooklyn!

Naomi and Rashid's place was nice and roomy.  The living room had a nice modern open feel to it.  There was a nice TV and good wifi. We basically just used this apt to sleep and didn't spend much time there.  We did have a few problems staying here though.  They only provided 3 bath towels and no face or hand towels.  I notified our hosts but unfortunately they were out of town and would not be able to provide towels right away.  Also, the toilet had a problem with something breaking inside which caused an overflow.  We had to use the few towels we had to clean up since we could not find a mop or cleaning supplies.  Our hosts did have someone come in to fix the toilet and provide some more towels later that day but still no face or hand towels.  I know a toilet breaking is something totally out of their control and no fault of the hosts but it did kind of ruin our morning taking time to clean up, no use of a toilet, and not having enough towels.  Also, no one took away all the dirty towels and the bath mat when they fixed the toilet so that was kind of yucky.  Another thing is be aware of is the walk to the subway to the apartment can be a little sketchy at night and will take you a good 15 minutes at least to get to the subway.  It is pretty easy to get into Manhattan by subway though and strangely it can almost take longer if you want to get into northern areas of Brooklyn.  So in summery although we didn't exactly have an ideal stay here i would recommend it if you need a reasonable place to stay in Brooklyn!

We had a good stay with Naomi and Rashid. The photos conform to reality. Large space in a popular neighborhood house. 10-15 minutes from the subway on foot, 45 minutes from Manhattan and 1h30 from JFK. Very responsive and discreet, Naomi and Rashid are welcoming and accommodating (having a late flight, we were able to leave our suitcases and stay later than the scheduled departure time). Don't hesitate to book with them, there are no bad surprises.

I didn't get to meet Francis, but I was shown how to use the code for the door by her son.  The key to the bedroom didn't seem to work, but I felt safe in the house.  The dog was very sweet.  The room is in a windowless basement.  The ceiling felt low and the lamp by the bed had a badly burned lamp shade with no bulb.  It didn't live up to my expectations for the price (I would expect to pay $60-80 for something like this, but the other reviews I read make me think I might be out of touch, they were all so positive).

This was our first official stay using Airbnb.  Eva had everything ready for us as planned.  The description of the place was as it is listed, and felt just like home.  The place is impeccably clean and and kept simple, which was a + for my wife and family. Clean towels were waiting for us, everything around the home was clean and organized.  No tv available, but who needs it when your on vacation.  We are a family from Southern California and it took a bit to feel the vibe around the neighborhood.  The delis were amazing, just across from the home and metro is only two minutes away, extremely convenient.    The negative is that the neighborhood has poor lighting around the streets , which scared my kids, but we felt safe and at no time did we experience anything out of the ordinary.  My wife and I highly recommend Eva Maria's home and we would most definitely consider staying here again on any of our future trips to NY.  I highly a taxi at night.  As a parent, my only recommendation for other guests would be to take a taxi, Uber, Lyft if you are going to be arriving late.  From Manhattan it was roughly $35 dollars, again we did this, because I had my 7 year old and two boys with me as well.  We felt safe in the neighborhood, but because of the lighting in the street, I felt more comfortable taking a taxi.  Other than that everything was perfect.  Thank you so much Eva and Jacob for making our stay so pleasant.

Eva is very responsive and it is easy to communicate with her.   Eva's place is a modern, spacious and very bright apartment located on two floors of a typical brownstone house. The apartment was clean and looked exactly as described. Our group was made of 5 people. There are 2 bathrooms upstairs and a toilet room downstairs. Worth noting for large groups, the couch in the living room does not turn into a bed. In our case Eva added a small foldable bed in one of the two rooms. That was good enough for us.  A few words on the neighborhood. It is safer than what the general appearance may suggest (poor street lighting, lack of care of public property). Do not let the first impression (especially if you arrive at night) scare you. However, if you want a shiny, clean and centrally located neighborhood, then Eva's apartment is not for you. But in that case you must be willing to spend much more. If you want a cheaper option and still be able to stay in a VERY nice apartment, then go for it. Eva's place is very close to two metro lines, even if the time it takes to go to Manhattan is a little more than optimal.   All in all, we liked the place and we had a nice time there!

We very much enjoyed our stay and would come back any time. The place is very close to the subway (metro) it is about 15 meters from the gate of the building. Getting to the sights in the city center is extremely quick and easy. If you are a tourist and want to see Paris this is an ideal place for you. The area outside of the building is kind of sketchy and you can easily get some unwanted attention. The building itself is very safe. The place has an easy to use shower and most notably a very useful hair dryer so you don’t have to bring your own which is awesome since they can be very clunky. There was a fan in the bedroom, that was great because the summer can be hot. There is also a basic kitchen and a fridge. Check in was very easy and Antoine was very friendly and helpful. We loved it.

Our first place was basically a scam. So to begin, I commend Airbnb for finding us a place on such short notice!  After some miscommunication about number of guests and money, we finally got into the apartment! (Mind you, while all of this back and forth was going on, we were waiting in our car - probably a 7 hour ordeal)  I would expect anyone that rents a place that allows pets to expects pets. Although I don't want to upset other guests, I did not, and do not like the idea of keeping my pet locked in a room 24/7. When I'm not there, sure. I'm okay with compromise. But I too would not appreciate being locked up against my will all day.  Add on the fact that the room I rented wasn't even the room I received! Due to another guest missing their flight, he forced us to stay in a smaller room that was less accomodating. It felt like a punishment. So when the room did became available and we were able to move our things over, we expected to have fresh sheets, linens, and toiletries upon entering. Nothing was made available to us. Plus WE had to remove the sheets and blanket from the previous bed and make our own bed in the new bedroom.  To sum it up, recall what it felt like living with your parents. The strict rules, the hovering, the micromanagement. That's what it felt like staying here. Add on to the fact that he's more in it for the money than making it feel like a home away from home.  Don't waste your time or money and lose your peace in the process.  Some people just shouldn't host.

This lovely apartment is truly charming! Comfortably furnished, very comfortable beds!  Delighted in this heatwave to have central air conditioning and showers with good water pressure to come home to.  The Multi-cultural environment and daily commute in and out of Manhattan via subway enriched our New York experience.  We never felt unsafe, even walking home from the subway station late at night. Charming neighborhood with friendly neighbors. All suggested tips for local amenities (markets, coffee shop, restaurants) were excellent. Overall a most enjoyable stay! The Hewitts

Everything was good! Very clean and quiet room. Very close to the subway. Reasonable price for this room. I like it! Rod is really good person! But this area may be some dangerous at the night time, by my personal opinion. Its Spanish Harlem! But everything was very good for me!

I was travelling alone (middle aged male, quirky) for a conference and a couple of days of picture taking and head 'defraging'.   Beverly the property hostess was easy to connect with and always available the few times I needed her (mostly for silly questions :).    I was delighted to find that her place was huge, and possibly even nicer than it looked in the pictures, and located in a great old brownstone.    Bed was comfortable, all the amenities were there.. For my first AirBnB experience, this was exactly what I hoped for... Casual, with a home away from home feel, and MUCH more affordable than a hotel matchbox.    The apartment is one minute's walk from the G subway line, and it's a no brainer to access Manhattan in a number of ways.   Convenience stores etc. were conveniently close :)    Bed was comfy.  Kitchen big and great.  Even an office area perfect for a little lap top focus.  I know Manhattan well, but this was my first time exploring Brooklyn as well.  Note that 'BedStuy' is not a major 'walking' neighbourhood as most of Manhattan is.  It's interesting for sure, seeming to be a combination African American/Hasidic Jewish cultural mix, and not 'scary' at all.. just not lined with shops.   All in all, a great hostess, a large comfortable place with a wonderful and slightly NOLA vibe (IMHO) in a very accessible location.  Hope to be back to my 'home away from home' soon!

Sabrina was very responsive, flexible, and the place was beautiful.   During Fashion week / 911 week, the apartment was also *extremely affordable*. With hotels in the neighborhood in the $600+ range, this apartment was a steal (and it was quiet). Nice memory foam bed, great bathroom, very clean and bright.

My two high school daughters and I stayed here for 5 days doing college tours/visits (e.g., NYU, Fordham, Columbia, etc.).  They slept in the bedroom (large bed ... maybe king size?) and I slept in the living room.  There was a "click-clack" sofa/bed in there, which I covered with an extra futon the host provided and I was very comfortable.  The "living room" has its own doors and curtains to make it like a private room unto itself.  The two rooms are separated by a hallway with a kitchen and a bathroom, so each room can remain undisturbed while people either use the kitchen or bathroom.  Both rooms had big screen TVs with Netflix, Amazon, YouTube, etc.  There was plenty of heat in each room.  The kitchen was well-stocked with all kinds of pans and spices/cooking oil, etc., and there was a dishwasher.  The bathroom shower was powerful and hot.  There was also a washer/dryer, but we didn't use it (but I'm sure that would be a fantastic amenity).  The building was secure.  I think each "floor" was a separate private residence.  You do have to ascend 3 flights of stairs to get to the top (the rental residence).  We did not find that a problem at all.  In fact, if you stairs-averse, then you are not going to like Manhattan, because it is a walking culture (to the subways, up and down stairs in the subways, walking throughout Central Park).  The neighborhood was nice (I think this is probably one of the nicer neighborhoods in Manhattan ... known as the "Upper East Side").  It seemed quite safe to us.  In fact, I felt everywhere we went was quite safe.  There are pedestrians everywhere (i.e., you are never alone), and these pedestrians generally consist of "regular" people -- mothers pushing their strollers, children walking to school, business people, little old ladies, and then an occasional "homeless" person sprinkled in there.  There were restaurants everywhere, from cheap pizza to expensive sushi.  The subway stations are nearby (3-block, 10-min walk).  There are metro card machines in each station.  We each bought a 7-day metro card with unlimited rides, and it cost $34.  Then, we rode the subways all over town to the different colleges and other places of interest. It was, in my opinion, very simple to understand and figure out.  Manhattan is a thin strip of an island, only 2 miles wide and about 10 miles long, and Central Park takes up half the space.  You are generally only going north ("Uptown") or south ("Downtown").   The streets are laid out in a grid by numbers.  So, the rental is on 73rd Street.  You might take the subway down to "Grand Central Station," which is, I believe, 42nd Street.    What else can I mention?  Central Park is 2 blocks west of the rental, so a very quick walk.  We are super happy that we stayed in this "home" rather than a hotel.  The owner was great, and he owns a business on the bottom floor, so he is always around and available.  We recommend.

We had a great stay at Bobby's adorable place!  It is PERFECTLY located - tons of great restaurants, bars, shopping, etc. right in the neighborhood.  The place was clean and well decorated (love the large fiddle fig and the great art in the place) and Bobby was super flexible with check-in and check-out times.  It was totally stress-free and we had a ball!  Will absolutely rent from Bobby again next time we come to New York.

I had a great stay at Andrea's apartment. She was very friendly and gave me complete privacy; the apartment was spotless, the very spacious room was clean and comfortable with a sunny, street view window. No noise issues, no feeling unsafe, no horrible smells coming from a random restaurant or sewer grate from the street below.......I had full access to the bathroom and never had to wait to get in to shower. The place is only 1/2 block from the 125th street subway station, so it was perfect for me. The neighborhood is safe, quiet, clean, and just one stop away from Columbia University. Andrea was kind and accommodating when I arrived about an hour late (about 10:15pm) due to a plane delay); I was given my keys to the place and was free to come and go as I needed. If you want a clean, safe, affordable place to stay, with complete privacy and easy access to the subway, this place is ideal. Thank you Andrea, for being such a great host!

Stay was unpleasant because of the: 1) nightly noisy music coming from the bar next door until 4 am. 2) beds were very creaky causing a lot of noise when getting up or turning and so disturbing others who are asleep

My husband and I had a great experience staying at Gregory's place. The apartment is lovely. It's bright, clean, comfortable, and quiet. There's a lot of natural light, and the balcony patio is a great place to hang out if you like the outdoors. The apartment is in a professional-looking, attractive building which is located within a very short walk to restaurants, groceries, coffee, and a subway station. We found a parking spot for the weekend right outside the front entrance. Gregory's communication with us was excellent, which made the reservation process (and the whole trip) stress-free.  I would definitely recommend this place, and we will not hesitate to stay there again!

Although I am grateful my friends and I were given the opportunity to stay in Brooklyn, I was a little disappointed with the experience. As soon as I entered the apartment, I could tell the pictures had been modified to portray a more “modern” look to the establishment by means of lighting and professional camera. Some items had been taken away as the apartment was a little bare. In addition, it was apparent the sheets had not been changed in a while as the odor was quite overwhelming. The couch had been displayed on the website as a bed only to attract potential guests. The microwave in the kitchen did not warm the food and the bathroom was quite small. The host had not disclosed that she had another roommate living there so that doubled the traffic throughout the house. Jelena was specific that we should lock the doors at all times; unfortunately when we came back from the city the main door was not locked therefore putting us in danger of having our belongings taken. On the website she was specific that noise travels which is true however she had music on the first couple of minutes of our arrival. To make matters worse, the roommate told us to keep it down when we had music on as it disturbed her sleep. Overall, Jelena had a friendly attitude, I’d hate to be submitting a displeasing review but I must be honest and input my experience.

Staying in Rob's apartment wasn't as pleasant as I expected to be. The description was accurate, except the "clean" part. Unfortunately, Rob wasn't present (he was in a Brazil) and his roommates were a little bit messy.   When I first come to his apartment, there were some stains on the bed sheets. Rob responded to me that it's a sweat stain probably. Luckily we had our own sleeping bags so we don't have to deal with this.   The bathroom was simply disgusting. The toilet wasn't working at all. I had to fix it twice BY MYSELF because Rob's roommates apparently didn't care. Once, someone peed into the toilet but didn't bother with flushing it. So I come to the bathroom and there was a toilet full of urine. I know that's not Rob's mistake, but he's the one who's renting an apartment and if he can't assure that his roommates are neat, he shouldn't rent the apartment at all.

You can book Sarah's Apartment without fear, it is clean, safe, less than 5 minutes from the subway, there are DELIs everywhere for you to have that breakfast. A short walk takes you to Dollar Tree, Marshalls, TJ Maxx, Old Navy, Bed Bath & Beyond. Wi-fi internet was good, towels were clean and smelling good, you just have to remember to have your bath and personal hygiene products, as it says in the description, if you haven't bought them yet, go to Dollar Tree and have a party there, all for $1.00. Sarah is very friendly and makes you feel at ease, I felt like I was at home, I have nothing to complain about. On my next trip to NYC, Sarah's Apartment will definitely be my first choice.

The place is clean, the bedroom is spacious enough to dispose of your luggage with the strict minimum of equipment (bed, nighstand and a chair) and the location is good : at 5min from the subway wich is at 20min from Time Square, we didn’t ask for more. I would just suggest to put a plank of wood on the bedhead to avoid the building opposite to have a view on your room like they have now.   Sarah is a joyful person and it’s visible that she wants you to enjoy your stay, but you have to follow the rules, so many rules. In fact, they are not really constraining at least for someone who just wants a place to sleep (which was our case), but when you receive a message at 2am to remind you to put down the toilet seat, or, more serious, when you wait 30min outside in the rain because « the check-in was at 12, not 11:30 » while she was at home, it put some stress on your nerves. We understand that she might not have been ready, but we were here in advance, not by choice, but because of the rain, she could have proposed to wait in the hall for example.   I’m not saying that Sarah isn’t a good host, she is kind and you quickly understand that she wants you to have a great stay, but she forgets that for most, you are in a city you don’t know and even if you want to be faultless, you won’t always be.  In short I would recommend this place, but remember that you’re an extra and must not be noisy.

Amazing place, few steps from one of the most linked subway station. Seemed a pretty safe neighborhood, don't let you scare from whoever says the opposite. The house was wonderful, very clean and with many features, even if we did not use the kitchen. It was like staying at our own house and Sarah is a wonderful host, she suggested some place to go and was at disposal for everything. The low price compared with other stayings is due to the fact that the main attractions of NYC are downtown and midtown, but the subway is very efficient and in half hour you can reach everywhere.

The room is specious, clean and cozy; has some hotel vibe, and I really like it. I wish there were outputs close to our beds though. When we checked in there was some miscommunication and we waited outside of another room for an hour, it was quite unpleasant honestly. Host has been fairly responsive and offer a new room eventually, I really appreciate that.

Couldn't have asked for a better location.  Two blocks from Times Square, right in the heart of Hell's Kitchen.  Lots of food and cafes close by as well as laundromats and drug stores if you need anything.  A safe neighbourhood.  Couple things to note: steep, narrow stairs to get in and there is a bar downstairs that you will hear all night.  It isn't as loud as you think it will be but nonetheless the noise is noticeable.  Hosts communicated well and it was perfect for our family of four.

We stayed 8 nights in this apartment. It is just as it looks in the pictures, maybe a little smaller, but there is enough space for 2 people. Everything was clean. The area is very lively, nothing dangerous and very close to Times Square and points of interest. Despite there being a lot of noise outside, the room was super quiet, you couldn't hear anything from outside and it is an area with many restaurants and bars. We had communication problems with the host a few weeks before the trip, but when the problem was solved they responded quickly.  They changed our towels almost daily and our sheets twice during our stay, without asking for it. The air conditioning works very well. The kitchen is very complete, although we hardly use it. We will return to New York and we will surely repeat this apartment, due to its quality-price ratio.

We had an awesome time in NYC and really loved Mels' appartement. It was spacious, clean and comfortable. The fact that it was so close to the Subway and bus stations made it easy to travel to Manhattan.   Mel responded swiftly to the questions we had and was a great host.  We can recommend this appartment to visitors who are not affraid to take the stairs to the 3rd floor.  @Mel: Thanks for the hospitality and your kind service!  Rob and Geraldine Gronau, Germany

Very good accommodation. Great location. We were in a room overlooking an interior courtyard so very quiet. Very clean. We appreciated the change of towels every day. Did not meet our hosts. We had no contact with them. Possibility of leaving your suitcases on arrival and departure on the stairs with a bicycle anti-theft system. Very practical when you have to check out at 11 a.m. and your flight is at 10 p.m. We highly recommend this accommodation, which is more like a small hotel than a room rented from a private individual. I would return without hesitation.

Everything went good. Apartment is as described, nice and clean. There is everything you need at the place. Close to a lot of spots, 5 min walk to the train station. HOWEVER. There was a very unpleasant situation with the host/manager. A couple of days after booking, he called to tell me that there was a glitch on the Airbnb website and the apartment price is higher than it was shown on the website. He asked me to pay him in cash upon arrival. In addition, he claimed he called Airbnb, and the representative said they hold no responsibility in such circumstances. I called Airbnb thereafter and representative said there was no glitch, and no one called them in regards to this apartment. This leads me to believe the host (manager) simply wanted more money.  After I told the manager about my call to Airbnb, he said he has the right to raise prices, even after the apartment has been booked. However he said he wouldn’t, because we are coming with a little kid! The weirdest thing I’ve ever heard.  Also, parking information was misleading. Parking on property is available for $25/day, but it seems like it’s free in the listing (honestly speaking, one can easily park on the street for free). When I said the prices are high and I will park on the street, manager responded with a threat saying it would be sad if something was to happen to my car!  I would cancel this booking, but Airbnb insured me, that they will cover all the expenses if something went wrong at arrival or during the stay. Piece of advice to the host, raise the prices instead of lying to people.  Thank you for your hospitality.

Excellent location!!! 2 blocks from times square! It couldn't be better, close to many subways. Room with private bathroom and shared kitchen where there is a refrigerator, stove, coffee maker and dishes. Climb only by stairs. There are locks to leave your suitcases if you arrive before check in or after check out. The street is very safe and busy, to walk at any time without any fear. They changed our towels every day, which doesn't happen in other Airbnbs.   I would return and recommend it to those who want to have a comfortable place with a good location!

I had an amazing stay! Melbourne’s place is just as advertised.   I came to town to onboard for my first week on a new job and, Melbourne’s place provided a nice, clean, peaceful reprieve after each stress filled day.   I will definitely return.

Staying at this Airbnb was one of the best decisions for our trip to the city! The place itself was cozy, quiet, and the perfect size for us two travelers. The personal touch with the interior design made us feel right at home. Greg himself was extremely hospitable as he let us drop off our stuff when we arrived earlier than expected. There  is a large market only a short walk away if you need anything (which also had easy, free  street parking during the weekend). The location was optimal next to the subway to get in and out of manhattan without any stress. With all honesty I would recommend this place to anyone looking to really relax when you come back from sight seeing. Thanks Greg and best of luck in your future!

This place is AWESOME! will definitely stay again, the location is 2 small blocks away from all the action, there is a great deli place on 8th called Carve is delicious and inexpensive, the private bathroom is super clean and you feel SAFE in this place. Love love love it! This was my first airbnb experience and I was afraid it wasn't gonna be as described, but it wasn't the case! Thank you very much.

A great experience! Beautiful apartment, very friendly, very well decorated and well appointed. The real asset is the location: very close metro stations which serve all of Downton and also very close to Central Park and therefore the biggest museums/walks We really have the impression of living in New York! Additionally, Rob is very friendly and flexible. He responds very quickly to messages. Really a very good address!!

We had a wonderful time staying in Rob's Airbnb. It was in a great area and a convenient location as stated. Within an easy walk to Central Park and 200m to the nearest subway station. The accommodation was comfortable, including a good sized separate living area. All the facilities required were available and the wifi worked well. Rob was an excellent host and gave very clear instructions on how to get into the apartment and provided information on local restaurants and shops. He was very responsive in answering my questions prior to our arrival.

Rob's place is simply amazing! Stay here and you'll get to feel what being a real New Yorker is like. Check in was a breeze and the location could not have been better, less than a few steps to the subway and only a short stroll to Central Park. The apartment has pretty much everything you'll need and for those little things you forget, there's a very friendly grocery store close by. I would definitely stay here again! Thanks Rob.

I found Rob's apartment to be wonderful for my visit.  I was primarily in town for business but because of its perfect location, I was able to spend evenings in the park or the enjoyable neighborhood restaurants.  I was able to walk to my office in midtown and also make use of the nearby subway line.  The apartment was very comfortable - especially the bed.  It was very easy communicating with Rob before and during my stay and I didn't experience any problems.
Rob's apartment is really well located, a few meters from the metro, very clean, the bed very comfortable. Perfect for the stay. I recommend

My evaluation to Rob's apartament is the best   the place is quiet, beautiful clean, very close to subway , supermarket and restaurant  The apartament is very clean and confortable 100 % I can recomend  You really

My stay at Rob's apartment was enjoyable. It has an unpretentious home-from-home feel, which I felt was a nice touch. It's not full-on luxury, but it had everything I wanted, was comfortable, clean, quiet and spacious. It has a big four poster bed with a firm mattress and I slept very well, knowing the flat was secure and safe. It is ideally located for sightseers, being 5 minutes' walk from Central Park and 10 from midtown. The subway is two minutes away. I'd recommend it to anyone who's on a budget, looking for good value in a midtown location.

We stayed at Markus apartment for 4 days. Communication is very easy and Markus responds immediately. We were  on the street with two children because of our booking was cancelled on arrival. I messaged to Markus, and he confirmed booking in few minutes. He helped us from being "homeless in NY". Only one inconvenience - we didnt have building entrance key and every time had to wait somebody let us enter inside.

We had a great stay in NY. Yann met up with us in the apartment. He was helpful and nice. He opened a bottle of Rosé and showed us around the apartment. The area is very nice! Big plus!  It was however unpleasant to find out that there were bed bugs in the apartment. Both me and my boyfriend got bitten during the nights. We also found a bed bug in our bag.

Perfect location and accommodations for a night or two in the city! The place is surrounded by bars and restaurants so it is noisy at closing time, in addition to the street noise, but the location is A+++. The bed linens were a bit worn and the fitted sheet had an index-finger sized hole, but I suspect that’s from washing with bleach (which I really appreciate!). Super clean top to bottom. Great value in dead center Midtown. Would stay here again and again!

This host is unsafe, unreliable, and invades privacy. She changed the location of the booking under the table, one night before we were due to arrive. She made false accusations and threats, which were confirmed by Airbnb representatives. She entered the Airbnb with her own key while her guests were trying to shower. She made us leave immediately upon checking in, because she wanted to sell her alternate spot (which we accepted to be accommodating to her) for a higher price.

Jae’s place is very clean and comfortable. She communicated all the necessary details and it was a stress free stay. She even left waters and fruit for us in the fridge. She’s great and the place is too.

I was looking for a month long stay in NY and Brian's place was perfect.  Location tick - A,B,C,D trains less than 1 block away. 30mins to midtown. Loads of food and drink options within 15min walk and great food delivery options if you get lazy (which i often did).  I was staying by myself and never felt unsafe in the area. There's always shady characters in NY but never ran into any issues even after hours.   Size tick - Brian's place is a proper 1 bedroom apartment with full size kitchen, spacious living areas, huge bed, big screen tvs :)  Comfort level tick - minimal street noise, bed was super comfortable, good water pressure and temp in shower.  WFH set up was great, proper desk, proper chair, big monitor, good wifi.  Communication tick - Brian was super prompt and super helpful with all my questions and went out of this way to check in on me. Much appreciated.  Only downside is not a huge amount of natural sunlight but happily trade that off for comfort any day.

First Airbnb experience and it was a pleasant one. Stayed 5 nights. Simple room was clean and just as described. It included tv, wifi, bed linens, clean towels, toilet paper (thin Scott brand but I suspect this is to appease the sensitive NY plumbing), shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and hair dryer. Found a couple of hairs on the bed sheets when we arrived but I'm hoping they belonged to the cleaning person when they made the bed. As other stated, no hand soap was provided so we picked up a pump at the nearby Duane Reade (Walgreens). This is a walk up so if you have any mobility issues or plan to take very heavy luggage, this may not be the place for you.   Bed was on the small side (matched description; full size)m and kinda noisy so I wouldn't really recommend this room for a "romantic getaway". However, the bed was surprisingly comfortable if you prefer firm mattresses.   You are provided door codes in advance and you're able to check in on your own after 3p. Check out is at 11a. They allow you to leave your bags in the common area before and after check in if you need. There are bike locks hanging from the stair railing as well as security cameras so we felt pretty comfortable leaving our bags for a few hours on our last day.   The hosts have several rooms rented out simultaneously in the building, all accessible by door codes. There is a common area on the 2nd floor with a refrigerator (although it did not feel cold when we checked), sink, and stove. Besides our attempt at placing leftovers in the fridge, we did not use the kitchen.   The hosts manage their rentals very much like a hotel so if you're looking for a personal Airbnb experience, this place may not be for you. If you're looking for a simple room with hotel-like independence for a good value, this is a great option. We did not meet the hosts, we only saw a woman periodically during the day who we presumed to be the cleaning staff. She did not speak English but appeared to be friendly.   Street can be a bit noisy since there are lots of restaurants/clubs nearby but I used a white noise machine and earplugs to sleep so it wasn't a huge problem. Really didn't hear the other visitors in the surrounding rooms.   Overall, accurate description, friendly communication with host, and good value for staying in the city. I'd recommend this to my friends.

Everything is perfect! It's like being in a hotel. Code entry is really convenient and takes the stress out of losing keys. The room is super clean and the cleaning lady changes the towels regularly. Ideal location! You can even leave your suitcases on the day of departure thanks to anti-theft devices designed for. In short, I recommend!

Be’s place was an excellent mix of hospitality and location. The two bedrooms and living space were perfect for a weekend in the city, while the proximity to the Q line was a perfect jumping off point for adventures throughout Manhattan. Be was communicative and left detailed check-in instructions, which made our arrival stress-free. I would definitely stay again when coming to NYC!

This place is great. Very convenient if you will be traveling into manhattan. The train station is located right around the corner. The area might seem a little sketchy but if that’s your worry, the police precinct is on the corner. The place is perfect for 2-4 people. And great for a 2-day or a week long trip. The host are quick to respond to any issues and very hospitable. Overall, it’s a great place and would recommend it to anyone who’s planning on making a trip to NY.

This is a fantastic apartment in a great location, however the host is unreasonable about the house rules. I visited in the middle of July, with temperatures in the 90s, and was told that I could not run the single window unit air conditioner during the day. I attempted to honor this request, but the apartment was sweltering when I'd arrive back, and I wasn't able to sleep due to the extreme temperature inside. I got multiple diatribes from the host about how I need to think about the environment, and how we are "in the midst of an environmental catastrophe," and how "the money you paid is not for the use of the AC", and how extreme indoor temperatures are "part of the NYC summer experience." It was so bad that I had to open an arbitration with Airbnb in an attempt to get the host to understand that access to using the air conditioner in July is included in the price I paid to rent the unit. Airbnb sided with me, and the host was told that I was entitled to leave the air on so the apartment would be a comfortable temperature for sleeping. On my last full day, the host or one of their roommates breached the arbitration agreement and entered the apartment (after Airbnb told them not to) and turned off the air. I was unable to sleep the entire last night, and did not feel safe there (during one diatribe, the host said that they "do activism to the point of my wife having gotten arrested in protests," which Airbnb arbitrators took as a potential threat of violence since we were currently having an environmental dispute). This was a very unfortunate situation since otherwise, this is an ideal place to stay. The apartment is large and has everything you'd need to be comfortable for an extended stay. The entrance to the 6 train is at the end of the block, directly next to a police station where police were always milling around outside. The area felt safe to me because of this, and I arrived after midnight multiple times and did not feel unsafe at all. This would be a great place to stay in the winter, when you won't have to deal with the constant harassment about using the air conditioner. (everything in quotes are exact quotes from messages I got from the host)

Esther's place is really great. Located just a short walk from Central Park and only up 1 flight of stairs. There are restaurants everywhere in the neighborhood, local drug stores, coffee, etc. This place is really her home so do be mindful of her things there. She was very flexible with check-in and check-out time.

B's accommodation is well located. the Q subway line is at the end of the street. But that's the only advantage. the accommodation is poorly maintained. Floor was dirty, toilet flush was leaking, bedside lamp broken and I'll skip the rest. the accommodation is designed for 5 but there are only two chairs and a small table. Lots of initial decorations, I would have preferred with extra chairs instead of a table at the end of the sofa or the high chair which serves no purpose.  In addition, we only had one roll of toilet paper for 3 people for 4 days which we paid over 1000 euros all the same. I don't think several rolls of toilet paper will ruin the owner. The kitchen bottom and medium. And there are no cleaning products. This accommodation is just made to bring in money on the backs of tourists. there is no comfort. The most unpleasant thing was the air conditioning which made noise throughout the stay even when it was off.  This is the worst Airbnb accommodation I have ever had. a tourist trap.

I rented the place for my parents who came for a visit. I live in the neighborhood as well and have rented my place through Airbnb a couple of times and so did some neighbors/friends of mine so I have a good feeling for the type of places you can rent in Fort Greene. I think the apartment is overpriced, and that the score people gave it is inflated. I would give it 3.5 stars.  It is a decently cute apartment, but it is small, under-maintained and feels thrifty. The host is I'm sure a very nice person, was very responsive and we haven't used the free bike rental which seems like a nice gesture, but some things in the apartment just through me off - for example leaving an empty olive oil bottle, empty shampoo and almost empty conditioner bottle for an 8 day stay are, in my opinion, worse than not leaving anything.  Another example - The bed frame was bigger than the mattress and had a sharp/dangerous corner that my parents had to wrap with a towel to make sure they don't bump their feet against. the fan was dirty, the stovetop was half dysfunctional, the AC was very noisy and did not cool very well, etc. in addition, there are 2 very steep flights of stairs in order to get to the apartment, so if you are older or have an issue climbing stairs with heavy laguge, you should be aware of that.  Overall, it was an ok experience since the main consideration for us was the location, but since the host charges a rather substantial cleaning fee and people "rave" about the apartment I wanted to bring in my own perspective, as a person who lives 5 minutes away and has rented their place through Airbnb a couple of times in 3 different cities.

Super person, location, and hospitality. We used this Airbnb when our son was in Columbia Presbyterian hospital and it was a 5 minute, safe walk in the morning and at night. Boris was able to accommodate us last minute and relieved our stress of where we were going to stay. Cats are so playful and sweet.

At first everything was perfect, it is an apartment with everything one needs and very clean, the beds are large and the bathroom is very very good, the problem was that when we woke up, my sister-in-law found a mouse inside a grocery package that we had bought, and well, finding mice inside the house I think is something very unpleasant for most people, for this reason it is important that Nneka carries out a deep cleaning of the apartment. She was very kind but the mouse problem is something that cannot be ignored.

A very small place but adequate for one night stay and was perfect for our purposes. Parking was surprisingly easy. The wifi was fast. The  place was very clean. I didn't like the quality of the sheets (sort of slippery plastic feeling), but thankfully I had my own blankets with me that I put on top of the sheets and it was great. When I was sitting at the small kitchen table and eating, a airfreshner on the kitchen table sprayed at me and it was very unpleasant. I took out the batteries and put it away. Otherwise everything was great.

I try to be fair with my reviews— good and bad.  Good: pretty decent amount of space for NYC— the hosts are also nice. Nice to have a fridge and microwave. Little Italy is walking distance. They tried to make it feel homey.   Bad: The price. They are way more expensive than any place I’ve stayed at in the Bronx with a similar amount of space that allow pets AND had parking. The street parking was a lot harder than the ad suggested. I’ve stayed at places in the Bronx like this before and generally the host will let the guest park in front of the driveway (blocking it) and they go and find another space. I spent a lot of money to have to hunt for a spot each night when I thought it was on premises. There is a spot for a VERY small car and the host would be blocking you in anyways. I felt deceived on this. I paid more for this place because it said parking on premises. Instead I ended up walking around the park late at night from rehearsal. Also fun is the parking game you must play every weekday from 8:30-10am for street cleaning. You can risk being double parked or ticketed OR get up every day early after being at rehearsal and work til midnight the night before.   Safety: the neighborhood seems sort of safe for the most part but my first night some guy was screaming about God coming for him and then he laid down on the ground next to my car. I watched him to make sure he was ok then ran to the place.  The second night I was thankfully being dropped off in an Uber — the driver waited with me because some guy obviously on drugs was rubbing himself on the gate to the apartment. I think it’s a safe enough neighborhood but within walking distance of some very bad areas and definitely not safe for a single female to be parking around a park at night and walking to the space.    it’s a basement— and not like I’ve seen basement rooms done before. There are pipes hanging down low enough for you to hit your head. I felt like I was constantly crouching.  I was uncomfortable the entire time using the kitchen because of this. They did add padding to the pipes so at least when I whacked my head every day the blow was softened. Once the lights are out it is SO dark it is impossible to tell what time it is. There were centipedes— which means more bugs somewhere else.

Kaz and his team were very responsive and the apartment was clean and exactly as shown on the listing. I stayed in this room for over a month as a woman traveling by herself and I had a wonderful experience. The neighborhood is great; there's public transportation (subway and bus) nearby, lots of restaurants and bars, many supermarkets etc. I never felt unsafe in this neighborhood. As it's located on a busy street it can get quite noisy, but I never had difficulties falling asleep. Thanks to the AC in my room, it stayed cool even through the hottest days of summer. The kitchen and bathroom did heat up quite a bit. Overall, I would highly recommend this room to any solo travelers!

I really enjoyed my stay in Brooklyn, the place is very small but it has everything a traveler will need, the place is very close to the train but it takes about an hour to get to Manhattan, if you are traveling in cold weather homeless people will use the J train to get out of the cold so it is not a good idea to ride alone at night
Near the train station. The area might seem unsafe at first impression, but it certainly turned out to be a quiet neighborhood, perfect for what we wanted. Go out to see the city

This host was absolutely amazing! Prompt communication, excellent and stress-free check in, full privacy, lots of local shops around, 2 minute walk from the J train. Host goes above and beyond to make sure your stay is great. The place was very clean! I was so impressed! I would definitely stay here again!

Lola has been an amazing host, always ready to help out the best she could. the studio is really clean, functional and well located. Lola will make your stay easier and stress free as she always responds to your questions and shows a great sense of duty. I really recommend this studio.

We loved our stay in Fort Greene! Obed is an exceptional host. 5 stars all around!! He allowed an early check in for us after we communicated in advance that our flight was getting in early. His instructions for everything were very clear and took the guess work out of check in and check out. Both of which were really simple. The apartment was immaculately cleaned. I’m not kidding. Spotless. The apartment itself is spacious, and a full apartment with a gas stove, full kitchen, full bath and 2 closets, Couches, and even a smart tv with a guest log in on Netflix for ease of use. For the listing price, it’s a steal. He mentions street noise bc Dekalb is a busy road, but we stayed for 8 days and it didn’t bother us. The bedroom is on the back end of the apt and not right off of the road. If you close the bedroom door you can’t hear anything from the street really. The neighborhood is very welcoming and almost quaint, which I wasn’t expecting in nyc, a pleasant surprise. Cute dogs everywhere! Everything we needed was within a block or two. Subway stations into Manhattan were very close. The stores nearby have yummy sandwiches and the restaurants are delish. The coffee spot across the street was so convenient. If we come back to visit nyc I would definitely stay here again! Thanks, Obed for everything! Highly recommend ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

We had a fantastic stay at Mariela’s place. She was extremely helpful and made our trip stress-free! There’s plenty of things to do nearby and it’s very easy to catch the subway around the corner into Manhattan. Very fun place! Would definitely recommend.

We had an awesome stay at Mario's AirBnB. The check in and check out process was quick, easy, and stress free. The apartment itself is a large studio with two queen sized beds in the common area. We traveled in a group of three, and were grateful to have two real beds to crash on every night - something that proved difficult to find during our Manhattan AirBnB search. We always felt like we had plenty of room to roam during our stay since the common area also included a living room space with two TV's and big comfy couches and arm chairs. So, space was never an issue even with two queen sized beds in the same area. Again, a rare thing to find in a Manhattan apartment.   Location wise, you couldn't ask for anything better. The AirBnB is close to lots of awesome restaurants, bars, and is also across the street from Tompkins Square Park. So, whether you're looking to eat, drink, or take a breather you have everything you need all around you. This AirBnB is in the East Village, which is centrally located to most sightseeing in Manhattan. A plus for first time visitors.

My stay at Carly's place was great! I could feel the extra effort she has put to make me feel comfortable and at home- a rare gem in many airbnb experiences I’ve recently had. The room was adorable, the double bed was comfortable, the whole place was very clean, and the flatmate I met was very friendly.  Location is fantastic. Very close to 2 subway stations, nice cafe’s and some urban parks. The neighborhood felt safe to me as a woman even very late (3-4am) at night. I needed a place to crush at the end of the night, when I’m back from my adventures, then wake up in the (very late) morning and drag myself to the nicest coffee shop around. For that cause the place was perfect.  Keep in mind, the room is very small. I didn’t mind, but if you were planning to stay in your room most of the day (why would you? New York is outside, waiting), you might find it too cozy. A little warning (about the city, not about this lovely place!) if you are used to european standards regarding public transportation- lower your expectations as much as possible. Nyc subway at night is super slow, where you have 2-3 connections coming every 15-20 minutes without any updates, unsynchronized, and you are surrounded by poor homeless people and urine smells in the stations, waiting for a track that knew better days in the 1950’s. Average commute time from manhattan / Harlem to Brooklynn took me an hour and a half  “thanks” to this extremely bad shape public transportation system. Thankfully the house was very close to the station...

Thanks for a great experience! At the beginning of the trip we were very scared to take the MTA system to get around, but Fabiola explained to us how to use and it was great and cheaper than ubering around NY!!! Newly renovated bathroom, cute little studio for such a great deal! Thank you again for being so accommodating

A really cozy place in a diverse neighborhood. I never felt unsafe. I felt it was a real authentic NYC experience staying here. The apartment itself was clean and stylish. No complaints. 100% would recommend and stay again.

The place was awesome we had a family of 5 we had plenty of room do not let the pictures fool you this place is huge compared to new york standards the area was good didn't feel unsafe at all easy to go from the airport and easy to go to Manhattan and back nyesha was quick to respond when we had a question I would  recommend nyesha place anytime to anyone I'm 100 percent positive when we return to new york we will be picking Nyesha place again.
An Amazing experience that will take so much stress away from you  and help you relax comfortably.

Val is the best host I have ever had.  Short version: there was a misunderstanding with the dates and he allowed us to sleep an extra night at no cost and always being kind.  Long version: Our flight arrived in NY on Friday at 12am and we would be with Val at 2am. Due to a communication error, Val was waiting for us on Saturday at 2am. Our taxi dropped us off 6 blocks from Val's house at 2am! Alone, without access to an Uber or Taxi, we walked to Val's house (tip: check maps carefully and check that you are going to the correct address). We arrived at 2.15 am, I was scared, the streets alone, I felt scared to be honest. Val didn't answer the first time we knocked, like until the 3rd time I answered through the speaker and out of surprise he opened the door for us, we talked about the misunderstanding, at that moment he swore he was going to send us straight to hell because 1) it was 2.30am and 2) he had scheduled our arrival for Saturday and the room was occupied!!! However, Val always maintained a friendly and warm tone. He invited us to sleep in the living room and he felt sad, obviously we were the ones who were sad, he shouldn't feel like that.

John was a good host the location was great. It was about a 5 min walk to the subway which is super convenient for getting around even during the late hours. the neighborhood was pretty quite with not a lot going on and it had a place to park which is a major plus. However, it did have some quirks the shower is much smaller then you think it is I'm 5'6 and weight 210 with a pretty average build and just barely able to close the door while in it, so hopefully that gives you some idea as to how small it is. If your left handed wiping while on the toilet may be a little tricky and awkward due to the fact that the counter is right by the toilet. Also there is no shade/curtain on the sliding door to the backyard yard which is shared with the downstairs tenant so no walking around in your birthday suite unless you don't mind showing off your goods. The TV is a little hard to work your going to need to make sure it's connected to the wifi ever time you turn it back on to make sure it works correctly and the remote didn't have working batteries. There was also a nail sticking out of the floor next to the closet in the bedroom so be cautious. It can get a little hot at night in the bedroom so you may want to bring a small fan with you like we did or sleep with the bedroom door open to let the AC. The only AC unit is in the living room. The freezer door doesn't open all the way and the fridge is pretty small.

Location - within 10 min walking distance to Times Square and touristy area; quiet street but also sketchy part of the city  Room - much smaller than expected; dirty, questionable sheets, thankfully no bedbugs. TV and remote did not work and there was a questionable camcorder on top of the TV that we covered during our stay.  Bathroom - provided clean bathroom towels each day; shower water pressure is good and water drained well.

This is the nicest Air bnb I’ve ever experienced. It’s so nice I can’t begin to explain it. The place was gorgeous. Not a single thing to complain about. You will definitely leave this place wanting to steal decor ideas for your own home. House goals!!!

Stella's place is perfect for the independent solo traveler who is not afraid to stay somewhere off the beaten path.  It is close to two subway stations and convenient to JFK.  The apartment is very clean with excellent amenities.   It is a good value and I would stay here again.

There are a lot of great comments that I generally agreed with But the location is not ideal. The cottage is located in an area with two big trash dumpsters, worn down houses nearby and the water out on balcony smells bad- maybe it’s just the summer time. However, we loved the interior- professionally  designed, very beautiful and clean. We enjoyed the inside of the house and game boards provided.  WiFi had some glitches but ok overall.  It’s hard to get the right water temperature in the shower. It is either extremely hot or cold- dangerous for children in the house. There were a few annoying flies in the house which my kids have to chase them down- please provide fly swatter.

Robbin’s apartment is really well located close to shops, cafes, bars etc. and convenient for the subway into Manhattan.   It’s also only 10 mins walk to the top edge of Central Park so an easy walk to lovely green spaces. Once we gained access it was all fine, but we had to contact the Airbnb Helpdesk as we didn’t get any response to emails for checking in and this was stressful.  Robbin’s family however, lived above the apartment and were all very charming and helpful - thank you.

Pleasant stay in Dawa&Phurpa’s accommodation. Located in Queens, the closest subway station is 30 minutes from Manhattan and several lines are direct. The accommodation is OK. The hosts are accommodating (our flight left late and they kindly agreed to hold our suitcases).
Wonderful air conditioner, clean and large rooms, pretty entrance, and a great location near drug stores and restaurants.

Very clean and cosy unit in a great location. General stores, banks, quick bites and the subway are all within a 5-10min walking radius. Gabriel was an extremely accommodating host and constantly assured me that he was on hand to help if need be. The check-in/checkout process was very straightforward and secure. This place was a steal for a short-notice booking and I will definitely consider Gabriel’s unit for future visits to New York.

Teresa's place is in a prime spot for NYC, right in the smack middle of it all! The room is great, the entire apartment has heating so we were very comfortable in there. The patio was very nice. The bathroom was very clean, overall I give it a very good recommendation. Exceeded my expectations above and beyond and especially for the price I paid, I personally think it was a steal! Thank you for letting us stay again

The place was located very close to a train station, in Harlem. For an Australian, it was quite scary staying in this location.   When we arrived the fold out bed was broken meaning we potentially had someone without a bed. Christina was very prompt to fix this issue which was appreciated considering we just got off a 6 hour flight.   There was also a few issues with the blinds and shower curtain falling off, however easily fixed.   The place itself is quite small, however quite nice.

The apartment is very nice, it is located on the 3rd floor and there is no elevator, travel light if you stay there. We honestly didn't like the area since we had an accident in which near the subway they tried to steal my sweatshirt and my girlfriend's bag. Outside the apartment there was a lot of garbage, we had to cancel our reservation due to the aforementioned mishap, we were only there for 1 night and when we asked for a refund despite what had happened, the only thing they refunded us was half of the reservation, since we only stayed one night and our situation was something extraordinary. We did a search for the most dangerous areas of Manhattan and Harlem is one of them. In short, the apartment is very nice but it is located in what I think is a dangerous area. From Christina I would have asked for more empathy when it came to the refund since we had to pay even more to move to a hotel. I understand that this is business but I think the fairest thing was that they would charge us for the night we spent there and return us the rest of the reservation.

Greg's place is even cleaner and neater than the pictures can portray. It's a comfortable place to stay. I was grateful for the ability to park in the driveway that Greg provided, and I was especially thankful for his communication and his help that made our daughter's move-in to Fordham less stressful.
Teresa is very accommodative in terms of communication. Her place was a steal and the location is superb! Will come back there for sure.

Definitely a waterfront luxury building with amazing amenities — a total steal for the price in the area. Tricky check in but Andrew helped us through it. The only down side was the place wasn’t that clean. But I’d totally stay here again!

Be prepared for a noisy area - the subway is literally right outside the window. There are sound proof windows but this does not cancel out the noise completely. Please also be aware there is no thermostat to alter the temperature. Bring your own fans in the winter - the heat is blasting. Also be prepared for a host that is non-responsive to issues regarding the reservation, he is not very easy to work with resolving issues. I would recommend calling AirBNB for any issues that arise. Great apartment, kind of in a sketchy area, but worth the money for a whole apartment in Brooklyn.

Jean and Aric are excellent hosts.  Communication is flawless, prompt and easy.  I consider it a plus that this studio is part of their home, and that they cared about us as guests. We have walked in the neighborhood very late at night and never felt unsafe. Thanks, Jean and Aric!
nice space good get away alot of homeless people in the area

The hotel is a great place to stay for a short period of time. The location is great in terms of being walking distance from Hudson Yards and Times Square. The only downside is the actual building is located on a somewhat sketchy/outdated block. The rooms have updated amenities such as a microwave, fridge, TV w/ Cable, adjustable climate control. The cleanness of the room was not great, but was acceptable for NY city standards. The staff was nice and helpful. Just keep in mind this is definitely not a traditional hotel or a traditional hotel experience. Overall, I would stay again but just lower your standards.

My stay at "The Spot" was perfect for a weekend getaway. My guest and I enjoyed it very much. The place was clean, modern and had everything we needed. The only little downside is the neighborhood is a little sketchy at night but I would definitely stay again. Thank you Dwain for your hospitality!

When writing a review I believe it’s key to state my lived experience upfront so anyone with a disposition in opposition to my lived experience can just skip this if they don’t find any of this relatable or relevant to what they’re trying to do or what they can comprehend. I’m a black man born and raised on the south side of Chicago I’m well acquainted with city living. I’m a working professional writer, artist, businessman, free lance investor. My siblings and I were headed to new york to shoot a poetry video for my sister who is a renowned poet who’s written two poetry books and working on a third. All that being said. This was a sibling trip AND  a WORKING trip. We were staying here for a week and planned to WORK AND PLAY and expected infrastructure that would support both of these things and provide us with sufficient hospitality to comfort us during the length of our stay. Unfortunately, I ultimately found “The Spot” Inadequate to suit my needs.  TL DR; All in all I felt like I should have got my money back and moved into a hotel. At this price point, at this value, “The Spot” seems like a place where you can rest your head for a day or two but it is not worth an extended stay for the modern day professional. I found Dwains service to be adequate. There were some things I found downright unacceptable but we discussed these things and have settled them. I don’t like knowing the owner of my BnB has surveilled me and I don’t like being contacted during my period of rest to discover that you’re outside and you want me to take out the trash. It soured the taste of my whole stay.   On Air BnB I’m a customer first and foremost. And in return, I’m agreeing to be a good steward and cherish the opportunity to dwell in someones home for an extended stay. I agree to maintain the place. And follow the house rules. But ultimately? I’m a paying customer. With the preamble out of the way, let me tell everyone coming after me what EXACTLY they can look forward to seeing at “The Spot” Because every review prior to mine is either an exaggeration, or simply a bold faced lie- not in a bad way, it’s just obviously fluff for the sake of writing review on Air Bnb.   Please read on for what The Spot is actually like…   The inside of the apartment is beautiful. You stay above others who dwell below you. There are air conditioners in every room. One of the rooms mattresses is drastically inferior to the other two. And the master bedroom has it’s own bathroom. The master bedrooms mattress is insanely comfortable. The pillows are way too firm, I ironically felt more comfortable sleeping on the mattress without them.   The water pressure is amazing and the temperature of said hot water is phenomenal. The dish washer wasn’t working when we arrived which Is funny because we were raised without a dishwasher anyway. The one time we thought we were going to have one… we didn’t.   Dwain stocked the refrigerator with half a case of bottled water but we decided to buy our own case lest we drink all of his. Dwain left one bath towel and one face towel for each of us who were staying. I may be considred boujee for saying this, but you gotta leave your guests a face towel, AND a body towel, AND a dry-off towel. Just saying. You expect me to wash my face with the same towel I wash my ass with?   In the master bedrooms bathroom there’s this bathtub shelf contraption that kept falling over. I get it’s purpose but as soon as the condensation from the shower got too ubiquitous this contraption decided to descend and  narrowly hit me on the head.  As an artist I like to think I stretch my dollar well, and there’s nothing more than I appreciate than a good value. On top of that there’s nothing more than I appreciate than good service. For the price I paid? Which was over a thousand dollars for a week… this was not a good value.   I could have stayed at 3 star motel 8 or druy inn and had a better time than this. And I would have gotten a pool and free continental breakfast. This BnB as it stands is quite honestly a scam.   I never got a ‘welcome to my home’ or something. And Dwain if you’re gonna pull up on someone after YOU said lights out was at 10 perhaps let us know you’re coming by? Perhaps ask “how are you enjoying your stay?”  I’ve been nothing but kind, cordial, forthcoming, and gracious to Dwain. I can prove it with screenshots of our correspondences. And Dwain (for the most part) reciprocated that. He’s done what’s required of a host so far. He’s responsive. Available. And sounds like a nice person over the phone. He even “complained to the cable company for us” Yea?   On Air Bnb Dwain says that we would ‘love having him as a host’. What kind of host pulls up on you IN PERSON at 11:30 pm reminding you to take out the trash? Then says ‘sorry about it being late. I only contacted you because i saw the lights were on’ WHO WANTS TO KNOW THE OWNER of their BnB is surveilling  them??! I reminded Dwain  again that I’m literally working. I’m creating something from nothing. I’m resting at 11:30 pm. Maybe its a symptom of New York ‘hospitality’ where people just expect you to move when they say move, but in the midwest we like to ask people if they have the emotional capacity before we ask something of them.   “Hey Khameron good evening. I’m in the area, just wondering if you’ve taken out the trash. If not no worries just please be sure the trash

Ayana was a wonderful host and went out of her way to see that our needs were met. The location allowed us to get to JFK in 15 minutes the morning or our flight. It took so much stress out of our travel experience. Overall one of our best airbnb stays.
Don't be afraid of the location. We were perfectly safe.

It is called a hotel but inside looks like a motel. Very old/mediocre motel. Inside the rooms are relatively clean- no refrigerators or space to put luggage down. I had to jump across my luggage to get to the bathroom. The wallpapers were ripped and falling apart. The bathroom was clean but sink is cracked which looks messy and there was leftover cement/glue from removing the shampoo/conditioner dispenser on the wall which looked unpleasant. Location is not too far from penn station.. A man came into my room and asked if anything needed to be ‘fixed’ noted down and left saying they still need to finish renovating. They should not let people use these rooms if they are not done renovating. This place is cheap considering other places in the city but I do not recommend. I also asked for a different room, front desk asked me ‘how many nights are you staying? one?’ and basically hinted me to stop complaining its only one night. I told him I am staying three nights and he told me theres no rooms available and come back next morning. One good thing i will say is Gabriel is very responsive which was nice. Overall would not recommend.

Place was great. Mary even met us to make sure we got in safely. She provided plenty of things in the apartment like coffee and water and there were plenty of towels and linens. Amazing location. Lots of space for a Brooklyn rental with plenty of closet space.  If you’re scared of dogs, you should know they bark loudly as you pass the first and second floor to get to the apartment. But once we were inside we no longer heard them and we never actually saw them.  Fantastic stay.

Mary’s place has everything you need for a few days’ stay. You will find plenty of dishware, food basics such as salt, pepper, tea, coffee, sweetener, etc. and a choice of bodywash, shampoo, etc. Mary also provided toothbrushes and paste, extra face masks and sanitizer, in case we needed them. The location is perfect, being in one of Brooklyn’s best neighborhoods and a few blocks from the subway. The building is charming but the structure is a bit old. However, the apartment has modern and practical furniture. If you are scared of dogs, bear in mind that as you climb the stairs there will be two dogs barking on the first and second floor. We had no problem with it since we have two dogs back home :) We had an issue with the cleaning but Mary promptly and effectively sorted it out and we really appreciated it. Overall, we had a pleasant experience.

I wouldn't recommend staying here because of Ernesto, the host. The place is sub-standard at most. Nothing spectacular. But dealing with Ernesto was a headache. He was unresponsive, he did not answer all our questions, did not try to resolve our issue with the stove - he told us to cook our eggs and waffles in the microwave. Ernesto is also an unpleasant liar who will say anything to try to get more money out of you. The white bed sheets also had stains on them and we found a centipede in the bathroom. You're better off elsewhere.

At first glance of the place it’s pretty good, I’m not going to say the stay is worth 2100 a month. Let me start by saying it was a nice stay the first month. The host regret to mention his son lived on the third floor. So whenever I got a call from Ernesto it seems that the “third floor” always had a problem. There was countless times where I felt unsafe staying here alone. I would turn my shoulder as I’d leave and would see his son watching me leave the apartment on multiple accounts. I also got calls from Ernesto threatening to kick me out if I had classmates over and said I would have to give him names and phone numbers. AFTER STAYING THAT Ernesto had workers in and out the house the following week. After getting threatened to be kicked out I quickly shortened my stay and got out as soon as I could with losing as little money as possible.

He lied on my boyfriend & also TRIED to lie too AirBNB. He said "I was never there". When I first arrived, I introduced myself & also I had on my HEALTH AND HOSPITALS ID & even told him how cute his dog was (My daughter was with me that night along with my bf & his brother, yet my daughter did not stay). This man gave us a big white comforter that was left on the bed with a huge peach color stain on it. We received Blue bed spreads that I offered too spread on the bed being that it was already late & he was just finishing up cleaning. This bed spread was supposedly "out the dryer" but still fairly damped & I didn't complain I hung it out among the chairs to dry. He tried to charge me   for the big peach stain AND HE KNOWS IT WAS NOT US... UNBELIEVABLE. The rules said the apt was suitable for kids but it's obvious he doesn't like kids because it was such an issue for them to play outside. He lied and said my kids spilled juice on the couch. My kids did not even spend the night there, they came the following day, but it is so ironic how in less than 12 hours so much things were damaged in this apartment.
