Reviews on NYC places are bit more difficult becauze I would have to have totally different set of standard in these places, than when im staying somewhere else. Autumn had someone else manage and take care the place, i never had to look for help but she offered some tourism informations and checked on us while we stay via messages. So it was very kind of her!  Its definitely 6th floor, and what i didnt consider is that i would have 30kg worth of luggage and .. two of them. So it was bit more difficult to come and go. Cleaniness of the place is rather less than average, that might have to do with the fact that the building is probably 100yrs old. But what was hard for me was also how it was located near areas that had unpleasant odors. But safety was fine and also subway line was near by. We were able to walk to china town amd brooklyn bridge, which might be a bit far for a walking distance for some. Oh i forgot to mention, there was no shampoo or toothpaste, but only towels, so people shoupd get them prepared ahead of checking in. But there were lots of utensils, wine glasses, and pots and pans for simple cooking. Which was good!. I loved having AC since we stayed in hot summer, and there were ample amount of sunligjt coming into the building. It was bright and welcoming every morning.  So to sum, it was great for the price!

Autumn was an attentive, responsive host. She was quick to answer any questions or concerns and supplemented various brochures offering information on sites and offering of the city. The apartment was just as it appeared on Airbnb. It was a small area, but that is expected for any NYC apartment. The outside of the apartment and the hallways leading to the apartment were by no means clean. Kind of off putting initially. The hike to the 6th floor is definitely not recommended for elderly or even children. The apartment was clean for the most part, however we did clean the shower prior to use just for safe measures. As far as the area of the apartment, we had mixed feelings. We never felt unsafe but we also didn't venture out/stay out late. It was a blend of Chinese stores and unique restaurants. There was a rite-aid and CVS within walking distance for anything you may forget. She provides dishes to cook and eat with. We used them to make breakfast each morning to save a little bit of money on eating out. She also has a hair dryer available.. We were close enough to the subway to get wherever we needed to go, but it was a must as it is fairly far from many of NYC main attractions (Times Square/Midtown). Overall, we certainly satisfied with our stay.

Very well located accommodation, close to the subway and many Manhattan sites within walking distance. It's small but 3 of us survived for a weekend. Erik is very available to help you if necessary. Studio to recommend if you are not afraid to take your luggage up to the 6th floor. Good value for money.

Staying at Danielle's Airbnb was a lovely experience.  She provided us with a fruit bowl and cold spring water for when we got there.  We were 2 couples who met for the first time for our sons' wedding in Brooklyn.  Having a welcoming place to stay helped to minimize any stress that we might have had from the weekend.  We loved the antiques, parquet floors, international artwork, Victorian woodwork and lots of space.  Danielle was even gracious enough to take our photo in the bnb before we left.  Highly recommend.

Autumns apartment was awesome- clean, comfortable, stocked with basic amenities and in a great location. There’s plenty do within walking distance and subway stations nearby to get uptown or to Brooklyn easily. Checking in and out was easy and Autumn was very communicative. Her guide for around the neighborhood was helpful too! I would recommend a stay here, don’t let the flights of stairs scare you away ;)

Be careful, landlords are unpredictable. We had booked and paid for 6 days. After the second day he denied us access to the apartment in the middle of the night and canceled the rental.  We had to call NYPD police. Thanks to their help, we at least managed to get our luggage and then had to go to a hotel. According to the police, the neighborhood is dangerous, especially at night you shouldn't walk through the streets with luggage. There was no reason, we weren't loud and we didn't damage anything. We are still waiting for compensation today. Afterwards he demanded $700 for a door lock that was stuck from the start because we allegedly damaged it. Incredibly bold. We have never experienced anything like this (we are both 60 years old). Never again.

This was a mixed experience. The place itself was clean, comfortable, and well set up. The location isn't great, but it's a close walk to good restaurants and bars and the train. Checking in was good, but the check-out experience was chaotic and stressful and not worth the savings.

Andrew welcomed us very kindly, the apartment totally matched the description, warm, very clean, everything we needed was available (bath towels, coffee, tea, water, orange juice, etc.). We really appreciated Andrew's little touches, a bottle of Côtes-du-Rhône was waiting for us and when we returned to the apartment the first evening, oranges and rolls for breakfast had been left outside our door. The apartment is very well located in Brooklyn Heights (subway, shopping street and Brooklyn Bridge within walking distance) and the icing on the cake is the terrace with a view of lower Manhattan, ideal for breakfast or a small drink in the evening when the weather permits. Andrew is very accommodating, our return flight was late, we were able to leave our luggage there and enjoy this last day hands-free. We really enjoyed our stay, thank you Andrew.
Hosts very nice and helpful, great location in a nice neighborhood 5 minutes from the nearest subway/bus. I was alone and never felt unsafe in the area. Apartment is small but very clean and quiet.
Good location. Close to everywhere. The atmosphere around is a bit stressful. Especially in the evening, but get use to it. The host was attentive

The building itself is a bit older but it does have an elevator. But Teddy’s place was modern, nicely decorated and felt clean. Two subway stations close by depending what line you want to take (7 or 15 minute walk) Takes about 40 minute by subway to get to Lower Manhattan which is not bad. And having the in room half bath is super convenient. It’s a little small but it certainly does the job. Didn’t feel unsafe in the area. Teddy is happy to give suggestions if you need any recommendations from him. I would highly recommend his place.

It was our first B&B experience. And it was a real luck to start it with Jason!  The house: situated in very clean and quite historic area of Brooklyn, very attractive, built 189..., nice area, quite close to underground subway station but far enough to hear no noice. The appartment: not too big, with a real touch of charm and what was really important for me very very clean! For our couple looked very romantic! I think a best value for its money! Strongly advise to everyone. The owner: And of course the great impression of appartment double stronger makes its owner Jason.... Jason and his mother Mrs Doreen not only great hosts, but also very good people!  They took a great care of us! Jason always was on touch and ready to help. But his attention was so poulite and delicate that our privacy never was disturbed. We felt really nice at his place. When my girlfriend got ill Jason's mother Mrs Doreen came to the place and drove us to the hospital.... What a nice woman she is! Was a real pleasure to meet her! Unfourtunatelly under unpleasant circumstances... Humanity, hospitality and respect! In this words I would describe

Dan's place in Washington Heights is certainly a steal for the price point. Accessible to the A, C, and 1 lines, you will have all the access you need to travel to downtown Manhattan or Queens (which were my frequents during my stay).  The apartment itself is quite lovely, very updated, has plenty of basics such as towels and extra pillows, and the AC unit in the room was such a nice touch for someone who likes to freeze when they sleep like I do (no sarcasm whatsoever).  While the neighborhood wasn't necessarily my cup of tea to go explore in, I never felt unsafe during my 10 minute walks from the 168th street station late at night. Dan seems to be a very caring host, and although I never got to meet him personally, he did message me halfway through my stay asking if my stay was going well, which I wholly appreciated. Terrific experience overall.

After using another website to book, what we thought was Prospect Heights, ending up being in Brownsville. Nothing that we were shown or told was even close to being the truth. That first and only night in that scary place, I stayed up to 130am looking for something last min in Brooklyn. After what seemed like forever I found this lovely place. JASON saved our family vacation!!! With his opening and accepting our booking so late in advance (less than 24 hours) we were able to spend the rest of our trip feeling safe. The place was wonderful, open and clean. We appreciated the full kitchen and was able to cook dinner for our family each night. Jason is a great host and I would recommend him to family and friends if they are ever in the area.

Jason's home was very good in terms of our expectations. Very close to A and C line metro station. It takes about 30 minutes to go to a metro station near Times Square. Location is very secure,we didn't observe any crime related activity. The only problem we had was the insulation of some of the windows. Jason attached airconditioning mashines' pipes through the windows and that leaves some holes which disturbs the insulation of the house. Although it is not a big factor for people staying in summer or warmer months,it could be a problem during winter. I can say that the heaters are working quite good,but the windows may be checked for better insulation.  Jason is a great host. He is a very welcoming man. We didn't have a major problem,but if we did,he would have paid attention to it. Overall,we recommend his house to everybody who are visiting New York and like to stay out all the chaos of Manhattan.
The place is super cute and so close to the metro! Jason was a great host and went out of his way to make sure our stay was as stress-free as possible.

Everything was perfect, we couldn't have asked for anything more  Dan is super friendly. Even though you live with him, you have your own room and he is very respectful of your privacy. He never broke into our room when we were there. He makes you feel at home, you can use the bathroom as you wish and he allowed us to use glasses and his fridge.  Super safe neighborhood, but be careful at night, we saw a lot of drugs but it's New York so it's kind of normal  It's hard to find a parking place but there is a company that offers parking for 40 US per day  The apartment is about a 30 minute subway ride from downtown, so if you are on a budget and don't mind the commute time, I suggest you go to Dan's

Dan is a wonderful host. He was communicative and made my trip stress free. His home is very relaxing and gets a lot of good sunlight. The park and bike paths nearby fit my workout needs and I was able to find food for take out and to make. I’m not a city person so I wasn’t used to busy sidewalks all the time but I was easily able to navigate the area and the walk to the subway wasn’t too bad.

We really enjoyed our stay at Jason’s apartment first, because it was place one could enjoy and second, because Jason is an awesome host. The apartment was sparkling clean, including bathroom and kitchen. No smell or anything that may give one unpleasant feeling. Shampoo, conditioner, body lotion, iron, etc. were all provided. I especially enjoyed the bedroom and the bed itself cause both were big and comfy. Free parking space on premises is available. Jason was very helpful and quick to respond any question I had during the stay. I definitely recommend his apartment for couple who wish to stay in Brooklyn.

Yves' Charming Cottage is everything advertised and more! The neighborhood is easy to get to, beautiful, quiet, and full of flavor. The Cottage itself is spotless and spacious, nestled inside a beautiful Victorian. You can park on site and are walking distance to excellent local restaurants, the bus line, and the subway.   Yves was a fantastic host! Very friendly and happy to answer our many questions about how to get to our destinations and provided recommendations to local eateries. If you're looking for a true Brooklyn experience, stay with Yves and don't be afraid to go on an adventure.

HOST: Jason is a very gracious host. He was full of helpful tips and info. He was happy to chat when we bumped into him. **Ask about the history of the house. HOUSE: The house is in the middle of a quiet shady street in the historic part of Stuyvesant Heights. Neighbors are friendly and it's located very convenient to the Utica subway.  TIPS:  a) There are yoga mats in the bedroom closet.  b) Ask to use the foldable wagon when shopping for groceries or going to the beach.  c) There is a tiny play park around the corner with a mist sprayer for kiddos to splash in. d) Instacart delivers groceries easy and conveniently from places like Aldis and more. e) The bathtub is a jacuzzi tub (can you say bubbles!) f) Playbill.com is where you get tickets to Broadway shows.   You won't go wrong picking this lovely little airbnb as your home away from home.

For my first BnB experience is was fantastic. I will stay here every time I come visit! Apartment was clean, spacious, private, and very safe. First time traveling alone and never felt unsafe once! I recommend staying here 100%!!

You'd be hard pressed to find a more gracious and welcoming host than Mehmet.  He is super helpful and does everything in his ability to make sure you enjoy your trip.  He's just a very friendly person.    The apartment is great!  It's a fantastic place to unwind and relax after a day on the go.  The room is spacious, more than enough room for two people, especially because you'll be out most of the day.  Mehmet has plenty of guides for tourists looking for something to do and will happily offer up suggestions of interesting places to visit.  He also has wifi for catching up on email and whatnot.    The building is quiet; not a lot of ambient noise or loud neighbors.  It's also a secure building.  And more than that it's in a safe neighborhood.  Plus the #1 train is right around the corner, which is super convenient for getting around.    Honestly, staying with Mehmet is an amazing deal.  It's practically a steal for the price you're paying.  I whole-heartedly recommend Mehmet to anyone who needs a place to stay while visiting NYC.

Danielle's place was very convenient. I had plenty of options for public transportation and I could always get where I was going efficiently. I never felt uncomfortable or unsafe even if I walked back alone from the subway at night. We didn't spend much time in Harlem itself but I'm glad we picked this place anyway.

We really enjoyed our stay here.  The apt was clean and comfy.  Walking distance to bus stop, great restaurant around the corner, we also felt very safe in this beautiful neighborhood. What you see is what you get:) this was our first time using Airbnb so I was a little scared booking.   But will be booking here again

Lesson learned.. The place looks nice from the inside, however the neighborhood is horrible. Some of the windows didn't have locks so my family felt unsafe to sleep.     I was also scared by the neighbor from upstairs late night smoking weed on the side patio. Seriously??? (Description is wrong by saying we had the place to ourselves.) Do research on your surrounding areas before booking anything. We ended up paying less money for a nice Hotel in Times Square. Save money and time, without having to drive in a disgusting city, and Do not bring anyone you care about here.   Yves seems like a nice fellow but unfortunately this place wasn't for us.

Hello, To be completely honest, this accommodation is perfect! We were not disappointed. It is located in a popular and lively area of ​​New York, far from the tourists and the overrated. As French people, probably with our stereotypes, we were not reassured the first days... especially coming back from the metro after 11 p.m. (there are two stations 10-15 min away). Indeed, groups of young people in isolated alleys with bottles, joints... But we quickly realized that this is how they live, they come together! No security problems in New York, it's incomparable compared to Paris or elsewhere. The accommodation is functional, we sleep very well (after 20km of walking obviously...).   Thanks to the hosts and their responsiveness and their instructions, it’s perfect. Nothing better when you also have the stress of traveling!

This little place was so quiant and comfortable. The planes were a little annoying but they quieted down at night. The canal was so pretty to enjoy on the deck, and the tea, coffee, and snacks were a lovely touch. I would only caution that the stairway to the attick bedroom is a little scary and for those who have at least average balance and ability. Otherwise this place was awesome.

In general, this basement apartment is a good value for dollars we paid and location is great. Communication with hosts is excellent and Blink camera at the entrance adds additional security. Although, I have to share some things that might help families with kids in their selection. 1) large sofa is broken and can’t be converted to bed. It was not mentioned in description and we won’t put kids on inflatable mattress on the basement floor. We’ve seen one centipede there. 2) tenants at the top DO NOT CARE about your sleep. They are very loud till midnight and start literally jumping on the floor at 5AM 3) some odd smell in the kitchen and living room, flavoured with aroma warmers in receptacles is unpleasant.  Overall, if we were without kids, for the price paid, I would be happy. But with kids (we have 2), we had some challenges.

The description and photos in the listing were accurate.  A hidden gem. When you pull into the shared parking lot, you wouldn't suspect that it would lead to such a peaceful, Place.  Clean, comfortable, full of character, a back porch that sits on the canal.  The sound of planes from nearby Kennedy airport didn't bother us, but something to be aware of.  A 15-minute drive to Jacob Riis beach.  We enjoyed fantastic beach days and cozy evenings, feasting on yummy food delivery from a great nearby diner (Crossbay Diner).  Wing was an exceptionally hospitable host and her communication and response time were excellent!

We had a wonderful time in this space. It was even more beautiful than the photos! And the deck/patio was a great large size that had a lot of sunlight, catching the sunrise was also a dream. There were an ample amount of supplies/ snacks that were given. The fridge was a great size and the kitchen had beautiful dishware. And the host was incredibly friendly and thoughtful! Now, the shower temperature fluctuated no matter what you did, the stove was a bit scary to cook on, and netting on the patio would have made a huge difference where it couldve been enjoyed even more. And I would absolutely come back a second time, however, a major issue was also the front door not having enough covering on the window.

This was fantastic!! The apartment was exactly as described and Rebekah was amazing! As soon as we got to the apartment Rebekah met us and gave us all the info we needed! The apartment is truly beautiful.  Great location and great neighborhood.  We came in really late one night and never once were we scared or concerned about where we were.  She had so many great recommendations of things to do and see in Brooklyn as well as in Manhattan!  Cannot praise Rebekah enough! She even messaged me throughout our stay to make sure we didn't need anything.  If you are thinking of using AirBnB...do it and choose this listing! You will not be upset!

This place was wonderful! Me and four other fellow classmates stayed here during our architecture field trip to NY. The apt is very close to the subway station and doesn't take too long to get to Manhattan.  Everyone slept comfortably. Me and another friend stayed in the bedroom on the top floor, while the other 3 got their own bed on the main floor with the pullout couches and other bedroom. Kitchen was well equipped with all the modern appliances, and the bathroom was nice, clean, and roomy.  The neighborhood is, for the most part, quiet. Just the occasional train passing through but it wasn't too loud or unpleasant. If anything, it added to the experience. Felt safe walking around at night.  Rebekah is an absolute gem and she is a wonderful hostess! :) Her lovely welcome guide is very detailed and helpful. Cannot praise her enough!  Unfortunately, our schedule was packed otherwise we'd have LOVED to explore Brooklyn a little more than we were able to so make sure to take advantage of that because from what we did get to see, it was great! :)

We had such a great time while staying at Rebekah's place! Our family of 6 visited New York for an entire week, and Rebekah's brownstone townhome was the perfect location for us to unwind after a busy day in the city. The subway into the city is very convenient and the subway station is very close to the townhome. I've always heard that the subway system in New York is confusing, but we found it to be just the opposite! It was extremely easy to use and get around everywhere. Not only did we take it to almost every tourist stop in manhattan, we also ventured out to a fun kids science museum in queens, and we went to Coney Island one night for a little beach and carnival action. We never felt unsafe, and with the 7-day passes for unlimited rides we really got our money's worth!  As for the townhome itself, it is absolutely adorable. It was extremely clean, there were plenty of towels for everyone to use for the entire week, and the air-conditioner works great in every room. The beds are extremely comfortable and we felt like we had plenty of space even with 6 of us in the apartment. You can tell that Rebekah has put a lot of hard work and care into her place to make it so inviting.   Rebekah had great suggestions too of great eats and shops in the neighborhood. I'm telling you, after just one week, we all felt like we were locals. It was so much better staying at Rebekah's rather than staying at a hotel where we wouldn't have had the space to spread out and we wouldn't have had the chance to really get a feel for living in the city. Thanks again to Rebekah! She is a wonderful hostess and just as sweet as she can be.

Rebekah was a wonderful, kind host who communicated frequently and made our stay very comfortable. Great coffee and tea in the kitchen, amazing appliances and well-stocked bedding and towels. The loft apartment is beautiful and big-- lots of space for our family of four. Our stay here made us nostalgic for NYC living again! The Bed-Stuy neighborhood is super cool, but can be a little sketchy after dark or early morning; take a cab back home if you're planning on being out late. We never felt unsafe in the apartment, however, and our car was totally fine parked on the street. Altogether, a great stay in a historic neighborhood in Brooklyn and we had the best brunch at Peaches nearby!

My stay at Rebekah’s place was amazing. From quick communication responses to the amazing place. It is very close to catch the subway. Plenty of nearby bodegas and delis. The neighborhood is also very safe. I walked alone two blocks to the subway at night time and am a young female and I never ever felt unsafe. I definitely loved the place it is very spacious and it is very nicely decorated. I would definitely stay here again.
We enjoyed our stay at Lenny's place. Great location, lovely neighbourhood close to Central park, never felt unsafe...

We spent 4 nights in the apartment. It is very well located, 10 minutes walk from metro station 1. There are shops nearby. Lenny was very accommodating for our departure, we were able to leave our suitcases all day until our flight. Exchanges with him are very quick and easy. On the other hand, the neighborhood is very noisy and the apartment is poorly insulated, it is not easy to sleep...
As I was turning on the shower the bathroom ceiling fell through and I had to go to the hospital. Very unsafe place and smells like mold throughout the apartment.

Great, affordable place for our family of 5.  Super close to Central Park and subway stations.  Had everything we needed.  We did loose heat and hot water for a day (building issue), but there were plenty of extra blankets. Never felt unsafe to n the neighborhood or building. We didn’t come and go a lot, so hiking up the stairs was never a big issue.  The floors in the apartment are sloped, which was a little dizzying at first, but wasn’t a huge deal.

We stayed in Dolphy's apartment End Sep for app 12 nights.The apartment was awesome .Specially the way we were welcomed with snacks,Cold Drinks,Wine.We loved and we forget all the stress we had from the long journey from India.Apartment was very clean.Nice beds and wonderful Sofa.Kitchen was full with utencils and gadgets .We got every we wanted for our stay. Dolphy was always available on the phone and she made us to get every thing we required. Great lady.... No words...only appreciations about her nature and her service.  Location was perfect.Calm place to live. Thanks Dolphy.Next time when we visit again to US, we shall definately  ask you to be our Host again.

I think I am the first guest since Beverly reopened (post-pandemic), and I can attest that it is still a great place to stay, and Beverly is still a fantastic host, per the earlier reviews! She is responsive, helpful, and gracious. The apartment worked very well for my month-long visit – clean and sunny with a well-equipped kitchen, comfortable furnishings and good wi-fi for Zoom and Teams meetings (for remote work). Loved the neighborhood with its beautiful brownstones and tree-lined streets, friendly neighbors, and amenities including many restaurants, grocery and drug stores, laundry, and an excellent wine shop. It’s a pleasant 10-minute walk to an express train to Manhattan with stops near the Brooklyn Bridge, World Trade Center, the Village, Times Square and Central Park (among others) so getting to Manhattan activities is easy. (There are also two bus lines nearby and plenty of Lyfts/Ubers around.) I highly recommend Beverly’s place and hope to stay there again soon!

The home is exactly as described. Omar was very accommodating and left special touches for our family. This was our first time to Brooklyn although we spent 90% of our time in Manhattan. We rode the subway everywhere with no issues (get the 7 day unlimited pass for $32 - totally worth it). We never felt unsafe and we visited the local grocery stores on our way home from the City every night. We were very disappointed in the cleanliness of the area (Brooklyn). We are from the City Beautiful (Orlando) and do not see trash on sidewalks, streets, and literally everywhere like we saw in Brooklyn. This may be normal for this area but it was foul to us. You could fill 10 large trash bags on your way from the house to the subway. If you are used to this, then this is a perfect house for traveling from Brooklyn to the City. This is no reflection on Omar's house, the city officials of Brooklyn should be ashamed of themselves for treating this area like a public trash can.

We had a fantastic stay at Omar and Kareema’s place in Brooklyn. There was plenty of space for our family of six, with a well stocked kitchen, really comfortable living and bedroom spaces - and three bathrooms! The apartment was spotlessly clean, and close to local amenities - five mins walk to subway, local supermarket called Key Food, and lots of takeaways. The neighbourhood is lively but the street is quiet and friendly, and we never felt unsafe walking around with our four kids. We had a great stay and would definitely stay again.

Angela's place is amazing! You will need to walk a few blocks for the subway, red and green lines, but the amenities and hospitality was top notch! As Angela recommends use the red line, trains 1, 2, and 3. The green line, 4 and 5, was in a bit sketchy part of town at night. During the day we felt safe at either station. If you ever need anything Angela's there for you!

I would highly recommend this place if you’re staying with a group visiting NYC. First off, I’d like to say that these hosts made our airbnb one of the best. Their communication and hospitality surpassed my expectations. We had the pleasure to meet the host one morning as she was so sweet to politely introduce herself and did not intrude what so ever. Traveling with a large group in an even larger city could be quite stressful,  but coming back to a warm and cozy home is more than we could have asked for.   We were a party of 6 and there was more than enough room in this property that we could have fit more to be honest. The rooms and bathrooms were spacious, and that is rare in NYC. The subway is about a 5 minute walk and will take you to all the main attractions. There were people hanging around the neighborhood at night which did not bother us at all.   We loved our stay in New York and part of the reason why is because of this airbnb. Believe all the amazing reviews! You won’t regret it )

Very good experience at Anita's.  The beds are very comfortable and everything was clean when we arrived.   Allow 35-45 minutes to get to Manhattan by subway. The apartment is located 15 minutes from Kingston Avenue station on line 3. We had no problem with insecurity in the neighborhood.   I recommend!

Great value. Quite easy to get into Manhattan from the subway which is just a few yards away. Place has real character and accommodates family of six well. Fun exploring the hidden goodies in the neighborhood. Host is fantastic and she, with professional ease and experience, rescued a homeless kitten stranded on a cold rainy night at the garden entrance to our building. Remarkably comfortable and homey. A fine, comfortable and safe refuge for my first visit back to NYC after a year of multiple massive surgical challenges.

I rarely write reviews on air bnbs, however there’s no way I couldn’t write one for Omar & Kareema. They were extremely accommodating before, during, and after our stay. The house is super spacious and fit our party very comfortably. It was a steal for the price we paid. We are very grateful and definitely recommend their home!
Overall a nice stay. Plenty of room. Neighborhood was decent for a group but would have felt unsafe being alone. Omar was a good host.
Accurate, parking was sketchy

Rolands place is the place to be if your ever in Queens, whether for a short stay or long term. His place is very cozy, quiet and sophisticated. The check in process was stress free and I admired the usage of the keypads on the doors to ensure privacy and security.

This room was just a place to sleep for the last couple days I was in New York. The room size and amenities were fine. Big comfy bed, smart TV with Netflix, YouTube, etc. Drawer, closet, towels. Checking in was easy. All the instructions were very clear and just involves putting in key codes. It seems like it could be safe except there was a common area with a mini fridge right outside my window, so really anyone that was staying there could have gone in; not to mention the area was sketchy, especially if you’re a girl walking in the area. I didn’t go into the kitchen, but the restroom was pretty dirty. Very grimy and there was a bug in the shower that looked like a bedbug. There were also ants in the room- probably because there were still crumbs in the drawers from previous guests. Under the bed was extremely dusty and the rug had stains all over it. Overall my biggest issue was the cleanliness, but you’re also getting what you pay for. About $20 lyft to/from airport.

Not recommended  We stayed in this apt for Christmas and New Years in 2021/2022 for 10 days. The location is excellent, but there are several things we complained about and you should know before booking this apt.  The apt wasn't cleaned when we arrived. The owner, who was on vacation herself, blamed the (cleaning) girl that was there when we arrived, she should have cleaned it better. Dirty dishes, dirty floor. We had to clean this ourselves. The owner later stated that the cleaning girl lost her job because she had to wait longer in the apt because we were delayed. She could have done some more cleaning in the meantime... The rest of the apt is old, rusty, dusty and greasy.  After a few days, we found cockroaches in the bathroom. After complaining, the owner claimed that NY is famous for them and then stated she had never seen one in her bathroom before. But, we found several, so that seems hard to believe. We bought bug spray ourselves and fumed the place and after that we didn't see them again. But still, the idea was just disgusting. The owner advised us to take out the garbage every day, which we already did.  There are people in the building heavily smoking pot. The smell lingers in the hallway and sometimes even penetrates into the apt. Not exactly the smell we like. The owner claimed that it's legal in NY now and it is normal to smell it everywhere. Maybe normal to her, not to us.  When we arrived, there were signs of drugs substance production or use in the stair case; pills, chalk powder, razor blades, a broken phone, just weird stuff. Maybe this was caused by the fact that the front door of the building is just always open and everyone can walk in and out. Not really a safe feeling. After complaining, the owner contacted the building cleaning lady and everything was cleaned up. We did not see any of this again.   Also, there was (and is currently and probably will be for a while) a construction site right across the street from the apt. This means every day at 7 am you will be awake from the drilling, hammering, metal grinding, and all the other building noises. Not really something the owner can do anything about, but she had to have known about this (she mentioned this could have caused the dust in the apt) and didn't give us a heads up; we probably would have stayed somewhere else if we had known this in advance.  All together, we did complain and asked for a partly refund for this apt, for which we paid a lot of money, but the owner denied this and said it was a fair price and claimed she did everything to impove our stay.   We did have a great vacation in NY, and again, the location is great, but had we known these issues beforehand, we would have picked a different apt.  Your choice.

The location is good but if you have trouble with steps, you need to stay away.  Each room is at a slightly different level and getting up in the middle of the night can be dangerous.  There are no outlets to recharge a cell phone next to the bed.

We were very warmly welcomed by Jennifer's friend Claire who resides on the top floor. The dogs are super friendly and we were met by them and Claire's beautiful little boy! Immediately felt at home.  Our room downstairs was spacious and very clean. We had our own private bathroom. There is a place to sit and relax and if you love to read like I do, plenty of novels to choose from to relax.  The beds were very comfortable and there is a portable air conditioner we used one night and cooled the room perfectly.  It's a downstairs room but the windows are gated and I never once felt unsafe.  The neighborhood has everything you could possibly need, all in walking distance and we weren't far from the metro! We met Jennifer as we were leaving. Such friendly, down to earth people, are Claire and Jennifer. We will definitely come back again. Thank you for such a lovely experience! Maureen Rose

he called me by “accident” a few times I don’t like being bombarded with issues while I’m at work.  It says self check In but it isn’t really I was bombarded at the door very unpleasant check in. Beautiful place enjoyed my stay just some weird things that bothered me

Loved the stay. It's easy to get to. The host offers codes for all entries so I didn't have any trouble entering late at night. The kitchen had open access good enough to cook your own stuff. The toilet has hot water for shower. Room was clean and comfy. There are stores right across street and a big marketplace some min walk away. The neighborhood has some population outside even late at night and the bus service stop is very close to the place, so I didn't feel unsafe coming back past midnight.

Amy was super kind even though she has trouble speaking english she showed me around the place and where everything was. Her son helps communicates, but once you're there everything is pretty basic and wasn't hard to get into the building. She was waiting outside for me once I arrived and there was even a place I could park so I didn't have to stress about looking for a place in the street. The room I stayed in was a decent size, but there is a bigger living room area that was open for us to occupy and a kitchen we could use. The bathroom was a bit small, but if you're looking for a place to stay a night like I did, it's really not a big deal at all. Shower water pressure was good and it was overall a good experience.

We stayed here for one month in August during the pandemic. I am not sure if this host has ever had a long term stay because the reviews are all very positive, but we did not have a good experience. I always give hosts and places the benefit of the doubt, but this stay was uncomfortable, disruptive and disappointing.   Please continue to read if you are interested in understanding the specifics behind our poor experience, otherwise in short I would not recommend this place for a long term stay. Perhaps a short stay would be ok.  Pros: - Location of this place is great, close to the park, grocery stores and restaurants, on a very quiet street, parking was easy and quick access to the highway. - Plenty of toilet paper, paper towels, cleaning products, soap, dishwasher and laundry supplies for our entire stay. That was really convenient.   - The other tenants living in the building were really nice and helpful when we had questions or needed to coordinate.  Cons: Issues with cleanliness and the house:  The house was only surface level clean when we arrived. I would be surprised if this house was ever professionally cleaned. If you are looking for a place that is clean and minimal design, this is not that place. This is someone’s home that you would be stepping into to take care of while they are away.  - The fridge had leftover food scattered about, half empty drinks, takeout condiments in plastic containers, spilled sauces and smeared jam on the shelves. Which we were asked to keep and push to the side, I found this to be pretty disgusting handling someone else’s leftover food and being asked to clean it up. It should have been done prior to our arrival. - The kitchen was fully equipped, but we had to clean anything we wanted to use as everything was visibly dirty. - Drawers had visible crumbs and dirt, pots and pans were sticky, the stove top had leftover grease stains.  - The bathroom had what appeared to be leftover toiletries that were collecting dust and just scattered about. I understand being considerate and providing basic necessities, but I don’t think leaving half used deodorant and mouth wash is considerate and having to organize it on the host’s behalf to make space for your stuff. - There were dog toys just left in the middle of the room and blankets stuffed under the couches.  - The house consistently smelled like dogs and musty. It now makes sense why the host asked to keep the windows open and air things out. - You couldn’t use the garden seating, because no cushions were made available - There was a grill, but it hadn’t been cleaned in a year, the host said we could clean it and go buy propane if we wanted to use it (this wasn't technically in the listing) - There was a half bent baby pool just sitting in the middle of the garden - The bed Is two twin size mattresses put together and they were put in sideways so they hit the middle of your back. It was extremely uncomfortable and we had to rearrange the mattresses so that we could each sleep on one mattress individually.   I am confident we left this place cleaner than when we arrived.  Issues with the host: - The host did not inform us that she would not be available during our month long stay until after we arrived and encountered a problem. She made it clear that she was 2 hours away and could not come to help and couldn’t send a maintenance person during this time. I had to reach out to her multiple times to follow-up on trying to resolve issues and she asked for me to coordinate with the girl upstairs to work through problems. I did not expect to spend that much time resolving issues during my stay. - Airbnb makes it very clear that you are a host and need to be available to resolve issues in a timely manner with guests. That absolutely did not happen here as she had no plan for resolving unexpected issues.  - Issues that occurred during our stay:     - The security alarm malfunctioned after a storm on day 2 of our stay and continuously beeped for 10 days straight. I had to reach out multiple times to get this resolved and push her to schedule a technician to come out. I had to meet with the technician and coordinate him coming again to resolve the issue. I received no follow-up from the host on whether it was fully resolved, no thank you for spending my time being inconvenienced with the technician. This was extremely irritating as we were working from home during this time.     - The outdoor furniture and lights had fallen the 2nd day we arrived, we had to clean up the furniture, broken glass and the lights no longer worked (She did ask the upstairs person to help with the broken glass, but it was not sufficient, dangerous and unusable so we ended up cleaning it up ourselves.)     - The air conditioning unit did not have the proper tube to use it in the window unit. We were asked to check in the basement, but no tube fit and the host suggested we could carry up an air conditioning unit from the basement. There were several old dusty units in the basement that we would have to carry up 2 flights up stairs if we wanted to use it. I don’t know how you can ask a guest to bring up a heavy air conditioning unit from the basement and figure out how to install it yourself. Keep in mind it’s the month of August in NY. The heat was extremely uncomfortable.

Mike's apartment is an Air B&B secret & a steal.  Great location, awesome space, incredible rate, can't say enough about it.  I'd be staying there today except that someone else reserved it  before me.  Thanks Mike & Busser..  Hope to see you soon.

Such an amazing place and awesome hosts! I don’t even want to say how special this gem is because I’m afraid it will be booked when we return to NYC. Mike, Busser, and sweet Major are wonderful hosts…super helpful, friendly, and great with communication. It felt like staying in an art gallery since Busser’s work is everywhere. We loved everything  about it!

The flat was spotless, and looks exactly as it does in the pictures. The bedroom is a good size with lots of storage space and the mini kitchen has all the essentials (fridge, coffee machine, microwave). The bathroom is lovely with a huge bath! Lilian herself was really welcoming, and flexible with check out times. The flat was well connected with subway and bus links, and it generally took about half an hour to travel into the centre of the city. The area itself was fairly lively at night time, so I'd recommend a pair of ear plugs if you are a light sleeper. That said there are some great places to eat - we loved Harlem Shake - and we didn't feel unsafe. I'd really recommend Lilian's flat and would stay here again.

Lilian's directions were precise, and I had no problem to check in even though she was not there when I arrived. The apartment exceeded my expectations: clean, nicely decorated, with pretty much everything I needed. I liked the location: walking distance to Columbia and to a good set of shops/restaurants. I was initially afraid of street noise (people talking aloud), but everything went quiet after 10-11 PM. On my way to NYC I lost my adaptor, but Lilian's husband quickly gave me one the first time I ran into him. On the overall, a very pleasant stay!

My husband and my stay at Lillian's was great! Lillian met with us to give us our keys and do a walk through of the apartment. She was very accommodating and allowed us to drop our bags off early and store them after we checked out as well! The apartment had all the amenities we wanted and was only a couple blocks from the subway line that takes you straight to Time Square (about 1/2 a mile from another station that has different lines).   One thing we found was that the morning city sounds were surprisingly loud. While the street looks fairly "residential", there are a lot of semis that drive down it for some reason (ones that aren't afraid to use their horns too). Additionally, most nights we would get back to the apartment late at night - walking the 2 blocks wasnt bad at all, but if you find yourself on other lines and walking 10-15 minutes, you walk through some streets that dont feel quite as safe. This doesn't change my positive experience at Lillian's, but I think it is something to be aware of!  Overall we had a wonderful time in NYC and being able to make ourselves at home and feel comfortable at Lillian's was a big part of our trip! Thanks!

Nice flat, well decorated, clean, good space. Good mattress and bathroom. Street can be noisy sometimes (both people and vehicles) but it wasn't really a problem. Never felt unsafe in the area and it was easy to access different subway lines to get around New York. Would definitely stay there again.

Staying in Eric's Big Ass Room in Brooklyn was a great contrast to the hustle of Manhattan. On arriving we were able to meet Eric and his friends, they were all so welcoming to us both; interested and polite, even after we'd arrived later than expected.  We had no problems, whatsoever, with the apartment/room or location, everything was incredibly easy to commute back and forth; Metro stop, literally, steps from the front door. The local area is nice and I never felt it to be unsafe, even when I was wondering around after midnight to find food I ended up having a nice chat with people.  Eric was accessible throughout our time in NYC, even making contact to enquire how our days were going & open to any queries/advice, and his flatmate was always polite and cool whenever we saw one another.  Experiences like this are the what AirBnB is about!...I'd recommend this place highly and look forward to staying again in the future!  If there were 6stars then i'd give them.

This was my first time in New York and Yulia was great with messaging me weeks before I even arrived.  The place was perfect with a great location. Close to a local market, bank, drug store, shopping and the subway.  The bathroom was recently renovated and the building has a nice elevator man.  Next time I'm in New York, I'll definitely pick this apartment again.

Amazing stay! Lovely couple. So darn clean in here. I love it. Kika has such a vibrant personality, warmest smile I've  seen. Doesn't stress about check out time. Unue is laid back and smooth. lol Love this couple. Example of what an Airbnb experience should be like. Unfortunately, I come across hosts like them less than 50% of the time. I would definitely stay again.

Chris  was out of town, but he was readily available via phone.  He communicated effectively with us.  Chris had a great place.  I really enjoyed his common/living room.  It was cozy and well decorated.  Overall, his place was small, but very cozy.  He provided great amenities, such as towels, organic soap, clean sheets, etc.  The key on the door locks were difficult to use at first, but after  much practice, we figured out how to use them.  Chris' place is about a mile from the 'L' subway which goes directly to downtown NYC.  It was a cheap way to get to and from Manhattan. Being that we are from Chicago and are very cautious with street crimes and dangers, we were very concerned about walking at night or around an unfamiliar city/neighborhood; however, we can honestly say that we  felt completely safe walking in the neighborhood, at all hours.  It was a huge difference from Chicago neighborhoods.  We'd love to come back!

This place is in a great location. a short walk to 2 subway stations. Air was stale from lack of flow, but the window AC did the trick when sleeping. Whole neighborhood was friendly, no problem with crime that I saw.

Anitha's place is nice and welcoming, and it is also cosy and private. Unlike some of the reviews I read, I had no issues with neighbors or other people living in her apartment. They were very respectful with us. It is a quiet area and Anitha was very kind in giving us extra sheets and blankets. The only thing I would say is that it is rather far from any subway stop (10-15 mins) and walking around that area at night can make you feel somewhat unsafe. Some sidewalks were not very clean and you see trash not very well picked up. We ended up taking cabs from the subway stop to her place, which brought the overal price a bit up. But,  it is definitely a nice residential area to walk during the day, even though there are hardly any shops other than delis and laundromats. I recomend this place if you dont mind the walk. A nice old-school brooklyn experience altogether.

Worse experience I ever had in Airbnb   I had horrible experience with this host. The apartment wasn’t described as the picture,the host wasn’t welcoming she so rude even not courteous with us. She allowed her dog to jump and bark on me inside of the apartment 10 minutes later electricity was off I was so scared. She was spying on me(follow my every move cause she live straight up on me)during my stay in this place my privacy was invaded. I do not recommend this place!

Shivaul was a great host. Very helpful and felt like he enjoys being a host- not just in it for the $$. The place itself is really nice (has character), clean and comfortable. The only caveat I had was the fact that after staying there I couldn’t understand why it got such a high location rating. It’s too far from the city. Parking is also scary hard to find - easier in Manhattan. None of this is Shivaul’s fault- it just should be mentioned. Overall, my stay at Shivaul’s place was very good and I felt like went above and beyond to make me feel welcome.

Had a great time. Red Hook is a cool place. Bed is not very comfortable at all. Location is decent but be prepared to travel for at least 40 mins by public transport to get to the rest of Brooklyn, manhattan, etc. There are fun dive bars around, a couple of restaurants and a good pizza joint.  Don’t be afraid to take the B61 bus, it drops off right next to the place. Marjorie is nice and non invasive, sharing a space with her was very comfortable. Would not recommend staying here for your first trip to NYC, although once you are ready to explore and stay in new places try this little fishing port. The ferry is also very close by and fun to take over to Dumbo, Williamsburg or even Manhattan.

I was looking forward to staying with Elle as it was my first time to New York and I chose her place specifically as she mentioned she will be around for tips and is in a great location close to shops and restaurants as well as having a kitchen inside her place. The location was great indeed, and I did brace myself for New York’s tiny apartments, however there were a few things that were not as mentioned. The bed sheets were not clean upon my arrival, as well as this there was a thick layer of dust in the only air conditioning in the space - she happily assisted in putting a net on the window to work around the heat however not ideal in summer in the concrete jungle. I have stayed in many private rooms on Airbnb, and I’m afraid I wouldn’t be recommending this one due to the state of the messy shared spaces and limited amenities. The listing mentions dogs during the day on weekends only, however unfortunately they kept me up at night during the week as well. Had I stayed for a day or two, it would have been ok however, looking back I would have much rather paid an extra $100 for a hotel with a clean space and guaranteed privacy.

Lovely stay! I was nervous about staying in the city, but Marjorie made me feel right at home. Great communication, beautiful apartment, great location, private room and bathroom. It’s a steal for the price! Definitely recommend!

Had a great stay at this beautifully put together space in Bushwick. Would stay again even if the neighborhood is not top. I didn't feel unsafe or so... good thing is that it's a very diverse and vibrant neighborhood. Subway really close too.

Katie was very easy to communicate with, and the location of this spacious (for New York) studio couldn't have been better. We were able to walk to the train, Guggenheim, Central Park, shopping, bars, etc. The building was very secure and we did not feel unsafe. The apartment was spotless, and we look forward to staying here again in the future. So much better than an expensive hotel!

Katie does not make it easy to get a key to the apartment. We had to try and locate a friend of hers in the very busy Penn station, to get the key because Katie was not available. Then when we arrived we saw that we had to climb 3 flights of very steep stairs. She did not describe this in her listing and it is not easy at all when you have luggage. The apartment was clean and organized and the bed was very comfortable. It is in a good location and "somewhat" close to the subway (about 4 long blocks) but prepare to walk and climb stairs ALOT. If you are from New York this may not be an issue for you. We did have yet another key mishap because I lost my purse and Katie was not prepared. So after losing everything (money, drivers license passport, camera, etc.) out of the gate Katie said it was going to cost us $250 instead of trying to help, which added more stress. Then I think she realized the precarious situation we were in and started to try and remedy the situation. In the end it did end up costing us additional time and money because Katie made us take a taxi to Brooklyn at 11:00 at night to get a spare key from her friend. This after she already told us there was no spare. When we were getting ready to leave, we asked where to leave the key and Katie wanted us to bring the key to her place of employment!! Try locating someones workplace in New York while also trying to be on time for your flight was not an option for us, so ended up making other arrangements without her help. Again, the apartment was nice, but Katie made it very stressful to gain access to it, did not help in an emergency and additionally made it difficult to leave. Unfortunately, I would not stay here again because of the host.
Great location and nice corner shady unit! Mel was very responsive and his unit was very clean. Thanks again!

My mom and I stayed four nights and had a delightful experience. Jovanna and her mother, Hellen, were the most gracious and friendly of hosts, making the entire process and experience so easy and welcoming. They were always available and great with communication. The apartment - in the basement of the building - is very spacious, clean, and homey. It was warm from the summer days, but nothing the ceiling fans couldn't fix! The building is on a quiet residential street right in the center of Crown Heights, less than 10 minutes from the Kingston-Throop station (C) or Kingston station (3). We never felt unsafe, even coming home after midnight one night. The delis and bodegas right around the corner were great for breakfast on-the-go. I'm moving up to Brooklyn myself, but will certainly recommend Jovanna's place to my visitors!

We felt at home.  Lilian was friendly and ready to help.  The apartment is very spacious and comfortable (we were two adults and two kids); it is newly remodeled and has everything one needs.  We enjoyed lounging on the roof-deck.  It is easy to have food delivered.  The subway is just around the corner, next to a CVS drug store and across from a Starbucks (for breakfast, go to Amy Ruth's on 116th, its really good, and comes with fresh biscuits - get the grits).

First off, I am a fellow Airbnb host, so I really pay attention to the small details. Lillian's place is GREAT! The apartment  was spacious, beautifully decorated,  and very clean and modern. The washer/dryer and ironing board were nice additions. The windows let in so much natural light. The location was also great. My mother and I were by ourselves and felt completely safe. Of course it is a big city and crime can happen anywhere so you should always be cautious. We walked late at night by ourselves. The trains were conveniently located and food within walking distance. It was easy to get pretty much anywhere.  I also appreciated the fact that Lillian was easily available but also gave us our privacy. She is a great host and you can tell she has put a lot of time, effort and thought into the apartment. It was a treat to stay in this beautiful Brownstone, and a GREAT Airbnb experience.  Thanks Again Lillian!

It was my first time visiting New York and I always wanted to stay in an New York apartment, and I came upon Herani and Nadir's apartment by a stroke of luck, and what great luck it turned out to be. If you're staying in New York, consider staying at Herani's AirBnb!   Why? Let's begin, their price is considerably WAY cheaper than most hotel in NY. If I'm staying in the "city that never sleeps", why would you pay $XXX amount a night to stay at a place where you're going to be out most of the time and just need a place to keep your luggage? As soon as I arrived, Herani was more than welcoming. Her energy is so warm and the apartment is so comforting. The listing is exactly as described. The apt. is decorated beautifully with artwork (photographs from Nadir) and the place is spacious. When you enter your room, it honestly feels like you're in a hotel. The room is clean, the bed is made with towels and soap for you to use, there are magazines for your viewing pleasure on top of the dresser, access to their wi-fi is listed as well (the internet is fast, like whooosh or zoom zoom mazda commercial fast), there is a personal air conditioner in the room, and the pillows on the bed were just really, really, soft. I've consider stealing the pillows but A. I only brought one suitcase, and B. I had to upload my license to AirBnb, so there's that. BUT I'VE CONSIDERED IT BASED ON HOW SOFT IT IS.   The host made you feel welcomed from the minute you walk in. Herani wanted you to feel as if the apartment was your during your stay and I did. You ever stay at a person's place and you feel like you're in a museum and you can't touch anything? Yeah, not here. I felt truly comfortable in their place. (BUT THAT DOESN'T MEAN YOU DON'T HAVE TO BE COURTEOUS, BE KIND AND CLEAN.)   Herani recommended places to eat and check out and she told me about the neighborhood and Astoria is a safe place. The neighborhood is homely and family oriented. Everything is accessible! The train station is less than a 5 minute walk from their apt as well as everything else. There is a Rite Aid, an amazing burger place, frozen yogurt, banks, neighborhood grocery stores, flower store, ethnic restaurants, all within 5 to 10 mins walking. The area is well lit so you're not going to get stabbed or robbed or anything like that. You might get drunk because there are SO MANY places to eat and drink around their apt! There is even a restaurant under the apt, Ovelia! How convenient!  Overall, my visit was wonderful, and it was because the host were wonderful. Because when you leave your home to come to a new, strange city, and you stay at their place, you're home. Thank you Herani and Nadir!   :-)

Lilian's apartment is without a doubt one of the best we have ever been to. All spacious, bright, beautiful, with great attention to detail. There is nothing missing that you may need on a daily basis during your stay, think of everything.  One block from the metro stop, in a fairly familiar neighborhood, with several delicious restaurants nearby, and one of the things we are going to miss the most: "Whole Foods Market", a supermarket for those of us who like to eat well, quality and very friendly and attentive people, I recommend it 100%. It is right in front of the metro stop.  Also recommend the Harlem Shake restaurant (their special chicken sandwich stole my heart!) and the restaurant that is right next to the "red loobster" (this one famous for its live music, it was full!), not being able to have brunch at the previous one, we went here and the truth is that it was wonderful, the pancakes were simply delicious.  NYC continues to make everyone fall in love with it, and this apartment only makes your stay even more special if possible. Enjoy!  Christina

Pro's- Lilian's place is beautiful. The pictures are exactly what the apartment looks like. It is spacious and has lovely windows for natural sunlight.  Lilian was very efficient with check-in and left the instruction book.  There is a whole food and the subway station a couple of blocks away.  Con's- The condo was not clean which was important to me especially after COVID.  It was picked up however, there was a bloodstain on the sheets. I had to wash all bedding after seeing that stain and the cover inside the duvet had multiple bloodstains. There was a ring around the tub, dirty dishes in the dishwasher, and old food in the fridge. The tub would not drain due to a major clog of hair about the size of a golf ball that we pulled out of the drain. There was a draino available that we poured in and that fixed the problem.  I spent 1-day cleaning (scrubbing the bathroom, sweeping, dusting, mopping).  I had to run to whole foods to buy Clorox wipes and paper towels because there were only a couple left.  The neighborhood is very unsafe with drug deals on every corner especially 1 building away next to a construction area. People were literally doing drugs as you walked by. Not what a young child should see.  There were shady people sitting on the stoop every other day as we got back from our day. It was very uncomfortable because they started at my daughter and would not move as we tried to go up the stairs. I was extremely afraid for her safety.  There were fights across the street at night and early in the morning. There was a shooting 2 days after we arrived a couple of streets down. This place is good for younger people if traveling in a group. I do not recommend it for single moms with young children, especially girls. My young daughter had a major panic attack from the screaming/fighting across the street. The people fighting were treating to shoot and kill each other. We had to stay in a hotel prior to our early check-out due to the drug and crime activity.

What a spectacular space.  My family and I came for a wedding.  We were blown away by the space.  Luxury does not even begin to describe how amazing the space was.   Beds were so comfortable and the place was immaculate.  Gonzalo always responded to my requests and questions promptly.  He made our stay in New York stress free.  I would highly recommend his place to anyone.  If your coming to NY stay here!!!! We absolutely loved it.

Christian's place made our stay in NYC during the holidays a little less stressful. He was quick to respond and check in/out couldn't be any smoother. With the Grand St. stop being right outside the apartment, it was easy to get into the city quickly. We got lucky and were able to park our car right out front with no issues. Noises from people entering in and out the building is to be expected. The apartment was super clean and had everything we needed. Thanks again Christian!

Christian was a wonderful host. I was not satisfied with the interior of the apartment and its sketchy location with the high price I paid for it. Otherwise, it was clean but not well represented in the photos. It needs quite a bit of updating to warrant the price asked. If he lowered the price, it would be commensurate with what you get.

There is NO AC in this apartment. Great location, great host, great price, safe area, but sleeping, getting dressed, or just hanging out in the apartment was torture because it was hot and humid and there is no AC. Also do not bring a ton of bags because you will have to go up a ton of stairs. I did not hate staying there but being from a place where AC is important because of the heat, I cannot stress how much I wish I was warned because I saw zero reviews that mentioned this and this would have been a deal breaker for me.

Louie’s place was nice and clean, it was what I expected. I just had one gripe and it was that Louie up charged me.   His place was listed at $78 but when I tried booking, he said that the price was wrong and that he had intended to list it for $202 for that night but that Airbnb’s website prevented him from doing so due to some error. He then went on to say that he would try to help me out and only charge me $130. Louie was a really nice guy but I just can’t help but find this shady. I still got the place because it was last minute and I didn’t have time to shop around.

We had a good stay with Scott, he is a pleasant person, available and responsive. The apartment is generally correct and faithful to the photos. On the other hand, it is located in a sort of “basement” and is much less bright than it appears. Some curtains do not rise and it was therefore impossible to bring light into the room.   When we arrived we found hairs in the bathroom, and the kitchen utensils were greasy. Cleanliness is clearly not the strong point of this apartment. In addition, we had a lot of trouble getting hot water, whether in the morning or even in the evening.  It is cold in the “master bedroom” which seems to be poorly insulated and almost too hot in the other bedroom.   Scott's apartment is generally well located with several metro lines nearby. Be careful though, for the top of Manhattan, allow for a 50-minute journey. The Bushwick neighborhood is not unpleasant but it is clearly not the best neighborhood in Brooklyn.

This is a beautiful brownstone with plenty of space, a great deck and a great location.  A short walk will get you to the C or G subway lines.  A great bonus was the grocery story right across from the subway station, which was very handy for picking up dinner items after a long day of sightseeing. Pete was very helpful and made us feel right at home. Just an FYI - the AC is in the bedrooms only. If you're traveling during a freak heatwave, the rest of the house will be warm. Pete had a couple of fans for us that we were able to put where we needed them. The deck was shady and pleasant in the evenings, and we enjoyed cooking meals on the BBQ grill so we didn't have to heat up the kitchen. It worked out just fine. We really loved this home and had a great time. Thanks for everything!

I happened to arrive to NYC at the start of the COVID crisis, but that did not stop Hannah from being an awesome host.   The location is in the east village, with so many restaurant and bars around (obviously could not make full use of them), with different subway line roughly 10min walking. It’s safe, relatively quiet, especially in this room.  The house is clean considering it’s an old building, but Hannah does a great job cleaning everything. It’s a tiny space but comfortable for one person, especially if you’re in the room or out and about. The bed is comfy, and you have enough space for yourself.  So easily this is a 6/5 stay, because even though this was a stressful time, Hannah managed to accommodate me anyway she could. She’s polite and kind, and will give local tips anytime you want.
Loved staying at Annie’s place. Great, easy, close access to subway station, grocery store, drug stores, Central Park. We started every morning enjoying our breakfast on the spacious patio.
Great accommodation 5 mins walk from the subway. Very good, prompt communication from host. A stress free and enjoyable stay.

The location is great. You have a metro station in the corner. Gulcin respond the message really quick, which is great. The kitchen seems to be clean and well equipped. (I didn’t use it). The bathroom needs to be cleaned urgently. I’m pretty sure they will. The room was big enough for me and my girlfriend and the mattress was comfortable. This is an apartment building and the apt is not located in the first floor. I’m mentioning this because the management of this building seems not to care about the cleanliness of the common areas. As soon as I started going upstairs I saw trash, shoes stacked by the doors, pizza boxes and other things. This make me feel scare about this place.

At first I was about sketchy with this, because there were no reviews. However I just wanna say that this is the perfect place to stay for people who are looking for an affordable, convenient, and last minute trip to NYC. The place is great. A bit smaller then it looks in the pictures but It's not a big deal. Elizabeth and her husband were great. Check in was smooth and they even left a gift basket for us. AWESOME !!!

Carla is very punctual and will answer any questions you have about your stay. The room has everything you might need and a tv with multiple subscriptions to different streaming and movie networks which is very convenient. The location is not the best, it’s about as far out in Brooklyn as you can get. About an hour from midtown Manhattan by subway. And the neighborhood is not the greatest. I highly recommend taking the bus from the subway stop to the house and not making the 20 minute walk. That being said, nothing happened to me to make me feel like I was in any danger. I am making my judgement based on the conditions of the houses and the people along the way. Once you get closer to where Carla lives, the area does improve. It is a good deal for the price, especially considering how much a place in manhattan costs. You just have to be ok with being very out of the way.

I’d happily stay here again. As far as New York pricing goes, this is excellent value. It is a long trip into the city, but if you plan for the extra time each day it’s manageable. The host gave me plenty of privacy, and the shared bathroom was free most of the time.   The neighborhood is perfectly fine during daytime, but at night time have your wits about you- it is Brooklyn after all, and it can seem a little scary at times. If you take the bus or Uber back from the station, you’ll be fine.

I was a tourist, so the location was awful, very very far for everything, very danger neighborhood if you want to walk in the night to get to the house. Every wall was full of rules, I felt like a 13 years old child... Very unfair because she charge me 45 dollars extra for cleanance and in all the rules around the house said that its going to charge you extra dollars if you don't let everything VERY clean.

FANTASTIC APARTMENT AND A GREAT STAY AT A GREAT PRICE! Modern and with an incredible fully stocked kitchen and HUGE backyard. The place had obviously just been renovated, and was full of great finishes and design touches (the kitchen and bathroom were just awesome). The place was very clean and actually surprisingly huge: With two full floors and two large bedrooms, it's plenty of space for a group or family. And the location is just about perfect: On a quiet tree-lined street right in the middle of Williamsburg, just seconds to all the neighborhood's famous bars and restaurants and shops. If you're looking to stay in the heart of Williamsburg, but are afraid of noise, this place is perfect. It felt like an oasis in the middle of the city! The L train was also conveniently located just a few minutes away, and made getting around very easy. A fantastic apartment and a great deal! I would gladly stay here again. 5 stars!!!

The location cannot be beat and Jeffrey is a wonderful host! We missed our bus and arrived to NYC about 5 hours later than expected but Jeffrey was flexible and welcoming which made a very stressful situation much better.  The space is very clean and bright. The bed was comfortable and the building was quiet. Overall it was a great experience and recommend you book your stay.

Upsides: close to ferry, close to a nice park for running, close to a nice branch of the NY public library, close to a supermarket (of middling quality), inexpensive. Major downside: several power outages over 20 days, the first of which lasted 2-3 hours (host wasn't home to repair). Major potential downside: the check-in procedure didn't work as advertised; if other guests weren't there to let me in, the wait could've been hours. (The occupancy rate of the 4 rooms wasn't high during my stay, so it's possible check-in could be a problem for others if the procedure hasn't been updated since my stay in June 2018.) Minor downside: the quality of the surrounding streets/area is uneven. Some people might feel at least a bit unsafe on some of the streets (esp. some streets near the market and the library).

Sketchy guy, took me to another building other than the address listed, texted me the day before check in to coordinate a time I said 3pm as listed was fine. Then texted me 9 am on New Year’s Day asking if I could check in earlier, when I said you should of told me this yesterday he responded with you’re not the only person moving in on the 1st and he has things to do.. basically a clown.

This is an amazing stay for the solo traveler or couple in the upper side of Manhatten located in the heart of Harlem. Situated only a block away from the famed Apollo Theater and a 5-minute walk to the 125th AC-BD (blue-orange) subway lines, I couldn't have asked for a better locale for the purpose of my visit to New York City. For the low daily rates it was being offered when I booked it, I felt like I was getting it for a steal (or maybe I was)!   The apartment itself looks quite like the pictures shown on Airbnb with minuscule differences. It's also located within a secure building, so I didn't have to worry about security while I was there or leaving my luggage behind as I explored the city. Everything was stocked for either a brief or extended stay; all I needed to bring was my own toiletries and groceries to complete the place for my stay.  The host, Arelis, was very friendly and accommodating, offering her time to get the place prepared for my stay as well as her knowledge if I had any questions after the initial check-in. She went the extra mile to make sure my stay at the apartment was a good one. If I return to NYC for another visit, I hope to stay at this place again if possible.

The worst experience with an hotel EVER. I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone, for sure this is not a place for families with young children like ours - families, please stay away.  We spot a mouse in our apartment (we could even film it!) and even if they were aware we had 2 children were left there with it for a night. The day after they said they would have given us a new apartment but then they changed their mind saying that - since they caught the mouse  (FALSE!) we could have stayed there. When we said that was not an option because of hygienic reasons (they have not even cleaned there) they said they wouldn’t have given another apartment because my children stained the carpet and they could have done it again. We’ve found ourselves with 2 young children without a clean place to spend the night in and we had to stay there another night with the mouse, the glue they put and what the animal left behind.  I felt discriminated because of the children and cheated several times. Also Wi-Fi connection in the room very poor in case you need to work from there. Personnel rude with the exception of 2 guys at the reception that have been kind with us (but with no power to make decisions). COVID Rules not respected, not even by their personnel. The cleaning lady laughed at me because I didn’t want to share the elevator with other people to keep distances even if that was in line with hotel instructions. Lastly I came to pick up some boxes / mails that were delivered there when I left and found 1 box open and empty inside. I think this is the worst review I have ever written - you can check in my profile, I am never that negative - but hope this helps other people avoid unpleasant situations such the ones I and my family lived.
beautiful sweet home. but no washing machine and the block nearby scared me a little though nothing happened.

How to enjoy this place:   1)      Spend a lot of time in the bed!  There’s a terrific mattress and nice sheets.  As long as there’s not a party nearby, it’s quiet at night for NYC.    2)     Enjoy the antique lamps and Moroccan light and the vintage gold mirrors.  Stefanie has a nice design eye.   The place is artsy, bohemian and nearby good restaurants and shops.  This was all welcome given the other problems...    3)     Keep the lights low all day so it will seem atmospheric and Parisian and you won’t see how badly it all needs a fresh coat of  paint and TLC.  It’s clean, just really shabby.   And yes, You may rightfully wonder as we did  why on god’s green earth you’re paying $400 a day—with fees—for a place where you shouldn’t turn on the lights…    4)         Stay alert. Our first night the police came to the building because someone had jimmied the mailboxes open to steal the mail.    5)         Just know the online photos make it seem nicer. It is small.   And, though you may see a bathtub online, it doesn’t work.  Nor does the stove, though there is a hotplate.  I already mentioned the general sense of neglect.  We’re gritty New Yorkers and not babies so this all would have been fine for half the cost or less.     6)         Find out ahead where the apartment keys actually are.  The pre-arrival text said, “Door will be left unlocked with the keys inside.”   But where?   After a hunt, we found then hidden on a shelf in a closet.   Ask ahead as you may not be told.      7)         Hope you don’t arrive as we did to surprise building repairs (Not Stefanie’s fault, but still a shock to not know ahead).  Our arrival involved workers screaming at each other outside our door, much hammering and drilling, dust everywhere, (as well as the aforementioned hidden apartment keys and spontaneous police visit).   Our worst  arrival to an air bnb ever and given that we were there to celebrate my BFs birthday I’m mostly glad we both have a crazy sense of humor. Sometimes You laugh so you don’t cry..   Construction went on for two days til we gave up and decided to leave early. To her credit, Stefanie apologized and refunded the last night.  (But also to be honest, I personally would have felt bad and refunded more… nonetheless we were grateful to get that).      8)  In summary:  I just wouldn’t pay more than $175-200 a night including fees for this spot.
