Though it has its unique charms, the main issue  is cost vs value! Even with NY prices this just isn’t  worth what we paid but you may get lucky on a big sale.

Host was extremely unprofessional, cancelled on me the same exact day hours before check in , wasted my time and energy and was  judgmental of a person she knew nothing about or never met . Repeated her “ no drug use” numerous of times which i took offensively especially being that I’ve never used a drug a day in my life . Just the worst .

Stefanie’s unit was charming and in a great location. However, the building that the unit is in is quite run-down and the check-in was not as described. We had a lot of difficulty opening the unit door after locking it, as it seemed that the lock would get jammed/the key wouldn’t turn. Hopefully the locking mechanism can be replaced or re-keyed  ASAP to ensure a less stressful stay for other guests. There are also a lot of ants currently in the unit. Overall, we had a fun stay and the location was exceptional, the bed was comfy, and the unit was cute. We would stay again, but only if the check-in communication was better, door lock was fixed and the ants were taken care of.

This is the BEST Airbnb we have ever stayed at. The location was perfect! Walking distance to the subway to get to Manhattan. Everything was very clean and the bed with comfortable. She had bottled water and snacks in the room waiting for us. Ladi is a wonderful lady! I can’t stress enough how amazing our stay was! 100% recommend!

Adam’s place is amazing and he’s an amazing host as well. We had a bit of a scare not knowing whether we would be affected by hurricane Florence in our area, but he was incredibly understanding and responsive throughout it. His place was very clean, he provided fresh towels, and although the place is right across from a fire station, we were never disturbed by the noise. I would recommend this place especially to those who want to live like a real New Yorker during their stay :) thanks again, Adam!
Its simple, just go with Alan's Airbnb. Great place for the price. He's not sketchy. He is very approachable if any issues arise.  10/10 experience and would book with him again.

This stay was maybe the easiest and expectation-exceeding stay I’ve had with AirBnB: the space was clean and nice, the bed was comfortable, the amenities were high-quality and easy to find (delicious coffee), the shower worked well, and there were thoughtful touches like a hamper and hangers in the closet (oh, and there WAS a closet, which I definitely didn’t count on in NYC). Lots of great food and interesting stuff to do in the Bed-Stuy area, all in walking distance. Plus it’s an eight-minute walk to the Utica station on the A/C lines, really convenient. I also appreciated what wasn’t there: no weird smells in the stairway, no sketchy door locks, no difficult check-in procedure, or any of the other things I’ve encountered in other places. Only one warning - there is a washer/dryer at the top of the stairs, but if you use them make your loads very small. I ought to have split mine into two or three; the spin cycle on the washer left my clothes sopping, and the dryer tried its best but I ended up having to hang dry my stuff in sections. Thanks for a beautiful space and an easy stay overall!

Great accommodation!!! The location is very good, 7-8 minutes walk from the Utica Avenue metro (line A-C). Utica Av. is an express station which is very practical for quickly reaching the Brooklyn Bridge or even Manhattan. The neighborhood is very good, quite quiet, small shops, no insecurity.  The accommodation is the right size for two people, it has air conditioning (essential in summer), it is well equipped.  Tal & Amarelle are very accommodating.  I highly recommend this accommodation!

I booked this Airbnb to stay for a month, well in advance. I arrived excited, the place looked clean and as described in the advertisement and photos. I checked in according to the time described in the advertisement, and a few hours after arriving, while having dinner, I had an unpleasant surprise, seeing a mouse inside the house. I was scared and at the same time I informed the owner, who only got back to me almost 5 hours later. I have a phobia of rats, and I wouldn't be able to stay in the place, which is small with a rat, which left the room and went under the refrigerator, in the living room. For this reason I ended up going to a hotel, until I got a position from the owner, who came 5 hours later. At first he remained attentive and helpful, he said he would send a professional to exterminate the place the next day so I could come back. The next day I came back, thinking the problem had been solved, but unfortunately, again while I was having dinner, I looked to the side and saw the mouse under the fridge again.  I sent a message again, and again I received a response just 5 hours later. One more night I had to sleep outside. The owner, although attentive, tried to tell me that he had never had a problem with rats, but when I took the refrigerator out of its place I could see that he had lied, because he had very old rat traps, dirt and a lot of rat feces on the floor. I sent photos to the owner and once again he sent an exterminator. The location is good, but unfortunately I didn't have a good experience, and after witnessing a rat in the house two days in a row, I ended up not having comfortable accommodation, because I was tense for the rest of the days, afraid of having a rat again in the place I had closed to stay. At no point did the owner give me the option of going to another apartment he had

The host and the place is fabulous. This was a short walk from the Utica station for the A and the C lines so our visit into Manhattan was fairly convenient. The neighborhood itself can be a bit noisy with sirens and weird people, but this is more standard New York thing. The water pressure for the shower is decent but the use of faucet in the kitchen doesn’t affect it. The bed and the loveseat was very comfortable. Place was nice and warm on subzero days. All of the amenities made out lives so much easier. I didn’t even need to go buy an envelope that I needed out of the blue. There was even a stapler if I needed one. The fridge was full sized so we could get full size jugs of water and milk and still have plenty of room for other stuff. There are local restaurants that are gems but walking too far either south or north of the street seem a little shady. Im used to the city life so it wasn’t a big deal but others may find it uncomfortable late at night. Stay here. You won’t regret it.

The place was very wonderful, clean, secure, and It just felt like you went to a relatives place and stayed the night. At first, it seems kinda scary because the room is on the lower floor but once you are actually in, turns out to be a nice, clean and organized place. Veronica will take care of you and make sure you feel safe and ensure that you fill safe. There is so much love in her place and pride in running a RBNB.

The time we spent at Shelly and Wayne's house was great. An extremely clean, fragrant and well-tidy house. Ample space with a large TV. The fact that there were 3 access doors and one with a password gave us a feeling of care and security. But the neighborhood is quiet and we walked around at night without any problems. Wayne extremely friendly and attentive. He made us very comfortable with the house and gave us several tips. Excellent location: 1 minute walk from the metro. Sensational for those of us who use the subway a lot!! As if that wasn't enough, they left us with a refrigerator stocked with water and juices. In the cupboards there were cookies and peanut butter. The bathrooms had soaps and shampoos. Air conditioning in the bedroom and living room, great for hot or cold NY days and nights. All in all, everything was perfect and we would definitely return next time. Very comfortable. You can stay without fear! Congratulations Shelly and Wayne because you are excellent hosts!

Amazing house and wonderful hosts! Everything was clean, organized and beautiful! They are very careful and helpful! The only thing I disliked about the place is the area, where it is located. It is very dangerous and some policemen told us to not arrive after 8pm and we were afraid of it.

Lauren and Ron’s place is quaint and easy to access. It was a little far from the major areas of  New York, but well worth it. Nothing an easy train ride didn’t fix. The amenities and space are simple, but for the price it is an absolute steal! Very comfortable bed, and a charming surrounding area. Right by a gorgeous park that is great for taking walks or runs in. Be sure to grab an everything bagel from Inwood Bagels for breakfast one morning!

This studio is in Inwood, which is located at the northernmost tip of Manhattan. While it may seem far from midtown/other touristy places, the A and 1 trains both serve the area and will reliably get you to where you want to go at any time. I lived in New York for four years and can confirm that Inwood is generally a safe area, and the location of this studio in particular is well-lit and a short walk from the nearest subway station. Walking back late at night, I did not feel uncomfortable or unsafe.   The only thing I will say is that this studio does not have a full kitchen, only a bar fridge. If this is a problem for you, you shouldn’t stay here, but there is no shortage of dining options in the area. Thus, cooking is absolutely unnecessary during your stay.   I recommend this place wholeheartedly; it’s a great deal for the price.

Javier's place is a homey house on the charming Sunset Park. The room is spare but has all the basics, and I really liked being able to access the keys without needing to rely on Javier being there in person, it made it really flexible and low-stress. Also, free coffee!

This was my first AirBNB rental. I want to be fair.  The prices as compared to hotel lodging in NYC was very cheap. But you can't make that comparison unless you are going to run your AirBNB like a hotel.  That being said, I didn't meet the host. No big deal but not very welcoming. #1 - The neighborhood. Its a very vibrant area. But its a high crime area (easily verified).  So I wouldn't recommend coming in late by yourself like I did . Especially not being local. #2 - The building. Its an older building with very narrow stairs. So carrying my luggage up 4 flights of very narrow stairs was a challenge. Its a very quiet building as I never saw one neighbor in 3 days. #3 - Apartment. The apartment is as described. Absolutely no amenities, not even a bottle of water. I understand the price was low but in my opinion you still have to provide more than bare bones and 10yr old (at least) bedding. The bedding was clean but musty because it was OLD.  Bedding is cheap just change it out. The chair at the table had chipped paint. How much is a chair?  Its a place to sleep that's it. #4-Wifi. I assume its the host router I was connecting to. A wifi extender is needed. For a business person such as myself I couldn't do any work at the apartment.  Wifi is almost useless in the apartment. Wifi Extenders are cheap.  #5 - Transportation.  The A train (8th ave express) is right there. But make sure you take express if you are going to midtown or lower. The local can take you almost an hour because of all the stops. The proximity is great but I wouldn't do it if all of your business is in midtown like mine was. I guess for someone like me even a cheap hotel with some amenities would probably be a better buy. Not sure I can recommend this place even at the price I paid. Calling it "Beautiful" in the description is in the eye of the beholder and misleading. All of the above is my opinion.

We had a great stay! The apartment was a perfect space for us to crash and relax after long days. The bed and couch were very comfy. The location was great, quiet and super close to the A train. Never felt unsafe.  Lauren and Ron were quick to communicate  and willing to accommodate.  We would love to stay again!

This apartment was about 7-10 minutes away from the subway - direct access to central city - time square, approx 20- 30 minutes away, cable tv , local grocer and take away food easily available - spacious , prices correct - super rapid response time and duty manager onsite, I've used airbnb in western , Eastern Europe , Asia and the U.S . The service on need is satisfied - I have done 63 flights and 13 countries this year , my opinion is based on past experience vs what Yolanda has on offer - this isn't a sales pitch . She offers a good environment at reasonable rate . Super comfy apartment shower is cool fresh linen , towels etc .  I traveled with my mum , ok , maybe a bit tough traveling due to walk to station and area might be perceived as intimidating , but non experienced . Local hood, resident people with history growing up here .  If u looking for value and space to suite . Don't mind a small walk , not afraid by local culture . And willing to embrace a very dope experience .. then I fully reccomend this listing. Uber   Readily available as well and never had to wait more than five minutes -! Well done Yolanda , blessings 2018!  By the way - Rita is super hot!

The place was very homey and lovely. It was better than I expected. Michael and Sharon were very accomodating and responded quickly to all my questions and concerns. I would highly recommend this place to anyone who is visiting NYC. It is a steal and a great place to stay!

Place near the subway 10 or 15 minutes from Manhattan, Erika and Atsuo are very good hosts and do not hesitate to answer any questions you may have about how to get somewhere in the city, I returned late to the place and I never felt unsafe!

We all have a mixed feeling about this place. Unfortunately,  the cons far outweighs the pros. I'll list them based on our experiences.   Pros: great host. Very nice & accommodating. She stayed up till late night/early morning to give us keys. Probably the only good thing about our stay.   Cons: pretty sketchy neighborhood. There were bikes and people outside late night screaming, drinking, and being obnoxiously loud. You definitely need to close the window so you dont hear it, but there was AC and smell issues that ill explain below.  We had to come late nights for our stay and finding a parking was always tough.  As soon as we entered in the room, we smelled piss. The ACs were turned off and every room had bad smell. The living room and 1 bedroom had piss smell. There was another bad odor too. Owner definitely needs to take care of this.  There was no central AC, every room had one and it was very loud.  You cant use too many ACs and multiple electric units (someone used curling iron) at the same time as it will trip the wire. That happened to us. Owner told us not to use more than 3 ACs at once, but power still went out for a couple of rooms.  Theres a long staircase at the door to get inside the room. That was a major issue for us as we had multiple heavy suitcases and taking those upstairs was tough. The staircase was not mentioned in the description. We wouldn't have rented this property if we knew. Cleaning has to be done by the rentee even after paying cleaning fee.

Excellent room in a trendy neighbourhood it’s quiet at night but still only around the corner from tonnes of cool bars and restaurants. Philip and Juan are great hosts with great recommendations for the local area and check in was super simple and stress free, just down the road you can get to the banks of the east river with stunning views of the Manhattan skyline park high we found unbeaten anywhere else we went. There is also very convenient links to manhattan via the L train on Bedford avenue or if you fancy a walk with great views you can walk across the Williamsburg bridge which is only a stones throw away. We still have a lot to see in NYC and hope we can book this place next time we visit. Couldn’t rate it highly enough!

Had a terrible (and unsafe) check-in experience, the hosts kept the wrong keys for check-in and hence we could not check in for 4.5 hours until the hosts finally responded late at night, barring that the hosts are very cordial and welcoming. Overall the place is decently clean, located in a convenient location with lots of cafes nearby and close to metro. When we stayed there were not enough blankets/bedding provided and that was a little inconvenient.

The apartment is about a 6-minute walk from the train station, which will facilitate access to different lines to get around New York. There are many homeless people in the area, but they don't do anything to you, but it is not dangerous, you can walk safely until very late. We shared the apartment with 2 other guests, in different rooms, we had everything we needed to cook in peace. Our room was private with a bathroom, everything was very clean and tidy, the hosts were super friendly, although they only spoke English.

We were looking forward to staying in Brooklyn, but unfortunately we didn't have a great experience at this AirBnb. The place is very nicely decorated as shown in the pictures, but not very comfortable. When we arrived it was swelteringly hot (we stayed in August). Once we turned on the AC units it started to cool down except for one bedroom unit. We informed Michelle of this issue and her response was that the unit was working fine and we should clean the filter. My husband was able to get the unit working by cycling it, but it took a while and made for an unpleasant night, especially because the mattress in that bedroom is not comfortable at all. I'm not sure even how to describe it, but it was more like a futon stuffed with plastic. My husband described it as "sleeping on a bunch of diapers." We also had issues with the water. It was either scaldingly hot in the downstairs bedroom or not hot at all in the upstairs bathroom. Please be advised if you have any mobility issues as all three bedrooms require you to walk up or down a set of narrow stairs. Michelle was not friendly to deal with. We requested early check-in when we booked the AirBnb and she could not tell me if she would be able to accommodate that request until 2 hrs before we checked in. Ultimately she let us check in 1 hr early. No flexibility with check-out. The location is pretty good, and easy walking distance to lots of restaurants. We recommend Luigi's for pizza and Al-Noor Halal Deli for Mediterranean food. Brooklyn is great, and we were hoping to have a more authentic experience by staying in an AirBnb, but now we wished we had just stayed at a hotel.

Jackie was an exceptional host and went the extra mile to make us feel at home. She helped us with local tips and advice when asked and helped make our stay in NYC stress free. We enjoyed staying in her home.
The cat is listed as friendly but regularly attacked us, scratched luggage and broke furniture around the room while we were sleeping or out of the room.

This was my first AirBnB experience. I had no idea what to really expect, and I had never traveled to NYC before. I was unaware that Brownsville is one of the “more underdeveloped” areas of Brooklyn. It was one of the last stops on the 3 train and the further out you went from the city (into Brooklyn) the more sketchy the neighborhoods became.   Onyx is a true sweetheart. I love animals. However, for someone who isn’t too keen to animals, it would be quite the inconvenience. Several times during the middle of the night, Onyx would use the bed to catapult to the window seal and unbeknownst to me would use my face, chest, arms as the launching pad. Like any true performer he craves the attention. Constantly climbing up the chairs, clawing at the furniture, and knocking over plants- for dramatic effect. He stole the show. <3

Such a AMAZING place. Stella is so nice and understanding. The house is absolutely beautiful! The backyard and balcony is gorgeous. Staying at this airbnb made my trip less stressful and better overall. I would recommend anyone wanting to stay in the bronx to stay here!

What more can I say about Stella and her place? First, she's a very good person. Her place is a steal in terms of value. Clean, quality and warm you really can't ask for more. I don't know why she's not a super-host yet! If I can get more days, am too sure that will be my permanent address for as long as I'll be in NYC for. Another reason some of us still believe in Airbnb. Thank you for being true and kind.

Stella's place was absolutely adorable! She has a very beautiful house, the room and bathroom were very clean and welcoming. She was kind enough to let me park in front of her driveway which made my trip much less stressful!

I can't say enough about my stay with Sue! So welcoming and I immediately felt right at home. The bedroom has a super comfy bed and I never had trouble sleeping like I often do in a new place.   Sue and her girlfriend were super helpful, giving me great tips regarding places to eat and navigating the subway. Speaking of subway, the Graham Street L train is a stones throw away.   This was my first Airbnb stay and I'm afraid I've been ruined by Sue's amazing hospitality! Highly recommended!

We are a family of 3, who used to live in Carroll Gardens, so we know the area really well. We've seen a lot of apartments and I can honestly Rob's place is fantastic! Airy and spacious - spread over two floors (with a bathroom on each). Newly refurbished throughout, modern, clean and super stylish! Gorgeous sleek kitchen with everything you could possibly need. The beds are super comfortable with lovely plush duvets and pillows, and there were plenty of thick fluffy bath towels too. The bedrooms are quiet because they are below street level (but it's a quiet street anyway). Lovely to have a washing machine and tumble dryer. Other nice touches include: a Keurig machine with a big selection of coffees and teas, lovely selection of books (fiction and guide), a great hairdryer, a little clothes steamer, and lots of drawer/cupboard space meaning you can really unpack and make yourself at home. And, the whole place was absolutely spotless!   Rob couldn't be nicer too! So helpful and responsive - the perfect host! He really wanted to do everything he could to make our stay as comfortable as possible and ensure we had a great experience, and we did! We loved the apartment, wholeheartedly recommend it, and are already planning to return next year. Thanks Rob!

The studio is how the photos appear and for 1 or 2 days it is not bad.  In my case, I stayed for 10 days in which no one came to clean the cat's litter box, which by the way is next to the bed, although I contacted them to ask.  On the other hand, the cleanliness in general leaves a lot to be desired, especially in the kitchen, which is greasy everywhere, so before using any utensils I had to wash them.  The sockets and switches do not have any protection which can be dangerous for children. The neighborhood and the neighbors of the building were very noisy during the night and early in the morning.  The window cannot be closed completely since it has the air conditioning pipe so you can hear everything more and it makes the room much colder.  Lastly, the neighborhood was pretty quiet and I didn't have any problems, even though it is supposedly one of the most dangerous in the city.

My girlfriend and I really enjoyed Tuttis place. Tutti was very accomadating and flexible when our check in plans didn't go as expected. The space offers a lot of privacy and has its own separate entrance. We stayed for three nights and didn't see Tutti one time. It has a nice private porch area too that's great for relaxing, grilling, having drinks etc. The location is great and we never felt unsafe. If I visit Brooklyn again hopefully I'll be staying here again!

Rob was a wonderful host and his space in Carroll Gardens was just what we needed for a getaway.  The home itself is very clean and spacious.  Upstairs, the kitchen is roomy with plenty of counter space, the living room has a great couch and TV, and the dining room has a large table that could also double up as work space.  The downstairs bedrooms were cozy and included perhaps some of the most comfortable beds I've slept on in a while.  The house is a short walk to Carroll Park, lots of great restaurants, and a short bike ride to Prospect Park.  Rob was very responsive throughout our stay, getting back to us within minutes for any questions or minor issues we had.  In short, I highly recommend staying here!

Rob is a welcoming, patient, and generous host. Although he lives upstairs and is quick to solve problems, the apartment feels completely private. I barely heard him upstairs, which is a major feat in a city apartment building.  The location is ideal, in my favorite New York neighborhood, close to great restaurants and food shopping. I enjoyed cooking in the beautiful, open kitchen as well. And it was super peaceful to sleep there... almost no noise whatsoever.   In case natural light is important to you, you should know that there isn't much of it in the apartment. The only two windows are at sidewalk level, so it's hard to leave the windows or shades open. And the bottom floor is a basement, without windows. That said, all the A/C units work perfectly and the place is very comfortable. It is rare to find such a large space (with two bathrooms!) in the city. Thank you, Rob, for a lovely stay.

We stayed at Rob's for just over 2 months and it was an excellent place for us to both work remotely and explore NYC. The location was great and easy to get to from public transportation. We especially enjoyed the kitchen, very well appointed and had everything we needed. We had an issue with the renovated shower but Rob was able to come in and fix it and we had no issues since. Thanks again!

From the moment I stepped into Rob’s place I loved it!  Immaculate, beautifully presented, cozy yet spacious, with all the amenities for which one could possibly wish!  I called this vast two-level abode home for 3 months and it was absolutely perfect for my lengthy stay and didn’t leave me wanting - I’d venture back in a heartbeat!  In terms of location, you’ve the best of Brooklyn at your doorstep.  The apartment is conveniently located amidst the lovely neighborhoods of Gowanus, Boerum Hill, Cobble Hill, and Carrol Gardens - with picturesque Brooklyn Heights just a hop, skip and a jump away!  Nestled on a lively corner next to a beautiful church and across from a great little music shop (which has occasional acoustic jams!), the apartment is conveniently located for effortless subway travel, amazing grocery selections (Whole Foods, Dumbo Market, Trader Joe’s, and Union Market are just short walks away!), brownstone browsing, toiletries/necessities (Rite Aide, pharmacy, etc.), and bars/restaurants and shopping (Smith Street, Court Street, Atlantic!)…you have it all right there outside your door!  Moreover, Rob is such a warm and friendly host who is happy to help and accommodate, but never invasive!  He was always so kind in receiving and delivering packages to me which I’d had delivered during my lengthy stay - and he always offered a cheery disposition, beaming smile, and thoughtful convo upon our neighborly meetings.  Rob even proved to be the most gracious of hosts when I had a future airbnb host cancel on me the night before my new booking, offering to let me stay a couple more days should I need the time to find a new place to stay - that was incredibly kind, above and beyond, and deeply appreciated!  Bottom line, if Rob’s place is available, book it, you won’t regret it!
Second time we’ve stayed at Rob’s place.  Rob is a terrific host and his apartment is clean, spacious and in an unbeatable location in BK.

The hospitality of the host was terrible. I spent a whole day trying to find the apartment because he told me to look for the key in a store that there are millions of in New York. We spent the whole day looking for the key, we went to several stores, he didn't answer me. We arrived at the store and the key was not there, we had to wait hours for them to notify us, I thought it was a scam. We arrived and the apartment was dirty, like it had just been used, meals from previous days, the bathroom was not clean. The truth is that I don't recommend it. I stayed two days in New York and ruined one. It doesn't have a table. It doesn't have dark curtains, the sun barely comes out and comes in, there is no way to cover it. Nothing to do with other experiences in other countries.

Abass & Sere were brilliant at communicating with us. We had some issues with lock code, but it was resolved in seconds! The place itself was very nice and cozy. Plenty of space with a nice kitchen area and all kitchen equipment you will need for your stay, especially a coffee maker. Flat was 5min walk from subway line C, which goes to Manhattan and took us basically everywhere we wanted to go. The only downside was the area, as it is not very nice to walk there when it’s dark. There were quite few groups of people hanging around and making some comments. Although it might not be as dangerous as it might look, but it was not the most pleasant experience either (which we understand is out of host’s control). Overall we would recommend the place (looks exactly like pictures)!
Amazing value, but the neighborhood felt unsafe. I would highly recommend for those looking for a great deal but not those not used to a sketchy neighborhood~

I enjoyed my stay at Stephen’s apartment. Main attraction is its location; right next to Bergen subway station, at the Bergen/Smith streets crossing. Smith street alone has loads of good bars and places to eat, and I loved it there. The apartment is nice as well. Not overly big, but a decent bed, a desk, a couch and a small kitchen. Nice art reproductions on the walls, and a working A/C. The bathroom is tiny and a bit outdated but everything worked. A small foldaway table served me as a place to put my clothes on for the week. All in all,it is better value for money than staying in a midrange hotel.  Checkin was easy, with clear instructions being provided before arrival, and communication before checkin was smooth.  Checkout was a bit more complicated as the place where one can store luggage was not open according to its website (I had to leave a bit before 11:00am which was checkout time) and the owner of that place did not pick up the phone. I sent a text to the owner (after trying to ring him first), suggesting I’d leave my luggage in the apertment (which I left spotless, even making the bed and sorting the little waste I had generated). Not receiving a reply and needing to leave, I sent a further text stating that I would leave my luggage in the apartment and pick it up within two hours. Somehow, my messages were not received - he was abroad - and I ended up in a back and forth with the owner’s partner (my main point of contact) through the Airbnb app. Him claiming I checked out too late (technically correct), me arguing the place to store luggage was closed (and sending screenshots to prove that I had at least tried to send messages/call). Too bad. When I casually mentioned that I had been bitten a few times by an unknown insect of sorts (yet not mosquitos), the conversation - on the owner’s partner’s end - became a bit unpleasant, unfortunatey. I did at no point claim that there were bedbugs, and I still don’t know what bit me. A bit of an unpleasant end of my stay.  All in all, my review is going to be neutral, despite the apertment itself being a good place to stay.  The owner (or rather his partner) has now threatened to negatively review me as a guest.

The place has unique vibe. Several rules to follow, which at first make you feel a bit scared but they are all in place to make all guests experience better. The house is colorful and full of personal artifacts. Evi is an amazing lady who has big heart, respects all people and shows care whenever you meet her. I will consider coming back again.

Well.  I knew it might be a bit funky yet it had gotten  mosy good reviews and the location was great for the Lower East Side and being near to  my son, friends, and colorful areas I used to live in. That said, the apartment and building  was quite a bit run down  like it might have been 40 years ago or more when hippies, struggling artists,  and my  immigrant grandfolk first came to the LES. For 2020 in an growing upscale neighborhood, the cost and cleaning fees seem out of line with the condition, amenities and service. If I can attach photos I  will.  The dog as noted is very sweet, yet hair is indeed all over and one might find the dog resting in the bathroom when you need to use it or blocking pathways  or trying to enter your room. The decor with some art and books is interesting and there are plenty of TVs.   The kitchen has some nice  newer appliances and is spacious,. Yet the place and rooms  feel a bit run down with holes in the walls, peeling paint, slanted flights of stairs  that can be dangerous  to navigate especially with luggage and no help,  slanting shelves which one cannot really put much on or it will slide off, questionable  loose outlets and rickety lamps, poor lighting,  and stained though presumably clean bedding. The communication and service was not very responsive.  Adonis, the son who manages it for his father was irritable, and did not extend himself to situate, orient, or assist me. From the start, although I was reassured by the host that check in would be easy and someone would assist,  it was not so.  He had forgotten to put keys in the  lock box  and even the photo and instructions for accessing the key were wrong.  I spent quite a bit of time trying codes on each of 6 boxes with no response to messages for help. Luckily 2 young males who were guests let me in and  helped me with my suitcase up 4 flights.  It was late afternoon, I had waited until a few hours after 3 to check in,  and  yet they had to wake Adonis up to get the keys. He was quite irritable and did nothing to orient me. the  room was quite tight, with no dresser or closet to put suitcase and clothes in ,  just a few mostly flimsy wire hangers on hooks in the wall, and angled ( not 90 degree) shelves.  a small table. here was a tissue box, basket, and TV . Towels were in a closet and clean, with 1 hook to hang them on . nothing was laid out. Adonis did not orient me to anything and seemed grumpy when asked. At least bathroom /kitchen was mostly clean and the  place quiet as most noted.  There was a broken screen in an open windiw so bugs could get in. mosquitos abounded by the front door so I worried about thst. when it was supposed to rain i asked Adonis to please close it and he was busy and I had to wait 2 hours before he came in, imbec on table breaking it and displacing my clothes which had to be thefmre since there was no dresser. He did screw back a leg and sort of applogized yet was clearly  stressed. a hairdryer had not worked and i asked him i he would replace it. ge said later that day he would, yet did not until the next day after i had made complaints to customer service. he thought I was rude when there was confusion in communication hey ye was the one that was reactive and as he seemed to sleep or stay up in the living room with the TV on and perhaps high, I did not feel welcome to use it or at ease i. aporoaching him for help. Alex did not answer  messages I left to try to resokve some of the issues.  there were clean towels, the bathroom was mostly clean yet in 4 days I did not see Adonis vacuum even after ither guests left. I ask to  vaccuum and did some myself. ( it did not work great on the fur balls).  Matressesqere stained as was my comforter though sheets may hae been clean. The sink in the shared  bathroom clogged a bit and although shower did get warm I am not sure if it was cleaned regularly either . there were shampoos, soap and lotion  and kitchen had teas and coffee , cocoa, spices,  yet it was not clear if that was for guests . the fridge was smelly when I arrive and garbage sat out the front door for several days. if one was young with low expectatiobs staying a day or 2 it could be fine. for a senior who is pretty used to even couch surfing for 4 days and needing and wanting to dress up, dry and style hair,  and stay clean,  it was a not quite up to other airbnb standards. at least the AC did work.

Value and location were fine. The stressful part was the lack of communication from the host and inaccurate info regarding check-in.  I had to get in touch with AirBnB support to get the host to respond and finally get in the building after sitting outside for an hour.  I was given the wrong lockbox code.  I spoke with two other guests renting rooms there and they also told me they had problems with check-in as well.  This was the first AirBnB I’ve ever had an issue with and the first one where the host does not provide their mobile #.

We had a wonderful stay here! Check-in was a bit chaotic due to an issue with the keys from the last guests, but the instructions were straightforward otherwise. The apartment is spacious for a studio, and has an incredible patio. Centrally located to most anything you’d want to do in Williamsburg (and a super short walk from Milk Bar 🤤 - dangerous), and very easy to get to Manhattan via the train. Bonus is that Trouble, the cat, was the sweetest kitty and we loved spending time with her.

Hello. Stayed from 25.03 to 5.04. The apartment is located not far from the subway. Pleasantly surprised by the presence of all necessary in the house for the first time. The apartment is clean, comfortable. The first thing we started to worry about was the presence of a nearby recycling plant, but there was no unpleasant smell. The next moment is a railway located not far away, the noise from the trains interfered at night. It turned out that there is a church in the neighboring building and sometimes loud services are held in the evenings. But overall, everything was fine. For all the time there were no difficulties. Left the best impressions of the trip. The owner turned out to be a decent and honest person. I strongly recommend to stay in this apartment.

Good, clean modern and well equipped little apartment close to local transit links and grocery stores. Some said they felt unsafe here but I never did, just bear in mind this is not as "hipster" or tourist oriented as other parts of Brooklyn are so be prepared to stand out a little if you're an out of towner. It does get a little shifty after dark but then so does 80% of NYC. Overall, I enjoyed staying here and would recommend it to anyone.

Good host. I never met her, but she communicated well, and the place really is clean. Be wary of the fact that it’s in East New York, if you’re someone who’s easily scared by 2017’s crime statistics. I didn’t have any problems but google definitely had me scared to go outside.

The area was a little scary at first but i enjoyed my stay better than i expected. It was very quiet and so close to the train which was amazing ! Also the place is very clean  and spotless . I enjoyed my stay. I wish it had a window but hey it’s amazing for the price !

Overall it’s a good place for a great price. Great for just needing somewhere to crash pretty much and not anything too fancy or expensive. The area is a little sketchy, but for most of my stay I was fine personally.

Location: Good connection to the metro (as Peter also writes); right next to a church, which sometimes plays very loud music until late into the night; We felt the environment was partly unsafe.  Apartment: very spacious, kitchen a bit poorly equipped - but sufficient; Printed out information about NYC including sightseeing tips were on the kitchen table when we arrived (we thought it was great).  House rules: should be reconsidered, especially volume.  We thank Peter for the good hosting! It's a shame that we didn't get to know him until we left - that's actually what Air BnB is all about... direct contact with locals. :)

Beautiful place! Super clean and practical, fast and kind communication with Peter, and 5 minutes from the A train. The immediate neighbourhood can seem sketchy at first glance but it is very safe. There is some City noise around, but it‘s the little down side of being close to everything: for us it was part of the experience!

Laura continues to be my favorite AirBnB host. This is my second stay and she's so lovely. Her apartment is beautiful and spotless. I didn't mention it last time but the window shade is blackout so it's perfect for a light sleeper like me. Laura is the best! Book now!
Peter's home is 7 minute walk from the AC line, the neighborhood is run down but we never felt unsafe. The home was spacious and clean.

The room at Deniz's place is excellent. Deniz and his housemate, Jear, were really helpful arranging my check-in. Although I got in pretty late, fresh off the boat, Jear was waiting to let me in, show me around and recommend some local hostelries where I could get a late beer and attack the jet lag. Very friendly and kind. The apartment is very clean, tidy and cosy and in a perfect location if you are looking to explore the LES. Would highly recommend and would like the opportunity to stay for longer next time. Thanks for having me.

This place is absolutely STUNNING! I was so pleasantly surprised by the location/neighborhood (felt super safe), apartment and room. The artwork in the place is quite something. I am by no means an art aficionado, but it's quite obvious he is a collector of very special things. I want to Coogan's right around the corner and loved the local vibe. The most stressful thing about the stay was parking, but Richard was super helpful and sent me the locations of a couple lots. I got very lucky though and found a space on 171st, where my car was safe for 2 nights. I didn't spend much time in the apartment, but the amenities are there if you want to cook or store food in the fridge. The resident family is very sweet and quiet. I would absolutely stay here again!

I did a shared room in the basement and it was terrible. I wasn’t able to stay the night there. Because the beds inside the rooms #3 and #2 were broken and be held up with tape! It was completely unsafe and unstable. I would not recommend anyone to stay here! I was completely out rage and disappointed.
Good value, easy location, stress free!

Personally there were too many people outside of the guest who had access to the apartment. Someone went into my closed room and stole my wireless earbuds, not sure if it was another guest or owner. The people upstairs were entirely too loud and the fact that there was loud music and people running around above my bed while I was trying to sleep was unpleasant. It should be in the description that I will be dealing excess noise from the above tenants.
Great stay for a great price. Bed frame was a little sketchy but in all it was a good experience.

Tonisha welcomed me she is friendly and the place is clean but (its far away from the city 1 hr & half  by subway and the area not safe at all its scary to go outside after 9pm also the neighborhood staring  NOT RECOMMEND AT ALL.. So i didn’t complete my stay  I asked her  through message to do a favor for me  if applicable to refund me half of my payment but she didn’t reply.

The apartment is pretty much as described as to location (save that it is at 249 Eldridge Street not 269 Eldridge Street as stated on the site-269 does not exist-see further below). It is very close to the West corner of Eldridge and Houston and, as Houston is a very busy two way crosstown street, there is a lot of traffic noise late into the night and from early in the morning. This may or may not bother you. It was clean and laid out as described. It is a 5 flight walk up, so be prepared for that.  The main reason for the modest star rating is twofold. First, after having committed to the letting, the managing agents will ask to you lie about the length of your stay (to say at least a month) if challenged by any residents of the building. This may have accounted for a certain hostility we experienced in passing, with obviously British accents, from residents of the building. It is difficult to imagine that this, plus the misdescription of the address on the site, are for any reason other than trying to cover up a letting situation which is at odds with the wishes of the residents of the building, and which is, perhaps, unauthorised under the building lease. Again this may or may not trouble you: it troubled us.  Second, the agent's communication and level of involvement are problematic. This is not a personal let by a person called ‘Ali’ as the ad suggests ('Ali's place'); we never came face to face with anyone during our stay. ‘Ali' works for Renaissance Properties who seem to manage the property on behalf of someone unknown. Although ‘Renaissance Properties’ is listed as having an office in New York (220 W 57th Street), the communications  we had seemed to be with individuals at head office, which is in Philadelphia.  Email communication was patchy and, at times, careless. Having given our ETA at the flat as likely around 10.00pm a few days previously, we landed at 8pm, to receive a message that said the Renaissance Properties' phones would be 'off between 8-10.30pm'. This was not welcome news after an 8 hour flight and we tried to make contact to repeat that we would be arriving at the flat very shortly. There was a reply and we were buzzed into the flat by persons unknown: again, we never had face to face contact with anyone involved with this listing, and this confusion over our arrival time was never addressed.  On arrival, things that a local owner would have identified and fixed were not done: the coffee machine was broken and needed replacing; the ironing board was broken and unusable (in fairness these were replaced swiftly once we drew attention to them); many of the wardrobe doors were non-closing or stuck in use rendering one of the two cupboards for storing clothes in the flat largely unusable as the broken door is propped up inside it; some of the towels were badly stained. All indications of limited presence or absence of on the ground owner/agents.  Similarly, a request to leave 4 cases in the apartment for 4 hours after official checkout was refused, ostensibly on the basis that the apartment had an immediately following letting, but it was still advertised as available on AirBnB.  The suggestion that a luggage store over 40 blocks (2.7 miles) North was a sensible solution indicates a certain lack of local knowledge or an unwillingness to be flexible with left luggage, which none of the four of us, in extensive use of Airbnbs in the past, had ever had any problems with.  All in all we felt that the letting situation was shady and confusing. For us, it was not a nice enough flat to compensate for the general sense that we weren't supposed to be staying there and that the letting agents were distant, not just about the address of the flat itself, but about it's condition in general. In conclusion, if the noise, absentee ownership/management and the request to lie would cause you concern, we would advise staying somewhere else.

I stayed for 11 nights during a conference and some extra days. Viviana and her family were really nice and welcoming. Her parent's English is limited, but we could communicate. The room was as advertised, very clean and neat. I was even allowed to wash a load of laundry, but that was not in the advertisement and should be therefore not be seen as a given in the future, the same as a few excellent meals I was invited to. The size of the bed is standard and was just enough for me, but if you are taller than 1.90 m (6' 2) you won't be able to sleep stretched out. Speaking as a naive, male European, I never felt unsafe in the neighborhood. Everything you could want is available and a subway station with good connections is only a couple of houses down the street. All in all I had a very nice stay and would definitely come back.

I really enjoyed relaxing in the apartment and I tried a bunch of the places around, like Kung Fu Tea and some takeout places. It was nice and quiet at night which I appreciated.   I also liked that it was right beside the Grand St. subway station and that the street was lit since I was staying by myself. I never really felt unsafe or anything (just stay aware of your surroundings if you’re walking at night, but that’s everywhere in New York).   The apartment had good wifi which was great for my work and zoom calls. It’s a bit of a hike to the rest of the city if you’re not used to long commutes. I had a great time!

This place is simply amazing..Simon and Stacy are great hosts. It was an easy checkin. The room was clean and comfortable. I was pleasantly surprised by the cute welcome note and the yummy snacks...The place is close to the train station and is a 40 min ride to Times Square. As it is in a very quiet neighborhood, even a little bit noise could be disturbing. So, for those of you who are light sleepers...do not forget to carry a pair of ear plugs. This place is value for money, a real steal and I absolutely loved it. Will  recommend it to anyone planning to visit NY.

DO NOT BOOK THIS SPACE!!!! DO NOT BOOK THIS SPACE!!!! DO NOT BOOK THIS SPACE!!!! DO NOT BOOK THIS SPACE!!!! DO NOT BOOK THIS SPACE!!!!  The address listed is completely incorrect, it is the home of an elderly woman. The host does not respond to messages, the number listed is out of service, and I have not yet received a refund even though I expressed that I could not check into a place that could not be found. PLEASE DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME OR MONEY, it’s a scam!

Steven is a very accommodating host; check in and check out time was very flexible. Everything described is accurate but a few details were left out/left for assumption.  -It is on the first floor and the windows face the street side so anyone walking by can look in if the curtains were open. However, not many do, so you're okay.  -the neighborhood looks a bit shady but it is only a few minutes away from the center of downtown Brooklyn. A 15-30 minute walk can get you to a lot of places around the area! -there is no AC as of now, so the studio was a bit stifling -understandably it is a new studio, but there are still remnants of paint flakes and chips on the floor + a few dishes in the sink and trash in a bag Overall, it works well for a one night stay, but I think it would be amazing once it has been lived in and cleaned up a bit :)

The host is extremely helpful and kind, dropped me off to my next location as well since I was scared to leave alone at night. I’m happy that I made a wonderful friend in the big city! Location is amazing, lot of great eats and near public transport and big stores. Don’t be surprised when you see your room being a living room enclosed by curtains! I was surprised at first but it ended up being very homely and I could peacefully do my work. I wish I had to the time to explore the vast amount of Xbox games he owns.  Everyone I met in the household was lovely. There are 2 rooms, one for the host and one for the other guest, and you will be in the living room. Kitchen is good for basic cooking, like noodles or coffee but don’t expect to cook any extravagant dishes (you won’t want to anyways, there’s so much to eat nearby!)  Overall, a great experience for a cheap price, will definitely come back again!

The apartment was cute and clean. The location wasn’t what we expected though... a 10 min drive to the metro and the neighborhood was kinda sketchy. But the host responded quickly to any questions and it was an easy check in process! Also, parking was easy to find on the street. Loved the heat/AC in both rooms.

Nini was very responsive and the apartment is so beautiful. Unfortunately coronavirus meant I had to leave the booking early due to travel restrictions being enforced globally. Nini was extremely understanding and flexible with my plans as this all unfolded during my stay in an unprecedented and stressful global time air B and B and my host Nini made everything a little bit easier and less stressful to navigate the crisis while travelling alone. I will absolutely be back to finish my trip and stay with Nini again when this is all over!!
Extremely dangerous neighborhood. Full of gangs.   The truth is I had to go somewhere else the day after I arrived.
Kyle”s place was lovely.. We had a stress free, enjoyable stay. I was wary about NYC but Kyle place put my fears to rest. Kyle is a thoughtful and considerate host.

Overall, I enjoyed my 3 months longterm stay here. Anna and Vittorio are both friendly and responsive, the apartment is clean (and gets cleaned approximately once a week), the room is spacious, and the interior makes you feel like you are living in New York. The apartment is situated very close to the subway and in walking distance to various restaurants and super markets. However, I wouldn't recommend staying in East Harlem, if you are not used to people looking/acting different than yourself. I didn't feel unsafe there, but one of my roommates moved out early because of the neighborhood. Also, I wouldn't recommend staying there if you are a morning person, because the floor is very squeaky. I was told to be careful with the floor, so I had to be sneaking around.

I stayed at Ali’s for nearly a month. There was excellent security, with 3 pass code entries required to access my room. The room was beautifully designed with remote controlled heat and a flat screen TV. There was plenty of closet space and a big kitchen shared among 3 suites.  The location is somewhat suburban, but there is a laundromat across the street and a big bodega next door. There aren’t a lot of larger markets or takeout options, though, but the Q65 goes straight to downtown Flushing, and you can walk there in 20-25 minutes. The neighborhood is generally quiet and I was never afraid of walking late at night.  There were a few noisy guests, but Ali was able to help out. She returned my messages in a prompt manner and found me another room when my floor was booked up for a holiday. The noise policy does need to be enforced.  I would certainly recommend staying here for a secure, attractive, and usually quiet environment.

We were really excited to stay at Bismillah place but the day that we were suppose to check-in I realized I hadn't received any check-in instructions. I immediately reached out to Bismillah to retrieve this information early that morning. My friends and I had a 5pm flight and Bismillah finally responded back to me about 3hrs before our flight took off. Things got weird when Bishmillah notified me that he was willing to pick us from the airport and take us to another location ( No explanation to why we weren't staying in the place we paid for).  I immediately called Bismillah and he explained their was no electricity at his place. When I tried to probe him with more questions about where this new location would be and basic details about the rooms etc he told me he would get back to me and send this information to me in a text. The entire situation sounded very sketchy and for the safety of everyone in my group I asked Bismillah to cancel this reservation because it was not ready for guests. Bismillah stated he was a work and that he had no problem cancelling. I ended up contacting Airbnb customer service because I didn't want to leave it up to the host seeing how everything else turned out. Luckily my group was able to find another place to stay before our flight took off but it would have been nice if Bismillah would have been more considerate to others. Imagine if I didn't reach out to Bismillah that morning we wouldn't have heard from him and possibly wouldn't have a place to stay during our trip.   My advice to Bismillah would be if you know you are having issues  with your place out of respect please try and give your guest advance notice. Also, offering guest to stay at an off-site location that is not listed on your profile is just bad business (insurance and safety concerns) . Guests have the right to know where they would possibly be laying their heads during their trips.

Myself and four buddies stayed at Bismillah's place for a weekend. From the outside the spot looks suspect but once you get inside it has everything you need. 4 comfortable bedrooms, AC, flatscreen tv, a comfortable common area/living room and kitchen. It's literally 2 blocks from the Subway and there are plenty of convenient eating choices. 2 of the rooms face the railroad tracks so if you're a light sleeper choose the rooms on the opposite side. It's nothing fancy but it's a great value for a short stay in Brooklyn. The place is pretty much as advertised.
Great cool and clean space with good locks. Neighborhood was a bit sketchy.

if you are looking to stay right smack in the middle of Brooklyn than this is for you. 1 block away from the 3 station, on a nice street and part of Crown Heights this place is a steal. Any issues I had they were on top of it, very quick response times and willing to help. I would highly recommend this place

The place is very clean, the house always smells delicious and everything is organized! Alan is a very good host and the room is comfortable and bright. It has everything you need. The shared bathroom is always kept very clean. The sector may seem a little unsafe, however, that's okay, we walked until very late at night and there were no problems. It is a great place to stay as it is close to everything.

Very nice place! My son lives nearby so location was perfect. Mixture of cultures in the neighborhood that made me feel safe. Very walkable and didn’t feel afraid—families, joggers, etc. near children’s museum and Brooklyn Museum.  The apartment is cute and has everything you need for your stay, including coffee and fixings (like half and half and oat milk!) Nicely renovated and extremely enjoyable. Communication and instructions were very good and thorough. Would definitely stay there again.

If you need to be in Crown Heights for shabbat or an event, this is a good location.  Otherwise, it can feel a bit isolated. The apartment is a basement unit so it's not very bright and can feel a bit claustrophobic if you just want to chill out during the day (LR is only room with windows; and they are basement windows so you can look out. It's one long unit, with the LR in front, then bedroom, then kitchen, then bathroom. The kitchen had a weird and unpleasant smell. I couldn't tell if it was something old in the fridge (there were condiments in the fridge door) or what, but I definitely didn't want to leave the kitchen door open due to the smell.  Soleil was very nice and very responsive when there was an issue with the unit (plumbing got overwhelmed in a rainstorm) and they immediately issued a refund when I had to move out due to that issue.  This would be a good place for a family to share it would be budget friendly and has a full kitchen.  For me as a single person it didn't really make sense for me to pay for all that space just to sleep.  Oh, and the sleeping was great.  Very quiet, soft bed, nice dark bedroom.

We very much enjoyed our stay in this apartment in Crown Heights and will stay again. Conveniently located,  it's a few blocks from Brower Park, a park full of people having fun, playing basketball,  playing with their dogs and sitting in the shade playing chess, cards and socializing. It's close to a supermarket and a drugstore. It's walkable to the subway stops on Eastern Parkway to the south and Atlantic Ave to the north with easy access to Manhattan.   It's very comfortable, with a private entrance, a modern bathroom (great walk-in shower) and a modern kitchen with new appliances. The bedroom is spacious with lots of storage, closet, and a very comfortable bed. There is 5g wifi  and a large screen tv in the living room.
Practical place to stay in order to explore the city. I was afraid it would be cold in the winter due to it being a basement flat, but it had central heating. Comfortable beds and amenities.

It was our first experience with Airbnb and I was pleasantly suprised. Apartman is very clean. You don't need to afraid of dog - she is very friendly. Thanks to Brooke and Elias for opportunity to stay there and Rebecca for her help with communication. Also thanks to cleaning woman for friendlines. You are great team! I recommend this apartman to everyone, who visits NY.
Perfect Apart from the bed which makes noise We were afraid of the noise from the street but we heard nothing. Brooks and his animals are adorable.
Quiet place and living area. Perfect after spending the day in stressful Manhattan or Brooklyn.

This is a great location. Right in the center of bedstuy and next door to the train. If you come to New York for work I would suggest buying ear plugs before your stay. The building is noisy and you can hear the train and pedestrians outside.  There is a really cool rooftop.   Other than that the host has a cat and isn’t always home to change the litter on time, so that will cause a smell. I was unfamiliar with cats so the litter box smell was unpleasant. The host does not provide clean linens or towels during your stay after he gives you your first set. Other hosts give you clean sheets biweekly and towels if you stay for a month or more...  Overall the stay was convenient.

My boyfriend and I stayed at Shuly's for a week vacation to see the sights of New York. Location was very convenient to the end of the N subway to go to either downtown Manhattan or Flushings which were our goals. It was just a nice walk down a street with a bunch of stores to the subway, including the Brooklyn Coffee and Bagel company which we had almost every morning. And walking back from the subway at night was really nice and not scary at all. Access to our booking was super convenient and we felt very comfortable with our stay.

It's in a good position and the host is friendly. I was unsure if the bed was cleaned, which was a major problem to me. I was also told not to mention Airbnb to anyone living there. I didn't feel unsafe, but that was uncomfortable.

I had a great time at Stella's! The room is simple but more than sufficient for a single traveler. The little touches left in the room made me very happy. In addition, Stella is very accommodating, my flight having been delayed, I was still able to access the room without problem.

Nothing i can complain about the place. Let me tell you why: 1. The place is SUPER CLEAN 2. Stella is really nice and sweet though we just met on the first day of my stay there. But she is clearly very accommodating. 3. Her house is so pretty, especial a little patio in back of the house and my room smelled sooooo nice!!  4. The house is indeed located in Bronx, but by the moment you get off from the subway, you will never feel unsafe, it’s a pretty, quite and peaceful neighborhood  5. The room has its own iron, iron board, tv, and refrigerator  6. The bed is so comfy, i had a hard time to get up and go to work every morning.  This definitely one pf my best experience in airbnb in NYC, and I’ve been in lots of airbnb in the city.

Amazing place to stay in New York City! Stella is such a kind and accommodating guest. I had a lot of privacy and was able to come and go as I pleased (always being considerate of quiet hours). As a man, I never felt unsafe in the house or the neighbourhood. Overall, great airbnb, would definitely recommend and repeat!

Such a cute and cozy stay! I loved all the added extras like bathroom supplies in case you forgot something or ran out (soaps, pain reliever, after shave, etc). Oh and the beer tap is such a cool touch!! The listing and pictures are accurate, besides I personally didn’t see the skyline view but I wasn’t going out of my way to look so I might be wrong. The walk to the back of the house looks a bit sketchy especially at night but it’s not bad. The walkway was lit up which was good! It seems to be in a nice quiet neighborhood too. I’d stay again
A great listing. Quite the steal

M was a great host. They responded quickly to our question, and gave a very detailed check-in procedure which was very helpful. The space itself is very nice,  awesome water pressure in the shower, drinks on tap, clean, quiet, and comfortable. The surrounding area seems sketchy by appearance, but we never felt unsafe being there at all. The house is on a dead-end block with like 4 other houses so a very low-traffic, quiet street. We really enjoyed our night there and would stay again.

There are a lot of electrical wires in the way to access the Airbnb accommodation: super dangerous!!! And in the 2 bedrooms the fire/smoke/gas detectors were out of service: super mega dangerous and completely illegal!!!!!!!  The shower was unusable because the hose connected to the shower head was coming out of the ceiling (???), which was not normal, and as a result the shower head was pointing in the wrong direction and therefore the water jet could not be directed in the right way and we could not shower, plus the shower curtain was covered in mold: horrible and disgusting. In short, we didn't manage to shower.  The whole apartment was dirty, and there was a horrible smell floating around (mold smell maybe???).  In short, it was truly a horrible place!!!! In addition, the apartment being in the basement, and being very poorly insulated, we could hear all the noise made by the owners of the house above our heads until very late in the evening (knowing that we arrived very late on the first evening, around 11:30 p.m.). Impossible to sleep. The neighborhood was also very disreputable, we didn't feel safe at all. Very noisy too.  Anyway, after a horrible first night and a horrible morning where we couldn't even sleep properly or shower, we left and took a hotel for the rest of the stay.

I can’t say nothing more, than we had a great time at Beni’s apartment.   All rooms were clean, and apartment was very well equipped.  Neighbourhood is safe. We spend there 8 days, and never felt unsafe at any time.  Well communication . Bus station is next to apartment, and bus drive is 10 minutes to ferry station.  I can strongly reccomended to everyone who want to spent nice time in NY, and not burn all money on apartments at Manhattan or Brooklyn :)

The apartment is conveniently equipped with everything you need. The beds are queen size and we found both comfortable- For us it was perfect that one was a little harder than the other, so we could choose the right one for us.  In the kitchen there is no microwave, this might be interesting for some.And within the house you can really hear everything (like someone walking upstairs or talking in the other apartment), which could be an issue for noise-sensitive people. And of course you can also hear the traffic from the street.   Besides some spots the apartment was clean and Beni promised that he'll take care of these spots.The location is not the nicest on Staten Island but we never felt unsafe. It is a little dirty outside and on the streets, which doesn't really make it look nice.   But it is really perfect that the bus stop is just right in front of the house and it takes only 10 minutes to get to the ferry station. In the first mornings we even walked down, which takes about 15-20 minutes.   Beni is always very helpful and caring, so this was a big plus because we could ask about parking, heating and anything else that popped up and he answered very quickly.We pointed some minor issues out to him and he already is taking care of those, so this should all be fine.  A little Deli is on the other side, so buying things like water or snacks is easy. A Pizza Take-away is right next door, pizza was ok for the first evening. On the way to the ferry station is a supermarket so we could buy needed stuff not too far away. About 20 minutes by bus you can find the Staten Island Diner which was perfect for us for breakfast.
Overall my family and I had a great time. The location was near everything which was great. The only thing was that the hallways had an unpleasant smelled, as well as the restroom.

Beni was a great host! Super responsive. The neighborhood is ok. It was very busy and loud but we never felt unsafe and there was a bus stop literally right outside the front door which was really great. We needed a place that could get us to Brooklyn easily to see family as well as the city and this was perfect. We got over the bridge and into Bay Ridge in like 25 minutes so that was great. We also were able to catch the bus and get to the ferry in a timely fashion so we could get to Manhattan in like 30/45 minutes (if you time it right!) There was parking on the street behind the place so we could leave our car most of the time which was really nice.  The only thing I can say is that there could have been more towels and toilet paper/paper towels but I’m sure Beni would have brought some over if I had asked. We just stole some from family. Lol!

Based on the pictures, and the comments we were expecting to stay in a nice clean appartement. Unfortunately it was a total disappointment. The place is filthy.  First of all, the main door barely locks and the chain on the door is broken. The bathroom was ok until I opened the cupboard under the sink to discover random items, an old hairbrush, used toothpaste, a bottle of Listerine, and the cupboard hadn’t been cleaned in a while. There were suspicious brown stains on the wall next to the toilet too… The kitchen is dirty. Grease stains all around the cooker, and on the extractor. The freezer is a block of ice, and again the cupboard under the sink is filthy.  The living area is bearable, but the bed area is stuck against a dirty wall with flaky paint and stains. And there are crumbs/skin flakes (?) under the mattress. There  were cobwebs on the ceiling.  Overall this place is a huge disappointment despite its great location in the city. I had to cancel the reservation the first night and escape to a hotel as I felt uneasy and unsafe staying there.  Avoid at all cost.

It is a place good for homeless. We found the fridge floading water down the floor, the place was in need of housekeeping more over the bedroom was without window front the street and was fullfilled by unhealty car smog. We remained there just 1 night and then we had to ask an other hotel provider for an hotel that costed less. I wonder if this is the service level offered by airb&b I wont use it anymore

The only good thing about this Airbnb was the location in regards to proximity to NYC nightlife bars, restaurants, cafes, and subway. Other than that, it was extremely cold, noisy, and uncomfortable. There’s a crack in the window which the AC is installed so we had to wear a sweater and jacket to keep warm when we slept. I actually left after the second night crashing on a couch of a friend of a friend in Queens while my husband roughed it. You can hear all the noise if anyone is walking by outside the window which is next to the bed. There’s a metal sidewalk cellar door that makes a loud sound anytime someone walks by. Across the street is Tompkins Square park which is home for a lot of homeless. It didn’t feel like a safe block.  It’s a small studio which would be perfect for someone who wanted to be in the heart of the east village and mainly used the place just to sleep if you’re out and about most of the day. Definitely should’ve booked a hotel instead!!Host offered an extra night
Very disappointed with the accommodation. No kitchen and rude host

Allie’s place is a cozy clean spot that worked great for our family. My husband and son were able to simultaneously work and learn remotely without any connection issues. The roof access was nice for us to have breakfast before the sun got, too hot.  One of the major pluses to Allie’s place that is not common in NYC is the CENTRAL AIR!! We recently left NYC after 8 years and are very familiar with parking uptown. There is a garage close by that if you are not used  to finding parking I would suggest you use to avoid any unnecessary stress.   Allie’s place is well curated and definitely a prime location for someone wanting a NYC feel and easy public transit options. The A,C,D and B are all at the end of the block from the apartment. You would not need a car at all. We would absolutely stay here again.

All the packages are located in one giant cage in the lobby, and during my stay I have seen packages that are damaged or stolen. The area feels a little unsafe to walk alone at night. There were also many bugs in the bathroom.

Good location in Astoria Heights.   Host was accommodating to  early checkin request and communicative.  Place is situated in a nice quiet neighborhood.   Waking distance to an Italian restaurant; Table 21 is a nice place to have dinner, the food and service was great.   Walking into the house music was playing by Alexa which was nice.    It ends there.  We immediately notice the unpleasant smell of weed  lingering in the place.  Glades plug-ins we’re not enough to mask that smell.   It was enough to bother me and my family.    I can’t stand the smell of it and that was a turn off from the start.  I guess it’s the new norm nowadays and it’s everywhere NY.     We were unable to access the internet until the next day in the afternoon do to password being incorrect on the Airbnb app.    After a couple of  attempts with the host in concern with connectivity, it was finally  corrected  when host sent a screenshot of the password and I realized the password  did not match what the host had listed on the Airbnb app.   It was frustrating not being able to have access to internet.   I addressed my concerns about the uncleanliness of the place.    Unable to take a shower immediately after arriving  do to the tub being dirty.  The shower mat was  moldy and smelly ended up rolling it and on Ave it under the sink. The tub had soap scum stuck to the porcelain surface which I had to  spray and let Clorox cleaner product soak before scrubbing it off myself.  The two bath mats were also  dirty.   I ended up rolling them up also and setting them aside as well.   I address it immediately to the host.  Host replied he did his best since I request an early check in.    If a place can NOT  be delivered  properly cleaned to accommodate early checkin requests, it’s best NOT to accept the request just to get the place booked.  It will  backfire.  I could have keep search for other locations.    Then noticed the floor was dirty as well with hair on the floor.   Nothing was done about the situation of the tub or mat , so I just let it go.  Went about my business.     Towels  were of very low quality.  When I came in contact with a towel, I had lint  all over my attire.     Bed sheets felt like sleeping on paper.   Pillows were very uncomfortable to sleep on.   The carpets in the bedroom were dusty underneath the bed and behind furniture.  Not sure if the carpets were even vacuumed.  The amount of dust in the carpet trigger an asthma attack, to the point I became miserable and did not want to stay another night.  In the kitchen, upon arrival I notice an open Pepsi bottle with a small amount of soda still left in the bottle left on the kitchen counter.   Microwave was dirty.  In the kitchen in place of a paper towel in the paper towel holder there was a Toilet paper Roll instead.   Not sure why.   In New York seeing a roach crawling in the kitchen is completely inevitable, it’s bound to happen.  I informed the host after the fact only so that the host was aware and  out of courtesy to prevent them from multiply.   There is a camera in inside of the apartment which it’s not ok with me.   The camera by the window ledge is facing the outside but it’s in the inside of the apartment.   I have the same type of camera back at home  and I know how it works.       Cameras placed outside of apartment, I have no issues  with but INSIDE the apartment I do.   That is  a violation of privacy to a guest.    Apparently, You can’t have all air conditioning units running at the same time.  I did lower the temperature to 69 degrees which  apparently caused the breakers to trip.  Power  went out on the entire 2nd FL because of this.   That was a FIRST for me, when I’ve been able do so in different Airbnb located in Queens before without any issues.  I was unaware that would happen; had I seen a notice  that it could not handle such power, I would have been more cautious. This happened  Shortly before 6pm On the first day.  Host was not able to come until after work which was around 9pm to resolve the outage on the 2nd  Fl.  were the bedrooms are at. We then decided to suddenly leave the place and wait at a near by restaurant.  Host did arrive earlier and I was very appreciative about it.    When I addressed these concerns with the host I was not interested in giving a  negative review.      Until After the host replies became defensive and unprofessional.   Copy and pasting below one  of HOST responses.    “when I and the electrician were there the night you asked for assistance there was food on the table out in the open and a open bag of chips and crumbs scattered now I'm not going to blame the insect/ roach issue on you but when we fixed the electricity the acs were turned to the max which logically means you knew you could blow the sockets and there's was food out that's why I didn't try to micromanage your stay and let you enjoy ourself since you probablv didn't know the acs were too high and that you shouldn't leave food out in the open”  Maybe this is not  the right business for the host if they can’t handle criticism or complaints from a guest without feel the need to lash back.    Host needs experience in hospitality.   Place needs deep cleaning.   Better quality Towels, bedsheets and pillows.  Not allow anyone smoke weed or any substance inside the house that can linger on the walls or surfaces.  Camera should be Placed outside of property not inside the premises.     Host needs etiquete on how to reply to concerns that are addressed by Guests without becoming defensive.    I’ve had better experiences staying

I had to clean the bathroom, bathtub had hair ,blood & dirty in it . Clean sink and toilet, rugs were dirty and stained.  Heat er in bathroom would make a loud banging noise around 4:00am.  Tv wasn’t available to watch in the of the guess bathroom with no cords.   The stair railing upstairs were missing poles where a child or someone could fall down the stairs.   It was about 10 steep stairs when holding on the rails going up or down it also was missing poles to whole up structure.  It was very unstable where you could not rely on for support!  Very scary!   The down stairs floors haven’t been mopped in quite sometime!  Very dusty everywhere, no lightbulbs in lamps.  We found roaches.   The kitchen counter tops and island was very dirty.  Pots were dirty with water sitting in them with food.    There was food and milk in the refrigerator & it was completely dirty! There was Trash already in the trash can in the kitchen.  I had to clean this unsafe house before  settling in.
Sketchy neighborhood but great value and close to subway station

The listing is accurate with pictures. We had a problem with the AC in one of the rooms and the host came and fixed it for us.
