Did not have paper towels and only 3 rolls of toilet paper for 10 people for 5 nights and neighborhood felt slightly unsafe. Otherwise very clean airbnb and good communication with host when needed.

Everything about the house was good but we did have an issue the first night with the upstairs neighbors making a lot of noise around 2 in the morning but otherwise everything inside the house was good. The location of the house is in a bit unsafe location.

It really didn't meet my expectations, the sector is dangerous, they never picked up the trash, few towels for the number of people we were, there wasn't even a mirror in three rooms or a table, we had to put everything on the floor like beggars, so it's not worth it, we're tourists, it's not worth what was charged, we were not satisfied at all, we felt cheated, he never called us 😭

BE CAUTIOUS!  He disappeared into the night before I can even say goodbye. I Never saw the place. Was spoken to in foul language after standing in a hallway, waited two hours for him to even get back and I notified him the key was wrong 3 minutes into my arrival so I’m pretty sure he couldn’t have gone that far , he only showed urgency when i .. contacted BNB 6 times.  I know it was sketchy when  he wasn’t concerned to get the key he gave me back. It took everything to keep my composure and patience while listening to him speak to me like I didn’t just pay my hard earned money WHICH I NEVER GOT BACK AIR BNB

The place was okay but the carbon monoxide was going off and the bad part is that I have a small kid that is dangerous and was waking her up and whoever is living there I couldn’t even go food shopping because things was left in the fridge and freezer dirty washcloth and towels was left for me to use they was Absolutely no space for me to use anything or store it during my stay last minute communication for me to check out early for the host to clean the apartment for the next guest not good at all one finally one broken A/C in the main room they have a laundry room located on the basement level but all the washers and dryers was broken
Joseph’s property is incredibly safe and secure to stay in. With everything you’d need to have an enjoyable time without stress. I’d definitely stay here again if I need to.

The apartment itself was ok, even if it wasn't very clean and everything was very unpromisingly furnished (cheap bed frame simply placed in old broken bed frame). The beds were also super uncomfortable.  But the location of the apartment was the worst. The area where the apartment is located is full of trash and homeless people and stinks. We were so afraid of walking around that we always had to take a tub to get from the subway station to the Airbnb. We felt absolutely uncomfortable and were just counting the days until we could walk again. Definitely not recommended! Especially not for women and families.

Here’s the thing… if you are not staying out late or will be using cab/Uber then it’s fine. It’s a dangerous location after dark so if you’ll be using the subway/walking after dark then it’s a NO.  All the furniture is literally falling  apart!!! It’s very hot at night, the AC does not work, there’s no place to put your suitcase, and the bathroom was not very clean. It was me, my husband, and my mom… we made it work, but we paid about $800 and just with that money the host could replace his falling apart ikea furniture.  The apt gets you quick access to a bunch of stuff and since I’ve lived in NY before moving south staying in town helped get faster access to the touristy places.  Sadly the host blamed us for scratching his dishwasher which was SO ABSURD to me to even hear that!! I’ve never had that kind of issue and was astounded, but I’ve told him I refuse to own responsibility of something I’ve not done, so many things wrong with the place but we did not complain to him.

Lina’s place was very clean. Had plenty of rooms and towels available. The driveway was private and gated which was nice considering the area around it was very unsafe. The house was a welcoming bubble in that area and we really appreciated our stay. Very close to the Metro, made travel easy. Check in and check out were very easy! Communication with Lina was great!!

The room is very nice and the location is just perfect. There was only one issue, the door of the apartment didn't lock. Not even the other guests were able to close it, because the locker was old and broken. Nobody came to have a look while we were there so it was a bit scary. Maybe you can ask about if you want to reserve the place. The rest of the apartment is really good.
The place was great, very spacious and great communication! I came pretty late and and then area was a little sketchy. Still a great place to book!
A bit of noise (someone arguing) at 3a.  I’m not fond of fabreeze air freshener so that was unpleasant. Otherwise as listed.

Jose’s place is a rare find. Beautiful modern and upto date amenities, settled in a calm neighourhood and close to the subway. We had a peaceful stay here, had a very comfy bed, useful humidifier, huuuuge TV and the cherry on top, a massage chair. Its a steal and close drive to all the hip parts of Brooklyn.

Host: Stephen is a great host! He lives on the same property and was there to answer any questions we had and able to provide when we needed something. Every interaction with him was pleasant!   Space: Very spacious, 3 bedrooms and 2 baths on the second floor (master has a bath and the other two rooms share one bathroom) and another toilet on the first floor. The place is mostly as pictured/ described with just a few minor flaws:  1. There are no blinds or curtains in the main living area- keep that in mind if you  value privacy!   2. Occasional holes in ceilings and walls, fixtures and finishes of the rooms or the overall place were mediocre. We as a group felt like it was lacking 10%.   Neighborhood: Airbnb is located in Brooklyn, Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood. Which is known for its high crime rates and considered more “dangerous”. We were a group of 5 (guys and girls) and it is probably totally fine during the day but I would just not recommend a group of only women to stay here or walking around alone at night. Also, expect it to be really noisy. Police cars were patrolling almost every night (were very loud) and the neighbors were extremely inconsiderate (were playing loud speaker festival type music late into the night, 1-2am).   Accessibility: I would say it takes about 30-40 minutes by subway to get to Manhattan. Not bad but also not a quick ride. We would always just get ready in the mornings and left for the whole day. You’re probably not going to go back to your Airbnb to rest and then go back out if you have a tight schedule.   Groceries/ restaurants:   1. BKLYN Blend- Many people already mentioned this place but BKLYN Blend is right around the corner and is fantastic! Definitely worth checking out- all of their food is great and their coffee is decent as well!   2. Several markets that are just a couple blocks away. Our group’s favorite was Lincoln Market- it has basically everything you need (from groceries to contact lens solution) and is just within less than 5 minutes walking distance.   Overall, the place was just what we needed as a group of 5 and we made good use of Stephen’s cozy Airbnb. I recommend this place to larger groups and people who are cool with staying at a traditional brownstone house where you can occasionally feel and see the age of the house.

Let me start by saying, DONT BOOK THIS PLACE.  Neighborhood is insane. There was a drug dealer outside of the place literally selling out of his car. I’m from the Bronx so I’m not someone who isn’t used to the element but it was right outside the front door. Never mind the junkies who were also smocking rock right by the corner store. Thankfully dude wasn’t too shady n partially friendly.  Now onto the space, while charming DONT BOOK DURING THE SUMMER. HOST will harass you about the air conditioner where as there’s no AC on the first floor…it was like 90 degrees on average each day on the first floor. The two small fans do nothing to help with the heat in there. Upstairs hallway is also hot, the thermostat read 85 DAILY, of the three rooms the middle one has adequate air conditioning while the other two don’t. Then the shower in the master has a broken knob when using it so that’s no good along with them only supplying like 3 towels for the entire stay that are raggedy and need to be replaced. All in all it was a terrible experience and if it wasn’t so last notice I would’ve switched sooner. Never mind that Airbnb customer service is handling this poorly.  AVOID THIS GUY, he will harass you, message you AND have someone come upstairs to adjust your air.

Be prepared for the Brooklyn experience. No parking, very noisy,  it takes a long time to get hot water. Not a bad place to stay, we did notice someone came into the house when we were not there, (that was creepy).

Hello, this is the first time this has happened to me. You can go and see what kind of traveller I am, on my profile. At Arty we are welcomed by Maria, at the beginning we say it is like a hostel of Jeunnesse with these good day and bad. But let the emotions and value judgment, the facts: -The apartment does not match the photos on the site at all -It is mega messy -It is dirty but we see much worse in some countries -No record player -No awning -No locked room -No possibility to put down our luggage before the hour despite our request -Woke me up in the morning no more toilet paper anywhere and told me that the Amazon order had not arrived and that the other tenant had to take the roll. -Later I knock on the other tenant’s door to get to know her and the manager Maria texts me to ask me why I’m banging at the other tenant, that’s when I started to paranoid.  Are we observed by Camera -I’m going over the details on a lot of weird and unpleasant behavior The location is really good On top they have a whole apartment they rent and the girls who were there when we passed were happy, autonomous in the apartment.  But we at the bottom had a bad experience, but our trip to Brooklyn was very pleasant. It’s a shame but naked will not stay there anymore. We expect a better atmosphere when we pay $700 for three nights.  Bonjour, c'est la premiere fois que cela m'arrive. Vous pouvez aller voir quel genre de voyageur je suis, sur mon profil. Chez Arty on est acceuillis par Maria, au début on se dit c'est comme une auberge de Jeunnesse avec ces bon jour et les mauvais. Mais laissons les émotions et jugement de valeur, les faits : -L'appartement ne correspond pas du tout aux photos sur le site -Il est méga bordélique -Il est sale mais on voit bien pire dans certain pays -Pas de tourne disque -Pas de store -Pas de chambre qui ferme à clef -Aucune possibilité de poser nos bagages avant l'heure malgrés notre demande -Me reveille le matin plus aucun papier de toilette nulle part et me faire dire que la commande Amazon n'etait pas arrivé puis que l'autre locataire avait du prendre le rouleau.... -Plus tard Je tape à la porte de l'autre locataire pour faire connaissance et la responsable Maria me texte pour me demander pourquoi je tape chez l'autre locataire, c'est la que j'ai commencé à paranoier.  Sommes nous observé par Caméra -Je passe les détails sur plein de comportement bizarre et pas agréable. L'emplacement est vraiment bien Au dessus ils ont un logement entier qu'ils loue et les filles qui étaient là lors de notre passage etaient contente, autonome dans l'appart.  Mais nous en bas ce fût une mauvaise experience, mais notre trip dans Brooklyn fût agréable tout de méme. C'est dommage mais nus ne logerons plus là. On s'attend a mieux comme ambiance quand on paye $700 pour trois nuits.

The apartment was very nice and clean and the complimentary coffee and water were great. I really liked the apartment, only the creaking and noise of the floorboards on the upper floor woke me up every night. I can't say anything negative about the apartment, it is beautiful and everything new.  The only thing is that it is far from Manhattan and all the touristy things in NY. We had to make several subway transfers. And the bad thing was that at Christmas time the subway stopped working early. Unthinkable taxis.  That and the fact that from the apartment to the subway station is also scary, it was dirty and graffitied, and garbage all over that stretch of the avenue. You get off the subway and almost run to the apartment. On that stretch of street there are several cantinas, which I suppose is what attracts people who stay there lying around or smelly. I enjoyed my stay and my roommates, but we all agreed that the area was not very cool. Greetings!

The apartment was good. The check in process is complicated and we had to ask for help to do it, which was uncomfortable. The location is close to several subway stations, although we found the neighborhood a little unsafe, but we didn't have any problems there. Thank you Ivy and Ally for your help.

Spacious apartment, in an area which apparently is not very well frequented, but that is just appearance because at no time did we feel in danger, quite the contrary. The neighbors are a little noisy but after a day in Manhattan you hardly hear them anymore.

WOW!  What a great place to stay! Jack was SUPER helpful and very attentive.  This was our first trip to NYC with a family of 6.  This place felt like home quick!  The location was great (I thought maybe the “close to Broadway” was a scam - I was thinking the shows! - but everything you need is on Broadway!!!)  If we ever come back (a trip for 2 this time) I would totally stay here again!
Is extremely promising responding to us! The house is very clean in this place is honestly a steal
Great space. It is close to the train and bus. The price is great and the host is wonderful. A true steal in NYC!

The address was not shown until we paid and it is the same place as a local hotel that charges far less for the same location. However it appears the hotel and Julia are not the same people and the reviews on the hotel are not the same reviews I would give her place. There was no hassle for 120 dollars when I arrived, (although there were signs posted to collect it for the hotel guests) the room was beautiful and clean. The handle on the faucet came off, the hallways didn’t smell/look great; but I did feel safe. Something should be posted that renting her place is different than renting from the hotel to ease the minds of the renter. I did initially feel scammed to see others could rent from the hotel at 1/3 the price; but overall I was happy with the stay and what I paid. I cannot say I would feel the same if I had rented from the hotel on Expedia/Travelocity.  It was clean, a good location, the shower was hot, and the kitchen was useful.
The building itself was a little sketchy, but the room itself was perfect for a quick 2 night stay. The communal bathrooms were very convenient and well kept. Julia was also a great host!

We had a fantastic trip to New York staying here. Csj was a very responsive host with great communication throughout. The apartment was clean and spacious and acted as a great base for exploring as very close to the subway. Minor issues - we had to buy shampoo as there was only shower gel provided and at times the area could feel slightly unsafe as a tourist. But overall great value for money and would recommend for people wanting to explore Manhattan

Great location! So close to subway to get quite literally anywhere. Vibrant area, never felt unsafe. The pipes in the walls were very loud and kept me up most nights. The loft was maybe 6ft. high, which I’m 5’ 2” so I didn’t have a problem, but the boys definitely had to crouch when in the loft.  But the Airbnb was clean and perfect for what me and my friends needed. Plus, a great price for being IN the city!  I would definitely stay here again.

Not what I expected!  Let me start by saying that the Airbnb host is there during your stay.  I feel the host was deceptive. Her advertising of the accommodations was not clear.  Granted, in retrospect, I realized it said private room. Her pictures of the downstairs area made it appear as an entire private area not sharing a common space.   Also, in reviews, it mentions that the Airbnb is clean. Honestly, I may have a different standard of cleanliness.  I did not agree.  I was greeted with an unpleasant overwhelming odor of cat litter.  I have a cat but this was not pleasant. So if you are ok with all that then this may be the place for you.  It was not a good match.  We decided not to stay. This did ruin our birthday weekend.   Advice for the host please be more descriptive in your listing.

Suspected Semen-stained blanket was on the bed. I reported this to host at 8:30 PM and got response at 11:45 PM: "It did not get out on laundry. But you can use the laundry in the house again if you like with speed wash. If you want to change it, i think i have extra one." I didn't see host's response until morning, but this doesn't seem like the right answer. After seeing the blanket, I looked closer at sheets and found hair, odd crumbs or dirt, and other faint stains in sheets. I brought my own blanket, slept in my streetclothes, but was still too cold to fall asleep for longer than a few hours. Room is street level with big leaky window. It was 21 degrees outside, and even with the wall-mounted inverter heaters at their highest setting, it was still freezing in the room and common area.   Couch in common area was covered with towels, drying laundry, which made me not want to use the one provided.   The place has the potential to be really nice, but I get the sense that host has a bunch of units and doesn't have time to care about the experience each individual guest has.   Shower was refreshing, but water temp could warmer. Check-in & security are hi-tech and super-easy. Area not sketchy to me, just industrial.
Hot Water Problem 🚿 Poor Attitude after poor communication…but typical! Random Hipsters eating next to window 🪟 lol Creepy! I wouldn’t stay here again but I did fold the towels when I left!

Experience was okay.  I wish we had did more research about the area/location. The area/streets was dirty and there was homeless people down the streets. It wasn’t what we were expecting as this was the biggest issue for us as we had 3 kids with us.  Check-in was okay.  I had another family member check-in as my flight wasn’t coming in until later. Communicated with Henry about it but the keys weren’t put under her name as requested. Took awhile for her to check-in but eventually she did.  The place was small as we anticipated but with 8 people in our party, 3 being kids it turned out to be too be small. Showers had to be taken the nights before as there was only one (1) small bathroom. There was also only 3 toilet papers placed and we instantly knew we’d need more as we were staying 5 days with 8 people. Henry did accommodate 2 more, however the time to pick up was a little troublesome.  We were also only given hand towels and 8 very thin bath towels and no wash cloths.  There is also only 1 AC unit where the bunk beds were and none in the other room. So the 4 in that room ended up freezing as the other 4 were waiting more air. We’d also wake up with stuffy nose and congested. The beds were okay, however the bedsheets, comforter, and pillows were very thin and not comfortable. After long days of walking and sightseeing a nice bed would’ve been nice to sleep in to rejuvenate for the next day.  We also had a spider crawling on the bed the first night. We’ve all used Airbnb before and this by far was our least favorite experience. But then again if you don’t mind dirty streets, comfort, or have kids and don’t want to pay to much then this is it.

I would absolutely stay here again! Clean, stylish and cozy as advertised. My favorite feature was the in room air conditioning unit. Also there is a built in heater in the bathroom! Lots of ppl in and out but the cleaner comes every day.  Very close to L train (doesnt run on weekends) and other metro stations. Right next door to a cafe (still thinking about how delicious their $1.50 cup of coffee is) and market/gas station where they had, in my opinion, a very conscious selection of items like plant based breakfast sandwiches, premium clean beverages as well as any other staples youd need--including beer and seltzers.   Regarding the "roach" comments here, i did not experience anything unpleasant. It appears that if that was an issue, it has been resolved. I advise just making it a point to clean up after eating/snacking and you shouldnt have issues. This goes without saying for most but just in case-- leaving dirty plates / open food out is asking for trouble most anywhere you live!
The neighborhood was a little sketchy but everything else was fantastic. Very clean and comfortable, and there's a gas station right next to it in case you want to get snacks.

This Airbnb apartment is in a great location in Brooklyn. It’s on the first block off Flatbush Ave, the neighborhood’s major thoroughfare. The walk to the subway station is short and easy. From there it’s easy to travel into downtown Brooklyn and to take the Q train into any part of Manhattan. There are too many great, affordable restaurants along Flatbush Avenue in either direction from this apartment. The neighborhood’s makeup is heavily Caribbean, so the food, the accents you overhear, and the smiles all  feel fun and welcoming.   It wasn’t too hard to find street parking, so I parked at no cost – no small thing when talking about NYC lodging! Plus, because the apartment is just a little further out than many people look, it has a lower nightly price that makes it a total steal.   For being a garden apartment, it gets great light, even in winter. That’s largely because the buildings on the block are all only three stories, so they don’t block the sun. There are two large windows in the front and in the rear of the apartment.   The apartment includes a comfortable couch and chair, plenty of places to sit to eat or work, a kitchen that is in great shape and has even more than I needed during my 5-night stay.  The whole place was meticulously clean when I arrived late at night, and the self-check-in process was simple and smooth. There were more than enough clean towels, and everything in the bathroom was up to date and in great condition.   Fraulein’s communication before and during my stay was prompt and very helpful. She is an experienced host who knows how to provide a great stay while remaining unobtrusive.   10 out of 10, would absolutely stay again.

What a great apartment with rooftop terrace. We enjoyed some wine while our kids slept. The service was excellent with luggage store available prior to checkin after checkout which was a huge stress relief. I definitely recommend this for a family of 5 like ours.

This house is a decent option if you have a larger group and need a place to stay near JFK and don't want to pay for multiple hotel rooms. It's about a 10 minute drive from JFK depending on traffic. We came in off a late international flight, spent the night, and took another flight out the following morning, so it's worked fine for our needs.  The house is small, but has three bedrooms with one bedroom having a bunk bed in it. There was also a small sofa bed in the living room, but the mattress was so thin and lumpy, no one wanted to sleep on it. Everything has a tired and outdated look, but was clean. The living room had a slightly funky smell, like a dog had been there, but it wasn't really noticeable after a while.   So overall, an adequate place for a quick overnight.   After the stay was over, I had a very strange message from the host accusing us of stealing a set of sheets off one of the beds and requesting reimbursement for replacing the sheets. He also claimed there were sheets put on the sofa bed, which there were not, so maybe there was some confusion on how many sets of sheets were in the house in the first place. At any rate, it's definitely the most bizarre (only bizarre) thing I've ever experienced with an AirBNB host. I'm still not sure what happened or why the host thought we took his sheets, but I would recommend maybe taking some pictures of the house when arriving just to avoid something like this happening again.

I cannot stress this enough, this apartment was extremely clean and a very great location. Henry answered every question I had ahead of the trip and always kept in touch with any updates. I will definitely book this room again during my next trip.  Thank you again

Patricia's home is just as nice as it looks in the pictures and location is absolutely perfect. Very classy feel as decorated and added to with the nice welcome touch of a welcome note on the counter. Location is upper midtown crossing with lower part of upper east side. This is away from the touristy part, more residential feel, but a short walk to the touristy attractions. Close walk to grocery store, drug store, several subway stops, coffee places, etc. Between Park and Lexington I think puts this place in a very nice block also. Anyway, I wanted a nice experience for my just retired CEO type husband that usually stays in hotels, not necessarily a city guy, and not sure if staying in a one-bedroom apartment would have us on top of each other. The apartment is spacious, clean, and broken up so that he was comfortable and so easy location for him to walk to most places or subway to far places since he is an office type and has just started (on this trip as part of newly being retired) to become a walker.

Absolutely LOVED this location. Alex is a phenomenal host and we were lucky to discover this gem. Reading the manual ensured smooth sailing. Check in was easy and hospitality was excellent. Communication was 10/10. I 100% recommend this spot, especially for those looking for a nice, quiet getaway, and looking to unwind in a stress free location. Will keep this place on my faves in NY. Thanks a lot Alex and Nastia!

Alexander's place is clean and cozy. The studio has all the amenities one needs for a comfort stay. The community is safe and it's nice to have a walk to the beach. Parking started as free off street parking and then there was an issue where the community started charging for overnight parking. It was rather annoying and stressful not knowing where the host would allow me a parking space every night. I just recommend discussing the parking arrangement before you book your stay to avoid any parking inconvenience. If you don't have a vehicle during your stay, you should be comfortable and safe in the studio.

The host was very helpful and kind in trying to solve our issues but the cleanliness just wasn’t up to our standard. The building is pretty shady and had some questionable residents, we saw stains on the mattresses, bugs that looked like baby roaches in our shower, and the hallway smelled very strange. If your main concern is location, then it’s a good spot that’s walking distance from some cool spots.

The owner was always prompt in responding and gentle. The place was spacious but not that clean i am afraid to admit. The owner had to bring us new sheets. The neighborhood was a bit challenging for someone outside US although it seemed quiet. To go to Manhattan you need to take a bus + metro.

Stayed for the night with a couple of friends; I personally didn’t have any issue with the apartment.  Host was very responsive, respectful and gave us a few recommendations.  But a couple notes from the other guests: -not the best area -odd scent of feet  -we thought there were 3 bedrooms but there are 2.  -shower has a weird slope towards the back that makes it feel very dangerous

This is the perfect place to have a very different kind of NYC stay. We loved everything about it. We struggled a little to get into the marina, but that was just our lack of familiarity with the system. It was fairly easy to figure out.  Very laid back marina. Showers and bathrooms were basic and clean. Almost always empty. People at the marina were friendly and quiet. We really enjoyed the mix of peaceful serenity as we enjoyed a glass of wine on the deck with passing swans contrasted with the huge planes taking off from the airport like rumbling ghosts through the low clouds. It was surreal.  Transport was right outside the marina door. Took the bus to the ferry and enjoyed a nice sail to Southstreet area.  We had everything we needed on the boat and anything extra was easy to get at the market right outside the marina.  Loved our stay. It was relaxed and easy and a very different way to enjoy everything that nyc has to offer with none of the stress.
Tried to scam me for a 100$ for some already broken steps. Think about it. How do you break steps? By using them right.

The boat was great. One part of the bed (a wooden slat holding the lower part of the bed) kept falling down (4 times over two nights) and it would produce a loud bang that would wake everyone. Otherwise super cute area, clean, and very short walk to the marina bathrooms which were never busy. I would not suggest drinking the water out of the kitchen sink, or even using it to wash your dishes- it does smell and leaves a smell in whatever you wash. The area was a little sketchy, and the surrounding gas station and market were not suitable for lone traveling females. The marina car gate stayed open for longer than safe and people lingering could get in and out whenever it was open. Inside the marina though, we felt incredibly safe and other boat neighbors were very friendly. The beach towels listed in the description were missing however and we couldn’t end up finding them to use. Emily and Hannah were kind, quick, and responsive to our questions.

I enjoyed staying at this studio right in Manhattan. It met and exceeded my expectations. It’s well furnished with amenities that you’d expect; Hot shower, dishes, silverware, tv, internet. This place is steal. Front desk is strict on letting anyone and that’s an important security measure. MTA train is 3 blocks up so you can get any where you. But you won’t be disappointed.

I wouldn’t book here. It was a very strange experience. The area is also very sketchy. It is up the street from a homeless shelter in Midtown. I was told by host that I could do an early check-in in the early a.m. hours, then upon arrival Henry said no that was impossible. This was all after him telling me to book it because it was available. The misunderstanding left me without a place to stay. I’m still awaiting my refund. I never gotten to see inside the place etc because my stay got canceled. So, I can just say be very wise and vigilant with this stay. Who knows you may enjoy your self and your time. I just don’t know Henry enough to say anything about him as a host. However my experience with the booking was very hard and so, I would never book it again.
Seriously you can not find a better place to stay in NYC. The subway station is close, also a grocery store right down stairs. Sasha’s place is even more beautiful than in pictures! Totally a steal 😊

Place out of nightmare.  Unsafe, located in ghetto area of Brooklyn NY. If you think you can have peaceful stay you’re wrong. The smell of weed, loud noises, someone banging on your door is kinda place this apartment is. Some guys spilled Coca Cola over my friend because he was simply walking next to them. Deep regret for choosing this place and waiting my money.

Henry was great from the beginning and we maintained good communication before and during our stay. The room was as advertised. We were there basically to sleep and get ready in the morning. Good to have a fridge and microwave, we really didn’t want to cook! The building and area is another story. The building needs an upgrade RUSH. Lots of drugs going on outside, but I actually never felt unsafe because there’s 24 hour front desk service. Found it too expensive for what it was, but so is Manhattan. Doubt I would stay there again because of the location and the state of the building.

Great location as everyone else’s review mentioned.   Close to lots of places. Apt was small but it served its purpose.  Henry was amazing at responding.  The only down fall was the drug dealers at the corner.   Did not feel safe when I walked out the building

Excellent place, super comfortable, very clean as it is in the photos, enough for 4 people, close to several subway stations and buses. super easy to get to. A quiet place to rest, we arrived very late at night and it did not feel unsafe. Many places to eat and shop. Definitely a highly recommended place.   Close to many tourist places.

Henry’s place was super clean and pretty! The place is quite small, so 2 or 3 people is probably okay. The bathroom is really small too, but the place was sparkling clean when we got there. The building is old, and sometimes smells like cigarettes, but once you enter the room you kind of forget about the building. The street has a lot of homeless people roaming around.  Overall for the price and location it was a great stay with a good host, and again really clean!

Couldn’t recommend this stay enough! Henry was incredibly responsive and kind! Our room was immaculate and cozy! The location was perfect for quick walks to Times Square, the subway, and shopping and food of all kinds! We were able to use Henry’s complimentary luggage storage for his guests only  as we still had quite a bit of time after check out before leaving the city. Super convenient! It was a stress free stay, even after being pickpocketed and losing the room key. Henry was so understanding and provided a spare free of charge. Please stay here, you will not regret it :)

Sharon was an amazing communicator and a very caring person in general but few things could have been better, Her hospitality skills are like a old school gentle lady. I felt like I can contact her anytime without any issues. Honestly, she was on top of things that I barely had to contact her. She had fresh towels, few snacks, and bottle of water for our stay. I really enjoyed staying there. Though this place could be better manage—  1) when I first booked this place, it only had 4  poorly taken pictures. Then after I checked out suddenly I saw that Sharon upgraded the pictures online and improved her listing details. I just wish I had known few things upfront—  2) like the upper part of the house is rented to bunch of guys. I met one smoking weed on the front steps on my arrival. Then I accidentally went into the one of the room upstairs because it wasn’t locked and description of the place were not clear when we first booked. Sharon said boys were not allowed to come down stairs but if their is no secure lock, who can stop them from entering Airbnb guest room in middle of the night. I don’t think that’s 100% safe for a lonely female or anyone. 3) I am a light sleeper. The boys upstairs slammed door and made loud noise all night. It’s an old house so you can wake by someone just walking upstairs. Honestly, I had worst sleep at this place,  I was scared the whole first night and never felt that my stuff is safe if I left the place. I didn’t feel safe or alone to fully get undressed and I am a dude so I can only imagine much going through a female head.  4) also change the lock box code to a better combo. The current one is easily guessable  5) lastly— accounting for how much hotel would cost in the area, Sharon’s place is well priced. But compare to other Airbnb in the neighborhood including the safety concerns I mentioned above. This place is way over priced. I won’t be going there again.   Ultimately, Sharon is a very nice person but she needs to make upgrades to address Airbnb guest safety and stay true to her post. Don’t over sell and under deliver.
Creepy staircase. Odd street. Generally a good place, clean and comfortable.

This place isn’t as described. It says it’s air conditioned and has portable fans, but there’s only one small window unit and one sad fan for the entire apartment. The bedrooms were horribly hot.   I’m disabled with chronic illnesses that make me very susceptible to heat stroke. I contacted the host to fix the situation and not only was she unwilling to help she was plain rude. I was hoping to stay there as planned, but that wasn’t possible due to the host. I’ve lived in NYC and traveled there many times so I didn’t expect central a/c, but if the bedrooms aren’t air conditioned then that should put in the description. When it became clear the host wouldn’t do anything to help I asked to cancel the reservation, but she denied it.  I then had to complain to air bnb and book a hotel last minute.   I’ve never complained about anywhere I’ve stayed and have given great reviews to most places, but I can’t be ok with this place and the host’s dishonesty and behavior as it puts lives like mine in jeopardy. The stress from the improperly air conditioned apartment has flared up my health issues and so far my vacation has been awful and I’m in unnecessarily feel even worse than my normal.   Avoid this place!

Henry was showed extremely great hospitality and made appropriate accommodations as necessary. It made our trip go by much more smoothly and lessened the stress of traveling to a busy city. Highly recommend and will be coming back!

My college friends and I loved what this Airbnb offered as far as space and cleanliness. We weren't thrilled that we would have to use our own login and password info in order to watch TV. Also, the neighborhood was a bit sketchy and there was a lot of NYPD presence. There were "locals" screaming and yelling at each other in the middle of the street late at night and also in the early morning hours. We know that the host has no control over this, however, even without this, we were not thrilled with feeling unsafe. Of course this is of no fault of the host, but I highly recommend researching the neighborhood before booking any Airbnb.

Henry is an excellent host!  This tiny apartment sits in an incredible location!  Just a short walk to Harold's Square, where you can hop on the subway to take you anywhere in the city.  A little bit more walking past Harold's Square and you'll find yourself in Times Square.  The space is small, but we didn't spend much time in the room, just needed a place to sleep and shower.  The price was incredible and we never felt unsafe.

I stayed at Henry’s place for the marathon, and it was very convenient. Walking distance to the race expo and Penn Station (which made travel between the apartment and Newark Airport super easy). It’s also close to a variety of attractions or a short subway ride from others. Being in the city, I expected some street noise, and it really wasn’t bad (I used earplugs Friday and Saturday nights and slept great). I traveled alone and never felt unsafe, even walking home after a Broadway show or early in the morning to catch the race transportation. The only real downside was something I don’t think Henry can control, so I don’t fault him for it—I could smell cigarette smoke, pot smoke, and cooking odors from other tenants, which was unpleasant. I ended up putting spare pillows against the door to help block the smoke from the hallway. I’m particularly sensitive to those things, so it may not bother others.

The place located in a very unsafe area and I didn’t feel safe at all and I don’t recommend it to anyone. The area was loud as well, you hear noise from the window and the restroom window as well.  The place has no AC or blankets.   I had to check out very early due to many reasons and the host refused to refund me and she ignored all my messages.

Henry was a great host! So communicative and very accommodating. Check-in and check-out was incredibly easy and when there were problems with my stay, Henry would always be there to help out. The location of this Airbnb is fantastic. My partner and I stayed in New York and only needed to use the train once during our stay. That being said, we loved walking and sight seeing the city so often times we would opt to walk. The place is so close to central parts of New York like Times Square, East Village, Chelsea, etc.   While my trip in New York was fun, there were some parts about the Airbnb itself that were just ‘ok’. There would be a faint smell of food in our Airbnb that would linger and never go away. However, Henry was kind enough to give us Febreeze (although it would only be a temporary solution). Time to time we could smell cigarettes as well. These smells made sleeping at night a bit uncomfortable, but at the end of the day it wasn’t totally unbearable.   Overall, my stay at Henry’s was easy and convenient. While it wasn’t the most comfortable due to unpleasant smells, Henry was an amazing host that would work to make sure we would be able to find solutions to our problems.

Very responsive and helpful team, the unit was exactly as described. Only downside were things beyond the owners and management control. Such as the neighborhood seems to just throw the trash out in the street in bags and then the rats come and eat it at night. I don’t know why they don’t put their trash in containers? Other issue is that the homeless situation seems to be getting out of control in the area but I think that’s a New York City problem and not the landlords problem.  So if you’re planning to visit New York City, don’t be surprised

This place is such a steal. Spacious, clean, and in a fantastic location in Koreatown. Close to subway. Henry is very responsive and made sure to help us asap when we had any concerns. We checked in early and the room was ready! What an amazing experience. Highly recommend

location: just a few mins walk to subway train7; however, this neighborhood is kinda messy, dirty and noisy — i chose not to go back until 1 or 2 am.  room: everything you may need is there;   everything is quite clean, but the room is kinda smelly, not the issue of cleanliness, just unpleasant smell of a old humid room; i only have a very sad fan to use as A/C and it’s very noisy so I never used it.  communication: the host is very nice, but sometimes reply late or no reply. I asked about how to get there for EWR airport and he suggests me to take Uber/Lift which costs like $90, but later i figured the train+ subway plan which only cost $5. All in all the host is very nice!

Not only price, but location, even room condition is perfect!  I was afraid because this was my first trip to New York.  But, thanks to your kindness, our family was able to enjoy New York very well!   If i have a chance to visit New York again, I have a willing to stay there again.

The apartment is very clean and very peaceful. We spent 5 nights there, with two kids and we did not have any problem. The neighborhood is a little bit scary with lots of people leaving on the street, but the location is very convinient, with 3 metro stations near by. My kids also loved the kids public library on the corner, 50m from the apartment. We spend all the afternoon reading there,this is probably what they remember the most.

Location is convenient, around the block from subway stop and Herald Square to check out the Macy's holiday windows and eat takeout at the outdoor tables in the park there.  We never felt unsafe and our 10 year old loved the Bear donuts next door!  Took advantage of Henry's recommendations for Eataly and Food Gallery 32.  We walked to Broadway theatres, New York Public Library, and Rockefeller Center.  Direct subway lines uptown to Central Park/Zabar's and downtown to South Ferry (for Staten Island ferry past Statue of Liberty) without having to worry about changing trains. I expected to hear a lot of noise at night but the studio was surprisingly, wonderfully quiet!

First off the space was great.  Amenities were good and Henry’s team was responsive and helpful when needed.  What ruined this for us was the incredible amounts of noise especially when we were trying to sleep at night.  We were offered earplugs.  That’s when I knew that I would not come back to this Airbnb as our stay was ruined by lack of sleep and what seems to be a sketchy location.  Again, nice space and helpful team but when you can’t sleep while on vacation, your vacation is as good as ruined.
Good but the neighborhood seems very unsafe especially at nights.

Easy check-in and communication, Henry is so nice and helpful. Location was perfect (close proximity to everything we needed, drug store, restaurants, subway station, Penn station). Room looks just like the pictures and was a perfect size for 5 people! The beds were surprisingly spacious to share with another person and everything was clean. I would definitely stay with Henry again next time!

Really great spot! If you’re in between choosing places, book this one! Really cute room, has all of the essentials needed. Check in and check out is so smooth which really relieves a lot of stress. Super clean & great location. We were super comfy as a group of 5 girls & loved staying here!!

Despite its apparent cleanliness and practicality in terms of accommodation, we unfortunately experienced the presence of a large number of cockroaches. This is a recurring problem, which the host has tried to resolve on multiple occasions using exterminators, but which persists. From the start of our stay we noticed cockroaches in the common areas and then, after a few days, in our bathroom. We tried to find an amicable solution to resolve this more than unpleasant situation, in vain.

Staying with Henry was a fantastic experience! Travelling with a group of 6 makes it very hard to find reasonable accommodations, especially in NYC, but Henry offers fantastic housing. The place was very clean and put-together, and was comfortable and cozy to come home to every day. While it isn't the biggest place, space did not feel like an issue. It is located in a fantastic area - metro lines are a block away and it was very easy to navigate the neighbourhood.  Henry was also very easy to deal with, making the stay much less stressful. Quick responses and flexibility made the trip a breeze. I would absolutely recommend staying here.

Clean and well kept up.  Location was fantastic being so close to multiple subway lines at 34th street.  Grocery/ Drug Store only one street over with plenty of dining options nearby.  Would recommend!

Was scrambling to find a place a little last minute after my original plans fell through. I was afraid I wouldn’t be able to find anything remotely affordable in a similar area until this spot popped up. I really lucked out! Chris communicated so well from the beginning and periodically throughout my stay to make sure I was doing okay and if I needed anything.   If you’re someone who really wants to take advantage of exploring the city and being fairly central to this area, and just want a comfy bed and bathroom to relax and rest up in in between sight seeing, this is the spot! I walked everywhere, and was so close to the subway to hop on and head into Brooklyn or up to Hell’s Kitchen where my friends live. I truly felt like I was living a true New York life… stairs and all haha but totally fine!

Henry was a gracious and helpful host.  The place was very nice and located very close to everything we were looking for, drug store, liquor store, eatery’s, shopping and train station/subway. Would stay again!

We were so grateful for our host and her place. We had a great time. It is close to the train which is both good and bad. Good in the sense that it's quick to get on the train, bad in the sense that you have a train passing very close very often. Our Lyft driver told us the neighborhood was a little sketchy, but we didn't have any issues. There were plenty of really nice places to sleep, but not many comfortable places to lounge/sit. The couch was comfortable, but since there were more than three of us that left the rest to stand or sit on dining chairs. Over-all we thought the place was excellent and wanted to thank the hosts!

The house is just as seen in the photos. The location is good. It is very close to the metro that takes you to any part of the city. It also has supermarkets and restaurants nearby. In the neighborhood during the day you don't have a sense of danger. At night it gives you more respect

The Bad. This place definitely has a sketchy vibe. The whole building gave off a illegal airbnb hotel vibe.  The interior of the room is pretty bad and needs some work. Things like the flooring panels were drifting to reveal a gross looking brown tile underneath. Stuff like a power strip with a screw drilled through it to mount it to the wall made me wonder what else was sketchy and potentially dangerous in this place that I couldn't see.   Beds are super uncomfortable and the frames appeared to be homemade. The rooms were extremely cold in early December. The host left electric heaters in each room but they didn't really help a ton.  Hot water was also scarce. After two out of the 4 people staying there had showered, no hot water was left for the remaining two people.  No stove, just an electric hotplate.  The Good. Three out of the 4 rooms were actually pretty spacious by nyc standards. The 4th one was unfortunately small. The Bathroom was quite large and somehow the nicest part of the entire space. The host left plenty of towels for everyone.   In Conclusion. The biggest benefit of this place is the cost to room ratio. If you need a spot for 4 people for a reasonable price and you don't care what it looks like or how the beds feel, its great. If you want a nice experience in an inviting well furnished place, this is not for you. Sketchy is the word of the day

Kasa was a safe place to stay with a comfortable bed, really the best I could ask for in NYC. However, our one problem was the mold. The smell was through the whole room, and we discovered it was coming from mold in the air conditioning unit - so we kept it off on some very hot days to avoid any danger. Other than this, it was perfectly fine.

For our first stay in NY, we couldn't have dreamed of better! Esmé's apartment is very spacious, well equipped, super quiet and super well located, with many metro lines within walking distance, supermarkets, restaurants, etc. And to make matters worse, Esmé is a wonderful and very responsive host, who was kind enough to find us a solution to store our luggage during the day before taking our return flight in the evening.

This place is an absolute steal. It is located close to the subway and the neighborhood is great. The apartment is big enough to relax in and recharge between trips around the city. I had no issue finding the place and when I did have questions Esme was very quick to respond. I would recommend this place to everyone!

For the cost of a “hotel-like experience”, our stay was not what we expected. The wifi did not work for our first night there & it was a challenge without front desk staff to get it fixed (they did fix it - but after some stress as we needed to work from home). The bed was uncomfortable & squeaky. The faucets in the sink were leaking. The ventilation in the bathroom is moldy & very dirty. The sound proofing is very poor. The “business center” is more just an entranceway to the rooms. Overall, the stay was doable, however it felt like a private room in a hostel & not worth the cost we paid. If it was $50 a night, this would have made more sense. We would not stay here again.

A really nice place to stay for your time in New York, easy to travel to Manhatten from here, about 30 minutes. The only thing I have to say, is that you have to share the bathroom with 2 more rooms, which can be a bit crowded and unpleasant after a long day in the city. Besides I would really recommend this place if you're looking for a place to only sleep!
Stayed for 9 months. It was a good room at a great price. Modern appliances and everything as advertised. Only complaints is that the apartment is in a kinda sketchy building

I wish I had seen this review before I booked:   For the cost of a “hotel-like experience”, our stay was not what we expected. The wifi did not work for our first night there & it was a challenge without front desk staff to get it fixed (they did fix it - but after some stress as we needed to work from home). The bed was uncomfortable & squeaky. The faucets in the sink were leaking. The ventilation in the bathroom is moldy & very dirty. The sound proofing is very poor. The “business center” is more just an entranceway to the rooms. Overall, the stay was doable, however it felt like a private room in a hostel & not worth the cost we paid. If it was $50 a night, this would have made more sense. We would not stay here again.  My thoughts exactly.  I complained about my damp, moldy room, and was told I’d be moved to another room the following day, but never heard back from the Kasa staff.  It was unacceptable.  I do not recommend to others.

They send you to external forms for any interaction. I filled out one that asked if I wanted an early check in. I said yes and planned around that because they didn’t say no or try to contact me. I arrived and wasn’t able to even get into the lobby when it was 100 degrees outside. I then got stuck on their external support chat, which kept crashing. They said they’d send someone to look onsite if there was availability. Someone eventually let me in and I noticed there’s no front desk or on-site support. I actually ended up canceling my stay because I didn’t feel safe at this listing upon arrival. This isn’t a hotel. It’s a sketchy apartment building that sends out a code to access the front door and another code to access your unit. They don’t support their customers at all. I would stay away.

Shelley is a wonderful host who is friendly and quick to answer any questions you may have. She communicates well and checked in on me frequently to make sure I was enjoying my stay. The apartment is stylish, spacious (with plenty of closet space), and clean. It is also conveniently located within walking distance of Prospect Park and the Q Train. I was unfamiliar with the area and it could feel unsafe at times- I would avoid being outside in the neighborhood at night. Overall, I would highly recommend this place and Shelley as a host!

For this price, nowhere else will be so close to all the major Broadway and Off-Broadway shows. The curtains and lighting are a bit cold; along with a lack of wall decoration/color making it feel a bit imprisoning in the winter. While the customer service representative on the phone did not seem interested in helping much, the virtual desk was so well done you shouldn’t need to rely on them anyways. The late check out at 3 PM was well worth the extra fee.   Yes it can get noisy but that is to be expected in New York. I still had no problem getting to sleep. The plumbing had great pressure and heat, while everything electrical worked great. The coffee, lobby area, and bathroom were more valuable than expected for those in-between location trips when I did not feel like taking 3 flights of steps and having digital code locks eliminated the risk of lost or stolen keys/cards. This was one uniquely genuine combination of New York City living with the comfortable amenities of a hotel.

The choice of this apartment has been great, I would repeat.  Silvia has been attentive at all times, helping and advising us.... The apartment is next to the metro. There is a lot of atmosphere on the street and there are various bars/shops/restaurants.  Quiet place, we have not felt afraid at night when returning to the apartment.

Location location location.  Jaclyn's place is steps from Bedford Ave, a bustling area in the middle of trendy Williamsburg.  The house is clean, simple and quiet.  Bedroom and bathroom are nice, plus the living room is great to chill out in and watch TV.    I didn't meet Jaclyn as she was away, but host Mattie was normal and friendly.  He was happy to engage in conversation if desired, but otherwise stayed out of the way.  Jaclyn provided a long list of suggestions relating to the neighborhood prior to my arrival, which was courteous and helpful.    The L subway line is a 5 minute walk from the house and from there it's a 5-10 minute ride across the river into lower Manhattan.  The Williamsburg Bridge is also a 5-minute walk from the house, then a leisurely 20 minute stroll across the East River into lower Manhattan.  I highly recommend doing this.    Bedford Ave is a safe area lined with excellent bars, restaurants, delis, specialty shops, bakeries, etc.  Anna's pizza next to the subway is fabulous, as is the Red Bowl Asian cuisine and Martha's country bakery. It would take a month's stay to make a dent in the many food places available.  The area is the "real" New York, as locals enjoy it, not a tourist area.    I got to experience the best of both worlds -- an authentic NYC neighborhood, yet easy access to everything the city has to offer.  For the price, location and experience, jaclyn's place is a steal.  I tend to be picky when it comes to quality of places I stay at and I would stay here again.  I recommend this to anyone visiting NYC.
Awsome room in Brooklyn! Check in was easy and stress free. Located close to subway stations and Jaclyn gave an amazing list of stuff to do in the area.

This was our first trip to New York and it was the perfect location, Jason & Ondine were the best hosts, very informative, looking forward to seeing them again. Checking in was easy and their directions were on point. **Do not pay for the ferry, its free, don't believe the scammers**  We used the subway our entire time and the train brings you right to it. Great place, everything we needed and more. Cozy, inviting and comfortable.

My stay with Maria was fantastic. She was polite, helpful and considerate. She was quiet and respectful of my space, which made my stay easy and comfortable. She was also accessible and communicative if I had any questions.  Everything I needed to settle in was ready when I arrived and very clean. The apartment and room are exactly as the pictures advertise. Comfortable room with plenty of storage for my things.   The neighborhood is quiet, safe, easy to get around and close to most anything you could need. I was working in Chelsea, and getting to/from Manhattan was never a problem, even late at night and on weekends.  An overall excellent and stress-free experience. I would stay with Maria again in a heartbeat any time I come to the city.

Me and my significant other stayed with Yana for more than 40 days. I highly recommend that you choose her place for your short term visit in NYC. For starters, the entire apartment is very cosy, warm and located in a great neighborhood in the Upper East Side. The room is exactly what you see in the pictures. It's more than comfortable for 1-2 guests, has a large wardrobe and an amazing bed to rest on.   Yana was a truly wonderful host. She suggested close-by drug and grocery stores, laundry stores etc. Whenever we had a question about NYC she was there to help us. Yana doesn't smoke, is really quiet and for the entire time that we stayed at her place she did not have any friends over.  Yana has a cat, George. He is just the cutest little guy ever. We loved having him around, so much so that we are thinking about getting a cat of our own. Even if you are not a cat person per se, it would be hard not to like him.   Also, if you need accomodation close to MSKCC or NYP, Yana's place is a 5 minute walk from these hospitals. Just FYI, the apartment is on the sixth floor and the building doesn't have an elevator, so pack accordingly or plan for a work out in getting your stuff up to the apartment.   All in all, if you are looking for a quiet, convenient room, definitely consider Yana's place. You are gonna love it there.

Elena tries to accommodate her guests well. If you have questions about attractiveness and good events, she will be happy to help. We were also able to use her bike free of charge. The fact that the apartment, as described in the ad, is something different and interesting is true, but not in a positive sense for me. The setup is very simple and partly made cheaply. Some of the furniture is not in good condition. The heat in the apartment was unbearable during our stay. If you turn on the air conditioning, you can't even think about sleeping because the noise from the devices is enormous. Our room had been painted a few days before, the smell of the paint and solvents was extremely unpleasant. Unfortunately, our criticism of this was not taken very seriously. Elena offered us her room, but with the comment that it wasn't any better. You definitely imagine something different when you think of a loft. The building in which the loft is located is in an industrial area, surrounded by predominantly industrial companies and companies. A disappointing stay for me and too expensive, I wouldn't book it again.

Very disappointing one-week stay at Yana's, apartment really not clean, a lot of noise in the apartment apart from the noise of the city (NYC is a noisy city). The cat's litter box is at the foot of the bathtub with cat droppings, dirty bathroom, door handles full of grease... strong smell of food every day, very dark accommodation, no welcome from Yana, not even a hello, just the first morning an unpleasant remark asking us to make less noise even though her apartment itself is very noisy. We did not feel at all comfortable in this accommodation.  6th floor without elevator, you should know that.  Location 10 minutes from the metro, well frequented area In conclusion I do not recommend this accommodation, Yana only wants to make money, accommodation too expensive for the services of the apartment

Exceptional and understanding hosts who went above and beyond to make sure our stay was comfortable and stress-free. The apartment was quirky cool with special touches of fresh groceries in the fridge and choices of shampoo/conditioner/bodywash etc in the bathroom. Dine & Jason were so friendly, knowledgeable and accommodating with their time, thoughts and advice to make sure we enjoyed our stay. We will definitely stay again!

Staying with Yana was fabulous.  Her apartment is super clean and very neat, and the guest bedroom was the perfect size for 2 people.  The bed is comfortable, the room had a big closet available for guests, and there is a small desk with comfortable chair for working on a computer or writing.   Yana is very quiet - I hardly even knew she was there, but when she is there, you'll find her very friendly and helpful.   The location was excellent, only a couple of blocks from the subway, and an easy walk to Central Park.  I ended up often just walking down to the theater district instead of taking the train.  There are grocery and drug stores close by, and a diner right up the block.  Great location, wonderful hostess, I'd stay there again in a heartbeat!

My host is so nice that we even chill a while in the living room and she served me some tea. The apartment is stylish with plants and upper-floor bed and it is so clean. You can enjoy your personal space in your room. In terms of location, I was afraid in the first place, since my perception of Brooklyn is not positive. The light is quite dim nearby  at night. However, after one night of living, I found this area is actually quite lively with many artists. You can find other stylish artist apartments. You can even go to bar at night where it is quite popular.  Even though here is safe, in general in US, it is always safe to walk with your friends (Though I went to New York City alone haha) :)  我的房東非常好人，我們會在客廳聊天，她甚至給我熱茶。住宅的佈置非常時尚簡約，有很多盆栽，感覺乾淨舒適。你可以享受在你的房間享受私人空間，房間設計很特別，樓底高，牀在上層，感覺很特別。訂的時候我也怕Brooklyn ，因為他給我的印象不太好，而且附近的地方比較暗，但是住了一晚以後，發現一點都不用怕，因為附近很熱鬧，很容易聽到附近有音樂，因為附近是酒吧吧，以及藝術人都住在附近，他們的房間佈置很有趣，我會建議大家住在這裏。但記住儘管這裏安全，最好都要跟朋友一起去玩，以防萬一。(但是我是自已一個去 哈哈)

Elena is a great host! I wanted to go to a rock concert in the area and didn't have anyone to go with and she happily went along and then showed me where to get some good pizza afterward. I liked the way her place was decorated with all the plants and the loft setup was cool with a nice shade to keep the morning sun out. I also enjoyed talking to her couch guest about Slovenian soccer. This was my first time using Airbnb and it exceeded my expectations thanks to Elena!

After a 15 minute Uber ride from LaGuardia Airport, my wife and I were warmly welcomed into Chuck’s home and given a tour of his apartment.  It was neat, clean, and exactly as described.  The walls are a bit thin, but we spent most of our time being tourists by day and only needed a place to sleep at night.  The queen sized bed is very firm, which is different from what I am used to, but my wife found it cozy and comfortable. There a plenty of places to eat in and around the neighborhood, all within walking distance…Chinese food, Colombian food, Pizza, Popeye’s Chicken, and McDonalds to name a few.  There are also nearby drug stores and a Target.  We felt safe in the apartment as well as in the neighborhood. There is a bus stop located right at the corner and the subway is only a 10-15 minute walk from the apartment.  Depending on where you’re going, plan on at least a 45 minute train ride to the other Burroughs. Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay.
Good location and clean room. The elevator is a little scared. Good place for short stay visitors.
Great host and for the price, it's a steal.

Shari is very pleasant and very available, the apartment is comfortable for two couples or two single people, there are two bedrooms with large comfortable beds, but the sofa bed in the living room is not very pleasant to sleep on and there is a lot of light in the morning because the curtain in the living room lets everything through and a hole forms at night in the middle of the sofa bed. The place is clean, well equipped, fridge stocked when we arrived, allow 15 minutes to reach the metro. Quiet and NOT dangerous neighborhood. But an area quite far from New York entertainment. Plan a little gift for her adorable, cute and curious little girl :). Thanks Shari! Kiss

This B&B is located in a quiet and peaceful area, which is a 10 minute walk from the metro station (86th street, R line). It takes about 90 minutes from the JFK Airport using ordinary public transport facilities. A cab will take you there in just 25 minutes for 40 dollars.  Besides, this area provides easy access to several restaurants, shopping centers, ATMs, laundries. This B&B is located in a safe neighborhood.   The room was very clean and well maintained. After a long journey it was a perfect place to relax.     The owner, Ms. Sophie, was very warm and welcoming. From the moment I checked in, Sophie patiently guided me attractions that are a must visit. She also explained how I should move around the city safely, sharing details of unsafe areas, good photographic locations, and other valuable information like making a trip to Washington DC. Kotaro (Sophie’s husband) was also extremely helpful and helped me book a cab to the airport on the morning of my departure.      I am grateful Sophie and Kotaro making my first visit to New York a huge success. Without any doubt the next time I visit NY, I will stay at the place. This place is equally great for first timers, well traveled persons, and for people who would like to make new friends.    この宿は閑静な住宅街にあります。メトロR線の86th street駅から徒歩10以内の距離です。  JFK空港からは交通機関を乗り継いで1時間半ほど、タクシーでは25分（40ドル程度）で到着できます。  近所には多数の便利な施設（各国料理のレストラン、ショッピングセンター、ATM、ランドリーなど）があり、治安の面も全く心配はいりません。 お部屋は清潔かつ快適で、旅の疲れをとるのに最適な空間です。  Sophieさんはたいへんご親切な方で、チェックインしたときには、約2時間にわたって、見るべき名所、おすすめの街歩き、撮影スポット、ニューヨーク各地の治安、ニューヨークからワシントンDCへのアクセスなどを説明してくださいました。Kotaroさんにもお世話になり、滞在最後の日の朝には空港リムジンタクシーを呼んでいただきました。  初のニューヨーク旅行を安心して満喫できたのは、ひとえにSophieさんとKotaroさんのご親切さゆえのことと思っています。心よりお礼申し上げます。 次回ニューヨークを訪問する際にも、またこちらの宿に宿泊することになるでしょう。 初めてニューヨークを旅行する方、アメリカ旅行経験豊富な方、旅行中の出会いを楽しめる方にこの宿を強くお奨めします。

I had the best time in bay ridge, I felt at home as soon as I arrived and was so sad to leave. As a student it was a perfect place to return to and relax, I felt safe, stress free and comfortable. The location was great and I loved the easy link to Manhattan and school! Perfect place for a NYC experience.

Since I have high expectations for a place that should be my home for three months, Sophie's room was the only option for me. I knew for sure when I booked the room months in advance that there would be no nasty surprises. The detailed descriptions and the fastest and warmest response emails I have ever received made me feel confident that I had made the right decision. And that's exactly how it happened. The welcome was warm. You will be shown everything you see in the photos here on Airbnb, plus a small room with cleaning supplies that you can use to clean your own room (this is very helpful for those planning a longer stay). There is always the current TimeOut in the living room, so you can always get an overview of what's going on in the city. The room corresponds to the impression given by the photos. According to my assessment and after a few glimpses of the other rooms, it is the room with the most storage space, which is very pleasant for longer stays. All suitcases and bags, clothes, learning materials, books, blankets, jackets, everything finds space in cupboards, under the bed, in the chest of drawers, drawers, desk cupboards and on 20 hangers in the closet. The absolute highlight is the large desk and a daylight lamp, which like all the other lamps in this room are dimmable. You quickly get used to the fact that the main light switch is not next to the room door, but on the opposite wall. Only one thing surprised me: the window in the room ensures plenty of daylight, but you don't have a view because there is a narrow building shaft in front of it. What you see is the bathroom window opposite, the window of another room and the wall of the house around it. You have an opaque curtain, so don't worry, no one can watch you in your room! No matter when and what it is. You can contact Sophie or Kotaro at any time. Whether you get sick and you need medicine or other help. Kotaro even brought food to my roommate once because she was sick. I ordered something, which works because the upstairs has its own bell that the delivery service can use. If you want new towels or fresh bedding, just text and you'll have fresh clothes on your doorstep in the evening. I put my used towels in a bag and put them outside or brought them down into the hallway. The bathroom is large enough and there is always a great selection of toiletries, as well as small touches in the kitchen such as fresh fruit, baked goods or homemade oatmeal cookies from Sophie. The kitchen does not have a dishwasher, but is sufficiently equipped. As a foodie, I ate out a lot. I didn't miss anything in the kitchen for snacks and my daily breakfast. You have your own area in the fridge (a large box that quickly fills up with everyday staples. Unfortunately, the temperatures in the hanging cupboard above the fridge were extreme...

Unfortunately, I would not recommend this place. Before I was let through the door I was made to feel incredibly unwelcome and unsafe. As a solo traveller in an unfamiliar country, a pleasant attitude and kind manner from your host is paramount to ensuring a happy and comfortable stay. The apartment was also unclean and untidy and I did not appreciate having to make my bed on arrival.

Elena was a kind, quiet and conscientious host. We had to book her place last minute after our original host fell through the day we arrived in NYC, and she was willing to let us check in a bit early and decompress after a stressful afternoon not knowing if we'd have a place to sleep.  The location is close to the L train and nearby some great bars and restaurants. The neighborhood seems active and safe, full of young people. The specific street the building is on is a little dark and creepy at night, though it was definitely fine for us and would be ok for anyone used to city life.  The unit itself is fantastic - clean, private room with lofted bed, great natural light but thick curtains if you need them. Elena has a flair for design and it shows in the apartment. Two things to note-she rents her living room couch as well so there might be another guest if you stay, and if you are super sensitive to smoke it might be tricky as there is some cig use in the living room. These things did not bother us at all though so we had an absolutely wonderful stay. Highly recommended!

Elisabeth is really helpful. I only stayed there for one day, but really love the time there. The interior of the room is lovely. My only problem is the location. It's not far but scary to walk alone at night if you're not familiar.
I had to book an air b n b due to a horrible snow storm and unsafe driving conditions on the way home from a concert. Elisabeth’s home is beautiful you won’t regret staying here!

For future experience.i would say do not book here. She is currently living in the apartment. Elizabeth is not even her real name. She requires too much and offers too little. She smokes cigarettes and only allows you to smoke in the living space. She monitors and chaperones your stay while your in the house. After my stay she accused me of stealing hand sanitizer and tooth paste. Which is ridiculous becuase I have my own items.  Her pictures were catfish and her furniture was broken.

Nancy graciously accepted my last-minute booking request, and made what could have been a bummer of a weekend (someone bailed on me last-minute to split a hotel room) a really stress-free and fun time! She was a lot of fun to hang out with when we were around the apartment, and even invited me to join her for a small party down the street. She has great suggestions about the area, and very interesting stories about life in general. Next time I'm back in NYC solo, I'll definitely be seeing if her place is available!
This stay is definitely a steal for its price. The room is very sizeable, clean, artsy and the location is also quite accessible.

(TLDR --- DO NOT STAY HERE, ABUSIVE HOST)   The airbnb itself was fine, the room was comfortable and spacious. However, the host, Elisabeth, was hostlie and abusive.  Upon arrival, Elisabeth began complaining about the Airbnb guests from the night before (one of whom was still there) and told me how much she hated being an airbnb host but needed the money. I felt uncomfortable but she was being nice to me, so I assumed it was a specific problem with the prior guest.   Then, I mistook her towel for a bath mat. I thought I was being polite by wiping the excess water off of the ground. After my shower, she sent an aggressive message to me through the Airbnb platform complaining that I used her towel as a bathmat. We were both in the apartment at the time of the message, so I felt really uncomfortable, and quickly went into the living room to apologize in person.   I explained it was a mistake and that I was very sorry. She started by saying "I'm actually really upset right now" and I knew I was in for it. She proceeded to tell me that she has never experienced this in all 7 years as a host, and this is why she doesn't like having people in her house because nobody respects her, and of course she doesn't use a bathmat because we would all get fungus and she is protecting me. She only gives herself one towel and gives me so many, so how could I have ever made that mistake. She hates being an airbnb host and would stop but she can't afford to, and she can't move to a new apartment because she can't afford it. She charged me $5 to launder her towel, despite my offer to use one of the guest towels that I hadn't touched yet. I probably apologized 10 times and she would not stop berating me about my mistake. She was clearly taking her frustration out on me, and I was on the verge of tears and thought about packing up right then to leave.   This is being dramatic, and I have rarely felt physically unsafe in an Airbnb, but I did wonder if my mistake was the straw that broke the camel's back. I did not feel safe falling asleep that night.   After the altercation, I read some of her past reviews, confused at how she is a superhost with this behavior. While 95% of her reviews are overwhelmingly positive, it seems the other 5% of people had a similarly unpleasant experience to me. What's more, when other people have given negative reviews, she degrades them online by calling them "ignorant, stupid, and pathetic". I await a similar verbal assault from her for my mistake once I submit this review.  I have never written a negative airbnb review before (despite having bad experiences), but I felt compelled to write this one.
The room is nice and clean. Location close to a subway station. I didn’t give 5 stars because initially we had an unpleasant disagreement with the host but after it was resolved she was very nice.

The apartment was perfect for our little New York stay. We were a little nervous about the location for getting around midtown Manhattan, but with the subway around the corner it was quick and convenient.  Carrie is very kind, she welcomed us, answered all our questions with patience and was attentive to the organization of our departure.  Thanks Carrie.

As a native of the neighborhood and area where Sophie hosted me, I did not need much attention, yet from the moment she opened the door to welcome me I felt so much more at home than I had in my old neighborhood than I have in years. Sophie is an outstanding host, she goes above and beyond to make you feel welcome, safe and comfortable in her beautiful and laid back home.  We had an amazing conversation and visit when I first arrived and our connection was immediate...it is impossible NOT to find Sophie infinitely interesting and engaging. She was so kind to have lovely beverages and treats set aside for me and let me know who the other guests were. On that note, I did not see the other guests AT ALL during my time at Sophie's and it was so quiet and absolutely relaxing. Sophie and Kotaro have made an oasis in the heart of Bay Ridge that will leave any guest feeling welcome, comfortable and completely at ease as if you were in your own home.  I cannot recommend Sophie highly enough as a host, the rooms and common areas are clean, lovely and charming. She is welcoming and warm yet unobtrusive and completely laid back and the home and rooms reverberate with her energy.  I am almost hesitatnt to rave so much about Sophie's place because I am afraid I will never be able to book it again. If you are looking for an affordable, chill and wonderful place to stay in Brooklyn, Sophie is absolutely the finest host with the most outstanding accomodations.

Olivier was very welcoming and although had moved out of the apartment, was still very accessible. The space itself was very clean and exactly as described; and the other guests were quiet and respectful.  The room and sheets were clean and smelled great! The neighborhood was fairly quiet and cute. Plenty of markets, cafes, restaurants within walking distance. Citi bikes nearby. Never felt unsafe. Definitely had a great stay!

Manny is a very accommodating and gracious host! We had a very enjoyable stay and are considering staying there in the future. The condo is clean, very spacious, stylishly decorated and doesn't feel like a basement at all.   The neighbourhood is also clean, very quiet, and is conveniently located between Brooklyn and Queens.
