The place is a real disaster, everything very dirty and messy. a super ugly place full of drugs, fights, other guests singing at dawn. When we arrived there was a lot of garbage in the kitchen and bathroom. things lying on the floor there was nowhere to go. The sheets were dirty and the comforter was the same. There were no clean towels, no eating cutlery.  The disrespectful host, without values, not at all cordial, insulted and discriminated against us. He attacked us emotionally.  The worst stay ever, a very bad experience. I don't recommend to anyone.

Conrad is pleasant, and let me stay an hour longer. Checking in at night is to be avoided if you can, I broke my phone screen trying to light the lockbox to work the combination. Make sure the code is correct, as I was sent an incorrect code by mistake.  The neighborhood is a little shady at night, but a lot better during the day. It's one of the more affordable stays on NYC though, and near the subways.

Great value overall if you’re looking for a place to crash after a long day. Pretty clean and check in was easy, he was even flexible with letting us leave our bags early. A couple blocks from the subway to the city. We walked home at midnight and never felt unsafe. AC unit in the room as well. Overall I’d recommend!

Very disappointed with the cleanliness of the accommodation. The bathroom was not clean at all. Hairs on the sink upon arrival and a general dirty condition. No shower head. There was a very strong and unpleasant smell in the apartment. Conrad was nice upon arrival and then spent the night making noise and cooking at 3am. In the room there are no shutters, no insulation, the window closes poorly. We left after two nights instead of 8 to find a hotel.

Fabulous! Book it - your search should end here. Read on for details...  First, I assume that you (unlike me) know that many (most?) high-end NYC places are scams. Why Airbnb doesn't solve this is unfortunate and a topic for another day. For a successful NYC stay you must limit your search to Superhosts. Gordon is a Superhost+, just the best. Great guy - like a new friend.   The place is better than advertised but be mindful, it is what is advertised. The location is incredible, but of course you have to love and appreciate the neighborhood. The size is stunning - giant, but it is old. It is called the "carriage house" so it is quirky (it was converted) but has tons of character. If you don't like these things, it is not for you, (and that is fine), but it is not fair to expect something different.   But, if you like character, some adventure, some quirks and love the neighborhood, you are in for a lifetime memory.   It would be fabulous for a guys, girls, or couples trip. Highly recommend for that. However, we went as family: 4 teenagers, 1 baby + adults. Everyone loved it!

TERRIBLE/ INACCURATE/ NOT CLEAN/ UNSAFE  This was the worst Airbnb experience I’ve ever had.  For starters at no point of the experience was it smooth, starting with the mix up of all the keys with the other guests. Not to mention the wrong code was given at the start when trying to get the keys to enter the space. I got to the Airbnb at my check in time and it hadn’t been cleaned since the previous guest. There were old sheets, old food and everything in the room when I arrived. The housekeeper was really rude about the inconvenience and Conrad did not communicate anything to us about the “hiccup” (as he called it). The room that we were placed in isn’t listed on his profile and was completely inaccurate. If I could share pictures here I would, because it’s nothing like it was displayed on the app. The blinds were busted, the sheets weren’t that clean and had that room been posted I would have never stayed here. There was dirt on the shower curtains, as they had not been changed and to say that he was upholding the health / cleanliness standards of Airbnb and COVID would be a complete lie. It was absolutely terrible compared to room #1 which is the one we thought we were getting.  Not to mention the dangerous area that this Airbnb is located in. Which in itself is a whole different story . There was a weird man sitting on the stairwell for most of the night and kept asking really personal questions. At a point he had even grabbed my arm aggressively to not go down the stairs. If you’re a woman going here I’d think twice tbh. It was such a scary experience.   Also the way that Airbnb handled the situation is sickening. They did not look out for the guest and did not stand behind their own policies. I ended up staying for only a few hours on the first day and left at 1 in the morning to a new place. I wasn’t given a full refund , even with all of the stuff that happened.   I’ve never had an experience like this before and I am never one to complain too much, but this was horrid. It ruined my entire trip and I’ll never book with Conrad or Airbnb again.

If you're looking for a comfortable refuge, I wouldn't stay here. If you're looking for a comfortable room with the bare essentials, still not here. The room was definitely not the same one as advertised (no workspace as advertised; the room orientation is totally different), and on top of that things were falling apart (wardrobe door had fallen off, tap was so loose it could turn 360, shower was unclean - also no body soap was provided). AC is provided... but it sounds like a lawn mower at your head  (you won't need the white noise machine).  Room aside - as a woman traveling alone I did not feel safe or comfortable here. Would not advise it. The host (Conrad) failed to provide check-in instructions even after I messaged 3x and called leading up, not until after the designated check-in time. When I got to the address the front gate was jammed and I was stuck in the rain (apparently "it does that occasionally"), meanwhile Conrad still did not respond to my messages or calls. Getting into the room requires  the longest check-in instructions I've ever seen + 4 sets of keys, none of which are labeled, and the way up feels sketchy.  Honestly speaking this was one of the first times I booked a place thinking I had scored for the price, but in hindsight, it was a waste of time and money. I spent my entire time there trying to search for another accommodation, I ended up canceling and asking for a refund and moving elsewhere. Read the negative reviews - a lot of them echo this review, and it appears nothing - gate, tap, etc - has been fixed. It might be hard to find a room with even just the essentials for a low price in this city, but this was just plain false advertising.

Michael is an incredible host, very kind and responsive. He always attended my requests and questions very quickly and on time.  I list below from my experience Michael's apartment as what worked for me and what didn't. On the +ve side: - the apartment is very clean -the location is great if you are staying there for a short time , close to museums, shopping and everything else  -the kitchen equipments are very clean and sufficient   -Michael is a great host and helpful.   On the -ve side or rather what didn't work for me as I stayed for 25 days -the apartment is located on the 5th floor (almost 84 narrow steps), on my arrival Michael was very kind to carry my bags all the way up but on the day I was leaving as it was 4:30 am, I had a great difficulties carrying down two large suitcases by myself! -some of the furnitures need renewing as they are worn-out and very old -the street where the apartment is and all of midtown can get a bit rough and has become worse since the pandemic with lots of people heavily dependent on strong substances who are hovering around and sadly homeless.  -there are two restaurants which they have their fans in the courtyard at the back of the building, which make continues sounds. Often they forget to turn them off, if you are a light sleeper like myself and have to work next day, this can be a major issue.  Thank you Michael for your warm hospitality...

Jasmins 1 bedroom Bushwick apartment was an ideal sanctuary for my daughter to enjoy the summer in Brooklyn. A secure building offered a true sense of privacy it offered video intercom system in an elevatored building. Neighborhood never felt unsafe even for a college student. Nice restaurants line neighboring streets. Nice sized bedroom with closets nice chair to relax in and 2 tvs are in the unit. You can Chrome cast to TV and the WiFi is strong. The living room/kitchen area is open and functional. Nice fridge, large sink and dishwasher are all useful. Bathroom has washer/dryer inside a closet and decent sized tub. Was a good choice being my first AirBnB rental. Communicating with Jasmin was super easy. Thank you for the great stay.
Beautiful view, so close to Times Square, but too many homeless people around times sq.  The building it’s so comfy and quiet.  I recommend this apartment so much!!!

I'll start with the positive. The bedroom, bathroom and kitchen were extremely clean, the bed was comfortable, and I was able to enter the apartment without any problems. It was a great price. The Airbnb is close to the subway.  The negative: The listing says this is a "business purpose apartment" during the week, with a room available on weekends. I did not know what this meant. I showed it to several friends, who all had different interpretations. It turns out the apartment is a day care. Normally, I would have no problem with that, but because of the pandemic, I was worried about entering a room that just a couple hours before had been filled with people too young to be vaccinated and their parents who were picking them up. I opened all the windows and left for two hours. I considered staying with a friend, but after looking into how long the coronavirus lives in the air, I decided that five hours with some ventilation would be safe. But it was a stressful decision. Had I known, I would still have stayed here, but I would have asked for all the windows to be open beforehand and it would not have been such a surprise.  Second, there was a video camera on the top of the refrigerator that should have been disclosed. I didn't want to cover it up because I wasn't even sure what it was. I asked Carmen toward the end of the stay, and she said it was a camera, it should have been removed and it was not trained on the part of the apartment that I was using, and also  she did not look at the recordings. That was good to know, but there is an expectation of privacy with an Airbnb (it's in the rules that cameras must be disclosed), and you have to walk through the living room/day care to reach the bedroom.  Third, the walls are thin, so it was loud at night ... I could hear the people next door speaking even at a normal volume.  So, great value, very clean, good location, but full disclosure in the listing would have made this a safer and less stressful visit.

This is a steal of a deal if your on a budget and just want to stay for a couple of days  this was our first time in NYC and wasn’t sure about the area but all in all it was a good experience … the host carman was accommodating to us while visiting! She was very communicative and flexible with us . Our flight arrived in NYC at noon and Check in was at 6 we were able to leave our luggage and go back  she nailed  the description to a T in her ad, and everything was as she said … if your looking to stay and go inner city the subway is only a block away - but if you plan on being downtown a lot I recommend getting the metro card to ride the subway - all in all it was a nice stay and I felt safe as soon as I saw the NYPD station! I can’t wait to go back, however I would like to try to stay somewhere closer to everything :) but like I said if your on a budget this a good little spot !

It's a great place to stay for a couple of nights. Be aware that this is exactly at the entrance of the building so it can get a bit loud some times. Also, the neighbor across keeps on making disturbing noises and screams. Not sure if it's because of a disease or drugs.

Jesica's apartment is just like the photos, very nice, the building too, the laundry is in the basement of the building. It is in an area that is not very nice and a little unsafe but it is manageable, the subway is 4 blocks away and you can reach Manhattan Times Square in 30 minutes and bus stops nearby. The room with a private bathroom is the best, although since it faces the avenue it is noisy at night, you may need earplugs but it has black out curtains. The other two rooms are quieter, they share a bathroom with a very small sink that broke during my stay and took a long time, like a week, to resolve. All in all, excellent value for money, Jesica helped us with all the orders we made.

Everything about the place itself is great! And the host! But I’d really recommend bringing your car when staying at this place. I had the unfortunate experience of being stalked/followed home, while walking, by a creepy man one night (around 9p.m.) and then I realised the area is very isolated and pretty much no one to call on for help, if needed. I hid though and eventually he left so everything was fine, but I’d recommend bringing a car, or not staying there alone!

Okay the pictures look just like how you see it. Which is great lovely. However the outside needs a lot of work. I honestly felt uncomfortable 🥴 I wasn’t at ease. This industrial 🏭 Airbnb which was next to a car mechanic shop was very unsettling. I think the area is mad Sketchy. But if your into that back alley industrial vibe. Then maybe this could be for you. But if you like beauty don’t come. Not for the weak. I’m weak, and I couldn’t handle it. Sorry Ant, your a cute guy but I couldn’t do it on the first day.

Rob’s home was amazing. We stayed for a month this summer and couldn’t have asked for a better place to stay. Where to even start? The layout, amenities, and comfort of the home was perfect. The location is ideal for morning strolls in the park or a quick subway ride downtown. Our communication during this time was perfect, quick responses when needed and amazing hospitality. The attention to detail and also flexibility he provided us made this just a wonderful stay. We are already planning to return! 5 stars all around.

3 months spent searching for a place to stay in Manhattan that would accommodate my family for 6 weeks was stressful. I don’t know what I put into the computer that resulted in seeing Rob’s place, but I remember being thrilled and thinking it can’t be. It was in the perfect location-based on our plans to walk to most places we needed to go daily, had a deck, was affordable, and available without restrictions! The ad was real, and resulted in finding our home away from home. 6 weeks is a long time. Being comfortable in the space we considered home was necessary. Rob’s place was perfect for us, and would happily do it all over again.

Our overall holiday was successful staying here. I've read other reviews and broadly agree with what others have said and so will just write about two issues we had with the accommodation. The first thing to understand is that this is a  basement apartment and we feel this needs to be made clearer in the advert. The thumbnail photo of the property could  be described as misleading. We accept of course that this is reflected in the price and does represent good value. The other issue is one of noise. On more than one night I was kept awake all night by what I presume was banging on a wall. This may not have had anything to do with Elisabeth and indeed was probably  outside of her control. Regardless, obviously I was not comfortable. I suspect this noise was because my breathing while asleep is audible and so it appears that noise insulation is an issue here. I wish to stress that Elisabeth was sympathetic and did make enquiries, but I feel people need to be aware of what I experienced when spending such large amounts of money.

Kermoni was incredibly attentive with communication even prior to arriving. Check in was amazing and not stressful at all (no time crunch or complicated instructions). The Melo place is located in a more quiet, yet beautiful part of Brooklyn full of some of the nicest people i’ve ever met. Location was perfect and only a 3 minute walk from the subway. We were blown away by the low price and wonderful stay we had! Would recommend to anyone.

Overall it was a decent spot. The location is a bit sketchy, but the room was nice enough. A bit too expensive considering the location and unit itself. Very very very noisy neighbourhood too. Loudest neighbourhood I've ever lived in. You will be hearing blaring loud music until the early AM. The carpets were a bit dirty too and is generally best not to have carpet in a shared living environment due to bacteria build-up. The host is great though, she communicates well, keeps up with everything and is very kind.

The Melo Place was a great and cute place to stay at for the weekend! The location can seem a little sketchy, but we had no problems leaving our car on the street for a couple days. The place also had everything we needed and Kermoni was very responsive as he made sure we were well accommodated! We highly recommend staying at the Melo Place!

I was lucky enough to be a guest during the magical time that Andrew babysat his sister's dogs. Let me tell you, it was a real treat. Although Andrew says on his posting that he rarely babysits his sister's dogs, and sometimes even fosters others, what he doesn't tell you is that he will leave the premises and have you be the one to actually watch them! I loved it! There was nothing better than trying to leave my room and being attacked by two (admittedly small), scared, howling, panicked animals! What worried me though wasn't really the dogs, it was the mindset of a host who decides to leave two animals with a stranger alone. Andrew should be lucky that these dogs (neither of which belong to him by the way--again, his sister's), didn't actually harm me, because something tells me Andrew wouldn't stand a chance in court. But if you're looking for a good civil lawsuit, by all means, take on this Airbnb.

If you like the smell of marijuana whafting under your door then this is the place for you. Saying you are 420 amenable is not the same as saying guests need to smell your drugs. She got nasty once I called her on her behaviour

Jakob is a great host and very attentive. Be aware that Parking is very limited. I had to park a couple of blocks away. Be sure not to leave anything in your car. My back window was smashed and my suit along with some other items were stolen from my car. This is not Jakob’s fault in any way but, just be vigilant if you are driving.

Easy to communicate with and nice to have access to the whole apartment. Well kept with some good modern amenities. Perfect for solo traveler to just have a space to yourself in the city. The area might seem a little rough, but at no point did we feel unsafe. Some loud music playing by the neighbors, but it is the city. For a budget-friendly spot, I definitely recommend.

My friend and I had many doubts about going to New York because of the Asian hate crimes that had been going on and felt threatened. Our two main locations that were on our decision list (on where to live) were Times Square or Wall Street, and we chose Times Square. We weren't excited to be living with other guests and had many doubts, but Eddie & Vlad as well as the other guests made us feel at home! It was a diverse atmosphere and during a time like this, I hope everyone can consider their place because it felt safe and the hosts made us feel included!

After the reservation was completed and the payment was completed, I was told that the reservation was covered(doble-booking) and I could not move in.  I didn't have time to move in and was very impatient, but the reply from the host was very slow.  I contacted around the host organization. The host side should have responded. It was very stressful.  When I moved in, I told him the arrival time, and I arrived on time.  However, the room I was guided to was not a room with a private bathroom, unlike the room I reserved.  When I showed the reservation screen and told that it was a different room, I had to wait for about an hour and a half to clean the room(with private bathroom)  Very uncoordinated.  It's a shame.

Gregor is such an accomodating, wonderful host. He was really easy going about a later check in & out, which was so appreciated. He left for overseas halfway through my stay & still replied to my messages quickly. The apartment itself is gorgeous, a converted warehouse with high ceilings & visible pipes. It’s decorated super cute & has everything you’d need for a long stay.  The only thing to note about the apartment is that the windows open on to the common area outside so I didn’t open the shades most of the time for privacy. The area is quiet & the bedroom has a black out shade. It’s a 5 minute walk to the L subway, in an area I felt safe walking in at night. Close to amazing restaurants, supermarkets & a bodega close by. All the amenities (gym, laundry, !!ROOFTOP!! with seriously amazing views were so amazing). Gregors place is such a gem in Williamsburg & I would be happy to stay again. Thank you, Gregor!

Pack lightly because you have to carry your luggage up 4 levels of small stairs ! also my bf & I had to share the same 1 towel for the week so bring extra if needed! 5/10 min walk from subways depending on what route you want to go ! walking in the area after 10pm can be a little scary but just be aware of ur surroundings (: buuut i enjoyed my stay great price for the location

Laye inaccurately described his place. Stove was broken, water was not drinkable, apt was dirty and smelled like weed. When i complained and said I needed to cancel we agreed he would refund me. Then when I requested from a refund, he harassed me, threatening me and cursing me out. He called, messaged, texted terrible things that made me feel unsafe and i had to report it to airbnb.

The place was as shown in pictures (very nice and clean) and included AC for every room, Wifi and TV services. Norma and Daniel met us at the door and were great to explain everything at the place.  It's a short walk to the boardwalk and beach and there is security constantly patrolling the beaches. The neighbors were friendly and we had a great time visiting Coney Island, Times Square, and my favorite the Museum of Natural history by Central Park (make sure to get reservations so you can reserve one of the special shows).   A couple of tips as I have been to NYC many times before: Generally, people of NYC are friendly but avoid eye contact as it is considered aggressive unless you are asking a question (directions, etc). Use situational awareness - if you feel something is wrong then it probably is and pivot yourself and then keep eye contact and get aggravated rather than show fear.  Restrooms are hard to find so walk into places (hotels, public access places) as if you were there before rather than ask. The people in costumes and cosplay in Timesquare will demand to be paid and may get angry if you attempt to use your camera and take a selfie with them. Nothing is free, so if someone offers you a CD they will tell you it's free but then bug you for a donation. Stay calm at all times if you drive into NYC as you will be cut off and see aggressive driving. Parking can run $36 to $50 in NYC and Norma suggested the water taxi which is inexpensive and less stressful.   Overall had a great time.  **

The apartment was clean and very nice. As other reviews stated, the first impression of the neighborhood might give you pause. Don’t let that scare you away, I would call the area transitional. The neighbors were friendly and the location is very convenient. Our hosts were very accommodating and responsive. I would defiantly stay again!

Great location.  Perfect for exploring NYC.  Penn Station subway/train is a five minute walk as is Hudson Yards subway station or if you prefer to walking it is about 20  minutes to Time Square.  We walked a lot in the area and never felt unsafe. There are a lot of really good restaurants around the area.  About the apt: Communication was great, checkin was easy.  The place has clean comfortable beds with clean sheets and towels provided.   The apartment has four bedrooms with one double/full sized bed in each and plenty of room to hang your clothes etc.  There is no living space, only a galley kitchen with a room for three chairs so don't expect to use the apartment for socializing in.  The kitchen area has a microwave, full size fridge/freezer, electric kettle, and a sink.  No stove or coffee maker.  That said, there are LOTS of coffee shops around.  The apt building is old and showing its age, the all tile floors are cracked in many places and could do with a lot of bleach, the bathroom needs some love - however for the cost and the location these are all easy to overlook - just temper your expectations with what you are paying!  Would definitely return.

I don’t know from where to start Its most horrible place I have ever rented .  First of all the instructions to check in was insufficient, I had to wait in the hall way for almost one hour to get in to the apartment. The host didn’t answer the messages or the call. And there was a peace of paper taped on the door in Spanish, And she knows that I don’t speak Spanish!!  There are cameras everywhere in the house , so there is no privacy!!! I have never seen this before in any airbnb !!  When I opened the closet I found mannequin head with hair , it was so creepy!! The towel was so cheap and old . I was begging her the whole time I stayed there ( 5 nights ) to turn the AC on . It was so hot in the apartment. She Never did !! There were no shampoo or body wash at all !!  The bathroom was so dirty. I will never go back there

Clean and cozy room. The apartment in general is quite clean. Rocelly has been a good host, she is kind and takes little time to respond when you write to her. As for the location, even though it is in the Bronx it is not a dangerous area, I never felt unsafe in the area. It is far from the center but there are two metro stops near the apartment (one of them practically next door) so it is very connected. Good quality-price ratio.

Great location - NYC. Penn Station subway/train and Hudson Yards Subway is five minute walk.  20 minute walk to Time Square. We walked a lot in the area and never felt unsafe. Lots of restaurants and small markets in the area.  Accommodation - Check in and out is super easy, parking lot available on the same block.  4 flights of stairs to get to apartment.  Place has  4 bedrooms with clean comfortable double/full beds with clean sheets and towels provided. Plenty of space for luggage and clothes.  There is no common area/living room for hanging out and no TV.  There is a small kitchen area that has a hot plate, microwave, full size fridge/freezer, electric kettle, and a sink - no coffee maker or toaster.  Minimal amount of utensils plates and glassware for all of us and one frying pan for the hot plate, but was more than enough to cook breakfast for two adults and three kids.  The rest of the meals we ate out in the neighborhood - awesome pizza place and deli right across the street which the kids really enjoyed.  Of the 4 bedrooms only one did not have an AC unit which really made that room unusable in the summer heat.  It had a fan and if you left the window open you got a lot of traffic noise (building is on the route for the Lincoln tunnel and there is a police station a block away).   We identified this shortfall to the owner.  Everything in the bathroom worked fine.  Wireless was strong and all electronics connected easily.  The listing states not suitable for children, however, we had a 7, 10 and 11 year old there and they were fine.  Each have there own tablet and it connected to the wireless so no one missed the TV, plus we pretty much only slept in the apartment.  Building is old and as others have stated really needs a re-model.  It was definitely clean enough and everything was serviceable.  If you are expecting high end hotel accommodations this is not the place for you.    For the space we had and the price we paid this is an awesome deal.  Two hotel rooms to accommodate our family would have been double the price.   Add in the great location and the ability to make meals when you need to and this place is a home run for a family visiting Manhattan.   At this price point it gets five stars in all categories except a four in cleanliness as we had to re-wash most of the dishes before using them.  Will rent it again on our next Manhattan trip.

Me and my friends stayed for a month in Stephanie’s place. When we arrived we found a really nice place located at a very family oriented and nice neighborhood in a great location very close to the subway station and bus stops (very convenient!).  On the hand, we had some issues regarding the temperature control (we cannot control it) because the entire house is separated in 3 (or 2 maybe) different apartments. This also scared us a bit the first day since we didn’t know there were other people living in the other apartments.  Also, these doors have a “do not enter sign” which could be, for me, a little nicer signs.  The rental had everything we asked for and even more (food, appliances, etc). Very good wifi, televison with Netflix and Disney+.   All in all I highly recommend this place I would only suggest Stephanie to try to let their guests control their own temperature somehow since in the upper right room it was very cold.  There was supposedly a plumber that had to fix the problem and never came.   However, the month was one of the best months ever! The place is very comfy and has everything we need (only lack a pair of chairs maybe in the kitchen).  We thank Stephanie very much and congrats on this amazing place. Would come back in a heartbeat

This place should not be on Airbnb. The apartment is dirty, that man never cleaned the bathroom, it's disgusting. The room does not have a key and is left open while one is outside, and that man comes in to visit, one feels insecure leaving the room open. The room has nothing covering a window and the neighbors can see you while you change. The smell of marijuana is unbearable, we tried to leave very early and return late to avoid being in the apartment and even then the nights were a torment because the smell of marijuana was very strong and sometimes the host made too much noise with other people he invited. He left his clothes thrown everywhere, he never cleaned up the dirt that was everywhere, he didn't take out the trash and it smelled disgusting. In the room there is no place to place suitcases comfortably, for two people the room is very small. There is a pipe in the middle of the room from floor to ceiling where the water runs through, this makes too much noise and gets hot, you can get burned with this, it is dangerous and noisy. He left us without toilet paper for a day. The first day we arrived I asked him to please clean the bathroom and avoid smoking at least at night, and he told me that he was not going to do either of those things because the rent was cheap, and I had nowhere to go because my time was limited and I couldn't move. The TV only works for Apple, we were never able to see anything. It is close to the subway, 1 and a half blocks away, but there are many homeless people. In general this Airbnb sucks. I have stayed in other places in New York at the same price or less and they are much better. What an unpleasant experience.
Booking was as described. Would definitely recommend and book again. Thank you so much Maricia for responding quickly to our questions and making our trip as stress free as possible.

The place is comfy looking but you hear noises from neighbors upstairs and next door (the other roomies if they are loud. They aren’t flexible with check out times regardless of the situation, I was almost kicked out. But one day I got locked out and nobody responded either via WA or Airbnb messaging. Also me and my roomies had problems with a noisy lady next door (another roomie) and we even had an argument as she was totally rude, discriminatory and inappropriate (she slammed doors and seemed uncomfortable with the presence of others in the property) and all the host did was telling her to calm down somehow (which sort of happened but the lady remained noisy and all that we basically had to deal with it ) so I would never return to this unpleasant place where a host does not move a rude person for the sake of the others . The way I was almost forced to leave was also rude, so they seem like all they care is the money and not the comfort of anyone. She did not even said a proper gbye

We missed our flight I needed somewhere close by JFK to stay until our next fight which was early in the morning. The room was super cute & very aesthetic! Plus they had surroundsound and a huge TV which made watching scary movies even more intense!!  We regret not staying there for our full trip.

New York is expensive and we all know it, so I wouldn’t complain about the price! Mariel and Jennifer were very kind with me and that’s undeniable! Location is just fine since the A train is very close and handy; you can be in the middle of Manhattan in 20 minutes! Good restaurants around too! The cons would be the stairs (definitely don’t go if you are older than 40 or too tired to think of going up 100 steps in the middle of the day to rest and go back in town later)  I had my mom with me and the stairs were definitely a problem for us! Even for me they were not easy; I know Mariel let this clear here but you can only understand them once you have to climb them; and if you are in a group of women, I’d suggest arriving during the day, Washington Heights can be scary at night, visually speaking!  But again, it’s all about New York!

The pictures were deceiving. The outside and leading up to the apartment is very dirty…my expectations may have been set too high. When we walked in the building, it was so disappointing. There was even a homeless man sleeping in the stairs. The heater/broiler is very loud. The neighbors partied all night. They provided towels but no wash clothes….the location was good. We were able to walk easily to the subway.

If your looking for a place to stay in the city the location is pretty amazing. Sketchy walk in and the elevators are super small. The room itself was small, a couple of us ended up hitting our heads on the stairs walking around the room and no one there was above 5’9. Don’t recommend the middle bed  its lumpy & there are no windows. It’s just as u see it in the photos, the bare minimum but the price is great for the location & amount it sleeps.
Great place. Great host, he answered every question and was very helpful. Helped us out with a stressful situation regarding leaving. Super nice. A great stay. Recommend.

The place has a few good spots - wooden floor. A/C in 2 bedrooms and fans in all 3 bedrooms. Our stay was mostly uncomfortable. The Furniture were very dirty, old and used. Worst of all, the place was ant infested. My kids were walking around on their toes scared to go into the kitchen, dining room, living room and bathroom. I had to buy ant spray from stop & stop and dollar tree for my kids to spray where they found the ants so they could sit and eat and watch tv. I don’t know if Airbnb has a policy to retrieve money from evil hosts?

Dalia's place is very good in terms of walking distance from the train to her place. All the streets were well lit, especially the street with a studio on the block. Me and my friends never felt unsafe staying out late and coming back at 11,12 at night. Great coffee shop with good coffee nearby is definitely a plus. The place also matched the pictures, and having a washer+dryer is another good addition. I didn't leave a 5 star review though cause the Brita pitcher was dirty. I did ask Dalia for a new filter in which she was very responsive in ordering a new one for us, but I ended up not using the Brita pitcher despite receiving new filters coz the sponge for cleaning also seemed old and not very sanitary. Another reason why I didn't leave 5 stars is also coz there was no body wash in the bathroom. I was just a little sad coz in the amenities it was mentioned it would be provided.

Me and my friend felt very unsafe. The neighborhood was dirty and infront of the house were men who said bad things to us. Also the window was very leaky that you could hear everything on the street and all night police cars were driving with sirens infront of the house. The Corridor and the bathroom was smelled like weed and one bathroom was full of empty and dirty shampoo bottles. Sadly, I can say it was a bad experience and not a nice and safe neighborhood (especially for a young woman).

Susan was a great host. I really enjoyed my stay there and never felt unsafe in the neighborhood. A bit more attention can be placed around the cleanliness of the rooms but the value is outstanding. Communication could be better but a good experience overall!
This place is a steal! Super comfortable and fully equipped with everything you need. We loved this place and will definitely return!

My friend and I stayed at this place for 3 of our expected 5 nights.   Pros: Excellent location: near to times square, many subway lines, range of food options. Floors were clean, sheets/towels were clean.  Quiet at night even with proximity to busy ave & times square.  Check-in, while a bit complicated to find to the key, was explained well by the host and I was able to follow the instructions.   Cons: The pictures on this listing are somewhat deceiving. While yes there was a couch, a full bed, a twin bed, a small kitchen area, an AC unit, and a bathroom, everything is very run down in comparison to the pictures. The side of the fridge was badly burned (hidden in the listing photos). There was apparently some major water damage since the photos were taken, as the trim/floor area by the table was badly damaged. Additionally, everywhere there was a gap in the trim, the repair was not done with caulk as it should have been, but with expanding foam, which contributed to the run-down look. The table and dresser were covered in cheap plastic tablecloths and there was an unexpected fabric wardrobe in the living room area. The couch was stained and that is not visible in the listing photos. The walls were dirty and many parts of the ceiling in the living room area were patched with something that was a very different color than the ceiling paint. The outlet next to the couch did not work, but other outlets did work.   The kitchen sink faucet has come loose from the sink and is somewhat challenging to operate.  Scented soap was used for the sheets, which can be off-putting for some people like myself who are sensitive to smells.  While the sheets were clean, it did not appear the comforters were clean.  The tiles in the shower are coming apart and some were poorly repaired with caulk. Additionally, the shower is badly stained.  We were only provided a single washcloth and towel each for a 5 day stay but were able to find other towels to supplement them in the dresser. There was not even a towel provided for drying hands in the bathroom.  While an iron was provided, there was no ironing board that we could find and the iron appeared to have gunk on it that made me nervous to use it on my clothing.  There was no place to hang clothing or any drawers available for holding our items.  What finally drove us to leave early was the smell from the bathroom. When we arrived, there was a diffuser plugged-in in the bathroom that was giving us a headache so we unplugged it. We later found that after using the shower, a mold/mildew/unpleasant smell filled the bathroom and filtered into the small room connected to it. It became challenging to sleep in the tiny bedroom next to the bathroom due to the smell. That bedroom also didn't have access to the AC unit when the door was closed.  The unit is very dark even in the middle of the day as it is a rear ground floor unit surrounded by buildings.  The host asks that you do not let anyone know that you are renting through AirBnB, but instead say you are subletting/are friends of the host. This made me more uncomfortable than I expected.   The host asks that renters clean all dishes used and the fridge before leaving, yet still charges a high cleaning fee. I have not experienced this with other AirBnB units, but usually do it as a courtesy if I have time.
The walk to the closest subway at night can be scary at times. The heating in winter can overheat the room. However, overall it’s worth the money.

Abdallah was an amazing host, his apartment was super clean, well stocked and beautiful with all the plants. I want to highlight how amazing my host was, he went above and beyond than any other airbnb host has ever done for me. He asked me what groceries I liked and he always went to get what I wanted and stocked the fridge with what I liked and he also dropped me off at the JFK airport which saved me time, money for an uber, and stress. What an amazing and warm human being I loved his company he is the sweetest! Also great value and location in brooklyn subway was accessible all the time.

Not sure if it was a one time issue but place was filthy upon check in. Stained sheets and broken shower. Left over food in the sink. Just bad. Communication was poor as well. I liked the location because of the park but overall it was an unpleasant stay.

So I have to say, I was initially kind of reluctant based on a former review. However, given how good of a price it was relative to the hotel pricing nearby in Midtown Manhattan, I couldn’t refuse. The room was of a decent size and had the basic amenities one would need. The furniture seemed a bit outdated, but the bed was comfortable. It seemed like some of the walls needed some work and the carpet did seem a bit ragged, but overall, it was a steal for the price I paid given it’s location. Check in was pretty easy and smooth. Front desk knew my reservation immediately after telling them my name. Overall very happy with the reservations. Would definitely recommend if you needed a place to crash for the night and isn’t overly picky.

We enjoyed our stay at Ishmael’s place.  It is very clean and the description and pictures are accurate.    The location is great.  It is close to bus stops, and subway. Also an easy walk to grocery store and drug store.    I definitely recommend staying here.   Ishmael communicated quickly with us and checked with us to make sure check in was smooth.

This place is great! Very spacious and clean on the inside. It’s only a block away from the 145th subway stop and you don’t even have to cross the street for it! The area itself has its own charm, and has everything you need: coffee shop, 4 convenience stores, liquor store, smoothie and vitamin shop, all within a few steps.  We never felt unsafe at all in this area at any time whether it was 2 pm or 2 am. Jeff was attentive to our needs and made sure to help us with any questions we had. He even let us know we were welcome to go to the roof and use the cute seating set up there! It is very nice up there. I would highly recommend this place to anyone who is looking for an affordable large space in Harlem with easy access to anywhere in the city. Thank you Jeff!

Good place for a short stay. Very close to J train (2 minutes walk). The room is clean and the host is hospitable.  However, the surrounding can get sketchy at night so I don’t recommend you wandering around the neighborhood at night.

Jeff and Mike's place is brand new - clean and organized! It was perfect for the four of us - my sister, parents, and myself. Not to mention, it's on a convenient and strategic location. It's surrounded by grocery shops, restaurants, pharmacy, coffee shops, a gym, and metro station which was an absolute help as my parents already have a hard time walking long distances. Overall, I'd rate it almost perfect except that you have to be cautious at night as there are homeless people that roam around sometimes. Although police visibility is high too so it's still a safe place. I'd definitely recommend their place. Check out their place - it's perfect for family!

Very nice place, I would recommend. We stayed here as a couple, and we were very comfortable. We had to work and do zoom meetings during the day, and we could stay at the place and have a quiet place to work.  The hosts are very welcoming and receptive, we had great discussions !  They also were very responsive: we wanted to have a bit more of shade in the room during the night and they immediately added a curtain for us, which solved the problem. Also, the neighborhood is very nice for those who like laid back coffee shops, thrift shops and street art.

I booked this place because of all positive reviews, specially concerning the location. So Ill go through the good, the bad and the ugly now, so you can take your own decision.  The good: The room is clean and corresponds to the pictures. The hosts are friendly and welcoming.   The bad: First of all, be prepared for a very thorough interrogation by the hosts before they accept your booking. Do you know the kind of questions that border protection officers ask you at the airports? Multiply that by 4 and there we go.  You will be sharing a regular-sized apartment bathroom with the hosts and a respectable number of guests, depending on the occupancy at the time. You will be handed 5 keys to lock and unlock 4 different doors, each of them with their own particularities regarding the way they can get locked and unlocked.  The mattress was way too soft for my personal taste and there was a plasticky thing under the sheets that made  that very present plasticky sound every time  you turn.   The ugly: It is definitely not a premium neighborhood, to put it mildly. All the reviews stating that it is a great location are hard for me to understand. On the short walk from the rundown subway station to this space, be prepared to walk through a creepy lot with a crashed and abandoned car, lots of trash on the sidewalk and on the properties along the way and people walking and standing with an intimidating body language, that might make you consider use the opposite side walk.

I stayed here for a month, and ultimately enjoyed the area and the management was very responsive and friendly. I want to make an extra note of how kind the housekeeping and front desk staff was! Very lovely people.  I have two negatives that contributed to my three stars.  1. Due to the conditions of the cooking situation, I wound up contracting bacteria and mold poisoning when cooking food in the apartment. I’m not blaming anyone, as these things are impossible to see, and the staff did their best to clean it immediately, but it did quite a damper on the experience.  2. While not the management’s fault, as a young woman I find it important to make note that there is a group of mostly men that sit on the front steps smoking, and I dealt with regular harassment from them. I never felt unsafe, but it made it very uncomfortable.
Little bit dangerous area but everythings okay

Amazing location and so unique!  We needed a place ideally within walking distance to the Barclays Center and this was perfect. The use of the driveway sealed the deal and made a trip to the city stress-less.  The neighborhood is very cute and there are so many things you can walk to and explore.  The carriage house is very roomy and includes a cute secluded patio to hang out on -- you definitely don't feel like you're in the city.  Justin was easy to communicate with and personally called us before we arrived to explain the check-in process and codes to get in.  We also appreciated the later checkout time (11am) -- it gave us time to sleep in, go get some breakfast and relax a little bit before we needed to pack up and leave. This is a perfect "home base" if you're looking to visit NYC!

Nice and clean apartment, in very good condition, as advertised. The area isn't the prettiest in Brooklyn and can scare some people at first, but we didn't encounter any insecurity problems, other than a few misfits we encountered late at night.  The skytrain is quite close, even a little too close because you can clearly hear it with the windows open.  The apartment only has one bathroom and one toilet, which is too tight when all 4 bedrooms are occupied. You have to be patient when using the toilets. Using the common areas in the evening is also difficult if you don't want to disturb the other tenants, as the bedrooms open directly onto the living room-kitchen.  Having spent 10 days in this apartment, we would have appreciated a change of towels and sheets, especially since it was very hot, but this was not offered to us.  Finally, the host was not accommodating and refused to let us leave our luggage for a few hours in the lounge while waiting for our departure to the airport, which we have never been refused in all the Airbnbs we have done. This spa gesture helps you avoid lugging your suitcases around town while waiting to leave for JFK.  We recommend for those on a tight budget, but if you can afford to get closer to downtown Brooklyn, I recommend it.
Was very clean and host was great. The location was a little scary at night so don’t go on your own, but was great as really close to a station to get into New York easily.

Ally’s place is very clean and closely resembles the pictures.   However, a week into our stay we were shocked to find a mouse in the apartment. The mouse came out not only on that one occasion, but two more times as well. Upon telling the host they were quick to set up traps, but unfortunately, they kept removing them when new guests arrived which could have been an attempt to hide the fact that their place has this issue.  I don’t recommend you stay here if you’re scared of mice.

The apartment is as seen in the photos. We had very friendly and silent roommates. The neighborhood seems dangerous but it is not, there are many bars nearby and the Dollar General around the corner is very cheap. The kitchen is equipped with everything. I highly recommend it

Very clean and tidy flat. Good sized rooms and bathroom. It was not made clear how many additional bedrooms there were for other guests. That and the very thin walls meant that we were kept awake by other noisy guests getting back late at night. Also the area felt unsafe after dark which is something to keep in mind if travelling alone.

Front room and back upper bedroom smelled of urine our wntire stay.   Reported on the phone to Sammy and he started screaming saying no it didn’t and that the cleaners had just left. Got so frustrated with him that I just let it go. Wasn’t until I brought it up on Chat in the app before he starts saying he would send somebody over to clean it.  Reported to him that his listing showed a washer and dryer but when I got there I couldn’t find them. Told me that I was wrong even though I showed him pictures of the listing. Wouldn’t listen. Sammy is an unpleasant man. I would not rent at his spot again

Pros:  - The host was flexible and responsive -  Pool table was a plus  - Netflix access - Walkable to shops and restaurants  - Smart lock check in   Cons:  The house itself is in MAJOR need of upkeep  - A strong odor throughout  - Broken faucet - Signs of mold and water damage, visible especially in the basement shower - Plastic wrap inside the basement wall air conditioner unit making it non functional  - Dirty walls - Backyard was fully cemented with uneven surfaces making it unsafe for play  - Sliding door and some windows have missing or damaged screens  Stay here if you want no frills and a walkable to the Queens restaurants experience. Do not stay here if you expect a pleasant, livable house.

The house was huge, the location made traveling all over the NYC boroughs and Long Island easy, and the drive way allowing us to park stress free was priceless. The neighborhood also had some good bagel and coffee spots worth checking out. My family of six had a great stay and would definitely recommend.

The apartment is lovely, spacious and very clean. Samuel and Gladys are lovely hosts, took us to the local stores and showed us round a little. Very friendly!  The two bedrooms have loads of the space and the shared area is great. Very good wifi, TV and equipped kitchen. The shower is fantastic.  It’s perfect if you’re heading in to the city and staying there for the majority of the day. It’s about 40 minutes to get in to Manhattan on the subway. The nearest station is Ralph Avenue about a 8-10 minute walk from the apartment. It’s on the C line which is perfect as it goes through central Brooklyn and all the way up the centre of Manhattan. The area that the apartment is in is lovely and chilled although not much by way of bars or restaurants within walking distance. The only slight downside is that the area immediately around the station felt a bit sketchy after dark. Absolutely fine in the day but we usually got a cab either from Manhattan to the apartment or the station to apartment so as to avoid that little bit of walk. Genuinely only the slightest downside and that’s nothing the hosts can control. All round a lovely apartment and host and would 100% go back in a heart beat.
Our stay was perfect! Asiatic was kind and accommodating.  The location was perfect distance to the subway, drivable to the city and the airport access was smooth.  I never felt unsafe, so thank you!

A very comfortable stay and excellent communication with Lucy. The flat is as described, very close to subway and supermarkets and in a rapidly developing part of Williamsburg. The flat and building are new, well appointed and contained everything we needed to ensure a pleasamnt and stress free 4 night stay. Thank you and I hope we'll be back.

Great apartment in one of the best areas of Brooklyn. Kristina was very quick to response to messages and was very welcoming on arrival....we really appreciated the hot drink after travelling in the freak snow storm! Lovely apartment which was very clean.  Would recommend to others. Jo and Rob

Jonathon & Nicole home is the best place, I always felt save and privated in their home, mia was adorable. The jewish comunity of the neigborhood made feel very safe as well, I got around 11 pm and many people were at the street. Nicole's cookies and banana bread are out of this world, is such a lovely gesture, as a guest it made me feel welcome and appreciated. All you need is close to the place, markets, drog stores, restaurants and the kingstong subway station. All you need to have an amazing time in NY.  The house is very beautiful and is so lovely to see the pictures of Nicole and Jonathon. I do recommend to stay with them, you will not be dissapointed at all.

Jonathan has no courtesy for female or solo-travelers. I was threatened to change my reservation with no explanation at 11:00 p.m. or he would vacate me immediately in the middle of the night. I brought a friend over ONE day and Jonathan scammed me into paying guest fees for SEVEN days. When I nicely asked Jonathan for clarification he refused to explain and instead used scare tactics and unprofessionally stated, "its business."     Due to being threatened and scammed into paying fees that simply did not apply to my stay, I decided to depart early. I refuse to stay in a hostile environment and do not tolerate scammers/grown men who use scare tactics on women knowing they are traveling alone and in a new city.   I do not recommend staying here.

Liliana is a great host. The bed was so comfortable and the bathroom was very clean! At first the location was kind of scary but anything bad happened to us. It's a little bit far from the downtown of manhattan but the subway is a few blocks away. I'd stay another time for sure

Friendly and accommodating hosts. They worked with us to check-in early and were very understanding when our flight was delayed. Personal AC and huge TV made the room a nice place to come back to after a hot day exploring NY. Quick walk to a supermarket and 3 subway. The bed is so soft and comfy! The bathroom is shared so sometimes you have to wait to start your day and the neighborhood can be sketchy at night. Overall would recommend.

Harlem is very interesting, it is quiet and easily reached by subway.  It's not unsafe. The people on the block were friendly and after seeing us so much they greeted us. The room is comfortable and clean. It is quiet at night and you can rest very well.

Very clean and comfortable and a quick walk to the subway station. Communication was excellent. We felt very at ease during check in and the host was always available via phone. The area around the outside entrance was pretty dark at nighttime, but we never felt unsafe. An excellent place to stay in Queens!

Very clean apartment is well located, the owner is very welcoming and available because we arrived very late due to a delay in our flight, the metro takes a good 20 minutes, quite lively area, lots of shops

I’ve stayed in airbnbs all over the world & this was the weirdest & most unpleasant experience I’ve had. I always book a place to myself whenever possible as I like my privacy. This time i was headed for nyc to spend time with a girlfriend who lives there, as well as to do some work related stuff. The apartment is nice, nothing special but fine. Checked in, left, didn’t spend night #1 there as i was at my gf’s place.  Next night she stays over with me. We arrive late, she leaves early for work, i walk her to the station.  That’s when it gets weird.  I came back to the place & found i had a message from the owner saying “you have had someone stay over so you owe me more for that”.  My response was unprintable. Yes, when i looked at the “House Rules”, it’s in there. But honestly who checks the house rules? Especially if you’re used to treating a property with respect, you understand the ground rules.  The really disturbing part was realising I was being watched by the owner. I assume there are cameras. I hope they’re not inside the apartment. But I have no idea.  I didn’t sleep there any other night. I felt too angry & freaked out by this behaviour. I just came back to change. The place turned into a more expensive version of a Port Authority locker.  I have a 100% flawless record here because i treat airbnb owners & their properties with respect.  But respect goes both ways.  Don’t stay here if you want a place to yourself. You can find somewhere they don’t want to squeeze every dollar out of you with creepy micro-management.

Amazing really big for a one bedroom ! Exactly as seen in the pictures! Great building and right in the center like a 5 min walk from Balthazar or Starbucks and I don’t understand why other comment mentioned noise- the Appartment and building lobby was dead silent! Stayed from may to July 2022. Very close to 3 metro station - 6, b,d and q! It was perfect- no communication with owner because it’s not needed, building manager very nice and polite! Where orders stuff from Amazon it was left in lobby - felt very safe with that? Nobody steals or anything… and laundry room is in the basement- it’s ok everything is clean and smells clean.. but yeah kind of scary lol… but way better then some chip laundry mat with coins!!! Perfect stay… will come back for sure!

Pros:  -private entrance with parking spot - 10 min walk to subway station - relatively safe neighborhood - exactly as advertised  - Apple TV is a nice touch  - literally took 20 minutes to TimeSquare   Cons: - loud neighbors during late hours of night / thin walls - getting to subway station involves walking through dark underpass, lots of homeless people sleeping there - no heater  Overall, this was a perfect stay for those who are going to be out of town the whole day. We did not mind that the neighbors were loud, but it became an issue when they were consistently making noise from 1-3 am. Thanks again Tashi for letting us stay at your place, we will definitely keep this place in mind when we visit New York again!

The place is just what you see in the photos. Impeccable and very comprehensive, Tashi is also very attentive when explaining everything. The place is also close to the subway and a supermarket, and the area is safe. Of course, if you are in the room in the afternoon or midday, the children will be playing on the upper floor and the noise may bother you. But the positive thing is that they go to sleep early so if you are out sightseeing all day you can rest easy. I recommend it.

We chose Karina's apartment because it is located a stone's throw from our daughter's house who has lived in the area for several years. At first glance we were shocked by the insistence and severity surrounding the internal regulations but hey, we are reasonable adults and booked anyway thinking that it was probably a slight act of caution.  Arriving there we actually felt a lot of stress in terms of reception, Karina categorically refusing to communicate with our daughter to organize the handing over of the keys, active surveillance cameras at the front door and all the regulations posted on all the walls of the apartment. The apartment itself was perfectly cute and spotlessly clean and when we asked for an extra blanket because we had been cold at night, Karina provided us with a duvet the same day without question. The only downside is that the furnishings, although clean and neat, are quite limited for 2 people. A tiny high table with 2 stools for the dining area and 1 single chair to sit on, not one more chair. The television in the room only allows you to watch it from bed (we never managed to get it to work but maybe we did it wrong). The mattress is wrapped in thick plastic that is uncomfortable and noisy under the sheets and the air conditioning placed in the window opening lets in cold air and the sounds of trucks on the street. The area is still quite nice, with many shops very close and a number of nice bars and restaurants within walking distance.
A very great location, and an easy place to stay stress-free!

We will DEFINITELY return! Beautiful home. Loved Sam's personal touches. Wonderful that he had snacks, cereal , water, juice, milk, and several other food. So welcoming. The kitchen was well appointed. Linens were top grade. Plenty of extra bedding and cozies (which we needed as the weather turned quite cold). Awesome helpful extras like bringing us an extra floor mat the day it rained giving us the extra room we needed to get into the apartment and remove our shoes. Sam has amazing taste. HIs place looked straight out of an HGTV show. The pictures online VERY accurately reflect the space. Think oversized studio with the bedroom seperated by french doors. The pull out couch in the living room was supringly comfortable. The neighborhood felt safe, but a tad sketchy in a few nearby areas as we walked about (we were travelling with two toddlers so were hyper vigilante). Felt VERY safe in Sam's home. Sam is very responsive to any texts or calls we made and accomodated our every need. He was out on the sidewalk greeting us when we arrived (SO welcome as it was very cold and we had babies). There is a fantastic park a ten minute walk away (a lesser one two minutes away), fantastic coffee shops minutes walk as well as laundry and groceries. All was very convenient. getting to the metro was equally easy and quick.

My husband & I live in Long Island City but booked this space because our wedding was going to take place    at a venue close by & we needed a place where my bridesmaids & myself could get ready beforehand. However it was just myself & my husband that stayed here overnight. The place was wonderful & clean. I loved the decor inside & it had everything we needed/was listed. However the issue I had was with how I was treated & spoken to by the host. I found it very condescending & very stressful. I believe part of their concern was that I was having more than 2 people staying at the location & I could understand how’d they’d think that since several ladies came over to help me with items for the wedding the day before & day of. I don’t take issue with being asked about this but I think there are better ways to communicate with someone when you’re essentially running a business & they’re your client. Regardless, it all turned out just fine.

Alexandra was an amazing host! She was easily reachable through texting and very fast with her responses. We loved the room we stayed in. It was clean, comfortable, and had the bare necessities such has shampoo and conditioner. We had our own set of keys and access code to the building which gave us our independence and made us feel like a real New Yorker. The location of her building was a short walking distance to the subways (only a few blocks). The area was pretty safe. We never went out alone after dark and never felt unsafe in the area. We'd rent from Alexandra again in the future!

Tali's apartment is very clean, and very pretty inside, we were unlucky because when we arrived and throughout the stay the facade was under construction, beyond the aesthetics it was a little dangerous because the workers were working which blocked the entrance to the door and made it inaccessible and impractical especially with suitcases... The apartment is far from the various metros, it is 15 minutes on foot, walking quickly and far from the city center of New York, for a first visit and a short stay I do not recommend... Tali is a very kind and accessible host and the apartment conformed to the description, very clean and very pretty inside. There are some very nice restaurants next to the apartment and Tali left us a book with various useful explanations and the names of restaurants to try, nearby supermarkets, pharmacies and medical centers. We thank Tali for her apartment and her welcome.

Very good value for money comparing to all other overpriced without reason places. Room exactly as seen in pictures. Really quick responses. No trouble finding and entering the apartment at all. Kind of unpleasant that the hole building constantly smelled like food from the other apartments and the stairs kind of tiring. Sheets didn’t smell so freshly cleaned. Apartment very warm and sunny. Toilet a little small.
Host is very unwelcoming and aggressive.  You cannot make any noise, not even talking a little loud.  The building has cameras everywhere and  it feels really creep in that apartment.

Sophia is a very nice and communicative host. She deals with each of her guests and provides additional information on the city  We appreciated staying in her very clean room. The second floor is nicely furnished and the living room offers a lot of space. Unfortunately, it took one hour to go downtown to discover Manhattan and the neighborhood we lived in seemed to be sketchy at night. However, the quality matches the price completely.

This was my first air bnb experience. The place itself is very good. I ran into few problems. One the location is terrible if you are traveling to NYC. You have to take a bus to get to a subway. I ended up Ubering most of the time because I work close to Manhattan.  Second was the host. She tried to charge me at the end extra $40 for early and late checkout. I checked in at 1 pm and the way it was worded on the direction; it said something of effect of before 10 a.m. Night before check out I packed all my things and put my suitcase in the closet as instructed by the host when I spoke to her. The room was left empty so she could clean it for the next guest. She did not mention any additional fees then tried to charge me for luggage storage when it says on her that sometimes she allows this as space permits. No mention of fees until I picked up my luggage. She had been harassing me for the fees ever since making this a very unpleasant experience.

The apartment was really nice and clean. It was bigger and more beautiful that it seemed on the pictures. The kitchen was wonderful as it had everything you need for cooking at home. It has a laundry a dryer in the basement too. The A/C was also working perfectly.  The location was really convenient as there were a lot of small businesses in the block. There even was a 7-eleven just crossing the street.  My girlfriend's iPhone's charger broke so we asked the host if we could borrow one. He was really nice as he lent us his own charger until we bought a new one!  The only drawback is that you just have to be careful at late nights with the subway station in 116th street as there might be strange people that may make you feel uncomfortable or unsafe.

Perfect welcome. Communication with the perfect host. Delicate little touches like little things for us in the fridge when we arrive. He helped us find a vehicle to get to the airport when we were leaving. One small thing to point out, even if the location is well indicated in the description, it takes a good hour's journey by subway to reach the center of Manhattan. The area is quiet and the host was very attentive to our requests. Our return flight was at the end of the day and we were able to leave our luggage in the lobby and pick it up when we left. In short, we highly recommend!!

J's place was clean and comfortable. The apartment was well furnished and could accommodate quite a few people. My family and I enjoyed the convenience of J's place. The R train in literally just around the corner. For just $2.75 a person we were in times square in 45 minutes without switching trains. We walked all around the neighborhood, checking out all the local shops and eateries. There is a drug store, sushi, pizza, deli and package store also right around corner. We walked down to Bay Ridge Ave. And caught the ferry which again for $2.75 each we were taken to wall street in the financial district. The ride is breathtaking. You see the Manhattan skyline and go directly by the Brooklyn bridge. The question friends ask me most about our trip was "did you feel safe?". While staying at J's place, walking around his Brooklyn neighborhood, or riding the subway did my family not feel safe. So from the moment we walked in and seen the refrigerator already stocked with milk o.j. and eggs. Or when J's father brought us up a handrolled loaf of 12 grain bread. We felt safe secure and knew this was a place we would come and stay at again. So I highly recommend J's place for anyone interested on a visit to the Big Apple.

Other reviewers accurately represent my experience.  I really enjoyed having a comfortable, spacious and well stocked place to stay before my  fourth plane flight in two days.  The day of my arrival had been stressful  with three flights and no boarding passes ahead of time.  I was grateful for Roseann's very warm greeting on my arrival.

I’m theory this place is nice. The hosts were very kind and we had no issues checking in or hearing from them. However, if you are taller or more on the plus size this Airbnb is not one to go with. Although they put in the description at the very bottom that the room is on the 4th floor they do not mention the flights of stairs are extremely long, and extremely narrow making it really exhausting to go up after a rainy, snowy or tiring day around town. Rough. Once you get into the apartment the beds are nice but the loft ceiling is very close to the bed so in the morning it’s hard to sit up without hitting yourself even if you’re someone like me who is 5ft tall. In the description it states this Airbnb has a washer and dryer so we planned and packed for the ability to wash our clothes especially after the heavy rainfall. There isn’t a washer or dryer in the apartment. And speaking of long rainy days if you want to warm up in the shower it will take about 10 minutes for the water to turn lukewarm and 15 to turn hot. And water pressure is non existent. Made it difficult to go anywhere quickly if we needed to shower. And finally, back to being plus size. I do not usually talk about my size in these comments but I think it is important. Bother my friend and I are plus size woman and the bathroom is so small (smaller than a cruise bathroom or hostel) we almost could not even get into it passed the door let alone to the toilet - very stressful for us and embarrassing that it was so uncomfortable. Overall I think if you don’t mind the stairs or can fit in the bathroom and don’t need to wash clothes this place is cute and well kept. However It was not for us..

Alexandra's accommodation was perfect for my NYC stay! I felt very comfortable in the tastefully furnished apartment (as in the photos) as well as in the house in general and the location was very good for my main interest (jazz clubs, especially in Harlem). The area didn't feel unsafe, especially because "116th Street" is a larger street where there are many restaurants and shops and cars also drive in the evening and at night. I'm even after midnight from the metro station or from clubs such as: B. "Minton's Playhouse" (along the major streets) went to the accommodation (which may not be for everyone). In the area you will find everything you need for everyday life, even a 24-hour supermarket at the 116th/Lexington Ave metro station. Carrying a large suitcase up (and down) is admittedly a bit tedious in the narrow stairwell, but that only happens once on vacation and the good news is that "4th floor" is only the 3rd floor. ;-) And yes, the warm water takes a while depending on the time, but it comes! The bathroom is very small, but that wasn't a problem for me (1.89 m). The bed was comfortable and the small kitchen was very practical (a sharp knife and a wine glass would be the icing on the cake, but it's not that important). Otherwise there are many details available, including things like a hairdryer, umbrella, etc. (and a washing machine and dryer in the basement - for a fee). Conclusion: Alexandra's apartment was ideal for my needs, I highly recommend it, especially because its size and amenities make it a rare offer in NYC for the price.

We’re a family of four with two kids and we’ve spent 17 nights in this beautiful apartment. Parents who travel with kids – and we love to travel – know about the challenges that this can involve. However, its safe to say that we felt right from the beginning that we were in good hands. After a long haul flight from Europe, we were welcomed with milk and bread in the fridge and coffee, oatmeal and other supplies in the pantry. The apartment is lovely, cosy and huge and has everything you’ll ever need, so we felt right at home. The kitchen is well equipped with lots of tools, all kinds of saucepans, skillets, bowls, a coffee maker etc. Our hosts went far and beyond to make our stay unforgettable – they even provided cots for our little ones and kid friendly soap. Due to some rain we spent a couple of days indoors. A couple of days indoors with kids – scary right? Nope, no problem whatsoever in this apartment: Our kids were happy campers and never got bored with all the toys, the crayons and books that were provided. We highly recommend this place for travelling families (and for everyone who’s looking for a wonderful apartment with all the bells and whistles) – not just because of what it has to offer inside but also because of its location: A big playground for all ages is literally just across the street with grocery stores, bodegas and drug stores all near by. A bagel store, where we bought bagels every morning is just a 3 minute walk away and it’s right next door to a pizza place that makes amazing New York pizza. Oh, and the subway station (R-train) is also just a stroll up the street and it goes directly to north Brooklyn and Manhattan. So guys, thank you very much for having us, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay here and hope to be back one day.   Jan, Marijke, Madison, Sam

Excellent place, if you don't mind climbing stairs or the subway being 2 blocks away, if you go to NY you have to walk a lot.  At night it seems unsafe but it is not.  My neighborhood in Mexico is more unsafe.

Upon entering this AIRBnB, I was immediately writing a bad review.  This place is old and worn out. I had a very important event that evening and first thing, started looking for a hair dryer.  I searched in the bathroom. I searched in the closets (which were full of 'stuff' and reeked of moth balls).  No hair dryer.  The ammenities on the listing did not include a hair dryer, but I thought I'd check anyway. I called Nina to ask.  Phone call - Me: Hello, is this Nina?  Nina - Yes.  Me: I'm your Airbnb guest on 55th St.  Nina: Wha?  Me: Your guest on 55th St. Nina: Who?  Me: 5 5 street Nina: Text, email, bye.   Ok - so Nina doesn't speak english - which is fine.  Although she communicates quite well via email.  I have a suspicion that "Nina" doesn't really exist, and the person in the profile pic isn't her.   Anyway - no hair dryer.  Whatever.  I went and bought one. The apartment.... I took pics and I wish I could post them.  This apartment is as shabby as they come.  The pics look cute - the apartment is NOT cute.  There is junk everywhere!  Empty pickle jar on top of fridge, expired food in fridge, multiple extension cords twisted up on the floor  in the living room. Shelves in the living room have an assortment of crap on them (screws, 6 wine openers, a lighter, a foam paint brush, 2 pairs of tweezers).  The couch is a futon with the saddest pillows that look like they came from a Korean foot spa 16 years ago.  They left me ONE towel rolled up on the bed that smelled like moth balls.  The toilet paper is Scott - which is the cheapest TP made.   Go stay at The Hudson - it's cheaper and SOOOOO much nicer. I really don't know how this place has every gotten a good review.  You don't want to hang out there for a minute. Positives - check in is easy, email communication is good, balcony is the only saving grace.

Alejandra is certainly friendly but her accommodation is not very comfortable. You must have your key to go to the kitchen and the bathroom which are accessible via the landing common to all residents of the building. The bar below is very very noisy and the windows are single glazed. There is no loan of bath towels. A dog lives in the apartment too. The padlock on the outside is difficult to open. The room is clean, however the cleanliness of the rest of the living areas leaves something to be desired. Strong point is the location close to the 50th street metro and two bus stops. We were also able to leave our suitcases while waiting for our flight, which was very practical.
This place is absolutely a steal when it comes to a realistic price in a prime location. Our host was absolutely amazing and very responsive when it came to any sort of inquiries.

The house is gorgeous and the location is fantastic. Was a great weekend getaway. Mike and Molly were very communicative and the whole process was stress free. It surpassed any expectations I had from the pictures (which were obviously already very high).

The space is four flights of stairs up, with access to a two-story space (kitchen, bath and living room on first floor and bedroom on the second) along with an adorable rooftop view of the NY skyline. The bnb is across the street from a school and is in a safe part of town. Don't be afraid to wander around - there were lots of community gardens, bbqs, convenience shops and friendly folk happy to lend a hand or directions.
