Classon station is only a 5 minute walk away, and the MTA was easy to navigate.   The space is very uniquely decorated with beautiful artwork and conversation pieces, and the host's roommate was very amenable to my sister and I the entire trip. We were given free range of amenities (the shower was fantastic! Gorgeous bathroom) and we took full advantage. The bed was so comfy some days we didn't want to leave it! The one downside is that the sun rising in the morning made the room heat up BUT there was a small, portable Vornado fan in the room that cooled us right down - just leave it on during the evening and you'll be fine.   My sister and I jumped at the price of this bnb and honestly it was more than we could ask for, which meant we had more money left to spend on NY experiences! When we did encounter a minor problem during check-in, it took Hubert less than 10 minutes to get back to us from Europe! He maintained consistent communication and helped us with our issue immediately. 11/10 would rent again :)

Check-in was a breeze.  My schedule was crazy, so Eva sent me the keys ahead of time, which made travel a lot less stressful.  It was much appreciated.  Apartment is extremely clean, has ample closet space (even for a month-long stay like mine), and is literally around the corner from the J, F, and M.  Eva was an amazing host and very responsive to questions when I had them.  I would stay here again without hesitation.

The photos are not accurate representations of the space. The space is old and and has been remodeled but the floors are not level so doors do not shut. They have laminate flooring but the floors are which causes the floors to sag and creak through out the space. There was dust on all the windows and in the cracks of every room. The front door to the space does not lock. The walls had dents and scratches everywhere. The walls have not been painted in a long time and had yellow spots on them. The doors were chipped. The bedsheets were still wet when we checked in. The bathroom had dirt on the floor. The neighborhood is unsafe.

We never had internet or wifi. The neighborhood is a little sketchy with an abundance of litter on the streets. They give extensive cleaning directions including floors, countertops, sinks. We didn't cook only used coffee maker, so maybe it's for people who cook, but it made us wonder why we were charged a cleaning fee.

It has been an absolutely exceptional experience staying at Amazing Oasis. Both the owner and host are very kind and professional. They made our stay absolutely stress free. Place is professionally clean, tidy, organized and absolutely warm. There is nothing we couldn't find. For instance, the place was equipped with wonderful toys for our kids following our note we have boys!! We received immediate support and communication whenever we needed. We loved the whole experience and we fell in love with the place. Thank you so much! Will definitely come again!

The apt was just as it appears in the listing. We never felt unsafe and public transportation was convenient. There were lots of nearby places to eat, get coffee, or groceries as well. All the people we encountered in the neighborhood were friendly. Would definitely recommend staying here! Thomas was also very responsive and made the check in and out process painless!

This was me and my family's first airbnb stay, and we were so delighted with our stay! I think the best part was the location. To be completely honest, at first we were a little scared on our walk from the 50th St D train subway at night since the houses were older than we were used to. But I have to say, seeing lots of families out and about and good foot traffic gave me the sense that this was a safe neighborhood. I was right. Once we reached 8th ave, right around the corner from the apartment, we were floored...this was our heaven! Never had we seen so many and such good food options and groceries right outside during our vacation. We felt so at home surrounded by the hustle and bustle of working class families, authentic (and cheap too) Chinese food, and easy access to everything from coin laundry to boba. We learned later that if you get off take the N train instead and get off at 8 Av/61st St, it's an amazing safe lively walk home amongst tons of folks through Chinatown even late at night. My parents repeatedly told me how happy they were living right at Chinatown and getting all our meals taken care of so easily thanks to this. It was a godsend. About the apartment itself, it was truly our home away from home. As others have mentioned, it is no frills and very simple. The remodeled kitchen and bathroom vanity is really nice and exactly like the pictures, but aside from that it's not a designer-finished apartment by any means. I would take that any day though given the amazing price and the huge space we got. Lily so graciously set up the futon for us (which was really comfy!) so that our family of four slept like kings. We had so much space. The living room where the futon is is kind of in the middle though between the two bedrooms and the kitchen/bathroom/exit, so whoever sleeps there doesn't have a door necessarily, but there is the benefit of being closest to the air conditioning unit. The two bedrooms each have a huge queen bed, and one room even has a closet. It was not completely dark at night since you're facing fluorescent lighting from signage of a shop across the street, so if you need pitch black to sleep consider bringing a sleep mask. But we didn't mind. The sheets were super soft and light and fluffy. The carpet and everything else was pristine and we could tell it was vacuumed thoroughly and extremely clean, the bathroom was spotless. And then there were a number of nice little things like umbrellas in the closet, a hot water kettle, extra pillows in the closet that made us feel so well taken care of by our host. Lastly we never met Lily in person, but she was an extremely sweet and thoughtful host through text. She always responded to my...

We had a very pleasant stay in Todd and Ashta's apartment. This one is located on a pretty street of brownstones in Brooklyn. The area is lively, lots of restaurants are located around. The metro line C is not far away, just a few minutes on foot. The apartment is very bright and very warm and comfortable. We felt very comfortable. Communication with Todd and Ashta was perfect. We were able to leave our luggage in the apartment on the day of departure even though our flight was a little late, which allowed us to enjoy New York a little longer!  This apartment is to be recommended!

I booked this apartment for my parents and their friends and they loved it. It's a very basic apartment that is spacious and very clean. Location is great since it's right by Brooklyn Chinatown. Only downside was that the neighbor was rude and accusatory which was very unpleasant for me. But Lily and Tim were great, and they were flexible with our check in and check out. They were also quick to respond to our messages. Thank you again Lily and Tim. Will be booking this apartment in the future when my parents return!

The place was very minimal with furniture (no dressers) but was exceptionally clean and beds were comfortable. The place was very spacious. It was hot and humid in New York when we went but fortunately there was an A/C window unit in the living room so we slept with our doors open so the rooms could be cool. The neighborhood had great culture (Latino, Chinese, Jewish community). Tons of little markets/ restaurants in walking distance. Walked the streets late at night to get some snacks and never felt unsafe nor threatened. Had a GREAT experience with our first Airbnb stay! Thank you Lily!

We could not have asked for a better place. Everything was ABSOLUTELY spotless. The beds and linens were of good quality and SO comfortable. Everything looked brand new - from the carpet to the bedding and curtains.  Huge apartment, tons of space!! The kitchen was well stocked and really nice. Beautiful bathroom.  Large windows throughout the apartment. Very quiet - just around the corner from everything.  We were in Brooklyn for a very stressful family matter and having such a comfortable and quiet place within walking distance to so many amenities was exactly what we needed. My mom is not used to the city and she felt safe and comfortable.

We stayed for two weeks at Linda’s place. It was a very clean and spacious apartment for the two of us. It is a 8 minute walk to the subway, which takes you directly in to Manhattan . It does take 40 minutes to get into the middle of Manhattan.  There is a very nice deli / supermarket at the end of the street , they are very friendly and provide som nice breakfast to go.  The neighborhood is very diverse and it’s got an array of different kind of people.  Around the subway , there could be some sketchy people. But the people around the neighborhood seemed friendly.  Uber eats works great and food can be delivered from a great number of resultants within 30 minutes.  Linda was very friendly and answered all our questions and accommodated us nicely.

This is a truly clean, very comfortable, safe & hospitable home. A most convenient location in Chelsea, next to the 1 or C/E trains and the vintage living police station. I regret giving other stays similarly high ratings because Ania’s  is superior to those. I loved the fresh fluffy white towel. Too often I suspect the towels are reused unfortunately. The home is open to your use with nice amenities though I didn’t need much.

Ania was an amazing host, she made sure to be there at my arrival to give me a quick tour and was very clear with communication throughout. I unfortunately ran into several insects during my stay which made it unpleasant. I found Ania’s listing to not be as clean as I’d expect. I saw many areas in the bathroom that could be better cleaned. I also found a large bug in the bathtub.  On top of that, there were several mosquitos in the unit due to the windows being wide open. She told me this was the first time hearing about this as an issue for her guests’ stay. The listing is definitely stylish and charming but the bug situation needs to be addressed for future guests. It was also easy for me to find the building and locate subway stops nearby. I only stayed one night here and will be finding other accommodations due to my experience.

As a single woman, the location was excellent in that a police station was just doors down.  The entrance itself was off putting as the steps were filthy and littered, no fault of Ania’s, but if it were my B&B knowin a client was arriving, I would @ the least sweep the steps. But that’s me. Our communication was poor two hours prior & at my actual arrival, but again that was not her fault.  Some of messages were only half received through Air’s portal and it caused stress for me. But Ania is a straightforward lovely woman and all was well going forward.  *she was very kind in that she washed my breakfast dishes.

The description is pretty accurate. What you see is what you get. Quite spacious for two with a room to put your bags and clothes in so that was nice. Wifi was fast and aircon was a lifesave given it was 30+ degrees (celsius). The L line into Manhattan is just around the corner so perfect for what we wanted. Nice and quite street too so no sleep disturbances. Negatives were just bad first impressions with the graffitied communal entrance, smell of rubbish in the communal entrance/stairway and suspect steps up to the apartment but you get used to it and the apartment was clean. Ana was very quick and helpful with communication so very easy check in and check out which was ideal.

We had a wonderful time staying at Marta's place. A cozy apartment in a really busy bohemian neighborhood, yet relatively spacious for New York standards. Exactly as portrayed in the pictures -- no unpleasant surprises. The location is outstanding, really in the heart of the East Village, half a block from Tompkins Square Park and within walking distance of literally dozens of bars and restaurants. Would definitely stay here again in the future.

Location with easy access to Manhattan, the neighborhood itself is not dangerous, you still have to be careful depending on the time of day, but there is no problem with that, the apartment is quite correct, warm, with a shower, a large and comfortable bed. Ed, Brandon's host who lives there, is very correct and helps you with everything you need, highly recommended.

Brandon's place is a great stay if you are looking for a place to crash, shower and use the kitchen, and you plan to be out and about all day. For what it is, the rate is fair and appropriately priced. The apartment is located in Harlem, within 5 minutes walking of the Subway 2 and 3, which can easily connect you to anywhere you need to go. Upon arrival, I had an issue with Brandon's roommate Eddie smoking in the apartment and spraying an insane amount of cologne to cover up the smell, which was extremely nauseating. Gratefully, this was quickly resolved by calling Airbnb and speaking to Brandon. Brandon had a cleaner come a few days later to make the stay more clean & comfortable. Overall, I enjoyed my stay and it was very affordable for 2 weeks in NYC, and perfect for what I needed (the bed is nice and large - I think it's a Full or Queen, but very firm, FYI - could use a topper for more comfort). Lastly, like many parts of the city, such as the neighborhood of Harlem, can be dangerous/sketchy. You need to have situational awareness and not walk around distracted with earbuds in or playing on your phone. You should do the same when in the subway. If you walk like you know where you are going, make eye contact with folks wandering around the street and subway when coming back late at night, you will be safe. I have been to NYC many many times and my husband is in law enforcement and shares his tips for safety with me, so I felt safe in Harlem as a single female walking around alone because my eyes were open and aware and I made eye contact with folks wandering around so they knew I saw them and I am not an easy target if they had bad intentions or opportunistic intentions. Moral of the story, just use your head and common sense and don't be distracted. Overall, great stay!

What can I say about this accommodation?  Just total perfection for 6 people (two adults, two teenagers, two children)!! Well located with charm in the heart of Brooklyn, less than 25 minutes by transport from the center of Manhattan! An excellent price despite a busy period. Darryl is an available, understanding host (despite the average English of a French couple). All accommodation instructions are clear and precise. Everything is functional, beauty products, cleaning products and even fresh eggs! Very pleasant after a transatlantic flight!! The neighborhood is quiet and lively with Prospect Park in the immediate vicinity. We recommend 200% and it is certain that our next stay in NYC will be at Darryl's!

The apartment was a great place for our family of 7 adults, a 3 yr old and a 9mth old to celebrate a special birthday and Christmas/New Year's. It was a little squishy at times but it was large in comparison to other New York accommodations. Looks just like the pictures. There were plenty of towels, bedding, kitchenware for everyone. The kitchen was great to cook in and beds were super soft. The J/M train was a 10 min walk (but there is no lift and lots of stairs which made it difficult with large suitcases). The A, C, E line was about 20mins walk. It took about 40mins for us to travel to midtown. The neighbourhood looks a bit sketchy, but we had no issues. Brendan very kindly provided a Christmas tree and decorations for us, which was a lovely touch. We didn't get to see Brendan, but he answered our questions relatively quickly, given the holiday season.

Staying at Steve & Virginia's place was great! The location was good. Walking distance to the train, buses & a strip of shopping (supermarkets, banks, coffee shops, restaurants, and much more). The neighborhood is nice, full of large beautiful homes and very safe. I never felt unsafe in any way walking from parking blocks away at 2 or 3am. Street parking is available but gets more scarce as the night goes on. The unit was was very clean and just as pictured. The bedrooms were large and comfortable. The covered terrace off the master bedroom was a great space to relax and read or sip coffee while getting fresh air and taking in the cool breezes. The entire space was comfortable. My family and I felt right at home during our stay. Steve & Virginia are very pleasant. They responded to communications right away and were available at later times of the evening as well. We actually plan on rebooking Steve & Virginia's place today! Staying with Steve & Virginia was definitely a pleasure!

A fabulous apartment, the perfect size for our family group of 7. I loved the chunky furniture and the beds are super comfy. The train station is only a few minutes walk away and we used the trains all week. I did feel a little unsafe in this neighbourhood and after one journey on the train late at night I didn’t do that again.

Carlos is a great host! He communicated whenever I needed. He even caught a parking spot for me, which was very helpful. Just be sure to ask him how to operate his radiator. It can be a little tricky to do it on your own. Lastly, don't be afraid to talk to him regarding anything. He is very outgoing!

Overall, we had a great time staying at Carlos' place. He was very welcoming and even took us to the supermarket on our first night. The location of the apartment is very good, considering the price. We never felt unsafe in the neighborhood and the connection to downtown Manhatten is good, too (there are several subway services and it takes about 30 min to get to central Manhatten). The apartment was indeed clean and very spacious. Carlos didn't mind that we used the kitchen for breakfast and sometimes dinner. If we ever return to New York, we would probably stay here again,

We have so much to tell about Carlos  and his apartment. Very clean like he have written and seems like we are alone in the apartment because he's a quite person but very friendly as well. The neighborhood is calm, not dangerous,  it doesn't matter what time you walk around. It's very close to line 1, A and C of subway station. From there you can go anywhere.  There is a 24 hours Mac Donald just one block  away and the very famous store Marshalls is about 3 blocks. You can walk to the New Jersey' s bridge and Carlos always encouraged us to enjoy the  city. Carlos, you definitely were the best host that we have  ever had. Tanks for all your hospitality  and trust.

Carlos is a great host. He was very nice, friendly and helpful. My stay went great and stress free. There are many food chains within walking distance. I would absolutely stay again at his place and would recommend it to others.

The accommodation was nice and the neighborhood was good so we never felt unsafe. The people there are very friendly and courteous. Carlos is a great host and helpful if you have any problems. The train station is only 6min from the apartment and the train leaves really often.

Carlos is a very kind person, although we did not talk or live with him much, he always behaved in the best way, he gives you a lot of privacy and the room as well as the bathroom and kitchen are quite clean. As for the location, it is quite good since the subway is a few blocks away and is quite direct to the main tourist areas, the neighborhood seems a little dangerous but we always arrived at night and we never had any security problems. I highly recommend Carlos's accommodation since in terms of price-quality it is one of the best options.

He stays there too, he told me and my friend  that it was his apartment. You’re not going to be alone. He’s only in there by himself, no wife. Never heard of the host staying  there with you. It was pretty creepy

The apartment wasn't clean when we arrived, but Carlos quickly got our room ready. Unfortunately the bathroom was really unpleasant, but it was enough for daily laundry. The room is completely ok, the bed just squeaks a lot with every movement. Unfortunately you can hardly open the windows, at night it is not an option as it is very loud outside. The air conditioning helps, but is also very loud. The area is very interesting and noisy, but well located, only 20 minutes by subway (3 minutes away) to Central Park. Carlos himself was really nice, gave us tips and looked after us well. Communication via cell phone was difficult at first, but then it worked.  Overall it was a pleasant stay, ideal if you're out and about all day anyway.

Cons: 1) It's a ground floor unit and it's clear Albert has some pets of his own (or maybe it was just a previous guest?) but regardless, it was pretty musty/smelly when we arrived.  You get used to it, and opening the back door helped. 2) It's a little run down, especially the bathroom and kitchen need some grout work, that sort of thing.  3) Not much in the way of natural light. 4) It's one of those places where Albert clearly actually lives in the apartment, and it's _full_ of stuff.  Not as much storage space for guest items.  Cluttered vibe. Pros: 1) amazing location, the park is great and super close, and there are _several_ subway lines that go through the area so it's easy to get into any particular part of Manhattan or Brooklyn you want to go 2) _great_ value, really inexpensive, especially for a pet-friendly place with a backyard. 3) Easy access and easy communication. Stress-free as it could be. 4) Nice queen bed.  Slept like a baby.   Overall a totally fine experience, especially for the price.

It was  my time using AirB&B services and it was great. Our host Anthony has a nice apartment with all you need for tired travelers from out of state. Apartment was very clean, welcoming and comfortable. Special touch for me personally,  our host provided good quality teas, coffee, cookies and also cold water in the fridge. It was a life saver! Anthony was quick to respond to our messages, provided us with all  information we needed.  Having comfortable stay relieved a lot of stress of our New York visit. Thank you, Anthony!

Where do i start from !!!  Cons: 1. Way too noisy neighborhood. Loud music is being played until late night and they also start playing from around 7am. Too difficult to sleep.  2. No lift . 4th floor apartment. It was too difficult to carry our luggage. 3. Shady Neighborhood  4. Unclean house 5. The host used the bathroom & his clothes were hanging around.  6. The host probably shaved his beard and did not bother to clean the sink. Very pukish feeling to see this 7. No toilet papers . This is basics which is expected . We had to ask for this 8. No liquid soap in bathroom to wash hands. 9. The bathtub was not cleaned 10.No Ac/heater working  Pros: He allowed us to keep luggage before our check in time .   Very disappointed to book this place. I will suggest to look for other options and think twice before booking this place.

We stayed in the apartment for 11 nights and only met Wesly the night before we left. Being a shared apartment, I think the hosts should go more, to verify that there are no problems. In our personal experience, one of the guests did not care much about cleaning after using the bathroom, which was quite unpleasant. That's why I think someone should go and clean the common spaces, because no one likes to clean other people's dirt. The garbage cans in the bathroom and kitchen were full and no one emptied them. Also, one day we dropped something under the bed, we looked to pick it up and it was all full of dust and even socks from previous guests! So I think there should be more care in that. On the other hand, when we had the problem with one of the guests, we spoke to Jessica and she was very willing to help us. He talked to him and he fixed it, so that's notable. Wesly was very kind in recommending things to do for New Years. Another notable thing is that the apartment is very well equipped, there are many kitchen utensils, and the rooms have an Apple TV.

We stayed at Wesly/Jessica place for one week. We were a little scared by the neighborhood, which is anyway safe. The area is a little far from the city center but thanks to the subway we were able to get there in about 30 minutes. There were three main problems: first of all, the host did not reply to our messages nor to those of other guests. Therefore, we could not use the TV (which did not know properly)  but we also could not know how to make it work because actually the owner did not reply to our messages. We could not use the Apple Tv as well because we needed the code, which was not provided by the host. Finally, there were no shutters in our room but just curtains, thus we would be waken by sunlight every morning (this was not written in the description of the apartment). In spite of these issues, the place was clean enough (the floor was a little dirty), warm and welcoming so we appreciated our stay.

Our stay at Wesley & Jessica’s place  was great and fitted our trip perfectly! Only about a 20 min subway ride into Manhattan. We did find the neighbourhood to be very loud throughout most of our stay but there seemed to be some sort of sports event at the end of the street going on, it did start getting quite frustrating near the end of our trip when we were lacking sleep but hey ho! The toilet stopped working on the second day of our stay but a quick message to the hosts and by the time we had got back from our day in Manhattan it was fixed! Quick and easy communication and a lovely clean apartment all round, for the price compared to other accommodation it’s a steal!
A bit further from the subway, in a semi sketchy neighbourhood . Air conditioner had some issues , half the room was hot and the other half cold ..

Worst Airbnb I’ve ever stayed at. Very unsafe and very sketchy. My guest and I got a hotel and left immediately because we felt so unsafe. One door has an extremely easy lock to break into. The type of lock you could put a pin into and open the door with.  No soap or hand towels, only two very low quality bath towels on a stained mattress with no sheet.   Construction workers coming in and out knocking on our door. We were only there for an hour and multiple times we had so I’m knocking on our door. Stay away. Terrible experience and a waste of almost $700. We ended up staying in a hotel for less than the price and it was so much better.

First two days/nights it was unbearable cold then we found out that windows cannot be closed and paper towel was used to fill the gaps. As it was unbearable cold we had to fix the window. The bathroom  was left with dirty towels hanging in the tub, used razors, shower was hard to use as the paint  was chipping and we had to clean the paint parts all the time while using it as the drain part was covered with paint parts. A lot of dust, It seemed that it was not cleaned for a long time. No clean bed linens/towels  so we texted the host and we were told where the new package is so we had to go and wash it before using it. The place where washer/dryer was so creepy that I was scared to go down and three of us had to go together each time. Bed linens on the master bad was dirty. We went to bed and there was hair and you could smell that someone was using it before us. So we had to wash that too. It was a long cleaning day for us. Easy access to trains and location was very good.

The apartment is very clean and comfortable. Rito provides very thoughtful amenities like water and juice for you along with some light snacks. That was most welcomed after traveling. They provide local suggestions for food, groceries,and transportation. The neighborhood is very active but we never felt unsafe as everyone was friendly. The place is beautiful! Thank you for being a great host and making accommodations for our schedule.

The hostess is very nice, communication was uncomplicated and you received a quick response. The apartment is small but cutely furnished. In addition to the hostess, another student lives there as a sublet. The guest room was very small, the floor and the bed were uneven, so you had the feeling you were lying crooked. There is an air conditioner right next to the head which is loud and where the filter needs to be changed. The air was unpleasant. The cleanliness was ok, but didn't quite meet my needs. For these reasons I decided to check out 2 nights in advance.

This place was extremely unsafe, we were unable to stay at our Airbnb during our trip due to harassment of the neighbours and people in the area. The place is not secure. The apartment itself is slanted and unclean. The host was not helpful in trying to come to a compromise to obtaining a refund due to us having to book an emergency hotel for our stay. I would never recommend staying at this Airbnb as you will be unsafe and scared and it will ruin any trip to NYC.

Amazing Location.  Spent 3 months interning in the city, and overall loved staying here. It was often just hard to get in touch with management. Multiple times they came into my unit without telling me beforehand and I asked serval times to be notified so I could be there, I worked just around the corner. Other cases they were slow to respond or took a while to come fix things such as a bird that was in the hallways for over a week and was attacking me every time I left or came home. Large place for New York.

Amy's place is a cute hideout in Brooklyn, but I expected a lot more quality for this price. Amy and Alesh were friendly and very accommodating to us! They gave us suggestions about places to eat and using the subway, which were very helpful! The bathroom was newly renovated and very nice, as well. However, the other reviews and listing description made it seem like the neighborhood is super friendly, but it really depends on what street you're on. Some streets, I felt like I had to be extra aware of my surroundings and we saw a guy get his wallet stolen a block away. I, also, gave it 3 stars because there were smushed bugs on the walls and ceiling. Along with that, the price for the quality of this place seemed unequal (I've stayed in houses for this price). If we come back to the city, we will definitely look into something nicer in a better neighborhood. If you're just looking for a place to lay your head at night,  this place will definitely do.
Place was fine just depends on who’s staying in the other room and their cleanliness and habits. Close to Manhattan with easy access to busses and trains, but does seem very sketchy at late night.

What can I say...the room is amazing. It's a great place to bring your significant other, and experience what the hostess has to offer. She was able to provide a nice collection books to read (I recommend the kite runner) and a bottle of bubble soap, as you take a lovely bubble bath to relieve some tension and stress. I could go on, but I'll let other guest enjoy their experience. As they enter the room and visit the neighborhood, who knows...you might smell fresh bread in the morning.

The stained bathtub, a lot of things stored in the hallway of the house, mop, toothbrushes, nothing to do with the photos...the portal with a bad smell. For €93 it has been a real scam. Little or no cleaning... the hostess sleeping on the sofa in the living room, since there were only 2 rooms, and both were occupied. In fact I haven't slept there. TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE and the worst thing was the money lost... almost €100.

After the arrival a little stressful: by taxi from Newark we expected 55 dollars but it was 90 (plus bridge toll?) anyway in the middle of the night we didn't take any other transport! Then a little stress again because we couldn't find the keys: they are hidden in a black padlock of about 15 cm (don't look for a smiley or anything else, it's all black - hung on the gate at the bottom left of the entrance) we called Eric who answered immediately - even though it was late and was close to coming - fortunately we found it in the end! Regarding the apartment, the location is great because quite central - supermarket right next door - completely consistent with the description - just a little noise (some nights more than others) in the bathroom but frankly take earplugs and a mask (no blackout curtain) they will be useful to you on the plane anyway! Because once you lie down: the dream! A bed so comfortable that you just want to walk all day so you can enjoy it in the evening!

Cute and affordable basement studio apartment offering private secure entrance and awesome location!   My boyfriend stayed here for a weekend in June. It was in the mid to high 90s outside but this place stayed cool - probably low 60s without us having to do anything. I honestly am not sure if air conditioning was on but I don’t think so because we didn’t hear anything. The bathroom and kitchen were  clean and functional as was the main area. The bed was comfortable. No issues!   The only thing I’d really warn people about, if you’d call it that, are there were a LOT of house flies around the outside entrance during the day. There wasn’t a smell or obvious source of what was attracting them and they didn’t make it inside or land on us or anything, but if you’re afraid of bugs this may be something to consider.   The host replied to our messages promptly and was kind and gave our privacy. I think we may have seen her once in the courtyard but I’m not sure.   Overall, great stay, great value, and great location in one of my favorite neighborhoods. Would definitely book again.

The studio/apartment is true to the pictures, its nice and clean and it uses every inch of space efficiently. The kitchen is fully equipped and tea and coffee are provided. Another reviewer said that it had a few mosquitoes at the door and some ants which is true; however they provided bug spray  which we used on the front door and some surfaces. We also kept all the food in the fridge and this didnt seem to be a problem.  For us the main issue was location. The neighbourhood is not hipster and upcoming but rather gritty and with trash everywhere on the streets. While we didnt feel unsafe walking around I would say we kept our neighbourhood outings to a mininum. There is a nice small uruguayan restaurant 10min walk, otherwise we didnt venture out around the place much. I was surprised at other reviews giving great points for location. Yes it is close to 2 subway lines (within 10-12min walk) but I would have l sacrificed that proximity for not walking amongs trash and (at night) rats.  The host was great at communication and made the check in process easy

Upon arriving I got the keys from the padlock (there were 4 keys on the key ring) I didn't know which was which and the door was hard to unlock. It was hot outside and there was no ac (should have been said right away in the listing). No microwave, toaster, or oven, just 2 burners. Bathroom is very small and tight. Shower was so small that when I turned around my butt stuck to the shower curtain. The 'beautiful garden" was just a table and 2 chairs surrounded by flies-not much to look at. Centipedes were present and at 9:20 pm each night a snake would slither by the window next to the bed in a strike position (it was outside the window but was still very scary.)

The location is amazing. Coffee shops liquor, drug stores and laundry facilities all within a block or two. The AC worked well, and it was bigger than I expected. The decor and area was perfect. Easy check-in and check out

There were lots of positives— great location, very pretty apartment, and incredibly comfy and luxurious bedding and towels! Eric was very kind to let me drop my bags early as well. The reason I could only give 3 stars is because the curtain rod to the left of the bed collapsed one night. I tried to fix it and discovered the whole ceiling bracket is dangling and practically about to fall off. I was eventually able to get the rod to stay up, but the rest of the stay was uneasy and unpleasant lying in bed wondering if the pole would collapse on me again. I messaged Eric 3 times when this happened, but got no response. I also feel like the value is not there— while the apartment is nice, it should say upfront that it’s on the 4th floor with a very narrow staircase and no elevator, which made it difficult getting bags up. The door also doesn’t even open fully and scrapes agains the floor. The trash can was very small and it seems unreasonable to have to lug garbage and clean the place when I’m paying such a hefty price and additional $155 cleaning fee. Overall, I enjoyed my stay but would not return again.

Unique airbnb in Brooklyn with friendly hosts. Supermarket nearby, trainlines are about a ten minute walk - easy to get into Manhattan. We participated in some great art tours in the area. Lots of vintage stores and cool places to eat and drink. The hosts were super friendly and responsive and we really enjoyed our stay there.   While the airbnb itself is awesome, Brooklyn (Bushwick) in general had a slightly different feel than the last time I was there. The pandemic (like in many big cities) has increased poverty and there were more obvious cases of unwell people around on the streets and on the subway. While we never felt truly unsafe, there were times we felt uneasy when we entered some residential areas. I think anyone traveling to NYC at this time should be mindful of the impacts of the pandemic on the community and just be a little extra cautious.

This property exemplifies the spirit of Airbnb. When looking for the perfect stay for our travels, I want it to be easy, I want it to be clean, and I want good communication. Carlos’ apartment checks off all the boxes and then goes the extra mile. This home is a basement apartment in a freestanding single-family house, so you aren’t dealing with people on every side. There’s an individual upstairs in the main part of the house, but in several months of staying there I’ve never actually seen her. Rarely can I even hear her. That level of privacy is unusual in NYC. There is a front door parking space available at your private entrance for an extra fee and the charge is well below garage rates. It’s most definitely worth it. There are so many little things that make the home inviting. There’s brand new flooring, a removable shower head, a screen door to let in air, the microwave is over the stove to maximize open counter space, the garbage cans are directly outside your front door for easy access, a new fridge, a washer-dryer combo, good outdoor lighting, a ceiling fan in the bedroom, and A/C for the warmer months. I respectfully disagree with the previous reviewer; the beds are great and I sleep quite soundly. You have two twins plus a queen and I think the couch might be a pullout. They’ve done a great job with the furniture arrangement to comfortably maximize space. It’s not too busy and there are plenty of spots to stretch out. Good availability of towels and extra blankets. The red 1 line for the metro is a 5 minute walk. It’s the end of the line so when you hop on it’s empty and you’re guaranteed a seat. That’s also nice when you’re headed home because you don’t have to keep track of the stops. That 1 line is a major line that connects you to transfers at several spots and goes direct into Times Square and beyond. I never felt unsafe in the area; there are security vehicles for the nearby school that patrol. It’s also rather surprisingly quiet. The local contact for the property is a genuinely warm individual and very quick to respond to any issue. I just don’t think you’re going to find a place that makes your stay in NYC any more effortless. Parking, washer dryer, subway, A/C all in one place? Yes, please!

Lovely four floor apartment in central Harlem. There are lots of great restaurants withing walking distance. The owner Rob is extremely helpful with everything, especially for the first time NYC visitors, from parking to our baby's bathtub to things to do to around the city. He lives in the building and we are meeting him everyday. He gave us good suggestion based on our daily plan. Try the sidewalk taco and des ambassades😊

Great spot in a great neighborhood! I stayed for a week during which I worked remotely most days and spent most evenings exploring the city. The wifi was awesome, which I have found is not always the case in Airbnbs. 7 minute walk to the subway that connects you to pretty much wherever you want to go in the city. Lots of great coffee places, restaurants, and grocery stores within a 10 minute walk.  Some of the furniture pictured is no longer there, including the red chair in the living room and the chest with drawers in the bedroom. Was just a bummer that there wasn't a dresser or anything with drawers in the bedroom into which I could unpack my clothes. Also, the bench at the work station has been replaced with one pretty uncomfortable chair. Not a huge deal, my friend and I just worked at the kitchen table or the couch, but just note that there isn't a great desk setup present.  The Latch app they use as the key to digitally unlock the apartment worked great, but we were almost in a tight spot after a long night out when my phone died and I realized I needed to recharge it to access the apartment or contact the host for assistance.   The bedroom is at the back of the apartment so with the door closed, the (very) noisy street below was not an issue. The washer and dryer just one flight up the stairs was so nice (and so rare in NYC!) and the dishwasher in the kitchen was super convenient. The kitchen was well-stocked with nearly all of the utensils and basic ingredients we needed to make simple meals. There were a few dishes that had food residue on them, and while the place was generally clean there were some crumbs and debris on the ground and hair in the bathroom. Not a huge deal but when paying nearly $2k for 7-day stay, I expect it to be pretty spotless.  With that said I would definitely stay again - the location, safety, and general setup in the apartment were worth some very small inconveniences. The onsite host (Rob) was also very friendly and attentive.

My visit to NYC this November was only made better by Mrs. Jaleh. She was incredibly welcoming and accomodating, and helped make my visit stress and hassle free. She even helped me through my awkward arrival and depature times. Her recommendations around the city were very helpful and I'm very glad to have been her guest. Thank you for being a great host, Mrs. Jaleh, I would recommend your place anyday!
We had a great stay at Cami’s and was well situated for great cafes, restaurants and bars. In a neighbourhood where some streets had some slightly scary inhabitants.

Oh dear!  You almost don't know where to start.  So from the beginning.  Cami appeared to be a very good and attentive host - and I am sure she is - though it started to wear a little thin prior to arrival when her house rules were stressed and repeated at least three times and probably more.  I was also unimpressed by the "oh, by the way" message the day before we arrived to say that we would be filmed entering and leaving the apartment by webcam - presumably to make sure we adhered to the rules (no guests, no shoes, no noise).  A bad taste was starting to form.  The first hiccup - and for this I don't blame Cami, though she proved hard to get hold of - was that the keys were not in the key cafe as promised (I assume the previous guest hadn't returned them - possibly as a gesture).  It took a good hour to get it sorted out but comms were a little stressful.  The first impression of the building is pretty appalling.  Granted, there is a lovely buzzing cafe neighbourhood just around the corner, but the building itself and those immediately around it take you right back to the tenement area.  It is an understatement to call it run down.  Filth, graffiti and even a hole in the front door; and the common parts were beyond horrible and dirty.  On more than one occasion, we entered or left the building to find some random sitting on the steps to the front door completely off their skull and feeling slightly threatening.  So on into the apartment.  The first impression was the noise assault on the ears........ from the fridge which was growling like a dinosaur.  The two bedrooms were much as expected, as was the sofabed in the tiny living room, though it was a side-to-side fold down - very uncomfortable - rather than a pull out with a proper mattress.  I had requested that it be made up, but it wasn't and we had to search for linen of which there wasn't much.  However, the worst thing about the apartment was the kitchen and bathroom facilities which were verging - in my humble opinion - on the illegal.  Certainly in my home country of England, they would have been against every law on the statute book.  The "kitchen" was in a tiny nook with stove and sink with the growling dinosaur of a fridge (which, every so often, shut itself down with a howling shudder of death that would have closed down a disco for noise) in the living room.  Dividing said "kitchen" (I think the description said something about preparing a gourmet meal - not on your life!) from the toilet and minute shower was a flimsy concertina folding plastic door that met neither ceiling nor floor and didn't close - much less lock.  It offered no privacy whatsoever but, worse, the toilet was sitting exactly next to the cooker.  I had told Cami in my introduction that we were three separate adults - two women (myself included) in their fifties and my adult son.  I think it would have been honourable and the right thing to do for her to have let me know that the apartment was completely unsuitable for this arrangement and that I would be better off finding something else.  The bathroom was embarrassing to use for all of us and I know that we all felt the need to find a restaurant for the more serious needs of evacuation, as the privacy to exercise these in the apartment was non-existent.  Oh, and did I mention there was no hot water?  As it was impossible my son to sleep on the sofa bed (pretty impossible anyway due to the discomfort of the thing) next to the roaring fridge, we resorted to unplugging it.  So no fridge for the duration; sanity of no horrendous noise being more necessary than milk.  In short this was a thoroughly unpleasant place to stay and thank heavens it was only for two nights.  It was with a huge sense of relief that we said goodbye and - having never written a bad Air BNB review in my life before - I can only advise Cami that she needs to have a major rethink.  And buy a new fridge!  If I try to end on a bit of positivity, the beds in the two bedrooms were reasonably comfortable and the linen had a nice high threadcount.  The towels were fairly new and a decent size.  I can just about see, at a push, that this apartment might suit a couple with young kids where the bathroom would be less of an issue (though the toilet would still be jammed up against the cooker) but that is about as far as I can go.

We stayed for ten days and were provided pre opened bottles of shampoo. Which I did not expect to get anyways so that was very kind of the host to provide. Only two rolls of toilet paper though; which did not last long and only one hand towel which needed changing after a few days. So it would be best to bring extras for your stay if you will be in New York for a bit of time. There is a drug store and grocery store just down the street if more is needed. The bathroom is small and with the cabinet over the sink makes it is very difficult to wash your face.. the host also went into our suite without us being there to pick up items under the bed. There was zero notice and she texted if we were home or not. I indicated we would be back shortly if she needed in. The host then said it was a false alarm and to forget about it. We got back within the hour and items that were there before were missing. I'm not sure the policy about going inside an air bnb or not but a little heads up would be appreciated. The host texts and emails back in a timely manner which I was very pleased with. Check in was a little rough. Our flights were scheduled to arrive at 2 pm and the host agreed to let us leave our luggage there as check in is 6 pm and she indicated she would try for and earlier check in. Once In New York, our plane was late. And we did not leave the airport till 3. I was in constant contact with host with updates of where we were per her request. The host then indicated she was running late and requested my husband and I sit at a pick a bagel or any other place down the street until further notice as you can not stand with your luggage outside the apartment. The host arrived around 4 and went through the instructions of her space (ie: how to take out garbage and open and close the doors. They are very particular about the garbage as they can be fined very easily. I found it best to just sort it the best I could in the suite and then left it at the door ready to go incase i screwed it up as the host talked about the garbage fines and issues with sorting for a few mins. The host then requested us to come back while she cleaned. Long story short we were unable to get into our suite until 7:30 pm and the host still requested the full 60 dollar cleaning fee even after being 1.5 hrs late in check in. I was just very exhausted from traveling... The location is amazing. We walked Central Park every day and the apartment is very close to the q train. Location is five out of...

Even by New York standards, the apartment size is incredibly small (the bathroom/toilet situation is the size of a single cubicle) and I don't believe the value was there in terms of pricing. The host also neglected to mention that there is a camera installed inside the apartment (facing the doorway) to monitor the amount of people entering... it is kind of creepy and unnecessary. We were also not advised about the sofa bed being very broken. The apartment's location is definitely it's saving grace and I think for a single person or couple it would be fine, but totally overpriced for what it is. Camila was pleasant enough to deal with, I would have just appreciated clearer communication.

Beth rocks. Our new year package was a steal comparing to residing in hotel two years ago. Wi-Fi speed was outstanding (more than 150 Mbps down and 175 Mbps up, write this note you will need this when you are traveling). Extremely knowledgeable, made us feel like we are living there as locals. She never minds for late night and keeps breakfast out there until noon. She kept confectioneries for us in the bedroom. Bed was comfy and rooms were just like home. She has car parking in NYC for free. Her cute cats accepted us as a family member. We want to stay at her place again the next time we are in new York.   Muchas gracias Beth.

The place is nice. It did not seem like it had just been cleaned. It’s a long walk from the subway in a sketchy neighborhood. The host did not follow through on check in procedures that she said. So after dragging a 40 lb suit case up to the third floor I had to wait 20 minutes in the sauna of a tiny staircase for her daughter to come figure out which key let us in. It is also a for 40-45 minutes on the subway to midtown. I would not stay here again. I would not work with this host again.

This place emerges you directly into the true feeling of Harlem and it is safe!  I had no issues nor felt in danger at any time.  Fire escape and view of buildings is what I loved!  Everything you would want to see is within reach with the Metro Card!

This was a great place. We just needed some where to stay for the night after a concert and hotels are so expensive in that area, this place was much more affordable and it was perfect for what we needed. The area was a little scary at night and some parts were sketchy but if you find a parking spot right out front it shouldn’t be a problem!
I am afraid to say how much I loved staying at Beth’s house for fear there will be no vacancy the next time I come to Brooklyn! One of the best and I stay at airbnbs all the time for business!
You won't find better hosts and you won't find a better space.  The price they are charging for their rooms is a steal and you should jump on it before someone else does because someone else will.

This stay was unpleasant. The main issue was noise from the apartment above. People walking up there sounded like they might fall right through the ceiling. One day it was a cleaning crew walking around for several hours. One night it sounded like two 300-pound guys stomping around, UNTIL AFTER 3AM. They never stopped walking around. What the heck was going on?  Seriously, it seemed like they were assembling something, or trying to get in a 6-mile run/walk in the tiny space between kitchen and bed. It wasn't just the sound; lying in bed we could FEEL each footstep. Oh, and the mattress is very firm, and there was no way to get more heat. If you are a light sleeper, this place is not a good choice. Sorry to have to write this, but I think it is my responsibility as a frequent airbnb guest, to let you know.

I stayed for 2 weeks here.   1)  Host - This place is taken care of mostly by Valentina's sister Maria. Check in was a breeze. She was always a text message away if you wanted to contact her. In my whole stay I would've seen her like 4-5 times at max. She was always there to help. All in all, a wonderful host.   2) Location - The place is 30 mins away from JFK and should cost you anywhere between 35$ - 40$ to get there via cab (don't book an Uber, use the yellow cab outside). It is around 50 mins from Newark Liberty International. It cost me 115$ to get there. The place is in a very good locality. Silent during nights to get a good night's sleep. It is primarily dominated by Greek restaurants but there's plenty of other cuisines as well. The subway is literally 5 mins walk from the place and since it is the origin station, the trains are almost always empty. The ride to Manhattan takes 20 mins via the N train/W train. There's a pharmacy and plenty of grocery stores as well. Never felt unsafe even for a second.   3) The Room - It is exactly as seen and described. The bed is cozy, the wardrobe has plenty of place for a month's storage, the desk was very useful and filled with magazines to help you explore NY. Also included were earphone covers and earplugs. There's a small TV with complimentary Netflix and other streaming services. The sheets and towels were clean. There's a mini fridge and a stand light which'll be useful if you like to read on your bed. The door is secured by a number pad lock whose number will be disclosed to you (And written on the handle). There's a mini dust bin and a small digital weighing machine.   4) The Hall & Kitchen - Again, exactly as seen in the pics. The hall was clean and the kitchen was very well kept. I'm not much of a cook. I only used the kitchen to get water and in my whole stay I used the kitchen once. The shelves were stacked with items so I don't think you'll have a problem with anything being deficit. The couch is comfortable if you want to take a quick nap too!  5) Bathroom - It was a hygienic and clean restroom. There's a bathtub and utilities (shampoo, earbuds etc) stacked so you're covered even if you forget to get any of em. Both hot and cold water run at any time of the day. The bin in the bathroom was regularly emptied.   Some areas where I believe there were room for improvements -   1) The central heating in the room had some issues but it was kind of solved within a day. It also made noises when active (the earplugs helped). If you are visiting during summer this shouldn't be a hindrance.  2) There's a big pipe running in the toilet close to the wall in the middle that is incredibly hot in the morning (in case you accidentally touch it).  3) The plug sockets in the place were pretty difficult to use as they were old.  4) The apartment is located in the 5th floor (Top most). So you if you have heavy baggage it'll be difficult to carry. But, this also results in good views of the city from the room's window.   However, none of these were deal breakers.  This was literally my first time in the USA and first time using AirBnB. I couldn't have asked for a better host or gotten a better place to stay in. Even as a first timer I felt comfortable and safe and the whole stay was a breeze. 9/10 would recommend.

The door knob is loose and the apartment is on the 5th floor I believe it’s not included in the instructions but it’s good to know. Pretty chill apartment not much noise neighbors are quiet. Nothing shady. I felt safe and the neighborhood is good.

The apartment is great, everything's works well and Alexandra is really kind.. in my personal opinion the neighborhood is not safe and sometimes is scary to walk (4 blocks from the subway) especially at nights.

The most thing I want to call out since it is not in the listing is that this is a 5th Floor walk-up. I could manage alright because I'm relatively young and didn't have a lot of luggage but I know that won't apply to all guests. I do feel like it limited me somewhat, however - I didn't want to just pop out for coffee in the morning etc if I had to haul up 5 stories afterwards. Maybe I'm lazy or crazy.  The building is also pretty sketchy but the apartment itself is very cute and charming and warmly decorated. The neighborhood is lively and has lots of good restaurants. I didn't sleep well on either bed - tried both of them - but maybe other people would be OK with them. There were a couple other small maintenance issues etc but overall I was OK there. I would not return, however.

It is unsafe neighborhood, where sirene went from all directions.  It can tell also that the first door is a heavy duty trellis door. Inside door is the door with deadbolt and look beat up.  From the front area, it looks uncared, dusty. The owner is out of the country.  The door could not even be open. Not a convenient place to get to food or even starbuck. Since the door could not be open I run away to the burger king near by, where people were fighting, yelling to the employees.  It was a scary neighborhood.

Rob's Place is located in a very convenient part of Brooklyn, if you aim to make it into the city. It is only about 20 minutes away via subway. The space is nice, clean and accommodating, but keep in mind that you may hear footsteps of people walking upstairs, on occasion. Rob and Portia are very nice hosts!

Melissa and Jorge provided us with their generous hospitality during a very stressful time for my partner and I. We arrived in NY looking to secure permanent housing and had difficulties with short term housing because we needed accommodations for our two small dogs are well. Melissa's place was a miracle for us and provided us with much needed shelter while we looked for a permanent home. Had it not been for their hospitality, our pets would have stayed behind in AZ. Melissa even offered her second bedroom to our family members when she found out they accompanied us to help with the move. Unfortunately, the hotel cancellation policy was strict. Otherwise, we would have taken her up on her offer without hesitation. Their home was spacious, homey, and close to transportation and restaurants. I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a home away from home. Our deepest gratitude Melissa and Jorge, thank you!

The accommodation was not bad for 10 minutes on foot at the subway station. I asked host to turn on more heat but she sais just cover it with a blanket. It was too cold every night. If you turn on the portable stove for about an hour, the power went out immediately, so it went out twice.The most important thing is not to lock the door in the room. So I was scared every night and even very scared because other guests open our door at night. I think women who travel alone should avoid it. I had to lock my carrier every time I left. Insufficient toilet cleaning. Last time I was packing, I was a little noisy, and the host came up to see if it was noisy. By the way, she knocked like a joke and kept laughing until we answered,  also I was offended when she made a joke like she thought I was coming with my boyfriend and this is why i made a noise.

Unfortunately, staying at Sunnyside was more like a hostel than the Air BnB we were anticipating. Upon arrival, we were allocated to a room with mismatched and incongruous furniture that was unwelcoming and inconveniently scattered, making it incredibly difficult for two people to stay comfortably. At first, we followed the instructions that detailed where we would be using the bathroom and kitchen, which was actually upstairs. This we found to be impractical each time we needed to use the facilities, as there was a kitchen and bathroom already on our floor. It took for the young daughter of the household to give us a proper welcoming and orientation around the place; before that we couldn’t even find the light switch in our room which was inconveniently located behind a wardrobe. Thankfully, she said we can use the bathroom on our floor which was to be shared with the grandmother residing on the same level. To start with the condition of our room, it seemed very much like a last minute effort of planning. The beds were two mattresses that for some strange reason were placed on wheels. The floor wasn’t vacuumed properly, and the room lacked basic amenities like a bin.  Crucially, there was no offer for a rotation of linen and WE had to take it upon ourselves to cover the cost of cleaning towels and bedding which isn’t the responsibility of Air BnB guests. The bathroom we used wasn’t actively tended to, and the bin remained unemptied, soap dispenser un filled, sink basin uncleaned and bath mats not cleaned during the entirety of our 9 day stay. One of our main grievances was the front door which was repeatedly jammed, and locked out not only ourselves, but also other guests outside at unsociable hours of the night which made for an unsafe experience. On that note of privacy and safety, we didn’t have access to lock our own bedroom door when we were out and had to lock our suitcases each time. One strange incident which upset us was finding that food we had kept in the fridge from the night before disappeared early the next day, without asking if it was ours or even informing us that it had happened. While Devika seemed pleasant, approachable and fast at responding, we were disappointed by her inattentiveness to us, we would have appreciated as much as one check in but this failed to materialise at all. Overall, this property suits guests accustomed to a hostel-like environment for short stays but was unsuitable for us.

Concetta's place is a hidden gem!  We were lucky to get a reservation in Concetta's place.  It was perfect for what we were looking for since it is very near my brother's place. It is also very convenient as it is located very near LGA airport and public transportation is just right at the corner of the street.  It is a steal being a 2 bedroom apartment in this area. Definitely a very good value for the price.  Most important of all,  Concetta and her family are very accomodating, understanding and genuinely nice people.  They were readily available for any questions or issues, and addressed them immediately.  I would definitely go back to their place again if I need a short term rental.  I highly recommend this place!  Thank you Concetta, Frank snd Charles!
Stephen's place was close to the subway and a drug store. There was bottled water and the wifi was fast. The air conditioners kept the apartment consistently cool.

Ron is an amazing host. He's super responsive and makes sure you have what you need. The place was very clean. The stairs were a lttle scary but other than that, the place was perfect. Lots of restaurants and stores around

The Appartement of Florence is wonderful. It’s clean, it’s stylish, it’s well equipped with everything you need. Even an Walk-in wardrobe.  Florence was super nice, she responded quickly and offered us a late checkout, so we didn’t have to park our baggage’s before heading to the airport.   The safety instructions of the housekeeper, who took did the check-in/out, were a bit strange at first and gave us a little uncertain feeling. The weed smoking people and the drug counseling center next door did the rest.  BUT: it was just an European first impression. We loved the neighborhood, the streets, the people.   We had a lot of possibilities to buy food and we washed our laundry at 1 min from the Appartement. The subway is at 5 minutes. You should definitely eat at Shake Shack in Harlem, it’s bigger than the others in NY and there are less people.  Would definitely recommend this stay and the area Harlem.  Thanks Florence :)

Perfect spot to live in when visiting New York. The room is large, and has everything you need as a tourist. Allen and Ann are great hosts, and they serve you excellent bagels for breakfast as well as great tips about things to see and do in New York.  The location is perfect, away from the stress of Manhattan, but just a few blocks from the Subway.

The best, Ociel's communication and hospitality. The house was always clean and communication has been constant, worrying about if we needed anything. Total flexibility in arrival and departure and they allowed us to leave our suitcases on the last day since our flight left at 11:45 p.m. If you have never been to NY the area may seem unsafe, but we have been there for 10 days without problems, the subway is two minutes away, neighborhood supermarket nearby, police, etc.

This place was much nicer than expected. Was very clean and the host was very nice.  The only downside would maybe be the location - if you wish to walk into the city, the neighbourhoods can feel quite sketchy. I would not recommend travelling around the area alone.  Otherwise it was a great place and I highly recommend!

This has been the worst experience I have had in an airbnb. The neighborhood, building, and apartment smell a marijuana. It is a terrible place.   I had to book a hotel because I could not tolerate the terrible smelling. The neighborhood also looks dangerous. Five guys were smoking in the door when I entered the building.   Do not go to this place if you want to enjoy your stay at NYC.
Very clean as far as the eye can see , I did come across a centipede which scared the crap otta me but I was fine 😂 10/10 for the stay because me and my guest were the only ones there.

I strive to be a positive person and it troubles me to write this sort of review. My friend and I were traveling to New York for first time ever. We usually would have stayed at a hotel or motel but we stumbled upon this listing and initially thought it reasonably priced, and decided to give it a try. It was definitely not what we expected.  The check-in process was fairly streamlined, not much different than other airbnbs I have experienced. The room itself was fine, containing a twin/twin XL bed with an optional floor mattress. There was a closet for personal items. It was a tad troubling that the room's door locked only from the inside so we were not eager to leave our personal items within the room in our absence but often were not left with a choice.  The kitchen was another story. The fridge and adjoined freezer had limited space. Obviously there are residents living there and it is a shared space so we did not expect much, but there was hardly any additional space for anything of ours without moving around the items that were already in there. The microwave at first was abnormally dirty as if it had not been cleaned in some time, especially considering the thorough cleaning Airbnb recommends. After a few nights, it was cleaned ever so slightly which I did appreciate and take note of. As for the listing stating "guests can use anything in the kitchen," this is incorrect. There were no cups or utensils clearly labeled for airbnb guests to use. Instead, there were notes on utensils stating "NOT for airbnb guests" and cups were nonexistent which was honestly unfortunate since one of the host's selling points was complimentary tea and hot chocolate for airbnb guests. There was a shelf with 4 plates that clearly stated it was for airbnb guests' use, and that was all we were left access to.  The living room is attached to the kitchen area. The TV was not functional once during our stay. I did not bother to inquire with the host as to having it functional because it was not of huge interest to me, it was just another note of my stay.  I would presume there are 4 rooms for residents and guests accordingly. I was understanding that other guests would be staying within the apartment, that the apartment was a shared space, none of which was inherently an issue. We were not notified if/when other guests would be coming and going which would have been courteous information to have been shared. While we were staying we would wake up to abhorrent noises outside of our room such as overly loud footsteps and keys seemingly being thrown around. It is unknown whether it was another guest, tenant, or the host.  On our final night of the stay, we were locked out of the apartment by another guest. Obviously, this is no fault to the host. The host was actually very helpful in helping us get back into the apartment, responding within just some minutes, but it was definitely the final straw of our stay. We left far earlier than check-out time because it became too exhausting to remain within the residence. We switched to an earlier flight and peeled out early morning.  Overall, the stay was not entirely miserable. There is only street parking available which is clearly listed on the airbnb page, though it was sometimes stressful since we were not familiar with that sort of environment. I would say it is in a  fairly desirable location. While we rented a car, we ended up walking to many authentic restaurants and bars nearby because they were within a reasonable walking distance.   Though I do not intend to visit New York again any time in the near future, I would not personally book here again. Above, I have stated merely a personal account of my stay and it is in no regard of malice toward the host.

Great communication and easy check in.  Tosin wasn’t staying there at the time, another air bnb guest was in the other room, so I did not get to meet him but he was quick to respond to any questions. The area felt unsafe for me though, and I would probably not stay there again. If you are a less risk conscious person though you’ll probably be fine. If you’re coming back later in the evening catch the bus which stop close by the apartment, or Uber, rather than catching the subway.

Under the bed was very dirty, which made the room dusty. Unfortunately, the air conditioning in the room was unable to cool the room, which made the place very hot.  I didn't like that there was a dog that kept barking angrily as if it was going to attack me. This bothered me a lot, because sometimes I was afraid to leave the room.  Detail: there is no elevator in the building and the apartment is on the top floor. So anyone with heavy bags, be careful.   Positive points: the bathroom was always well cleaned, the living room and the kitchen too. It really is easy to access Manhattan with the subway that is very close to the apartment.   I believe that to host someone, there cannot be an angry dog ​​in the house. This should be reevaluated by the owner.

The whole house is VERY GOOD and we can tell how much details the host takes care of the house BUT!!!!!! the location is totally not safe for tourists especially Asians and woman. We were checking-in around 7-8pm, were already got followed by the street guy and got stared. the next day, we decide to take a cab to go back before 5pm and finally felt safe.  The host told us there are another guest living in the front room and which it totally fine to us. but the guest came home like 3-4 morning am, and even brought another man with him on the next day. That makes us feel so scary and feel like dont know what to do if bad things happened.   Strongly suggest to help yourself or be award of this area, cause the host is not living with you and will not show up to pick you up.

Eufemia’s room is fantastic! I HIGHLY recommend staying here if you’re looking for a place to get to explore all New York has to offer! Her, and her mother were both very pleasant, and made me feel very comfortable in their home. The price she has listed is an absolute steal for the convenience of the area, and cleanliness of the home. Honestly this place should be booked all the time, that’s how good it is. Thanks again you guys!  Madison

If you’re looking for an Airbnb that doubles as a boarding house for immigrant dayworkers, you found it, but let’s  cut to the chase.  -Sketchy neighborhood,  hard to get to -No food/restaurant options within miles -Dirty bathroom, mold in shower -No towels -No room furniture, one overhead light  -Wouldn’t touch anything in kitchen -A boarding house for dayworkers -No communication from host -Room across from only bathroom in house -Lots of foot traffic all night -Trucks pass by starting at 3am -There’s an infant. No mention of it  I can go on but what’s the point. I can’t recommend this Airbnb. Save yourself time and aggravation,  and possibly your health. Look somewhere else. At least half the blame must be on Airbnb for not vetting any of their hosts.  I’ve used Airbnb  a lot over  the years but this is my worst experience by far.  You’ve been warned….

I knew that this place has no refund policy. But I had to cancel my plans and another reservation just returned my money, even though they have the same policy. I've just asked Eufemia if there is a chance that I can get a refund. She even didn't bother to reply. She knew she already had my money and didn't bother to communicate. Pretty creepy

I stayed 12 days at Edna's place and it was really much better than I expected. Edna is so special, always trying to make you feel like if you were home. She is very kind and the place has plenty of small details that make you feel comfortable. The location is also perfect, you can get there by subway in different ways, it's very good connected. You can be in Manhattan within 30 minutes. The Bronx used to be a slightly dangerous place I believe, but now it's different. I never felt insecure, I always saw cops around. It's also very very close to the Yankee Stadium and a free training field next to it, which I especially value because I needed to train for a competition.  In terms of restaurants and markets, there are plenty, even a laundry in the same street.  In summary, I loved the place and specially the host. Enjoyed our talks very much. I highly recommend Edna's place, you won't regret at all.
Great spot everything was perfect, however there wasn’t no cable, didn’t really stress it though.

[Pros] - Location is not bad as it is 5-10 mins walk from Yankees stadium so it is quite close to Manhattan, also close to JFK. - There were almost everything I needed, actually more than that. It has smart TV, couch, queen size bed, small desk, speakers, wardrobe. Wardrobe is quite small but it was okay because I can just throw my clothes on the sofa. In addition, lamps are not bright enough.  [Cons] - Building elevator’s condition is terrible. It is just not available for a day, sometimes for 3-4 days. You should hope it works when you check in or check out, or when you have heavy belongings. - House rules are extremely strict regarding cleaning in kitchen and bathroom. She gets so upset when she sees two or three 1 inch hairs or some foam in the bathtub or in the sink. And I had to wipe water sinks in the bathroom and the kitchen every time, because she doesn’t like “roaches”. - You cannot put your bath stuff on the bathtub or on the sink, or she gets mad. She seemed mad all the time, barely smiles, quite scary tbh. - You can’t put your food in the fridge for more than 5-6 days, or she gets mad. - When she gets mad, she will say like “I am so much disappointed in you, I feel bad in my soul, in my heart, I am so mad, etc, etc” for like half an hour, in the middle of the night at 4-5 am, I don’t remember exact time, but I was extremely tired from doing some coding assignment, and I had to hear it standing in the hallway. I paid 1500 for about three weeks yet I had hear this when I am exhausted and also she even complained I use too much electricity and I am home all day, which was not the fact. She sometimes turned on water for like hours for her food in the sink, though she complains over and over again because I one time forgot to turn off the lights. During that, I said I’ve never seen a bath tub being used with no stuff on it and she was like “Now I understand it, now I understand why every guest got surprised when they see the bathroom.” Then she weirdly looked pleasant.  Funny part was after all this 30 minutes bs, she begged me for a good review. She kept asking for a good review and when I said that I usually don’t write a review, then she was like “after all I did for you, are you not gonna write a review?”  What could I say? - Honesty, it was very uncomfortable staying in this house.  I can’t even remember how many rules she set. One word to describe this place is “rules”. Also, she works at her work station located right next to the room, and calls a lot, so in the week days, it was not quiet and relaxing. - I also lost one of my packages, but I don’t know how it ended up being lost, and I am not gonna blame this building or the host. But, if I were you, I am not going to send very important stuff to here.  [Conclusion] If you think you are a extremely clean person, and don’t often stay in the house, go for it. There are not many places with TV or stuff like couch, desk, speakers in the room. However, her character is absolutely the opposite of easygoing.  [Recommended restaurants] Happy garden - there is a menu they named ‘Best dumplings in the world’, I don’t know if that is true, but they are really good, at least best among the ones I had in New York.  Avenue Gyro - Pork gyro and their desserts are very good.

The place is well equipped, it has what you see in the photos, my communication with Edna was not the best, perhaps due to my English, however I must mention that a situation occurred that bothered me a lot and that is that she woke me up by knocking on the door in a very impolite manner, saying that I had disconnected her internet, which was not the case, after that I felt very very uncomfortable during my stay, I was afraid to even use the bathroom. Otherwise it is a good space, if what you want is to go to the stadium. I can't evaluate the rest since I only used the room and the bathroom.

Really enjoyed the stay here. Our host responded extremely quickly to all of our questions and was very accommodating to us. The home is equipped with all of the basics you need and is perfect for hosting a large group. We had a 1.5 year old with us and the space was excellent for her as well, as she had a lot of freedom to move around without ever getting hurt.
