Some odd things; we had two guests but there was only one towel, there are potentially three beds (bed, fold-out couch and futon in a room connected to the bedroom) but no extra sheets, and we couldn't find any silverware.  Overall I would say this place is a decent value and worth considering, but again just make sure you check with the host on some of the things above.

The Airbnb is perfectly located in a quiet neighborhood and close to the subway. We never felt unsafe. There are also some great stores and restaurants around.   Doug is a lovely host! He made it a point to make our stay as smooth as possible and to make us feel at home. Which was the case.  We thank him again for his welcome and his precious advice (especially for the arrival).

We stayed 2 nights in her apartment. Good points: Dana & Doug are very welcoming, it's a great & quiet location, close to restaurants, bars, drug store, etc. The bed is comfortable. There is just a lack of cleanliness and the bathroom is very small with a bad lighting, but for a couple of nights it's not a big deal! I would definitely recommand this apartment!

Our stay at Peter Michael's groovy apartment was quite an unforgettable experience, and I mean this in the best way possible. The place is within walking distance to everything from Time Square and many tourist hot spots to the local Village scene filled with various cute eateries. Being two females, we never felt unsafe or uncomfortable with the surroundings. The place was very clean and Peter even went as far as to leave us a goody basket for our stay! :) Overall, it was a fantastic experience and I will definitely stay here again when I visit NYC in the near future.

It was wonderful staying with the Bedis.  The location is quiet and yet very close to Columbia, to Morningside Park, to grocery stores, drug stores, and also to bus lines, including the M60 direct from La Guardia.  The room was spacious.  The Bedis were warm and welcoming.  I recommend their accommodations.

The Bedis are helpful and were great hosts. Just watch out for their tiger- it scared me a few times!  :) Their apartment is in a wonderful location- I loved being so close to Columbia and to the subway station. A great place to stay if you need to be near Columbia. I often came home late and felt safe walking in the neighbourhood due to the security around the campus.

Spacious bedroom and bathroom, with a very practical in-room dining area. Access to the kitchen is appreciable. A downside regarding the dilapidation of the house which deserves a good refresh. The metro station is really very close which is very convenient. Tippy is very available when needed. She was very accommodating so that we could collect our suitcases at the time that suited us best on the day of departure (flight at 9:30 p.m.), which allowed us to enjoy the last day without this worry.

Ade's apartment in Williamsburg was perfect for my needs. It's clean and well decorated, quite roomy (at least compared to NYC hotels), and very convenient. It has a clean, nice shower, a comfortable bed, a roomy sitting area and a writing desk. It also has a small, very practical kitchen that you can use to cook meals when not eating out. There's a medium size flat screen TV in the bedroom, with Netflix, and the internet wifi connection, which is immensely important to me as a tech guy on the go, was lightning fast.  The building is a little old and unkept, but don't let that scare you - the apartment is in perfect condition. Do be aware that it's on the 4th floor and the stairwell is quite steep, so don't stay here if you have a disability or very small children.  The most wonderful thing about the apartment is the neighbourhood. Williamsburg is charming, and there are numerous cafes, bars and restaurants literally a few steps away. I particularly liked "Samurai Mama" and "Snacky", check them out if you're into Asian food. There's also the Williamsburg Music Hall and the Knitting Factory - well known venues where you can sample the local rock bands. And, importantly, the streets felt to me safe enough to walk around alone at night.  The apartment is a few minutes away from the subway station where you can take the L train to Manhattan - a few stations away.  Ade herself was friendly and very helpful. I found her to be the perfect host - responsive enough when I needed her, but she didn't bother me at all when I didn't.  I travel to NYC a lot, and I will be more than happy to stay at Ade's again next time I get there.

Adela's place was absolutely perfect for our trip.  The location is ideal and everything was exactly as advertised.  Plus her apartment is just really cool.  Ade was responsive in communicating upon check-in and check-out and made our trip stress free.    Highly recommended.  -Kris

Adela's apartment was a great place to stay for 2 weeks. The bed is comfy and there's a blackout shade in the bedroom so we slept very well :) there are lots of cafes and coffee shops in the area, and the L and G trains are only a short walk away. The bathroom is a bit small but we got used to it after a few days.

To add to the list of nice things already said about the host and room, the large bedroom has a small pantry with a washing basin, microwave oven, fridge, toaster, basic utensils and window that overlooks the backyard. Wonderfully convenient.  The place is so accessible with the subway, yet it is quiet and peaceful at night against the constant noises you hear staying in Manhattan.  The bed is especially great for people with back problems like me. It is nice and firm, but not hard. I did not flip the bedsheets up to check. But I suspect it is orthopedic. The room is as spacious as the photo suggests and as delightful with good sunlight. Since it has 2 big windows plus another in the pantry, the room is well ventilated by the fresh air around.

My wife and I stayed at Gordon's house over the Memorial Day weekend.  Very comfortable and in a quiet neighborhood away from the crowds and noise.  Very good location - several restaurants (eat in and carry out), deli's, drug store, etc. nearby.  Multiple subway lines a few blocks away.  FREE on street parking.  AND, Gordon was a most cordial and accommodating host.  Thanks for making our stay a great one!

Beware! This listing is NOT as described or photographed. If you stay here, you are taking on a let that is NOT as described. Note: I have NEVER written a bad review on AirBNB, but AirBnB is kept safe by and relies upon truthful reviews in order to safeguard others from being exploited via listings which breech consumer rights as they stand under Trading Standards law. I travelled thousands of miles to stay here based on the photos and description: I was failed by both and in addition failed by AirBnB in not vetting this host and let thoroughly. I told the host and AirBnB that this place was dirty and not as described within 24 hours of arriving there. I took (and provided AirBnB with) over 20 photos of this let, evidencing dirt, rust, dilapidation, general dinginess, poor cleaning practices (I found nuts under the bed left by someone else) and poor workmanship. The bedsheets were creased and smelt of someone else. I was told by AirBnB to stay put and not to cancel the let otherwise I would be, essentially, homeless. Each of those three days involved washing at friends houses. I felt unclean after stepping out of the shower at this let. Three days after my arrival, I was still there awaiting clear direction and a phone call from AirBnB. On the third morning, after a phone call with AirBnB and being told to stay put that things were in process and that a case manager would call me, I left, taking refuge on a friend’s couch. The case manager has still not called. Yes, this place is old (and believe me I love vintage) but this place would need a re-haul to make it suitable as a professional and therefore AirBnB let: a repaint, new curtains, new kitchen light fittings and light shade, a new working fridge (rather than a failing one with an ice box clogged with a large lump of ice), wires need to be chased into near the kitchen, there need to be more sockets in the kitchen, rather than an extension lead right near a kettle with risk of water getting into electrics. There needs to be a new, clean shower cubicle. The place requires a deep clean by professional cleaners who know what it is to clean dirty places. The shower is grimy, the flooring composed of badly fitted tiles held by dirty grout at the edges. The let is advertised as having a kitchen: it isn’t. This is a small once-was bathroom space with a 1980’s microwave on its last legs and a toaster whose bottom falls out, the kitchen splash-back is rusty and dirty, the bin cracked and dirty, the table in the kitchen propped up straight by a wodge of dirty kitchen paper, the kitchen light fittings are dirty and grimy, there is evidence of rising damp in the kitchen ceiling – the ceiling paint is stained by damp, puffed and bubbled and protrudes. There were breadcrumbs on...

We loved having the chance to stay in one of the iconic brownstones of Brooklyn, in the most conveniently located place imaginable. The bed was cozy, and the room well-appointed.  I only had two things that took away from our stay: the cleanliness and the lack of security. The room was surface cleaned,  but seemed like it could use a good scrubbing and airing. The shared bathroom smelled strongly of urine, and I kept having to put the seat down because the other guests (!) were men. Throughout our 5-night stay, I contemplated giving both rooms a thorough cleaning.    I wish I'd been clearer that I would be staying in a guest house with multiple unknown people, and that we had been provided a key to our bedroom, as it was left unsecured when we were not there. If I had been staying alone, as a woman that would have felt unsafe.   That said, Kathleen was incredibly responsive to all communication, let me check in late when plans changed, and had a lovely home. I would love to see her get some help with cleaning that huge place!

To avoid certain metro connections, do not hesitate to take the ferry on the East River... There is a stop on the 34th for the Empire State Building, one for Wall Street and another for Brooklyn. It’s also very nice to take it at night. India Street west coast. The street is under construction but it is at the bottom, despite the sign! Danger... Cost $2.75 per person. You can take them before leaving on the platform, via an application or on board...

Jeanne is a truly wonderful host. Incredibly attentive, really helpful and willing to go out of her way to make sure your stay in NYC / Brooklyn is relaxing and stress free as possible. Local amenities are very close by, and getting into Lower Manhattan is only a short walk away. The Ferry was the most relaxing and spectacular way to get around too.   My husband and I went to a fantastic local restaurant on Manhattan Avenue called “Esme” which everyone who stays here MUST GO and visit! The food was absolutely delicious.   Overall - This is in a fantastic location, the bathroom, lounge and bedroom was great and I’d stay here again in a heartbeat.   Thank you Jeanne!

Garon is a great host, very laid back, wise and open minded. We had some great chats and it was refreshing after having a stressful time finding a place to stay. He also is very accommodating and happy to help out with directions and enlightening you on the area you are living in. The room itself is great, very comfy bed with aircon. Quincy street is very friendly, everyone will welcome you when you open up to them. I enjoyed my stay!

Laurie provided a comfortable clean apartment which myself and my teenage daughters stayed in for a week. Highlights were the great beds, breakfast items which were available for us to use, access to an outside garden and air-con. An added advantage was location - Brooklyn is such a different area to Manhatten and it was lovely to escape from the crowds and get some peace after a long day! Laurie is a friendly host and made sure that she helped us get started on making the most of our trip when we arrived. Her advice was spot on and resulted in our visit being much more fruitful than it otherwise might have been. Laurie was also quick to help with queries when they arose. As described,  this is an older property with the quirks that go with that and is charming and authentic. The small print it may be useful to know is that although the apartment is on the ground floor and separated from the rest of the house, there is direct access from the flat to the upstairs area. The house washing machine is in the apartment and is accessed through the day whilst you are on your travels. I would stress our privacy was never invaded when we were in and this gave a lovely communal feel to the property,  as we also went upstairs and met other guests staying in Laurie's rooms. However, this is not the property for you if you are seeking a more isolated experience.  I wouldn't hesitate to recommend Laurie's place. Above all, we felt very safe there and would love to return some day.

I thoroughly enjoyed staying at Alicia’s place.   Communication was extremely easy from the very beginning on (she was the first host who preferred to exchange a couple of mails before accepting my request) and stayed like that throughout my time in NY. The room is as described and has everything you need — a private bathroom, several electrical outlets, enough space, a comfy bed and an incredible view. The entire flat itself is huge and has its very own charm to it.  Although it is officially in Harlem, I have not once felt uncomfortable or unsafe in the area, not even in the middle of the night. The subway (line #1, which covers almost all of Manhattans attractions) and a supermarket are literally around the corner, maybe a minute away.  I really recommend this place and look forward to coming back whenever I’m in NY.

This was my first time using air bnb and I stayed in Alicia apt for 9 days and it was really nice relaxing felt like home away from home, it's only a short block away to the red 1 Train that took me to all my attractions that I wanted to see.and if I needed anything Alicia was always here to help made my trip so much easy and stress free,   I also had a little fever while still on holiday and alicia checked up on me making sure I'm fine and didn't need anything really helpful,  Alicia apt if located minutes away from restaurant,  grocery store, Mcdonald " 24 hrs", that came in handy. The neighborhood is very friendly and safe I would recommend Alicia to anything none looking for a cheap place to stay.

This has been my first bad experience on Airbnb and despite this fact; I shall attempt to give an objective review of the place because of my responsibility to future tenants.  Pros.  * There are supermarkets close by as well as a great park (Von king park), which I greatly enjoyed, just two and a half blocks away. *The bed is comfortable, the Internet connection is good and water pressure in the shower is perfect.  *The area was generally quiet and peaceful during my stay.  *The connections to the subway are ok. Four and half blocks to the G train and 9 and a half blocks to the A train but the walk is pleasant in both directions.  *My check in was good and Garon was courteous for the first 5 days of my stay as well as with the other guest in the house.   Cons *The apartment is a walk up on the fourth floor. And I had a hard time carrying my luggage down the stairs upon checking myself out.  * parts of the room and apartment not seen in this picture are generally cluttered although well organized  *There was no key provided to my room. As a woman in a small apartment with two strange men; I did not feel safe as a result. (I requested the key and was told to try it out and I did not want to be difficult at check in so I dropped the issue). *Further more on one occasion I left the apartment with the air conditioning on (realized it on the train) and came back in the evening to find it switched off so I have reason to believe Garon entered the room in my absence with my stuff all over the place.  *Garon asked that I take my shoes off upon entering the apartment and so I would enter the apartment in my socks, which would then be covered by cat hair by the time I got to my room which I felt disgusted by.  *The cat shed everywhere; especially in the shower drain filters, which Garon asked me to clean out every time I took a shower, which I also found disgusting. The cats are however generally friendly and mellow.  *There is a generally unpleasant smell in the apartment, stuffy and rank (I assume from poor ventilation and the kitty litter boxes)   About the main reason for my dissatisfaction; my request for a refund on the last three days of my stay (which i made on the 5th day of a 13-day stay), led to a hostile altercation and an offensive thread of messages on this platform. I must say that I have received a halfway apology from Garon and a refund of $75 but it did not make up for the fact that i was bullied and insulted. Had I known there was a one in a million chance that I would have had such an experience, I would not have chosen to stay here.

Garon was awesome. He was right there to meet me at the door and show me the space. He even was cool with letting my mom crash one night. Overall, it was a positive experience (I even got to hang out with his cats)!  My only grievance was that the bedroom door didn't lock. That being said, however, I never felt unsafe or threatened by Garon, the apartment building, or the neighborhood. He put me at ease from the minute I met him!

We had a lovely stay at Ted's apartment! First of all, it's a very spacious apartment with an open layout and lots of daylight which makes it a perfect space to relax. Another plus was the closet space; we were able to put all our clothes away (I hate living from a suitcase for a long period). Airco and shower worked well and the bed was soft and very comfortable. Wifi was good quality and lots of towels were provided. Another plus is the spacious shared terrace and the doormen. They're very friendly and the 24/7 service is nice and gives a feeling of security. The neighbourhood is excellent, lots of coffee shops, bars, boutiques and museums nearby. Whole foods, subways and citibike stations also near. The apartment is located on a busy street, so you do get some noise, especially the ambulances and fire trucks can be loud. During the day it wasn't really bothersome, but at night we slept with earplugs as a precaution and that worked fine (I have to say that I'm sensitive to noises in general and you're in NY so some noise is to be expected). We think there is an organisation for homeless people next door, so we saw them often but they dont make trouble and never linger in front of the entrance.  In summary, everything was in order and to our taste. The only downside is the lack of TV. Also, the interior is not the most new or modern. That didn't bother us, but check the pictures to see if it's your taste or not. The pictures give a pretty accurate idea. Finally, the communication with Ted was very smooth. He even helped us out when another host cancelled on us very last minute. So we were very happy with Ted's service! In conclusion, if we're in the area again, we won't hesitate to book Ted's place again!

Great location (generally, except that homeless people do congregate downstairs from the building next door), friendly doormen, good mattress. Room is very bright, so bring an eye mask or plan to wake up early. Furniture and pots and pans need an update, and the place maybe needs a deep clean.   But the location really is great, so you can't go wrong there.

Stayed here for a week and would definitely return. the bed was so comfortable, it was private and quieter than other parts of the city.  Based a 30 min subway ride away which meant cheaper food and drinks. I didn't feel unsafe walking alone at night which is important. Alicia wasn't around much, we kept missing each other, but when I did see her she gave great advice on where to go and what to do.

Cristina was amazing. I got in touch with her 2 hours before getting the keys. I was 'homeless' in New York and she welcome me to her home with no problem. Thank you so much Cristina. The appt is in one of the best neighbourhood of New York.

I stayed with Trish for two weeks in July and i must say it was great! The room was big and nicely decorated. There was a bed in the floor which i preferred and it was quite comfortable. The deck was nice but a little dusty, so i didn't spent to much time there, although i must say it is perfect in the morning for having breakfast. The shared bathroom and kitchen were clean. The kitchen has all you could need to cook and Trish left some space in the cupboards and fridge for me. Also she provided towels and left a big closet in the corridor for me to use. There is a fan in the room which was great for the hot summer nights. The neighbourhood was quiet and i found the houses and buildings nearby charming, it's a nice place (not at all scary even at night) and the building is a 5 min walk from the subway and 25-30 min ride to manhattan. It is an old building without an elevator but you only need to go up one floor. There were some restaurants and grocery shops nearby. Overall Trish was a great host! She was really nice with me during my stay. We didn't get to talk much because i was out a lot but when we did she was really helpful and easy to talk to. During my stay i lost the keys to the apartment which made me really nervous and she kindly gave me another set. I would highly recomend staying with Trish!

I've enjoyed staying at Patricia. She is a kind, warm person, and she respects privacy at the same time. The room was nice and I loved being able to use the deck to the backyard with all the plants and trees. I stayed at the end of a warm summer and this place was cool and shady and enjoyable. The location is great, close to the subway and restaurants.

I HIGHLY recommend using Kathleen through AirBNB. The area is populous & safe, the location is close to the subway, and the hospitality was lovely.  Kathleen is located in the Park Slope/Prospect Heights area - good food, not far from downtown Brooklyn and the DUMBO area. I never felt unsafe walking back at night, even so it’s  only a couple blocks from the subway.   This is located two blocks away from Bergen Street Station - a 2 or 3 train that (after changing to a 4 or 5) can bring you to Grand Central within 35 minutes, give it take. Kathleen was very knowledgeable about transportation and gave suggestions on how to move about and transfer trains.   Finally, the house and experience was outstanding. The four story brownstone had much character & charm, and Kathleen was generous in allowing me to sit out and read in her back garden. My private room was equipped with a mini-fridge, microwave, kettle, television, WiFi, roomy closet, and an AC unit. As if that didn’t take care of the basics, Kathleen supplied a new set of towels (towel, wash cloth, hand cloth) and bed sheets weekly - I did my own laundry at the laundromat not even a 1 minute walk from my front door. Kathleen was very respectful of my privacy, but yet I always felt comfortable to reach out with any questions.  This was my first stay with her, but hopefully will not be the last!

We loved staying in Maya's apartment in Greenpoint. Lorimer Street is close to a post office, drug stores, the Garden Market (on Manhattan), Ovenly bakery and Paulie G's pizza on Greenpoint Ave., and the G subway line to downtown Brooklyn (south), Queens (north), and Manhattan (either direction). The apartment, on two levels, is comfortable, clean, and well stocked. We felt at home there.

A lovely lovely apartment. We have no complaints except the spiral staircase connecting the bedroom and larger living space is probably unsafe for small children. If you are traveling with little ones you might consider another space or invest in some duct tape to restrain your naughty kids :)

Maya's place was one of our favorite Airbnbs!  Just as described and very centrally located, but still on a quiet and shady street.  It was great to have a kitchen since we traveled with our toddler and the bedroom was very comfy.  Would definitely recommend!

I made this reservation for my niece and these are her comments: I didn't get the chance to meet Reka because she was traveling but Erin and Rob (Erin's BF) were really nice and the place was amazing.  The bedroom was very comfortable.  I would absolutely stay there again.

We didn't meet Reka, but her housemates Erin and Rob were home for much of our 9 day stay. They were so easy going, helpful and kind, and were playful and incredibly patient with our one year old. They were happy to help 'baby proof' the apartment, and shift furniture in our bedroom to fit the portacot. They also made it easy for us to have hired baby gear delivered before we arrived. Room Pros: The WiFi worked as expected, the aircon in the bedroom was a lifesaver, and the washer/dryer in the complex was very handy. Room Cons: The gym was very small (maybe 3 cardio?), and the curtains in the bedroom weren't very effective at blocking out the light. (Thankfully, Erin got us a thick rug which we draped over and it did the trick. She also kindly offered to get new curtains...we declined!) The apartment location was wonderful- we felt safe walking around day and night, and there were so many great restaurants and bars within walking distance, of varying price levels. There aren't too many retail stores within a mile, but plenty of delis, pharmacies, and grocery stores. Both the bus and CityBike were super close, but we used neither - instead we walked to the subway (which was only about a 10 minute walk). Once you're on the subway, we found you can get anywhere in NYC very easily.
Kathleen, thanks for my wonderful, stress free stay in Brooklyn.  It helped with my visit with my visit with family.  You are the best.
Great place, Erin and Rob (Reka's roommates) were really fun to hangout with

Maya's apartment is a very good place for a break in the New York area. Greenpoint is a good neighbourhood. We often walked about the area after dark and didn't ever feel unsafe. I was able to sleep ok at nights as there isn't much neighbourhood noise. Nearby is Transmitter Park, a great waterfront location with a pier or over the East River, providing a fabulous viewpoint to observe Manhattan. We took our breakfast coffee & Danish there many times and also liked to watch the nighttime lights. The apartment is good and comfortable. The bedroom is downstairs, accessed via a metal spiral staircase, which is safe enough but is not suitable for anybody with any mobility issues.  I recommend this as a good place to stay and would return without hesitation.

We enjoyed our stay in Maya’s apartment. It is in a great neighborhood close to everything you could possibly need including a diverse mix of restaurants and eateries. We especially enjoyed the convenience of grocery and produce stores within two blocks of her apartment. Her kitchen is well stocked so preparing meals in the apartment is a real option. The G line subway is also close so access to Williamsburg and Manhattan is a short walk away. Communications with Maya were always quick, clear and informative. She made the door key transfer easy and low stress. She is very personable and an excellent host. NOTE: access to the downstairs bedroom is via a narrow spiral staircase.

This is a convenient and interesting neighbourhood.  I liked being able to walk out and go to the grocery store or get a coffee or a meal without needing to go far.  It is also a fun place to just walk around.    For those concerened about Harlem, I found the people friendly and never felt scared or threatened, even when walking around in the evening alone (not late, but after dark).  There is a police presence that is not overwhelming, but - to me - reassuring.  Wayne is a wonderful host.  He is warm and friendly, and very concerned with his guests' comfort.  He likes to meet with this guests and had all of us over for dinner one night.  However, he will also resepect your privacy if you prefer to be alone.  He had good suggestions of places to eat and jazz clubs to go to.   The apartment itself is spacious and has everything you need for a short or long stay.  I was there with two children for a week, and we were happyp with it.  It is not a five-star hotel, but certainly well worth what we paid for it.  I would have no problem recommending this apartment to friends.

I absolutely loved staying at Reka’s place! It’s located on a very quiet street, just a few feet from Tompkins Square Park. (I did a lot of dog-watching as I walked through). I stayed for one night; and Reka was very lovely and welcoming. I am pretty quiet, so I kept to myself when I was in the apartment. It was very, very clean and so comfortable. The room is a really decent size, and the bed is awesome. She also has a really great selection of books in the room. I couldn’t help but admire all the titles. The view of the city from the window is gorgeous, especially at night, and when I woke up Sunday morning, it was so quiet and peaceful which is super-surprising for being in the city!   The area is very accessible. I walked about twelve minutes to the L train to head into Brooklyn during the day Saturday; and at night I picked up some awesome pizza at F & F Slice right around the corner, and also visited Ray’s Candy Store on Ave A. Ray is about 90 years old and he made my fried Oreos. A legend. Also check out Death and Co.; an incredible bar about ten min away. There’s so much to do and see within walking distance of the apartment!   I didn’t drive into the city, but I could’ve. There was plenty of parking in the East Village and it’s so safe. I was alone at night and didn’t feel scared at all.   If you need a cool, comfortable place to crash; book with Reka. I had to head out early Sunday so I didn’t get the chance to say goodbye and thank you in person; but she was wonderful! (Next time I’ll check out the view from the pretty terrace in the photos!)

You will find an old apartment in a comfortable area but at night it is very unsafe and noisy. The host is clearly incapable of helping you with any big problem, but we liked the experience in such a big country.

relaxing and exciting all at once.  house and room/bath are lovely, well maintained, and everything you need is there.  when I discovered a problem with the cable box, Joy Carol and Phyllis all gave it a try but Carol persisted until the cable company solved the problem....I really appreciated that since I NEEDED to see the USOPEN tennis matches!  Impressive service. The block is shady and quiet, but so close to the action!  Perfect.

Although there is no question related to this, we found that the initial price changed because we weren't aware that there was an extra charge for a second person (my husband) and that there was a cleaning fee. As advertised, the room was clean and comfortable, but there was inadequate space to unpack two rather small suitcases, because the dresser and closet were filled with extra sheets, pillow cases and comforters. Basically, it was a bed enclosed by four walls and a bathroom that was challenging to use, space wise. And rather dangerous, considering the big step to enter and exit the bathroom. There was no lock on our door, and there was a separate guest room across the hall. This concerned us. If you are going to rent two rooms to separate guests, there should be locks on both doors. Instant coffee was absurd. How about some real coffee? We're not expecting breakfast, but nescafe instant was almost insulting.

A great place to stay in Brooklyn and made my last-minute trip so easy and stress free. Very close to subway stations to get you where you want to go, and close to restaurants and coffee and everything! There was no issue checking in when my train came in late. I definitely would stay here again!

Stayed in Ted and Jenny's apartment from Oct 26th to 30th and enjoyed every minute of the experience! The apartment was a large ensuite room in their house with its own private entrance. It had  a small kitchenette ,loads of wardrobe and drawer space and a large very comfortable bed  . During our stay we never met Jenny but were greeted by Ted when we arrived. He couldn't have been more helpful. He put us on the right track immediately by bringing us to the local subway stations (close by) and sorting out our tickets for the week, which made life very easy for us. (The commute to all the main attractions was only minutes away.)  Ted even offered to bring us to a jazz show in Brooklyn on the first night but we were unfortunately too tired after our journey. He also very kindly brought us fresh coffee every morning and freshly filtered water.  The apt is situated a few blocks north of Central Park in Spanish Harlem and felt relatively safe although I think it could be quite scary for a woman travelling alone late at night. Having said that, I would definitely stay there again if ever in NY an would highly recommend it to anybody planning to head to Manhattan.Thanks Jenny and Ted.

This was awesome! My first experience with AirBnB and it was great. Hosts were excellent in terms of timely communication -- room was spotless and as advertised. Neighborhood is walking distance to the 2/3 and the 6 train but it was also easy to hail a taxi. Wi-fi access was consistent, bathroom was very clean and I didn't feel the least bit unsafe. If I ever come back to NYC I will try to stay here again!

I had a great stay at Anthony's guesthouse- everything was spotlessly clean, modern and comfortable, and the apartment was very quiet- almost no street noise- a rarity in NYC!  Anthony is a gracious and responsive host.  Only downside was it is  in a slightly sketchy neighborhood, and the doors to the apartments are thin so everything that goes on in the common area can be heard in the rooms.   Overall though this is a fantastic place- would stay here again!

A great place to stay if you are visiting New York. Really convenient to the subway, but Nostrand is a little sketchy, especially at night. The room is basically hotel quality and has its own AC unit and TV with cable.

I was given a large clean  room with comfy bed and pillows with a great reading light and a beautiful view of lower Manhattan.  The nearby Avenue D is a little sketchy, but Avenue C has a great restaurant and the Ninth Street Exoresso, for the best cappuccino.

this is a remarkable place to stay in New York City.  Reka’s rooftop garden and deck offer spectacular respite from the city.  The bed was extremely comfortable, and clean, and the pillows were plump and ample.   The view from the bedroom is also awesome.   Checkin was a little rocky. but only because I really had no idea what time in the afternoon I would be able to get there.  The street around the corner (Avenue D?) is sketchy, but in the other direction there was Tompkins Square, and one of the best cappuccinos  ever at the 9th Street expresso coffee bar.  Reka is a generous and welcoming host.

Anthony was very helpful. Although I arrived very late he gave me a warm welcome. The house is very clean and nice even though you could be a little bit afraid of the neighbourhood, when you arrive late in the night. But in the area of Anthony I met the most friendly and helpful persons in NYC. So don't be alienate of the area - you can really enjoy your stay at Anthony's home. If I will come back to NYC I would request a stay with him again.

Nice room! Cable TV, heating machine, and a kitchen hall. Anthony is a helpful and kind guy ho also respects your privacy. At first look the 'hood may seem insecure but it isn't! It has cops, is kinda quiet and within the 2nd day you get used to the subway, there are many nice local businesses around. When you walk around you don't feel like a tourist you feel like one more guy from there. Thanks Anthony!! / Agradable cuarto!! TV por cable y calefacción, y una cocina común. Anthony es una persona muy amable que respeta tu privacidad. El barrio puede parecer inseguro pero no lo es hay policías rondando, es tranquilo y al segundo día aprendes a usar el subterráneo, hay muchos negocios alrededor. Cuando uno sale no se siente como un turista, sino como un vecino más del barrio.

Anthony is a great host with a great home!  I was in Brooklyn for seven weeks for work and it was wonderful to have a nice, clean, comfortable space to come back to night after night.  Anthony was very welcoming and checked in throughout, though the space is very private -- a room and bathroom in the garden level of a beautiful brownstone which houses one other room with its own bathroom.  The private entrance, fridge, and quiet tree-lined street make this a fantastic place to stay in Brooklyn.  Seven minutes from the A train provides easy access to Manhattan, and three minutes from multiple bus stops allow for quick trips to downtown Brooklyn.  Nearby Nostrand avenue is line with older businesses and apartments, but there are literally always people walking up and down the street so it does not feel unsafe.  Also check out Elsie's Doughnuts just around the corner!  I highly recommend staying with Anthony if you're going to Brooklyn, and I will definitely be back next time I need to stay there -- short or long term!

Jenny and Ted have a lovely house in Harlem. The room is very tidy and clean. A lot of private space. Bathroom for yourself. The room is well equipped with toaster, microwave, fridge, cooker. Ted made us a very nice breakfast one time with home made bananacake. The other time he made us some waffels. And every morning coffee!  They are very helpfull with tips about musea and finding your way around.  They have a small garden with chickens beside the house. Sometimes you can hear them. But most of the time you hear the train running over the tracks, half a block away. But it is very quit between midnight and 6 in the morning. After one night we were used to it. Besides, it gives the place a metropolean atmosphere.  The 6 train is really close by and takes you in 25 minutes downtown. Central Park is in walking distance. You can have a nice walk trough the park to the Met or Guggenheim. Or the Natural History. Enough to see.  One night we visited the Apollo and walked back in 25 minutes. Never felt insecure.  There is a really good italian pizza restaurant around the corner and a sketchy supermarket on the other side. For Mexican beers and small shoppings.  Very affortable place with lovely people!

We had a great week with Jenny and Ted. The two of them are great landlords!!!! You enter the apartment and immediately feel at home.  The contact in advance was great. Always prompt answers to questions. The directions from the airport to the apartment were perfect.  The apartment was very cozy, extremely clean, the bed was comfortable and the hospitality of the two of them was simply unbelievable! Immediately after our arrival, Jenny showed us a few corners of Harlem and gave us restaurant/bar recommendations. If you had any questions about NYC you could always contact them.  In the morning you were allowed to send an email and 5 minutes later you had a tray of coffee on your doorstep.  We were there for a week, about half way through our towels were washed :) It was a service like in a hotel.  The apartment is in Harlem, you never felt unsafe. Public transport connections into the city are excellent. In about 20 minutes you were absolutely in the center (without changing trains).  Great and absolutely recommended!!! If we had another trip to New York, we would book with them again at any time!

Anthony's place is excellent, rest assure this is where you want to stay for comfort, privacy and an overall great Brooklyn experience! Parking is close and isn't hard to find, if you'll be walking the train is literally a few blocks up. It's very convenient for everything: getting to Manhattan, finding food, washing, drug stores, you name it... it's all within a few steps. The neighborhood isn't noisy, it's safe, kept up and diverse. Everything from booking, checking in, coming and going to checking out is flawless. The price for all these features couldn't be any better, it goes way beyond being a great value. Anthony is a great guy as well, he's accommodating, easy to get in touch with and plesant. Can't say much more than all the other great things everyone else has said already. You can book this room and feel confident in knowing that you've made an excellent choice, I'll definitely be staying here again!

This place is a gem for our NYC visit.  It has made our NYC vacation stress-free and memorable. Jenny & Ted made sure that our accommodations live up to our expectations and more! Not only is the place spotless clean, it has all the amenities as stated.  Ted would serve us hot coffee and croissants in the morning. The place has easy access to the subway, and bus stations which allows us to visit various NYC sights conveniently. We would certainly book here on our next visit to NYC.

Cleanest bathroom I have seen in an Airbnb! Great water pressure and water temperature. Showers are important to me! Anthony is nice, great at communicating, and the apartment is safe. The walk at night might be a bit scary for a female walking alone from the subway, but that could have just been me unfamiliar with the area! Cable tv and mini fridge in room is a nice touch. Great value and would recommend staying there for sure. Thank you for being a good host, Anthony!

I had a fantastic stay with Jane. She's a genuinely kind and helpful person which made my first month in NY a lot less stressful than it could have been. She's intelligent and has a great sense of fun, I think her cats grew to like me as well. I was initially a bit worried about the area but soon discovered it was a great neighbourhood with a lot of character. Everything is close by as well.

Wonderful room, we were greeted by Ted, who helped us and explained everything we needed, very friendly and welcoming. The wonderful and comfortable room, everything very very clean and no one bothered at any time. Ted also suggested we recycle our trash and provided us with different trash cans. Very good idea 👏🏻. As for the neighborhood, if you use the green line metro station (train number 6) on 116th Street, it can be a bit unpleasant since it is very, very dirty and there are many people with drugs on the street. However, it is a 100% safe neighborhood, I walked with my camera and a lens that attracted a lot of attention and I never had any problems. However, if you want a cleaner and calmer subway trip, I recommend using lines 1 and 2 (red line) on 116, 4-5 blocks from the house. It is worth the extra walk and avoid bad smells from the other station.

I had a great stay at Gus and Holly's lovely apartment, which is super close to countless bars and restaurants and a short walk to the subway. I was travelling solo and never felt unsafe in the neighbourhood. The bed was really comfortable and the room stayed cool in the warm weather. It's a small room but they've made smart use of the space - it feels bigger than it is.  Holly and Gus are a very chilled, friendly couple who encourage you to treat the flat as home.

Myself and three friends stayed at SpaHa Loft for 6 nights as we were celebrating our 60th birthday. It was large for only 4 people (2 ended up not coming), but we loved having the space, especially the 2 bathrooms. It is in a working class neighborhood which makes it more interesting than staying downtown. Subway is very close and easy to use. We would definitely recommend walking in groups of 2 or more from the subway at night as the area becomes very lively. Another alternative is to walk down 3rd avenue from the 125 subway station as it was brighter and less sketchy. Having said that, we always felt safe and enjoyed the local restaurants. We were met by George (as Robin had to leave town) and he gave us lots of good information and was willing to help us if needed. The loft was very clean and the beds comfortable. There is a lot of street noise and we had the windows open so it was a bit noisy but nothing we couldn't handle. Kitchen is well equipped and there is shopping just around the corner. It was a wonderful place to stay and we would recommend it to anyone considering it. We bought the $30 7 day ride as much as you want Metro card and it was well worth the money. We also had the hop-on hop-off 2 day bus pass which is such a good thing to do. We took the downtown, uptown and night tour. We were thankful to have such a nice place to stay while in New York. Thank  you Robin and George!

We have just returned from a fantastic week in New York where seven of us stayed in Robin's stunning loft in East Harlem. The accommodation is fully as advertised. Spacious, not to say huge, located on the 1st floor near a small square (closed at night) little frequented except by squirrels, a school in a quiet area. All the household appliances available, very good bedding, a large living room with "vintage" sofas to accommodate all occupants, a large and practical kitchen, two bathrooms very useful for the capacity of this loft and large bedrooms, the walls of which do not actually rise to the ceiling but that is what gives it its charm. The apartment is secure and located close to two subway stations (116th street and 125th street) and a number of shops. Although being in Harlem, we did not feel unsafe even when returning late at night.  Regarding the reception, Robin was there to welcome us and introduce us in French please, the apartment, advise us on the tourist sites to see, ... For our departure, she made the driver of our shuttle wait for the airport since we were a few minutes late. She was perfect. An address that we warmly and highly recommend. Big thanks to Robin and her husband

We stayed at Charlie's studio for 6 days in Spetember and were really comfortable. Charlie's studio looks just like the photos. We had no trouble finding it and the check-in process was easy - Edwin is very responsive and helpful. The bed was super, i/net worked well and water pressure and temperature really good! I was a bit alarmed at the neighbourhood but that was just initial culture shock and after walking around we were really glad we had stayed in a place like Harlem which has a lot of character. We never at any time felt unsafe. Very easy to get downtown - just 3 blocks to the #2 & #3 subway (15 mins to Times Square) and a bit further to other lines. There are some great restaurants - we went to 'Native' and 'Ristorante Settepani' and they were both excellent and not expensive.

We just returned from our visit and we can not say enough good things about these apartments. We had the opportunity to spilt our stay between both apartments. From the moment we arrived, we knew we had chosen the right space. The street is beautiful! Edmond is onsite, and made us feel instantly welcome. We had questions during our stay and Edmond and Charlie always were there to help. The apartment is beautiful and just as pictured! The location is super convienent! Mu husband and I would leave at about am and not return until around 3am. We never felt unsafe riding the subway at all hours, or on the walk back to the apartment. Our favorite restuarant during our entire stay (and we ate alot) was located about 3 blocks away and is called "Native".. try it out! We will see you both again, Charlie and Edmond!

My husband and I had a wonderful 2 nights stay in the City Room -Private Bedroom, it is really spacious and has a comfy bed.  It was only last week (July 20-22nd) that we stayed so it was very hot but the powerful air con helped cool us quickly.  We enjoyed talking with Wayne and eating in his large roomy kitchen.  Wayne showed us some good dining spots around his neighborhood and educated us a little about the area.  The apartment is very convenient, it is about a 5min walk to W 125th Subway station, getting us to Times Square in 15mins which was perfect for our needs.  On the last day, we needed to go to JFK to fly home so Wayne suggested Supershuttle.com which was a HUGE help and so EASY, we were worried about how we were going to make it to JFK with all of our gear without having to pay gazillions. Thanks heaps Wayne for a great stay, we really enjoyed staying in your apartment and your shuttle suggestion was valuable in saving us time, money and stress.

Wayne had hosted us during our NYC visit in October 2011. It was our first airbnb experience and even though we spent some time researching about the airbnb experience, purticularly staying at a shared accomodation, the neighbourhood, and the commute options before we took the decision, we were honestly feeling a bit uneasy about it. However, Wayne is such an awesome person that we felt comfortable as soon as we met him. He did all that he could do to make our stay hassle free. The subway and bus stations are located about 4 blocks away and it took us about 5 minutes to reach the stations by walk. The neighbourhood was pretty safe. We had returned back to our room after midnight on most of the days and we did not see or experience anything to make us feel unsafe. We visited NYC in October when it was pleasant, so we did not have to turn on the AC or heater. The room looked exactly the same as in the pictures. Wayne shares a full fledged Kitchen with his guests however, we did not make use of it.To sum it up, we enjoyed our stay at Wayne's and would love to return for our next trip. Highly Recommended!!!

What can I say about Wayne.. He's one of the most polite persons I've ever known. He took care of us like we were family, and for us it was a great experience, especially because it was our first time in NYC. The house is great. Clean, comfortable, and just a few blocks away from the metro station. The room is big enough for two and super clean. Harlem is a great neighbour. Despite the bad reputation, we never felt unsafe. You won't find a better place to stay than Wayne's!

This apartment feels safe and comfortable and the bed is uber-comfy.  Arrangements were easy to make and Edwin was really welcoming and available if I needed anything. Noise from upstairs can be a nuisance but I suspect this is somewhat unavaoidable in NYC. I stayed in this apartment for a month and it was easy to live in for that period of time. Thanks for a great stay!

I feel like I'm repeating the many positive comments, but it's true that everything in this apartment is perfect. First of all it is really very large and friendly with a real large table. The rooms are large, there is plenty of storage and all the necessary equipment. For our group of 8 adults in 2 families it was ideal. The fact that the partitions are not completely closed did not bother us at all. Then, it is very quiet, which is rare in Manhattan, while being really close to the center, the subway being just a stone's throw away. As has been said, there is a very convenient supermarket just around the corner open 24 hours with everything you need. Finally our hosts Robin and George are really charming, Robin speaks French, she took care of our transfer from JFK, and waited for us with a smile despite our 3 hour flight delay until more than 11 p.m. while she and her husband were leaving for a trip the next morning. On the day of our departure, we were also able to leave our 8 suitcases until the afternoon because our flight was in the evening. In summary, our stay was perfect, and if we return to New York, we will definitely return.

Beautiful apartment conforming in all respects to the description, spacious, quiet street, 4 blocks from the metro (without danger), supermarket at the bottom of the accommodation where you can find varied and very good food. Family neighborhood where you feel safe. Ideal for large families or several families. A big thank you to Robin for her welcome, her sympathy and her smile, as well as her valuable advice. We had a very good stay in your apartment. Address to remember!!

We arrived at Wayne's on November 18th a little earlier than planned. We contacted Wayne to tell him we would be a little early and he was directly available. Once you arrive at the accommodation, a very pleasant surprise. Very very clean room and bathroom and very comfortable bed. The accommodation is located just 5-10 minutes from the nearest metro station with a metro line (the red) which goes to Times Square in 10-15 minutes. Despite ideas about Harlem, it's a very quiet neighborhood where I never felt unsafe. Wayne is an extraordinary host, always attentive and always there to give us good tips about New York. He invited us on Saturday to have breakfast with him and his wife, thank you Wayne, it was delicious. His wife and Wayne are adorable and I thank them for the good times we spent together during breakfast. I will definitely return to Wayne's place during a trip to New York and I recommend it to anyone looking for cheap accommodation in New York. Thanks Wayne!!!!

Robins apartment is huge and very comfortable. We are a family of six with our youngest being 4 years old. The space was so good for her after full days of exploring nyc. The beds are very comfortable. Two bathrooms was also a huge advantage. The kitchen is well stocked with some basics like salt, pepper and olive oil in the cupboard. There are two markets just around the corner that have everything. The subway is just a few blocks away and you can take the green 4 or 5 express to Grand Central station.. it was all very easy to navigate. We did have a day off the subway and used Uber as the subway at 125th is a bit confronting if you’re not used to Harlem. The trains are full, people are generally friendly but there was a few incidents when we felt a little unsafe. An Uber is about $25 and takes up to 40 mins from downtown depending on time of day. If you have a car there is street parking, just don’t park in front of a fire hydrant!  Robin and her husband, George are the loveliest people and just live upstairs.

Beautiful apartment, very well equipped, warm. Very quiet apartment, appreciable after days of exploring New York (walking, noise...). We were 6 adults, very comfortable in this accommodation. Metro and supermarket nearby. The neighborhood is surprising but we felt safe there. Robin had organized round-trip transport for us from the airport to the apartment, which was very much appreciated. (125 dollars + tax) for 6 people. Luis, the driver is very pleasant. Both Robin and Luis were responsive despite the flight delay problems that we had. Robin is very welcoming, warm, and available to answer our questions before and during our stay. We recommend this apartment.
Highly recommended. Harlem is a very very interesting neighborhood. And nothing dangerous, despite the movies.

Wayne is a great host! He met us to check in and gave us a tour of the apartment. The first night we had no AC but as soon as I told him the situation, Wayne fixed the problem.   The apartment has a very good price/value ratio and the area is quiet and not dangerous. There is a subway station an 8-minute walk away. We didn't agree much with Wayne because we were only arriving to sleep, but the times we saw him he was very friendly.   I would highly recommend the apartment if you are looking for a good, quiet place to sleep at a good price.

We had a hard time contacting Wayne at first, despite writing to him several times. He only responded by also doing so with Airbnb customer service, which worked very effectively. In addition, he wanted to charge us for the crib, something that was not indicated in the description. However, after talking to him, he finally gave it to us for free.  Despite an unpleasant episode on the first night, in the form of an alleged robbery at the accommodation (not from us, but from Wayne himself), our stay there turned out to be very good. It is true that the neighborhood gives a little respect at night, but in general, there are always people on the streets and it is located a few minutes from two Subway stops that connect directly and quickly with the center of Manhattan. In relation to quality/price, it is the best there is, so I would say that the accommodation is highly recommended.

The apartment is large, charming and perfectly equipped. Robin's welcome is warm and the organization of transfers from the airport is a real plus. The neighborhood confused us a little but we didn't feel unsafe.  To recommend

This apartment is brilliant, I’m so pleased we booked it.   The first thing I’d say is listen to robin (the host)’s advice. Everything she said was 100% correct. She knows her local area very well.   We spent a week in NYC, our first piece of advice would be buy a 7day no restriction travel card for the subway ($33 per person) we bought one on day 3 but wished we’d known how much we’d use it. We travelled up and down manhattan many times and would have saved ourselves a fortune!   The apartment is so well stocked, washer dryer was perfect, dishwasher was fine, fridge was massive and was perfectly sized for 6 of us for the week.   My mother and father in law used the bedroom at the front of the apartment (next to the TV) and one of the bathrooms, my 16 year old nephew used one twin room (just off the main bedroom) my 14 year old stepson used the other twin room and my partner and I used the big room. There was loads of room, drawers in each bedroom and hanging space in the closets.  The iron and ironing board were used a couple of times   We used the subway on 125th street (about a 10 minute walk) . As Robin explains in her handy book of local knowledge (in the kitchen) this station is very busy with ‘interesting’ folk...mainly homeless people, some with addictions. As robin explains you can use the 116th street station (about 5-6 minutes walk) which is fine and no where near as busy but I can honestly say that we didn’t ever feel threatened at 125th. I can understand that people with a nervous disposition might be overwhelmed by it but we were absolutely fine.  The reason we used 125th is for the shuttle subway which takes you down to lower Manhattan much quicker by missing out many stations. 116th is served by the ‘local’ train which stops at every station on route.  The supermarket around the corner is brilliant, full of many different branded and non branded products, fresh sushi, salad bar and cakes.   We will definitely go back to Robin in the future. We loved our stay, it was everything we wanted and more!!!

Very spacious accommodation, enough space to retreat even with several travelers.  Good kitchen equipment. Supermarket right around the corner, all of Manhattan's sights can be reached very quickly via nearby subway stations. East Harlem has flair, we never felt unsafe, like in all big cities you should use common sense and keep an eye on your valuables. The biggest plus point of the accommodation is the charming host Robin - very helpful, easy to reach, and has both feet in life. We stayed in the accommodation for a week and can recommend it without reservation.

Super loft, exceptional cleanliness, very well equipped with lots of towels available, laundry machines, dryers, hair dryers, lots of dishes, even stoves in good condition, which was rarely the case in all my last reservations with AIRBNB. A somewhat surprising neighborhood when arriving homeless and a marijuana user near the metro but police officers on every street corner until very late in the evening. We returned home until 1 a.m. by metro with our 16 year old sons without any problems. I highly recommend this rental, and Robin is a truly kind host, very accommodating and full of good advice.

A very nice apartement with everything u need....comfortable bed, big flatscreen with just a few programs. The apartement was clean and Charlie answered fast and nice on upcoming questions. Harlem is a hip area und Full of life. Your will see poor homeless people but nearly everybody is nice and Kind. You can reach several Metro stations from Charlies apartement in about 5-10 minutes. Trains take about 25 minutes to lower Manhattan. There is a Supermarket, a gym and everything you need around Charlies condo . We felt very well and can definitly say that it has been a great Home. Thank u, Charlie!

A pretty major disappointment. On the one hand, the shower took 15 minutes to get hot water, then the water pressure was terrible. Secondly, the kitchen was DIRTY. There were pot lids in a drawer full of oil, the oven dirty, the floor too. There isn't even a plug to plug in the toaster. On the other hand, when presenting these complaints to Edwin (the manager) he had a disastrous and somewhat dangerous reaction. When I showed him the dirty oven, he told me: "I personally cleaned the oven yesterday" and I told him that I hadn't dirty it since I had arrived the night before and hadn't even cooked. After that he responded to me in a quite aggressive tone: "ARE YOU CALLING ME A LIAR???". Secondly, after that he turned on a gas valve on the stove and blamed me for leaving it open. A regrettable and quite dangerous attitude, on top of that I was with my 1 and a half year old son and my wife. It is really to denounce this attitude of a person.  Well, the truth is that it was a rather unpleasant experience, finally it turns out that the apartment was really dirty since without even requesting it I received a refund of U$D 50 dollars for cleaning that I had paid at the time of reserving the place.

We stayed in Roberta's apartment for 5 days. We arrived around 11pm due to the flight and the storm that day, which is very late. But Roberta's friends have met us at the door and showed the apartment and everything in it. They were great and very friendly! The first thing we noticed is that the apartment is actually way bigger than we expected from the pictures. It also looks better than in the pictures.   In the morning we found fruits and coffee, which was great, since we had nothing to eat for 12 hours or so. Thanks again Roberta!  Concerning the neighborhood, we didn't find it that great as previous reviews mention. For the first couple of days we (2 guys) felt a bit unsafe walking to and from the metro - later we got used to it and felt fine. It is about 45 minutes to manhattan during the day and about 1-30 minutes late at night.

We stayed at Roberta’s place for 8 nights. Roberta was very nice host and she made us feel welcome. Location was good. Even though we headed to Manhattan every day, the journey didn't feel too long for us. Bedford-Stuyvesant was a nice neighbourhood, and we didn't feel unsafe. At night time we went home together (three girls) thought, and I think it's always best to be careful in a foreign city. The beds were very comfortable, and we slept well. We always wore earplugs because without them we found that sounds coming from the street were too loud without them. The apartment was spacious and there was a lot of natural light.  There was a wireless network in the apartment, but a few times over the week it became dysfunctional. But altogether, clean, cozy and comfortable. Would recommend to my friends.

The description of the accommodation and the photos are very accurate. Everything as expected! Roberta bought fresh fruit and breakfast for us, which was very nice. Check in worked perfectly. It was also no problem to leave our luggage in the apartment on the day of departure until the flight took off. Everything very easy! The environment is very quiet, everyone is very friendly and helpful. We never felt unsafe, even after midnight! Thanks to the proximity to the A Train, everything is easily accessible!

Roberta was very nice and helpful the whole time. The apartment was just as described and it even surprised us how big and roomy it was. The beds were good and there was enough of everything for three people. AC worked great in both rooms, and as we were in NY during the horrible heat and humidity, we even got a fan to help with the few hot nights. The neighborhood is really up and coming, we didn't feel unsafe at any point and there were plenty of restaurants and deli/grocery stores nearby and the subway is close too. All in all a very good home base for visiting New York.

I loved this apartment so much, the neighborhood is fantastic authentic New York, and there are so many restaurants, coffee shops, theaters and things to do in the East Village. It was close to the subway and great groceries,drug stores, and all you might need.. Anna is a great host, responsive , caring and her house was one of my all time favorite AirBnB's, it had so much charm. I think what I liked so much was the care Anna took with all things in her home, it really feels like a home. I was also working down the block so it was so convenient to my work and also really safe when I returned home at night. There is all you want and even though it is on the small side , it feels generous and abundant  - hot water, coffee, the best tea pot ever, clean and orderly but not anal, beautiful sheets and towels, quiet, a cool old stove that works great, wireless,- I was in heaven.Also Anna was a great host, responsive, charming, and generous- always in contact for questions.There were flowers when I arrived and the house was also cleaned so beautifully while I was there. Highly highly recommend!!!!

Sheila was an amazing host. As soon as we booked her apartment she sent a very informative email detailing everything and anything we would need for our stay. It was very helpful while we were planning our trip and during our stay. Even with the 12 hour time difference Sheila was easy to get a hold of when I needed to ask her questions. She was also very accommodating. When we arrived before our check in time she was kind enough to let us up a little early so we weren't walking around Brooklyn with 2 large suitcases. The apartment isn't super fancy but we loved the cozy lived in feel. It was exactly what we wanted for our authentic trip to NYC. The neighborhood was great, overall clean, not too noisy and I never felt unsafe. We found Mia's Bakery on Smith St and fell in love. We ate there almost every day before venturing off into the city. The apartment is centrally located which made using the subway very simple. We had an amazing trip. I would stay at Sheila's place again if I ever get the chance to make it back!

The location is fantastic.   Right in the middle of the action of Brooklyn.  I have stayed in this area many times.   The building is old.  The apartment would appear to be one used for rental only.  Has all that is needed.  Thin walls....Noise can be easily heard.   Stayed in the summer so the air conditioner was on at night but I suspect not the quietest place in the world otherwise.  The apartment was likely not original and looks as if it was created as an additional unit from the original building..  Communication was great , but I have stayed in lots of airbnb places and I have to say I do not rate this highly as an apartment.  Its one of the lower rates in the neighbourhood and one can see why.   Not terrible, but not one that I would stay in again nor recommend to a friend.   If budget matters though, you can not beat the location.

Sheila is a fantastic, warm & friendly host. Check in was very easy, totally stress free and the apartment was spotless. Everything we needed was there and the air conditioning was extremely helpful when the unseasonal temperatures hit 26+ degrees!  Even though Sheila was out of town, communication was there at all times & when we needed to extend our stay, it was organised quickly.  The location was spot-on. We are no strangers to NYC but this was our first time in Brooklyn. Not only is the apartment surrounded by fabulous shops and restaurants etc., it is incredibly easy to get around as the subway is so close by.  I wholeheartedly recommend this apartment.   Thanks again, Sheila!

My review is a little more mixed (and maybe balanced) than other reviews.  The good: The studio is well located: on a quiet street and nearby various subway lines which will get you to Midtown in 10-15 minutes. It's fairly sizeable. The host, Chris, was available, helpful, and easily contactable. Checkin was smooth.  The less than good: Although the studio is well positioned there were several noise disturbances. It's near a boiler which kicks in at any time, and I was woken up several times by a homeless guy rumaging through the bins which are outside the apartment's windows. But overall it's still quiet for Manhattan.  Because it's a basement studio it is quite dark. Several reviewers have commented favourably on the furniture and decor. But this is a matter of taste. I found the apartment cluttered - skins, masks, religious paraphernalia, all over the place. If you prefer minimal this apartment might not be to your liking. The bathroom has become somewhat grubby and could do with a thorough clean - and indeed makeover.  Despite my misgivings I had a satisfactory stay.

Christopher was an excellent host, although he was not on site.  He attended to all my needs and even had the building manager meet me and offer me any assistance.  The location was great!  I was only minutes from my destination, drug stores, and some awesome restaurants.  The accommodations exceeded my expectation.  The place was neat, clean, and had all that was promised and more.  He even allowed for me to stay an extra day.  I would definitely both stay again and recommend this location in Central Harlem.

The place is nice!  Very comfortable and with all the necessary things for a some days visit to NYC.  If you go on summer, I recommend to talk with Christopher about air conditioner because believe me, you will need it.  The place doesn't have natural light and kitchen, although it has microwave and refrigerator for fast meals. Also there are a lot of restaurants, coffees and deli store near.  The place is located 5 little blocks away from the subway station and 2 blocks away of the bus stop.  In harlem is very usual to see a group of people in the corners so it could be a little scary at the beginning, mainly at night but everything it's fine and I didn't saw or heard something wrong near the place or during the walks for the bus or subway.  Definitely, I would stay again at Christopher's place, who also would be ready to help you with all your doubts!
Clean place with unique pieces. Easy access to subway. We came home late in the evening for two nights but did not feel unsafe walking from station to the apartment.

We try to make it to NYC every year and always stay in a different part of the city. Chris’ place was the perfect introduction to Harlem. The proximity to public transportation, the quiet street, and great restaurants nearby all make it extra special. Easy check in and a stress-free stay. Highly recommend.

Ana's place was perfect for our girls trip! Great location. Clean and spacious apt with everything we needed. She communicated promptly and made some great suggestions for our trip. Ana's place made our New Years trip easy and stress free! I definitely recommend staying here! Hopefully we'll be back to visit again soon.

Ana's apartment and location were exactly as described. She was more than available during the stay, I felt as if I could get in touch with her whenever. I would stay here upon visiting the city again, as well as, recommend that friends do too.   Can't stress how solid the experience with Ana was.

First this place is in the hood. I didn’t realize this when I booked. At night time it’s very colorful and I didn’t feel safe to walk around with my elderly mother. Lots of drug heads around and shady looking people. The host was very nice and responsive and helped us with issues. The place is cute and he has lots of interesting books. The small bed that I slept on was incredibly uncomfortable and you could feel the springs in your back all night long. My back is in knots so I found the bed unacceptable. There’s also no drinking water which was in inconvenient. He did leave 2 bottle. Would be nice to have a 5 gallon jug.

The location is definitely in Harlem. The street the apartment on is nice and fairly quiet, it's downstairs in a pretty brownstone building. An older building, but it's nice inside, very livable. Only about a 5 block walk to the subway which was great, not the greatest area to walk through due to some homeless people, but I never felt threatened at all. Next to the subway is a bus stop that can take you to or from LGA airport without any transfers. Chris and David (who checked us into and out of the apartment) are both very nice.

Rachel's place is really amazing. Huge for NYC, and the bathroom is truly exceptional. As a musician, I loved the opportunity to open the window to Park Ave on a sunny late-afternoon and play a bit in the amazing space. She also has a wonderful wireless stereo to help set moods of all types. And Gogo is every bit as-advertised; a true sweetheart who loves people. The place is loud (floors, building, and street below), so be prepared with your own earplugs (or the ones she's kind enough to provide). I also wish both bedroom windows had a blackout shade rather than just one, but for most people it should be fine. If light bothers you that badly, you'll probably bring your own sleep mask anyway. Other than the noise of Park Ave, the location is amazing. Tons to see and do within just a few blocks. This was a great value, Rachel is incredibly sweet and accommodating, don't hesitate to book.

The space is small, particularly the bathroom which requires you to really cram in to in order to shut the door. The host was very nice in our limited interactions. There is a cat, and the cat will claw at the bedroom door in the night. I couldn't get cell service in the house, and I don't know if there was WiFi (didn't ask nor think about it until inconvenient times). Has AC for guests and will leave you alone. Neighborhood is nice and not scary.

The apartment is in a great location and is very spacious and comfortable. You will be in a central location and within walking distance from restaurants and other exciting neighbourhoods. In relation to the upkeep of the apartment, almost everything was intact. During our stay, the air conditioning unit upstairs started to leak, and there was a leaky roof right above the TV. Keith said that he would fix it over the weekend that we were leaving, so I hope it is fixed by now.  However, during our stay there were a few glitches:   1) Like Alex, we did not have access to the internet. This caused a problem for some of us who wanted to Skype or keep in touch with family. Also, it provided a hindrance in regards to planning our days (luckily we came mostly prepared).  2) Vague communication: Not a deal breaker, but I believe Keith is quite busy managing properties so his responses to your questions can be somewhat vague/or unclear. Also, he sometimes asks for things without clarifying. For example, during our stay he asked us to leave our keys out on the table for someone to pick them up (without any prior explanation why). During another day, he asked us to open to front door for someone (without prior warning; which is pretty scary for 4 women!). However, if you press him for more information or clarification he will do so.   3) Poor coordination of tenants: When my friend arrived, the place was dirty (towels on floor, food in fridge; unmade beds). I don't think he arranged for the cleaners to come in between us and the last tenants. When I notified him of this, he called the cleaners and they came. Now, the day we were leaving the next set of tenants woke us up at 11:00am wanting to come in. I guess he double booked us and there was some overlap with the timing. We had to rush to get our stuff packed and cleaned in a short amount of time while the cleaning ladies were cleaning around us! Big source of confusion and stress!   To put things in perspective,  you have to take into consideration that the property isn't a hotel and there may be "glitches" during your stay. It is the risk you take when renting out a property- quality and service are not guaranteed. With regards to the problems, I do have to say that Keith really made an effort to try and resolve them. He also made himself very available, and responded to our queries quickly and professionally. For the price, location, and space alone...I would say go for it!!!!

A very special and unique apartment. It definitely has a soul! Rachel is a great host - very friendly, helpful and cooperative. Edith is very sweet and shy cat girl. By the way, there wasn't any smell of cat litter at all, so don't be afraid. I hope to stay at Rachel's apartment again!

Keith's apartment is a steal!  For the same price as a hotel room, you get two floors, two bedrooms, and two bathrooms!  The apartment is in a great location and we didn't have any issues with getting the key or with street noise.  It is a little wonky in that to get to the apartment, you walk though the first floor apartment's kitchen, up more flights of stairs, and keep going until you reach the final door.  Then, open the last door and go up one more flight of stairs.  But it's a small price to pay for the space to rest up between eating and sighseeing.  Keith was also very easy to communicate with.

I am sorry to say it, but we had a bad experince, the A/C unit in one of the rooms was licking so bad that we had to turned off, otherwise the floor had suffer a major damage, unforrtunally that day was the first day of summer, we had 101"F, so we moved downstair, we call Seith and he told us the plumber was busy, i imagine all the A/C collapsed that day, we checked out 3 days later and no one showed up to solve the problem, just one last message from Seith asking what time we were leaving,   i called AIRBNB to try with them and their answer was their responsability is to contact the host (Seith).  Neiborhood, is well located if you want to eat etnic food, but in front of the building there are at least 6 homeless people sleeping and the view is decadent.  One last thing, the stairs are endless, please do not go there if you are over 60 or under 10, definitly not a friendly family place.

Overall we had a good experience and the actual apartment was perfect for our family of five. Having two newly renovated bathrooms was the best! What turned out to be the only problem was the front lock key. Apparently new keys were made but the lock on the outer gate was loose and the keys stuck. We got "locked out" until my husband returned one night and we had continual trouble locking,  unlocking  and un-sticking the keys. Also, there was no cable. We had no TV for the week. Ok - we were forced to talk to each other - but I really did want to catch up on the news. The internet was sketchy and not reliable. However, there was balcony the kids thought was terrific and the beds were very comfortable. Most important - the place was clean! So I would  recommend this apartment - as long as you don't mind the walk-up. Just fix the front lock, please.

Average stay. Great location. I wouldn't call the place brand new. Had 2 bed/2 baths as advertised.
