This is my second Airbnb experience, the first was more than great, so I won't tell you how disappointed I was when I found myself in conflict with this host… At first, she seemed very nice, and answered very quickly, I told her directly all my concerns about the virus of the moment, speaking about the fact that I had a baby of less than a month and an elderly person with me, and beside that I am foreign so I am obviously not familiar with the different districts, that is how she reassured me by telling me that I was making the right choice and that the apartment, in short, was the ideal choice for us. Big surprise, when I arrived there, not only to mention the fact that the apartment was really smaller than expected in the photos, but also her neighbors warned me that the apartment was very dangerous for my family because it was situated at the center of the pandemic… So I got scared and I decided to leave immediately, I did not even stay 30 min, this is how we got into conflict for questions of reimbursement, and she even felt comfortable to ask me to give her half of the money because "she was going to have a hard time renting her apartment due to the current situation"… I found this experience meaningless and dishonest, we shouldn't put dollars on human lives.

OMG!! I don’t even know where to begin! 😭 The hosts were extremely friendly and communicative! Even before booking, they responded promptly and were very helpful with my questions.  Upon arriving, I was welcomed with all smiles and a welcome tour of the space.  Walking through this space blew me away! It is exactly as pictured, very spacious, and I truly felt like I was home away from home. It was immaculate, smelled terrific, and the fresh air circulating via the space upon arrival was such a nice treat after driving in from Maryland.  I will NEVER stay in a hotel in NYC again! Ever! This will always be my go-to space!  Wow! What a steal!!

Everything was exactly as it looked , the area wasn’t as comfortable for me somebody tried to attack us not to far from the Airbnb & there wasn’t enough police around that area also the spot was clean I still was startled by the roach that was crawling on the mirror , didn’t not how to work the hot tub properly & didn’t know the jet’s didn’t work in the shower other than that everything was fine 👍

We stayed in Ashley's apartment for 1 week. The apartment was big enough to fit all 4 of us and Ashley provided everything we needed. The location was perfect! An easy and short walk to the subway station and it's easy to get around with the 1 trains. Ashley always answered within minutes and was very friendly and answered all of our questions. Also there's supermarkets, drug stores, taco bell, KFC, dunkin donuts, domino's pizza and other stuff in short walking distance which is very convenient. Since we needed to go to the airport late, Ashley let us leave our bags until 6pm which was absolutely perfect! :) thanks for everything

I had a wonderful stay with Sharon. She made me feel right at home without being nosy at all, responded quickly to my messages and phone call, and is just a nice, understanding person.  The room was perfect for a solo traveler not planning to spend much time in it but out in the city all day. While the Bronx is not particularly close to all the action, the train is right there for you, and the Bronx itself is great to walk around. I never felt unsafe during my stay here.

This advertisement is a scam. What you paying is not what your getting. They show you a fully furnished apartment carpeted, tv’s, a nice house. When you actually get inside you see that the apartment is being renovated, looks nothing like what you think you’re paying for. I would never recommend this place to anyone because I wouldn’t want you to get scammed like I did.

Jewel’s place was the perfect home base for a little 2 day trip my partner and I took to Brooklyn for a 2-night show at the Kings Theatre. Being so close to the subway into Manhattan (where we caught our bus in) as well as the venue pretty much eliminated any travel stress, as it was incredibly convenient to get anywhere. The room was as advertised - Moosey, very clean with a comfy bed - and Jewel was very thorough with check-in as well as perfect with communicating before, during, and after my stay. We didn’t see her after check-in as we simply weren’t in NY for that long doing as much as possible, but it was a wonderful and easy spot to return to after walking around all day and dancing all night at Kings. Thank you Jewel for opening your lovely apartment to us!

Sometimes NYC can be a scary place when you are coming from a spacious and quiet environment like our city in Alabama, yet we felt right at home with Sharon and Mike in the Bronx. Sharon met us in front of the location and directed us to the perfect place to park. She walked with us back to the house and for two nights of staying there, we felt like family. Sharon offered to join us as we had to take the metro for the first time to meet a tour guide on Broadway. She taught us how to pay for our passes and gave us many tips on riding the metro. We walked so much and she hung in there as we enjoyed ourselves and took lots of pictures on Times Square. One of our friends had a birthday during our stay and Mike cooked a whole meal for all of us! We've never ever been treated like that with an AirB&B host. Sharon and Mike's kids were also welcoming and helped us with tips, walked us to the store, and sat with us. We received more than we expected out of this visit and plan to book with them again in May. We can't think of a better place to book with. The Bronx was a safe neighborhood, we never felt unsafe. There are three metro stations nearby and we used all three to get around. The place was clean, spacious, and accommodating. As much as my family and I use AirB&B, we consider Sharon a Superhost!  What amazing service!

Conrad's place was a safe, clean, quiet location for the hustle and bustle of Harlem that surrounds it. It is on a quiet street around the corner from the more active Malcolm X Boulevard, which hosted the 2/3 (red line) subway as well as a variety of eateries including Sylvia's (Melba's, we found, was much better and is owned by Sylvia's niece: 300 W 114th St), Red Rooster, Corner Social (very loud and incredibly rude hostess, but great wings), and Harlem Shake (which was quite good -- get their fries with the jerk mayo). It is also about a block away from the Apollo Theater, which not only has amazing shows, but also amazing tours (be sure to get one led by "Mr. Apollo"). Our favorite stop, however, was the A&S Deli at the corner of 127th and Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard. It has a good selection of food and drinks, but one employee in particular, Mo, was so incredibly friendly and kind; he really made every trip to that store worthwhile. Also right around the corner, also on Powell Blvd. is the Shop Fair Supermarket, which had everything we needed for our 10-day stay.   Conrad's home was well equipped with essentials like cookware (though no baking sheets, and oddly no foil), salt and pepper, a coffee maker, microwave, gas range, full-size fridge, soap, paper towels and toilet paper, as well as a very comfortable bed with extra linens, and plenty of towels. His bathroom was well lit and had a full-size tub and a nice shower. His back porch area was beautiful and looked over a very cute patio and the backs of other apartment buildings. This was a favorite spot of ours to wind down on with a glass of wine and/or a cocktail at the end of our busy days.   Conrad met us upon check-in and was incredibly friendly, kind, and helpful. Having him live below this apartment made us feel extra secure and was also great to know in case we needed him for anything (which we didn't).   This area of Harlem is busy and comes with an assortment of people, both day and night, but we never once felt unsafe. In fact, most people we encountered were incredibly friendly. However, it is New York, so being on guard is necessary, no matter where you are in the city.   This apartment is about a block away from the 2/3 subway line and a few blocks away from the D line, both of which we used for the majority of our stay. It can also be easily accessed via taxi and Uber.   We recommend Conrad's place and will consider it on our next visit to the city!
The location is amazing. Cannot stress enough how great it is. It's one of the last non gentrified neighborhoods in NYC and by staying here you'll see things you'd never see if you stayed downtown.

Dayne's space was in an excellent location.  We were able to walk to the metro stop which was about 3 blocks away.  She met me when I arrived at the place and gave little tips for the area.  The rooms all connect, so if you have guests that like a little more privacy, this is good to know.  The beds were very comfortable and the sheets were nice and smooth!.  She had coffee and milk available for us to use.  We appreciated that because we were all coffee drinkers and like our morning cup of coffee before attacking the day.  Dayne was quick with responses.  The apartment is in a quiet and safe area.  The backyard was nice to enjoy cool evenings.  I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a nice area that has easy access to the metro to go anywhere.  We went to a mets game and enjoyed that we could access the metro to the game and going home and not have to find parking.  The only thing that might be a little difficult is parking, there is street parking available but fills up fast.  There is a parking garage that we used on crescent street.

Dayne is a great host that is willing to keep in touch , answer questions and thoughtful as well. The apartment was as advertised with no surprises. The location was fantastic. The subway, food , groceries , drug store all within 2 blocks

Staying here was great! There was 4 of us and we all slept comfortably in the apartment. Even though Angelo couldn't personally meet us, he did a good job of communicating with us to make sure we were comfortable. His friend Rob did a great job as well stepping in and helping us with whatever we needed!

I found Rebekah's place to be very easy to get around from and Rebekah was incredibly helpful.  She provided a very nice handbook with useful tips, she communicated in a timely manner - I never once worried about not being able to reach her or get information.  The apartment is cozy and simple, it worked out great for sleeping / eating and getting ready for the day.  It is on a quiet dead end street, coming in and out of the neighborhood with my teens I was not really worried about danger and I definitely felt safe / comfortable in the apartment.

Rebekah is a great host. The communication is impeccable and always quick, long before our arrival we had a detailed description of everything possible (arrival, equipment of the apartment, things to do and see, shopping, etc.). Since winter suddenly set in again in March, we needed a few extra blankets, which she brought to us super quickly. Rebekah even organized us a loyalty card for discounts at the nearby supermarket. Really perfect! The subway is a two-minute walk from the apartment; the C-Line goes directly to Manhattan without changing trains. The area as such is ok, we never felt unsafe (we are a family with 3 children). However, if you are looking for cozy and lovingly furnished cafés to linger in, you won't find them here.  The apartment itself was very clean and the kitchen was equipped with all the trimmings (we donated the peeler). She is in the basement, in the morning the sun shines into the bedroom, but during the day it is rather dark. The nearby road hardly makes any noise, rather the Long Island Express, which runs over an elevated route on Alantic Ave. Overall, really recommendable if you don't want to spend all your New York budget on accommodation (you're on the go all day anyway) with a great landlady!

Franck is very responsive to messages. There were 5 of us and Franck's apartment was spacious. The strong point is that the metro is really close by on foot (less than 5 minutes) and that all lines are accessible. 20-25 minutes from Times Square. The neighborhood is very pleasant and safe, I don't regret my choice. Small shop accessible less than 5 minutes on foot. The only weak point is the dust, otherwise the rest was clean. I recommend this apartment.
This place is a good place just the neighborhood is a little sketchy.Frank was good at communicating with us.
A very comfortable place to stay. Deirdre was very accommodating with some specific needs of mine. It made the trip less stressful.

My wife and I had a wonderful experience. Stacy is  an amazing host from the very beginning when she was able to accomodate our very last minute request as we had checked-in the night before at another Airbnb in the East Village (which unfortunately turned out to be a bad scam) so decided to get out of there the following morning and that's when I found Stacy's apartment. She had guests checking out then and she had to clean the apt, but she was kind enough to let us stop by to drop off our bags and get keys.  The place is great, spacious just like the pictures, super clean, everything well organized and operational, with plenty of extra kitchen and bathroom supplies. Easy access to the building, elevator. We loved the two windows facing south with a beautiful unobstructed view and plenty of sunlight pouring in. The bed is very comfortable. The building is super quite and we slept like babies. I travel a lot to NYC for business and this is great find which I recommend to anyone.

We had an amazing stay here! It had everything you could need and more, from a hair dryer to an ironing board. Everything was very clean which made our trip stress free and extremely comfortable! We would definitely stay here again.

Overall, our stay was okay. However, we would definitely not be staying here again and would rather spend extra on another place.   Location- This was really good because of the close proximity to Times Square, Subway and a variety of other facilities.  Host-Jason was polite and responded to all our messages.  Entrance to the accommodation-The hallway had a very unpleasant smell and looked dirty. The building has no elevator, but the flat was after two small flights of stairs.  The door to the apartment was a bit tricky to unlock.  Apartment- This was smaller than the impression the pictures gave us. However, it was clean, the bed was comfortable and there were WiFi and Roku TV which both worked.  There was no microwave which was an inconvenience.  Bathroom- Cleanliness was okay. However, the bathroom was very small, water spills easily onto the floor and anyone bigger than an average sized person would struggle.   Noise- There was a constant drilling noise that came on around 7am and lasted for most of the day which was very annoying. Apparently, it had to do with ongoing construction work which we were unaware of until after check-in.  There was no sound insulation in the apartment which meant that we could clearly hear the cars and people on the street.  The apartment is directly above a pub and the music from it can be heard from the apartment. We were also able to smell the cigarette smoke from outside the pub.   There was a constant draft coming into the flat which meant it was cold.

Nightmare Rental!! Danger, Danger. I should have listened to Kim's August 2017 review and Libby's October 2017 review. Don't make the same mistake!! Missing smoke detector, Missing a leg on the fold out couch making unusable. The air conditioning unit in the window does not have a cover, thus the freezing New York winter continuously blows in to the apartment directly onto your head as the top of the bed is less than two feet away from the open window. We had to literally use the band-aids from our first aid kit to try to arrange towels around the a/c unit in a way that would stop the flow of air. It did not work!!  Not to mention, the window is street side so you can hear all the noise from the street (I witnessed a fight, an accident and heard sirens and horns blaring all night and into the morning). If that wasn't enough you could hear loud music all night coming from the bar directly below. Additionally, the imagine on the TV was fuzzy and there were no curtains on the bathroom window so the neighbors could see in. The place was so miserable and unworkable that I spent over 4 hours the night I arrived trying to find a hotel to stay for the night during one of the busiest times of year, Thanksgiving weekend. Then another 4 hours communicating back and forth with airbnb to make other arrangements. Still after all that Jason refused to refund my stay so after the trip I spent many more hours over the course of 2 weeks communicating with Airbnb staff until I was finally granted a refund as well as a credit toward my next trip because of the hell that I was put through as a result of the rental. Save yourself the trouble and avoid this rental like the Plague. You can't say you haven't been warned!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

What a steal this place is. It's close to everything. Tons of food options as soon as you walk out the door. A few blocks from Times Square, a long walk to Grand Central and easily walkable to the Javits Center, which is why we were in town. WiFi is a little slow but worked well enough to stream the world cup on the provided Roku. There's a lot of foot and vehicle traffic right outside so be prepared for the accompanying noises of a second story walk up. Overall a great stay that I'd be happy to book again.

Convenient to beach and essentials. We came on the train so took Ubers/Lyfts to get further afield. I also know the area so was excited to be near the brewery and their tacos. Place was super comfortable with shade, AC, beds were great and Tory was accommodating and responsive.

This apartment was perfect for my two-and-a-half month stay: surprisingly quiet (there is currently a construction site next door but once you were in the apartment you wouldn't know it, and little traffic/street noise), secure and cosy. It's petite (although I suspect generous by NY standards!) but well equipped, including most kitchen bits and pieces you might need, and has plenty of storage. Because it's on the ground floor and looks out into the air shaft it stays very dark all day - great for sleeping but for me not so great for waking up. My host was generally responsive to queries/requests  but did not interfere otherwise. The location is convenient to transport and mid-town. Recommended.

Stayed here for 3 months on a work assignment. Location is AMAZING. 3 min walk to Madison square park and a few min walk to the R/W and 4 line subways. The building itself was nice and clean and the super & Eran were both really helpful when I had any issues and got back to me quickly. The apartment itself is honestly a great size for being a studio. There are 3 closets which was a necessity for me and all of my clothes. The kitchen is your classic nyc kitchen. Super small but has the basic necessities. Towards the end of my stay we had a few really hot days and the two AC window units worked extremely well. I was always comfortable. The only issue I had during my stay was several packages getting stolen so keep that in mind if you’re planning on having things shipped during your stay. The super was very helpful and told me I could let him know when things were delivered and he would grab them for me but unfortunately I had had a few things go missing already. All in all I definitely recommend Eran’s place if you’re going to be staying in NY!

Jay’s place was like everyone said, the perfect place to stay if you want to be able to see all of New York quickly and easily! We loved how close it was walking wise to all of the fun attractions, and we were easily able to catch a subway to explore the areas outside of midtown. Yes there is street noise but that’s what you get with an authentic manhattan apartment, ( we wore earplugs and had no issues sleeping), so I would not let that scare you away from this great place. It was fantastic to live like a local for a week and stay in this fun, cute apartment. Would definitely recommend to anyone! Also, Jay leaves a binder with tips for your stay and the luggage storage company for late flights was spot on. We really appreciated that input!

Unfortunately check in and finding the apartment was difficult. I suggest arriving during the day light hours to reduce stress if it’s your first NYC visit. The apartment was super clean, bigger than expected and an easy walk to Times Square. There’s a good bit of street noice; it didn’t bother us but it maybe disruptive you’re a light sleeper.

Nice convenient place to stay, next to Times Square and with nice amenities in the apartment. We used the subway to go all over New York. The bathroom is very small but the bed was comfortable. It was nice being able to watch Netflix with no issues. The location of the apartment has a lot of homeless people wandering about, sleeping around or doing drugs. But if you ignore them they won’t bother you for the most part. Overall, I thought it was cool to experience living in a New York apartment for two nights.

Among all the similar options there were to rent in New York, I chose this apartment because in November (when I booked) the description said "one bedroom apartment". It was very disappointing and frustrating to arrive and see that it is a studio apartment. At some point between my reservation and my check in, Jay changed the description to "midtown apartment" but he never informed me that it was a studio (I definitely would have canceled my reservation with this information). The apartment is well located but it should be noted that there are many homeless people and people taking drugs in the surrounding area. When the sun went down, it no longer felt safe to go outside. The apartment is OK for a two-day stay, but for a long stay like mine, it is NOT comfortable. It does not have enough kitchen equipment to cook, it does not have a kettle (one was visible in the photos) and you cannot use the oven, only the stove. The bathroom is very small and the shower area is very uncomfortable. The photos of this apartment are strategically taken so as not to notice that it is not what it seems.

I can not stress how wonderful this home is. After traveling through Europe in small single room hotels it was an utter delight to find a clean, warm, homey, open space to spread out and enjoy a relaxing integration into the states. From the tea kettle to the slippers and bathrobe, this space will help you feel like you are cared for. And if you love antiques... then you will appreciate Emily's eye for detail and accessory. Lastly, the hosts themselves were gracious, generous, and a wealth of knowledge about New York as a whole and the neighborhood. What a lovely find here in the Big Apple.

centrally located cozy place in Brooklyn. Perfect to get a New York trip with a hideaway from tourists and the stress.  Access to the apartment is through a stairway in the house that is separated from the living area. There are many really good cafes and restaurants close by and the F train around the corner will take you most anywhere in the city or at least connects to other trains that will. Great place!

The location was pretty good. Close to Restaurant Row and the Theaters. 10 min walk to a few different subway entrances. Jay is a good communicator and sent videos explaining where to find the lockbox and how to open it. One thing I didn’t realize before arriving is that you share a wall with an Irish pub. From Thursday to Sunday there was live music from there and several other bars close by. Bars close at 4am, so that’s when the music stops and you hear all of it, live or otherwise.  The lock on the apartment door is hard to figure out. The shower decides for itself what temperature it wants to be and it changes from scalding to freezing in a second.  The number on the building door is also different from the address listed, so it was confusing to get in.  The area is a bit sketchy at night, especially with all the bars. And with marijuana being legal, it smells everywhere. That’s not the host’s fault, but worth noting.  The apartment itself was fine. The kitchen is a lot smaller than it looks in the pictures. It smelled a bit musty and we heard clanging on the pipes all night long. We got used to the music, but the clanging (not sure if it was caused by wind or the heat running) was hard to sleep through.

Location is good, but overall the positives stop there. Unit is very loud - not just the traffic outside, but things beyond just the usual NYC experience. The pipes creak and rattle, the radiator and vents ding and crackle, the upstairs people stomp and shout. Also, keep in mind that there is a bar directly below the unit, where they blast music til around 1-3AM on most days. There is no trash can in the bathroom and nowhere to hang a towel - you have to walk out of the bathroom with soaking wet hands if you don’t physically bring a towel with you.   BIG warning about the keys and getting in and out of the unit and building. It was extremely difficult to get into the building. I’ve had my fair share of finicky locks, but that door is an absolute puzzle, and it needs the most EXACT touch to open. Not fun in the freezing cold. The door to the unit itself is basically busted and can’t be locked from the outside unless you “pre-load” the lock with the lock knob from the inside first.  When we had these problems, the hosts literally never responded to our requests for help. Also, they insist on communicating outside the Airbnb app for some stuff, which was understandable but a little sketchy. Be careful what they send you on there - Airbnb can’t hold hosts accountable for stuff they say outside the platform, so don’t get burned. Nothing directly sketchy happened, but just a fair warning.  OH and the address they give you on Airbnb is outright wrong - weird. The street number is different. Kinda off putting to be texted a different address from the one you thought you were going to until a half hour before you get there.

Sam and Emily's basement apartment was perfect for the trip I planned to New York for my husband. It was clean, comfortable, and allowed us to come and go so easily. Their keyless entry system meant I wasn't worried about carrying or losing anything extra. They are so close to an easy to navigate subway station which allowed us to leave our car parked (on street) throughout our entire weekend stay. They live within reasonable walking distance to plenty of places to eat and a drug store or two for anything you may have forgotten or need for your stay. There is not a tv (that I noticed) if that's something you like to have, but the wifi worked well. They request no shoes in the apartment and do provide slippers for guests but if sharing footwear is not your thing I would recommend bringing slippers or socks from home. We arrived prior to when I said we would be checking in and Sam and Emily were very flexible in allowing us to drop off our things as we set off exploring. They were also quick to respond to any questions and extremely friendly! I would definitely stay here again!

Although we didn't meet Sam and Emily they were very thorough and thoughtful hosts. The information provided before we arrived helped for a smooth check in and the guide book placed inside the apartment is filled with useful information. The on street parking wasn't stressful to find and we kept our car there while ubering to our destinations for the weekend. Sam and Emily's place is perfect for a quick Brooklyn stay with a mini fridge and some small amenities. The beds and couch were comfortable and we felt very safe there. *Bring some slippers although some are provided if you need them because the apartment is shoe free and the floors can be slippery. Cute and eclectic place. I would absolutely recommend to others. Thanks Sam and Emily!

We had a great stay in the apartment of Mark! It is small but beautifully decorated and in a super location - in the middle of a great neighborhood with nice bars and restaurants and very close to the subway. You live there quiet, safe and comfortable. The shady garden is a dream! Mark and his wife were very helpful and hospitable! If we should come to Brooklyn in the future, we like to stay with Mark again!

Emily was SO helpful & nice! Being a first timer in Brooklyn she was very fast to respond to my questions, making my trip way less stressful! check-in & parking was extremely easy and the location was perfect for an event we had at prospect park. Apartment was clean and very comfortable. We will definitely be back! ❤️

I can’t say enough good things about Sam & Emily! My boyfriend and I spent two nights in their space and LOVED it. They were awesome hosts and very communicative with us. Not only was the space super cute and comfortable, but it was also in a really great location with easy access to everything you could need. As both of us were not familiar with the area at all, the welcome packet they provided for us was full of great suggestions of things to do and see, and made the whole experience of being in an unfamiliar place super stress free!! I’d definitely recommend staying at their place to anyone. I know we’ll be back this summer :)

Our experience with Mark has been stellar - from fast and detailed communication before our stay, to one of the easiest and most accommodating check-in + out experiences that I've ever had, to a great room, this spot has it all. You can definitely tell the amount of thought and care Mark and Deanna put into their room. They provided us with multiple resources for getting to know Brooklyn, and considerately had many and all items a traveler might need in case they've forgotten something (toothbrush/toothpaste, band aids, feminine products, kitchen utensils + plates/cups, etc). The room itself was quite comfortable and well air-conditioned, with a useful sliding door for increased privacy in case one does use the pull out sofa bed. For the price, this room is a steal! Couldn't recommend it more!

Overall, Valentina’s place was fun, stylish, and in a great location. Williamsburg is awesome! We had a fun New Years weekend in Williamsburg and I’d come back. Beware of how loud it is outside, the walls are paper thin. And it was LOUD outside until 4am on the weekends.  We also arrived to the apartment a little earlier than check-in and couldn’t get in. Our host was completely unresponsive before we arrived and when we were trying to get in, so that was stressful. Luckily another woman helped us.

This hideaway is charming, clean and comfortable. Great location near the subway and beautiful Prospect Park! Lovely vibrent neighborhood with some great ethnic restaurants and shops. Sam and Emily are perfect hosts attentive but not intrusive. I especially appreciated all the information they supplied about the area and how to navigate the city. Honestly saved me hours of work and stress!

Shamaine was a fantastic host and made our New Year's stress free and fun! Check in was a breeze since Shamaine was easy to reach and very responsive. The room was EXACTLY as advertised and very spacious and comfortable. Shamaine was an easy going host and made us feel welcome and at ease. She was flexible with our check out time which was helpful since it was New Year's Day!

The appartment is really comfy and superclean. Shamaine is really polite, answers fastly and respects privacy (which I find really respectful). The room has air conditioning and is pretty large. It is not located in the best part of brooklyn, but I never felt unsafe. It is also really close to the Q and F train, which take you directly to Manhattan. Overall, this is a high quality place I would recommend, and Shamaine is a kind host that will make your stay in NYC easier.

Conveniently located close to the Church Ave Station that services the B | Q lines.  Shamaine was an excellent host who provided great information for my stay. She is very informative, personable and genuine.  The space is accurately depicted in all pictures and the interiors were well appointed. The room is larger than 75% of the hotel rooms in NYC and the price was definitely a steal.

Highly recommend this place for a multi night stay. Restaurants, drug stores, whatever you need directly around the corner. The Q train stop is a 5 minute walk away and got me to my job site in Manhattan in under 30 min daily. Best of all, the hosts are great at communicating and anticipating your every need.

The space is beautifully appointed, perfect size, perfect location. Right near the park and several subways for easy access to the city and the rest of BK. The skylights are a MAJOR plus! My boyfriend and I stayed here for a month and it felt just like home. Only thing that was sometimes stressful was cooking -- there's a gorgeous marble counter top in the kitchen and we needed to take extra care -- but other than that, Gigi's apartment can't be beat. She's super responsive too and even left us a bottle of wine upon arrival!
INCREDIBLY spacious! Easy to access and very cute. Minutes walk to Prospect Park at the most. If I could steal their shower room and put it in my own house, I would.

Good place, great neighbourhood!! Lots of restaurants, supermarkets,drug stores, shops and food trucks safe to walk at night for woman, close to LGA and JFK, M and R train to manhattan not so far, and of course, friendly host

I had a lovely time at Jasmina’s place! Though she was not there, Ileana (her roommate) and Chacha (their cat) made me feel right at home. The bed it big and comfortable, the room is clean and spacious. There is a nice desk and you even get some closet and fridge space. This is such a steal for so little per night and also in a safe area of NYC. One thing I would note is that it is located a little over a 10 minute walk from the closest subway station. Overall, this was an awesome stay and I do plan to return!!! I would definitely recommend their place for any single woman looking to visit the city!

This is a five star review. Zero stars for the communication and hospitality and five stars for the life lesson I learned based on my experience with Sam and Emily - a lesson on power of prejudice, perception and negative expectations.   I have no doubt Sam and Emily are fantastic hosts in the right circumstances. Mine were not. Looking back at my experience, it went south before we even arrived.   I had one bad review on my profile out of many. The review mentioned a cabinet door being broken off and a child. The reservation at Sam and Emily's was for adults only not but I had to make a very last minute change and had to bring one of my children with me. I informed the host. They called me, quoted the review. This is valid, I would do the same since we are staying at their place, I would also want to discuss my concerns. But it didn't end there  as they shared their thought with me - a thought of me tricking them into accepting the reservation by telling them it's just for adults when I knew all along I will bring my child. They even asked when I bought my child a train ticket. I paused. I didn't know how to respond to an idea (let alone a serious question) about planning my life around an Airbnb review. No, I didn't trick them. Yes, this was unexpected. We finished the discussion, both agreed to proceed and they charged me an additional fee for my child to stay with me.   Fast forward to the checkout day. I was so relieved to leave as it was so stressful to be in a place where you can't relax and feel unwelcomed. I was cleaning the entire time, moving thinds around and bugging my kid to not touch anything. On top, it's an old house and things seemed fragile. I was so relieved on the check out day, we were not only leaving but also leaving the place in a pristine condition. I proved their prejudice wrong. Not so fast! I was closing a bedroom door to make a last call before taking off, as I was closing the sliding door that leads into the bedroom, it came off the track. No force, no door slamming, simple human action to close a door. I informed the host. They asked if there were any damage to the door,  there was none. They told me they would take care of it after we leave. In the evening I received a long message with a passive aggressive narrative that only force and a 'bit of manhandling' could have caused the doors (plural) to be 'torn out it's track'.  The narrative also  included my child and my inability to keep a promise that my child won't break anything. Plus a damage bill. It didn't even cross their mind there could be a different scenario here. Maybe it was an adult who was closing the door? Maybe the track was getting loose? Maybe previous guests (over 350 of them) gave the door hard time and it was on its last breath when we arrived? Of course not, they already made up their mind before we even arrived and nothing said and done would have changed it. We had an issue with a sink during our stay, it didn't drain well. I informed the host about on day one of arrival. They were surprised to hear about it but didn't make a fuss, charged us or accused us of clogging the sink. I wonder if they would, had we had a negative review that talked about us clogging sinks?

I would not stay in this place again. I felt really unsafe by an unlocked door to a basement that it seems to be connected to other place and had some lights on. The door code was only one number repeated 4 times,  like a general number that anyone could actually open. Also the place needs some paint, the walls are extremely in poor condition as well as all the electrical outlets hanging off the walls and some don’t even working.

This place is a gem. Extremely clean and so spacious, very quite all hours of the day, kind neighbors, proximity to restaurants / grocery / shopping just down stairs. I've lived in several neighborhoods in NYC and Bay ridge is one of my favorites. It's also close to several parks and short walk to the Brooklyn Greenway.  Chris was very accommodating to my move in and move out dates with very fair pricing. Cannot stress enough that your not going to find a better deal in this city. Highly recommend to anyone needing to a place to stay!

Communication was great. Could not take a shower all week because there was no hot water. Was told we needed to deadbolt the door or it can be easily broken into, but the deadbolt was broken. Felt unsafe to sleep there and leave belongings there. Please fix these for the next guests. Otherwise these things, was good.

The area is quite sketchy and unkempt. We didn’t expect it at all and felt like the listing should specify more including pictures of the front of the house. Lexia the host should have made an effort to greet us with the area looking unsafe ( we was told by the host to not wear expensive items and stay together). Overall house was quite clean, however bathroom constantly had bugs and the living room each time we would come in from outside. You can hear the host from upstairs, the walls are very thin. However this didn’t bother us just as long as we knew who it was. Quality of pillows and beddings could be a lot better ( 1 pillow per guest is ridiculous) and also the water pressure in the shower was awful. Host was helpful with giving us clean towels when we asked for them. However no spare loo roll or beddings for us to change the bed which was annoying as we were there for 10 days. Our stay could’ve been a lot better, we‘re surprised Lexia is listed as a super host. Getting around was pretty easy the train station wasn’t a far walk, however an unpleasant one at times ( the locals can be verbally abusive). Lexia was a nice host but we had to be honest.

Lexia’s place has been gutted and turned into this minimalist yet very functional apartment. 30 minutes from Downtown to an hour from Times Square, it proved a comfortable and quiet getaway from the hustle and bustle of Manhattan. Though the neighborhood can appear a little rough around the edges in some parts, it never felt unsafe and had a good variety of grocery stores and restaurants on offer a few minutes’ walk. Lexia and her husband were beyond welcoming and accommodating and made our stay one that we look forward to experiencing again!

I loved staying at Eduardo's place- the price was a complete steal. It's clean, cozy, plenty of pillows, and everything you'd expect in a small NYC apartment. I stayed here for my visit to the zoo and would 5/5 recommend for sure.

Location wise honestly it’s really convenient with the bus located just nearby! However if you’d like a short walk (1km), you can easily make your way to the subway! The place was extremely clean and a definite steal for what you’re paying for! The heated bathroom floors made me want to stay in the bathroom! Having the host leave behind an entire book of recommendations was really helpful and not to mention having a fridge & a microwave came really in handy!

Clean super cute studio apartment with everything you could possibly need, even a cute updated kitchenette. She has a toaster for bagels, coffee maker for morning coffee. Iron and ironing board. Bed sleeps wonderful!!! Thanks again Katrina for your quick responses and reasonably cost apartment. Close to subway and even shopped at market on corner that is open to like 2 am. We never felt unsafe at all!!!

I stayed here with my mom for a week and it was a wonderful experience! The apartment was super clean and stocked with the essentials. It’s also very roomy and bright, exactly as pictured. Only half a block to the subway, and there is a sizable supermarket one street up, as well as a few good delis and a bakery on the neighboring streets. The neighborhood was pretty quiet, street noise was never an issue.  We never felt unsafe walking around the area. Just be smart and aware of your surroundings. From JFK, you can easily take the AirTrain to the subway, then get there with just a couple of transfers - much cheaper than an Uber/Lyft and really simple. That trip (one-way) also only took us about an hour and 15 mins total. It’s only about a 20 minute subway ride to Midtown.  All around it was a really cool place. I would absolutely stay here again!

It is the Latin American region (Bronx) near the subway rides, very noisy. Across the street whorehouse(brothel). Frankly, I was afraid to leave the car in the street it seemed to me it's not safe. we didn`t  met owner, he simply left the keys in the Lock box. As soon as we entered the house I immediately felt the nasty smell, I do not know what the smell it was but I just started allergy. The room what we rented was closed with a key. The room looked exactly like the photos from the website. But the bed linen, I thought, nobody never changed. Lying in that bed I frankly disdained and I always had to look out the window to check my car intact. Bathroom had no soap, no towels,  no toilet paper , nothing. And bathroom was very dirty. We decide to didn`t stay there even for one night. When contacted with the host, which would cancel the reservation, he said, "you need to wait my brother, and speak to him." We had to wait 1.5 hours. When his brother came, he just checked everything well, but on the cancellation of the reservation did not say anything! And then we could go, canceling reservations through the site. I definitely do not recommend this place!

Donald's accommodation matched the photos perfectly, the room is spacious and clean. We were welcomed by Donald's brother who was very nice.  The wifi connection (which by the way had excellent speed) was available for the first 5 days, then nothing. But it didn't bother us because we were so exhausted from our days that we didn't pay attention to this kind of detail! TV was available but we didn't use it. The location of the room was perfect, we were 5 minutes walk from the train which took us to Manhattan (it takes at least 45 minutes to reach the city). There were several shops nearby, which was very convenient for us to buy breakfast.  On the other hand, we encountered two problems: the first concerned the dirt in the bathroom and the second concerned the inhabitant of room 3, who was very noisy and very unpleasant to the point where he woke us up at 3 a.m. for a cup problem. We were very disappointed. Apart from that everything went very well. And I wanted to point out that the neighborhood was very quiet.

We had the opportunity to contact Fe at any time, she was absolutely helpful and our questions were always answered. Everything was totally enjoyable and good. The nights weren't always quiet because the apartment is in the flight path of JFK Airport. Nevertheless, we were able to sleep with the window open. It takes about an hour to get to Manhattan by bus and subway, but it's really easy. The bus stops are right on the street. The unlimited Subway weekly pass includes the entire route to your front door. We never felt unsafe and even around 11 p.m. we had no concerns or unpleasant situations on the way home.

Great place. Awesome hosts. The only drawback is that there’s very little natural light. I’d argue that you end up paying too much for what you get.   The communication was comprehensive, but it is a little overwhelming. Dozens of long messages and emails and documents and lots of questions and detailed instructions that all seem to go on and on - it can get a little stressful. I really appreciate the time and effort put into this, but it would be even better if it was all simple and straightforward.

We have had a fantastic two weeks stay in this appartment. It is very nice decorated,it has a good cozy atmospfere, a well equipped kitchen, a good shower, a very good bed and a nice place outside. The appartment is located in a quiet neighbourhood and we never felt unsafe there. The J-line is very close by and connects you to Manhattan with a beautiful view from the Williamsburgbridge. There is a supermarket nearby, as well as agood deli at the corner two passes away. Martin is a nice owner who lives with his very friendly wife upstairs. The communication with Martin was fast and helpfull. We would return to this appartment again.

We didn’t have the best time at Martin’s place and are only leaving a review as we rely on reviews for making decisions on where we should stay. Firstly, I’ll say that the property was in a good area, really accessible to 2 subway stations. The bed and living area were very comfortable and the kitchen and bathroom facilities were great. However, we had a really big problem with the noise level coming from upstairs (the host’s home). The hosts’s wife was home all day with a baby, and in the morning, afternoon and late in to the evening there was banging, stomping, screaming and other ridiculously loud vocal noises that were inescapable. In the mornings if we wanted to sleep a little later, we couldn’t. In the evenings, we couldn’t come back to relax after a long day exploring without turning up the volume on the TV. It was our honeymoon and we certainly wouldn’t have booked anywhere with a child if it had been mentioned. We tried contacting the host to ask him to lower the level of noise but if anything it only got louder. Taking things through Airbnb, it only got nasty and he went as far as calling us scammers and trying to blame the noise on the fact we were staying in Brooklyn, when the sounds from outside didn’t bother us at all. It’s safe to say it spoiled our honeymoon quite a bit so I can’t say I recommend this place.

My husband and I arrived near 11 pm to NYC and made it to this Airbnb. The property was located inside the owner’s primary residence. Not our usual choice, but for the price, we decided to give it a try. We were greeted but the owner, she was kind and headed out for the night. Exhausted, we head in the unit and lay down. The bed furnishings were stale smelling. We cracked a window to air it out. We began to unpack and noticed the stains on the chairs and carpet. We covered them with a blanket. Still willing to stay. We laid back down and a roach crawled across the floor. It’s NYC we thought! What’s one roach?? I jump in the shower- asked the husband to check the bed for anymore creepy critters. The bed had multiple blood stains on the sheets and mattress. This was the final straw. At 1 am, we packed up and braved the city for more suitable housing. We were glad to get a full refund. I would not recommend this property until it undergoes a serious cleaning/renovation. Save yourself the trouble and book elsewhere.

A beautiful old brownstone walk up on a quiet street with a great host. Gorgeous woodwork and a very funky bathroom. We felt safe, even at night, but be aware there are a lot of homeless and addicted people on the busier streets nearby. It feels mostly sad and disturbing, not dangerous.

Martin & Hande’s place is exactly as described and pictured. Super convenient location close to multiple subway stations (4-6 min walks), which makes it really easy to get into Manhattan and around Brooklyn. We walked home from the subway past midnight on several occasions and never felt uneasy or unsafe. We had a wonderful stay and would definitely come back. Thank you!

At the time of my booking (late 2019), there was an omission from Victor's listing description which will be relevant to most travelers: he also rents out the common living room to a guest - the sofa shown in the photos turns into a bed. This means when you go to use the restroom, you will be crossing through another guest's sleeping area. It also means that potentially 3 or more people are sharing one bathroom, instead of 2 as one might think from the incomplete description. So, I was surprised to find out another guest was staying in the living room when I arrived. On the night of my check-in, I searched on Airbnb and found Victor's separate listing for the living room. Most people will not think to do this search - THIS listing should give a complete description.  Victor also handled some communication inappropriately. The day after I arrived, he had another guest checking in. Out of the blue, before talking with me about it, he sent me and another person (let's call her "Jenny") a WhatsApp message saying "Hi [Jenny], I am adding you to this chat for possible backup assistance accessing the apartment from Chad...in case my two self check-in options fail." Later on, I got a message  in a separate thread from Jenny saying "Hi Chad this is [Jenny] I'm supposed to get a key from you? I ordered a Lyft and should be there..."  The appropriate way to handle this would be for Victor to talk to me first and ask me if he can refer me to his other guest as a backup. Suddenly, I'm getting messages from a person I never met before and I feel responsible for checking her in.  This was in addition to an earlier message I got from Victor where he asked me to move some bedsheets, linens, and comforter from my room to another location. In isolation, I wouldn't consider this a big ask. But this combined with Victor referring his other guest to me made me feel like I was responsible for checking in his guest for him. I understand Victor was out of the country, but that doesn't negate his responsibility towards his guests. If he's not able to appropriately handle check-in while he's away, he shouldn't rent out his room on those dates. As a guest, he shouldn't be expecting me to help him manage his Airbnb listing, even as a "backup."  Finally, it ended up that although Victor intended to have only one guest stay in his living room, it ended up there were three people staying in living room my first night there. They were also drinking and making noise until at least 3am. I alerted Victor to this and he apologized and offered me earplugs (which don't work for me). This other guest was mostly at fault here, but the host also shares some responsibility for this for two reasons: 1) As of late 2019, Victor has only one house rule for both listings - no smoking. That's it. He has NO rules about noise past a certain time, outside guests, or parties. If he had more house rules as most other Airbnb hosts do, he would be less likely to have more guests than he intends, and he'd be more likely to have respectful guests. 2) Airbnb hosts have some degree of responsibility for vetting their guests. As a host, you don't have to accept all requests that come in. It could be that Victor did vet this other guest, but given the situation, it calls into question whether this vetting was actually done.  On a positive note, I ended up cancelling after the first night, and Victor gave me a full refund for all three nights (minus Airbnb service fee). However, this did not make up for the stress and inconvenience of the situation. Victor might say it my choice to cancel - yes it was, because I felt uncomfortable after everything that happened the very first night there. I think many other people would too.  I could be misunderstanding - given that Victor has practically no house rules, it's possible that he intends this listing for partiers. I would say given the low cost of the listing, lack of house rules, and the fact that's it's fairly clean, I would recommend it to people who intend to party, stay up late, and don't care about sleep. I would not recommend this place to somebody who wants to sleep at normal hours because you're effectively rolling the die - maybe the person in the living room will be nice and quiet, maybe they won't. I also recommend verifying that Victor will be in NYC before booking.

We stayed at Keona's place for 5 nights. She was extremely helpful and welcomed us into her space. The apartment was extremely close to the train station for easy access to Manhattan. There is a police station a few hundred meters down the road and it is a family neighbourhood, so we didn't feel unsafe even when walking from the train late at night. If your looking for a place to stay in Brooklyn or somewhere close to Manhattan I recommend staying at Keona's place

Good apartment, very well located close to everything so definitely an excellent bang for your buck !  We noticed some insects around the kitchen but Ajitpal was super fast addressing the issue so nothing really scary to call out, it’s definitely a super good deal !

Great place to stay while I looked for apartments in the area. For a second floor apt and the location this apartment is a steal. The management was super easy to work with and quick to reply. Place was clean and easy to maintain, this is NYC so you will see mice and cockroaches, don’t freak out. I mentioned to them to update the TVs and fix the water pressure so hopefully they do 😉

My family (2 kids + 2 adults) had a great stay in Gordon's two bedroom apartment.  The apartment was very clean and had easy access to public transportation, shopping, Central Park, gym and free COVID testing sites.  It was very welcoming to have dishwashing liquid, paper towel and toilet paper provided so we didn't have to stress about getting the shopping done during the first two nights. Though located on a busy street we didn't hear the traffic, the windows are well insulated.  The building does not have an elevator so be prepared to use the stairs and the paid laundry is located in the basement. The kitchen is well equipped. There is good WiFi, we  comfortably worked and attended school remotely. Gordon was a very good host, very responsive and helpful.

This place is amazing! Daniel and his wife were wonderful hosts. Even after me and my bf were 3 hours late daniel still welcomed us with a warm smile. The place had everything and more that's expected at an airbnb. Amazon fire, all kitchen supplies, they even left coffee milk juice and some snacks for us, and the bathroom also had all toiletries in case you forget yours. They really go the extra mile to make your stay comfortable and stress free. They had ac which was perfect for the summer heat/humidity. They also had some maps and bus info laid out for us which helped us navigate the public transportation. The location is a bit further from Manhattan but we didn't mind the commute. I recommend downloading the nyc subway app it comes in handy. The neighborhood was lively during the day but died down at night. There's plenty of stores around and places to eat that stay open late or 24 hours. I will definitely be staying here the next time I visit.

It was very nice to have the whole place to ourselves. A little farther from the city than I would have liked but it was very straight forward to get there. The area seems a little sketchy at first, but we had no issues at all.

Decent little nook for a short stay in Brooklyn. My partner and I took a short trip together (he from Austin, I from London) and were looking for a crashpad for a few days. The apartment is basic but it's charming and has pretty much what you would need for a few nights' stay.  It has air conditioning and a great shower which were both great during the summer heat.    Check-in was easy and convenient as it used a self-service lockbox to retrieve the keys. However the hosts were minimally communicative/responsive; I didn't get any welcome or even thank you message after booking, and they were very slow to respond to messages I sent with updates about our arrival (since our flight was cancelled) and questions about amenities of the apartment. Once they did respond they were friendly and informative enough, but I would expect responses within a few hours not the next day. For people who are okay with hands-off hosts this might be fine, but personally I like Airbnb because of the personal touch and feeling reassured that I have some support when I'm in a foreign unfamiliar place.   The neighbourhood around Utica / Church is bustling and has a lot of West Indies food spots -- we had some amazing vegan Jamaican food at Nanni Health Food Store (enjoyable not just for vegans!).   Getting around Brooklyn and travelling to Manhattan was straight forward once we knew the way but we were surprised by how long it took to get places (to get to Prospect Park took us almost an hour and it didn't seem that far on the map, but maybe it's all subjective depending what you're used to). We soon became familiar with taking the B46 bus just a block from the apartment, which takes you to Eastern Parkway where you can get the Subway to various places. The apartment's location is okay but not the most convenient -- if you're planning on going back and forth to Manhattan keep in mind you may need to factor in over an hour each way, and even exploring Brooklyn you may want to check in advance depending on what you want to visit during your stay. We definitely didn't get as much in as we had wanted. Of course this is not anything to do with the apartment, but something to consider for folks who may not be as familiar with getting around New York.   Some things to note about the apartment:  1. The apartment door only has the one lock, and the handle/keyplate on the inside seemed to be held on with sellotape which was a bit disconcerting. The door seemed to lock just fine but more security- or safety-conscious people might not be comfortable with this. 2. Being in a lively part of Brooklyn it was quite noisy, with the sound of sirens and street noise coming through the closed windows quite easily. This wasn't a problem for us and it didn't prevent us sleeping but for light sleepers it might be something to keep in mind.  3. The linens provided were very basic: there were only a couple of towels and a couple of facecloths (which may not be ideal in the middle of summer when you might need extra showers after exploring the city all day), there were no dishcloths or teatowels in the kitchen (we had to use one of the facecloths to dry glasses/dishes which was not great), and there was only the one thin sheet on the bed (and an uncomfortable-looking synthetic sheet on the sofa bed) and no quilt or blanket. Even though it was summer I would have expected some spares or extra linens in case we got cold or wanted the comfort of an extra (if you have a partner who steals the sheets for example!) 4. The lid of the garbage can in the kitchen did not close so I had to weigh it down with a book as I was worried about cockroaches. This may have been a temporary thing but something to note if you plan on eating in the flat.  Overall the apartment was good enough for a couple of nights as a roof over our head and was decent value for money, but I probably wouldn't stay here again.

During my stay, I was mostly out exploring the city, but the time I did spend in Victor's apartment was very pleasant. It's in a great location and is easily accessible by foot and multiple subway lines.  I never felt unsafe walking back late at night. Victor and his girlfriend were accommodating, kind, and easy to talk to. I would definitely stay with them again.

Is it creepy to want to be new best buds with your hosts? Then call me a creep! They were super accommodating of my ever changing work schedule, the place was sparkling clean, perfect location, they constantly checked in to make sure I was comfortable, great TV options, lovely downstairs neighbor...what else can I say? They are wonderful hosts and humans.

My friend and I booked this place for a two week trip and ended up moving to a hotel for a few days in the middle of our visit because this airbnb was so different from what we were expecting for the price and the listing materials.   First, the condition of the unit/the building are much worse than the photos in the listing would lead you to believe. We did not expect luxury and we understand that airbnbs are well-loved homes, but were pretty shocked to find a bulge that looks like poorly managed water damage on the ceiling of one of the bedrooms and cracks on almost every wall. The white paint that looks really nice in the photos is actually a patchwork. The furniture has aged and discolored a bit, which is natural - but there are stains on chairs and nightstands, the kitchen light consists of a lightbulb on a wire looped around a cabinet handle, the microwave is missing a door handle and there is no other mechanical release mechanism, so you have to pry it open with your fingernails. The building itself has somewhat sketchy stairs - they are narrow (probably no more than 2.5 feet wide), and the landings all sag.  Second, the noise is significant, even by NYC standards - aboveground subway tracks run near the unit and there are no buildings in between to absorb any of the sound, so the windows rattle a bit when a train goes by.  Third, the hosts were sometimes hard to get ahold of - we called, texted, and messaged via airbnb at our pre-arranged check-in time about literally not being able to access the keys to the apartment, and didn't receive a response (or acknowledgment?) until the next day. Thankfully the unit was left completely unlocked (which was another surprise, but the building and the area felt quite safe), so we were able to get into the unit that night.  In short, we would not have stayed here had we had been aware of all of the above. We hope this information offers an update to the other reviews here, which might be outdated.

Timothy & Katrin's place is the most welcoming home away from home!!  The first word to describe the apt and them is GENEROUS and IMMACULATE. It is treehouse cozy and they have made such ample, beautiful use of a small space - which ultimately feels big. The apartment is furnished as if you live there - love the furniture and so many places to sit - great closets, hangars, extra drawers - full kitchen with an incredibly generous array of food basics including organic rice, gluten-free pasta, every appliance and utensil - coffee/tea, etc. It isn't the typical bare kitchen with minimal, cheap items which gives you the feeling of "this isn't stocked because you might steal nice items" - the bathroom is small but super cute and modern. There are ACs in each of the bedroom which does surprisingly keep the rest of the apt cool. Note that the location is right next to the Williamsburg bridge and major traffic intersections so you're sleeping with a high urban noise factor.  I popped in earplugs & they did the trick. Timothy & Katrin's communication is downright amazing and they're right there no matter what you need. I don't know how they do it while having their own lives :)  It is hands-down the best Airbnb I've ever been to and I look forward to returning!!!
I had an amazing time! Victor was very welcoming and super helpful! Cannot stress enough that if you look for something good at a great peor, go for Victor’s place!

Positive points: 2 bedrooms, air conditioning, exchanges with hosts Negative points: very dirty neighborhood, homeless person in front of the front door, very noisy (car traffic, skytrain, etc.), very dark living room, no blackout curtains in one of the two bedrooms OK for a short stay but I do not recommend for a long stay, I chose Brooklyn to be a little quieter... Bad choice!

This was my very first time using the app. I will never use it again now. It was very suspicious and the host even asked us to be discrete because he was illegally hosting people. There happened to be even more people staying in the living room and we were not able to use the bathroom in the morning due to there being only one and the place was basically a hostel.

It was my very first time using Airbnb and going to New York from Georgia. Needless to say, I was extremely nervous and scared. Having Memo as our host was the best decision we made on this trip! He made us feel so welcomed, gave us nice tips about the city, made sure we were always doing alright. The place was very clean (no shoes in the house), the room convenient, and the apartment building had security so only residents could enter which for me, was a huge bonus in safety. Obviously anywhere in New York will be a bit spooky if you’re a girl and you walk alone past midnight but the community was easy to get around and close to the station like described (Times Square about 20 mins away)! Memo also offers a service to pick you up/drop you off at the airport which really helped. If anyone ever asked me to recommend an Airbnb to stay at for New York I’d 100% tell them about Memo’s place no doubt. :)

The WORST Airbnb experience I’ve ever had. Our flight was delayed several hours due to Hurricane Michael. I’ve told Matthew prior to boarding that we would be late and he was okay with it. Upon arriving, I find multiple messages from him on my phone *mad* because I wasn’t replying to him right away (of course, I was on the plane). The texting didn’t stop for the entire time we were at the airport trying to retreive our bags. After hours of stress and being extremely tired trying to arrive at our talk at Columbia, I had to feel insecure when waiting for a cab at LaGuardia because Matthew essentially said he was “tired of waiting”: “We don’t accept check in this late”, “You received our message but didnt reply” and “Please take a taxi and get around before we sleep” are just few examples of his behavior that implied we would be left without a place to sleep at almost 1 am.    The rude messages started after I said *again* we didn’t need him to pick us up at the airport. He kept insisting that he offered a pickup service at the airport, to which I politely declined MULTIPLE times (I didn’t want to be impolite by asking whether the service would come with an additional charge, so I just said we wouldn’t need it). He just kept pushing it and even wrote “And We offered you pick up” as if I ever said I wanted it.  The room was extremely noisy, the pillows were horrible and there were no towells/soap etc on the bedroom or bathroom. The bed sheets were not clean and the bedroom was dusty.  Also, as his listing does not make explicit that the bathroom is shared, we imagined the bathroom would be only for us (indeed, that’s why we ended up booking with him instead of with other options, as these had “shared bathroom” clearly stated). The address is also wrong. He texted us while already on the cab on our way to his home with the correct address information, which I imagine if you’re traveling from abroad without LTE service would be a huge problem.   All these issues with the apartment, however, are minimal compared to the behavior he displayed prior to our arrival with multiple messaging and really, really rude texts. I’ve already had not so great experiences with other Airbnbs, but I always held back from writing bad reviews. I know this is important for many hosts, and most issues can be dealt with. But this time I felt that I wouldn’t want anybody else to feel the way we did, particularly under the circumstances we were facing.

the host is very nice, a wonderfull person who was very accomodating of our very late (midnight!) arrival. he had some great suggestions of places to eat and things to see and do!   couple of things to note: -the location is actually inacurate on airbnb, its just down the street a little bit, still close to the subway -you will be sharing the place with the host and very likely 2 others each night (plan your bathroom and showers accordingly). one person will be hosts boyfriend (seems nice) and the hosts 'new yorker friends' (who often had luggage but also kept to themselves in another bedroom) -the host may ask you to meet at a nearby mc donalds, its safe as best we could tell, just seems a bit sketchy, he took about 10 mins to pick us up and helped us with our bags. it meant we didnt have to wait in a dark street which was ok.  -there are about 6 flights of stairs and no elevator to get up to the apartment -byo towels, none provided -the view of the bay requires you to literally stick your head out of the window but its nice -be very careful when you book that the number of people is correct, airbnb made some error and booked for 1 when we had 2. host charged us 50$ extra.  -the bed is ok, nothing amazing or super comfortable (a little lumpy) but you can sleep in it ok.  -the room itself is huge with a closet and desk, very nicely decorated too! -the carpet/rug in the bedroom prevents the door being opened fully, perhaps it just needs to be moved? -location is great, less than 5mins walk to the 1 train that takes you to times square in 20minutes  overall, great host, ok accom, great location, price was a bit more than i would have liked (after the additional charge the value was not as good). 4/5
The nicest host, who I ever meet. Anthony is very helpful in any problems or topics. I was afraid of the neighborhood, but its also very calm and safe. I can recommend this place for everyone.

Pro This place has a really great location, metro is just across the street. Host was wonderful, he is very kind and also helping us brought luggage up the stairs. The second floor toilet is big. A lot of stuff in the kitchen that you can use, they even got a rice cooker!! It have 2 mirrors in the room, one of them is full body mirror!  Con You gotta climb a stairs to get in, not that high but kinda rough for people who have a big heavy luggage. There are 2 cats in the house, people  who allergy to animals fur might be a bit problem, however we saw the cats just once. Room might be a bit small for a really large group, our group has 5 people, 8 luggage (4 huge luggage), it don’t have that much space to open the luggage.  It’s a good place for staying in brooklyn, neighborhood is not scary, location is perfect for people who travel by metro.

Pro:  1) The location is great, you can get to the subway within 1 minute. 2) friendly host, Anthony checked in from time to time and are really responsive, he tried his best to accommodate your need.  Con:  1) since it’s at a really convenient location (right across the subway and right next to a major road), the noise can be loud. If you are sensitive to noises you might want to stay somewhere further away from the major roads 2) as the listing says, expect there to be multiple cats in the house (not in your room), and it could have some unpleasant smell 3) depends on the time you are there, you might encounter some inconsiderate tenants in the house, I have an issue with the noise from the tenant with a dog upstairs, the person is constantly making loud noises going up and down and walking around in his room or moving furniture 2 in the morning. The dog on the other hand is super quiet.  Overall, Anthony is really helpful and is a great host.

Fanny's place was exactly what you see in the pictures. Lovely interior designs with lots of great books. Really thankful she added a sofa bed for me and my friend for our stay. She responds very quickly and checks up on you via message! Everything about her place was fantastic except for the location. It was a bit further than we expected and felt a bit dangerous for me and my friend to come home to at night so we ubered home most days.
Large 3 bedroom. Plenty of room, large rooms,  and within a quick uber if all the trendy Brooklyn spots. If you are splitting a few ways its a steal.

Lisa asked me for our flight information so she could be there and welcome us. She checked the arrival time and messaged me to see if everything was okay. Lisa took care to explain to us the operation and rules of the house and also mentioned that she was available if we needed anything. I was staying in New York with my 5 year old son and Lisa had taken the trouble to put toys for him in the apartment. A welcome bottle of wine was reserved for me...  The apartment is bright, the decoration soothing; it is located in a quiet street, close to several supermarkets and restaurants. Access is easy as it is served by several metro lines; but be careful especially on weekends, there is often work and you need to check the metros that are running. Central Park is just a 10 minute walk away!..  There are so many things in New York that you can't get bored!!... And with a little organization, even when leaving Harlem, a lot is possible.

The apartment is really clean and nice just like the pictures! The neighborhood is quite. Lisa, the landlord is really nice and patient! There are enough towels available in the room and there are enough tableware sets to fulfill the needs. The only thing I am worried about is the soundproof of the floor. I like to stay up late. I could hear the sound of the floor when I was walking so I afraid that if I bother someone. The apartment is close to the subway stop. It only takes 3 stops to The Times Square if you take Line 2. But it is a little expensive(approximately $40-50) for taking Uber to downtown Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn. Overall, it is a wonderful place to stay and relax！

Lisa is an awesome host! Her communication with us was incredible!  This is a very nice and cozy spot to come back to after a busy NYC day.  Lots of little extras and attention to details were so appreciated.  It was nice to have a very well stocked kitchen to make breakfast in each morning!   A couple of small issues... heating/cooling was preset and made for very hot sleeps and trips in the night to get the AC going and the neighbourhood was a bit scary at times.  Also LOTS of stairs up to the suite.  Subways were quite close but parking is not easy to find on the street.

Everything was exactly as it was advertised. Spotless bedrooms, bathroom, glorious shower. Clean towels and sheets. And even though the neighborhood never gave off any dangerous vibes, there's something about a lot of locked doors between you and the outside that makes you feel secure. No complaints whatsoever.

Very nice unit and location, but not ideal if planning on having any guests due to extra charge. No cable tv available. Communication with host was not as relaxing as I would have hoped. In the end, host was accommodating, but there were several prior stressful exchanges before resolving the guest fee issue.

Razia and Harvey's appartment is beautifuland located in a nice neighbourhood! We were welcomed by Harvey which is a very ice guy! Turns out he could speak pretty well Dutch so that was a surprise! We had a great time! Subway is close and it's pretty quiet at night if you look at the newyork standard. It was also very clean and the beds were very comfortable!  Not much kitchen utilities but that's Ok for newyork!  I guess razia and Harvey must have had bad experiences with clients because theynhave pretty strict rules and it's gonna ciost you when youy break them! So that's a bit scary! But overall pretty nice!

Raquel's apartment was great for our trip! The apartment was spacious and clean. There was plenty of room for the four of us who stayed. Raquel was easy to work with and always responded quickly. She helped make our trip stress free.

Raquel was amazing, she helped us a lot. Even though her english isn't very good, she was able to communicate and give us all the necessary information. The apartment was very clean, but the building wasn't. So, don't be scared, the building is a bit smelly, but the apartment was totally the opposite. Bedrooms: It was hard to sleep because only one of the bedrooms had blackout curtains. But the beds were very comfortable, and the bed sheets were clean. There weren't any blankets, just a comforter.  Kitchen appliances: Excellent refrigerator, excellent coffee machine (small, but great!), we didn't use the stove, great toaster. Kitchen utensils: forks, knives, spoons, glasses, plates, cups, everything was ok. but there were no cereal bowls. Bathroom: quite small but great. Very clean, and everything was working perfectly. There were no towel holders, this was a bit of a problem. After you take a shower, there's no place to put your wet towel. And there's no towel holder for hand towels. Internet and TV: Perfect! We didn't see a lot of TV, but it was working. Internet connection was awesome! Fast and excellent! Ironing clothes: The iron was good, and the iron table was very good. Location: 5 to 10min walk => supermarkets, subway stations, laundromats, restaurants. Neighborhood: We felt very safe. Some nights we got home at midnight, and there were police cars driving around the streets, and people were very friendly.

I was looking for a quiet, clean place that would be a quick commute to my office downtown and got exactly that with Priscilla's place. She is a great host and made for a great roommate, as I was staying at her place for close to a month. She was beyond accommodating - allowing my girlfriend to stay with me the first night before she took a flight out of NYC, although I had booked the place just for myself; allowing for an easy check in/check out; seemingly constantly cleaning the place; communicating quickly and well. The place itself is nothing marvelous - your usual pre-war Astoria building that is maintained just enough...but it was sufficient for my needs and exactly what I was looking for, since I know the neighborhood well and have lived there myself. Over the course of ~4 weeks I saw Priscilla roughly 5 times - she was either out working; our schedules did not overlap; or she was quietly keeping to herself in her room. Could not have asked for a better place and a better roommate, so thank you for making my stay a pleasant and stress-free one! ;)
Charlene was very amazing and a great host ! She attacked any problems we came across first night so we had a smooth experience. She kept in touched and was overall very good.
