Laurie has a helpful son and two nice cats, so don´t be afraid of Badman and Robin (the cats), because they might jump to your bed in the middle of the night..... :) Would recommend this place!

Our week-long stay with Laurie was very pleasant. We arrived quite late on the first day but Laurie waited for us. The next day at breakfast she gave us some explanations in French about the visits to be made and gave us the keys to her house so that we could come and go as we pleased. Every morning we used the refrigerator to prepare our breakfast and make ourselves at home.  Laurie's house is located in a very quiet area. We often returned quite late at night without ever feeling unsafe. The metro is very close to the accommodation, providing access to Manhattan in around 3/4 hours.

Thanks to Chris we had an unforgettable experience in New York. He was a great host who let us as much privacy as we needed but was always there for a chat and very good suggestions of what to do and to eat. His condo is absolutely great, clean and in a nice neighbourhood. This way we got to know a lot of Brooklyn we wouldnt have seen if we had stayed in Manhattan. And even at three o'clock in the morning it was still not dangerous to get home for two girls like us. We would definitely stay with him again!

Laurie lives in a beautiful historic home in Park Slope, Brooklyn. The location was ideal for us. Travel time from JFK with subway 1 hour 15 minutes. We really liked the area, a huge selection of shops, restaurants, cafes and services; everything within walking distance. You live safely and have a good connection to the subway to Manhattan, about 30 minutes to downtown. We explored Manhattan during the day and went back to Park Slope for dinner in the evening, where there are also numerous bars with live music. The area around Laurie's Airbnb is a better alternative to Manhattan, better restaurants and cafes, cheaper and slower, far away from mass tourism and stress. The restaurant “Tambour” is highly recommended, excellent quality and great value for money, good wine selection, the lasagna is a must!! Laurie is magical as a host, she is very helpful, with lots of tips and tricks, provides maps and information in the house, she knows the best restaurants in the area. Laurie is very loving and we had great conversations with her. We would always love to come back!!

The host was present in the apartment every night, but at no time did he have contact with us, he did not introduce himself and did not welcome us, which was quite strange and uncomfortable. It was a quiet coexistence.  From the fourth day of our stay, the wifi stopped working and we were without internet until the last day.  The published photos do not match the real state of the room and apartment. The apartment is very dirty, with an accumulation of things in the common spaces, it is messy and very deteriorated, with broken furniture in the room, plugs with the cables sticking out, the floor dirty and all scratched, the windows dirty, the chest of drawers also broken. It is not a liveable place, I would not return under any circumstances. In fact, the photos published at the time of my reservation were different, the ones now look much worse and the reality is even worse. The bathroom was dirty, the water in the shower was impossible to adjust, either cold or boiling, and bad water pressure. The kitchen has nothing to do with the photo, very dirty, with a lot of accumulated things, dirt and smell. Very unpleasant in general. The apartment is abandoned, dirty, disorganized, deteriorated. Despite spending the whole day outside and the good location, it is not justified to reserve this apartment to sleep, it is impossible to bathe, use the comfortable bathroom and sleep peacefully due to the disorder and dirt, it is very uncomfortable to sleep there, with very dirty padding that does not make you want to use or touch. I clarify that I booked the accommodation because I read many good comments, but reading the comments in recent times negative comments began to appear and now mine. I'm sorry I booked, those positive comments had nothing to do with my experience. The location was the ONLY good thing about the accommodation, and it does not justify its reservation. I clarify that I have stayed in hostels and very basic and simple places, but comfortable, cozy and clean, you don't need much but you do need the basics, and I didn't find it here. I'm sorry to be harsh, but I prefer to tell my experience honestly so that others can avoid bad experiences.  And if you ask me why I stayed, it's obvious, because going out to look for accommodation was impossible due to the high costs in Manhattan.

The location and hosts were great and super easy. Would definitely recommend staying here. The only downer for us was the shower only being freezing or boiling hot which was a little bit unpleasant. But apart from that it was perfect for us! Thanks

Good neighborhood, ~10/15 minutes to Downtown with the C train. Awesome room (huge, clean, beautiful!). I would stress over all, the hosts: Chris and Jen and are great couple and make you feel like you are at home. Zero complaints.  I couldn't recommend it more.

Chris and Jenn are fantastic hosts! Made us feel very comfortable and at home. Chris gave us a lot of great tips on local restaurants and things to do. Neighborhood is safe and very convenient to the subway line into Manhattan. Room was nice, clean, and bed was comfortable. If you're craving Mexican food check out Xochtil Taqueria. For a local low-key bar check out Hudson dry. Great Atmosphere and friendly people. Overall a 10 out of 10 and a great location to check out Manhattan and Brooklyn! Don't be afraid to explore! New Yorkers are very friendly and helpful!

My stay at this apartment was not the best experience, but if what you care about the most is a great location, then this is the place for you. The picture is a good reference of what to expect, although simply add an unpleasant layer of grime to everything and you have a more accurate idea. My main issue was that the room, while tidy, felt unclean and the bathroom was unpleasantly dirty, to say the least. The apartment looks really worn and it is right next to the trash room, so opening the door you smell the trash and it can be pretty disgusting. However, the inside of the apartment smelled fine. I appreciated that the room is independent of the owner's space, as a door separates the room and the bathroom from the living room and the owner's room. It was also very convenient that the room came with a fridge, microwave, toaster, and even plates and cutlery. It is pleasantly large and the bed was more of a full-sized futon. The a/c worked, but not very well, which is not an inconvenience unless one comes in the summertime like I did. Our host provided us with a room key, so it was nice to be able to lock the room and feel my stuff would not be disturbed. I didn't really see much of the owner, as a friend of his welcomed me when I arrived, and I believe that if I hadn't proceeded to ask him a few questions the one day I saw him at the apartment, we might never have talked, as he always left before I did and arrived apparently after. However, the main thing about this apartment is the location. Incredible location! It is walking distance from  Columbus Circle and all the theater area and Times Square, which made it very convenient when I got out of a play late at night. There are also a number of grocery stores nearby, including an organic whole foods style one. There are nearby subway stations and tons of restaurants, so it is easy to find anything one might need within a few blocks.

Looking for a good place to crash for a few days at Shunichi's place is a good idea. Though it was very hot and hard to sleep, Shunichi provided us with another air con and it worked well. The bathroom had some stains, grime and mold. There were old curtains but it got the job done. The bedroom was dusty and dark but the bed was a good size and the host/host's friend provided us more blankets and pillows if needed. Overall, for the price and location, it's definitely a steal. But the cleanliness can be worked on.

This is a perfect Airbnb. All that the previous reviewers say is true. This is a spacious, comfortable, well appointed and equipped apartment a block away from Central Park and close to the 1/2/3 line (CP North to Times Square in 3 stops) and the 4/5/6 line, as well as great bus routes. Per has anticipated your needs: Great kitchen equipment, convenient laundry and gym in the building, sharp knives, black out shade. The balcony is lovely and contributes to light filling the space. At the edge of East Harlem, this is a 20YO condo building of 11 units that feel like Amsterdam inside with the sounds and smells of East Harlem outside, iconic Central Park and Museum Mile behind you. Lots of NYC also in the framed prints of NYC scenes and art. Terrific stay!

Our stay with Waldemar was great.  We were in town looking for an apartment during a heat wave, it was a stressful time to say the least.  To be able to come back to a lovely brownstone with air conditioning AND a ceiling fan was indispensable!  Waldemar was very helpful with any information we needed about the city, especially regarding fixing our flat tire!  It is a great neighborhood with lots of cute restaurants and alot of soul and character.  I would recommend Waldemar's to any travelers looking for a genuine Brooklynite experience.

Our stay at Violetta's apartment was wonderful.  The apartment was spotless, light, and comfortable.  The location was absolutely perfect since we needed to be on the Upper West Side.  There were plenty of markets, coffee shops, drugs stores and restaurants nearby, and the subway stop is right out the door.   Violetta was easy to get a hold of, and very flexible.  We would certainly ask to rent Violetta's apartment for another stay.

Before I booked this room, I read the reviews. It's hard to believe they were so complimentary. I can not even give 1 star. We left before spending one night. Before checking out, we explored the area, but while we were out, I grew more and more uncomfortable with this B and B. I did not ask for a refund and I do not want one. I knew that the cancellation policy was 5 days prior to arrival.  I was not honest with the host and I should have been, but I did not want a confrontation and wanted to leave as soon as we got back to our room. There was little to no lighting to get into the home. Very poorly lit front door and it felt unsafe after dark. The door to get into the apartment was difficult to open and close. The living area extremely dusty and unkept. Master Bedroom also very dusty and unkept. The linens were very worn and not fresh. 2 flat pillows were on the bed. Bathroom was clean, but there were used soaps in a dish which I found to be unsanitary. We could lock our bedroom door from the inside, but we were not able to lock it when we left. This is NOT acceptable.  The host appeared nervous and uncomfortable.  This is a case of "you get what you pay for" However, I have stayed in many Bed and Breakfast at a similar rate and I have never stayed anywhere as dirty and unsafe feeling as this. I have rented a small apartment in Paris that was less than this per night and it was excellent!  I did not expect this to be the Ritz Carlton, but I did expect a clean environment and to feel safe.  It is doubtful that I will ever use AirBandB again.  Fortunately our weekend was not ruined by this experience, but it would have been we had stayed there. The hosts cat Kitty was the best part of the B ad B. A very lovely cat.

Me and my other half stayed at Cynthias from 28th Dec until 4th Jan 2011. The apartment is in a great location about a ten second walk from the subway, and then a quick route straight down to times square. The area is lovely with a great smoothie shop with cheap prices just round the corner which Cynthia kindly took us to. The apartment itself is AMAZING!! Me and my other half absolutely loved everything about her place it was very homely, clean and just stunning!! After a stressful 18 hour journey thanks to many delays, we arrived in the middle of the night and what a relief to arrive to such a nice welcoming apartment was fantastic. Cynthia is a lovely kind hearted, warm person and we are very grateful to have met her and stayed at her beautiful home. We look forward to visiting again hopefully in the summer :)    ps... We stayed in the Grand Room, the bed is extremely comfortable and you will get a great nights sleep!!

Having worked in customer service for many many years, I hate to give negative reviews because I understand people have off days. However, upon first walking in the door my friend and I should have turned away. We arrived at 5:15. The check in listed is at 3 so I comminuted to the host that my flight wouldn’t get in until a little later so I would arrive around 5. Their was some traffic so I. Was a couple minutes behind but nothing crazy. Upon entering, our host told us to sit on the couch and to have the WiFi keep us busy because the linens were not dry. Of course, that’s not a huge deal so we sat there. Time dragged on and it was 45 minutes of us just sitting there waiting. The linens were dry about 5 minutes after we walked in as he took them up to the room. The rest of the time we could hear him frantically cleaning the room. I understand running behind so i didn’t say anything although your check in was 2 hours before and he wasn’t prepared at all and did make a little comment about us being late. As we sat there, we did notice cat poop on the ground. I didn’t say anything about that either as I figured he would see it as he was tidying up in the sitting area. As soon as we went into the room we left set our things down and headed for the city. We noticed the door to our room didn’t lock from the outside. but figured everything would be okay. Nothing was ever stolen but we did enter our room multiple times after leaving the lights on (purposely as we knew we would be returning after dark) and we would come home to find them all turned off. That left and uneasy feeling knowing that someone was in our room. I don’t know if it was the host or another person staying there but their should be a way to lock the door from the outside. There was a point where my friend had ordered food in and I told her to make sure to lock the gate and not the front door. We didn’t realize it until later when another person staying couldn’t get in and I was woken up at midnight being told to call my host. I called him immediately and he began yelling at me about how it was ridiculous that I locked the door and their was no reason for it. I explained that it was a simple misunderstanding (language barrier with my friend)and apologized and he proceeded to yell over me. Not listening to what I had to say. He did not apologize for his behavior over any part of our stay and I don’t not take any sort of joy in writing a negative review but I honestly wish I would have just spent the extra money on a clean hotel. (...

The place was really quiet and looked just like the picture, which is great. However, when I first arrived it took me 10 minutes to get the door unlocked. The lock seemed jammed and then the key got stuck in the door. I tried calling and messaging the host. He returned my call about 30 minutes later once I had already figured it out. When I first walked up the stairs and opened the room door the cat jumped on the bed and dug its claws in when my cousin tried to remove it. Other than the key getting stuck and the cat being on the bed my stay was not bad. The place is fairly clean and really quiet. However, both mornings as I got up to leave the host was sleeping on the couch downstairs which I found a little weird and made me somewhat uncomfortable. I wouldn’t recommend booking this place alone, it just seemed somewhat creepy to me, but booking as a couple would not be bad for a quick stay in Brooklyn.

Very cool house. The stairs are a bit narrow and could be tricky for an older person. Home owner is super nice!! I had nice conversations with he, his Aunt and his sister. The tub/shower was the only downfall of the house. I would book my 70+ yr old parents here just because stepping in and out of tub could be dangerous for them. I on the hand would definitely book here again.

Silvia's apartment was exactly as described in the listing and is extremely well located close to the subway, near Lincoln Center, and lots of great restaurants. From my first contact to the last, Silvia responded very quickly to my questions and concerns. I was staying for over a month while my home was undergoing a renovation, so the kitchen was important. I was able to cook an entire Christmas dinner in the well appointed kitchen. Midway through my stay, I heard my renovation would be delayed, and Silvia allowed me to extend my stay. The whole experience was delightful and stress free!

Silvia’s place is a steal in NYC. The room was well layer out plus the location is great. However, in NYC it’s easy to have a bugs visit if you do not keep the area clean especially in the kitchen. Overall, I think her place will worth the money you spend for sure.

Cynthia’s endearing comments about Judy and I as her houseguests make my eyes misty.   Staying with Cynthia gave our fabulous trip an added dimension for enjoyment.  Cynthia’s persona is very spiritual to me.  She has a unique quality that captivates you….and she is also funny.  Cynthia’s home had never-ending artistic discovery on a daily basis for us, such as the totally unique water basin, the odd choice of a lamp shade in the kitchen, the mosaic mirrored kitchen back-splash as well as the shower surround, etc.  Cynthia’s highly acclaimed photographic artistry translates to her home décor.  Cynthia’s warmth and kindness were so appreciated as she escorted us around the neighborhood with dining recommendations, subway lessons—which we flunked on our first adventure differentiating UPTOWN vs. DOWNTOWN, but her subsequent tutorial straightened us out.  Cynthia and my traveling companion are twin “neat freaks” as far as cleanliness whereas I required forgiveness from time to time; to wit, the ultimate infraction of  wearing my boots in the house.  However, after Cynthia recovered from the shock to her cleanliness gene, she quickly forgave me with the admonition, “NO SHOES IN THE HOUSE.”  Cynthia’s blended energy drink in the morning enabled me as a 79-year-old broad to keep up with my young sidekick Judy.  Cynthia became our “House Mother,” waiting for our safe return at night with our daily report.  The most surprising revelation on this trip was how sweet and helpful the local New Yorkers  are to tourists.  There is a misconception that New Yorkers are rude, brusque and arrogant.  The opposite is true! In all my travels worldwide, I have never encountered nicer people who go out of their way to help you.  ·	Judy and Carol        ·	 ·	 ·	 ·	 ·	 By: Cynthia K This is one of the beauties about airbnb, you get to meet people that you would not normally get a chance to meet. Carol came with her friend Judy. The 2 took to NYC and rode the tour game in joy and laughter, making the home-towner me see the city again. Carol is also the hero, where love wins the day. She married her high school sweetheart, while now in her late 70's, she wears the smile of a happy ever ending story. I can only hope that more people will get the chance to meet this fabulous woman. Thank you Carol and Judy for staying here, I had fun.

Silvia's apartment was perfect for my extended stay. Her place is right around the corner from the 72nd subway station, which is extremely convenient because it has the express 2 and 3 train. I never felt unsafe walking from the train station to the apartment at night because it was so close. The apartment is surrounded by an abundance of great places to eat and is about a block and a half walk to central park. Her place is beautifully decorated and a wonderful space for 1 to 2 people. She made a difficult situation that I was in with my own apartment hunting so much easier with her flexible dates and perfectly located apartment. Silvia is a quick responder and very clear in all of her correspondents. I couldn't have asked for a better stay. Thank you :)

Rodents, hair, soiled linens. My check in was complicated by the host providing inaccurate check in instructions and not responding while airbnb agents and I tried to contact her repeatedly. She eventually responded and insisted that her instructions were correct, even though she had moved the lock box location and changed the code. After an hour of waiting on a hot sidewalk with lots of luggage, I entered the apartment. It is not well stocked, had to purchase my own paper goods (TP, etc) and cluttered with a lot of personal items. I counted 16 partially used and hair-covered bars of soap in the bathroom. There are large clumps of the host's hair all over. Sheets on the bed had clearly not been cleaned between guests, and a second mismatched sheet set stored in the closet was also dirty and stained with menstrual blood. I purchased a new pair of tennis shoes, which were ruined overnight because mice peed, pooped, and chewed the inside of my shoes, which I left by the front door. At night, you can hear the sound of creatures skittering across the floor. The air conditioning is not effective, even on the strongest setting, and it makes a loud unpleasant screeching sound that kept me awake at night even with earplugs. The location is ideal but because of the poorly maintained interior and extremely poor communication with the host, I would not recommend this place.

Sahr's place was really great and comfortable - it worked perfectly for our stay.  The location was really great - close to a lot of lovely restaurants and bars.  Sahr is attentive and professional.  We had a 3 month old baby, and she and her son were really sweet and patient about the unpredictability of a baby!  When we arrived, Sahr and her son even helped us carry our massive amounts of luggage. Their little dog, Chester, is adorable and SO SMART!   Because of the baby and flight times, we had a couple of additional requests to make of Sahr, and she went above and beyond to help us out and accommodate our needs.  It was incredibly appreciated, and really helped to make our stay much easier and way less stressful than it otherwise could have been - especially traveling with a baby.   Overall, we really enjoyed our stay - the space is clean, cool, and comfortable!

Ben, Sarina and the Cats were all gracious hosts and made my first AirBnB experience completely enjoyable!  The loft is truly gigantic and was a great place to stay for Thanksgiving weekend.  Ben and Sarina left information on anything that could possibly happen and info on every happening place in the neighborhood and made sure that their home was clean and comfortably.  Easy communication and coordination made it a stress free rental.  Thanks!

Could not have stayed in a better place.  The apartment is just as described and bigger than it looks in photos.  It was really clean and homely.  The cats are super-friendly.  Greenpoint is a great part of Brooklyn: lots going on without being as busy as Williamsburg, yet just a moment away from there.  Everything was totally organised by the hosts and there was absolutely no stress.

Thai was a great host, and her place in the Bronx was perfect for my needs. You’ll also be communicating pretty frequently with the building supervisor, William. William is who I actually met face-to-face and who let me in through the garage door when I arrived. This place is a STEAL! No place else in NYC will you find both PRIVATE PARKING and IN-UNIT WASHER & DRYER! I stayed here for 4 months during a residency at the VA. Within walking distance of VA, a coffee place, a sandwich place, and the 4 and 1 subway lines. Also very close to Target. Great location for my needs, 10/10 will keep this place in mind anytime I’m in the area. Neighbors did sometimes play music and rev engines later at night.

I have never written a negative review in my life, but I feel obligated to share this horrendous experience staying at Vanessa's.   I spent the entirety of my "stay" here crashing on other people's couches, as I was not able to live in the stuffy rabbit-shit-smelling sauna that is Vanessa's apartment. I luckily was able to sign an early lease on another apartment, and Vanessa kindly agreed to allow me to find someone to crash in my stead. I returned my keys to her and spent a full day cleaning the room - scrubbing surfaces, laundering the sheets, sweeping floors - in preparation for the guest's arrival. It was around this time where Vanessa became emotionally manipulative, causing me incredible anxiety and a general feeling of fear. She treated me like an infant, blaming me for not cleaning the room properly, though these arbitrary guidelines of hers were never vocalized to me (i.e. I should have washed the duvet cover, despite never having used the duvet). She totally lost it, accused me of causing her distress whilst canceling my replacement's reservation 20 minutes before he was supposed to arrive.  There is no AC available in the room, though it is listed as an amenity. Furthermore, the room has no windows to the outside, so it is incredibly stuffy and hot. It is uninhabitable during the summer. Vanessa is also extremely frugal with the tiny AC unit in the kitchen (often passive aggressively turning it off minutes after I turned it on), so whatever semblance of air exists in the apartment is inaccessible to guests.   She is not communicative and made me horribly uncomfortable during my stay. Even worse, there is no privacy, as all there is separating the room from the kitchen is a fully transparent curtain. The only good thing about this place is the location, though I wouldn't wish a stay analogous to mine upon even my worst enemy. Go enjoy New York and don't stay at this scam of an apartment.

Amir was a friendly and gracious host. When the wi-fi was unavailable a couple of times, he quickly resolved the issue within a few hours. This is a beautiful apartment with tall ceilings and lots of natural light. The bed and furnishings were very comfortable. There were some maintenance issues in the kitchen and bathroom (which I tackled) and those areas could still use some improvements. The television had spotty reception and a limited selection. A thorough deep cleaning of the whole apartment would help as well. The outdoor deck was torn up and not as pictured due to a roof leak that required the removal of the wood planking and retarring. The neighborhood is in transition. There are longtime residents mixed with newly-arrived yuppies mixed with homeless people. I thoroughly enjoyed the diversity, charm and friendliness of Harlem. I had a wonderful stay and would definitely stay here again.

Deck is unsafe to use, there’s a lack of bedding. Was given two towels to use for the month. Not allowed to use washer and dryer (though they were on premise). The water smelled, as did the kettle (scrubbing and cleaning it didn’t help). One of the beds is broke, tv damaged, and holes in walls. Closets had trash, or filthy foam bedding. Not very clean. Pictures don’t reflect reality. The nicest thing I can say is the host is nice, and the fireplace and mirror are pretty.

This's My first time to U.S. and travelled alone. I'm glad that I chose Cynthia's place which was definitely  elegance and museum atmosphere as many reviews, and it also made me feel relax and safety. I slept well from first night and went to toilet every morning on time and productive.Sometimes traveling can cause stressful,but Cynthia and her apt helped me end up with a wonderful trip and memories. Thank you,Cynthia! Every part of your amazing house art works, and the movement I spent there will be unforgettable for me.

This may be our favourite Airbnb stay yet! Everything about this place is perfect. The location is so close to such good restaurants, bars & cafes but remains such a peaceful retreat. It’s spotless with lots of natural light. The bed was so comfortable, we had the best nights sleep. The bathroom and kitchen were modern and immaculate. But the best part was the hospitality shown by our hosts! Ming and Matt were the greatest. They both went beyond, helping us settle in after a stressful flight. If you are reading these reviews wondering if you should book, you should stop looking and immediately reserve this apartment and you’ll have the best time in New York City

If your in a car especially a rental car it is very difficult to find parking near this place also there are stairs so if you have lots of luggage beware for a trek up several flights of stairs. Neighborhood seemed sketchy, we drove around looking for parking and seen two individuals looking into cars for valuables, didn’t take a chance on parking and got a hotel instead! Best decision for us since we had a rental car.

We have stayed here three  times, for a week each time. It is everything you could ask for in a getaway. It is homey, very spacious and beautifully decorated. The kitchen is on the opposite end of the space so you don't have to creep around in the morning if someone is sleeping. And you couldn't ask for a nicer host. The neighborhood is lovely, interesting and people are very friendly. You can easily walk to the Brooklyn Academy of Music in ten minutes, where we saw three first run movies. There are plenty of bars and restaurants and you are close to Fort Greene Park and public transport. You won't be disappointed!

We enjoyed the proximity to several subway stops.   We were within 30 minutes combined walking and riding time on the subway to anyplace in manhattan.  J's place is close to good stores, drug stores, a nice wine shop and good restaurants. The place is exactly as pictured.  We really liked the historical brownstone building.  We felt safe.  J was very responsive and helpful.

Thanks to Irene, my girlfriend and I had a great time at in New York CIty over New Years Eve!! We recommend this place to anyone. Irene helped us a lot to arrange our stay. Her apartment is very new and clean.  The neighborhood is supposed to be very safe. We saw some creepy people on the streets which made my girlfriend feel uncomfortable. Other than that the neighborhood is quite nice. Access to the subway is very close and convenient.

The appartment was exactly as in the pictures and very clean. Irene was not at home, so her husband showed me the place and gave the keys. He was very flexible with the arrival time.  However, the neighbourhood seemed a little creepy to me, especially if you are travelling along,

We recommend that you contact Keith without delay. We have just returned from a 9-day stay in NYC and in addition to the magic of the city, we enjoyed our stay largely also thanks to Keith's welcome and the functionality of his apartment. Keith was very available for our arrival, even though it was chaotic with a flight that was almost postponed until the next day. Her apartment is very well located, two blocks from the 2-3 line serving all the highlights of NYC, in a very nice neighborhood. The apartment was very clean, tastefully decorated and extremely well equipped. The little extra, Keith provides you with a manual full of good addresses in the neighborhood and in NYC. And he welcomed us with croissant, cookie and fruit juice for breakfast the next day. Thanks again to him for trusting us. We will not hesitate to contact him again for our next stay in NYC... because we will definitely return!

Irene and Silvan were so accommodating- we enjoyed their advice about navigating NYC. If you're looking for a cozy place to be this is definitely it. Be aware that this isn't a neighborhood like E Village or Soho though- nothing unsafe, just be aware of your surroundings.

Irene and her hudsband Silvan are really nice and helpful.  There was a snow storm attacked NYC the second day I came and my car were buried on the street parking spot. Silvan helped me to dig the car out!  So if you want a warm place to stay, you should definitly stay here in Irene's.

Irene’s place is one of the best property you would find in and around New York City.  Irene was available to welcome in when I checked in. Gave all the instructions needed to settle down well. She is friendly!   Subway is 6 min walk from the property. The area is pretty much crowded so you won’t feel unsafe walking around alone! Has good restaurants around too!   Irene is helpful and also suggested me some good shops around for shopping! Room was clean and nice!   I will definitely come back to stay here!

Terrific location on a quiet shady street in Ft Greene.  Just a block from the park and very convenient to nearby restaurants and shops.  Jane is an excellent welcoming host, and the space is very roomy, welcoming, well appointed and spotless.  We had a great visit with our daughter.  “Perfect for parents” indeed!

First off, this was my first ever AirBNB experience, and it was great.  Patty was a great host, very easy to get ahold of, and responded quickly.  She was very friendly, and left a great list of suggestions in the area.  I would give Patty 5 stars as a host for sure.  The apartment is very cute and comfortable, I shared the room with my best friend, she slept in the loft and I slept on the daybed.  We never once felt cramped or crowded or in each others way.  The pictures are an accurate representation of the unit.  The location is great, close to the Grand/Chrystie subway station.  It gives you a great authentic NYC experience. The 24 hour deli/market under the building was very useful.  We stayed out until 5 am most nights and never felt unsafe in the area or walking back from the subway station.  The only Con I can say about the place was the heat.  That is beyond Patty's control and she checked multiple times to make sure we were comfortable.  The AC unit works, but it does not cool the whole unit.  Being from the South we cling to our AC, so after walking all day in the NYC heat we would come back to a hot apartment.  We kept the blinds closed to not let in any extra heat and it was still hard to handle. The bathroom is also very spacious by NYC standards but it has very little ventilation, so since two of us were trying to get ready it often felt like 1000 degrees in there, so we would shower with the lights off, to not add any extra heat. This is a personal preference as far as temperature is concerned and may not be an issue for everyone.   Overall, I would 100 percent recommend this apartment, just know that it may be hot in the dead heat of summer.

Patricia made us feel welcome despite us running an hour late due to transportation issue from New Jersey.  We really enjoyed staying in the apartment and it was very convenient, and well stocked.  Noise was an issue but I suspect this was common in New York and you'll need to bring ear plugs.  Brooklyn is very easy to get to from Patricia's apartment, but travel to upper Manhattan does take 20 - 30 minutes on the subway. Chinatown is very cheap to stay in compared with the rest of Manhattan, and there are extremely cheap take away eateries nearby ($4 - 5 for a box of rice with meat, $1 buns).  We did leave the apartment without successfully contacting Patricia, so we hope she got the keys, and the cleaner can access the apartment in time for the next guests!

I have had 3 boats and an apartment up on airbnb.  I try to do exactly what Nathalie does.  Open up a warm, cozy, personable and charming place to stay.   Nathalie's apartment is 5 star!  I loved the beds, the decor, the east  coast woodwork.  The cool patio in back.  Tub and shower were great.  I met Nathalie, and she was superb. Look no further this is the spot.   Its close to the train.  Never felt unsafe.  And of course, its NY, so you can find some really good food in walking distance.
Patty's place was exactly as described. She was very accommodating and flexible with check in and out times. Location was good and never felt unsafe. Close to subway stations, easy to get around.

A very nice and spacious apartment in which four people won't step on each other's toes. The subway takes you to Manhattan in 15 minutes. The neighborhood is very okay and not really gentrified yet but not dangerous in any way. You get a good impression of the original Brooklyn. We were there with two children (11 and 13) and had great fun in this exciting city. Communication with Nathalie worked wonderfully from the start. 100% recommendation.

Nathalie’s home is an absolute dream in the heart of Bed- Stuy. Booking couldn’t have been a simpler process as Nathalie is extremely communicative and responded nearly immediately. Read the rules! Everything is very clear! No stress check in, arrive and use the lockbox whenever you’re ready. Once you open the door you’re going to fall in love and want to cancel any and all plans to go out (you’re also going to wake up on Sunday and immediately extend your reservation.. just trust me and book Sunday night as well.) The backyard space paired with a glass of wine and the essence of whatever vibe is happening on the block is prime entertainment in and of itself. You’re in the heart of Bed- Stuy with access to the train only a few blocks down giving you the accessibility to explore whatever part of town you’re in the mood for although you can find almost any vibe you’re looking for within a few blocks. Early mornings in Nathalie’s space was really prime time though, the natural light that streams through all the windows in the apartment was so beautiful to wake up to. As someone who’s been traveling to New York over the past few years, Nathalie’s home was genuinely everything I could’ve asked for. Do yourself a favour and experience it for yourself!!

We had a great stay in New York. Patty was super helpful. Location of the apartment was great and we loved the area. China town and little Italy right on the door step. Good food and bars, don’t be afraid to wander around you will find some right gems. Grand street metro only a short walk away and also metro station on Canal Street itself. Great food in little Italy and also found a great place called The Antique Garage up in Soho area. The High Line is a great place to visit as if the Chelsea market. Patty was a great host and even arranged a local taxi service for our return trip to JFK airport at half the price of the yellow cabs. Felt completely safe in the area. Thanks Patty

This apt. has a really groovy, funky decor and vibe - tons of character - I loved it!  I felt very comfortable there. It's small but not at all cramped. Laurelle (Tommi) was super responsive and a good communicator, and very friendly and welcoming. All the info was clear and there were no surprises with her place. The building is safe and I felt very comfortable staying there as a single female. The building itself is on a quiet residential block, but the street one block away is chock full of restaurants, bars, cafes, diners, grocery stores, drug stores, etc. A great location convenient to all that Midtown has to offer. Enjoyed my stay very much!

Staying at Matthew's place in Harlem was a relaxing, cozy experience. The apartment was very clean with great extras like the snacks in the kitchen as well as the bath products. Although we didn't speak very much during the trip, he was always checking up on us to see if we needed anything. The location right next to the subway worked well since we like being in more than just midtown during our visit. The price was fair and I thought it was a plus not to have to pay a security deposit. Matthew was also flexible during our departure which helped make airport day less stressful and that was appreciated. I would definitely recommend Matthew as an excellent host. Thank you!

Teri was lovely, relaxed and great to chat too. The apartment is a 5 minute walk from the subway A train downtown to Times Square, Empire State etc, and local to shops. The apartment is close to the hop on, hop off tour bus near Apollo theatre. There is a supermarket 2 blocks away. The room was decent sized and had good storage. We were very pleased we could use the kitchen and store food in the fridge. Apartment was tidy and we were given everything we needed. The only downside is the neighbourhood is extremely noisy with locals, traffic and sirens. The local shop assistants later told us the neighbourhood is dangerous and not to go out night.

Matthew has been very very nice with us, we found fresh flowers and cold drink at our arrival! He helped us several times, suggesting places to visit, or for shopping, or anything else. The apartment was exactly as shown in  photos, nice and comfortable. The subway was SO CLOSE, that we could'n believe it! We had just to cross the street and that's it, we were in subway! The street was very very quiet, day or night, but if Harlem scares you remember that subway is 20 meters from your house door. Absloutely no long walking to reach it! All furnitures working good, we use washer, refrigerator, microwave, tv, stereo (or, to be precise, iPod docking station)...anything. So, what else? It has been such a wonderful time, thanks to NYC and thanks to Matthew!

Matthew's place was like we expected, even better!  We had no problem with Matthew,  he's a perfect host. The apartment was clean when we arrived, the location is PERFECT, the mattress was comfortable, fully equipped kitchen, nice shower, you will not be disappointed!! This was our first experience with airbnb and it was so great we are scared to be disappointed the next time! FULLY RECOMMEND this place!!!!!!!!

Where we stayed was not the place shown in the pictures. I was very disappointed in the state of the place - it was quite dirty. The doors were all sticky with dirt, the carpets were trashed, and the bathroom smelled like a college dorm bathroom.  That said, for $50/night, it's not a terrible value. The A/C worked great, which is important for NYC in the summer, and our sheets and towels were fresh and clean. The person who greeted us was very nice and made sure we had enough clean towels, two sets of keys, etc.  Although in a relatively sketchy neighborhood, the place felt very secure. If you decide to stay here, make sure you don't get lost - we almost got robbed after we took a wrong turn from the Subway station a few blocks from the place.  If you're doing NYC on a budget, this is a suitable option.

Accurate pictures except TV much bigger! Clean bathroom but appliances dirty. Jen was out of town and David just moved out, so we had place to ourselves - total bonus. A 'concierge' checked us in which was unexpected. She was great, willing to meet us early and super nice even tho we were late. Just took us by surprise that altho communication seemed to be with Jen, a totally dif person met us. The place is decorated a bit... creepy... but if you're into that, this place is great.

We stayed at Mathew’s fantastic apartment in West Harlem for 7 nights. Mathew is a great host and a very nice guy. He lives upstairs and was on hand anytime we needed him. He gave us a very warm welcome and some great advice on the subway, local area and things to do when we arrived.   The area felt very very safe, even coming back late at night.  The apartment is very close to two subway stations (three if you include the short walk to 125 st which the express stops at) that get you down town and back extremely quickly. There are grocery shops local should you want to eat in.  We can’t stress enough how safe the area felt.     From the minute we arrived we felt very at home. The apartment is very quiet, much bigger than it looks in the photos and very well equipped. There is plenty of hanging space for clothes in the wardrobes and we found the bed to be very comfy. We both slept better than we do at home!   The kitchen is well equipped with cooker, large fridge, washing machine/dryer and pretty much everything you need to cook for yourself. We absolutely loved the double toaster!   The living room is comfortable and has a large TV, sofas and dining table.  The bathroom is nice and clean and the shower is brilliant with lots of hot water.  There is a lovely sunny back garden which was great to have breakfast in and plan our day. We were even visited by a Blue Jay while we had breakfast.  We had an absolutely lovely time in Mathew’s apartment and a fantastic time in New York. We are already planning a trip back there next year and would love to stay in Mathew’s apartment again.

We very much enjoyed our 1 week stay in Brooklyn. The place was perfect for day trips around Brooklyn or to Manhattan. Subway station is very close. There are two Delis across the stress and numerous cafes, bars and stores only a stroll away. We did not get to meet Angela but check-in and out worked fine and she was very quick in answering any questions.  The apartment is rented out to several people so you share kitchen and bathroom with strangers, but being out the whole day, we didn't really run into each other much. Make sure to bring earplugs, there is a trafficlight right infront of the house which makes traffic noisy.

All in all a fantastic value and perfect spot - not remote at all, but feels like an oasis. Matthew's place is a lovely, restful spot just a hop away from the bustling pace of the rest of Manhattan. My husband and I had intense and stressful work to do downtown and in White Plains, and Matthew's place was so convenient to both areas. It's just steps away from the subway, but a world apart in its peace and quiet. Matthew is generous and responsive. We took advantage of the sweet backyard space. The whole apartment is so spacious and comfy, and there's a washer and dryer to boot. Didn't have time to use the kitchen but it has all the fixings for guests who want to cook. The Harlem neighborhood is full of history, liveliness and good eats. It's a joy to stay there.

The location is great: you can access 3 different subway lines from here. Although I used the L/G train the most. The room is very clean: no need to be afraid of bed bugs here The room has A/C which is crucial in the nyc summer. The hosts are very friendly and are familiar with travellers and their needs. I would definitely come back. Its walking distance from some great restaurants and the main street in Williamsburg. Staying here equals winning.

Gus and Holly have the whole airbnb thing sorted. They're happy to give you the run of their place, answer your questions and yet also give you a lot of privacy. Every amenity you could need is within walking distance (laundromat, car service to airport, M and L train). It's an easy walk to Bedford Ave or the river. The air conditioner was a blessing in summer which Gus installed the day we arrived. Their apt is not super clean, it is their home, and they treat it as such - so don't expect it to be like a hotel. The cats were a strange mix of timid and curious - they are in a constant state of confusion over who you are, but harmless. I'm actually allergic but had no problems with them. I never felt uncomfortable or unsafe staying here, and once my partner left, I stayed 5 nights by myself here. I recommend breakfast at second stop on lorimer - great coffee, cheap bagels.

Jennifer’s place was great! The room is bright and comfy. The neighborhood is great. I have a very light sleep so I was scared of non being able to sleep but with ear plugs no problem. Very happy there was AC in the room! I met Jennifer quickly when arriving and she was super nice. Great value for Manhattan.
Good place with a nice fire escape you can chill on. I couldn’t lock my bedroom, but I was traveling with a lot of camera gear and nothing got stolen!

Staying in this room at Holly and Gus's apartment is easy!  I really enjoyed my stay. Their home is quirky, stylish, bright, and really comfortable. Not to mention a wonderful spot in Brooklyn. What a great place to live!  The kitchen is well-equipped for the cooks and long-term stays, and I felt comfortable going in and using it if I wanted to.   Coming and going was easy. Being able to moderate my own check-in and check-out reduced the stress of that process by a lot.   Even though this is a shared space, it feels welcoming, and it never felt strange when multiple people were here. The space is large enough for personal space and quiet time, even if someone else is home too.   Thank you for creating a space like this for us to stay!

Great apartment... quite, private, a nice space, very clean.  Not the greatest neighborhood, but for the price this place is a steal!  On street parking was easy to find closeby unless you were coming in late (after 11pm) and wanted to have the luxury of being within a block of the apartment.    About a mile away was a really good coffee shop called Outpost, I would recommend to hit it up for coffee, a snack, free internet, good atmosphere.  Renee was very accomodating and had great communication.

Laurie is a great host. Even tough theres a lot of stress just before christmas she found time for me to give me really good recommendations  every day. She knows where to eat, where the best christmas windows is located and when the museums have special offers. If you want to try being a Brooklyner for a short time, this is where you should stay.

We had seven wonderful days in NYC and this apt in Brooklyn. It has been an ideal home. It was clean, it was big, like on the photos. If you want to go to Manhattan it takes 20 min by metro and you can sleep at night cause it's not so noisy and stressful there. Bedford-Stuyvesant is a nice brownstone-place to be for a stay in this town and the given hints from Renee & Sergei (Cafe, Bar, Restaurant) have been very useful for us, beeing new in the hood. If we come back to the new world, we will come back to Renee & Sergei again.

Our stay at the 1 Bedroom apartment of Renee and Sergei was wonderful.  The apartment is fully consistent with the description and photos. Very bright, clean and comfortable.In the apartment is everything you need.  Wi-Fi, all the necessary equipment in the kitchen. Very convenient was to have a washer and dryer - you can take a minimum of clothes and save space in your luggage for shopping in New York. In the bedroom was very nice linens and lots of towels. Sergei has given us a lot of useful tips about New York. Four days before our arrival to Renee we were leaving for Washington and it was very nice, that our hosts allowed us to leave our suitcase in their house before arriving. The first day we were a little scared of the area where the house, but later we saw that there's not dangerous, and returned after walking in Manhattan at 10-11 pm.  On the way from the subway there are lots of  places where you can eat - cafes, delis, fast food, shops and a supermarket. Deli are open 24 ours.  Excellent apartment for the money ! We recommend  this accommodation!

Laurie’s place is a gem, perfectly located in prime Park Slope, which is basically New York’s version of Islington. The house is a quirky, older home, warm and welcoming. Laurie is an extremely interesting person, friendly, knowledgeable and delighted to chat about everything from the locality to the state of the world. The upstairs rear bedroom I had was quiet and comfortable - I slept particularly well. It’s probably worth noting that the house could be tricky for anyone not steady on their feet as the stairs are narrow and steep. But don’t worry about taking bags up there - Laurie is more than happy to let guests keep heavy bags downstairs. The bathroom is shared if there’s another guest in residence, but the arrangement wasn’t at all stressful - and even though the plumbing isn’t in it’s salad days, the shower is super powerful in the best American tradition - which was a pleasure each morning. Highly recommended, an easy subway trip to the varied neighbourhoods of Brooklyn and to Manhattan beyond.
Clean room, messy kitchen and living spaces. Dangerous stairs!

Thank you Corey  ~ We had a spectacular stay.   Your apartment really felt like a home and it was great to come back every day from exploring the city.  We felt very comfortable and the bed is dangerous .... so comfy we slept in every day.    Thank you for the great directions, the recommendations.   You truly have the best restaurants within a leisurely stroll.  I had a lot of "best of ... " experiences!!!!  We had such a wonderful time and we want to thank you for hosting us during our trip!  All the best!  Hannah & Jason

Staying at Corey's place was an absolute pleasure! The apartment was fantastic and in a great location!  Everything was simple and easy and Corey is a great host.  I am definitely coming back and when I do Ill definitely be looking to stay at Corey's again!  Ps Im stealing some of your decorating ideas, great taste!!

Pros:  1. The apartment itself is very comfortable and includes all the required facilities for a pleasant stay. Also, the kitchen is equipped with everything you need. 2. Renee was very polite, considerate and helpful.  3. The apartment is very secure (Locked entrance gate + locked door).  4. If you are a TV addict, the apartment has got tons of channels in the cable TV in the living room (note: No TV in the bedroom).  Cons:  1. The place is a 10 minute walk from the nearest subway station and 30 minutes from the city (Up to 60 minutes at night).  It is a quiet residential area, that's a bit creepy at night. If you wish to experience the hustle and bustle of the city, you may wish to consider another location. 2. a 125$ cleaning charge in advance is a bit harsh and makes the price go up significantly from the original offer (For a short stay).  3. We could not fill the hot tub (The drain's closing mechanism is not working).

Good things: Lovely apartment, lots of space, lots of light, great kitchen, original 1920's floors and doors- very nice preservation. Very clean!!  Renee was very nice!  Not as good: The bathroom door doesn't completly close. Not a big issue, theres a loundry basket we used to keep it closed. The neighborhood seems unpleasant at first but it was not a probleme, no one bothered us.  Thank you Renee :)

We have been ten days in this apartment and we can to say that it's very comfortable. It's got good calefaction, the kitchen has all the neccesary for cooking and It has washer and dryer. Renée is very friendly, she always helped in everything and plus the last day she called us a taxi for to go to the airport. About the transport, you have a subway around 5 minutes walking, the line A goes directly to Manhattan, you only must to know that it's not recommendable to come back very late home because the subway can to be dangerous. we were good in the neighborhood but the people says that it's better not walking for the street in the night because Brooklyn can to have not good areas. thank you so much.

I had a very nice stay at Renée place's.  It is my second time with her and not my Last for sure. The appartment was clean as usual.  Very nice to stay and very safe. Renee is such a Lovely person and she does her best to make sure her guests stay in very good condition.  The appartment has everything we need and it is about 15 minutes to get Manahattan.  I 100% recommend this appartment .    J'ai passé un très bon séjour chez Renée.  Ce fut ma deuxième fois chez elle et pas la dernière c est sur. L'appartement était propre comme d'habitude. Endroit idéal et sans danger.  Renée est une personne très charmante qui fait son maximum pour que ses clients soient satisfaits.  L'appartement à tout ce qu'il faut et est à seulement 15 minutes de manahattan.  Je recommande à 100% cet appartement.

Overall an alright place. This was very last minute for me, as it made due.   Maciek is very kind. Met me and showed me around the place.  My issue is the location. It is located in a rather sketchy area. Directly by a bus stop. The neighbors on the floor are strange and I overall didn’t feel comfortable going in and leaving.  Also there is a lot of noise and it was difficult to sleep. Due to the city noise, as  well as the uncomfortable pull out couch.

To tell the truth - it was  our worst stay ever!  The room's locate in the basement (that was not explained in Edward's descriprion and we were struck on coming there after arriving in NY). A dusty room of a closet size with a tiny window, through wich one can enjoy an unforgettable landscape of stinky trash cans. Don't believe the view of  Manhattan in one of the pics in the room's description. It's fake.  We made a grave mistake when having booked the room for our entire NY vacation (2 weeks). We could hardly spend there a couple of days - in that stuffy room with bed sheets that seemed not to have been cleaned ever. The last drop was when Masha got an allergy attack and became covered with rash (though no cases of such strengh had take place earlier).  Se, we were forced to move ASAP.  BUT!! Attention - we lost approximately 300$ on it. The AIRBNB compensated only 50 % of the total sum for the rest days with Edward's(yeah, you won't believe!) and detained their fees. We had to urgently find another place through BNB and pay their fee again (is that fair?).  So, please, be careful with this choice!  P.S.On leaving Edward, we stayed at another place - for the same price - it was excellent!

Cute EV place-- definitely stay to live like a local... But the stairs were absolutely awful (mainly because I came/went a lot and had several large bags)... so be prepared for that. Bathroom is a really awkward size/layout with the shower basically pouring into the incredibly tiny sink/mirror area. While it clearly says no TV, I was a bit disappointed there was no netflix/hbo/dvd player in the house. With everything said, Xiren was very responsive to everything and welcoming with lots of suggestions for the area. When I ran into a lost keys mishap, Xiren and her bf worked out a low-stress back up plan with me the next day-- even though they were eventually found.

The apartment is located in a very nice neighborhood with lots of restaurants, bars and several of the subway lines nearby. I never felt unsafe in the neighborhood during my stay. The text and pictures in the ad correctly describes the apartment, there were no unpleasant surprises.  Xiren is a wonderful host, very responsive and easy to get hold of. She also gave good recommendations of places to visit in the neighborhood which was greatly appreciated.  I had a very nice stay and would gladly recommend Xirens place!

We spent 6 days at Xiren's cosy apartment as a base for an exploration of New York. It was exactly what we needed! The apartment is located in a great neighbourhood, we felt that we could have easily spent the 6 days just exploring the diversity of restaurants, bars and shops around us. Also, we never felt unsafe walking home. It's a little walk (some 10 mins) to the nearest subway station (F line) and from there we had easy access to all of Manhattan. Whereas the neighbourhood is rather busy (particularly on a Friday night), the apartment is surprisingly quiet, as it's on the 5th floor and the windows face the back of the building. We could hear steps from the neighbour sometimes and the radiators made a few noises at some point - but nothing to bothersome and otherwise the building was really calm.  The apartment was lovely, exactly as charming as represented in the photos. The bed was comfortable, the pillows too. The kitchen is a bit basic but it had all we needed to prepare light meals at home.  Xiren was an excellent host, responding promptly to any communication and giving us flexibility with the check-in hours. She also provided precious advice of good restaurants and other places in the neighbourhood.  In summary then, I strongly recommend this apartment, and would not hesitate to contact Xiren if I ever find myself in New York again.

Edward is a very good host. He allowed us to check out late and helped us a lot during our stay there. His place is cool, everything is there. Even though it's quite hot down there you can always steal his portable fan ! :)

Edward's place is in a fabulous part of the city!  The price was a steal for a place in Manhattan.  The sheets were clean and the atmosphere quiet and chill.  Edward is very easy to get in contact with, super friendly and a great host.  He offers up everything - towels, NYC books, kitchen, fridge, tea, house keys - that you need to make your trip comfortable. Although the room is clean, the guest bedroom's window is ground-level on a garbage-filled alley, so if the window/fan is left open, the smell in the room will reflect what is going on outside - one evening we could smell vomit (however, the next day no problems). To avoid this, keep the window closed if it's not hot.

We were met by a friend of Edward's as he had gone camping. There, an unpleasant surprise: the accommodation, which we understood to be on the ground floor, was in fact a cellar in a courtyard full of garbage, trash cans, and used furniture. "The apartment" had no windows, no ventilation, was really questionably clean, the fridge didn't work...The first evening while cooking, we had the unpleasant surprise of encountering a cockroach, then two, then three...Same in the courtyard where they were swarming. The second evening we noticed that there were fleas in the bedding, so we left. Even though we had paid for five nights. We never met Edward, who still sent us an email to find out if there was a problem... I forget: the encounters with the local tramps who hose themselves off in the yard or rummage through the trash when you go out in the morning.   Even if it is eminently well placed in NY (although the East Village takes on the appearance of a court of miracles during the day, with gatherings of marginalized people), inexpensive, and not far from transport and a supermarket, an address to absolutely avoid, therefore, unless you are a very very very hardened backpacker.

FANTASTIC!! Really enjoyed having this place as a base in New York - the location could not have been better, endless bars and restaurants.  And we were lucky enough to have a week long Italian street fayre taking place a couple blocks away. We used the Spring Street subway to get everywhere although there was a subway station just around the corner... just enjoyed the stroll in the sunshine to the 6 line. I'd forgotten to bring a British to US plug adaptor but an electrical shop in China Town like a block away had them in stock for $3. It felt like anything and everything I wanted was on tap. Lots of interesting shops selling weird and wonderful interior fittings - yummy stuff for a property investor. The apartment looks exactly like the photos, and there's a full length mirror on the inside of the wardrobe door... didn't find that until about day 3 haha!  Koray was super helpful with recommendations and instructions on how to use his amazing audio visual system, and very flexible re allowing us to leave our bags in the apartment on the last day as our flight was pretty late. Everything about this space was perfect.  I even enjoyed the walk up to the top floor - healthy stuff!  the bed was super comfy and sitting out in the sun on the fire escape taking in the view was magic (and an adrenalin rush if you're scared of heights). I can't find any fault with this place at all...   The glass wet room within the bedroom is a genius use of space.  Thank you so much Koray for sharing this space with the world.  I feel really privileged to have experienced it.  Like something out of a movie.  You clever chap!

We can recommend Koray's apartment on the Lower East side. It is really beautiful, spacious, modern and fully equipped. Koray lives with his family in the apartment himself, so that you can enjoy the advantages of a fully equipped apartment in addition to the comfort. The apartment is designed according to a modern industrial style and the kitchen is simply stunning and contains everything you need; Olive oil, good pepper, tea...etc. The apartment also has exceptionally comfortable beds, which is great for rest. It is also centrally located in Manhattan. At least two subway stations are very close to the apartment, so you can get anywhere quickly (15 minutes Central Park, 10 minutes 9/11, etc.). You can walk to Little Italy in 5 minutes or in chic Soho or in Broadway shopping street in 10 minutes, where you have endless possibilities for dining or shopping. Koray is above average attentive. Having spent two weeks in NYC, we had many questions for him. He is always very polite, quick and precise in the answers. We see this as an exceptionally valuable service. The only special thing is the Lower Eastside area. You can feel that there is a lot of up-and-coming potential and that the area is developing; but the area is rough. You see many homeless and begging people and the cleanliness of the streets is not yet of the highest standard everywhere. On the other hand, this also gives room for many original small coffee shops, artistic shops and wonderful culinary shops where you can eat fantastically and internationally. ... We were able to spend two wonderful weeks in NYC and were very happy for Koray's apartment so that we could retreat to a nice place in the evening after exciting days.

I wanted a place for my parents to stay during their 4 day long visit to NYC. I had never tried airbnb before and I was a little skeptical. But the place was great. It was clean and Karen and Julian had even kept a box of cereal and cookies for us. The subway station (J) is literally 5minutes walking distance from the place. I think it took like 15-20 minutes to get to canal street in Manhattan.  What made the experience even better was that Julian and Karen are great hosts. We probably called Karen a million times and she was really very patient and helpful with all our questions. My parents had a great time, and overall it was great value for money. If there is anything at all that I saw negatively, it was that the place was in Brooklyn, and it seemed a little creepy to walk around at night.

Stayed here in late Oct. 2011 for 4 days. It's really close to the subway station, about 2 blocks away.   The location doesn't have any interesting eateries to walk to so it's best to catch a cab somewhere or the subway.  The location might seem scary to some, but was pretty safe.  We would get back almost every night passed midnight and would walk back from the subway to the apartment and it was always safe.  It's really loud upstairs and if you're a light sleeper, it can be quite annoying so you might want to take some earplugs. The room itself is small, but perfect for 2 and if you're not planning on staying indoors then it's not even an issue. Julian was kind and friendly and the room was clean.  Everything that you might need is there, except for TV so take a laptop if you need it. The free wi-fi was a PLUS for netflix movies at 3am when I couldn't sleep from the noise upstairs.

I was very happy to Stay at the House on Henry - it was clean, warm and cozy. I don't have any negatives for Annette. I considered my stay a relaxing jaunt with no stress. The area is very lovely and a pleasure to walk to cafes or restaurants with reachable distance.  Norma

This large F2 is as shown in the photos. Very clean, large bathroom. Karen & Julian are very friendly. Every time I had a question they answered it straight away. The neighborhood is typical, and no problem of insecurity. Very positive.

Very positive experience. Julian is a welcoming host, very friendly and accommodating (we were able to leave our luggage on the last day, to enjoy our day while waiting for our evening flight). The apartment is well located, close to the metro, clean and in all respects conforms to the description given. A good address in New York, then!

Julian, our host, was extremely welcoming and accomodating during our stay.  Overall, the apartment was clean and comfortable.  My only complaints would be that the surrounding neighborhood was sketchy and felt unsafe at times, especially during late night walks back from the Halsey J Train subway stop.  In addition, the apartment was very hot and humid with no air conditioning, although leaving the fans running for 24/7 made the situation bearable. Overall, decent stay for the price and gracious hosts.

Our hosts Julian and Karen were very nice and welcoming even with us arriving late past our check in time. The surrounding neighborhood isn't the best, and can be a little scary at night walking back from the subway. But everything you need is within walking distance; a laundromat around the corner and a supermarket and the J train just down the block. They have private parking in the front which made it VERY convenient. The apartment was well stocked with everything that we might need, but the floors seemed a little dirty and it looked like the place hasn't been dusted in a while. There was no AC, but there were 4 fans going constantly at all times which made it a little bearable but still pretty hot. And the wifi connection was horrible, which made it a little inconvenient. Overall, it was a good place to stay for the price and pretty close by to most of the boroughs.

We appreciated the discount for our long stay (43 days, visiting family nearby). However, as our 8th Airbnb stay (plus 4 from other sites) the contrast with the others could not have been more pronounced, and for the first time we’d hesitate to make a positive recommendation. Had it not been for the ‘Strong’ cancellation policy we would have moved out. The three main reasons (which you couldn’t know from the listing) are: 1. Dirty. Cracked walls around bath/shower with accumulated grime and mould; mould-encrusted shower curtain. Dirty windows with unremoved anti-hurricane tape. Apartment lacing what’s needed to keep it clean – dustpan but no broom, mop but no bucket, no vacuum cleaner. 2. Unpleasant atmosphere. It was fine to be asked in advance to agree explicitly to Annette’s rules about no shoes, quiet hours etc, but another thing to be greeted with imperative instructions about these rules attached to the outside of the apartment door (plus another on the exit door from the building), as though we were children and would not have understood or remembered what we’d already signed up to. We had two adult friends to stay and even though we’d spent little time in the apartment and crept around quietly, we were again given instructions in writing about how they should behave, and again (with elaboration) when our two grandchildren came twice for sleepovers.  3. The least usable kitchen by far of any apartment we’ve stayed in – almost no bench space, no light over the work space, lacking basics (not even a chopping board). But given the house rules, you could hardly have had people to eat, which rather spoilt our whole purpose of having an apartment rather than a hotel.

The apartment is functional with its equipped kitchen which allowed us to come home to eat every evening, its separate bedroom and its pleasant bathroom. We didn't feel unsafe in this area of ​​Brooklyn even when we returned at night. There is everything you need nearby (supermarkets, restaurants, stores, etc.) and above all the metro (line J) which passes very close to the apartment, which makes access to Manhattan quite quick.  Julian is a welcoming host. We immediately felt at ease.

I am very happy with our choice. The apartment was clean and the beds were still comfortable. After a long day of walking, even the sofa bed was comfortable. The apartment is very well equipped. We were a little scared when we arrived in the evening because the key wasn't there but fortunately Julian arrived very quickly. We could hear water in the pipes and people walking upstairs but it wasn't really disturbing.   The metro is a 4-5 minute walk away. The neighborhood is very safe and there are several small businesses and restaurants. Very practical!!! Julian was very available as a host. It is always very appreciated. He was also very kind during the reservation. I would return without any hesitation. Thank you Julian and Karen.

PROS: - Apt is 3 blocks away from the J train to Manhattan, and halfway between JFK and the city (it takes about 30 mins to each end) - It is a quiet neighborhood - There's free WiFi. Although, bandwidth is not mindblowing, it's ok to check on emails and stuff - Although being in the basement, the apt gets good sunshine through the garden's door. Oh, and the garden is a nice add on  CONS: - NEIGHBORS!! Apparently other Airbnb guests were staying in the apt above us. They'd start walking around the house with high heels and boots and non-stop flushing the toilet at 1 AM and would not stop until 6. The walls seemed paper thin because we could hear everything. The last day, the couple seem to had been gone and we could finally get some sleep. Julian & Karen tried contacting the guests upon our complaint - The place would be small for 4 adults. I would recommend it for 3 people or 2 adults + 2 kids - The neighborhood seemed unsafe. Nothing happened to us, so this could be just a misperception  Overall, I recommend this place to travellers staying in NYC for up to a couple of weeks. It's good value for the money taking into account NYC prices.  Thank you guys for receiving us!

Annette's place has everything I needed for a great weekend in Brooklyn. She was quick to communicate and answer questions I had. The check-in process was seamless. The apartment is close to a highway, as one can see on a map, so I had trouble sleeping the first night. However, the host (or another traveler) had left a jar of foam ear plugs for others to use, so I was able to sleep after finding those. The apartment itself is very comfortable and convenient to transportation. The neighborhood is beautiful, with lots of places to eat and walk around. I never felt unsafe (as one can in a city) walking around at night. I would definitely stay here again!

The location is great; close to many restaurants, pubs, entertainment venues,etc... in east village.  The host is very communicative; I haven't met Edward but he was always helpful in his replies to my messages. I was delayed to arrive to New York and check-in was flexible. I've also had a last minute visit from a friend and Edward agreed to let my friend stay with me for one night.  One negative aspect. The flat is in the basement as mentioned in the ad so it is not very pleasant having to walk next to the building waste disposal containers to go in the flat. But the main unpleasant aspect were the cockroaches in the room, kitchen and bathroom. I suggest for the sake of future visitors to make an extra effort to apply additional spray treatment in the flat for pest control.

The apartment was clean and it worked good with getting the keys in the lockbox. We met with Julian and he made us feel welcome. The J train is very close by and it will take you to downtown Manhattan, and other exchange hubs for other trains. It did take a while some days due to many trains in queue, so for us getting to Uptown Manhattan it took more than 1 hour. It was, as mentioned earlier, a bit noisy from upstairs, but it was acceptable. The neighborhood may look a bit unsafe at night, but nothing happened to us. We also used UBER when getting in very late.  We recommend this place for staying in NYC. It is good value for the money taking into account NYC prices for hotels etc.  Thank you from us! Helena & Patrik October 2015

Overall, great experience! The apartment was in a basement, but it was in the excellent location, just 5 minutes walk to the subway station, so it wasn't scary to come back home late night. The hosts were super nice and friendly, and made sure we were happy with the stay. The apartment had everything we needed for the short stay, we liked it! The only thing we would change is the fact that every morning around 8am it was disturbing to hear steps, and the sound of water from the floor above, probably it was due to poor noise isolation. But if you have good sleep, then no worries!

This is our second visit to Julian's apartment and we don't regret our choice. It was clean, it didn't have any unpleasant odors and it was comfortable again.    The apartment is well located with small shops that are really convenient for a quick lunch in the morning. A 24-hour pharmacy very close to the metro station. The metro is also located very close to the apartment.   The only negative point is the noise from the apartment upstairs. The apartment is not soundproofed and the neighbors seem to live at night so it is sometimes difficult. Despite this noise, I would return to this place without any hesitation. For the price and the savings we make by renting this apartment, it is really ideal. After all....it's only to sleep a few hours...... Thank you once again Julian for your availability and your listening. It is very appreciated.

Julian was a great host with good communication and instructions. The place itself was a little bare, with no table and chairs for eating at, minimal implements in the kitchen, a greasy floor and some unsafe broken powerpoints. However the place was secure and otherwise clean and Julian responded to requests quickly.

Julian's place is a small studio in Brooklyn. the location is great because the J train is only like a 2 minute walk away and can get you anywhere you need to go. The neighborhood is definitely not the nicest but it didn't feel unsafe. It just older and more rundown and has a lot of trash in the streets, but its New York so I mean its expected. There is a couple of food place around so that was a plus too. The studio is like any regular studio. Its clean overall. Nothing fancy. If you are not picky about where you stay and just need a regular inexpensive place to stay during a trip this is a good spot. It doesn't look exactly like the pictures so that took me off guard at first , but after a few hours I was actually really liking the little studio. Since its underneath the apartment complex like a basement or something it feels very private and cozy. I liked it overall.

My husband and I stayed with Julian for a week and had a great time in NYC. The check-in was easy and autonomous. Although we never actually meet Julian, he was always only a message away. The apt was awesomely close to the train station which meant we only had to walk two blocks to and from. Apart from that, there was a grocery store, licores store, dominos, and Popeyes a block away for any extras we may need or last minute bites after a long day. Julian had a futon in the sofa, which I was apprehensive about, but it wasn’t uncomfortable at all like typical futons. It laid out like a queen size bed and I slept so good! Plus, their sheets and towels were so soft and comfy! The only thing that my husband and I did not like, which may be due to our upbringing, was that whenever we’d walk back from the train, on that same block, we’d always pass a large group of adults smoking marijuana and hanging out outside of their apartment. Literally anytime we walked by... morning, noon, and night.
