They turn off their music.  In short, the O'Dell house was an excellent option for my family and me. And we really liked this form of hosting based on trust. O'Dell is a kind, friendly and trustworthy person. He looked after us before the trip, during the trip and after the trip. He sent us a message to let us know that we had arrived safely back in Mexico.   O'Dell's warmth made a big difference in our travel experience. He resolved our doubts and supported us in every way he could.  Thanks O'Dell.  Thanks Airbnb.

My mother and I really enjoyed to stay at Diana's place. Everything was clean and comfortable. Also, Diana is friendly and so kind person. My mother visited me from our country and was so tired because of the long fright. Diana provided us two bedrooms to relieve my mother's stress and her suggestion was perfect. My mom relaxed in the bedroom she gave us and enjoyed the trip in New York. I really appreciate her kindness and definitely would like to stay Diana's place again.

We will stay at this same place as soon as we have the opportunity to visit NYC again.  The house looks deceptively small. However, it turned out to be larger than we needed... with five sleeping areas and six beds we could have fit eight guests easily even though this stay was for only two adults, one senior, and two children. The house has a backyard with a table, and chairs, and a grill, and gets shade during the hot summer afternoons making it quite comfortable to relax before dinner. The eating areas in the kitchen and dining room gave us plenty of elbow room during breakfast; there were plenty of utensils, dinnerware, and cooking pots , enough to cook for an army squad if needed. We were even able to have a driveway parking spot for our monster SUV, a Chevy Suburban we drove from the Southwest to Brooklyn.  On our first day, walking home after midnight from the subway station was uncomfortable, but it was just our apprehensions. By the third night we were comfortable coming back at 1 or 2 in the morning since there were plenty of people walking about, plenty of lighting, plenty of auto traffic to make us feel safe. Every single night we came home after 11 pm, and it was just as if it had been 11 in the morning. Friday and Saturday were just a bit noisier, and it seemed everyone on the streets was out late, talking, playing dominos, listening to music. The greater neighborhood came alive Friday and Saturday nights, and it was a joy to see and hear so many people as we walked home from the subway station.  It was quite convenient to have a supermarket and a laundromat within half a block of the house. And the best part was having the laundromat wash and fold our laundry while we were out and about in Manhattan. And the house has a folding cart we used to carry our laundry back and forth.  This was our first experience with Airbnb, and we were pleased with the ease of booking, ease of checking in and out, and with the savings we realized compared to staying in a hotel suite.

Our stay with Diana was absolutely perfect. We stayed for 3 days while we looked for our own Brooklyn home, a stressful situation for anyone. But Diana's wonderful home offered us a quiet respite after our long days of showings. Diana greeted us upon arriving and showed us how to get around the house, making us feel instantly at home. She provided us with coffee and tea, and checked to make sure we were comfortable. Both the very large room and the bathroom were clean and comfortable. I would highly recommend staying with Diana.

I enjoyed the stay for what it was, though for the price there should've been more to offer. If there was any real thing i would point out it would mainly just be the loud aircon in the bedrooms. I also felt the area looked a tad sketchy.

Sun's house was cozy, clean and welcoming.  We were traveling as a couple. The bed was reasonably comfortable.  The check-in and check-out was smooth and easy. Sun was responsive via text and we didnt run to any problems in the house. The neighborhood was a bit sketchy and might make some people uncomfortable but we were ok with it. The house is located right above the metro station which was good due accessibility and bad because you hear metro noises in the living room area. Overall, we  recommend this place.

This space was actually much larger than I expected. The inside was pretty clean, although it is an old building and difficult to get it up to the standards of newer buildings. The bedroom was really cozy and the bed was very comfortable. It was hot when we visited but the air conditioning units did a pretty good job. The outside smelled constantly of trash due to the trash cans being set by the staircase and the block we were on had some homeless people and was slightly dirty. I would have appreciated being prepared for this although I would visit again.  The price was very reasonable for the space and Sun was a very considerate and responsive host. The apartment is conveniently located right next to a subway stop and a doable walk from the Botanical Garden and the museum (although it is on a slight incline). Tony's pizza around the corner on the next block was the real New York experience and Prospect Park was really cool.  In all, everything that Sun had control of was very nice and he was a great host. I would have simply liked to be able to match my expectations a little more closely to what the reality is and I hope this review will do that. In all, we had a pleasant stay and felt like we had a realistic experience of New York life!

Jaime's place is clean and spacious.  The location is convenient and just steps away from the subway.  The neighborhood is a bit noisy, so we had to put on earplugs often, but I suspect that's true for most neighborhoods in Brooklyn.  Other than that, the apartment offers a comfortable and homey stay.

Chad's place is the real deal and so is Chad. Before my three friends and I even left home for our visit to NYC, Chad was emailing me to see how I was doing and to give me weather reports.  Chad had three pages typed out of all the information we would need:  emergency contacts, drug store, grocery store, recommended restaurants,bars, and sites. Throughout the weekend he was accessible at all times cheerily to answer any questions we had - no matter how minute.  Chad's home was the perfect size for up to four people - well appointed and in the perfect location. We four women felt safe in the neighborhood and always felt like we were at home at Chad's. Before leaving, Chad took time from his morning to sit with us and chat about our lives and he about his.   We will definitely return to NYC and to Chad's spacious Chelsea apartment. Thanks Chad!

Adrienne was accommodating to my late check-in and on our two encounters, she was very friendly and nice! We had so much privacy during our five night visit; the apartment was really ours to feel at home. While it would have been nice to see Adrienne more, she made sure to text us to see if we were comfortable or needed anything at all. She encouraged us to use the projector and was responsive to our needs.   Arriving at the apartment was a warm surprise after a long day. The pictures are really spot on of the unit, but I was still surprised at how charming and quaint the place is in person. The kitchen and bathroom were clean. Also the neighborhood is GREAT with the subway and a good deli just two blocks away. We experienced so much convenience going downtown and uptown adding more time to our vacation and less stress. I enjoyed the area during the day and night; it is quiet but still bright and lively being away from central Harlem.   My friends and I agreed on how much we liked staying at Adrienne's place.   Bonus: Fresh plants and flowers and recycling bags.   Thank you Adrienne! We had an unforgettable time at NYC.

Karen was a wonderful host she made this process so easy and stress free. Her home is cozy and has everything you need to be comfortable and its in a great location. I hope to stay there again on future visits.

Daniela is awesome and Cozy Cave is a true steal. Its got a lot of room plus is superbly decorated. Daniela is very accommodating and friendly and not weird or scary at all - so if you're going to take a chance on anyone you should take one on staying with her. We had a great time at her place, it is the perfect way to enjoy NYC for cheap. The only small setback is it takes a while to get to and from Manhattan on the train, especially at night when the trains are local stops only. But other than that it's grade A. At the beginning of the week we were initially worried about whether or not the area was safe, but it seems to be as safe as anywhere and we trained the whole time with no problems. All in all, Daniela is a great host and staying at her place was an awesome experience.

Keiko's apartment is located in the heart of Greenwich Village, near transportation (a detail that is far from trivial in NY), in a typically New York building, with its ladders that descend from the facade. We feel good in the neighborhood, good in the apartment, there are many things that we can do on foot (the Whitney museum, the high line, the walk along the Hudson, Union Square, even Chinatown or Little Italy for the brave). Everything is not perfect, the kitchen is small (but who cooks in NY?), the sofa perhaps sinks a little, but if we are asked the question "would you come back to this apartment?", the answer is without hesitation: yes!! We didn't meet Keiko, but her welcome is very relaxed, stress-free, it's very pleasant when you arrive after an 8-hour plane ride.

My accommodation experience in Brooklyn was sensational. The apartment is well maintained, with incredible vintage furniture and new appliances. The bed (spring) and sheets were so comfortable that I asked where they had been purchased. Wade received me punctually and showed me useful places nearby (there's a market a block away), in addition, he also answered any subsequent questions I had via message. Although the address is a little far from Manhattan (about 20/30 minutes by subway depending on which lines you use), the neighborhood of the apartment was calm and friendly, I walked the streets even close to midnight without fear. And if your idea, like mine, is to explore Brooklyn or visit places like Coney Island, I would consider the accommodation option as the cost-benefit ratio is great.  ::::::::  My experience in Brooklyn was sensational. The apartment is well maintained, with incredible vintage furniture and new appliances. The bed and sheets were so comfortable I asked where they were purchased. Wade received me on time, pointed me to useful places nearby (there is a market a block away) and in addition answered some subsequent questions by message. Our experience in this house has been great. Wade is a great host but in spite of living a few meters away he did not interfiere in our stay unless we asked for something. We had a little problem with a shade in our room and he fixed during the same day. The house was real confortable and in a quiet neighborhood 30 or 40 minutes away from Manhattan by subway. We recommend this place absolutedly.

After a very fraught journey from the UK to New York, we eventually made it to Alan'  place. After  the stress of the journey a beautiful apartment awaited myself, and Mark my husband. Alan and his family were perfect hosts, and made us feel very welcome indeed from the start. Alan and Ann were easy to talk to and gave us lots of information about Park Slope, where to eat and of course places where we could find craft beer. Following Alan and Ann' recommendations we visted the Gate bar which became a firm favourite. We are hopng to return to NYC next year, and will no doubt be contacting Alan again to hire this 'little jewel in Park Slopes crown'.   A perfect place to stay and we hope to return to Alan' apartment again next year. Roll on September 2016 it can't come round soon enough!

My wife and I can recommend Erika's apartment. The studio is friendly and well furnished and offered us everything we needed for a pleasant stay in New York - from a comfortable bed to the necessary kitchen utensils. Erika was an attentive and friendly hostess who had already put the first groceries in the fridge and answered questions and gave us insider tips during our stay. The area surrounding the apartment is non-touristy (that is meant in a positive way) with a great ethnic diversity and many small, good restaurants. We never felt unsafe (not even in the evening). The subway connections to Manhattan are regular and quick. It was a completely successful stay in Brooklyn for us. Thank you, Erika!

Alan is a great host. Very responsive to queries, requests and needs within the unit. The unit itself was very comfortable, and walking distance to a number of restaurants, coffee shops, drug stores, transportation, etc. The neighborhood was safe and inviting. All in all, great place to stay when you find yourself in Park Slope.

Great spot to be based in Brooklyn while being close to Manhattan. The accommodation itself is simple but complete and super functional: it's very simple, everything is available (perhaps missing a microwave to possibly heat up a takeaway dish). The wifi works very well, no problems with it. The terrace at the back is a real bonus for morning breakfasts, or simply for relaxing at the end of the day. The street has little traffic and despite the presence of major roads quite close, you can hear absolutely nothing at night, except perhaps a few fire sirens in the distance. Commodore Park opposite is full of life during the day, and its public swimming pool is a real treat in the middle of summer after a busy day. The shops and the metro are not right in front of the door, but not too far either, a little walk allows you to immerse yourself in the neighborhood and its inhabitants.  For shops, the Red Apple supermarket or better yet the NYC Fresh Market, both on Myrtle Av. are very good. Marisa recommends two metros, the one on Dekalb Av. and the one on York St. I would also add the one on Jay St. Metrotech which is not closer than the other two, but which, being on Myrtle, allows you to do your shopping on your way home in the evening, and also to pass in front of the La Defense restaurant, which has the advantage of offering French dishes for those who would like a change from American dishes... The area is very popular, but we never felt in danger day or night: people are most often charming, greeting you easily, or at worst ignoring your presence. We never took the taxi in the end. And finally, Marisa is a great hostess, always available by email to answer questions if necessary, very good contacts before arriving in NYC. Its reputation on AirBnB given its numerous positive feedbacks is not usurped at all

We had a fantastic time staying at Drew's.  He was incredibly flexible at arranging both check in and check out times, making that a breeze.  The location is perfect...just steps from amazing restaurants, bistros, bars, shopping, and the subway (only one block away).  Just one block to the LES Tenement Museum as well, where the gift shop alone is worth a visit.  The 2 bedroom apartment is nicely furnished and arranged well.  Everything you would need in the kitchen is there and Drew was quick to offer use of anything we needed, including condiments.  You don't go to NYC to hang out and watch tv but the Roku and computer (with wifi and printer) provided a great outlet when we were there and needed it.  The 2nd bedroom has a blow up mattress but it was taller than a standard one and with the foam topper, it was incredibly comfortable and you wouldn't even know it wasn't a regular bed.  Closet space was also provided in both bedrooms.  Drew also typed up a listing of recommendations in the area for restaurants, shopping, drug store, coffee house, etc.  It is 2 flights up but after all the amazing food and delicacies in NY, the exercise was good.  ;)  We also made the unfortunate mistake of locking both our set of keys in the apartment on our last night there.  Drew was quick to respond to our text with 2 nearby neighbors who could let us in and it was resolved quickly.  We definitely recommend this apartment!

Karin and Kevin were fabulous!!!  Their apartment is very convenient to subways, restaurants and shops, and the neighborhood is quite safe.  The room itself was small but fine for my needs, especially since it had a sink, small fridge and mirrors. The common bathroom was immaculate as is the rest of the house, which is full of well-chosen artwork. Karin and Kevin are both very cultured and lovers of the arts, especially jazz, so conversations with them were delightful.  They were also personally very helpful and generous to me.   They were so wonderful I hesitate to give them this great review, because I'm afraid the room will not be available for my next visit to NY, but since they were so kind, I'm taking the risk.
Very welcoming. Cool, safe neighborhood. Super close to subway. Came home late many nights and never felt unsafe or had any issues otherwise. Other house guests are all very quiet too.

Susan is a wonderful friendly host.  Location is perfect - 100 yards from 1 Train station at 157th St.  Room is small but hey this is NYC and the price is right.  Two wonderful, friendly cats.  Some folks might think it's dangerous neighborhood but we had  only typical NYC friendliness to strangers.  Thank you Airbnb for bringing us together.

I stayed here for two nights (Fri and Sat) and it was great. Room is cozy and clean (Susan had a cleaning person come in the day I arrived). Susan is a great host: very friendly, easy to communicate with both in person and through email. Her cats ARE incredibly cute. And yes, the place literally is two doors away from a subway (though only the north bound track, you have to cross the street to get to the south bound track... still really close though).  It takes about a 25 minute subway ride to get from this place to the center of Time Square. As for location, it's not bad. It definitely isn't as developed as lower Manhatten. I've heard that it's a slightly more dangerous area, but I never had any incidents. For the price, it's totally worth it.
Was great! The building looks a little scary from the outside but the inside is nice!! Really close to great amenities and the subway isn’t too far either!!

Everything was perfect!  We were able to collect the keys very easily and the metro is right next to the apartment, very convenient for visiting New York.  We were also able to leave our suitcases in the apartment before a night flight and retrieve them during the day.

Wow! I stayed here the entire month of August and it was awesome. You’re own private studio w/ private bathroom and A/C unit in the heart of Bed Stuy. Revel or Subway anywhere you want. Metro market a block away. What a perfect location! Everything was clean and accurate to the pictures posted. Jwajiku is an awesome host who was responsive to texts and provided everything you would need from clean towels, sheets, toilet paper, water, etc!! 10/10… I wasn’t expecting much but Jwajiku’s place is an absolute steal!

We stayed here for 6 days and below are the Pros and cons: Pros: 1. Great location 2. Host was very responsive and good communication 3. Checkin/checkout was easy  Cons: 1. Very smelly apartment- it seems like the smell of smoke had settled in the apartment. By day 3, our friends started commenting that we were smelling of smoke. Very unpleasant experience 2. The cleaning lady did not do a good job of cleaning the apartment. Host did mention that he couldn’t get hold of his regular cleaning lady a f this person was a temp.  3. Overall, place felt very pricey for what it offered

The accommodation is not quiet. The footsteps upstairs can be heard until late at night, and the host often hums, plays the movie loudly, and snores when sleeping.  In the first picture, the two spaces seemed to be separate spaces through the door, but the room belonged to the host, not to my room. My space is all about one bed and even that is covered by very thin curtains. She insist on closing the curtains if it's not time to sleep, and my space is completely violated and I can't find any privacy. The host's words and actions are very unpleasant. As soon as I met her, I was very uncomfortable with the crossing-line remarks such as "It's different from the picture" and "Act like a woman." She tried to talk more than communication for the accommodation, such as what I eat and where I go, and I couldn't relax in the accommodation with it.   The location is good and the price is cheap, but I will never go again even if i can stay for free.

Stayed at this room for about a month. it was very clean, and had everything I would need and more. The pictures are accurate. If you are looking for a long term stay, this is very comfortable and a good choice for that. There is a washer a dryer and it’s very new and nice. Lots of cabinet space to store dry foods. Ampere was very accommodating and friendly. Location is good too. I am a 26 year old female and personally never felt unsafe walking. And it’s very very close to the M train which takes you into the city. And ampere would occasionally make soup for guests. Overall great stay thank you ampere!
Great place, Rob and Ampere are very hospitable and I enjoyed my stay. Will definitely stay here again.

This was a really perfect spot to stay at for a week... it's a very communal space (kitchen, laundry, bathroom). Everyone also treats their spaces privately keeping their bedroom  doors closed and the noise level was always respectful. I'd definitely stay again and wish there were more places like this! It was well stocked for daily living without having to buy anything extra (paper towels, cooking oil, etc) Thanks Rob + Ampere!

Rob and Ampere are excellent hosts! There were several other guests living on the same floor and during my stay, I mostly interacted with Ampere who was very dedicated in maintaining a nice and welcoming environment for all the guests. Ampere was responsive and helpful with any questions or issues I had and even shared some Malaysian cooking with me once! The area is a bit far from Manhattan, but it is extremely close to an M subway station that takes you directly into the city. Overall I really enjoyed my stay and would come back if I were to visit NYC again.
Great great great host !  I can’t stress this enough Alia apartment is so beautiful, I wanted to live in the bathroom. This place is a hidden gem in Brooklyn and would stay/recommend anytimeeee !

My partner and our 4 year old stayed here for about 6 weeks while work was being done on our own apartment. We truly loved our time here and were even sad to leave. The apartment itself is immaculate with updated  with high quality fixtures and appliances. Having a washer/dryer is like winning the lottery, it was such a nice touch for a busy family like ours. Same thing with the 2 bathrooms and dishwasher. Rosario is a very kind host and allowed us to extend our stay when some unforeseen circumstances made that necessary. The building is quiet. The neighborhood is great with so many restaurants, grocery stores, drug stores, playgrounds, and the Q train just steps away. We quickly felt right at home.

When I arrived at the listing, it was not as nice & beautiful as it looked in the photos. It wasn’t decorated or set up how it is in the photos which is the only thing I have to go off of when renting an Airbnb. It was also messy and dirty in the other rooms outside of the private room. The last 2 things to note is 1, as another review mentioned it is on the 4th floor and there’s no elevator which makes it difficult to go up and down if you have heavy luggage. And 2, the private room is sort of cut off from the rest of the apartment. So in order to shower or use the bathroom, you have to leave the room, lock the door behind you bc now you’re out in the hallway, walk down the hallway, and unlock the main door to get inside. I personally hated doing that and a little unsafe bc I didn’t know who I might run into.

The flat looks exactly as in the photos. It is quite strategicaly located, subway station and some shops are close. Flexible time of arival thanks to housekeeper is excelent. The worse experience is the housekeeper as person. He insisted on some for me irritating rules. I was not allowed to let my things in common areas (kitchen, living room). I understand that it is important to keep the kitchen clean, but when I let there clean glass and plastic bottle for next day (when I wanted to use it again), he left me unpleasant message that it is unacceptable and I should clean after myself. The same situation was with shoes which I always had to hide somewhere not to be visible in common part of the flat. It was annoying rule and I have no idea why should I always bring everything out of the kitchen especially when I want to use it again in a few hours.

Rob's place is super comfortable and conveniently located to so many great parts of the city, amazing restaurants and fun bars. Nancy, our co-host, was very helpful and readily available to help out during our stay. I give this place a perfect 10!
Rob has a wonderful apartment. Perfect location. The communication was great and he was very flexible with the check in/check out time.
Great place to stay. Rob was extremely communicative made for a very smooth check-in experience.  I always felt like if I needed anything, Rob would respond immediately

Carlene’s place is really nice. I definitely enjoyed my stay in the room. The neighborhood might seem a little sketchy but it’s safe to walk even late at night from the subway station (10 min away). The place is clean and has everything you need. I would suggest not having someone clean the house every single day but 3 times a week, as guests could have more privacy during their stay. I would stay in this place again without doubt.

Excellent accommodation, quiet neighborhood, I never felt unsafe even at night. There is a subway station a couple of blocks away and the bus passes in front. Everything clean and identical to the photos, I would return without thinking!

I felt very comfortable at Carlene’s place. My stay was for 10 days. I really recommend this place. It’s near various metro stations and buses. The only thing I was worried about is that the neighbourhood wasn’t safe, but it was okay. Some parts are sketchy but mostly is nice. That was important to me because I’m a female solo traveller. The space is very clean and organised. Malose was very helpful and attentive. I would come again.

It was my first time staying in a Airbnb and it was the best, I was kinda scared at first renting an airbnb but It was worth it, Bathroom was very clean, smelled great, had cleaning supplies and extra bags in case you wanted to throw trash out. Room was exactly like the pictures and the ad says, only thing was that it didn't have an AC i don't know if it was cause it was cold the days I was there but I didn't have a problem with not having an AC but Would've loved if it did.  I will definitely be renting again with Wilson. Thank You for a wonderful stay. God Bless.

I would have given Wilson the perfect rating had I not been a victim of Asian Hate Crime in the area. I know it is not his fault but I thought to let potential clients know that this might not be the safest area for Asian minorities. I was randomly hit in the head by a neighbor a few houses away from the AirBNB when I was simply walking towards home in broad daylight as the guy blurts out racist comments while running away from the scene. It was so disappointing and traumatizing to say the least and I apologize that I had to write this review. The ignorance and stupidity of others affects the thriving businesses in the area. I hope and pray that my incident will be the last.

Nothing sketchy, it was just like the pictures. A very relaxing room to come home to after a busy day in the city. A few short blocks away from metros, a laundromat and Broadway. About 25-30 minutes away from JFK International Airport by car or about 50 minutes away from JFK by metro. Convenient and inexpensive location. Mr. Wilson seemed to by a kind and caring host. Gave us space but was always there to check on us and respond quickly. Would love to come back!

Great place! Cozier than the pictures. Clean and had everything we needed for the weekend. Parking wasn’t too bad during our stay. It’s definitely a lively neighborhood and the neighbors are up pretty late playing music but coming from a similar neighborhood it didn’t bother us. We never felt unsafe but I will say it’s not the most walkable neighborhood out there and it’s a pretty decent drive to downtown Brooklyn or into the city. Depending on what you’re looking for a though it’s really a great little spot!

Fikile is a lovely person and was a great communicator who sought to make my stay comfortable. But unfortunately, this place is overpriced for the amenities. The pictures make it seem much nicer than it is. If you're here in winter, since the day ends at 4pm it gets dark very quickly and the lighting in the apartment is very dim so it's not quite comfortable. The biggest issue was that the ceiling had a huge mold issue which made it unpleasant, and if you're allergic to mold I would suggest staying elsewhere.

I’m from NY but I don’t live here anymore and needed a place to stay. This place was amazing, very close to mass transit, close to the drug store, coffee shops, and restaurants. Stayed here for Christmas and New Years. The room has a separate entry in the foyer so it’s great to not wake everyone up. They were very accommodating and very sweet.
You can expect a no stress welcoming experience.  We felt like they were happy we were there.

Sion's and Narim's house is beautiful, just like the pictures, and after few days even better. We are familly of 5 with 3 teenage kids and house felt like an oasis after whole day in the city. At first we were scared that it's to far from Manhattan but 2 subway lines are close by so the subway ride was easy. For a family visit I would certainly choose the same house again.

Angela’s place was absolutely perfect for our two week stay. The space is conveniently laid out, with a comfy bedroom, great living room with projector, and functional kitchen. For the price, this place was a steal and just as good or better than much pricier options. The area is filled with great places to eat. I would highly recommend to anyone.

I had a wonderful stay at Josiah's BK apartment that is perfectly situated on a quiet street in bustling Williamsburg and a convenient block away from the L stop - getting into the city takes less than 10 minutes! The place is comfortable and spacious, exactly what I needed in the midst of a stressful month. Josiah was kind enough to let me stay after checkout when my cat disappeared and wait for her to come out of hiding. Would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a cozy and quiet stay but wants to be close to the city!

Me and my cat stayed at Hyonce's beautiful space while we were in the middle of a move. Hyonce's place was so welcoming for both of us, was even bigger than the pictures made it out, and during a pretty stressful month - her apartment was a safe haven for us. I knew the area well already, Myrtle Ave being so close is great for groceries and restaurants, and multiple bus options to get you to downtown Brooklyn or just over to Fort Greene Park.  It was more than I hoped for and would happily recommend for any friends of mine coming in town.

This hotel is precious! With the décor and details of the lobby and rooms to the staff it was just heavenly staying for even 2 days. Location was perfect to walk around Brooklyn and for a little trip over to Manhattan.  I would note that you should make sure Airbnb communicates with the hotel that you have a reservation. Just give a quick little call before heading there. It would’ve saved a little stress at check in. The staff was quick to rectify and put me at ease- everyone there is amazing!  Definitely would recommend them!

We had an incredibly disappointing stay at the Hoxton. The fire alarm went off twice during our stay for lengthy periods both times and staff handled it terribly. Both times we evacuated to the street in NY winter only to find hotel staff continuing on their daily duties as though nothing was happening without communicating anything to guests. After asking staff what was happening we were told it was a false alarm and that they were trying to fix it. No one came out to proactively let guests know who had evacuated to the sidewalk. Unfortunately, the second time the alarm went off it was 10.30pm and my baby and I were asleep in our room.  I was told I could return to my room with my baby even though the alarm was extremely loud, at sound levels that are not safe for a baby, and continued to sound for the next ~hour. Hotel staff shouted at me when I complained that the handling of the fire alarms was appalling, and unsafe. We finally returned to our room exhausted at 11.30pm when other guests (not hotel staff) told us the alarm was no longer sounding on our floor. No apology or assistance was offered by hotel staff. Would avoid this hotel at all costs.

Provided us with only 1 towel for two people, had to call to get in contact with the renter, felt unclean, but that might just be New York. However, a quiet area and did not feel unsafe when traveling, multiple bus stops very close.

Ampere and Rob were great hosts (they're co-hosts of this multi-family unit) - they always kept the place clean, made me feel at home, and welcomed me to New York with open arms! I moved here to NYC and stayed at Airbnb for a month! It was a great place. I would highly recommend their home as a long-term rental. Ampere - I'm still waiting for those Mayalasian restaurant recommendations! :)
Y’all best to book for i book. It’s a great steal

Had a lovely time in NY- first time visiting. Darko was an AMAZING host. Really helped me out with the whole subway system. Neighborhood is super safe. I was walking home some days close to midnight and never felt unsafe. Really appreciated the coffee machine! Highly recommend to stay here!

Very good experience.  The apartment is very well located for visiting Manhattan. In the heart of Chinatown and close to Little Italy.  The apartment is simple and clean. The room is clean. The sheets smell clean upon arrival. After a long trip, we appreciate it.  Beyond the apartment, if you choose a stay of a few days you will live a superb human experience with a very friendly person Moying.  Moying is very attentive to travelers (check in and out flexibility / baggage storage in the event of a late flight), shares her good advice and good addresses.  Moying thanks for everything. You make my trip to NYC unique!

This apartment is a great place to stay! It is right by the 125th street subway station (< 5-minute walk), which means you can take express subways, making it super easy to get around. The apartment itself is beautiful and spacious, with two similar-sized bedrooms (a struggle when trying to find a place in New York!).  There were never any problems with noise (it is on a side street). There is laundry in the building, a backyard space to use and it is only a short walk to Whole Foods. It is also about a 20-minute walk to the Columbia University area (although you do have to walk up a hill). If looking for fun activities to do in the neighborhood, I recommend Paint n Pour. I (20s female) never felt unsafe in the neighborhood, even walking around at night (although general safety precautions still apply). There is also a park nearby where there are always people playing baseball and having BBQs (I have been advised to avoid the park at night though). Overall a really nice apartment, a fun neighborhood, and close enough to the subway to easily get around NYC.

I would overall stay here again! I was greeted by Jose’s Wife, Anna. She was extremely kind and caring and easy to talk to. They were both very accommodating and courteous concerned for my comfort and wellbeing. I felt like I was in a home away from home. The place was VERY clean, this is HUGE for me because the slightest thing I see that is dirty will turn me off. This was not the case here. Upon walking in, there was a fresh scent and I could tell the apartment was really cleaned before my arrival. There were bottles of water in the fridge that I didn’t expect but was really grateful to have! My only minor complaint would be lots of noises by the washer that was next door and the heat made lots of noises but nothing crazy! I also don’t think the space is suitable for 4 people because the sofas are pretty small. This would be better suited for 1-3 people IMO. This property is located on a very quiet street. I would advise you to LOCK your cars though. I saw somebody walking by cars looking in windows possibly to steal items. That was a stray compared to the rest of the area. I grew up around here and That Street is normally unproblematic.   I will definitely stay here again and recommend my family and friends to do so also!

I stood at this apartment and despite of all the virus scare across the country. This unit had a 5 star grade of cleaning by housekeeping. They disinfected and sanitized their place. I felt ZERO concerns with the high grade of tender love and care that they put into making sure this place is top notch in NYC. A gem in the Bronx for sure. I highly recommend this place

The place was fine. The lack of WiFi was disappointing and made it difficult to do the small bit of work I had to do. Also, I didn’t feel unsafe, per se, but having to meet the host in the apartment to get the keys was not ideal. Also, the apartment door has clearly been broken into. And no chain on the door to lock from the inside. Also, the super instructed me to tell anyone who asked that I was “staying with family.”   Mattress was surprisingly comfortable. But the bottom sheet, which was torn in several places, didn’t fit properly and came off the bed several times.   Bible verses listed on post it’s on the fridge made me a bit uncomfortable.   Other than that: The place is fine—small but comfortable enough. Would be better with the above details fixed. Would not run to stay again.
THIS BNB IS A SCAM, DONT BUY!

Only 2 small rooms , no WiFi during the whole stay . 2 bunk beds in 1 room . 1 of the 3 had no mattress at all only the boarding . No blankets , toiletries. And the host constantly watches your though his camera. I had 2-3 guest over for a few hours , and every time they came in he called asking “who  is that” and “how long they’ll be staying”. It made us feel unsafe . And let’s not forget about the wiring , it’s very hot outside and as soon as we turned the ac all the lights blew . This happens constantly over the space of 3 days .
Fantastic value. Quality housing in the upper west side for a steal of a price 👍👍

The images of this location looked far better that the location itself. The mattresses and pull out couch were both stained with what appeared to be bodily fluids. The divider for the double room was not present at all, offering no privacy. The location is on the third floor of the building, with no elevator access which made attempting to bring large luggage cases to the room near impossible. The bathroom had half used toiletries left behind, presumably from previous tenants. The kitchen was stained and looked unclean as well. Due to the severity of the unkempt nature of this bnb we decided to stay elsewhere for our trip, which caused unnecessary stress but we believed it to be preferable to staying in this bnb. I’d recommend elsewhere until images of this place are updated or until the location is taken care of.

This house is beautiful, roomy and comfortable! The host was amazing at communicating and always making sure we were happy and we really appreciated the attentiveness of just making sure we had a great vacation! It took anywhere between 40-60 min to get to the city depending on what part we were going to but it was worth it so our whole party could stay together and comfortably not being too cramped!!! It is ambitious to travel NYC with a large party and knowing when we got back we could unwind and all had plenty of space was worth the commute! When we 1st arrived we were a little weary of the location, but honestly it doesn’t look the most glamours place but we never got the feeling of being unsafe once we were walking around, and the train was only a few minutes walk. We loved this place, you can tell how much Chani cares and puts it into taking care of her home! We appreciate the care and attention and would definitely stay there again if traveling with a large group! Thank you so much for everything!!!

This was a great stay.  The hosts were super responsive.  The attention to detail inside the place was fantastic, they even provided written materials which were super helpful in our commute. HOWEVER, there is no off street parking and I specifically asked if it was safe to park in the neighborhood, since I had driven my personal vehicle to NY and I was told that the neighborhood was safe to off street parking.  On the second night I parked around the corner of the block and the catalytic converter was stolen from my vehicle which will be costly to repair since they also tore out the wires for the oxygen sensors.  The place is great to stay IF you are not driving your own vehicle.  That’s my opinion based on my experience.  The hosts were fantastic and I know that what occurred is not their fault, but as a frequent traveler it is important for me to share my experiences so that others can be cautious.

I was a solo female traveler and I would say it was good amount of space and because of NYPD station nearby, I wasn’t feel that much danger but I won’t recommend to go out by yourself after sunset. You need to mentally prepare to climb A LOT OF stairs😅 I only had a backpack and carry-on luggage but it was tough workout lol So, if you have bigger and heavier stuff, you might want to consider other places where it has elevators lol Things are look exactly same as listing pics but something wasn’t expected. First, if you are planning to cook, kitchen sink doesn’t have normal function. It means that you have to check underneath and there is a small tub and all dirty water go there. So, if it’s full you have to draining somewhere. Moreover, check under the bed. When I stayed it was very dirty and if you have allergies it might cause heavy allergic reaction.  This was my first Airbnb experience but I realized how picky and tidy I am. I’m not sure I’ll stay in Airbnb in the future but this place was alright if you save money or you’re solo traveler.

Sasha is a perfect host! He is very informative and makes the whole experience simple and stress-free. The location is perfect for access to transportation, sightseeing, and living like the locals. It was perfect! I can’t wait to visit again. 💕

While in the middle of a stressful apartment move, Sasha accommodated me for the night at a stellar rate - and with tons of patience and understanding. Without him and Pupa, this difficult period would’ve been a lot more difficult. Thanks a million!
Great stay! Made my trip easy and stress-free. Would definitely book again.

This is a wonderful find in Brooklyn.  So close to everything. It is perfect for a couple or a group of 4. The bed and pillows was so comfortable. Eat in or eat out, yourchoice.  our favourite was  Ix just a few  blocksaway wonderful Guatamalan food. Thank you Claudia and Doug for your hospitality Kathleen and Rob

This apartment is in a great location as the 1/2/3 are 7 min walk away and there is a station entrance for the B/C at the end of the block. The apartment is nice and clean with lots of natural sunlight. The bed is also quite comfortable and there is a monitor/TV with an HDMI cord you can use. The couches are also large and comfortable. The kitchen is very well stocked and even has a moka pot and french press. Carlo is also super responsive to anything that needs to be fixed. Surprisingly the water pressure in the shower is very good.   There are four things I'd like to point out about this apartment.   The first thing I would point out is although the street is generally quiet, because both the bedroom and living room face a one way/one lane street, every couple of days the street will get backed up and there will be a lot of cars honking at the same time for minutes. This was very unpleasant especially when it happened very early in the morning. Other than ear plugs there isn't much you can do about it. Next time I would probably opt for one of the apartments facing the back of the building.   The second thing is the apartment is a walk up with three very long sets of stairs you need to go up (20+ steps each) so if you have heavy luggage or have issues with lots of stairs I wouldn't recommend this place.   The third thing is the wifi here is not very fast. I wasn't able to stream things on my phone in the bedroom so I used cellular data for most of my stay. In the living room I was able to do work and participate in conference calls so didn't have issues there. There does seem to be a coax cable you can plug into a modem to have your own internet for your 30 days+ stay. This is assuming you pay for your own wifi. The wifi provided is from a modem/router not in the apartment so the signal is not very strong.   The fourth thing is that there is central heating for the whole building and most of the time it was too hot so I needed to keep the windows open. I visited in the fall so it wasn't too big of an issue. Carlo also was very accommodating and turned the thermostat down for the building. There does seem to be one window AC unit in the closet so I assume in the summer you can use the AC in one of the rooms.

It is a very cozy space. For long stays, if you like to prepare some of your own food, you will find limitations with the kitchen facilities, few items to cook, and also few options to change towels and sheets. It is a central, quiet and safe place although it is common to see quite a few homeless people around.

I spent about a month in Michael's apartment, communication with him was very effective, always responding to my questions. The apartment is on the fourth floor, without an elevator, only stairs. When I arrived, Michael helped me carry my suitcases and showed me around. The apartment is in perfect condition, it is just as you see in the images, everything was very clean, they gave me hand soap, a dishwasher, and towels. The bed was very comfortable to sleep in, the shower was also very comfortable and the water always came out hot. The kitchen was well equipped, with all the necessary utensils. The apartment does not have a washing machine, however, a two-minute walk away there is a laundromat where you can leave your clothes or wash yourself (Laundromat). The apartment is very quiet, you can sleep very well, it is worth mentioning that they are doing construction work next door, but they start working at 7 in the morning only during the week, but it is not a disturbing noise, for me it was not a problem. The heating in the place works well, when there are rainy or cold days the heating in the apartment is felt more. The building is very quiet, it has cameras at the entrance and they have a recycling system for garbage. The sector is close to Time Square, a 14-minute walk, Macy's, a shopping center and other stores on 34th Street, as well as subway stations to transport you to other places such as A, C, E, and restaurants. On the other hand, in the sector, you see many homeless, also sleeping on the streets, but it is a situation that occurs in many parts of New York. For the apartment I would stay in this place again.

We came into Queens  for the wedding of my daughter .  Perfect location for us as only a couple blocks from her apartment . Neighborhood  is very safe .  We never felt unsafe walking around even at night . The place itself is just as described . Very clean . There was a hiccup with some supplies but Esmael was very responsive and fixed that quickly . We will definitely stay here again .

Several things wrong with this property. Dishwasher and microwave oven not working (though microwave was fixed while we were there). Only 2 bath towels for six day stay. This remedied somewhat by new towels from Target provided by Brianna.  Place not well stocked with soap and other necessities. No written instructions re: operation of TV. Homeless population on same street.

First off, I would like to say that the space itself has potential, but many things were wrong with my stay. When first reserving the apartment, it was advertised as an in-unit washer/dryer. This is not true; the laundry room is in the basement. I used the laundry room twice, and I do not recommend it; many machines either don’t work or are highly unsanitary. There’s also no cell phone service in the basement and as a woman I was concerned for my safety. There are many people that live in that apartment building and they have guests of their own. So you never really know who can walk down there while you’re alone and have no way to contact anyone on the outside. The gym in the building also doesn’t have cell service, so be mindful of that. The building is located in a central area of downtown Brooklyn, but there is also a homeless shelter nearby (less than a block away). With that being said, stay safe; I’ve witnessed many mental health episodes that included screaming/cursing/ violent behavior. The unit itself had a broken dishwasher, the oven was so dirty that it was burning old crust of food when turned on. The air vent in the bathroom was exposed for the entire six weeks of my stay. It was dusty and dirty, and dust would fall often. I asked the super of the building and the caretaker of the unit, and it was never fixed. Upon arrival, the unit seemed clean, but upon further inspection, it was filthy. I cleaned it myself and bought cleaning products, a trash can (because they had a mini trash can for the entire unit), and more towels. Upon arrival, I was told by the caretaker that if a guest is staying for an extended period of time, it is mandatory for them to clean the unit weekly. This happened once of the six weeks I stayed at the unit. The caretaker and I would schedule a time for her to come, and she would cancel, reschedule or not show up. I can’t tell you how many times this would happen; she was even unresponsive or unreachable for days at one point. After some time, I told her not to come over and clean and that I will just take care of it. Then on my four weeks, the caretaker asks me if I have left yet, and I said no, that I have two weeks left, then said that she has to clean the unit. Again more trouble with communicating and commit to actually coming to the unit. Once she finally did arrive at the unit. I walk into my apartment, and she is eating my fruit without permission. Then she says, “sorry, I was feeling dizzy, and asked if it was okay.” Keep in mind she lives in the building and could have called me and asked or just went to her apartment to eat. Then takes 6 hours to “clean” the apartment; she came to clean it at 7 pm and was there till midnight. Also, last-minute, she tells me that she is removing the couch, takes the sofa out, leaves it in the hallway in front of the door for a week. I was without a couch for a whole week and couldn’t use the living space much. I asked her repeatedly about getting the other couch and again more canceling, rescheduling, or not showing up. Three days before leaving, I finally got a couch in the unit. The whole thing wasted a lot of my time and gave me so much anxiety. I did express frustration and asked for things that I needed but I didn’t want express frustration or the fact that I was expressly unhappy because I didn’t feel comfortable to do so, they live in the building and had a master key to the apartment. I just didn’t feel safe or comfortable. I don’t recommend staying here.

DO NOT STAY HERE. THIS HOST IS A SCAMMER. I'd leave a 0 star review if I could.  This host advertises falsely and he knows it. Says the apartment has 2 beds for 4 adults, which it does not. Apartment does not match pictures or description. When you try to resolve the problem the host gives you a runaround, saying "you're welcome to leave" as if you have time to spend figuring out new accommodations while on a short trip visiting NYC. We are now in a lengthy dispute process trying to get our money back.  Don't make our mistake, avoid this host and do not stay here. It's a scam and you'll regret it. The host is not trustworthy.

The Check-in and Check-out were so easy. I only met Fazia omce in oerson but she was super nice and even offered me to drive me downtown that day. The room was ckean abd so was the bathroom and kitchen. Everything was as discribed, simple but good. I enjoyed the stay there.  The neighboorhood is a little sketchy but when you are not alone it is totally fine. There is access to a subway to Manhattan 13 minuted away from the Airbnb. I had a mini fridge in my room which was nice and I felt pretty safe within the house. Overall I have very little complaints. Sometimes it was a little loud in the night but other than that it was good.

Overall a good place to stay for a short term period. Communication with hosts was good.  Unfortunately area feels unsafe. Despite easy commute to Manhattan, every evening we felt uncomfortable coming back, so if you are traveling alone or with a child, keep that it mind. Please, bring earplugs with you, since it’s very loud (outside and inside the house). A couple times we had to ask neighbors upstairs to stop listening to loud music in the middle of the night.

Pro’s: -Easy entry from ground level -bed pillows are comfortable  -bed linens are soft -backyard was where we spent 90% of our stay   Con’s: -difficult communication with owner -sketchy encounters with other gusts having access to our unit + no explanation from owner -two doors not pictured in listing: one connected directly to unit upstairs, one leading to a basement. Both taped shut with duct tape. Access to our unit felt unsafe. Security measures were a joke -paper thin walls, floors and windows. You can hear every word, bodily noises, conversations on the streets.. highly disturbing for wfh and sleep -couch (if you can even call it that) in the living area is outdoor furniture cushions. Very rough and uncomfortable.  -leg of the dining table is broken and unstable + broken dining chair leg  -backyard is much more overgrown with weeds and trees than photo shows, no outdoor dining area as listing says -bed is hard as a brick  -the ac units produced a horrible smell -we had an issue with the radiator producing a foul smell and the owner refused to wait to send maintenance crew until after we were done with a very important work call. 4 loud men attempting to get into the apartment spent 2 hours climbing into the crawl space under the bedroom making incessant noise and did not fix radiator -when confronted about this issue, owner was incredibly rude and chose to harass us about our service animal (though his house rules do not list “no pets” and service animals are protected by Airbnb policy and ADA Federal law). When we stood our ground and reiterated our rights, he told us to leave the property and find somewhere else to stay. Direct discriminatory and illegal actions here. Our stay was cut in half. Do not trust anything about this place. Do yourselves a BIG favor and look elsewhere.

John and Ania were two of the nicest, most generous people I’ve ever met. The apartment was beautiful with wood furniture built by John himself, and grape vines growing on the windows up to the fourth floor of the building.  They live on one of those shady streets of Boreum Hill with old brick houses. Cannot recommend it enough. Take a walk to the Brooklyn Heights promenade.
Overall just a steal. Highly recommend!

Great space, better than expected, great amenities, private, clean, basic kitchen essentials, full kitchen, jacuzzi, relaxing ambiance and nice decor, free parking in driveway, and local drug stores. The host was reachable at all times and responded within minutes. Host was accommodating on decorations for an extra few bucks which was a great surprise for my partner. Thank you Wanda!!  I will definitely visit again in the future.  I highly recommend.

Super clean with snacks! There are full time residents upstairs which makes it a little noisy. Floor boards are real creaky. It’s relative location to the ferry to Manhattan and the water front shops makes it a neat location. It’s a little sketchy though. Went for a 5 mi run and definitely didn’t feel safe. If you wanna run, I’d save that for Manhattan and central park.

Mary’s space was clean, inviting and made our trip to the City memorable because it felt like we were house sitting for a friend; stress free, chill energy, and cozy. Lots of local businesses close by for food and fun. Just an all around great experience. Highly recommend.

This place is great if you are a hard core backpacker, it is very minimal, the neighborhood was safe we came back late every night and didn't feel unsafe but we were a couple. Transportation is close but you do have to walk at least 10 minutes.

A perfectly appointed apartment that's a steal in a great area. Tia is the most generous host and she made my stay very comfortable. Beautiful kitchen, excellent bathroom, fluffy white towels, a big closet with hangers and hooks. Little to no street noise at night -- just normal NYC noise. Great WiFi.  Subway access is astonishing -- a stone's throw away from two major subway lines so you can get anywhere in the city very easily.  A few things to know: Go to Perk Kafe and to Madame Bonte for coffee. Contento in East Harlem for Peruvian food. Check out a concert at the 92nd St Y, which is very close by. Central Park is an easy walk -- and so is the Guggenheim Museum. This is a 5th floor walkup, so if you have low stamina or expect to be carrying a lot of things in and out, please know that there are about 65 steps to climb.

It’s wonderful place. You can walk to subway for 11 minutes but less dangerous place. You can park near resident home side way, best time to park during morning because that’s where everyone left to work. This local doesn’t have much restaurant or convenience store  near by but you can walk to that place. The owner is very sweet!

The accommodation is in southern Brooklyn, which is radically different from Manhattan. This made our New York experience an interesting second look, this place in Brooklyn being much more popular than the famous Island.  The people we met there were quite friendly and spoke to us in the street in a very cordial manner (even in French sometimes!!).   I had a bit of the same feeling as in Harlem when I visited this area in 2019. We must therefore go beyond the clichés of "difficult" suburbs where certainly a large majority of people who live there are certainly less privileged than those who live in Manhattan, but we never felt unsafe, even if the police are much less omnipresent than in Manhattan.  This accommodation will therefore have allowed 5 people to discover this sector which is not lacking in interest.  A metro less than a kilometer away connects us to the rest of the world, there are 3 comfortable bedrooms and a small living room, a working kitchen, we don't regret going that way.... Dom
Good connection by bus and subway. Right outside the door. We didn't feel unsafe at all.

2nd stay. Paul’s place is very convenient, less than 10mins walk to 145 station. Quick train ride downtown. Its in a quiet part of Harlem and we did not feel unsafe at all. Paul is very easy to talk to and accommodating to reasonable requests. Will definitely consider staying with him again if we are back in NYC.

Where do I begin! If you are looking for a hotel, this is not it, because it’s much better than a hotel! It’s a home away from home! I was supposed to be in nyc for two weeks but got stuck for over a month because of what’s happening in China. Diana did everything in her power to help me through the crisis. Yet this is perfect for anyone, everyone, it’s close to everything, subway stations, bus stops, supermarkets, nice restaurants...I can keep going. And it’s also very easy to get to anywhere as a tourist. I hated to leave when I had to literally! Diana is the best person in the world, she treats everyone like family even the homeless guy on the street! Book it and you won’t regret it!

Very very nice place. One of the best places I've stayed in Flushing. The apartment seems to be brand new, with a lot of amenities. Comes with a kitchen, stove, and some cooking utensils. The beds are incredibly comfortable. The living is spacious and is cleanly decorated, and doesn't feel cramped at all. Living here is great. The only negative I can say is that the surroundings seem a bit shady and isn't well lit so I wouldn't stay out alone coming home. Also it's a 10-15 minute walk to the 7 train and therefore Flushing Main St. Not the closest but certainly not bad at all. Overall, a great place in Flushing, and I would definitely give it a try if you're looking in the area.

The neighborhood will make you weary but I’m from Chicago so it wasn’t scary for me. the people are very helpful and keep to their selves. Parking isn’t guaranteed so expect to park a block away but that was the least of our worries. There is a convenient store at the end of the street with everything from snacks to small toiletries if needed. It does get a bit chilly at night in the apartment but Rosana will make sure you’re warm and comfortable.

Host was very quick responsive at all the time. Great location if you're going to Randall island and also wanna visit Manhattan. The place has everything you need and was pretty clean too. We were going to electric zoo everyday so we were only looking for a good place to sleep. This place was perfect for what we wanted for sure. We loved the neighborhood because of all the options of Hispanic food. I personally didn't feel unsafe although a few people stopped me and my friends when walking around the area to tell us to be careful. People in this area (at least for the most part) was actually very friendly and helped us to find the right metro a few times. Definitely out of all the options of Airbnb in NY this was a very good deal. I recommend this place.
It is a Beisman, the space is small, I was there in January and it was very cold although it was very clean; The area is the Bronx and although it is close to the subway, it is a dangerous area.

The attention is very good, it looks just like you see it in the photographs, super clean, it is super equipped, Mr. Lou is always on the lookout for the guest for anything that is needed, the accommodation is very good!  the only disadvantage is that the area where the property is located is not very good and it is a bit scary, but nothing happened and we had a great time!

This is a beautiful apartment with a gorgeous, large backyard in prime Park Slope. The apartment is about a block from the Park, and within a few minute's walk of a number of great restaurants (especially Pasta Louise!).  It's on the street next to Methodist Hospital which is actually really nice because as a former resident of the neighborhood I can tell you that no one drives up that street because they're scared of getting stuck behind an ambulance. So actually the street ends up being really quiet. You're right up the block from the Purity Diner, a few blocks from Union Market and a bunch of good wine shops, and two blocks from the subway (as well as Smiley's Pizza). The apartment is a gorgeous classic garden apartment with beautiful crown molding and excellent amenities. We loved the espresso maker and the hosts were extremely good at communicating whenever we had questions. They also have plenty of extra towels and linens. It's a very good spot in a great location where I would definitely stay again. I was really grateful to find this spot.

Brou was great and the room was good but the building itself is not well kept. The apartment unit was nice. At no fault of the hosts at all, the building was dirty and the elevator was sketchy which posed a problem because the unit was on the 6th floor.
Stayed here a little less than a month while doing a quarantined apartment hunt. Great touch of home in an otherwise stressful period plus coffee, snacks and laundry!

The place is amazing. Communication with Denise was very good. She replied very quickly every time. Don’t get scared by the fact that it is close to the airport. It’s very quiet and peaceful. Only small downside is the fact that it takes some time to get from the AirBnB to the city center using public transportation only. Other than that there is really nothing to complain about. We felt like home from the moment we got into the AirBnB. 😊

This place was nice. It isn't in the busy city so there isn't a ton of noise. It's also righy by the bus stop so we just walked to it everyday and rode the bus and train using a helpful app. It was just a hair colder than I'm used to but I'm from Cali 🤣 bring some long pjs in the winter and you'll be just fine to sleep comfortably plus there's lots of extra stuff to use, especially if you forgot anything. Denise also answered all of my questions and provided nice accomodations and was very flexible with us checking out since our flight got delayed the morning of. It is a nice space, we couldn't figure out how to close the front curtains? But it was fine because we stayed in the room anyways 🙂 also, if you plan to use the jet tub remember to use the rule of thumb and run it a few times first to clean it out, that was our bad. Overall, super comfy, very good price, very quiet, convenient, and don't be afraid to ask questions because she has answers! We had a great time, felt like home.

I booked this place for a summer internship. The room is amazing and just like the pictures. Huge, plenty of light. Good sized closet. Comfortable bed and couch. Nice desk. The AC is weirdly placed in the room so it does get hot in the summers and if you have people over. If you leave food out in your room, you will get rats. Don’t leave food out.  However, I didn’t really know I would be sharing the apartment with 2 other Airbnb tenants. There is only 1 bathroom with no vent, so smell and heat stays in there unless you leave the door open.   One time, the toilet clogged and overflowed. Apollo was quick about bringing over a plumber. However, he kept asking me if I had flushed feminine products down the toilet, and like…. no. I did not. He claimed management found feminine products in the sewage system, which doesn’t really make sense because the building sewage is all connected. So how can someone pinpoint it on me?   Because the toilet overflowed, the downstairs neighbors wrote us a note and demanded we paid them because their bathrooms flooded too. Just ancient building things.   Kitchen is small and when I came in, didn’t even have a microwave. I had to ask Apollo to order us one. I also think there’s one fork in the entire kitchen.   The address was also different from when I booked it to when I checked in by a couple blocks. Not a huge deal though.   4th floor walk up, so get ready for cardio everyday. I got used to it within 2 weeks.   Location is good and bad. If you’re a young attractive woman, the LES is not the best area to be in, especially at night. I was harassed multiple times by men on the streets. However, it is very conveniently located to good restaurants and bars. But do I think that’s prioritized over safety? No.   A laundromat is right around the block, but it’s expensive obviously and you have to bring your own detergent, which is really dumb.   Let’s get into the bad. The host is having legal issues with the landlord, so we were served 2-3 eviction notices in my time. The host kept trying to convince us that it’s fine and he has a lawyer on it, which might be true. But it was extremely stressful to have to deal with. The super downstairs, who works for the landlord, constantly harassed me and my visitors verbally as we were entering. He tried to physically stop me from entering the building too. One of my roommates checked out early because she couldn’t handle it. Apollo asked if my statements could be used in the legal case with his landlord, but the last thing I want is to be involved in a legal case. Also, Airbnb Support will not help you because Apollo has convinced them that it’s going to be okay.   Building management changed the locks 2-3 times in my stay, so we had to struggle to get new keys. Oh yeah, there was also a robbery in the building recently. Fun.   Overall, I had an okay time. The apartment is cozy and comfortable but I dealt with a slew of other issues that was stressful and should not have been issues in the first place. Apollo is usually nice and responds pretty quickly. This wouldn’t be my first choice place to stay, but I guess it was a good NYC experience.
Very good dangerous area at night

I was a little bit worried to book a room in the Bronx from all the Media Attention they got decades ago. This was completely unnecessary because i never felt unsafe in the Area even when i got home from a party in the middle of the Night!  The Room is small but it's more than enough to sleep and be comfortable! The Room was completely Clean, the Bathroom aswell. I didn't used the Kitchen but it seemed like they had everything someone could need.  They don't have a Washing Machine or a dryer because a laundromat is only about 0,1mi or 200 meters away.  Overall i had a great stay, i would recommend this to everyone who has more than a few days in New York. The Subway Connection is great btw. Only 45minutes to Grand Central!

Despite the bad fame of this place, I personally (as a solo female traveler) didn't feel unsafe even for a second. To be honest, I liked the neighborhood. Almost every day I came back past 11pm and no strangers bothered me, everyone was nice and helpful, so I don't know... I don't complain about the location. The room itself was nice. Cozy, with a comfy bed and a lot of tools to organize your things. The only detail that made me a little bit annoyed was the construction work that was happening through at least three days right next to my window, which I couldn't close due to the AC machine. Maybe it's good? Otherwise I wouldn't like to leave that perfect bedroom... Some places are shared, but I never saw other guests. Host was kind and hospitable and I also made a friend from the next door (the only guest I actually saw) with who I spent some crazy days in NYC. To sum up - I highly recommend Fazia's place. Close to the shops, subway or buses, very well air-conditioned.

A beautiful space, Nir and Ari were friendly, the apartment was super clean and they were helpful with local places to eat (all delicious!). It was a perfect place to feel safe and clean during the pandemic and get away from daily life without feeling unsafe. Such a beautiful space and fun area to explore!

We had a good stay in Brooklyn Comfortable apartment: - Good bedding - Pleasant living room - Spacious kitchen Apartment well located 10 minutes walk from two subway lines to Manhattan and Lincoln Market (very good). The neighborhood is lively and pleasant. No feeling of insecurity even in the evening. The apartment is clean (small insects in the bathroom in the evening probably due to the humidity but really nothing to worry about).  Good communication with our host. Recommended if you come to NY.

Apartment is super clean and the bed is awesome. Owner is very communicative and instructions are easy to follow. It was very well thought out…there was even had an extra hdmi cable connected to the TV.   Apartment is very near multiple subway lines which is great, but some travelers may need to be careful in certain surrounding areas. For example, Franklin and Eastern Parkway is a little sketchy, so be careful, use common sense and exercise good judgement.

One of our favorite AirBnbs we have ever stayed at! Olga's place is clean and is conveniently close to a subway station. She and her family were excellent hosts -- personable, respectful, and great to visit with. We found parking pretty easily -- it's still NYC so you'll have to circle and walk but it worked out for us. Also, don't let the mention of pets scare you off -- I have cat allergies and I wasn't sniffly at all. Her pets are super well trained and Olga keeps the place very clean.

We had a nice stay at Olga's place. Yes, the place is close to Central park, but It's very close to Harlem, which felt a bit dangerous when returning back to the Air bnb at night. Pilows were a bit too flat, making it hard for a good sleep. Shared bathroom is clean, and the room is also clean.  Check in was super easy, Olga's daughter just buzzed us in and gave us keys afterwards. There's a AC unit in the room, so it was nice and comfortable for our stay in September. They do have a small dog and a cat, so make sure you aren't allergic.

Everything was great, room and bathroom clean, perfect contact with Olga and the girls, everyone is very nice.  Only a minute to the subway and 15 minutes to lower manhattan location, we were not afraid to come back at night.  There are very cute animals in the house, if you want to pet them they are very willing, but if not, okay too. When we come back to New York we will be happy to stay here again :)

what a lovely short stay in chinatown! egor’s place is so cute and homey, the decorations are a beautiful touch! plus, there are a lot of restaurants near by! the subway is only a 10 minute (maybe?) walk which was super great. i really want to emphasize how safe i felt! it ended up being only me staying this time, which i was nervous for because i haven’t been to the city alone, but there wasn’t a second that i felt unsafe in this area!   thank you so much, egor! i will definitely be back!

We just returned home from staying at this AirBNB and everything was just as the owner said it was.  Her description is detailed and accurate. Our biggest worry was that the area wouldn’t be safe, seeing that we planned on walking a few miles each night.  The owner told me how safe it was but we were still concerned. We walked during the day and night and never had the feeling of being unsafe and we walked about 16 miles in a two mile radius of the Airbnb.    If we head back to NYC we will be booking this AirBNB again! Thanks Sophia!!!  Also, we really enjoyed talking to the young man who builds the bikes in the garage. He was very friendly and my wife is into biking and really enjoyed the conversation!!!

Horrible experience.  We paid $179 for a hotel with a base price of $119 plus fees.  I paid $179 through the app, then was asked to pay the fees again when I arrived at hotel.  They had no booking on file for us despite the fact I called to make sure they got the reservation and to request a handicap room.  Charged us $42 more at the door and then another $159 when we left, all for ONE NIGHT.  $159 was refunded but I had to argue and show my receipt.  Handicap accessibility is a joke - avoid this place if you are wheelchair bound.  They gave us a handicap room on the 8th floor, so we had to traverse narrow halls and a tiny elevator to get there.  Got stuck a few times but we made it out alive.  Very stressful stay; will not be returning.

She basically scammed me I never stayed with her because she couldn’t accommodate me. She told me that the there was a problem with the check in time and that I would have to have to check in at 10 pm. I couldn’t do this because my event for the evening started at 10 pm. Airbnb policy says that if the host can’t accommodate you ask them to cancel it. Which I did, however the host lied and never canceled the reservation so I was charged $205.41 I’m currently going back n forth on the phone with Airbnb trying to get my money back.

We had a great stay at Louis's place. There were 4 of us women and we stayed very comfortably. We were very glad there were 2 restrooms because that is unusual in the area, especially for the price. Louis was always available if we needed anything. Each room has their own A/C and the living room/kitchen are also had one. I know that's important in that area. There was usually someone working at the front entrance, kinda like security. It was comforting since there were 2 other units in this house and the area isn't the best. We never felt uncomfortable, but it was a little sketchy at night since we were only women.  It was about a 10 min walk to the subway. There are a few bodegas (corner stores) in the area and one restaurant/bar at the corner. Overall, we're glad we stayed there.

My stay at Lu's place was wonderful! Not only is the location great and the subway very close (that takes you to Times Square and all the stuff) but also Lu as a person and host was just amazing!  She did everything she could to make the stay as convenient as possible and was very helpful.  Internet is blazing fast and the room very nice, too. (also had a desk)  All in all, 10/10, couldn't imagine a better AirBnB and host to stay in Manhattan.  Thank you Lu!  PS. I didn't see Lu too often because she was either working, out or even handing underwear to homeless people (I mean wow!!). Never had such a great host!
Nothing bad to say. Good, simple, and stress free!

I wasn’t sure about a shared room via Airbnb having never done it before, but I had such a great experience I definitely will again! Nicole’s home was clean, quiet, spacious and very comfortable. She was a kind and thoughtful host and overall, my stay was a little oasis during a stressful week. Highly recommend and would defiantly book again!
Unsafe

Let me begin by saying that the co-host was very nice, gracious and friendly. However, a major hiccup/problem is that all of the guest rooms have door handles that only lock from the inside. The outside handle, has no keyhole slot. So, as you can tell where this is going, I accidently locked myself out; apt keys, wallet, cellphone…everything was in my room. Knocked on co-host’s room, no answer. Upstairs guest, who wouldn’t come out of her room told me she would text the co-host. With no response or follow thru, I sat for 30mins. Finally knocked on downstairs guest, who was across from my room and very gracious and helpful, attempted to call co-host twice. No answer. She finally helped me shimmy one of her own credit cards in between the lock and threshold to jerry it open. Entire situation took all of 45mins. Mind you, no call back from co-host, no follow thru at all. Despite having two of her other guests attempt to get a hold of her. Door was left intact, no damage. Not sure what the co-host would have done even if she had shown up, because there is no physical key to use. Other than that, room is very well kept, neat, but basic. No TV, furniture is very cheap, new, but not quality. No real common area (apt lay out is odd, it’s on the 1st floor of a walkup –no elevator for you who are unfamiliar with NYC apartment buildings- with two guest bedrooms downstairs, which is technically the basement of the building and one bedroom upstairs.
