Not much natural light, its mostly dark as there are not many windows). The half bath downstairs, when you place facet on cold, makes loud thudding noise, when I approached co-host about it, she said, “oh. That’s normal”. Ok?? So, to avoid waking the guest next door at 5:45am (time I had to get up to leave for work), I had to set it on hot. In short, if you’re out & about and don’t care much for where you sleep. Fine. This place works, its 2 blocks away from A & C trains and Central Park is basically at your doorstep. I never felt unsafe, however, not being able to secure my belongings when I left for the day was a bit unnerving.

Place was overall okay. Convenient location with the C subway train a couple blocks down, and Central Park is super close. Clean & quiet. But there are a number of things that we found to be a bit unpleasant (some of which have been mentioned by others):   1 - The loud noises from the drainage system coming through the walls were unbearable at times, and it made it very difficult to sleep, and we woke up a lot at night.   2 - The bathroom door downstairs gets jammed, and it can be difficult to open/lock at times. Also, the sink gets clogged easily / doesn’t drain quickly.   3 - Very thin walls, which we didn’t expect.   4 - We couldn’t get the thermostat to work for some reason. We tried adjusting it a bunch of times, but it stayed at the same temperature throughout then night when we were sleeping.   Not sure if what I described above is considered normal in the upper west side. The lack of sleep throughout our stay was a huge problem.

Esther made my trip to NY very welcoming and easy. The key was left for me with clear instructions, the room was spacious and the bed comfy. It is a basement room with a little window down a breezeway- it felt a bit like being in a hold of ship but I was expecting that and it was so close to the park and the subway that I didn’t need it to be anything more than a place to sleep. I didn’t realize the light could be dimmed until I was turning it off- so, there is a good bright light and nice soft lighting. The hosts were gracious and timely in their communication. It made traveling cross country less stressful and I appreciate that. It is not a spot that I would hang out during the day, but it felt safe and clean and a perfect place to land for the night.

The stay was as expected, with a good location. We had a few issues with the key to gain access into the building as it didn’t always work. There could have been more basic essential items in the flat, such as sugar. The manner in which we were treated after our check out, although an apology was eventually given, was unacceptable. Accusing your guests of stealing without conducting a thorough (although the comforter was left in a logical place) check around the property was rude and disrespectful, and the threats during these exchanges were uncalled for. Please consider this in future dealings.

Wonderful experience. It was a bit of a culture shock because that location is very busy and very diverse. It is in the process of gentrification as well so that adds to the business of the community. With that being said there is so much to do at that location. However, the only downside as a vehicle owner, it is extremely stressful to find parking; other than that the location is ideal for train, bus or taxi travel. Chris&Suly's was very responsive and very flexible; response time was within minutes. Instructions to get access to the apartment was very easy. Entry through the lobby door requires some patience (but that's a building management issue.) The apartment was good for my stay. The bed was extremely comfortable.

Ian is a good host and very responsive when we had requests so I am sad to have to leave a negative review but this apartment is absolutely not suitable for a stay for any longer than a few nights, particularly at that price.  On a positive note, the bed is comfortable and the place is quiet at night. The apartment itself was quite clean and the shower was great.   The neighbourhood is excellent and the apartment is very well located in terms of transport and restaurants etc. but it is on a less desirable block next to a homeless shelter in a very old building that isn't well maintained. I feel like it is genuinely close to being condemned. There was a murder in the homeless shelter during our stay and I would not stay here with children.  Other not so positive points to be aware of:  1. There is a building being erected next door which means construction 5 days a week 7am until 7pm. It is incredibly loud, drilling and banging all day. The new building has now blocked any natural light the apartment used to have.  2. The steam heating system means the apartment is literally roasting hot all the time in Fall and winter and the temperature cannot be controlled.   3. The apartment does not sleep 4 people. It sleeps 3 people at a push. We ended up buying an air bed for when guests stayed over which we left in the property as the "sofa bed" is totally inadequate.   4. A number of items were initially missing such as iron and bed linen for the sofa. To be fair Ian ordered these for us fairly quickly when we asked for them.  5. We had a severe mosquito problem in the apartment from August through to October. There were no attempts to help with this. We could barely sleep at the height of the problem and were killing c.10 each night. There were occasionally other pests too but I do appreciate this is a NYC issue and Ian did offer assistance if the issue got worse which thankfully it didnt.  6. We had to collect the keys from a building in Gramercy which increased our cab fare by around $20 which is unacceptable.   7. The building itself isn't great - it isn't cleaned so feels grubby and smelly.    In summary, we stayed here as we didnt have many other options and were working so didn't have to spend much time here. I wouldn't stay here again or recommend it other than for a few nights and purely because of the location and quiet night sleep. I wouldn't recommend for longer term.

I had great time in christina plce! It was cozy and cool. When i read the review  that some times noise there. And i figure out when i get there. But i was ready for my earplug. So i dont get about  that stress when i sleep.

When the host takes time with the little things, you know that they really want to make your stay as enjoyable as possible.  A well-stocked kitchen with coffee, tea and sweeteners, very clean rooms, mints on the beds, notebook with tips and ideas on visiting the city (we used it and it was very helpful), extra towels and blankets, umbrellas, soap, etc.  Kerri thought of everything!  Umbrellas?  I have never stayed at a place that had umbrellas.  Her job as host began as soon as we made our reservation.  She immediately contacted us to find out our plans.  She contacted us several times up to the time of our arrival.  I really appreciated the messages because it relieved a lot of stress and worry about the trip and she also gave us lots of tips.  She was very accessible during the visit to response to any issues.  I have to say Kerri is as close to the "Perfect Host" as one can get.  I highly recommend Kerri as a host because I think she really cares about your stay.  I recommend this lodging because it is in a great location, a very nice apartment, and because it is hosted by Kerri.

If, like me, you are looking to the comments to know if Karla’s place is the one you need, stop looking: you got the perfect AirBnb!  I staid at Karla’s place for a whole semester while studying at NYU and what I can say is that it was even better than in pictures: enough place to store everything, a lot of natural light, a view on the garden, a functional kitchen, and  the bed is literally softer than any hotel I staid in.  Everything you need is here, it is like being home. Karla is the loveliest host, very reactive by texts, and anticipated all little needs in this apartment.  The subway (with both local and express lines) let you reach Manhattan easily and smoothly, the big supermarket close to the place is more than convenient and neighbors are discreet!  The comment section is not big enough to explain how everything makes this place a perfect choice! To make a long story short: it can be « scary » to rent a AirBnb in a city you don’t know but here know this is the best option!

Diana's apartment is excellent. It's greatly located and actually really near everything if you are planning to walk the city and want to know it all. The pictures are really accurate and everything was as we expected. There some minor things that can be improved to be even greater, like for example an extra stool if you are renting the apartment for more than 2 persons, the same with having some extra blankets or if you are in need to use the couch for sleeping, improving the mattress. The rest is really impressive; I recommend to rent this apartment. There is one thing though that I would like to mention, please beware with the stairs, they are actually to steep and they can be dangerous. If you are not afraid of them or you take really care in going up and down don't doubt in renting this property.

BUYER BEWARE!!! As a disclosure, I do not blame the host for what happened during my stay but instead, how she responded.   For background- I'm a medical school student who spent 14-16 hour days at the hospital with little time at home. The time I spent at home was extremely valuable as I showered, ate, and went to bed immediately at the end of everyday. I was doing a sub-internship at the hospital and needed to stay close by for approximately 1 month. Although the price for this apartment was outrageous, the listing was advertised as a clean, safe full apartment.  WEEK 1 When I first arrived to the airbnb, the location felt a bit sketchy with a lot of guys on the street doing nothing and watching people. However, walking into the airbnb felt like a breath of fresh air- the decorations were perfect, the bed was soft and superb, and the kitchen afforded me a space to work outside of the hospital. I was surprised though that for the steep price, there was no microwave anywhere in the apartment.  Approximately 4 days into my stay, I found a huge cockroach in my bathroom. I immediately notified the host and she informed me that since I couldn't be home to let the exterminator in (i was away at the hospital from morning until night), she'd have a friend stop by in a few days. Unfortunately the friend couldn't find the cockroach. Fast forward to 6-7 days later and I began finding cockroaches all over the apartment- anytime I opened a cabinet there would be 2-3 jutting away. I would say there was at least >20 cockroaches at this point.   WEEK 2 I was at a point where I barricaded myself into the bedroom because I was afraid to go into the bathroom and the kitchen. There were cockroaches everywhere in the apartment anytime I woke up and came home. I was begging the host to bring in the exterminator or I would leave the apartment. The host was responsive and sympathetic with my situation. However, the host couldn't get the exterminator into the apartment until the weekend of week 2 (Primarily because people she was counting never showed up- not her fault).  WEEK 3 Despite the exterminator coming, I continued to find cockroaches on my ceiling, under my hair brush, next to the toilet, in my cabinets, on the walls, and eventually in my bedroom. I felt like I've finally had enough- I was barely in the apartment and the times that I were, I was scared. It was at this time that I asked the host if I could leave a week early due to the inhabitable conditions to which point SHE REFUSED ANY REFUND!!! Once again, I understand it's the summer and cockroaches may come and go, but as a host, she responded inappropriately and refused to refund the last week of my stay despite a cockroach infestation. In order to FINALLY get a refund, I put in a personal request to the host twice (to which she refused) and report these conditions to 2 separate airbnb support members. The first airbnb support member worked with the host and she agreed to refund me a whopping $200 (22% of what a full week cost). I found this completely insulting and sought a second airbnb support member of which he was able to refund me the full amount of my final week stay.   IN SUMMARY The host refused to refund me for my last week airbnb stay despite having a full cockroach infestation. Her actions were completely inappropriate and demonstrates that she would rather keep the money than make sure her airbnb was livable. DO NOT I REPEAT DO NOT GO HERE!

About what you’d expect from an apartment in New York. The room is exactly as it is in the picture, quite spacey. Huge closet with a mini-fridge. The apartment is right next to the above ground subway tracks, not too audible from this room but I could still hear it (no problem sleeping). Slight molding in the full bathroom. Unpleasant odor in the apartment (not in the room) because of one of the guests who seemingly never showers : the stench coming from his apartment is quite repulsive. As I said, expected from a room in Bushwick, still very cheap for its location and I’d still say the price-quality ratio is good especially if you don’t mind it a bit rough and can split the room in two with your partner.

Very nice and cozy apartment - as shown in the pictures. Gaspar was always respondig to our questions fast and suggested us lockal places to visit. The apartment is definitely big enough for a couple or even 4 guests, the kitchen is fully equipped and the neighborhood gives you a representative feeling of Brooklyn. Underground station is just 5 minutes away and Manhattan around 30 minutes. The apartment was very clean, WiFi was very fast and all the appliances were working properly. Would definitely suggest this place to everybody who wants to get the feeling of "living in an NY apartment" and being away of the cities noise and stress.

Vas was incredibly helpful and put the effort in to making our experience the best it could be. The location was great as it didn't have as many people in comparison to other places in the city. It was very easy to get to everywhere we wanted to within half an hour and, although slightly weary about the distance from places like Manhattan, we ended up preferring it! The room was immaculate, all toiletries were provided, check in and out were stress free, and Vas was an incredible host. I would not hesitate to book a room with him again and you shouldn't either! Especially for the value, it was perfect.

We stayed with Andrea and Randy for 8 nights.  The check-in was flawless and Andrea is very responsive to text messages.  They were staying with family the night we arrived and Andrea texted me the code to the lockbox to get the keys.  She had made some last minute changes to the room (bed changed from a queen to a double).  I told her we really wanted a queen or larger and she allowed us to change rooms to the queen bed.  The apartment is small.  You enter the front door into a small work space with desk and a small kitchen immediately to the right.  The room we stayed in was in the front of the apartment immediately off the kitchen.  From the kitchen you go down a short hallway and the shared bathroom is to the left and the hosts room is at the end of the hallway.  The air conditioning are window units (bedrooms) and wall unit (hallway) between the bathroom and bedroom at the end of the hallway.  A TV is provided in the room with Netflix (no regular TV so I missed watching Tiger win his first tournament in 5 years...luckily I recorded it and saw it when I returned home).   Andrea has bread, bananas, grapes, OJ, eggs and coffee available for your to prepare every morning.  And, she offered to cook us pancakes on the weekend, but we already had plans for breakfast.  We did have the chance to run into  both Andrea and Randy throughout our stay and they are a lovely couple.  I felt they would do just about anything you requested within reason.  I wouldn't hesitate to stay with them again.  You do share the one bath in the apartment.  We prefer a private bath, but since you only share it with the hosts and not any other guests (it's only a two bedroom apartment) we thought we would give it a try.  As it turned out, the bathroom was ALWAYS available when we needed it.  And it was always clean with soap, shampoo and conditioner available.  We were out late most nights and slept in.  Although you can hear a few footsteps when they left for work...I never heard them talking and we were able to sleep in without any trouble.  The apartment is very quiet too.  The only noise is from outside since you are in the middle of Manhattan.  We kept the window open at night (we were there the last week of September) and you can hear talking, police and fire sirens, and cars (beeping) the hum of air conditioning units on the street and traffic.  I chose to wear earplugs, but my wife didn't .   A couple nights we used the window unit air conditioner which is fairly noisy.  I don't think I would want to visit NY in the middle of the summer.  The location of the apartment in the Upper Eastside is fantastic.  We always felt safe walking from the apartment to the subway.  The station at 86th and Lexington (4 min walk) and the one at 2nd Avenue and 85th (6 min walk) are both a short 3 blocks away.  We didn't see any homeless people or other scary people even at 2 am in the morning.  It's a very safe neighborhood!  The Met Museum and Central Park (8 min walk) are only 3 blocks away.  There are also plenty of stores (grocery and drugstores) bars and restaurants all a short walk away.  You don't need a car in Manhattan!  We had a wonderful visit with our son and his girlfriend who live 3 blocks away and her parents who live 3 blocks away.  So the location was perfect for us.  We can definitely recommend staying with Andrea and Randy.  We had a lovely time in Manhattan!

Laura's place is incredibly conveniently located--close to a couple of subway stops, and easy walking distance to lots of great cafes, restaurants and bars. The apartment is bigger than the pictures make it look, and completely lovely! Check in and check out were very easy and stress-free. Thanks Laura!

I can only recommend the apartment. It is about 5 minutes from the subway station and even as a woman I did not feel unsafe at night. The apartment is very bright and big, the bed is comfortable and the kitchen has everything you need. But if you are a light sleeper you might be disturbed by outside noises or the fridge that keeps turning on from time to time. The hosts help with every problem, answer very fast and are always friendly.

Kerri is a great host, responsive and helpful.  Location: About 10 min walk to Times Square/ theater district. Several subway stations, including Penn Station, within 10 min walk.  Felt safe walking to and from unit, although you will come across groups of sketchy people, smell and maybe be offered weed, see an occasional passed out druggie. Pretty standard for areas that are on outskirts of tourist areas. We were ok with our teenage daughters walking to Times Square without us, but would not allow that at night.  There are so-so food options in the surrounding couple of blocks, and a couple good ones, but we opted to subway to selected restaurants for dinners. Nice coffee shop right across the street.  The unit itself is an older apartment but well kept and clean.   Bathroom was well stocked with soap, shampoo, extra TP, hair dryer. Shower has decent water pressure.   Nice little kitchen with everything you may need if you want to prepare some meals. Ironing board and iron as well. Nice TV and air conditioning.   The main bed is a plus or minus depending on preference:  mattress and pillows are SUPER soft.  There are dressers to unpack your clothes if staying a while.  I appreciated that there is a nightlight for navigating the space when waking up at night. Also it was nice that there is a small portable fan for the second bedroom. Also nice that there are a couple keys for the door to the building.  Something to consider is noise. Most places in NYC will have some traffic noise but this particular intersection is the loudest I have ever experienced. The horn honking was incredibly aggressive and persistent, and goes late into the night. Your tolerance may vary. Keri was kind to put packaged ear plugs by the bed.  All in all, we had a good trip and thankful for a good host like Kerri who made the whole process easy.
This place was beautiful! And Rob was an amazing host. I’m more than pleased.

We booked Stacy home last minute after our original Airbnb booking I t he same area was cancelled upon our arrival because the key was "stolen" and the host is a world Traveller so no one was on site to help us. After arguing back and forth with Airbnb on the phone for 5 hours and missing my bestfriend's rehearsal dinner, we had to spend a night in a hotel and booked this home last minute. The host fro. The moment we booked was responsive and understanding of our situation. We were so relieved when we got to finally put our bags down. The host is on site so if there is any issues they can assist you. Now that we went through a situation where the host is no where to be found we realize how valuable that is. Her home is a basement apartment , very traditional New York. It's warm and inviting. There is no kitchen but a fridge to stretch your snacks. The place was clean and ready for us consider the quick turn around. The location is perfect for Queens, you are in the thick of it. Please be aware they are a family living above you and as such you can hear the going abouts but not an issue for us as we were happy to have a place to stay last minute. Would stay again.

This was our second stay at Robert’s home. The first stay was far beyond our expectations this time our experience wasn’t the same. His amenities and house rules were conflicting with his home description. It says there are pots, pans and stove for guest to prepare their own meals however there is actually no cooking allowed. Only a microwave.   I also got locked into the home from the inside I had to contact the host to open the door in which he accidentally locked in order to leave the premises. This to us was very unsafe as there is only one accessible exit. Thankfully he was there and there wasn’t an emergency.   Unit was also very cold he did turn up the heat when we called however it seems as though it was turned back down or off at night as we were literally freezing. We honestly did bother to even message him at night as we felt after one communication this should have to been considered at night when the temperature drops.   He definitely communicated very promptly within a few minutes, accommodated an early check in which we appreciated after an early flight in. His place is a really beautiful and CLEAN. Unfortunately, we won’t consider this place for future stays.
this room is such a steal in a vibrant neighborhood with its own rooftop. Renato was very friendly and helpful, I would definitely stay again

I’ve never stayed at an Airbnb with a private room before as I was always afraid of not having privacy or staying in a home alone with a male, but this place was great. Vic lives with his fiancé, so you are not alone. The upstairs is sectioned off from the hosts bedroom downstairs by a door, so the whole upstairs is for yourself and the other private room available for booking. It’s like staying at a hotel, they have great amenities and are so hospitable. We had issues getting in touch with the hosts via the number on Airbnb, but that was our only real issue with our experience here. Great place!

The flat was extremely dirty, I suspect bathrooms and kitchen had never been cleaned considering how difficult it has been taking off all those dark and greasy stains. One of the two bathtubs was totally impracticable. We spent the first night cleaning the bathrooms (after 12 hours traveling), the day after I asked the owner to bring at least a vacuum cleaner and she replied that the house had been previously cleaned but if this didn't match my expectations she had no problems dropping a hoover to let me (she did, a wireless hoover with no charge, so I actually could use it only few minutes). The apartment is far from the subway (15-20 minutes walking), although the announcement stated it was 2 blocks away. The check-out was another problem because the owner not only denied a late check-out, but also the chance to leave luggage somewhere and our flight was at night, so we had to buy a short stay in a hotel... I hope this review will help to set matters right otherwise, if you plan to book this flat, don't forget to bring gloves and sanitizing with you!

Entrance door of the apartment very fragile and without security lock, makes the house completely unsafe to stay.  How can someone rent a house without security ????  Rooms were not clean, the whole floor of the house was dirty.  House very rundown, bedroom doors hinged on hinges, windows spoiled, bathrooms very old and spoiled, faucet spoiled, always running water.  Bad experience.

Our stay was wonderful. Before our arrival, Olivia was in contact, guiding us along the way to welcome us and she did so in a very warm manner. The apartment is even prettier than the photos show, impeccable and provided with everything you need and more as it is full of details to make your stay perfect. The bed is very comfortable, with adequate air conditioning at high temperatures, the bathroom is spacious and has a very good shower. It is 350 meters from the subway, which is very comfortable to get around and we did not find it unsafe. We would definitely return to this apartment.

Melissa did a great job in terms of checking in on us and making sure we had everything we needed to ensure our stay was wonderful - and it was! The apartment was sparklingly clean, the bathroom was renovated and modern, and there was more than enough space for myself and my friend. The location was great, within a ten minute walk from Central Park and the MET and only a 20-30 minute train ride (no transfer) to lower Manhattan, where there was more nightlife. It was affordable and close to bars/night life scene without feeling unsafe late at night. There was also a great Mexican restaurant right across the street with a nice BOGO for happy hour - a must for anyone staying in this apartment! I'll definitely be booking with Melissa next time I'm in town!

I ended up booking this room last minute after some friends I was traveling with had to cancel… and I’m glad I did! This spot is so cute, so convenient, and so comfortable. And an absolute steal. If you’re considering getting a room in a different AirBNB, don’t. Get a room here. It will feel so much better than crashing in someone’s spare room. The Beverley feels like a home, and I will definitely be back the next time I’m in NYC.

My wife and I came to NYC for our honeymoon. It was the first time either of us had been to New York and also the first time we’d stayed at an AirBnB place, but Milton made things incredibly smooth and stress free. The suite is gorgeous and about a 7 min walk from the train station, giving easy access to Manhattan and a nice place to come home to. Milton’s a thoughtful guy and was really accommodating to our needs over the week we stayed with him. Would stay there again without any hesitation.

The place is decorated in a very upscale fashion. The upgrades are magnificent to say the least. Everything is brand new and fresh. Expensive wood planks on the floor round off this glamorous setting.   Karilyn went out of her way to make us feel like friends. She delivered us chocolate bread , bagels and lots of things. She even brought down a Buddha statue for my friend to meditate with.   Appliances are too pricey to be in common areas of an Airbnb- hostess seemed anxious about the use of “the machines “  I enjoy staying at Airbnb’s for the homey feeling I get while away from family. It is important for me to feel as comfortable as I can be away from home. Here the apartment had a Do Not Touch feel.   It was more of a shared room Environment- door rings followed by barking dog when you come in, lights go on automatically and take a while to go off-Or else you can climb up the stairs and turn them off. After a long day visiting New York City climbing a staircase to turn the light off it’s not something you want to bother with.  The fans hang too low, at least for me at 6ft Tall.   Toilet paper was rough-bring your own  Water bottles would be a nice touch   Need knives in kitchen  White towels not a good idea. Guest feel embarrassed about making them another color for whatever reason   Overall- a beautiful place that looks really nice however I did not feel I was welcome to enjoy any of the homey touches. The host is overly concerned about everything in the apartment. I was afraid to totally relax. I worried about the place my entire stay.

This is a really nice 1BR apartment that has been recently renovated. Everything is in fantastic shape. The apartment is on the basement level of the owner's house, so he is right nearby if needed. The street is super quiet, as is the apartment. You might hear the upstairs residents walking around, or the occasional tick and hiss from the radiators, but neither are bothersome. The apartment has all of the basics and then some (e.g., some assorted spices) and came with ample breakfast fixings. The neighborhood is definitely not the high-rent district, but we never felt unsafe. There is a small grocery less than a block away, and a large, very nice grocery about five blocks away, along with a drugstore and some small restaurants. The nearest subway (#2 line) is about six blocks away. I'm sure there is bus service nearby, but we just walked to everything - it's about a mile and a half to the botanical gardens (mostly via some nice park trails), and about the same distance to the zoo. We brought our car, so we definitely appreciated the availability of off-street parking. Milton was extremely responsive to any questions we had. Checkin and checkout were a breeze. This was a great and reasonably priced base camp for exploring the Bronx and Manhattan.

After initially leaving a kind review for my stay here and letting bygones be bygones, I just received a $200 request from her to repair chipped paint on a radiator that was behind the bed that we did not touch and for some coffee grounds (and a coffee stain from her leaky coffee pot) being left on the table intended for eating. Here is my real opinion on this airbnb: When we first arrived, we were excited because the place was clean and well furnished. She provided lots of food and thoughtful amenities and I thank her for that. However, that great impression quickly faded away. The first red flag was all of the rules. You were only allowed to eat on one table in the house (understandable), you were not allowed to be barefoot in the space, you could not put anything on the dresser beside the bed (including glasses), and several others that made me feel uncomfortable being in the space being afraid that I may break one of her many rules. Next, as a 7 foot tall man, the fact that she didn't list the ceilings being exactly 7 feet tall and the ceiling fans hitting me in the chest really made my trip a bear. Getting up at night to use the restroom lead to me hitting my head 6 to 7 times every time I moved through the house. I spent the entire time in the space hunched over only escaping that when we laid on the bed which was incredibly uncomfortable. It was a queen size air mattress that slanted to one side which lead to me falling off the bed several times a night. The bed coupled with the low ceilings led to me having pretty significant back pain for the whole trip. I realize most of that can be looked past if you are not my height, but there is more. The biggest element that made the space feel uncomfortable is the fact that the host was constantly coming into the space. We got calls about men needing to install window alarms while we were staying there so we hid out in our room while that happened. Later that same day, the host let me know she was going to use the washer in the kitchen of the space while we were gone which was fine, but she proceeded to open the door to the  bedroom we were staying in and take the sheets off of one of the two beds we were actively using in order to prep for the next person (this was halfway through our four day stay!!!); in the process of stripping the sheets, she moved several of our belongings (including my girlfriend's underwear) which is a complete invasion of privacy and made my girlfriend and me incredibly uncomfortable. I would not recommend staying here unless you are ok with the host being in the space daily, if not more than once daily, can sleep comfortably on the twin bed next to the air bed, and can somehow avoid making any sort of mess at all.

Karilyn has a very beautiful cellar apartement, with no windows to open, perfectly clean with a brand new kitchen. Splendid indeed ! But if you intend to enjoy it, forget it ! It is for no use. No cooking at all. We were very disappointed, since rented a whole apartement for precisely having some home meals, maybe just some eggs for breakfast. You can grill bread, use a tiny 1 person coffee machine, the micro wave and the plastic cutlery.  ( I bought some decent for 2 and left it for the next guest ) Read carefully "details"  At the arrival we were asked to take off our shoes, and not to walk barefood, to wear socks. Beautiful floor indeed !  We were right away not comfortable, afraid to touch anything. The train Grant City St. 3 minutes away, and about 40 minutes to the free Staten Island Ferry to Battery Parc Manhattan that goes every 30 min 24/24. Taxi is 20 minutes for around $ 18.  I really just hope, that we succeed to leave everything just as we found it. Thank you.

Loved staying in this little apartment. It is super conveniently located with subway access and a coffee shop right across the street. Easy to find street parking. Made it to Manhattan every day within a half hour. Hosts checked in on us throughout the week and were always kind and available if we needed anything. Area is a little sketchy at night but not horrible. Super great for the price. Would definitely stay again!

I’ve been booking Airbnb’s for about 4 years now. I pretty much travel all over the country and I don’t think I’ve ever once complained about a location. First the location is really cool, and it’s literally next to Chinatown, which is a plus for food. There a few things I wanted to address about his location... I completely understand that’s it’s NYC and everything will never look modern from the outdoors... but his location was literally in the basement. The entrance is so sketchy. The the apartment is basically dark the entire stay, and it didn’t make it feel like it’s was home. The place really needs a good wipe down, all the floors were dirty, all the dressers were dusty to a point it made my eyes irritated. The microwave wasn’t connected, I had to push the refrigerator 3 ft forward to connect to connect the plug since the microwave was on top of the frig. At night time the people that lived upstairs were super noisy, barely slept the first night and the hot water takes 10-15mins to get hot to take a shower or wash your hands. The bedroom windows don’t have curtains, so when you turn on the light in the room people can see you from the outside. That was definitely not private for my girlfriend to change her clothing, since the bathroom is only 2ft x 4ft. Sorry Dan, it was one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had at a Airbnb that I paid a good about to stay at. Somehow, I’m going to contact Airbnb to get a refund or some sort.   Angel

We got off to a slightly rocky start! Karilyn told us to text her 30 minutes before arrival. I wasn’t sure how long it would take to get through airport security and travel to her place so I just said it’d be late. We werent told there was a cut-off check in time and after we had a nightmare trying to get to Karilyn’s we received a text from her at around 1am saying it was too late to check in and we’d have to wait until the next day. We hadn’t contacted her yet as we were still about an hour away. We then spent a very stressful hour still making our way to her place, worrying we’d have to sleep outside in an unfamiliar place, after being awake for over 24 hours travelling! Luckily Karilyn did meet us there to let us in and we’re very grateful for that, especially considering it was 2am! We appreciate that it was very late and we never expected to arrive as late as that!  After that Karilyn was very helpful and accommodating. She gave us some food and there were things in the fridge we could use. Her place is lovely!! The photos don’t even do it justice! We had the place to ourselves and there is your own private entrance so you can come and go as you please. It’s in a lovely and quiet area right next to a 711 and the train station. You can hop on a train for around 20 minutes which takes you to the ferry and then a half hour ferry over to Manhattan.  I would say the downsides were we spent a lot of time each day travelling around to get to where we wanted as it was out of the way and sometimes there were no direct routes from Staten Island, the place is so nice and looked after that you worry about making a mess, as it’s connected to her house if you come back late you feel you have to sneak in so you don’t disturb anyone, and limitations on arrival time. Perhaps one of those key boxes could be used and guests arriving at inconvenient times could put a code in to get the key. But overall it is a really lovely place to stay and we enjoyed our time there, also it’s a lot more cost effective than staying in the city, and you get a lot of space for your money!

Good and cheap place to stay in NYC for a few days, subways 4 183th st), B, D (182-183th st) are really really close and it makes it easy to go spend the day in Manhattan and come back from different locations. The bedroom is enough spacious for 2 backpackers, and pretty clean even if you see the building is old. Neighborhood is OK. Mariela seems to be a nice person even if we didn't really had the chance to talk much. We were a bit afraid as we didn't had any news about arrival and check-in until when we arrive at JFK (2 hours before arriving at Mariela's place) but then she answered and her mother was there to welcome us so everything went well. We recommend Mariela's place !

Mariela was very helpful in her quick and precise responses. Though she was on travels herself when we arrived at her place, we were able to enter without a problem and everything was left ready for us at the bedroom. The bedroom itself, as advertised, is rather small, but it wasn't a concern for my boyfriend and I (the bed is very large, so it takes a lot of space). There was a closet and chest where we could store our clothes and belongings, a bedside table, and a window through which morning light came in, which was very nice. The place definitely surpassed our expectations, especially for the price. There was even a small TV with Netflix, Youtube, Amazon, etc. There are two bathrooms, one shower, which were all very clean. Mariela also left some shampoo, soap, towels, an iron, lotion (and other things) for us to use. Keep in mind that this is a shared Airbnb (a second room next to us was occupied during our stay). We didn't feel we particularly lacked privacy but it's something to keep in mind, though you are able to lock your bedroom door with a key. The kitchen had everything we would've needed, had we cooked, and was also very clean. The location of the place is also great, just a couple blocks from several subway lines, which allows you to get to Harlem and Manhattan pretty quickly. We walked throughout the neighborhood at night and felt no danger. I felt almost at home with all the Latin American people, shops, and bars around me. It's a very vibrant and popular neighborhood. We were very grateful to have found this place at such a good price and felt comfortable and could move easily anywhere at any time of day and night throughout our stay in New York. Thanks again Mariela! See you maybe in the future.

It was so much better than we expected, great place, great communication, very clean.  We arrived very late and had a problem with the check-in because other guests hadn’t left the key were they were supposed to, but Mariela was quick to help and soon we were inside the apartment.   Also, even though people say that Bronx is dangerous, we never felt scared, even when arriving after midnight(maybe that’s because we are from Brasil hehe). There were lots os markets and places to eat close by and subway stations We really recommend this place!   Thank you Mariela!

We came for 9 nights but only stayed 1 night. The accommodation is really very clean and secure but being 2 girls aged 18 and 19, we were worried about the neighborhood... It was not dangerous but at night we were not reassured (especially regarding the metro). We preferred to change for this reason. Despite everything, Mariela's mother (whose Airbnb is) is very kind, even if she speaks very little English she tries to answer our needs or questions! If you're not afraid of the distance on the metro and you want to experience less touristy New York, go for it!

I actually enjoyed my stay at this place. The positives : the room was clean, TV was great, the bed was very comfy. There were towels, blanket and other stuff available for use. The Mom that stays home is a nice lady. Bathrooms were clean and well stocked. Negatives were not the house itself. It was the neighborhood and I have to keep it real on this app. The neighborhood was sketchy. A lot of crime notifications came into my phone from real-time crime apps which spooked me out. The walk from D Train to home was scary. I got stuck in elevator between floors once. There’s no washer and dryer in the unit but there’s a laundromat in the building which I didn’t check out because the host said it takes 2 days to get a card after you pay for it. I didn’t find that necessary. Overall a homey clean and private space for a good price. I appreciate this stay!!!

Isaac is an amazing host. He was very kind and helpful, giving suggestions about where to go and what to do.  Everybody thinks the Bronx is a dangerous area but my friend and I walked back there very late at night and nothing happened. There are guys that say stuff though but do no harm. I guess it's normal. The room is very big and comfortable, just like the pictures. Everything is super clean. You can use the kitchen to make breakfast, lunch or dinner. The place is super comfortable.  I recommend it 100%. It's a little far from everything but the subway takes care of that. All in all, we had a great time!

Bathroom is outside of loft.  There's a closet  that smells like drugs peripherals.  There's one small window.  There's no in-house heating, only a portable heater.  There an "office" next door, so limited on privacy/ reasonable noise.

The host is willing but greater effort could be placed on details such as cleanliness. The house is a reasonable size for 6 - 8 guests and has all conveniences but it is aged and would be good if it was updated including appliances, flooring and furniture. The stairs are slanted which felt unsafe but it held up. This should be corrected for safety.  proximity to the subway was good even in -2 weather. There is a Dunkin Donuts and lots of shops nearby which was convenient.
Great clean space. Although it's on the 4th floor, It was really stressful taking my bags up and down the stairs. Good for short trips.

This is a great place for a large group! I stayed with my family and we had a lovely time in NYC. We visited the nearby cloisters and it was breathtaking, not to be missed. Bodegas and eateries close by. Really a lovely neighborhood, with the nearby church bells chiming :) we had plenty of towels and necessities. The beds are not hotel quality, but they did the job and we had plenty of space. Check in was easy and low stress. I’ll look back on this trip fondly!

We felt quite comfortable in Rhonda's small apartment. She was very welcoming and available at any time. Everything you needed was there. The location was ok, we didn't feel unsafe, but the walk or drive to Manhattan took about 45 minutes.

I stayed here in June 2019 in a group of 3. The check in and out was seamless with the keypad, making it a stress-free arrival. Bashiri and Ivy were very prompt in all responses. The apartment looked exactly as pictured, and was very comfortably sized for 3 people. It was nice having a common area to hang out as well as separate bedrooms, and there were some kitchen supplies available, helpful for eating takeout.  Everything was in good working order and clean. The neighborhood felt safe and fairly quiet. We would stay again.

Unfortunately for the hosts (and I do regret this incident), my family literally fled after finding out an infestation of bugs (we are still not sure what they were) had taken over the whole apartment. I made the check-in between 3-4pm, everything was okay, and by 12am, the four members of my family left the Airbnb as it was inhospitable. There were bugs all over: walls, floor, furniture, ceiling… Our hosts did their very best to repair this and refunded us immediately. I do appreciate their good disposition. But this incident truly threw my wedding weekend off. When I should’ve been resting for the big day, I was solving this for my out-of-town relatives for hours with the hosts, Airbnb and accommodating a family in NYC of all places at 2 am. We lost a lot of money trying to get a hotel nearby during Pride weekend and just made everything harder.  The apartment is in a nice area, bit old and some noticeable deterioration, however (ignoring the bugs) was clean. I thought a lot about posting this review because it seems that it was out of the host’s hands? I want to believe so. But I want to spare anyone from going through what we went through. In our case, it was involving one of the most important events of our lives and it added so so so much unnecessary stress.

Sophia's place was great. The location was a little walk from a subway station but not terrible. Across the street from a very fun bar. If you stay on Houston the neighborhood seems fine though it got a little sketchy if you went south a bit. Sophia was very responsive and checked in to make sure things were fine with the stay. Overall a great value for what you got.
It was the third floor, and the stairs are so high that it can be a little dangerous when you carry heavy loads.
The place is in a very good area, the subway is close and my family and I were able to walk without fear through the neighborhood at night and we felt safe. I recommend it 100%

The apartment was very nice and very close to the subway. You have everything that you need in the neighborhood and right next to the apartement you can even go and visit Prospect Park. It is important to note that on AirBnB you don't get a Hotel experience but to live in a place that is or once was a home. Of course small details are not what you would expect to see in a hotel, such as the shower head being slightly inconveniently placed or what not, but it came with everything that made you feel at home and at ease. All in all it was a great apartment to stay at.   What was especially nice that Lorna has stocked the shelfs with nice kitchen equipment such as salt, pepper, spices and the left over, non-perishable foods are to be left for the next tennants, so that there would be no waste. Recycling is also strongly recommended which we apreciated. The same goes for the bathroom where you have shampoo, conditioner, q-tips, desinfectant etc. Very convenient.  The only gripe I have with the apartment is the faucet in the kitchen. On the first day, the water wasn't running and Lorna told us to give it time, it will turn on after some time. It indeed did. A plumber was to be scheduled she said. Fast forward to the last day and me being tired, human error and Lorna not fixing the faucet in time, resulted in a minor flooding (after the Water stopped running while doing the dishes at night and I left the faucet open and it started running again early in the morning) of the apartment that leaked through the other floors. Due to that we had a very unpleasant day of check out that consisted of cleaning, apologizing to the other tennants and talking to AirBnB, worrying whether everything was going to be okay.   I am sure that Lorna has taken action by now and there should be now nothing wrong with the apartment at all, in which case I can 100% recommend for this place being a safe and smart alternative to a hotel room in Brooklyn. Here you can get the real Brooklyn experience. I also must add that communication went very smoothly throughout our week, especially during the mini-flooding, Lorna was very relaxed and handled the situation very well. Another big plus were the AC units in every room of the apartment that made 2 of the very hot nights very bearable. Apart from that the fan at the ceiling was more than enough to sleep through warmer nights.

The apartment was spotless and had everything we needed. The pictures gave a really good sense of what the apartment looked like and we had a great time staying there.   The area is up and coming and there are some really nice shops very close to the apartment: two big supermarkets, lots of smaller ones, laundromats and food shops. The apartment is a two minute walk from Prospect Park subway station, with trains directly into Manhattan. My family and I never felt unsafe walking around the area and people were very friendly but it did feel slightly different later at night.  There are three good-sized bedrooms: two at the back of the apartment and one at the front. The front bedroom was very noisy with noise from the road 24/7. It was difficult for me to sleep at all on the first night but, luckily, we had a teenager who slept in there for the rest of the trip with no problem.  I have stayed in many apartments and this really is one of the best I have stayed in.

Lorna is a welcoming person and very responsive when you send a message. As for the apartment, it was very clean when we arrived, it is large, ideal for a family. The neighborhood may seem unwelcoming at first, but our stay went very well, at no time did we feel unsafe, even late at night. Several small supermarkets nearby, with everything you need. Ideal neighborhood for exploring NYC, with a metro station 3 minutes' walk away, with lines to Manhattan. Easy return to JFK… I recommend 👍👍

Mitch is an excellent host, communication is very easy. In addition, she is very attentive.  The room is really very spacious and matches the photos perfectly. The “lounge” area with TV is very pleasant. Everything is very clean, new and functional. The metro is a 5-minute walk away in a neighborhood that is not scary.  It was a pleasure staying at Mitch's place. How lucky to have this accommodation to discover New York!

The communication with Garcia is excellent...a very responsive host...the area is fairly quiet with a supermarket and drug store not far from the place and the value of the rental is definitely worth it,and MOST importantly the place is VERY clean.

Wonderful location—close to Brouwer park, which is a lovely place to sit, especially in the summer as there is plenty of shade. The apartment looks exactly like the pictures, with beautiful decorations and plenty of space. Christopher and Nina are really responsive for any questions you have and they even left us a bottle of rosé!! Just a lovely apartment in a great place to be, with those extra little touches that make it feel really special.

Great place, well furnished and stocked, cool location in the Little Caribbean neighborhood.  Nice responsive host.  Perfect for our family vacation.  The only issue was that the keys were not in the lockbox when we arrived as the check in instructions had stated, but 10 minutes (and one mini heart attack since we had small kids and were worried about quickly finding a plan B if we could not get in) later Garcia had made arrangements with the cleaning lady to let us in.  Fortunately he did reply to our message immediately to fix the problem.  Other than that one brief stressful event it was a nice trip.
I had a great stay in Christopher & Nina’s spacious studio. It was well equipped and very comfortable. Subway only 2 blocks away. I traveled solo & never felt unsafe. I would stay here again.

The Beverley Social Club is a very charming and cozy home. It is a very old property with an interesting history. Our host was kind, responsive and very helpful. The details that she has worked on from a brochure giving you an overview of the house, to the organization, plus cleanliness of the home made the stay comfortable and inviting. I was personally afraid that I would feel as if I was Intruding into someone’s house but that is not how it felt at all,  the way that everything is set up makes the property feel like a cozy but also professional business that is being ran. Nothing short of what you would expect from a stay at a hotel (except that it doesn’t have the commercial feel to it) My stay felt personal, human and catered too. Which is something that is important when you are in the hospitality business. The area that the property is in, is a nice neighborhood. It’s quiet and safe, there is parking but most of it is street. I recommend this BnB to any one that is staying in the city .

Absolutely a steal of a deal for staying in the Brooklyn area. The rooms and beds are incredibly comfortable and the location in convenient for travel across NYC. I loved staying here and would definitely come back in the future!

Pros:  A) My room faced the back of the building and was peaceful and quiet, which was great B) The building is a short walk from a subway stop and a relatively short walk to Prospect Park C) It’s an interesting old house that used to be a synagogue, so it has character and certain charm D) There were fresh towels for use in the bathroom at all times Cons: A) The shared bathroom was not cleaned thoroughly once in the week that I was there. The shower floor should have been scrubbed as it had that orangey-pinkish stuff that starts growing in the bathroom when it’s not cleaned properly. The sink had a few unpleasant things stuck to it for several days and the toilet should have been scrubbed as well. B) The shared kitchen sometimes had coffee stains and kitchen towels were not replaced over the week I was there C) There was a guide to leaving Airbnb reviews in my room which felt somewhat exploitative D) On the last day there was no hot water for 24 hours, so a shower was not an option

This was perfect for what I needed! A safe and clean place to sleep. The value for what you get is absolutely outstanding. Clean, very independent, and super easy. Just be aware as you make your way through the neighborhood if you are alone. It feels a bit unsafe after dark (as does much of NYC without crowds though, I suppose), but the home itself feels secure. Be aware there will be other guests, but everything is so organized and efficient that bathroom time and privacy were not issues in the slightest. If you need a place to crash, you absolutely cannot do better than this!

The instructions listed for this room is different than the instructions listed for their other rooms. The instructions aren't clear and make you jump through unncessary hoops. I've provided screenshots to AirnB.  I called the number listed for the door code (because again, it isn't listed for the room) and the "host" told me to contact the real host online through message. Odd because I'm calling the number listed for the "host". I've reported this to AirnB, not answering their phone and seemingly listing a non host as their number. Unsafe and unacceptable.  Guest BEWARE

The apartment is excellent, it has everything close to the market, the train station, some places to eat, the apartment has almost everything new, impeccable, we only found about 2 cockroaches, it has everything to cook, washing machine, dryer, towels, hair dryer, the location is 30 minutes from Time Square and Manhattan, the train station is 2 blocks from the apartment.

My first bnb experience and I was very scared. But I am glad I decided to try it out. Place was clean. Communication was timely and location was great. Space was wonderfully put together. The place was so much better than I anticipated that I asked to extend my reservation and got an immediate response, which I loved. Will definitely book again.

Great place in a great location. Was here for the Pride parade and the apartment was in the midst of all the action with good walking distance of restaurants, drug stores, bars, etc. Everything went a smoothly except a little mishap regarding check in. Zander was kind enough to let me check in a little before 3 and was very accommodating to my needs. Key Cafe was a little difficult to navigate but in the end it worked out. Highly recommend.

Ruben was an incredible host and so, so welcoming. I loved staying at his place and am planning on staying again next week! Quiet, cozy, beautiful, spacious apartment - in a great and safe part of Bushwick close to the best lines - the L and M (only 30-40 min commute to Manhattan - M goes to a lot of popular tourist spots too if that interests you).  Ruben was super kind and awesome to talk to - we hung out and he prepared a beautiful shrimp noodle soup for me on my final night. I felt like I made a new friend, haha! The bathroom was spotless and seeing that I'm a soap fiend, I loved using the different variety of Dr. Bronners liquid soaps available! The bed was extremely comfortable - tons of pillows and blankets - I had the hardest time getting out of it every morning. I loved having a desk in my room, seeing that I am here in New York to job hunt. The living room was open, filled with plants, and well decorated. I found myself hanging out in it a lot with a cup of tea and I would say it is the epitome of a cool,  yet humble Bushwick living room. Honestly, this is my dream apartment and set some pretty high standards during my own apartment hunt.  But I have to say, what really stole the show for me was THE BATHROBE. Ruben, being the amazing, gracious host he is, provided a bathrobe for me upon arrival. It really made me feel like a special guest and that I wasn't just crashing in someone's spare room. My job hunt has been so stressful, and there was something about that bathrobe that sent me into another dimension - a realm of paradise and serenity that my busy, anxious self does not often slip into. Not too plush, but not too thin - just the right amount of "waffle cotton" (I just googled that right now, I'm no bathrobe expert). There was nothing better than waking up, picking out a Dr. Bronners soap to match my mood, and then wrapping myself up in that heavenly bathrobe and hanging out in my room. It's also one size fits all - so you all can feel like a divine creature too.

Patrizio's place is phenomenal!! Highly  recommended. I was on a business trip and found the space perfect, functional, sparkling clean, comfortable, and the list keeps on going!  Very close to different subway lines and within walking distance to Fidi, Tribeca, soho, little italy, etc.  Patrizio, was very prompt to respond all my questions and provides very clear instructions for check in and check out making process super easy and stress free. There is no elevator but I didn'tmind, the experience and place was so positive making the walk up unnoticeable.. plus I didn't mind the exercise walking up and down the stairs.

The apartment itself was ok. It looks exactly like on the pictures.  The location is ok, very close to the metro station, and just a couple of blocks away from the Central Park. There are a lot of cafes and restaurants near and a very good grocery store. However, the experience was not the best. We had the problem with the doors and entering the apartment. One of us is not the strongest person and one day she came earlier to the apartment and was not able to open the door herself. One day it was heavily raining and the ceiling in bedroom leaked right above our heads. There was no place for the four of us to place our stuff. We were not able to place our suitcases anywhere where they would not be in the way. Four people with suitcases are not able to easily get around the apartment. Also, there is no wardrobe to hang some of the clothes that needs to be on the hangers. On our last day, we had a really bad encounter with our host. Up to that point everything was ok but onthe last day everything was terrible.  We were falsely accused of stealing her belongings and the entire matter was handled in very unprofessional and unpleasant manner.

The pictures are deceiving as the first photo is NOT where you’re staying. There is no way to control the temperature in the room and it was freezing when I stayed here. The space is very clean, but very bare so sound travels in the room. It echoes when you speak, and you can hear EVERYTHING in other units and outside.    Also- never knew who the host was as when I booked, the host photo was that of a young woman, then the weekend I was arriving the host photo was that of an older man, then when I picked up the keys, I was met by an older woman who could not speak anything but Russian. This scared me a bit.   In the bright side, you’re close to the subway, and there’s a lot of spots to eat 10 minutes away.

Be aware of this host!!! He is a big scammer!!! I have ordered and paid for 2 bedroom apartment but instead got a studio with 2 beds that I couldn't use for the purpose. At some point the host stopped answering my phones and his administrator said "take it or leave it". When I approached him by email afterwards, he said "What do you want, I provided you with 2 separate beds". Now he start claiming that I broke his TV asking to pay for it. I hope Airbnb will be able to resolve this somehow.

I had a great stay with Kioko. The room was cozy and warm, Kyoko was private and respectfull and so am I, so it worked out great. When a minor issue arose she was very helpfull and solved it for me. And the location was amazing. Super close to the subway and bus and restaurants, markets and laundromats. The neighborhood is very working class but its very busy and with many businesses so you never feel unsafe. In short, great value for your buck, especially in Manhattan.

Kyokos accommodation is great if you are on a budget but still want to live in Manhattan itself. I stayed for a month and had a good time!  Pro's: - Kyoko is very nice, reliable, eager to help and she answers quickly!  - You have a lot of privacy in this aparment. Great if you have to work or want a quiet place to stay at. - Very comfy bed, clean sheets, a desk to work at, a small refrigarator and more than enough space for one person. - Great Wifi! Hallelujah - Great location. Might seem a bit dangerous at first but it shouldn't be if you stay aware of your surroundings (which you should always do in NYC). You have literally *anything* less than 10min away from the apartment: supermarkets, laundry, subway, bus station, 24/7 shop, café, post office, lot's of things to eat (legendary Patsy's Pizza is only 5min away!) etc etc  Con's (aren't really bad, I personally just wish I knew before booking): - No daylight in the room - There is an A/C right infront of the window, so if you have sensible sleep you might get something to cancel the noise. - Bathroom and kitchen could have been a bit cleaner  All in all I had a great stay and will definitely come back! :)

We had a fantastic week long stay at this great NYC place.  It was great for two couples and our dog. The location is great! Everything was described accurately. It is NYC so there is noise but it didn’t bother any of us..it was just background noise.  Our dog was a bit scared at first but got used to it. We walked her daily to Washington Sq park where there is a great dog park.  My husband and I were able to work during the week and had no issues with the Wi-Fi. Gabriella is very responsive and a great host…checking in to make sure all was good, which it was.

It was an experience arriving at 8.30 pm at Susan's place. Starting with the taxi driver who couldn't find the location and at the same time, he wasn't sure if the area was safe.    With fear, I got out of the car to see if it was the address number that Suzan had given me. When we found out that it was the correct house, the taxi driver promised me that he would be waiting in the car until I entered the house. Suzana's house is clean and cozy, with a good bed and with drinks, water and Coca Cola as a welcome.  Thank you, Suzan called me and tried to explain to me how the alarm works and the rest of the house.. But because of how nervous, tired, I was and at the same time arriving at an unknown house at that time, without having someone to receive you to give you an explanation how the Alarm works and the rest in the house.. Well, it was a little unpleasant.. It was not a night to rest/sleep after a long trip from Europe.  Also something beeped all night... supposedly the battery of some device that was already used up...

Suzan was very hospitable - she got up very early with me to show me the breakfast options (the availability of breakfast was a great touch).  The place was clean, but there was an unpleasant odor in the bedroom - it wasn't clear where it was coming from, but it was distracting until I fell asleep.  One other distraction - you could hear conversations outside the door.  But overall, it was a good value for the money and the proximity to JFK airport is nice.  FYI - The cab/rideshare services each cost about $15.

Sebastian’s place was very nice. It smelled great and had just about all we needed, except the food. He left us a nice fruit basket that included some snacks. The kitchen was stocked with all pots and utensils needed to cook, eat and drink. There was even some coffee in the pantry for us to make coffee. The bathrooms had tissue, towels, soap and other things not normally provided in an Airbnb. The beds were comfortable and the blankets were nice and fluffy! Everything was great with his place. The only thing I’d say is if you need to sleep with a TV on, there are no TVs in the bedrooms. Also if you have a car, the parking is on a very steep slop in front of the building which was a little scary for us cause we are not used to that but we soon learned there were many hills in the area, hence the name. I’d definitely recommend his place. We only seen him once when we were leaving but didn’t have any problems that warranted us to contact him. He provided all the details we needed for our stay and we were good to go!

Suzan is amazing. She is delightful. Polite yet sassy and fun to talk to.  She made me feel at home. I truly enjoyed my stay. If you need anything don't be afraid to ask her. Please be respectful she is a really nice lady.

The host waked me up in early morning to talk about the Air Conditioner. You cannot wake me up from my sleep. It’s above 90 degree and I wasn’t using the AC.   Also, the host entered my room using the key while I’m outside, which let me feel unsafe about my belonging.  The TV is ON 24/7 with volume of 26 or above. It’s too loud and I cannot tolerate such volume.  There is no space in the refrigerator. I could not buy any food and put it there.  The host let me feel uncomfortable as guest and always direct me of what should be done.

Sebastian’s place as exactly as we expected. Checking in was a breeze, everything was clean and in good condition. The beds and pillows were comfortable. We happened to visit during a VERY hot week with temps over 90 degrees, but the apartment was comfortable. Kitchen and laundry amenities were much appreciated. Coming from a rural area, I happily found it was quiet with very minimal city noise.  We very much appreciated use of a parking space in the driveway, as this makes everything easier and less stressful. I will note that it is sloped, for anyone with serious mobility issues. It was not a problem for us. The location was convenient to the Staten Island Ferry and also to my son’s soccer camp at College of Staten Island. The area was nice and we felt safe at all times.  My family was pleased with our stay at Sebastian’s, who was always quick to answer any messages or questions from us. We would definitely stay again and heartily recommend the apartment.

Everything very good. The location is about 10 blocks from the subway that you can combine with all the lines to get around the city (even the buses too). The neighborhood seems unsafe at night, but nothing ever happened to us. The room is spacious, the bathroom is very clean and the heating worked perfectly! We would stay again. Thanks for everything, Ibrahim!
Very good place, it was always clean, the truth is that despite hearing bad comments about the Bronx, it didn't seem unsafe to me at all. I liked it, I would definitely return.

This stay was one of my best AirBnb experiences thus far. I don’t have anything bad to say about my time at this apartment. The amenities really helped you feel right at home and we were never short on hand sanitizer or disinfectant spray in the common areas. We absolutely loved how clean it all was and we truly appreciated all of the small, thoughtful touches that were put into making us feel comfortable. Having a fridge, microwave and AC unit all in the room especially allowed us to maintain privacy and distance ourselves amidst the COVID outbreak. The host was a very kind soul and always cooperative, even at times when it was inconvenient to them. I wish Ibrahim continued success in all of his business endeavors and I would recommend this space to anyone looking to stay in the Bronx. There’s plenty affordable shops and restaurants within walking distance of the building and the neighborhood was not an unsafe place during any of my walks or outings in the public parks.

ANTS!!!   This experienced sucked. I bought a bag of groceries home since I was staying for a few days. By the morning the entire bag was covered in ants AND I had ants in my bed!!!!!   This review will probably get deleted because I'm sure the host will complain enough to have it deleted but nothing I'm saying here is false or inaccurate.   Wendy lives in a barricaded side of the apartment. Theres a lot of clutter everywhere; honestly this place isn't meant to be an airbnb but New York rent is pushing people to turn their homes into airbnbs. I was reprimanded twice by Wendy because apparently I missed two of the many rules she has written out. Make sure you read her entire handbook because there are about 50 rules you need to memorize when you stay here.   I found this stay unpleasant. I couldn't reach Wendy when it came time for me to check in so rather than waiting around I headed to the apartment. I was greeted with her complaining to me that check in wasn't until later. I told her I had been trying to reach her for hours and she didn't acknowledge this at all. When It came time to check out I was rushed out the door.  The general feeling of surveillance is very uncomfortable. This felt like staying at an airbnb run by Ma (Octavia Spencer).

Staying here made this trip extremely helpful. We had a safe space where we could lay our heads free of any stress the city has to offer. Wendy went above and beyond in ensuring we had a everything we needed to be comfortable. Not one negative thing could be said about this trip. Highly recommended.

Wendy's lodging was more than perfect and a 5 star review is not enough, my husband and I would give it a 10! The price is really good for what you really get with is a more than great stay.  First, Wendy is really kind and gives good recommendations, she let us leave our luggage before check in and after check out, and both are really easy to make.   The apartment is really near the subway as listed, you have a lot of great places to eat and a supermarket around the corner (with is perfect), location is good, is not that far from Manhattan, and the place is not dangerous at all.  The room we stayed is perfect, clean, good space and enough space for 2 people with luggage. There is a fridge with water, a desktop to work, dresser, lamps ( very pretty), enough windows, lights and the bed is really comfy with enough bedding.   The bathroom is really clean at all times, great water pressure and hot.  What really surprised us and showed us that Wendy goes above and beyond for you to feel as home is the amount of detailes she covers, in the room and the bathroom, forgot a razor? she has them, soap, shampoo (different kinds), towels, pens, a map, scissors, etc etc etc.   We also loved the decoration, you feel welcomed at all times and Wendy gives very good advice about a lot of subjects (we loved the Roti Restaurant she recommended).  She is an amazing person, easy to talk to, helps a lot, cares for your stay to be more than perfect.  I can't say enough good things about Wendy and her house, don't think about it more, this is a perfect stay and believe me, the price is more than perfect.   Wendy, thanks again for everything. Hopefully we can visit again and for sure we will stay with you If possible. My husband and I appreciate everything!

Amazing location. This was our first time in New York and didn’t really know what part of town to stay in. The apartment is about a block and a half away from the train station and you will be able to see all of NYC via the train system. The entire apartment was very clean and had a great kitchen. The host was super attentive and made for a frustration free visit. The neighborhood is extremely safe and cultural. We came home around 1 or 2 AM several nights and never felt in danger. There are a few amazing Asian produce supermarkets you must try. The unit itself had great amenities. There is an iron that works and pots and pans for cooking.      A lot of the amenities were very nice quality like the towels and desk. Overall everything was very clean and we didn’t feel grossed being  germaphobes. Would definitely stay here again and recommend to everyone.

The apartment is very well located. The subway station is three blocks away, allowing for easy arrival and mobility. The lines are R and M. Several bus routes also pass nearby. It has nearby stores such as Marshall, Macy's, century21 and others where you can make purchases at very good prices.  Also in terms of food you have restaurants, bakeries and cafes where you can have breakfast and lunch.   The apartment has everything you need to have a good stay.  He highlighted the cleanliness and quality of everything bedding, towels and the bathroom in general.   It also has order and very nice decoration.  The building where it is located is quiet, has an elevator, recycles and is safe.  You can walk safely in the neighborhood at any time. We never felt in danger even though we had days when we were very late. Overall an excellent stay, the apartment is ideal for those who want to get to know or walk around NYC.

First of all, I want to thank Charlene for the special attention she gave us. My family and I traveled to New York for the first time and our expectations of the city were met since Charlene's house was able to allow us to see the city from another point of view. In general, we are very influenced by the movies that for 40 years have shown us a dangerous and disorderly Brooklyn, very far from the truth, since after getting rid of these prejudices we realized that it is a very quiet and safe area, we will not stop seeing people on the streets who personify these beliefs, but who are far away. If they are a danger, they only reflect a tradition in the way they dress and act, but they are very integrated into a quiet community with values of coexistence, this was our impression. On the other hand, the fact of being half a street from the bus that takes us to transfer with the subway to the center was very comfortable and cheap. If you consider that we are 35 minutes from the center of New York City, we can only enjoy the incredible multiculturalism that you can see on the subway in these 35 minutes. Charline's house is very well connected by bus and metro everywhere, I suggest you buy a metro card that is valid for both the bus and the metro and enjoy the different areas by organizing the routes well before leaving. Charline's house is comfortable and we feel very taken care of by her to help us at all times to resolve any questions that arise. I have no hesitation in recommending the apartment and the experience of seeing the city of Brooklyn and New York from the inside is another interesting way of sightseeing. Location, place was perfect,  but it was very unpleasant to meet a bug(cockroach) every day. :(

Cozy place,  totally private bathroom, kitchen and living room with cable TV available at every time. The room is big enough for 2 people (Robert was so nice to let stay a friend of mine for some days!) and for all the stuff I needed for an entire month. Very safe neighborhood with many different restaurants, Whole Foods and many other supermarkets and a laundry in the next street. Convenient location, with red subway local and express lines in the next block, Central Park and blue subway only 2 blocks far.  The host doesn't invade your space, but is very friendly and helpful if you need. It was my first time with airbnb and I was a bit afraid,  but I think that it would be very difficult find a host better than RRobert!  Thank you

Roberts apartment perfect suited our stay in NYC, it's in a great location being only 1 block from the nearest metro and less than a 5 minute walk to central park. Rob was away while we were their but was always at hand on the phone if we needed anything. The apartment was clean and spacious and I would recommend this place to anyone looking for somewhere to stop in NYC for a great price.

My friends and I had a lovely stay at The Box House Hotel. The location is impeccable - easy access to Brooklyn, Williamsburg as well as Manhattan. The free shuttles they offer guests to any spot within 1 mile of the hotel was also fab. Would definitely consider staying here again. Shout out to Angel at the front desk for a stress-free check in, even though we arrived after 3am!

Great place to stay! Casey for sure has a taste for interior design and was really quick to answer every question we had on the appartement and the surroundings. We never met in person, but from the messages we exchanged he seems to be a really fun guy ;). Also the appartement was clean, really quiet - for NYC standards - and perfectly situated to the subway. There are grocery markets on every corner and some cool places for coffee and a quick breakfast pretty closeby. For dinner or going out I'd say you are better of taking a short ride with the subway, which is not a big deal as they are running all night. In my personal opinion the area is more Bedford-Stuyvesant than Clinton Hill and to me there are nicer areas within Brooklyn, but on the other hand we enjoyed staying where the "normal" New Yorker lives and...we never felt unsafe or uncomfortable at any time.
