He was always available when I messaged him about any concern (small or big) and was very accommodating.  I would recommend you book this place ASAP, because it is an absolute steal at this price to enjoy this type of luxury!  -P.

This was our first experience using airbnb. It was a very positive one. Ferris and Aaron were kind and welcoming. The house is clean and organized for the needs a traveler might have. Since we were traveling with our two kids, our main concern was with safety, I can just say that we NEVER felt unsafe in the neighborhood. We walked around with the kids, went grocery shopping nearby and took the train every day. We highly recommend Ferris' place. We will be there again in our next trip to NYC. Ferris and Aaron thanks a lot!

My family and me spent 4 amazing days at Ferris place. We have two girls (10 & 13) and being in a safe neighborhood was a must. We loved Harlem atmosphere and strongly recommend Lenox saphire restaurant very close to Ferris place. The location just a few blocks from the bus station and M60 to La Guardia was a plus. We never feel unsafe even when we came at night after spending the whole day at different places all along Manhattan. Ferris was a great hostess and I can tell the days we spent there will be unforgettable. Go to Ferris place, no doubts... Thanks Ferris!! See you in Uruguay some day..

A good apartment to make your stay in New York cheap and authentic. The area is quiet and has a children's playground just around the corner. The Brooklyn Children's Museum is also nearby, and on some days you can even get in for free.  Neither the area nor the apartment corresponds to the German small town ideal. If you need it to be immaculately clean, both inside and outside, you'll have to look for a long time in New York. However, Joyce's apartment is absolutely fine considering how old the house is. The apartment is unusually large by New York standards. It is shaped like a tube: you enter the kitchen, on the left there are 2 bedrooms (one as a connecting room with a couch) and on the right there is the kitchen.  The apartment is on the ground floor and is accordingly dark. This can be an advantage on hot days.  We recommend the JEMZ restaurant nearby, very good Jamaican food.  English: Authentic, spacious apartment on the ground floor. It provides shade on hot days. The host Joyce and her family are very nice people. We recommend to stay here.

The house is just as in the photos, except that I thought we would have a patio available but we did not have access to it. Simply equipped but sufficient for what is basically needed. Prospect street is very nice, quiet and well lit. Access to the subway is not convenient, to go to the AC Kingston Troop lines you have to walk 10/12 blocks which with a small child and late at night we did not like and it was complicated. It is better to walk to the Kingston AV station on line 3 in the Jewish district and there is also always a police patrol car which makes you feel safe at night and the distance is shorter, you just have to be careful since there is no service on weekends. My recommendation and after a few days studying the area and the maps well, I advise checking the bus lines near the apartment that helped us make better connections with the subways. Keep in mind that waits at night are around 20/30 minutes. To go to Manhattan in general and without stress it took us an hour and a half. Delis and some supermarkets are in the area. For dinner in a good restaurant we have not found any nearby, only a small place for pizza and restaurant Basil towards Kingston Av. For our child it was good to be 3 blocks from the children museum and in the corner of the apartment we had a park with games to take advantage of. We have very much enjoyed our stay. I hope my tips are useful for other guests.

Location was perfect! My wallet was stolen in Times Square and hosts went out of their way to assist me!   Apartment was adorable and better than we pictured. Three girls in the city...and we enjoyed every moment of downtime at local coffee spots and eateries. Seriously, would stay again, absolutely in love with Harlem and this listing!

Hello Ferris, this is the first time I have rented online and the truth is I was afraid of arriving and not finding the place or that it was a lie!! But I arrived and everything was perfect!! Thanks for the chocolates, the perfect WiFi, the location too!!! It is a safe neighborhood and it is a beautiful apartment!! I congratulate you and I am going to recommend you!!! Kiss!!!

We enjoyed our stay. Aaron and Ferris are friendly and helpful, and their apartment is perfect for us. Comfortable bed, good sized living space, kitchen, and plenty of soft towels. The neighbourhood is interesting. Lots of churches, stores and restaurants. Everything we needed was on one street: a laundry, supermarket, coffee and food. The people we came into contact with were friendly and spirited. There are one or two crazies on the streets, but we didn't feel unsafe. While we were visiting, several of the residents set up a temporary DJ booth on the street opposite. The music played loud and late into the evening. The noise was a nuisance in the lounge, but not a problem further back in the bedroom. Would we stay here again.. absolutely.

I had a wonderful experience. I stayed for two weeks time for work. The room is very clean and everything she provided (towels, pillows) was freshly laundered. It became hot in NYC and she set me up with my own AC. She also helped me carry my heavy suitcase the first and last day of my stay up the four story walk up. The place is a five min walk to the subway. The neighborhood is very safe. I walked in the early mornings and after late nights by myself and never felt a hint of danger. Neighborhood has a laundromat a block away, amazing restaurants and dozens of stores. The host was kind and let my bf stay one Friday night. The bathroom does not have a sink so I brushed my teeth in the kitchen sink. Christina provided shampoo, tooth paste and a first aid kit. The previous guest had stayed three months and I'm not surprised because this is an excellent space with an excellent host.

I had a great time staying at Christina’s. The room was exactly as described and the location couldn’t have been better! Christina was also very nice and helpful, and made the experience stress-free. Would definitely stay again.

We enjoyed an easy and comfortable Christmas holiday week in Ferris's Harlem flat, with just a few small reservations.   On the plus side, the flat is cozy and secure, and the location is truly great both for tourists (my wife and son) and for former residents who are looking for a different take on New York City (that would be me, in this case). The flat is in very close proximity to some of Harlem's finest restaurants, offers quick and easy access to excellent grocery stores (Pioneer is less than a block away, and there is also a Whole Foods within five blocks), and the MTA options are outstanding too (the subway station at 125th and Malcolm X Boulevard offers the 2 and 3 express trains, and there is good bus service along both Malcolm X and Adam Clayton Powell Jr Boulevard). Also, the neighborhood itself is a joy to explore, especially in my case as when I lived in NYC in the late 1980s it was thought to be a truly dangerous walkabout for non-residents. Virtually without exception, everyone we encountered in the neighborhood was friendly, forthcoming, helpful, polite, and patient.  We did have a few gripes, all with regard to the flat's kitchen amenities (and all of which I expect can be easily remedied). For instance, the dishwasher does not work as the door cannot be closed (because, we were informed, it had been pushed too far under the counter). We resorted to washing our dishes by hand, of course (we are game travelers!), however this provided to be quite difficult due to extremely low hot water pressure in the kitchen sink. Also, the plastic water distribution arm in the coffee maker came apart in my hands when I first went to use it (I rigged it to work, but this is something that will no doubt plague future users until the the mechanism is replaced). Finally, the kitchen setup could do with a few knives for food preparation (using a steak knife for chopping and slicing is a fun exercise once, but over a longer stay this becomes somewhat demoralizing).  Ending on a positive note (and our experience in the flat really was quite a positive one, in a great many ways), Ferris was very responsive to all of my communications both before and during our stay on West 129th Street. Her instructions for getting into the flat were perfect and very easy for jetlag-weary travelers to follow.

Mrs. Ferris is a wonderful hostess. She helps where she can and answers all questions immediately. Even ordering and accepting packages worked. The area is a wonderful area to leave the stressful New York day behind. A great contrast to the rest of the city. The apartment is comfortably furnished and is perfectly equipped for everyday needs. She is fully equipped. Would come here anytime again. Highly Recommended.

The house was just OK. For the given price, the location was not very far from the center but it was quite dangerous during nights and the people nearby weren't very hospitable. The house was in a very good condition except an almost broken couch that was fixed as soon as we let them know and the fact that the pillows and blankets were a bit smelly. Apart from these, the stay was very good. Communication with the owner was very fast.

Ronald was an awesome, helpful and respectable host. He was always there when I needed him; he goes out of his way to accommodate me. I was pleased with the private room just as he described. The neighborhood is quiet just as he also described; I never felt unsafe. I’m glad that I had the opportunity to stay there. He exceeded my expectations and ensured that my stay was a pleasant experience. Thanks!!
Great place to stay! Never felt unsafe. Great location with quick access to multiple subway trains.  Very clean! Only stayed for a weekend getaway, but would stay again when back in the city!

The room Ronald provided me for my stay exceeded my expectations. I had my own room with large bed, cable TV, closet & drawers to put my stuff in, air-conditioning, wireless internet connection. As for the neighborhood, Ronald's apartment is situated in a residential part of Bronx, so I never ever felt unsafe while staying there. There are many grocery shops in the area, Subway & McDonald's just around the corner in case you get hungry and don't feel like going sightseeing (which was not my case, since I spent most of my time in the city like a genuine tourist, lol). Subway station (Elder Av) is only a few blocks away, and it takes you to Manhattan fairly quickly, approx. in 45min. As for Ronald, he is the best host I could ever imagine. He is a nice person to talk to, really friendly, helpful and respectful. In case of any issues, I could let him know literally anytime, day or night. Moreover, he offered to take me to JFK airport in the day of my departure from the US, which is like 2 hours by subway, but less than half an hour by his car!! This was really a tremendous help, because I had a lot of baggage, so I can't thank him enough for driving me there and dropping me off right in front of the terminal. I really enjoyed being at Ron's place and I can only recommend him for other travelers who are looking for a nice, safe and cozy place to stay at ;-)

Ronald was one of the cool people I have met. He helped me to get to his place by giving me a ride from my old place to his. The neighborhood looks sketchy, but it is actually nice. There is stores and fast food restaurants nearby. I highly recommend to stay here

In short, Ronald was a great host.   He went above and beyond what was expected.  I live in New York and needed a place to land because I had to move from my apartment and had not locked down a long-term living situation.   Not only did Ronald allow me to arrive with 11 boxes and two small chairs, he helped me move them out after my month's stay when my movers bailed. This was several trips in his compact car! (NOTE:  No more 11-box clients).  He made me feel very welcome, giving me a tour of the place and encouraging me to alert him to my needs. He entreated me to phone him anytime of day or night if I were stranded or felt unsafe.   He offered me dinner if I was around when he was cooking. He's a good cook with a love jones for corn on the cob who is committed to eating as healthfully as possible.  The apartment is on the 11th floor of a mid-rise building with 24-hour security. It is home to mainly lower middle-class and working-class residents. Good, kind, decent folk -- the type anyone should welcome as neighbors. The type  who bid you good morning and good evening when you are standing six inches away from them on or at the  elevator.   Ronald's apartment is clean and quiet. It has a homey feel. The photo does not do the room justice. It is very comfortable and reminds me of a New England B&B.  The neighborhood is a quiet area of the Bronx called Soundview Park. It is named for the nearby park, an unspoiled, unmanicured mass of nature as God may have intended it.  Of course, Ronald's place is a bargain. This is mainly because it is in the Bronx, not a stone's throw from Manhattan. Anyone who needs to be in midtown in 20 minutes should live elsewhere.  However, if you don't mind a longer commute -- around 40 to 50 minutes to midtown -- and want to live in a quiet, clean spot that is very easy on the wallet, with a congenial host ...  Ronald's house is the place!

You can go to Ronald's with complete peace of mind.   I didn't even close my bedroom door because I trusted him so much.   I encountered no danger in the Bronx: every evening, I took the subway home in the middle of the night.   At the end of the street, you can take the #5 bus to the Hunts Point Avenue subway.   I recommend this address.   ---------   You can go to Ronald in peace. I have not even closed the door of my room so I trust him.  I have not encountered any danger in the Bronx every night, I took the subway to go home at night.  Down the street you can take the bus n° 5 which leads to the underground 5 Hunts Point Avenue.   I recommend this address.

I'm extremely happy I chose to book Ronald's room - he made my stay as comfortable as possible. Not only did he pick me up by car from the Bus Terminal in Downtown Manhattan at 7am in the morning, but upon my arrival in his living area he gave me a lot of helpful tipps of which metros/ busses to take to get to his place. This might not seem to begin with, but makes your first steps so much easier!  Of course, before booking, I hesitated for a moment. Did I really wanna book a place in the Bronx? Because after all - if you've never been there and all things you hear (from the very few moments that happens anyway) are rather linked to gangs or crime... Well, you better start dropping those prejudices immediately. I never felt unsafe in his area, neither early in the morning nor late at night.   About the room - I was tremendously surprised to find it to be much bigger than it looks in the picture. I seriously had trouble to get going in the morning since I found it so comfy. Plus the great furniture, plus the great view from the 12th floor - what's there left to say?  Thanks a lot Ron for the amazing stay!

What a great time in NY! Ronald was the best anfitrion (he is a nice, kind, helpful and also funny men) I've never had! He drove and helped me to buy a Metro Card (Subway) and drove me to the places where I could buy groceries or take the Bus. He made my stay as comfortable as possible and always offered his help. I never felt unsafe in his area, neither early in the morning nor late at night. The room was much bigger than it looks in the picture: Comfortable, clean and tidy! I'm extremely happy I chose to book Ronald's room.

Rachel's place is great, and spacious for a NYC apartment! The check in process was easy and Rachel was great at responding very quickly. I probably wouldn't hang out alone in the neighborhood at night, but we never felt unsafe when coming and going or when in the apartment.  You're only a few blocks from the subway and just a mile from Central Park, so we were able to get everywhere that we needed without any hassle. The apartment was clean and also includes great amenities, like a nespresso machine! I would definitely stay here again.

My boyfriend, myself, and our 2 children stayed at Rachel’s place for 4 nights and had a wonderful time! Rachel is an incredible host and was extremely accommodating with check in and check out, as our flight arrived early and departed late. When we arrived to the apartment she met us and let us in where we had a bottle of wine to greet us as well! She was very friendly and responded timely to messages. My daughter is 14 months and she had the pack and play and high chair available, and ready on arrival, which was so great! I did request an air mattress for my son in the bedroom prior to arriving as I knew he wouldn’t want to sleep alone in the living room, and a cot was provided and made up for him in the bedroom as well. The location of the apartment was great! It was about a 3 block walk to the Subway and there is plenty of restaurants and stores within walking distance. I read a review prior about someone not feeling safe in the neighborhood, and I have to say I never felt unsafe. We walked everywhere with both kids and never felt uncomfortable. I love Harlem, and I love all of the brownstones! The one issue we did have was with the WiFi connection. While we obviously weren’t sitting in the apartment a lot, in the evenings when we stayed in it was difficult to get a strong enough connection for the smart TV to access Netflix, etc. Which was a little challenging with two kids. I did address this with Rachel, who was very responsive, and we were able to get it reconnected at one point. Unfortunately it was hit or miss the entire stay.  Thank you Rachel for being such a great host!

Rachel is such a kind, friendly, responsive and accommodating host! We traveled with our toddler, and her flexibility with our check-in and check-out times made our trip that much more stress-free. Rachel was also just a text/phone call away with anything we needed. Her apartment is exactly as pictured, and located just a few minutes away from the subway station. The bedroom also backs into the quiet backyard, which made our sleep was very restful. I'd highly recommend this apartment, especially if you're traveling with kids!

This apartment with a few touches and some changes is ideal for spending a few days in New York, it is well connected to public transport. It is in a neighborhood that may initially seem dangerous but it is not at all (we went with an 11-year-old girl and we were not scared at any time). Rachel left us many details such as coffee, wine, yogurts.... Etc.

The ares wasn’t so great, although it was easy to get to Manhattan, time square & other tourist attractions. It just seemed a little sketchy. The neighborhood to the right of the apartment was a little scary to walk through at night and the neighborhood to the left seemed a little more safe.  The reception of the location was also very bad and the wifi didn’t work well.  My family and I stayed for 2 weeks and we had enough toilet paper for just a couple days, although she does say to let her know if she needs to replenish any toiletries, I think it could have been better stocked.   My niece was moving into her dorm and we needed an ac for her & the host was nice enough to let us get it shipped to her address. She also accommodated us by letting us leave our luggage in a few hours before check in, so that was perfect! Thank you again.

We had a reasonably nice stay, and there were no serious problems.  The apartment is roomy and was adequate for our group of 4 adults and two kids.  It is not a very fancy or modern unit, and it feels more rundown than the photos/description led us to believe.  Oscar/Marietta were fine hosts, although our one request for replacement lights never got taken care of.  The neighborhood is quite convenient for access to the city, but does have a bit of a sketchy vibe to it.  The wifi was just barely adequate, running around 5-8 mbps.

The pictures are inaccurate. This is not what you will stay in. Noise bad kids crying cars and sirens all night. Tub is gross gross !!! Neighborhood unsafe. I did not sleep at all night one and the other nights I slept because we had walked all day! Felt dirty and you have to haul all your bags up a very narrow tight flight of stairs. Kitchen had no dish cloths so cooking was out of the question. Just not a comfortable stay. Would never go back. Tried to find alternate place and couldn't.

We never had the chance to meet Oscar. We were greeted by a rather unpleasant person, not smiling and who visibly got out of bed. She was clearly showing us that she couldn't wait to get rid of us and go back to bed. Whereas we hadn't slept for almost 24 hours.  So no wise advice for the stay, no greetings, nothing. We were upset and so tired. Despite everything, I immediately saw that something was wrong: it was not the same apartment as the one presented on Airbnb.  It has the same surface area and the same layout but not the same comfort, not the same decoration, not the same cleanliness and not the same general state of maintenance. In the presentation we see 3 different bedrooms with double beds, suggesting that there are 3 bedrooms. But in reality there are 2 bedrooms and a small storage room which only leaves room for bunk beds. So what does a photo of a bedroom do that doesn't exist? And everything is like that.  The furniture is damaged, the walls are dirty, there is a big hole in one wall and another in a door the size of an adult's hand, all the windows are very dirty, the bathtub is in a terrible state, the cupboard doors are broken, the furniture completely different like the table, the sofa, the headboard, the chest of drawers. The living room sideboard and the very large bedroom mirror are missing.  The carpet is very poorly laid with creases. The sink was blocked, then the bathtub and finally the toilet (there we gave up).  This apartment does not correspond at all to the asking price but above all it is an illusion.  The visual is inaccurate, we would never have rented this apartment and our choice would have been another proposal if we had had the real photos. We chose this one because it seemed clean, well decorated with personal items, as well as quality furniture. Every morning around 8 o'clock we were woken up by children screaming and crying from the apartment below. As there is no ceiling insulation between the staircase and the entrance to the apartment (not easy to describe), it was as if the children were in the room. One morning we had to intervene in order to get them to react because obviously it seemed to be completely normal for them.  The common entrance is small and in complete disorder, there are a large number of shoes piled up, lots of junk of all kinds, mail strewn on the floor and no cleanliness. The carpet continues to age and the tiles are cleaned with margarine.  For us there is deception and we consider that this announcement causes great harm to Airbnb.
Very conveniently located near the subway. Location felt a bit unsafe. Bare minimum comfortability. Felt as though the owners rent out when they’re not there rather than a comfortable stay.
The house was nice, the sofa was a little uncomfortable to sleep on.

When we arrived we were disappointed with the cleanliness. Images not representative. Property needed thorough deep clean large areas of dirt, dust, filthy carpets, rusty bathtub, grime and mould in bathroom. Sofa bed broken on arrival so 2 people had to find other boarding, no central  heating only small electric unsafe heaters shorting out, sparking and smell when used. Unsafe loose electrical sockets. I informed the host sent her some images her response was ‘feel free to leave’at first. She sent the cleaner to do a “deep clean” this was not done just a few areas cleaned from images sent.  Doors and handles are all filthy and the window areas thick with dirt and dust. Window was broken and was “fixed” stain on walls. Some of the curtains disgusting and she did change one of the sets in bedroom. should have known better as the price was too good to be true. Linen and towels smell.I didn’t expect a palace but just cleanliness. Kitchen and living area not bad. Could be a lovely place

This place is a death trap! It’s unsafe and clearly there has not been enough upkeep from the owners to maintain this space. There are light fixtures hanging on by a thread, the upstairs railing is fragile and not safe at all to hold onto, and the bathrooms don’t even have locks on the doors! Also came crashing through the staircase because the “stairs” were simply wood planks slotted into place with no screws, glue, or any kind of reinforcements to secure them in place! There are better places to stay in NYC where you don’t have to fear for your safety and wellness for the entirety of the stay.

My brother and I stayed with Ryan for 5 nights in April and it was great. It was one of our first airbnb experience and I'm glad Ryan made this experience a good one. He met us at the bus terminal, because we couldn't be at his apartment on a certain time. When our bus had delays, he waited for about an hour to give us the keys and tell us the way to the apartment, so we don't get lost and because of that he was even late for his own meeting. His apartment is really clean (and even more, considering he has a dog). Ty (his dog) is super sweet, very quiet (especially when he is in front of the TV watching animal planet :D) and welcomed us nicely every time we entered the apartment. Ryan's roommate was also nice and barely noticeable. The room itself is clean, has lots of storage and the bed is sooooo comfortable. The only minus (which is not even a real disadvantage about staying with Ryan more the American way of building houses) about our stay was that you could hear the traffic outside. But as far as my experience in America, you always hear what's going on outside and especially in New York there is a lot of traffic to hear. But because we wanted to wake up early in the morning anyway it didn't really bother us and if not you could just turn around and keep sleeping. As his description says, if you're outside the apartment there is nothing fancy about it, but as soon as you enter his apartment you feel home and welcomed. We could use the little bathroom mostly for ourselves and shared the big one for taking a shower, which was never a problem. About the area, in the Beginning we were kind of deterred about it because I heard that Harlem is unsafe and when we arrived the streets weren't that clean and many people were hanging around in the streets, but I think it depends on which street you are and what time you walk around, because not all of them are at all times like this and we felt even "safer" at night then the day. After a while we got used to it and we had no problems getting around or feeling unsafe and I'm sure if Ryan can live there for a couple years, it should be safe ;) A supermarket was also close by and I would recommend buying a 7 day unlimited subway ticket for getting around New York if you stay for a couple days. Last and most important some facts about our experience with Ryan. It was really nice meeting him. He was so helpful and nice in every way. You could write him all the time and he would give you advice about what to do, where to go,.... He was our perfect phone tour guide. Every once in a while, especially in the beginning,...

Jennifer ws a perfect host. Not only was she awaiting us at the apartment although we arrived pretty late at night, she also made sure our fridge was filled with lots of fruit juice, eggs, bagels and other necessities for breakfast the next morning. The apartment was completely as expected: nice and clean, each room airconditioned, nice linnens, 2 tv's, wifi, microwave, toaster, espresso and coffee machine. And a great couch for relaxing after a day of site seeing.The neighbourhoud was a mix of locals, students and tourists, nothing fancy. The subwaystations were a 1 minute walk to either side of the street. Perfect for getting around and to Manhatten! Our first day we took the subway to Brooklyn Heights and walked the Brooklyn bridge straight into Manhatten. A great way to start your visit to NYC and great photo opps! A nice Dunkin Donut shop was also at the street corner and a small supermarket was a 5 minute walk. We haven't felt unsafe at any time. Jennifer also brought us some fresh produce and herbs from her own garden and we made some deliciously tasting omelettes with them! Jennifer was always reachable and open to small talk and giving hints and tips when bumping in to her. She also arranged a taxi for us for getting back to the airport early in the morning after our great two week stay.  Jennifer, thanks for being such a warm host and making us feel right at home in your apartment!

My friends and I stayed for a weekend at Althea's place and had a wonderful time! Upon arrival to Althea's, she personally walked us through the keys to the apartment, linens, bed/sofa bed situation, and even showed us how to use the shower. She also kindly left us a guidebook for navigating the amenities of the apartment and the neighborhood. She was supremely sweet and very kind. The place was just as I expected from the listing. We were a group of 4 girls and the ample mirrored spaces was really helpful when getting ready during the day.   I cannot stress enough how great the location of this place is. We were a 5 minute walk from the 2, 3, 4, & 5 MTA options, making our daily travel incredibly easy to plan out. There's a killer bagel place around the corner called Lula's Bagel that was perfect for breakfast and coffee on the go. I would definitely recommend Althea's place as well as Crown Heights for those looking to travel to NYC.

Susan's place was perfect. It was very spacious, comfortable, and with everything you could possibly need. The location is also incredibly convenient. Communications were easy and stress-free. I would highly recommend staying here!

Aaron's place is a nice apartment, pretty clean and spacious. It's close to Central Park and the metro is about at 10-15 minute walk. During the day the area is fine but at night it can feel a bit unsafe if you go walking around. However, I did not experience any actual problems.

Jennifer's place was perfect! She was very accommodating, friendly and understanding. She made the reunion for my friends and I stress free since we were all coming from different places and different times. Her home is so cute and comfortable! If I ever visit NYC again I will definitely stay here

Angelo's place is amazing! Close to everything you'd really need, and in a beautiful part of Brooklyn (I'm a photographer so that's really important to me). Not only is his home beautiful, but Angelo himself was one of the most helpful and kind hosts I've ever had using airbnb who made trip stress free!

I was traveling alone and a little afraid of getting lost in this big city. I'm a very lucky girl, and being at Gaudhi's house was such an experience: I found myself a home in NY. In this nice and cozy place, with awesome localization, I had a good reception and felt comfortable all the time. Kaity (the dog) is cute and calm and I enjoyed very much the company of each one that live in the house! Gaudhi's good nature made the experience all the better.

Host just needs to standardize their check in/check out communication. Apartment was perfect for a group of friends who all wanted their own room. Area was not as sketchy as it looks on Google maps. Very easy to transit downtown (40 mins, 1 line change). Very clean, lots of towels for our group and had 2 sets of keys.

A pleasant stay, everything was as described. Gordon was very responsive. The location is a few minutes walk from a subway station with easy access to Manhattan. This is a very good value in a city like New York with absurdly high hotel prices. Bleecker street it self is fine, however the few blocks to the subway station is somewhat sketchy. Overall, I would stay here again.

Gaudhi, Teresa (his mother) and his brother are amazing hosts, they'll make you feel like a member of their family. Gaudhi took me out one of the nights to show me the Lower East Side, it was really cool. You got to know that you're renting only a mattress, the room where is located is free access and next to the kitchen, so if you have sleeping problems, sensitive with smells (kitchen) or needs privacy this probably is not the place for you. I had some sleeping problems due to the external and internal noise, but I guess in a city like NY this is common and I wasn't adapted. If you're willing to crash late and wake up early you won't have any problem. Easy access to the subway, close to Central Park, restaurants and bars. The neighborhood might scare you at first sight but I walked late (2 am) and nothing happened. Ring the bell once you're there, 1B.

Yes, this place is in Harlem, but I never felt unsafe. I'm from a similar neighborhood in another city so the noises and loitering outside are things I'm used to. If you're a light sleeper, I wouldn't recommend since it's on the first floor, but if noise doesn't bother you, it's a nice cozy apartment. Gaudhi, his brother, and his mom were great people, very friendly. Their mom was a lovely lady and treated me almost like family. The subway is not far, just go down 3 blocks. And it's easy access to the Bronx. Also really close to the north part of Central Park, I spent my last day walking around there as I made my way downtown.  It's nothing fancy but for the price they ask and being in upper Manhattan, you can't beat it. The bed itself is now a full mattress that's lofted with some underbed storage compartments for keeping your stuff out of sight. There's drapes that you can enclose around the bed area to give you privacy, and Gaudhi's family is very respectful about letting you be and not disturb you when you're ready to go to bed. Overrall I had a great time in NYC, and felt very at home at Gaudhi's place after being out on the town all day. Harlem was very chill, and calm to walk around and explore in, and the convenient subway lines allowed me to make me way down Manhattan, going from Harlem to the Upper West or East Side, and keeping on down. In short, expect few amenities, nothing fancy, but cozy and highly recommend.

Gaudhi and his family are very nice people. The problem is that the window in the room does not keep any noises or smoke outside of the appartment. Extremely hard to sleep even with the earplugs. I saw some drug trading so this also made me feel uncomfortable. Luckily it is pretty near to the metro station. Gaudhi kept good connection with me and was very kind.

Pros: Great location host is VERY responsive. I locked myself out and he gave clear instructions how to gain access.  Cons: Apartment is not in building shown in pictures it's down an alley way in the back. Dirty linen blood on the pillow, roaches in the kitchen, patio area couldn't be enjoyed floor boards come up in a dangerous way when try to walk and cloth furniture soaked from the rain. couches and chair in the living room torn with tape all over. living room glass table balanced by tissue so you can't place anything on it or it will topple over.   The space has great potential but I'd definitely not recommend it until there are improvements.

Everything was perfect... And according to the value... I felt super comfortable... I would not hesitate to return to the same place if I return to New York... The best thing is the subway, it is very close and in a few minutes you can reach the places of interest... The central park is one block away... There are laundromats and supermarkets a few meters from the apartment... I must also highlight that at first I thought the neighborhood was unsafe, but as long as you continue on your way no one bothers... Maybe a little noise at night... But nothing that interferes with the stay from this chaotic and beautiful city.... I'm leaving happy :)

Good for the location (close to the subway and shops) and price. The bed is different to what is in the photo (a cushion on top of a counter). The smell of drugs wafts through the window almost every night and crazy people talking on the sidewalk are also common at this time. Host sometimes comes in and makes noise in the "room" in the early hours of the morning. The price is justified due to the defects, which were acceptable to me.

Bradley was very welcoming and his place is just like in the pictures. It's perfect even for four people and has a grocery store right around the corner and even more stores, delis, bars and restaurants just 1.5 blocks away. Als9 the g-train is just a 10 min walk away and don't be afraid to use the 62 or 57 bus to metro-tech which both have bus stops right around the corner. When we arrrived it was really hot in New York and Bradley just installed a completely new AC for us (plus one huge fan). One evening Bradley even offered to have a little barbeque in his small but lovely backyard and we had an absolutely amazing evening. Thanks again :) I highly recommend Bradley and his apartment.

I'm really glad that I chose to stay at Alexi & Dennis' place during my month long holiday in NYC. Their home is true to the description and picture. Alexi has made sure I had space to put my belongings (which was quite a bit given  that I was in NYC for another 2 months before I moved to theirs), and got what I needed.  The neighbourhood is safe and has lots of cafes and restaurants. I often came home in the early morning hours and never felt unsafe. There's a taco van that is always there on my way back from the station so I was never hungry at night! The location is very easy to get to Manhattan, too - 3 stops or about $20 taxi which is similar to a taxi ride from UES to Midtown.  They also have a lovely dog Troy - which is big in size but very very gentle in his demeanour!!   All in all, I've enjoyed my stay very much and would definitely recommend it!

I stayed 9 days.  On the last day of my stay (saturday) at about 11am, i recieved an email from the host through airbnb (she had my number but chose to email), in her email, she said:  "Hi Priya, I am not sure if you are home or not but just wanted to touch base about check out tomorrow which is at 11am. I will be leaving at 5pm and won't be back tonight. I hope you enjoyed your stay. We do have another guest checking in after you, so I will be having the room cleaned exactly at 11am. Thanks, Alexi"  to which i politely replied and thanked her for her hospitality.  her email clearly stated she would not be returning that night, and obviously gave the impression her return would be after I left the next morning. i observe a common practice of locking any apt/house door wherever i am before going to sleep, especially in a new unknown place.  Went to bed around 1am on saturday night, locked the door, thinking of my own safety.  I woke up the next morning and left the keys on the dining table when I left, texting to let her know.  She replied rudely saying she was locked out last night and had to use her "small wrists" to undo the slam lock, "it wasnt a nice feeling to be locked out of her apartment by a stranger."  while I can understand that sentiment, she made it clear she wasn't coming back that night and her guest bedroom in which i stayed, was located at the opposite end of the apartment. With the ac running inside it, no activity at the front door can be heard, especially when a guest is sleeping.  Her replies indicated she had, in fact, returned in the middle of the night, called my name, and "woke up the entire building, except me" with the dog barking nearby. (a dog upstairs barks whenever someone enters the building, it's not out of the ordinary).   Why she did not send a text/make a phone call instead of calling my name aloud/emailing, i didnt understand, this woman had my number.  It was beyond ridiculous that I should compromise my own safety and well-being to leave the door open for the host/or stay up to let her in at 4 or 5am (whenever she came back) after being explicitly told she would not be returning until after i left the next morning.    there was one night when a big black suv sat outside the apartment for many hours with two gentlemen sitting inside it the entire time. so that was pretty creepy as well.  other than this, my stay was fine, but it wasnt a necessarily great neighborhood and theres construction going on across the street.   i'd say, given more options, look for another more hassle-free place if possible. avoid yourself the headache i was caused.

This was a great place to crash after long days of visiting friends, hanging in the city, and braving the cold. Very nice and cozy. The bed was super comfy (pillow top- yes please!) and the kitchen was perfect. The hosts and their kid are very sweet and welcoming. I'd stay here again due to having everything a traveler could need and for the price. It's actually a steal. Thanks again Brad and Natasha.

Miriam is a top notch host. My team’s experience from booking through departure was flawlessly simple. The house had everything our team needed to relax and unwind from long stressful days of auditing. Highly recommend. Thank you Miriam for everything.

This Airbnb is beautiful!  It was beautifully decorated, comfortable, and clean.  Even with only two bathrooms, it was the perfect size for our party of 11, we made it work!  Miriam had informed me that our party was the first one booked in the last 18 months because of the pandemic (she had switched to long term rental) - said we might encounter a few snafus, which we did, but Miriam was quick to provide solutions.  Her speed in returning messages was greatly appreciated.  About the Airbnb, it was very clean & beautifully decorated.  All of us slept very comfortable.  At no time did we feel unsafe, the neighborhood is a nice one, a school, I believe an elementary, is right across the street.  Restaurants, coffee shops, bars, grocery stores & even a laundry mat if you’re not one to venture in the basement :). But most important, the subway is within walking distance & will get you anywhere you need to go. You will not be disappointed with this Airbnb, I would book it again!

Todd's apartment is in a charming old-school building on the fringe of Inwood. The building is clean, remarkably quiet (as is the neighborhood) and safe with older neighbors smiling wide and wishing us well.  Parking is incredibly easy. Directly in front of the building, NYC's notorious Alternate Side of the Street Parking is in effect once a week. That's just divine intervention.  The Dyckman Street A train is two blocks away, as are markets, coffee shops, the library (about six blocks) and drug stores... The apartment itself is nicely furnished, clean, comfortable and provides more than enough room for four (queen bed / sofa bed). For us, the shower was a little meh... but, it was clean with fresh towels and soap provided and NOT in any way a deterrent from our wanting to book again.  The kitchen is typical tiny little kitchen with basic cooking utensils provided.  A very nice dining table and four chairs is on one side of the living room while on the other is the sofa bed, large chair, table, tv...  Any questions or concerns we had were promptly handled by our host.  Key pick up and drop off was easy, very convenient and quick, while a little unconventional for me.  I suggest chatting about the process prior to finalizing your reservation.  And while we never met in person, Todd and I did speak over the phone and texted making communication smooth and effortless.  If the space is available, I'd gladly stay again if he'll have us.

Todd was very pleasant to work with. He provided instructions before our stay that made our check in very easy and stress free. The apartment was clean and super comfortable even though we didn't spend much time in it(sight seeing) . I would definitely  recommend booking with Todd. This was my first time booking through airbnb and I am so happy I did.

Staying at Todd's was like a homecoming of sorts for me, because I lived in the building next door over 30 years ago. It seemed very familiar to me as a result and representative of the feel of the neighbourhood, which is part of the allure of airbnb. You will never get a feel for Washington Heights staying in, say, a Holiday Inn. Not throwing shade on the hotel chain, which I've had the pleasure of staying in on multiple occasions over the years.  Just a realization that living like a local is part of the immersion experience that makes travelling far more visceral and memorable.  At check-in, I had the pleasure of meeting Angela, Todd's cleaning lady, who had just finished up, so I knew the place would be clean. And it was.  "Cozy and comfortable" is how I would describe it. Some nice touches in the living room, such as an oversized couch, throw pillows, a large TV with a wide variety of channels and an electric piano.  In the kitchen, there was a nice selection of alcohol (although I refrained) and an appropriate array of appliances and supplies (e.g. aluminum foil) for home cooking.  The bed was very comfortable. I slept like a baby. And, despite staying over on Friday and Saturday nights, street noise was not an issue.  Quiet.  Location is great. Trains are a short walking distance away (e.g. 2 blocks to the A station), bus stops nearby, and a plethora of restaurants, bars, grocery stores, banks, hair and nail salons and more.  The shower worked just fine (always a plus) and last, but not least, the service was exceptional, with Todd keeping in touch every step of the way pre, during and post-stay.  We had an almost comical Facetime exchange on day #1 with yours truly being walked through the TV set up to access the channels. While not a Luddite, my relationship with unfamiliar TV remotes and TV systems has always been a bit like Charlie Brown, his kite and a tree. But Todd walked me through it, such that I didn't require a follow-up lesson.  I'm looking forward to my return stay here next year.

My boyfriend and I staid at S&G's apartment for four nights. The location was amazing, close to everything. East village is one of the most vivid neighborhoods. There are lots of cozy places around (bars, cafes, restaurants). We were afraid that the street noise would not let us sleep (because of other comments but this was not the case. The room was very cozy, a bit small though (but we already knew that). Both Shala and Guillermo were really friendly and ready to help us. We would definitely recommend the apartment.

Excellent organization, arrival in the middle of the night due to a flight delay but everything is planned to be able to enter the apartment without worries, the room is very bright and comfortable, a little away from the rest of the rooms so good privacy, and impeccable apartment in terms of cleaning. Very quiet, despite the location in the heart of a great, very lively neighborhood. There is everything you need nearby, including the metro.

Having a place to yourself across from a park is a steal in NYC. Todd is friendly, responsive, and the apartment is just as described. I was able to do my remote work, run to Starbucks in less than 10 minutes, and get on the A train (which is a great subway line for getting most places in the city) in just minutes. You can't go wrong.

Lovely, clean apartment in a great location!  Modern and uncluttered, which makes it feel pretty spacious for Manhattan.  Central Park (perfect for a morning run), Whole Foods, drugs stores, and subway stations all near by.  Easy walking distance to Rockefeller Center, MoMA, Times Square, and Broadway theaters.    The neighbors were very helpful when we had some trouble unlocking the door on arrival, and the doormen were always pleasant and helpful as well.   Raees and Nida are wonderful hosts!  They were very communicative throughout our booking process (which was last minute) and our stay.  The house manual was comprehensive and easy to follow, and their restaurant recommendations were appreciated.

The three of us absolutely loved staying at Brandon's place for the weekend. There was plenty of room for each of us to have our own beds, and the linens and towels were very high quality, the beds very comfortable. the place is perfectly located in a great Brooklyn neighborhood steps away from shopping and fantastic restaurants. I arrived by myself at 8:30 at night and I didn't feel unsafe at all. Brandon response almost immediately to all messages. And he was so kind and generous to accommodate some special requests that we made of him. I'm absolutely sure that we will go back and rent from Brandon again!

At first Brooklyn was very close, she was tracking us to be home once we get there, she gave us all the needed instructions to get by subway (it is really close to B,C and 2,3 lines).  She is pretty nitty, all was in place and exactly as promised. The house is warm and cozy, still well ventilated. It is a first floor, so a bit noisy (you get used to it).   The neighborhood is secure, scary at first (we got to NYC at night), but all the people is nice and don't mind others business.   Staying at Brooklyn's was one of the best choice we made for the trip.

S & G’s space was the perfect home base for a traveler’s first trip to NYC. I cannot stress enough how perfect the location is— the street itself is beautiful to sit on the steps and look out to, but you’re also within walking distance of some of the most renowned bars and restaurants. Amazing space, wonderful hosts. ✨

We had a great time in the 2 weeks we stayed at Brooklyn's place; it was super clean when we arrived, and Brooklyn didn't mind us being a bit late than expected because of getting turned around on the subway! She did drop by 3 times in the first 3 days to pick things up. Kitchen was well equipped with lots and pans; great gas stove as well. Was a little lacking in basic spices/seasonings (no extra sugar, no flour, baking powder, garlic powder, things like that. It did have a few different seasonings in the cupboards). Also no coffee pot, but there is a Dunkin Donuts around the corner. The bed was super comfortable, it was amazing to come home to after a day exploring the city. There was a bit of noise in the hallway and outside the building nightly. They're super respectful, and if you ask them to move their party, they relocate without any problems. :) the apartment is really well located, about 2-3 minutes from the red line, and about 5 minutes from the blue line. We never felt unsafe walking at any time, day or night. Made the city really accessible. Taking everything into consideration, the positives car outweighed the minor inconvenience of a little extra noise; we were happy with our choice, and would stay here again if ever back in NYC!

Thank you Brooklyn for the bottle of wine, clean sheets, clean apartment, prompt response and going the extra mile just to make sure I get to your apartment safe. Your generosity went a real long way.   The apartment was located in the middle of a few metro station which made traveling smooth and easy.   There were eateries, grocery stores, laundry service, pharmacy which are all walking distance.   No unpleasant noise not even during NYE which made the stay extra comfortable.   The neighbourhood is not a fancy set up but throughout my stay I was comfortable and felt generally safe.   Overall I truly enjoyed my stay and going back to Brooklyn’s apartment really felt like heading home.

We went to New York over New Years time. The apartment was a perfect option as a stay since it's a good place to escape from the stress in the city. We got a lot of help offered so there haven't been any problems regarding the stay, taxis, restaurants etc. City island is a beautiful place and the apartment is right at the waterside so I bet it's a great place to spend summer. We enjoyed the stay very much! Thank you Noelva and Alex and many greetings from Germany!

We were visiting my husband's mother in a nursing home in the Bronx, NY which can be very stressful.  We found Alex's place on City Island and were thrilled at what we found!  The apartment is located right on the water, it is clean, comfortable, stylish and peaceful.  There is a beautiful new kitchen for cooking, we did not see a coffee maker so we asked our host and one was waiting for us the next day!  The bedroom was super with down comforters and a great mattress after a long day.  We highly recommend this apartment for all,  The Host was more than welcoming and accommodating..thank you Alma & Alex!

The room was just as described. The place a quiet, and the tv/microwave in the room was very convenient.   The location was very close to the J line (maybe 4 blocks, if even) where you can either ride to Manhattan (a tad less than an hour)  The host, Antonio, was great! Very nice, helpful (guided me from the train, and helped me calm down after a very stressful day.)  Lastly, the bathroom was VERY clean! (Definitely a plus)

The apartment is soo beautiful. Just like you can see in the piture. Kerri was very helpful, even though we didnt manage to meet each other. She replied to all my question.  It is only a twenty minute walk from the apartment to the subway. I stayed there by myself. So the first night when I went I was a bit scared to walk home from the subway station. But the second day not anymore. The area is very save even for a lonely girl.  I would recommend the apartment to anybody who stay longer than 3 days in New York. Otherwise you should take a closer apartment to Manhatten so see everything in Manhatten. All in all the apartment is nice, charming, very clean and the bed is veryyy comfortable.  Thanks for hosting me.
Erin was a spectacular host. It was perfect for what my wife and I needed and the location can't be beat (check out the little Italian place right next door!). Totally stress free and quite comfy.

I stayed at Tom and Lily's place for six weeks.  It was an absolutely amazing experience. The apartment is exactly as shown in the pictures. Absolutely beautiful and filled with light. It was very very clean, thoughtfully furnished and equipped, so that everything I needed was already there. Tom checked in regularly to see if everything was fine. The location of the apartment made my stay even better. Even though I had to commute to Manhattan every day, the subway station is right around the corner and the L line was just perfect to get anywhere I needed to be. The neighborhood was stunning. Apart from the beautiful street art everywhere and the great restaurants and bars I never felt unsafe walking home in the dark (of course while being as cautious as any person should be in larger cities). If you are looking for a genuine Brooklyn experience in a beautiful loft and don't mind meeting new people that will be sharing the apartment with you, then this is the right place to go to!   I would always come back here, thank you for everything!

Jessy's place was as described - close to transit, restaurants, and Times Square. Loved that it is only 1 floor up from the ground.  We arrived while she was cleaning up after the previous guests and saw her changing the sheets. The place was clean (see below though). The chain in the toilet tank broke during our stay and she had it fixed within a few hours. All communications were prompt.  Only concerns were that mice were spotted several times, but this is to be expected in an old building in an old city. Nothing to do with Jessy's place, but the building itself. There were no droppings anywhere and the mice were more afraid of us than we were of them. Also, people in the building were not fond of those they don't recognize. Thirdly, there was a metal rail on the floor by the sofa bed and the corner sticks up a bit - my friend tore her slippers on it. Other than those three things and the wifi being spotty, the place was as expected.

Location is perfect as noted in the description. But, the host responded to me very rudely, telling me that I need to just go home and some therapy. She is a very unkind and irresponsible host for the issues that I reported to her several times. I was very unpleasant during the stay. She did not apologize or took any good attitude at all. I am a traveler and she is the worst host ever in my travel life.

Hello everyone. To not forget anything and to be objective, I start at the beginning. After collecting the keys in a box, as is often done in New York, we enter the apartment. Very well located geographically, clean, on the other hand, noisy is an understatement. The feeling of sleeping on the street. After three days, it gets bad. A message telling me that we are being evicted, and that we must move before 10 a.m., subject to court proceedings. There, through messages, Jessy tells us that she is going to take our luggage to put it in another apartment and that we must collect the keys, this time from a garage or someone under a pseudonym............. I stop the car, worthy of a James Bond film. I point out that I still have not met Jessy. I refuse. We preferred to waste our morning, but to know where we were going to land. At 10 a.m., an angry woman burst into the apartment, without knocking or ringing (with her spare keys), not a hello, and urged us to go out to go to another address. after a 10 minute journey with our suitcases through the streets without care, at a very fast pace, here we are in front of our new address. Clean apartment, but very quiet this time. We take our new quarters, with I admit, given his insistent recommendations for discretion, the fear of being expelled again. The rest of the stay went very well, until departure where, after a second very cold welcome, we had the impression of being quickly kicked out. not a GOODBYE OR A SAFE TRIP RETURN, we collected our luggage between the legs of the new tenants, not very gracious, not very comprehensive, bordering on unpleasant. Waiting a little half an hour more would not have changed much for them. Finally, courtesy is not everyone's daily life. As for Jessy, renting and taking money is simple, but for vacationers, we expect more friendliness, courtesy, kindness, not to say politeness. To conclude and be very objective, the second apartment value for money, good. if you are not afraid of finding yourself on the street in the middle of your stay, at the mercy of the good will of Jessy who will certainly go out of her way to find you other accommodation, without you having a choice of course (good or bad surprise). plan an international subscription, because otherwise, you risk a nice surprise when you return from your day of walking. And finally, if Jessy is only doing this for the money, which I believe, given his borderline unpleasant attitude, and given the rest of the experience, I would not recommend either your host or .......... sergil

Jessy’s place is very well located,  closed to Times Square (15 min walk) and to a lot of good restaurants. One issue was the cleanliness . I had to clean a little because the previous guests used the bathroom before they left and the host was already gone. In the living-room we couldn’t close the window and we heard mice in the courtyard. The beds in the living-room are not really beds they are leather coach pretty uncomfortable. The pipes make a strange noice but overall the place is super quiet. I think Jessy’s place is more made for 2 since you don’t have a lot of privacy with the shower  in the kitchen. Our stay was ok at Jessy’s place even if we were a little bit afraid of being expelled. It was nice to be able to cook and to stay closed to Times Square. Jessy gave good tips of what to do in the area and was very responsive.

This is the perfect I’m just looking for a place to sleep and keep my stuff place. It was clean, safe, and relatively quiet. It is close to the subway. A few of the procedures seem stressful but are totally doable when you get there. If you are a heavier person the bathroom is a bit small but it’s New York.

The room and entire apartment was very nice and clean! The room was better than I had imagined. I had minimal interactions with the other guest but I was only there to sleep. The only negative is the location, although the trains were within 5-10min walk away, it did feel slightly unsafe to walk alone when I got back late one night. Other than that, the apartment was amazing, everything is there, easy check-in.

YooMi place is as I expected. The best location in Williamsburg & the entire Brooklyn. It is safe to walk around even after midnight and surrounded by drug stores, cafes, Whole Food & a Sephora by foot steps. YooMi was easy and a very nice host. The place is stylish and super convenient. Bathroom is spacious and clean

The place is really good for few days, the location is good and the room is clean and big. Herman is nice and he helped me with my luggage at my check in. I would suggest the room for short term! But keep in mind:  #1 Don't leave any kind of food outside the fridge  #2 Unfortunately the window is right over a warehouse and few nights (i would guess 7 nights on 15 of my stay) there is a download of huge piece and all the process is really really loud. If you are not too afraid of noise you can solved the problem with earplugs as i did, don't forget to buy them! :)  #3 When i arrived all the house was clean but after 1 week the standard become lower and the last 3 days I found the bathroom unclean (shower and sink)
He did not let me in the apartment and then asking me to cancel. It is a SCAM!

For the very affordable price you get great accommodation with a central location to 2 different subway lines, which makes commuting to Manhattan or the remaining parts of W'burg or Bushwick very easy and quick. The surroundings seem a little unsafe, but in fact you can move around without any problems even in the evenings. There are a few cafes and delis within walking distance. The door lock at the entrance to the house gets stuck here and there and the stairwell smells a little, but these are things that you can ignore.

Nice locations, nice room, great value :) I can get subway within 10 min walk and the county seems not so dangerous. House are always clean and lovely, nice host and his friend always concern the guest. Fast communications also!  혼자 다녀서 걱정했는데 일단 맨하탄까지 지하철이나 버스로 이용할수 있는 루트도 많고 밤에 걸어다녀도 그다지 위험하지 않은 동네인 것 같아요. 강아지가 매우 귀엽습니다 스트레스 받을까 걱정했는데 슬슬 만져주면 매우 다정해져요 😍😍
Beautiful, clean house that we enjoyed staying here.They have a dog here so if you have allergy or scared of dog, be mindful of that :) other than that, it was great!

Jennifer herself was quite friendly but there were way too many people sharing one bathroom. We cleaned the toilet seat so many times cuz it was dirty. Building has a really gross smell. Dog poop in the corridor nobody bothered to pick up. Gotta say that the building is not safe at all. Was waiting in the lobby & heard a man yelling, lady crying, ppl running like there’s a fight going on, quite scary, had to run back upstairs. I told jennifer and she asked me never to use the stairs which clearly means the building’s not very safe. Me and my sister were wating for the elevator and a guy kept staring at my sister which made her really uncomfortable, I looked back at him but he dint even bother to look away. Booked this place cuz the Gun Hill rd subway was close but there were so many shady people at this station, one guy kept bothering me & then tried to hug my sister she literally had to push him away. Had to spend so much on Uber cuz we couldn’t use subway at night for safety reasons.
The space was decent. The price was good. The area is a little sketchy. Wouldn’t recommend for women traveling alone especially at night.

Kumar is a 5/5 host! We wish we could give him a 5 star rating, but we did have issues with the humidity. An investment in a bigger dehumidifier would have made all of the difference.   Keep in mind this room is very close to Harlem which can be a bit scary to walk to travel through at night. Would not stay here by myself but with someone else, it was fine. It’s also super close to several subway stations!   Thank you Kumar!

Kumar's place was better than we expected. The furniture is brand new and vibe is homey and clean. We can find everything we need there. The amenities and stuffs provided are thoughtful and in good quality. Location wise also close to subway and bus,  and located in a warm neighborhood (definitely not the dangerous harlem we thought at first)  Kumar is a nice and communicative host, he invited us for coffee and we had a nice chat with him

The place was okay. Cheap but the area is a bit shady. Only stay in this area if you know the New York area.  The hospitality needs improvement. As only 2 large towels and 2 small towels were provided for a 6 day trip.  The bed was not comfortable. It was old and made noises each time we moved in the bed.  All in all, the place is a bargain but you get what you pay for.
Yves is a super chill dude. No stress, easy check in, clean room, clean bathroom. Enjoyed my short stay!

I’ve stayed in a quite a few Airbnb’s and Salisha’s was by far the best one - being super clean, convenience, and even safety. We walked in, and instead of feeling like we were in someone’s home, it felt like a super comfy 5 star hotel suite. I would highly recommend to anyone looking for a place that’s not only accessible to greater NYC, but is also placed smack dab in the middle of its own adorable Brooklyn neighborhood.  Close to subways, restaurants, and scam TARGET. And street parking was easy for us to find.

This is a perfect simple no-frills basement studio in a safe and convenient corner of Manhattan. This is a rare affordable find in NYC, I was happy with my stay. It was exactly as expected, description and photos are accurate.   I even had the pleasure of accepting Kumar’s offer for a cup of coffee to meet him and say hello. He’s a great host and takes good care of his building.   Ignore the reviews that say this is an “unsafe” area. I had no problems at all walking around late at night, never felt uncomfortable at all. Hamilton Heights is a diverse and vibrant NYC neighborhood, well worth exploring what it offers.

Great host with awesome hospitality! It’s in a very nice quiet location, very close to the subway station, going into manhattan was really convenient. I would strongly suggest this place and the host for such a price it’s a steal.

Kumars place was just as described, however there were some issues. The key kept getting stuck where we couldn’t even open the door. As 2 young women being stuck outside at 10pm felt really unsafe and it was freezing. The shower door wouldn’t close all the way so water was dripping from under the door so by the time I was done, the whole floor was soaked. Kumar was very helpful and answered my calls quickly and came out to help us both nights we were there. He emailed me and made sure we had a smooth check in which made me feel great since he is the first host to ever do that. I will definitely come here again and recommend Kumars place once these issues are fixed :) thank you for your help!

Yves is very friendly and helpful host. Don't be afraid of his dog. She is the most lovely dog you'll ever meet. The apartment was clean and very well maintained. The shared space that includes kitchen and living room was very big and comfortable. There is even a balcony from which you can see the highest of the Manhattan's skyscrapers. Be careful of the mosquitos as unfortunately there ara no meshes in the windows (but AC works so you may have no need to open the window). The location is very good as well. Bus stop is just next to the apartment and subway which takes you directly to the Times Square in less than 15 minutes is just 10 minutes walk away.

First of all, I was a bit apprehensive about staying at an Airbnb especially one this cheap. I was scared the place might not be as described or that I could be putting myself in an unsafe situation.   But Uri’s place is EXACTLY as described. It is also super clean and doesn’t have any funny odors, unlike some hotels I’ve stayed at. It is literally around the corner from the subway station (about 1-2 minute leisurely walk). It is located in a mostly Jewish residential neighborhood in South Central Brooklyn and has a lot of local shops and restaurants nearby. Just keep in mind, that a few restaurants in the area are cash only.   The neighborhood felt safe and the apartment was super quiet. You would occasionally hear some cars outside (like anywhere else) and I could hear what I think was the heater but trust me, you will not have a noisy stay at all and I think I was probably louder than all of the noises combined.  If you’re worried about distance to Manhattan, don’t be. If you think transportation will cost you more than what you’re saving by booking this place, it won’t; not unless you’re Ubering everywhere. Simply buy an unlimited weekly metro card for $34 and you’re good to go. It doesn’t take long to get to Manhattan and it only took me about 45 minutes to get to the Times Square area during busy hours and about 25-30 minutes to get to Lower Manhattan. You can get to the apartment from JFK in under an hour (about 40-55 minutes with wait times) if you use the Air Train and a combination of LIRR and the subway.   The beds are super comfortable and the WiFi worked perfectly. I would say, if you have mobility issues of any kind, keep in mind that you have to go down a set of narrow stairs to get to the apartment. It is only like 6 steps or so but I know that might be a problem for some.   All in all, I don’t think there’s a better deal out there than Uri’s place. It is cheap and you get a private space that’s really clean and has a comfortable bed + easy access to public transportation. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend his place to anyone going to New York.

Overall we had a great experience at Marlee's place. When checking in there was a mix up with the keys, but we were able to drop our luggage off and go explore the city, then come back later and get into our room. Other than that, her and her roommates were very accomodating. They checked up on us to see if we had everything we needed often and gave us their second bathroom to ourselves. The apartment was just a few blocks away from the subway, and it was an easy 30 minute ride from the L train to Manhattan. We read some things about Bushwick being a dangerous neighborhood before visiting but never once felt unsafe walking around at night. The room was a great deal and we'd stay again! Was a great spot for someone visiting the city for the first time!

Uri’s apartment was so cozy and peaceful. It was in a nice safe location. I never felt unsafe. It’s a quiet neighborhood; parking was easily found on the street. Host was excellent with communication always checked on us. Check in was extremely easy and checkout process as well. I liked he had very simplistic rules, easy to follow and more than reasonable! Will stay again in the future!

The place next door was abandoned so every time we walk pass at night to go in the house it was really creepy cause the door was open. It rained & the Next morning it was ants EVERYWHERE I hate ants I almost passed out seeing so many but Kumar came right down to spray them. They were all over our clothes table literally everything. I think the family lives upstairs so you can hear every foot step someone takes .. so if you can deal with all that it’s a great place to stay .. right next to food & subway.

A really good place in Brooklyn, we thought that it would be some dangerous because of the neighborhood, however it was really safe and there was a neighbor’s market around the corner. The subway and bus station was really close around 4 blocks. All was very good during our days staying in Thais&Luiz’s place! Highly recommended to enjoy a NYC experience!

The apartment unit is super clean and cozy but spacious enough for one or two people.  The high floor unit advantage gives a great open view of city lights.  The apartment building has handful of great amenities including indoor full-size basketball court and newly equipped gym.  The host, Ricardo is very attentive to his guest to make sure that the guest will be stress-free from the check-in to check-out.   He is super easy to communicate with and responsive to my inquiries quickly.  Thank you for your warmth!
Great place, shift sketchy neighbourhood, but very close to subway

5 stars! 5 stars!! 5 stars!!! This place was  so nice!! Judith and her sister were the perfect hosts!! They provided everything we needed and more. The place was spotless and so comfortable. I felt like I was at home. This was a steal for the price!! Highly recommend!!

Judith and Sonia's apartment is PERFECTLY equipped for 4 people! It is super clean, spacious, homely and is right around the corner from the Shepard Avenue metro station, from where you can get to midtown Manhattan in a maximum of 40 minutes on the C line! The WiFi worked perfectly at all times, communication with Judith and Sonia worked great and they always replied very quickly! All the usual shops for daily needs can be found in the surrounding area, and Judith and Sonia had also filled the fridge with drinks and other small items in advance. Coffee and tea were always refilled for us. We recommend the apartment without hesitation and will definitely book again if we travel to New York again. Thank you very much again for allowing us to leave our suitcases with you after the official check out and thus saving us a lot of stress on the last day! A wonderful AirBnB experience and THIS is how everyone should be a host! Would give 10 stars if it worked! Kind regards from Germany

The house was excellent and as described. The communication and check-in was beyond easy and on point. The metro station was just a short walk away (6-7 mins).  The neighborhood is a typical NYC neighborhood, if you are looking for Park Ave. This isn't it. I took my 7 y/o daughter with me and we never felt unsafe walking around or taking the subway/bus at anytime. I would recommend this spot to anyone looking for a place.

1. I didn’t not have a good stay because she stayed coming upstairs bothering me & my guest 2. We got there on time check in was at 6:00pm we didn’t check in until 7:05pm 3. The remotes was removed the 2nd day me & my guest was there 4. Anybody that came in the unit as (guest) she would bother .. 5. She have a room with bedsheets that are pink i am a gay male & she said “ this room must be for you “ which was offense. 6. My guest heard one of the host walking slow up the stairs to “ spy “ she looked throw the peep whole & the “ host “ tried to run down the stairs! this was one of my first experiences working with AIRBNB & this was an unpleasant stay for me!
This air BnB is great and to our surprise the owner lives right down the stairs. The area is a bit shady especially at night. But overall the experience was good.

This place sits right in the heart of the action of the city in Hell's Kitchen, mid-town, the upper west side.  You're close to trains, cabs, restaurants and shopping. It's a classic New York City apartment, with exposed brick in the bedrooms that add a touch of old school class.    The apartment is small but perfect for a few people, with its two bedrooms.  One of the bedrooms is close to the street so if you aren't used to sleeping with the sounds of the city it might be a slight challenge, if you're a light sleeper.  Fortunately, I lived in New York for many years so it felt like home, even with the sounds of the street.  The owner also smartly leaves ear plugs for guests, just in case, but I didn't need them.  The second bedroom is away from the street and very quiet.  The host is incredibly responsive and I would highly recommend this place as a steal if you aren't planning to spend all day in your apartment and you just need a place to crash after a night or two out on in the city, or after a day of business meetings and networking.

Sonia is a very particular host.  She comes in everyday to pick up the garbage and does not have a set time for this pickup. Expect for the host to come at various times to do this. I have my suspicion she just likes to keep an eye on the apartment and the air conditioner which is why she insists on picking up “nonexistent garbage”.   In a span of 24 hours, the host came in 2x times to pick up the garbage (yet there was very minimal garbage) and attempted to talk to me a third time. It felt intrusive as I’m a very reserved person and just wanted to relax.   The host provided keys to the apartment but on 3 separate occasions she locked the front door with a bolt and had to personally let me in. I’m not sure if this is due to safety issues in the neighborhood or her own preference in letting guests into the apartment. Either way, felt a little like asking your parents to let you into your own home. On one occasion, a relative of hers (not Judith Or Sonia) opened the door and had the meanest look on her face and did not say one word to me. It was unbelievably awkward and added to my negative experience.   Upon arriving you will be required to listen to a 20 min review of the rules that are already listed on the app. Despite us driving 16 hours to get to our airbnb and not having slept, she continued her spiel. Again, she’s very particular about her airbnb and the rules.   She complained that I kept the air on when I left the apartment. I explained my reasoning for having them on was that it was 90 degrees on an August day and if I turned off the AC it would be unbearably hot. It would take a while for the apartment to cool back up again. The next day after she complained, she came out to meet my bf in the hallway to say “it’s a nice day out, you can open the windows today”.  Clearly, she has a preoccupation with the electricity bill which is unfair to transfer that pressure on the guests. If you cannot relinquish control then being an airbnb host is not for you. Overall, these incidents just left a bad taste in my mouth. The airbnb was in a less than stellar neighborhood and right in front of a junkyard.    I’ve been nothing but a great guest who follows all the rules so I don’t understand why she needed to hover over us.
What an amazing low stress experience and great alternative to local hotels. Brady’s ‘super host’ status is well deserved.

Travelers can expect a large room, great security, a bathroom and kitchen shared only with a great son. The home is clean and in a lively, safe and secure neighborhood within 7 minutes walking time to the A and 1 train, 1 minute to the bus lines, Several grocery,and drug stores and dozens of great restaurants and bars.

We stayed at Akon’s place for 4 nights. It’s in a good location, close to Broadway and Central Park, although the nearest subway station is a 10 minute walk.
