The apartment is small, as I suspect all apartments in central Manhattan are, however all the necessaries are provided. Akon was great to work with, always a quick response and very helpfully, he enabled us to drop our bags early and collect the keys prior to check-in.

Brenda was a great host! I would highly recommend her studio for a 2 person stay. it's about a 7-8 min walk to the subway and the neighborhood was very quiet. Church Ave can look scary or weird at night, but from our experience the locals were friendly and helpful if needed.

Ilgins apartment is stylish, comfortable, clean and in a prime location.   This spot is within close walking distance of some of the best bars, restaurants and shops in Williamsburg. Not to mention that her room has one of the best views of the Manhattan skyline you find for the anything remotely near the price. Directly across from a park that has weekly food and wine pop ups. A large balcony for activities :)   The room is beautifully decorated and has the touch of a designer. It was neat, clean, and has a powerful fan/ac for when the Williamsburg heat gets unbearable in the spring.  Her roommates were extremely gracious, fun, helpful and interesting. I genuinely enjoyed their company. Very willing to share common spaces and, just generally accommodating and respectful.   This place is an absolute steal - - do not pass it up if you have the opportunity.   Thanks Ilgin!

I was very pleased with how responsive Akon was to all my questions, as I had concerns about all the stories about Airbnb scams on the news. But he's a real guy, very friendly and his place lived up to all the descriptions. Pleasant NYC neighborhood within walking distance to Broadway, Central Park and many entertainment options. We were pleased with the space, the location and the owners were very nice.

Anna's place was beautifully decorated and comfortable. She had terrific communication, a couple personal touches for my wife and I on our honeymoon, and made the process the easiest it's ever been for me and Airbnb.  The home is located near a Subway station and is easily accessible. Like most places in Brooklyn you will need to be careful at night, but never did we feel unsafe or uncomfortable. I would stay again when visiting NYC.

Jackee's place was an absolute joke. The pictures online do not describe or show the place at all. The place is beyond small. The pictures give an allusion that it is larger. The description states 1.5 bathrooms we never found the .5 bath. The walls were empty and the place had no charm. The description stated oasis it was far from that. The picture of the front porch leads to her house. She lives on the property. If I had known that I would not have stayed there. It is not an entire place with someone living at an arms length with access through an adjacent door. Jackee called at 830 pm inquiring where I was at like a mother would. I did not know this place had a curfew. Upon arrival Jackee met us at the door before I was able to enter the code. We felt violated. Why do you need to met me at the door (hotels dont do that). We have stayed in several other Airbnb places and neither of the things listed above happened. I accidentally clicked on 1 guest in reality it was 2. Jackee asked about it. I explained the situation she said no problem she would take care of the modifications. She did alright. Jackee proceeded to underhandly have us thrown out a day early. Two people 8 hours from home in NYC. Beyond low. I believe she did this because we came home around 11 pm from sight seeing in the Manhattan and had adult relations. Maybe she heard us I dont know. She turned the wifi off that night so we were unable to watch television and were forced to go to bed. Jackee previously in the day emailed if we needed anything. I replied no maam. I assume the coming in 11 and adult relations upset her. Jackee attempted to ruin our trip but didnt. I would never stay at her place again. I would not recommend this place to anyone. The location was horrible in a sketchy part of Brooklyn. You have walk half a mile to a subway stop. She acted very unprofessional.
It was a little creepy at night but but host and his mother showed a great amount of hospitality

This place is so neat! I was worried because it was in Brooklyn but it is right by the subway. There are enough convenience stores within walking distance and didn’t feel unsafe. The place is so homey and had no issues during our stay. Would most definitely stay there again and highly recommend!

This place is a SCAM. Disgusting place, horrible host, will steal your money for even ONE night. I do NOT suggest staying here AT ALL not even under any circumstances even if your living on dirt. You will get robbed from your time and money and please take this review in consideration before booking with this Host.

Our family of 5 enjoyed staying in Beth's apartment. The kitchen had everything we needed. The beds were very comfortable, the decorations were stylish and sparked fun conversation. The location was convenient, although a little sketchy at night. We felt safe, it was just a bit noisy with some loud partying outside (of course it was the weekend). We would definitely stay again!

We stayed with our 2 year old, 3 year old, and 18 year old. We never felt unsafe in the area. It was convenient and close to the subway. The stairs were steep and narrow, but I would assume many NYC apartments are (nothing we couldn’t manage). It was convenient having access to a washer and dryer, too!

Absolutely beautiful building and apartment. The neighborhood feels sketchy and unwalkable at first, but it was actually very comfortable to walk around both day and night, coming from the train with kids. Parking was easy right on the street a few houses down. I would definitely stay here again!

This was a lovely place to stay, while in Brooklyn. Right next to the train station. You can definitely hear the nightlife from one side of the apartment, but other than that it was great. We never felt unsafe. The place was clean and beautiful. Beth was very responsive to my messages and was kind enough to let us leave our luggage in the living room while they cleaned so that we could do some more exploring before we left that day. It looks exactly like the pictures on the listing. It was about a 30 minute train ride into Manhattan. It was super easy getting to all the sights and restaurants we wanted to go to. I would definitely stay here again in the future.

My boyfriend and I stayed here for 2.5 months. Pros: - Excellent location, super convenient and in close proximity to multiple subway stations/lines. Plenty of walkable restaurants and shops. - Very responsive hosts - In unit washer/dryer & dishwasher  Cons: - In our first couple weeks, we saw a bunch of house centipedes and a cockroach. We were surprised since none of the reviews mentioned bugs, but we learned it's pretty common for NY garden level units. The hosts promptly arranged for an exterminator when informed. The extermination seemed to help, but we did find a few more centipedes and roaches (at least the roaches were dead post-extermination). Overall it was a bit of an unpleasant surprise. - Overall quality of the space - there's very little natural light (especially in the living room) since garden level is below ground. The space was also furnished with pretty old, shabby furniture and lacked ergonomic seating. I probably wouldn't describe it as luxury, but it works.

Ivan is an extremely hospitable and accommodating host. He was eager to address everything immediately, and ensure we had a relaxing, stress free stay. His place was immaculate, the location was excellent, and it offered a tremendous value for our buck to boot. We are fast approaching triple digit stays, and Ivan’s place is now on our go to list of preferred locations when visiting NY!!!

I read the reviews of what the experience was like for others so lemme start with what I wanted to do specifically.  I showed up to essentially explore around town and I needed a place where it was easy to come back to to recharge for the next day, and this was perfect for me. Had a bathroom, had a bed, everything was in good condition, though sleeping was a bit uncomfortable due to the lack of air conditioning (but the ceiling fan helped!)  Jermaine was very nice when I spoke to him, and gave me a fair amount of recommendations for my travels and took what he said about the local area to heart. Brooklyn looks sketchy but I see why so many people fall in love with the place. Overall, I had a fun time with my little adventures and having a spot that's close to various places and modes of transportation was great. If you intend to do a bunch of exploring for long periods of time like me, I would recommend this!

We visit New York City twice each year and we typically stay in an AirBnB and usually in the Long Island City/Astoria area.  So we’re very aware of what to expect and what the neighborhoods there are like.  This rental probably falls in the lower half of all our stays.  It isn’t bad, but there are a lot of things that could be better.  The hallway leading to the apartment is very worn and doesn’t feel clean.  There is a sign near the front door requesting guests to remove their shoes.  I’m fine with that, but I don’t really see the point when the living room carpet looks quite dirty and worn.  There is a mish-mash pile of cloth slippers near the door—I presume to wear in the apartment.  I’m not about to put my bare feet into those community slippers—ugh!  Fortunately, the temperatures for our June visit were very mild.  I wouldn’t have wanted to be staying in this apartment if there was any kind of heat wave.  There is one window a/c in the back bedroom.  The only way to cool the kitchen/dining area is to leave that bedroom door open.  Another window a/c is in the living room and if you want to cool the front bedroom, then you have to leave that door open.  So, if you don't want it too hot, there is no privacy for the bedrooms if anyone wants to use the kitchen or living room when others are sleeping or changing clothes.  The kitchen is poorly organized and stocked.  For 4 people there are 4 wine glasses and a few mugs—nowhere near sufficient.  We only had cold breakfasts in the apartment and we ate other meals out.  But, if we had intended to cook, there were practically no pots and pans.  The kitchen cupboards are a disorganized jumble.  The most common cleaning supplies were air fresheners and spray renuzits—enough said.  The wifi was fine.  The beds were comfortable.  The towels weren’t so good.  The shower is a bit dangerous.  If someone turns on the kitchen sink, even for just a very short time, the shower becomes almost instantly scalding hot.  There should be some kind of warning sign in the kitchen.  The front bedroom’s closet was full of junk and open and it was kind of spilling out into the room.  The AirBnB listing for this property says that breakfast is provided.  Usually that means that the place is stocked with a variety of breakfast items like eggs, bread, cereal, jam, butter, milk, coffee and tea.  There were a few Keurig coffee pods and some tea bags—that’s it.  Since we really weren’t that happy with other aspects of the apartment, I didn’t bother making a fuss about it.  Instead it was easier for us to buy those things for ourselves.  When communicating with the owner later, I mentioned about the breakfast and she said that we didn’t ask for it.  That’s kind of lame.  If the listing says there is a/c, I shouldn’t have to ask for a/c in order for it to be there.  Same for breakfast.  The location is good with lots of different subway lines at a couple of nearby stations—one a five minute walk and the others about 10 minutes.  There are a few small shops in the vicinity but no decent-sized grocery store that we saw.  Most AirBnBs have a notebook in the unit with lots of information about the house and the neighborhood.  Practical information like how the owner wants us to lock up the outer doors at night and where to take trash and what restaurants and stores are nearby would be very helpful.  This isn’t a bad place and for many people it would be just fine.  With a rather small amount of work (and new floor covering in the living room) it could be very nice.  In any case, I’ve found too many other better places in the area on previous visits.  I wouldn’t plan to stay at this AirBnB again.

As for Barbara's attention, she is attentive at all times and is very kind. I haven't met her in person, but she responds to messages very quickly. As for the apartment, the only good thing is that the beds are very comfortable and it is very close to the metro station, 8 minutes walk. As for everything else... The apartment is very old, smells too much of air fresheners and feels too confined. The kitchen has the basics and the utensils are scarce and of poor quality for cooking. The carpet was very dirty, at Barbara's request, we left the shoes outside the house but the socks ended up black. The carpet needs to be cleaned urgently. I opened a closet to look for the iron and the smell was very unpleasant, old and closed. The dishwashing sponges smell horrible, musty, and there are old oils and spoiled food in the fridge. The apartment has hot water, however if water is used in the kitchen and someone is bathing, it becomes freezing or boiling. The bathtub was very dirty, we noticed it the first day we came to take a bath and the water that ran into the drain turned brown. It requires a lot of maintenance. Yes it is like in the photos but in the old version.

Location was great. It was a bit of a struggle getting the key once we arrived in New York as the host was not in the country. She has a person who lives 4 blocks away that has the key. We thought there would be a box somewhere but there wasn't.  Also the bed was uncomfortable to sleep in. It was a clean location but there was another setback that my wife was disturbed with. The host has several scary masks and dolls hanging on the walls. I did sent a suggestion to the host that those should be removed to make the place more inviting.

Honestly the worst experience I’ve had with airbnb. From getting absolutely no response. To the shower not working. Freezing cold air coming from the window which is right by the bed. The blinds don’t shut completely so light comes in when you are trying to sleep. We sent a picture of the shower being broken and they did nothing about it. Didn’t even respond to us at all. From the minute we reserved until checkout it was nonstop issues. We accidentally selected the wrong dates and we tried to correct it and they wouldn’t reply. Finally after Airbnb support contacted them we were able to fix the dates. Then we had the room issues they didn’t bother to respond to us. Then at checkout they hit u with facility fees that they don’t tell you about at checkin. They just say they hold a $200 deposit for incidentals. Complete scam. $400 a night for a disaster stay. Please go somewhere else!

The stay was ok for one night. The location is great, but the space itself wasn’t very clean. Also another unpleasant surprise about the additional fee that was charged during the checkin and was not communicated to us. We left the credit card for deposit, and later 34$ were charged. The property certainly should communicate that beforehand

Overall, the place is nice. It's really close to lots of subway stops and public transport as well as some really fun shops/restaurants. However, the apartment is hard to find at first and the shower is kind of sketchy and three floors down. Good value

The apartment is very pleasant, very well equipped and very clean. The room overlooks the garden and is very quiet. There were 5 of us, 2 adults and 3 children aged 10, 13 and 15 and it was perfect.  There is a metro station for lines 2 and 3 150m away as well as a Wholefood supermarket. Diane also recommended some good places for economical meals in the neighborhood.  Our flight was only in the evening, so we were able to leave our suitcases at the apartment, which was very practical.  We recommend this apartment

I found that the room more than met my expectation. There was nothing that I needed that was not available. My whole stay was great. Ploy even managed to organize that I stay a few more days so that I could see my family. Although you shared amenities with other guests and Ploy , everything was kept very neat and clean. My room was very private and secure. I got back most nights near midnight and never felt unsafe or that I was bothering other people in the home. Thank you

FANTASTIC! What a great place. So lovely — it’s like stepping into history. This is the garden level of a brownstone that retains much of its original details. Original parquet floor in the front room, gorgeous original fireplace (coal-burning, I believe, not in use now), lots of original woodwork — just spectacular for anyone charmed by old homes. Great little totally modern kitchen, TWO full bathrooms, tons of space, view out the back windows of the backyard with a dogwood tree, and the park right across the street. The neighborhood can be a little on the real side right around 125th and Lenox, but I never felt unsafe. The houses in the immediate area are so gorgeous and the tree-lined streets are lovely. Excellent restaurants and friendly businesses line Lennox, Adam Clayton Powell, and many of the neighboring streets. The food scene in Harlem is outstanding! I’ve never spent much time this far uptown before, and I’m so happy to have found Diane’s and Craig’s place. Highest recommendation!

SO clean! Toufik is so incredibly accommodating for check in time which makes it easy for travelers who cannot predict what travel delays they will run into (that can be so stressful). He is so hospitable as well and goes out of his way to make sure you have the best trip. Great spacious place. About a 7 minute walk to the subway and a 15 minute ride into Manhattan. My friends and I were super pleased with our stay! Great host!

Our stay at Toufik's was perfect. His apartment is very close to the subway and you can reach Manhattan very quickly. The neighborhood, rather popular, is friendly and welcoming. We must not deny the drug problems that exist but at no time did we feel in danger or threatened of any kind. I highly recommend Toufik, a very attentive, discreet, erudite and pleasant host to know.
Very nice guy. He always tried to make our stay as comfortable as possible. Never felt unsafe in the neighborhood. Manhattan is just a few minutes away and the metro is nearby.

We were a large party of 8 adults and a 10 month old. The home accommodated us well. The garden was very nice. Eric was great to work with. The home was easy to find. Parking was good. Packing light, the washer and dryer were great! Being unfamiliar with New York, we had some concerns about staying in an strange neighborhood, but we never felt unsafe. Public transportation was just down the street and we had no difficulty getting into down town and back. Great value! Would definitely recommend Eric and the Garden House.

Marc was a great host. He was very helpful, answered questions immediately and took care about all relevant issues. The place itself is fantastic, clean, furnished tasteful and equipped with all stuff you need (except a hair dryer). Also the beds are very comfortable. The location was great, because the subway with 3 different lines to Manhattan is only 50 m far away (but don't be afraid, you won't hear it) and you have everything you need in near surrounding. Next time same place :-)

Greg is a very nice person and when my flight was four hours late, he was very gracious about my late check-in. The bed itself was just ok- it was an older queen mattress on a box spring on the floor. It had some stains and I hate to say this, I found a live bug and a dead bug in between the mattress and box spring (not bed bugs, but still unpleasant). The mattress and the curtains smelled a little bit musty and the shower was a tad musty too. There weren't any toiletries in the bathroom except handsoap, though they are listed as included. The windows didn't have properly installed screens and the lock on the door to the apartment was very insecure- it would have be easy to kick the door open, so I didn't feel safe leaving my laptop in my room. The furniture is stained and kind of beat up, which you can't see in the photos. This place would be fine for college kids, and again, Greg is a very nice peraon, but I guess as a 32 year old, I have higher standards. The price was good and the location was very good too, but I wish I had done more research.

The apartment was great and very close to the metro station. You can shop here 24/7 (for snacks, groceries and medication).  We felt incredibly safe and comfortable here. It's quiet at night.   It takes about 40 minutes to get to Times Square, but the metro runs every 10 minutes, even at night. It really wasn't stressful!!  The apartment offers everything you need for a city trip. Towels, a comfortable bed and a kitchenette with a microwave, kettle and toaster.   Communication with Ayesha was PERFECT. We were able to check in and out as we wished.   Any time. We had a wonderful time in “the Bronx”

Accommodation meets expectations, the photos are exactly the same as reality, the neighborhood is not fun but I did not feel unsafe and the residents of the Bronx and NY for that matter are very friendly and always ready to help. The accommodation is functional: kitchen well equipped with dishes, glasses, frying pans etc... Always hot water even if you wash 6 people in a row, the beds are comfortable, the decor is a bit of a culture shock for the French who like modern and refined things but we are only there to sleep! Buses 39 and 27 to get to subway 6 are right in front of the house, however it takes 1h30 to get to Manhattan South but the price and size of the accommodation is there: really cheap compared to accommodation near Manhattan, in short an owner who speaks French, very available and friendly and an unbeatable price!

Eric's apartment has a fairly rare asset among the apartments offered in New York: a very nice exterior and very appreciable after "city" days. The bus stop is nearby, the boat is a 12-minute walk away, there are grocery stores nearby also the Bronx district is a little far from the center (about 1 hour by transport). from the city center but it is easily done. The area is quite quiet and we did not feel unsafe. Eric was very responsive when we needed him and the text messages were very nice.
Loved it here, made some tiny memories. Great place to stay, warm, cozy and aesthetically pleasing. This was a huge steal.

Greg's place is great. The best thing is that he and his girlfriend are always willing to help you and recommend places to visit in the city. The neighbourhood is quiet, ideal to have a good sleep at night. At the same time is close to the best bars and restaurants in the area, and close to the L train that gets you in Times Square in 15 minutes.  Do not be afraid of their dog, is very friendly!  The room is exactly what you see in the picture, and the bed is very comfortable.

Maria's apartment is perfectly located to explore Williamsburg and is very cozy - her bed is incredibly comfortable to sleep on. Communication was very easy and quick, and everything was organized without any stress or glitches. Although the  bathroom is tiny, I would recommend this place with no hesitation.

First off, Elena was an awesome host! She made sure I was well accommodated throughout my stay. I was never really at the apartment but whenever I was there I felt comfortable. Very green apartment, clean bathroom, and nice chill area by the window. The couch was pretty comfy, no complaints there. Oh & if you've never been around this area of NY or Brooklyn don't let the graffiti scare you away. It's a super cool & vibrant area that's always poppin'

Elena was one of the rudest, most unpleasant people I've ever dealt with. As soon as I walked in the door, and without even saying responding to my greeting, she issued a series of instructions and demands. When I returned that evening to sleep she did not even acknowledge my greeting or thanks for bringing me a towel. She did everything she could to make me feel unwelcome and unwanted. I understand that she may have preferred a female, but it was entirely optional for her to accept my request. Reading her description of herself as "fun" and "super-easy going" is downright laughable.   The place is mostly as advertised, though the room was incredibly hot in the summer despite my asking for the air conditioning to be turned on.

I do not like posting negative reviews since I have almost always had great experiences with Airbnb. But I clearly did not have the same experience as most people who stayed with Elena, despite my best intentions and efforts to be nice. While the stay started out smoothly, over the course of the stay, I felt unwelcome and disrespected. Elena was very rude and even cursed me out when I used a microwave that wasn't supposed to be used (this hadn't been made clear beforehand). This negative attitude towards me stayed until I checked out. The only salvaging part was that it was cheap and I was busy so not there most of the day. If I had not been so busy and staying for longer, I would not have continued to stay due to the disrespect I felt.  Location seems a little sketchy due to desertedness and grafitti on all the buildings, but is actually very safe and close to the L Train to Manhattan. Couch is a couch, heating can become a problem in the winter due to the fact that it is a loft.   Based on my experience, I would not recommend. I hope Elena treats other future guests with a better attitude.

Sharon & Family,  Thank you for opening your loving and beautiful home. Your home was used for an intense emergency board and executive development meetings for an LGBTQIA+ not for profit that works with LGBTQIA+ youth and young adults of color ages 13-26. Many who are homeless, suffering from trauma and or HIV positive. Simultaneously we hosted 2 interns, one from Paris and the other one from Spain.   This was such a safe great space, we accomplish a lot and was able to develop a budget, review our policies and procedures, and plan our next amazing gala.   Looking forward to staying with you again soon!  Thanks, Kels

Elizebeth seems nice at first but is actually very rude, racist & manipulative. My first time staying with her was decent but this second time I came there were like 30 flies swarming in the living room upon my arrival. She smokes often so her place has a permanent smell of cigarette smoke and leaves the buds lying around. The keys weren’t available the first night so she said she’d open the door for me when I left, on my way back she texted saying she’d throw the keys at me through the window, she lives on the 5th floor, I found this disrespectful so I asked that she hands comes down like she originally said and hand me the keys. She flat out told me she doesn’t actually like me and to find another place to stay in new york because of asking her to not throw keys at me from the 5th floor. I was shocked at how asking for something small would lead her to try kicking me out the first day. She is extremely sensitive to the slightest criticism and tried to manipulate me in to thinking I was asking for too much. When I got back to the place she was trying to be fake nice to make me feel comfortable after verbally attacking me. She also felt the need to let me know she has a black friend which if you do that has nothing to do with me & you’re only saying that so you can seem like you’re not racist. Almost felt like she purposely left the space dirty so that I don’t come back. Elizabeth only accepted my stay because she told me she needs Airbnb to pay her rent. She said likes her guests to be like friends her friends I’m introverted & have anxiety so we weren’t compatible in that way. If Elizabeth likes you and feels like you can be friends you should enjoy your stay.

Rawn's place is amazing. The room is exactly as on the pictures and has a bed, a desk and a TV. Every time I saw Rawn he'd ask if he could help or of I need anything. It's close to the station and has a very good connection to Manhattan. I've never felt unsafe in the neighbourhood.

Excellent location and hospitality from Rawn. Room is just like in the pictures, quiet clean and organized. I totally recommend this place to stay in. Access to Manhattan is pretty easy and fast. I never felt unsafe in the neighborhood.

Be careful not to take too much (over 45 seconds) of her time by texting a total of 3 simple questions. She’ll want to charge you for it and will be rude & unpleasant about it.  If you value kindness in a person look for a different place.  One of the most unempathetic humans I have ever deal with, not to mention unprofessional given she’s in hospitality.

I stayed at Rawn's for about a month. It was a very enjoyable experience and convenient for a longer term stay. There are a full kitchen with fridge and pantry space, and a washing machine and dryer available to use. Rawn was also an amazing host and provided lots of good tips about transportation, places to eat, etc.  The location is a bit rough, but I don't think it's dangerous. It's close to grocery stores and a few nice places to eat. There's a metro station 5 minutes away. On most weekdays, the train frequency was good during normal commuting hours. However, there was some track maintenance during my stay which resulted in poor coverage during weekends.  All in all, I would highly recommend staying at Rawn's!

The apartment is clean and very close to the subway but in a sketchy and noisy neighborhood (expect some noise until 00am during weekdays). Shower works great and the couch serve its purpose, not the most comfortable but also it won’t destroy your back. Once you meet Elisabeth she’s a nice and kind person,  but make sure to follow all her instructions (even before you book it) or she can sound rude over text. The check in hour is quite unfair: 7pm to 9pm, basically you pay for a day but get half of it.

If you are looking for a clean, beatiful, modern apartment with a spacious and immaculate lobby for less than $100 a day in Brooklyn, this is not the flat for you (and good luck finding the one that is!) However, if, like me, you're looking for a roomy and reasonable apartment in a safe yet reasonably central area and don't mind too much that here and there a few things (toilet lid) are a bit broken and the tub has a slow drain sometimes, then I recommend this one. The bed is comfortable, wifi strong, surroundings not dangerous and very accessible to public transportation. The owner, albeit perhaps not very experienced in airbnbnomics,  is very thoughtful, communicative and clearly cares about her guests' well-being. I was thus able to have my wife enjoy a work trip with me, in which my goal was to keep a low overhead while still remaining, for her sake, a cut above my usual gravitation toward s**tholes. Bottom line, if you're not too fussy, this place is a bargain!

Bridgette's apartment is perfect for a couple or two friends. A metro card will take you anywhere in Manhattan and Brooklyn in 30-50 minutes and you get to experience the city as a local. You're also 30 min away from coney island! As students, we wanted to be able to cook our meals to save some $$$ and the kitchen has all you might need which made it super easy. All amenities are on point, it is surprisingly spacious and the AC saved us from the heat wave at the time.  Super close to the groceries store, the metro, and the amazing Brooklyn museum (do not miss it, it's amazing!). Entering the apartment went super smoothly and was a very easy and a non-stressful experience. The neighborhood is a bit noisy on the weekends but nothing some earplugs can't help you with. The real plus of this place is how reliable and easily reachable Bridgette is! Overall, we had a great time and would recommend this to anyone looking for a similar traveling experience.

Overall if you're looking for a place to crash while running around New York this is a reasonably priced, reasonably located place to stay.    Three blocks from the metro, the #6 line will get you pretty much everywhere.  The room was small but serviceable, the 3 of us had no problems.  The building and neighborhood was very quiet (except for the Puerto Rican Cultural Festival day).  The building key was very hard to work in the locks: we always had to jiggle, wiggle, rock, fiddle and wrestle with them every time we came back.  The first night we thought we were locked out but THANK GOD one of her neighbors buzzed us in.  There were always people on the street so it felt safe, although there were some shady characters by the metro at night.  The hot water went out on us the last 30 hours of our stay.  Not the hosts fault, but it was inconvenient.  The host was very accessible via text message.  The building was pet friendly so if you're sensitive to dog/cat smells this is not the place for you.

This apartment was in a good location.. Just walking distance to 8th Ave where a lot of restaurants and stores are. It's also located next to a couple other restaurants/bars.   Lana was very responsive and easy to work with.   We were there with 5 guests and we all slept comfortably with just enough space.   While the overall stay was good, there were a few concerns that we had. We noticed some ants in the bathroom (maybe due to weather) and the chairs in the dining room were a bit wobbly. We were scared to use it because we didn't want it to break. Otherwise, everything else was great!

Mike is a very friendly host and the subway right next door allows you to quickly reach Manhattan. But very dirty apartment, expired products found in the fridge, microwave with leftover food, same for the oven, filthy stove tops. Washing machine and dryer outside the apartment, shared by the whole building, also dirty. A bathroom in very poor condition, we found hair, broken and dangerous tiles, not to mention a rusty radiator.  Main room, a real mess with no place to put things, electric wires everywhere... Some are hanging... Are bare... No television, the apartment is underground, probably an old converted cellar. The inner courtyard is shabby, dirty and dangerous.

Mike is very serious. He responds quickly to messages. The neighborhood is the number 1 asset of this accommodation. The apartment is small and very cluttered. The electrical installation is scary with the cables and extension cords on the sockets. We slept well because it is very quiet. We appreciated the proximity to transport. The neighborhood is very safe.

Mike's place in Long Island City is a great place to stay for your trip to NYC. The #7 subway entrance is literally seconds away and you can be at Grand Central station within minutes. The subway line towards Brooklyn is also just a couple of minutes away as well. But before leaving LIC, don't forget to spend some time on the park-like waterfront with a view of the Manhattan skyline as well as checking out some of the local coffee shops, restaurants and (my personal favourite) craft breweries. Also to note is that there is not only a medical clinic on the same block as the apartment if any situation was to arise but there is also an NYPD precinct which gives a serious sense of safety and comfort for any of those who may have had a preconception of staying outside the typical tourist-y areas. We did not for a second feel we were in any type of unsafe neighbourhood - lots of people out walking their dogs, jogging or commuting to/from work. We were out late at night and still felt like it was very safe.  The place is well equipped for all your needs during a stay: a small but fully equipped kitchen, comfortable bed and pull out sofa, computer desk and wifi. Note that the wifi provided did not exactly match what was provided in the check-in information, but the proper connection information is just written on the bottom of the router. We did experience one small hiccup with the air conditioning, but with Mike's help it was solved.   That leads me to finally say that Mike's communication is second to none that I've experienced throughout my many Airbnb stays. He was quick to answer any questions, provide suggestions and was ready to help resolve any issues we had.   I would not hesitate to stay with Mike again and I'd encourage anyone to give LIC a try for your next stay in NYC.

Mike was a responsive host. The unit is in an amazing location and at least during the winter when spending time in the unit, it is the right size for one person or a couple.   When I stayed, Mike seemed to be having a problem with his maintenance team. The unit was fairly clean but not as tidy as I usually expect an Airbnb to be. Also, most of the light bulbs in the unit were out, which was kind of unpleasant because it’s a basement. When I told Mike he responded immediately, apologized and ordered light bulbs (and plenty of spares), which arrived the next day. Mike also offered to refund me the cleaning fee, which was really good of him.   In all I felt safe and comfortable during my stay, but left three stars because the quality of the place seems a little unpredictable. Note that, as pictured, it’s a basement and don’t get much natural light.

Our stay at Katie's apartment was great! To get the keys was super easy, no worries! When we look at the map we thought it might be far from the metro but when we got there we saw that is very close, as the neighborhood is beautiful it was great to walk to the subway! The location is super safe, we did not feel unsafe at any time, even at night! The apartment Katie is beautiful, spacious and very clean! Made orders over the internet and Katie was very helpful and quick to doubts as to receive the package! The only thing I have to score is on the bed of Katie who is very good and we could not wake up early to enjoy it haha! I have no doubt where to stay next time in NY!

Katie's place was just as described. In the best location for exploring Brooklyn and super quick into Manhattan. Lots of shops etc near by and we never once felt unsafe. Will be looking to make this my regular NY pad should it be available on my next visits!

We very much enjoyed our stay in Matei’s apartment. It’s a convenient location, easy to all of downtown attractions. While the view of the park was enjoyable, the homeless was a bit of a distraction. The apartment was lovely and well appointed. Matei was a helpful and easy to communicate with.

Positive aspects: comfortable bed, soft towels, good transport connections, well-equipped kitchen, bathroom large enough. View of two New York landmarks (if you lean out of the window) Negative aspects: The apartment is quite "rocky" and needs to be renovated, washing machine not working, door lock can only be locked once because the second lock mechanism is broken, on the 4th floor without an elevator with steep stairs, the area is a social hot spot, lots of homeless people, drug consumption and sales practically on the doorstep, a lot of "strange characters" overall, we didn't really feel safe in the area, so that would be one Another locking mechanism was good. The apartment overall was okay, but the information about what the area is actually like would have helped us if we were looking for an apartment in a different area. In my opinion, not very suitable for families with children (it certainly depends on the age of the children). Going to the apartment at night with two people was okay, but I wouldn't have done it alone.
Apartment was clean and well stocked.  Definitely a sketchier neighborhood then I was expecting.  Also the four flights of stairs got old pretty quick.

The apartment was impecable, cosy and very well furnished. The subway was 5 minutes away and the neighbourhood was safe and lovely. There was a beautiful park just around the corner. Although Tom scared us a little with the keys instructions we had no problems. There are plenty of shops and sotres nearby to cover all needs. We will definetly return to this place again.

Craig was awesome! So friendly and super accommodating. Our train from Philly was late and he was so easy and quick to respond. He also let us stay a little bit after check our time since we chose a later flight. His flexibility made the stress of travels so much simpler.

Love‘s appartment is in a perfect location to explore the city (metro around the corner and all day/night running lines bringing you to Downtown). There are severeal places where you can find food and drinks in the area.  In the appartment you can use the bathroom and the kitchen (+plus your room of course). Love has 2 cats so don’t get scared if you see them around. All the spaces are clean and tidy. The room itself offers everything you might need, and if you need more Love is always reachable to help you.

Will and Kim's place is great for a weekend getaway! We liked the proximity to the subway and Coney Island and had a nice time there. The neighborhood is a little sketchy but once inside the apartment we were safe and sound. We got quick responses to all of our questions and appreciated their hospitality.

Our stay was amazing, such a great location. The place was super clean and had extra blankets and towels. Asaf was super helpful in finding the place and getting in. The self check in and self check out really eliminated some stress on us too. All around great experience, will book again!

This basement unit is spacious, uncluttered, & has all the basic amenities. The location was convenient and safe. Asaf was very communicative and was even helpful in my finding a long term rental. Overall, the value for the basement unit was fair.  During my stay, I had a few concerns:  Minor: There was an obnoxiously large bug that was pretty difficult to get rid of.   The bath towels did not smell fresh at all so I went ahead and purchased my own.  Major: Loud clanging & scraping noises intermittently throughout the entire night. I honestly thought someone was doing a home renovation project all night. Turns out it’s their pipe system? That was very disruptive to a restful night’s sleep.  A putrid smell engulfed the entire unit on my last night forcing me check out early & search for an available hotel for the night. It was a foul, gas-like odor which actually ended up making me very nauseous.   All in all, it’s a good place but the banging & foul odor were extremely unpleasant.

I was in New York for work...and for a week-end when a friend came to join me.  This was the PERFECT place to stay.  Super close to a good subway station without being scary for a single woman.  Very diverse neighborhood, so I didn't stand out.  Close enough to Manhattan, so I could commute in - and see a show and still get home at a reasonable time.  And also close to Brighton Beach and Coney Island.  We rode a roller coaster for the first time in a zillion years.  :-)  Access is easy and private.  Will & Kim are very responsive and think of all the little things that make staying in their place a joy.  Note that it is close to the train line and can seem noisy...but, like others have said, I slept like a baby and didn't even notice.  Instead, it was a total bonus because the station is so close.

Our stay at Catherines was an absolute nightmare! Not only were TWO of our bikes stolen from directly in front of the property, but we were falsely accused of throwing a "party" by the neighbors downstairs and kicked out. Not once did we receive a notice that the noise level was too loud, or we would have gladly been quieter going forward. The walls in the apartment are extremely thin and 6 guests under one roof is going to cause some noise. But to accuse us without any proof or notice is baffling and insulting. Catherine was unwilling to reason with us on the phone and adamant that we evacuate since her listing isn't supposed to be rented out to guests. She even went as far as to disrespect a military veteran by hanging up on him while he was speaking to her calmly!    We would have appreciated Catherine first speaking to us instead of assuming that it was our group that had made the disruption. I hope for the future that she does not treat any guests like she did us. We were forced to find alternative accommodation within one hour, which ruined our vacation.   The place itself is nice and the check in process was easy. But maybe it's not a good idea to list the property as "good for groups" and not expect a little noise. As for the location, I would not book because of the theft that occurred on the street.

Kristin's place is great and amazing value for money. I would highly recommend if you're looking for an impeccably clean, comfortable, well located, yet still affordable place to stay in Brooklyn   Space and amenities - the space is pristine and makes you feel like you're in a clean environment you can trust. The house rules are there for a reason, they help keep the space and furniture in great state for everyone to enjoy. Aside from that, Kristin made sure we had bottled water on arrival, fresh towels + extras, toiletries, tea and coffee  Location - while it's not hipster-posh Williamsburg, it's 35-40 min from Manhattan and the area feels perfectly normal. The street has nice brownstones. It's a gentrifying neighbourhood, but we didn't feel unsafe. For the price, it's extremely good value   Responsiveness - Kristin and her husband were very helpful when we needed (they even helped with a keycode mix up). They live downstairs, so there if you need them, but never impose. So, ease of access to them is also a plus.   Would totally recommend and stay again :)

Nice place that is relatively quiet. Host has a lot of rules, if that doesn’t bother you you’ll have a fine stay.  Wasn’t in the nicest part of Brooklyn, though I didn’t feel particularly unsafe.   Host made an effort to educate us about things nearby and make us feel welcome which was nice.

I highly recommend staying at Mac's place. It's a very clean and cozy place that makes you feel at home immediately. This was my first Airbnb experience and I was a little scared. Especially as an alone travelling woman I felt absolutely safe. I didn't meet Mac, but getting the keys and finding everything was well organized. Fred who is living there, too, is a very  nice host. Communication was very good. The place is located in wonderful Williamsburg, very close to the L Train, just one stop from Manhatten. I'll be back!

David and Asaf are the absolute best hosts. The apartment is as cozy and sunny as it appears online w/a sweet little back patio off the living/dining area. Close to grocery, coffee shop and drug store. Quiet, safe neighborhood. I was there a month to welcome my first grandchild and will definitely rebook on my next visit to NYC.

The apartment is in an ethnically diverse neighborhood with good transit options. However, the kitchen area was not kept clean as bugs came out at night around the sink and drawers. Also, the bathroom drain was clogged when I checked in, but the host did not proactively resolve the issue when I notified him, making the shower an unpleasant experience by the second day.

Perfectly located for easy navigation all over the city. A short five minute (or less) walk to a drug store, convenience store, subway station. great  restaurants, live music, etc. The apartment itself was so easy to locate. Jeremy gave perfect directions on entering the place. The apartment had plenty of room for us three girls and we loved the cheery bright interior. Jeremy has his own art on the walls which added a great personal touch. I would definitely recommend and stay any time I happen to find myself once again in the big apple!

Marc is  a lovely host, always available for any need. The apartment is located near two subway stations (Bedford ave/Marcy), from where you can reach Manhattan in 20 min. Many bars and restaurant around the corner, and a wonderful view of NYC skyline from Domino Park, a couple of blocks from the apartment. Just outside of it there 's also a citibike station that I would highly recommend if u wanna discover the city and its sourrounding without too much stress to cover distances.
Cannot stress enough how awesome Dominique and her place were. Great location, great host!
The dogs might seem intimidating to read about, but they are 100% friendly and docile, nothing to be afraid of or worry about at all. We had a great stay.

Super clean, modern, small space perfect for a single person or couple. Has all the modern amenities you need. Elizabeth even went above and beyond by emailing me recommendations and tips with links to websites to make our quick trip more enjoyable.   The home is in a nice, quiet neighborhood in Brooklyn. We walked for morning coffee at Steeplechase. It was delicious. Ask Elizabeth for food recommendations. She gave us a few and they were all good. If you need a convenience store (like 7Eleven or Wawa), walk over to Bolla Market just off the main drag. It was clean, well organized, lots of convenience snack food options and the owner was very nice.   We took an Uber from Penn Station when we arrived and quickly learned that was a $50.00+ trip with all the taxes and fees. What is a black car fee anyway????? We got comfortable with figuring out how to travel everywhere by subway very quickly. Buy the $33.00 fare card for a week unlimited and make the most of it. Well worth it. We would have spent hundreds in Uber rides and it wasn’t worth the time spent In traffic. Subway really is the way to go. We even rode it at night after a concert and didn’t feel unsafe. The Fort Hamilton Station near Elizabeth’s Airbnb felt safe as well.   Overall, great experience. I highly recommend Elizabeth’s place and I’ve traveled and used Airbnb a lot the last several years.

A nice room, clean and perfect for me and my friend. Mark was very helpful, we had problems with the airlane and I could borrow his phone (real exepensive for me otherwise). Near metro. Its like 30 minutes to central7 lower manhattan. If you are afraid of dogs, don’t live there =). They were nice Marks little children, and hungry =). If I come back to NYC, I could easily stay here again!   Vänligen   Maria Eliasson

Very good room in Harlem, spacious, clean and quiet. The apartment is located a 5-minute walk from the subway leading you directly to southern Manhattan (30 to 40 minutes).  The hosts, Mark and Will, are charming and available. Despite a big delay in our flight, we had no problem getting into accommodation. The neighborhood has all the facilities you could need. We recommend this room

Nicole was extremely helpful and a great host! She was easy to contact and helped where she could. The space was very clean and comfortable. The neighbourhood was safe and easy access to the subway, food vendors and attractions. Check in and out was super easy and made our trip that much less stressful. I only wish I could give more stars!

Mark and Will’s apartment was the perfect place to stay! I was traveling to New York for some job interviews. The hospitality Mark showed and the overall comfort of the apartment took so much stress off of my trip. He has very helpful and had information sheets with lots of tips and resources to just about anything you could need. He was also excellent with communication. His apartment was very spacious and super neat. The apartment is in a great, quiet location. I will definitely book this place again whenever I have to come back.

It's a nice flat in Harlem, NY. The area is not dangerous, but coming from the countryside and being there at night can seem like a bit of a culture shock at first. With the metro, you are in the city centre fast.

Accommodation meets our expectations. Spacious and very well located geographically (metro station 2 steps away). We had a great stay. Zainab and Thimothy allowed us to stay a few hours longer because our flight was in the evening (extremely accommodating and attentive)

Timothy's is the perfect place to base yourself when staying in New York. The location is fantastic. The brooklyn locale is a relaxed authentic place, to start or finish the day, after exploring the concrete jungle of manhatten. It is real NY neighbourhood full of a melting pot of cultures. But its also super safe, we often arrived at the subway around midnight and never felt unsafe. So close to Atlantic Ave Station. A couple minutes easy walk. which as a major station will get you to anywhere you want in New york in one ride. The place itself is a basement flat in a super cute brownstone. It's a lot bigger than it looks in the pictures tastefully and thoughtfully decorated with plenty of room for me, my partner and 3 boys. When we arrived Timothy had made the 3 fold out beds for our boys and had a bottle of rose in the fridge for us, a much appreciated touch. There's a pile of reference books to teach you all you need to know about your stay in New York plus a folder from Timothy sharing his local knowledge. The beds were great with a cupboard holding plenty of extra bedding if needed. The bathroom was clean and was well stocked with soaps, shampoos toilet paper etc. There was a pile of towels for us with more in a drawer. The kitchen is fantastic with double door fridge full oven and well stocked cupboards. A back door leads to a tranquil garden space which was an oasis in which to relax. It was also very quiet day and night which is no mean feat in the city that never sleeps. If we are lucky enough to visit NYC again we will be staying at Timothy's.

This was not the right place for me for a long term stay. While other guests seemed to have had a positive experience, I experienced several safety concerns that made living here alone not ideal, particularly for several months.  The biggest disappointment for me was that after communicating my concerns (#1-3 in the list below) within 24 hours of checking in, and asking to move out earlier mostly due to worries about safety, their immediate response was that it was "absolutely not possible." Given that Corporate Housing, the host, has several other properties, I imagined there would be some flexibility or even the option to move to another location. It was very stressful to feel unsafe in a longterm space, particularly at a time when we’re home almost 24/7, and it was disappointing how inflexible the host was.   After several tense messages back and forth, they ultimately let me remove just one month from the reservation. I ended up moving our early anyway and wasting several thousand dollars in rent in the process. Funny thing is that even after all these messages about safety concerns and how I’d be moving out ASAP, they actually messaged me a week before the official end date asking me if I would like to extend my stay…   The issues were as follows:  1. Safety around the Airbnb - not sure how this area was pre-pandemic, but as of summer 2020, there are often people hanging out on the street in various levels of intoxication. Groups of people will sit on the step directly in front of the door. The worst moment happened the day I moved in, where I was aggressively catcalled right in front of the Airbnb. As a woman living alone, I did not want this individual to know where I lived.   2. No COVID-19 protections - not only are the folks hanging around the building/street maskless, but mask wearing inside the building was low. I'd estimate ~25% of people wear masks. The few maintenance folks I saw there never wore masks inside, and that is the primary reason I did not push harder for fixes for broken items in the apartment. I also wish I’d asked for more details on cleaning procedures before move-in, as I would’ve liked to know if the cleaning crew were taking precautions (masks/gloves). Given what I saw of the cleaning crew while I was there, it seems unlikely.  3. Broken items - These are less of a big deal, but not great for a longterm stay. The biggest problem for me is that the mailbox doesn't lock, meaning anyone can access your mail. I experienced a lost package on the first day I arrived that I had pre-ordered. I let the host know on day 1 and they say they would fix it, but they never did. Within the apartment, the cabinet in the kitchen was not connected to  a hinge and almost crashed down on me the first time I tried to open it. The sliding closet was stuck/broken as well.   4. Noise/Smoke levels - as of summer 2020, this is one of the neighborhoods in NYC where fireworks often happen at night, on weekdays, anywhere from 8PM - 2AM. Marijuana smell levels can be high throughout the day in the building. Sometimes it was strong enough for me to smell inside my apartment.  On the positive side the apartment itself is a good amount of space for one person. The pictures capture the space well, though it should be noted that the couch has no support (it's all springs). Otherwise, it's nice to have a dishwasher and laundry in building. They also let my friend see the space before I moved in. However, this was during NYC lockdown, so the building and neighborhood were completely empty when he came. I’d recommend checking out the area first before you book. Personally, due to the safety issues and inflexibility of the host regarding these problems, I would not recommend this place, particularly if you're like me and living alone.   Note: if a longterm reservation is altered at all, Airbnb can't help you cancel the entire stay even if you alert them within 24 hours. Don't make the same mistake I did.

The place is comfy and pretty. I was lil afraid of the neighborhood since I am a young college kid, yet the neighborhood is quite safe and there are also a couple of places that you can get a cup of coffee/yummy food which is not so far from her place.

Pamela is very sweet and thorough when checking in. Unfortunately, the bedspread smelled really strongly of urine so I couldn’t use it, there wasn’t water in the bubbler, and an incident with another person staying at the Airbnb banging on everyone’s door and yelling in the middle of the night made me feel quite unsafe as a single traveler and I likely won’t stay in a shared Airbnb again.

Great spot in the heart of Brooklyn. Accepted my last-minute booking after another listing proved unsafe, which was a lifesaver! This particular room is tiny but the bed is comfortable, and there's a full kitchen. Overall a great experience.

Isaiah is a very nice host; he is responsive and friendly. I called him when I arrived and he immediately showed us to the apartment.  The living room is quite spacious, the two bedrooms are about average sized (we could fit a travel crib in our bedroom), and the kitchen and bathroom are on the small side. The couch/futon in the living room is large. At some point we asked for more sheets and towels, which Isaiah delivered in a few minutes.  The pictures you see are accurate. The one big downside is the neighborhood. It's on a big street, with lots of auto-body shops, and there is a lounge next door. I didn't think too much about it, until in the middle of the second night there was a shooting death involving the police. This was of course sad, and Isaiah was contacting us next morning to see how we were doing. The area in front of the apartment turned into a crime scene.   (We had to leave our car parked, as it was part of the crime scene).  How much can one make out of such an event?  I don't know.

The location of the apartment is great, very close to the metro station. The neighborhoods look nice. The kitchen is convenient. However I worry about the security, the entrance lock is damaged and the lower lock of my room does not work well. So I feel unsafe.

The apartment is a great, clean and roomy apartment in a rather rundown part of Brooklyn. It is on a very busy main road which impacts the enjoyment of the main living area and would impact sleepers on the futon in that room. We really appreciated the stress free lift to the airport.

This apartment was perfect for my sister and I on a four day adventure in New York. The neighborhood is a bit gritty, but never threatening or unsafe. And once you’re upstairs, the Galt is everything g you’d want at this price.  Lots of clean towels, four pillows on each of the beds. Plenty of glasses and dishes. The abundance of live plants was a good touch. We would definitely stay here again.

Super clean, nice apartment rental. This apartment is very comfortable inside, but definitely in a somewhat sketchy area outside after dark. There are locked doors downstairs and at the actual apartment door, so once inside, we felt fine. Just be aware of surroundings. We would come stay again, but also has to park a few blocks away which we weren’t expecting—there is closer parking, but only on certain days. All in all, a great value and spacious place in the city.

I ended up having to stay here for two weeks during the start of the COVID-19 pandemic here in NYC, and this was an extremely comfortable, clean, and conveniently located place. The room was spacious, clean, and has a skylight which I loved since it provided me fresh air and sunlight. The host was very accommodating and constantly made sure I had clean sheets and towels available. While I didn’t get to enjoy all that the neighborhood has to offer while I was staying here, I did like the fact that the stay is located to a nice number of restaurants and a subway station. I highly recommend staying here for anyone looking for a room in this part of NYC. I’m not sure you’ll find anything nicer, cleaner, or with as wonderful a host at this price. It’s truly a steal of a deal.

Our stay was okay.,  more a place just to sleep than to hang out. The apartment is scrupulously clean, beautiful wood floors and lots of nice plants. Plenty of blankets and towels but only two chairs at the small table so with 3 we couldn't sit together. Bathroom a bit cramped , those with long legs need to sit sideways on the toilet. The location on Atlantic is in a bit of a rough-sketchy area which at night is a bit deserted feeling, unsure how safe but we had no problems. Short walk to supermarket, cafes. Communication was slow and impersonal but the self in- and outcheck was easy.

Edna was a great host - I had very challenging week of welcoming my brother from oversea in the last minute, but she made my life a lot easier this week by accommodating every need we had, which I really appreciated. Their place was very spacious and clean, a little unstable WiFi for work but overall very cozy and warm and very conveniently located.  The area gets a little sketchy at late night but as long as you are being careful you are completely fine. Overall I would recommend to stay in their place if they are visiting Brooklyn area.

Spacious and clean, and nice kitchen, but this place is on a rough commercial street in what is otherwise a mostly residential area. Lots of loud traffic. We were disturbed at night by the hissing and popping radiator pipes, and the overheated bedroom which forced us to open a window. We had no thermostat in the unit. I think this is common in old New York row houses (overheating without individual unit controls), but unpleasant nevertheless. And, yes, per a prior reviewer, you do have to bang your knees or sit sideways to use the toilet. Overall, disappointing for the cost.

The Wrights have a very nice and clean place in a very central location. Getting to and from Manhattan is very easy, something we really enjoyed. The place is orderly and clean, and pretty calm considering the distance to the city. The neighborhood was really enjoyable in the daytime, though it could feel a bit unsafe at night. All in all a great stay for the price, and we would stay there again.
Great and clean room! Neighborhood is a bit sketchy but overall experience was great! The stay experience would be better if they could communicate more effectively.

The neighborhood is pretty scary. Very run down, and some homeless people outside(though the homeless are very nice and we even offered them some water and snacks). So if you are nervous of scary neighborhoods, I would steer clear of this place. BUT, if you can handle the scariness outside, the inside is cute and clean and decorated like an IKEA showroom! 😍😍 I loved it. It's very close to the airport and we had no problem inside the apartment. Not sure if we would stay again, but definitely an eye opening first time AirBnB experience.

The wrights have a good service, they  are really kind on their messages and  flexible people.  The apartment is a kind of mini hostel not a house 'per se' the neighborhood is not the best (homeless people right in front of the door but it's safe to walk at night) also its not really in Williamsburg but the experience was not bad at all, they are really professional and the services are good I would recommend the place if it's not your first trip to New York. They won't respond to the  mentioned  WhatsApp number but they would on the Airbnb chat which is nice overall a good experience far from the city  but price/quality is good.

The location in Brooklyn is ideal for discovering NY. Clean and quiet accommodation. Everything you need is there. Thank you for the little addresses in the neighborhood, to try!  3 rooms rented in total in the apartment and two bathrooms to share.  No guests on site: Small, very well-run “hotel”.  Please note: in front of the building there are homeless people, but harmless.  I recommend for my part, good address

Second time at the Wright’s. Could have been better... didn’t see the host in 4 days... not that I came to see them but at least a quick « welcome » would have been nice. The neighborhood is still as creepy as it was last year, a bit worse I’d say. Finally, it was so cold in the room the first 2 nights I had to buy an extra pyjama. Then, coming from nowhere the 3rd night, a huge heat wave blowing from the roof in the middle of the night with the heavy noise that comes with it. I’m not sure I’ll be back.

Great place to stay in NYC. You get tips where to eat, what to see and it's really close to subway. Not a scary location we weren't afraid to come back late at night.  Many places to leave your car in front of the building. You can leave your things when you check out. Really comfy bed ad lots of space. Two bathrooms so we didn't have problems with using them and colliding with other guests.

I book this place two weeks ago because my bf was coming to the city. The place was really nice and clean. The subway was pretty close, just two blocks away from there so you don’t have to walk a lot. I get to the apartment pretty late some days and it was not scary to be walking alone by the neighborhood that late.  The bed was clean and comfy.  They are pretty flexible w the check out.  You won’t have the best experience if u don’t get this place:)

Clean, all the basics provided (+ umbrellas), nice linens. Not a place to hang around as there's no space other than bedrooms and a tiny kitchen table with uncomfortable folding chairs, but a great retreat in a fantastic neighbourhood. I suspect it must be very hot and stuffy in summer.

Staying with C.D. Was perfect for a traveler in my situation. I was a single person traveling alone that just needed a place to sleep and shower and this is exactly what she recommended in her description. The one negative review she received was clearly from a customer that did not read the description. C.D.  Was very accommodating and amazingly flexible on check in (I got in at a very late hour). Her communication was great and she really made my first solo vacation a lot less stressful.
Nathan is very accommodating, kind and funny! If you need anything, don’t be afraid to ask - he will help you out!

Excellent apartment, exactly as shown in pictures, had everything we needed to be comfortable. Brought our five year old and found it to be a good size for our family, with plenty of room and quiet neighbors, and the puppies in the shop window next door were a bonus for her. Close to everything you need: restaurants, shopping, subway, drug stores, parking. Contactless entry was perfect and Fernando was quick to reply to any communication or questions. Would stay again!

The place is definitely as described. It's prewar building that adds personality to it. Place is clean with comfy bed and linens. The cats were well behaved and will not bother you at all -- i tried to pet them but theyre afraid of me :( . James is an awesome host! Very fast to respond and will make you feel at home. I had no problem from checkin to checkout!! Really awesome experience -- will book again or recommend if time comes.

Sarah's place is so well decorated! The beds are very comfortable and the fixtures are all updated and really beautiful. We spent five nights here and really enjoyed it. The location is a little seedy, there was a police incident across the street during our stay. However we never felt unsafe.

This place needs to be repaired, for example the last day of our stay the toilet and bathtub got clogged that we were not able to use, the whole place got wet even the livingroom and we had to check out 1 day earlier because the place was not livable, the couch was broken the kitchen was not that clean this includes cabinets and kitchen towels kitchen duster etc. the location was an hour away from Manhattan, if you are planning to go to Manhattan you have to waste about 2 hours, I wish we had less stressful new year vacation because we had to look for a hotel to stay the new year eve there on the other hand KIM was very responsive and helpful, I hope she fix the place before renting it out again.

The place is cozy, there are things nearby not too far from food , there’s a Walgreens and etc , there wasn’t a microwave though & the kitchen wasn’t super clean , but I was a short stay so I didn’t stress it that much ,check in was easy
-Kv was a great host. Everything we needed it was there. Area appeared to be unsafe but was very chill. Home is beautiful! Thanks so much!

Interior: In good condition. Only things of notice were some wall damage and the creaky stairs, but the living room and kitchen are quite up to date and modern. The bathrooms are in good condition as well. The bathtub/shower downstairs is a little high, just as a heads up for vertically challenged people like my girlfriend. The bed is comfy, but if you get cold easily bring an extra blanket during the colder times of the year. The space heater is helpful to an extent, but being able to insulate yourself will be a better option.  Exterior: It looks like your average Brooklyn neighborhood. A few liquor stores and deli's in the area. My girlfriend and I did learn from a local that the area used to be a bad part of town, but it is improving. I didn't feel unsafe, but just out of precaution we took Uber (about $5) from the subway station to the home at the urging of the local we spoke to.

Sarah was incredibly friendly, helpful with local recommendations, and the description of her home was accurate. It was especially a great space for our young family. Lots of kids toys and books, a pack-n-play, and colorful children’s dishes all made for a nice experience for the kiddos.  The neighborhood was OK. Not a place I’d be excited to walk around with the family but also not dangerous per se. It was however within close proximity to nicer areas.   Best thought of as a hub to go out and enjoy the city. And since that was our primary purpose it worked great! We’d definitely stay here again.

This place almost met my expectations. Certainly you get a lot more space and amenities and style than you pay for (although I suspect the price per night has been reduced due to the pandemic). But some pictures of the space paint a rosier picture than reality. While the upstairs is true as advertised, the downstairs, where the bedroom is, feels like you’re sleeping in a basement. It’s dark with no windows and lower than expected quality furnishings. After the first night of fitful sleep on an uncomfortable mattress breathing in stale air, I seriously considered whether I should take my sheets upstairs and sleep on the couch — where there was natural light and fresher air.   Location was decent and Kv was a responsive host. I would have given this place three stars if I judged the unit based solely on how far it fell short of my expectations, but for what I paid for it, I really can’t complain too much.   The upstairs living area and kitchen and backyard are gorgeous. Loved the art and the books on the shelves.

My mom and I stayed here for a girls getaway after a stressful semester in my nursing Masters program. This was just what we needed. We were greeted sweetly at our arrival, and the place was spotless and smelled wonderful (and we are picky)!! The bed was soooo comfy and the decor was in such good taste!! We loved the little snacks and having the essentials already in the fridge when we arrived! We enjoyed our breakfasts of toast, fresh fruit, and hot tea, and the ferry rides and early morning/late night walks through the cute neighborhoods were thoroughly enjoyed! Thanks for being such amazing hosts and for the great communication before, during, and after our stay!! HIGHLY recommend this place if you want a quiet cute place to rest away from the big city!! Would love to stay again!! (:

Great value for money and has everything you need, stylish and comfortable, location was a little far from everything and the metro station is 15’ away but it’s kind of sketchy area, my fault for not researching properly, other than that we had a great time and we love the place! Thank you

Kv’s apartment is beautiful, comfortable, and well managed. We particularly enjoyed all the kitchen appliances as well as the waterfall shower-head and decor <3! Communication was great and the space was clean. Our only stress was walking to the subway from the apartment. We did it once and decided to Uber to Williamsburg before taking the train into the city at night. Other than that, it was a perfect stay!!

Unfortunately, the Airbnb was left wide open when we arrived. We felt unsafe to enter and sadly the host did not understand our concerns. There was also a picture of a man with a gun but I suppose that may be some thing many people are fine with, but I personally felt turned off by it.

The room was as described in the photographs. There were no communication problems with the host (all through the Airbnb page). The place is neat and has 4 rooms. The common areas (bathroom and kitchen) were well kept. It is located about 5 or 10 minutes walk from the metro, station 36 av is the closest. The sector is quiet, although at night it is very lonely and dark (we do not perceive it to be dangerous). Recommended accommodation.

This place was great. I stayed here with my girlfriend, and we both appreciated how clean it was. Check-in was easy, and the bus picks you up practically at the front door. After rush hour, the bus arrives every half hour, however if you plan your travels, it shouldn't be a problem. The neighborhood didn't feel unsafe, even though we arrived back home close to midnight some nights. The pictures in the ad are also accurate, which we appreciated. We loved the shower's high water pressure, especially after walking the city all day. We recommend this place.

Tracey’s place is amazing. It’s located right next to Central Park, so we were able to walk there, as well as a lot of locations right around us to get things to eat.   If you’re planning on going to Times Square and such, the subway is right near this apartment so it’s a quick walk! It’s also just a few blocks from the American Museum of Natural History, which was cool!   In addition, Tracey was very accommodating. She had everything we needed— towels, blankets, pillows, kitchen appliances, etc.. For the price and location, this was place was a steal!!

I’ve stayed in Harlem at a couple of other apartments before for around the same price point. This building is nowhere near as nice as many other apartment buildings nearby. Twice when we went to open the front door, people from the street who did not live in the building tried to come in with us, which was awkward and unpleasant. So be ready for that, which was not an issue in any way in other rentals. The apartment itself is basic and clean enough and surprisingly quiet considering it’s on a busy street. The main problem was that the bathroom sink was clogged when we arrived. I texted Kennedy, and we were out all of the following two days and it was not fixed. As a result, we used the kitchen sink and tub. I almost never write mediocre reviews, but I’m not sure this place justifies $200 a night when there are so many other places nearby.
A real steal. Comfortable, cozy and spacious within walking distance of the subway.

Me and my friends spent a week in Courtney's place and we really enjoyed our stay. Since the cleanness of the place was really important for us,it was a great choice. Before arriving NYC, it was stressful for me to manage my trip because she responded with delay. But, after we arrived, she was responsive and we had good check in. Totally, I rate our stay great.
Cute, fantastic apartment, and Masoud is so nice! The outside door looks sketchy, but don't worry: inside is lovely.
An amazing place. It would be a crime to not stay here if you visit.

This was my 2nd Lower East Side AirBnB stay. I love the neighborhood. Easy walks to a diverse selection of restaurants and bars and shops. China Town, Little Italy, Kosher Shops. Also just 4-5 blocks to the East River. F Train right around the corner. Connect to the J Train at Delancey and Essex for JFK flights. Unlike other stays, you will meet at the property in person for the keys and a tour of the apartment. Stocked kitchen, we reheated leftovers for lunch a couple of times. 4 person dining table. Futon and a couple of chairs in living room. (note-no TV). Bed is on the other side of living room bookcase. A little to firm for my taste. Bathroom is basic and was clean. (note-no Exhaust blower). The unit is on the 2nd floor of the building. So a few steps up from sidewalk to front door and then a flight once inside. Do not fear the neighborhood appearance. Plenty of graffiti to go around. Homeless in the E. Broadway subway station. Never had a problem though. Stay here. I recommend it

First of all, to get a place this affordable in LES is already a steal. Ha keeps in touch every step of the way, the cleaner was also very nice and the place is great for couples or a get away rest spot for travel in the city. The sage was even available for energy clearing! The bed is comfortable, the shower is great pressure wise and the vibration overall is hip. She offers a lot of chairs in the space as well so if you have a few guests at least you can be able to hang out. The street is very nice and calm as well. There’s a deli right up the st with an atm and the patio in the back is very nice.  Highly recommend booking before it fills up!

It was an amazing trip. Mark, a great person always kind and willing to help and answer our doubts. Rooms were big and nice. His house is located in a part in the city which makes it easy for to the travelers to visit other places and, it is a 'safe' place. At the beginning we were afraid about the language, but, there were not huge obstacles, communication was kinda perfect.
