We actually celebrated the 4th of July with a barbecue picnic at her place--she has a beautiful outdoor grill & yard, which is shady in the afternoon. The kitchen is also well equipped. Lauren was very responsive to any questions that arose.  We plan to return for a future stay.

I traveled to the city with my parents to spend Thanksgiving with my sister who lives in Brooklyn.  We needed to stay several days and knowing how impractical a hotel would be price-wise, I decided to try this site and found Lauren's listing.  Just let me say that her apartment is exactly as it is presented; it really is as nice and clean as the pictures show and the neighborhood is also very nice and close to the train.  You can easily get around the city from here, but once you're done with the hustle and bustle of some of the busier parts, it's quiet enough at the end of the day to settle in.  There's a deli across the street that has good smelling food (I didn't try but just watching them prep the food made me hungry) and a variety of foods perfect for your stay such as dairy, meats, snacks, beer etc.   Lauren is a very accommodating and helpful host. She responds to any questions or concerns extremely fast and makes sure you have everything you need to make your stay comfortable.  Any time I emailed her with a question, I had a response within a few hours, if that long.  I was very impressed as it can be stressful to coordinate a stay like this, but she made it very easy and comfortable!  I cannot recommend Lauren or her place enough, and I promise if you choose to stay here, you will NOT be disappointed in the least!

We had a wonderful stay at Lauren's place in Brooklyn (Williamsburg).  Her condo is absolutely lovely and our entire stay was stress free and comfortable.   We couldn't have asked for a better location (just a few blocks from the subway) or a nicer property. Lauren was great host - she communicated throughout the process, was flexible with key pick-up and left us a kind welcome note :)  It was our first experience using airbnb and everything was top notch.  Thanks so much Lauren :)

Great location on a safe street. You can walk to stores, restaurants, and pubs. About an hour walk to the St. George ferry or a quick uber ride. People in the neighborhood were very friendly. Made friends right away which is nice for a month long stay. The hosts were so great....quick to respond to anything that came up. It is an older home so you will hear every footstep but it would be a great place for a weekend getaway. Plenty of hot water and a great little countertop oven if you're scared of gas ovens like I am! They placed an A/C portable unit in there and it kept the bedroom nice and cool.

The apartment is very clean and ok if you're only looking for somewhere quiet to sleep and will not spend time inside. On the other hand, if you're looking for a place to live and cook, it's quite dangerous since the first oven isn't heating and just leaking gas when you turn it on and the 2nd one (electric) is almost unreachable for someone 5'3 and I burned myself with its door that is as hot as the inside even with gloves on. Many basic kitchen tools were missing (scissors, oven gloves, cutting board, soap, blender,...) and I had to buy most of them. The hosts are rather polite and they repaired everything that broke quickly (the fridge and AC were not working and it was really hot, windows were locked at first, it is not the sunny apartment described). If you're looking for people who won't talk to you (so no instruction given about anything but they definitely will send you a complain e mail if you put something in the wrong garbage can for example) and respect your intimacy (which is good because the lock doesn't work from inside), this place is for you. Otherwise, it won't be a very friendly air bnb atmosphere despite all your efforts to get along with them. Moreover, I wouldn't recommend Staten Island since it's very tiring to live so far from most places and you have to take a bus to the ferry (it takes 30 minutes + another 30 minutes on the ferry to Downtown) and the bus is often late. So, living somewhere else, closer to Brooklyn or Manhattan and paying a bit more would have been worth it in the end.

This apartment is just as gorgeous as it looks in the photos, and accurately described. (Niya is one of those rare designers who can combine old and new in a really appealing way.)   He also has a lovely sweet, kind, energy and I thoroughly enjoyed visiting with him and meeting his son.   He was really flexible about check-in times and helpful in figuring out how to navigate the subways.  He even recommended some local churches to visit for their architecture.  (Be sure to check out his list of recommended restaurants etc.  I didn't really hang out in the neighborhood, I was there for a conference, so I didn't have a chance to explore those places.)   The room was quiet and roomy, the bed was comfortable, and Niya has included a number of thoughtful amenities— coffee pot, teapot, iron, small ironing board, hair dryer etc. and various extra items in the medicine cabinet.     The street itself is tree-lined and features architecturally interesting old row houses, though parts of the surrounding neighborhood are somewhat rundown and therefore might be intimidating to someone accustomed to more gentrified districts.     I'm not saying they are necessarily unsafe, just that they might "feel" that way to some.  So, if you're sensitive about this sort of thing, do your homework with something like Google Street View and make sure this is a good fit for you.  (I would definitely stay here again and stroll around during the day. Though as a safety-conscious single woman I would probably take cabs directly to subway stations at night, which is probably a good idea in ANY part of town.  As it happened, I had a male friend with me, so I felt fine walking around at night.  (I should add that I only really walked in one direction—toward Fulton.  I have no idea what sorts of neighborhoods might exist in the other directions.  They might be more gentrified.)    Lovely place.  Lovely host.  Highly recommended.  Thanks so much Niya.

Niya was an amazing host! He greeted me right when I was at the door, and did a wonderful job answering all of my questions. He also ameliorated all of my fear based on what I have been reading online about the dangers of New York. On our first night there, we couldn't figure out how to unlock the front door, but Niya graciously stepped away from what he was doing to come to our rescue! Couldn't have asked for a better place to stay!

Donna's East Village Apartment is a fantastic little gem.  Perfect in size for a single or couple.  The room is cosy, the bathroom is king-size and that bed is heavenly.    Donna is also a perfect hostess... the arrival/departure process was perfectly organised and I appreciated Donna's efforts in making my stay stress-free.  Would definitely stay there again.  The actual position of the apartment is great.  The East Village is a fab place to use as a base to see NYC and the subway is close by.

I stayed in Anthony's flat for two weeks. The place was, as advertised, extremely clean (that floor was actually shining!) and cozy. I've seen Anthony just a couple of times but he gave me all the informations and indications I needed to get there and move around.  The place is just few blocks from the A and C trains that gets you directly to Manhattan. Few words about the neighborhood: it could looks slightly scary if you come back late at night, but it's actually really safe. I didn't have any kind of problem, and I came back every night really late. Plus, if you are interested in music, Brooklyn has an incredibly vivid music scene, with tons of cool venues. So I strongly recommend Anthony's place to those who want/need to stay some days or weeks in NYC without spending a lot of money to stay in Manhattan.

We had a superb stay in part thanks to Donna's accommodation. The studio is spacious, very well located (5 minutes walk from lines 6, R, N, B and even L. The neighborhood is very lively with very good places to eat which is appreciated after a day of walking in New York. Donna remains available and responds quickly if necessary. There is a small fridge, coffee machine, microwave and everything you need for breakfast. The building is secure with the addition of the neighbors' dogs doing their job :-). Donna even offers a solution for luggage at the end of the stay if your flight is late. Finally you understood it if we come back to NYC it will be at Donna's.

Excellent, A very good location, central to any destination, nothing dangerous. I was looking for privacy and I had it and Donna was always attentive to any questions I had. the room is beautiful and very warm. It has what you need to rest after a hectic day.

The host was responsive and answered questions as they arose quite quickly. The apartment itself was nice but small and very noisy as it is on 2nd floor on a major intersection. Also, it was like an oven--awfully hot and no heat control so we had to end up turning on the ac every night which was ridiculous when it was freezing outdoors but oh well...Light comes in early as there are no blinds, just some loose curtains--so we got some eye masks and also some earplugs and that helped. The bed is a futon and a bit tight for two people but comfortable enough, though only one pillow was provided. The key pick up was a real drag as Kimball had someone else who we needed to contact to arrange a meeting place to get the keys..she also gave me the wrong apt # so in the middle of the night we were left wondering if the whole thing had been a scam as some other folk were staying in the apt we thought was ours...however, I must say that once we called the airbnb folk they got thru to Kimball pretty quickly and he called us right back and told my husband how to turn the key in the right apt which was across the hall from the one we thought we had. All turned out ok in the end...and the neighborhood is great for the museums, some nice brunch places nearby etc. I did not see a "manual" that airbnb sends along with your confirmation...that is a must-read before you go.

I'm trying to think of something to complain about here, and coming up short. Hmmm ... the full-length mirror on the wall wasn't quite full-length – it topped out right around my hairline. But so what – how many airbnbs even offer a full-length mirror, especially right in your room? (I've probably stayed at all 5 of them.) And the bathroom mirror more than compensates, with generous headroom and solid, balanced vanity lighting. Hmmm, also the in-room fridge had hissy fits from time to time – nothing very loud, just sort of unusual. But again, if you simply must have cellar-temperature chardonnay at your fingertips (55 degrees, say the experts at Reininger), it would behoove you to man up, bite the bullet, and turn a deaf ear, n'est ce pas? Because, again, how many airbnbs even have an in-room fridge? (I've probably stayed at all 5 of those as well.) Or if zen quiet is a priority, you might end up pulling the plug. It's "all good" (slipping into the vernacular here). Of course, these quibbles wouldn't even be worth a mention if I weren't getting paid by the word. (Actually, I weren't – I mean, who in the Dickens gets paid by the word – I just thought it sounded good, or at least better than the alternatives.)  But seriously, folks, my nit-picky bellyaching aside, Anthony's place is basically a self-contained, ground-floor studio, clean and trim, in muted tones, with quiet, solid floors, a desk and TV (not shown), and good WiFi (once you get the l33t-sp34k password straight). Anthony runs a tight ship, leaving little to chance, and is focused and consistent in communication; I suspect also, but can't prove, that he continues to refine the experience that awaits you here.  Streetwise™ note: Silas Deane was a socialite, lawyer, merchant and assemblyman in Connecticut before attending the First and Second Continental Congresses. Deane was then dispatched under "non-official cover" to Paris, secretly negotiating diplomatic ties with the French Crown, securing materiel for the Continental Army, and recruiting French officers – notably the veteran Johann de Kalb (leveraging his own undercover assignment in the colonies several years prior) and an inexperienced but idealistic nineteen-year-old, christened Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier – but recognized here by his title, Marquis de La Fayette.

Location, Location, Location. Having never been to New York, I didn't understand how valuable it was being near two major train lines and a cross town bus route. And, having said that, we were able to walk to many of the things we wanted to see - museums, restaurants, comedy clubs, and parks all around us.  The apartment is great and had everything we needed. Most importantly, it was exactly as described. There were no surprises. Kimball's friend met us at the door (by arrangement) and made an excellent recommendation for our first New York restaurant visit. I did have a question while in the apartment and when I wrote to Kimball, he replied promptly with a resolution.  My teenage son loved the loft and I crashed on the very comfortable futon every night. I suspect this apartment might even work for two young couples or a mom and dad with two kids, but I'm not sure of Kimball's limit on occupancy.  What more can I say. I have no complaints and will try hard to get this apartment when I come back to New York. I'm afraid to say too much more cause I'm afraid Kimball will raise his prices.  Simply put, we loved it!

Had a great stay at Kimball's apartment- it's a really beautiful space in a great neighbourhood and close to trains to get anywhere else in the city. Had a scary few hours when we first arrived and realised we couldn't get into the apartment and couldn't get in touch with Kimball, but it worked out in the end and the rest of the stay was perfect. Thanks for having us.

This AirBnB is a good value, but I would have liked to have known that it is on the edge of a rather seedy area. We walked from the closest A-line stop twice and felt somewhat unsafe, so we then navigated to it from the subway line to the south and felt the extra 3-4 blocks walking was well worth it. I hadn’t planned on using Uber, but found it felt safer and saved the walking for Manhattan. Other reviews made it seem like Anthony was a helpful resource, but I did not find that to be the case. In my initial contact I asked for subway advice, and he did not give any guidance regarding it. Later, I messaged him because there were 2 conflicting sets of info about the WiFi and instead of clarifying or helping, he replied that the info was posted in the room, so we never were able to get on. The place has the feel of a budget motel, so if you’re on a tight budget, value having your own bathroom, and are not spending much time in the room it will probably be okay for you.

It was an absolute joy staying at Tokunbo's beautiful apartment! First off, it was a steal to get an entire apartment at this price. It had everything I needed for my two week stay and was conveniently located on the border of Bed Stuy and Crown Heights. The two closest subway stops were only a 10 minute walk away from the apartment which made it super convenient to head uptown/into Manhattan. Also, Tokunbo was SO communicative and made check-in a breeze. Be wary that this apartment is on a main street and on the third floor (which puts it right at the same level as the LIRR train) so if you're a light sleeper this may not be the right option for you. Luckily, that's not an issue for me, so I thoroughly enjoyed my stay and would return in a heartbeat.

(This was my first Airbnb and my first review) Pro: It is very clean. Con: This space should not be placed in the entire apartment section, because IT IS NOT. It is a room with a kitchenette in it, as are all the rooms in the brownstone so if you are looking for complete privacy this ain't it (shared bathrooms and all). They also double booked me for part of my stay, so I ended up feeling cheated financially by this airbnb. I checked in later than usual (by their request) and assumed that I would check out around the same time to make it fiscally fair.....but I wasn't notified until the night before that I was to check out  5 hours earlier than I expected. They were profusely apologetic but nonetheless I was left out in the lurch and feeling slightly robbed.  I would never stay here again and I now feel extremely cautious about Airbnb (ask a lot of questions is my advice to first time Airbnb'ers). Good Luck!

I was in need of a place on short notice and Marylyn got back to me right away. The place was clean, and in a great part of town. I am from CT so as far as it being dangerous well that's not true!  There are some great food options within a 15 min cab ride I would suggest Do or Dine. Well worth the experience! No problem with shared bathrooms as they were really clean and kept that way.      Update: I fixed the TV so you can get the local stations. I watched Football on Sunday so the locals were fine for my use!

Edward was a very welcoming host. The apartment was exactly as advertised, really good value for such a great location in LES. We visited in Oct so we did not require air con at all, though it was available if needed. Thanks to all other reviewers who have given a very good picture of this accomodation. i should also stress that my husband and I found it very safe to come and go from even at 2 and 3 am. Oct 13

I am very pleased. Edward was always helpful and easy to ask for help regarding our accomodation and the city in itself. Furthermore, it was lovely to be based outside the most stressful parts of Manhatten, in spite of staying in walking distance to more or less anything.   Would recommend this as a good budget option for anyone planning to stay a few days in Manhatten.

Marylyn met me at the property and showed me my room and the kitchenette and bathroom. Deciding a check-in time was easy and I did not have any trouble finding the place. The proximity to the A train is very helpful. The shared bathroom is something that different people have varying degrees of comfort with. I am not used to it, but I had no problems. Everything was clean and even though the house itself was old-ish (most NYC houses are) it was in good shape. It was mostly quiet and the large windows let in good sunlight. The neighborhood appeared to have a few rough edges, which made me a little anxious, but I returned one Friday night at 1 am and there were still a lot of people taking the train back and getting off at Nostrand Av station, so I didn't feel unsafe. Overall, a decent value for the money.

1. The photos do not match the actual images of the apartment inside. Tokunbo had changed the furniture and there are no longer two couches in the space, but rather just one and an uncomfortable and unusable chair.  2. The coffee table in the living room does not have a glass to protect it and is more or less unusable as things can fall through the holes. I’m pretty certain it’s meant to be a luggage rack rather than a coffee table. Good luck keeping coffee on there without spilling.  3. The noise in the area has been a major issue and I STRONGLY RECOMMEND NOT BOOKING THIS SPACE:   4. A marching band practices for multiple hours in front of the apartment and has done so three times during the course of my stay. When I asked the host about this, she disclosed that she previously knew that this is something they do and is part of the "culture" of the neighborhood. This was not in the original listing of the apartment and something THAT THE HOST KNEW ABOUT AND DID NOT DISCLOSE ABOUT THE APARTMENT ON THE LISTING. This marching band was complete with a full drumline and crash cymbals. I have documented evidence of this band on these occasions. Many of the members of the marching band do not wear COVID masks.  5. There are very loud trucks at night which load and unload in front of the apartment. They also drive very loudly at night and during the day to the point where it would wake me up in the middle of the night.   6. Atlantic Ave., the street on which the apartment sits, is a VERY loud boulevard with constant motorcycle gangs, loud cars blasting music and constant honking during the day and at night.  7. The Long Island Railroad track is right in front of the apartment and constantly has trains rumbling every 10-20 minutes every day.  8. I reached out to AirBnB about the loud noise and it had affected my health and well being and rendered this space uninhabitable. I vacated the unit as the space was a hazard to my health and well being, leaving the keys in the unit. AirBnB tried to force me to pay their cancellation fee, however I never gave explicit consent to cancel as I clearly explained that the space was untenable and unlivable given the extreme noise pollution AND the fact that the host withheld information regarding that the unit has an extreme amount of noise. I vacated the unit because of these reasons because I could not live here. I left the keys where the host asked and left.  9. The host left the keys in a lockbox outside that was very difficult to open as the box was heavily rusted out. It took a long time to finally open. The host was hard to get a hold of by phone to ameliorate this issue.  10. This space was ridiculously loud and untenable as a result. I had to vacate the unit as a result of the noise (see: above). Also, my package was stolen in the building as message from another tenant in the building had noted. This place is unsafe, loud, noisy and generally awful.  11. The combination of noise pollution, an unresponsive and unhelpful host, the lack of cleanliness and the lack of accurate pictures or accurate disclosure regarding the noise leads me to give this place 1 star or less. Do not live here. Do NOT book here. It's awful and save your money.

Looking for a place to stay in Brooklyn? Look no further. Great location and amazing host. The room was incredible, everything was high quality and very clean. Very comfortable double bed,  huge plasma tv with cable, dvd/blueray player. Plenty of wardrobe space and empty drawers. Most  places are only suitable as a base to sleep, wash and change, but this place is so much more. I actually enjoyed spending time here.  Fred made me feel right at home from the moment I arrived. He, and his girlfriend Jan, picked me up from the airport in his lovely Lexus SUV. I was really hungry, so Fred kindly stopped off in downtown Brooklyn so I could grab a sandwich from Junior's Deli (pastrami is a must).  Fred's place is a 3 minute walk to the J line train station, and within a 10min walking range of plenty of fastfood eating places, McDonalds, Subway, Dunkin, Popeye's, chinese takeaway. There aren't really any nice restaurants nearby, but due the great location near to the train station, great restaurants are so quick and easy to get to. For example, one of the best Steak Houses in New York, John Luger's, is only several minutes by train, the steak was incredible, the best I've ever had. Also, Manhattan is so easily accessible from here, and the trains run 24/7. Fancy a Pizza in Little Italy or a meal in China Town? no problem. The train goes directly there, takes 25mins. I purchased a 7 day unlimited travel card anywhere in New York, Trains or Bus, cost about $28. This made getting around so simple. The subway system is all over New York and is safe and simple to use. I'm a photographer and would often use the subway after midnight on my own, carrying expensive camera equipment, and never felt unsafe.  So if you're looking for a place to stay in Brooklyn, I don't see how it could get any better than Fred's place. He is a great guy and very trustworthy. I would often leave the house for the day and leave behind my camera equipment and cash, I would never worry about it. Fred is a very honest guy. He has lived in Brooklyn all of his life and knows the area very well. If you need tips on where to eat, things to see and do, then Fred is your man.  Fred, and his delightful girlfriend Jan, made my business trip feel more like a holiday. If I ever visit New York again, I would not consider anywhere else, I will be staying here, no question. I certianly struck lucky with this place.

Laura's apartment was perfect for our New York vacation. Great location, a stones throw away from all the action in Williamsburg, and a short L train ride into Manhattan. Laura was very responsive in her communications and was a brilliant host, giving us a list of great dinning and night spot in the neighborhood. No issues and stress free.
Professional, fast, clean, comfortable and stress-free.

The room is super cute, and had everything my daughter and I needed. The refrigerator was a godsend, as the first night we mistakenly ordered a HUGE meal from Carmine's (an AMAZING Italian restaurant in New York, NY), and had leftovers that literally lasted us the length of our trip.  The room was clean and welcoming, with bottled water waiting for us in the fridge (I drank TWO the first night after our trip to Manhattan!). There was a queen bed and a sofa-bed. My daughter ended up just sleeping on the sofa, and I slept on the bed. We were both super comfy! The street outside gets a little busy at night, but definitely not as loud as Manhattan, and the background noise of the A/C unit made it easy to fall asleep.  One thing to note is that the bathroom is outside the room and down a short hallway, so be sure to bring some sort of jammies in case you need to use the bathroom during the night. There are a couple additional rooms on the same floor that share the bathroom (if they're occupied); however, there weren't any other guests there until the last day of our trip. That made it easy to use the bathroom whenever we wanted, but when/if other guests show up, you'll need to be aware that you're sharing the bathroom with them, too.  There's a TV in the room, which we never used. We literally woke up in the morning, went off to Manhattan, and came back at night for bed. I was warned by a friend before my trip to be very careful in Brooklyn, and to not ride the subway late at night because of how dangerous it is, and how dangerous Brooklyn is at night. However, the first night we inadvertently stayed later than planned in Manhattan because we were talked into comedy club tickets (lol!), and then we took the wrong train and ended up Uptown/Queens, so we didn't get back to Brooklyn until after midnight. The subway ride and the short walk to the house went just fine. We just smiled and waved at everyone! Haha. Seriously though, we were careful and aware at all times, but didn't have any issues at all. We found the people hanging out on our street at night to be friendly, or they just minded their own business. We never felt like we were in any danger.  Our plane back home was late in the afternoon, and Marylyn was gracious enough to keep our luggage in her hallway while we traipsed off to Manhattan one last time.  Overall we had an AMAZING trip! Marylyn was a spectacular host, and the room was just perfect for us, and a very short walk to the subway. If we ever visit again, I'd definitely try to get the same room with Marylyn! It was an incredible experience my daughter and I will never forget.

Marylyns apt is well located in Brooklyn, being about a 3 min walk to the Nostram subway station. Easy connections and direct routes into Manhattan and to both JFK and La Guardia. The apartment we had was on the 3rd floor, so it did require a few trips up and down the stairs, which really is no problem if you're in shape.  The bathroom is shared, but it never became an issue for us, as there didn't seem to be many other guests in the building. There is 1 per floor, so even if it would have been occupied, (which it never was) you could always go to the next floor. It was also very clean, and there was good water pressure, and plenty of hot water. The room itself was warm (weather when we in NYC was very chilly). The bed was firm and comfortable. There was also a couch that folded into a bed. There was enough room for 2 people to cohabit  comfortably. Though we never really cooked, there was basic kitchen amenities to prepare a simple meal should you choose.  The fridge seemed fairly new and worked well, and we did toast bagels for breakfast.   The street that the apt is on is very quiet. Having stayed in Manhattan on  previous trips, you realize how traffic/honking sirens go on all night and can be very disturbing. Not at Marylyns.  The main street (Fulton) has lots of shops and services, including grocery stores, and a lot of fast food outlets. It is a little sketchy at night, but we never really felt unsafe, as there always seemed to be  a lot of people around.
An absolute steal in the Heart of manhattan, great value and Edward was very helpful and accommodating.

Staying in Crown Heights offers a somewhat affordable NY experience but at a certain cost. Thankfully the place is very close to the subway but it's still a trek to go to midtown or uptown. So once you are out - you're basically out for the day and night. Going back and forth from CH to Manhattan wastes a lot of time.   It's also a neighborhood you dont want to be walking at night alone. You'll definitely want to Uber it back after a night out. During the day it's fine though.  The first night I was there I heard 7 gunshots on the same street half a block away. It was scary. No one died but there is gang violence in this neighborhood so be aware of that. I talked to the police about it and they said this part of Herkimer St is "a war zone." That freaked me out.  I didn't realize that Airbnb Is actually outlawed in NY. That's why there isn't much availability on the app and everything in Manhattan or better parts of Brooklyn are very expensive. There are also tenants and landlords renting out their affordable housing units on Airbnb instead of living there themselves or renting out to a local. I didn't realize this was an ongoing issue in NY.   You can find hotels in Manhattan at less than $100 USD a night. That's what I'll book next time I visit. It's more convenient and safe.  But for those, looking to save some money and don't mind a real Brooklyn experience, this place is clean and close to the trains to take you into town.

This is my second time in New York and I lived around the east village on both trips. Lots of bars and restaurants around the neighborhood but you don't usually notice any noise. I guess that's one plus with the basement unit.   Easy commute to anywhere due to the subway. Although the subway station is a bit further than I thought. Alternatively, you can take a bus that connects you to the subway station. Bus stop is very close by.   The room itself is ok. It looks exactly like shown on the pictures. I guess I was lucky too because I didn't see the other person that is in the other room and I don't need to wait to use the bathroom etc. The entrance of getting in/out of the unit was sketchy and you can see something unpleasant. Once you are in the room, you don't feel it much and the room feels comfortable.   Overall, it is a very affordable accommodation option if you want to budget your trip on dining or events!

Judith and her husband Ralph were great! Their place was very well kept, clean and pleasing to the eye. My last minute booking was quite scary for me but Judith was able to get me in right away. The pictures are 100% accurate and the pricing for "Emma's Place" is great. With the couple living so close, it ensured great contact. Judith was very prompt and kept in constant contact. The A train is about a 10 minute walk... in the cold this can be a bit discouraging. Nonetheless, great hosts, great place!

We had a great stay at this apartment. It was clean and the bed incredibly comfortable! The location was great - just a short walk to the subway and Williamsburg had great cafes and bars. Larissa was really responsive to messages and made our stay very stress free.

Friendly pleasant hosts. Comfortable self contained (mostly) apartment.   Close to subway (and light rail - which I wished I knew could take me to the airport quite easily). Plenty of local food outlets and supermarkets.   With 3 children directly above and 3 adults, it was incredibly noisy, so no chance to sleep in past 6 or 6.30am.  Sirens of emergency vehicles and plenty of local assaults (crime stats for the area avail online), makes me think it was perhaps not the safest part of Brooklyn. Indeed, this was demonstrated when I had people banging on my door in the middle of the night seeking assistance for some ruckus outside.  Mattress was average, pillows were dreadful, more kitchen items should have been available.  Access to laundry and basement is only available through your living space so you may have a small amount of traffic.  An outside space was available for relaxing but plenty of space inside was sufficient for me.

Location is the best part of this studio. There a lot of places to go in the neighborhood, whether it be shops, restaurants or bars. It is also a good starting point for doing touristy stuff. The AC worked well, which was a relief during the hot summer days.  This room would be best for those who are going to be out all day and just need a place to sleep. I'd say it best accommodates 3 people because the extra "mattress" is actually a short sofa cushion with a sheet on it. Sheets and towels were clean, the room was a good size, furnishing were a bit "rough" but posed no problems. Bring hangers if you have clothes that need to be on a hanger.  I did have a few problems with this place, however:  1. Keys. I was supposed to pick up the keys at a certain location, but when I got there, there were no keys. I contacted Keith and it turned out there were no available backup keys for me to take at the moment. Keith later asked one of the other lodgers to give me a set of keys, and I ended up waiting about 8 hours to get them. This is something Keith could have prevented by making a few more keys beforehand and stashing them in several other locations.  2. Internet. One of the amenities listed for this place is wireless internet. I did not have internet access during my entire stay. After a lengthy conversation with Keith, he called the provider to solve the problem. He tried his best to get it going, but in the end there was no internet service. The internet issue was due to certain circumstances I won't mention, but it was another matter he could have prevented.  3. Toilet paper. If there are guests staying over, there should be extra toilet paper in the bathroom or at least somewhere in the studio. Because toilet paper eventually runs out. And sometimes...toilet paper is even stolen (which is what happened to me). This is one more thing that Keith could have definitely prepared for.  I don't know if these are constant problems for this place or if they were just a one-time set of complications, but that was my experience during my 3 nights/4 days stay.

I really loved staying here! The location could not be better. The place is truly all about location. It is a very basic apt the decor is in no way inspiring.. that said we really didn't care because we were in the heart of Manhattan!! I brought ear plugs as I knew it would be noisy and it actually wasn't so bad. The fridge and washer were both busted but we made due. We washed our clothes by hand and used the freezer as a fridge. I would not recommend this place for someone who wants to be in beautiful apt. I would recommend it for people who want to be in the heart of the city and don't really care about the aesthetics. the place is falling apart a little but for the price and location it is a steal. The bed was pretty comfortable and when we got cold there was a heater that worked fine.  Keith got back to me most of the time very quickly about concerns and I picked up my key at the corner without a problem. I would definitely stay here again!

We stayed 3 nights in East Harlem and enjoyed it a lot. The appartment is clean, freshly renovated and Ted and Blanca are the best host one can imagine. We arrived at night, and the front of the house looks shady. What a positive surprise when we entered the door...

The apartment has the best possible location. All the surroundings and the neighborhood are excellent. We have walked back from the subway at night and we have never felt afraid. Maybe the photos of the living room and bedroom do not match reality (especially because there is less furniture), but if you are only going to use the apartment to sleep, it is fine. The building looks very safe. I recommend it.

The best. Larissa is personable, helpful, patient, friendly, and communicative. 10/10 person and host. She has made my stay far easier and more pleasant and stress-free than I could have hoped for: The space is homey, spacious, full of character, comfortable, and private but it an excellent location. 10/10

We had a wonderful time in Carroll Garden. The appartement was great, very clean, comfortable and much bigger than you can see in the pictures. Huge bathroom with a wash-machine  and dryer witch was very nice because we were traveling with our 3 year old son and need to wash his clothes a lot. Really nice bedrooms with comfy beds. The kitchen was great with everything you need. So we even cook dinner. Total bonus is the backyard were we enjoyed breakfast in the morning with beautiful singing birds. Our host. Melissa was great. She had a box full with toys for our son, he loved it!  And a special chair upper, so he could sit at the table and I was afraid if my son would fell out sleeping in a big bed. So she also provides a camping toddler bed for him. The neighborhood is the best. Beautiful brown houses, old trees and wide sidewalks. Shops and restaurants around the corner. The F-train just 2 minute walk. Train wil bring you in 15 minutes to Manhattan Union Square - Greenwich - H-line, very safe and fast. And if you want to stay with little kids. This is de best place, one block away is Carroll park with several playgrounds for all ages. Grap a coffee at Smith Canteen and sit down. Very relaxing with nice people. So we loved it!! I We will come back.

To sum it up in one sentence - "It was an unpleasant check-in experience but pleasant checkout experience". Everything in between was good. The place is nice and clean and the neighborhood is ok (some loud music at 3am from the road notwithstanding) with great connectivity - bus stop right across the street. Perhaps better suited to single / couples than families with kids - given that kids will jump and hop and that makes a noise on the wooden floor which is not welcome.  Jullett was very nice in agreeing to our late checkout request - really appreciate that, though during check-in, her coldness (my wife introduced herself and did not get a response!) was surprising.  I would strongly recommend the place for single/couples who play strictly by the rules (its like zero tolerance, I gather)...

We had a great stay at Dee's place! It was very clean and exactly as shown in the pictures. She was very nice and flexible with check in/out times. The neighborhood was ok and close to the metro...the only thing that was a little sketchy was walking home after dark...just take a cab! Thanks again Dee, we'd definitely stay here again!!

Dee's wonderful room was the perfect resting place at the end of busy days.  We were there during a heat wave and the airy, air conditioned accomodations were perfect.  We slept well!  The private bath and entrance made it stress-free, also.  Dee is warm and welcoming.  We have already recommended her place to others.

This has been our most disappointing AirBnB experience. While the descriptions have since been updated, at the time we booked we were led to expect a self-contained studio. It is not. It is a bedroom that opens onto a kitchen that is the passageway to two upstairs units. The bathroom is at one end of the kitchen and the shower at the other. As others have noted, the bathroom is so small that you cannot sit square on the toilet. The price is misleading: as others have mentioned it costs over $200 per night. Sleeping was a challenge. The bed is a full size, not a queen. The bedroom windows don’t block out much street noise, which also leaks in through the gaps around the air conditioning units. One of which works. We were woken the first night at about 4:00am by heavy traffic through the kitchen. Soon after the apartment filled with the smell of marijuana. On the second night a small group laughed and talked loudly in the kitchen from around 2:00am.  We went to New York to see the sights, not to spend time tracking down a drug-store so that we could buy toilet paper. One roll between two people for four nights just isn’t enough.  On the bright side, it’s close to some nice cafes and bars and a ten minute walk to the Metro. But if we return to New York city we’ll be looking for a real self-contained studio that doesn’t serve as an access way to other apartments.

This apartment is a great size, has a nice balcony, piano, and lots of appliances that make you feel at home.  One thing to be aware of is that it is directly above a bar which opens daily at 10am and closes at 4am. The building was built in the 1800s and has a strong smell.   The window blind in the shower appears to have mold spots on it. I wouldn’t recommend staying here until this shower mold is taken care of because it is unsafe to breathe in.    Our second to last day, while looking for a ziplock, we discovered an anti-Semitic WWII relic that was very concerning and offensive to us. I don’t understand why anyone would have that, let alone in a main drawer when they’re Airbnbing the place.

The place is at a very cool location and Seith was fast to respond to our messages. The bad things about the apartment is that the carpet in the bedroom is dirty and the heat cannot be changed. The bathroom situation is a bit weird, the bathroom and shower are in two different rooms across a shared area. The bathroom is supposed to be private but other people that stay on the floor above used it during our stay, and only after that Seith gave us a key for it. Not for the shower though. The room is closer to a private room, not an entire place. The last bad and bit unsafe situation is that the outside door is always unlocked, that we were the only people in the house that locked it, so there is nothing from a person from the street to get it and use the bathroom or be have lunch at the share kitchen.

No issues encountered. The check-in instructions were clear and easy to manage. We had locks on all doors and never felt unsafe in the neighborhood or misled by the host. Good location for walking or taking the subway to many locations of interest. Will definitely consider the next time I visit NYC.

We were ultimately very unhappy with the choice. The area is ok, but we would have liked a different location, more to the north. As a tourist, you should think about whether you always want to take the train.  The worst thing, however, was that the photos looked much better than the reality. Mega rocked down, not the least bit nice or comfortable. Just a bad apartment with a bad layout and mega small bathrooms that was “somehow” prepared to live in and rent out. We would have preferred to invest the money in something else.  I thought about the mega steep climb to the apartment and possibly older guests and guests with families. I imagine that to be unpleasant. It was clean. There is space. Everything you need can be found in the kitchen. But we weren't really keen on using it. We would not book the accommodation again.  Maybe I should also say that I am a somewhat more relaxed person and am writing this review. My fellow traveler actually freaked out at first when he saw the apartment and always said “fine, then we’ll go back into the hole”.

Unfortunately this was the first negative airbnb experience I had in my year of using the platform. Until the host fixes some serious issues I cannot recommend this unit to anyone.  I arrived at the exact time I told the host I was going to check-in, and when I walked up the stairs to the unit a random person was just getting out of the shower in a towel. He proceeded to get dressed in the kitchen. I asked if he was the host, but he said he didn’t live here and was just using the shower. Very strange and sketchy. So even though the description says it’s your own bathroom, it clearly is not. During our weekend at the apartment, multiple random people of all ages walked in. This made me feel unsafe because I did not know if they were actually allowed in.   The host also mentions that there is great AC in the apartment. The AC in the room is labeled DO NOT USE and is broken. We had no AC in the apartment. It was awfully hot and hard to sleep at night.   The description also said there was an air mattress at the apartment. There was none and when I messaged the host about it he did not respond. Really frustrating. Half the outlets in the bedroom did not function. All around a horrible airbnb experience.

We had a great stay. The studio is perfect for a couple, very clean, practical and independent.  Dee is very friendly and helpful. In addition, she speaks French. The neighborhood is quiet and pleasant. We never felt insecure. The metro is not far away, 10 minutes on foot, and along the way there are food shops closing late. We also often stopped at a pizzeria that sold really cheap slices. This metro is convenient to go everywhere.  We highly recommend this apartment.

First of all his name is Keith not Seith. And he is not even the one who is listed as a contact person. I believe his wife Hannah is who was extremely rude btw. Just want to put that out there.  Now let’s get right into the review. At first I thought this was a nice peaceful private space for my husband and I to get away but boy was I wrong. We originally checked in on Friday and was going to leave Monday but due to a change of plans we had to extend our stay to Thursday. During my stay there I noticed that there were mice droppings behind the coffee machine on the kitchen table. I also saw several mice running  around the kitchen in the evening . I had no idea that this apartment was infested with mice.  Also the garbage can  in the kitchen wreaked of a garbage land fill. The kitchen was so ill-smelling that I had to hold my nose every time I wanted to use the bathroom or shower because the toilet and shower were both in the kitchen. There are so many horrific incidents that took place during my stay.  I’m just naming a few.  Here’s one on my way out the door with my 2 year old son there was a drug attic on the steps in the hallway. I was so frightened that I ran upstairs to grab a knife. I couldn’t believe that the door wasn’t secure enough for this to happen.  I was going to call the cops but I managed to scare the guy away by showing him my knife. Thank God he did not return but that definitely was a scary situation that could have gone left quickly. I explained to Hannah all of my concerns and she didn’t do anything to resolve the issues.  She offered to call the cops when I notified her of the drug attic on the property. I feel a more serious action was needed such as doing something to make the door more secure. What if that man would have hurt me? God forbid. What if he comes back and hurts the next person who rents? And as far as the filth she just apologized and told me her cleaning lady would be there Thursday, the day I was checking out. If your place is not up to par or you have a mice or any bug infestation you should not be renting it out. And that brings me to my last issue; when I got home today I discovered bed bug bites all over my 2 year old son.  I do not recommend this place to anyone who values cleanliness. This place is not for you so don’t book. Trust me!

This was an incredible trip. Tony is an amazing host ... communicates above and beyond what you'd ever expect, gives great recommendations, and hosts a wonderful and QUIET apartment. There's everything you need in this place, including lots of room. But again, can't stress how quiet the place is! The place is in a great spot - walking around downtown is a breeze. It was a pleasure to stay here and we look forward to returning soon.

Fantastic, comfortable, mostly very quiet AirBnB in a great location.  The unit has a great layout with a big living room with high ceilings and two bedrooms in the back. Perfect size for 1-2 people. The abstract art is tasteful and relaxing.   There are no voices from the street because it's at the back of the building, which is wonderful. When it's quiet, it's really quiet. There are a couple of bad intersections nearby that produce a steady stream of honking at rush hour and weekends, but it's not as bad as you might think. It is muffled, and if you put on some music you won't be able  to hear it at all. The absence of street sounds and voices, and the deep silence most of the time when there is no traffic, make it a total oasis.   A lot of places say they have a great location, but this has a REALLY great location that gives you the most amount of options. You are right on the edge of Nolita, LES, Little Italy, and Chinatown. You have access to all of them. The Bowery metro station is around the corner (same block) and several other stations are just a few blocks away. Quick access to Williamsburg on the J, or take a CitiBike across the bridge! There are some homeless people that congregate in the immediate vicinity, but I didn't feel unsafe as long as I was walking straight through.   There are lots and lots of amazing restaurants all around. Nolita and Soho are gorgeous, with cozy streets and high-end restaurants and retail throughout. You can just sit outside of some restaurant and see so much amazing fashion. LES has a grittier, more youthful spirit which is a lot of fun. There isn't a great park very close, just strips of median parks here and there, but you can walk 15 min or so to the East River Park which is something.  If you get the chance, stay here, you'll love it!

This apartment is a fantastic find for the area! Compared to surrounding hotels, Tony's please is a steal. Tony's swift response and friendly recommendations are a perfect fit for anyone looking to spend time exploring NYC.  The apartment is clean and exactly as described. It is in a prime neighborhood with plenty of bars, restaurants, and activities to do. Book with Tony whenever you can!

The apartment is centrally located in the Lower East Side, on the border of Chinatown and SoHo. The location is perfect. Across the street is a small, unfortunately very dirty park where many homeless people and drug addicts live. During our stay, homeless people who were obviously under the influence of drugs blocked our front door twice in the morning - in one case the poor person couldn't be spoken to and other residents had to call the emergency doctor. Anyone traveling as a family or with children should take this into account. This comment is not a criticism of the apartment and does not factor into my rating - this is simply New York City 2022.  Public transport is not an issue - there are important subway stations in the immediate vicinity. The location is very convenient for transport. There are plenty of shops and restaurants, bars, and a Whole Foods is two blocks away.  The apartment is quite dark - Tony informs us about this very transparently in advance: The living and dining room has two windows that look out onto a multi-story brick wall at less than a meter. The small kitchen also has such a window, which meets a brick wall in less than a meter. In these rooms, almost no direct light comes into the apartment.  The small bedrooms (approx. 3 meters x 2.5 meters) face west and look onto an inner courtyard. These rooms receive direct light - but the apartment does not have a view.  The small bathroom also has no direct light and has a window that faces a dark brick wall. The bathroom is quite clean, although a bit shabby.  The small kitchen is functional and equipped with simple, basic things. Unfortunately the kitchen does not have a dishwasher. Unfortunately there is no washing machine or dryer - but there is a laundromat one house away.   The living and dining room is a bit tight for five people, but okay. The apartment is overall quite clean, but a bit shabby.  The bedrooms are quite small (approx. 3 meters x 2.5 meters). There are cupboards, but also many of the landlord's personal belongings. If there are five people, the fifth person must sleep on a mattress on the floor.  The WiFi is very good, stable and very fast (300 MBit/s down). The apartment is quiet, A/C works - although a bit loud. Overall, in my opinion, the price-performance ratio is not very good, even compared to other AirBnB offers. In my opinion, the apartment is significantly overpriced, even by New York standards.  Communication with Tony is exemplary, very good and friendly, Tony is a very professional host.

I can't give Tony enough praise for this trip. He was incredibly accommodating to our large party and the price was a steal for the great location. The neighborhood around the apartment was fantastic, and there was fantastic food everywhere. Tony was also super helpful in getting us checked in and out on a flexible schedule and he gave us some great recommendations for us to try over the course of the weekend. I have been to the city before, but this trip was the best yet! The location itself was snug for our party of 7 but even still we were perfectly comfortable (and we also expected as much for a single bathroom shared with that many people). Still, Tony did great in preparing the place to accommodate that many. Strongly recommend this location and owner to anyone interested in visiting!

I never complain and am not difficult.   But I strongly advise against it for future visitors.  Apartment dirty, noisy, not as nice as in the photos. Please note, there are not 5 beds. There is a common, uncomfortable sofa bed. The mattress is hollow.  It's right above a bar so a lot of noise at night.  The cleaning lady comes while we are having breakfast.  And what's more, Seth doesn't respond to messages. The only positive point is the metro which is not far away.  Be careful.... Scam

We were a party of 5 in Giancarlo' s place. He explained clearly how to reach the place and once arrived we should meet Ebony, the housekeeper, but unfortunately our flight arrived late and we couldn't meet her. They forgot we were 5 people, so everything was prepared for 4. Giancarlo and Ebony have been both very kind and responsive so we fixed the situation easily, moreover the apartment is well equipped and well furnished, there were extra sheets and pillows.  It is quite clean, although I would suggest a more thorough cleaning once in a while. It's close to the subway and Central Park, as well as located in a safe neighborhood. We have never felt unsafe. You have to consider the 5 flights of stairs with no elevator, but it wasn't a problem for us. I think it's a good base to explore NY.

our stay at Stefano's went very well. the apartment is comfortable, well located and close to all amenities. Stefano was very responsive, attentive and super friendly. our flight was canceled and he was able to extend our stay by one night, thus reducing our anxiety. I will come back with great pleasure!

I would recommend Stefano's place to anyone looking to stay in Brooklyn / the Park Slope area. The apartment was beautiful and had everything that we needed.  The apartment was very clean and comfortable. It was super close to a lot of restaurants, coffee shops, and Prospect Park which was lovely in the morning. I was also able to bring my dog, which makes every weekend away from home much more stress free. Lastly, we had changes to our travel schedule last minute and Stefano was very flexible in working with us to make sure we could get the key and get into the apartment. Thank you Stefano!

What a great spot:  so conveniently located to all of Brooklyn and Manhattan, great neighborhood, really nicely decorated and comfortable apartment with plenty of room for a couple.  Wonderful library!  And a totally private little green garden with both sun and shade, all your own.  Sleep wonderfully.  Stefano was clear, responsive and easy to work with. Would come again happily!

Vanessa and Isaac were very nice and helpful whenever we had any questions. The place is convenient to reach by the subway train and is really not far from the station (a 2-minute walk). So if you want to explore New York and are looking for an affordable and safe accomodation to stay, choose Vanessa's! The only concern we had before was about safety in the Bronx, but we found that really the part we stayed in was not dangerous at all and we were never afraid or anything. So if you are concerned about this as well, don't worry. There is also supermarkets close by, but we recommend Trader Joe's on 72nd street in Manhattan if you want inexpensive but healthy food ;-)  The only drawback to the place is that is in a basement, so you don't really get much daylight, but that's not a problem, as we spent our days outside in NY anyways. You have a cooking plate and washing machine too. So enjoy your stay!!

The short version: Great, nice hosts, great value!  The long version: The host: Perfect hosts, couldn't be better. Always someone at home to help, everybody super nice. So friendly and beautiful people. 5 stars  The place: You have everything you need for your stay in NYC. Nice bed, plenty of space, good shower, fridge, towels, privacy and on top of that, this place is silent! There is some leakage problems in the basement, but it is taken care of by a dehumidifier which is very effective. 5 stars  The location: Of course this is not downtown, and it is reflected in the price. We always took subway line 4 from 183st street station (only 2 minutes away which is a big plus). It arrives every 7 minutes in the morning. We were always out by 10 or 11AM, and always came back home between 9 and 11PM. Subway nr. 4 takes 15-20 minutes to get into Manhattan (Harlem), after that it becomes express train. So another 15 minutes to grand central station (which you will use the most). As 183st station is pretty far from downtown, you will have high chance of grabbing a seat in the train, which soon fills up as you get closer to downtown. Conclusion: Longer traveling time, but good change to get seats in trains, which is necessary for long commutes. 4 stars  The neighborhood: There is not very much to see in Bronx relative to other neighborhoods. We did go to one restaurant "Mexicocina" in other part of Bronx which was very nice. Also the supermarket Bravo is very nice with everything you need and only 50 meters away from the apartment. The downside was that we were the only white people in 3 km radius, which could sound frightening to some people. We were never scared walking from train to home, but also not 100% secure. Overall ok, but you shouldn't arrive home later than 11pm in our opinion. 3.5 stars  The pricing and value: We surveyed tons of cheap options in NYC and decided that this place was the best deal. And yes, it surely is, at least for us. We sacrificed 30-40 minutes per day for longer commuting, and did take a little risk being in this neighborhood, but it was definitely worth it. It's impossible to get private bathroom, plenty of space, nice hosting, i.e. everything you need for 20 bucks per person per night in NYC. Vanessa and Isaac are very nice and trustworthy people and deserve your booking request.   Olof and Jon Iceland

We enjoyed our stay at Vanessa´s house very much. Vanessa and her family are great hosts, very friendly and helpful all the time. It took only a few minutes to reach the next metro-station which takes you to downtown in about 35minutes. We aren´t s scared to move around in the bronx but I think you shouldn´t stay out until deep into the night. (of course, there were some weird situations outside or in the metro)  We would recommend to stay at Vanessa´s house.

The place is located in the middle of the Bronx, very close to the subway. It is around 45 minutes from NY center, so, do not expect to buy gifts and to come back to the place to let them. You will lose lots of time. The place is confortable with the small fridge, the kitchen and the bathroom. But I think that the room is too small for 2 people when you have 2 huge luggages. I do not think that it is a good idea to stay outside when you are a girl and alone. I was a little bit scare even if I am a man.  But I will keep a good memory of this experience. Thank you Vanessa

Vanessa`s room is just as advertised: affordable and cozy!,   Since she was pregnant and had a baby while we were there we didn`t get a chance to see Vanessa and her husband Isaac a lot, but she was flexible and helpful to coordinate our arrival and her husband Isaac was friendly and made us feel welcome at their place.  The room is clean and is located in the basement and I guess that`s the reason why it does`t smell that good. But for us, that wasn’t a problem and all our stay with Vanessa was good! The room and bathroom are small but at the right size for our needs. We could use the kitchen to have breakfast and even cooking in the evening. The house is located in the Bronx, which was said to be unsafe, but we actually felt safe in every moment and we were never afraid of anything even when came back to the house late in the night. There is also a supermarket close and there are stations on 2 different subway lines conveniently located a few minutes walking away, so it was easy to catch trains into Manhattan.  For sure, I and my wife will have no hesitation in returning to Vanessa's apartment in our next trip to New York City.  If you plan to explore NYC full day and just need a room to sleep in and don`t need anything fancy, we recommend staying at Vanessa`s room.  Our stay in New York was very nice. So enjoy your stay!
No stress, clean space in a great location. Thanks again!

Affordable one-bedroom apartment in Upper Manhattan just off the 1 and C lines! I was in the city for some work and loved the accessibility of the place, direct trains to almost anywhere downtown or midtown.  The pricing is absolutely amazing -- I have seen other similarly priced apartments in Manhattan and they are extremely congested/downright suffocating. If you're a solo traveler and need a place to work, stay, this is great!  Minor things to note: 1) I did not realize this earlier but the house does not have any toiletries -- try to carry your own soap/shampoo/facewash or stop by a corner store. 2) The place is well equipped with an A/C, but its not central and only works in the living room. I was there in an extremely hot 90+ week and the first hour or so when I entered would be quite unpleasant unless you stood right in front of the vents. The cooling really does not reach the bedroom so you're at the mercy of the ceiling fan (which is not too bad in the nights).
Steal of a deal. As pleasant of an experience as can be hoped for. Great attentive hosts. Gorgeous accommodations. Really zero complaints. Setting up another stay as we speak☺️

Unfortunately there were some problems with communication and also the neighbourhood was kind of sketchy. The shared bathroom was pretty dirty, wet towels on the floor and the sink + toilet was dirty too… I was not too happy about all of this and think it’s not worth the money. The room was clean and we had cold water and snack, which was nice. Thank you anyways.

This was a great value stay! Our bedroom was comfortable enough and was a steal for the location. We were like a 10 minute walk from the A/C lines (that take you right into Manhattan) and not too far from Prospect Park either. The bathrooms were shared, but cleaned every day. The bathroom and building as a whole has some signs of wear/age, but I think that’s normal for a NY brownstone.  The AC in our bedroom was a GODSEND especially as it was 95+ every day we were there. If I’m ever looking for a comfortable bargain stay again, I will definitely book here!

Michelle's place is a gem! It is only a 10 minute walk from the subway station. We loved exploring Brooklyn and taking the subway into Manhattan. The place is convenient, clean, and a steal for the price!

Area…well it’s east New York. Do with that what you will. As far as the place, it was accurate to description. Comfortable bed, other tenants were respectful during quiet time, good communication. Would I stay here again, never. Maybe if you took the place and and moved it to a safer quieter area than yes. Felt super unsafe. C train is also questionable.
Unsafe place to stay as a tourist. I do not recommend it. Lots of noise, loud music from the neighbors until 5 am.

We stayed for 8 nights in the private room, which is excellent: very spacious, with a big closet, excellent climate control and a very comfortable bed and everything clean. Nice bathroom, with a good shower. Check-in and check-out quite easy. Nice room for a couple of days. Communication with Nick and Tiffany is excellent and they are very kind and cooperative. They helped us during our stay and the responses were always very quick. Nothing negative about the hosts, they were awesome! Special thanks to Tiffany who was there whenever we needed.  Sometimes we feel unsafe in the neighborhood (especially in the first few days), even though nothing has happened to us. However, what bothered the most were the neighbors who are VERY noisy (especially if you are in the private room, which has a window to the street). During the week it was quieter, but on weekends it was pretty bad - nothing the hosts could do, it's something cultural in the neighborhood - so, be prepared for this. We bought some earplugs protectors and managed to get a good sleep after the first 2 nights which were terrible. Even so, the property is very close to the train station, which helped us a lot to have an excellent commute to Manhattan.  Tks Nick and Tiffany!

A++ airbnb experience - Great location. Literally 2 mins walk from a metro station. In 30-40 mins you will be in Mahanttan. - Safe neighborhood. A safe and quiet residential area. I didn't feel unsafe walking alone at night. - Apartment is squeaky clean, and everything is true to the pictures shown. - Great communication. Nick takes time to make sure I understand the check-in process and provided a lot of useful tips as to getting around the city. - Did I mention the best mattress I've ever slept on?  Would definitely return in a heartbeat. Strongly recommended!

So I booked this place for my friends so I'm leaving a review and I quote what they said: "We arrived a little bit early because check in was at 3pm, which is really bad if you ask me but we were allowed to leave our luggage at the house hall so it's all good. If we talk about apartment as just apartment, I would say 10/10. Clean, smellying good, equipped with everything you need. The only concern is surroundings. Subway is pretty close, est. 4min of walk but when you come back at night those 4 mins are really not that short. When you're a tourist you can't really hide that and we felt really uncomfortable walking to our house because a large group of poeple were just staring at us and at one point one guy ran across the street and approached us behind our back while putting hand in his pocket but thankfully police just came across the corner so he just stopped and turned around. We stopped to talk to the police and told them that we're kinda scared to walk to our home and they told us that we need to stay safe here. So for the next two days of our stay we got the uber to get us to our apartment and driver told us that we have to be careful around the area that our apartment was at. I read one review about tourist feeling not safe around here but really didn't take it seriously, now that we have experienced that, I wouldn't recommend this place that much because of the surroundings and that's the only reason. Two girls arrived day after we did, and they left very next morning because they too felt unsafe. And they even booked the place for a whole week. I would say again, apartment was 10/10 but I would rather feel safe when I'm visiting."

The apartment was very nice. The only few things I didn’t like was the neighborhood, it looks so dirty and a bit dangerous, the other thing was the noise from the street and  also not to be able to graduate room temperature, Other than that it was ok !, nice apartment, just to go and sleep and that’s it.

Michelle's Air BnB was beautiful and clean. It was around a 10-12 mins walk to the subway station and a little scary at night to walk around but overall a wonderful stay. Michelle was very prompt with responding, she was flexible, understanding, and sweet!
The simplest check in I ever had! Sometimes when you come to a new area/country the check in can be a stressful experience but everything was flawless.

In general Jack is a really good host and I appreciated his rapid response to my questions and requests.   Pros: The place's photos are accurate The locations is great (Close to a time square, public transportation, grocery store and restaurants).  Cons: The heater didn't work and it was really noisy  The fire alarm was broken.  We found homeless people in the building's reception in two opportunities and there was nobody to take care of it.

Thank you!  We have thouroughly enjoyed our stay at Michelle’s house.   It’s in close proximity to Subways that will have you in Manhattan in one go within a half an hour. Very convinient  Close to Nordstrand Ave. with convinient stores, dine in and out as well as shops to explore  Relatively quitet neighborhood depending on what you’re used to. For a rural countryside Danish couple it was busy, but never did we feel unsafe.   We experienced Michelle as a quick responsive hostess, who went out of her way to ensure we had a “home” that worked perfectly  If you are contemplating staying at Michelle’s, all we can say is that we would do it again

My friends and I stayed here two weeks ago. The apartment is pretty close to everything so we didn’t have to take any long walks or Ubers. It’s a bit small and cramped for the price but it worked for us. When we used the shower the water was coming out weirdly. We just assumed that it was broken and didn’t think anything else of it. After leaving the air bnb on December 2nd, I received a message from Jake asking me where the shower head went, which confused me because we left the shower how we found it. But Jake is accusing me and my friends of doing something to his shower head and asking us for $40 in damages, which is absurd. There was no shower head when we got there and there was no shower head when we left. The shower curtain fell on the third day, the sink clogged not too long after that , and the toilet stopped working the night before we left. Not only that, I messaged Jake the first night of our stay asking where the remote for the tv was and never received a response or heard from him until he accused us of damaging his shower head. I don’t recommend this place unless you want a host that accuses you of stealing his belongings and a tv that doesn’t work.

This is wonderful space. Having 2 floors was great, as my daughter did online classes from one of the bedrooms  and I worked from the kitchen. WiFi, was fast! Beds were so comfortable. Communication with host weasel seamless. Parking garage  1/2 block away was so convenient and stress free, as we ended up walking ever where. All new working appliances. This felt  like home for 5 days to connect with my daughter.

I stayed at Halima's studio for a month. The location is excellent; you are very close to Central Park, the 86th St subway station, and tons of restaurants.  Though I enjoyed my time outside, most other factors about the stay were unfortunately quite difficult.  I was unable to check-in for my first night due to the host being unavailable to let me into the building and having not left a key with the doorman prior. As a result, I ended up having to spend the night in a hotel, with all of my boxes and my cat (I had just gotten out of a break-up so I had several boxes and suitcases with me). I am grateful that the host apologized and agreed to pay the majority of the cost for that night, but this was an extremely stressful and exhausting experience for me, especially given it was the middle of the workweek and the host could not let me in until well into the work day on the following day.  Once inside, the studio was tiny, and was already full of the host's belongings. The tiny amount of closet space I would have had was almost entirely unusable due to the host having piled many boxes and suitcases within it. I had to reorganize significantly in order to get any space for my stuff at all. Many surfaces in the home were covered or full of other things, such as fake plants on almost every available surface. Basic items such as dish-soap and a coffee machine were not present in the apartment. The bed is essentially a mattress on the floor -- which of course means even less available surface area for your items. There were several concerns with cleanliness as well which I will not get into here.  The host was frequently unresponsive to messages. Several times I could not reach her on iMessage, Whatsapp, or Airbnb message.  Overall, I am grateful to have had a place to stay at that time, and in a lovely location, but I would only recommend this if you are on a really tight budget, don't have a lot of belongings with you, and are only planning a very short stay.
Such a great stay! The place was super clean, check-in was so easy, and parking wasn’t anywhere near as stressful as I thought it’d be in Brooklyn. Definitely want to come back!

Only highlight is that it’s centrally located to a subway station. The unit is inside a building with a lobby. The lobby is a hangout spot for druggies and drug dealers the receptionist seems to be working with them and not regulating the traffic definitely scary. The building seems like a brothel you can hear sex and half naked woman in and out at all hours. The room is not well ventilated and super muggy and hot no fan provided the window needs to be left opened for any hope of some fresh air that will never come only weed and cigarette smoke. The beds are extremely uncomfortable no cushion feels like your literally sleeping an wire. The bathroom only has two rolls of toilet paper and no WiFi in the room. I got zero sleep from all the smoke, sex noise, slamming doors, and yelling from the hallways and windows. Definitely ruined my trip I was running around with no sleep the location is OK but definitely not worth your safety and sleep. I would like to warn all females coming here alone or with children this is not a safe location you have to get passed the front door full of men hanging out and just looking for an opportunity to harass you then you walk into the lobby and see people on heavy drugs trying to enter the elevator some did get passed the reception like I said definitely inside job and this is a no kid zone sounds like a porn movie playing all night.
The room is alright, but the building that the place is located in gets is quite sketchy at night.
there was no deadbolt. really sketchy hotel. place was clean tho

The bed is broken. I weight 155lbs (70kg) and each time I stepped to the top bed some bed straps started to break. It was very scary! In addition there were stains on the sheets.  The shower is very small and the shower head is blocked by dirt. The stream of the water was terrible and burned my eyes. The location was great but not it definitely not suitable for more than 2 people. Also there is no hot water for coffee

Good little no-frills place right in the center of everything, so location is 5 stars for sure! We only used it as a base to sleep in so didn’t need anything fancy, and this was great for our sisters’ weekend in NYC. I liked having a fridge and en-suite bathroom as other places we considered had neither, and it was good value for money.  However, there were a couple of minor issues: the security lock on the door was broken, the bottom bunk had a broken rail under the mattress, the only light was overhead (could have done with a side table lamp for evenings, etc.), and the curtains were really just light gauze so they offered zero privacy or shade. With those few small improvements this would have been 5 stars overall. I’d still recommend staying here though.

Jake was a great host. He communicated quickly and the room itself is very clean and beds were very comfortable. Subways is really close by, as well as a lot of nice stores and restaurants. The Empire State Building is literally less than 5 minute walk away!  While the room is great, the street and building made us feel a bit unsafe. Police were called to the building at least twice while we were there to settle arguments and theft. As two female travelers, we were often scared to walk on that specific street past dark due to the people who would hang outside the building, which is a shame since so many nice stores and restaurants are around. Again, the room is as pictured and clean but a slight warning to anyone who expects full comfort.

While the property manager was responsive most of the time to my inquiries this was an unfortunate experience, unprofessional and unsanitary. They say they have “enhanced cleaning protocol” meanwhile basic cleaning wasn’t even done. I have never had a bad experience in an Airbnb so this was a first.  Very Dirty. Not as pictured. The second bedroom has no window or second door, so not only does it feel like a closet, but it also feels unsafe. There’s a hole in the wall above the door that has no window so it offers no privacy or useful natural light.    The bathroom sink was clogged and didn’t drain as soon as we got there.  The response from the manager was “I’ll talk to maintenance about any tips.” I finally asked for draino the next day and somebody dropped it off. Worked like a charm. I felt like the maintenance line was said for the umpteenth time.   The floors were disgusting and hadn’t been vacuumed or properly mopped in I don’t know how long. There were dust bunnies of previous guests hair all around the apartment. There was a sticky film all over the floor that was black when I finally got down on my hands and knees with paper towels to clean because there wasn’t a mop. I didn’t want to walk on it barefoot let alone have my toddler walking, sitting or crawling on it. The paper towels I used were black  after one swipe. Sent pictures to management.   The bath mat looked and felt like it hadn’t been washed in ages.   The mats in the kitchen hadn’t been vacuumed.  The kitchen sink was dirty.  I feel like this is a mill that just churns guests in and out and doesn’t care about actually providing a good experience. The bathrooms are the only thing that match the pictures.
