The apartment is even nicer than it looks in the photos. The location is superb with many great restaurants, parks and activity nearby. It's a beautiful building, and the apartment is in the back so it's very quiet. We had everything we needed and Owen responded quickly to all of our needs and questions. There were no unpleasant surprises, and many pleasant ones.

Great value for money. If you dont have much money to spend i would recommend this place but please note the following: - the appartment contains 3 rooms dedicated for airbnb. We stayed 7 nights and at the end of the stay the bathroom was dirty as we were 6 people to use it. There is another bathroom upstairs with no window and with a low ceiling (if you are tall it wont be confortable) - as there were mosquitos there were a lot of mosquitos dead on the walls (probably scratched by people using airbnb)  - I used to live in manhattan during 18 months and i must say i was expecting the area to be more like in Bedford and the nice williamsburg area. This is not to be mean or hard, but to be honest we had to face all the week long people using drugs (not weed) right in front of the door. People fighting in the park next to the subway. It is not the landlord fault but i feel people should know where they are staying. Nothing to report during day time but at night time ( the latest we got home was 9:30pm) this is not a great area. At the end you get what you pay for. this is ok for a 2 nights trip but i would recommend another area/not airbnb shared appartment for a longer period. The room/bathroom was clean when we arrived and the host was very responsive

In regards to my stay- there were cleaning issues were there from the start, there were gatherings and the loud music on some nights that lasted until 6am...  I have serious COVID concerns in regards to being around people I do not not know, and who are using the same facilities I am using - it wasn’t ok.  So with the place not being as clean as listed, the gatherings that were happening, I requested partial refund because it was definitely not worth the full amount paid. The tub was clog with hair, the sink and toilet was gross, and the tissue roll was replace with a paper towel roll ... that’s not acceptable.   My biggest concern was having people who didn’t live there or who weren’t  guests, coming and going and using the same facilities and spaces I paid to use. This goes along with my COVID concern - I didn’t pay to be around people I didn’t account for - I accounted for being around the hosts and other guests, that’s it.   Airbnb didn’t do a thing about it after contacted them - they told me to try in touch with the host about the refund knowing damn well they wouldn’t respond.   I was scammed.

It felt a bit unsafe in the beginning as I wasn’t sure who was staying in the other rooms or who the hosts were. But after a day I felt OK as I bumped into a few folks. Host was quick to respond and helpful. Area is great but as a girl it felt a bit unsafe after dark just on the block as it’s a semi industrial area. Only a short Uber from the station though. All in all would probably stay again as good value for money and good location.

Communication with the host was easy and good. Overall would recommend this to everyone. Clean apartment with nice decoration and easy check in. The overall area is fine but the street is somewhat sketchy with half-abandoned industrial area next to it. The shower has no lock which might bother someone.

Coco was very helpful during the booking process. Checkin instructions were clear and easy to follow. Even though i landed around midnight coco was texting me to make sure i reached safely and was up still till i got in the studio. A welcome note and fruit basket was a pleasant surprise. Studio looked exactly as listed. Cozy clean modern quiet and gets plenty of sunshine. Cant stress enough on location, its in one of the nicest areas in manhattan in my opinion after spending a week visiting different areas. Very well connected by metro and in walking distance from many areas filled with shops caffees and restaurants. Coco knows the city too well and her recommendations and advice abt all the nice places in the city saved me a lot of headache. Definitely would try to book in the same place next visit.

This is very messy apartment with creepy art and dirty floors ; there are personal items every where, cracks on the windows, dusty beyond words, creepy old bathroom topped with chemical air fresheners ; the host gets defensive when you complain instead of taking care of things. I couldn’t even make coffee because the outlets didn’t work in the kitchen and she didn’t have a coffee maker. My short stay was very unpleasant , I don’t recommend staying here.
Aaron is a delightful host. Very kind, helpful, affable, and communicative. This place was a steal for the price.

Pros: The location is great and conveniently located, the host stayed in communication with us, the bed was comfy and the host was accommodating in offering ealry check in and preparing the second bed.  Cons: the apartment was not as clean and fresh as the photos lead us to believe, the shower body wash was empty, the paper towels had only a couple left on the roll, the bathroom soap dispenser had gel soap in foam pump which made it not work, there was no bidet as listed, the lock box was open and the apartment door wasn’t even shut all the way which made us feel unsafe at first, and we saw at least 10 roaches in the bathroom

Dear Travelers, especially young women  I would definitely avoid staying here. The host Ross does not communicate well and I could not unlock my door to get into my Airbnb. It was awful and very scary as it was night and I was alone in nyc thinking I had my place to stay and didn’t. My host Ross didn’t help at all and when I asked her too stopped all communication with me. Don’t stay here it’s not safe. Thanks

I’ve never stayed at a frat house before, but I can imagine this is exactly what it would be like. Extremely dirty and unlike any of the pictures, bugs everywhere(dead and alive, smashed onto all surfaces with or without blood), black mold everywhere, broken furniture(just for decoration, heard several guests breaking glass downstairs because they thought the table that was standing actually was a table until they put their glass down and the entire table fell apart). We thought the mattress was filled with air since our bodies completely sunk to the bottom but turns out it was not air, just a horrible mattress. The water pressure in the shower was actually good, if you could ignore the fact that it took 25minutes for the water to heat up while the mosquito nest in the bathroom(I’m not kidding, it was like a horror movie) attacked you from all sides. If you are my height or taller (or even shorter), 1m78, you will be hitting your head several times around the second floor unless you crouch the entire time. Good news is: you get big, uneven, chunky, smelly, old pillows to rest your head bumps on! If you actually manage to fall asleep with the mosquitoes in your ears, the street noise starting at 5am won’t let you sleep much longer. By far the most terrifying experience I have had on this app, what a huge scam.

Second time staying here, everything was great! Check in was very easy and having the option for a parking spot made the trip that much more stress-free. Will definitely keep this place in mind for future trips.

Hard to do better on a budget in New York. Area is a little bit sketchy at night, and room was not vacuumed before we stayed. Shower drain was very blocked but eventually fixed itself. Nice hosts and easy check in at midnight.

The space was very nice and the staff at the hotel were friendly and helpful. There were a few small issues with washer dryer and toilet, and the area felt unsafe (lot of yelling and fighting throughout the night on the street). Aside from that I would stay again.

The welcome was perfect, precise and in French (this is a strong point). The apartment was very clean. The neighborhood is popular but not dangerous. The apartment is close to shops and the metro (5 minutes walk). We had a good stay

Perfect location.  Very quiet and peaceful (we lucked out getting a higher floor).  Reception and doorman were fabulous.  It was lovely to arrive to an already stocked kitchen (Amazon fresh!).  We saw a few broadway shows and just toured around nyc for a week. Only bad experience was scammed by a pedicab (just use Uber or the subway).  Perfect vacation and highly recommend aka Times Square.

DON'T SHIP PACKAGES TO THIS AIRBNB  It's a shame I am writing a negative review cause I liked the Airbnb. It's probably not in the best neighborhood of Brooklyn, but it was super close to the train, which was helpful. The room is good and much more spacious than it seems (the TV isn't Smart, FYI), and I think it was great value.  Unfortunately, even though I asked the host in advance and he said it was more than okay to send packages to this address, none of the ones I sent arrived. Three packages were either lost or stolen - they appeared as delivered and received by a person whom the host doesn't know who it is. Another package was returned since it couldn't be delivered properly. A shame all around due to all of the troubles that these things involve, especially during a vacation. Host was communicative but ultimately didn't offer a solution.  Again, it's a solid unit if you don't mind the area, but I don't recommend shipping things at all. Save you the headache, especially if they're of value, and use an Amazon Locker instead.

We felt very comfortable in the room, everything was available in the bathroom and in the kitchen. Daniele was also very friendly and helpful. We were thrilled with the roof terrace as well as the furnishings and furnishings of the room. The kitchen cupboards and bathroom cupboards were not completely clean. In addition, it can get cold in winter because the insulation is poor and you lie in bed right next to the window and it drafts cold into the room. There is a good subway connection and there were many restaurants nearby. There was a lot of garbage on the streets, a lot of homeless people, a lot of rats. Otherwise we were very enthusiastic about the apartment and also about Daniele and would come back.

Exactly as described, this is a very homely little room on a quiet picturesque Harlem street in a convenient location. A great base for getting to anywhere in the city hassle free, and for escaping from the clamour and stress. Lovely art work in room. Highly recommended and good value.

The place is well located, the neighborhood seems a little dangerous and although it is dirty we did not have bad experiences, the location is very close to the subway stations, the bed is very comfortable but you have to consider that the family that lives there is there all the time which can be uncomfortable for them and the guests, the apartment is very small and the bathroom is not clean, the hosts are friendly but despite that it is uncomfortable that they do not consider the guest as a priority for example in the use of the bathroom, the bathroom is located when you enter the apartment so if you want To bathe you need to cross the entire room where the hosts are regularly in order to go to the bathroom or bathe which is very uncomfortable for your privacy, the curtains in the room let in a lot of light so you cannot rest since the public lighting comes in at night plus there is a park in front and there is a lot of noise all the time, it is frustrating that you do not have access to the kitchen to prepare or heat any of your food since as I said it is for daily use by the hosts so you have to consider eating all your meals outside the accommodation.

A safe bedroom to use for a one-night stay in Sunnyside. Apartment was not as I expected, but description of the room was accurate. Building felt a little sketchy but I only had to go in and out a few times. Mario had great communication and responded very quickly to my questions. Good deal for the price.
Keilyn was a fantastic host, and the stay at her place was absolutely stress-free. Plus, Bushwick's an awesome area and well worth exploring!

The room is better than what is published, it is comfortable, a large bed, a mini refrigerator, a closet, and although it is at the end of the house, the uncomfortable thing is going through it to the bathroom, since it is almost at the entrance. The neighborhood gives a dangerous feeling however although we arrived late we never saw anything suspicious, but it was gloomy, the Subway stations are close 5-10 minutes walk, Christine is a kind, sociable and honest host, she helps you with whatever you need, it is a good cost-benefit ratio, in the US the consumption of Marijuana is allowed so you will smell it inside and outside the house if someone consumes it that was an annoying point for my wife and me, respect the Non-use of Shoes inside the house as the host's rules, and otherwise we can recommend it if you are looking for something not so expensive in New York.
A nice cozy room in an apartment in Harlem. The hosts are friendly.  The surrounding area was a little scary to walk through in the evening.

We really loved it. Price quality ratio.  The room is very nice and comfortable. The bed was a beauty.  Christine is a very kind person and even gave us some tips for shopping. Some metro stations are close by and that is incredible. Although I read comments that the neighborhood could seem a little dangerous, we never saw anything strange or felt unsafe even though we arrived somewhat.  If your plan is not to spend so much on lodging and like us, you only need basic things to get to rest and take a shower. This option is for you. I would definitely return again. Thank you Christine!

Unfortunately, we found the room very dusty and the coffee maker was dirty. The room was also different from the photos, without air conditioning and without a lamp, which was a bit annoying as the days were very stuffy in New York. However, our biggest disappointment on the trip was with the neighborhood. We know that Harlem is not Central Park West, but we live in São Paulo, and we know what a dangerous neighborhood it is. It was an unpleasant surprise that we witnessed on the first nights: 1. street fights, 2. drugged people shouting at us in the street, and 3. cries for help at night from neighbors who wouldn't let us sleep. We contacted Airbnb support and after a lot of hassle and days of stress, all we got was being told that we were "doing drama" to "try to get a room for free." As we arrived in NY a little early, we didn't have the flexibility to leave our bags at the house, despite it being self check-in. What we were offered was a fee of 30 dollars to leave our bags early, due to the fee charged by the "cleaning staff". Surely what they are earning to sweep all the dust and dirt from the room under the bed would have been enough. We were uncomfortable getting water from the kitchen, as the host says in her welcome text that upon entering the house, if you reach the kitchen, you have "come too far". Finally, if all this drama hasn't changed your mind about staying in Christine's dusty room, we recommend that you actually use the 145th station near the park. And if you need to go to the pharmacy in the early hours of the morning to buy anti-allergy medication for your rhinitis due to the dust, I highly recommend ordering a delivery. Finally, we loved the shower and a nearby cafe called Common Goods.

I stayed here with my friend for a semester and it was fantastic. I fell in love with the neighborhood and Queens-if you’re going to be in the city for a while this should be your first pick because it’s much more convenient and much less expensive than any other area I’ve seen!  The area is very nice, safe, and relaxed. I appreciated that it was so much quieter than Manhattan and that helped me have a less stressful semester. It’s super close to the 7 train which will take you straight to times square in about 30 minutes (I couldn’t even get to times square that fast when I lived in Harlem!).   The apartment was cute and clean, there was one other guest staying and it wasn’t hard to share the common areas between the three of us at all. If you plan on cooking a lot there is plenty of space for your food, but you may need to bring or buy some cooking tools. The bed was a little hard to share between two people, but if you’re a couple it should be fine!  I would highly recommend this airbnb. My favorite things in the area: the Jackson Heights farmer’s market, the taco cart by the Duane Reade, and La Flor restaurant.

Host: Aarron was a top tier host, he assisted me several times and was always 100% responsive and helpful! Really awesome person.  Room/Apt: Small room but it’s NYC, get used to it. Nice comfortable bed, there’s a heater in the room, and you get to lock the door. Great for just touching base after a day out. Apt is has nice vibes you get to use the kitchen and stuff. Other guest were not an issue at all either. No elevator so if you have a lot of luggage it may be a task to go up the 3 flights of stairs.  Location: Safe area, didn’t feel unsafe. If you’re from somewhere else it may look a little scary but it’s not.   It’s a little distance from subway about ~15 mins but still cool.   Overall: It’s great for what you pay with awesome people.
Very clean & true to pictures, only problem I had was the creep sounds coming from the back bedroom which creeped me out my entire stay .. other then that the apartment was perfect

This was probably our best AirBnB stay we've ever had. Everything went perfectly. Check in/out is sooooo easy and stress free. Michael is a great host. His communicaton is quick and friendly and he provides a lovely place to stay in a really fun area. 100000000+/10 would recommend. We can't wait to come back someday soon :)

Great convenient little place. Two other rooms in apartment with other travelers, great to connect and meet other people! Area was a little sketchy at night, but Im a blonde white girl who was traveling alone and didn’t have too many problems. There are police on most corners from the subway that make the area feel a lot safer. Great high tech apartment, quiet, and great ac!

Small room in Brooklyn, in a somewhat secluded but safe area. When we arrived at night we were scared but the rest of the days we saw that it was not a dangerous area. The best: the fantastic mattress!!! We have rested wonderfully.

I am never using Airbnb after this experience. I’ve booked at least 30 airbnbs across the world in the last 10 years. The unit was clearly not cleaned for multiple stays given the hair in all the drawers and the dust layered on all the surfaces. On top of that, the building front desk explicitly stated that the host was not authorized to have airbnb guests in the unit. However, after contacting Airbnb, they didn’t seem to think this mattered despite NYC regulations and said that we had to keep the reservation given their policy.  So I paid for the full 30 day lease and did not stay there for a single night since it was incredibly dirty and the guy was clearly very shady and lied to Airbnb about the legitimacy of the unit.   Stay away unless you want to robbed. It’s also not a true 2 bedroom; the living room has a not full ceiling height wall that has been counted as a 2nd bedroom.

Steph was an incredible host! She was very communicative, kind, and everything was as advertised. The apartment is very centrally located with lots to do around. The train is also around the corner, so you can get around pretty easily. The three cats in the house are very cute. They are also very friendly, so you should keep that in mind if you are so-so about cats. All in all, I highly recommend Steph's place. It's a steal and I hope it's available the next time I am in NYC!

Very good place for couples on budget. Apartment was very clean and organized, easy check in.  Quick access from Manhattan (10-15 minutes from Union square), parking is available on the streets. Neighborhood looks shabby but I didn’t feel unsafe.   This room didn’t have pictures in the listing. So, although the details were accurate in the description, room wasn’t the one I was expecting to see. It has bunk bed and very small space left for moving. Good for people who explore city and spend less time in the room.

This is a charming house with an excellent location round the corner from restaurants and the bay, and just a few blocks from the beach (and even closer to the main drag of shops on Rockaway Beach Blvd). Jessica was a wonderful host who made our stay incredibly comfortable (the bedrooms are especially cozy and inviting) and who provided nice touches such as beach towels,  bikes for rent, etc.  The eat-in kitchen is a great size and while the outside patio is small, it really is a lovely space to catch some shade.   Thanks so much for everything— we’d happily return if/ when the occasion presents itself!

Staying here made my NYC experience so much more welcoming.  Steph and Marie-Claire were very communicative and helpful when I had any questions and always offered to help with anything. The cats were adorable and mostly were in the background just chilling. The subway entrance was only a block away which was perfect to get to the subway and go to all the tourist attractions in lower Manhattan. I traveled alone and felt very much at home at this location and never felt uncomfortable or unsafe. I will def be staying here again in the future!

I had a nice stay here.  The hosts are generous. They provided a lot of practical tips and spent a nice luner new year eve with me ^^ Quite recommend to those who need a short stay or travel alone.  Olivia is the most clingy and welcome cat I have seen. She loves to be pat on the head and massaged on the cheeks meow meow The neighborhood seems to be a little bit scary but most of the people here are actually nice.

Erica was an amazing host and her villa is absolutely gorgeous! We arrived in the late evening and Erica picked us up at the train station to give us a full tour of her backyard and the upstairs apartment we were staying in. The backyard is beautiful and really spacious, we spent quite a bit of time in the hot tub; it has a privacy curtain which is a great touch. She provided complimentary bagels for breakfast, beer, wine and soft drinks. They have a great grill and smoker in the backyard which Erica's husband lit for us. And the place is only a 5 minute walk to the beach! Her placed felt like you weren't in NYC anymore, and was an amazing getaway from all the stress of the city. We will definitely be going back!

Overall, 5 stars for our stay at Erica's lovely apartment with resort style backyard in The Rockaways!  Booking: Erica's apartment was listed twice, with slightly different names, ratings, and very different price points, which caused some confusion when trying to book. It looks like the difference in price has been fixed, but it is worth double checking before you book! Both listing titles--Beach Heaven and Beach Bliss provide an accurate description of our stay here.  Residence & Host: As a host, Erica is thoughtful, friendly, and accommodating. We so appreciated her flexibility with check-in/out times! It is clear that she pays close attention to detail and finds happiness in others enjoying the space.  Inside the apartment, the comforts of a home away from home are abundant: the memory foam pillows, fully stocked Keurig, adjustable A/C, Thomas' bagels, beer/wine/water stocked fridge, were somehow overshadowed by her very generous welcome gifts and decor.  The outdoors of Erica's residence includes ample space to lounge in the sun or shade, a hot tub which had been immaculately prepared for our arrival, outdoor cooking options, a Tiki bar with a mini fridge stocked with cold beer, wine, and water... It is absolutely beautiful and perfect for a day/night of fun and relaxation or even an event!  The walk to the beach is a straight shot and less than 10 minutes, even if you're walking slowly like we were.  On our final day we decided to forgo the beach in favor of the backyard and its resort-like amenities, which was absolutely wonderful.  We would definitely consider booking here again!

Clean, cozy spot in Williamsburg. I didn't meet Cherri, but Drew was great. Bed was comfy, water pressure was good, and the price was a steal, especially for the neighborhood. Would definitely stay there again!

This location was absolutely amazing and Erica, the hostess was as well. It was the perfect stay for the relaxing getaway that I needed to get myself centered and release some stress. Would DEFINITELY stay here again.

Scam! Big scam! Report it to air bnb within 72 hours of your arrival, otherwise no action possible and Drew and Cherri whose deaths!  You can definitely find better, worse I don't know... Location: False ad!  The accommodation is located at 142 south 9th street and not in Bedford which is the area we wanted. We were looking for the dynamism of Williamsburg => we should rather go towards Bedford Avenue located 15 minutes away on foot. The apartment is located in the heart of the ultra-orthodox neighborhood of Brooklyn. It's great for culture, but not when you have to go to the supermarket and be almost insulted, and stared at every day... Otherwise the accommodation is located just 5 minutes from the Marcy Avenue metro station and buses leading directly to DUMBO. It's great!  The apartment: The lobby of the building was very dirty when we arrived (it was cleaned after 4 days). The apartment is very noisy although it overlooks the courtyard. We hear everything that happens with the neighbors (premises with lots of children or Air Bnb).  The accommodation is not pleasant at all. The photos aren't from today... There are lots of things lying around everywhere. The bathroom is filthy and full of mold on the ceiling and on the bathtub joints. We took 2 showers in 5 days (and it was torture). For the rest, we preferred to go to the gym. From our room, we had a view of a disgusting courtyard (the word is weak) and windows that had not seen rags for years.  The bed is nevertheless very comfortable. This is appreciated after long days of walking.  Hosts: Before arrival and during, communication was very smooth with Cherry. She even let us drop off our luggage 3 hours before. Drew and Cherry don't live there. The people sharing the apartment at the same time as us were very noisy.  In short, it's NYC, so we had a good stay overall, but frankly you'd prefer to add a little to your stay and stay somewhere other than this revisited slumlord apartment. It's the type of city that you only visit once, it's a shame to tarnish the experience with an apartment whose unpleasant smell (of humidity) remains in your memory :(

The host did not use professional language at the property (frequent use of F*** word plus other similar words).  However, not at us. Might have been the host’s way of being social. Seemed to be under the influence.  We felt unsafe!   The bathroom tub and shower tiles were grossly dirty and with mold. So, we couldn’t take a shower! The painting of the bathroom ceiling had turned brown from white and had partially pilled off!  The host put on extremely loud music close to and after midnight for himself (while guests were in their bedrooms trying to sleep)! However, when a guest asked him to lower the music, he did that.   We had to pickup the keys to the property from a nearby deli. Not at the property. Unsafe neighborhood at night with plenty of drunk homeless individuals.   There is no Cherri at the property.  Only Drew.   Other guests there shared similar feelings and we got their contact info incase of needing a witness.   Most definitely, I will not book there again.

Do not stay at Drew and Cherri's place—especially if you are travelling by yourself. We do not think that it is safe for solo travellers or even couples. We were woken at 4am to the sound of a man—we think Drew, though we never met him—conducting a loud and poorly executed drug deal in the living room, metres from our door. The man had invited a drug dealer to the apartment we were staying in. He was clearly high, and proceeded to haggle with the drug dealer and insult his wares. The degree of poor judgement that this displayed makes me confident that he cannot be trusted as a host or roommate. I strongly recommend that future guests avoid this place.  In addition to the drug deal, Drew or the man also played loud music in the living room from 4am through to the morning. Other reviews have reported similar behaviour, so this at least is clearly a pattern. We also never met or heard from Cherri, and there was no evidence of a woman living in this apartment.

Our stay here was great! It is conveniently located for everything we wanted and the train got us to all the places we wanted to see without any stress.  It is also immaculately clean! Dan was very helpful when we needed him and responded really quickly to our messages.  We highly recommend this apartment to anyone going to stay in New York!

The stay at Liqin's was exactly what it needed to be and then some. It was very clean, the room was very simple and straight to the point and Liqin was very helpful and sweet. Loved the attached bathroom that added another layer of privacy for me and my partner. Very quiet and comfortable. Biggest challenge is parking. Wouldn't advise driving if you can avoid it as the search for parking can be stressful. Overall, would definitely recommend the stay for those who just need a private, quiet, clean, simple place to rest their head.

I’ve been to prison before. A prison cell is far more comfortable than this. Maybe even a homeless shelter for recovering drug addicts. Whole crib smells like weird beans. The BUNK ROOM IS ABSOLUTELY FILTHY. FLOOR IS COVERED IN DIRT, LOT OF BLACK STAINS, WEIRD HOLES ON FLOOR DUE TO MITES I THINK, IVE HAD TO KILL ROACHES N ANTS THAT COME IN FROM THE WINDOW. WHY WAS THE WINDOW OPEN?? CUS APPARENTLY THE HEAT DOESNT TURN OFF N TURNS ON RANDOMLY MIDDLE OF DAY OR NIGHT. THE ROOM WAS ALMOST 90+ DEGREES. I HAV EBEEN SICK FREE WHOLE PANDEMIC. STAYED HERE 1 WEEK GOT SICK. ROOM TEMP IS LIKE 100 CUS OF HEAT. FEELS SO NASTY, LETS NOT MENTION THE HUGE ASS FLIES THAT COME IN FROM IDK WHERE. DO NOT STAY HERE. CLEAN THIS SHIT THE FUCK UP. PLEASE.

We had a wonderful stay at Kat’s apartment! It’s bright, super clean and very well decorated. We had all we need and could even check out a bit later, which takes so much stress away on the last day. If we can, we will definitely stay again on our next visit to Bushwick.

Maxime was super helpful and it was clear he genuinely wanted us to have an amazing time. He made sure the fridge was stocked with water and milk, the apartment was impeccable and he checked up on us several times to make sure everything was okay. I would say be careful when walking around the area at night, as 2 youngish girls we found it a little scary at times - other than that it was perfect and amazing value!

I stayed here for almost a month and it was a perfectly fine time. The host is attentive and very kind. She was great at explaining everything you need to know and she's very unobtrusive. There aren't excessive amenities but you definitely get virtually everything you need. There's a kitchen with a big fridge and a mini fridge in your room as well, so it's a great place if you plan to cook your own meals.   There isn't in-house washer/dryer for guests as far as I was aware, but the host was happy to provide fresh sheets and towels as needed, and there's a couple laundromats nearby that take cards instead of coins.  The apartment is very close to the Myrtle Ave J stop and a ton of great food options all along Myrtle and Broadway, as well as a deli literally next door. I found it a great location altogether for spending time in Bushwick, Bedstuy, or lower Manhattan.   One note: there was a user who left a review that they felt this was an unsafe area - to be honest if you've ever lived in a big city in America you'll feel fine. I never once felt unsafe (granted, I do read as male), and I came back home quite late many nights. Even in poorer neighborhoods, New York is still one of the safest cities in America, and I found people in the neighborhood to be really friendly (as friendly as New Yorkers get, anyway). Exercising situational awareness and street smarts will get you far, just like anywhere else. That user *was* right about noise at night, though; a lot of people love to play music late into the night, especially on weekends. But honestly that's like half of Brooklyn, so if quiet nights are important to you you'd probably have to look pretty far afield.  Over all, this is a great home base if you just arrived in the city and need to secure housing, or do temp work in the area, or visit friends who live in cramped boxes that can't host you themselves.

Neighborhood is in a project, people are on drugs everywhere and it did not feel safe. Check in was also a hassle, I was unable to reach the person who was to let me in. There was no shampoo. The bed itself was cheap and uncomfortable. It’s about an 8 minute walk through the projects to the nearest subway and I ended up ubering everywhere. It’s also a shared Airbnb with other airbnbers but there is no vibe, just rules of what not to do posted everywhere.

We had a group of 7, and had no major complaints. With 7 people it does get a little tight on space, but we didn't mind that too much. The location is good, close to the subway and not too far from the ferry. (I would actually suggest taking the ferry, especially on days when the weather is nice.)  The neighborhood is good, never felt unsafe. Overall pretty happy about our stay here!

Maxime may seem a bit to upfront with all the rules you get sent in advance. But just at first glance. As soon as you arrive you realize that he is a very enjoyable character – and just one with one too many bad guests. He gave good recommendations (Silvia‘s / The Shrine) and the apartement allows you to understand a little bit more what Harlem means. And if anybody tells you that Harlem is dangerous, you just reply: not this part. Even to think about safety is unjust to this neighbourhood and its people.

Lovely, arty place in Brooklyn, with great hosts, who are easy to get along with and know the area well! The area seems a bit scary at first, but don't worry it's perfectly safe and you'll find the people who live there are actually really nice and friendly.
if you travel alone, and you'r not afraid to share an appartement  it a good place

Yuting’s apartment is very cute, and exactly what the pictures look like. I was so excited to stay, but when I arrived onsite, everything was dirty. It looked great from a glance but I looked underneath the covers and in the shower and found hair and dirt from previous guests - gross! Yuting also does not great her guests on site, she is usually travelling which made communication difficult. The problem of the dirtiness was never fixed and I had to find another Airbnb that night. It was stressful, but luckily, things worked out.

The stay at this airbnb came with many pros and cons but unfortunately for us, the cons outweigh the pros. The location was great, although that was why we chose it. The Airbnb itself was indescribable. I will give you a detailed visual and mental tour: The front patio entrance of the space is decorated in an ensemble of trash such as a random pile up of cardboard boxes, a rusty old bike, and trashbags scattered about. As you step into the unit, you are welcomed by hardwood floors tattered in months of built up dirt and crust remains. It had a stench of old water and wood which I imagine can’t be good. The stairway leading up to the second floor is in the same shape and aesthetic as the wood floors, except slightly worse. When you find your way to the top of the staircase there is, for lack of a better word and I mean quite literally, an abstruse garbage dump of dozens of pizza boxes, a couch flipped upside down and to the side, and other unknown items at the top. There is a couch fragilely leaning up against the overhead banister, as if one of us could bump it slightly and it could topple down onto the floor below. That’s enough to look at to go back down stairs and take a shower. You enter the unit through a questionable door that is in desperate need of either being replaced or sprayed down with a pressure washer. Just to be clear, almost everything in this house was filthy except the bathroom and bed. Entering the actual unit, it is a nice set up with kitchen, bathroom and bedroom. However, you can’t help but notice that almost every wall in this unit has been tattered in years with mysterious scuff marks, residuals of dirt, random grime. The dirt build-up on the walls and doors would make you think that whoever stayed in this unit walked on walls with muddy shoes. Not to mention the overwhelming amount of large house flies buzzing throughout the space and little gnats lingering around. The bathroom is somewhat tidy and clean, minus the dead cockroach waiting for us on the floor upon arrival. It also did lose some points as there was only two clean towels waiting for us and a third used one hung on the door. We had to wash the third towel in the host's washer and dryer downstairs in the basement, which was currently filled with a mix of his own personal laundry. Yum! The laundry was in the basement of the unit, which had the appearance that it was undergoing a renovation but had a lot of random clutter scattered throughout. The kitchen also lost some points. When we opened the fridge, I began to wonder if someone occupied this unit full-time because there was an array of different condiments and other food products that were outside of the standard Airbnb expectations. The silverware was nowhere to be found, there was no microwave, and the swarming gnats were unpleasant. Overall, the space felt a little too lived in especially when you considered all of the dog hair that laid on all the furniture and floors. Sadly, we couldn’t walk around the unit barefoot without picking up dirt and hair. Lastly, the host was pretty responsive until we asked for the wifi password. We ate up most of our cellular data that weekend and couldn't utilize our laptops because of it. On the plus side, the AC units worked well, as did the faucets and shower head. But that is about it. Considering how unpleasant and uncomfortable the stay was, I am politely asking for a refund. Airbnb should promote better quality stays and experiences. With this being a representation of Airbnb, it is not a good look.

Anthony’s place is very nice cozy and clean,with a very comfortable bed. Anthony was an awesome and accommodating host even though I did not see very often because I had to leave early in the morning and came back late at night. I came back late at night most of the time and never felt unsafe in the neighborhood. I highly recommend!!!

The Freehand is a very chic, well designed hotel. While there, you should definitely take advantage of all the bars and restaurants. The Broken Shaker and the George Washington bar are definitely a must. The only thing I did not like was the size of the room. I was there for 3 nights and the lack of space and light started to get to me even though I was rarely in the room. The bathroom is tiny and I could not wash my face without splashing water everywhere. On the other hand, the shower was lovely--perfect temperature and water pressure.  All in all, I would recommend this hotel for short stays (2 nights max) and only if you do not plan to be in the room much. The rate is really a steal compared to other hotels in Manhattan and even other Airbnb listings. The location is great if you like the East Side (I am more of a west side kind of girl). The subway is only a block away and you can easily walk to Union Sq and SoHo.

Apartment looks amazing, but is very badly insulated. Might be nice in spring, fall or Summer. There is an AC, so the summer might be fine. But it was freezing in the winter.  The room temperature was fine, but because the window and the floor were freezing cold. It was unbearable and I had no choice but to turn on the oven a couple of times to heat the room.  I asked Michael for a space heater, which he did not want to give, because they are expensive. He also said that turning on the oven is dangerous. I fully understand when there is no smoke or carbon monoxide detector in the apartment.  The listing said a completely different apartment nr. on the app. Which I found out after unlocked the key (out of one of the 6 lockboxes that all look the same and I got sent the code after I arrived in the country)  Michael was very responsive and helpful, but also quick to call me a liar and stood on the bed with his shoes when he came to check the windows.  Anyways, it’s a very old building with a lot of issues and a grumpy old manager/owner.  Don’t believe me? Book the room, look at the water damage that was on the ceiling in the hallway. Take of your shoes, feel the floor and see if there is any condensation (bad insulation) on the windows. I would not recommend this apartment or even more so this host.

The apartment is just as it shows in the photos, we only had one problem; The Neighborhood. From the moment you arrive you know that something is not right, everything happened to us; They chased us at night to the entrance of the building, the next day a patrol armed with helmets and shields entered the building, kidnapped a child and killed an Uber in the same neighborhood and we saw a few fights with bricks included.... very bad experience and a lot of fear every time we knew we had to go from the center to the apartment, which is about 1 hour from Times Square. It was very bad for us because the apartment is really perfect to stay in, but I inform you that that area is not the most suitable.

The apartment is great and the location is perfect. Nothing wrong with the house, its clean and its beautifully decorated. BUT!!! Sophia was the most terrible host I have ever met. Already from the beginning I felt a bit uncomfortable with her. She was very snappy in her reply when I asked for something. On both the Airbnb messages and in person. I felt she didnt like me at all. She even talked behind my back with her husband when I asked if it was ok to do laundry at night. Also sighed when she had to come down and say hello the first time. I also didnt feel comfortable using the open spaces. When I asked if I could work in the livingroom for a little bit her husband immediately told me that there is space to work in my room or on the top floor.  Then when the other guest arrived (a 60 something very vulgar man) they both welcomed him and were all open arms to him. I think they just didnt like me. Which is fine but I dont think they realized who I am.  Hosts are not supposed to be your friends as her husband told me and ofcourse I know that but to host someone means to not let your guests feel uncomfortable and to not be rude to them!!! And let me add that I walked out from the house at 8 am and came home around 10 pm almost everyday. I was quiet and I didnt even buy food to eat at home cuz I felt so unease. The couple also had many arguments at home and were very load doing so. Which to me is very disrespectful to the other guests.  When I did laundry I asked Sophia if she could take it out and put in the dryer for me since I had to leave the house. She replied she would do it but added later that this is normally not usual for her to do so. Well on the description in the bedroom it specifically says that the host can put the laundry in the laundrybags and she will fix the rest. So she was basically lying and trying to make me feel stupid about it.  The final day is still a bit of a trauma to me. Sophia told me it was ok to leave my bags since I had a late flight. But suddenly she changed her mind and told me to leave asap. I asked why. And she told me the guests coming in are coming in early so she cant have trespassing guests. To me this didnt make sense. I have left my bags a million times before and never ever been kicked out this early without any notice. And I already put my stuff in the hallway which didnt take up much space at all. I got a bit emotional about it and lost my temper. But here is the scary part, Sophia ran up to me and stood face to face and yelled almost spit came from her mouth and told me to leave now!! I got very scared. No one has ever screamed at me like that, not even my mother. Her husband had to tell her to back off. I have never in my life been through such a traumatic experience with Airbnb. I think this couple need some anger management!!!! And also might I add some training in Racism awareness and valuing cultural diversity!!! Aswell as a course in how to host someone!!!  The trip ended up on tears and had to carry my bags alone in the streets of NYC on my very last day. I feel the whole experience being in NYC got taken away by the way Sophia treated me. Also the toilet got flushed over twice!

My Airbnb host cancelled unexpectedly and I ended up staying at Anthony’s place. I had low expectations given the price, and then I was just completely blown away. Anthony’s place is a STEAL. Phenomenal location, comfortable bed, super clean, and very well designed. Anthony was very friendly, always willing to help, and in general a genuinely kind person. Stay here! It’s an amazing place! The only con was having to leave!

You’re getting your moneys worth with this... well sort of. The apartment is messy and checkin will make you feel like a criminal sneaking around. The apartment is convenient to 145th subway station but expect a $30 taxi ride from anywhere in lower Manhattan.   My biggest issue: someone entered our room during our stay unannounced and messed with the window unit on the wall. (Unacceptable) The host is anal about conserving energy and water and has signs posted about it everywhere.

Pretty terrible experience for a long-stay air Bnb. The host did not inform us before we came that he had rented out his own room. Therefore, he was living in the living room, right next to our room and the kitchen. Making it even more uncomfortable was that he slept in until 11am-midday everyday so we couldn’t cook breakfast or start our day. He also fell asleep early at like 9-10 so we had to creep in, pitch black to go to our room. It was weird. One bathroom for I think like 3 air Bnb rooms and the host used that bathroom as well. He gave us keys but they didn’t work. When we kept questioning the host about the keys he told us we were wrong and we are just putting the key in on a bad angle (even though the keys didn’t work for another guest). We wanted to cook but when we got there, the kitchen was a mess with no counter space, dirty dishes and cleaning mops and brooms in the kitchen. We couldn’t even open the fridge there was so much stuff in the way. When we asked the host to make it more accessible he moved a couple of things, so we just ended up cleaning it so we could cook.   One night we came home after a show and someone had dead bolted the door so we were locked out, when we told the host he said “you have keys, what’s the problem”.   We were supposed to stay for 10 days but we ended up leaving as soon as we found another air Bnb, with Hongzhi telling us he will change the booking on his end if we give him 5 stars - air Bnb said we had no obligation to do that, so here we are.   Maybe good for a one night stay but would not recommend.

This place is super great. Awesome location if you’re looking for something a bit out of the bustle of Manhattan (but still very easy to get there on the subway). The area itself is interesting and has a nice vibe - I never felt unsafe at all. Anthony was an amazing host and went above and beyond - also made me feel instantly at home.   Would definitely recommend staying here 👍 especially for the price. Thanks again!

Liqin’s place is a really solid stay if you’re goal is to spend the majority of the time exploring New York. It was super clean and the check-in/check-out instructions were clear and super easy to follow. The place feels like a hybrid of a hotel and a home which we found cool! The private bathroom was a plus too. Wifi is provided and parking is available for an up charge which was convenient.  The location felt very safe as we were two girls traveling and did not feel unsafe when walking around the neighborhood late at night.  It is about a 10 minute walk from main street and the metro station too. You can easily get to Manhattan by taking the 7 and transferring to another train in about 45 minutes. Otherwise, there’s a lot of great places nearby to explore in Flushing that are easily accessible via walking.  Overall, we loved the place and would definitely stay here again for a NYC trip. Don’t hesitate to book this airbnb!!

Don't hesitate to come to Teola's A comfortable and well-maintained place with the metro not far away to access Manhattan all in a sector of Brooklyn as you imagine it with all its authenticity But without danger

Wouldn't stay here again. The apartment was clean but looked a little run down. The fan in the bathroom made an obnoxiously noisy sound every time you turned on the light, which was especially annoying late at night when everyone else was asleep. The battery in the thermostat control needed replaced so we couldn't control the temperature. There was also a washing machine in a basement area near the apartment that made a very loud and unpleasant squeaking sound every time it was used, which was often. (Imagine a creaking door badly in need of WD40, being opened and shut over and over).   The best thing about this place was the location - a nice, family friendly neighborhood within walking distance of the subway station and a 45 minute ride to Manhattan. If you're not too picky and just want several clean beds for a lot cheaper than you'd spend at a hotel, then this is a decent value for the money. But for me personally, this was far below the standard of what I've experienced at most other AirBNB's.
Travis is an awesome host. Very helpful and flexible. He did whatever he could to make things stress free and relaxing for us. Definitely one of the better hosts I’ve experienced.

Travis' place was just as stylish and beautiful as the pictures. Great location and access to all the stores and restaurants you could want.   On the downside, the kitchen counters and fridge were unfortunately barely cleaned when we arrived. Someone apparently had stolen all the forks except for one right before we got there. When I messaged the host his response was "The new ones don't arrive until Monday. Sorry for the inconvenience." I can think of 5 things I would've tried to get my guest another fork.

We enjoyed our stay at Travis’s place — it was a quick turnaround for work, but we loved the place! If you have a lot of luggage, it’s two floors up, so be prepared! There’s one key to get in, and it’s requested that you leave it at the front door when you leave. My wife and I were a little weary of this, because we didn’t know who else was staying at the apartment, and we had a lot of expensive gear in the place.   I preface this part by saying we agree with the rules and would do the same with such a beautiful place… but there were a lot of rules that needed to be followed, which made us feel nervous to fully enjoy the place. No shoes inside, no eating on the couch, don’t change the heated floor temperature, no oil in hair or on face before getting into bed, leave shade open for the plants… all agreeable, again, but we felt a little nervous to just relax while being there.   I would recommend this place to anyone, and  would love to come back! Just wanting to be as detailed as we can for whoever wants to book after us. Travis was quick to respond, and was even gracious enough to let us have a later check out. You won’t regret staying here!

This place is very clean, super cute, and comes with pretty much any appliances you should need. The only thing that I wish was different is the parking. I feel like there should be a designated parking spot for those visiting so that they don’t have the stress of carrying all of their luggage from possibly a block away if street parking is full.  This may not be possible due to rules/regulations that I don’t know about but if it is possible I think it would be a good idea. Otherwise the stay was awesome and I totally recommend it!

THIS AIRBNB IS AMAZING. I was supposed to have a hell-layover at JFK- the kind where I couldn’t decide whether it was worth booking something or trying to sleep for a few hours in the worlds hardest to sleep in airport. I saw this place and decided to go for it. I felt unsure if I was making the right decision, but opened the bedroom door and knew immediately I had made the right call. The bed. SO COMFY. The towels and sheets. SO SOFT. The pillows. SO FLUFFY AND PLENTIFUL. There was even a tv to help me unwind. Heater, ac, sparkling bathroom and good shower. The self check in was easy and I didn’t have to worry whether I’d be disturbing anyone with my late arrival and early departure. HIGHLY recommend. This made my stressful 36 hour travel day so much better. Thanks to the hosts for really getting it!

Jaran's place was really cute, convenient, and clean. Communication was prompt. The only thing that I regret is that it seems due to some recent bad experiences with guests, they have a really strict rules policy. Not being able to have anyone on the property that wasn't a guest turned out to be inconvenient and stressful. We were hoping to have a local New York friend hang out for an hour while we got ready to go out and that wasn't allowed under threat of being expelled from the property. Even meetings were against the rules. If you don't plan to have anyone over at all, then it's an otherwise nice place.

Our stay at Linda's place was great, would definitely return. The neighborhood is lively with lots of restaurants, coffee shops, and bars within walking distance. However, the street itself is very quiet and peaceful. My boyfriend and I spent a week working remotely and it was a very pleasant place to work during the day and explore during the evening.   Linda was a great host, she was extremely responsive to any question or issue and provided some great recommendations for local places. Definitely try Saraghina for dinner, and if you're visiting on a weekend try the Jamaican catering from the tent outside BedVyne Brew.   Bed-Stuy has a bit of a negative reputation for being dangerous but I felt very safe walking around the neighborhood. I really enjoyed staying here and exploring a new side of Brooklyn that I was unfamiliar with. There's also a lovely park just a few blocks away which was nice to visit during lunch hours.
Great location! I cannot stress that enough!! The check in process was very simple and Leigh was a phenomenal host. I would definitely stay again.

What a pleasure it was to stay with Shondel!   I was on flight layaway for 48 hours and am so glad I decided to stay here rather than a hotel. The hostess is very attentive, flexible and communicative throughout - meaning that, even though I was arriving at a very antisocial time of the morning and at late notice, all aspects of my stay were made very easy for me.   The flat itself has everything you need for a complete stay. I was able to cook, relax and enjoy my time in New York during what may have otherwise been a stressful couple of days.  I would highly recommend this airbnb as a solution for your business or vacation needs whilst in New York, particularly if you’re arriving to/from JFK.  I hope to return again in future for a proper holiday and chance to explore Queens.   Many thanks to Shondel for having me.

Though my guest and I only stayed at Shondel’s place for a night, it was everything we needed. Given we just had finished a 11hr trip, we were relieved of some stress due to how close this place is to JFK. There’s some nice restaurants close to the place as well, about a mile—give or take—away.  Her place was very homey, cozy, and has the adequate appliances that one would need if they were in need of them.  Shondel was also very caring, considerate, and very communicative with us. She has some folders full with info. regarding tours, transits, restaurants, etc. I thought this very helpful and handy, especially for those who stay longer.  All in all, we enjoyed our stay and had no issues whatsoever.
Shondel's place is as seen in the photos. She is a great host, making sure her guests are comfortable. Her check in process was stress free.

This has been the best hosted AirBnB experience I have had. It’s hard to imagine how it could have been better.   Cherisse and Patricia define the meaning of the term amazing, excellent hosts. I felt totally at home and was catered to in many ways that I had not expected. They go above and beyond in making their guests welcome and comfortable.   I am not one for granting five stars but I do so unreservedly in this case.   Thank you ladies, your place is really nice but it was you who made the experience.   Rob

Lovely, spacious room in the middle of everything and just a minute walk to the closest subway station. Loads of restaurants and cafes around so there's always something to do. Mariluz was really easy to contact and check in is completely at the  leisure of the  guest and so simple. The entry hall is scary and rickety (nothing to do with Mariluz) which was a surprise but other  than that we loved staying here and will hope to stay on our next trip to NY!

The stairs up to the apartment are a little sketchy, but the apartment is clean and comfortable. Expect other people to be staying the room next door and in the common room outside.  Great price and location.
Clean and convenient. The owner communicates very well and makes everything super easy and stress free.

The place is as showed in photos, bathroom and kitchen are shared. The room is tiny for three. The entrance is super dirty and the neighbors are wired, one of them get into our place knowing the password and shout to us that he he would call the police because it was an ilegal place. We get really scared. The location is great.
A normal bed was expected but instead a stretcher which causes lots of backpain. Other guests were making lots of noise/slamming doors during the night. Also drugs were used in the appartment.

I loved my five-day stay in Evelyn’s spotless apartment, with all the wonderful  art and books, comfortable bed and ample furniture, plus having a private backyard was beyond luxurious.  i felt safe and welcome, and the kitchen was very generously equipped.  Plus I loved being in a neighborhood that really feels like a neighborhood, full of flowers, enormous shade trees, and people chatting over fences. i can’t wait to come back.

I like the place. It was clean. I like how the bathroom was in the room. I didn’t have to share the bathroom. We paid $5 a day for parking in front of the house. The only thing I didn’t like is the fridge and microwave was downstairs. If I was there by my self I would have been scared. Other wise it was  great. I really like how they respond to my request right away I knew right away I didn’t need to worry about the next day for in answer.

Kandi's place is a comfortable, clean room in a great location in Williamsburg, just a convenient L-train trip away from anywhere you want to be on your New York vacation. Kandi is very friendly and communicative, making for an easy, stress-free stay.

Kandi's place was absolutely perfect for a short weekend in the city. Very close to the nearest metro station, Manhattan was reachable in a couple minutes. I never felt unsafe in the neighborhood (where you can find great eateries; restaurants and coffee shops just two blocks away). Checking in was really easy as the instructions given by Kandi were simple and clear. The room was absolutely lovely and faithful to the pictures, which actually don't do justice since the room is very spacious and cosy. I would definitely book it again whenever I go back to NYC!

The location its perfect; I came by night on bus from LAGUARDIA so I didn't know what to expect.  The building doest not have a lobby and its kind of creepy; also the elevator; but once you made it, everything its as it looks. Vanessa is really nice; I dint meet her in person, but she was always available. The only thing I couldn't find was the light when I came in, but that was nothing.

Daphnee and Allan’s place was clean, easy to find and all amenities were modern and great! Their responses to any questions were also super quick and helpful!  My only criticism is of the neighborhood itself which, as a young, female, solo traveller I sometimes found to feel a little unsafe when walking to and from the train station.  Other than that I thoroughly enjoyed my stay!

The place was just as the pictures, really clean and a lot of amenities. Host were fast to answer all of my questions and left some Subway cards for us to use, which was a really great attention. Subway station at just 15 minutes by foot. However, I really felt like the neighborhood wasn't safe at all and felt scared to walk at night. Also, walls are thin so you can hear everything from the main house.
What a steal for NYC. Two thumbs up.

It was a lovely week staying in Kanti’s place. Clean, comfort, with details that help you forget pressure - the dream catcher on the wall, the stress-release body washer and more. I was super busy at day and night so didn’t have a chance to meet Kanti in first several days, she sent text message to checked in if things are ok in middle of week.   There are groceries and restaurants 1 or 2 blocks away, you can find food easily and no need a kitchen at all. Recommend Win So bakery and if you are vegan Champs Diner has great sandwich.  The room is right next to the street but it’s quiet at night, you’ll hear people walk by in day time sometimes. Personally I don’t feel it bothers me a lot , but if you are a light sleeper and don’t like wake up early, that might be a thing to consider.   Overall I highly recommend Kanti’s place for individual visitor- a nice place to recover from high speed city.

Cool room & rooftop! The room is comfortable. The resident cats are sweet. I met up with friends in Brooklyn Heights and never felt unsafe walking anywhere on the way. Several good restaurants and parks nearby.

Yang’s place was great, exactly as pictured. The J train being literally a 5min walk was super convenient to get pretty much anywhere.I walked late at night and never felt unsafe as there was always lots of young people around. Check in and out was easy and Yang came to the rescue when I left without a key one day.  Super cute cat too that always greets you when you come home :) Yang as a host was super easy going and friendly. If you’re looking for a quiet early night place then I would re-consider as its an active block with lively neighbours and street noise/music. Overall I enjoyed my stay and for the price & location it cant really be beat.

Yang was very accommodating and relaxed, it was like staying with a friend. The room is comfy and the AC was a welcome relief in the heat. Walking to the house from the 2 nearest stations can be sketchy at night.

The apartment is just adorable and it is nice to not stay in a stuffy hotel and actually just feel like you're chilling in Brooklyn. It's close by to a LOT of stuff, and I went to a bar nearby called Birdy's which has pretty cheap drinks and a chill vibe. I didn't feel unsafe in the area at all, and it was easy to get around. the only thing that sucked was having to carry my bag up the stairs, but of course that's not in anyone's control LOL but just be prepared for that! I have only ever stayed in Manhattan, and I really enjoyed my time in Brooklyn at Yang's place. A big thank you to Yang for being a great host and to the kitties for being great companions while I was away from home :)

The upstairs unit was very homey and well furnished with plenty of space.  Make sure to always use the St. Thomas Boyland st subway exit, as Rockaway st can be sketchy at night. Ksenia was an excellent host and very responsive. I would stay here again. Quick access to the A/C trains was very convenient.

Everything was amazing. We came for a funeral and it was a very rough time for us, but the lovely apartment, the ease with which any issues were solved, and the great communication with the host made our stay much less stressful. It's a great, comfortable, welcoming apartment. You'll love it.

Personally, I don't like it. The location area seems unsafe, it is all dirty on the streets. It does not have secure car parking, it must be left on the street. The entrance to the apartment is dirty and full of objects, shoes and other things that give a bad impression. The apartment was clean and organized. That made up for the rest but it was not a pleasant experience.
Great value for money, very friendly hosts. Flexible check-out time. We never felt unsave in the neighbourhood, as opposed to some reviews that implie an unsafe neighbourhood.

This apartment is in an amazing location near great restaurants and more.  Sunlight went above and beyond to modernize the place.  However, we were bothered by the super coming to the door accusing  us of stealing an air conditioner several times.  When we communicated this to Sunshine, he stopped.

Defiantly would stay here again, I had no problem with the wifi as mentioned in other reviews. The water pressure in the shower is nice, the bathroom is well done AND IT HAS 2 PLY TP!!! Katie is super kind and is super responsive; don’t feel afraid to ask any questions. Other than that, if love to stay here again one day in the future!

Katie’s places was simply awesome.  Great location, right in the heart of lower east side.  The apartment was very clean, stylish, and peaceful.  My only regret is that I didn’t book a few more days.  Katie was very quick to communicate, accommodating and made the whole process stress free.  Would highly recommend!

GREAT spot! We enjoyed the central location very much. It very was easy to get to sub stations, restaurants, shopping, museums, etc, in no time at all. Communication from the host was timely and helpful. We would definitely stay here again, and in fact hope to.  A minor note about some of the complaints on other reviews... New York is a just a noisy place. That is not the fault of the location or the host. In fact, this apartment was relatively quiet in comparison to other places  I have stayed. I didn't hear a peep from the neighbors in the building, and the apartment was far enough away from large roads to minimize traffic noise. I'm sure that being a light sleeper and being unaccustomed to the environmental noises of New York makes for an unpleasant stay, but that's not the fault of the host, folks!

BEWARE!!  DO NOT RENT THIS APARTMENT!!!   This apartment is unsafe, dirty and the host is completely unprofessional and unaccommodating. An hour before check in I still had not received check in information. I contacted the host who told me I would have to wait an hour to check in because they hadn’t cleaned it yet. It was 95 degrees outside and we were stuck on the street with our luggage and all the drunks and drug addicts that lay outside the front door of the building.   When we finally got in, the apartment was filthy - hair in the shower and bed, dirt smeared on the walls. Stools in the kitchen were broken. Pillows didn’t even have pillowcases. There weren’t enough plates or glasses for the four members of our party. The listing also said there was wifi in the apartment, but no access to wifi was given. We were incredibly uncomfortable in the apartment.   The final straw that caused us to leave and find new accommodations was when we realized the THE DEADBOLTS ON THE DOOR DO NOT WORK! It’s a very unsafe part of town and we didn’t feel safe in the apartment with our children when we couldn’t even lock the front door!   I contacted Katie to let her know all the problems. When she finally responded she denied the apartment was dirty (despite the pictures I sent) and claimed that I should have contacted her to ask for more dishes and to learn how to lock the front door. Sorry, but those seem like things I should be able to expect without having to ask for them.    I told Katie we were leaving and asked her to work with me to refund the the remaining nights that we paid for but would not be staying. She refused.   I filed a claim with Airbnb. They told me that due to the seriousness of the issues they would refund the maximum amount they are allowed to give, but it was only 30% of the rental amount and did not include the cleaning fee or Airbnb fee. We lost over $600.   PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF THE TROUBLE AND DO NOT RENT THIS APARTMENT.
The neighborhood felt a bit unsafe at times (and would definitely recommend not walking through the park). It was also quiet loud in the suite.

The Apartment ticked all the boxes.   The area itself was a bit sketchy at first, arriving late at night with luggage, but once we settled in and got our barings in the day time everything we needed was close by.   For cheaper supermarket walk to trader Joe's. Many subway stations are close by.  I highly recommend 7th Street burger 20 mins away with The Grisly Pear opposite. Happy hour is 4-7pm and $4 a pint.   A recommendation from Katie was 'El Castillo de Jagua'. The food here is much cheaper compared to everywhere else we went. The beef stew was stunning and at lunch time only $10 with rice and beans.   Another tip is that the Staten island ferry is free and goes right past the statue of libility and great view of the city. There is an clothes outlot center the other side.  Communication throughout was excellent.  Detailed check in instructions were sent 24 hours before check in.

The place is well located but... the heating pipes make a horrible noise that simply won't let you sleep just like that...!  I have visited New York on multiple occasions and nothing like this has ever happened to me anywhere... very unpleasant.

Katie's listing was perfect for our stay in NYC. The apartment is well allocated. And everything was as described and as the previous visitors stated in their reviews. (the apartment has very little natural light, but hey - it's Manhattan and we were there not to hang out in the apartment but outside, and the heat pipes make really really strange noise, especially arund 5 am!! One from our group of 4 really couldn't sleep beacause of that- so concider to take some ear plugs if you're sensitiv sleeper. For the rest of us it was not as annoying, eventhough it sounds more like there is someone hidden in the basemant and tries to get attention. Creepy thoughs).   But Katie is very kind and responsive. The shower was great and clean, the kitchen well equipped, wifi worked great for all of us.   In general: I totally recommend and would stay again!

The Sunday apartment is super comfortable. It has everything you need for a nice stay. The bed is spectacular, the bath water comes out strongly, the room temperature is excellent and even though it is a private room, Sunday is quiet and makes sure you feel in your own place! Super generous, one day he uncovered the bathroom for us at 10pm after the paper jammed since we couldn't.  The only thing to highlight for those travelers: there are two subways near the house, one is the L - Myrtle Av. and the other is the J - Morgan Av. I DO NOT ADVISE YOU TO ARRIVE FROM THE AIRPORT OR TO USE THE MYRTLE AV. STOP AT NIGHT, since it seems unsafe and you will not feel comfortable, better to take the J. Everything, a 10!

If you are someone looking to have an great skyline view of NYC, AND not afraid to spend a few thousands dollars, this is it.  There are multiple balconies for you to take amazing pictures.  We’ve stayed at a few high rises in NYC prior and this offers the best view despite being only 26 floors.  Note: for those who sleeps early… there is a bar on the 15th floor.  Also, we have a few issues with cleanliness.  Not sure if it was a one off situation but the bath tub’s water was disgusting.  They also forgot to make our bed on the day we arrived.  Not something you’d expect for the money we paid.  Other than that… we absolutely loved every seconds we stayed there.  If you’re coming here with a romantic partner, things could get really frisky.
Literally there were 6 homeless people having a pizza party in the lobby on my second night staying there

I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone. The convenience of the metro (4 or 11 minutes walking depending on where you get off) doesn't make up for the area that it's in. When you get off the metro you see trash instantly and continue to walk past trash, random chairs, grafitti, and all types of garbage.  The location of the home is also strange because it's not surrounded by other homes at all. It's by empty yards and packaging factories and then the house suddenly appears. If I had been by myself rather than with family I would have felt uncomfortable walking by myself.   The airbnb itself provides you with what you need but for the price (similar to other airbnbs) it doesn't make sense to book an airbnb that's in a shady area. It makes you think that Brooklyn isn't a nice area. Again don't book this place. There are other nicer places that are a little bit farther from the metro but worth it.   Also the area is loud even though there aren't any other homes. The host did say there was a promotional event going on  but it was still loud from other cars and random fireworks before the event happened.

Nice and very clean place! one block away from an L metro station and 10 min walk to C. Easy to move around. It is located in the middle of an industrial area, so in that sense, the area is not very nice, but I never felt unsafe or anything like that. From what I saw also, looks like the power of gentrification may be on its way there too!  I would totally stay there again.

Lenny's place was good. I had a last minute cancellation a day before my trip so this was a last minute booking. A few pros and cons to the listing.  Pros: Very spacious, actually bigger than the photos; bed was very comfortable; if you're traveling with a lot of people this is a good space with the two bedrooms; very quiet block (I am from New York so when I say quiet I mean silent)   Cons: As mentioned in her listing, if you are visiting New York to see friends and family as I was, I would not book here because absolutely no one can visit unless you pay to have the max amount of people on the listing. Again yes it is stated in the listing but its a hard no. So if you enjoy company this isnt the place for you. Its above where she lives so I felt like I had to tip toe to not disturb her when come back to the place late at night. Lastly, the tub in the master bedroom was rusting which was a little creepy.   Again this was a place airbnb had to book for me due to a unforeseen cancellation so I would not have booked this myself. Lenny was gracious to let me stay here even with my extra guest. Just giving a full heads up to next guest.

This apartment is lovely. Spacious bedrooms, super large living room, a true kitchen with lots of full size appliances. My favorite part was the balcony.   Bed was super comfortable and I think this was the best pillow of my life!  Bathroom came with Body wash and shampoo. Don’t forget your own lotion… like I did.   Great internet. Beautiful neighborhood. Safe.   Communication is as great. Host was warm and helpful. Checkin couldn’t have been easier.   Street parking was usually available depending on time of day, but having a designated place to park in the driveway was a life saver.   About 7-10 minute walk to food, drug store, Dunkin, laundry mat and more. Or drive. A lot of the stores in this area have parking. And of course everything delivery is an option for grocery or Door Dash/ UberEats.

Lenny's apartment was very clean, comfortable and close to the subway line.  The neighborhood is more commercial/industrial than residential, but we never felt unsafe even when returning late at night.  It was actually very quiet because all the businesses shut down every evening and all weekend.  The place had been remodeled and updated with new appliances.

CLEAN, AMAZING VIEWS in every room, a comfortable space and an accessible and safe location.    My husband and I stayed  for a week...easily integrated into the neighborhood, amazing restaurants and grocery in every direction, walking distance to Central Park, City MD for easy COVID testing required for our travel, Hell’s Kitchen, Times Square....convenient location to so many city spots.   Host was very responsive.   Part of our goal with this visit was to recoup after many stressful months...definitely was able to in the space.  Slept in a very comfy King, enjoyed the TV’s as well as morning coffee all while taking in the amazing views. Also had enough room to setup an office space for both my husband and I.   The city experience with COVID: restaurants were 25% capacity going to 35% today 2/26, everyone was masked, temperature checks, everyone was safe and cautious.

The Airbnb is in a very, very good location! Especially for the party people. There are numerous clubs nearby. In general, everything can be achieved wonderfully. Unfortunately the towels are not changed and if there are three of you there are a few for a week. The apartment only has a refrigerator and a microwave, so you can't talk about a kitchenette. But completely sufficient if you don't want to cook yourself. We thought the keyless system was great because you didn't have to worry about losing keys and having to leave the party separately.  It was also clean by American standards.

Good spot for my quick trip for business at The New School. It’s barebones, so don’t expect a posh experience. But it’ll meet your basic needs and keeps you convenient  to anywhere you need to go. I also would suspect that staying here on a weekend would be a very different experience. But as a weekday visitor, I didn’t encounter much in the way of issues with noise, etc. staff on site was incredibly nice, too.

Great communication!!!  Good central location within walking distance of Times Square, subway stations, and many other things!  The street was kind of dark walking home at night but we never felt unsafe.  Would stay again for sure!

Great stay! Overall a cozy, clean 1st floor apt in a great location! Check in was easy with a kind host. Easy walking to broadway shows, various landmarks, and restaurants! Safe neighborhood, never felt unsafe walking around even late at night. Would stay again when visiting this area of NYC.

We were able to drop our bags early which was very much appreciated! The location of this unit is wonderful. Short walk to the subway, eateries, and Times Square. The space is a corner unit and fairly large. The mattress is not as thick as the picture shows and is a bit hard and uncomfortable. We had issues with the wifi the entire stay. It was inconsistent and we had to unplug multiple times for it to work temporarily at best. The description mentions Netflix, which is has, yet you are asked to log into your own account.
