Getting locked out of our place in Midtown Manhattan in the middle of the night was inconvenient for my son and I, but it could actually be dangerous for say an elderly couple or a  group of young girls, or a single mom with young kids  etc...

I had to cancel my stay due to finding religiously offensive (and scary) graffiti on the wall, which was painted over but you could still see it. The host wasn’t there and never appeared in person. I complained to Air bnb but was given many excuses and only got a portion of the money back. The host denied the graffiti being there and when I asked to go together to check it she didn’t answer.

This location is ideal for a Brooklyn visit. The building is well-maintained with a beautiful luxuriant front garden and a lovely back yard with lawn furniture and shade. Michelle is the host and she takes great pride in her home. It shows in the cleanliness of the room and bathroom, which is shared. Our room was large with a comfortable queen bed, a frig, microwave, and a closet. Linens are provided; the shower has shampoo and body wash. Be prepared to climb stairs to get to your room; ours was on the third floor.  Great location, great host. And very reasonable.

I had a terrible experience with Susan for a short period of stay. My intention were to stay there for a little longer period. Stairs were very unsafe to take my stuff on third floor. No safety, no security. I was not told the i'll be on third floor, it was very hot there and lots of men were staying and hanging  around in the kitchen and in the hallway. She didn't mention that lots of men will be there. The room was very messy and smelly. I asked her to move me to the 2nd floor if she can. She took me to the 2nd floor and it was the same situation... 3 men were hanging in there and staring at me and that was very uncomfortable. Air-Conditioning was not in working condition and fan was broken. She had small dirty pillows for the pets which i couldn't even use it. So called blanket... can't even name it as blanket if i cover my upper body then my legs were out of so called blanket and if i cover my legs then my upper body was out of blanket. There was no security lock on the doors. She was calling me every after 5 minutes don't use the fan continuously while it was 90 degree outside. I spent all night staring at the door and broken fan. She knocked at my door 20 times just to make sure that i'm not using fan continuously. Washroom was dirty and unsanitized. Water wasn't draining from the bath tub. Washroom was very smelly and dirty. Cockroaches were crawling on floor and near the stove. There was no lock on the front door and anybody can go in and out. There was no smoke alarm or fire extinguisher. Floors were dirty. The men pee while standing on the toilet and never clean the toilet and smelly. She didn't offer any help to clean the toilet then i had to buy soup and cleaners to clean her toilet and the smelly tub, so i could use it. Water was not draining in the sink and in the tub. What a horrible... Plz safe other people specially females for this horrible experience. Well Susan always says... I NEED MY DOLLAR, I NEED MY DOLLAR. She is uneducated/ illiterate woman with lots of unnecessary attitude!

This is a lovely little apartment on the bottom floor of a brownstone.  You have everything you need besides toiletries and groceries, and communication is quite easy as the housekeeper (a very nice man named Malose) is usually on site.  The plumbing, heat and cooling, and cleanliness is great.  There’s Netflix in the bedroom.  The beds were of good quality as my mother and I stay in separate rooms.  That’s not to say it’s perfect.  The mirror in the bathroom is too high and the door into the brownstone is tricky, as well as being located in a sketchy neighborhood (try Williamsburg instead of Bed-Stuy if you’re worried about this).  The major downside, however, is that this Airbnb is treated like a regular apartment listing.  I had to sign a separate “guest agreement” as did my mother and talk to the lister on the housekeeper’s flip phone upon arriving and leaving.  We had to give our IDs so photos could be taken also.  This is more than I’ve needed to do with actual apartments I’ve rented in 3 different countries, and Airbnb takes care of this so you’re not inconvenienced when getting in.  Otherwise the communication was nice and prompt.  I would actually stay again if it weren’t for the neighborhood and the door—you have to be shown how to open it by Malose.  We took lyfts instead of hazarding the subway, and they were really affordable to get to any of the boroughs or just to Williamsburg or Downtown.  I highly recommend it for low maintenance guests and short stays.

Great apartment with an amazing view! I had to book this apartment last minute because of renovations in my building (I live in the neighborhood) and Jason was very accommodating and friendly. He made the whole stay and experience very easy and stress free.   The actual apartment is really nice, quiet, very clean, modern and open with one of the best views of Manhattan I've seen - it's just like the pictures. The building itself is really nice too, I wish I had packed better and got to use the gym in the building, it looked really nice.   The apartment is in a really cool part of the neighborhood right by the water with bunch of cafes, restaurants, bars and venues in close walking distance. It's also very close to the train and the Williamsburg bridge which made getting to Manhattan really easy.    I would definitely stay here again and highly recommend to others! Oh and there's a nespresso machine and coffee for the morning too!!

Great apartment, I had a great stay there! Jason thought of everything and we immediately felt at home.  The view from this apartment is breathtaking! I could have spent hours looking out the window! Very well located in Williamsburg, however you don't have to be afraid to walk a little sometimes :) the metro is easily accessible, but what a minute's walk! I will return without hesitation.

What can I say? My stay at Caroline’s place could have been better.. a lot better. The 1st night I checked in with a hurried and impatient greeter. She was the Hosts’ niece and I must say, she was not pleasant. She quickly gave me a tour, a brief tutorial on how to unlock the front door. (Which proved to be incredibly difficult, if not impossible.) She then asked for a $30 late check in fee, although my flight was delayed beyond my control. I did mentioned to Caroline that I may need to check in late, hoping she would understand. I guess that came with a price.. Nonetheless, I pressed on. I couldn’t rest as well as I would have liked, as the bed was incredibly hard and the sheets were dingy. (I ended up purchasing my own - an additional $30.) When I returned from an evening out, I attempted to unlock the door, but I found it nearly impossible. The front door had a jam tighter than dr. Dre’s beats. After suffering with the lock and key and slipping on the steep, front steps, I accidentally rang the doorbell and a mysterious man from upstairs let me in. To my surprise, he had access to the bathroom and kitchen in my area. Since we hadn’t been formerly introduced and since I paid for an exclusive space, I felt even more uncomfortable, with only the hard mattress to look forward to. I decided to unwind with a nice hot shower. Unfortunately, my shower was cut short because the hot water only lasted about 5 minutes, not even enough time to rinse the disappointment off my face. The next day came and I began to notice a faint gas smell, which had me concerned. After I spotted the mysterious man (who was later revealed to  be the house keeper) exiting my “shared” kitchen, the faint smell passed. With the long list of rules Caroline left, steep, slippery front steps, hard mattress and unpleasant welcome, my stay here was sub par. If I had the choice I would not stay here again. Too many surprises at Caroline’s and none of them pleasant, had me wanting my own home and my own bed.

Alan is very prompt and nice. He will try to make your stay as comfortable as possible. And I want to be as accurate and fair as possible as I rate this place.   Overall, the place is great if you don't mind walking and want to save money.   The place is very clean (some guests were not, but that’s not really the host’s problem), great kitchen with many amenities, comfortable bed, enough space to move around…a pretty nice place to stay.  My only problem was the commute. Because I had to travel to Times Square for work everyday, and I usually hang out in the city, this wasn't the best value for me. I have lived in the city for 4 years now (had to airbnb for work reasons), and maybe I was spoiled but the idea of walking (esp in the cold) to the subway stations that were 15-20 minutes away was not the most enticing one.   And I think the posting needs to change – this place is not a 28-minute subway ride to Times Square. Also the neighborhood is gentrifying but it is a bit rough and sketchy. But I felt safe during my stay there. Just don’t walk around late at night.   So overall, if you are okay with walking, this place is a good deal.

I never got to meet Alan personally, but he responds quickly to all messages and called me back quickly when I had an issue getting into the building.   The apartment is set up like a mini-hotel or hostel, with a fully-equipped kitchen and a dining area.   The room I stayed in had a bunk bed with a double bed on the bottom and a single bed on top. There was also a coffee table and a large flat-screen TV (more on that later). In terms of space, it was good for one person, and I think if I'd been there with a partner (or child/teenager) coming back at the end of the day after exploring the city, it would be fine, but it would be difficult for more than one or two adults to navigate the floor space at one time. If you are good at coordinating that, though, and looking for a clean, well-equipped space with a wonderful host, then this is an excellent choice.   Alan doesn't allow guests to wear shoes in the apartment, so you don't have to worry about getting muck all over your socks or feet. The place is also cleaned daily (including the bathroom), so unlike some Airbnbs I've stayed at, you won't be scared to brush your teeth, take a shower, make coffee, or eat breakfast. The apartment is also pest- and vermin-free, which is also sometimes a rare commodity in the Airbnb world.   The large flat-screen in the room was a Roku TV, offering Netflix, Amazon Prime, and other shows I didn't check out because I was busy watching the other two.   The only negative experience I had was with some of the other guests who checked in the second to the last night I was there. I came back to an unflushed toilet and dirty towels in the bathroom. When they returned to the apartment so noisily they woke me up (at 3am), they disregarded the no-shoes rule (as they did the duration of their stay) and proceeded to turn on their TV full-blast, preventing me from getting back to sleep until after 7am. And throughout their stay they continued to disregard the rules, leaving dirty towels in the bathroom, hair in the bathtub, empty toilet paper rolls after using the bathroom—plus that TV blaring nearly 24/7 & wet, dirty shoes all over the floor.   In no way do I blame Alan for the other guests being jerks; he did contact them right away to remind them of the rules—but this had no impact on their behavior, so remember that this is the risk you take when you are in a hostel-like setting with the host of-site rather than staying in someone's home or in another situation in which someone is there to to take care of problem guests face-to-face.

Allen's place was in a hidden gem of Brooklyn not quite yet gentrified but not unsafe. I stay there alone with my eight-year-old and we were quite comfortable coming in and out at any time of night I especially like the key less entry. A bit of a walk from his place to the subway where you'll have to make a connection to get most places in Manhattan however a nice walk to the AC E train as well.  On the last day we did have a plumbing issue but it was fixed before 8 AM the next day and I want to refunded us quickly and was available at 2 AM when the malfunction occurred which I very much appreciated. The trash was taken out every single day and apartment was clean I barely noticed the other residents although the people I met briefly were very kind it was hot the week we were there and we were always anxious to come home to the air conditioning that blue cool air 3 inches away from my heads up my major plus. I would absolutely stay here again and recommend it to anyone else I would buy at a building in the area if I could.
Had to take a ride from the train station because the area seemed unsafe. Was greeted by dirty, stained sheets. Space much smaller and not as well kept as appear in pictures.

We had a lovely time in New York. Sharon was very nice, always approachable and was happy to answer all of our questions about the city and give us good tips.  The room is small, but that's not a big deal since you're only there to sleep anyway and you can also spend time in the spacious kitchen. The residential area is safe and you don't have to be afraid at night. Subway is 5 streets away and you can also reach Willamsburg in 15 minutes by Citi-Bike (station 50m away). I can only recommend exploring the city with a city bike. I found the traffic generally very relaxed and the drivers much more considerate than, for example, in Berlin.

We have mixed feelings about this apartment: 1. Shanie was always very pleasant through the Airbnb chat, allowing us to leave our bags on the last day and even allowing us to receive a postal delivery. 2. But there is a problem with the cleanliness...there were too many bugs, including cockroaches that made the stay unpleasant. Shanie attributed it to us not taking out the trash...but that's not true. There were cockroaches and it is a problem they are aware of as they have several bug inhibitors placed throughout the apartment.
Close to JFK, tucked away lower floor unit in Queens. Although neighborhood can be a little scary, the proximity to public transport is great!

This apartment is located in a beautiful neihborhood with lots of great conveniences and a very safe environment for most good and peaceful people.  The area is surprisingly clean for NYC, and actually reminded me more of Boston in its cleanness and style.  The hosts were outstanding and very flexible to let me add on a night at the last minute.  They are very friendly and really make you feel like family by going above and beyond the expected, for example they offered to let me use their coal and supplies for the grill out back.  The comparatively low price per day makes this place a real hidden gem for most people, and I highly recommend it for families and people who don’t go outside at night.  There is a large police and secret service presence because the mayor lives somewhere near by, so the area feels very safe during the day, but unfortunately, unlike anything else I’ve ever experienced in Brooklyn, police officers harass you if you go for a walk to catch some air or smoke at night.  It’s really disheartening when the people who usually make you feel safe and secure in their presence decide to turn on you and make you feel threatened.  For example, they pull up next to you and drive really slowly right next to you while staring at you for a couple blocks, others follow you around on foot and make a point to keep passing by you and veer towards you as they walk by, and others still try to scare you by speeding up extremely fast when they drive by you and then backing up to right where you are walking and then speeding forward again repeatedly.  They do this in police cars as well as black windowed undercover cars until you feel intimidated and go home.  Unfortunately, despite the excellent hosts and the gorgeous and convenient area, this behavior ruined my experience because I like to take walks at night.  Not a good area for people who like to enjoy a peaceful reflective walk at night, but highly recommended for anyone who doesn’t leave the house after midnight.

Maria was so incredibly nice and accommodating!  After much back and forth messaging about our apartment hunt (moving to NYC from out of state), she even invited me up for tea and conversation to sooth my sore throat and my stress. Couldn’t ask for a more hospitable host. 😊

Great location! Near park and restaurants. Grocery store and drug store nearby along with subway access.  Not fancy, but clean. Space as pictured and listed except for "central heat or heater in listing".  Unfortunately, heat in unit is not controlled by tenant, but by landlord upstairs.  We were cold......

Had a very nice time staying here, Daniel was here upon arrival and was happy to give me a tour / guide to the place.  Initially I was slightly skeptical of the location, however I never had any problems nor did I ever feel unsafe when walking about. The property is in the heart of a Jewish neighborhood with a Center on the other side of the road. There is a supermarket around the corner where you can do your shopping (less than 2 mins away).  Subway-wise, the entrance is literally on the opposite side of the road. No transfers required, you can get to Manhattan within 15-20 minutes on a single ride and an extra 10-15 mins on the same train will get you to Times Square. If you are planning on using the subway frequently during your stay, I would highly recommend getting a 7 day metrocard for $32 (includes the $1 new card fee). Fares are a flat $2.75 so you get your money back if you've used the subway 12+ times.  There was no TV, however this was not an issue as I was spending most of the time exploring the city. There is WiFi and was very fast / reliable.  This room was based on the ground floor (1F as Americans would put it), however the entrance to the property is on the first floor (2F) so you have to go downstairs to get to the room. The stairs are abit creaky so you will notice is someone is coming down. The property has a Kitchen area and bathroom on each floor. As this floor only has one bedroom, you've effectively have your own bathroom.  One thing to note was that this room was next to the kitchen / dining area, so you will hear if anyone is being particularly noisy.  Its not a premium place, but you're not paying a premium price. Considering the price and ease of getting into Manhattan, this place is an absolute steal. Would certainly recommend this place to anyone wanting to stay in the Brooklyn area.

I stayed here for 3 weeks while apartment hunting. The location itself is in a super boring orthodox Jewish neighbourhood, but as a girl traveling alone it felt safe to me. At about 30 min train ride to midtown Manhatten  the price is really a steal.  I think it's important for anyone staying here to know it's really pet friendly. I brought my dog and some other guests brought 2 small dogs themselves, Daniel feeds the neighborhood stray cats in the yard and has a couple cats himself. He really keeps the place immaculate considering all the animals/ people coming and going.

Sharon is a nice person, but the advertisement is not sincere, there was not much privacy, there was an unpleasant smell covered with a lot of air freshener and a little mess, in short it is not what we expected, we still thank Sharon and Lola for hosting us

Caroline was a very kind and gracious host. She was able to work with our schedule, and it was an excellent and stress free place to stay in New York. Her apartment is very cozy, and has everything that you could need available. It is very close to public transportation, the Q47 bus line is about 50 feet from the front door. Will definitely stay again when I’m in New York.
The place is a little old, and the decoration is outdated and borderline creepy. The host was awesome, and the location is ideal.

We stayed in Giorgia's apartment for 15 days and we have no complaints : it is a large, clean, fully equipped apartment. Comfy bed, great shower, nice furniture, all-new appliances, and the outside terrace and garden are a nice bonus. Location's ok: residential, quiet neighbourhood, seems bit sketchy at night maybe, but we had no problems. Nice breakfast place 2 minutes away, corner of Saratoga and Macdonough. Close to 2 subway lines, maybe a bit far from tourist attractions (25-30 min train ride to Lower Manhattan), but great value for money overall.

Giorgia's apartment conforms to the photos and the description given. His instructions when booking were very clear and detailed, we arrived at the apartment without difficulty. We had some problems with the keys when we arrived, it was stressful but the neighbors helped us and Giorgia was responsive by message and everything was sorted. The apartment is a large, comfortable studio, pleasant for a family or a couple. The garden is a plus that we were able to take advantage of (sun in the morning and early afternoon). It is generally well equipped. We didn't take advantage of the area much, the shops are nearby. The subway is accessible and allows you to get (30-40 min) to southern Manhattan. Perhaps a little far from the center to take advantage of tourist activities if it is a short stay in New York (this was our case and the return to the apartment seemed long in the evening).
Sidney was great! Super fast response and stress free booking.  Place was great felt like home.

Overall, it was an OK place to stay and good value for the money.  Pros: The bed/mattress were comfortable; it was an elevator building which was key since it was on the 3rd floor; there is laundry room in the basement that required a keycard payment, though Lisa was nice to lend me her card (and a cup of detergent) for a $5 load wash/dry, which I paid back to her in cash; the location was pretty decent near Columbus Circle.  While neighbors on other floors can be loud, Lisa’s neighbors were pretty quiet.  I was there for 2 weeks and didn’t have any problem with noise.  Cons: While location was good, you walk another half block west and it gets sketchy… there were homeless and sketchy looking people on the corner of 10th/57th.  It’s a big busy street, but it felt slightly unsafe at times.  The bathroom didn’t look and smell as good as it could’ve been; there were mold on the bathroom sill which wasn’t pleasant and then there was the smell of rank water/BO as well.  Most of the smell may have been from the shower curtain or the slit between the tub and sink pedestal where water could catch.  For the price, it’s pretty good.  You get just the bedroom… no living room as the owner sleeps in there.  Lisa invited me to use the kitchen, but it’s pretty small.  It’s basically for sleeping and bathing with no frills.  For the same cost, I would probably pick another place next time.

We stayed at Ricardo's as guests for a total of two weeks.  Communication in advance worked without any problems and it was very pleasant that we were able to check in relaxed despite the flight delay. When we arrived the room was clean and as per the pictures. The residential complex/building complex seemed very safe and tidy to us the entire time. The neighbors we met were very nice and we never felt unsafe in Harlem.  On the first morning we noticed that the bathroom wasn't that clean and didn't meet our expectations. There is definitely still room for improvement there. It also seemed a bit strange to us that as guests we were supposed to clean up after ourselves (of course), but we would have liked the host to do that in some places in the kitchen (e.g. dishes in the sink).  As we have read in other reviews, we can agree that it is sometimes noisier at night due to the neighbors. However, you can still sleep well if you are tired from sightseeing.  During that time there were several shootings in the apartment (as described in the ad), the people were always nice and we didn't feel disturbed.  If we had any problems, we were always able to turn to Ricardo and a solution was sought and found. Overall, he was very hospitable and repeatedly asked how we were doing.  The check-out also went without any complications.  Overall, we can recommend the apartment because you're actually out and about all day and don't come back until the evening. In summer it can get relatively warm in the room, but the AC helps with this problem, although it is a bit louder.

I booked this Airbnb in hopes that it would be safe, with the kitchen, and close to a subway station that goes to Rockefeller Center. Upon booking, I asked Ricardo if there was free parking outside of the apartment. He said yes and so I believed him. After driving around for 30 in the neighborhood, realized that parking was a lost cause. I parked in a paid parking garage for $50 tonight. It was my only choice. While walking the 3 minutes to the apartment, I was approached by one homeless man and two children asking for money. While walking into the apartment building, I smelled an overpowering scent of weed but I brushed it off in hopes that the apartment would exceed expectations.   Once I got into the apartment, we noticed that the kitchen is in the middle of his Photography Studio. For anybody trying to cook during the day, this very difficult as Ricardo works out of his Studio during that time.   If you're looking for a place to feel like home. This is not it. With a constant amount of different people coming in and out of the apartment, you never really know who's going to be in your home at what time.   I tried to settle in at night and it was near impossible because his young child was screaming outside my door from 9 p.m. to 12 a.m. Which I have audio and video recording of.   Ricardo is a photographer. And that is obvious because in his photos studio lighting is used. There is one light in the room on the ceiling. The way that Ricardo saturated and overexposed the photos of the room makes it look as though there's more light than there really is. In reality, the room is more of a tan tone with no full white walls.   I paid $1450 for an entire month. After staying one night and feeling unsafe, I left the apartment with all my things and let Ricardo know that I have changed my mind. Ricardo was very nice, but offer any kind of refund. Meaning, that I had paid $1450 for one night at the Harlem apartment. After days of going back and forth with Airbnb support, Ricardo offered a $300 refund. So now I only paid $1150 for one night. The Airbnb support people said that Ricardo explained that that's all he had, meaning that spent the other $1150.   I'm extremely disappointed with my stay. I'm out $1,150 and I only stayed one night. Ricardo was great in person, just was hoping for more from him.

We had the best stay at Nick & Margo’s apartment! On arrival we were met by Margo who was lovely and went through everything we needed to know, and made it very clear that they are always around to help in any way possible!! The apartment was super clean, spotless when we arrived, fresh linen and towels with plenty of spares in the wardrobe. The neighbourhood was really nice too, as a young couple we never felt unsafe walking in the day or the night, and there were subway stations only a 5-10 minute walk in both directions with about a 40 minute journey into manhattan.   As stated in the description of the apartment, there is a slight noise in the mornings and the evenings with the family living above, but this was never a problem for us and we barely even noticed it most of the time! If we were ever staying in New York again we would definitely stay here again without a doubt.

A terrific place and wonderful spot for bunking, gathering with family in the city or anything. The neighborhood is on the rise so amenities aren’t necessarily at arm’s length but food and coffee and breakfast not far at all. And Prospect Park is only blocks away which is spectacular. A stress free visit for my father visiting. Thanks so much all.
Don’t be afraid of Harlem... this a fantastic gateway to the city! Good value for money

Some of these reviews make me suspect guests did not realize a few fundamental truths about staying in Harlem.  Harlem is always: Noisy. Exciting.  Harlem is often: Dangerous. Unrelenting.  This apartment is located in a building that offers a reasonable person a perfectly manageable sense of safety and security.  The hosts are very responsive, and the check-in process was clear.  While the host has some things to iron out regarding basic amenities, staying here is still much more convenient and less expensive than a hotel. The grocery store and a few corner markets are within easy walking distance.   There are more than a few upscale eateries and coffee-shops in the neighborhood, or in adjacent neighborhoods.  Expect Harlem to be Harlem, and you won't be disappointed.  Important: The closest bagel spot is CLOSED on Sundays. (You have been warned; plan accordingly.)
Very comfortable apartment. The only bad thing is the neighborhood. Very noisy outside and dangerous

Vie was very responsive and paid attention to the small details, making our stay in town stress-free and enjoyable.  Also, the place was comfortable for our whole family and access to public transportation was very convenient.

Our stay with Karen and Brendan was fantastic! We stayed in their studio as our first location after moving to New York. This was an incredibly busy (and stressful!) time for us, but Karen and Brendan made sure our temporary housing wasn’t one of our stressors.  The studio is extremely clean and just as pictured. We stayed in the studio for a month and Karen even made sure to have our place cleaned twice during our stay (and even offered more if we needed it!). Karen and Brendan are very attentive and sincerely want to be sure that you’re stay is fantastic - and they succeed.   I would recommend their place for anyone , and we will certainly be recommending it to our friends and family.

This was overall a fantastic experience. The accommodation is better than I expected - the area is very safe, it's Park Slope, a residential area in Brooklyn; the hosts have been living  for 20 years and are well-stocked. I also loved their pets! Ethel the cat is very friendly - she kneaded on me, purred, and nested in the pillow. Maybe she was hoping I would feed her? The dog (forgot the name, sorry) does bark, so if you're afraid of barking dogs then be careful, but she's friendly as can be and begs for food in the cutest way ever.  The only thing you should take notice is that public transportation to Williamsburg / Bushwick / JFK is not the best. It's easy to get to lower Manhattan though. I highly recommend going to Prospect Park if you end up staying here, it's a normal park with people jogging and having BBQ - big contrast to the touristy Manhattan.  Overall I really enjoyed the stay. It made me feel human again after mingling with fancy superhuman-looking shoppers in SoHo for a whole day.

I greatly enjoyed my stay. Kathleen has been very kind and welcoming in all respects. Her place is exactly as described. The room is large and offers much storage space. The room is oriented south (distant from the other rooms), close to the second entry door of the apartment, hence offers good privacy. The apartment is well equipped, to make the stay easy going. Notice, however - but this has nothing to do with the apartment/room itself ! - that the area outside is lively. There is a fire-station further down the road, a hospital and police nearby, so sirens can go off any time. 14th Street is lively in general, but the advantage is that you find everything down the street (foot, haircut, bars, etc.). 14th Street in front of the house is particularly nice because it has many trees along the road, which makes it a nice neighbourhood. Also, the location is great to explore the nearby East Village area, or running down east river if you are interested in sports. Note also that the building is a traditional NY townhouse, with much of it in its original style. So, for example, don't be afraid of steep stairs and a bit of a rough-going stairwell. But again, this has nothing to do with the apartment itself; it is about authentic NY environment. Kathleen's apartment is truly authentic too, artist-style with many photographs, books and music instruments. Finally, her cat Bella is very charming, too. If you are looking for a true NY authentic experience, ready to never resting life in 14th Street, Kathleen's place will be a good choice for you. Also, 14th Street is a good starting point to explore any area in Manhattan (Union Square, Greenwich, etc.).
Anna was a great host that goes that extra mile to make sure your stay is stress free. We will be back to stay here again the next time we are in NYC.

Everything fits the description of the photos. Very clean. Plenty of amenities in the kitchen and linens in the closet. The balcony was a nice feature, we spent plenty of time out there people watching. The corner and side street are very active ones. I don't recommend it for someone who wants a quiet night. Fireworks, loud music, traffic noise. The neighborhood is slightly sketchy at night. But people seemed to mind their own business. Other then that the apartment was wonderful! We enjoyed the bottle of wine ! Also the check in process was very quick and convenient. Host response time very quick and helpful.

The apartment is great, clean and well decorated. The owner of the house Mario is a charming guy, when it came to communicating with him it was very easy since he knows how to speak a few languages ​​other than English, we were Spanish and we were able to communicate with him in Spanish without any problem.  The apartment is located just 5 minutes walk from the metro, in an area that, although at first it may seem somewhat ''dangerous'', we do not encounter any type of danger. By subway to Times Square it takes about 20 minutes and that in a city like New York is nothing. I would repeat, I have been very good.

When I arrived at Mario's place, I was welcomed with an italian pasta from a very kind friend of his. He showed me my room, the bathroom and gave me the keys. The apartment is clean, not to big, and simple. So this was perfect for me. I was afraid there would not be AC, but I was mistaken. Both the living room and bedroom have AC.  The location is close to the center with the subway, so this is a big plus. It is in a residential area with loads of apartments and everything looks quite the same, so I won't be making romantic walks outside there, but that was not a problem at all for me. In 20 to 25 minutes, you arrive in midtown Manhatten. I would even say that I was impressed to see how people live just next to the city.  I could always contact him via mail, but more often than not he was around and I could just talk to him in person. He answers very fast and always tries to help.  Although this is my first Airbnb experience, I dare to say that you won't find such a hospitality and kindness very often.  And even if all of the above would not have been the case, the eyes of his lovely dog would have made me leave with a positive feeling anyway. Man, I miss that cute creature already!

It is a great place. Mario is a great host and he has a very friendly and warm dog. We didn't talk much because I spent my days downtown but whenever needed Mario was prompt to help. The apartment is very organized and the common areas were all very clean as well as the room. It is super easy to get Midtown/Downtown with the subway station just a few blocks away and even though the neighborhood might seem a little sketchy I didn't have any problem walking there even late at night. Overall it is a great place for a good price in the city.

Mario is very friendly and the Department was always impeccable, and the attention he gives you is very good. The neighborhood seems to be a little unsafe, but I never had any problems when it came to going out.

Very good ! Just as the ad describes, Mario is very friendly and helps a lot with everything! Completely reliable!  The neighborhood seems dangerous but nothing happens. We came back very late sometimes.

We enjoyed our stay! The apartment is clean and comfortable. It is definitely in Harlem and can feel a little sketchy at night however, we never had any problems and the apartment building is super quiet. It was nice to have the subways close by and taxis and Ubers were always available. The apartment did get a little stuffy and hot at night (we were there during a hot spell).  All-in-all we enjoyed our stay. Thank you!

Amazing room and fantastic hospitality! Spike and Jaye were wonderful hosts and helped me out a lot as I was trying to find my feet in NY. Breakfast was great and their house is really spacious and warm. The room itself is great! The window looks onto the backyard and it's sunny and warm in winter. It's about 2 and a half blocks from the F/G line and the same for the R line so it's super convenient to get to Manhattan or anywhere else in Brooklyn, plus it's a super safe area! I often came back late and never felt unsafe walking from the subway. Can't recommend this place enough! Thanks for having me! :)

Pros:  Location- amazing, right next to union square, accessible to multiple subway lines, safe, lots of bars/restaurants nearby  Price Privacy: whole space with private bathroom Check in/out: contact free, very convenient   Cons: Bed! Most uncomfortable I’ve ever had. It’s actually criminal. Noise-above bar but I’m a deep sleeper so didn’t bother me at all
Tamicka was a great host, very helpful and friendly. Other rooms are on rent in this house, don't be scared by other guests. Aware of some traffic to bathroom in rush hours. Good wifi.

Martin's place was quite ideal for our purposes, as my son and I were sightseeing in NYC for a couple of days.  We got there late in the evening and had no issues with our self check-in.  If you are not used to urban settings, Bushwick may at first seem edgy, but we had no issues and never felt unsafe, day or night.  We enjoyed the restaurants and other businesses in the area, and the M line was only a couple of blocks away. Martin was a very approachable, helpful host.  This is a roomy (except for the bathroom), if humble basement apartment, and suited our needs at a great price in a city where lodging can be very expensive.
Would definitely use again. Very easy to get to and from JFK. Host was helpful and made the stay very easy and stress free. Also 3 blocks from the A train and a 40 minute train to Times Square.

Lovely room, very comfortable, easy access to public trans and local shops (coffee, beer, food)  Hosts were very pleasant, helpful, and nice to chat with.  Parking ANYWHERE in Brooklyn, not just here.. well.. save yourself some stress and find a spot and/or pay to park, and then use public trans.

Location, location, location! The apartment is situated perfectly for Lincoln Center, AMNH, Central Park, Riverside Park, MoMA, City Center, Carnegie Hall, and myriad eateries and shops. The apartment is homey and very much lived in, the polar opposite of a bland, empty hotel room. Lei is a superhost, responsive and accommodating.  The listing description is accurate, with the omission that the apartment lacks a microwave. Although isolated from street noise, the courtyard between the buildings on 75th and 76th street, which the apartment's outdoor terrace overlooks, can be noisy with children in the afternoon and social functions in the evening (but not after 9 pm during my 10-day stay). Sound is readily transmitted through the apartment's windows and walls. Someone in the building did morning (loudly creaking) stair exercises for 30 minutes between the 3rd and 4th floors that reverberated through the apartment. However, I found all such noise far less disruptive that sirens and traffic noise in accommodation facing a busy street.   The neighborhood and apartment were safe during my stay. However, both the outer and inner doors into the building were unlocked 24/7, which meant that anyone could walk into the building and confront the (non-security) door of the apartment. Having lived on the UWS for six years and had my apartment's security door breached by thieves while I was out-of-town, perhaps I have acute security awareness.   All in all, a wonderful NYC visit!

The apartment is quite well located for visiting New York, allow around ten minutes to reach the metro. There are many places nearby to eat or have a drink. The accommodation is quiet and very clean, located in the basement but still with a window and a mini terrace. We came at the beginning of September, it was still very hot (around 35°) but the apartment has air conditioning which is quite pleasant.  Leo was kind enough to welcome us at 2 a.m. (our flight was 2.5 hours late) and let us enjoy the accommodation until late afternoon on the last day because our plane was leaving in the evening. Great experience

There are really not enough stars in the AirBNB system to rate our stay in Aracelis' home. Here are the corrected rates: Cleanliness: 10 Accuracy: 10 Check-in: 10 Communication: 10 Location: 10 Value: 10 We do not make these corrections lightly. In fact, Aracelis' place is so clean we want to steal away her cleaner, if not Aracelis herself;  In fact, the accuracy of her listing can't match the height of the ceilings and the comfortable feel and functionality of the place; Communication before, during and after would shame Zoom; The location is but a few minutes away from the subway to say nothing of nearby stores for groceries; and finally, we were, and are, astounded at the value.  Thank you, Aracelis and we look forward to your visit!

Coming from Idaho, we thought we'd have a week without sleep, but Leo's place is surprisingly quiet. We'd come back exhausted from our New York adventures and heard nothing. Great sleep. Super comfortable bed. We loved our stay.   Leo greeted us on our arrival and referred us to a number of great delis and bars. Our favorite was Sunny and Anni's on Avenue B. We also discovered that his place is near Vazac's Horseshoe Bar (108 Avenue B), where they filmed the first Crocodile Dundee.   We were there a week and never felt unsafe. For transportation, it's near the "L" subway and the Stuytown ferry to either mid-Manhattan or Wall Street.   Overall, highly recommended, especially for country bumpkins like ourselves. We'll be back.

Andrew and Adriana were dream hosts, and their apartment was a dream stay! I only met them during my check-in and didn't see them after but that was because I spent the entire day exploring and out of the house. On arrival, they greeted me personally at the door, introduced themselves, and gave me a tour of the apartment and my room. Everything was very well-organized and nothing was left unclear or up in the air. I also appreciated how insistent they were on cleanliness, especially since it's a shared bathroom.   Adriana is a graphic designer and has deigned a cute little guide to NYC, including a section on the couple's favorite local restaurants that I used (and enjoyed) multiple times. That felt like they were going above and beyond to me. They also have various cool NYC-themed coffee table books in the room for you to browse if you wish.  I can''t emphasize how important it is that where you stay is near a subway stop, and this apartment is as close as you can get. Walk out the front door and turn the corner and you are there. Even better, the subway stop they are near (4 Av/9 St) serves 3 major lines - the F, G, and R, all of which will take you into Manhattan and to all of the major NYC sights as far as Central Park within 35 minutes. The trains also have decent connections to other areas of Brooklyn, allowing you to explore areas of the borough you wouldn't otherwise normally. Carry a backpack and a book and the time will fly by. It is such a steal being so close to the train, in such a desirable part of Brooklyn. Within 10 minutes walk are several delicious restaurants, bagel shops, and the gorgeous Prospect Park. Wonderful stay altogether, and if I am back in NYC in the future and this room is available, I will be booking again!

This is a very nice apartment in an ‘interesting’ neighborhood.  The apartment is large and clean.  The neighborhood is a bit tougher and with less developed amenities than you might expect given the geography.  The neighborhood is the trade off for the size and price.  I did not feel unsafe but close by grocery, restaurant and shopping options are limited.  Subway service is excellent and it is a three block walk to Central Park.  Innis provided excellent service and super fast responses.  If you want more space and better value and don’t mind a slightly more difficult neighborhood this apt is for you.  I enjoyed my lengthy stay and had great service
The place was exactly like the pictures. Our arriving flight got cancelled and we couldn't get in until the following day. Vincent was very accommodating and worked with us to ease the stress.

This was my first time using Airbnb. We enjoyed staying at Vincent's place. He was very nice. He left us some soda & water in the fridge which was nice of him. The location was good, I wasn't afraid to go outside and take my dog out. Also, it was super close to food and stores. The most important thing for me when I stay anywhere is the cleanliness & it was super clean at Vincent's place. Like seriously, even in the small corners of the bathroom floor were clean! You can tell that Vincent takes care of his apartment. Free wifi was a definite plus. The only issue I had was the comfort of the bed. It wasn't the worst bed Ive slept in but certainly not the best. However, I have a very back back so that could have contributed to the comfort issue. Anyway, I would definitely recommend staying here and I would stay again. I had a great experience.

Vincent’s home is exactly as described, and then some.  He left towels, water, and treats.  Even a cute dog bed for my pup.  You can tell he takes great care in getting ready for his guests.  I felt safe, clean, and happy.  If you are looking for a home away from home, or something comfortable and easy, this place is a great choice! His home is near the F express train at 74th st.  It took me 20 minutes to get to the city, and 10 minutes after that to get to work. I was in transition waiting to sign a lease, and this place was exactly what I needed during that high stress time.  I highly recommend this Home!!!

It is clear why Vincent earned his Super Host badge - He is AWESOME! Very responsive and checks in on you to ensure you are having a good stay. Everything was easy - from check in to check out. Our flight wS delayed 2 hours but Vincent made sure we didn’t stress about checking in. His description was spot on (no surprises) and he provides many thoughtful touches like water, soda, coffee, tea, plenty of towels, etc.  Vincent provided great tips and local information - couldn’t have asked for a nicer host!   While the space is small, it fit 2 people comfortably. Very clean and the best part is the location. Accessible via the E (74th St station) or the 7 (82nd & Roosevelt). If you prefer car, Lyft or Uber is available as well. TONS of restaurants on 37th as well as pharmacies and grocery stores. Highly recommend if you are visiting NYC.

I couldn't thank Vincent (host) enough for his hospitality. He was present to check me in and on time. His place was very clean and he left us everything we needed to enjoy our time away such as much needed coffee, snacks, and especially water! I couldn't have had a better time during my stay in Queens NYC. This place has everything you need to visit Queens and NYC including soap and shampoo! Wow! Its better than a hotel. I cant wait to go back and stay at his place again. I was very careful choosing this place as I was new to the area but, it was the ideal location to experience Latin -American cuisine and relax in a safe place. THANK YOU VERY VINCENT for making my stay hassle and stress free!

Miss Dy her family are absolutely fantastic! They were so welcoming and even moved the car up in the driveway so we could park our car safely. Since there isn't quite a formal kitchen area yet, Miss Dy brought down breakfast both mornings of our stay and it was delicious! Highly recommend this place for a weekend away. If you want rob get into the gen city the bus and subway systems are very close to the house - which was another bonus for us foreign visitors!

Miss Dy's place is warm and cozy! It offers complete privacy, yet her friendliness creates such a comfortable and open environment. If I needed anything, I was not afraid to ask. She accommodated us coming in at 11pm and leaving at 5am the next morning. Her place is stocked with fresh towels, tooth brushes, toiletries, breakfast, and beverages! I couldn't have asked for a homier and better accommodation ! It was wonderful and I would definitely stay again. We were a quick 5 minute ride from the JFK airport and everything was super easy and stress free !

This is a great value option for staying in New York. The apartment is big and clean. The only thing with the place is the location. It scares you a little bit, specially the walk from the train at night,  but if you are alert and travel in a group you are fine, we were fine. Vic was very attentive and responded right away when we contacted him. We stayed 4 nights, this was a great deal.

Kelly's place was fantastic! Great location and lots of space, one of the big beds is in the open space so please take note if that's an issue for you.   I would definitely recommend ear plugs if you're a light sleeper, the radiators make noise but they are my preferred type of heating. The city is also loud, however Kelly's place is relatively quiet, especially for NYC.   Kelly is also a fantastic host, she was helpful and accommodating the entire time. We had such a jam packed trip, and without this relaxing and reliable place it would have been so incredibly stressful.   I would definitely stay here again, my friend and I loved it. Kelly also has great and interesting taste, so it felt like such a home as opposed to some other places that feel so staged and stiff.

Well I loved the house and the room it felt cosy, the house is near several subway stations the ABCD metro and 123, I never felt unsafe in the neighbourhood… pablo always helped me and told me best routes and helped me with planning my days in Newyork… I highly recommend this house and whenever I come back fi Newyork I will always try to book this Airbnb

First off, Raymond (the owner of the AirBNB) was very communicative and helpful throughout the whole process. NYC is so busy and so expensive, so we looked into Brooklyn for our family of 5 to stay. This place turned out to be perfect on so many levels. Being from Texas, we had heard war stories about how unsafe Brooklyn was. Never for a moment did we feel unsafe in this neighborhood.  It was a short walk to the subway station, and very easy to get around. We got to know the subway very well and never did we have any issues walking to or from the AirBNB. The place was comfortable and quiet (except for the obvious street noise which you could expect anywhere in NYC).  Right around the corner is a little deli name "Kats" with a super friendly employee named Brian. My three boys loved him b/c he was always greeting them with questions about what we did and recommendations on places to go. The deli had all the little knick-knacks you might have forgotten at home, plus great food. In the AirBNB, there were plenty of towels and other amenities. The washer/dryer came in handy, too. We would definitely stay there again!!

Risha’s place is unique and has a wonderful rustic feel - Red Hook is amazing and a great place to be when you want to be in New York but also feel part of a unique waterside community. I didn’t want to leave!  It’s so easy to get to the city via ferry which is a few minutes walk from the house, or there is a subway (G) . Also frequent bus service up to central Brooklyn and Prospect Park.  The kitchen space inside is spacious for sitting - it’s quite shady and is very relaxing and great for a quiet stay. Bath is special! Bed is firm and comfy! Air con works well to cool down the bedroom area.  Risha is so helpful - anything you need, any problems, she’s right on it.  Recommended!!
Kartika was very helpful and accommodating to our needs on the trip.  The neighborhood felt a little sketchy when we got back to the room, but it was a quick walk from the subway as advertised.

This was a great place to stay! Kartika was very flexible with check-in, staying up late to allow me access to her apartment even though my flight was arriving just before midnight.  The apartment is very close to several subway stations, including an E train express station which will take you to Manhattan in a flash. The immediate area is very lively during the daytime, with a large number of Asian and Latino stores and restaurants - it really showed me a new side of New York! The area is quieter at night, but not in a way that ever felt unsafe.  The room itself was of a great size, clean, and with a very comfortable bed and good wifi. I'd stay again!!

Reasonably priced great communication but quite an inadequate space. Miss Dy was great with communicating when I initially got there. Unfortunately we were not satisfied with the space as it had a very unpleasant odor and was quite creepy. A car parked in the driveway made it a little difficult to get to the back of the house with our luggage. While the pictures in the description were accurate to a point there were areas of the space that were left out and pics of those areas would definitely have been a deal breaker for us. We quickly left within hours. We made an attempt to tough it out as we were booked for 5 days.  I sent Miss Dy a message thanking her for her hospitality and letting her know we were uncomfortable and would be leaving. She never reached out to find out what the problem was. Which led me to believe customer satisfaction wasn’t a top priority.

Both Ian and Aisa were very friendly and helpful when needed. We didn't have much contact because we were always out in NYC but they were always there when we needed them. The room is exactly as the listing and the photos say. We felt welcome in it and Ian has one of the most awesome book shelves I've seen.   As far as the neighborhood is concerned, it might not feel that safe at times, especially at night (some suspicious people and pretty much always, weed smell). We didn't have any problems whatsoever in the end but it just didn't feel like the most safe place we've been.  The subway is relatively close (12 min or so) and from there it's a 15 min ride to manhattan.  Price wise, hardly any place can top Ian's. We would definitely stay there if we would visit NYC again.

My stay at the privacy den was pleasant up until i lit an incent to take out the smell of the fish i was eating in the apartment. The host accused me of smoking when im not even a smoker ! Not to mention i was afraid when my husband left me alone because i started hearing a door open like someone upstairs wanted to come down so i do not feel like the privacy den is so private

Kartika, is very welcoming and accommodating. She was very helpful during check-in and check-out. Her kindness just shines through.  The room itself was very cozy and well decorated. There was even a closet with hangers! If you open the curtain there is a lot of natural sunlight. There are a couple of  tables. I had a place to place for my laptop. I was able to connect to zoom meetings and do other work stuff.  Bottom-line is, you have everything you need whether you are just traveling or to NYC for work.  The building was also great because there are doormen, a laundry room and an elevator!   Lastly, the location felt safe and convenient. You can take advantage of deals at local supermarkets or try out the local cuisines! Everything is around the corner from the apartment! Laundromats, drug stores, supermarkets, hair salons ( I got a cheap haircut), bakeries, restaurants, the subway (M, R). The 7 train is up to 10 min away. Each is 30-40 min from Manhattan and some parts of Brooklyn.

The value is correct for the place. It is very simple but super clean and rather quiet. Michael is super responsive and helpful. The location might seem shady at night but we felt comfortable and safe going back home even late at night. A couple of nice cafes around for breakfast. The heater might be loud at night and the sound insulation is not amazing, so I do recommend earplugs for visitors who are very sensitive to noise when sleeping. I would highly recommend this place.

Its quite far from the subway station and I feel a bit scared when I go back to the place during evening. Also I was disappointed by the cleanliness. The floor of the bedroom wasn’t cleaned at all. Nevertheless, its still a good deal with this price.

Impeccable, spacious apartment, perfect for families and very close to the metro. The night atmosphere may not be the best but in no case, I repeat in no case, dangerous. Perfect, and friendly hostess.

Pascal is a great host, very polite, helpful and responsive. The apartment was exactly as described, clean and comfortable.There were 5 of us and the apartment was big enough for all of us to share and sleep in. There was central air heating in the apartment which was very convenient during the cold days. the shower works great and the apartment also has a washing machine. The check in and check out process could not have been any easier. Pascal gave us clear and simple instructions to gain access to the apartment and  kindly messaged us to forewarn us about the winter storm. The location itself is good and peaceful. We had absolutely no problems and weren't bothered by anybody. the apartment is situated only a few stops away from Times Square on the express line and the apartment is close to 2 subways, although I'd recommend using the 2 and 3 subway in the evenings as 4, 5 and 6 subway is a bit sketchy at night. All in all it was a great vacation and we'd definitely stay here again!

We were so glad to have been able to stay here! It was great to have such a lovely space to come home to every night, and to be able to prepare food when we needed to. The apartment is bright and spacious enough, with basic kitchen supplies and a gas stove. It could have used a few more kitchen cloths and a recycling bin. The queen bed is nice and high, and our 8 year old daughter really enjoyed sleeping on the futon. The cot didn't really hold up for our 12 year old son, so hopefully that issue gets resolved. The apartment is located just a few blocks from the subway, with plenty of shops nearby (grocery, pharmacy, deli, pizza, coffee, etc), and a late-night Mexican food truck right by the subway station. The neighbourhood is really interesting; it doesn't feel sketchy, and everyone we encountered while walking to and fro was friendly. There is an astonishing number of churches in the area. We didn't actually spend much time there. Most of the 8 days we stayed, we were gone by 9am and home between 9pm and 1:30am. Everything was pretty quiet at night, but on the weekends, ear plugs may be a good idea.

Super clean with gleaming hardwood floors and high ceilings. Located in a section of Brooklyn which may at first glance seem sketchy but the area is actually very friendly and culture rich. We loved getting up each morning and walking to a different coffee shop each day; there are several in less than a mile. Coming back to the brownstone each day made us feel like we were in the movies. It took less than 3 minutes to walk to the train station and in 15 minutes we were in Manhattan. Michelle was very responsive and accommodating to us. We very much enjoyed our stay.

Apartment is exactly as described - It is close to many restaurants and is a mere 7 mins walk to subways. Neighbourhood was lively in the day but quiet at night so that we can all have a good night's rest. Only downside was that the heating pipes used for warming up the apartment are exposed and might be dangerous for families with young children. Otherwise, would highly recommend this place!

We stayed at Marc's apartment for 14 days/nights and it was generally a good experience. We didn't get to meet Marc as he was away on a work trip but he did get a friend to come help us with check in and provide info on the neighbourhood, so that's very helpful. Marc was also quick to respond whenever we have any questions and very flexible in agreeing to our requests for early and late check in due to our flight timings. We truly appreciate his graciousness. Apartment and amenities- the apartment is big, 2 good sized bedrooms, 1 bathroom with a tub, a living room and a kitchen. The amenities and photos listed by Marc were true to descriptions. We enjoyed the entertainment system at home, often binge watching TV series while we get ready/wind down in the day. The washer and dryer was also very handy as we stayed for 2 weeks and needed to do laundry. The apartment is somewhat dark with little sunlight, but that could be due to the dreary weather we were experiencing during our stay. We cooked a fair bit, Marc's kitchen is fully stocked with the cooking utensils we needed so it's good. The corridor/hallway leading to the apartment is oftentimes drowned in a very weird/unpleasant scent- this is of course no fault of Marc's, but we were often baffled by the smell as we can't identify the source. As I read through previous reviews, I saw someone mentioning that it's cat's scent, not sure if it really is, but if cat's scent bothers you then take note. Location- the apartment is in Brooklyn and is close to 2 subway stations- Parkside Avenue with the Q line (about 2-3 mins walk) and Prospect Park Avenue with the Q and B line (about 5 mins walk). Both Q and B will bring you to different parts of Manhattan in approximately 20-30 mins or so. Q line has scheduled interrupted services every weds onwards with no train to Manhattan at specific timing- be sure to check the info before heading out (I can't remember the exact timing/dates) Having said that, it is important to note that you can hear the train some what loudly in Marc's apartment. It didn't bother us, but if you are a light sleeper, it might bother you. But this could be fixed with a pair of earplugs I think. The entrance of the building faces one of the entrances of Prospect Park, which we appreciated as we love to talk walks in the park. There are a few supermarkets/grocery stores (one of which is a slightly specialised store selling organic products- which is right next to the Prospect Park station) within 5-10 mins walking distance from the apartment which is super convenient as we did cook during our stay. The neighbourhood is very functional with many services available but not necessarily one you'd like to hang out in. As 2 women travelling, we felt generally safe walking home from...

There must be a few qualifiers to this review. My four-star rating has nothing to do with any negative experience I had with Marc personally. To the contrary, he was always quick to respond and pleasant to deal with. The star I removed was for the apartment itself and the location. Let me explain. First of all, the pros: - The kitchen is and the bathroom was much bigger and better than I expected. Even looking at the photos I didn’t get the true sense of them. For a New York apartment, they are excellent. - The décor of the home is fantastic too. There is a great eclectic flavor to the place. Marc has done a great job decorating his home and his pride in the place is clear every direction you look. - The kitchen and bathroom were very well cleaned when we arrived. - The washer/dryer combo in the kitchen is a new model. It’s easy to use and works well. Now the cons: - The place is really pretty dirty. I know that we weren’t staying in a hotel and I didn’t expect hotel levels of cleanliness. That being said, the large build-ups of dust around furniture and on most of the surfaces was pretty bad. - The area is pretty sketchy. I know that this is a subjective judgement and we didn’t get hassled or mugged or anything like that. So apart from my feelings, I’ve included some objective points of what I mean (would be great if you could include photos too). The entrance to the park directly across from the building had a homeless man under a big pile of stuff permanently camped out on one of the benches right near it for the entire 3 weeks of our stay. Expect to see lots of people going through the trash looking for bottles all up and down the street the building is on. The nearest subway (Prospect Ave) is littered with trash and graffiti. The main street just around the corner isn’t somewhere you’d really like to spend a lot time either. Fortunately, Park Slope is only just across the park or a short subway ride away. - The photos are a little misleading and so is the description. The furniture in the apartment has been changed since the photos have been taken. This isn’t a super big deal but it’s worth noting. Also, the listing describes a TV that wasn’t there and “Access includes a large bedroom with walk-in closet for guest's convenience.” The closet was completely full of Marc’s things when we were there, only one drawer was made available for us to use in the nightstand. I asked Marc about the TV and he said it ‘fell off the wall’ just before we got there. Any future guests might want to enquire if the TV has been replaced before you stay. - The building itself is a little sketchy too. Just kind of an old dirty apartment building. There was...

We really enjoyed our stay in New York and Marc's apartment contributed greatly to that. At first we were a little afraid of being far from the center of Manhattan but that's not really the case. The apartment is located 5 minutes from Prospect Park station, well served by the Q and B lines in particular and it takes around 20/25 minutes to come from the heart of Manhattan, nothing insurmountable especially for people used to public transport in Paris. Moreover, the New York metros are more similar to the RER than the Paris metro in terms of their size, frequency or location, but even in peak periods and with suitcases, you are more comfortable there than in the Paris metro... The apartment is very pleasant and decorated in a modern way. As this is an apartment where one person usually lives, you should not be surprised or offended by the presence of some personal belongings (clothes hidden behind a screen, for example). It is also pleasant to arrive in a particularly clean apartment, at least as clean as the one in which we usually live. The wifi is very convenient and works perfectly. Essential for checking the weather, planning your visits or managing your return flight! Television disconcerted us a little at first but that’s just because it’s not quite like in France. In the end, we managed to watch a few movies on HBO. There are, however, a few things to note about this apartment. First of all, it's not very bright. We left in the morning and didn't return until late afternoon, so it wasn't very disruptive. Only on the last day when it rained, we stayed in the apartment for the afternoon and we found it really very dark. The second point to note is the passage of the train. In fact, the line passes (as the crow flies) quite close to the building which is poorly insulated. As we were tired from our daily visits, in the evening we didn't pay attention to it but for people who are light sleepers, it can be disturbing. However, despite this insulation problem, the building is particularly and surprisingly quiet! No loud music, no noise, no commotion, it’s really very relaxing! We also hope that we were not noisier than the residents of the building. The neighborhood is quite pleasant. The entrance to the building is located on Ocean Avenue directly opposite a park entrance. As indicated, the metro station is a 5-minute walk away. It takes just a few minutes longer to get to the Brooklyn Botanic Garden and the Brooklyn Museum. It is possible to find supermarkets not far away and something to eat (either on Lincoln Av or Flatbush Av) not to mention Smorgasburg which is in Prospect Park on Sundays. We did not have the chance to meet Marc, however, we communicated by email and he was very considerate and his explanations were...

Marc's apartment is a fine option when staying in the Bklyn & NYC area. Its proximity to the park and the subway is ideal and the building itself is relatively quiet, safe, and clean. He has done a nice job decorating which offers a friendly and enjoyable aesthetic.  The kitchen is well stocked with cooking tools, and the bathroom is newer and was quite clean and pleasant.  Also, the entertainment center was a nice bonus on the rainy day we were visiting, providing streaming media on a big screen.  We did not have any communication with Marc beyond receiving impersonal and pre-formatted messages regarding check-in and check-out which were accurate and thorough.  However, there wasn't the promised 'How it Works' or 'House Guide' in the apt when we arrived so we were unsure of how to interact with the space.  This meant we were walking on eggshells a little bit: afraid of disturbing personal items and not knowing what we could use in the space.  FYI - the sound of the local subway line mentioned above is quite noticeable in the apt-even more so if the windows are open.  Its not overwhelming nor do the trains shake the building but its definitely a feature of environment. Even sleeping with earplugs, I could hear the trains most of the night. That said, I am a light sleeper.   So, if you are too, bring your earplugs.  Also, you will be required to do some light clean up (stripping bed, collecting towels, empty trash cans/recycling, dishes, etc) which isn't much to ask.  However, that isn't clear in the listing so this is a heads-up for those who would prefer to not have to do chores before checking out.  Generally speaking, its a fine place to rest one's head.

With all the great reviews, I was excited and hopeful about staying at Marc’s place for the summer. Unfortunately, I encountered many preventable, careless issues from day 1. First: when I arrived, the apartment was very dirty. Keep in mind we’re in a pandemic. Floors, rugs, counters, surfaces, bathroom had dirt, dust, dog hair, human hair, etc. I swept floors and cleaned the kitchen and bathroom on my first night. I let Marc know about the lack of cleanliness and asked to be reimbursed for 1-2 nights. He said no but agreed to send a cleaning lady the following week. She was not thorough, and on her way out she commented to me about how dirty the apartment was. A couple weeks later, Marc came to the apartment and cleaned while I was on a trip. I returned to a very clean place. He eventually took accountability for the place being dirty, but initially got defensive and offered excuses. [Also, when I had checked in Marc let me know that he left a bottle of prosecco as a gift for me in the fridge, which I didn’t get a chance to drink right away. When I finally went to drink it, it was gone - he must have taken it back when he returned to clean the apartment.] Second: There was a roach infestation. I was seeing on average 5 roaches a day. As a New Yorker I know how this goes, but a full extermination should have been done before I arrived since Marc was already well aware of the issue. He sent an exterminator and made sure to let me know exactly how much it was costing him. Third: for the first couple weeks of my stay, I was breaking out in full body hives. When I finally thought to check the bedroom AC filter, I found it covered in mold, dirt, and dust. It clearly hadn’t been replaced in a very long time. I threw the filter away and the hives eventually tapered off. I let Marc know and he said he would take care of getting a new filter. I slept in the summer humid heat with no AC as I waited for Marc to follow up about the filter. He didn’t. Ten days later I researched and ordered a new one myself and sent Marc the receipt. He reimbursed me but offered no apology or acknowledgment for dropping the ball. Fourth, Marc carelessly left a heavy marble tabletop leaning against a wall behind the door to the TV room, which fell over and cracked when I opened the door to the room. He was very apologetic, telling me not worry about it and repeatedly stating how relieved he was that I didn’t get hurt. Closer to check out, he let me know he was submitting a damaged property request for it. I sent photos of everything that went wrong to Air BNB support staff. They were appalled but weren’t of much help and told me to speak directly to the host about my issues. Meanwhile, the host told me Air BNB was supposed to be reaching out to me to resolve everything. I went back and forth for weeks with both Marc and Air BNB support about my desire to end my 2.5-month reservation early so I could find another place to stay. Marc offered to refund me for 50% of any cancelled nights, but I let him know that I would not be able to find another Air BNB in the middle of summer in NYC at that rate. After more back and forth, he agreed to fully refund me for any cancelled nights, so I was finally able to end my reservation a few weeks early. Marc made it a point to tell me that he didn’t profit from my reservation and that it put him “in the hole”. He also emphasized how many hours he spent on the phone with Air BNB about all issues I encountered in my stay (none of which were my fault, all of which could have been prevented with planning, thoughtfulness, and attention on this part before check-in). The reservation was very costly for me as well. I sunk thousands into an almost comically bad and stressful stay, which I had booked months in advance. I’m disappointed that I didn’t get a 5-star worthy experience like most other guests. It’s a great apartment and I wanted to be able to enjoy it in a relaxing, hassle-free way so I could focus on the reasons I was in NY to begin with. I hope my experience was unique and will be the last of its kind.

Hello my name is Jonathan and I want to tell you that pass two weeks pleasant and tranquility, harmony and great peace of all, I think it was the perfect place to stay in peace and quiet if you're looking to de-stress, this is the place , a quiet family home but where attention vine and is in charge of the Great Lord Lloyd, a great host, very good person, very humble and very concerned about serving you and lend you the attention you need, believe me, the truth that the pass super great and wonderful there, it was an experience I will never forget and never lose this communication I had with the host is and was very attentive to me, thanks Mr. Lloyd and that God will continue to bless and caring much, you appreciates and take you in my heart and will to a forthcoming.

Joris has been a terrific host!  He knows every little tips you can use on a trip, and isn't afraid to share.  The place is comfy, with all facilities and the neighborhood is pretty quiet, not far from the subway to Manhattan or JFK.  We were a family of four to go there and it was the perfect alternative to an expensive hotel in Manhattan.

Joris's apartment is wonderful!  Spacious, clean, close to all amenities, safe and private.  The apartment is perfect.  Shower pressure is great, location is fantastic with lots of great places to grab some food, groceries, drug store/pharmacies etc close by. Closest subway stop is Halsey Street, however I liked the extra walk and would join the L or M train at Myrtle and Wyckoff - it's a straight forward walk there and back, even in the early hours of morning, perfectly safe. If you stay here, you will not regret it for a minute - it's awesome!  Thanks Joris for an easy going transaction - see you next time.

If all hosts were like Joris, then there would probably be no more problems. The apartment was exactly as described, simply perfect. The neighborhood was great, we never felt unsafe. There really isn't much to say about Joris, other than that you absolutely have to get to know this man, and it's best to go and have a drink with him at "Zu Stammtisch". We have never met such a friendly and friendly host like Joris. He gave us lots of insider tips, which made the holiday even more enjoyable. He also offered to pick us up from the airport or drive us to the airport.  So in short: There is no better place to stay in NYC than at Joris. Hopefully we'll see each other again soon.

Our trip to NYC was unforgettable! Joris was more than a great host who even picked us up from the airport (thanks again!). The place was exactly as it is in the pictures, the bed is very comfortable, the next subway is around 8 min walk from the house and it has a very good connection, you are in 20 minutes in Manhattan. The area around the apartment is very active, with lot of shops and a couple of supermarkets around the corner. I really liked it, we didn't have any problem and we didn't feel unsafe at all. Excelent quality-price relation! We would like to come again!

Our stay in NY was excellent! As we were arriving early in the morning, I was afraid I wouldn't be able to get the key, but our host Joris left us very calm and at 3 am we arrived and got in without any problems. The apartment is exactly like the photos, the building inside is a little different from what we imagined, but nothing special. The neighborhood is a little further from Manhattan, but the value for money is great, we looked at places closer and the price was much higher, the subway is three blocks away, 20 minutes to the city and a maximum of 40 minutes to any place making a connection. We got back at 2 am by train, great! There's a great bar two blocks away! Supermarket, pharmacy, shops, everything very close by. We met Joris twice, he was very attentive and gave us valuable travel tips. We recommend the apartment!

Joris was a great host. Answered questions promptly. My husband and him became quick friends :) The subway is about a 10 minute walk. We never felt unsafe walking to or from. Traveled with our 14 and 17 year old son's. About 30 to Manhattan. The place was spotless and smelled clean upon entering. WiFi did not work well in the back bedroom, but was fine elsewhere. Make sure you lock the door when you are in the apartment. We did not once and a little girl came in while we were watching TV. Joris had complimentary shampoo and conditioner for us which was nice. Make sure you understand the street parking rules if you drove.

This Airbnb is great if you don't want to stay in Manhattan. You are a few blocks from the subway and the L Line gets you everywhere. I felt safe walking at night. There are grocery stores, local shopping and a drug if needed store. Made breakfast in the room every morning. Nice roomy place with your own bathroom.

This place was an amazing value! Joris was a great host and so helpful! He let us leave our luggage there since we got in earlier than check in which was wonderful! His instructions and directions were spot on! If you don't mind taking the subway into Manhattan this is a wonderful place to stay!
