We explored the neighborhood of Ridgewood the first night we were there and really enjoyed it as well! I never felt unsafe walking around at night. I will definitely be recommending this place to my friends who want to travel to NYC.

This was my first Airbnb experience and it was excellent. The place that Joris provides is located in a very nice neighborhood, with lots of nice shops, restaurants and markets/delis only steps away. The neighborhood is quiet and I never felt unsafe or uneasy no matter the time of day or night.  As detailed in the description and other comments, the subway is very close. I could walk to the M line in less than 10mins which takes you right into Times Square.  I have nothing negative to say at all. The apartment was clean, spacious, quiet, private, truly had anything I could need and check-in was incredibly easy. I have stayed many times in Manhattan and Queens for personal and business trips and no place has offered near the quality of place that Joris offers for anywhere even close to what he charges.  I want to thank Joris for providing an incredible space at an amazing price.  He is providing an amazing service by helping make a trip to NYC affordable. Saving on accommodations allows one to afford to take in the incredible sights, theatre and night life the city has to offer. I did not meet Joris or speak to him other than through a few brief messages as I had no issues or concerns during booking or my stay. However, when I did message him he always responding politely and in a timely manner.  I would definitely recommend Joris and his place to anyone thinking about a trip to NYC. Thank you again Joris for an incredible stay!

This is a very nice and spacious duplex apartment on a beautiful block.  There are many restaurants, cafés and shops nearby on Amsterdam, Broadway and Columbus and Central Park is just a few minutes walk. It was a relief to come back home to a cool and very quiet apartment after a few very hot NY summer days. The backyard is lovely, and drinking our morning coffee in the shade of the magnolia was a rare treat. While - as is the case in most NY brownstones- some of the plumbing is a bit old, and there does not seem to be much hot water for long showers, the apartment is very well equipped, and the hosts very responsive. We had a really nice time.   We would mostly recommend it for summer, as it may get a bit dark in winter.

We arrived around 11pm and due to there not being any address number on the apt we had a very difficult time finding which apt was the correct one. The directions stated there was lockbox with a key to the apt which we could not find. We called the owners who described the entrance and that the lockbox was on the Second entrance gate! Once we were inside we were opening up doors and windows as it was quite stuffy only to find on the 2nd floor a door/window without any screen or  warning that it opened to a 12 ft (one story) drop..no barrier!! So unsafe!! The photos don't accurately portray how the house looks. The furniture has spill stains, etc which is understandable with a small family but can be easily covered with slipcovers for guests.

I arrived much later than planned but Lloyd was so accommodating. This place is ideal if you’re looking for something simple before or after a flight. Only 10 minutes drive from JFK, (just beware of the taxi scams at the airport!) can’t recommend this place highly enough.

It was our first experience with AirBnb, and it was perfect!Linda was very nice to us,the room was clean with clean towels on the bed, classic music in the room and bathroom.the bathroom was really nice, with a japaneese design and all the toiletries you need.Linda was very funny, talkative and helped us with every question we had.she even had books and maps on NYC for in in the room to help us get along in the city.the neighbourhood is the chinatown of queens,it's not very loud or dangerous.the house is 10 walking minutes away from the subway station and 2 minutes from the bus station

The room we stayed is very closed to the street and it rained the first night, so it's pretty noisy. Plus, we found out the bed sheets and pillowcases were not washed and because we checked in late, so we couldn't get clean sheets and comforter to sleep with. We had a pretty awful first night. We mentioned that to Linda and she apologized and gave us some refund, and got us the clean sheets the second day. The second night was okay. Linda is a helpful and friendly hostess. The bathroom is clean and well decorated, but it's located on the second floor and our room is on the first floor, so it's not very convenient to us. Plus, we didn't know there are multiple rooms for renter/Airbnb-er. Sharing the bathroom with other people without a lock makes me feel unsafe.  Bedroom carpet floor seems to have a lot of dust. We dropped the towel and it picked up so much dust. The location is pretty good if you love to eat in Flushing. 16 mins walk to Flushing Main St Subway.

David’s place is lovely and exactly as advertised. A steal in the West Village, and a scenic walk in all directions. He had a nice personalized note for us regarding our travel logistics and made us feel right at home. Lots of nice touches in the place and incredibly quiet. It’s everything you need.
Great location -- and don't let the stairs scare you.  Charming apartment, super-clean.

Staying at Linda's was such a great experience and peace of mind for a somewhat stressful short trip. I am female and was worried about traveling alone, but felt very safe in the neighborhood, and right at home at Linda's. The description is 100% accurate. Great communication. Very cozy room makes you feel right at home with thoughtful added touches like a charging station. There are two cats and I am allergic, but the place was so clean that I really wasn't bothered at all. The blinds are thin and don't block all the light from the street, so bring a sleep mask if this bothers you. You will hear the occasional car go by, but it's not often, and it didn't bother me, even though I am a light sleeper. I also found the bed a little hard even with the foam topper, but that may be a personal preference as I like a very soft bed. I did sleep well. Overall, I really enjoyed this quaint little refuge. Linda is clearly committed to making your experience pleasant.

An amazing host such a nice lady Linda and her beautiful family and adorable cat, the house is so beautiful and scary, decorated top to bottom in and out full of spooky Skelton and spiders, I can't say enough how much we enjoyed our stay and felt so welcomed in her house
Linda was a very helpful, and accommodating host. She provided us with a extra heater because she was afraid it might get cold in the evening.
Amanda is a gracious hostess. The accomodations were pleasant and comfortable. There are some sketchy people in the neighborhood.

Amanda was very kind and welcoming. The neighbourhood is easy to get to on the 3 line or by car. The apartment is comfy and the bedroom comfortable. I like her dog too. But my kids were a little scared because he started off by barking at them. A cute little animal.   I guess there was a double booking by mistake. So Amanda wasn't there and I was with another couple guests in the other room. Thankfully they were very very nice people as well, but it could have been awkward. But it worked well.  Amanda was very very pleasant, and helpful introducing us to the neighbourhood as well. Even taught us some rules for cribbage.
This apartment is so comfortable - lovely, spacious, homeless, spotless. Great location and bed is very comfortable too!

I would like to start by saying, our stay in New York was amazing! I was there with my teenage son and daughter for a week and we truly had a wonderful time.   My first impression of Teresa's place was somewhat disappointing. It definitely does not live up to the pictures that are shown. No crisp white walls or cute decor to be found. The apartment is small and most areas are packed with the owners belongings. This leaves very little space for suitcases, especially if you have 3 or 4 people. The kitchen has no microwave or coffee maker and is minimally equipped for cooking. It has a three flight narrow stairwell that should be considered. The walk to the subway for us was 0.4 miles. Laundromat and food market close by.  All this being said, the neighborhood is very active and energetic. We never felt unsafe and there is an endless supply of restaurants and bars to visit. My son and daughter really felt like they were part of the New York life. All said and done, we had a great time.

Me and a group of female friends stayed here. We were initially worried about the location being college aged girls but it was completely safe and in a quiet neighborhood. None of us ever felt unsafe once. The subway is  right across the street. When we would come home late at night there was no one else around. Again, very safe. There are also three doors and three different locks to get inside. There are two flights of stairs to get to the apartment. It was very clean and as described in the description. Kakuna was very sweet and answered our messages quickly. She was very helpful. It takes about 30 minutes by subway to get anywhere in the city. I highly recommend staying here! We had a great time!

One of the best places I've stayed on this site!  Accurate description and helpful pictures.  The apartment was very clean and was stocked with just about anything you would need (e.g., coffee and filters, dishwasher and laundry detergent, shampoo/soap, tissues, etc.) .  Location was great and the apartment had plenty of room for the 5 of us.  The hosts were very communicative and helpful before and throughout our stay.  There was a minor issue with a broken lock to the apartment door, but with 2 entrance-way doors that locked, we never felt unsafe or hesitant to leave our belongings unsecured in the apartment.  Would definitely stay here again and would recommend without hesitation.

The room (and the whole apartment) matches the photos well, it is spacious, simply furnished with everything you need, a large closet with hangers and drawers to store your belongings. The bed is very soft and the heating works very well (but we recommend turning it off at night). At the moment the living room is no longer available and there is no table in the kitchen. The apartment loses its conviviality but find out this is a temporary situation.  A downside, the cleanliness is approximate, freaks refrain.  The apartment is well located, west of Harlem in a quiet, popular and safe neighborhood. Nearby, there are all the necessary shops (supermarket, Starbucks, Dunkin’Donuts, pharmacy, Jacob soul food cafeteria)  The express metro (A and D) is a few steps from the apartment, which is really nice, it takes 40 minutes to reach Manhattan South. The ideal is to take a 7-day unlimited metro card for $31. One subway stop away, there are some great restaurants (don't miss Red Rooster) and some great value stores on 125th Street.  The ultimate strong point is the kindness and availability of Agnès who will give you maximum information, good addresses and who will always ensure that you will not miss anything.

There was nightly yelling from upstairs that I could hear quite clearly. It would start around 4pm and sporadically continue until 10pm. I would then be woken up every morning at 6:30am to stomping feet right above the bed, more and more yelling. I'm very sensitive to such things and so this completely put me off. This might not bug people who yell at home or have kids.  I found it very stressful to overhear. Great birth control! 😂

Agnes' apartment was very well kept and extremely clean. I LOVE that she kept snacks and drinks in our room for us, was a nice touch! The location is in Harlem and walking the short distance from the apartment to the subway during the day was fine, but at night definitely scared me a bit. Agnes was very helpful! If it wasn't for location, I would stay here again forsure!

Agnes was just great! Even though our flight was delayed and we arrived in the middle of the night, Agnes waited for us and welcomed us. We hadn't missed anything for 9 days, breakfast and ingredients for sandwiches etc. were always available and she made sure we had a good diet (almond milk, organic fruit, 3 different types of bread, etc.), which was incredibly pleasing to us.  Small gestures that we absolutely didn't expect made the stay a wonderful first Airbnb experience! It is clean at Agnes's, it is cleaned regularly and the bed linen and towels are changed for longer stays. It should perhaps also be noted that Agnes was so incredibly helpful, no matter what! She always had good tips, an open ear and didn't hesitate to offer help with problems or requests. Her stories about New York and her work were just great and we loved talking to her and our other roommates (also from the USA). It is perhaps also important to note that the area was incredibly safe. As a woman, it was particularly important to me not to have to be afraid and you realize relatively quickly that horror fairy tales are exactly what they are: fairy tales. The two of us never felt endangered or harassed.  All in one: a wonderful stay and one thing is certain: we will spend our next stay in New York with Agnes again!   Agnes was just great! Although our flight was delayed and we arrived in the middle of the night, Agnes was waiting for us and welcomed us. We had 9 days missed nothing, breakfast and other ingredients for sandwiches etc. were always available and she paid attention to good nutrition (almond milk, organic fruit, 3 different types of bread). Small gestures that we had absolutely not expected, made the stay a wonderful first Airbnb experience. The apartment was very clean, it was cleaned regularly and the bedding and towels were changed at longer stay. Agnes was so incredibly helpful! She always had good advice, a listening ear and did not hesitate to offer their assistance with problems or wishes. Her stories about New York and her work were just great and we loved the conversations with her and the other roommates. It is also important to say that the area we stayed was incredibly safe. We felt for two never threatened or harassed.  It was wonderful! Our next stay in New York we will stay again at Agnes!   Thank you so much, Agnes!

Agnes was more than great starting from I booked the room weeks prior by proving great communication to the very end when we left our amazing trip in New York. Our flight came in around 6am and even though "full check-in" wasn't until later (other guests still occupied the place), Agnes let us drop off our bags, clean up and chat a little before we headed out to explore before our long day.   The apartment complex has old-school charm in a great way as well as the apartment itself. Everything was very clean and I noticed the bathroom was spotless every time I went in the next day. The room we had was excellent with plenty of space including a comfortable bed (I like firm), television and Agnes even provided an array of snacks, water, juices, coffee, soap, toothbrushes, etc in the room which was awesome. My friend and I felt extremely comfortable in the apartment and used the kitchen everyday for breakfast. We talked to Agnes when she was around and she is an awesome person to conversate with. Very calm, but passionate and well rounded in many areas so you can talk about almost anything. If you need any tips on places to eat or how to get around she will have them for you too. Very responsive via messages/text too, which I'm a big fan. The main bathroom (with shower/bath) is shared, but we never had an issue or wait when we were leaving for the day. It literally felt like a home away from home. I've used airbnb multiple times and this was my best experience using a shared space. I'm usually against it to be honest, but if all hosts are like Agnes and her place I'm open to it again :)  We loved the location as well....literally one block away from the Train/Subway station (both express and local) to get you anywhere you want to go. One train can take you to many of the tourist sites, Central Park etc and we found this to be great. The airport was a simple Express train away as well as the AirTrain (must take this in and out of the airport) which was very convenient as well to save on taxi. Plenty of places to eat around (late too), groceries, and we came in late at night and had no feeling of being unsafe whatsoever anytime. The building is also locked and secured and to note has both stairs and an old style elevator (smoother than expected as I fear elevators).  Overall, more than Excellent experience and my friend and I would recommend Agnes and her place in a heartbeat for a stay in New York. If I go back, I would hope to stay again.

This was my first time using airbn, I honestly was afraid of what to expect but everything was beyond any expectation. If you're afraid of sharing bathroom, don't worry! Agnes keep it always clean and satinized. You won't have to be worried about breakfast, Agnes is ready with plenty of food of many flavors and needes.   Room is also provided with everything you need for a comfortable resting.

Vana's place is the best East Village has to offer! Extremely spacious and cozy, and the garden steals the show. In a very lively and bohemian part of town, and Vana is very upfront about what to expect regarding noise, but that's part of the local charm. As a bonus, the host happens to be a world-class jazz musician!

This was my first experience with staying at an AirBnB and I was a little nervous as to what to expect. First I will address the actual apartment.   Very very clean! I can not stress this enough. Yes, you must take off your shoes before entering. House rules. I stayed in the first bedroom for 10 nights. I was provided 6 towels (3 per person) and our sheets were washed twice during our stay. On the table in the bedroom was a supply of beverages, snacks, and toothpaste/mouthwash/toothbrushes. Some of these drinks were very nice and definitely above what you will get anywhere else. Agnes also provided a gallon of water at the start, and actually kept replacing it as we used the water.   Every day I noticed the bathroom being cleaned. By the way, Agnes provides a host of shampoos/body washes/bar soap.   The kitchen has a supply of breakfast foods, some very very nice, for guests. This was such a treat to have some fruit and the option of bagels and eggs and organic foods there.   I have seen some reviews mention that Agnes was not very friendly. I don't know how they could have gotten that impression at all, unless perhaps they were not used to the New York briskness that some people there have. She was an incredible host, very accommodating with check in Times. She constantly provided us with ideas and suggestions of places to see and restaurants to visit and even gave us some of the history/trivia of the areas around the city. I was genuinely welcomed and happy to stay in her home.   For a neat freak like me, I was thrilled with how clean the apartment was. I was so happy to have a taste of the real 'New Yorker' experience.   I would completely recommend this place to anyone wanting a safe place to stay. I was nervous about staying in Harlem but truly to neighborhood was incredible. I felt safe and completely comfortable, even as a small town gal from Alaska.   Ten out of ten, would stay here again!! I highly recommend this place to everyone!!

The apt is excellently located, close to public transportation and stores in Park Av. It is like pictures published by Mario. Although he was not in NYC during my stay he was always available by e-mail and phone. The stairways is somewhat dangerous at the begining, but as soon as you get used to it, there is not any problem. The apt is cozy, well equipped, ideal to go alone, or on a business trip. I d definitely go back.

This was the first time we checked out 2 days earlier than paid for and found alternative accommodation. We have stayed at Airbnb apartments more than 25 times over the past few years and we always (with a few minor issues) have great experiences. The issue was not related to the apartment but to the host. I probably should have read through the public reviews a bit more carefully - and in particular should have read the host's the responses to the reviews - so I would have had a better sense of the personality of the host. It's fair to say we didn't get along very well, and I was disappointed in how some of the issues were handled. I felt that some actions were handled in a passive aggressive way, and she made us feel like she was doing us favors all the time - while at previous Airbnb stays, hosts have been predominantly accommodating and communication has always been pleasant. She appeared compulsive about keeping her house clean (I normally love clean apartments, but in her apartment we had the feeling that we were not allowed to touch anything - although she will say continuously "make yourself at home") and has many rules for keeping doors open, or closed, for light, airy, humidity, etc.. She likes to be in control and will tell you immediately when you do something she doesn't like or is not in accordance with her habits or rules. There is not much privacy and if she is not traveling she seems to be around a lot, spread out on the couch on her phone or laptop taking to friends on speaker phone. I felt she was doing this on purpose, so that if you don't feel like very actively engaging with her you will retire to your room immediately, and will not use the "public spaces". Our main issues were the following: Firstly, the host was coming back herself from a trip and had asked if the check-in time on Sunday evening could be at 9 pm at night (instead of 3 pm). We nicely suggested a few times that we could pick up the keys the Friday before the weekend before she left so we didn't have to wait for her to return from her trip, but she didn't want that. So on Sunday my son (10) and I were coming back from a tiring road trip to DC, had been dragging suitcases through NYC since 6 pm and were waiting for check-in when she informed us that her plane was late and that check-in would be later. In the end she only showed up at 9:15 but ran past us while we were waiting with our suitcases right in front of her building door. When I suggested that leaving a spare key with neighbor friends would be an option for the future, I got the response that she was "only" 15 minutes late for check-in (while normally check-in would be at 3 pm), and made it sound like she was doing us a favor....Then she rushed into the bathroom to take a shower, not asking us if after our long wait we might have wanted to use the toilet first. Secondly, after making the booking, I realized I should have booked for another day, so I informed the host and she said she would block the extra day and we shouldn't make an additional booking and could pay her in cash instead. After check-in I asked again if we were still good on a Sat check-out (instead of a Friday check-out) and she said we were ok. The next evening we got back she told us she had "by mistake" blocked the wrong date and that new people booked a long 10-day stay with her starting on Friday, that she had accepted that booking and that we thus would have to check out of Friday morning. That Friday was our last day in NYC and I had follow-up medical procedures planned (we live in Zimbabwe - so we often travel abroad for medical care), and I asked her what we had to do as it was a quite inconvenient development. She offered to help us find a new place or we could sleep on the couch (the apartment was super tiny, and with the new people checking on Friday there really would not have been space to breath). I felt she was only offering us this option to make sure that later on she could proof to Airbnb that she did "all she could", but I felt she didn't like us and had unblocked the date in the system on purpose and gladly accepted the new booking instead. Finally, on Tuesday evening we came home around 9:30 pm, said good evening and retired to our room. She was spread out on the couch and spent at least another hour on speaker phone on her laptop yelling at the phone company for some sort of issue she had (while her earbuds were hanging around her neck). I felt she was doing this on purpose (who makes so much noise until 10:30/11:00 when there is a 10 year old trying to sleep next to the thin installed wall that separates the bedroom from the living space?). Anyways we let is go as I didn't want to confront her. That same day I had casually mentioned to a friend the challenges we were having with the host and she kindly offered her apartment. As I was afraid the host would pull additional stunts, we didn't tell the host we were checking out in the morning and left quietly in the morning. Somehow I had the feeling she would have put us out on the street the evening before would she have known we were planning to leave and the reasons why. I felt like one of those people leaving a relationship by just disappearing in the night as reasoning with the person would never...

After receiving a damage claim, the following is my reply to the claim support rep. Hope this reveals what kind of host she is. ================================================================= Hi, Sxxxxx. I am very sad to have to deal with a situation like this and want nothing but a fair resolution with your help. Let me tell you what has happened in chronological order.If you have access to our messaging, you can see exactly what we conversed using the Airbnb app. If you don't, I can send you screen captures. By the way, my two daughters (both college students) stayed there 4 nights, Jan 8 - 12.  1/11 1:36PM (my kids were still staying there and they were out) She sent me a message saying that she entered the room and found her marble tray "permanently damaged" by spills from my kid's facial oils.I asked for the product info so that I could find its fair value on the web but she claimed that she bought it at a store in London for $150 + tax.She wanted $150 in cash and I was willing to pay. But when I told her my kids didn't have enough cash, she even asked me if they had an ATM card, which they didn't.Finally she accepted the idea of me sending her money via PayPal and gave me her phone# and email address. Then I told her that I wanted to take the "permanently damaged" tray since I am paying for it. I was going to use a marble oil stain remover hoping to remove the stains and use it. As soon as I mentioned this, she said she's going through Airbnb all of sudden. Then she claimed that, though she paid $150 for it, the tray's real value is $450.(her exact words: "I got it on mark down but the value is $450 because of the gold and marble") Very interesting logic!  And then she started sending me some photos of a torn pillow.I checked with my kids and they had no idea how a pillow could become like that after simply sleeping on it a few nights unless it was in a vulnerable condition in the first place. It is also suspicious that she brought this up only after she decided that she couldn't get $150 from me. The next day (on the 12th) she sent me more photos, this time ones of the bed sheet, and told me "they also stained the duvet cover with chocolate and a pen". So what? The sheet was slept in for four straight nights and it's time to wash it.  Sxxxxx, it's very simple.She initially just wanted easy $150 in cash.When it turned out she couldn't get it, she's now requesting $668.22. When I declined her request, I wrote back the following for the three items she's claiming "damaged". See if it makes sense to you.  Marble tray: this kind of trays are intended for such things as cosmetics and it's common that oil based cosmetic items leak a little. If she placed the tray in the guest room, she should've predicted this and applied a protective coating or something. I do this for all my marble surfaces if I think they are worth protecting. If she didn't want to bother, she should NOT have placed it there in the first place.  Pillow: The pillow ended up like this after my kid slept on it four nights. She didn't do pillow fights or anything rough with it. I am very certain that it was in a very vulnerable condition from the beginning. I need proofs that it was in a perfect condition before the check-in.  Duvet cover: My kids used the sheet for four nights. How many nights and guests does she use the sheet without changing? Wash it with good detergent. If we use things, they get stained and that's why we wash them periodically.  Overall I am very suspicious of this host.It did bother me that she entered the guest room repeatedly during my kids' stay while they were out and it didn't feel safe for my kids. Her house rules spelling out that no room service is provided during the stay, why should she intrude the guest's privacy without permission like this? Looking for damages on a daily basis?  I have a gut feeling that she's made damage claims way more than average hosts. Also, if you go through her reviews, you'd find similar concerns to mine without much trouble.  To be honest, I had no idea when some people told me that they never use Airbnb. It's a great business model and even saves me some money for lodging. I even considered being a host someday. However, after experiencing a host like the one I am dealing with right now, I begin to understand what they meant. Now I am telling my daughters to avoid Airbnb.

I stayed 8 nights in their apartment. The fact of sharing a bathroom before booking I thought it was going to be a problem. But the truth is that it never was. Excellent place. Many say Harlem is dangerous and it wasn't. We walk through the area at any time and never a problem. Just around the corner is the subway, literally two blocks away, a super market where you can buy things to eat or do things in the department. We use the kitchen to make breakfast. She was always very kind at all times. He answered our messages almost instantly. He gave us suggestions. The impeccable room. I even had money!!! The details he left us upon arrival are very nice. We did have a small Wi-Fi problem because it didn't reach very well in the room, but there was Wi-Fi and by looking for places you could find it. I booked knowing that detail but the truth is that because I was awake for 3 hours or so in the apartment, the wifi was not a problem. The bathroom is super equipped and there are a lot of things for breakfast. I 100% recommend Agnes, she is super friendly, fun and her apartment is the best. Cleanliness in the apartment is essential, so upon entering you have to leave your shoes in a basket. And you walk around the entire apartment and it's super clean. Every time I saw Agnes we stayed chatting. Telling us the story of your New York. And we of our country. We had super pleasant moments. Thank you !

I had my doubts when I first chose this airbnb, but agnes managed to excel in everyway possible. I felt silly doubting her at all. Every amenity you may possibly need is provided (toothbrush, toothpaste, towels), the location is honestly super prime. There are trains that lead directly to almost all parts of manhattan (I never needed to change trains), and her place is literally around the corner from the station.   I thought that it might be unsafe, but far from it. It was well-lit, busy, and very safe. Yet, it is very quiet in the room. It is also incredibly spacious for the price.  Agnes is very friendly, and multi-lingual. She provided so many recommendations that we were spoilt for choice. Honestly, a very big bang for your buck.

Quite surprised by our experience in this Airbnb. In fact, we reread the comments several times during our stay and obviously did not have the same luck as the majority of people.  The apartment is very good right next to the metro. HOWEVER, the wifi does not really work in the room contrary to what the host denies in the comments. The radiator stopped working in the middle of the stay in January, we informed the host, she replied that she was not responsible for the water heater.  But ABOVE ALL, Agnes’ communication made us very uncomfortable. When we arrived, a hello was exchanged and then directly an accusatory sentence which told us that we were going to have to comply with the rules. Hard to get into the material. What followed was a series of questions regarding our vaccination statue (which is mandatory to enter the USA by the way) and finally we were lectured on the different variants of covid. We had to wear a mask everywhere in the apartment and we understand that we need to take precautions but after the welcome we received it really created a feeling of uneasiness that we didn't even dare to express to our host for fear of saying the wrong word.  You should know that Agnes communicates a lot and only by message. We received a lot of messages from him during our stay, some with good intentions, others out of nowhere reminding us of basic rules of life in the apartment that we already respected, such as turning off the lights and taking off our shoes.  Agnes is however helpful, she offered to print documents for us and hold our suitcases a little after check out but it was always accompanied by a weird remark, out of nowhere which reminded us that she really didn't have to do that, that she was doing us a service and that she was not an employee (?).   All of this combined made the experience anxiety-provoking and quite unpleasant.

We are very satisfied with our stay. The apartment fully corresponds to the photos and description. We even had some good surprises: washing machine and wifi (although this is not indicated in the advantages of the apartment). The accommodation is perfectly located (in one of the best areas of New York for restaurants, bars and various activities). It is 5 minutes from the Astor Place metro station and not far from the Union Square metro station which directly serves quite a few must-see places such as Time Square. Only downside: the insulation is not great. So be careful of the cold in winter (although our host provides a small additional heater) and the noise at night. To summarize, this apartment has very good value for money! As for Seith, our host, he responds very quickly to emails sent. In addition, the keys are left in a small grocery store which closes very late (so no stress linked to arrival time!)

The two of us were guests at Waldemar's for a week and we can neither understand nor share the positive feedback. We are not particularly demanding, we have traveled a lot all over the world, both with Airbnb and as Couchsurfers, and have lived in various shared apartments for many years. There has never been such an unpleasant experience as with Waldemar. If you look at the few, honest reviews to which Waldemar has never reacted self-critically or with an apology, you get a small, authentic impression of him, the accommodation, but also of his interaction with (the paying!) guests. Waldemar reacts aggressively, defensively or unobjectively to critical feedback. Despite clear agreements about arrival times and the fact that we come directly from Germany and therefore have no internet, Waldemar was not there when we arrived, so we had to wait in the heat in front of his front door for almost two hours because he had spontaneously driven to the beach. Despite repeated calls, he did not answer the phone and did not respond to voicemail messages. As it later turned out, Waldemar had simply left a message online via the Airbnb portal that he had left the key in one of his flower pots. Despite this unfavorable start, we tried to assume there was a misunderstanding and remained positive. However, when asked later, he behaved rudely and aggressively because he felt he was in the right, after all, he had left a message. The fact that we couldn't get them wasn't his problem. That was the end of the issue for him. The tone was inappropriately loud and aggressive.  To give another example of several such: One day he told us not to lock the door because he was sitting in front of the door. So the next day, in a similar situation, we just closed the door. This time he ran after us on the street and shouted why we didn't lock the door. When we answered that he didn't want to do that the day before because he was at home, he screamed hysterically that we should always lock the doors and slammed the door in our faces.  Waldemar supposedly lives in a separate area, but actually he was almost always in the (messy) living room, which you have to walk through to get to our room. The TV, which you could hear all the time in our room, was on continuously until at least three in the morning at night and you could get the impression that he lived on the couch in the living room. In the morning from 7 a.m. the noise started right outside our room with people loading and unloading the dishwasher, feeding the cat, etc., so there was no serious thought about privacy or sleeping in. It doesn't matter what Waldemar claims or whatever definition you want to use: it's not clean there! Our room was run down and dusty. The shared bathroom has not been thoroughly cleaned even once, despite changing guests. The litter box in the kitchen area, which started right outside our bedroom door, smelled unpleasant. Conclusion: Unfortunately not recommended...

The location was great and super easy to find. The rooms were clean, though it could get quite noisy outside. The front door didn't lock, which was kinda scary. Otherwise, great place and we would definitely stay again.  Just a quick note, the stairs were quite steep (or at least steeper than what I'm used to). We had no problems carrying our carry-on size suitcases up the stairs, but we'd imagine anything bigger would be quite difficult.

Josh and Marilynn's place was exactly as depicted in the pictures. The house was lovely and the location was excellent. While initial communication was a bit sketchy as they were away in a remote area without mobile service, I truly believe they tried their best to make contact and ensure everything was ok. Overall our stay was exactly what we wanted and would definitely consider staying again when in the Brooklyn!

The apartment is as it appears in the photos. We found it very clean and well stocked with towels and blankets. Seith was flexible with check-in and check-out times and allowed us to leave our suitcases in the kitchen during non-stop hours after officially leaving the house. The neighborhood is central, well connected and has many establishments (bars, restaurants, supermarkets, laundries...). For those who are concerned about security, you should know that there is a police station two blocks away.  Now, I have several points. The first: the entrance to the house was not in the photographs of the advertisement, it was described to us by the host. Honestly, it's scary: it's a blue door that always has to be open, behind a gate (also open) where the garbage bags are boxed. When you open the blue door you find a very steep and dirty staircase that leads to another door (closed) which is actually the entrance to the house and is in a deplorable state. To access the apartment you still have to go through a common kitchen and climb another flight of stairs, so I would not recommend the stay for people with mobility problems or who cannot carry weights. The second point has to do with the windows of the apartment. Fortunately we had good weather in New York, but two days before we left the weather changed and a lot of cold came in from the street through the cracks. I would suggest the owner install double glazing to resolve this issue and, in the process, muffle the noise coming in from the outside. Finally: the mattresses on the single beds are quite thin and can be uncomfortable.

Wow! I have to say I like Edward so much. It is the best host ever. We became good friends. He is a caring person. I have to face a lot of difficulties when I was working that month. I am really stressful and exhausted with my work but Edward brought a lot of happiness to me. He makes me feel at home. Of course, people choose open their home space on airbnb to make money but when you not just care about money but care the people, the love start to flow

We love the east village and Seith's apartment is in a perfect location to get to all parts of the city. If you want an authentic NYC experience, staying here will give you a glimpse into apartment living in New York. We were traveling with our two children and the 2 bedroom set up was comfortable and perfect for us - each kid had their own twin bed to sleep on. Grammy even came for a night and slept in the living room. It was 90+ the week we were there and the air conditioners kept the place cool (thank goodness!). The sharing of the kitchen downstairs was no big deal - we never did cook anything but it was nice to know there was the option. The one tricky thing was the staircase - it was super steep which ended up being fine but felt a bit scary at times with small kids and grandparents. I would recommend Seith's apartment to anyone who wants an authentic experience in NY - the apartment is not new, but it is comfortable and has all you need for a great stay in NYC.

Very expensive for what you actually get. Very run down and in serious need of modernization. The 2nd single bed is shoved in the corner with a mattress no more than 10cm thick incredibly uncomfortable and should not be classed as a bed! Bathroom is very old with grotty brown tiles, with live open electrical bulb in the shower EXTREMELY DANGEROUS! On the plus location was fantastic and communication with host very good prior to visit. Unfortunately will not be staying again.

I’ve waited couple day before I write this review.  I was hoping our host would return my messages before I write any bad comments….. unfortunately the host decided not to answer.  Long story short, the check in was easy and smooth.  The place is small, but perfect for 4-5.  Before we arrive the host seems nice and reply quickly on the questions we have.  When we first arrive, we notice the unpleasant smell, but we didn’t mind it too much since it’s New York.  Everything seems well, the shower water was hot, the bed is quite comfortable….Until I witnessed a rat climbing out from the wall in the middle of the night!!  I admit I’m phobia to rat, I can’t sleep at all knowing it’s presence.  So immediately I contact airbnb support team to cancel the rest of the reservation.  Looked up an hotel and moved out in the middle of night.  Then I wrote to the host explaining why we left, hoping the host would as a courtesy to reply me.  I’ve send couple messages, but the host doesn’t seem bother to answer at all.  It’s seems irresponsible from my point of view that the host doesn’t even apologize or acknowledge anything after the incident.  And definitely will not stay at this place again.

This was my family's first AirBnB experience and it didn't disappoint. Noemie was very responsive in her communications with us from the minute we reserved her place. Both she and her husband, Rob, greeted us when we arrived where they promptly gave us the keys,  got us familiar with the place and then offered to be of assistance with any questions or needs we might have during our stay. We parked our van right out front of their place and then were able tomuse their driveway on a day where we needed to be off the street.   As for the apartment itself ... When we walked in I could tell it had been cleaned within the last few hours (still smelled fresh). The place was spotless. It was also comfortable. There was a master bedroom for my wife and I and my 9 and 4 year old daughter slept in the 2nd bedroom. My son was very content on the pull out couch. We ate breakfast in our place all three days. The TV was great with numerous cable stations. The bathroom was small for a family of 5 but it was recently remodeled and clean. We also appreciated the fans in each bedroom since we like "white noise" when we sleep. The fans also blocked out any noise of walking on the floors above us.   As for location ... It was probably a 7-10 minute walk to the subway station at Kingston and Eastern Parkway. On the first day we took a 20 minute subway ride from there to Battery Park to see the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island (although we went the wrong way to start). The next day we took about a 30-35 minute subway trip to the southern end of Central Park.   All in all it was a great stay and I would heartily recommend Noemie's "urban retreat" for anyone looking to visit NY City.

My wife and daughter spent 2 nights in Noemie's apartment in Brooklyn. Both Noemie and her husband, Rob, were great hosts. The apartment is spacious, comfortably and nicely remodeled. We were mostly on the go while there, but I could've easily spent more time enjoying the apartment.

Honestly, we had a superb stay with Noémie and Robert, 12 magnificent days. Their welcome and the apartment were consistent with what others have already said: top notch.  Their children are magnificent, too bad they were a little scary with my photos. Too kind, and environment too, the people of Brooklyn are super welcoming and have a lot of empathy, we were pleasantly surprised by its New Yorkers always ready to inform you and be of service to you, we see that they love their city and want to make people appreciate it. A great lesson for France to take.  Thank you again Noémie and Robert for your availability and your kindness.  We recommend this address, quiet environment, accessible (near metro), practical (near grocery stores), well appointed and with great taste. Very popular sofa.  We hope to be able to come back one of these days..... Nathalie, Didier, Ninon and Léa

A peaceful place to get work done. I was going through a stressful month and this place was perfect to rest and do work. Quiet place, very well decorated, and close to great things. Including my favorite pub, Black Swan.  There is a large dinning room table that is great for the remote worker. And the art is very good as well.

An amazing host. We did a small film shoot at Noemie's, and could not have asked for a more flexible, gracious and stress-free experience with the family. Not only did they ok the shoot, they let us take liberties with the space and even helped us change the lighting! It's above and beyond what we could have asked for. The apartment itself, of course, is a dream space for someone vacationing in New York. Clean, gorgeous and comfortable, it feels like a real home. We are so grateful to Noemie and her family for being so generous with their home; the space really made the film a million times more interesting.

Noemie and Robert were great hosts. They were very friendly and made us feel welcome. She provided very helpful information before and during our stay and was very accommodating with our requests. The apartment was exactly as described, there were no unpleasant surprises. Very clean and nicely decorated. We loved the exposed brick throughout the apartment. There was plenty of space for our group of 4. We didn't feel cramped like we would in a hotel. It is very close to public transportation which was a huge factor for us. We didn't feel unsafe at anytime even coming back in the late night hours. The cost was very reasonable and we didn't feel like we were breaking the bank for a place we didn't spend that much time in. We will definitely keep Noemie & Robert in mind the next time we decide to make our way back to NYC.

Noemie´s place was perfect. Really perfect. We were 4 adults and a baby and we felt like home, with everything you might need. The neighborhood felt OK, and we never felt uncomfortable or afraid. Distance to subway (2 lines available) was very good and in Kingston Ave we could find lots of delis and a groceries market. Noemie is the best!!!! She made everything so we feel at home... and more!  La casa de Noemie es perfecta. Realmente. Eramos 4 adultos y 1 bebé y nos sentimos como en casa, con todo lo que necesitamos. El barrio se sentía bien, y nunca sentimos incomodidad o temor. La distancia al subte/metro está muy bien y teíamos 2 líneas disponibles. En la Avenida Kingston encontramos muchos delis y a unas cuadras más un supermercado. Noemie es la mejor!!! Ella hizo todo para que nos sintamos en casa... y más!

Noémie and Rob were remarkable and warm hosts. They are always ready to help us and give us good advice. Their apartment in Brooklyn is very well equipped and located close to the subway. It is large enough to hold 5 people without problem. The environment is very pleasant and the inhabitants very welcoming. We spent 9 very pleasant days in New York in the middle of summer... the air conditioning in the apartment is perfect without being noisy. We recommend this address and we hope to come back to visit New York!

Noemie was always very responsive and she made me, my mother, wife and 5 year old son feel very welcomed.  She sent us information ahead of time and ensured that we found the apartment safely.  The apartment is lovely and while it is located about 25 minutes from Manhattan, it is close to the subway lines so that we could get anywhere we needed to.  The street is extremely quiet at night time.  Because I was traveling with my mother and young son, we did not stay out past 8 pm.  We followed Noemie's suggestion and took cabs back to the apartment at night time.  The neighbourhood is up and coming and still in the middle of its gentrification.  While it is not unsafe, general awareness of your surroundings is a good thing as it is with any large city.    The apartment itself was nicely laid out and well stocked with pots, pans, utensils and dishes.  The beds were extremely comfortable, including the sofabed which I slept on.  The washer and dryer were a nice feature as it allowed us to do laundry half way through our trip.    Check out was a breeze and all I had to was message Noemie when we were leaving and leave the keys on the counter.    All in all a great stay and I would stay here again when I am back in NYC!

Alicia is the perfect host! She is there for you when you need her, and leaves you freedom and space if there is no need for communication. I have stayed almost 3 weeks and Alicia's appartment and I liked it a lot. Great location, not too noisy (which I was very much afraid of), quiet and nice neighbours. Appartment itself is clean, well equipped. I had everything I needed during my stay at Manhattan. Thank you Alicia.

Staying in this place was really uncomfortable and awkward. The whole time we stayed in this place Waldemar and his sister was present the entire time leaving us no privacy what so ever except in our bedroom. The bedroom was like a 5 star jail cell. We weren't able to lock our door from the inside; however it could be locked it from the outside. Not to mention the door was designed like a caged door with a sliding bolt locked. The room had cobwebs and bugs. Our last night there I saw a bug crawled on my son's face while he sleeps. There was no AC only a ceiling fan. The entire place was very hot and add to that a smell that is indistinct and unpleasant. They also have a cat that walks all over their sink and the kitchen area is always dirty from their dishes. Waldemar is not very attentive to detail and rude. He charged me an extra $165 for my husband when I clearly mention as well as put 2 guest on my reservation a whole month prior and decide to  notified me this two days before to checking in. He was rude to my brother who was helping me with my luggage (not staying there) questioning him with an attitude who he was. Overall the stay with Waldemar was definitely a one star for me. I hope his future guest will not experience the same experience we have.

Extremely comfortable environment with all the amenities of a home to feel good. Quiet neighborhood served by two metro stations.  The distance to the main tourist attractions is around 30 to 40 minutes by metro, avoid late hours of the day and avoid leaving work. Extremely attentive and dedicated hosts, thank you very much Noémie and Rob!

Me and my guest never rented an Airbnb this place was our first experience. Unfortunately we did not enjoy it at all. I understand that we are renting a room with a backyard. Which reminds me, the doors going outside  was broken. The door to come inside the roll felt like a jail cell. Why is there 2 doors into entering a bedroom. The set up was weird. I suggest for him to take that black door out. the fact that the bathroom was out side the room it was uncomfortable to use because we either felt like we needed to be respectful enough to keep opening the doors, and the fact that him and his sister was in the common area the whole time. He even slepted in the living room the whole night which made it seem like we were going  to take his things. Don’t rent out a room if you going to feel unsafe. Pretty stupid. Or at least put cameras. The whole stay was just unsatisfying. However, he was very polite and kind. Just the experience was not my cup of tea. Sorry but I would not recommend anyone to stay unless he actually decides to sleep in his bed

We felt very comfortable in Noemie's apartment. The apartment was very clean and we didn't miss anything. Shops were within walking distance in the area, Manhattan, the rest of Brooklyn and Coney Island were easily and quickly accessible by subway. Check-in was excellent and problem-free, Noemie was always available and answered our questions, sent information and immediately sent Rob over when we had problems with the hot water. We just hadn't turned the tap on far enough... stupid Germans ;-) On the last day we were able to store our luggage in the apartment after we checked out. All in all, a great, clean and affordable accommodation with very friendly contact. Gladly again!

Our stay was great because the apartment is really pleasant to live in, the comfort of two bedrooms with a double bed is great! we appreciated the appliances available (dishwasher, dryer, kettle, etc.), the bedding and the connected channels Netflix, Amazon Prime, etc. on the giant screen. The desk and office chair were very useful to me. The street is quiet, with little traffic, an asset too! We walked to Prospect Park, a 35 minute walk! Very cool! Thanks to Noémie and Rob!

This was my first Airbnb experience and I was very pleased. I liked it so much I'll be back for New Years Eve! Didn't get to meet Ana but her husband Willem was the perfect host. The rooms were roomy, very clean and very private. Also appreciated the option of our own kitchen if needed. Willem also walked us to the subway and made sure we knew where we were going. Subway was just a few minutes walk away. The neighborhood reminded me of Sesame Street and I found myself breaking out in song with "Sunny Days". I never felt unsafe walking around the neighborhood. TIP: If you drive and park on the street be sure to pay attention to what side of the street you're on for the specific day if you're not used to parking in the city. Thanks to Willem and Ana for providing a great place to stay! See you again soon!

The place is good, in a black neighborhood, which was an interesting experience, but if I had gone alone I would have still been scared.  He didn't pick me up, like he said, but we went by taxi. The room was not big, but sufficient. Ana and her partner are very nice. We've had a good time.

The room and neighborhood is very nice. I gave a 3 star mainly because we had such trouble getting in touch with the renters. They asked us to call them to set up a meeting time but never responded to our voicemails. We actually arrived in NYC with no idea if we would have a space to stay or not. I was pretty stressed about that. We took the subway out to the brownstone but they were still not there. We were actually let in my another tenant. That tenant even lent us a copy of their key so we could go get dinner.  It was nice for us but also a little disconcerning- they didn't have any idea who we were but they let us in. Eventually that evening we met the owners (I never actually met Ana but her husband) who were very nice and apologetic and got us a key.  The room is nice and comfortable. And you just can't beat the neighborhood for walking around, people watching, food and location. We just had a bad taste in our mouth due to the stress at the beginning of our journey. We probably will not stay there again due to this.

Toni's studio apartment is very conveniently located in the Harlem neighbourhood.3 minute walk to the 2/3 Express train, and takes around 20 minutes to get into Time Square.There's also street parking, and the neighbourhood did not feel unsafe.   My husband and I didn't get to meet Toni when we checked in because she was out of town, but she had a friend meets us to give us the keys. Toni was very responsive from the moment I contacted her to enquire about availability and kept in touch whenever I had a question.Her check in and check out times are also very flexible.   The aparment itself is quite small, but there's room to unpack and hang up some clothes, and the studio has all the basic amenities you need for a comfortable stay. The room has an aircon which bcame handy for us on some evenings.   Overall this was a great place to stay for a week in New York. We'd come back here and recommend it to others.

I am afraid I cannot give a good review to this one. The room is not as shown on the picture - there is a large sofa and a glass table with chairs near the window. This adds comfort but makes the available space in the room a lot smaller than appears on the picture. The inside of the house is very dark. Communication before I arrived at JFK airport did not happen. Above all (what I have said above would not matter to me so much) the neigbourhood is NOT a safe area of NYC, especially for a white female travelling alone. I was verbally abused and called racist names while walking down the main street (which you have to do if you intend to use public transport). As a result I had to move location after 2 nights. I was never re-imbursed any of the money I have spent.  I didn't ask for a refund, because my primary concern was to move to a safe location as quickly as possible.

Carly wasn’t in town for our stay but was helpful with organising our arrival. We were greeted by her friend but there was some miscommunication regarding meeting time which made our arrival a bit stressful. The place is a good size for a short stay but there is no space to store clothes which meant we had to keep our suitcases open in the living room. It's a very comfy and homely apartment and Carly kindly offered use of her smart TV for our stay. We were a little disappointed to find that there are minor things wrong in the place - the most difficult of which was the door of the apartment which was temperamental for the first few days. However, the apartment block felt very safe and the surrounding area was a nice place to stay. The location is very good being so close to Central Park and the Metro as well as there being plenty of restaurants and supermarkets nearby. Thank you for having us!

We had a great two-night stay at Michelle's. We took a bus into the city from DC late on a Friday, so our arrival to Brooklyn was both late and a bit unpredictable, but Michelle was really flexible and happy to meet us when we got in around 11:30 p.m.  The Clinton Hill neighborhood is cute. There are a few nice restaurants right around the corner. One called the Drug Store, which appears to be an upscale Italian place (we didn't go but it looked great), and another one called Speedy Romeo, which is more casual and super yummy. It also has a cameo in a recent episode of Girls.   We thought the place looked even better than in the pictures. It was clean and had a great light. There is also a lot of interesting art work in the place, as well as more books on art than I've ever seen in my life. I guess that's fitting since this place is really close to the Pratt Institute.   Michelle was really nice, helpful and laid back. She was full of recommendations and helpful advice. I'd definitely recommend!

I cannot recommend Amber highly enough. From start to finish, she represents the gold standard of the airBnB experience - she was responsive, friendly, and supremely helpful. We had great communication from the get-go - she sent me thoughtful notes throughout, checking in with me to make sure I had everything and was enjoying myself - and she was very welcoming from the moment I showed up to the moment I left! She was the best kind of host - warm but not intrusive; if you want to chat, she's down, and if you need to rush or some private time, she's cool with that too.  The room is perfectly described - cozy, quiet and with every touch you could think of (and a bunch you might not have!). There's room to store all your belongings between the closet and the dresser, a box full of information on NYC and helpful house tips, space in the bathroom for toiletries... the entire apartment is immaculate, beautifully decorated, warm and welcoming, and great to return home to after a long day. It's also very convenient to the 125th Street MTA station - less than a five-minute walk.  I never felt unsafe in the neighborhood as a single female traveler. If you're city-wise in any respect and use your common sense, you'll be perfectly fine staying here.  I really enjoyed my time in Amber's place, and I hope to stay there again. :)

The host was very good at communicating.  I didn't meet Laura but she was available by text and she called me to make sure that I had checked out before going in and cleaning.   Her place is overall great and as advertised.  The only downside is the five story walk-up on a narrow flight of stairs, but that is as stated on airbnb.  The unit itself is fully equipped and has AC.  I took off a star because picking up the keys downtown during rush hour added stress and increased my travel time  There are very few places to stay in Inwood, and if you are looking for a basic, clean, and affordable spot for a good night's sleep, this is it!

Overall, I enjoyed my stay at Ny's place. It is clean, cozy and very quiet. But I felt uneasy about the check-in.   Long story short, I clicked the directions on the email that Airbnb sent to me and somehow it directed me to a wrong address. It was midnight and I was anxious to find the correct place. I called the host several times and no one responded. Finally, after struggling for 15-20mins or so, I realized that the address was wrong and I found the correct one in the check-in instructions on Airbnb.  I should also mention that during my entire stay, I never met my host although we kept message communication during the daytime. I heard someone entered the apartment around 2 am in the morning, but never know who stayed at the apartment. I felt a bit unsafe about this and wish the host could inform me about this in advance.

Second time Biren has hosted me in a week.  Great household.  Bed was lovely.  Space much appreciated around the bed.  Was able to accomplish a writing project in 10 hours there sitting by the window, and enjoy wonderful food from around the corner (Taste of Lahore).    Need to address a recent reviewer from 6 months back who was rude - I did not find any of the aspects discussed by that guy (whose own reviews were mixed- being generous).  I feel empathy for wonderful folks like Biren who open their homes to potential difficult visitors and want to stress how hospitable and open Biren and his whole family are (and no- they are not all there all the time!  Quite the contrary).  A WONDERFUL pick for Jackson Heights.  Highly recommended.

The apartment is quite old and unrenovated, which means it has it's charm but also some scary parts. While it is sunny, as promised, don't expect much of a view. The neighborhood is wonderful during the day and everything important is close by.

I was a very nice experience, I like to live with other people from other places and talk about our cultures and different ways of life, everything I liked in the department is very comfortable and has everything you need to live the time you're traveling, Oliver he is very attentive and very understandable, though not in all in the department, he will always answer a message whether or contacting and always as help you look, it is a very cute and nice person, I recommend one hundred percent stay, I would the city is very interactive and there are many places to visit, the area of ​​the department is not dangerous and can walk at night without any problems, and I think the department rules are fine, I had no problem, I loved(:

Two thumbs up! I really couldn't thank Jeanine enough. The room is cozy but fits my exact needs, it's clean, well-lit, and quiet. I slept very well in the bed, and I have just the right amount of space for my stuff. The apartment is well-kept, very clean, just a wonderfully and comfortable place, especially the kitchen and the bathroom. Jeanine really took care of it, and it also showed that she cared about her guests having a nice place to come home to. I enjoyed all the conversations and I know I'm in good hands when I stay at Jeanine's place. The location is perfect, easy distance to so many subway lines. Harlem does have a lot to offer, and I feel safe walking home late at night. Elevator in the building was a big help so take advantage of that. Again, I can't stress enough how much I appreciated Jeanine's top-notch hospitality! Thanks!

Jeanine and Sergio, her boyfriend, were great hosts to me and they would go out of their way to help me with whatever I needed: from my earlier check-in and the providing of information to get me from the airport to their place to tips on where to eat, where to go and how to transit in the city. Despite their very busy routine, they did make a point of sparing some time to talk to me and get to know me better, which made me feel a lot more comfortable in their place. As for its structure, the appartment is pretty big and cozy and it is exactly as shown in the pics: I just can't help remembering the awesome time I had in NYC when taking a glimpse at them. Well, it was a great start to me in AirBnB and there's no reason I wouldn't recommend you Jeanine and Sergio as hosts! =D BTW: No, Harlem is NOT dangerous and it is a lovely place. I would easily live there! S2

Staying with Jeanine and Sergio was most enjoyable. Arriving there was very easy, everything was ready, the room exactly as described on their page, the bed comfortable (I have terrible shoulder problems, so I really appreciated the bed being good), the kitchen and bathroom impeccable. Jeanine and Sergio were both lovely people and very, very helpful, so much more than I would have expected :-) I had nice chats with them and the other people staying there, too. Everybody was very respectful of the privacy of others, never had any trouble with bathroom turns or such. The atmosphere was relaxed and pleasant. When it comes to the neighbourhood, it was a lively and safe one, many nice places for eating out and some grocery stores just around the corner. I personally like Harlem best out of all NYC areas, it is interesting and groovy, and I never experienced anything unpleasant there. This was my 3rd visit in the city, and based on previous experiences of Harlem I especially wanted to stay there :-) 125th street is a fun street to hang around and do some shopping. Central Park is a 10 walk from the apartment, and a few blocks away is the subway that will take you downtown in no time.  I would definitely stay at Jeanine and Sergio's again if I had the chance to revisit New York any time soon!

I had a great time at Jeanine's. She is a wonderful hostess. Friendly and helpful. She made sure I had an amazing time in NYC. The accommodations is as desribed, no surprises. Very convinient area - quiet area within 5 minutes walk to subway and coffee shops and restaurants. Few minutes walk from central park. Direct line to JFK airport - takes about hour and half, but very easy without any stress even with a huge suitcase and cheap - only for $7,25. I can only recommend for exploring Manhattan. Accommodation itself quiet and very clean.

Since this was my first airbnb experience Daniel made it very easy for me to want to try this out again. Daniel was extremely prompt with contacting me. His abode was very cozy. It was conveniently nestled around plenty of restaurants, drugs stores and a grocery was directly across. The closest entrance to the subway was just a block away so I could easily commute to work. Full on cable channels. The building was quiet which I liked because with my work schedule I'm normally asleep during the day. I definitely would like to stay again or in that matter actually look for a place in that area to reside.  Thank you again Daniel!

It was my first trip to NYC and live 1 month to Melanie was just fantastic!!  When I arrived I was so stressful but Melanie was So kind with me ! She's a very thoughtful, friendly and nice person.  I LOVE HER PLACE. The apartment is very well located and very clean. The district is good as well, safe and not so noisy. Melanie is a native from NYC and is always available for goods advices. I shared a gorgeous moments with her! I miss you Melanie
Clean. Building undergoing construction so unpleasant at the moment but once done is convenient and nice. Gary is very easy to deal with and accommodating.
I had another amazing stay at Gary's apartment. Incredible location and a very easy stress free check in/out process. Can't wait to stay there again. Beats any hotel experience I've had in NY.

My husband and I ventured to NYC for our mini-moon and had a great time! It turned out to be a busy week for both James and my husband and I, but the time we were able to share together was great. James is a fabulous host and really made us comfortable in his home and neighborhood! He is super friendly, and I know we would be great friends if I lived in Brooklyn! His place is EXACTLY how it looks in the pictures: spotless, spacious, cozy, and welcoming. The bed was super comfortable, and we had a restroom to ourselves a few short steps from our room.   James' place is about a 5-7 minute walk from two different train stops on the J line, which was wonderfully convenient. We were also near several bus stops which we utilized as well. The neighborhood is pretty quiet at night, as it is very residential, and safe (not to mention it is located a block from a giant police station). We walked to his home after 1:00am several nights and did not have any problems. But as in any neighborhood, including your own, you must be aware of your surroundings at all times.  You know, no headphones and don't be engrossed in your phone. And don't be afraid to say hi to the neighbors. Folks are pretty nice around there!   His particular neighborhood has SEVERAL delicious restaurants in walking distance, a few of which are:  Saraghina's--Scrumptious pizza and pasta--gets super crowded so get there early!   David's Brisket House--Mouth-watering hot pastrami sandwiches. Quick service and is a whole in the wall.   I would also recommend trying Brooklyn Bowl. Super fun restaurant venue, and ?uestlove from the Roots DJs every Thursday! You will have to take a bus or train/combo to get there. Totally worth it!   *Side note: For those of you traveling to NYC, I recommend getting a 7-day metro pass for $30. Between all the subway and bus rides, you get your money back in two days!!!  Anyway, James is great, his home is great, and his community is great.   I love Brooklyn!!!

Dana was in contact with us the whole time and is amazingly attentive to any questions. The apartment is beautiful! The building is very new and everything was so nice and clean! (That's hard to find in Brooklyn!) The apartment is just the right size for two people and Dana had everything to make us feel at home. The 'C' line has a station about 2 blocks away which put us in Manhattan in minutes. We also found it was very easy to get to Williamsburg too, not to mention that her apartment is only a short walk to Park Slope. In all we had a wonderful, easy and stress-free stay at Dana's and would certainly stay again!

Everything was perfect about the 8 days that we have spent in James's house. The house is fairly big and spacious, it was good not to get stuck in a small hotel room. We wish we could spend more time in the house but it was not possible to do so in a restricted time. It took a little long to arrive at Manhattan (approximately 35-40min.) but not a big problem. We always arrived home after midnight and the subway (J train) was quite full, so it seemed safer =) normally i expected it to be empty and scary but wasn't like that and the huge police station on James's street gives you confidence anyways. I recommend his place if you're looking for a really nice and safe place to stay in New York.  Merve.

James was the perfect host - great communication before we arrived, and perfect directions for how to travel on public transportation from the airport.  We arrived during some very warm weather (we were sweating like crazy) and James saved the day with an AC unit in our room.  The room was good sized, comfy bed, a place to hang our clothes, and our own private bathroom.  We didn't do any cooking, but it was nice to have access to the kitchen to store food, and we did eat our breakfasts outside on the deck which was great.  If you are looking for a well priced, comfy, easy to access place, this is a great choice...just don't expect trendy restaurants all around you.  We rode the subway at night and walked home late at night and never felt unsafe...that was a huge concern for me so I am glad it worked out.

Experiences in this apartment: We don't recommend this place for several reasons, in the first place the terrible management of the owner, the total lack of cleanliness of the apartment and above all this, her absolute lack of interest in problems caused by her awful management. The price is far above what it's worth. We were forced to pick up the keys in a nearby supermarket at night after a transoceanic flight. They gave us the wrong key and we were in the middle of the streets, with luggage. We had to return to the supermarket to get the right keys. How did we know that nobody could copy the keys and rob our stuff? When we finally got the door open we found that they had left the washing machine on and a note where they told us to "put the dryer on". Between that first night and the next day we saw the serious deficiency of cleaning, hairs everywhere, even in the drawers of kitchen utensils, the refrigerator with dirty expired food, anyway, we bring photos where you can see even the dust accumulated in different elements of the apartment. Or the condition of the pillows, etc… There are hostels and pensions of $10 a night that don’t have these bad conditions. We have never had problems with our accommodations through Airbnb, where we always met wonderful people until we stumbled upon this lady. If someone is interested and wants to see the real conditions of the property, I’ll add some pictures with the sole purpose of you not being scammed with what the owner puts as photographs of the apartment. María Carmen Cruz. Experiencias en este alojamiento. No lo recomendamos a nadie, la mala gestión de su propietaria en cuanto a la concesión de las llaves, como la absoluta falta de limpieza del apartamento, como su absoluto desinterés ante problemas provocados por su gestión. No está absolutamente justificado lo que cobra por día al estado del inmueble. Las llaves nos las hicieron recoger en un supermercado, por la noche, acabábamos de llegar de un vuelo transoceánico. Nos dan la llave, que no abre, nos quedamos en medio de la calle, con equipaje, de noche. Regreso al supermercado a por las llaves, y rebuscan hasta que me dan las correctas. Y además como sé yo si durante mi estancia cualquiera no ha hecho copia de esas llaves y me va a robar mi dinero, pasaporte, y enseres mientras estoy haciendo turismo por la ciudad?! Cuando por fin conseguimos abrir la puerta nos encontramos que nos habían dejado la lavadora puesta y una nota donde nos indicaban:”que nosotras pusiéramos la secadora”. Entre esa primera noche y el día siguiente vimos las faltas graves de limpieza, pelos por todas partes, hasta en los cajones de utensilios de cocina, la nevera con comida caducada y sucia, en fin, aportamos fotos donde hasta se ve la capa de polvo acumulado en diferentes elementos del apartamento. O el estado de las almohadas, etc......

I stayed at Dana's place for 3 months so my experience was a tad different. I'll be listing the pros and cons.   Pros: beautiful studio, comfy, comfortable bed and pillows, room darkening shades, grocery store right across the street, C train 3 min walk, bus stop right in front of the apartment complex, cute and tasty bakery downstairs and a lot of restaurants nearby   Cons: As someone mentioned, the dryer doesn't work that well but It didn't affect me as much. Better than walking out in the cold to get laundary done.  I had things arise that required someone to be home to take care of things. I'm a medical student working at the hospital 10-12 hours a day then I have to come "home" to study for the rest of the night. It got really stressful as Dana wasn't in NY for the entirety of my stay. She was very quick to respond and did her best to get who ever she could to help me but this was just my personal experience. I would've obviously preferred to stay in a place where any issues regarding the apartment could be taken care of by the host while I just worry about my work/school.   Regardless of my personal experience, this should be a great place for anyone. It's absolutely beautiful, convenient and she provides almost everything you need: iron, hair dryer, towels, coffee maker, sheets, pots, pans, utensils. She also responds to you within minutes.

Staying at Dana’s place was great in some aspects and challenging in others. Pros: location close to the subway into NY and near lots of up and coming neighborhoods, cute design in the studio, and right across from the grocery store and nice yoga studio. Cons- right on top of the subway line so you hear the trains (and feel them) in the apartment. The windows didn’t have very dark curtains so it was hard for us to sleep. The area is in a more sketchy part of Brooklyn (in my opinion) and I felt a bit unsafe walking outside. Host left the place pretty dusty and then when we left accused us of breaking her sink (which we clearly didn’t) and had very strict rules for living there which didn’t let us feel like we could relax. We had to go through disputes with Airbnb to remove charges she wanted us to pay. We stayed as a couple for a month and it definitely felt too small for us to live comfortably - but for a short time it’s a nice spot close to NY for sight seeing.

My stay at David and Sean's apartment was my first experience with airbnb and it was more than what I had wished for. The apartment is located a minute's walk away from EVERYTHING and anywhere you would imagine to go in the super trendy Williamsburg neighborhood.
