My friend and I were staying for Tribeca Film Festival, so we spent the majority of our time in the city but thanks to the awesome accessibility of the apartment we were able to explore Williamsburg quite a bit. Blue bottle coffee, Peter Luger steak and burger, Brunch at Egg, Drinks at multiple bars and beer gardens, Mast Brothers' chocolate, an excellent wine shop, drug store, grocery store, posh independent film theater, Japanese comfort food restaurant were all places we went to and were literally, 1 to 6 blocks away. The L train is a minutes walk away too. Not only is the location killer, David is an awesome host. He carefully walked us through what was in the neighborhood, like the fact the L train would be out of commission on certain days of our stay and gave us tips on alternate transportation. He lended us his Moma card. Welcomed us to have food and drinks in the fridge and let us feel like we were really at home. Whenever we had a question about the neighborhood or the apartment he was quick to respond and very clear.  On top of the host and location being great, the apartment was absolutely gorgeous. The photos are accurate. The long nights in the city was definitely memorable but the short time we spent chilling in the living room was equally memorable. I could see how living in a beautiful and relaxing home like that relates to the kind demeanor David and Sean showed as hosts.  Thank you for making our stay in NY an awesome one. We'd love to come stay at your beautiful home again.
Beautiful place. Beautiful energy. Harlem is a real quarter, not dangerous and the house is very close to subway.  I’ll be back

This listing was a nightmare. Holes in the walls covered by duct tape and floors, so bad that my foot went through them several times. The address is inaccurate: 46 Charles street instead of 56 Charles street which is a completely different property. No running hot water, when contacting the host he offered little advice and never sent anyone out to resolve the issue. There are stairs in this building, no elevator which is false information in reference to those who have difficulty walking up several flights of stairs. The host made us travel nearly 20 minutes away from the listing to his luxury apartment complex for the keys to the building. Did not even greet us himself, gave to doorman instead. Biggest waste of 700$ in my life. Yes, the west village is an ideal location, however there are nicer and safer locations that have cheaper stays that I have had better experiences with in the past. When contacting the host about retribution and Airbnb, neither were helpful. This scam that he is running knowingly is called a bait and switch scam. It’s fraud. So if you respect your time, money, and the chance to take a proper shower this isn’t the place for you. Nor is it the company you want to book with.

Fantastic location - 5 minute walk to a subway with direct links to times sq. An array of bars and restaurants to choose from right on the door step. As described. Powerful shower. Very spacious. Friendly host. The apt does not have air con but there were 2 big fans that helped with that. However I left with a lot of suspicious bites on me.

Rick's apartment on 3rd street was a great place to stay to be near my son , who lives on 4th. I arrived very late after flight delays and Rick was very kind to wait until midnight until I arrived . He was very helpful in his tour of the apartment. If you are looking for a clean place to stay, you have found it. The building is pretty quiet and don't let the 6 th floor address scare you; there is an elevator. I found it convenient to take a short walk to the subway. We had a very busy week for my son's graduation and it was nice to be able to put our feet up on Rick's couch and relax. The neighborhood is quiet in the day and a little noisy at night but, it is N.Y. I don't think there is quiet at night in the city that never sleeps . We had nice weather. The apartment has amazing ceiling fans and with the windows open at night there was a cool breeze. If you are looking to stay in the middle of the East Village, this place might be perfect for you.

Mayra was super responsive and helpful; I felt very well taken care of even though we never met. Her apartment is very clean and the location is great. The building was kind of shabby and old but it's in a really safe part of town close to loads of food options. The bedroom is really warm, so bring cool weather pajamas! I was afraid the bed would be small for two but it was pretty spacious.

The apartment was not really what it seemed to be in the photos. The bathroom smelled of must and was not clean at all. When I woke up I had a dozen bites on my hands which resembles those of bed bug bites. The host was not communicative about the problems I was dealing with the place and I feel somewhat scammed for what I was looking for. Would not recommend this place.

Overall, I can't honestly say whether I would recommend this apartment. There were several things that we loved about the space (the location, it felt very safe, minimal noise from the street), but there were also several things that made parts of the stay unpleasant. Checking out the keys was difficult and I had to reach out to Lorena to figure it out. When we arrived to the apartment, the cleaning lady was still there and she left pretty quickly which left us with the impression that she didn't finish cleaning the apartment. The towels that we were provided did not smell great and we chose to purchase our own to use while there. We were also told that the superintendent needed access to the apartment during one of the days of our trip to fix a leak in the shower, of which we were understanding but it did feel like a bit of an intrusion.   The apartment is clean, but very cluttered with personal items that make it feel like the owners just left town for the week while you're staying in their space. There also was not a pull-out couch (as the listing stated when we booked) but there was an air mattress. The photos are misleading and it honestly wasn't exactly what we expected, but again that did not affect the quality of our trip.   I think that my overall opinion is that the space itself is/could be great. The location, the area, the apartment itself were lovely, however it felt like the management of this property as a rental space was lacking and could have been better executed. It felt like the things that I disliked about the rental and the stay could be attributed back to the owner and could potentially have been avoided or negated.

When I booked this place I was so excited because it’s located in East Village and was super cute from the pictures. I texted Lorena 3 weeks in advance to my trip about just dropping off our luggage early because we would arrive earlier from  check in and she never responded. Once I got to New York, I assumed she would respond I guess but she never even sent me access to get the key to the Airbnb or anything. I texted, I called her and our check in was at 3 pm and nothing. My mom and I had no idea where we were going to go and it was extremely cold because this happened in late November. Thankfully we got a hotel for one night and the next day Lorena texted and said she hoped everything was okay because we had to cancel, I thought that was ridiculous. I advise you do not book with Lorena because she does not respond and I don’t want this to happen to anyone again, it was extremely stressful and disappointing but we still had a great time in New York despite all that.

We are a couple who was looking for a last minute place to stay in Crown Heights on our way home from a camping trip. Miryam was able to accommodate us on short notice. First, the apartment: it was just as sunny and bright as described, high ceilings, hardwood floors, etc. During the day, the sunlight was sufficient – there wasn’t any need to turn on the lights. The apartment was immaculately clean, with plenty of towels, soap & shampoo. The furniture looks brand new. We slept in the blue “sky” room. I’m picky about my pillows and these were great, high quality pillows and good cotton linens. The luggage rack in each room was super helpful. The bathroom was clean and your basic standard bathroom. The kitchen was stocked with paper goods and coffee (Thank God!), tea, sugar, and a few spices. The electric tea kettle was great – we had coffee in minutes. Coming in from a camping trip and having the washer/dryer right in the apartment was incredibly helpful. I was able to put in two loads of camping clothes so we didn’t have to travel home with dirty laundry. The living room sofa was super comfy, especially with the air conditioning blowing. In fact, all the air conditioning units work really well. The bookshelves only have a few books, I suspect because it’s a new rental they haven’t had time to fill it up yet. The location was great, centrally located on Eastern Parkway, and we found there to be sufficient parking on the street. In regards to the hosts, Miryam and her husband were on-site and were warm, welcoming, and fun to be around. They have plenty of good restaurant suggestions as well! While we didn’t need the other rooms they also looked brand-new and the same linens, etc.

We very enjoy our time in this place! It's a very good apartment for many people! Pictures are fully compliant! The apartment is very clean, well located (40 minutes by metro from Time square), the metro is only 5 minutes and the neighborhood is well! No one we felt unsafe!! Oh and the beds are super comfortable!!!! It's important after a long day of walking to visit New York!!!  Do not hesitate if you're looking for a place to stay in NY!  In french: Nous avons beaucoup aimé cet appartement! Il est parfait pour plusieurs personnes! Les photos sont tout à fait conformes! L'appartement est très propre, bien situé (40mins en métro de Time square; le métro n'est qu'à 5mins à pied) & le quartier est très bien! Du moins nous ne nous sommes pas du tout sentis en insécurité et ce même le soir. Un petit plus pas négligeable: les lits sont très confortables!!! Plutôt sympa après une longue journée de marche!!!  Bref si vous cherchez un appartement à NY, que vous êtes plusieurs et que vous n'avez pas trouvé votre bonheur dans le centre n'hésitez pas!
Loved the house and neighborhood. Tiffany was an awesome host. Totally stress free transaction. Parking was easy.  My first experience with Air BnB was super.

we had a great time at Diego's place, nice flat, spacious bedroom and comfi bed. We didn't see Diego that often, cause we spend most of our time exploring town. But we where able to have a drink together. Everything was smooth from arriving to checking out, his lovely dad welcomed us when we arrived. We did run into problems with the shower and we didn't have hot water for a day, but that was fixed asap. I also like the neighbourhood, never felt unsafe and some great food to buy in the street, and close to the subway 6 line that brings you straight into town. So overall great time, I can defiantly recommend staying here.

I have already left a very long comment but which obviously has not been recorded...  the apartment is quite large and functional. the bathroom a little dated and not very secure regarding electricity, bulb very close to the shower. The decor is rather funny, Legos and Star Wars everywhere. the room overlooks 116 st, very noisy, I slept very poorly for 4 days. Diego was not present when we arrived, myself accompanied by an 11 year old child, did not answer the phone or my text messages, which was quite stressful. Finally he finally came forward and apologized. The apartment was still occupied by the tenants who preceded us, a big mess everywhere. Diego promised to clean up. when we returned in the evening around 10 p.m., everything was clean but Diego was there, to my great surprise! I thought I had rented the entire apartment, but no, I had read the ad wrong. Fortunately Diego went on a trip and we were able to have peace of mind. the neighborhood is cool and nice, Diego probably too, but I didn't appreciate his bad faith, claiming that I had not informed him of our arrival at 12 p.m., even though I had sent him an email and a text message the day before, then the morning of our arrival.

Four family & friends in town to see a show in the city and to explore the brewery scene in Brooklyn.  Tiffany was a great host.  Gave accurate instructions on how to get in using the lock box.  The apartment was so cozy. I’d live there.  It was nicely appointed, clean and completely comfortable for the 4 of us. Coffee in the morning was a nice touch, too.  Location was spot on for what we wanted to do.  Direct train into the city from Atlantic Barclays Station 5 min walk, and dropped us off right across the street from where the show was. Fast (40 mins to upper broadway 96th street area) and convenient. Never felt unsafe in the neighborhood. Found a parking spot on the next block over. And then we walked everywhere.  We will definitely stay there again.  Thanks Tiffany!

We only stayed in Walker's apartment a couple nights, and we were gone most of the day, but we had a great experience. The apartment is wonderful and the subway is practically right outside the door. Walker was very welcoming to us and our stay here was stress-free and enjoyable. Would love to stay here again.

The apartment is very clean and spacious. Diego is very friendly and listens and gave us all the information and advice possible. He allowed us to enter the premises very early in the morning as our flight was arriving very early. The apartment is quite quiet and is about an 8-10 minute walk from the first metro station. Otherwise, a bus stop is a few meters from the apartment. The area is lively but you can find everything there, food, coffee, photocopies, hairdresser, etc... I recommend Diego's accommodation without reservation.  The only drawback is that the apartment is located on the 3rd floor without an elevator, which can be an inconvenience if you have heavy luggage.

we were two weeks at dee apartment, and it was higher than we expected (inspite the sandy huricane at our last day there). first of all the wonderfull apartment, high in the 33 floor (nothing to be afraid off) with a fantastic view on new york, the  hudson river and jersy city. the apartment is equipped with everything for a long stay, and is positioned within minutes of walking (safely at any hour of the day and night) from the subway and center of the city. second but least dee was a charming hostess, waiting for us when we came, and leave. helpfull with advise and guidenece. to sum up we recomend the apartment with all our heart. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ etty & ishaiu

Couple of thing for any future guest:  1) the location is close to: Target, Marshalls and Bloomington’s so if we need to economy shopping this is good. 2) 7- eleven is literally next door so for a quick snack, water and other quick shopping is another plus. 3) the Subway station to downtown is 2 blocks away (6 train) and the bus stop is across the street. 4) if you are looking to a place just to crash and sleep and you are an easy guest this place will work fine. 5) The room is just in front of the street so if you are a light sleeper you might want to consider due to the noise. Ok our case every day came exhausted of walking like 25K steps so wasn’t a deal breaker for us. 6) if you are not into soft mattress maybe this is not your place. ( I know this is a thing for some people as myself been a host too) 7) Fernando have 2 roommates that basically never around. 8) this is a 420 friendly house so if this is not your vibe again not your place. We don’t do that but it doesn’t bother us either. 9) the area is relatively safe, but you will notice some of the not nice stuff of NYC like some homeless people, maybe some street discussion, but even though we walk late at night nothing happened. Of course been down lown to avoid the attraction of been “touristy” people.  10) Food, you will be able to finde all type from fast food (wendys, BK, Dominos) to some locals like Chinese, Mexican, Dominican, Chinese and of course the famous street food and street trucks.  So if you are looking for a fair price and traveling on a budget and you are not into fancy travel this will be a perfect spot.  Finally Fernando was very helpful even lend us his Costco Membership to buy some stuff.

Fernando's place is 2 blocks away from a subway station. His room is clean, spacious, and can easily fit 3 people in. It is complete with a television, fridge, and heater among other things (several comfy couches too). The neighborhood is crowded at certain points of the day and can be a bit scary because of the recent incidents that happened during the time of our stay. Will recommend and stay again if given the chance.
Fernando is a nice guy, he let us check in and check out at any time ! We were a bit scared about the neighborhood at first but everything went well, we had a good trip
The room is spacious, but the location looks and feels unsafe, the room lacks cleanliness, but it is acceptable.

Apartment in Hispanic Harlem. Very interesting neighborhood and rather well served. Not dangerous neighborhood.  Fernando is a very cool and caring person :) the apartment is very clean and well appointed.  Two small downsides: the bedroom window overlooks the very noisy 2nd avenue + the bedroom does not lock from the outside (but the apartment is very safe)

Fernando is very helpful and accommodating, however the apartment is not as clean as it seems, the shared bathroom and toilets are not cleaned. Regarding the room, it's true that it's very noisy, the neighborhood is rather unusual, as a girl you can feel in danger, but nothing too bad in general. The bedding was comfortable

I hate to give a poor review to anyone, but buyer beware of this one.  THE GOOD: Location, and easy/quick check in. THE NOT SO GOOD: Very dirty, very small, unpleasant smell, hot water unreliable. Overpriced better off getting a hotel room.

I’m hesitant on how to rate this, but given that I tried to speak to Outpost Club first directly and was given a half-ass and rather hostile response, I’m laying out my honest review here instead. Keep in mind that I’ve lived in nyc the past 6 years.  COST: you are being overcharged. Go directly through Outpost Club to avoid Airbnb fees or negotiate, or book elsewhere.  CLEANING: The cleaners, as advertised to come weekly, came one time in the four weeks I was there. There were fruit flies everywhere, people were bad at cleaning up after themselves, and floors were always sticky.  SUPPLIES: again, as advertised, there would be cleaning supplies, etc. Paper towel and toilet paper was consistently low or nonexistent, so I bought my own.  LOCATION: there are a ton of great bars and restaurants within walking distance. It’s a 15 min walk to the C train, your best bet to get to Manhattan. It’s ~40 minutes to Herald Square.  SAFETY: the smoke alarms are all pulled out. I told Outpost Club this and was met with a “show us proof or we don’t believe you” response so I sent them photos. Maybe they’ll be replaced soon.  COMMUNITY: I lived here because Outpost advertised community events and I wanted to meet new people. I understand that during the pandemic this might change. In reality, no one is told when someone new joins the apartment. This is also a safety concern of multiple people in the apartment. We never knew if people in the living room were guests or friends or guests unless we asked.  RULES: not really followed (e.g. quiet hours, cleaning, etc.). Overall it served well for working from home but at night it was loud.  ROOMS: there are 8 rooms in this apartment on 2 floors, and some rooms have 2 people to each room. There are 4 bathrooms.  OVERALL: I would never stay here again given all of the above. I met two great people while living here but overall I felt that I paid far too much, even in nyc, given how dirty, disorganized, unsafe, and loud it was.

A very enjoyable place to stay. R. J. provided complete and thorough instructions prior to check-in that made everything easy and stress-free, and was responsive and communicative throughout the stay. The apartment was clean and comfortable, and suited our needs very well. This apartment is also in a great neighborhood with lots to do in the area. I wish I'd had more time to explore during my stay!

Upsides: Great location close to the G and lots of bars and restaurants. RJ was  communicative. Decent price.  Downsides: Lots of little things just a tiny bit off. Handles loose, hooks that fall out of walls, wobbly beds, etc. Nothing that is unmanageable or dangerous. Just tiny little things that aren’t quite right.   If you are coming to NYC and just need a crash pad to sleep in, this’ll work great. If you’re planning to hang out at the Airbnb for a lot of your trip, I’d recommend looking somewhere else.

DON'T stay there, it's a scam Neither Airbnb nor the host wanted to respond to me, she wanted to give me my money back, the house had broken windows, everything was rusty in an ugly neighborhood and even the floor was untidy and unsafe. She never wanted to respond to me for my money and she has already done it more than once because you can see it in the comments and you already know the process. on the outside because it's horrible!

Nour’s place was perfect for our 3 day stay in Harlem. Centrally located, it was the most low-key, no stress place we’ve ever stayed in NYC. For a quick place to lay your head and baggage, it was private and efficient. We used to live in the neighborhood so we had no problem with the area. The bedroom was warm with a street view and the bathroom was nice and clean. We appreciated the vibe of the apartment and will return

This is a really fun place to stay in for a group of friends coming into celebrate an occasion, as Louis has all these fun little things to help get the party starter - karaoke mic, disco ball, etc. I wouldn’t recommend this space for kids or older adults. There was a bad cigarette smell all throughout  the apartment but we weren’t there long (just one night) so it was sufficient.   All of your guests just check in by showing security your ID. It’s not really security but more so a guy with a laptop in a hallway. It seems a little sketchy in my opinion but the security was super friendly and helpful when I had questions. It’s also nice knowing they’re there 24 hours, given the neighborhood. If you’re planning to have people stop by, you must add them to your reservation and pay an additional fee - even if it’s just for a few hours. That part really frustrated me but there is no way around it really.

The subway station is about 7 minutes away, you get to everything quickly. In terms of safety, at no time did I feel any danger. The place is quite far from tourist sites, but using the subway everything is quite fast. Regarding the space: Keep in mind that the bathroom is shared, Nour has a policy of leaving shoes at the entrance, sometimes the smell of marijuana was intense, the bedroom window faces a fairly busy street and you can hear a lot of noise throughout the day.

Although communication was good with the host, in our case we would not repeat the stay. The room was clean and had positive points like television. However, it was extremely noisy.   We accept and respect the rules such as eating only in common spaces, but it was quite unpleasant to dine constantly smelling of marijuana. However, it is legal there and the advertisement said “smoking allowed”, so we understood that it was not a reason to say anything.  The neighborhood precisely did not give us a feeling of security or hygiene.

Sophie’s apartment is lovely decorated, clean and has all the basic things you can posible need (it even has two TVs!)  I loved the big windows, even though I was not able to get the original one I had reserved, which was supposed to have really nice city views.  It is just a few blocks from Times Square and there are plenty of restaurants and grocery shops, being the Amish market the best (just make sure you bring your own bags or you can purchase them there for about a dollar.) Besides Time Square, you can easily walk to Hudson Yards and Central Park. Hell’s Kitchen, is a very busy area, and we felt safe. The block where the apartment is located at looks a little sketchy, but it’s perfectly safe. There is a doorman and he is very friendly. Also, there is a great restaurant a couple of blocks away called Mom’s Place. I highly recommend it. Sophie is great at communicating with you and fast at responding your questions. We loved staying at her place!
The check-in process and location should have been more accurate, clear, and less stressful but the place was okay.
he keeps calling and harassing me i had to call the cops guys a real creep with hidden security cameras i found and left the house and he threatening me now so i cal cops

Woodside is a lovely neighborhood. This Airbnb is more than double the price of subletting a room somewhere else. This is mainly due to cleaning fees. The pots and pans need updating and the television does not work (shuts on and off while watching every time).   The rules are wild. No men, $10 fee per night for a female guest who has to be pre-approved, and the guest isn’t allowed to shower. Because there is a cleaning person, there is no personal responsibility with cleaning the bathroom or taking out trash.   You must advocate for yourself when living here. I had a food package stolen and was reimbursed after showing photo evidence and time stamps from the delivery company. While there is a fast response time, there are lots of automated messages and middle men who have to check with the actual host to clarify things.   There is daily construction on the house next door and you can hear the subway from the bedroom. This is out of the host’s control, but should be noted when considering the high price.

The host is terrible and rude. On the first day I came, I had to wait over 40mins for her finishing up her business. I thought she might drive from somewhere else. Absolutely not, she told me that I need to give her 1hr to be here. In reality, she arrived in 10mins and she just lives in a few blocks nearby the house she listed on airbnb. Secondly, the house  that listed on airbnb is an old and on sale house, which is uninhabitable. I walked with her in a few blocks to get into her new house. Also, the room she listed was not the same one I've been stayed. That room was piled with her garbage and I've been slept on the airbed during my stay. Thirdly, nothing was provided upon arrival. I have to use my own pants to cover my lower body. I asked for shampoo and body wash on the same day and those stuff was hidden by her on the second day. Also, no paper tissue was provided. She gave me a few pieces of tissue on the first day while I requested. On the second day, she posted a some ridiculous bathroom rules on the door because her previous guest messed it up. For example, no shoes in the bathroom and don't lock the door while in use and such such.... Fourthly, after her previous guest left, she cleaned up the guest's room during the midnight, which was totally intolerable. She was making a lot of noise after her cleanup, such as watching videos, playing music, and talking on the phone out loud. I couldn't fall asleep. Also, she was like an inspector who was constantly checking everything after I finished using them. There was no room lock and she tried to get in your room without your permission.  Lastly and most importantly, on the first day I came, the AC kept leaking dirty yellow water all the way soaking the rug that is underneath the airbed. I told her to fix it and she ignored what I've said. On the leaving day, she framed and blamed me for urinating the rug, which was totally unacceptable and ridiculous! She now tried to scam me for over 500 bucks for damaged rug because of her broken AC. As you can see from the pics I provided, her broken AC was covered with black plastic garbage bag to prevent leaking. On the leaving day, she tried to fight with me and threw my staff away while I was packing myself. The most worst ever staying experience since Ive been used airbnb.   This terrible place: Stay at your own risk!

Steven is a wonderful host, always quick to respond to any needs you may have, very friendly and communicative.  What you see in the photos is what you will find.  However, I did make several suggestions to him that I hope will help him make the place more cozy and great for guests.  On our first day we found small cockroaches in the kitchen and bathroom which was very unpleasant, Steven said that he has been working hard to completely eliminate them and offered to send an exterminator which I thought was very responsible of him.  We did not accept the exterminator because we would only be there for 3 days and we are asthmatic, so we did not want to have problems with the chemicals and possibly more would open up walking everywhere trying to escape the pesticides.  He reimbursed us the cleaning fees, which was not enough to make up for the problem but it was acceptable.  I also recommended him that wash the sheets and towels with some detergent with a scent that wasn't as strong, because they didn't smell good.  Some Pros was that it was close to several train lines and if you are looking to spend a few days to visit the city, it is a good place.  But nothing more.

it was awful, a lot of cockroaches that were running around on the bedroom ceiling.  Can't sleep, noisy neighbors.  Terrible area, where it is dangerous and a lot of rats.  BUT THE MOST TERRIBLE THIS IS THE COCKROACHES.  I have a video of them crawling.  They were in every room.  They crawled across the bed. We moved out early because we were afraid to stay with the COCKROACHES. Don’t rent an apartment, don’t spoil your mood!!!!

Pros:  • The room is aesthetically pleasing in a great location.  • 5m walk to the Q train, laundry mat, and corner stores.   • The room comes with Air conditioning (that you can control), heating (that the building management controls), and Wifi (has its issues but otherwise good service).   • good cabinet space In the kitchen.   • the shower water stays hot for a long duration.  • lots of sunlight ! But you have black out curtains in case that’s not your preference (which works amazingly)   Cons:  • The room does not have a lock on it (I personally had a camera in my room) • Communication with the landlord wasn’t satisfactory (for me in my experience) as he did not inquire about issues I had regarding a particular roommate. And did not address any issues that I had but he was sure to approach me on issues she had (without her communicating with me first).  • desk was wobbly (which Eugene did offer to replace but it was stable enough)  • building maintenance has a long response time (we went two weeks with an unlocked door due to issues with the lock) which I find particularly unsafe considering we are 4 ladies living alone, we had the elevator out of service for 4+ weeks, and the laundry room has been out of service since I moved in in May/June.

The check in and cleanliness was good. The only two issues i had was the extremely loud train  passing every 10 minutes. The bathroom situation, having to lock and unlock ab additional door to get to it. A lady that lives at the other side of the apartment, told me not to walk around in a towel because of her husband....I had on shorts and was covered with a towel because I went to shower.  I had no idea she even lived there. How it that appropriate to tell a guest.? She also threw out my food and accused me of stealing her lighter...

It's fine if you're on a budget, the ac worked for us, but I strongly recommend not arriving at night, it can be dangerous specially if you're arriving via subway. It can be dangerous. Overall is fine.

Overall, what you see is what you get here. The rooms are small, but enough if you spend most of your time outside. Common spaces were rarely used during my stay. There is a revolving door of tenants, but most of the tenants I interacted with were friendly.  My main concern was that during my check in, my sheets were dirty and the room amenities described in the listing weren't accurate. I couldn't reach the host or the company that this listing is through (Outpost Club) after numerous calls. Subsequently, I contacted Airbnb's customer support and discussed moving to another location. I was given fresh sheets and a new, larger room the next day.   Given the stress of dealing with the host, I will not stay here again. That being said, if you're looking for an affordable place to stay in NY, then this fits the bill.

We are a family of 5 (3 boys under 15). At first I was a bit concerned about the fact that the house is so beautiful, and so many of the fixtures are elaborate, precious and (I suspect) irreplaceable that I thought we’d kind of be walking on eggshells; worrying constantly about our kids breaking something! Eduardo made us feel so at home. Nothing was too much for him. He constantly helped us during our stay but we didn’t really know he was there. There are some amazing restaurants in the neighbourhood and the 4 different 125th Street subway stations meant all of Manhattan and the Boroughs were easily accessible. The locals were kind and friendly - especially the lovely lady who ran the local shop a couple of doors down. Overall we had a memorable stay in Harlem, and I’d very highly recommend the People’s Brownstone!

Honestly this place is not worth it it’s located right next to the Salvation Army there are some shady people that live around the area also the room was really dirty when I went there the floors were really dirty a week into my stay I noticed that there are rats in the house there was rat Doodoo all over my things on the kitchen countertop I wouldn’t recommend this place to anybody but if you want to you can give it a try

On the plus side Location in Hell's Kitchen not far to public trans and restaurants on 9th Ave but I had a challenging stay. I was told by DM all apts on 1st floor but it was 4th.  No A/C unit - had to get installed the day after arrival, internet sketchy even after 4 'adjustments' and TV not working (no guide).  AirBnb tried to contact owner via their call center but after 6 hours (no response) it was too late to get me a hotel for the 1st nite (with AC).   A lot of basics missing - closet but no hangers, a single knife and spoon and 2 forks (but 6 serving utensils and 2 can openers!), nothing to clean or sweep with (Per Previous reviews) and some cleanliness opportunities (grout mold, dust).  I was there for 5 weeks so this was tough but maybe fine for lots of people!  I have shared this all with owner in hopes that they will address some of these things but given some of these are repeats, I'm not sure.

I stayed here for 3 months over the summer. The place has housekeeping both periodically and when guests leave so it stays clean. The bedroom was usually quiet unless guests were in the adjacent kitchen. There are lots of eateries on 30th street, grocery options nearby, and a laundromat just around the corner. I usually see young families out and about on the streets in the morning and did not notice anything unsafe about the area. Although it is rather far from the N and W line, the Q18 bus to the station is only a block away. Will definitely consider staying here again!

When we first arrived, the place was a mess. Dust and debris everywhere. There were bugs within the crevices and the bathtub had mold and rust that anyone could tell was not properly cleaned. Specifically in the bathroom, there was also a cockroach within the bathtub, and hair all over the floor that made the place even more frustrating and unhygienic. The toilet paper holder was also broken off, and the sink faucet was broken and would not regularly give hot water. The kitchen had leftover food particles everywhere and the floor had not been swept; when walking through the place, the dirt and debris would stick to our feet. All in all, it seemed as though no one had cleaned the place after the previous tenants.   After seeing this, we contacted Airbnb for a refund because we were greatly frustrated, but they told us that they could not relocate us nor give us our money back as the property owner refused to compensate.  As we were tired from our trip, we decided to unfold and lay down on the futon because while the futon was folded, the seats had 0 support and were super uncomfortable. After I unfolded it and laid on it, I quickly toppled over onto the unclean floor due to the futon not being able to balance with weight on either side (half the futon lifted into the air leaving me on the floor). Not to mention, when laying in the center of the futon, I clearly felt a rod going up and down my back forcing me to pick a side of the futon; the quality of the furniture was very sub-par. With that, the mattress in the larger room was very squeaky and unsupportive. Any minor movement throughout the night would wake us up due to how loud the mattress was.   On our second night, we arrived at our Airbnb around midnight, to a homeless man sleeping in the entrance of our building. We called the contact phone number given to us on the Airbnb app, a woman answered and told us to give her 10 minutes to reach back to us. Around half an hour later, she sent us a text message saying that she was unable to reach the property manager to handle the situation, and that we should call 911. Keep in mind, we were standing outside of the property in freezing temperatures in the middle of the night trying to get inside the building, and we had work the next day. We proceeded to call 911, who took another half an hour to arrive, and handle the situation before we were able to enter the building.   After experiencing this, we again contacted Airbnb because at this point we did not feel safe, secure, or that the property manager cared about our wellbeing at all, but Airbnb was not able to help with the matter because the property owner refused to compensate.  Throughout all of this, we still decided to stay another night and were bitten up by bed bugs in one of the rooms. There were blood stains underneath the mattress and both hands/arms were bitten up and had swelled into huge bumps. On top of that, my roommate attempted to sleep on the Futon one night and woke up with pink eye the next day, further proving how unhygienic this property is. After this, we decided to leave the place as it was not clean, felt unsafe, and was poisoned by these types of bugs. Airbnb did not provide any relocation benefits, basically no compensation (nothing compared to what we paid) and even mentioned that if we canceled the reservation, we would not get any money back. As a result, we were forced to pay for a place that we were not even staying at and on top of that, had to pay for a hotel for the rest of our 30-night stay.

I stayed at this property for about 2 months and it was a great experience. I had my doubts of moving to NY and stayed here while apartment hunting. Leana and John were the best host possible and made me feel right at home. They definitely made my move less stressful. This is a rare find and very inexpensive for the quality of stay.

No wifi & hot water goes fast no personal space they have cameras and watch every move and will contact you about it. I couldn’t enjoy my stay was being watched felt like I lived with my mom again they literally came down to close the outside shade door because we left open watch everything contacted me cause someone came to the Airbnb and wasn’t on reservation mind you person wasn’t even staying they came to see a family member. Host contacted me right away to charge for extra person. DO NOT RECOMMEND

Good hip/trendy minimalist hotel in a convenient but somewhat unsafe location on Bowery (close to Chinatown and East Village). Rooms are small but intelligently laid out so very comfortable despite small size. All room functions (lights, blinds, tv, etc.) are controlled via an iPad that works 90% of the time and is sometimes buggy. May be pro or con depending on your preference.

This was a perfect hotel for my partner and I. The room is small but there was sufficient space to unpack and lots of shelves to store items. Loved having the cafe and bar downstairs where we could meet family. The only downside is the hotel is close to the Mission and there are a lot of people experiencing homelessness on the Bowery. Next time I wouldn’t pay to upgrade for the view - a family member didn’t upgrade and had the same room.

From the first moment the communication with April was great, the place is very clean, beautiful and well prepared. It is for four people, we were 5 adults and it was a little small, as a suggestion I would add pots. April left kitchen, cleaning and personal care items. It is very important that the place has a washmachine, since there is no laundry nearby in the area. One night we had problems with the washing machine and within minutes a technician had already been sent to repair it!! The location has its pros and cons, you are 2 blocks from the subway, buses, and all the businesses you may need... but the location seems dangerous to me if you are not in a group, at any time, especially in the morning when there are still those who were partying during the night. The apartment is silent, sometimes you could hear the footsteps from above, but nothing more. It helped us a lot. From there we walked to four of the five boroughs of NYC. Thanks April and Armine

Stayed at the Bowery location. First the bad. There is no complimentary parking as advertised in their listing. Host is unresponsive. I contacted host 3 times through Airbnb and never received a reply. Finally was able to reach someone by phone who confirmed no parking. They blamed Airbnb. The good. Our stay was good and as expected based on the reviews. Expect a lot of homeless in the front area. Room was very small but functional as expected. We paid extra for a panoramic view and it was great. Also paid extra for the very good and complete breakfast, which includes espresso drinks. Good location and a short walk to Little Italy’s Mulberry street.

Ok so where should I even really start. The wifi is horrendous. You’re better off using your cellular data. The room is tiny barley 2 people can fit in it. Staff is very unresponsive with their timing. Staff does a poor job communicating with one another when you extend stay. The room is either too hot or too cold there is no in between. It says queen bed but its more like a full size bed. They charge a cleaning fee of $35 which you shouldn’t even waste your money on. They accused me of smoking when I don’t even smoke thats one. Their whole lobby up to the second floor smells like someone was smoking. Their guest also smoke in front of the property. The walls were chipping as well. We also heard people going to poundtown for about 3 days straight. Several of their guest tried to sell me & my partner drugs. Also police and ambulance were called to the property which kept us up for 3 hours at night. I do not recommend staying here. Oh and on my last night I saw roaches even though I bought my own cleaning supplies to keep the room clean and still was bugs. You’re better off sleeping in an Mta cart than staying at this hotel.

My husband and I stayed 3 nights and LOVED the location and everything went very smoothly checking in too!  The host/hostess is very friendly and wants you to be happy taking good care of us.  This location has everything you will need for a fantastic stay—great coffee places, restaurants, drug stores, wine and beer stores, and easy access to all the great things to do in NYC!    What surprised us is such a great location and potential but the space needs some attention.  Older lights and electric, extension cords run across the ceiling, some electric/lights working some not, holes in walls, attempts at “repairing” the doors, holes and damages with none of it repainted, cracked tiles, missing vents, etc.  Some you can see in the photo’s.  It’s an old building and we didn’t expect perfect but definitely could use more attention “repairing”.  A couple days of electric work by an electrician, a week or two of repairing holes, doors and a few gallons of paint and the space would upgrade dramatically!  However, if your plan is to be out and about and see the city and all it has to offer we would recommend this location.
Good location and good security -- stayed alone and never felt unsafe, plus there was a safe. Nice amenities, no complaints.

Fabulous location, extremely spacious, quiet, complete privacy! A gem in the city.   Ask Kar about the status of the hot/cold water. For us, having to wait for hot water (to wash hands and take a shower etc.) and then having it turn scalding (out of the blue) caused us stress. If this issue gets remedied, the townhouse would be a true dream!
Great place, it's clean and it was recently renewed. On the other hand, the neiborhood seems a dangerous

This place is fantastic for an affordable vacay spot. My boyfriend and I traveled from California to NYC for 8 days and wanted something simple, clean, affordable and the Chelsea Inn was everything we needed and more!  Location is prime - tucked away in the West Village. The streets aren’t insanely packed at all times, there are great restaurants just a small walk away and if you want to head to Soho, Brooklyn, Uptown, Etc., they’re all less than a 15 min subway ride away.  The room is small - but if you’re just looking for a nice, clean space to rest and sleep in between your busy days, this place is perfect.   Had a fridge, closet space, microwave, a small desk, a TV and the wifi worked perfectly!  We were a little afraid about some of the reviews saying the AC didn’t work - but we had our tan blasting at all times and felt very comfortable in the insane heat and humidity we experienced.   Thank you Chelsea Inn! :-)

Our stay at Luster’s was awesome. We had a very stressful journey before our checkin but Luster was very flexible and understanding and was willing to accommodate us. He was very pleasant our whole stay and when we needed him he was very quick and responsive . The room was cozy and comfortable and the place was very clean . Don’t hesitate to book Luster’s place !

Nahuel is very responsive and a great host.   Check-in instructions were very clear! The room looks just as described and contains things as provided in the listing. The bed is a bit noisy and felt a bit unsafe walking around the neighborhood at night during the 10 minute walk to the closest subway station,  but it was a good price for a weekend. I would recommend if you are looking for a fair place for a good price.
This place is a scam. Save your money and book somewhere else.

Had a very nice stay. The hotel is new, modern & clean. The location is also very good. The check in and check out process was extremely quick & well done. The staff is very polite - provided free tooth paste, tooth brush & razors upon request. The room has an iron board and iron. As others have stated, the room is a little small but if you will be out all day and just need a nice place to crash, this is perfect. The room has a balcony with a beautiful view but unfortunately these days it’s closed due to construction. The only issue was that there was a weird smell in the room. Nothing unbearable but a little unpleasant. Justin is a lovely host. Was very quick in communication and even allowed me a complimentary late check out. Would recommend to others
Had to submit credit card info and ID through a third party service, but besides that, everything else worked out. Haven’t had my info stolen yet so knock on wood

Stanley’s is a solid good accommodation with all the basic amenities you need for a long stay. The place is in a good location by all transport. It was clean, had a good kitchen with basic cooking supplies and an on site laundry. It has an old NY charm and the place is well run and I felt safe. I particularly appreciate that in time of covid, the hand sanitizer was always filled by the elevator and the one person per elevator was respected by everyone in the building. All in all a very pleasant and stress free stay. I recommend.

good value for location, near train and grocery store. definitely sketchy at nighttime. No TV on arrival; tried to confirm that there was no TV, as place was left unlocked upon entry, but no response given.

Apartment was very clean except for the sink in the kitchen and burnt-in residue on the stove. Unfortunately the dishwasher was loose and fell on us. We then preferred to wash by hand.  The bathroom has been beautifully renovated and the bed and other furniture are perfect.   From the surrounding area, just 3 stops from the 135 St subway. Everything important is about 20-35 minutes away by subway and can be reached. Quarter itself is rather run down. Some homeless people... But there are plenty of supermarkets right around the corner.   From Newark with taxi and Uber about 95-110 dollars.  Overall we were satisfied and I think the price is normal to good for New York.   Thanks for the stay!

good apartment; I especially appreciated that the host has the kitchen stocked with s few foodstuffs, as my work schedule was such that it would have been unpleasant for me to go out and buy groceries after such a long day. Recommended

Amazing!!!! Loved everything. The PERFECT stay. Loved it so much. I would recommend this. The outside looked iffy to me but the inside is beautiful and clean and very modern. Netflix and bluetooth on the tv. Amazing city view with view of water. Beautiful! I would stay here a million times over. The price is a steal.

Everything was as expected, slight issues with the plumbing towards the end of our stay. Didn’t make a big deal of it bcuz we were leaving the next day. A smell coming from the bathroom made it unpleasant when we walked in. Other than that everything was just like the posting listed. Would definitely stay again, just would prefer a different floor or something.

The main criteria for the place to be rented by us was the geographic location to price ratio. We wanted to stay in a close proximity ( walking distance) to WTC and Wall Street . We also did not want to pay all money of the world for that. The place met our expectations with both.  The view from the window we had was not the best , but we could see the beams going up into NY sky commemorating the 29 th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. We were accompanied by two 11 year olds who were absolutely blown away by the view, and “ a cool place to stay”.  Thank you for your hospitality. We definitely recommend the place for other travelers.

This place was really cozy with excellent hosts. The only downfall of this place would be the location (borders an area with a lot of crime from my understanding) and the parking is scarce and driveway is steep my suv even bottomed out getting into it. Pros outweigh the cons in this place the hosts thought of everything for a great stay and we’re very accommodating. Very nicely remodeled older home.

After a two night stay at Paula and Andre's, honestly we can't  rave enough - they have outdone themselves. From great communication at the start, then a very thoughtful welcome gift upon arrival, add that to graciously allowing a special request - our only disappointment was that we had to leave so soon.  Their pictures are spot on and actually the house was bigger than we expected. If you appreciate homes with tons of character and charm,  along with every amenity and detail met for travellers - look no further.  Comfort and a stress free stay is top priority for their guests. My wife and I also agreed that this was the cleanest Airb&b that we have ever stayed, which was an immediate sense of relief upon arrival.  Overall, we can't wait to come back and stay again.  If there was a 10 star out of 5 (for exceeding all expectations), that's the rating we feel Paula and Andre  deserve!

I book this place at last minuet for my trip to Manhattan, secretly worried I would get no response.  However, the host get back to me immediately. It was a wonderful experience to stay at this place. Well furnished apartment with lovely decorations, the location is blocks away from Washington Square Park without crazy noise at night; more importantly, the place is really clean and provide excellent service. Sanitation has been my major concerns during this pandemic, but living here makes me stress-free. When searched on Airbnb, I did find some places with cheaper price, but I am really glad I chose this one. The amazing experience make my trip much better, and definitely worth the money!

It's an okay option last minute, but they skimp on refilling soaps if you stay less than two days.  The host was gracious enough to give them to me when I asked for them but it was a little disgusting to have to deal with pre used soaps and shampoos when I arrived. it was also suspect whether or not the bedsheets and towels were being replaced. I found the sheets itchy and the towels had an odd smell and texture to them. The floor itself had not been cleaned as my socks soaked up the dirt pretty quickly. Finally, you're charged an additional 1/4 of your total in taxes after you book. it lists this charge on the listing but it's not made clear until after you book. This can trick you into thinking this listing is cheaper than similarly priced alternatives unless you're really paying attention.

I booked and they accepted the reservation and when I came to check-inI was NEVER able to get in contact with the host to arrange check-in. I had to sleep in my car with my younger sister because they never responded and I had to call Airbnb 5 times to get a refund but by then it was already past 10pm and I couldn’t book anything that short notice. Unless you want to experience momentary homelessness, I would NOT recommend this place at all.
Super easy check-in and the front desk staff were friendly and professional. Our bathroom had an unpleasant smell, but other than that the place was clean and well-kept.

Gary is very friendly and was attentive to what we needed, the accommodation is close to the subway but it is quite far from Manhattan, it is nice that you have the services such as a bathroom and kitchen near your room, which is quite spacious and bright, I think one of the best things is the projector, it is fantastic to have it in the room, the things that need to be improved, basic elements are missing such as clothes hangers in the closet and unfortunately we had a very unpleasant experience with a mouse that got into the room one of the nights, we understand that it could have been a fortuitous and specific situation and that New York in general has serious problems with rats, but since we are from a city where we are not familiar with this type of pests, it caused us quite a bit of displeasure and I think that the host did not give the necessary importance to the matter.

Gary is a great host, everything is available and he is very responsive! However, the cleanliness leaves something to be desired, there is dust and one of the towels we had available was dirty, we had to clean the room when we arrived because I can't tell you the state of my white socks, and the edge of the shower as well as the sink were dusty and looked sticky. There is everything you need in the kitchen (food and utensils) it just lacks a pan and maintenance. Otherwise the place is not ideal, it is a little far (1 hour from New York by metro) but the metro entrance is not far away, it is very close to JFK and it is easy to get there. On the other hand, being a woman, I didn't stay late at night because the neighborhood was a little scary. Otherwise I had a good stay and felt safe, there is Netflix and Disney, as well as a fridge and microwave in the room.

If you want to get away from the stress from your neighborhood, this is the place..   The place is always clean, the people are always respectful. The check in is quick.   The beds are comfortable…..    the area is quiet.      Come and relax…..

Contact with Jovanna was always friendly and quick. The location of the apartment is good. The way to the ferry, which runs free of charge to New York every 20 minutes, is short but tiring. We were a little dissatisfied with the cleanliness. The bathroom (mold) and the carpet of course do not meet European standards and were too dingy for our taste. What you also have to take into account is the way houses are built in America. It's incredibly noisy, you can hear every word from the upstairs apartment (which is occupied by the landlords). The children are really loud and one or two arguments kept us awake in the evenings. That was uncomfortable because, as I said, you understood every word. If you are a deep sleeper and are only there to sleep, the apartment is ok. It's also nice to take the ferry back to Staten Island every evening and come back in the morning. We were generally satisfied, but I wouldn't do it again for a long stay because we didn't feel comfortable and didn't sleep well.

We stayed at Marc's place for a month and it wildly exceeded our expectations! The place was clean and tidy and Marc had left us plenty of room to unpack our things.  Marc was so kind and accomodating to all our questions and requests.    The apartment was bright and had plenty of sunlight throughout the day along with the breathtaking corner view of midtown and the hudson river.  The Hells Kitchen neighborhood has ton of food options and even a new local Target down the street. The food delivery apps deliver from all across Manhattan so the options were endless.  The residents and doormen at the building were extremely mindful and courteous when it came to wearing masks and asking if about sharing elevators. I never felt unsafe or uncomfortable while in the building.  We worked remotely at the apartment and there was plenty of space utilizing the bedroom desk and living room table for work; we never had any issues with internet speeds.  Noise was not really an issue, only when the lincoln tunnel was backed up did things get out of hand with honking but that was only on two or three days.    For those with a car, there is a connected garage in the building which made it super convenient - the parking attendants were always on top of things and kind.  We would not hesistant to come back to the place - Marc was an outstanding host!

I'll keep it short. The apartment is good. It's very clean, thoughtfully decorated, and has everything you need for a short stay in NYC. It's small,  but exactly what you would expect for Brooklyn (with typical noise from neighbors, noise from window unit, trains next door). We had no problems with anything in the apartment. The only real negative was the location. When we arrived, there were a good number of homeless folks loitering and calling to us (there's some kind of medical clinic halfway down the block, a liquor store at the other end, and a subway station immediately next door). We didn't feel comfortable walking around the neighborhood or to any nearby attractions for this reason. But if you go a few blocks toward Prospect Heights or Park Slope you'll be perfectly safe.

The location was awesome, right in the heart of everything I wanted. Pretty upset my room smelled like cigarettes the whole 4 days I was there, that was very unpleasant. I even went back home smelling like cigarettes myself
Exceeded expectations. Neat. Modern  Quiet neighborhood. Nothing sketchy going on
A great place to rest, quiet, confortable bed everything very clean, a few steps from the subway 20 minutes from Times Square. Neighborhood a little scary but safe.

Very cozy bedroom and relaxing bed; though, I was given bath towels but didn’t have a bed sheet, just comforter. Great if you’re just staying for a weekend and need a place to crash. ( can’t use the full kitchen ) It’s also great if you are comfortable with using the Subway / Uber or buses since the neighborhood is a bit sketchy to walk out at night. The AC helped for the warm Summer nights and their dog is just the cutest thing.   There was a party on the block and it was really tough to sleep but they had tons of individual ear plugs in the nightstand drawer to use.

Overall good experience! I will warn you, at first it can seem pretty sketchy if you are not used to new york living. You enter into the apartment through a small glass door in between a gift shop and a bank. However we did feel safe, just not what we were used to.   Perfect location! Good value!

Homeless people sleeping in the area. Very dirty building, construction all around, felt like a prison, smelled really bad in hallways. The room was clean but sooooo small, just literally three beds in the room, no place for suitcases or shopping bags. We were there for a girls trip and on the third day a guy that worked for Nomad knocked on our door while we were there and wanted to get something that was left under a bed. We were all on our beds (because that’s the only place to go) and he walked in, moved the bed, and took an old bed frame under the bed. So weird, so rude! I will find a real hotel next time.

The first day I arrived I called to let him know I was outside. I was greeted by a man shouting “no marijuana” multiple times as he brought me upstairs to the unit. He made sure to show me every no smoking sign before handing me the keys. He called about twice a day and became upset when I no longer answered his phone calls. Durning the stay we experienced brown water coming out of the faucet and a broken bed frame. Unfortunately this was a very unpleasant experience.

This space was far from what I expected! The room itself was set up nice and neat. However, the floors were unclean and we encountered several roaches in the Kitchen and Bathroom area. The toilet had issues and would clog sometimes which was a hassle. When it came to the building, if I had 2 sets of hands I’d give it 4 thumbs down. The building reeked of cigarette, as someone was smoking in the lobby when we checked in. To top it all off it was VERY loud at night. The people who stay there have no care for others. It is unacceptable that we were woken out of our sleep because of incompetent people fighting and screaming in the hallway. This experience was very unpleasant and it’s unfortunate that I probably won’t be able to be compensated. Wouldn’t recommend to ANYONE!

I needed a place for my relatives to stay while visiting New York for the first time. This was a great location for them and a comfortable place to not stress about where to go or what to do. Their host was great. I recommend.
Top holidays with this hotel located a stone's throw from the brilliant time scare
SCAM. THIS IS NOT AN AIRBNB IT IS A HOTEL. THE HOST IS ADDING AN EXTRA 40$ PER NIGHT IN EXTRA FEES. SAVE YOUR MONEY.

The staff was amazingly helpful. The breakfast was poor quality food. A lot of sugar and prefab food. Luckily there was an apple too. The food was so much we tried to give unopened food back, but the hotel did not accept. We distributed it to homeless people. We would wish there was a hotel policy on healthy food and combatting food waste.
Please don’t get scam

My room didn’t have the best view but that’s ok. What bothered me was that the curtains didn’t fully close because they were broken so I was scared that the people in the building in front of me would see me. On the day of the checkout the cleaning lady came knocking on my door at 8:30am to let me know I had to checkout at 11:00am (it said 12 on the app but I still don’t know why she’s knock at 8:30am when I’m still asleep. Other then that, the staff were so friendly and it was a good area. I would stay here again👍🏼

Can’t stress this enough… steps away from Times Square, a block from the Bryant Park and ice skating, Whole Foods, you will not be disappointed. A deli across the street has the best sandwiches in town. Definitely booking again!

The place was great and spacious. Three bedrooms with A/C in each room. The kitchen was quite complete as well if you decide to make food before heading out. Location-wise it's close to transportation, restaurants, and groceries. The area never felt unsafe at any point. Would definitely stay here again!

Suzan was attentive to all my needs and has a lovely disposition. She took care of everything and I felt very safe. The premises are extremely clean and the bedding was very clean and fresh. It’s located less than a 10 minute drive from the airport and making my flight was easy and stress free. The neighborhood is very safe. I will be returning.

Alisha, thank you for your outstanding hospitality! Thank you for opening up your Home. It was definitely a home away from home.  You superseded my expectations!! This has been my best air b n b experience thus far!! I will definitely book again!  Upon arrival, I was able to find parking immediately. Alisha came outside to greet me. I followed her into the second floor of her home which did have it’s own separate entrance. I appreciated the privacy.   Upon entering, I was blown away.  - Beautiful, clean hardwood floors.  - 3 Simply decorated, clean and neat bedrooms with lots of natural lighting. Each bedroom had comfy beds ( I tried each one, haha) as well as comfy pillows and sufficient blankets/quilt. She also provided each room with multiple towels.  - A beautiful and great size living space and full kitchen with complete amenities.  - Alisha was kind enough to leave a welcome note with suggestions for dining and sights to see, along with snacks :) Thank you for this!  - There was a full bathroom, clean and fully stocked.  - The location was super convenient and only a 28 min drive from the city. This made my commuting back and forth stress free!  - Communication with Alisha is phenomenal. She provided swift responses and beat me to any questions I had. She was so, so sweet, thoughtful and very helpful.    Alisha, thank you again for your hospitality!

Alicia was incredably kind and responsive  every step of the way. The place was impeccably clean.  This was for 4 guys going to the PGA at Bethpage. Was convenient and good value for us.  Can’t speak for how convenient it would be to go into Manhattan. But the Long Island Roalroad  passes only a couple blocks away.  We walked to three  restaurants. Never felt unsafe.  Would certainly stay here again.  Thank you Alicia
Not bad. The area is a little sketchy and not very clean however, most reviews were positive so maybe had a one off situation! Decent space and newly renovated

I was greeted by husband Yossi and blossoming wife Marina with a bundle of joy on the way. She kindly gave me a tour upon my request. Enter a freshly renovated nook in a two-story townhouse. The use of real estate exceeded my expectations as it is essentially one big room that cleverly couples a bedroom, kitchenette, dining room, and workspace all in one! The cozy kitchenette is equipped with refrigerator, conventional toaster oven, hotplate, coffeemaker, and sink. Two laptop friendly areas include a humble dining table w/tall modern stools for two as well as a work desk and comfy chair. The bedroom neatly ties up the space with two nightstands and a closet to house your luggage unleashed.  The charming first floor level apartment is nestled in quiet family-friendly Kew Gardens Hills neighborhood. Linger long enough and you’ll find there is a lot more residential ethnicity than you would suspect just looking at the commercial stuff. The neighborhood has not only Chinese, Korean, Afghan and Latino citizens, but also diversity within the Jewish community, including a growing number of Bukharian Jews, from Central Asia. The location is generally close to just about everything you might need and offers a generous invitation to discover the variety of nearby kosher restaurants along Main Street.  Things I loved about this space was the level of thoughtfulness in hosting. The last guest happened to leave behind a MetroCard which Marina gladly shared. The freezer keeps an ice tray with rubber bottoms so you can pop the ice cubes out - clever. There's an HDMI cable available so you could connect your laptop to the mounted large screen TV if you’d like. Travel size Pantene shampoo and conditioner for your exclusive use await you in the shower along with fresh towels readily available overhead. You’ll find earplugs if you’re a light sleeper. If you need to expand your breathing room, there’s backyard access. Free parking is always a plus! All simple items but brilliant to making a guest feel right at home.  My only quirk about the space is that it isn’t immediately near the subway. This might actually be the blessing in disguise that contributes to the small town feel of the area. And likely the reason why you can see the sun instead of high-rises and indulge trees and flowers instead of the noise of Manhattan.  Marina was pleasant, accommodating and helpful. Our communication was always conveniently prompt. I rarely needed to ask her for anything because she covered all her bases! She and her husband even provide an informative binder complete with direct contact #s, house rules, transportation, locations of grocery stores, restaurants, pharmacies, banks, you name it! With service like this, it’s no wonder more and more people are checking out of hotels and into Airbnbs.  Helpful local tips, amazing amenities, thoughtful touches, outstanding hospitality, quick friendly responses, and stylish x sparking clean space - the recipe for the perfect staycay. I would recommend Marina any day.

I actually booked this place for my friend and he said that it was very nice and clean. He was expecting it to be much smaller therefore he was happy with the outcome and sizing of the listing. Not going to lie I was scared the the owner would be mad that I rented this place for a friend and not me but she was very understanding and I couldn’t be more grateful. Thank you marina for letting my friend stay in your home, would most definitely book again!

Good part: lived on the 2nd floor of a Victorian house. High ceilings, moldings and beautiful floors. Small but very complete kitchen. Well connected to the metro 2 blocks away. Bad part: fair cleaning. Dirty skirting boards, moldings and windows. The shower was very bad, outdated and without any water pressure. The access staircase inside the house is a shame because it is beautiful and the carpet and its condition are very bad. All this has a solution. Presence of rodents (rats) in the front yard and in the garbage containers of the house (in the yard).  The neighborhood in general was dirty, perhaps unsafe.

Positive -nice room, comfy bed. Locations is quite good to get into the city. Our room was clean.   Negative -kitchen is super basic. No knife for chopping vegetables only blunt knife that you eat with.  Bathroom isn't always clean... it depends what other guests are there.  At 2am on our last evening someone came back late to get into another Airbnb room, their roommate didn't hear the person knocking... the person proceeded to spend an hour knocking very loudly which woke everybody up! A little scary as we didn't know who was outside and who was knocking.. and annoying as we all woke up and were awake for an hour until someone told her to stop disturbing everyone. Perhaps having 'quite hours' as a rule would help other guests have a pleasant stay. In some Airbnb's they say from 10pm to 8am are quite hours... that's helpful.    Inspections! While we were out one day the host said they had to go into our room so that someone doing an appraisal could take pictures or at least look inside. We weren't comfortable with this but were already out and had no choice. Nothing was taken but it was still strange... if i rent a room i expect it to be mine for that time.

Staying at Oscar’s Airbnb was an amazing experience, and we highly recommend it to anyone visiting NYC. He went the extra mile by providing free amenities (sodas and water, toiletries, maps to NYC), kept the areas very clean, and added homely and sweet touches through decoration. Oscar had key pad locks installed for both the front door and your specific suite, which we loved because it added an extra level of comfort and safety.  The bathroom is shared among the four separate suites, which worked out well because everyone had different schedules and never seemed to need to use it at the same time as someone else. The location can be interpreted as both positive and negative depending on your priorities, but it simply depends on how/where you plan to spend your trip: the Wilson Avenue subway station is VERY convenient given that it’s only a four minute walk away from the apartment. However, it is located in Bushwick, Brooklyn, so you can expect anywhere from 35 minutes to an hour of traveling by subway to get to Manhattan (shorter distance if downtown, longer distance if uptown). That was never a problem for us because we’d simply get up earlier to accommodate for the distance and we enjoyed the experience of the subway, but if you’re someone who wants a quick, transfer-less ride to Manhattan or doesn’t plan to use the subway, it might not be the best option for you on that front. It isn’t located in the hipster, stylish area of Brooklyn and that concerned us at first sight, but we never felt unsafe in the area. We felt comfortable walking home at 2 AM after a night of theatre because there were still groups of people also getting off at Wilson (it truly is the city that never sleeps). There are two nearby shops that we frequented during our stay: a One Stop Supermarket and a New Texas Fried Chicken. The former is great for any cooking or snacking needs you’ll have, and the latter is wonderful for a late night bite. We had an incredible stay, and we’re so grateful that we found Oscar’s Airbnb when we did because he’s usually completely booked. It’s in a great location, is clean and comfortable, and is at an incredible and competitive price point as well. Book Oscar’s Airbnb for your next trip to NYC!

MICE! Upon arriving, he helped me park my car and carry my bag up, which was nice. Also met his sweet daughter. The room seemed tidy enough, and although I saw a bug in the shower, I figured you get what you pay for. HOWEVER, when I arrived there my second night to stay (exhausted), my friend and I watched a mouse run from behind the dresser, to the TV stand, to under the BED! I calmly told Damien of what we had just saw (so not to upset his daughter) and he looked around the room for it. He then proceeded to tell me that it's probably gone now and won't come back out from wherever it is because "mice are afraid of humans" and that it's not that big a deal. When I expressed that my friend and I would like to leave since the mouse was not trapped or removed (but rather still hiding somewhere in the house) and that I wouldn't get any sleep knowing that, he nonchalantly said that's fine and that he would leave us to discuss. While we were discussing the matter in private, he decided to text me (ironically) and tell me that it would be an extra fee if my friend were to stay the night, but that he would consider waiving it if we stayed! At this point I had no intentions of staying the night there, let alone pay EXTRA in a room where a mouse was also residing. When I asked him what the refund policy would be for a situation like this, his response was that there was no refund because it is an "uncontrollable matter and the city has mice." I requested a partial refund via Airbnb because I didn't stay the second night and he sent me a text with my message copy and pasted and said "Really? Oh wow." This whole situation actually ruined my trip as you can imagine and I'm never booking an Airbnb ever again.

No complaints, only plaudits. Check-in, as handled by Damien's gracious and curvaceous young female assistant went well. The art-deco apartment is clean, the private bathroom is spotless, the kitchen is modern, the TV has more channels than there are stars in the heavens, so what's not to like? The detractors must be apprised of a  most felicitous recent development, the addition to the household of a courageous attack cat named Hennessey. This noble warrior stands guard over the residence and protects those who live within from all enemies foreign and domestic, two-legged, four-legged, or otherwise. In combat even Mighty Mouse could not defeat this Fantastic Feline! The sojourner who dwells in Damien's dwelling can sleep safe and secure in the knowledge that Heroic Hennessey has got his back!

I went to the Brox on a 3 day weekend for the Rockies/Yankees series. Damien has the perfect place if you are in town for a ballgame. It only took me 7 minutes to walk to the stadium from his spot. There are a few bodegas right there for anything extra you need and I had a small private bathroom which I'm big on. Damien himself is a super cool dude. He was welcoming and accommodating and even invited me to the neighborhood block party one of the nights I was there. I also felt like I got a real NY experience staying in his place. I've stayed in Manhattan before but it was way different. Walking down the street to the games there was people playing music in the windows, at night folks chilling on the steps, dancing on the sidewalks and I thought that was dope. No one bothered me or made me feel unsafe so I have no ill comments toward Damien, his place or his city.

Erica and John's Beach House experience is truly one of a kind. My girlfriend and I wish we could rate them ten stars because that is what they deserve.  I was looking for a place in the city to celebrate my girlfriend's birthday and relax away from worldly stress. Based on the reviews, I knew Erica's and John's Airbnb would be the right place, and they did not disappoint!  The Airbnb itself is VERY clean, cozy, and filled with lots of nice touches. Erica even provided bagels, snacks, and wine for us. We believe it was such a thoughtful gift. I asked Erica to decorate the room for my girlfriend's birthday, and it was perfect. The bedding choice, balloons, chocolates, rose petals, and gift bags. My girlfriend was over the moon, thanks to Erica.  The backyard is spacious, stunningly handcrafted, comes with a stocked outdoor bar, and the jacuzzi was an outstanding highlight of the weekend.  We spent hours in the jacuzzi. We even spent time in the jacuzzi with John, an incredible host who knows how to have a good time!  As if the weekend wasn't already fun, Erica wanted to give my girlfriend one more special surprise. She designed and decorated a cake table with balloons for my girlfriend. How many hosts would do that for their guests?  This weekend was magical. Staying at Erica's and John's felt like we were at home. A huge thank you to Erica and John for their hospitality and generosity and the Sunday vegetarian soup (so good)! We had a blast and cannot wait to visit again!!!!

The location was great and close to 2 convenient subway lines. The studio was adorable just like the pics and clean. The building is old and you can hear ppl outside, but that seems to be everywhere inside Manhattan. It never felt dangerous, but pretty residential.
