Thalia has super helpful notes/labels around the house that helps ease you in to living in a new place - labels like where the recycle/trash is and the location of the "communal" food space vs. your own personal space, and kind reminders to give others a heads up if you'll be in the bathroom for an extended period of time. It takes a while to get used to being in any new place, and Thalia has done a phenomenal job of helping you get into the swing of things quickly. This is particularly true in terms of living with other people sharing common spaces and being courteous of one another. Nearly all Airbnb places in NYC are private rooms in shared apartments, but Thalia goes above and beyond to make this an arrangement everyone can genuinely enjoy.   The neighborhood itself is quite safe. As a female traveling alone, that's always one of the first things I notice, but there was never a time when I felt unsafe, even when I'd come home from work or visiting friends pretty late (anytime between 11pm to 2am).  Her place is 7 minutes away from the Q/B train, which takes you into Manhattan in 30 minutes. It's also about a 10 min walk from the 2 and 5. Prospect Park is also less only 7 minutes away, perfect for runners or just anyone who loves to get away into nature for a while! There's a laundromat, pharmacy, takeout restaurants, and deli right across the street.   Without a doubt, I would absolutely love to stay at her place again. I cannot recommend her place enough. Thalia was tremendously kind and such a fun, engaging person to talk to, she's got you covered! She's wonderful at giving recommendations on where to go (especially on a budget) and generally helping you have a wonderful experience while you're here.

The Box House Hotel was amazing. The rooms are huge with high ceilings. They have modern kitchens and our bathroom had a nice size tub. The skylights had electronic curtains on them to block out light when you want to sleep in. The lobby is a great meeting place with Apple iMacs and free internet throughout the hotel. The staff was easy going and very helpful. Special thanks to Rob who went beyond the call of duty several times for us! The hotel is near Manhattan Ave in Greenpoint which has supermarkets, Polish bakeries and subways to Manhattan. The hotel also has a free car service that will take you anywhere in Williamsburg (very nice!). There is nothing like this hotel for even double the price in the area.

Hi, We had an amazing time in The Box. All the staff is wonderful, friendly and very helpful ...from the cleaning crew to the reception to the drivers. The suites are amazing, with all the facilities to feel like at home. The area is rough ( don't expect trendy Williamsburg vibe!) but we never felt unsafe and there are very convenient supermarkets and coffee shops at 10 minutes walk distance. Overall great holidays- thanks to all The Box employees!

The apartment is great as in the photos. They are super welcoming. The courtesy car to take us and pick us up from the metro line which is 4 minutes by car and 10 minutes on foot is a great plus. Great stay. We were even able to take a shower before catching our flight home. Really it's GREAT

Worst Bnb experience is not even enough to describe it. This was the worst experience of life. I stayed in Marc's apartment for two weeks and had such a great experience! The place looks exactly like the photos and it is clean and super comfortable. The area is great too- orchard st is filled with great bars and cafes, and I never felt unsafe walking home late at night. Marc also answered any questions I had almost immediately every time which was awesome. Would come back in a heart beat!

This is our second stay at Liz's apartment, and our first using only the private room.  The private room alone is a bit cramped for three people (2 adults + 4-year-old) but Liz gave us the run of the common areas and made it a comfortable, stress-free visit.  And (as I said in my first review) the apartment is beautiful, in a great neighborhood close to the subway.  We will return!

Marc was not there and not responsive, but Lataya was helpful. The flat is conveniently located. The kitchen lacks the standards if you expect a coffee maker, toaster and boiler. The bathroom, although large for a NY appartment, needs refreshing (the toilet seat does not seem to have been changed for the last 15 years). The electric plugs are hanging from the wall, almost dangerous, but we loved orchard street!

Wonderfully spacious and clean, walking distance to transportation and busy streets. RIGHT NEXT TO CENTRAL PARK. Can’t stress that enough and the patio is a wonderful space. Excellent communication and very tidy.

My elderly parents flew in from Asia to spend the end of the year with me and they had expected a cozy, warm 4 nights at Marc’s one-bedroom. But due to the issues below, we had to leave less than 20 minutes after checking in and canceled the reservation. 1. Lease violation When I called Marc to arrange check in, he told me that check in is only available after 6PM because the cleaning lady would be there. I asked when we should meet up and that we might get to his place around 10-30 minutes early and that I would call him as we walked to his place. That is when he asked how many bags we have, and he told me that he didn’t want us to be around there with our baggage carriers because the neighbors would become suspicious. He asked for a heads up before we got there, so I agreed to call him. Then, when we were 10 minutes away, we called him and he said he was on his way and would be there soon. When we arrived at the front door promptly at 6, he said he was on his way and he would be there quickly. 5 minutes later, when I called to ask where he is, he said he was actually in his place trying to clean up a bit because the cleaning lady left some things. He wouldn’t come down so we had to go up to his place and knock. That is when he finally came out. (There does not seem to be any other entrance. We went around to the back and there wasn't an entrance so we know that we was in the house before we arrived.) When we got in and he was introducing the place to us, he told us that he is not allowed to rent the place out to us unless he was there with us. He said be careful of the neighbors and please do not make too much noise. We were never notified of this arrangement and we realized that we may become liable if there was a legal problem regarding his lease with the homeowner. This was completely unexpected and the whole situation made us very uncomfortable. We were not planning on being loud, but we certainly did not expect to have to keep our Airbnb a secret from anybody. We believed we should notify Airbnb about this problem as soon as possible since Airbnb also has potential to be directly or vicariously liable. This is not an environment where airbnb travelers can comfortably enjoy their stay nor is it legitimate. 2. Sanitation issues The host told us that a cleaning lady would clean the whole place. However, when we arrived we instantly noticed the stained rug and stained sofa that was supposed to be the sofa bed. There was leftover food in the sink and the fridge was full of half-eaten or old food. The freezer had an ice...

Check this very carefully before renting. It is cluttered, and stressful to be in because of someone else's 'stuff'  It is not really a one-bedroom, but a studio with a parapet divider and no door or wall between the kitchen and bed area.  Be aware that there is no TV (see photo).  Amenities like toilet paper, and bin liners were not provided when we arrived. There was no working kettle.  The couch is very old, the cover grotty and very uncomfortable. There is no table and chairs to sit at.  Make sure that the loose and open electric plugs have been fixed.  It is a good location, but then let's face i, so are most places in NYC.  Do not expect deep cleaniless, nor any 'extras'. Marc's stuff is everywhere, and you live on top of his things (eg a fridge with his stuff pushed to one side.) Yes, NYC is expensive, but you can do better.

Very good address that we do not hesitate to recommend, given its good value for money. Certainly, the neighborhood is not exceptional, but 10 minutes walk from the Vernont-Jackson metro (after crossing the Pulaski bridge), 3 stops from Time Square. Concept between hotel and independent apartment. Impeccable 24/7 welcome, warm, always attentive. We occupied a studio for 4 people for 6 nights (unfortunately, no larger apartment available, but ultimately more than sufficient surface area), consistent in all respects with the description and photos (neat decor, all in perfect condition, very clean) We had the choice between 1 apartment overlooking the exterior (window opening onto the street and the bridge) or interior to the structure, with skylight via 3 skylights. We chose the 2nd option which had the advantage of ensuring very quiet nights. Very good sleeping arrangements: 1 large, very comfortable double bed and a 2-seater sofa bed that our 2 "children" of 1.80m and 1.85m appreciated. Possibility of washing and drying clothes (laundry room in common areas). Gym that we didn't have the time, or the courage anyway, to use. ATM on site. A plus: we were able to leave our luggage in storage on the day of our departure (flight at 11:20 p.m.), the Reception having taken care of booking a taxi for us.

I want to start off by saying this was my first experience using Airbnb. I feel as if I may have lucked out because my entire experience was flawless. I was headed to NYC to visit some friends and had the hardest time finding a place to stay. My friends live in Greenpoint and I really wanted to stay as close as possible. After tireless research I came across this listing for a gorgeous private studio loft. It was perfect.! Location, space, accommodations, and best of all communications between myself and the property was amazingly prompt. It turns out this property is more of a hotel than someone's actual abode. This made it even better.  My actual unit was very clean and well laid out. It had a small kitchenette which was very nice to have. Two large televisions and a nice outdoor patio. Beautiful high ceilings with really cool remote controlled windows which allowed you to open and close the shade as well as tilt open the window to let in fresh air. The second night I was in the room with some friends and it felt like home. I honestly couldn't imagine staying anywhere else in Brooklyn. I work for a very high end hotel in Austin Texas and have stayed in nice hotels all over the country and this is honestly one of my favorite places I've ever stayed. I highly,highly recommend this hotel to anyone who's headed to NY or Brooklyn.

Marc’s place was a GREAT value for the price and location. You honestly can’t beat it. Close to the F train, you can get anywhere in the city very easily. Tons of cool restaurants and bars within a few blocks. My favorites were 169 bar on E. Broadway and Holy Cow on Canal. There was a sushi place about a 10 minute walk that was SO good. This apartment is a 7 minute walk to a Target and Trader Joe’s, which made things SO easy.  The space itself was more cluttered than the pictures show, but the bathroom was clean and I didn’t feel unsafe or like the building was falling apart, which can definitely happen in New York. I used to live in the city so it was nice being close to friends and made it easy to catch up with people instead of staying further out in Brooklyn or Queens. Marc supplied towels, sheets, pillowcases, paper towels, toilet paper, dishes, wifi and more! Marc was also flexible with my checkout time, as my flight was in the evening. Good  experience overall!

Friendly, welcoming and very helpful staff.  Clean apartment and well equipped.  Metro was accessible and no problem to use.  The hotel provides its own free taxi service to local destinations - a great idea.  Box Street is in a part of north Brooklyn that is yet to be 'gentrified'.  While we never felt unsafe, it is not as classy as Williamsburg or DUMBO.  The hotel presents exceedingly well, including lovely gardens externally and funky interior design.  A refreshing and distinctive place to stay, unlike so many formula-driven international hotels.

We were very warmly received by Toni and the apartment corresponded in every way to the description. The neighborhood is very pleasant, well served by the subway and very relaxing after a day in Manhattan. The supermarket around the corner is really convenient. No insecurity problem. Staying in Brooklyn, in this neighborhood, allows you to discover another aspect of life in New York.

This is the one of my first and the most horrible experience in my trip. I didn’t expect any fancy stuff show up in this house but the roommate who is live in with me is super aggressive. I feel I was bullied in this time. First I wanna clarify Im not that sensitive and childish person. When I walking to my room after check in, the roommate who tell me he is Landlord’s brother just suddenly come out and tell me a lot of rules. I was like yes I will do it.  But everything was out of control. Every time when I walk out my room he will come out at the same time, and he is omnipresent and will order me to do some of the thing which is his personal will. This is a lovely spacious house, well decorated and furnished, lovely crockery and kitchen ware and with all the basics so you're not having to rush to the shops to even make a coffee. Very close to the subway and JFK airport - it cost us $26 including tip  by taxi. Tom was very prompt, both in confirming the booking and responding to minor queries.  The location is very far from Manhattan, so if you're planning to spend every day there, you'll struggle as it's about an hour door-to-door to Times Square. The neighbourhood is also pretty tough, as in policeman-on-the-street-corners-at-night-tough. The area comes with a pretty bad reputation as I found out from my uncle and a friend of mine who came to pick me up one evening. My cousin and I, however, didn't feel unsafe at any point, but think it's worth mentioning.

Positive points: -The house was as seen in the photos -Next to a metro station and grocery stores -Fully equipped kitchen to make food at home -The house was very spacious, even for our group of 8 people -Hosts were very flexible about check-in and check-out times  Negatives: -40 minutes by subway from Manhattan -The neighborhood looked rough, but we didn't feel unsafe -The 2nd floor (the bedrooms) was not sufficiently heated  -The house smelled a little like mothballs

We stayed for a week at Toms place. It looks as described in pictures, very clean, well kept, and nice. It is comfortable and really does feel as if you are in your own home. Tom kept in touch with me throughout our stay to see how things were going and if we had any concerns, that was kind of him. He allowed us to drop off our bags prior to checking in so we could explore the city. The place is very near a subway line (about 2.5 blocks), which made it very convenient to plan our day. There are a few small grocery stores nearby for small items, and a larger grocery store across from the subway station for produce and such. We are comfortable in large cities, so we did not feel unsafe, however, it is not a quiet suburban neighborhood, it is busier than others so one will encounter different kinds of people. Something to note if you are coming back late in the evening.

The description was great. The train areas are a bit dangerous, but closer to the house the neighborhood is great and peaceful. Tom was difficult to contact on the day of check-in, but was a great host and was always answering any questions asked. The great was perfect and spacious. However, I did get charged for damages that I am completely sure were not made by me other my 3 guests that rented as well.

First, I never intended to write such a long review, I actually did not want to at all because I wanted this experience to go away and be behind me, but I strongly feel that my story needs to be heard. My employee and I came to NY for two business meetings and checked in to Tom's place late Thursday night. There were 2 doors (one to the front and another to the entry of the home) We only got 1 key to the front door but never got a second key to the inside. Mind you the second door was already unlocked upon our first checking in and, since we did not have a key to this door that is exactly how we left it; unlocked. The next morning we left for our meeting only to come back later that night and find all the lights on and that second door that enters the home, (the one we left unlocked) locked. We were totally obstructed from getting in with all of our belongings inside. Gratefully had that 1 key and were able to get in the front door and sit in the hallway (it was chilly outside) but now we are afraid and panicked that we had been swindled out of our money and worried about our belongings. I thought to first contact the Police, however I contacted Airbnb. Unfortunately the first representative I got refused to help and actually hung up on me but after trying again the second rep Danyel stayed on the phone for the entirety of this debackle. She tried to contact the host as well but could not reach him either. By this time I think I'm having my very first panic attack because I am sick to my stomach nauseated and throwing up because I was scared that we (two women) had been scammed and would be stranded and have to spend extra money on a hotel for two nights (which according to airbnb would not have been paid for, unless taken out of the money for the rental *side eye*) Finally a stranger (not our host) comes while we were standing in the hallway (tells us he is the hosts "brother") goes through the basement and and opens the door. Again never hearing from our host and still having airbnb witness this we were scared sh**less... who is this random man and why hasn't our host still contacted nor alerted us that anyone else was coming?? We were not so sure this was a safe place to stay and had been hindered from our quiet enjoyment of this home that we rented so I opted to stay at a hotel. Unfortunately we never got a chance to go thanks to Airbnb cancelling our hotel reservation (*another side eye*). Needless to say this experience made for a very frightening and uncomfortable trip that ruined my entire focus and vibe of my business meeting and could have possibly cost me an employee. Did we...

My first Airbnb experience at Christina's could not have been any more perfect. Her loft is gorgeous, spacious, in just about the best location you could ask for and also home to an adorable cat called Winky who really steals the show. The bed is really comfy and the room is huge. As I'm sure you know, Williamsburg has just about everything you could want; great bars, coffee and food and the L train gets you to Chelsea in 15 minutes. Now stop reading this, and go and send Christina a reservation request! Oh and when you're there, make sure she is practising her guitar, ok?

The house has enough space and the cleanliness was good. All that you need is present. However the kitchen inventory is rather old and sometimes ready for renewal.  People write about how good he is at communicating, very helpful and hospitable and getting you anything you're missing.  Unfortunately our experiences were not that good. We did not know how to close the key box. We never got an aswer so we took the keys with us everyday. We finally figured out by ourselves. The wifi information came one day after our arrival. There were 4 light bulbs broken or absent. We mentioned it but got no reaction. We asked where the laundry basket was, again no answer.  I read in other reviews that he lives downstairs in the basement. But we have noticed nothing. We haven't seen him in the entire period of 8 days.  If you want a more lively area with good shops, nice restaurants en bars, I cannot recommend that part of Brooklyn. Although we did not feel unsafe in the neighborhood, it is not the best location in Brooklyn.

The location is wonderful, close to great grocery stores, entertainment, and great access to all the trains. The area is amazing, this place is truly a gem in a beautiful brownstone. This stay was very comfortable and stress free, easy access to the area and overall very convenient, 10 out 10 recommend this airbnb!

I had the pleasure of staying in this beautiful apartment for 3 months and really loved it.  It's nicely decorated and very spacious, especially for New York.  It felt like home right away.  For anyone hesitant to stay in Harlem, don't be!  This is a good area with lots of restaurants and shopping nearby.  I never once felt unsafe here.  Would definitely stay again!

Dimitry is the perfect host. Welcomed us to the apartment and gave background on the neighborhood and what's around. The apartment was sparkling clean and fully equipped from kitchen tools to an extra blanket. Neighborhood can look a bit scary at first, but on a second look you will see its totally safe. 2 blocks away from the subway. About 15 minutes to time square via 6 train. Dimitry was responsive for every request and question we had. If the location suits you, choose this apartment

The situation of the flat is good but not as sunny as the description announced. The floor was dirty especially around the bed... And the heater stopped working for two days.. 4degrees celsius is a good way to feel yourself homeless... The stay was like the decoration of the appartment :  epic!  As a conclusion the stay was too expensive compared to hotels...

I stayed at Kristina's place with my boyfriend, and family for 4 days in july 2012. It was perfect.  First of all, even before we arrived, Kristina was very helpful and responding quickly. We found her to be a really nice person. Then we arrived, she gave us the keys, her precious tips about the neighbors then disappeared to let us enjoy our stay. There was beers in the fridge. We found her to be a really, really nice person. We spent 4 amazing days in NYC and Williamsburg, which is definitely the place that makes you wanna move in as soon as possible. Everything was perfect until sunday, when we found out that our car had been towed. She was the one to help us confirm it had not been stolen ("thanks God it's towed!!" ;) ) and as we had to wait until the next day to pick up our car, she offered to stay one more night. Then we found she was a really, amazingly nice person.  The appartment is spacious, perfect for 4 people. Nothing over fancy, but it's comfortable, very clean and modern, with everything you need to feel home. We loved the bathroom.  Conclusion: be careful where you park your car and book without a worry!

I stayed for four days with my wife and two young boys.  What a great location, it was in the middle of lots of bars, restaurants, and stores.  There's two drug stores nearby. The apartment was simple but clean.  The kitchen had everything you would need for a visit to NYC.  I also brought a car with me and was able to find free, on-street parking everyday (you just have to move it around on garbage pick-up days).  Would gladly stay here again.

The apartment is easy to find, there is a grocery store called the Deli and it is the door to the right of entrance number 177. So we have everything we need to stock up on food when we arrive until midnight. It is not unpleasant in the morning to make fried eggs with cheese or ham, orange juice etc... The location is really in a neighborhood full of life and I would even say that it is "THE PLACE" to stay in New York currently, you don't feel any insecurity and plenty of places to discover for a drink or something to eat. A Whole food market is just a stone's throw down the street and there you can also find everything you need to eat or buy sandwiches and good salads for the next day's visits. The metro is very close to the apartment and on the metro road there are some pretty shops. We met Kristina who is adorable and very sociable. She is always ready to be of service. bring a line and clothes pegs to dry your laundry and elastic bands to fix the curtains in the rooms as they are seen from the street. Otherwise everything is like home and the bedding is very comfortable and Kristina's little written words are fun and useful. good family stay

Andrea is great! The space is on a beautiful block of Park Slope with enormous shady trees, a cafe, grocery, and several restaurants right on the corner. We rented the space for our elderly folks, who were coming through NYC during a long vacation. The bedroom is quite large which was great for their 6 bags. The kitchen was very clean, and well stocked. She thoughtfully laid in some basic provisions - fresh fruit, cookies, bread, eggs, milk, butter, etc. It was much appreciated. The bed and seating areas were a little too low and hard for our elderly visitors, but they managed. I'd think most guests would find it ok. Most of all we were so happy to have found such a nice place near where we live so we could visit with them, and share our wonderful Brooklyn neighborhood with them. Thanks to Andrea, and Gus the dog (lives upstairs, not in the Airbnb) for their hospitality during my in-laws' visit!!

Apartment was really like she described it. Not too fancy and modern, but very clean and has everything in what is needed for a stay. Beds are comfortable. On a busy road (thats why we choose the location), with closed windows it is ok to sleep.  Enjoyed the breakfast with coffee and crumble cake from the bakery.  Kristina was very responsiveness, quick answers and helpful! Thanks again!  The neighborhood is very interesting and you could already spend a whole week without visiting Manhattan... Great restaurants, bars and bakeries... Its a bit messy all around but we never felt unsafe, even mid of the night. You get breakfast, lunch an dinner just in a few steps around all corners.   Over all I would say this is New York without filter #nofilter :-)

Jacqui is a lovely host who made us feel comfortable and helped us out anyway that she could. Jacqui really made us feel that her home was our home and we felt relaxed the whole time we were there, which ended up being a little over a month all up!  Some people we spoke to before and during our stay said they thought Bedstuy was a dangerous area but this is not true! The neighbourhood is friendly and we never had any problems whatsoever, even walking home at 4am in the morning after a night out. The trains are the best! We didn't encounter any problems on the G line. It usually took 25 minutes or so to get to Union Square from Bedford Nostrand and it's so easy to navigate. My friend Gen and I would stay here again but perhaps it would be worth renting out the larger room as we found staying in the guest room for nearly a month a bit tight, this was only through fault of our own due to the amount of shopping we did! We also had large suitcases but Jacqui is so easy going so we could spread out throughout the whole apartment which we were so grateful for!  We also enjoyed an amazing home cooked meal and met her friends who are hilarious! Also, even if you aren't a cat lover, you will be by the time you leave! Jacqui has a beautiful cat called Zoe who we fell in love with. My friend Gen normally has allergies but had no problem with Zoe at all.  We loved staying with Jacqui and only wish we got to spend more time with her! Luckily we have the rest of the year in NYC to catch up :)

Kestrel was a truly lovely host! This was my first Airbnb experience and Kestrel was always helpful and continually kind. The apartment is small, quaint and clean. I stayed for a month while taking a course in Manhattan, and it was the perfect place to come back to after a long day. The apartment was cozy, everything worked well, and was well organized. The neighbourhood took a little bit of getting used to, but I never felt unsafe despite traveling by myself. The location was perfect; a 10 minute walk from the A/C train which took me into the Financial District for school. Plenty of little cafes, restaurants and grocery stores in the immediate area. The Quincy Market downstairs is surprisingly gourmet! I also recommend visiting Dough (10 min walk) for AMAZING doughnuts.   One thing that took a bit of getting used to was how loud it is. The windows are quite thin, so you hear a lot on the street below. Once I got used to it, I hardly noticed it at all and now I'm confident I can sleep through anything!   Kestrel was very quick to reply to me throughout my stay and made me feel comfortable and welcome even when she was out of town. This is a great little place to stay in Brooklyn and I would certainly come back!

The apartment is very well furnished and super clean. It is a fun, pleasant place to be, which is not typical of most basements! It is very brightly lit, and the windows let in a nice amount sunlight; this is not the typically gloomy basement apartment.  The bathroom was well stocked.  The neighborhood is pleasant with shopping/restaraunts about a half mile away (15 minute walk or less for most). The subway is about a mile away. Busses into Manhattan run from closer if you prefer that. (I am a subway fan). I was very surprised at how easy it was to drive into the city during my August 2022 stay. I suspect traffic is still off from pre-pandemic times.  Street parking can be found nearby, but you will have to hunt for a while and most likely walk a few blocks to get back, so depending on your comfort wit that, you might want to get the parking add-on to the reservation.  Orit is a kind and communicative host.  I wish we had had had more time in our somewhat busy schedule to chat.   The place is great.  I highly recommend it!

Upon arriving to kestrels apartment by myself. My lyft driver told me how "unsafe" the neighborhood was. Turns out he was from Jersey and had no idea. Once my boyfriend arrived we explored and found that there was nothing to be wary of at all. Please don't let first impressions in the dark put you off! Kestrels apartment is a strange set up, with the bedroom down the corridor to the rest of the apartment. But it wasn't an issue. The apartment was kooky in the best way and had everything we needed and more. we even used the studio to do some yoga! It is super near to transport so we spent most of our time exploring nearby williamsburg, and getting into Manhattan is easy. We were expecting a little more privacy (there was another guest in the main bedroom) but we got over it because we become very very fond of the apartment and neighbourhood. If you want to live like a local and stay somewhere that feels like the real new York. Stay here! Thanks for being so responsive and considerate kestrel. Our preconceptions were completely overturned and we were glad we chose this over a hotel. Would recommend :)

We enjoyed staying at Kestrel's place. It was very cozy and comfortable with regard to public transport. We didn't feel unsafe at night, however we took the G-Line (Bedford-Nostrand Aves) to be nearer to the flat at nighttimes. The apartment itself was very nice and well equipped. We enjoyed having a warm bedroom; the rest of the apartment was not too warm - that might have been a problem of the heating.   All in all it has been a nice Airbnb-Experience and we might come back when we are in NYC again.   Thank you very much Kestrel!  Julia & Stephan

Zora and Chris's apartment was lovely and homely. We were greeted by Zora on arrival and she made us feel very welcome and gave us lots of useful information about the area and how to get around.  Manhattan is easily accessible by the A train which is an express and takes around twenty minutes to get to the downtown area. The area is nice and quiet by the apartment but there are shops and food places nearby too.  The apartment had everything we needed, including towels and toiletries, cold drinks, coffee maker and the option to buy wine. We felt very much at home and enjoyed our stay very much.  Another thing we appreciated was Zora and Chris arranging our taxi to the airport which took away some of the stress.  Oh and free wifi!  Thanks Simon and Claire

We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Barbara’s apartment.  Barbara was a fantastic host; welcoming, approachable, friendly, knowledgeable, and eager to accommodate our needs.   All communication prior to our arrival was transparent and efficient.  The apartment was exactly as advertised; designer chic and spotlessly clean.   All essential amenities were provided; Barbara had added some luxurious touches to make our experience extra special, by surprising us with a complementary bottle of Champagne.  Although the accommodation is not central, the subway is located just two blocks away within easy reach of all tourist destinations ($2.50) a journey.  Taxi ride approximately ($20 -25), easy to catch a taxi at the end of the street (Black Sedans).  We would recommend this apartment and host for a pleasant, stress free, romantic stay.  Thank you Barbara for making our stay so memorable.

Zora and Chris were fantastic hosts. Everything was as expected, the space was fantastic for me and my mum. We each had our own spaces, I used the pull out couch which was better than most pull-outs. Location was great, I love Bed Stuy. A bit sketchy at night but would definitely stay there again. Uber is best way home. Zora was helpful in suggesting local restaurants and sights to see. Lovely stay overall!

I found Richard's place on short notice after my other accommodations fell through. I'm so grateful to him for accommodating me the same day! The apartment has a really unique layout with the rooms almost being like separate living spaces from the rest of the apartment. It's a much older building and doesn't have too many amenities but is pretty comfortable despite this. There is no AC in the bedroom so if you're visiting during a heat wave it might not be the best choice, although there is a pretty strong table fan in the room which sufficed for me along with keeping the window open. The bed is a bit hard but I used a doubled up blanket to pad it a bit and slept very well with no issues. The area is safe and relatively quiet at night. The subway (L and M) is about 2-3 blocks away and will take you straight to Manhattan. There's also a sweet cat who stays in the main part of the apartment with Richard but she's a little scared of new people so you don't see her too much unless he's there too :) All in all, this is a very comfortable place to stay for the price and convenience. Richard is a great host and makes sure you have everything you need. Thanks again for accommodating me on such short notice!

Richard is SUPER KIND and responds quickly but his place has issues: 1) Everything is very DUSTY (if you're allergic that's NOT the place for you). 2) The floor of the room was incredibly dirty, like it hadn't been washed in weeks.  3) I found NAIL CLIPPINGS on the floor.   Finally, and this is the most personal detail: 4) The cat--albeit considered by other guests sweet--attacked me twice and scratched me once. I don't know, I usually get along with pets, and maybe you have better luck.  In the attempt to make things better, Richard borrowed a vacuum cleaner from the neighbor to let me clean my room but unfortunately it didn't work.  After the second attack by the cat, I decided to spend my last night (of four) elsewhere. He tried to offer me home-made hummus and kombucha, and a refund for my last night which I refused because I winded up leaving my bags there until check out.

We have been at John's house for a week.  Although the neighborhood seemed a little unsafe to us upon our arrival, over time we felt very well and without any problems. Quiet area with places to eat. The subway stop to Manhattan line L is a 5-minute walk away and in 20 meters you are in Central Park. The house is very clean and bright and although old it is very comfortable and spacious. The great bed. Jonh was traveling during our stay but we were able to contact him at all times. It is highly recommended if you want to be outside of Manhattan in a working-class neighborhood with good bars, supermarkets and nightlife.

The place is just as expected...the room itself probably nicer than I expected. I had several changes of plans around when I was available to "check in" and Chris was really patient and understanding although I suspect he had plenty of other things to do - so if this place looks like what you are after, go for it. Thanks Chris!

This place is a steal for the location, and Chris is a great AirBnB host - quiet, but around if you need him. He gave me an extra blanket because I was cold. I'd a great stay, and thought that the apartment was safe, nice and a great weekend halt.
Great place with stress-free secured parking.  Easy walking access to Greenpoint & Williamsburg.

I had a great week in NYC even through my trip was only supposed to last a few days and was unexpectedly extended due to Hurricane Sandy. I absolutely LOVED staying at Michael's place, he was such a gracious and generous host. The location was ideal - just around the corner from the subway, right in the heart of Harlem with plenty of great shops and surrounded by little hidden gems like: Chocolate (amazing brunch on Sundays), Mocha Lounge, Bake My Cake bakery and many more. Staying at this place and in Harlem is the way to see the REAL NYC. The apartment was very clean and comfortable and safe and the shower was amazing!! I never got bored or felt unsafe walking the neighborhood and in fact walked home many days from my outings as there seemed to be something of interest around nearly every corner of the city. I would love to come back to NYC and would certainly check to see if this apartment is available for rent ahead of anything else. You will not be disappointed staying here for such a great price. Thank you Michael!!

This was by far the best B&B experience I have had.  Michael is the PERFECT host.  I didn't get in until 2 pm in the morning and not only was he totally gracious about letting me come late but he walked me part way to work the next morning to make sure I would know the best way.  The house is stunning.  Michael's an amazing art collector and the house reflects his smart and thoughtful personality.  The neighborhood is fun!  In the heart of Harlem.  It is alive and exciting yet I never felt unsafe and I traveled alone.  I will be making this my top choice for my trips back to New York .

A private mini-suite with garden in a quiet, safe neighborhood, a short walk to the subway and ride to Manhattan. What's not to like? This was my second stay. I enjoyed my first, in April '13, so much that I returned in June '14. A heat wave hit NYC, so I was grateful for the new seasonal amenities, an air conditioner and fan. They kept the suite cool. Jeruschka is a host who puts in extra effort to make a guest feel welcome and comfortable.  Advice to other guests: try Jeruschka's recommended neighborhood coffee shop (I'm afraid I forgot its name). Good latte and pain au chocolat.

Jerushka was incredibly welcoming, even when we were unexpectedly 3 hours late arriving! She came by to show us around the space personally, and was helpful pointing out local favorites.   The garden was probably our favorite part about the space. It was perfect for sitting after a long day beating feet in the city, having a glass of wine and reading a little. The cafe lights made it even more romantic, and my husband and I found ourselves out there many an evening.   The neighborhood was sleepy during the week and perked up on the weekend. It seemed to be lots of families, which made me feel very comfortable. There were many amenities within a few blocks, including drug stores, multiple delicious restaurants, laundry facilities, and several lovely parks. The F train into the city was a quick walk in either direction and it was easy to get into and around Manhattan from our location, but it was about an hour round trip, so it was necessary to pack for multiple scenarios when leaving for the day.   Truly it was a lovely stay, and we were very happy with the accomodations. Jerushka even provided many things, like shower goodies and hand sanitizer and an umbrella, which made our stay even handier.

Evan's loft was just as beautiful as pictured and he was great. The space itself is large and convenient, decked out with all the conveniences you could hope for (AppleTV, fully functioning kitchen, etc) and the location is true Williamsburg, BKYLN.   We had a great time chilling at the place, reading, cooking and watching tv, and it was a great point of departure for Manhattan (you can easily walk the W Bridge to SoHo) and the rest of Brooklyn (Green Point is only a few min walk away, the rest are easily Uberable).   The place was clean and easy to use, the house rules were more than fair and easy to follow and Evan was straightforward and easy to communicate with.   Though the neighborhood was a bit 'too cool' for us, we are glad we went for a true Williamsburg experience as the place is on prime real estate, with a great waterfront view to Manhattan and an easy walk to any one of the Williamsburg's countless cafes, restaurants, bars and club.   Though other parts of Brooklyn might be cheaper, none are more central and (more importantly) convenient, simple and coherent. The area is not large and just chuck full of anything you might need - definitely worth the price and the at times overbearing hipness.   The only 'downside' of the location was that due to its proximity to the bridge, it can be super windy and cold and at night it might seem 'scary' to walk back home (though in reality it is super safe, both by Manhattan and Brooklyn standards)   If you want to feel young, cool and in the know this is the place for you.

Majar's place is very conveniently located on the J line. We were able to get there by subway from the airport in less than 45 mins without any transfers (JFK). Getting into Manhattan was very simple too and the trains run all night, even on weekends. However, we did run into some closures due to construction and maintenance at the station the weekend we came so be sure to read all the signs.   The room was very clean and so was the bathroom that we used. We didn't really go into the kitchen for anything but it looked clean. Fresh linens and towels were provided.   We had access to wifi and many tv channels (but didn't have time to watch any). There is a grocery store(key foods?) located just a couple of blocks away where we bought all our snacks and water. Wine and liqueur shop even closer.   I saw some negative reviews for this area before, however us being 2 young girls weren't bothered by anyone. one night we were returning way past midnight and didn't feel unsafe or scared, everyone was very friendly- except the rats on the subway... but that's another story.   Our host, Majar, was very welcoming and kind. He helped us carry our huge suitcases up the stairs when we arrived and offered advice on how to get to places and what is available in the area. We only saw him twice but he was always available via phone/email and lives on the lower level of the house.   Overall, I would stay here again and wouldn't hesitate to recommend his place to friends.
Hello! Very nice and clean overall. It's not clear on the ad but it's a shared bathroom. Also the area is a bit sketchy but not too bad!

Majar provides a good-sized and comfortable room in Brooklyn. Note that it is in a shared apartment and with a shared bathroom, Majar lives downstairs. That being said, we never really had to wait on the bathroom.   It very is close to the Subway (a couple minute walk to the J Line) but does take time to get into Manhattan if that's what you're in town for. As other reviewers have stated, the neighbourhood does feel a bit sketchy but there are plenty of people around so we didn't feel unsafe.  Majar was a great host, answering all our questions with speed. He even put in an air conditioner when we said that the room got hot at night.

I had a lovely stay at Majar;s Place. Majar and his Mother were very welcoming on my arrival. The room was clean and spacious and the place was only a few blocks away from the J line, which was an easy line to get into Manhattan. Majar was friendly and helpful and check in and out was very easy. The neighbourhood is a bit sketchy at night but other then that had a wonderful stay.

Just got back from an awesome trip to NYC which was made even more amazing by the wonderful accommodations provided by Majar and his family. My friend and I were out late most nights so we didn't interact with Majar very much but any time we happened to run into any one they were always so friendly and welcoming. Majar even sent us a text when we left to wish us a safe trip!   The room is exactly as pictured but it's even better in person if that's possible! The bathroom is shared for the entire floor but it is incredibly clean and I think I may have waited once to use the facilities the entire time I was there so don't let that deter you. There is also a kitchen that is available for your use should you like to have a cheap night ( NY is expensive y'all) and they even keep it stocked with coffee and tea for a morning pick me up!   Also in terms of getting around there is a metro station really close by and like I mentioned before we got back very late most nights but I never felt unsafe in the neighborhood. Also if you do wind up getting back late, make sure to be careful closing the screen door as it is very light and I accidentally slammed it once! Sorry!  Honestly if you are hesitating to book this place, don't! All of these glowing reviews are not a fluke, it is an amazing place run by a family that is the epitome of hospitable and caring. I would definitely come back if I'm ever in the area. 10 stars!

Despite our good communications via email before arrival, Majar was dismissive and arrogant at reception. After opening the door to let me in, without waiting for my daughter to get out of the car and enter, Mr. leaves to take the key and gives it to me, telling me just where the shower/kitchen is and how to close it if we get out and leave without any words. The reception was very unpleasant.  The ad specifies 2 beds. As there were no sheets or duvets for the sofa bed, I sent him a message to ask for some. Monsieur comes down, and without a word hands me the duvet and sheets. I take the opportunity to ask him where the parking is (specified in the ad - free parking). Monsieur tells me that we must leave the car on the Avenue in front of the house. Except that it is an alternate location (prohibited from 4:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.) and you must change places before 4:00 p.m. Which requires you to return from your visits every day at 4:00 p.m. No solution is proposed even though Mr. has 1 free space (in addition to that of his car) in the interior courtyard. When I offer to put my car behind his so as not to bother him if he goes out because I don't need it for the 5 days of our stay, Mr. gets angry and leaves without saying goodbye. The noise from the old air conditioner must also be reviewed and corrected. Maybe we arrived at a moment where Monsieur was worried, but it wasn't pleasant at all. Despite everything, we had a wonderful stay in NY and took very little advantage of the accommodation.

Firstly, James is super communicative and was always checking in. I booked his apartment for my parents visiting from Australia. It's the perfect location - in the heart of hip Williamsburg. It's the epitome of "New York". Something you'd find in an Andy Warhol movie. Huge loft ceilings, big bedroom and great kitchen for cooking meals with produce from Wholefoods (just around the block). The only thing I would mention is it's on the 3rd floor and the elevator is a bit tricky. It's really for cargo and not for people... So, if you don't like walking up & down a few flights of stairs everyday and are slightly scared of elevators (my mum is!!); I would look somewhere else... I personally loved the fun of using the old school elevator and don't mind walk ups (good for the bum!). I'd definitely book again for visitors coming to NYC.

Andre was a great host and was very open to receiving us. He and the apartment were as close to perfect as you can get for Airbnb. When we arrived we were lucky enough to greet him and he was easily accessible throughout the trip. The apartment was in great condition and we had no problems with anything. Amenities included having a great tv and being close to many great shops. The apartment was easy to find and was close to the prospect park subway which brought us to Manhattan in 15 minutes! This apartment is a steal in New York and I would not hesitate to stay there again!

Wow!  What an AirBnB experience!  Andre is one of the best hosts I've met and was very gracious in allowing us to use the back patio.  Don't expect it, but use it if given the opportunity!  The welcome flowers are an awesome touch!  The location couldn't have been any better!  Walk to the Q in under ten minutes, go to the market in under 5. Any type of food delivered for free! Spacious digs, free Keurig pods, Netflix!    Prospect Park is extremely close. Subway to Coney Island in 30 minutes.  Beer/Liquor stores within stumbling distance.  I would stay here again upon my return to NYC.  I suspect I'll convince friends to stay with Andre too!
Felt scary because it's an old place but very nice to stay. Close to food and everything.

Thoughtful, Historic, Nostalgia, LOCATION.   I really enjoyed my stay. The place was very comfortable. Most importantly I was able to bring both of my dogs. The owners have done a good job of telling you what to expect in the listing, and the pictures are very accurate. I've had to cut the review down a few times but I wanted to get across how great this place was. Below I've listed some stuff, it certainly is not an exhaustive list.   ~~Thoughtfulness~~ You can tell that the owners care. There are many small touches that I don't expect from an Airbnb. Here are a few:      -The nightstand in the front room has an outlet which has a standard plug and a USB plug      -Roku TV that's already connected      -There is a survival guide on the desk in the front room with tips, maps and FAQs      -There is a bottle of wine and an emergency station with toiletries      -There is a water filter in the fridge and ice trays      -The kitchen has utensils. cups, glasses, plates, TEAS, sugar etc.       -The bathroom has towels, shampoo, conditioner, shower gel, several towel hooks and of course toiler paper  ~~Historic/Nostalgia~~ NYC is an expensive place to live. For this reason people often reuse, repurpose and refinish. Some do a better job than others. Andre and his wife hit the nail on the head. I loved this apartment. The front room had solid wood doors one of which was a  fully functional pocket door. The windows had solid wood shutters. There was a hallway library with a great collection of books. The floors were sturdy solid wood. In the kitchen the fridge was updated with cute black hinges and black iron handles.  I read a review saying that the place was old. This is what makes Brownstones so coveted. Yes they are old but they were well built and have passed the test of time. I live in a three year old house which I had built. My floors are nothing like the floors in this apartment and my doors are flimsy. The decor in the apartment is cohesive and functional. It felt like an updated Brooklyn apartment not like a faux SOHO apartment which is the new trend in Brooklyn :-(.    ~~LOCATION~~ It's so close to Prospect Park, right off of Flatbush and the street is tree lined with tons of shade. `Being from Brooklyn I prefer the Park Slope neighborhood however this block felt like that but with more accessibility to a variety of stores within walking distance.

My sister and I had the most incredible 7 day stay at Sara’s New York apartment.  We arrived to find the apartment exactly as depicted in the photos online. It is clean, quiet and the perfect spot to rest after busy days exploring the city! The apartment is very well located in a safe residential neighbourhood on the Upper East Side – we felt like real New Yorkers rather than just tourists. The apartment is a ten minute walk to the Met, a fifteen minute walk to Central Park, and just a few blocks away from the 86th & Lexington subway station which very conveniently took us to all of our other destinations.  Sara was very easy to communicate with and responded promptly to any and every query we had. Check in/check out went very smoothly – it was a truly stress-free experience.  It was our first time booking through Airbnb, as well as our first trip to New York, and we would not hesitate to recommend Sara’s apartment. We can’t wait to return in the future!

Two friends and I recently completed a six-day stay at Verena's apartment.  We were extremely happy with our stay.  The apartment was exactly as advertised, and immaculately clean.  Everything we could possibly need was there, and we all wanted to pack the beds and take them home in our suitcases, they were that comfortable.  The subway was a two-minute walk away, and even walking back and forth at night, we felt perfectly safe.  Verena was a gracious host, going out of her way to be sure that our stay was smooth and comfortable.  She went above and beyond to accommodate the travel schedule of my friend who was arriving internationally from Brazil, which was a huge stress relief.  All three of us agree that staying in Verena's apartment was the highlight of our trip - a comfortable, safe place to stay that was exactly as advertised.  If you're traveling to NYC and staying in the Brooklyn area, I can't recommend Verena and her apartment highly enough.

The accommodation is very pleasant and clean, well located 200 meters from a direct subway station to Manhattan. Quiet environment, Verena and Daniel are charming hosts, available, attentive and good advice. Far from the frenzy of the center, this comfortable accommodation allows relatively quick access to all of Brooklyn and Upton. Arrival and departure are made easier, which is very welcome before and after a long-haul flight.

Lisa and Angus were amazing hosts . They made my time on the boat a pleasure. .Angus is very helpful and has a great knowledge of the area. Picked me up from the station when I could not find my way. Lisa was a star she made booking very easy and stress free and on top of that kindly took my uncle and myself on a day out to remember we had a great time lisa we thankyou.. the area and boat were very nice in a great neighbourhood..cinemas and great lobster restaurants a 2 min walk from the boat ..also the small community on the marina were so welcoming we drank we ate and shot the breeze..in short if you want a place too stay and people to remember you can't go wrong booking the barge...This one is a must and you will want to go back for sure

Verena is very responsive and very accommodating. She allowed us to leave our suitcases for our departure day and our late flight which allowed us to enjoy the day.  The house is very well located with metro lines 3 and 4 which avoids having to walk a lot.  The accommodation is provided with sanitary equipment and bath towels; as well as numerous products for cooking at home and making a few meals.

It is a wonderful place to be, you have enough space and a nice backyard,where you can sit under a shady tree with your coffee. You have busses and trains nearby to go to Manhattan. The district is very green and you find there a Jewish community, very interesting. When I come again, I would like to stay there again. Thanks for the fully equipet household. Bye karin, Markus and family

I had a fantastic experience at Omri's loft in Williamsburg.  I was staying there during a stressful time, apartment hunting in NY, and Omri was not only helpful and accommodating as a host, but also helped me a bit with my apartment search.  The room and shared spaces overall were very clean and we had everything we needed.  I would stay here longer if I could and would recommend staying here to anyone looking for a nice, clean, quiet place to stay with a very friendly host.    The room: comfortable bed, nice towels and toiletries he allowed us to use in the bathroom, AC worked great, no complaints.  The bathroom was very spacious and nice.   The location: really ideal location with access to Graham L down the block-- made it so easy to get to Manhattan or around Brooklyn.   Zero complaints, there was no elevator and it is on the 4th floor, but it's a nice building and it wasn't an issue.

Thanks Pat, I had a great time at your place!  Everything was as advertised.   Though less than 80 stairs I think ;) Exemplary communication. Detailed instructions beforehand. Arriving and checkout very uncomplicated. Very tidy kitchen, bathroom and living area; nice room with a nice view; more storage space for clothes would be nice.  Hell’s Kitchen is vibrant, friendly, communicative, very rainbow, lots of dogs and bodega cats, close to Hudson, and awesome connections with metro A,C,E. The janitor Rob is also fun to talk to.  Sharing the apartment with Pat and other guests was pleasant, and mostly invisible. A sure thing to recommend.  Cheers Pat!  5/5 Con

The location is great and Michelle was a great communicator and very helpful. With this being said the place was not like shown on the pictures and the building’s interior (walk up stairs make you feel like you are in a haunted house of 1800s). The floors in the apartment are in horrible condition and the shower is scary. I don’t mind paying more for better accommodations but this was totally not worth the money :(

The location of Patrick's place is unbeatable and I found the decor interesting and cute. The beds were also comfortable. I was taken aback by the "historic" aspect of the apartment. The floors are super old and incredibly creaky. It didn't bother me too much, but I suspect that the person downstairs has to wear noise canceling headphones on the regular. Getting bags up and down the stairs was a feat, but this isn't unusual in NYC. The only real con of the apartment is the bathroom. The shower stall is super small and it's impossible to take a shower without the curtain touching you. Don't plan on shaving your legs! But again, the location and convenience of the apartment make it all worth it.

AWESOME apartment! I'm sure anyone who stays there is going to LOVE it. Although it's located in Brooklyn, the area is not too sketchy. It's actually convenient. The apartment itself has all the basics, such as pans, pots, several ingredients, towels, shampoos, etc. The house is clean when I got there. I stayed there for 3 weeks, and found myself feeling really comfortable there. It's a great location that's not too far away from the subway station either.  Next time, if I'm going to live in NYC for a while, I'm definitely going to choose this apartment again. Worth spending your money staying there. Enjoy your stay there!

I was travelling to NY on business and had to stay for a month. The communication with Jasmine was very good from the start, she was responsive and polite. That's why it is a bit hard to write this review. Upon entering the apartment the first thing that was noticeable was an unpleasant odor  sort of like a musty smell.  Then I walked through the apartment and the only thing that seemed to me like in the pictures was the kitchen. The bathroom looked unkempt, bedroom felt very stuffy and I couldn't sleep (no windows to open there, and the only ones were in the kitchen). It felt dusty. I wasn't expecting a new or a modern apartment, I know I booked an apartment in an older building but this was too much. I felt very uncomfortable and couldn't finish my stay. I've returned the keys to Jasmine after 5 days (I've booked 30) and found other lodgings. But sadly we couldn't agree on a refund and that also disappointed me because the whole situation in the apartment is not shown in the pictures

This apartment is a steal for the price. It is a lot bigger than I thought it would be. There are two nice sized rooms and decent size kitchen. The location is a 10 min walk to the subway but you close to a lot of stores and etc. The host was extremely nice and very understanding. If you are coming out of town with a friend, I would highly recommend this place.

Although Julia was not in the house, everything worked well. The room and bathroom were very clean. The bed is really comfortable. The neighborhood is very quiet and safe and a good alternation after a day in Manhattan. Transport links are also okay. The only thing that may sometimes feel robbed a bit of sleep is the noisy heating, because it is an old building and it is not likely to change it. However, we would come back.

The place is very usable. It's comfortable enough, no frills, but not unpleasant and nicely sunny. We had problems with noisy steam heat -- first the apartment was too hot, then Vero (nicely responsive) turned it down but it was still banging and we lost a night of sleep. By the second night things were fine. A little expensive for what it is, but maybe that's the market.

Apartment conforms to the description, with two bedrooms: one very large and one smaller which overlooks the street (a little noisy in the morning). The neighborhood is pleasant, very family-friendly with a large park right next door, as well as the Brooklyn Museum. We actually liked going to have breakfast on the terrace of Dizzie's just downstairs. In addition, the accommodation is very close to the subway, located on the corner of the street, which makes traveling easier (allow around 30 minutes to get to Manhattan). We did not meet Vero, there was no need for a key since access to the apartment is via a digital code, it is very practical, since there is no stress about keys (especially when there are several people) and this also makes arrival at the place quite flexible. Only small point of improvement: I will say that some small necessities were missing (only one roll of toilet paper for the week, no coffee, no shampoo...).

Julia was a wonderful host.  She was very accommodating, making sure I felt at home.  My concerns were her concerns...I woke up one morning with a small stomach ache & she gathered a few things for me to eat & drink, I felt better within no time.   The room was very roomy.  The bed was incredibly comfortable.  The neighborhood was safe, walking home alone after midnight I never felt unsafe.  Shared bathroom was exceptionally clean.  Bedroom was clean.  Nice view of New York City from bedroom window.  Quick ride to midtown.  Good fruit.  I would recommend Julia's to any friend of mine.

The apartment was comfortable and impeccably clean, and Ben was an exceptional host and made me feel right at home. As an incoming Columbia student looking for housing in the area, I could not have chosen a better place to stay. Ben is very knowledgeable about real estate, leasing procedures, and all the neighborhoods on the west side, and was happy to help out. He even saved me from most likely getting scammed!  The apartment is in a really cool, diverse, up-and-coming neighborhood. I always felt safe walking around late (sometimes there are kids out playing past midnight!) The noise wasn't a problem for me but if you're a light sleeper you might want to bring earplugs. He and his fiance are out and about most of the time so it's practically like having the apartment to yourself at a ridiculously good rate--highly recommend for anyone looking to stay in the area!  Thanks Ben! :)

Ben was quick to respond to my last minute booking request - I am very thankful for that. He was very accommodating and answered all my questions, I could contact him at any point of my stay if I had any questions - all out great guy! So I do recommend if you're going to stay in NYC, to stay here. There is a subway station located proximal to the apartment (which makes going to city centre easier) as well as drug stores, eateries etc.

What is promised in the publication of "flexible departure" is not respected... Adding that there was no gas service available and sleeping with dirty sheets is something unpleasant, from then on... Central to get anywhere.

It was such a pleasure to stay at Lulia’s place. Room was spacious and cozy. everything i need was in the room including television, hair dryer, water, fridge, etc. Lulia was a kind host and she helped me whenever i asked. Her room takes 30minutes from Manhattan, should walk 7minutes from the metro though. i was just a little bit scared when coming back to the room at late night so usually took the Uber after 10pm (cost about $25 from midtown) Otherwise everything was fine. Thank you Lulia! Hope to see you again~ :)

Eada was very friendly. The apartment was just as advertised. It was really cold while we were there and she was very liberal with the heat which we appreciated.  Some neighborhood suggestions: Peaches Hothouse has great fried chicken and drinks, and One Last Shag is a bit of a hike, but it was a fun bar (and much less scary than the name implies). Overall we had a really great time there!

The good: Eada is charming and easy to work with. The apartment is on the first floor, and Eada's sister lives upstairs on the second floor. The apartment is clean and well stocked with cooking necessities and wonderful, fluffy towels.  The funky: Let's start with the neighborhood. It's a working-class neighborhood a good schlep from the nearest subway, with no tourist amenities anywhere nearby (nice restaurants, shops, etc.).  You can catch busses to the subways, but it took a few days to figure out what bus goes to which subway which goes where.  10 blocks to the south the neighborhood is full-on scary, but Eada's neighborhood, while a bit ragged around the edges, felt safe.  And the late night trip from the subway back to her place by bus was fine.  Would I stay here again?  As a tourist, probably not.  I'm willing to pay more (typically a LOT more - Eada's price is really good!) for a place in a more tourist-friendly neighborhood.  But if I was looking for a home away from home in Brooklyn, and I wanted to save a buck, and I didn't care about (or was willing to overlook) the lack of local tourist infrastructure, sure, I'd stay here again.

Eada was so welcoming and her place is lovely! Checking in was a breeze, and she helped us find the best transportation from the airport.  The bed was SO COMFORTABLE. My boyfriend and I slept better than we do at home.  While we didn't have time to cook, Eada has a great setup for that, along with other amenities (k-cups for the keurig machine, bottled water in the fridge).  This place is an absolute steal for the price, and Eada is a great host!

Stayed here for two nights. This was a great place to stay and Eada was a wonderful host. I got a chance to meet her daughter who was lovely. Her place is just like the pictures....very nice , clean and has everything you can possibly need.  I mean everything.   The only thing was that the mailman came early one morning a couple of times while I was sleeping to deliver mail and packages. He kept ringing the doorbell, which was pretty loud and scared me right out of my sleep. I wasn't properly dressed, so I couldn't get to the door right away. I'm sure this hardly ever happens. I just left the gated door open, in case he came back, so he could leave the packages, so I recommend future tenants to do this as well. Other than that it was a perfect place to stay and I would definitely recommend her place to anyone.    Also, I rented a car and it was quite easy to find parking. Really loved that. Also loved that she had cable. So perfect when you just want to stay in or have a little down time before going out.

Eada was extremely accomodating to us, always checking on us and gave us tips about places near the house. The place was just as the pictures, super clean and colorful. When it came to transportation, buses were within 1-2 blocks of walking distance and the nearest train stations were about 10-15 minutes. The neighborhood is very cultured and we never once felt unsafe. Definitely would stay here again.

If I could describe this experience with one word, it would be: amazing!!! Ryan and Leda's place was absolutely perfect for our needs and Ryan was extremely responsive to my inquiries via text. There were a lot of details that I would not have considered that they had already taken care of without me asking: (e.g. soap for the dishwasher, clean towels available, and trash bags, etc.). And after someone had apparently stolen their lightbulbs, Ryan so graciously stopped by with more even though we had a convenient work around or could have bought them ourselves.  This was my first Airbnb experience, but I would definitely do it again if they were all like this. When we return to NY, we are checking for Ryan and Leda's availability first, for sure!
Flat as pictures, far only 10 minutes walking from subway and 3 minutes from a big supermarket, quite zone not dangerous, Eada Is fast with answers and very kind, cleaning to improve.

Jane's Airbnb is lovely. The location, just a block away from Fort Greene Park, is stellar. The streets are lined with historic brownstones and large shade trees and the neighborhood is filled with fabulous restaurants. Jane is a gracious hostess willing to share her gorgeous home with lucky travelers. The third floor space is a generous size for lodging in NYC and is furnished with beautiful, well cared for antiques. The bathroom was large and updated . It was stiflingly hot during our visit but the space was air conditioned and served as a much needed  reprieve from the heat.  If you are  looking for a place to cook and watch TV, this might not be for you. But if you want to spend your time in NYC out enjoying all that the city has to offer then look no further. Consider yourself fortunate to be able to end your days in such a beautiful home!

Jane's place is a gem. The space is airy and elegant, and the bed is to-die-for comfy. Jane was an attentive host and quite fun to talk to. The location is perfect: a quiet residential street very close to bustling commercial areas and the waterfront. It was such fun to sit on the spacious, shady porch in the mornings and watch the neighborhood come alive. I generally avoid listings where I have to share the bathroom, but that proved to be no hassle at all, and I'm glad I didn't let it deter me.

Pretty great experience, it must be said at the outset because that is what it was. If I had to take a pin and pick out the perfect location to stay in New York City, this exact apartment might be the place the pin ends up. The actual neighborhood itself is one of the most interesting places you could possibly stay for sure. It has the best cafe in all of NYC in Brooklyn Kolache Co. Don't worry I checked every other cafe in the city and the backyard of this coffee shop is the best place to drink a latte. And the small lattes are only 3.25! Which is obscenely cheap, which you quickly learn after trying to find a cup of coffee in the village. The apartment is literally (I mean literally) right next to the subway (so for those worrying about late night walks home down dark secluded alley ways in a big dangerous city, worry not), and the subway will take to pretty much any other neighborhood in NYC you would want to go within 30 minutes. Williamsburg is 10 minutes towards Queens on the G. Long Island City is 5 minutes more. The family neighborhoods of Brooklyn like Cobble Hill and Park Slope are 10 minutes the other way on the G. Bushwick is a transfer away, the Lower East Side is a transfer away, Washington Square and Greenwich Village/Soho/Tribeca/Chelsea are all a transfer away. The museums in the Upper East Side and Central Park are a bit farther but riding the subway is so easy! You just sit there and people watch! Admittedly later at night the subways run less frequently so the travel times get longer, but the people waiting with you are good to commiserate with. As I said it very well may be the best location to stay in NYC, if only for the ease with which all the other places are reached, and because I know people who live in the lower east/west sides of Manhattan and the have the habit of never leaving Manhattan. Don't never leave Manhattan! The rest of NYC is great too. I'll just say that if you stay in Manhattan you probably won't make it out to Bed-Stuy, but if you stay here in Bed-Stuy you'll definitely make it into Manhattan. As the for the apartment and the room: it does the job. The kitchen is small, the room is small, the apartment is a little on the dirtier side (less from neglect and more from the dirtier side being the apartment's natural state). If hyper-cleanliness is a massive thing for you, maybe this isn't your place, but I consider cleanliness to be kind of a thing for me and it was fine. Also you'll save money since the surrounding environs are generally cheaper than other places. As I said, 3.25 for a small latte, which in the uber-hip enclaves of the LES might run 4.50. It's a great place to stay, is what I'm...

Elaine, was so polite and Consistent person, however I just hear her through phone. the apartment was on the old and Crowded building. First time when I arrived there, I chocked when I saw 5 other young boy and girl were on the apartment. the room was good and clean but other part of the apartment was Intolerable, in kitchen, sink was full of unwashed dishes, refrigerator was completely Erratically occupied. Some time I afraid other persons in the apartment, Imagine that  you have to live in a apartment that some people smoking!!! and drinking!!! in the salon and each time you see different person there. I tried to cancel my reservation, but Airbnb asked 1 night penalty and I had to stand it. The metro station is 2 min to apartment but I suggest return home before 9pm because the neighbor seems not so safe.

It's my first airbnb experience staying here. I was abit sceptical after reading some negative comments about this place. But it didn't turn out that way. Communication with Elaine was good, though she wasn't at home during my stay, she provided me detailed info on how to get to her apartment via email and SMS. The building is old, not for fussy people, but its really cosy with adequate facilities and privacy. The room and bed is clean, comfortable and spacious enough for me. There is a cool retro-looking elevator in the building but i didnt use it most of the time as Elaine's apartment is only a floor up. Nice kitchen, living room and bathroom/toilet. Friendly and cool roommates, who are very helpful in giving advise and directions. Situated in a nice quiet neighborhood where everything is conveniently located nearby with supermarkets, pharmacy, convenience store, mobile phone/phone card shop, eateries, etc. Subway is just a block away, getting downtown was not a problem at all. Walked around the entire neighborhood and didn't feel anything unsafe about it. It's a really great experience and stay in NY. Would love to be back!

This place -- formerly part of the host's bookselling business -- is a true sanctuary.  SO QUIET AND PEACEFUL!  Rooms literally lined with fascinating books, and comfy cozy beds and pillows.  Literally (ha) every bookworm's dream retreat.  A big beautiful garden with trees out back, in which to read and drink your tea (or coffee if you like) while taking in the air.  Or if it's raining, there's a daybed by the window where you can listen to the rain and watch it splash in the garden. The kitchen is fully appointed and has loads of dishes and space, and the bath is beautiful with a proper tub.   So -- this was the best, most serene retreat possible during a stressful time in my life (mom undergoing heart surgery).  Located a short walk from the excellent hospital (Columbia-Presbyterian), in a busy, cheerful, civilized neighborhood (fantastic restaurants, convenient grocery stores).  One block from the subway if you have other places to go.  (If only I'd had more time!  Mom's surgery was a complete success, and she's doing great and I'm incredibly glad that's over.  But I wish I'd been there to visit museums and hear music too.  Or even just to read more of the books!

We had a lovely time at Nicole's apartment. Everything was as it looks in the photos and as described; she kept in contact and was available if we needed anything; and she was really flexible on check in and out which was very helpful. We couldn't have asked for more. The area is nice and we never felt unsafe. It's close enough to the C, J and Z subway lines to make it easy to get around. Also the bed was super comfy!

Jacqui was a wonderful host! Her place was quite lovely, and full of charming, turn-of-the-century details and nooks and crannies. The bed in the Master BR was quite comfortable and, in general, the room evoked a nice sense of Old Warm charm and hospitality.   While the areas to the east of the apartment are a bit sketchy, there are a few, cute cafés, restos, and coffeeshops sprinkled around, as well as lots of old-timey Caribbean takeout joints. Additionally, staying in touch with Jacqui was easy, with her responding to my questions in a timely manner. Too, Jacqui was happy to suggest local options for dining and going out.  The only possible drawback was the sometimes overzealous and enthusiastic behavior of the cat. I am a cat lover and owner and all, but the cat repeatedly cried/jumped on me while sleeping/trying to sleep, something of which proved to be a nuisance.  I would not hesitate to stay with her again!

I had a fantastic experience staying in Jacqui's apartment. Although she was out of town during my stay, she was very attentive and accommodating and accessible via text message.  The apartment is gorgeous. Appointed with lovely vintage furnishings and all the touches of home that one would otherwise surely miss at a comparably priced hotel stay. I'm referring to things like candles,  a coffee press, extremely high thread-count sheets, Turkish kilim rugs, etc. ;) Quite luxurious, especially considering the price!  The location was great. I travel to NYC often and while I've never stayed in Bed Stuy - this raised a few eyebrows among some less adventurous friends - I loved it and never once felt unsafe in the least. Just a short walk to the Nostrand A and C trains, very convenient public transit commute. There's a deli/bodega downstairs too, in case you need anything.  Moreover, Jacqui's house is located within 2 blocks from 2 excellent culinary estabishments - the Tiny Cup cafe (great espresso drinks and breakfasts), and Do or Dine (kind of an upscale gourmet soul food place that also has a cute bar in back). So you've got your daytime and evening go-to spots if you wanna have meetings nearby.  Highly recommended, would definitely stay again.

David's apartment is just about the most beautiful space I've stayed in using AirBnB over the years.
