It's stylish, warm, inviting, and features all the amenities you expect when checking into a good hotel -- except this is a giant apartment in the middle of Brooklyn right around the corner from a subway station that can get you anywhere in the city for cheap. I highly recommend it, and I plan to stay here again the next time I'm in NYC (if it's available, because, well, it's perfect and I suspect the word will get out).

Rachel was wonderfully helpful, staying up late for our check-in and booking us a car to the airport when we left.   I really can't say enough good things about the apartment or the host; both were lovely. We were close enough to walk to Chinatown, but far enough away that we missed out on the noise. The LES had a nice village-like feel that other parts of NY seem to lack. We'll be back soon, I suspect.   I'd also echo Rachel's recommendation of Kossar's Bialys, a Jewish bakery just up the road; it does wonderful bagels.

This was absolutely my worst Airbnb stay ever. My wife and I booked Nicole's 2 bedroom apartment for 7 nights. Upon checking in we noticed signs all over the place, one of them saying that for any extra person visiting, she will charge an extra $100 per night. My 12 year old son came to visit and Nicole called me to let me know that I would have to pay an additional $50 per night. That did not make much sense to me as I booked a 2 bedroom and he's my child.  I spoke with her and expressed my disagreement.  She then said she would leave it up to me if i wanted to pay. The day before our checkout she hounded us for the extra fee and told us to place it under her door. We felt like we were being watched every moment which brought on anxiety to my wife.   It made no sense to have to pay extra as we rented a 2 bedroom. If we knew there would have been a $100 or $50 extra fee per night for my son, we certainly would have booked a much better place. We felt that her and her husband was trying to extort extra funds from us. Moreover, we saw bugs on the bed  water pressure in the bathroom was extremely low and no pots, utensils etc.... Worst host, place and trip ever!!!! Please be aware of these scammers

I really enjoyed my stay! I'm a multi-disciplinary performing & visual artist and  I was in NYC to record some songs, it was great having a place that was both in walking distance and a short bus ride away from where I was working on my project. There are many nice stores nearby, such as an art supply store I like that's in the area I live in, I was pleasantly surprised to see one in Brooklyn. and I was able to easily find tasty vegetarian food to eat!   The apartment smells good and the paintings were BEAUTIFUL! They are one of the reasons I selected Nicole's,  to be surrounded by artwork. There is a BIG wonderful tree in the front that helps provide shade and some privacy.  Another one of the reasons I was in Brooklyn was to buy a new harp and I needed to replace my strings on it, after arriving I realized I had left my wire cutters and asked Nicole if she had a pair I could use and she did. I got to meet her in person and she is very sweet.   People in the neighborhood were respectful and friendly to me.  I felt very welcomed and would certainly stay here again!

I was in town to help our 23 year old move into the neighborhood. Nicole is a superb host. Warm text greeting when I arrived, well wishes when I was leaving. Everything I needed was in walking distance - shops, restaurants for the foodie in me, green space to be in a little nature, and public transportation to get anywhere in Brooklyn or a quick subway ride into the city. Quiet street. Nicole gave me the privacy I needed during a stressful time for me. The energy in the apartment feels calm and peaceful without a lot of clutter, allowing me to think clearly without distraction. The bonus bedroom was great to have just in case I needed an extra person to stay with me, and it served as a perfect work space for my purposes. Very clean and organized. Very spacious. Plenty of closet space. Bright rooms with wonderful skylights throughout providing a lot of natural light - no need to turn on the lights during the day. Nice wood floors. So happy to take a bath in a nice clean bathtub after a long day. All the kitchen basics. I felt very comfortable cooking there. Good communication with a whiteboard and signs for information so I knew how Nicole wanted me to do things in the apartment - where to put recycling, etc. Everything was even better than described. Thank you Nicole -  I will definitely be back.
Awesome place!! Very clean and comfortable and the host is really helpful! The area is full of good restaurants and bodegas so good food is always close! This place is a steal for the price!!

HOUSING TO AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!  Accommodation was easy to find. 1 hour from the center of NY by transport (trains, buses, metro, walking...) If we could believe that everything would go well, we were wrong.. Several big problems upon our arrival No heating or in any case almost non-existent when we arrived: we had to ask the host for the heating to be turned on (19-20 degrees, not great either), especially since it was -7 degrees outside and the insulation of the windows and the roof are almost non-existent. The paint is not finished, which gives the impression of dirt. Electric cables connected to the sockets are placed directly on the various radiators in the apartment without being fixed. The dishes are almost non-existent and dirty: - 3 plates - 3 cutlery - 2 worn and mostly dirty pans - a few mismatched "glasses" which look more like jars of jam than anything else - lots of spices of all kinds, only all expired for at least 3 years and some 7-8 years... We also had the chance to observe traces of humidity on various ceilings Only two bulbs out of five work in the living room The mattresses are of good quality, but the sheets are worn, stained and there is no duvet in the master bedroom (still -7 degrees outside), and a small extra duvet in the small bedroom. As a cover we only had a bedspread in one of the bedrooms and a blanket in the living room.  The living room windows overlook a garden, this one filled with trash cans and waste of all kinds... When we pointed this out to AirBnb and they contacted the host, she came to see us one morning at 8:30 a.m. being extremely unpleasant.   A real shame, we left earlier than planned.  We still don’t understand how it can be a “superhost” with such good ratings…

Although I never met Ryan face to face the process was smooth throughout with the check-in and out managed by his friend.  The apartment is great and large by NYC standards! Very cool little neighbourhood with some nice eateries and indoor markets.  It seems the neighbourhood is improving and I didn't at any time feel unsafe.  If you want a spacious well positioned apartment then I recommend Ryan's place for you!
Cold, uncomfortable, creepy entrance, lock box was difficult to open.

the space is affordable and in a great location in williamsburg. it’s only separated from the owner’s unit by several curtains/blankets - not an actual door, but it was fine since they respected our privacy. there is definitely a rat infestation in the ceiling so i wouldn’t suggest this stay to any light sleepers or those scared of rodents.

Ok listing for someone travelling solo for a short trip. One major issue was the host designated this listing as free parking on premises, but the host informed me as I was arriving that I would need to find street parking, which I spent almost an hour trying to find in the dark. I purposely booked this for the parking on premises so this was a big disappointment.  Apartment was small but clean, nice that I had it to myself. Note there is no kitchen, you are provided a hot plate and some plates/utensils, which was fine since I ate out most of the time. Bed was comfortable and clean. Surrounding gate provided added security to the premise. Walking distance from a Walgreens, gas station, and multiple good restaurants. About a ten minute walk to the nearest subway station which I used frequently. The area itself was ok, don't think it was dangerous but it's a big city so just practice street smarts.
Wonderful hospitality, thoughtful gifts and gestures, CLEAN, cozy, and I never felt unsafe. You are in good hands here and I would so stay again in the future.

I can’t stress enough how great of an experience this was. Me and my friend came here with the intentions of getting a preview before we moved here from NC and was always looking forward to coming home to this delightful stay after a long day in the city! Beautiful experience!

Clean, bright, and airy, Miso's place was wonderful.  It is ideally situated in the bustling neighborhood of Bushwick; central to just about everywhere I needed to go.  The check-in process was a breeze and keyless entry was a stress reliever.

Located conveniently near 2 main subway stops. Unfortunately its quite far from any of the noteworthy food spots. Plan ahead to navigate the subway effectively if Cronuts or Katz's was in your itinerary. Rooms were fully stocked with laundry detergent, dish soap and pump style shampoo, conditioner and soap dispensers in case you didnt bring any. If you run out, you can grab supplies from the front desk.  The luggage lockers are very convenient as is the roof (which is the only place you can find a bathroom). The roof served as a good spot for us to plug in and plan our next sojourns. I'm sure it must be nice in the summertime.  Slight complaint: there was an outlet that simply didnt work, and in one socket was jammed a broken-off electric prong. This seems like an electric/fire hazard. Second is just that the refrigerator stunk bad. It tended to fill the room with the smell whenever we opened it to store our drinks.  All in all a good stay! We never felt unsafe.

Don’t recommend for more than 2 nights. The apartment showed in the listing does not match the apartment that was provided for my stay. It is very important for me to have a quite and comfortable place to stay as I often work from home and since COVID my apartment became my permanent office , therefore my first question to all hosts  has always been is it quite and in this case I was reassured that the area where my windows are facing is an enclosed courtyard like shown in the listing photo . Instead of a promised enclosed court yard  the windows of my apartment looked out on a construction side in the middle of 53 street all through out my stay which lasted 33 nights  (I have picture proof)  Also I did not receive the information needed in time (48 hours before my stay as it was stated by the host )  Upon further investigation it was admitted by the host that my check in information was sent to the wrong person , there for I felt like my safety was compromised witch caused me to have  severe enxiety during my stay .  When I pointed out that my information was sent to the wrong email the host chose to completely dismiss this information and still failed to send me the check in information without me reminding them to do so . I ended up getting the information a few hours before I needed to check in which made it extremely inconvenient and hectic. (proof in my screenshots if AirBnb needs it)  After all I was charged a good amount for a cleaning and hotel fee when this host didn’t even provide such necessaries as a dish sponge or paper towels, when I attempted to resolve the issue with the host and asked if they provided cleaning supplies for long stays to keep the apartment looking presentable I was told that they do not provide any cleaning supplies in a very rude manner. In the listing it was stated that the WiFi was included however when I moved in I quickly realized that it was not promised because I had to use my mobile data to work from home for the majority of my long term stay as WiFi was super slow. I checked reviews on other apartments from this host and it’s other complaints about WiFi speed. The reason I did not file a claim sooner is that I was scared to not have a place to stay until my complaint was reviewed in the middle of a pandemic I do not have extra money to spend on paying twice for my reservations. Location is great - if you need couple nights in the middle of Manhattan it might works for you.

Left my shoes inside of the closet ,called an hour later when I was on my way to the airport asking to keep them for me so I can pick them up later.Was never found .And shoes were there .Shoes was stolen and hotel was never able to help me with this. It is  not even a hotel ,it is a dorm .

They are professional scammers. The riverview accommodation I booked had a heating failure from the first day. I was forced to move to another room (no window, cheaper room). The heating was not fixed, I requested a refund. Sonder gladly promised a refund. I trusted Sonder. After that I moved to another hotel (I didn't want to stay long in a room without a window). After that, they did not reply to my messages. When I asked Airbnb to arbitrate, the refundable deadline had already passed. Sonder gives guests peace of mind and prevents them from contacting Airbnb. In the end I didn't get a refund. They lie. I will not use Sonder and Airbnb in the future.
A great place to get away from stress and relax like home away from home.

Room with no real window (deceiving photos) and very rude people at the reception and all around. Rought neighbourhood so be aware of strangers offering you drugs around and homeless people (they are actually the kindest). You can find better for less. The only good thing is Anna (admin) and her intentions to make you feel comfortable. Although they fall short given the limitations she has. Sorry bot not recommended for more than 2 days or so. I stayed for 7... and counted every day!
I can’t stress enough how PERFECT this location is!!!

Ideal for solo travelers who wants a very clean and quiet place in Hell's Kitchen. The description is accurate, and the location is awesome. Even though the area is really popular day and night, Ebul's unit is very seclusive and free from any noise from the street. He cares a lot of the hygiene, which is no doubt a big plus during the pandemic if you want to travel safe. It's close to Laundromats (two from 1 block), pharmacies (DR one block away), and lots of good food. For anyone who's planning to work remotely a bit during the stay, you'll find strong WiFi here provided by Specturm 200/10 Mbps down/up. It's good for any work and entertainment that most will need on the go.  The room has a window with relevantly limited light exposure and a brand new A/C unit on it, which should be good for most.  All in all, it's a steal for the price in the heart of New York.

Very well put together Airbnb apt. Good location, speedy WiFi and good desk space. Balcony is great if you want to work out there too (in COVID we were working from home).   You do get a LOT of comms before you arrive - make sure you pay attention to the address as it's different to the one Airbnb gives you (a building site).   We had some issues with the elevator which ended up with our dog having a panic attack but Angelo (possibly someone from an Airbnb management company?) was very responsive.   Overall would recommend.
Great stay! Quick walk from the subway. Don't be scared by the area, it is not bad at all and was close to some lovely local spots. Recommend the stay.
This place is a bit of a scam because no tv and soap and only 1 towel and u always have to see people as you leave.

Absolute worst stay we have ever experienced. Ultimately, we had to fight for a refund after mold exposure at this property. The experience was unpleasant from check in so I will start at the beginning. Upon arrival we found the driveway was so steep it is a hassle to park and back out of each day. We were also offered drugs by the upstairs tenant who appears to be the neighborhood drug dealer. The unit also smells like pot especially in the bathroom which is likely why the host has three different air fresheners in there to try to mask the smell. The unit was warm and humid and we ended up having to buy an extra fan to try to keep cool during our stay. The dryer is obstructed by a rack so you have to lift up the rack and pull the dryer open each time you want to use it. The right side of the fridge is practically unusable as it is so close to the wall that you're left trying to squeeze to get things from the left side of the fridge. The sheets are old, pilled and scratchy and there was a shooting and subsequent murder on the block over from us during our stay. The cleanliness of the listing does not match the listing photos. Everything may look clean from afar but when you look closer there is dust and grime on most surfaces. My husband and two young kids as well as myself began to have respiratory issues and upon further inspection we found mold in the portable a/c unit used in the bedroom, the gasket lining on the fridge doors as well as the shower in the bathroom. Upon finding the mold, we immediately notified our host and requested a refund as we would need to check out ASAP earlier than expected and take care of our health after the mold exposure and were met with nothing but rude responses. We asked for a full refund as our health has now been impacted and we would need to find last minute accomodations. My husband who just had surgery this week is having the worst symptoms as the a/c unit in the bedroom blows directly on the bed on the side he was laying on and was filled with mold. He also was not fit to have to lift our heavy luggage to pack the car as he still has his drainage tubes in and incisions that have not healed which is why we booked a long-term stay in the first place. The host initially only offered a partial refund and stated the previous guests did not have an issue and was adamant that we were lying and that the pictures were not of their unit. I took videos and photos of each area as proof as well as videos showing the surrounding areas of the mold as proof it is the same unit that we stayed in. My iphone also records the timestamp and location of each photo as further proof that the photos of the mold were from the host's unit. I opened a claim with Airbnb who ultimately ended up siding with us as they saw all evidence I presented was accurate and truthful and issued a full refund. I also took photos upon leaving that showed that we cleaned up after ourselves before checkout, washed all dishes and laundered the towels so that the host cannot say we were unpleasant or dirty guests. We did everything on our end to be gracious guests, left everything exactly the way that we found it, put up with multiple inconveniences without complaints until our health was affected and we were ultimately let down by our host who showed no concern for the mold that we found or for our health. The host then harassed us multiple times that they would be showing up when we planned to checkout without any prior instructions that we would need to meet upon departure. We did not stay and wait for their arrival to the unit for checkout as my husband had a doctors appointment we needed to get to and again we were not notified that we would need to meet for checkout which felt unsafe with such a hostile host. Please look for another place to stay if you care about your health and safety.

If I had to describe my experience with the USB Area/ St. Albans Airbnb in one word, it would be TRAUMATIC.   I booked this reservation for my parents (an elderly couple in their late 50s and 60s). I did not spend a night at the rental, even though the reservation was for three (3) people.  USB Area/ St. Albans Airbnb was selected because it offered amenities vital to my parents' comfort during their long overdue vacation. Kindly note that this was their first trip to the United States of America, so they approached it with grandeur expectations and childish gleefulness.   Upon our arrival, I contacted the Host about some cleanliness concerns I had noticed in conjunction with an unplugged cable issue. The Host indicated that she was out of State and attributed these noticeable discrepancies to the inattentiveness of the Cleaning Lady.   While exploring their temporary home away from home, we decided to venture into the backyard to explore the private backyard and outdoor furnishing, mentioned in the listing. Deplorable would not do what we saw as any justice. The gazebo was a tattered remnant of past grandeur, the chairs were dust crusted, and their cushions were soiled and haphazardly scattered. It was a very disappointing sight clearly that the Host needed a replacement for this inefficient Cleaning Lady.  The apartment has one window, and the dated air conditioning unit was insufficient for cooling the apartment, especially on the days we were experiencing heat waves.   On Day 3, my parent became impatience about the cable issue, so I contacted the Host for an update. The Host indicated that she would provide us with a refund for the first two nights for the inconveniences caused and visited on Day 4, to address the cable situation. We were not on the premise, however, in good faith, approval was granted for the Host to enter the rental to rectify the cable issue. After she left, the host mentioned that during her unaccompanied visit, she noticed that the refrigerator door was left ajar (keep this in mind).   At this point, my parents would have already made their grocery run: my father is diabetic, is on medication, and has dietary restrictions, which connotes that the refrigerator was stocked with perishable groceries necessary for the preparation of his meals. It is highly unlikely that my parents would willingly choose to jeopardize the integrity of the medication, or the fresh ingredients needed to prepare their meals (that’s what eventually transpired due to the rental being without a functional refrigerator for 4 days).   Day 5 is where everything went left. There was a problem with the refrigerator, due to the hassle encountered while reporting the cable issue, I delayed raising this new issue with the Host until I was sure that it was necessary, MAJOR LAPSE IN JUDGEMENT.   The Host came out on Day 9 and by Day 10 it was evident the refrigerator was damaged.   Subsequently, the Host kept repeating that she noticed the refrigeration was left ajar when she first visited.   Side note: I will never grant another Host permission to enter the rental during my absence. Naivety can no longer be an excuse.  At this stage, the Host became tumultuous. Threats of cancellation were being thrown around, it was close to mid-day and the Host was demanding that my parents leave by 3 pm. I panicked and started looking for alternative rentals. Of course, with such short notice, my efforts were futile, so my parents and I sat anxiously awaiting the dreaded message, from Airbnb, about the Host Cancelling our reservation. It never came, instead, we got another irate call from the Host enquiring about our decision to Cancel, I calmly indicated that we were not the ones who opt to cancel (at this stage, my mother was sobbing uncontrollably, and my father was trying his best to console her).    In my effort to defuse an already tense situation, I implored the Host to wait until a technician's visit before making a final decision.    After the technician's visit, the Host requested reimbursement for the damages incurred, and of course, I declined the request because I had a video recording of the visiting Technicians clearly stating that the damages to the refrigerator were due to “Wear & Tear” and could not have occurred over 3 months (my parents had only spent 10 days at this point).  Amazingly, during the Host submission for reimbursement, the Technician’s Report was presented, and strange enough the report stated that the refrigerator compression had gone bad and attributed the “door being left opened” as a possible cause (sounds familiar?). I explained to the Host that the Technician told me something completely different (at that point I decided to not mention that I had video evidence to support my claim) and indicated to her that I was willing to have a 3-way discussion with her and the Technical since it’s clear that something foul was afoot. The Host refused and proceeded to present the Claim to Airbnb Resolution Center.   By 9 pm that evening, after presenting the requisite evidence to the representatives at the Airbnb Resolution Center, I received a correspondence clearly stating that we were not liable for the damages.   On one hand, I was relieved but on the other, I was anxious because the Host’s action and unprofessionalism had already traumatized my parents.  The new refrigerator was delivered on day 14, which means that the rental was without a suitable amenity for 4 days (a mini refrigerator was left at the front door, by the Host, but since she didn’t have the professionalism to knock on the front door, present it, plug it in and ensure it was working, my traumatized parents took in into the house and gently put it away, they were afraid of being accused of being responsible for any other damages). I stayed here for 6 weeks during the summer while working remotely and LOVED it! Lauren’s place is bright, clean, comfortable, and incredibly quiet. It’s on the fourth floor of a small building that feels very safe. Lauren provided clear instructions for how everything worked was responsive with any questions I had.  The space: The apartment is more than enough space for one person, and could fit two comfortably. The furniture fits the space perfectly and it all felt new.  The place was spotless when I arrived and there was plenty of space for things throughout the apartment. Very comfortable bed (I will be buying the same mattress!), enormous walk-in closet in the bedroom. The living room has a nice desk by the window where I worked remotely 9-5 each day. I had occasional Wifi reliability issues when videoconferencing, but got an Ethernet cable to plug into the router directly below the desk and then had fast and reliable internet. The kitchen has a good amount of counter space and is well appointed with pots, pans, spices. The bathroom has a lot of storage for New York and I had no trouble with water pressure or temperature. There is an AC window unit that is Wifi-controlled (really nice to be able to turn it on while walking home) and the ceiling fans cool down the place well.  Location: It’s located on a quiet residential street but is just one block from restaurants and shopping, and about 8-10 min from 3 different subway lines (ACE, L, and 123). It’s also extremely close to the High Line, Whitney Museum, Little Island, and Chelsea Market. You have a view out of the back of the building (so it’s even more quiet) of One World Trade Center. There is a grocery store 5 min away and a CVS 8 min away. You can walk down into the West Village, up into Chelsea, great location!   Final thoughts: I can’t stress enough how QUIET this place is, for any city, especially New York! It’s an extremely peaceful, cozy, well-lit space. It was a great place to stay for the summer while working remote and exploring the city, I highly recommend it!
Rosa's apartment was warm, inviting, clean, and at a wonderful location. I really enjoyed staying in her apartment and suspect you might too!
Very clean and close to subway. Area is otherwise looking a little sketchy, but no issues while we were visiting. Blinds in one bedroom were missing.

The apartment overall was okay and nice. I wouldn’t describe the stay as “elegant” at all, we typically stay in higher end places when we travel and we chose this spot because there was a balcony we could enjoy as it is more rare to find a place with one.   I believe this is a property the owner lives in and just puts it on Airbnb to let guests stay whenever it works for him which is fine if the apartment wasn’t full of personal items. Closets were pretty full with the home owners stuff, and lots of stuff laying around that is not typical of a normal airbnb.    Pros- balcony was nice to hang out on when the weather was great  The space worked well for our group to be able to enjoy time together without staying in separate locations  The beds are comfy and the pillows are nice too super happy with that especially since we were staying more than just a couple of days  I would give the host a 10/10 on communication, always was helpful to answer questions and be flexible with us on our checkout which we appreciated   Cons- besides the things already stated above the main one is the area the Airbnb itself is in. We weren’t familiar with the area so we booked just based off of distance between things we were going to be doing in town. Our group was fearful to go outside once it got dark as it gets pretty sketchy at night so generally only would go outside quickly to get groceries or to Uber to the locations around town we were visiting. Overall the area ended up not being an issue for us and it worked out but definitely just something to note.

My husband and I stayed in Nat's apartment for a period of 2 months and we really enjoyed it! It is as modern and comfortable as shown in the pictures. I especially liked the bathroom with its clean and properly working shower. It is located in a Dominican neighbourhood with the subway within walking distance. We have never felt unsafe. Since the apartment is located at the back of the building, you're not disturbed by noice from the streets (since Dominicans like to play really loud music ;)). Nat was very easy to communicate with. We would definitely recommend!

Qing's place is a steal for the space and price! The place was cute, clean and comfy. Definitely one of the better Airbnb's in the area and I would definitely stay again. Easy to find, easy to check-in, and easy to check out.
Maria and Brooke are as sweet as can be! Everything was very easy and stress free! We will deff be considering them again next time we are in New York!

On the plus side, Teki’s home is cute and cozy and is good value for the money. We really loved her style and found the bed very comfortable and her communication clear. On the other hand, we didn’t always feel great walking around the neighborhood at night. We had a few sketchy encounters and we walked just about everywhere. Maybe we just got unlucky, but it’s definitely not in a posh area. We thought it would be closer to a train stop, it’s about a mile walk to the closest station going into Manhattan or around BK.
Great stay- location is central to Subway and grocery options. Neighborhood is up and coming with ongoing improvements- don't be afraid to give it a try. Facility is amazing and a great value!

Our stay in Riverdale was just what we needed. The location is great, especially for the price. Not having to spend 40 minutes or $40 on a parking space was fantastic and made our late check-in stress free.  The space was a great spot to land after a day of traveling or exploring the city. Lyndsey was also quick to respond "no problem" when we asked last minute if having another guest would be an issue.   Definetly would suggest staying here

Marla's place was everything we needed! We came to town for a stressful family situation, and Marla's efficient check-in, well-appointed, easy, easy place made it so our accommodations didn't add a bit of stress. She provided clear, complete information, timely check-ins, and was very responsive to our one question. Additionally, the neighborhood is fantastic, the apartment is quiet, and the beds, linens, supplies were all great. Thanks!

Very clean, quiet, and light-filled space with modern kitchen and a great shower. It was perfectly located for us near our family but it would be convenient for anyone who wanted to walk to markets, a drug store, etc. Michael is a kind and super accommodating host and was quick to respond anytime we needed anything. Couldn’t ask for more!

Pros: Location and apartment are ok  Cons: There were few more issues which were resolved by host and Airbnb, but the  biggest disappointment was check in experience.  I don’t see similar review, so maybe other people had different experience (host was busy at that day, haha). Maybe I’m staying a lot in Hilton and Marriott properties with digital check in option and have high standards , but during covid era even Airbnb hosts started to offer contactless check in, release form and other stuff can be done online. This particular host did not offer that option, so from the beginning I knew what I’m signing up for, but we did not expect this:  1) It was too much pressure with check in. We like to relax on Saturday and don’t feel constant pressure. We usually arrive at the hotel in any time, usually at night, we like to travel and make spontaneous stops during drive.  But with Airbnb we do our best to arrive sooner (when it is not contactless check in). Host messaged and called us very early, we are from California and he saw it on our profile , but still thought it is ok to make calls at 7am, there were few more calls/messages until we arrived.  I understand that host want to deal with the guests as soon as possible and proceed with his stuff, but I don’t feel it should be done at the guest’s expense, especially if you are the one, who opted in for personal check in.  2) In our family I’m the one who do check in and my husband is staying in the car watching luggage. When we arrived, he dropped me off on the wrong side of the road and I went to apartment from there ( host knew about my arrival). I got into apartment and host was not anywhere to be found, I called him and he told me he is outside. I waited a little and then went outside to look for him.  Instead of meeting me inside and do quick check in, he tracked down  and approached our car. He offered help with the luggage, my husband told him “no thanks, we are good”, but he still grabbed our luggage and took it. It was odd and too much into your face, then later we realised that he was just checking out our car under excuse to help. He wanted to make sure that only 2 of us arrived ( no additional hidden guests).  It was unpleasant to be treated as criminals, when we did not do anything and I felt like our privacy was violated.  3) When we were inside, he told us we need to sign release form, otherwise we cannot check in. We were tired, but still inspected apartment somehow. We signed the form, but mentioned that if there are any issues pop up later, it doesn’t mean anything ( Guess what? Issues popped up later)   4) Host asked for my spouse’s id, I provided my id and it should be enough  5) In the final,  he started to do walk through. While some people like it, I feel it should be optional. You should ask people , if they wanna walk through or not.  a) it takes my time b) I quickly forget what I was told, so instructions written in Airbnb or on the fridge work better in my opinion.   Conclusion: too much pressure and unnecessary communication, not pleasant check in experience

Had a great stay at Ricardo’s apartment. The apartment itself is great, super clean, very nicely organized and everything works fantastic! Ricardo is super friendly, responsive and helps out. I’d give the apartment and Ricardo 5/5!   The only problem is the area which isn’t great, feels unsafe, I was approached multiple times by weird people on the street - I guess it’s just part of NYC / Brooklyn type areas :) otherwise great!

Good location in LES. Two bedrooms and two bathrooms were comfortable for two couples. Common area/kitchen are small but probably average for NYC. Alejandra also allowed us to check-in early, which was nice. However, the apartment was below 50 degrees when we arrived. It is completely heated using space heaters and you can't move the space heaters without electrical breaker tripping (breaker box is behind picture frame in the hallway). It felt a bit dangerous and it was annoying to wait hours to heat the apartment to a reasonable temperature when we arrived. Then managing the temperature was not easy for the rest of the trip either.

Great location in Chinatown within walking distance to Little Italy and Nolita as well. Great restaurants and boutiques in area as well. Check in and check out process was seamless. Loft looks just like the pictures as well. It is quirky and well designed. Overall a nice home base while you are exploring the city. For seasoned travelers or people who are in the city a lot, this is a gem!  Note: If you are a nervous solo traveler who worries about walking alongside people with visible mental health issues on the street or if you do not like a sketchier vibe this may not the neighborhood for you.

The accommodation was amazing! It looked exactly like the photos and description in the ad. It fully deserves its 5 stars! The apartment is very well equipped, everything was there. It is located in a very quiet area, easy to access, 5 minutes from a metro station, which was very nice! The hosts are responsive and very friendly. There is even personalized attention upon arrival, which is really nice after several hours of flight. We feel at home in this accommodation 😌 If we come back here, we won't hesitate at all to book this accommodation again, we won't waste time looking for another one, this one is really perfect, go for it without hesitation!

Beware, this listing is not a condominium as stated by the host. I normally don’t write long reviews, so please be patient.  This is located in a rental building with regular tenants ( nothing wrong with is ). This wouldn’t be an issue if only not misrepresented by the host. This was the most stressful Airbnb experience pre and post check. First, she changed the check-in time from 3pm to 10p to 8pm a day before arrival because she had an event to attend to and were informed we were going to be locked out until the following day. What? we managed to barely make it on time after the flight delay,  them, when I arrived at the building and knocked on her door, I was left waiting outside before opening the door, then, she had your belongings including food that were cooking during the time we paid for ( she should have had her stuff out by 3:pm regardless of the time we were arriving, if it’s within the time specified, I noticed dirty dishes  in the sick, cool ( she washed them while I was there), I could have reported it. The TV and internet didn’t work.  She sent correct wifi log in. I should have reported right away,  we were too exhausted from the trip plus had a toddler, the floor was dirty, yes it was I took pics and recorded. I recorded it just in case. I been staying at Airbnb for years and never had an issue.  There were no chairs as shown on the pictures except for 3 beach chairs (1 was broken), had a pet dog and didn’t disclose, the TV never worked and the host never followed up with me to find out if it worked. The day before check out, she changed the time from 12pm to 11am. This was my personal experience!

Ed is an incredibly responsive, kind, and helpful host, and his apartment is lovely. There are so many thoughtful touches throughout the home - we only wish we could have stayed longer! I can't stress enough how comforted we were to arrive to find wipes, sanitizer, and a truly clean environment. We felt at ease right away and were able to immediately relax and enjoy ourselves. We highly recommend this very special apartment in a wonderful neighborhood.

My fiancée and I stayed at Lindsey's flat for 10 days and it was absolutely incredible! The apartment was just as pictured and is just wonderfully designed: the use of space and lighting was great during the day and during cozy evenings, and it really felt like a wonderfully warm home. The apartment also came equipped with everything you'd need for stay in New York, with ample fridge space, the comfiest mattress I've ever slept on, and a great shower/bath combo - the Disney+ and HBO Max were also fantastic additions.  Every time we met one of Lindsey's neighbours in the hallway they were very lovely, and the apartment itself is so quiet. I've never felt so safe staying anywhere in a foreign country, especially somewhere I haven't been before.  The apartment area is really fantastic too! We felt 100% safe and were within walking distance of grocery stores, a CVS, a Target, and Central Park itself. As we were so close to subway stops - and with ample taxis and ubers available - we managed to travel around New York safely and quickly from the apartment and never felt unsafe, which is a bonus as an LGBTQ+ couple. Another bonus is that there are loads of citibikes and rental bikes available nearby if you want to cycle and there's some lovely areas for walking (or even taking a boat out rowing in Central Park!)  Our check-in and check-out were very smooth and Lindsey very kindly sent us an information pack beforehand via email that was extremely helpful with this and with suggesting places to go to (getting coffee at Ralph's is a must!). Lindsey really went above and beyond as a host: when our flight was severely delayed on our last day she helped us with baggage which was a really lovely thing to do, and she was always fantastic with communication.   This was our first time in New York and I'm so glad we chose to stay at Lindsey's. We'd definitely love to stay again in the future and highly recommend it. The apartment is gorgeous and is the perfect place to stay whether you're in New York for business or on holiday - it really gave us a feel of living in the city which we absolutely loved. Huge thank you to Lindsey for being so awesome, we couldn't have asked for a better host! :)

DO NOT RENT THIS PLACE UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES!!!!!!!!!! Very unsafe and detrimental to your mental health. One of the boarders assaulted me, and I had to get the police involved in. You also have boarders who steal-food and personal belongings. The same boarder that assaulted me also broke into another boarder's room, harassed another boarder until he moved out, and used discriminatory language towards both of them. Calling them a f****t, a r***rd, etc. Threatened to kill them, tampering with their food and belongings. This same boarder also dumped my food out in the sink, and as a result, I moved not only out of the house, but New York completely. You have boarders who use the bathroom and do not flush. Both for the Number 1 and 2. You have aggressive, nasty boarders. Lastly, a lot of the boarders are just mean with bad vibes. They will not even say hello to you when you say hello them. This is a poisonous environment that you do not a place you want to be in at all. After having left, I am doing so much better mentally. Save yourself the grief-DO NOT RENT THIS AIRBNB!

Annie does not live there. Lee does. Which is very misleading. Only Lee lives at apartment.  I told Lee all of this so he is aware.   The Apt: The place generally was dirty looking, smelly, and not what I consider clean.   The kitchen is make-shift and old. It is definitely not “The kitchen is fitted with modern stainless steel appliances and silverware, kettle toaster, microwave & coffee maker.”  Amenities wise: I do not know of: iron, ironing board, toiletries (there is toilet paper), hair dryer, night lamp, hypoallergenic linen & towels?    So apt appears to have 3 bedrooms and 2 baths. And is split on 2 sides.  So Lee has his side bedroom and bathroom.  Then there are 2 rooms to rent on Airbnb and you share with the other airbnb.    The room I brought my own towel and sheets.– to cover me.  And I brought Clorox wipes to wipe down the room.  The headboard to bed is gross.  The bedroom was freezing. Minimal - no heat.    Then there are 2 rooms to rent on Airbnb and they share 1.  The bathroom is very clean – and cleanest part of house – so that is saving grace.  There was no hot water when I showered though. So low/ minimal heat and cold shower.   As for covid protocols  -	Everyone wears masks in common areas.  -	No temperature check.    I think they donate some proceeds and this pays the rent. So it comes off money goes to employee Lee  to feed homeless and pay his rent.  Would I stay here again – no way. Do I think it was worth the money – no way.  I’m from New York and I know what real estate costs and what apartments look like.    It felt hostel- like to me.  I actually would prefer a partial refund.

PLEASE RESD THIS BEFORE BOOKING!!  Some things we dealt with and have issues with while we stayed...  First, we had  NO toilet paper for almost a Whole Day...we had to go and buy some because the host didn’t respond to us when we asked him for where we could find some....  The “head of the bed “ is gross and without any cleaning at all... lots of hairs and dirt from past guests   There’s SO much noise at night even with the window closed...had to buy some ear plugs. Also there’s almost no shade from sunlight so you get sunlight from the sunrise till sunset  The windows are super stiff and it can barley open   The bed has some weak spots and broke at some point  No common areas, the host works and watches movies on the “desk/living room” and there is no “regular” kitchen whatsoever   No likability or even communication with the host...we communicate with Annie and she’s not even in the apartment or even met her. And with Lee we barley talked...when we welcomed us he could even say “hi! How are you? Where are you from” or ANYTHING like that...He literally just waved us to come in and gave us the keys. And when I told Annie that I wanted to talk to her about the situation in person she told me that I should call her instead and later didn’t answer my messages in 13 hours +  and even after that I told her everything that had been going on...no responde  We got out at our 3rd night (payed 6), went to a hotel instead   I will ask for a refund and hope I get it

I stayed at 2 different units in this building for several weeks working nearby. The location was the draw and was even more convenient than I had anticipated. The building staff were friendly but not intrusive, and Axel is the most responsive building manager I have ever encountered anywhere. As compared to rooms in the dozens of NYC hotels I've stayed at, both units were very spacious and well equipped with a full size kitchen, although the washer-dryer in neither unit was clean enough for me to want to use (not a huge problem since there are plenty of laundry services). This not the type of design-forward property you may be accustomed to finding on Airbnb, and there is wear showing here and there (broken but functional handle on the microwave door, broken window shade), and the one unit was much cleaner with newer furnishings (most noticeably, a much firmer mattress), but everything worked that I needed (fast wifi throughout the unit, well lit workspace, good water pressure with plenty of hot water) or was fixed promptly when it didn't. It was important to me that the building and neighborhood felt safe to walk around at any time of day alone. Many of the residents are longer term so they seemed respectful of the place; I never had any issues with noise from neighbors, and the communal areas were tidy. You also are given a proper address so you can have packages and mail delivered to you if you wish, which I didn't need but is a convenience that not all Airbnbs offer.

My stay at Sita Cozy Budget Private Room was exactly what I was looking for. Both Annie and Lee were attentive, helpful, and friendly, and they were fast to respond when I contacted them. The room is small but private and cozy. There is also a shared space, and the whole apartment was clean and warm (yay). It's also awesome to know that my money will be used for a program that feeds the homeless. I would recommend this Airbnb to anyone who wants to spend their daytime in Manhattan and needs a place to crash at night.

Great location, very easy getting access to the spot and checking in and out, so this stay was chill and didn’t stress me out at all. And Bianca was so friendly and gave great suggestions for spots to check out nearby. I felt very safe during my stay which was probably the most important factor for me being able to relax. There’s a shared bathroom and kitchen, so that can feel a little cluttered if you need more space to spread out, but that’s New York! Plenty of space in the room to myself so that made it cool! Also the doggy Eva is a sweetheart.
Small, kinda dirty and sketchy, weird guy lives there, very cluttered
a nice spot to chill and relax for the moment away from any kind of stress

Stayed at Annie and Lees in the past and it seems to get worse with time. First, the place itself is unkept and very loose. Feels like you are stepping into some random persons home as opposed to an Airbnb. There was moldy food in the refrigerator as well, which should have been thrown out. The shower door is still unsteady. The shower is small and cramped with poor water pressure. The bed has no box spring with several broken slats, not to mention very uneven and uncomfortable. There were dark circles around all the electrical, which after doing some research, usually indicates incorrect wiring which can be very dangerous. And last but not least.. THE BUG BITES. My partner and I have never had issues with any sort of bugs in the past.. until staying here. On the second night we were both scratching several red itchy bites. Host denied ever having bugs. Pay a little for something better and avoid staying here. The hosts clearly don’t care for this place at all so why should you.
Clean, private , host is very respectful, overall good stay, hotels in the area are very sketchy  this is much better

One of the worst host I experienced so far on Airbnb. I wouldn’t recommend a homeless person who had nowhere to go to this host. Confirmed my reservations but didn’t have the place clean and didn’t reach out to inform on the situation.
Expect little empathy from the hosts, the only positive thing about their place is that they allocate a portion of their rent to people in need and homeless

Our stay was nice, the location is amazing and check in process was easy. The shower has hot water and is very clean. Otherwise there was other people who stayed in the apartment we did not hear them at all nor had to share a bathroom with them. The only things that you will hear is the nightlife and traffic outside at night time per usual. It did not bother us. I will mention that we had to show proof of vaccination when we checked in. This was not an issue for us but just an FYI for those booking.   Plus side: You get a key to lock your bedroom door and secure your belongings. We were also able to drop our bags off at 11 AM before checking in at 3 PM.  Con: We were afraid that we were going to break the bed not that we were disruptive or Messing around just because the bed frame was old and falling apart I would suggest being cautious. The only thing I will mention is that the room is very small I was not able to open my large suitcase on the floor to pick out my clothes or get my items out ; I had to do it in the common area.

The accommodation is very well located! Perfect for a short stay in NYC. However, the noise from the street is very unpleasant, especially on weekends (loud music in the street) and as the room is poorly insulated we had a lot of trouble sleeping the first evening.

Jo has been very accommodating and flexible especially when I had a late flight out from the city. She was happy to allow you to keep your luggage in the kitchen area while you went out to do last minute shopping etc. Her area is very convenient and walkable to many different attractions which is a bug plus point. The neighborhood is pretty legit and not sketchy at all cause I was a lone traveler and I did not feel uncomfortable at any point. Lastly Jo is extremely responsive, you'll get a reply within 30-60min which I appreciate a lot.

A "hotel" without any of the "hotel" services. We didn't get any cleaning, no intelligent communication, no positive response to any of our needs! All the answers we got started with “unfortunately”. I've traveled all over the world and nowhere I've stayed has 11am check out. They did not accept our late check out request as well, like everything else. Even though it was 11 am check out time, the cleaning women knocked on our door intermittently from 9.30 in the morning and drove us crazy! We stayed on the street in extremely hot weather on Saturday with our 5 suitcases until our evening flight…because they refused our request to keep our luggage at the hotel for 2-3 hours. They did not send the information e-mails until we asked and when we asked, they also lied that they had sent them. Check-in time is 4 pm! NONSENSE! It was a trip with homeless people sleeping in front of the hotel. They put 2 toilet papers in the room, they don't renew it like a joke! We stayed for 3 weeks and we regret it very much. We were disgraced with our money. Never again!

I’m absolutely in love with this air bnb. Everything in the description holds up. Starting with the best part: Benson. Why else are you reading this? He is so sweet and chill and the best answer to a stressful day! Or at least a long day in the city.  Speaking of, the Halsey metro is super close. You can see it from the apartment (it’s heard as a very low rumble inside). It was super easy to jump on the A train and get to Manhattan. Usually one transfer to the J. Average ride there was 45min. There are, of course, Citi bikes to rent around the corner. Also around the corner is Rite Aid which is convenient. And some low key food, shops, etc. If you do drive there is indeed enough parking on the street but note that NYC has street sweepers throughout the week and you have to swap your car to the other side of the street every morning. I actually did this only once because no one else was doing it and didn’t get a ticket but there is a sign.  When you first walk around it seems to be a “other side of the tracks” situation (it’s the edge of Bed-Stuy and still up and coming) but in the end I felt safe enough to walk down the block at night to the comedy club The Tiny Cupboard. On that note let’s talk about things to do in the area - first you have to check out the aforementioned! It’s either free or cheap and they have an amazing rooftop show with a view of Manhattan. Cathy’s Green Gold has a bodega cat. Little Skips East is hipster and boujie with great coffee, brunch, and sundries. Father Knows Best has OK drinks but is hipster if you’re looking for that. As they’ll suggest to you, LunÀtico is classy and cute and their cocktails are amazing. Their food is good too! I didn’t go out dancing but apparently there’s a great spot on Sunday’s - you’ll have to ask Jonathan. Overall though, for what I wanted to do there wasn’t much within walking distance of the neighborhood itself (20min+ walk for good stuff).   OK let’s not gloss over the second best thing to Benson - the hosts! They are super cool and I wish I had more time to spend with them. If for nothing else I’ll be back to turn them into true friends. We had a fun rooftop hangout one night; they’re cool, real, honest people who are very interesting! My last day I even stopped in at their jobs and our convos were breezy and comfortable. :)  You can tell they bring that same energy into their home. The room is perfect from plants winding around the gorgeous sun soaked bohemian decor to the private bathroom in the room itself. So relaxing! (I’ll note that the shower pressure is amazing though the water doesn’t get too hot if you care about that). They keep the apartment at a nice temperature that’s comfortable to sleep in (late July trip). If you’re a late-riser like me you may not appreciate the lack of blinds as the sun rises in your direction. The windows are filled with plants (as they should be!) so bring your eye mask as that’s the solution. :)  I came here on a whim and worked during the last few days of my trip. It was quiet and the internet was fast enough to handle my bandwith-heavy work. No matter the reason you’re visiting this is the best choice for a cozy, private room, instagrammable apartment, a good neighborhood, easy access to the metro, and a really cool dog! Oh and wonderful people. :)

They own several units in this building. Our was a small kitchen/couch area with a cute loft. Exposed brick and hardwood floors. Clean. It is an older building and we loved the charm of that. The businesses outside the entrance make a sketchy first appearance, but inside was clean with very nice staff/security. Very near everything. we loved being right off Broadway.   Air is a window unit. It kept it cool, but we were grateful to have fans to help it out. It was really hot in New York this week.

Hello.  We traveled to NY for our birthday and stayed at this Airbnb for the most part it was ok.  On our first night , there was a party going on with loud music at the apt next to us and random people coming upstairs.  I was not able to sleep because of the loud noise and was  scared someone would try to come into our apt by mistake.  I did report it and the noise didn’t stop and I ended up falling asleep at almost 2am.  We noticed a few small roaches in the bathroom at night so we tried not to leave any food on the counters or table.  There was a coffee maker but no coffee for coffee makers only instant coffee.   NO creamer, no sugar.  The paper towels and toilet paper rolls had been started already and was not a new roll and had to ask for more.  I believe all Airbnb’s should have a new roll of papers especially when we are in the middle of a pandemic. The beds were comfortable and appeared clean.  Thank you.

Brett's apartment is truly a gem. It's conveniently situated across the street from the A train which takes you downtown within 20-30 minutes. There is a grocery store right behind and many, many green spaces around. It's definitely something you will not find anywhere downtown.   The apartment was clean and completely renovated. I have family and friends living on the same street and it's the nicest apartment we have seen.   Brett was prompt in replies which was super helpful. The apartment had everything we needed! People we met in the building were friendly, and even the people in the neighborhood in general were friendly. Lots of families around, a shul not too far, it was really perfect for us.   I highly recommend (but also not because I'm scared it will be booked next time we go! 🤣)
This place was terrible, scam, didn’t give me my money back, house was ran down. People were there, terrible spent more money on hotel , don’t waste your time here.

This was unfortunately the worst air bnb experience I have ever had - and I have stayed at dozens of places over the years, both in the US and out of the country. I don't understand how it could have gotten 5 star reviews - it makes me wonder if they are not authentic guest reviews. I had to leave this location and find a new airbnb last minute. The furniture was falling apart, aspects of the apartment were not clean, the bedding was so strongly smelling of synthetic fragrance detergent I had a physical reaction to it, the kitchen was not fully stocked as the description said, there was not a trash bin in the entire place, and the wifi was not set up, and the tv had about 7 channels, and then went to total fuzz a few hours later. To the host's credit, after being adamant that I would not be staying there, he did cooperate with airbnb to give me a full refund. This was a stressful and disappointing experience, and I was fortunate to have relatives in the city to help me find another airbnb - and if it weren't times specific to corona virus, I am sure I would not have been able to find another listing available for a long term stay in such short notice.

Overall decent stay in nice location (close to good subway stop) with all the basics you might need (desk, dresser, bed, kitchenware, etc.) but WiFi was not strong enough to WFH. Slow loading speeds, couldn’t FaceTime, spotty signal, etc. Raised this issue to host at the beginning of my stay. Host said he sent a maintenance person who confirmed the WiFi was working. Communicated it was still not working well enough to support my needs (was going to be on Zoom calls all day) and was forced to get my own internet once host became unresponsive. Put me under a lot of stress given that I’d never visited the city before and was starting a full-time internship the next day (which I told host). Since listing promises WiFi strong enough to work and study but didn’t deliver, I asked host to cover cost of monthly bill. Had to escalate to AirBnB each month because this request kept being denied by host. Only other less than ideal detail is that the bed comforter was folded between two top sheets when I arrived. Once I realized, I peeled back top sheet to reveal huge stain. Was clear the comforter had not been washed when I took it to laundromat next day and sprayed it with stain remover. Stain came right out.

Please, if you care about your safety or well-being, do not book this place.  My family along with my two small daughters were traveling to New York for a church conference.  We were traveling at night, and I made sure my host knew that our arrival would be around 12 AM midnight.  She sent over the code, but unbeknownst to me, I actually had my old number saved to my account, so when she sent the code to me, I have never received it.  I messaged her back promptly, asking if she could resend the code and she never responded. We called and called and her phone went straight to voicemail.  We were never able to get in touch with her.  We were in New York, with a car full of women and my two small daughters in the middle of the night, desperately looking for a new place to stay.  It was dangerous and a huge inconvenience.  A professional host would remain attentive until her guest confirmed that they were inside and that the code worked.  We received no apology the next day, only an excuse that she was in Jamaica and had no service.  She is very unprofessional and lacks empathy. Please do not book unless you are ok with a lack of communication and a chance to be left out cold on the street.

Would book again 10/10!  Amazing apartment in a killer location (Prospect Park at your feet, plus 3 min walk from the Q). Loved the decor. Bed and sofa are both very comfortable. And a really nice TV. Would book again 10/10.   Hot tip #1: Respond to Frank when he messages to verify your visit (a day or two in advance). Otherwise, you might get a minor heart attack (and stress him out too). He's got a bit more of a personal touch than most Airbnbs I've stayed at, so when I didn't respond, he almost cancelled my res.  Hot tip #2: Grab a nice slice around the corner (Family Pizza on Flatbush). Or a unique & tasty scallion pancake (among other delights) at Slow Loris nearby.  Oh, and about parking. This was one of the biggest stresses of the trip, so can't say I agree that there is free easy street parking. Perhaps Frank knows the spots! Everywhere I went (and I searched!) had morning street cleaning like 5x days a week so I would've had to move my car every day. I ended up paying $30ish/day at a parking lot on Caton Ave. nearby. My experience in other NYC neighborhoods (further from the park) is that there is easy street parking. Here, it was not my experience.  Overall, excellent stay! Thanks Frank!

For the price and location, this spot is truly a steal, especially for groups. My group of 6 were only there to rest and get ready but when we were home, it was a comfortable and pleasant experience. Great communication on the host’s end. Very accommodating. Thank you, Crystal!  Walking distance from the J train which takes you right to JFK airport and connects you to the rest of the train lines. Bodegas, many food options, and Rite Aid nearby. Safe neighborhood, just be aware of your surroundings esp. if you’re navigating. This some is a huge perk!  The listing is very accurate - walk lightly as the floor can be loud. The walls truly are thin and you can hear a lot, bring ear plugs if you sleep light (helped me sleep like a baby).   The apartment was clean and everything was easy to find/use. Appreciated the good natural lighting, the heater (cold in winter!), the equipped kitchen area, Netflix when we were tired. Thanks for everything!

The location is good in relation to the metro line. JZ line approximately 30 minutes to Manhattan.  Arriving in the neighborhood is a little scary because it is a poor neighborhood. However, people are kind and considerate to us.  The apartment lacks cleanliness, especially the sofa and the products left in the kitchen have animals in them. It calms down when you arrive.  The soap rest in the bathroom is broken and sharp, therefore very dangerous and the variations of hot and cold water are very annoying.  Furthermore, not saying that there are chickens screaming at 6 a.m. at the back of the house is not normal.  The nights are very noisy with howling neighbors, dogs barking from dawn and fire and police sirens because of the single glazing.  Otherwise, neighborhood with supermarket, pharmacy, bike rental. …

This place is in a great location with an amazing price as promised in the description. Very close to Trader Joe's, which helped me save money during the stay, the central park for the Thanks Giving Parade view, a laundromat whose staffs were very helpful, easy access to the packages or mails I asked to send to this address, which gave me a lot more chances to order through Amazon than other Airbnb place, and etc. The host was literally always responsive and I had no stress in getting the information you need. The room was small and the one you see in the picture is everything except for the bathroom, so just mind that this is strictly for one guest.

This is an absolutely stunning place to stay. Everything including the bedroom , bathroom and view are fabulous.  it is the best Airbnb I have ever stayed in and better than most hotel rooms . I was visiting my daughter who is studying at Pratt and this apartment was just across the road. The location  is great close to subway and and really easy trip to Manhatton . There are great bars and restaurants really close to the apartment and it was really nice after a busy day to have dinner in one of locat restaurants which were really relaxed and chilled. Rob and Anne were so generous in spirit and so lovely to stay with , you would not get this experience or level of accommodation in an hotel. I am recommending Rob's place to everyone I know and am planning to book myself back in sooner rather than later. Thank you for everything , I really appreciated it.

Rob and Anne were warm, generous, and welcoming hosts. Communication was easy and prompt. The bedroom and the bathroom were both clean and well appointed. The views are spectacular. The deep tub is a nice bonus. Rob went above and beyond in making us feel comfortable, from coffee together in the morning to treats in the room, we would definitely stay here again.

Elle's place is beautiful!  Its spotlessly clean, with full kitchen, extra linens and blankets, enclosed backyard, in a  quite, and safe neighborhood.  It is convenient to restaurants, drug store, corner grocery market, and other buisness, and a park is only 6 blocks away.   Elle checked in on line to be sure we were comfortable and our stay was trouble free.  We will definately be back.

The apartment is exactly as described and a perfect hub spot to travel around. Very nice and what we needed for what our plans were.   Elle was extremely helpful and not in our business which was cool. Very simple and easy communication throughout the whole process.   There were a couple incidents however that I should address:  We did have a few incidents with house centipedes and they scared the whole family as we never seen them before. Took a lot of googling to figure what they were and found out they are not dangerous but still scary looking. (Check for yourself)  Shower pressure was not so great but we have come a custom to this in America. Hard to find high pressure showers . So my daughters and wife  (who all have long hair) had a rough time washing it.   Of course the paper in the garbage and not the toilet was different for us and with 6 people kind of disgusting, but again something we got used to.   Other then that we were relatively happy with the place and would recommend it to others (assuming the house centipedes are addressed). They really freaked me out !

Rafael’s place was simple and tidy. There was a mold issue that he said he’d take care of while we were there that never got cleaned. For bedding, there was just a quilt and a fitted sheet on the mattress, which I thought was odd. The quilt had an unpleasant odor that probably would’ve washed away if there were sheets. The padlock to the outside was not working meaning that there was only a flimsy door/lock between us and the street. We felt safe in the neighborhood, but I would assume everyone wouldn’t.

The accommodation does its job and Natasha quickly answered my questions at all times and was very accessible with the check-in process, which I thank her for. I found the neighborhood a bit lonely and dark coming back at night/early morning however I couldn't say it is unsafe or not only consider it if you are a solo traveler.

Pros:  - Located near lots of restaurants and shops, anywhere from 10-30 minute walk depending on where you want to go - Safe area to walk around, didn’t feel sketchy for two girls - Bed was comfortable and lots of closet space to hang clothes, good space for two people, but probably not more than that  Cons:  - The basement has the low ceilings and only one tiny window so there wasn't much airflow and it got stuffy - There is a fan located in the unit but we noticed the back had a lot of pet hair/fur and the fur was blowing around so we turned it off - Our first night here, the heater was on blast and we couldn't access the thermostat to turn it down, so we had to move to a hotel for the night while the host replaced the AC unit they removed from the apartment. They refunded us for the night but it unfortunately didn't cover the hotel stay or the travel to/from the hotel.

Overall, experience was okay. Location was good for what we needed and the apartment was quiet and affordable. However, it was a bit dirty when we arrived. The sheets and towels and shower were clean which was good but the floor was sticky and didn’t seem to have been cleaned. There was trash from previous guests, an opened drink bottle and some makeup debris on the floor which then got on our shoes, socks, bare feet, etc. both the kitchen sink and bathroom sink seemed dirty and had debris in them. It was not dirty enough for it to be uncomfortable but it was slightly unpleasant. The biggest issue we had was that the floor was not well cleaned, and didn’t even seem to have been swept. Also the heater didn’t seem to be working, which wasn’t an issue since it wasn’t very cold during our stay but might be a problem in the winter months

Charles and his wife Nikky are great hosts , they’re really sweet and communication is all there . They do have two big dogs but don’t let that scare you , they’re SOOOO sweet & adorable ! I got to play with Phantom and Ghost during my stay for a bit and i didn’t want to stop . The space overall is big and clean , really nice place to relax. My boyfriend and I would stay again and again

The room was clean, as was the private bathroom inside. Small kitchen area and microwave was ideal. The only thing we didn’t like was the building itself — lots of shady characters hanging outside, around the lobby, etc. we encountered a Physical altercation & some sort of criminal investigation just in the three nights we stayed (and we were out and about for 95% of the trip). The building for entering and exiting the room wasn’t the best so we wouldn’t use the accommodation again, but the room itself was clean and good so we don’t regret the stay. Host is very responsive.

We had three people stay in this AirBnb and it was great!  Pros:   -LOCATION! My friends, you are in the heart of Manhattan, so countless tourist attractions are just a hop, skip, and a jump away. It was honestly insane how close to everything we were   -The room itself is wonderful! It seems newly renovated, and was extremely clean.   -The room is pretty much the same size as it appears in the picture, which means it’s in very close quarters. But we didn’t spend much time at all in the room, so it wasn’t bad at all.   -I didn’t communicate with Lydia, but I did with Fernando and any problems we faced (the WiFi not working temporarily, etc), he answered back very quickly.  -The people at the front desk were extremely helpful! They told us about a grocery store called Jack’s a block away that is affordable (unlike every other store that hikes up their prices for tourism) and we saved SOOOO much money. I HIGHLY recommend going there.   Cons:   Since it is located in the middle of Manhattan, we definitely noticed some sketchy stuff happening directly outside the building and in the lobby countless times, so just be mindful (and careful) of that.   Even though it said there would be towels, there was only one hand towel which isn’t helpful for 3 people staying multiple days who need to shower. Thankfully, we brought our own, but if we didn’t we would be straight out of luck. With that, there was also no soap and no paper towels so we had to buy our own.

Cute place and a nice room in a shared house. Room to share in the fridge, bathroom, and other spaces. The room is at the back of the house and is fairly insulated from the business of the street. We slept great and felt pretty comfortable.  Good location as well. Bushwick used to be a really sketchy area back in the day, and I’m sure pockets like that exist still. However, we felt very safe and even ventured out many times into the AM without any safety concerns. We used the subway from the Myrtle Street station to get into Manhattan with great success. It’s about a half hour to 40 minutes using public transit. Uber and Lyft is normally about $30 into Manhattan.
The beach is great and clean a walking distance to the metro that can take u all over New York. Overall a great place to stay but just the area it self at night it’s a bit scary.

Lisa made us feel extremely comfortable and welcomed. We were celebrating our wedding anniversary and she had champagne and a beautiful card awaiting us at check in. Clear communication made the entire experience stress free. The location worked out very well. One block away from a train station, grocery, cafe and restaurants. A very quiet building. Would highly recommend Lisa’s Urban Oasis for your stay in NYC.

We loved this apartment from the first time we saw it until we left! It was well decorated with art works and a wide variety of plants. The apartment was a comfortable and relaxing place to stay when we were visiting our children and their families.  We took full advantage of the well-equipped kitchen to prepare meals for ourselves and our children.  Anna welcomed us upon our arrival, gave us a tour of the apartment, and left us a folder with recommendations for restaurants and things to do!  (By the way, I highly recommend the restaurant Lea, which was on her list. Delicious!) This Airbnb is within walking distance to grocery stores, drug stores, laundries, restaurants, and bagel places! Anna was a kind and gracious host and was very quick to respond any time I sent a message.

Yael was very kind and the communication was always there. As for the place itself, it was spacious for an apartment in NYC. Please note that it's beside a school, so there were parties and loud music playing from the other buildings/rooms. During our stay the AC started to tick in the middle of the night and the bathtub was on the more dirty side. The subway was a 7 min walk which was very convenient, however coming back in the evening did feel unsafe especially walking back to the airbnb. Aside from these things, we overall had a good trip, and everything in the photos/ads is what you get.

Arrived to the management office (a block away, on foot, with all of my luggage) in the basement of an unrelated building after the host wasn’t responding to messages or picking up their phone. I told them I was checking in for an Airbnb and this is when they just tossed me a set of keys, no checking of my ID or providing any info on my stay. I arrived to the unit and found it hadn’t been cleaned aside from switching out towels and maybe sheets. There were blood, feces, and urine all over the bottom mattress protector and sheet. There were dead cockroaches both inside the unit and throughout the building itself. The bathroom floor was covered in mold along the wall due to a shower which was left somewhat on from the last guest. The sink, which doesn’t have cold water, was completely clogged and would take ≈ 15 min to drain. Garbage from other units scattered the hallways.   Homeless wandered near the entrance and on the front steps, not great when trying to come in at night.   After messaging the host about these issues, only half of them were fixed and after over a week of waiting. They obviously forgot about me and eventually issued a $500 credit. This was not really sufficient considering my stay was $5000 and half of the issues remain unfixed until the day I checked out two months later.   Overall I am sure the host could have been well intentioned. Maybe they are short staffed. Maybe they have so many other units where things fall through the cracks. I do have to mention, I was locked out once and they had an employee leave a key for me in a lock box. This was great service.  Additionally, the location of the unit is great for getting around Manhattan. Lastly, the laundry machines in the basement were quite convenient.  Overall, I am so happy my stay is over!
Unclean to the point of being potentially unsafe.

I throughly enjoyed my time at Angelica’s. Everything about the accommodations was thoughtful—from the decor to the amenities. Being a great host, Angelica communicates promptly. It’s a convenient location with a plethora of options for food and transportation. The house itself is on a quiet street, which was nice. Considering the price, it’s not even a bargain but a steal. I’d definitely stay here again if the opportunity to visit comes up, and you should too. Thanks Angelica!

José was an excellent host. He allowed us an early check in, he answered  all my questions very fast. The apartment  is very complete and comfortable. Bed, towels and sheets are very good. There are 2 lines of subway close.  We had a problem that José had no way of intervening.  In front of the apartment there was a gang fight with shooting.  He helped us as much as possible, and as we were scared we preferred to leave . José understood our problem and refunded us the remaining days. We were very sorry to leave early because we enjoyed it so much.

The apartment’s location is great for getting around the city- we walked to Soho, Chinatown, Battery Park, etc and used the metro stop that’s very close. Also lots of restaurants, coffee shops, etc right nearby. We also were glad for 2 distinct rooms to sleep for some privacy- nothing else at this price point seemed to have that. The apartment is very basic, and there is quite an unpleasant smell in the hall way. The reason for renting is location and affordability- no bells and whistles.
