On the first day they arranged an appointment with a cooker repair engineer without notifying us and then told me when I answered the door "sorry we expected you to be out." On another occasion a young lady who also lives upstairs entered the apartment through a private staircase, (which up until then we assumed was a locked cupboard door) that leads direct into the living room, she came in while my dad was sleeping which gave him the shock of his life.  Unfortunately we felt unsafe as we had a young child with us and valuables in the apartment and it was a very uncomfortable stay. They refunded us $60 on the first day after the first incident for the inconvenience of the cooker engineer but I would have preferred a peaceful stay instead of the money.  Also there is no lock on the bathroom, the cooker still doesn't work after the two hours of waiting for the engineer to finish and multiple times the door lock to enter the apartment did not work properly even after the batteries were changed! This stuff gets really annoying.  I personally won't be stopping here again but one of the hosts - Rick - was a nice guy and did try his best.

This was my very first time visiting New York and I ended up booking Charlene’s place because I wanted to save money. I gotta say, I was a little nervous before my trip, as I’ve read on google that it is a dangerous neighborhood..... BUT LET ME TELL YOU, GOOGLE IS WRONG! I never felt unsafe or nervous in this neighborhood and we got back really late most nights. Charlene’s neighborhood was one of my favorite places to be. So many cultures in Brooklyn to experience. It was much quieter than Manhattan and really easy to navigate. The train ride into the city wasn’t bad at all! Charlene’s place is exactly what you need! Charlene is a lovely host and made sure to check in on us! I plan to recommend Charlene’s place to anyone that I know planning a trip to New York!

I never even saw the room. Still got charged full price.  Stefan refused to refund me, even though I couldn't get in touch with them for more than an hour while trying to check in. I ended up paying for a last-minute hotel instead of staying in the room.  Fully expected to get a quick cancel and refund so we could all move on. Instead, Stefan kept my money.  Airbnb support wasn't able to help; apparently I needed to have waited on the curb for at least another hour before their refund policy would cover me.  So all told I had a very stressful travel day, I'm out the full price of a week in this room, and also had to pay for the last-minute hotel. Would not recommend.

Traveling alone to NYC for a stressful audition is a daunting experience, but staying in Elizabeth’s home made it so much better! There are special touches all over to make you feel at home. Additionally, the house itself has the coolest history. I will definitely come back on my next visit. The checking in/out process was incredibly easy and well-communicated. Thank you Elizabeth!

Best air bnb experience yet.  Responsive friendly communication, professionally run and organized.  Exceptionally clean and nicely presented home.  Made my week less stressful and was able to relax in my private space.

I’m writing this out of 100% honesty from a situation I experienced while staying at this place. I know this is long but if you are considering staying at this home, YOU MUST READ!   Elizabeth could not have been more of an unwelcoming and disrespectful host towards me and my boyfriend. We came to stay at this place hoping to receive warmth, safety, and comfort; as Airbnb’s should offer. Instead, the expected hospitality turned out to be some of the worst and most inappropriate behavior towards me and my boyfriend. Reading the other reviews that people left for the host, I am shocked at how untrue it was and am even willing to believe we experienced a different person completely. We were genuinely surprised to see such rudeness as guests staying in her place. The incident that first occurred that made us feel unsafe and extremely uncomfortable staying there was the way she verbally treated us one night. Me and my boyfriend came back to our room one night after feeling exhausted and drowsy from spending time out, and as soon as we got back we encountered a loud, obnoxious event that was happening on the first floor that we could hear up in our room on the 3rd floor. Which she did warn us about, but we had no idea it would be a huge wedding party. Already being drained, we wanted to take a bath and in the middle of it we got a yell from outside the door from a man shouting at us that the bottom floor was starting to leak water from the bathroom. Upon hearing this, we immediately got out of the bathroom and we’re concerned about what was happening. From behind the door we could hear both the host and a man yelling about us needing to get out in an extremely hostile and aggressive manner. We came out of the bathroom worried and afraid and instead of getting a gentle explanation from the two, they both immediately started screaming at us over what happened. I want to make clear that the host did not make it clear that guest couldn’t use the tub or that specific bathroom for showering. We had absolutely no reason to believe that would cause a leak in the lower floor. The host was sitting waiting in the stairs for us to come out of the bathroom and right away ambushed us with attacks and an intense scream. She started insulting and harassing us, saying things like, “NEXT TIME YOU TWO SHOULD JUST GET A HOTEL!!!” And “IM NOT THE TYPE OF PLACE THAT ALLOWS TWO PEOPLE TO SHOWER TOGETHER!!!”. Right away we were shocked with her tone and tried to explain that we had no idea that this would cause any trouble simply trying to use the bathroom. I literally cannot explain to you how rude and verbally abusive her tone was towards us. Her and the man came at us with more bullying and harassment after we heard Elizabeth yell, “20 YEAR OLD ASSHOLES!!!”. Mind you, this was our very first interaction with the host. We never received a warm welcome or greeting upon arrival. She never thought of being nice to us even after we tried to apologize over and over again, even after not knowing how using the shower/tub would cause a leak. We couldn’t even offer any sort of help or assistance with the incident because we were immediately berated by the man and host. The man soon got right in our faces and yelling at us, “THIS HAS NEVER HAPPENED UNTIL YOU TWO USED THE BATHROOM!!”. As though we did anything on purpose. All we did was take a perfectly normal bath. Any amount of water on the floor was the normal residue that comes from a bath. If the leak was caused by the bath, it would have happened regardless of who was taking the bath. It was probably their drainage system, given that it’s an old house it’s perfectly reasonable to assume this was some sort of drainage issue that was unavoidable by the two of us. After this first interaction with the host, we right after felt extremely uncomfortable and unsafe to be staying at the house the remaining of the night. We went up to our room after continuously trying to engage in a helpful conversation with them and trying to apologize repeatedly. After being harassed by their tone and behavior, we went up to our room and locked the door and felt way too uncomfortable to even leave our room the rest of the night. We didn’t even feel safe to go outside the room to use the bathroom if we needed to. We also needed to ask the host if we could have a few more bath towels but couldn’t even feel safe enough to ask her.   We overheard them talking about coming upstairs and we felt nervous and afraid they would come up to our room with a key and possibly attack us. I know it sounds like a dramatization, but the way they were acting towards us seemed like she was unhinged enough to actually attack us in some way and hurt us. We would constantly be making sure the door was locked, tip toed around the house, and overall felt extraordinarily uncomfortable and unsafe for the rest of our trip. We were even willing to leave to go to a hotel at 3 am but lacked the funds to do so. We only had a night left so we managed to hold through but it was so unbearable. I have genuinely never encountered someone that treated me with so much disrespect. Especially someone that I am personally paying money to. That is such an awful way to run your business on Airbnb. To be disrespectful towards your guests right to their face after the very first encounter and then to continue to disrespect and bully us behind the doors as if we wouldn’t
Easy enough check in and out, clean bathroom, loft slept hot and very dangerous if you have a child, cool vibe, location seemed safe, enjoyed the rooftop view

Cool space. Very large. Simple. Location is not the best in one direction as there are projects across from the building but Carrol Gardens is in the other. Check in was very stressful, check out was not so stressful.

Gabriel was very attentive and responsive, the place was just as I looked in pictures. Comfortable to work in as well, the area is a bit sketchy at night and may be difficult to park. It’s very lowkey and in the cut of Brooklyn, but my stay was very pleasant

I stayed at Rebecca's apartment with two friends and really enjoyed our stay there. It's absolutely comfortable for 4 people, two bathrooms, what you see in the pics is what you get. Well located with two Subway stations almost three blocks away (lines 2,3 and Q to go to Manhattan). It's located two blocks away from Prospect Park (a must see) and close to Fullton Mall and Atlantic Barcley shoppings. You can have all the amenities you need and Rebecca and her husband were always available to help us. Brooklyn is a beautiful borough so don't be afraid to stay there if you have almost one week to enjoy New York City! Thanks for everything!

This garden apartment is on a shady quiet street in an excellent location in Park Slope.  It is convenient to nearly anything you could want and the detailed information Bruce gives his guests is available both online and in print inside the apartment.  The queen-sized bed is comfortable, however quite low to the ground which might be a problem for some people.  The air conditioning (in July) worked very well and provided our "white noise" during the night, although could be extra loud at times when cycling on and off. The biggest negative is the strong musty smell upon entering the apartment and particularly in the bathroom which someone with sensitivities may wish to be aware of before booking.

Gabriel’s flat has a huge problem. You want to own the place from the moment you set foot in it. The more you live in Red Hook, the more you realize what a gem of a neighborhood it has become. Not too hipster, no longer shady, a stone throw from everything and very “real”. Gabriel’s place is spacious, smells amazing (I think it’s the old wooden floor), has great energy, it’s so properly decorated (with real style in the choice of materials and furniture, nothing is tacky or out of place), stunning large plants.  A very rare find, I wish I could have stayed longer. No wonder the place is always booked. Could easily be priced at a much higher price (maybe even 2x) and it would still be good value.  Bravo Gabriel!

While this is an amazing space in Brooklyn, it was not as pictured. It was cluttered with personal items, including mail. Plants and a broken mirror covered the table making the table unusable. I was there for over a week and only one roll of toilet paper and no bath soap was provided. Coffee was also not avaiable so other guests may want to come prepared. Most importantly I felt quite uncomfortable sleeping in the loft which did not have a railing to the floor below. It appeared that there was one at one point but the open floor was a potentially dangerous situation.

The place was clean and as described, but the building has lots of issues. The skylight in the central stairs has a massive hole, so when it rains the stairs are wet and dangerous, so please be careful. The hot water and heat in the building are hit or miss some days. Generally, it was ok, just know what you are getting.

I was woken up at 4 am by Kemar’s and his hook-up’s loud and obnoxious conversations in the living area - right by my door. Couldn’t go back to sleep afterwards. Not just because there was also loud music, loud prolonged sex, and the whole apartment smelled like weed, Kemar had zero respect for his guest. I also felt unsafe to fall back asleep.

The stay at this place was incredible.. it feels like being at home, it was super clean.  Downstairs there was a place to buy everything which made our stay easier. At first we thought the area was dangerous but then we changed our mind. The location is excellent. If I go to NY again I would definitely stay there again.

We enjoyed Steven’s place. It was clean and accommodating for our family of 5. We enjoyed having 3 bedrooms and a living room where we could relax after long days filled with walking. Not too far from 2 different subway access points and easily within walking distance to the northeast corner of Central Park and some good restaurants. One caution: be aware that your climbing up two flights of seriously steep and crooked stairs to get in and out of the apartment. These could be dangerous for young kids or older people. Overall, we would recommend Steven’s Airbnb.

BEST STAY! Awesome place! The location is a little scary at night, but the Airbnb was AWESOME!!! Super comfy beds and was always cool! Super nice to walk into after everyday! Be prepared for some narrow stairs up with luggage, but overall would for sure stay again!!!

Had a great stay at Jenny's place. First and foremost, Jenny is incredibly kind and responsive. She generally replied within minutes. Before my stay began, she was helpful in confirming the best subway routes for me to take to get to and from the conference I was attending, and the train station.   The location is good! It's about half a mile away from the subway station. There is a grocery store a block away! It's a nice residential area, but within walking distance of lots of shops, restaurants, and coffee shops. It takes about 20 minutes to get into Manhattan if you're taking the subway.  A couple of notes for those who want to stay here: make sure to check with Jenny on how to unlock the door! I was making it way more complicated than it needed to be, but it resulted in some stress as I stood there trying to figure it out. It's super easy, but make sure to check in with Jenny on how to do it. When I was having trouble, she responded within minutes! So appreciated.  Second-there is no coffee maker. I forgot to check this and was surprised when I got in. However, I went to the grocery store that is just a block up and got these cool pour over coffee singles, and was able to make coffee easily with some hot water.   This is a cozy and lived-in apartment that is super safe (the building is locked!) and stylish. It has everything you need, and is a nice home-base while you explore the city!

The location is intimidating and sketchy especially when arriving at night however there were no safety issues regarding this. The keys weren’t in the lock box and it was a hassle to get in to the location had to call the phone number provided and find keys ect.  The owner then called me approximately 10/15 times in the first night about the keys asking where did I put or find them. Mind you I was arriving at night time for the first night and time in NYC. not the best way to start a trip. The stairs are a death trap I literally fell going up them the first time and broke my finger. Having luggage and walking period on those stairs is very dangerous. This Was not the best way to start my vacation. The home was clean but a lot of things did not work wifi, living room ac, there is a strange door in one bedroom that is taped shut along with a lock. At night time the bedrooms were very loud and you can hear all the outside noises. There were holes in the wall from what locked to be were a TV once hung. Although besides my finger there were no safety issues I would not stay in this location again. Pictures made the location seem much more appealing that it really was.

Sarah and Jens were very welcoming and very helpful. Gave us directions to which nearby subway stations were best for each of our destinations, both in Brooklyn and in Manhattan and to JFK airport. One and a half short blocks to nearest subway station. Short rides to anywhere in Manhattan. Half a block walk to wonderful eateries, coffee shops, bakery, small grocery stores, other colorful ethnic shops. They gave us suggestions about where to eat and shop in the neighborhood, and sights to see farther away in Brooklyn. The apartment was immaculate. Private entrance. The beds were very comfortable. Full, well equipped kitchen. Cool, tree-shaded private area just outside the back door. A shady,  tree lined street. Our host was always very quick to respond to our texts and calls. Will definitely stay there again on our next trip to NYC and Brooklyn.
Great place, clean, convenient store right below. Sketchy characters here and there but nothing serious, would definitely recommend this spot to anyone looking for a good spot in upper Manhattan.

The place is nice once you are there. The area feels very dangerous especially if you are arriving at night. The host was very helpful giving us instructions and speaking to us until we got there. We stayed for one night instead of 6. We were unsatisfied with the location. We wanted to speak to Anthony  and see if we could meet half way and get a partial refund. He never answered back. Worst experience Ive had on airbnb so far. Also super shady that once you get there he doesnt want to speak through airbnb chat, he prefers personal numbers, that made us feel very uncomfortable.  The place inside is very comfortable though and very well equiped. We had a misunderstanding of where the place was located and never got an answer to help us deal with it. We sent tons of messages to him before this review and he never answered back.
A great place to stay if you just want a place to sleep, however a bit dangerous to walk back to very late at night.
Crystal and her daughter are very nice and sweet! A convenient location, just a few blocks away from a subway station, and not as dangerous as I imagined!

Cons: 1. IT IS NOT A PRIVATE ROOM, it is an area in the common room separated with a curtain. I had sleep problems – every night when host came from work (1-3 AM) because of noise.  2. THERE IS A CAT and it is very ill-mannered. You have to lift your mattress when going out otherwise it will pee on your bed. 3. THERE’S NO FURNITURE FOR YOUR STUFF – a tiny table & hanger only. Be prepared to keep everything in your suitcase. 4. KITCHEN IS VERY DIRTY, with stains all over (microwave, counter etc.) 5. LEAKAGES IN THE BATHROOM (water coming from the ceiling upstairs). Almost every day there were pools on the floor. It is dangerous (there’s electricity etc.) but the apartments’ owner doesn’t do anything with it.  Pros: 1. VERY CHEAP. For $20 a night you could have lived in a refrigerator box on your street but you live in an apartment with water & light. 2. CLOSE TO MANHATTAN. It is still Bronx but it takes only 30-40 minutes to get to midtown. Subway lines 2, 5 & 6. Bronx has a bunch of spectacular and / or just nice places to visit too. 3. HOST IS A NICE PERSON who responds really quickly, she is really friendly and kind. I had great time talking to her.  To sum up, it is a great option to save some money for city attractions if you are not picky.

All I can say is: If she has availability grab it! The location is central to several train lines, close to several stores including a Walgreens and the neighbors are very nice. It will take you about 20-30 minutes by train to get downtown and when I couldn’t wait I never had a problem getting an Uber. Obviously you have to exercise common sense as we are still in New York, however I never felt unsafe and the open pool nearby in the heatwave was an added bonus. Crystal is an AMAZING host and her dog Sweetie is just like her name. I’ve never had a more enjoyable Airbnb stay where I was in the same space as the host. Crystal is how all hosts should be. Been on Airbnb for a while and this is in my top 3 stays.

I strongly caution against booking to stay with Crystal, especially if you are a black woman or ally. As an experienced Airbnb guest, who primarily relies upon the company to look for short term housing as I conduct archival research for my PhD, I have been very fortunate to only have had positive experiences thus far, and appreciate that this deeply unpleasant experience is certainly singular. The situation became so untenable that with a week to go of my stay, I contacted the Airbnb customer service team to report that I felt unsafe at the host's home due to her racism and poor communication. The Airbnb team were brilliant and arranged for me to rehoused for the remainder of my reservation. The one saving grace was that I barely had contact with the host during my time there - though the moments I did have contact were deeply problematic- including a microaggression upon arriving asking me to be sure to clean my hair out of the drain as it could block it (I have thick, curly, Afro hair and did not appreciate it being treated as some threat to her plumbing). In addition to this, the host was exceedingly slow to deal with a plumbing issue regarding a blocked shower drain (the problem pre-dated my arrival and grew steadily worse and wasn't not resolved until 12 days into my stay). The issue also affected use of the bathroom sink and its contents which would empty into the bath/shower. The host asked that myself and another guest not use the shower on the day it was to be fixed and informed of us this with a note posted in the bathroom (I myself had not used the shower for two days prior to this as it was extremely unhygienic. I had a good friend visiting for a business trip and used her shower). Unfortunately, use of the sink, of course, could not be avoided and I overheard a conversation the host had on the phone at 2am (which woke me up from my sleep) complaining to someone about the guests using the bath after she’d instructed us not to. No accountability or self-reflection about the fact she failed to prioritise addressing the blocked drain until it became much worse, nor any thought of the fact that the water in the shower clearly came from the sink which she knew emptied onto the bath. This was not the only issue, more worryingly, there was a sewage leak from the apartment above. I was the only one home at the time and contacted the host who asked me to call her. Instead of leaving work to deal with the urgent issue, the host asked me to enter the bathroom, with the sewage leak and record it for the superintendent. I felt under pressure to do so as the issue needed to be attended to urgently. I then dealt with the superintendent and ensured the issue was resolved and updated the host. I think it was enormously irresponsible for the host not to offer to address this issue herself, as I am not a tenant but a guest. I'm a PhD student visiting from the UK and have added Crystal’s listing to a database for students conducting archival research in the US, under the NYC entry, so students know not to book with this host. Again, I would urge you to consider staying with another host during your time in Harlem or Manhattan more broadly. I have since stayed in two other places in Harlem booked via Airbnb and have had a wonderful time!

I can’t say we enjoyed our stay here. A few things:  1. Although street parking is free, it’s difficult to find one later in the day (obviously it being NYC) 2. To be able to get inside, you have to call a guy named Ernesto, who will then give you the keys to the place and your provate room. No contactless check-in. 3. The room locks from the inside, but you do not have to have a key to unlock it from the outside. We were genuinely afraid for our belongings. 4. We stayed in Room #1. The bed was awful, not comfortable at all. Any movement and it makes a squeeking sound. Pillows are terrible. Not a very comfortable sleep. 5. The bathroom is really dirty. When trying to take a shower the tub fills with water and drains really slowly. 6. No kettle, could not find a coffee maker either. 7. For anything you need, you call Ernesto. We needed an iron, which the apartment listing said it had, Ernesto got us one, but it would have been so much easier if it was somewhere where we could have access to it anytime we wanted. 8. Although the listing says no noise after a certain hour, other hosts were having a good time past midnight.

Host never responded to several messages to request check in instructions. This was even after check in time. My son and I stood in the train station, past check in time not knowing what to do. Then a few mins AFTER the reservation was cancelled because I was with my son and afraid of not having a place to stay, the host messaged me saying “We hope you enjoy your stay.” What does that even mean??

Kelly was, one of, if not the best airbnb hosts I have ever had the pleasure of doing business with. Kelly provided everything that one could need and was constantly and consistently available for any requests, questions and help, with any matter of things. She is an above and beyond, high quality host.  The Panda Pod was in a safe, residential, Queens area, in College Point, with convenient, and easy to find, transportation means, at any time of the day, whether that be,  by bus (Q25) at the end of the street,  Uber, which picked me up right in front of the door, at any time of day, or train which is a short and inexpensive, few bus stops away. The Panda Pod was homely, clean, completely comfortable and the perfect distance from the entrance to the rest of the city. Where, you're in the city, but living around the calmness and security of a residential suburb. It is in walking distance proximity, to many different kinds of cuisine, a good spot, and again easy to find,  for food delivery to the air bnb, and also walking distance to CVS and other places where you can find simple groceries and shopping if you need or just want to browse.  There is a nearby laundromat, where the owners are kind and helpful. I want to stress that I felt completely safe in this area, while maintaining the thought that this is New York City, as a young woman in their 20s, traveling alone in NYC, and Kelly played a good part in creating that ambiance as well. I would 100% recommend staying in Panda Pod, if you're looking for a homely, comfortable, safe and convenient stay in NYC, provided by an EXCELLENT host! I can't wait to stay here again!

I would 100% recommend coming here, downtown is about a 10 minute bus ride. Very convenient area, amazing air conditioning and amenities. We were robbed (not near the house) and she assured us to get new keys at 7am, very communicative. The beds are very comfortable and plush, the neighbors are friendly as well.

Fallon was helpful and hosted me last minute, which was a saviour! All in all the apartment is alright and situated in a neighbourhood which is still the "old-school" Brooklyn, not far from the subway (Wilson Av - L). It could appear a bit shady at first but didn't feel threatened in the four days I stayed. The room and apartment have a particular decoration style of art. Downside: the apartment was not very clean and had strong odours, which might be an issue if you mind those things. Since the room was cheaper than average, it's something you might compromise. Didn't have much interaction with the housemates and Fallon was away when I arrived. All in all thanks for the stay Fallon!

This was a special trip for our family, having waited over a year to finally get to see the show we have been holding onto tickets for. Taylor was an exception host and everything she did made this trip so much more enjoyable for all of us. Her replies very quick and tremendously helpful, easing any worry about maneuvering the ins and outs of the city. Coupon codes provided for services saved us money and time. We were astonished at the value of this wonderful place given it is right off of Times Square. As older travelers we loved the coziness and capacity to rest and relax, along with convenience of our most meals delivered. our adult kids loved being so close to all of the fun of this wonderful city. I cannot stress how much we enjoyed our time here, and how grateful we are for all that Taylor did to assure our visit was a good one. She is a wonderful host and we would feel fortunate to stay at her place anytime. We and AirBnB are fortunate to have her. Taylor thank you so very much for everything!

The location is as described. It is in Time Square. No problems with that. Be advised there is no elevator so if you plan on having an elderly person with you, this is not ideal as it is on the third floor. Also, I would not advise you to stay here if you are taking kids. When we would get back home there were lots of crack heads at the bottom of the steps openly doing drugs. We did not feel safe walking in. They were even there when we left for the airport at 6 a.m. Once we were in the building it was fine. The entire restroom needed to be scrubbed badly. The shower/restroom is so small. I know it’s New York and things are crowded but if you are a taller and a bigger person you probably won’t fit in the shower. We are all short and had a hard time maneuvering in the shower only to have the shower curtain stick to you and shower has a huge window in front of it. We had to get dressed in the living room after showering because it was so small. Ask for a picture of the restroom before you book. The stand alone fan had tons of dust on it. We didn’t want to use it for fear all that dust would just blow onto us. We had trouble finding our key and getting in the place. Our host was instantly available, which was awesome. The room itself is very spacious. Two of us slept on the bed and the other slept on the couch. It has a beautiful original brick wall and wood floors. The kitchen was spacious and clean but we didn’t use it, we were mostly out and about. Would I stay here again? Probably not. I’d get a hotel nearby even if it costs a bit more.

Camille’s apartment was a good base to explore Manhattan.  Central Park is short walk west and there is a subway station a block away and there is a parking lot next door if you have a car.  The apartment is small, but you expect that from Manhattan, but the apartment has a lot of natural light and high ceilings to make is seem larger.  Couple of other nice things about the apartment is that it has a washer and dryer and there are separate air conditioners for each room that are very quiet and work well.  I’m a light sleeper and have a hard time with air conditioners at hotels and apartments but the AC’s at Camille’s were really quiet.  Communications with Camille were good and she was flexible with late check in.  The only issue with the apartment is that it borders an area north that could be sketchy at night.  We walked around the areas south and west of the apartment and there were many other people walking around and we felt very safe.

The apartment great and nice for two people. Great location and also clean. However we had a very unpleasant experience during our stay.  The landlord had contractors do work on the apartment without letting us know, so early in the morning 2 strange men came into the apartment without knocking or asking. Then proceeded to stay in the apartment.  We contacted the company that was managing the apartment (you don’t even get the owner!)  They told us that the men were not supposed to be there and that they’ve told them to leave. The men stayed, even used the bathroom etc. We overheard on the phone that they had previously entered the apartment while we were not there and used the facilities.  To get to the bathroom you have to go through a bedroom, my girl friend was taking a shower and the guy proceeded to walk into the bathroom without knocking. I had to physically stop him.  Called the company that manager the company to tell them what was going on and they replied with a ‘we work with these contractors for a long time, please don’t mistake their familiarity as a bold intrusion.’ Thanks for undermining how unsafe we felt having a strange man try to enter the bathroom without asking or knocking!!! The responses were very generic, it’s through a third party and was not helpful at all! Considering how serious it was the host did not care to address the seriousness of it!! It ruined the whole experience and made us feel very unsafe!  Terrible experience!!

Great room. Very clean. My flight was delayed and Jhonny was responsive and available. Great geographical location, right next to the metro. If I have to come back to New York, I'll come back to Jhonny's.

Clean, quiet and bright apartment, very well equipped, oven, microwave, dishwasher, washing machine, dryer...nothing is missing. A supermarket just around the corner and another a little larger 10 minutes away, New York prices of course but enough to stay with the family without worry (I stayed 10 days with my 2 grown children - 18 years old). Very friendly welcome, and Julia was always kind enough to answer all my questions in French and very quickly. Line 7 (metro) 10 minutes on foot, super convenient (grand central, 5 av and times square direct), we also appreciated the ferry (east river line), whatever the time, no problem getting back. The heart of Manhattan is not far away and we appreciated the calm and comfort of having 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms!! a true luxury in NYC. We were even able to leave our luggage at the apartment to enjoy our last day (late evening flight) A very pleasant stay.

Freeda was so friendly and accommodating. She even canceled her 4th of July weekend plan because I had a last-minute change of arrival time (which was very stressful). I had no working mobile data upon arriving in NY and she made sure I got to her place alright. That's very much appreciated.  Her cute little apartment is probably one of the most chic airbnbs I've ever been to. She got class 😁  I was there early July and prior to arriving I was afraid it would be hot in the room because the listing doesn't have AC. Turned out my worries were for nothing. The temperature was just perfect, a little bit too chilly for me even. I didn't turn the ceiling fan on the whole time, and even still able to wear blanket when I slept 😄  Overall, very much recommended. Thank you, Freeda 😊

The accommodation is in the middle of Chinatown and accordingly very centrally located. You have to like living in Chinatown, it is quite noisy in this part of town and especially on warm days it does not smell good there because the garbage is on the street. You can get to the accommodation via the stairs on the fourth floor. The staircase is quite dirty and a very unpleasant smell comes over you. The accommodation itself is very clean and the common room is cleaned daily. Two of us stayed in the double room with private bathroom for 10 days. On request we got new towels (unfortunately the towels smelled musty). It would have been nice if within the long period of 10 days the room would have been cleaned again - but I suppose that could have been requested. Since the room is directly adjacent to the common room, it can get very noisy when other people are there and talking - earplugs are recommended.  All in all, an apartment that is fine for a few days when you are probably only there to sleep anyway.

The apartment has good location, near subway train station (local), many grocery stores, restaurants and different shops are around. The area is safe, not noisy, but the upper parts of East Harlem have some "strange" people wandering around (125 street express train station), but it is still far away from the apartment. We felt more uncomfortable than unsafe up there.  Building is an older one but fine, shared washing machine is in the basement (2 USD per wash).  Apartment had all necessary amenties  Irina was quick to respond for all questions.  If you are looking for a budget accomodation outside of center Manhattan, this is a good option.

Irina was a wonderful host. I got into the city around 8AM and she held my luggage safely all day until I was able to check in. I was supposed to check in at 4PM but she allowed me to check in early around 2PM. I loved this location! Seriously a perfect medium of the hustle and bustle mixed with the culture and chill vibe of Harlem. I traveled alone and never felt unsafe. The apartment building was so clean along with the apartment. The best is SO COMFY!!!! It’s the perfect apartment. I 10/10 recommend for anyone visiting New York.
Such a great host! However the neighborhood is a bit dangerous.

I had a fine stay at Aimee's place. Everything was clean, check-in was easy, the bed was comfortable. The amenities here are basic, but that's what I was looking for and the price:value was right. Chinatown is a little sketchy in the late night / morning hours, and it's a 10-15 min walk to most subway stations, but overall I'd stay in this neighborhood again and Aimee's place is clean and quiet.
great place, a bit unsafe neighborhood during night time. house is great

if possible i would give 0. not so charming i would say.... first of all....   The day we got the place, i expected to relax.. this did not happen, my baby was on the floor and i picked him up, and his legs were all black from dirty floors. i decided i need to wash the floors. took me 5 times to clean the floors. also dusting. needed to dust the whole place. This was adressed to Yaffa and also was adressed with Airbnb personally. According to the host, my expectations for cleaningness is too high, i am sure anyone who would be paying about 3k to stay at a place would expect the place to be cleaned.   NEXT!!!!  MICE!.... i was asked by the host to write a good review and not to mention mice.   I am sorry, but this is unacceptable.   they were walking all over the kitchen and all over the dishes thay were out drying in the sink. when the exterminator came, he told me personally that from his experience mice dont appear from anywhere. and he said that most likely that they have been there before we even came.... well.... airbnb asked for me to get some sort of proof that exterminator said that.... GUESS WHAT!!! the exterminator is a close friend of the host who will not say anything against her.... I had a 9 month baby living in mice infested apartment. Babies food, bottles, our food, everything pretty much was in contact with mice.  (i have pictures)  Mice poop everywhere....disgusting.. also,  LOOK UP! the fan in the living room is disgustingly black and dusty. .... do not turn it on unless you want to get asthma.  According to the host the apartment became dirty because she had windows open for one day... ill say thats impossible, that dust and dirt on the floor has not been cleaned way long before we came. I am guessing floors were never cleaned.  Also, you are welcome to the host, i cleaned around before leaving and made sure no garbage was left behind and the towels were in one area to be washed.    lets keep going.   there is no privacy, host was having things done on the roof, i was given 5 minute notice that there will be a man on the roof. but why everyday. no privacy at all..  next  before leaving i asked the host to do final walk through the place before we left. SHE REFUSED, and did not go up. I took pictures of the place before leaving. Now two weeks later she asking for 300$ to repaint her whole hallway, according to her we scratched it up with a stroller. how?!?!? the stroller was kept downstairs on the stairs. i do not have the strength to pull the stroller back and forth.....   Also, it is a ghetto. i would say not safe for people with families. i was scared to leave without my husband being around.    IF LIKE LIVING IN DUSTY, DIRTY, MICE INFESTED APARTMENT IN A GHETTO, it is a perfect place for you!

Place was what I needed for one night, though I will say checkout is at 12pm, and the person cleaning the space had knocked on my door in the morning three different times before noon to get me out. Was a bit stressful in the morning, but ultimately solid stay.
My brother got robbed in front of this air bnb please be very careful in this neighborhood. The lady told my brother he was going to get robbed the day before

The room corresponded to the description and the photos, with a slightly dated feel, however I would have liked to know that my window overlooked a wall and that I would not see daylight during my entire stay.    It feels a bit like being in a youth hostel (for exchanges with other tenants) which means that the cleanliness of the bathroom and the kitchen also depends on others, for me everything went well.    The accommodation is in a quiet street, with shops nearby including a large supermarket.  I was afraid of the distance from Manhattan but the 2 m° lines 5 minutes away on foot are perfect for all visits and walks.

Rivka's place is cozy, quiet, and clean.  Great a/c, comfy bed, great water pressure.  There are no unpleasant surprises like with a lot of places.  The room itself is very nice, with some artful flourishes and conveniences like shelves and a dresser.  All in all a great stay, would recommend to anyone.

It’s really 4 flights of steep stairs and a little creepy navigating the house but the room is clean, private, comfortable and quiet. There’s a small single bed in the room and it appears to have been a part of a closet or larger bedroom at one time. It has no windows but it was perfect for what I needed which was a good nights rest, a hot shower, peace and quiet, and I was on my way. The room and house are being used as storage and for some type of commercial activity and it reminded me more of a hostel than a home, but the neighborhood is nice and safe, and room was very clean and bed was comfortable. The bathroom was clean as well. For the price and area you can’t beat it! I will stay there again!

What a neat little place! This is definitely a budget room, but it has everything you would need for a short couple night stay. The carpet is clean, bed was comfortable, sheets and towels were also clean, and the check in process was very clear. Some things to keep in mind: this room shares the 2nd floor with a business. So you have to walk through one of the offices where a gentleman is editing jewelry photos in order to get to the space. The employees of this small business were welcoming though, showed me where the kitchen was, refrigerator, microwave, shower etc. All of that being said, the room locks and you are provided with a key if requested, so I never felt like my belongings were unsafe. It's not the type of room you would want to book for weeks on end, but as a budget last minute suite, I couldn't have asked for more!

Loved the location about an hour in train from manhattan & very accessible with bus & train transportation i never felt unsafe & was a clean airbnb loved the host she was very nice! definitely recommend

This room was not a room in a building. It was a room off of the public side walk of a busy street. The rooms door opens to the street. The host did not handoff the key to me instead she unsafely put in a plastic box that attached with a magnet to a poll next to the rooms door which made it more unsafe. The lock was old and I couldn’t get in and she would not respond to my text or calls. Then she said that the lock was tricky. I couldn’t get out either as the door would get stuck. The shower was dirty. No place to put the luggage. No hangers or space to put clothing in. Her small closet was filled with her clothes. I checked out early as a suspicious man was behind the room and had cut a cord in front of it’s door. I called the police.it was very unsafe. The host then asked me for more money claiming that I had broken the key box that holds the key. Good think I took pictures and video taped my leaving. She’s just trying to make a quick buck. Unsafe, unclean, and no show host who’s deceitful. Worst experience ever.

My stay was lovely and I’m  grateful I found Scott’s place. Scott and Jillian were incredibly responsive and flexible, making check in stress-free. There’s a lot more space than I expected. The place is clean and newly renovated. A great place!
Very clean. Check in was easy and stress free

Clean and comfortable stay for a long weekend in NYC. Couldn't beat the location on the UWS, between two subway stops. Walked a block to restaurants, grocery, drug store, etc. Felt safe and slept well. Thank you!

Private space in the basement of the house with a private detached bath. A mini-fridge and microwave are available. I stayed only one night during transit via JFK. The location is  very accessible either by public transport (the Q7 & Q10 buses) or costs about $15-20 with private UberX. The place is self check-in but the process is smooth and very systematic (it may take a few moments to figure out the door latches though). The advantage is that you can check-in anytime after 2 and I arrived at 9:00 PM. Despite that, I did not really feel unsafe in the neighborhood. Therer are also multiple options for commuting to other areas of New York.   The place itself was very clean with clean linens, pillows, comforter, dresser, TV and closet/hangars in the bedroom. The bathroom was awesome with ample toilet paper, towels, soap and shampoo available. Although I did not interact with the hosts, they did a couple of things that brought a smile to my face. Hosts left 2 water bottles in the fridge which was very nice because I had forgotten to purchase some at JFK. Also, it was supposed to rain the next morning so they left an umbrella and a feet-wiping towel when I returned the next morning from my excursions. Although I had my own umbrella, it was still nice.  The only thing that alarmed me initially was that there was a dog in the vicinity (maybe the hosts' or someone else's) who got restless when I arrived. It also started running around and barking around mid-night for some reason which briefly woke me up. Other than that minor hiccup, it was a very pleasant stay.

The apartment is a safe part of town, we didn’t feel unsafe coming back late at night! The space is tight, but we knew that as the listing states it is a micro studio. Julia was very responsive and instructions to get into the apartment were very clear.

This was honestly the best little place to stay if you’re doing a couple days in New York! The studio was so cute and clean and cozy and Julia had great attention to detail.  Also, as solo female travelers we wanted to stress how safe this place felt. It is on the ground floor, but there are sturdy bars on the window and a big iron door before the front door that made us feel very safe and comfortable. Plus it was in a very safe feeling neighborhood.  Overall I cannot recommend this place enough!

Not a bad place if you are a medical student looking to stay for a rotation or two but some issues.  1. The air conditioning unit has to be left on 78 degrees so basically it’s worthless from June through August.  2. The house is very old and noises of any kind can be heard throughout every wall day or night.  3. My reusable meal containers after washing them would just disappear. They would not be in the cabinets, garbage, etc so likely someone was stealing them or throwing out Tupperware which is just braindead.  4. There was a neurotic guest in the house when I was there. Very confrontative for no serious reason. Felt very uncomfortable there and would leave as often as possible.

I stayed here with my two friends and it was wonderful. They keep the space very clean and the location is great. We walked home late multiple times and never felt unsafe. There is so much to explore in this area! I would absolutely stay again.

I stayed in this room at Carlos and Yvette's house for 16 days. I can say that it is the perfect place for anyone traveling to New York. Starting with cleaning, the entire place is always 100% clean and organized (bedroom, bathroom and kitchen). It is worth mentioning that all bed and bath linen is of quality and super clean and fragrant. Yvette has a special dedication to cleaning, which made me very happy, as I spent 16 days in a very pleasant place. As for the location, it couldn't be better, exactly 3 minutes walk and you'll be on the subway, and then quickly anywhere in New York. There is no warmer welcome. They welcomed me very well, explained everything to me, showed me places that I loved, always responded to my messages promptly and never let me miss anything. They have an unparalleled education. Not to mention that in the room they leave everything you need, umbrella, soap, shampoo, conditioner, toothbrush and toothpaste and first aid kit. And the room has all worked on the details in terms of decoration. I certainly hope to return to NY and stay again with Carlos and Yvette and I will recommend this place to all my friends. If you are looking for a good place to stay in NY, you can rent their room without fear. Best value for money in NY!!!

I stayed for ten days at Carlos and Yvette's house and my experience was wonderful. Before arriving in NY, they always responded to me very quickly and politely, answering all my doubts. The person who welcomed me when I arrived was Yvette, an amazing person with whom I got along well from the first minute. She gave me tips on public transport, places to eat and interesting spots to visit. The location is great, several buses and subway lines that take you to Manhattan in just a few minutes. The place is very safe, even at night. I was traveling alone and sometimes arrived late, at no point did I feel unsafe on the way between the subway and home. There is everything close to the house: lots of places to eat, pharmacies, supermarkets, pizzeria, stores that sell fruit 24 hours a day, it's all very practical.   The hosts are wonderful, very friendly and helpful. Yvette took me for a walk and to eat, she is amazing.  The place is very quiet, I was never disturbed by any noise.   The cleanliness is impeccable: the bathroom and kitchen, which are shared with other guests, were always incredibly clean and organized. The shower, wow, what a shower! Wonderful!  I didn't cook, but for anyone who wants to cook, the kitchen is very complete, it has everything, absolutely nothing is missing.  The room I stayed in surprised me, it's bigger than it looks in the photos. When I entered, I already felt a pleasant smell, demonstrating the affection of the hosts in every detail. You can see that they take care of everything with lots of love and care. The room is complete, very clean and has very cute decor. The bed is delightful, with clean, fragrant sheets and pillowcases, a beautiful quilt and a blanket available. There is a large closet, extra towels, hangers, first aid kit, personal products available (toothbrush, soap, toothpaste, dish soap, hairdryer). There is a huge mirror, which allows you to see your entire body. Next to the bed there is a nightstand with a lamp and a very useful pin socket for charging your cell phone. For those who want to work or study there is a table with a chair and lamp. There is also a map of NY and several menus of delicious places to eat nearby. I also thought it would be great to have a blackout curtain and hangers behind the door to hang towels.   Anyway, Carlos and Yvette's house is a splendid place to stay. I hope one day to return to NY and stay at their house again. Carlos and Yvette, thank you very much for the care and attention with which you welcomed me! God bless you always!

We needed to check out early because of the dust issue and the stairs.  This house is also not able to be rented for less than 30 days, but we did not know this till after booking.  The dust around the home and the clutter was A LOT.  My mom was there for surgery and we needed to be close to the hospital.  When I let Kim know that it was unsafe for my mom, the stairs were much steeper than I thought and the cleanliness was less than ideal, she said she would contact airbnb for a refund for us.  Airbnb said she was unwilling to return any of our money.  Even one day would have been kind, yet she chose to keep it all.  We moved to a hotel and everything worked out fine, but the thousands of dollars she was able to pocket without us staying at her residence.

Cozy apartment in a safe, attractive neighborhood in Manhattan.  Everything we needed was nearby - subway station, grocery and drug stores and more.  Easy walking distance to Central Park and Museum Mile.  Apartment was just as described - the kitchen is fully equipped!  Yulia was easy to communicate with, quick to respond and all our dealings with her went smoothly.

I traveled from Atlanta from visiting to see my fiance and family. My flight didn't land until after 11.00 p.m. so I asked my fiance to pick up the key. When she went she was met by George but also met with spider webs in her face..and a basement full of dust. The sun hit different parts of the house and you can see cobwebs in the Windows and on corners of the floor. The spiders and bugs made themselves at home with a heavy load of dust. The chairs were stained..you couldn't even sit down comfortably without feeling dirty. It was also presented to her 2 rusted pots to cook in. Little utensils. So now I get that brief feedback from her. She asked me could she text him later to see if he had cleaning supplies and told him it was spiders everywhere and dusty and that she has asthma and it has to be cleaned. His response was yes he does and he will leave the swifter near the broom. Instead of going down there and cleaning it himself. We shouldn't have to come and clean thoroughly. So she goes and buys cleaning items herself and covers to cover the chair and couch so I can sit down when I get there. Now I finally arrive and see more than she did with her brief quick tour. The stove was dirty..pots rusted as she stated..go in the bathroom sink is dirty..cobwebsb on the ceilings...cobwebs in the tub. The tub with dirt rings around it..with dead bugs on the shower mat.  Dirty used razors on the side of the tub ..old soap bars in the shower and sink..toilet stained. Now as she stated as you walk into the basement cobwebs everywhere regardless if you live in a basement it can still be properly cleaned of all that. NOTHING...the tv area full of dust..floors were dirty...he did add two additional pots but they weren't cleaned...my fiance after trying to dust with the cleaning supplies guess what triggered her asthma. For $100 a night she shouldn't have had to clean nor catch an asthma attack we had to contact air b and b for another location which was a long time consuming ordeal with no place to stay until today. So we had no place to stay with a vacation that went left all because of basic essentials as far as cleanliness. Instead of leaving a swifter..mop and broom he should have utilized them before renting.

If you want to stay in Brooklyn and are looking for somewhere to stay this would be a great spot! Read the reviews and description everything stated is accurate. We were looking to save on accommodations and parking (by parking in a nearby lot for 100$ for 5 days => a steal if you compare to other city parking prices). Had a safe enjoyable experience the perfect spot for a couple who are willing to explore Brooklyn and commute into NYC by subway!

I was afraid about Airbnb , this is first time choosing to stay sharing bathroom with more peoples and I said its overall I expected!!! . The room is super clean , blankets, bathroom. nice scent . Security is A plus . Location its five stars . Closed to all !!! Definitely I will come back same place .

I stayed here for when I visited nyc. It’s a cute place in Brooklyn, not too far from the subway. It was fairly quite in the Airbnb, the walls are thin so you can hear other guest when in your room or in the halls. From what I could tell, the bathroom was lightly cleaned daily. The only problem I had was my ac was broken, and there wasn’t good heat in the room. The blinds in my room were missing panes and the windows wouldn’t shut all the way. There was only a few times I felt unsafe, and it was when the front gate of the house froze and wouldn’t lock. Otherwise it a fairly safe place to stay in Brooklyn. I don’t think it was worth all of the service and cleaning fees though.
Good apartment for 6 people,only one twin bed was very stiff, is not convenient for tourists, is so far away from Manhattan,didn’t like the area, unsafe and the host is not very kind

The building was a little bit sketchy but the apartment itself is clean and very cute. Perfect for a couple or small group. Nice area and very close to restaurants, grocery stores, bodegas and the subway. Was able to get to Time Square in a 10 min walk to the sub which we took for 4 stops. Definitely recommend

What a pleasant and effortless stay in BK! The cute home is located near a bunch of good eats, a playground/park, a farmers market, and several coffee shops.  Check in was smooth, the bedding was comfortable, the kitchen was fully stocked, and checkout prep was stress free.  We came with a toddler and the place is pretty kid proof and there were toys and books available.  David and Anh were so helpful and responsive.  We are so grateful to have them host our stay while we were in town for a wedding.

I’ve stayed at Jessica’s Airbnb, and Jessica is the best host you could ever ask for. She is always very communicative and strives to make sure your experience is as great as possible - any questions or concerns were always taken care of quickly and with kindness. The place has a very exquisite, modern touch and is extremely clean. Moreover, almost everything you need is there for any duration of stay - from toiletries to a plethora of kitchen amenities. I cannot stress enough how caring of a person Jessica is to her guests and how great of a place this is, and I would highly recommend her place to anyone looking for a stay in a warm, safe, and lively location in Brooklyn.

The home was awesome. No complaints with cleanliness. The property looks just like the pictures. However the couch from the pictures is not the one in the home. But it was fine. The issue was with the host’s communication. There was no air mattress as advertised, and when we asked about it she was irritated with us, and stated we were supposed to request it. When I informed her there was no indication of that in the notes or descriptions she had nothing to say. Basically this same back and forth bad communication continued regarding different questions. Like gaining access to linen for the extra mattress once it was delivered was such a struggle. She really let us know we were getting on her nerves when she told us we were becoming stressful on her daughter because she had to tend to us while they were also on vacation. I was sorry to hear that but that was very professional and not a good host move. In that same message she asked us if we wanted find a new place to stay.   This could have been a easy simple stay if communication was better, again lovely home. But would not stay with her again.

Although Sarah’s AirbnB was beautifully decorated, clean and a great location, we will not stay there again. We felt very uncomfortable with her rules, though not difficult for us to follow, we were on edge the whole time feeling as if we were being monitored. At one point she message asking us to remind everyone about the no shoes policy. No one wore shoes in the apartment The whole weekend but obviously she was listening “just in case”. It was creepy. We also felt uncomfortable that our son and grandson who live nearby were not welcomed to stop by to say hello.
Neighborhood appears more sketchy than it actually is

I was not happy with this place.  The inside and outside stairs are not safe, especially if one has a heavy suitcase.  There was no luggage rack or place to put my suitcase.  The room was set up so that the only place to watch tv is on the bed, even though an easy chair was provided.  There were no instructions for wifi.  I thought there was no hot water in the shower, but it turned out the hot and cold are reversed.  The tub is unsafe -- no mat, non-slip strips or grab bar.  There was major construction going on across the street, and the view was of a roof with the construction beyond.  I would not stay here again.

The apartment is nice, well decorated but the environment in our opinion is very dangerous, it is not recommended for a traveler who buys things or who wants to enjoy going out some night.   20 m away is a liquor store where there are many drunk and drug addicted people from morning until dawn.  There is a lot of garbage.  The metro is approximately one km away but on the way they tried to rob us twice in 15 days, we had to call the police and run the second time.

Very nice, the room is just as in the photos. The only thing is the location, since the closest metro station is an area full of homeless people. It is not dangerous, but it creates insecurity, especially when it gets dark. The impeccable apartment.

This place was nice and cosy and had everything you needed. It actually had a full kitchen with proper cooking facilities which was great. There is a supermarket down the road and it was close to the train lines. Took us about 30 - 40 mins to get in an out of NYC. The neighbourhood was a little sketchy even though we were right next to a police station but the security at the place was good.

This was a great apartment for us as we wanted to be in the Bedford-Stuyvesant area of Brooklyn. It's a fun neighbourhood - the areas with increasing numbers of hipster cafés and bars were really nearby, but the street itself is nice and quiet, safe feeling and opposite a good-size park. For us, travelling with a baby, this was perfect. Also we knew RJ didn't have a travel crib listed so we'd just decided to turn the sofa bed into a nest. We asked for an extra bottom sheet and with this and  ample pillows/cushions this was totally do-able. Another advantage for us on this front was the yard straight out the back of the apartment. RJ chooses not to flag this up on the listing, so accordingly I have no comment on what the yard is like,  but for us, having access to a couple of chairs and some shade out there was a really helpful escape when the baby was napping. There's a front yard too (this is on the listing) which was a nice spot to feed the baby outdoors and people-watch at the same time. As to the rest of the flat it was clean, comfortable and well equipped, and RJ was an accessible host.

The apartment conforms to the photos, it is located on the ground floor on the interior terrace side, this one is not really presentable.  We did not find the cleaning satisfactory because it was carried out in a very summary manner.  The host was responsive to answer our questions.  Concerning us, no arrangement concerning the departure time and the storage of our suitcases until our fairly late return flight (we had not yet left when the future tenants were waiting in front of the door).  Metro line G is about a 10-minute walk away.  We found it pleasant to find shower gel, shampoo, toilet paper, dishwashing liquid, hand soap, tea, coffee... etc. upon our arrival.

I booked the property at short notice and the host got confused and didn’t realize I was arriving on the date I was arriving. The host did not provide the check-in instructions on airbnb, other than “will give instructions when you arrive”. When I tried to contact her on the day of my arrival, there was no response, so I ended up stranded on her doorstep. Only got a response after contacting airbnb customer service. The host also implied the whole thing was my fault for booking at short notice. The whole thing was rather stressful.

The place is awesome. You can expect everything. My stay was for 4 days, so I have no idea with the laundry thing. The neighborhood is a bit shady as you know Queens. Other than that, everything about this place is just perfect & great so does suzan.
Small room for the price, but the type of people who stay in the building, consist of active drug dealers, crack heads, and prostitutes. Saw a fight in the lobby within the first hour.

On the day before my check-in, the host and I trying ti find a time that worked for both of us. Since I had an early morning flight, she suggested I come straight from the airport and the room would be ready for me. However, when I landed the next day and I let her know that I was going to be on my way from the airport , she told me that the room would not be ready yet and I decided to explore Manhattan in the meantime and since I only had one backpack with me that wasn't a problem. I also asked the host if she had any recommendations on her favorite things to do in the city and she promptly replied with something along the lines of, "I am busy with work, let's talk later. Thanks" I was quite taken aback with her response as I was just trying to be friendly and other hosts in the past have been more than happy to share their recommendations with me.  When I finally arrived to check in one of the first things she said to me was, " you send so many texts, you talk so so much". I also wanted to mention that this place is on the 4th floor and there is no elevator, I don't see that mentioned anywhere in this listing, but I'm sure Deycke would be able to help you carry your bags up if you needed.  My room was quite nice. It was well lit and airy however the desk in the room felt a bit sticky and unclean. The towels that I was given had a very strong smell of laundry detergent and an undertone of mildew, they also felt a bit cold, like they had not been dried properly. The bathroom is pretty small but that's just how it is in New York so no complaints there, however there was black mold in the caulking between the wall and the sink and there was a large amount of dust and debris in the gap between the tub and the sink, like it hadn't been cleaned in years. When I attempted to take a shower the water started to pool at my feet and I looked down and the water was grey. It was really disgusting and I did not feel clean after my shower. The shower curtains were made out of a material that absorbs water and they also smelt of mildew there was also brown stains on one of the shower curtains. There is also no bin in the bathroom.  The kitchen had a very strange unpleasant smell but it didn't bother me too much as I was hardly in the kitchen during my stay. There wasn't any clean sponge for me to use to wash my dish so I ended up putting the dish detergent on my hands and washing the plate/spoon with my hands when I needed it.  The highlights of my stay were definitely the cats, the location, the proximity to the subway station, the natural sunlight, and the comfy mattress.

The place was nice but I felt like I was being stalk he has cameras everywhere. I had a couple of my family members come to chill for a few hours and he tried to charge me $20 a person.He watched the  camera and told me how many people was there which was creepy

I was welcomed when checking in. The location is great to nyc . Very nice neighborhood. This place did have roaches. The host was nice when communicating. My room had a ceiling leak, turning out to be sewage :( the smell was really bad. This saddened me because I liked the location. Also someone ate my food everytime I used the shared kitchen… as well as my drinks … no camera so people can steal from you. Be safe. ❤️
Overall a cozy spot especially if you want the whole place to yourself. The area was a little suspect at night but overall it was an enjoyable stay.

I stayed at Britts appartement for three weeks and had a very pleasant stay. Everything you need is there, including handsoap, food containers, shampoo, scissors, a freezer etc. There is some room for improvement concerning the cleaning (it is dusty and the microwave was full with splashes). If you are a light sleeper please take earplugs for the sound of the heating system. The heating pipes  make sure that the overall temperature in the appartement is quite high so don’t bring your thick sweaters;)  The appartement is located in a quiet neighborhood en close to line 6 that can bring you downtown. I never felt unsafe. Please try a cookie @Janies bakery at the corner of the street, they are the best!  Britt is a wonderful host and has a very fast response time. She even allowed me to check-out later. Overall, I would highly recommend this appartement!

Pros:  I paid only $65/day for this midtown location; right near the Empire State Building. A fantastic price for the location. If you only need a budget place to sleep, I DO recommend this location. If you need comfort and civility, don't use this location.  Cons:  The building has public showers (my room had its own shower). As a result, in the evening people in need of shower would negotiate with the security guard to take a shower for a fee.   Homeless people sleep in the staircase area if they are able to sneak in without being detected.  Smoking is prohibited, but people do smoke.  I also witnessed a verbal exchange between a security guard and a resident. The guard was critical of the  resident bringing a new person overnight every night for a sexual activity which was against the rules of the building.   I had to call police at 1AM in the morning due to a severe next-door domestic violence incident. I thought they would kill each other if I didn't do something. Police came and took away the offender. Next time, there was another couple fighting, but not to the extent that would warrant a 911 call.  These episodes should give you a good understanding about the overall climate of the building that mostly hosts very low-income residents.  A drug dealer sells drugs right near the entrance of the building. And "nothing can be done because he rents out a room in this building and pays daily to stay" - according to a security guard. There is only one entrance, and it is impossible not to see this guy. He is extremely skinny, unhealthy looking person who feeds his drug habits by selling drugs to homeless drug-addicts right near the entrance. I even witnessed exchange of money for drugs. I personally saw him several times a day surrounded by several homeless drug addicts.
I wouldn't go back. I understand it's air bnb and the location and buildings are left a mystery but nope. Felt unsafe and it was confirmed in the morning when the host barged in without knocking.

We mostly enjoyed our stay but there was obvious prostitution and drug dealing going on in the building.   The Good: Great location in midtown manhattan, friendly (but passive) front desk, two sets of elevators that we never had to wait long for, and the apartment seemed pretty clean. Small but useable kitchen (although why cook when you’re visiting New York? 🍕) You’re 1 block from the 34th street subway station where you can catch a bunch of different trains.   The Bad: It is not a family-friendly building. It is an 8 or 9 story building with all studio apartments. There are friendly people working the front desk, but they’re not really security. Front door is unlocked 24/7 and they dont check anyone coming in and out, from what I saw. While it’s a nice neighborhood, this building is the roughest spot for a couple of blocks. When we arrived late Friday night, with a small child, there were what appeared to be drug dealers and prostitutes out front. There were also lots of college-age kids partying, likely because it was the cheapest room in manhattan. A kid was passed out in our hallway. That first night was the worst of our 4, probably because it was Friday night. We did suspect prostitution on our floor the rest of the week, though, as we noticed one or two women walking in and out of our hallway every hour or so until the wee hours. Thanksfully, with all of the shady activity, most of it was quiet from our room, so we slept well.    Bottom line: If you dont mind a little bit of rough edges and you just want a good location, clean room and a door that locks, this will work for you. If you are traveling with young children or if you dont like the sound of this, look elsewhere.

The location is great, but that’s really about it. The building itself is pretty dingy and sketchy looking, but the worst thing is that our room had a roach infestation. Within literally 15 minutes of checking in we saw a big roach crawling inside the microwave door, one in the cabinet, and two dead smashed ones on the floor around the bed. The host was polite and accommodating when we brought the issue to her attention, at least, and offered a refund when we said we would not be staying. The the security guard downstairs who checked us was a bit pushy about offering us another room. However, we decided to cancel and stay elsewhere because we didn’t trust that anything in the building had actually been cleaned adequately. It was really disgusting and unacceptable, and I would not book a stay here again.

The first night we could not sleep at all because of big roaches in the walls, under the bed  and bathroom, and also bugs in bed. Next day I informed this to the host and they send somebody to clean and placed an electric device near the bed. The situation improved, but there were still roaches in the bathroom area and shower. I asked the host to put another electric device also in the bathroom and they did the next day. I also asked them to leave an antiroaches spray to use if necessary. The situation improved but I had to used the entire spray during our stay because little roaches emerged from time to time. Of course this situation was horrible for us, and I let the host know that I expected to receive some kind of discount, specially because we could not sleep at all the first night. They gave me a 40 dollars credit, which I considered not enough. All I expected for the studio was to be clean and well located. During the night we were bitten by bugs in the sheets, that is inacceptable. They should had discounted at least an entire night to the bill. The location in near most attractions but you cannot enter the building from sixth avenue at night, because every night around 5 or 6 men were selling drugs and stalking at women in the corner. The studio is very small, it doesn`t have a real window, there is a kitchen but we couldn`t cooked anything because were disgusted by the insects.  People smoke in the hall all the time so the entire studio smells like marihuana. Also is very loud during the night, with people screaming at the hall. The price for the studio is to high for what you get.

The location is excellent. Unfortunately there are many negatives.  Our packages that we ordered on the internet were a headache to get because the porters would not deliver them or they would go to an administration which would charge us 5$ per package.  The place is full of homeless people. There was a fight in the corridor and the shouts and blows were quite loud. When it was late they gathered to smoke marijuana outside the main door and this gave quite a lot of mistrust and insecurity.

The room was clean, cozy and the perfect size for 3-4 people. The location is unbeatable, close to Penn Station and MSG. We had concerns about the people living in this apartment building - we witnessed two different fights (that were scary and physical) outside of our room in the same early morning. The residents and front desk security guards were not good about wearing masks. There was always some type of confrontation going down in the hallways, at the front desk, and right outside the door but I guess that’s NY for you. We all said we would stay here again but maybe with a second lock on the door and definitely not during coronavirus.

For a cheap place to sleep, this is a place.   Unfortunately there were lots of familiar smoke odors and EDM bumping through the walls throughout the nights we stayed. Sketchy front desk service too. The location is decent though!

(!!!BED BUG!!! warning) This place looked exactly like the pictures, as listed. The host was kind and communicative as we checked in. It’s in a good location. Unfortunately, as we were packing at the end of our stay, we found BED BUGS. We informed both the host and Airbnb support and they were not incredibly sympathetic or helpful. And if anyone has ever dealt with the precautions you need to take after encountering BED BUGS, you know it’s a pain. I suppose if you want an inexpensive place to stay in NYC, this is a good place. It’s exactly what we expected to pay for (smells like drugs and has some riff raff, which was all expected for the price). However we didn’t expect to pay for BED BUGS! Suitcases cost hundreds to replace!

I was lied to and my money is gone . I left 9 hrs of being there on a 3 night stay  and thought the owners would do the decent thing after I sent videos and pictures of what I was dealing with but they didn’t . They acted like things would be refunded and played the time game and then ghosted me. They only Refunded me the cleaning fee and told me they would handle things when Airbnb cashes them out my Payment .  So now I’m out of money for a place I didn’t even stay at that had Baby roaches and broke beds. She even acknowledged the prior renters had kids who could of broke the bed. This was a cemetery trip and they made it even worse. I’m grieving and got robbed out of my money. God has my back though and I promise they will write some lies that I cannot respond to but that’s ok. Karma is a bihhh and god will always bless me because I’m a good person.  Now I will be done and let them comment lies on me. I wish we could upload screen shots and videos so I CAN PROVE MY POINT!!

The stay was fine but after the host exorted me for an extra 1000 for damages I know nothing about. He stated I must pay him 1000 or else my card would be charged 2000. I was scared and payed him the 1000 and then he continued to harras me saying I must pay him 500 more. I reported him and unfortunately since that was not directly through air Bnb I can’t even get my money back. Money I didn’t have to begin with. Not sure if he’s done this to anyone else but stay away from this guy for your own good.

Michael is a super kind host who goes out of his way to make sure you have a good stay. His place is super clean, has a really well equipped kitchen, and he’s a text away if you need a hand with anything (he responds to text super fast in a really nice way). Getting in is stress-free, and he had a bottle of wine and some snacks waiting for us. We were excited to grill and use the firepit, and he had cleared off the snow in the backyard to make it easy, and set up a heat lamp... it was the coziest thing.   The only disappointment for us was that we’d fallen in love with this listing for the hot tub, and it wasn’t accessible (we were there in February, and it was covered with ice and snow). Mike went out of his way to try to make sure we still had a good experience (including finding a stock tank that we could fill), but it still wasn’t quite what we’d hoped for—only noting that just in case anyone else might be doing a winter stay and had hoped to use it, too.
