She provided us with maps and other info, along with snacks and water to grab should we need it. All in all a comfortable stay.

The neighborhood felt a little unsafe:  a group of guys leered at me at 5 in the morning and there were always people hanging about too the point that I felt uncomfortable walking there and got taxis instead. However the building was secure and there were plenty of ammenities provided. Was also well located for subway stations.

I loved my 15-day stay at Barbara's house. First of all, the room, there is a large bed with a super comfortable mattress, a cupboard, for storage, several bath towels available, sheets changed every week, and a fridge with various juices, water and small cakes (when I tell you that she is attentive) Everything is very clean, the bathroom is spotless, I never had to wait to have access to it. May the avenue be noisy did not bother me in any way. A digression concerning the place, it is a very lively neighborhood, the metro (line Q) is less than 500m away, There are always a lot of people (I was alone during my stay) even after 10 p.m., I have never been worried, and I have never felt unsafe, so it was without any apprehension that I took the metro beyond 9 p.m. I will now tell you about Barbara, what a beautiful person, discreet, very attentive, available, very available, anticipating needs, always there to listen to you, and help you if necessary, joyful, and a patient (I had to with my light English!) and her banana cake, yum, Miami!. It was a beautiful meeting, and it is with sadness that I left her, because I I had a great time with her. You guessed it, during my next stay, it will be at her place.

Very clean and very beautiful and artsy place to stay in. Really enjoyed my stay here except that it was too far from all the places I have to go to. Uber costs so much because there's not a lot in the area. The neighborhood is tricky as well coz it felt sketchy. One wrong turn and you could end up somewhere not safe. I would recommend this if you were by groups. But other than that, Still a very good place to stay. The house is very homey and accomodating and gives you privacy as well which was very important for me.

We stayed with Barbara for 3 nights in October 2017 and felt very comfortable. There was a comfortable bed big enough for 2 and even a fridge in the room. Barbara offered us drinks, snacks and breakfast and everything was clean there. It's only a few meters from the subway and we didn't feel unsafe in the area and would come again. Thank you Barbara!😃

Brady's apartment is located in a quiet area of ​​Brooklyn... We never felt unsafe.. The area, however, doesn't have many nice restaurants or nice bars for going out nearby. .. The apartment is on lines j m and z gates avenue stop. It's direct from the airport and for Manhattan the M line allows you to go up to Rokfeller Center while the J and Z allow you to go to the south. .. It takes 10 minutes to walk to get to the metro and 30 minutes to get to Canal Street station. .. So it's a little far from Manhattan. .. The house itself was very quiet, it's actually a hostel. We had the room next to the living room and we didn't hear any noises. The kitchen is very well equipped and in the morning you can make coffee, tea and eat cereal bars, all provided free of charge. There is a supermarket not far away to buy extra things or could cook in the evening and a large fridge to store everything. The first downside was the size of our room. . Very small in fact impossible to open two suitcases at the same time... downside also for the impossibility of opening the window. .The only ventilation is through air conditioning. .. the last downside was that according to house rules you can't make food before 9 a.m.... It's a little late for a hostel and besides everyone was making their coffee from 7 a.m.... despite these three points which didn't prevent me from having a good time, I recommend this place.

The stay is 2 min walking distance from Subway station Church Av on B & Q line. The home is clean and tidy. Host is very friendly. Our flight got delayed on the day of check-in and we reached at midnight on a cold spring night and Barbara offered us tea. Stay is Good value for money, you won't find this price anywhere else in New York. The only thing that bothered me was too many homeless people on the street. It felt little unsafe to come late at nights.
Everything was clean and comfortable and it made my stay enjoyable and low-stress.  Would definitely stay again.  :-)

My stay was wonderful! Lisa’s place is very large for a one-bedroom apartment in NYC. Specifically, the bathroom and the kitchen. The apartment is furnished to be very cozy and it is very clean. The kitchen is a cook’s dream! Lots of counter space and amazing All Clad kitchen utensils. The apartment itself is a 3rd floor walk up but not tiring at all. Perfect location, a block away from the 20 minute C train to Times Square and within quick walking distance to Central Park. Great grocery store right across the street. Lots of coffee and bakery’s all around the corner (all better than Starbucks, don’t go there!). The trash room in the basement was very well lit and clean. It’s a bit noisy on the street outside at night, but that’s to be expected as it’s the city. Tons of people and restaurants all around! I never felt uncomfortable or unsafe. Lisa was a great host and very communicative and willing to help with anything. I would definitely stay again.

The place is very, very nice, a great building and lovely interior, there's a large living room with books and big dining table and a clean and well-equipped kitchen (coffee and tea are provided and there's a fridge to store some food). The bathroom was also very clean. The room (I was right next to the living room) was very comfortable and I slept very well. The house is located pretty close to the Subway and to a bus stop, so getting around is no problem. I didn't feel unsafe in the neighborhood and there are some delis and restaurants nearby. Overall, I would highly recommend this place :)

I very much enjoyed my stay at this place. The location is great, close to subway and bus. Just 1 min to bus and around 8 to subway  I asked a few locals about the safety at night for a solo girl, and they all said its fine, so I just took their word and I was taking late night transport ( 11-12 midnight) and walking home alone.  Although first night it felt a bit shady but then over time I felt absolutely comfortable.   I never got the chance to meet Brady but the communication was great and he arranged what I needed while he was in a trip. He is very responsive. I had a small unexpected problem in my room, and he and Omar (the manager) kindly changed my room immediately to even a more nicer room with the same price! Thank you Brady again. You are awesome.  Omar himself is a gem. He is so kind and sweet and super friendly like someone that you know from long time ago. And he is keeps everything super clean! I miss him and our talk already.   The other guests were nice and everyone were doing their own thing. So hanging out is optional like said in other reviews. And they are making the place even nicer! Don’t miss it.

Brady is a great host and super responsive.  The room was basic and small but clean and great for a short stay.  The house overall was clean and charming and I had no issues with noise or anything. On the neighborhood, it’s got some way to go  - it’s not dangerous but still pretty rough around the edges and not the trendy part of Brooklyn. That being said there are some cool places to eat and drink and you’re not that far from the subway

This was by far the best Airbnb experience I have ever had. Noelia is so sweet and she kept the kitchen and bathroom consistently clean. Isaac responded to texts very quickly and was a great source of information. I didn't meet Linda until close to the end of my summer, but she was very nice and welcoming. The brownstone is pretty close to the subway stop and I didn't feel unsafe walking back, even late at night. Highly recommend!

This place is represented exactly how it is. I only give 4 stars because the listing says microwave, and unfortunately it was broken for 8 out of 10 days I was there. They have now replaced it with a brand new one so don't worry going forward! Laura is a FIVE STAR host, extremely communicative, friendly, and hospitable but if you don't want that she's out of your way. Honestly she and her husband were the best part of my stay. I got to feel like I was coming "home" instead of to a super-rando spot. The bus lines are right around the corner from their home, and you enter through an alleyway behind the house. I would recommend staying here with a travel buddy. As a woman alone it was a little bit sketchy (can't change the neighbors!), and I definitely know the neighborhood of Jackson Heights, so the 'hood was not a surprise/unfamiliar to me (former New Yorker of 7 years). 7 train express line only runs from 3:30pm-9:35pm so keep that in mind if you're commuting for any reason. If you're looking for a place on a budget - this is your stop! 5 min from LGA, 20min from JFK. Quick in and out, and you're saving a boat load compared to Brooklyn/the city.

The location of this spot is incredible to say the least. Beautiful spot, nice and sunny loft. It is a very short walk from some of the best shopping and great restaurants. Aurora’s was great, nice vibe and brunch. The bar across the street was cute and lively. I would highly recommend this spot for the location because it truly was great. The host was responsive and hospitable.   With that in mind, the sheets were stained. The first night - we reached out to the host regarding this and he said that the housekeeper cleaned them and that there were more in the closet. There were more sheets in the closet and they were also badly stained. They may have been clean but they did not look it. We feel that the sheets should be new and free of stains/dirt. This was a bit unpleasant, but OK. The comforter was grubby. A new comforter would be more appealing. As well, the bathroom had hair on the counter and in the sink. Again, not a major issue but we would’ve appreciated some more effort to make sure it was clean.

Upon arrival the apartment seemed nice, we were a bit surprised at the number of flights of stairs since that was not mentioned in the description, 4 full flights.  It was decorated fine, a pretty good size space the sofas were stained which did turn me off and there was a Kurig by the front door but no coffee pods.  The worst part of the stay was the evening, first of all the air conditioner is hung on the ceiling right above the bed and it was dripping water on to the pillow through the night.  Earlier in the day, I found the controller for the air conditioner and I wanted to change the settings, but the controller was not working, batteries needed to be replaced.  We reached out the the host and he instructed us to go to the second floor apartment to get their controller since they are the same and would work.  Very noisey location and the shade that is closest to the bed was not working properly and I was not able to close for the evening.  When we woke up Monday, we left and checked into a hotel in Midtown.  It was not going to work out for the 4 nights that we booked.  I was not satisfied with this location and would like to work with Airb&b for a refund for Mon, Tues and Wed nights.

The place is quite far in Queens, however, it's in a calm area and good value for money. The room is big enough for two people. But there is a really small and dark window which can be scary for some visitors. It was clean and good equipped. Laura is a nice person, helpful and will tell you in details how to get to the place. If you don't mind spending more time in public transport, I definitely recommend it.

if you're just looking for a place to crash for 300 bucks a night it's solid!  but I feel like you could do that cheaper elsewhere, it's a nice aesthetic and location but it's not too well upkept, there's lots of clutter - items littered everywhere including drug paraphernalia. The door lock was broken upon arrival and wasn't addressed untill the morning of my checkout, when informed about the issue they told me to just leave it unlocked untill I realized I could just use the deadbolt. The internet speed was unacceptablly slow, were talking 2003 wifi speeds, and that's when it even connects.  The shower backs up and is in need of rodding. I could go on but those were the main things.

Frank was an amazing host-- responsive, quiet, and friendly. I stayed here during my internship in the city. The apartment is extremely close to a subway stop (Q train) and it consistently took me about 40 min to get to Rockefeller Center which is pretty much Downtown/Times Square. Soho/Chinatown is 20 min.   The neighborhood feels very authentically Brooklyn. I never felt unsafe, but it definitely had the ~trendy~ grunge and multicutural-ness that one would expect when thinking about stereotypical Brooklyn. It will be a shock if you're coming from a quiet suburb (like me), but I adjusted quickly.  The room was big and comfortable. The bathroom is a bit utilitarian, but a lot of it can be accredited to the "historic/authentically NYC charm" that the building has.    Overall, this felt like a very NYC apartment. Not Gossip Girl NYC, but closer to what it would actually be like to live in the city.

Super convenient stay for traveling. My boyfriend and I had a late flight info JFK and needed to fly out early the next day from LaGuardia. We had a peaceful nights sleep in Laura’s place and left restful. It’s very close to LaGuardia which saved us lots of stress!

Susan was wonderful on working with us for check in and making sure we had everything you need. It can be an arduous task to be in charge of a large group of adults and make sure everyone gets there alright and has what they need. Susan went above and beyond to make us feel comfortable and helped relieve some of the stress that comes with a trip like this. Our group loved the house and their was plenty of room for everyone. Highly recommend, wouldn't hesitate to rent from her again.

We, a family of four, had I great time visiting Brooklyn, not in the least because of the modern, clean and roomy apartment John has to offer. John is very helpful, resourceful and easy to reach. Clinton Hill is close to the subway and even better, it has a Citibike rental station right in front of the door! There are plenty of good restaurants and shops in the neighborhood. We absolutely recommend this place! Rob Beuse and Nicky Nicola, The Netherlands.

Comfortable for 5 adults, this house is on a quiet street, but only a half a block from Maxcolm X Blvd., which has some of the best restaurants in the City, drug stores, banks, groceries, both subway and bus routes, and places to buy almost anything else you need. Host is accommodating. Wonderful place to anchor a visit exploring New York City.

10 country mice to the city for a wedding!  Our ages ranged from 10 to 74.  The space was terrific. Everyone had a comfortable place to sleep with an air conditioner in each room. There was enough room that we weren't in each other's way. All 10 could gather either in the kitchen/dining area or living room when we wanted to be together. Travel into Manhattan was easy with subway within walking distance. Uber drivers also did not have trouble finding us.  Plenty of restaurants in the area and green grocer around the corner for when we wanted to have dinner "at home". A bank and drug store also near by.  Keypad entry meant we didn't have to worry about trading keys.  Family members came and went from early to late without disturbing others. The apartment is very quite and street noise is minimal. John, our host, responded to our requests immediately - always with a smile. We felt it was important to him that we enjoyed ourselves...and we did! We will recommend this space to any friends who travel to the big city.

House is a perfect brownstone in a great part of Harlem. Local food and scene was fantastic. Locals hanging around, always with a “good evening”. Proximity to the subway could not have been better. We used the 1/2/3 train multiple times a day. House is well stocked with everything you need. Susan communicated wonderfully and helped with a special check in accommodation that made the arrival so much less stressful. Would love to come back at a warmer time if year!

AnnMarie (and Michael) are wonderful, welcoming hosts. They've lived in Greenpoint for a while and are happy to share with you the best spots for the well-heeled and thrifty alike.  The room's as advertised-- well-appointed, clean, and comfortable. The rest of the apartment is equally ideal. My stay was particularly quiet and restful, which was perfect considering the nature of my work. I'd stay here again in a heartbeat, although I suspect I'll need to book far in advance considering the quality of the residence and the hosts' generosity.  RECOMMENDED!

Excellent place! Rob and his friend Adam were always online and answered all questions that we had. Adam did a great job of making us feel at home and the entire process was very easy. The room itself was spacious, clean and the bed was very comfortable. Adam provided comprehensive information about apartment, towels, iron and all appliances. Also, a great location for the price. Having the subway station (5-10 mins walk) so close made meeting friends downtown easy.

It's a nice experience to stay in Rob's apartment. Although I didn't meet Rob in person but he is always aviable in email. And his housemates, Adam and Joel are very nice and friendly guys. The location is great, walking distsnce to little Italy and SOHO and many nice restsurant around. My husband had a good time in 2 days stay.

Rob is amazing, friendly and careful host. I really like his apartment with unique style. Everywhere was clean, towels were provided and bed was SOOO soft that I didnt want to get up in the morning. The location was perfect as it is less than 5 minutes away from the subway. I highly recommend staying at Rob's place.

This place is really AMAZING! Cozy and soooo New York! The brownstone is adorable, and the room is really huge and clean. It is sunny because of the 2 big windows but also very quiet. The house is well furnished of anything you may need during your stay; there is also a TV with a big screen that comes really in handy when you just want to relax and watch a movie after a long day in Manhattan. The location is simply perfect: in the heart of the best neighborhood in the city, tons of restaurants,pubs and bars just a corner away. Rob and his housemates are literally the nicest people in the world, always kind, funny and just a text away in case of any question. We really loved our stay at their house, we would definitely suggest it.

I stayed in Rob's place for three weeks and it was a wonderful experience! It is an extremely large apartment for Manhattan with large bedrooms. Air conditioning in the room and the coziest bed I've ever slept in. Great amenities including clean bathroom and kitchen and room to eat dinner at a large table. Big couch too. The friendliest roommates ever and all of them extremely willing to give recommendations for food in the area-- on that note the Lower East Side is the coolest neighborhood in Manhattan. My boyfriend and I couldn't get one block out the door before seeing dozens of restaurants and coffee shops that we wanted to stop at. In the three weeks we were there we were not able to cover all of the places we wanted to in the area! Very easy to get to the subway station too. Overall a very great experience and I would highly recommend staying at Rob's place!

Our stay with Rob and his rommates was perfectly fine - the flat was compared to other NY offers very spacious and has a great rooftop located in lower east side.  Rob was easy-going and super helpful regarding all our enquiries and questions, the boys living in the flat are very nice and welcoming - super fast communication.  Even though there are other people living in the flat, we often enjoyed the luxery to have to whole apartment to ourselves.  We had a great time in New York and can only recommend it!

The accommodation corresponds to the description, the room is large and very quiet. The area is very well located, the metro is nearby and it is very easy to access all the sights. Excellent value for money, even though we couldn't meet Rob, we had the whole apartment available, thank you very much.
I stayed with my friend at Rob's room.. the stay was amazing, location is great for going out, awesome roommates, huge room and amazing rooftop! We had a great time

Rob responded quickly to all of my messages and was super accommodating about check in/check out times, which was very appreciated. Walking distance to the East Village, Chinatown, and multiple subway stops. The neighbourhood was a bit loud on weekend nights but that's to be expected given the location and wasn't an issue at all. Friendly housemates who gave excellent recommendations for restaurants and places to visit :)

Im afraid I would not stay here again.  The pictures do not accurately depict the property.  It is quite worn down and is set up with the bare minimum, which was not enough to house a family of 6 cooking at home for a week.  Simply far too expensive for the quality you are getting.

We had a great time. Like the other reviews, it's tiny. But you are in Manhattan, and when we compared hotel rates, this was a steal when you factor location and full kitchen and one bedroom.   It's definitely cute and homey. It has a total NYC feel complete with views of water towers and parts of the sky line.   It's a block from Citarella for grocery shopping and the NJ Path system and NYC west 4 train station.   The location is right smack in the middle of culture and amazing restaurants.   We were a short walk from Union Square and the farmers market.   We stayed with our 4 year old son and the three of us fit perfectly.   If you want to feel like a real New Yorker this place can definitely set that stage for home base.
My stay was great… quiet, clean, peaceful, and stress-free. I already signed up for another visit.

Very comfy and clean. Great location close to the airport.  Tannise was responsive and timely.  Only thing, I had to get used to hearing noises from the occupants upstairs. I haven't lived in an apartment in years so not used to hearing others walking and or moving around in home other than me.  it was a bit scary the 1st night alone until I got used to it, LOL. But other than that, I'd recommend this place to anyone looking for a home away from home feeling.

Nora would be my definition of a super host. She is helpful, even arranging for me to pick up the key elsewhere, quick to respond, hospitable, and personable. When I woke up in the morning, she made coffee for me (INCREDIBLE!) and made us breakfast. Her house is comfortable, welcoming, and spacious. She has the most adorable dog, Simba, who can steal your heart in a minute. Honestly, I felt she had a way to create a sense of community among other travelers who were visiting - offering to have dinner and breakfast with you, etc. I can go on and on.

Nora is not only a wonderful host but she is also a wonderful human being! From the very beginning until the end of my stay she was very hospitable and helpful every step of the way! Her home is very comfortable and is seconds away from a train station that could take you anywhere in Brooklyn and Manhattan! She's also lovely conversationalist, whom I could've spent hours talking with and her little adorable dog Simba will just steal your heart! I'm glad to say I was able to make a wonderful new friend out of this experience. :)

Susie was very welcoming and was always responsive through phone. She described everything in the apartment accurately and everything was as represented. You get what you pay for! The apartment is nothing fancy but a steal if you're looking to spend the night in NYC. If you're in NYC, you're outside all day anyway! Why spend a ridiculous amount for a bed? The apartment is on the south side of Manhattan and convenient located close to the subway.

Alexandra was a perfect host! Very friendly and dedicated to making sure our stay was the best it could be! She left us out umbrellas when it called for rain and gave us great suggestions for food and entertainment. She also went way above and beyond by booking a taxi for us that allowed for all our stuff! We travelled with our five month old for the first time and having such a spacious and clean space to call home really made the trip as stress free as possible. I’d highly recommend this space!

Marie was very helpful with everything and very responsive to texts. The first day We locked ourselves out of the room and she wasnt home but she helped us with suggestions and ideas via text throughout the time we were locked out. That was very kind of her. 1. The room is small and has no air conditioning. Added to this is the fact that it is on the top floor(5th) so it gets even hotter. We visited in July and it was hard without an AC. If you are planning a visit in fall or winter, it is a good place to stay. 2. The bathroom and kitchen are quite clean.  3. The place is very close to the subway for trains 2&3 . Penn station, times square etc are only 5-6 stops away.  4. I was a little sceptical of Harlem, but i found it quite safe. We used to come back late at nights and never felt unsafe. It is a reasonably priced listing. If you dont want to shell out a lot on a place in Manhattan then it is a good deal given that wherever you stay in NYC you need to take the subway to various places.

I stayed for two weeks while working at Columbia. The area is relatively quiet - for NYC standards - and nicely located just around the corner from the 2,3 express subway, so getting to the UWS and downtown really only takes 10-20 minutes. Columbia is within walking distance. The Harlem neighborhood is vibrant and I never felt unsafe walking the streets alone. The apartment is charming. The permanent housemates, who are very nice, had just moved in when I arrived and were doing everything to make the place a home. The room was as pictured and had everything I needed (bed, closet, desk) while the living room was a welcoming space to hang out. The kitchen had everything I was looking for, too. Overall I had a great experience.

Room was nice, but kitchen was dirty. Would also advise bringing your own bed sheet, the one provided was too small for the mattress and easily slides off and the mattress itself is dirty. Most nights there was a group of homeless people outside the front door of the building.

A lovely welcome and very friendly however the map takes you somewhere else. We booked at the last minute got to the address on the booking which wasn’t the address. Was pretty stressful as we couldn’t get hold of anyone and I’ve also spent a fortune calling and leaving messages. That said the home was nice it is very much a shared space just maybe don’t have auto bookings on if you arent in town.   Right next to the subway and great to get to Coney Island too!

The apartment is clean, the living area is very comfy and the host is great. Even though the neighborhood is not the best, but at least you’re right next to the train station ( something you really need when you’re in NYC for a few days only ) For the price, it was a good deal and you het what you paid for. One thing I didn’t like is the cameras thing. I understand that it’s there for safety reasons, but it made me feel that I’m being watched 24/7 and I technically don’t have any level of privacy, except inside the bedroom and the bathroom, I just felt like I’m under the microscope, it felt creepy and uncomfortable to some extent. Other than that, it was great experience!

The room with a separate bathroom is well located about 10 minutes from Timesquare surrounded by various restaurants.   The room is furnished, there are two very hard beds, a table, a TV and two chairs. However, there is no heating, only an electronic auxiliary heater that you don't want to leave on during the day for fear that the whole accommodation will burn down. This means that it is very cold when you come home in the evening.   There is also an air conditioning unit where the connection is simply placed through the window. But that's not a German standard.   Otherwise the accommodation is ok. Unfortunately, the area with the surrounding restaurants and bars is very loud, which means that you don't get much sleep at night. Unfortunately, the landlords react to this with a strong lack of understanding and also somewhat rudely.   If I were to go to New York again, I would definitely choose another place to stay. Too bad!

Susie's place is a great place to stay at for a great price! It is near China Town and Little Italy and near the F metro station. I was scared about using the metro, but Susie explained it a bit better for me and gave me tips on how to use it and I was able to get around fine, Susie also allowed us to check in a bit earlier since we arrived early and was very friendly. I enjoyed my time in New York and in Susie's place.

Isaac and Noelia were incredible hosts, very communicative, helpful and kept the space clean and well-maintained. This is a great value as the room was much larger than expected, with a kitchen and bathroom just right outside the room! Close to transit and beautiful Sunset Park, this is a value and a steal for anyone wanting an authentic New York City experience. Thanks again!

Esteban and his family are very friendly, they took care of us very well as in a hotel, the house is very clean, the breakfast was delicious and the conversation too, the Subway is very close to the house, you can do it perfectly by walking, although it seems like an unsafe area, it is not... thank you for your attention...

Rigoberto’s apartment was everything we needed during our 5 night stay. It was very clean and stocked with everything you could possibly need. A group of 4 of us stayed comfortably. The bathroom is small but it does the job.  The beds and couch were comfortable. The full kitchen is an added bonus. Rigoberto was very responsive and helpful and even brought us extra blankets one evening quickly after we messaged him.  The location of the apartment isn’t the nicest neighborhood I’ve ever visited but we never felt unsafe and everyone we met was very friendly. The apartment is a short walk to the subway station which is convenient for traveling outside of the area. It is about a 25-30 minute train ride to Manhattan. Overall, would definitely stay again.
The host was very welcoming, and the place was fantastic and in a very convenient location. This airbnb is a steal!

Great value for money! I was little suspicious of the shared space in the beginning but it turned out to be great. Literally 1 minute from the Subway. I didn't get to interact much with Gil but he was very helpful. Instructions were clear and easy. Perfect for solo travellers.

I have no words to describe how much I enjoyed my stay with Susie's family. They are the sweetest, nicest people ever and made NYC feel like home!  Susie is very professional and easy going- definitely makes guests stay easy and stress-free :) Thank you so much!

Not a bad person, but dishonest on the listing. Photos are nowhere near the quality of the actual apartment. The water was shut off during my stay so I couldn't shower one night. Noise was also a issue at night. Place had a unpleasant odor.

I stayed for 2 nights. The location is geographically convenient, being adjacent to the Q train and very close to both Coney Island and many lively spots in Brooklyn.   While the area seemed safe, there was a lot of litter on the streets, and lunatic homeless people out and about after around 10pm.  The apartment itself is kept neat, tidy, and well-prepared for all guests, with fresh linens, a towel, blanket, and a fully stocked kitchen at your disposal. The bathroom has shampoo, conditioner, toothpaste, toilet paper, etc etc, but no toothbrushes. However, for anything basic you might need last minute, there is a convenience store immediately outside the residence, as well as delis and grocery stores within a 5 minute walk.   The host is extremely responsive and cordial, and very knowledgeable about the area. She even invited me to hang out with her.   For the price, I’d say it’s a pretty good option should you be coming to explore Brooklyn.

This apartment has a shared bathroom! Be aware! You are basically renting a bedroom in an apartment that other people live in. This is not stated in the description on the website (unless he has since changed it). The pictures do not match what it really looks like inside although the bedroom (that we only stayed in 5 minutes before booking a nearby hotel) seemed very clean. The building looks abandoned from the outside though and the neighborhood is pretty shady. Carlos was very nice and quick to respond although he did not give us a refund when we told him about having an issue about the bathroom situation.

Stephen was a great host! He checked in with us regularly and made sure we had everything we needed. His place is a close walk to the subway. We also never felt unsafe wandering around the neighborhood. The apartment is on the fourth floor, so if you have difficulties with stairs it's something to keep in mind. Overall our stay was fantastic! Thanks Stephen!

MUST READ!! BEST AIRBNB I'VE EVER STAYED AT!!  Ok, so this was my first Airbnb, but I've traveled a lot both in the US and abroad, and I truly do think it's deserving of "the best." Why? At the risk of never being able to find this apartment available again, here goes..  1. JENNIFER: She is awesome. The best. Very nice, very responsive (text, phone, app), very flexible, very up front and honest, and I definitely got the sense that she wanted me to have a great experience and a great time in the city as well. Just reading her very comprehensive description of the apartment and neighborhood initially gave me that sense. And it's true - she definitely cares.   2. THE APARTMENT: Great size (bigger than many NYC hotels I've stayed at), great renovation, very well equipped and supplied (everything from high end appliances and ample dishes to toiletries to cold water in the Brita in the fridge) and very clean. When Jennifer says you can walk around without shoes and feel comfortable, she isn't kidding. Her comprehensive description is very accurate.   3. PRICE: For 1 person, this is a great, great deal. For 2 people, it's an even better deal. For 3 or 4 people, this is practically stealing!!  I am so blown away by the pricing relative to the amazing apartment that you will get, I must continue. Price could actually have been listed first in my review (as great as Jennifer is). Per Lonely Planet (http://www.lonelyplanet.com/usa/new-york-city/money-costs), you will likely spend more on dinner for 2 people at a mid-range eatery than you will on this apartment! And Jennifer is currently offering weekly and monthly discounts, driving your cost down even further.   If you are visiting from abroad you may be currently experiencing a stronger US dollar relative to your currency, so cost may be more important than ever.   4. LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION: This I feel I am very qualified to review as I used to live in NYC years ago, both in Manhattan and Sunnyside. Manhattan is great, but Sunnyside is a great place to live, or stay for your visit. It has more of a neighborhood feel, is quiet, is easily accessible by public transportation and cars, and I've always felt safe. You are able to reach midtown Manhattan in the same short amount of time that it could take you from downtown or the upper east or west sides of Manhattan.   In other words, if you've never stayed in Sunnyside, don't be intimidated that it's in Queens. It's likely just as close to where you are going to go, if not closer, than many other locations in Manhattan (especially Airbnb's in this incredible price range).  5. JUST DO IT! If you are lucky enough to find Jennifer's apartment available, look no further. Do not hesitate!! Because then I might get it first..

My boyfriend and I had a wonderful stay. It was very close to the subway and the space was a lot bigger than I expected. There is a big window in the bedroom that allows for lots of natural light and doesn't feel like a basement at all. It had a very comfortable bed and a desk that was perfect to use as a vanity! There were lots of hangers in the closet and even a full length mirror, which of course I was a fan of! The neighborhood was very safe and easy to navigate, even at night. There is a drug store right next to the subway stop that is 24 hrs and we found ourselves there a few times to pick up essentials or even use the ATM machine late at night. It only takes 25 mins to get to Times Square from the time you leave the door which is not far at all for anyone used to commuting in major cities. Jennifer is also an amazing host and was very easy to communicate with throughout our trip. I would definitely recommend this place, it's a great spot with everything you would need and it's just outside the city.

Petya and Diva are both caring, hospitable, warm and friendly hosts. I have to give special mention to Petya as she went out of her way to help me during my stay and made it the least stressful possible. Petya genuinely cares about her guests and is very understanding and kind. Definitely recommend for future guests. You are in great hands, and Petya will certainly look after you!

The area is very quiet, I recommend taking a walk around the area to get to know it and discover that it is a good neighborhood. The hosts were very friendly, we couldn't spend much time with them because we were out practically all day getting to know Manhattan and sightseeing and when we returned it was late. But every time we met one of them they were very kind and attentive people, we really liked knowing that they were nearby in case we needed anything. The area is quiet, I guarantee it, we returned late on the subway almost every day and at no time did we feel in danger or anything similar, on the contrary, everything was very safe. To get to Manhattan it took us about 40 minutes on the subway every day, but that time is worth paying the huge prices on the island. The apartment is very clean and comfortable. The metro stop at the foot of the house, very close.

This place is an excellent value, charming and roomy. The check-in system is a breeze, and the owners make it so you can really go about your business on your own. The private kitchen and bathroom are a steal at this price, were clean and well stocked. Transit is close by. Will definitely book again.

We stayed 10 days at Mia’s and it was a perfect place for us as a family with 1 child. It’s close to different subway stations and lines which connect you quickly to Manhattan and beyond.  The appartment is as shown in the photos and is extremely well equipped. It was very clean and we had everything we needed for our stay. As a neighbourhood, we never felt unsafe, even when walking late at night. The local people were friendly  Mia was not in town during our stay but was responsive to questions, even providing a new fan as we arrived during a heatwave! We would definitely return - thank you Mia!

That is a quiet neighbourhood, make us feel safe.  Even if you come back at very late night, we tried one day came back at 2 am, you won't feel unsafe. The house is very clean and spacious that the rooms are more than enough to accommodate four of us.  And there are 2 set of TVs, very good. The host is so helpful. They provided all information as requested quickly during the reservation and when we arrived.  Since our arrival and departure time are different from their check in/out time, they are more than happy to work together to fit our needs.  That is a thumb up.  And there is all utensil  we need available for our use.  The only comment is about the NY subway, I know that is NOT the host fault. Overall I will recommend this location to my friends and I will look forward staying at the location again when I visit NYC again in the future.

This is a budget-friendly place for commuters/small families. Although the location might seem a scary at night, it's reasonably safe, and everyone in the area is very kind.   Donald and Verena are excellent hosts. They were quick to respond to everything we needed. They went above and beyond to make our stay comfortable and helped when we had any issues.   The living space is small, but that is to be expected for an apartment in the NYC area. The bedrooms are a good size and the WIFI and Cable work well.   We enjoyed our stay! Thank you!

We stayed for 5 days. The apartment was very comfortable, the bedrooms where spacious and had comfortable beds. We heard absolutely no street noise despite being feet from the J train. The apartment had towels, clean sheets and and an equiped kitchen. The J train took you straight into Manhattan in 45 min. or connection to other trains throughout the route​. The neighborhood was quiet and we never felt unsafe. We would definitely stay here again. Highly recommended

Sergio was not there when I arrived, but he left someone in charge that was welcoming and made sure everything was OK. After arriving, he and his wife made sure that my stay was as pleasant as possible, which was really nice. The space itself is nice with lots of closet space and a desk to place your belongings. The neighborhood is not for everyone; though not unsafe, it is definitely rough. That said, the location is conveniently two blocks from a subway, so it is easy to come and go.  Overall I would recommend the stay at Sergio's especially for shorter one to three months stay and if you don't mind the location.

Unfortunately I did not have the best stay here. I booked Carlos' apartment for a Monday - Friday trip. When I arrived on Monday, I was greeted by a nice lady who let me in the apartment. Shortly after I received a message from the host, Carlos, that said I had a balance due for my pets. I replied "OK" at first. I have two pomeranians and had booked the listing because it had said pets allowed. Carlos threatened to end our reservation and lock us out of the apartment if we didn't pay. Asked airbnb for help and they advised not to pay. After multiple threats via text form host, we left the apt Tuesday. Airbnb paid the fee on our behalf and the host let us back in but did not offer any apology. We did not have access to the apartment until 7pm. In addition, he said my bf had been rude and demanded a photocopy of his ID so he can send it to the NYPD if any more issues arise.  When I refused and said it's just my mom who might stay, he made it a point to say he had me in record saying there will be no other guests.  Wednessday I could not enter the apartment after leaving for a few hours. They key worked but the door was still locked. Carlos asked me to meet his colleague on the corner instead of in front of the apt. Shortly after we see the lady walk out of the building and then help us use the key which magically worked when she was there. We think she was in the apartment the whole time or had entered while we were out and locked the lock we didn't have access to on accident. Then tried to cover it up like we accidentally locked ourselves out. Why else would he want us to meet on the corner?  I did not feel safe with my dogs in the apartment after this and did not go to a concert we had tickets to on Wednesday night because I didn't want to leave my dogs alone. I wish I could go into more depth about how rude and unpleasant Carlos was but these reviews are limited to 500 words. It's sad because he probably thinks he is the best host. This reservation has made me question using a site like airbnb when you could pay more for a hotel and not have your trip ruined like ours was. Stay away!!!!!

We stayed at Carlos' place on East 54th St for about 3 weeks while our apartment was being renovated. The location was great! Plenty of restaurants around the area, lots of fitness centers like Equinox, Blink, and Soulcycle across the street, and walking distance to the Subway. The place is a bit darker than the photos would lead you to believe (the apartment is in the back of the building so not a lot of natural light) but it was quiet and clean.   We had a few issues with this place. Firstly, when checking in, the room was not cleaned yet. This was due to a mix up in check-in time. Secondly, during our stay there was construction on the roof and they were throwing debris over the edge of the building, landing in the terrace. This made the terrace unsafe to use for all of our stay, which was a bummer. Carlos handled both of these issues promptly and professionally and we were able to resolve them both.   Note that it's listed as a 1-bedroom apartment but it's really a studio with a room divider.

A good value. A modern apartment, big, clean kitchen, and AC plus a good desk in the room. Unfortunately the room I stayed in got almost no sunlight, but other than that everything about the apartment was very good. The location is maybe a little trickier--there are certainly positives, it's nearby a couple subway stops, Metro North, Central Park (half-mile away). The less positive is that the immediate area around the apartment----2 or three blocks--isn't great. There aren't really any cafes or restaurants, mainly delis, a liquor store, and a good number of homeless people, unfortunately. Once you walk a few blocks though, there are some really cool places worth checking out.

Space and common areas, kitchen, bathroom, etc  was very clean, hosts were very attentive. Other residents were cool. Right next to 125th st on the 4/5/6 line and metro north. Neighborhood is sketch. I didn’t have a problem with anyone, but lots of drugs/dealers. I would stay there again though.

The location was superb--tons of places to eat and parks within walking distance. Also, the subway was close and convenient for going into Manhattan or visiting Coney Island (we did both).  Julia's apartment was cozy and fit our needs nicely. She is a laid-back hostess who made the entire experience simple and stress-free. We have two young children, and staying here worked well. I could see it being even better for kids who are a little bit older (over 5 years), but we had no problems whatsoever.

Overall my stay at the brownstone corzy corner was positive. Majar was very flexible with check out and is friendly. Evelyn is also very friendly and welcoming. The room looks just as described in the pictures and i found the bed to be very comfortable. The bathroom is shared and  wasnt supplied with toilet paper. Thankfully We were provided with towels.   My only concern was the area. Its a bit sketchy and could be a bit uncomfortable walking at night especially if you are a tourist who wants to travel to the city at night. The good thing is that the train is a 5 min walk.

-WORST EVER AIRBNB EXPERIENCE-  I booked this apartment for four months (there was a 120-night minimum REQUIRED stay!) and, unfortunately, I couldn't afford any alternative solution than to stay for the whole duration, from September 1st till December 30th, 2020. This is my experience:  1.	Location: the apartment is located two blocks south of MSG stadium and PENN Station. Very practical, good commute, almost in the middle of the city, you have quick access to many places. Unfortunately, due to the current difficult situation as well, the whole area is full of homeless and mentally unstable people. Moreover, poor lighting in the area makes things even more difficult at night. A short time after I moved in, I found FECES on a rug INSIDE the main hall. I called the host, who is also the building manager, and he took care of it in short time.  2.	Apartment: the building is very old and so is the apartment.           a.	I found old and rusty appliances and furniture, a broken wardrobe and a bandy mattress (probably overused). Very dirty, too. All the narrow spaces (sink-stove, behind the fridge, behind the heater, below the bed) filled with spider webs, dust and small pieces of trash.            b.	The toilet is extremely narrow and sensitive. I had to buy a plunger because it would clog after a simple use, with absolutely NO paper throwing whatsoever.           c.	The window curtains are smaller than the actual window, so there’s no shade from morning light.            d.	The window DOESN’T have a mesh screen. That, along with the fact that the apartment faces a lame backyard FULL of rats (and not the two-block-away-HighLine, in case somebody thinks that because of the pictures on the listing), meant that I had to be right next to the window every time I opened it in order to avoid very unpleasant intrusions.            e.	Why did I have to open the window? Because there was NO ABSORBER in the kitchen. I had to finish cooking and then try to clear out the smokey room, so I could be checking the window. I even had to take the batteries out of the “remote” (a.k.a. uninstalled) smoke detector that the host handed me, because the alarm would sound.            f.	Washer/dryer: the best and the only true correspondence between the listing and the actual apartment. Does exactly and efficiently the job it’s made for.   3.	Noise: the walls in this building are the THINNEST you can possibly imagine. I could hear all the other tenants, even when they were just talking, as if they were in my apartment. But what was absolutely unbearable, was the 24hour screeching sound of the old, wooden floor from the apartment just above me, where the tenant was just living his life and nothing more than that.   4.	 Heating: the absolute disaster. I complained many times to the host about its inefficiency, and he told me it was generally regulated to work at 70F during day and night drops to 65F. I didn’t use a thermometer to verify. All I know is that there would be times during day that I was stifling (especially when I had the stove on for cooking) and had to open the window (and do the whole process that came with that!) to put cold air in and there would be times during night that the heating just wouldn’t go on, leaving me freezing. The heater is very old and every time it took on early morning it would wake me up with its loud release valve sound.   The host offered me as a solution a second comforter implying in a pejorative tone that I’m not used to cold climates because of where I come from (Greece). FYI, my hometown, Thessaloniki, has the same latitude as NYC, so I have quite some experience with real cold. As a result, instead of suffocating under the weight of two comforters every night, I ended up buying a small heater which helped a lot, even though there were some incredibly cold nights where nothing could be done. Adding to all that, the significant heat loss from the “in-out” air-condition unit with scotch tape and aluminum foil around as insulation.   Final Conclusions:     The listing and the actual apartment have absolutely NO CORRESPONDENCE to each other. Renters, save your time, your money and your HEALTH by not booking this apartment.  Owner(s), gut renovate the place or put it out of the market because right now it’s absolutely NOT LIVABLE, especially for long-time stay.   IMPORTANT NOTE: my review is SOLELY regarding the apartment and the building. The tenants have been absolutely great. The host was reachable and typically accommodating (offered the comforter solution, cleared the feces, gave me the mailbox key when I asked for it), not willing to go the extra mile, though, and be of actual help.  He went rather moody every time I expressed a complaint and almost “talked me out” of even writing a review in a conversation we had, when he realized it wouldn’t be a completely good one. He even had the nerve to call "fabricated" the pictures I sent to Airbnb when I requested a refund, as if I had nothing more "pleasurable" to do than taking and fabricating photos of dead rats on the street right in front of the building's main hall.

I came here with my fiancé when our college semesters were beginning. We’ll Just give an honest overview of our stay here, I’m sure many others can have a good stay here as long as they quench Michael’s greed.   Well here goes  Every experience we had with the host (Michael Joseph Gregg) after a time was so horrible that it outweighs all of the pros of living here. We felt unsafe and were harassed for way too long. We even filed a police report after he took a picture of my fiancé (my second guest) undressed in the doorway. He blocked me in the hallway while I was trying to pick up my groceries, trying to hint that he suspected me of stealing them; and used it as an opportunity to harass me about the rent. We were late on the second payment and that’s what started his mental flip. At first Michael seemed like a decent host and nice guy. He became a very mean spirited person after we were a week late with the second payment, unreasonably so. To the point where money meant nothing to him and he just wanted to bully us out. So of course even when we had the money to pay for the second payment 2 weeks after. We decided to spend it on a different apartment. This is honestly the worst place I’ve ever stayed in which is saying a lot seeing that I’ve had to live in a shelter. No place have I ever been a week or two late on rent and been this incredibly harassed.

This apartment was a mess and felt unsafe. One side of the apartment was apparently used as storage, and there were piles of junk on the floors, barely hidden behind a screen. The room door had a lock on it but the bathroom was in the hallway, along with more junk. The bed was positioned squarely in the middle of the room (this is not visible in the photo). The only reason I could fathom putting it there was to keep bugs from crawling up the walls and onto the bed at night.  The host was not specific about whether anyone lived in the rest of the apartment or whether anyone would be "in and out" during the night. This made me feel unsafe, to know that he may or may not be in the "junk room" at night, even thought he didn't live there.  He mentioned that the tub was not draining well, and showed me a rickety metal stool that he had placed in the middle of the tub. He suggested that I stand on it when I took a shower. This also struck me as unsafe, and even indicative of my host's poor judgment. I left the premises disgusted and forfeited my reservation and room payment. That was the last time I will book with Airbnb.

Gil was nice enough to add  an air mattress to the room after we requested it when we got into the apartment. The room includes a fridge and microwave and other guides to New York. The washroom is right outside of the room as well which is nice. Gil was very nice and gave us recommendations on where to go and what to do around the area. The room was nice and neat but the hallway outside wasn't in very good shape with newspapers and garbage on the ground, however it did not affect our stay. We had a feeling maybe Gil rented out his only bedroom and weren't really sure where he slept during our stay. He seemed to be on the sofa chair by the front door in the mornings when we woke up each morning leading us to believe maybe he slept on the chair at night. However he was very gracious, always asked if we needed anything and recommended the best way to go to certain places and cared about our well being. The apartment isn't in the greatest neighbourhood, lower middle class, but at no times did we feel totally unsafe. The subway is about a 10 minute walk which isn't too bad. But we happened to go during a very cold time so it wouldve been better if it was closer, during the summer however it wouldn't be too bad.   All in all for the price it was a good stay. Room is nice, bathroom isn't too bad, could be a better neighbourhood but a great host who caters and helps when needed.

Gil’s place is located on the other end of LES, right next to the Williamsburg bridge. The area is not as bad as I thought, even though it’s notorious for being unsafe, but as a single woman I was advised not to hang around there too late in the evenings. Part of the apartment was under renovation, when I stayed there so the kitchen wasn’t completely accessible. But Gil was kind enough to setup a coffee maker and I also had a refrigerator in my room as well. The room itself wasn’t quite up to standards with a very stained carpet and a musty odor, but apart from that it was quite comfortable with clean linens and a cozy bed. Gil also was very enthusiastic to share tips about the city and had a great collection of guide books to browse.

Michael is a truly amazing host! I rented Michael's apartment for two (as it turned out very capricious) friends of mine, and Michael's service was above and beyond excellent, so the ladies were happy all their stay long. I have never thought it could be this quiet anywhere in Manhattan, not speaking about busy midtown area. It's deadly quiet. The apartment is pretty compact, but there are plenty sleeping surfaces. I bet you can easily place 4 people in here. There is a little kitchenette (fridge, oven, Microwave, coffee-machine), so you can make and store your own food if you want to. TV, cable, AC . Michael provides a bunch of towels, pillows, linens - whatever you need for a comfort stay. And, of course, location-location-location! Steps to everything. You won't even need a metrocard - just walk.  Steal-deal overall!!! Thank you very much, Michael for the wonderful time my friends had in your apartment. Sorry for bothering you too much. You were exceptionally nice to us. :)

We had a lovely three-night stay at Michelle's apartment during our visit to NY. We arrived on Friday night so Michelle had helpfully arranged for us to pickup our apartment keys from the front desk which was very convenient.  Our schedule in NY was pretty packed so we only met Michelle the one time just before leaving for the airport, but she always easy to contact via Airbnb and proved to be a very welcoming and helpful host - providing us towels in the room and even a hairdryer for when my wife needed one. Michelle works from home but, as we were out of the apartment exploring NYC most of the time, this did not affect our trip in any way. The apartment is situated in a Harlem neighborhood on West 117th Street and the apartment was as described and pictured.  There was a 24-hour Rite Aid pharmacy next door which was useful and plenty of places nearby to eat/drink (we do suggest trying the chocolate chip cookies at Levain Bakery!). The area was also well serviced with buses and a metro just a few minutes walk away that we used extensively during our stay. At no time did we feel ourselves to be unsafe at any time of the day. All in all we had a good stay in NYC and would definitely recommend Michelle's apartment as a good base to explore NYC!

I stayed here for a month and commuted to Lincoln Hospital. I would NOT stay here again, nor would I recommend it to anyone. Ad is very inaccurate.  Martine and her son are very nice & mostly quiet. I had space in fridge, but very little space in freezer or cabinets.   I had several very tense encounters with drug dealers and was nearly mugged while walking to subway. I was followed for several blocks. By email she told me many times that it was a safe neighborhood and that she never had problems. Once I arrived, she told me there had been many problems and that she did not walk at night.   They are inside SMOKERS and the house smells awful! Old butts were placed in the kitchen trash. It was almost impossible to use the kitchen/main areas.   The bed is a FUTON, not a "real bed" as stated in the ad, and just larger than a twin (smaller than full). During booking, I was told that it was a large bed that could accommodate two people. None of bedding fit properly. Very cheap polyester pillows.   The small desk is impossible to use due to the room arrangement.    The bedroom reeks of moth balls.  The AC is right above your head so it blows on your face all night (diverter did not work well). The main house does NOT have AC and typically hovered above 80-90! Windows were NOT fully opened so NO air flow.   There were FLEAS in house! I told her about it and she did nothing while I was there. I was covered in flea bites. DISGUSTING!   They have a CAT, not in ad, that goes in whole house. On arrival, she said it stayed downstairs - NOT TRUE!  The house is dirty - food on the counter, spilled stuff in the fridge and freezer, moldy washing machine, mildew all over the bathroom, dirty handprints on walls/doors, splattered food on cabinets/walls/floor/ceiling. Everything felt grimy. "Clean" kitchen items frequently had food/oil/bugs on it. I had to always wear shoes in the house because the floors were dirty. They fry a lot of food and never clean the stove (several mm of grime). I HATED being in the kitchen.  The house is full of flies and other insects, and EGGS, especially the kitchen and my room. The heat, moisture, poor air flow, and lackluster cleaning was a haven for bugs. It was impossible to prepare food without several flies descending onto your food.  They frequently left uncovered food on the counter and in fridge. The fridge smelled badly due to rotten food (not just strong smelling food).  The kitchen is poorly equipped, it lacks a: microwave, coffee pot, large cups, food storage, non-porous cutting boards, strainer. Every knife is dull. They keep leftovers in the pots, so the two regular size pots were often unavailable to use.  Most days I would find all six of the ice cube trays EMPTY in the freezer.

Martine’s apartment is beautifully filled with art and the room/ en suite is perfect for a couple or by yourself. Although we didn’t use it the kitchen and lounge area is spacious and easy to navigate. The area the apartment is in may appear a bit suspicious but as 2 young female adults we felt safe the whole time and had no problems late at night. As it’s an industrial it is pretty quiet! It’s takes around 35 mins to get to midtown from the apartment which isn’t too bad the subway is very close and it’s also close to another line (around 15/20 min walk) I’d highly recommend the apartment if you want to explore NYC.

Really there are no words to describe how awesome of a host Ravanna and his brother were. Before I even started staying in the apt, they were more than happy and willing to assist me in what I needed. I was throwing a surprise birthday gathering for my boyfriend, so I had a birthday banner mailed to them so that they would put it up and enhance the surprise. The place was in a great location close to everything and I never really felt unsafe. The place was super clean and there was literally nothing more that we could have ever wanted for, everything was readily available. He was even able to accommodate for us to stay an extra night at a rate too good to pass. Although this was my first airbnb experience, other airbnbs have big shoes to fill. Simply the best.

Christa and Zach are wonderful hosts. They provided me with a plethora of information about transit options and places to eat. You can really sense their warm hearts, and It almost felt like visiting family. I would hands down stay with them in the future! You really can't beat the fair and honest prices either. If you're looking for a no stress and proper stay then look no further :)

Christa and Zach were awesome. I felt right at home from the get go. And their two dogs were friendly. The neighborhood would be scary to those used to suburban living but really it's an ok neighborhood even if walking home from the train at night. The room was small but not too small, the bed comfy and the air conditioning a welcome addition during the hot and humid days--which during my stay-it was pretty much every day. All in all a very pleasant stay. I hope to stay there again.

I had really good time at Christa& Zach's house. When i think of the place to stay, the price and cleanliness, safe neighborhood are always important for me.  Their house are all completed!  It was so comfortable and nothing to say bad!  on the first day, i actually felt scared about their neighborhood and i asked her. She kindly explained well and made me feel safe:)  i would like to come back to stay for next NY trip. Thank you!

The apartment was very clean and included all we needed. I was afraid it could be a bit cold, but it was just warm and cozy. Perfect to feel at home after spending the day out in the freezing NYC winter.  Whenever we had any doubts, Moses was prompt in replying by email or phone.  In my next visit to NYC, I'll definitely try to stay in Moses' loft again.

For this to be my first Airbnb experience I'm glad I choose this stay. Being from the time of check in the host communication was awesome. He was a call/text away. He assisted with area information and did not hestitate to respond to any questions. The living arrangements were just as described in the description if not better. Although I was in and out with tiring the city the host gave me privacy which was a concern I also had. He was willing to accommodate my scheduling as far as allowing me to drop bags off, check in early, and check out later. Coming from Orlando FL where we have center AC I was afraid I was going to be in discomfort but I wasn't. There was a fan provided and the temperature dropped at night. I would recommend others to this location. Thank you again for all your help (especially because I had a lot of questions)

Great stay.  This should be a model for other airbnb hosts--they're THAT good.  I thought that the way these hosts Christa and Zach handled the coded-entry locks was extremely easy and straightforward and respectful to the guests, and not stressful on anyone.  Also, the folder with the things to do and see in Brooklyn and Manhattan was particularly well-written along with being extremely helpful. In addition, I'm also highly recommending them to anyone who doesn't mind traveling a bit into Brooklyn.  Amazing shops and health food store near their place, on Rogers, just north of Church.  Subway access is so easy, to the 5 and 2 train, except the 2 train doesn't run on weekends --and weekends start on Friday evening...this is a little bit important to know.  Thanks again guys for a wonderful stay.

The apt is very nice. I really just slept and showered, but the bedroom was very nice and comfortable, a/c worked well,  bathroom had all the necessities. Hosts were really nice and friendly. It was very convenient to the subway and lots of stores close by.  I am a native NY'er and used to live fairly close by so I was familiar with the neighborhood and knew that it was safe. This is definitely not SOHO or TRIBECA so If you are not used to a real NYC neighborhood, it might seem kind of sketchy, scary, and overwhelming. It definitely is busy, crowded, a little  grungy, and ethnically diverse. But really totally safe. I am a 53 year old woman and was totally comfortable walking alone there.  But how you feel about the area is really dependent upon your attitude.
Great, comfortable space. Host was very accommodating which made for a stress free stay.

I stayed at the apt during a stressful work time. The whole family was very accommodating, and even with a minor key issue, they answered all of my questions with kindness and patience throughout. The apt is cute, spacious and I love that neighborhood.
Amazing apartment, a true gem. Great people, thanks for having me. Super recommend and price was a steal for the areas. Subway right there

Great value and solid place to land for a visit to NYC. I think Chris and Zach do a good job of prefacing what a visit to the NYC may be like for someone who is unfamiliar with urban environments.  I'll add my perspective as well, as someone who lives in San Francisco but grew up in the midwest. Spaces may be smaller than you are used to. People may be different than you are used to. Infrastructure may work differently than you are used to. But if you come with an open mind to see things for what they are, for the most part, people are people, life is life, and there are new valuable experiences to be had.  As an example of how things can work differently, sometimes unexpected loud things can happen at night in big cities. For example, my first night staying here, a homeless man loudly turned on a radio and started ranting as he laid in someone's yard. Having lived and visited many urban environments with similar sleeping hazards, I had earplugs at the ready to deal with this. If I hadn't, he would have kept me awake all night. It was the only night this happened and he never came back to the neighborhood again. I'm sure it was an unpleasant situation for everyone in the neighborhood and Chris and Zach would have had no way of predicting that this event would happen on my first night. But that is the nature of cities.  I've had similar experiences in village in Cuba where there were roosters crowing in the morning or a condo in Mexico City where there was a bar open on the bottom floor until 3am playing loud music and in San Francisco at my own apartment with every kind of strange situation occasionally occurring outside my window. You just have to prepare.  Like I said, after preparing mentally and logistically for the realities of an urban environment, there are great experiences to be had. This was a fantastic stay for the value in a small but perfectly adequate room in an interesting house very close to a quick subway ride to Manhattan where I had many fascinating experiences.  One note that on the weekend the nearby subway station was closed so I had to take Lyft to the nearest open one to avoid a 40 minute bus ride. I would check Google maps routing and do the same.

After many unpleasant experiences with other hosts, Ravanna was shelter from the storm. Her place was cozy, quiet, clean and accessible. Whether you’re looking to spend your time in BK or to roam the city, her location makes travel accessible and easy. Her quick response time made planning very simple and straight forward. It was a true pleasure.

First, I would like to be clear that this is a very honest review. I am a people-pleaser, an optimist, and I truly get along with anyone. It really is hard for me to say a negative word about anything, so this is coming from a place of genuine concern. I felt so bad bringing up the issues I had with this place to Chris and Zach that I was entirely silent about them because they really were kind hosts. However, I think it is very important for prospective guests to know what they are getting into because there are some components of the advertisement that are very misrepresentative of the actual experience here. LOCATION (MOST IMPORTANT!): To be quite honest: the location was the worst, most misleading component of this Airbnb and is something I am still very frustrated with to date. I have lived in inner cities in Philadelphia, Providence, Baltimore, and Washington, D.C. I am very comfortable with city living and know what precautions to take so that I am safe. I never walk anywhere while I'm on my phone and am always aware of my surroundings. However, I have never felt so threatened by a living situation before. I am a single, 20-year-old woman who was in town for a month for an internship, and I was CONSISTENTLY harassed while living in this neighborhood. The number of times I was cat-called, whistled at, and approached by men while on my way to work was innumerable. This has happened to me before in cities and, yes, it is an unfortunate part of life for most women, BUT the way Chris and Zach advertised the neighborhood made it seem like a family-friendly, college town or suburb, which is not at ALL the experience I had. I was followed home on one occasion that became so intimidating, I had to begin taking the subway to a station about 10 minutes away (Prospect Park) and Ubering every evening back to the Airbnb from work. This accumulated to upwards of $300. Let me be clear, again: I was never putting myself in a dangerous situation and (not that I have to justify what I was wearing) I was ALWAYS in professional dress because I was coming to/from work at a courthouse. Some of these intimidating occasions were as early as 7 AM and it was never later than 6 PM when I was walking home and it did not MATTER that there was a police station nearby. It is also only a three-block walk to the Church AV station closest to their home, something I should have easily been able to complete without fearing that I was in severe danger. Additionally, the neighborhood was LOUD. There were MANY occasions when I was woken up by people rattling through the trash right outside my bedroom window. Also, there was a man who would be up as early as 4:30 AM screaming at the top of his lungs. This didn't happen merely once, but at least five times and would continue for hours in the early morning. It was toward the end of my stay when I realized it wasn't someone roaming through the neighborhood, but a close neighbor. The location was a terribly devastating part of my stay and absolutely ruined my month-long experience in New York City. The description of where they live, in my opinion, is totally inaccurate and it is VITAL that young women, in particular, know that. If I had known what I was getting into, to be honest, there is no way I would have stayed at their place. In fact, I tried contacting Airbnb so I could leave about a week into my stay after I started getting harassed on my way to work, but the customer service was not helpful whatsoever and I was unable to secure a different place. A week into my stay, I actually paid for a hotel for several nights because I was having severe anxiety attacks (for the first time) about returning to the neighborhood, where I felt unsafe. Some examples from the description that should be updated as I found they are not very accurate: - "typically quieter than most urban cities" (false) - "the neighbors are friendly," "people with hearts of gold" - "young children" (of which I saw absolutely none) - "many students, young professionals, elderly, children live around" - "you're sure to get a friendly "good morning!" or "God be with you!" --> (in reality, I got "good morning, sexy," "give me your Snapchat, baby" (and then was followed), among many other lewd comments) CLEANLINESS: Overall, the house was clean, but when there were problems, they were quite jarring. About halfway through my stay, I discovered that there had been mice in my bedroom, leading to another anxiety attack and night at a hotel in Manhattan. I found droppings and a bag of old food that I had left in the room on accident completely chewed through. While I should have been smarter than to leave food in my room, apparently mice weren't a new problem for Chris and Zach. Chris informed me that when they renovated the house several years ago, they had found mice nests and needed to call an exterminator. This time, she set up traps and was able to trap a mouse in the kitchen. Chris was very helpful in resolving the situation -- this was a plus, as she was responsive to any problems that I encountered and she did refund me for the night I discovered the mouse. Additionally, there were several occasions when I saw water bugs in the shower. This can be a part of city living but it was unfortunate, especially for someone who doesn't like the thought of critters. VALUE: I paid over $2,000 to rent this place for a month while I had my internship and it did not live up to my expectations in the slightest. I truly was so frazzled by the location...
The stay was easy and simple to find once you know you're looking for a basement step set. The area is a mixed area in transition but, did not feel unsafe and easy distance to food and transport.

I was lucky enough to find such a great home in such a perfect location. Moses is very friendly and easy to communicate with, making the whole experience a breeze. The loft itself is incredible! The setup is done well and it's quite spacious. There is tons to do within blocks from the loft, which made wandering around a lot of fun. I can't stress enough how much of a wonderful time I had here and would certainly recommend it to anyone who enjoys exploring non-tourist sites.

Moses's place is an ideal Stay if your coming to New York but don't want to stay in the city. It's only a 10 min walk to the subway and a typical ride into the city (depending on where you are going) is anywhere from 10-30mins. The apartment is private so no one will be bothering you. The shower is amaze-balls!!! The perfect remedy after a stressful or just long day. Everything we needed was provided. I never had to look far for basic needs like soap, towels, blow dryer, toilet paper, etc. Overall, my friend and I were very satisfied! 👏🏼

So where to start. Arrival at 9 p.m. in a cellar with windows that we cannot open, dirty sheets with hair and smell. We shower, the towels also smell bad, we ask to change them ok! On the other hand apparently no other sheets so for 1 rbnb blah blah!   So we sleep 3 nights in unclean sheets. At the beginning of November at night it is cold and there is no duvet on the bed or blanket.   We slept with our coats and towels on us. Again we have to complain so we come across as annoying people! But we were cold and in the evening we were kindly given an acrylic sofa blanket.    These people have no sense of cleanliness either! Bathroom not washed, stained and dirty carpet, not to mention the entrance to the cellar.    On the other hand, we are asked to take off our shoes because of the entrance full of rubble and cobwebs!   But if you are afraid the light stays on all night!    We did what we were asked when we left. Gather the smelly sheets and towels, throw the trash outside, clean the glasses and bowls in the bathroom sink....BUT My daughter and I do not recommend this place, not secure at all in the evening to return even at 8 p.m. and in the suburbs of Brooklin.   Finally, when we live above and our guests have requests, we take the trouble of going down 1 floor.    So no human consideration.

Nice and quiet area to stay, perfect clean appartement and great hospitality. A bit far from downtown and about 10-15 walk from the next subway station, but while walking through the upper east side we discovered beautiful restaurants. cafes and places to take a break. If you are not afraid of a little walk, this is a great place to stay and definitely can recommend to do so.

I think the best things are convenient traffic (around 7 minutes walk to subway station), quiet blocks, and well-equipped facilities (comfortable beds, fridge, hair-dryer, microwave etc). Very nice experience in Ruth's apartment. One thing to note is that the air outside the basement smell unpleasant but will not influence the indoor space.

What more can I say except that our stay in Omar's apartment was perfect and completely consistent with the description. The apartment is really large (with 3 real bathrooms!!) and very pleasant to live in (beautiful decoration with old furniture).
