The two upstairs bedrooms are also spacious with two different types of bed (a fairly firm bed in the guest bedroom and a softer bed in the master bedroom). What to choose according to your preferences. We couldn't really enjoy the outdoor garden because of the 20cm of snow we had in NY during our stay. In short, this apartment was perfect for the three of us, especially after these long days of walking. I must also say that we were very satisfied with the calm of the neighborhood. We were a little afraid of the noise coming from the street but in fact there is little traffic, hence very little noise pollution. In terms of geographical location: no problem reaching the two metro stations which are a 5-minute walk away and which will take you either to the west or the east of NY. Central Park is a 10-minute walk away.  What can I say about Omar if not compliments? He was very pleasant and very easy to contact. He made sure everything was okay and we weren't missing anything. We even had a phone call from Pakistan for our very first contact. A very welcoming, warm man who also speaks very good French. (he was not present in NY during our stay but the neighbor upstairs very kindly came to see if everything was okay)  We therefore have very good memories of this rental and we strongly recommend that you book it for your next vacation in NY, you should not be disappointed.

I want to preface this review by saying Ruth was a great host! Any negative experiences listed in this review weren’t necessarily in her control. The room itself was accurately described. It did get stuffy and hot in the room, but there is a fan provided which helped. It’s a pretty small unit which works well if you’re planning on being out most of the time. The location was perfect! Very close to many restaurants and the subway. We were mainly disappointed with the cleanliness of the entrance to the apartment. You enter down some stairs next to the building where there’s a horrible sewage/trash smell, lots of flies, and occasionally rodents. After you pass through the first door, then you have to pass through a small hallway before reaching the actual door to the room. The hallway between the two doors smells horribly of sewage/trash and is swarming with flies. It was impossible not to let some in when coming and going. The smell from the hallway would creep into the room when the fan wasn’t on. Also, the building was being treated for rats/mice when we stayed. On our last full day here there was a sign outside of our door saying “Warning: keep out. Poison baited area.” Again, the room itself was nice for the location, but I think it was a little overpriced for the size, smell, and pests.

I enjoyed my stay in Brooklyn.  Natasha is willing enough to accommodate me even if my arrival on NYC is very late.  The room is spacious and clean.  Do no expect a fully renovated room or house, this is not a hotel.  It is a good place to stay especially the proximity of it with the subway station and eating place in Flatbush Ave.  It is around 40mins away from times square.   The room that I occupied have a double bed which will fit 2 people and  there is another single bed near the door.  On my last day, I visited my cousin in Jersey City and I asked Natasha to extend my stay in few hours instead of checking out at 11AM and she agreed without extra charges.  Here are the difficulties I observed while staying here: The train line is not that frequent and you only have one option on going to Sterling Station (station near the place). It is a bit scary at night walking on the street on the neighborhood but it is just a feeling and I did not encountered any bad experience regarding my safety.

Natasha’s place was a good option to stay in lower cost accomodation. The neighborhood was safe, yet a bit sketchy later at night. The walk to  the nearest subway station (Sterling St) was about 5 minutes and the subway ride to the city central (for example Time Square) took around 30-40 minutes depending on the time of the day/ amount of passengers. The bathroom and the kitchen were kept clean, but the beddings and towels were old-looking and a bit gross. Kitchen had enough supplies to cook and eat. Overall everything worked well and the stay was comfortable!

The upside of this apartment is that there are truly a ton of beds, so it was great that there was enough room to sleep my whole family. The major downside for me was that *very* strong cleaners, detergents, and air fresheners are clearly used to clean this place-- and the smell gave me pretty extreme nausea. I actually opted to stay elsewhere for part of the trip because being in the apartment was so unpleasant. Aside from the scent issue, the apartment itself was reasonably as represented. The furniture was a bit worn, and the doorknob and lock were flimsy, but if it hadn't been for the smell I believe we would have enjoyed our stay.   I never actually met Ravanna-- his sister let us in, and his nephew (very nicely) brought us more blankets around midnight because I thought replacement blankets might smell less strongly of industrial detergent. However, he was incredibly responsible by phone and text. I think this would be a good place to stay for a big group of people planning to go to NYC and not spend a lot of time in the apartment (and who aren't sensitive to scents, obviously).   Very sorry to give these nice people a 2-star review, but the apartment unfortunately didn't really meet our needs.

Had another great stay at Lola's place. This was my 2nd stay in the same room. The room came with an AC unit so I was able to keep cool during the warm June nights. The room was just the perfect size for me and the space was kept very clean.  The location was amazing for me to get to WC-NYP which is only 5 mins away and is very close to the Q subway line which can take you all over (from 96th Street to Coney Island in Brooklyn). There are also a lot of exciting restaurants and bars close by. Lola is a wonderful host and definitely goes out of her way to make your stay as relaxing and stress-free as possible from check-in to check out. Hope to return for a 3rd stay soon.

I just had a wonderful experience staying with Nicole in her modest NYC apartment. She's a smart, lovely woman, and a terrific host. Staying with her was a comfortable, calm, and easy experience - uncomplicated, and stress-free.  Her listing was ideal for me and everything she says in her listing is 100% perfectly described. It's a superior location. It is indeed a Sm Comfy room.  Actually, it didn't seem that small but just right -  for a weeks visit (or more!) it's plenty of space. The room is in the front of the apartment, close to the bathroom, set apart from the back room, and entirely private. There's nice clean, but older bathroom, with a decent shower.  The bedroom (and decor) is discreetly sweet and simply furnished. The single bed is very comfortable, the air-con  works great and came in handy. There is also a ceiling fan on the hight ceiling. Nicole had coffee available for me in the morning, and let me keep some milk  and things in her fridge.  Back to the location: it couldn't be any better: near everything - Columbus Circle, subways, shops, Whole Foods, Lincoln Center, a short walk to the theatre district, grocery stores, great places for breakfast on the corner - I couldn't have been happier. I must admit, the resident canine ambassador Simon Bates, was a highlight of my stay. He's the most charming little dog you can imagine - I couldn't help but fall in love with his serious little face.  This room was perfect choice for me, and I would recommend this room to any woman wanting private, a low-key visit. I would stay with Nicole again "in a heartbeat". Thanks for everything, Nicole!

Nicole is a very nice person and her dog is soooo cute. He's not scary at all and very adorable. Nicole made me feel very welcome and was eager to offer advice and help with anything I needed, from directions from the airport to popular food places.  The room was nice and clean, plenty of hot water.  Nicole also knows how to respect privacy and is a very good roomate.  When I come back to NYC, if she has availability, I'll definitely stay with her again!  Thanks Nicole!

Nicole and Simon the dog, are really good hosts. The location is everything it supposued to be, not expensive, near every subway, close to Central Park, and a walking distance from lots of restaurants. As it was described in its profile, is the best you can get for the money.  The communication with Nicole is very easy and clear, what really helps to enjoy your stay without inncesary stress.  I will definetley recommend it.

This was a marvelous stay, one of my best Airbnb experiences yet. The apartment is adorable, and Andrea provided really helpful and thorough directions for navigating the apartment and the neighborhood. This is really a steal for what you get. Thanks for everything Andrea!!

We had a great stay at Jill's house. The place is very beautifully decorated, the kitchen big, next to the back yard so you can enjoy the sunlight during breakfast. It has a lot very interesting cooking books (a lot of vegetarian ones), a great collection of pots and pans and many interesting spices in the drawer, (you could guess Jill is a great cook). They left us a welcome tray with bagels and wine which was very appreciated! There was also a note saying we could help ourselves to everything on the fridge (packed with a lot of organic and gourmet stuff) which is a dangerous thing to say to a group of Argentinians. :) We also enjoyed some of the cds of their big collection in a great sound system they have set up. Books all over the place.  Would definitely stay there again.

Jill made us feel very welcome and we had a great time staying in her house and going around the area. There is lots of space downstairs and in the bathroom and bedrooms - especially the main bedroom which is fantastic.  We loved Prospect Park and the Brooklyn Museum of Modern Art and we liked the shady walks down the Eastern Parkway - it was very hot and sunny all week.  We liked Barboncino and Mayfield restaurants very much.  We appreciated having three keys as there were four of us.

Apartment almost consistent with its description. It is located 15 minutes from an express metro station, in a pretty and quiet street. In the surrounding area, there are many small shops. we felt no sense of danger even in the evening. There are 7 real beds. We are 10 minutes by express metro from southern Manhattan (by metro omnibus, it's 20 minutes).  Do not forget that the surface area of ​​the apartment is only 70 m2, and that therefore at 7 people the space is limited for the occupants, and that the additional furniture is limited. There were 4 of us sleeping in the large bedroom, 2 of us sleeping in the small bedroom and one person sleeping in the living room. detail: the openings of 3 windows have air conditioning systems. The published photos do not show the wallpaper on the walls.

Andrea's place is a lovely appartment, that feels both very personal/intimate and very welcoming as well. A good choice of books and Netflix (but that is all, no cable TV) and the perfect addition of a "roof terrace" for a drink under the stars.   The apartment is really not far from Prospect Park (which is huge!) and really just 2 min walk to the subway going to Manhattan. For those who tend to feel "unsafe" when traveling, the area near the apartment may seem a bit "sketchy" by night, but it is actually totally safe and did not have any issue at all.   I didn't get to meet Andrea personally but she was always very quick to answer my messages and was very helpful when I had a "last-minute special request" (thanks again!). Also, her little guestbook is a great idea, as well as the drawer full of delivery menus ;-).  I would definitely book this place again.

Anu and Sarah are very attentive hosts who take pride in insuring their guests have a comfortable stay. The apartment is spotlessly clean and warm. It is also conveniently located; close to transport links, supermarkets and a number of good restaurants, cafes and bars. There were a couple of completely unforeseeable hiccups with the heating system (which I believe has been updated since our stay) but Anu and their lovely concierge Rob were on hand literally within 15 minutes to make sure the problem was resolved. I have stayed with other hosts in the past and I have never encountered such prompt assistance which is always appreciated. If you are looking for a cosy retreat in a convenient neighbourhood, Anu and Sarah's place is ideal and I hope to visit again.

The space is clean, slightly smaller than it looks on the pictures (we were 4 people). The kitchen offers options to cook basic meals. You cannot open the windows; instead you can use air-condition (or rather loud built-in ventilators) to cool down in hotter months. The location offers line A and C, 7 blocks away, which will take you straight to Manhattan, otherwise G train 3 blocks away, to get you to Manhattan, if you change once again. You can find multiple supermarkets around, the best was Metropolitan city market around the corner. On Nostrand around the corner there is a good diner to get some tacos or burgers. The neighbours were silent and civil. At nights we didn’t feel super safe in the neighbourhood, specifically we would advise to stay away from crossing Nostrand to continue on Gates avenue, as the street has various shelters for homeless, not alone groups of young individuals who will not spare you from feeling intimidated. In general, this is Brooklyn and keep your heart open, and on the street you might bounce into people selling good old fashioned lemonade for good cause, how delightful it was to see it. The communication with Ravanna was straightforward before the arrival, the instructions were clear and all worked out well with the keys etc. At the end of our stay we repeatedly asked for a favour, however our emails stayed unanswered, which took us aback. Enjoy your stay and do not dare to miss Brooklyn Bridge (High street station).

Olu was a great host and made my first experience with airbnb a pleasant one. I got delayed due to customs when I landed, but he made no trouble of it. He was very friendly when I managed to lock myself out one morning and made no issue of coming to rescue me despite getting him out of bed. (Still so sorry about that.) He was always courteous and would let me know beforehand if he needed to pick anything up from the apartment.  Everything in the apartment was in order. For New York standards, this is very spacious. The apartment is between two of the most useful subway routes and close to other buses. It's very easy to get around NYC and see the sights.  There's supermarkets nearby that are open until very late. I never felt unsafe in the neighbourhood and there's always people around. This is the one drawback as there is a lot of street noise, but then it is NYC.
Conveniently located next to major subway lines and good food. Cute little place! It’s a 5th floor walk up but don’t let that scare you. It’s a great way to sneak in exercise. :)

Daniel was amazing. My flight was supposed to get in at 3pm and I told Daniel I'd be at the house hopefully by 5pm since it was my first time in the city alone. My flight came in at 7pm and I got off the train at the farthest point from the house. From the airport, he kept in touch. Eventually I got to the house by 10pm and he was so patient waiting for me to show up. He gave me a tour of the house, explained the nearest stations and got me settled in before he left.   For someone used to living in the suburbs and private neighbourhoods patrolled by cops, I was a bit suspicious of the neighbourhood. But it is safe. It's quiet,the bus stop is close by and the people are helpful with directions. There are bodegas, the subway for A and C line is about a 10 min walk and Manhattan is close by for shopping and food. For the price,this place rocks. There were two other people in the house,but I never saw them. I had a great experience,thanks to Daniel's patience mostly.

A great place to relax and recharge from the stress of the city. Subways around 8 minutes walk. The room and the bathroom was super clean and tidy! When I'll visit New York again I will definitely come back to stay there!

I stayed for a month. Overall happy with the experience! Some difficulties of being a long term stay include - no kitchen or freezer, no water access besides bathroom sink. Pros: The room was very spacious with plenty of storage, a comfortable bed, and a large desk (great for a student!). Door to my room was able to be locked with a key (important to me as a female solo traveler).  Felt very safe. The bathroom was right across the hall. I was pleasantly surprised as it had great water pressure and was spacious and clean as well, even though it is an old house. Daniel was also a kind and responsive host! Cons: The walls are quite thin - I could hear breathing and conversations of those in the room next to me. I felt bad for my neighbors as I had to come in and out at odd hours for my early/late hospital shifts, afraid to wake everyone up. However, the noise was not a deal breaker for me and I still enjoyed myself. Just put some headphones in maybe.   I would return to stay again! Thanks

This place is a steal. Sunnyside is amazing! I found it relatively easy to park in the neighborhood, FYI. Super close to the subway but not too close to hear it. Good A/C. Well stocked kitchen. Convenient laundromats and groceries.

Andrea's location was perfect!  Location is everything...right?! Even the location of the unit, within the building was perfect.  There is great food and access to the train within blocks.  We came up for a Broadway show and the trip into Manhattan was no more than 30 min. We did not feel uncomfortable or unsafe at all and the folks in the building were friendly.  So, check it out for yourself!

The apartment is just as it looks in the photos: nice, comfortable and spacious (and the heating is excellent for the winter). The only downside is that at times it can be a little noisy, because you can hear everything that happens on the floor above. Shelley, our host, is very friendly and always responded to our queries promptly. You have to keep in mind that the neighborhood is really far away, at least 45 minutes by subway to Manhattan. It's a nice neighborhood, but very lonely, you don't see tourists at all, and at night it can seem a little unsafe (although nothing ever happened to us).

Shelley is an awesome host.  This was our second time using Airbnb and we were not disappointed.  Shelley is very good with her communication.  She met us right on time.  She also checked in on us via text to make sure we are ok and that our stay was good.  That was very much appreciated.  Because we were attending a convention she also let us use her iron.  We were very grateful.  The apartment is exactly as pictured and even better in real life than in the pictures.  There is definitely an artsy and island vibe which we loved! The neighborhood is quiet and lovely with beautiful front yard gardens.  Neighbors were very friendly.  We were able to find parking with no problem (we did arrive before 5pm).  This apartment is walking distance to EVERYTHING (supermarkets, restaurants, drug stores, corner deli, wine store) etc.,!   Shelley has a great guidebook.  I would not hesitate to stay again!  Thank you for everything.  Our stay was lovely and very relaxing.

The house is organized and the host is very nice! It felt like home! I was a bit scared about the neighborhood in the beggining, but after talking to Shelley and getting to know it better, I felt fine.

Shelley is a very pleasant host. She knows her neighborhood well, and she gives very good advice. The apartment is completely consistent with the photos and the description, even larger than the effect given by the photos. Perhaps missing a few dishes, for the rest, everything you need for daily life is there. Popular neighborhood, very lively, we never felt in danger. Very pretty apartment street, brownstone style houses, very quiet street and apartment. However Newkirk Ave subway stop, good starting point for exploring Brooklyn neighborhoods like Dumbo or Park Slope, but far for Manhattan, allow an hour door to door for each visit to Manhattan.

This was the best possible first experience with Air BnB. We hardly saw Shelley, but she made sure we were doing well and was only a text away. The place is very clean and comfortable, although a little chilly at night; but that's because it was spring and rainy. Bed was comfortable. The kitchen had everything we needed when we cooked dinner one night. Bathroom is clean. Loved the quirky decor. We're glad we ended up staying in Brooklyn even though the commute to Manhattan is around 35 minutes by train. Neighborhood was safe and drug and grocery stores are walkable distances. Would love to stay with her again in the future.

Overall, the atmosphere of Shelley's apartment is very urban and cute and comfortable.  Due to travel plans of her own, though, I had difficulty getting check-in information from Shelley until just a few hours before my arrival.  She also hadn't had time to clean thoroughly so I had to do a little sweeping, scrubbing, and bed-making.  The neighborhood is a working-class city neighborhood, with all that entails-- You need to be aware of your surroundings at night, but there's nothing to be paranoid about.  There are a couple of good delis and restaurants over on Flatbush Avenue.  Parking on the street was easy during the day, but very difficult at night.  Once the stress of check-in was past, my stay here was perfectly fine.
Perfect quiet location to escape the stress of Manhattan. Public connections are very easy to reach (3 minutes). Spacious apartment fully equipped. Good beds, you could sleep well.

Shelley went above and beyond for us! It was our honeymoon, and I had never been to NYC! I was afraid and didnt know what to expect! Shelley's space was a home away from home for us! We loved the style! The personal touches did so much for our hearts! It truly was a great place to stay! I'd recommend it over and over again!!

For the most part, Mari's place was as advertised.  I especially enjoyed her neighborhood. Plenty of good restaurants, grocery stories,  a drug store and services . And having subways stops relatively close was a plus. Although I am a healthy and active senior,  the stairs to her third floor walk up were a definite challenge.   I an a light sleeper so I asked Mari in advance if she had a fan which I could use  foir white noise and she graciously offered me the use  of her own.  In the end, however, I had to purchase a white noise machine because her upstairs neighbor (s) neighbors directly above her place walked around constantly, until past midnight the four nights I stayed there. Unfortunately, the white noise could not mask what was really an annoying problem. I am not sure there is anything the host can do to control the situation,  but those, like me,  who need  relative quiet to sleep should be forewarned. Also, though a TV is listed as an amenity, there was no cable. Only streaming. Fortunately I had a netflex account but regretted I had no access to TV news. Other pluses in her home were its cleanliness, shower water pressure, well stocked kitchen and storage.

Nice spot for Bed&Breakfast, good connected with subway to Manhattan. the owners are really friendly and always open for communication. the streets around the neighborhood looks like dangerous in the night, but all good!

Sebastian was THE perfect host. We came to Brooklyn very late late by car due to traffic jam in NYC but he was still up and explained everything to us. He is a very friendly and easy going person. We didn't have to use our car a single time during our journey as Sebastian's place is a 5 minutes walk from Q line which goes directly to Time Square. South Brooklyn may sounds scary for some but the streets were very safe, even when coming back late at night. The place is as described, clean and well furnished (laundry , 2 TVs,etc...). When i come back to NYC , i would definitely come back at Sebastian's , he made me feel at home within a second and was always here for our every needs.  To sum up, i highly recommend Sebastian and his party home!

I'm sorry but this room was not what I expected. The air was so thick from the smell of fried food that I felt I couldn't breathe and had to buy odor eliminator from Duane Reade. The listing says there is a full bed and a twin bed but there were only 2 very very uncomfortable twin beds. The entire apartment was cluttered, including right in front of the doorway to the room. This made it very difficult to go to the bathroom in the night, and enter and leave the room in general. There were towels on the floor as carpets. There were very thin sheets on the uncomfortable beds, with no blanket in sight. My friend and I were forced to use towels as blankets as it got quite cold during the rainy night. What was described as a "clean, white bathroom" was very cluttered, with a broken towel rack (that looked unsafe). The only saving grace was that there was a window with a fire exit that you could sit on for some fresh air.

My friend and I stayed for a week at Edda's! She is very friendly and helpful, always ready to give you tips about what is interesting to see. The flat is close to the subway that goes downtown and the neighborhood is not sketchy despite what we were told about Harlem before coming to NYC. The air cooler is a bit old so it takes time to cool down the room and is noisy. But in the end it's a real bargain if you intend to stay for a couple of days.

This is the most beautiful home I've ever stayed in! I loved every detail. I wish I could have stayed more than one night. Ann is very kind and accommodating (and I suspect very cool given the various art pieces in her home). The views are gorgeous (so many windows), and the location is also the best that I've ever been lucky enough to be in for a stay in NYC. Right around the corner from famous places like Cafe Wha? and the Comedy Cellar, and in a five minute walk you can get pretty much anything on the planet. And in the bedroom there's a little station for water and hot tea, a bunch of cool lamps of different varieties, a space heater, a white noise machine, and a million books!

Nice and economic option for someone who wants to stay at upper Manhattan. For me, it was a great location, except parking. But that's because it's NY.  I'll be honest with the future potential guests for this place. It is an old building. Nothing fancy or stylish. A bit shaby. But for the price, it is a great place to stay, specialy if you are visiting NY for short time and don't wanna rent expensive hotels. My major concern was cleanliness and a working AC. I very much liked how clean the room and bathroom was. The ac was working. Extra fans helped too. There was fresh bed sheets, towels, toilet amenities (as described). Nothing i can think of which felt uncomfortable or unpleasant. There are rules clearly mentioned in booklets, which helped me understand the do's and don'ts.  Overall it was nice to stay two nights and would certainly come back considering the price and my necessity for a location in manhattan. Great stay!

Do not believe the good reviews we do not understand ourselves after renting this apartment. So that our stay was as pleasant as expected we had to relocate at our expense. Otherwise the apartment would have really ruined the trip. We did not find the cleanliness that we were entitled to expect and we felt very uncomfortable. The neighborhood is noisy and the drug is very present. Ne croyez pas les bons commentaires  que nous ne comprenons pas nous-même après avoir loué cet appartement. Pour que notre séjour soit aussi agréable qu'attendu nous avons dû nous reloger a nos frais. Sinon l'appartement nous aurait vraiment gâché le voyage. Nous n'y avons pas trouvé la propreté que nous étions en droit d'attendre et nous y sommes senti très mal à l'aise. Le quartier est bruyant et la drogue très présente.

Cosy and comfortable stay in a fantastic location. This is the ideal place if you are a foodie as there are some amazing restaurants just a few minutes walk away. The metro connections are great, you can get anywhere pretty quickly! Quite a few sites are within a 30 minute walk. Ann was very welcoming and hospitable and made sure my stay was comfortable, enjoyable and stress free! She responds to questions very quickly. I would love to stay there again!

The place was exactly as described. It is very simple but clean. The communication with Andre was very good! Whenever we had a question he and Maltoni were available and supportive. It was also great that we could leave our luggage in the hallway. That way the check in and -out was not that stressful for us. Thank you!

Great communication with Andre whom also provided great descriptions of how to get to the place from the airport. Harlem is a cool area to stay, however,  it’s still New York and you might bump into plenty of homeless people in the area, however that factor is less important for the overall vibe the area gives which is diversity and a lot of history. The room was super clean, the only thing I would say about the room is that the bed could have been a bit more comfortable and stable. Thx for hosting us, we would book it again if we would visit NYC again. Cheers from Sweden 🇸🇪

The room is as seen in the photos, communication with Andre was very good and he was always attentive to everything we might need, but we were not comfortable. The entrance to the building and the common areas were very dirty and smelled very bad.  Everything around the accommodation was very dirty. There was a lot of garbage in the street and a lot of rats.  The area did not seem safe to us, we saw drug use and sales.  If we had known all this when booking, we would have looked for other options.

this was actually a great spot. I loved the check in to the end. location was great. this isnt a danger zone. it was  a late night. food truck was down the street at 1  o'clock in the morning. loved it. I will definitely be back to this location. 5 stars

Everything as seen in the photos. Price-quality ratio is a 10. Maltoni is very friendly, he was always there for any questions and concerns, he always responded quickly. The only thing we didn't like was the aroma there was, they would have to ventilate more between guests. The location is very good, just 2 blocks from the 145th station that connects you to Times Square in 15 minutes. At night the place was a little scary but nothing ever happened!!! For the price, it is an excellent accommodation.

Really good communication, the place was absolutely clean and beautifully decorated. A lot of snacks, coffee etc and even a bottle of wine awaited us. It's a quiet neighbourhood and, since that seems to be an issue for many NYC travellers, we never felt unsafe in any way.  Also, try the pizza place around the corner that you will find a flyer from in the apartment. The food is great!

Upon my arrival, Ann opened the door for me and did not greet me with a hello, a smile, nor did she introduce herself. Instead, she brashly told me to take my things upstairs to the room, and stated, “Do not plop yourself on the bed. Because of your heaviness I’m afraid you will break the slats.” (I am a size 12.) I was completely taken aback that her welcoming me to her home was to fat shame me. I have never even been called fat by anyone ever. I quickly recognized what type of woman I was dealing with, and quietly went up the very awkward stairs to the room. The spiral stairs are awkward and steep and there is no railing or anything to hold on to. Another thing I noticed as soon as I entered the house, is it was dirty and very cluttered. She hung clothes to dry on the upstairs railing, looking down into her dining area or whatever it was. I wouldn’t know as I was never invited to go into any other room than the one I reserved.  I put my bags away in the spot she instructed me to, and I stated the room was very cold. The space heater that was in the room was inoperable as the plug was completely cut off. She pretended not to know about it. I asked her if she could please provide a small space heater for me, as the temperature was in the low 40s, and the room was very cold. She stated she would order one from Amazon. I told her I would need one for that same night. She mumbled something as she was leaving the room, and I left out to eat. She did not get a heater that night and I had to double up my socks, shirt, and pants, where I was so cold. I woke up freezing and went downstairs and asked her why she did not turn on the radiator to heat up the house like she told me she would. She harshly stated, “Linda, I was not going to turn it on at night after it not being on for the last 8 months and have something happen.”  I asked her once again when she was going to provide a space heater for me and turn on the heat. She stated she was looking into it. I told her I could not go another night without one, and if that was going to be the case to let me know because that was not going to work for me. I informed her I have COPD and did not want to get sick while on vacation. She rudely stated, “Well, you should have told me about your illness prior to reserving the room.” I told her I did not think I had to share my medical history with her when I assumed she was going to provide me with some heat. She grew more visibly upset with me and brashly stated, “Linda, I am only required to provide you with a reasonable amount of heat. And I have done that.”  I told her, “You have not provided me with any heat!”  And told her if she was not going to provide me with a small space heater that day, then I was going to leave and ask for a refund. She claimed she turned on the radiator but that it was not working. I left the house, and it was actually much warmer outdoors than in her home. While out, she texted me worried asking me if I was preparing to leave. I told her, no, and why was she asking. She stated, “Because I looked in your room and it looked like you were preparing to clear out.”  I told her that is the way I always leave my room; clean, everything put away, and the bed made. And she actually complimented me for that. She finally had someone deliver a small space heater that evening. When I came back from dinner that evening, I saw a whole bunch of cat hair all over the rug in the room. The cats do not go into the room on their own.   Her space is not as she depicts it, and quite frankly I have no idea how this woman has anyone saying anything nice about her or her home. She is clearly not a people person. I am a very friendly and extroverted happy woman, and I was dealing with a woman who was the complete opposite. With me at least.  All of my previous hosts have praised me for my happy and fun personality, and how clean I leave the room.  The restroom is 4’ x 4’, if even that. The old window does not shut completely so cold air is coming in while you are showering. Also, there was never any hot water to brush my teeth with or wash my face in the morning. I have been to NYC seven other times, and once stayed outside of Times Square. But no noise machine can drown out the extreme amount of LOUD noise that came from the downstairs restaurant and bar patrons, being at their loudest until 1am. Not even Times Square was that loud at night!  There is not sufficient lighting in the room; just a couple of reading lamps. This lady has a thing about not locking doors. Because there are two holes in the bedroom swinging doors where anyone can see in and out of, as if the doorknobs had been removed. Also, the restroom door does not lock at all. It doesn’t even have a latch on it. So, anyone and her cats can walk in at any time you are using the restroom or showering.  One morning I heard her on the phone at 8:25. I got up to use the restroom, and when I came out, she says, Linda? I said, yes? And she stated, oh just wondering if

We stayed in Elizabeth's apartment for 2 weeks, and it suited our needs perfectly. There were 3 of us so 2 shared a bed and 1 had the smaller room which was absolutely fine for us. There was a ton of space to put our clothes etc which was needed as we are 3 girls with a lot of stuff! The apartment itself is very spacious (and true to the pictures) and we never felt on top of each other. The subway is about a 10-15 min walk, which again was fine, and you can get a train straight to Manhattan which takes about 25 minutes. We had our initial reservations about the neighbourhood on our first night as we ventured out in the dark, however during the day it was fine and we felt safe. Like anywhere new it felt better and safer to be out and about in a group, however on occasions when we did venture out on our own we never felt unsafe. Overall Elizabeth made us feel welcome, was great at communicating via text when we needed advice, and provided us with an apartment that felt like home.

Negative points: We had some problems with "little animals" which stressed us out quite a bit because our 10 month old daughter does all fours and puts everything in her mouth, the treatment products are dangerous for her health. The kitchen is a little lacking in equipment (no microwave, no bowl). Me who likes to sleep in the dark, there was no curtain, so I woke up at 6am every morning. For the positives: the apartment is large and quiet and Elizabeth is a very kind, responsive host who speaks fluent Spanish and a little French.

Short but very good stay.  Charisse's place is very nice and bright.  Everything was perfect.  One very small detail, but I really appreciate the way she manages to give keys.  The system is efficient and no need to stress about missing each other.  Other than that, the location was nice, near subway station and nice neighborhood; perfect!Thank you for the lovely stay.

Lovely apartment ideal for our stay in NYC close to the subway, we spent the majority of our days uptown and it was a nice relaxing place to return to after a long day of sightseeing. The neighbourhood was lively and never once did we feel unsafe, people were very friendly.

I booked this place for my parents when they were visiting since I live in the neighborhood.  I cannot stress strongly enough how fantastic Michael was as a host and how great the apartment is.  It was immaculately clean, and stocked with everything you could need.  He was even kind enough to include some basics in the fridge - beer, OJ, etc.  There were nice touches that made it feel like home for the weekend, reading and a few magazines on NYC out on the coffee table.  Windows on both sides of the living room provided natural light all day.  A 1 or 2 block walk from the subway, and no problem coming and going as needed.  A working washer and dryer which we used over the weekend was an excellent perk.  The bed was really comfortable, and overall the place has a really great vibe to it.  I hope to use Michael's place again in the future.

A wonderful big, tidy and nice furnitured room with own bathroom on the same 3rd. floor, where nobody else comes along, so I had really my own privacy. There are 3 dogs and a cat in the house, which like to get in contact with you. So, you shouldn't be afraid of that, if you want to stay here, even if you can smell in the house, that there are animals living too, but not on the 3rd floor where your room is located.  Lynn and Dave are wonderful hostes. Dave bbrought my heavy luggages upstairs and showed me the neighbourhood area, so that I could find my ways. Bus stop is right across the street and goes every 30 minutes to the ferry, which is a 15 minutes ride. The ferry ride itself is free and amazing, so you cross the statue of liberty and see the amazing Manhattan skyline from the waterfront every time. It takes you 50 minutes to go downtown Manhattan this way and than it depends where you want to go to in the city. If you have something to do uptown, it'll be a long ride. But you can catch en express bus as well, brings you over there in about 45 minutes. I never did thath, because I enjoyed very much the ride with the ferry every single time. So overall I recommend this AirBnB location, if you are not afraid of dogs and like to have that every day ride via ferry to Manhattan.

This cozy bedroom located on the 3rd floor of a beautiful home was a delight to stay for the 4 months I did my rotations in Staten Islansd University Hospital. All the amenities were provided and my place was always neat and clean. The house is located on Bay st with many restaurants and bars. I had to take one 15mt bus ride to the ferry to manhattan and the bus stops right in front of the house. The dogs sunny and ziggy are such a delight to come home to after a stressful day of work. Dave and Lynn are absolutely great and I guarantee a relaxing stay at their place.

Lynn and Dave's home was the perfect place to stay and rest after a long day! They were amazing guests who respected my privacy and attended promptly to any of my needs. They also recently added a mini- fridge with a freezer right outside the room so there's no need to walk all the way down to the kitchen, huge plus for me! You really get the third floor all to yourself and the room was very warm, homely, and comfortable. There's plenty of storage space, a desk to work at, and the wifi was excellent. They also have two adorable, very well- behaved golden retrievers and a very affectionate cat, unlimited love and petting! As someone who doesn't drive, I had access to the S51 bus right outside the house which takes you to the ferry one way or down the shoreline the other. It was an easy transfer to the S79 bus if you're going somewhere near Hylan Blvd including SIUH. I cannot stress how highly I would recommend their wonderful home to all. Thanks again Lynn and Dave!

Visiting Jamie and William  To put it bluntly: PERFECT!  Jamie and William are absolutely friendly hosts and will take you in as if you have been part of their family for years.  The room is really like the pictures. Bed is soft and very comfortable. Own bathroom with toilet, hand basin and spacious shower.  Air conditioning and ceiling fan in the room and WiFi throughout the apartment.  The apartment is only 2 1/2 blocks from the 110th Street subway station. That's about 5-7 minutes walk.  There are plenty of shopping opportunities in the immediate vicinity. Supermarket, bakery, pizzeria, McDonald's, Chinese food and and and... Everything you need is within walking distance. Absolutely TOP.  The area is completely safe, I and my wife never felt unsafe. Even at 10 p.m. I walked to get pizza. Good area.  We were allowed to use the living room, television and the entire kitchen. Jamie and William have two cute cats who both love to cuddle.  The roof terrace on the 8th floor is awesome. You can have a wonderful dinner there and drink a glass or two of red wine.  If I visit New York again, I will definitely stay with Jamie and William again.  Thank you for everything. Greetings from Berlin-Germany  Axel and Rosi (Axl Rose

The apartment was great. We arrived late into JFK during a rainstorm and so it was amazing to arrive and everything work so smoothly. Jae was a great host - he has lots of useful information and made our arrival and departure very stress free. The apartment is very well provisioned and extremely comfortable.  The local area is really nice - the organic market on Montrose is great and there is a big supermarket just up the road. Danny's pizza just next to the apartment is great for a slice and around the corner on Montrose there is a good bar - Duck Duck - serving a great selection of beer.  We had a great time - would recommend it highly.

Your host Emmitt is a affable sort who isn't afraid to share a story about the history of NY or where one might go get the most of your visit...His apt is cozy and well appointed making your stay comfortable in the midst of a city that at times seems like it never sleeps...Subways and buses are mere blocks away that will take you anywhere from The Battery to 1 World Trade Center...l highly recommend Emmitt and his home...

Jae's Flat is very nice, clean and spacious with everything you need. You don't need a key, so the check-in is very easy. The communication with Jae was good when we were in NYC, the days before I was a little afraid he could cancel because he answered only after I send a few messages. Two things were not so nice in the flat: we had a mouse and a lot of mosquitoes (although there a fly-screens on all windows, so Jae did everything he can, he also suggested to come and lay traps for the mouse) and I don't know if it is a bar around or just neighbors but there was very loud music two nights, so we could not really sleep. But in all it was a nice experience and we would come back.

The place was clean and spacious, with a nice bathroom and kitchen. Rob answered our request and our messages fast, and was very helpful. Our first airbnb host cancelled our reservation in the last minute, so it was really appreciated that Rob answered our request within minutes!  It takes some time to take the subway to Manhattan, but the place is super close to the subway station! The only bad thing was that the room's AC in one of the windows made the window stay half open. When it was raining during two of the nights it was really hard to fall asleep since you could hear the dripping from outside. But maybe it's just a temporary solution!

I am really happy I chose for this airbnb in Brooklyn. For me it was very important to see different perspectives of the city instead of being all time in Manhattan.   First of all Rob & CS are great hosts. They will help you and also sometimes asking If you need something. Great service!   For me personaly Brooklyn and the appartment were reminding me of Rotterdam in The Netherlands.   The appartment tells a story and it felt home for me. Also the area is really nice; close to the subway, a really nice supermarket around the corner, many restaurants and also the prospect parc that is designed after Central parc is really beautiful to relax sometimes or just to go for a walk.   I defenitly recommend✅

Emily's apartment is perfectly situated - the Williamsburg bridge and metro are a few minutes walk. Awesome restaurants and bars, grocery and drug store are all within a short walk. The apartment decor is spot on, I found myself staring at so many items!  Emily is a great communicator and I never had a problem reaching her before or during my stay. She kept me appraised of her comings and goings (even though she didn't need to) as she worked late into the night during my stay. We got to chat on a few occasions and she is quite lovely. Her hospitality made my trip that much more enjoyable.   Then there's Dish her fabulous cat who enjoyed an episode of game of thrones with me (and seemed to like it just as much as I did) and would hop onto the bed in the middle of the night and promptly knock out.  My stay was delightful, I would certainly stay again!
Emily's apartment was very comfortable and cosy, with a unique and special charm. A real steal for the price!

I agree to everything that was said in the other positive reviews, but wanted to add some other things that most didn't touch on. It was my first experience also using Air BnB and it was great. I felt like I was staying at my own apt. oppose to a hotel and it was soooo much more relaxing. Even though it was a comparable price to the median scale hotels I checked out, it was much closer to Manhattan via the subway and had more amenities. Jae (host) was very professional and attentive when needed. He responded to emails or text message very quickly, but never intruded on our visit. He was there when we arrived and gave us a short tour of the apt and even offered to carry our suitcase up to the 3rd floor apt. Check out was also a breeze, when Jae just asked us to lock up and leave the keys in the apt. The apt is very modern, bright and clean with almost all its furnishings from Ikea. There is a window a/c unit in the bedroom, but it's more than adequate to cool the whole apt. when we went in June. Someone mentioned street noise in there review, but with the windows closed it wasn't too bad. The noise was what I expected from a city neighborhood. We also never heard a peep from the neighbors. There were two of us staying at the apt. and we were each furnished a set of keys to the place. There are two sky lights that make the apt. bright. One in the living room and the second in the bathroom that can easily be opened for airflow. One of us slept in the bed and I on the fold out couch and it was comfortable. Even though I have herniated disc in my back, I still slept like a baby. As far as the neighborhood being safe, I'm in law enforcement and can say the neighborhood felt safe at all hours of the day. I checked out a street view on Google Maps after booking the apt. and it looked a little scary for those who live in the suburbs, but once there it was just a typical bustling urban neighborhood you'll find in Brooklyn. All the merchants in the area were friendly. I have a relative who lives in Brooklyn and they said the Williamsburg area where this apts located is a very sought out area to live. The main entrance door into the building has a deadbolt and door lock, along with the apt. There is a laundry mat a couple businesses down (if needed) and I discovered a good pizza place also a few doors down that also offers gluten free pizza that I recommend. There's also a small 24 hr. corner market and the L subway train that goes to Manhattan is about 2 blocks away. We took a cab from La Guardia Airport that cost approximately $30 and is about...

When I checked  into Michaels apt.....a man named Tommy brought the keys as promised, but couldn't explain any details about the apartment, because he didn't know how the tv or the washer/dryer worked. He also said that it was not his job to know these details. This seemed a rather strange welcome as Tommy did not appear to represent the host, and Michael never showed up for the meeting that we had scheduled earlier. I entered into a small studio apt with a full size bed and not a queen size as was described in our correspondence. This was totally unacceptable. Neither was there a second room, separated with a wall and door with another queen size bed as was also mentioned. There was only one small room barely adequate for one person. The room smelled of tobacco from previous smokers. The large sunny garden was an absolute wreck, full of cigarette butts and dirt and piles of trash plus broken tiles and no furniture and separated by caution tape from the neighbors garden. I also couldn't find a trash bin except a tiny bucket.! At first sight I was already disappointed about the 29th st environment, which seems to be the worst in the prime Chelsea area. The whole street seemed piled up with different trash every day and close to the apt appears to be a major depot for homeless drug addicts. I did not really feel safe in the garden apt . Also I wouldn't describe this address as a large sunny garden apt in prime Chelsea. ! The apartment and environs are totally unacceptable for a longer stay......the cooking facilities and microscopic kitchenette were totally inadequate, and the apt was falsely advertised in my correspondence with michael which he later excused by writing that it was late at night and he was confused. Furthermore......there were no shelves or closets to unpack my suitcase which barely fit inside.....only a few hangers There were two small stools and a tiny butcher block that served the kitchenette and other than the bed the only place to sit was two high stools by a tiny table I stayed for twelve hours and i would not recommend this place for anyone staying for longer than that.

I would definitely recommend Michael's place, and it will be the first place I check for availability next time I need to be in NYC. This place is clean and neat and plenty of space for a studio apartment.  Michael is an excellent host, checking in with us to make sure we didn't need anything and always quick to reply with any questions we had.  The location is perfect, just a couple blocks from Penn Station and only a few more to Times Square.  There are grocery stores, drug stores, convenience stores, and plenty of restaurants in the immediate area.  But the apartment is maybe 1/2 block from the nearest avenue, making it quiet in the middle of all the noise of NYC.  We felt perfectly safe walking in and around the area, and building is secure.  Thanks for making our stay in New York City great!

Evan and Maria were great hosts. Can't recommend enough. Great communication and if we had questions they would always respond straight away. They always asked if we needed anything during our stay. The apartment was just like described. Quiet neighborhood but also walking distance to most main attractions. They made our stay a stress free and enjoyable one.

I highly recommend Evan and Maria's place. I was pleasantly surprised by the amenities and services they provided. Somehow they made sure that we had all we needed, even though I did not see them at all during my travel. They were patient, flexible, and easy to work with, especially when things got stressful. They are one of the reasons why I had the most wonderful time at New York City.

Our  favorite thing about this place was the location. You are close to everything. Plenty of restaurants and pubs and grocers. Everything you need is close. Bus and subway right around the corner.  It's an easy walk to Times Square but yet you are far enough away to be away from the sea of people over there. Our second favorite thing was the bathroom. They did a great remodel. The shower is huge and the bathroom was spotless. Lots of room to put things away and to hang towels. The hosts were very responsive even though it was over the holidays. They left a bottle of wine and some Hershey's kisses for us. The only real problem we had was the heat in the building seems to be controlled by the building and it was kept hot. There is no individual heat adjustment in the unit so we had to run the AC and keep windows open the whole time we were there to cool it down. The windows are right at the fire escape with no screen on one which felt a little unsafe at night.

Joy is a great host. She responded quick on each email or text messages. Her place is a perfect place to stay In NY. It is close to the subway or stores. Her place is very clean and it has everything what u need. The neighborhood is not bad, so don't be scared about Harlem. So, choose her place and u will have a good time in NYC :-)

Our experience exceeded our expectations.  We loved our stay at Joy's apartment!  Joy is incredibly responsive to texts and is a very gracious host.    The apartment itself is AMAZING!  It is spacious and is situated very near the subway.  The neighborhood was safe and quiet with some convenient shops around the corner.  There is a larger grocery store a few blocks away.  We never felt unsafe, even when we got to the apartment late in the evening.  We would recommend to anybody that they stay at Joy's apartment.  We would definitely stay here again.

Bernardo and Andressa are friendly host. I don't get to use the common area much, but the bedroom and bathroom are as described, very clean and spacious.  Location is superb if you want to explore Williamsburg.  And its a doorman building which makes you feel safe. Great restaurant and L train are in short walking distance.  However, wifi is weak and slow so trying to work became very stressful. But I guess you should enjoy having a Manhattan skyline view from the bedroom  instead of working while you are there! Overall, I had a good stay and would recommend staying at Bernardo and Andressa's apartment highly.

I stayed there for 10days, which was very comfortable. The hosts, Andressa and Bernardo, were so kind and friendly. Also Shanti, a puppy there, was so pretty:)  The bedroom and bathroom were clean and neat furthermore their apartment is decorated with sophisticated furnishing and arts.   The location was great. There are nice shops and cafes around the house. On the way to the room from a nearby station, some people were walking even in the midnight. I was never afraid when I went home alone after Broadway shows around 11 pm! In addition, I could enjoy Manhattan’s night view near the house.  Lastly, I had to change my book several times before the stay, they gave me prompt responses each time and cheerfully accepted the changes.  I wish to back there in summer next time!

If you are visiting Brooklyn and love great restaurants, beautiful views, and adorable dogs, STAY HERE!  Bernardo and Andressa's condo was absolute perfection for what we were looking for.  We had never rented a private room in someone's home before through Airbnb, only entire rentals, so we were a little hesitant about booking at first, but all the great reviews were spot on.  We would definitely stay here again when we return, as it's in our favorite location in all of Brooklyn, is decorated so nicely, and Shanti steals the show with her cuteness.  Bernardo and Andressa are very kind, and balanced the exact right amount of helpfulness/friendliness and allowing us to have our own space.  Not sure if it's mentioned anywhere in the listing, but we were pleasantly surprised to learn that the condo is just a 3 min walk to the ferry to Manhattan, and only an 8 min walk to the L line subway.  So easy to get around everywhere.  And the restaurants in this area of Williamsburg are incredible.  Don't hesitate to book this place!
Our host was excellent.. the accommodations very good.. entry is a bit sketchy but once inside.. great!

Good things: my room had a large bed and for me it was comfortable, with drawer space to store my clothes. The kitchen has everything you need to cook at ease. The bathroom always had hot water and body wash and shampoo. The house has central heating and it doesn't get cold at all. There are supermarkets, laundry, shops and metro very close to the apartment. The owner, Carlos, is very friendly and I had all the facilities in the world to get to the apartment at dawn and to ask him anything on Wathsapp.  Bad things: the apartment is located in Harlem, a neighborhood that, although they say it is no longer dangerous, is not at all pleasant to walk through the streets at night, although I never had any problems. Both the building and the apartment are quite old and it is a 4⁰ without an elevator. At times, cleanliness was poor. The noise from the heating at night is the worst, I had to sleep with earplugs.

Great value, given uncomparably low prices! The house and room is not the biggest, but no issues for me other than the bathroom being a bit small for a 6'0 guy. I had few occasions spotting a bug or two, but Maria was very accomodating in making sure the room was cleaned throughout the stay. Maria is a lovely host with great coffee! Broadway station was conveniently close by, with other beautiful parks of Astoria. The neighborhood is not scary as well, with a school right by the block.

The accomodation was really great to stay for a couple days. Easy to get from the subway to the place, lovely family clean room and free great breakfast. For first look the surroundings looks dangerous but we were feeling safe. Asolutely no problem with nobody. Great place to stay. I would get back sometime.

Comfortable and spacious apartment true to photos and description. Plenty of clean linens, the coffee machine and hot water kettle were also nice to have.  I did not cook during my stay but the kitchen is equipped for it. The 1 train subway is just up the street less than a 5 minute walk away and there is a drug store and supermarket conveniently located at the same intersection. Sherry was a warm and helpful host!

We needed an affordable place to stay for a multi-day visit to New York, to see family, and we wanted a place to ourselves. This apartment was perfect, and the location optimal.   Sherry was very accommodating, our flight arrived late but she arranged for us to get into the apartment, so we didn’t have to get a hotel room for that night.   The apartment is in a charming older building on the Upper West Side, with many of the original features, such as a wooden interior staircase and railings up to the first floor (the ground floor apartment is a therapy office, common in New York City). The apartment is very clean inside, and very comfortable. It is very secure, and safe.  Sherry and her assistant were very communicative, texting us to welcome us and make sure we got into the apartment. They were very responsive to our requests, which made our stay exceptional.   We had a rental car, and were able to find street parking near the apartment.  Once we settled in, we  mostly took the trains, though, as we didn’t want to spend time looking for parking spots in midtown and the Village. We took advantage of the break between storms in New York City, and we walked as much as we could.   West 145th Street is a perfect starting place for walking around Upper Manhattan. We discovered Alexander Hamilton’s house, Hamilton Grange, which is a museum, on West 141st Street and Convent Avenue. Admission is free, and they have a short documentary on Hamilton’s life. We enjoyed looking at the beautiful churches in the area (but sad to see that many of them are closed up). There are countless beautiful brownstones, many exquisitely refurbished. We saw many boarded up brownstones on our walks, and we would love to see the City take them over, and fix them up for affordable housing, or for the high-functioning homeless.   The Cloisters, on the tip of Manhattan, is one of our favorite museums in New York City, it is part of the Metropolitan Museum now. A tip: the admission fee is quite high, $25 per person, but a native New Yorker knows that this is just a suggested fee for any museum in the Metropolitan group, and you can pay whatever amount you’d like. If they ask for a zip code to prove you are a New Yorker, give them the zip code of the apartment building. But know that they have to accept whatever you offer: there was a tourist couple in front of us, from another country, and the person at the payment kiosk kindly told them they could pay whatever amount they wanted, but when we handed her our payment ($5.00 each) she snarled at us and demanded our zip code. Go figure.  There are many restaurants in the area, Harlem Public is good for lunch, for a breakfast bagel visit David’s Deli and Grill, at 344 West 145th, for a sit-down breakfast/brunch visit NBHD Brulee, 2620 Frederick Douglass Blvd.    If you need your cell phone repaired, for example a cracked screen (!), we highly recommend Lights of Broadway, at 3346 Broadway. Not every electronics/phone repair place is as honest, quick and friendly as this place.      We highly recommend SuperHost Sherry, and the apartment on West 145th Street!

I had a really nice stay at Ellens. She made me feel like I belonged in her apartment. I would definitely come back for sure.  My room was cozy and just the right size for one person. It had everything I needed, a closet and a bed. I was there for two months. I could use the rest of the apartment space if i felt like it, so the living room and the kitchen area was great. The neighborhood was good, I had heard a lot of things about East Harlem, and didn't know what to expect, but I liked it there. I never felt unsafe or anything. I would definitely recommend this room for anyone coming to New York, Ellen was truly the greatest host.

Chikie is a very welcoming host, he received us at his home at 1:30 a.m. because our flight arrived late at New York JFK (allow two hours of transport from JFK). He always tried to best meet our expectations when we needed advice for our stay.  The bedroom is as in the photos, it is equipped with a dressing room and two large mirrors. The bed is comfortable and perfect for two people. It is the room that is for rent but the entire apartment was at our disposal: living room (equipped with a TV + home cinema), equipped kitchen, bathroom. Chikie, when he was at home, stayed in his room and was discreet.  The only two small downsides: - The room which cannot be locked with a key (the lock is worn and opens without much force even when the handle is blocked by the key). Nevertheless, Chikie seems to be a responsible and trustworthy host, he never even came to knock on the door during the stay. - My wife saw a small cockroach in the kitchen (twice). The apartment is however very clean, maintained and uncluttered, this surely comes from the neighborhood.  The apartment is very well located, in the Harlem district, a three-minute walk from the 137th street station on line 1 of the subway. You can get to Times Square in 15-20 minutes and Central Park in 10 minutes. There is also a bus right outside the building on Amsterdam avenue.  The neighborhood is really friendly, we didn't have any feeling of insecurity. Puerto Rican atmosphere! The neighborhood is very lively during the evening.  To conclude, I can only recommend that you choose Chikie as your host, especially for the quality/price ratio that it offers. We really enjoyed our stay!

When we arrived, Chikie left the keys available to access the apartment. The room is exactly in the photos, clear and practical (a dressing room, chest of drawers) There is an Ipad with Wi-Fi connection which is practical for carrying out our research. We had access to the entire apartment. The kitchen and bathroom are clean. The neighborhood is lively on weekends, no feeling of insecurity, people are smiling. The apartment is located 5 minutes from the metro and a supermarket (very useful for shopping) Despite odd working hours, Chikie took the time to welcome us by inviting us to dinner. We discovered a friendly person, smiling and caring towards his guests. We had a pleasant stay with him.

This space is truly centrally located to so many things and at no point did we ever feel unsafe. We meet a few of the neighbors and everyone was very welcoming. Though we didn’t use it we appreciated the French press being available. Peter and Kathy both checked in with us during our stay to make sure we didn’t have any issues and offered great advice for things to try while visiting.

Ross's apartment was a great home away from home for our stay in New York.  The location is a vibrant area with many offerings of restaurants and bars to choose from, but all the while the street the apartment is on is quiet and safe.  The subway is located an easy 5 minute walk and was very easy to navigate to.  Staying in the East Village was fun and a lot to experience.  But still very close to get to mid-town, downtown and other points of interest.  Ross and his wife were so friendly and met us at their apartment to give us the keys and make sure we got settled in ok, even though we had a late night flight coming in from JFK.  They provided a very detailed list of near-by eateries, places to go, site-seeing, and information on how to get to public transportation.  They also gave us suggestions for dinner the night we arrived that were still open after 11pm.  The apartment itself is very comfortable - we had 3 people stay and had plenty of room.  It was a great place to come back and rest and recharge after site-seeing all day.  The elevator in the building was also very much appreciated to not have to walk anymore stairs after a long day.    Ross provided clean linens as well as having the apartment very clean and neatly organized.  There is a portable AC unit in the back living room area which kept that room very cool and the fans throughout the apartment helped circulate the air.  Ross was available anytime throughout our stay for any questions we had.  I definitely recommend staying in this apartment - it's in a great location with plenty to see and do, and not in the midst of the hectic, non-stop tourist areas.  There are plenty of restaurants and transportation is easy to navigate.  There are groceries near-by and a drug store on their street, to stock up on your food and water, snacks, for the apartment too. And getting to the apartment from JFK was a very easy ride too.  Thank you for a great stay for our trip!  Cheers!

Chikie made our trip unforgettable, he is a truly unique person and very friendly, he even invited us to the restaurant. The moments spent with him were the best memories of our trip, so don't hesitate to talk to him, he will put you at ease straight away.   As for the accommodation, nothing to say, everything was perfect especially the location 15 minutes by metro from the center. The neighborhood is great, no danger full of restaurants and bars. The room was very clean!  I highly recommend this accommodation to discover a great person!!

We had a nice stay, however, we were expecting a key to the room but never got it. Its well located, but you need to walk a few blocks to the nearest subway station. There’s a fire station right in front, but we could not hear the noise, which was a surprise.  There are plenty of deli shop, restaurant, parks and beautiful places nearby.  The place is slightly older than the pictures portrays, and the walls/doors slightly dirtier too. But the place/floors and linens were clean. We missed having a blanket, and due to never seeing our host, either early in the morning or late at night, we ended up not getting one for our stay.  Although it was a long weekend, we were not expecting to have so much noise so late at night, especially from non airbnb guest and on the last day, which made it hard to rest and sleep.  We unfortunately also had a very unpleasant experience while using the washroom. Found the garbage in the middle of the bathroom, the mop inside the tub, and the tub was full of blood, which I had to clean to be able to use it. It might have been the other people staying in the other room or the overnight guest, not sure who, but the fact is that it was all dirty and seemed that no one took a look at it was somewhat disappointing.  Overall it was an ok experience.

NOT recommended! TERRIBLE!  The host is ARROGANT and UNPLEASANT.  In the advertisement, he is talking about 2 rooms but there  are only pictures of a room that is in the apt but is actually locked. He took pictures of this room from different angles and with different stuff in it and he is pretending that the second room looks like the other one.  The real room for rent is so TINY and BAD and DIRTY, the bed itself is super tiny and the window is a kind of fissure!  He even removed the advertisement after we booked so we were not able any more to check what we paid for.  We felt like robbed, that's why we asked to be refund.  Horrible experience! As arrived in NY we spent 3 hours talking on the phone with him trying to understand if we could have be refunded and trying to find a better place to stay.  Because of him we lost our first night in NY   ?_?

Perfect accommodation! Very well located, 5 minutes walk from the Columbus Circle metro station (which serves quite a few stations). Clean apartment, equipped with Wifi, quiet. VERY GOOD VALUE FOR PRICE. Very warm welcome, despite our flight being 2 hours late. Eddie is there to advise us and offer us some good deals. He sleeps at the apartment in the evening but remains very discreet, leaves for work early in the morning and anyway we come back late in the evening.. Small downside: the bed presented on the site is not ours but Eddie's, we slept on the bed next door... a little more aggressive for our vertebrae... but hey, it's bearable for 1 week. Thanks again Eddie Pauline and Benoit

More care should be taken with cleanliness, especially in the bathroom, the papers were in the basket for a long time during my visit, the same in the kitchen. The bathroom hand towel was always dirty. The bed is very uncomfortable and the space is very limited. We were worried that during the stay the heating did not work and THE OVEN OF THE STOVE WAS TURNED ON, that is very dangerous!! When the heating was on, it was very noisy. Chickie is a very nice person as is his girl, but it is not a very clean place.

We were made very welcome by Chikie and Manuela. They are exceptional hosts who knew how to put us at ease upon our arrival. We arrived very late in the evening (evening flight) and they were super accommodating and understanding in explaining to us the details of collecting the keys. In addition to being welcoming and cool, they made us feel at home by being available and responsive for the slightest question.  Chikie will be able to advise you on places to visit, he is a very pleasant host, smiling, and very open to discussion. The neighborhood is at. Ord of Harlem, a nice, lively and cosmopolitan neighborhood, its pleasant inhabitants, and with a little touch of Latino atmosphere in the evening, super cool. The metro is a 5-minute walk away and is close to most places to see (central park, Time Square, etc.). I advise you to have breakfast at IHOP 10 minutes away, and dinner one evening at “Fumo”, the restaurant on the corner of the building where Chikie lives. These are two addresses to really do. We loved our stay and we really recommend Chikie as a host, you won't regret it. A touch of humanity in a wonderful city. It was a real pleasure to have known you, Chikie and Manuela, don't change, you are hosts with enormous hearts. Your Frenchies Nisrine & Kevin.

this is a good spot for exploring brooklyn and manhattan in a great corner of bed-stuy. loved the neighborhood and the apartment was fine overall if a bit shabbier than the photos indicate. this was not a problem for me personally but might be for some. there was an issue with a lock repair that took much longer than necessary to fix, but the upstairs neighbors were very helpful which made it a little less stressful.

Coats was responsive and helpful, even providing wonderful suggestions of neighborhood restaurants and conveniences. We loved the neighborhood which was vibrant and fun. We felt very safe and it was always easy to grab a cab if we wanted one. There is a UPS place a block away, a 24 hour deli across the street, a grocery store and a drug store less than a block away. We easily walked to theaters, Bryant Park and Times Square and more. The apartment has fabulous panoramic views and is quiet, clean and restful. We would love to stay there again!

Everything about the experience was top notch and stress free. Communication with the owner was fast and all questions were succinctly answered. The quality of materials in the property were very nice, there was a balcony, and the master bath had a nice glass shower enclosure. Wifi was speedy. You have the option of watching three different TVs.  The views were of course amazing, and the location is fantastic. I would stay here again someday.

Absolutely wonderful hosts. Everyone in that household is so friendly, down to the children and cats! Amazingly adorable kids, which helps occupy time and act as a stress reliever. John, Steph, and their friend Alana had so many suggestions on what to do and are very knowledgeable about New York living. The area was great; very safe neighbourhood and super close to nightlife/NYC. Thank you again, I will definitely be back!!!

Stay at this place was overall very good! The place was very clean and beautiful. Jose was a a good host and asked us to contact him if we needed anything. The good thing about the location was that it was a few blocks away from the metro station. The only thing that we didn't like as much was the neighborhood, we were a little scared every time we walked from/to the metro, particularly because of the crackheads in the streets and not-well-lit streets.

The apartment is just like the photos, comfortable and spacious, the bathroom is large and everything works perfectly, the building is guarded 24 hours a day, José and the people in his business are very friendly, the area is a little far from the lower and at night it can seem dangerous, but I felt safe, and the price is half that of the apartments of those characteristics in the hippest areas of Manhattan, if you are not worried about being 38 minutes from, for example, Soho. I recommend the accommodation.

The apartment overall was great and as pictured. We were personally shocked to be solicited on the streets with ppl begging for money or yelling at us full on drugs, we had no experience with these situations and this happened in every part of NY we went to. So checking in with someone downstairs actually was super positive for us in feeling a lot safer in the apartment. thank you Jose!

very good location, next to line 6 which allows you to get around Manhattan very easily. The building is secure and the apartment is very good for a 1 week stay for 2 people. Jose was attentive to all the requests we had and we really appreciated being able to leave our luggage at the office on the last day of our stay so we could fully enjoy the day. This allowed us to visit New York freely before taking our return flight.

Please make sure to read that your part of the unit only has a half bathroom and you have to go upstairs in the hosts part of the unit to share a shower with the three people that live there, you can also hear everything that’s happening upstairs. The outside door to get into the laundry room has no doorknob but does have a lock. Sometimes though other residents would leave it open which is kinda of scary because your door to your part of the Airbnb unit is through that room (luckily it has a separate lock that you and the host can only access). The host is chill in person but his messages are just a tad too aggressive for my taste.

Wonderful communication! Excellent location. All necessities were included for stay. You will need to bring your own water, and food but fresh towels, shampoo, soap, and body wash are provided. Clean apartment and easy check in. I really enjoyed the driveway parking as that takes away a little stress dealing with street parking. Beds are firm and there’s a tv in each room.

Overall it’s a nice place to stay if you aren’t planning to spend much time at the rental.  BEWARE- There were no smoke detectors. We didn’t notice until the last night we were there. It’s a basement apartment so no smoke detectors can be very dangerous.

Thank you so much Andrea. You are so accommodating. We loved the space. It was the perfect set up for us. We love the attention to detail. It smelt great and had everything we needed. We appreciate you setting it up with the red and black color scheme for us. We are definitely going to be back!!! Loved it!!! Book this space for a easy stress free lovely stay.

There was multiple rats in and out of the apartment unit. When I ordered a cleaner to come, they found fresh rodent droppings, a rodent nest under the sink, and rodent droppings that had aged at least a few months (all in the kitchen and bedroom). I tried to work with Cesca to resolve this, and as much as she communicated with me, she did nothing to help my stay or provide any compensation or support.
