This incident escalates into a yelling match with my friend saying F it and leaving to find another place.  Disrespectful staff. After contacting the staff, they played dumb in DMs saying they didn't refuse access and asking when he came in. They refused refund even tho I was clear that I wasn't checking in after that incident. I would eat the cost if it was my fault but they were clearly in the wrong. I paid them $6200 for the specific service of "one apartment, 6 nights, 3 guests". They provided me none of those services while leaving a bad taste. If there was a miscommunication between the concierge, the staff and the management, then that's on them. It's not my responsibility to manage a broken communication stream at Beekman.   I hope this review was useful to some. May my loss be your win.

This space was nice and clean. The only thing is the door that leads to the top roof is always unlocked and made me feel a little unsafe. But other than that it is a great place to stay. I would definitely recommend
Its on an industrial state which made us feel quite unsafe. Its not near a subway. It’s okay for the money you pay for one quick night.

Victoria’s place is one of the best Airbnb’s we have stayed at in NYC. It’s styled beautifully, very clean and homey. The whole apartment is well stocked with kitchen utensils, nice linens in the bedrooms and towels and robes for the bathroom. Having previously lived in Brooklyn for 8 years Clinton Hill is one of our favorite neighborhoods. Everything you need is within a few mins walk, great restaurants, bakeries and transportation. Victoria is very warm, welcoming and easy to communicate with. We travel with two small children which can be stressful so staying in such a nice place with a great host really helped make our stay much easier and enjoyable. We will definitely be staying here again!
very  old Building  even you can't open the door the owner  just chats with you and if have kids or older people is very dangers Because of the irregular stairs

I had my one week stay with Lucas and Natasha. The room is nice and big as in the pictures. A fresh towel was prepared when I checked in. The toilet and shower are in the house for everyone, but it was always clean. Everything is a bit older, including the bathroom, but it's really good for the price. A perfect room for spending the whole day in Manhattan and coming home tired in the evening and sleeping. The location is perfect, it doesn't take long to get from the room to the subway, there are many small restaurants and fast food chains nearby. It takes about 20 minutes to get into Manhattan by subway. The neighborhood is very quiet and there are also many schools nearby. So you didn't feel unsafe when you came home at night. A walk in the area is also recommended. For someone who is just looking for somewhere to sleep without any special luxury, this is the place for you. For me it was perfect.

This place is somewhat convient for a short stay. I never met the host and stayed in a house with other strangers who all entered via self check-in. The bed was comfy, otherwise nothing too special to the room. I kindly asked the host to change the key pad code on my door as I noticed that the exact same code was used on the front door. I wanted to be sure since no hosts were present that former guests couldn’t entered as I stayed there. Former hosts have reassured me and reset the code in seconds. This host took a while to respond and denied the request. Needless to say - I felt very unsafe - like anyone could enter that house or my room throughout the night.

we did not have any gas and could not use the stove .we were given a hit plate. she said it was outside of her control because the utility company shut off gas .however the notice posted on the building was placed there early enough where she could have notified me so I could have found something else .I had elderly parents and young children. huge inconvenience. also the area surrounding the unit was not safe..my son and I went for a walk and saw someone shooting drugs on the street. I tried to make the best in of it. But it is not somewhere I would stay again.. Sorry.

Wasn't aware that this listing is more a hostel. There are about 6 rooms in total in the house and you share 2 bathrooms. This room is very minimal and looks a little creepy at night as the light is not bright. The downstairs bathroom's fixtures seem to be falling apart.   The whole place just has no personality. if you don't mind, you can def save a buck here. Location is great.

Lucas and Natasha were great hosts. The room looked bigger in person than it did in the photos, and for the price, it was an absolute steal. If you are looking for a nice, simple room to stay in for your trip to Astoria, this is a great option at a very affordable price.
Very good stay at Sammy's with excellent value for money!! The accommodation is a little out of the way but it remains very easy to access and safe. Go for it!

Our stay was ok. we were surprised that there was not an elevator in the building, so we had to lug up all of our luggage to the second floor. Constanza has a soap making business in her apartment, so the materials used were very strong smelling. The neighborhood was OK, we didn't feel unsafe, but ehhh. It was warm with only one window unit for the entire apt. It was an ok stay.

I guess you pay for what you get, but there should be some sort of bare minimum. This place was dirty. The bathroom especially made me uncomfortable with how unclean it was. The reservation was for 2 people, and we were given one towel. After I took a shower and dried off, I had the unpleasant surprise that the towel smelled like urine. I immediately messaged the host explaining that and asking for two new towels, and he said he’d bring them in the morning. I never heard anything else from him.   Also, the host said that we could do an early luggage drop off. We said 10:00 am but were given no instructions. When we showed up, no one was there. I messaged the host again and he first didn’t remember that I asked for luggage drop off, then he told us to wait 20 minutes for him to show up to let us drop our luggage off.   The host were so bad at communication and the place was dirty. Location was good though.

Patrick was very patient and kind with the check-in time, since we arrived in the early morning and he was waiting for us to welcome us and show us around, which I really appreciate. The apartment and the room need maintenance and remodeling. It is literally half a block from the subway, so it is easy to access public transportation that will take you anywhere in NY, consider almost 1 hour to Manhattan. The location of the apartment at first glance is dirty and seems dangerous, however we did not have any insecurity problems, if you are a light sleeper you will not be able to sleep because from the bed you can hear the subway every time it passes.

The location is not very good, there were cockroaches in the kitchen and we found some in the room. The sink was not clean. Update: we started getting bites all over our bodies so you assume there were bed bugs in the bed. I wish they wouldn't allow it to open, it's a danger to public health.

Lovely, spacious apartment (esp for NYC), and Patrick is super responsive and helpful. Super clean, wifi was great for working, and convenient location in Chinatown, though I will say that for solo female travellers it can can feel a little unsafe at night - not much more than average nyc but just to be aware. Would still recommend!

Even at 5:00PM check-in the apartment was not quite ready. After a long drive and the stress of finding a place to park and my wife waiting outside in the rain I was not in the mood for small talk. Your attitude was disappointing as well as insulting.   I have met several hosts and  they all  were welcoming and pleasant. You were the first one whose behavior motivated me to write  a review that was less than complimentary.

Had an amazing stay at Nina's place. The apartment had everything the two of us needed for a relaxing stay. Loved the neighbourhood, brownstone buildings, walkable distances to the subway as well as nearby drug/convenience stores, and great restaurants in the area too, from local coffee shops and bagels all the way up to fine dining. Comfortable king bed was perfect for a great sleep after a long day out. Loved staying in Brooklyn and at Nina's apartment specifically this time around in New York. 100% would stay here again for 2 people.

Boris's place is wonderful and he's a very generous host. Me and my 2 daughter's, ages 12 and 15, were very comfortable in the space and it's in a great location. It's also a great value, everything you'd want in a small apartment. The personal touches are very nice. Boris is topnotch. Rob

Helen’s place is in a very convenient location in Astoria - we could get to anywhere in Queens or Manhattan by walking 3 minutes to the subway station. There are plenty of restaurants around that are open late as well as grocery stores and pharmacies. The apt itself is spacious, clean and quiet. Helen was very prompt to reply to our messages and made our stay stress free.

the apartment is located 5 or 8 minutes from the metro. very convenient to get to Manhattan. we had no problems in the neighborhood.  the apartment is large and bright. air-conditioned. the beds are comfortable.  the toilet is in the bathroom. there is no access to the exterior but that doesn't matter. we could see raccoons through the window. it was funny. the building is small and therefore quiet. it's appreciable. I recommend! Léa was very responsive to messages. She allowed us to leave our suitcases longer in the accommodation because your flight was in the evening, which was very appreciated. THANKS

Our stay was good! The three bedrooms are great if you have multiple guests staying and want that extra layer of privacy. The apartment was clean, the building is safe, and the location is amazing - truly the highlight of this place. Quick walk to the B/D and F/M/J trains. Target and Trader Joe’s within walking distance. The only thing I would stress is that the apartment is on the 5th floor of a walk-up building. So, you must be able to climb that amount of stairs, but this is very common for NYC. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay here.

William is a super nice host and very accommodating with arrival and departure times.  The accommodation is close to the buses, a little less close to the metros (10-15min walk) but it's still good enough to reach the city center in 35-45min.  The accommodation is very basic, take it if you are looking for the cheapest possible with little comfort it will be sufficient. If you are afraid of cockroaches or various dirt it is not for you.  The little dog is cute.

It was a wonderful place to stay for my first solo trip. Traveling as a women, I was scared about just renting a room from a stranger, but Isamar made me feel right at home. It was nice and the perfect place to rest after a day of exploring NYC. Very walkable! Minutes away from coffee shops and cute local shops. Loved it! Would stay again :)

This is the most horrible experience I had since I use Airbnb since last 10 years. This host is super late response (next 24 hours) to u, after confirming the unit if any assistance he won’t entertain. Did not provide heater and we request for it he provide the broken heater.   When I check out, he accuse me break his window which I’m not until need to provide my personal photo. Luckily I have it. He is not honest and full of scam. I do not recommend anyone to stay here unless u are ready to be cheated

Location is the only positive.   Nowhere to sit except on brittle plastic chairs or on the beds with stacked pillows against the wall. Lacking basic amenities that should be available at any Airbnb.. coffee maker but no coffee, broken ice tray, no tissues, no extra towels or soaps, no salt, pepper, oils, anything in the kitchen space. The few amenities that were offered were all painfully cheap (bring your own toilet paper). There is a huge draft coming from the window, likely due to the ac not being properly mounted and sealed.   We were happy to pay our pet fee upon arrival however they wouldn't send the request via the Airbnb app.. cash or 3rd party app only. Very shady. Realized later we were overcharged for the pet fee and after sending a msg to the host for reimbursement, I received a reply (a day later) saying the listing was wrong. Still no reply or resolution.  I've lived in tiny NYC studios and this place is the worst use of space imaginable. Cheap everything, shady practices

Loved everything about this place!   Great location. Super cozy. Comfortable beds. Great water pressure in the shower. I would stay here again in a heartbeat!     My only (minor) issue was that leading up to our stay, we didn’t have the info regarding how to get into the apartment and which unit # until the morning of the day we were checking in so that was a bit stressful.  But aside from that, our host was was responsive and made sure we had everything we needed.   Alexi is a reliable host and I hope to stay here again on my next visit to NYC!  One of my favorite Airbnb rentals ever!

The bedroom has a bed, a table and some space, but overall crowded with furniture and things from the host. It’s ok for crashing a night or two, that’s it. Close to metro stations to get to downtown Manhattan in 25min. Neighbourhood and surroundings at night are really scary.

Easy communication with Javier, flexible arrival which is pleasant. Ideal location for visiting the city, metro 200m away. However, the accommodation remains small and very poorly maintained: sofa with stains, bathroom in a dirty state, dirty shower curtain, broken trash can, hair found in the beds, draft in the windows, the heaters make a loud noise which wakes us up, the electricity is rudimentary and even dangerous because some sockets come loose from the walls. To summarize, the apartment really needs renovation as everything is old and in poor condition, which is disappointing when you pay such a sum. I do not recommend unless the apartment is undergoing renovation.

Alberto is a great host - very helpful and quick at responding. The place was clean and had just enough space (typical for NYC).   The toilet needs maintenance because the chain kept falling off, causing it to run on and off. I would have liked to have some extra hand towels for the kitchen and extra trash bags for the garbage. It may have been available downstairs but they were closed when we needed things.   The location was pretty good, although was about 10-15 minutes from Times Square, not the 5 minutes that was advertised. The street corner we needed to walk past to enter the building was always surrounded by shady people that bothered everyone as they walked past. Someone needs to get them out of there. Once we entered the building, we did feel safe. The security guards were always present and friendly.   Overall, the place had a fair price and gave us what we needed! Alberto and staff do a nice job.

Considering that Manhattan itself is very expensive, this accommodation is one of the cheapest you will find. If your idea is just to sleep, the place meets the objective, there are hygiene details that would improve, for example, cleaning the room on the walls since there was one side with blood on the plaster, which was unpleasant.  There is a television that we couldn't turn on. The bathroom was perfect, the kitchen too and the dog is by far a sweetheart.

Alex was not the issue at all he was actually very sweet to us! To be honest the apartment was not very clean specifically our room. There was dust everywhere, the sheets seemed dirty, and there were other peoples belongings in the room such as other tenants clothing in the drawers of the room we were staying in, leaving no space for us to store out belongings. The  dog was cute but he shed A TON, there was hair everywhere and it got all over our belongings. The permanent tenant we shared the unit with for the weekend was very inconsiderate. He was very disrespectful during nighttime hours. He would come back extremely late during the night with friends and women. They would be so loud that we were not able to sleep. The second  night he came back around 3am with a woman. I woke up to the noise of them having sex in the room next to us, we could hear everything clearly so it was an extremely unpleasant and inappropriate experience. Our last night there he had a couple people come over very late at night and once again they were very loud, causing us to be unable to sleep. I actually got up to use the restroom and I could see that he was aware of the noise he was making because we made eye contact and did not acknowledge the noise level. He also did not have the consideration to clean up after himself and his guests, as the toilet was unflushed, filled with pee. His conduct and the conduct of his guests, who may not even have been informed we were staying at this apartment, made the experience of staying there awful. Otherwise, the location was excellent and made for a good base to jump from. Easy walking distance to subway and bus lines. Tons of restaurants, bars, bakeries, clubs and clothing stores just a block away.

I booked this for a business listing and made it very clear who would be checking in. This was ignored so there was a stressful expierence for my boss after a transatlantic flight. Not good! Please sort

I had a great stay at Jemg's hostel! She accepted my accommodation request at the last minute and I was surprised by the speed of her responses. The accommodation was clean in a quiet area where I didn't feel in danger. Jemg made it easy to get to the accommodation and key collection can be done even late at night. Plus, I met the girls in my room and was able to have a good time with her. I thank Jemg for his kindness and for allowing me to visit New York in complete serenity!

The location was great and the host was nice although it sometimes took him some time to respond. The neighbor is really weird and even scared us a few times. The room is clean and everything you need is there. We really enjoyed our stay here

Location is perfect, really close to subway station, markets, Madison Square Garden, Empire State Building or Chelsea market. The room itself was also very cozy and well equipped - air conditioning included.  Big downsides are common areas, hall, shower, toilet of the building. These are were neglected and kinda dirty. There was very unpleasant smell across the whole building. Also, wifi was struggling at the last day.

It's not bad but the building is not the best on the street either but very well placed for a short stay The room is good for two maxi A bit basic but clean We can't open the window to get some ventilation it's a bit lacking after 6 days Our next door neighbor was super weird and not very clean it's a bit scary for girls arriving alone

I really liked the room. It was comfortable and clean.  The bathroom was okay. Although i would have liked to know beforehand that you have to share the bathroom. Overall good experience. The only thing i did not like was the person living next door. He would always leave his door open and one morning he started screaming something about drugs which really creeped me out. Nevertheless, nothing bad happened.

There was a crazy man in the room next to man making demonic sounds all night, stomping and thumping. I could hear it in my room for hours. The shower and toilet are shared with 5 other units on the same floor (so it could be shared with well over 5 people if there is more than 1 person per unit). I felt very unsafe as a solo female traveler having to share the toilet and shower with a creepy guy next door high on drugs. Koichi was understanding and refunded the entire stay.

Anna was nice to accomodate us quickly. The stay looked fine at the beginning until we realized that it was not yet cleaned with trash left and no clean towels were left for us even though she insisted that we should not use the ones in the cabinet. We unfortunately didn't find neither kitchen nor bathroom amenities to help ourselves which does not really match the price of the night. The next morning all the appartment was submerged by construction/gardening noise and loud music and bass. Since it wasn't enough, we were shocked to be woken up by glass workers almost breaking the door's locker chain bringing two big plexiglass panels and asking to see the shower located in the room where our friends were sleeping. They were unpleasant and in hurry we didn't even had a chance to take a morning shower we just urged to pack and leave quickly.

The apartment is very nice and clean, it looks just like the photos! Esra and her husband are very attentive, very kind, and are great at communication. We were only staying for one day to attend an event and they helped make the entire process stress-free. The park across the street is a great place to have some lunch and there are a lot of great shops and places to eat near by! We look forward to returning!

Mishelly’s home is better than what’s listed! The location really can’t be beat, being a short five or so minute walk from the Halsey L-train station. If you need the M, its just a 15ish minute walk up Seneca. Theres lots of great restaurants and bars near by, plenty of places to get your morning coffee and NYC bagel! There’s also several bodegas within a block or two. Off Norman there’s even a grocery store with a Walgreens right next to it. The neighborhood seems to have a lot of families and the place is near a school, and overall it feels incredibly safe even late into the night. The street is covered by a beautiful canopy of trees! Mishelly does a wonderful job at making you feel right at home and I felt very safe my entire stay. She kept the common spaces very clean over my month long stay. I could tell the bathroom in particular was frequently cleaned and stocked with toilet paper. You are given your own washcloth and towel, and if you stay long enough Mishelly will  get you a fresh pair! If you need to do laundry during your stay, there’s a laundromat literally a minute away. The bed was very comfy!! AC works like a charm. There’s even an Alexa in the room that can turn on overhead lighting, which you can change the color of! So cool!!  The vanity was also a massive bonus for doing makeup and getting ready, but it also can double as a great desk. The window faces another building which wasn’t the biggest deal because I was out and about as much as I could be, but that would be my only complaint and thats saying A LOT. When it comes down to it this stay easily beat out two other stays I had in Ridgewood. In fact this is my second time staying here!! This is definitely a stay you don’t need to stress about booking.

The flat is really lovely, well equipped, and in a great location. Marina was a perfect host - great communication, flexible and understanding, and super helpful suggesting places to check out. She made the whole process seamless and stress-free. Would love to stay here again in the future and highly recommend it for anyone thinking of booking.

This is the best airbnb I’ve stayed in. Everything that you see in the pictures is what you would expect to find when you get there the first day. Justa was a wonderful host and she was always a message away from answering any question or helping us get anything we needed. Your hotel/place can either make or break your trip. I can’t stress enough how much of a good experience this was. This was my First time in New York and when I return I will definitely rent this place again. 10/10

Amazing location. Close to everything  and never felt unsafe. The apartment is a basement apartment so there was absolutely no light during the day which was pretty bad for my jet lag. Bed was very stiff and the walls were very, very thin. Could hear the apartment across the hall very clearly, and they would talk and watch TV until 2am.

John and Annie are wonderful hosts because they always responded to the messages with details in a short time. John also greeted us when we arrived out front. He is kind and humorous, which reduced the stress of finding the building and the keys to the house. The house is clean and tidy, just like the pictures. The location is perfect because you can walk to Time Square and broadway to watch the shows. There are also many great restaurants around his place, which can save lots of time and energy to find good food anytime. This place is also private and quiet. Highly recommend anyone who wants to explore NYC!
Great place, super chill, great internet. The price is a steal!

Airbnb is perfect and clean. The location  was kinda ok- a little unsafe. I just didn’t feel safe not being able to lock my personal room door at night . I wish i knew this-being a women i’d prefer to beable to lock my self in my room at night - and lock my stuff in my room. I had to hide my vaulbles in the car because i don’t know who these other guests are in the other room. other than that- it was a nice place to stay!

Tracie was extremely pleasant and easy to communicate with. The space is adorable and perfect for a few days stay. The neighborhood seemed a bit sketchy, especially by the metro stops, but I felt safe. I’d stay here again!

we were two ladies traveling to New York and we were very skeptical about the place and after lots of searching, we finally chose Nilufa's place.   It was a wonderful experience to stay at her place as the room is aesthetically furnished with homely feelings. The area is near airports and easily approachable by all local transport. Though few friends made us scared of the area, but nothing  bad happened to us. Host was very responsive and cooperative lady and she helped to get my Uber as I wasn't having my sim working. Best place to make your trip memorable with minimal budget. we were Muslims, so finding Halal food within walking distance and special arrangements for wash in washrooms was a treat in New York. Recommended
Nice apartment close to subway C (3 min walk). 30 min subway ride to Manhattan. Well equipped. Nice and cozy rooms with AC. Great communication with the host. Little scary neighborhood (night hours).
SCAMMER DO NOT BOOK EDWIN !

The location is maybe the best you can get in Manhattan. But between the door busting and being trapped in the apartment with no help. Then the cockroach and the check in experience wasn’t great and I was being bothered about when and how quick I could get there after I landed because the host was unavailable and was having someone meet us. Honestly from check in where there were no instructions on the garbage or other essential info really set us up to not have an enjoyable time. The fact that there was no way to lock the door had me extremely uncomfortable and felt unsafe. I basically didn’t sleep for a week. When I contacted the owner with problems I wasn’t given any real help. Honestly the place was in a fantastic spot even if not the location posted. Yes,  I arrived and then they switched the address. I am sad that this trip ended so poorly and that the owner didn’t even try to make things right. I hope Airbnb investigates and I get a refund.

It was so relieving to find this private apartment  in New York City. We enjoyed chilling out there watching TV. We walked to Central Park in 15 minutes, and then Times Square. The only unpleasant surprise was the  loud noise level in the middle of the night while we tried to sleep. But I guess that’s New York City.

So, This place was the most unsafe and baffling place I have ever had to stay.  so many issues, cleanness, safety, basic issues all wrong.  I had to message anthony once at the property, for him to give me the passwords as somehow it was not sent or in the listing as it normally is, there was no toilet paper at the property, I had  to message him again to provide me with the minimum and basic, like towels, dont use the towels there, he doesnt wash it after the guest leaves, he just keeps it there for the next guest when someone else finishes the towel, the toilet stank like a dead body was on the floor below it, iti was a truly horrible smell, the toilet and bath were all dirty, with black marks of not being cleaned for a while, the lock doors some days didnt work which meant I was locked out of the property and had to call airbnb, another day the owner or someone left all doors wide open, both the outside door and the d oor to the living room, anyone could have gone into the property and done some horrible stuff, the beds have massive metal things sticking out of it, which I got hurt in one of those, as I said, I felt unsafe one of the days, because anyone could have got in and done whatever, the  lock doesnt work, the sheets remain the same, someone will use it and the next person will use the same bed sheets and towels.   He charges a 60 dollar cleaning fee and another 30 and a bit totaling 100 dollars for a service he does not provide. Had to ask for wifi password and on the last day, a group of people came into the property somehow, I messaged the host, nothing was done, completely unsafe property.

We really enjoyed our stay here. Communication with the host was great, the self check-in process was super easy and convenient, the room was large enough and just perfect for two. Bathroom size and shower pressure were fantastic and the bed was sooo comfy! Location is incredible, can’t stress that enough. A couple blocks walk from Central Park and subway station is close as well. I’ll be looking at Shoreham again in the future. Thanks for helping make our NYC visit so great!

Cozy yes, but past the pictures and what you won't see is the scam of host this particular AirBnB is. My check in and check out went without incident. On the day I left however the host complained of a stained bed sheets that could have easily been washed and preyed on my willingness to comply to extort money out of me. Do you decide to make this place an experience, take pictures and, videos(optional) of everything. Good Luck and be safe

I actually did not stay the evening after giving it a lot of thought. I realize I may be a nervous traveler, but for anyone else that thinks of safety as a priority when staying at an Airbnb, I suggest you be mindful about the following:  There was a lack of egress in case of an emergency (fire, etc) and that was really unnerving being a basement space. There are so many dead-bolted doors and gates just to leave the house. Really low ceilings.  No window (except for a tiny tiny one that was covered on the outside by wires) and a barricaded/taped up exit door to the outside.  It just felt so incredibly unsafe in that regard.  Otherwise, adorable decor and convenient location.

Juana is such a sweetheart! Staying with her is like visiting a favorite aunt or grandmother.  Though the neighborhood is initially a little scary, I got over that feeling after the first day. The building itself is secure and just seemed like any other NYC apartment building.   The room had everything I needed, plus Juana included a microwave and mini fridge (very helpful!). Plus, Juana stocked the fridge with small bottled waters and supplied tea bags and cups. Plenty of towels and blankets, if needed, and I slept great on the bed.  The bathroom was clean and functioned fine and I rarely had to wait when I wanted to use it.  But the real feature of the place is Juana, herself, who tries very hard to make you feel welcome and at home. She seemed delighted to help with whatever I needed, usually just a bowl or utensil,  but when I had a special urgent request for some duct tape (I'm an actor and I needed a prop for a self-taped audition that suddenly popped up), she didn't hesitate and was happy to assist.

Juana is beautiful inside and out. It was a real pleasure to spend time at your house. He got to know me face to face on the first day and at the end of the day, he guided me to the subway station. He advised me where to go, where to eat, and asked if I was comfortable, if I was sleeping well, etc.  I don't worry about the location, I feel comfortable even though I often arrive late at night. There are always people outside and that's why I'm never afraid. The neighborhood reminds me of the neighborhood I was born in, there is always music in the streets and you can hear Spanish every day. The room/apartment is clean, calm, and Juana offers fruits and cold water for breakfast. A plus is that it is close to Harlem and Washington Heights. It is located on the corner of a bus stop. You can't get any better than that!   I can't wait for next time.  Juana is beautiful inside and out. It was a truly pleasure to spend time in her house. She arrived to greet me face to face on the first day and on the final day, she guided me to the subway station. She provided advice on where to go, to eat, and asked if I was comfortable, if I slept well, etc.   I wasn't worried about the location, I felt safe even though I arrived many times late at night. There are always people around so I never felt scared. The neighborhood reminds me of where I grew up, there is always music and Spanish being spoken. The room/apartment is clean and calm, and Juana offers fruits and cold water for breakfast. A plus is that it is close to Harlem and Washington Heights. It's on the corner of the bus stop - can't get better than that! I can't wait to return.

Wonderful host! Beautiful home, clean and spotless. Juana is very welcoming and the best I’ve encountered since using this site. Would not be afraid to recommend. My daughter and I will definitely return

Juana is a lovely host, she made us feel like we were at home. If we come back to NY, we will come back to her place, that's for sure! The neighborhood is nice and safe. The metro is easily accessible on foot and 10 minutes from Juana's place.  The bedroom, bathroom and kitchen are spotless!  Thanks to Juana for making us feel welcome!

Our one-week stay in NY went well in this apartment. There is nothing to say, in terms of the welcome or the cleanliness of the apartment.  However, you should expect a bad smell, whether at the entrance to the building or in the elevator... very unpleasant.

A kind soul who treats guests like friends and family. we were overwhelmed by his hospitality, in a good way. We were afraid of the summer heat in New York but all rooms had AC [3 total]. stable internet, I had no problem working from the apartment. the elevator smells funky, I advise wearing a mask to cover up the smell.  Daouda's place is cozy, I like his setup and the modern touch.  Very responsive and is willing to go above and beyond for his guests. other than the smell in the elevator, everything else deserves a 5 star. However, the elevator is probably maintained by the property management and is out of his control.   In conclusion: look no further and book this place now!

Where to start?  Thank you Daouda for your welcome and your generosity, we are so grateful.  Don’t hesitate if you need to stay in New York, Daouda will be the perfect host for you.  Don't be afraid of the location of your apartment. Harlem is a safe neighborhood and a stone's throw from the metro.  We were two girls, we never felt insecure.  The people are lovely and will be happy to help you if you need.  Daouda's accommodation is very clean and functional, you will feel at home and he says it himself "you are here like at home" We are leaving New York with a head full of memories and with the chance to have crossed your path. Thank you again Daouda for everything and look forward to seeing you soon Cécile & Laure

Hotel itself was fine, but there was no shortage of sketchy people staying here. Was followed by a fellow guest one night and it made myself and my friend feel unsafe to the point we didn’t want to leave the room again.

The code we were given didn’t work and the app crashed every time we tried to use the unlock feature. I had to call customer service and stand outside the room for 45 minutes before they unlocked it for us. Super stressful and really made us worry for our trip. Overall, once we were in, no problems and nothing special to report. Location was phenomenal and the room is great if you’re just looking for a place to sleep when in town.

Not super cool for not having a microwave and mini fridge in every room; my leftovers went bad because as a consumer, I always assume at least a mini fridge will be available. Super barebones and is a lot smaller in real life. The pictures were well taken. The $100 cleaning fee and a $34 service fee? Ridiculous. Just put that as the first price we see. Cleaning and service fees aren’t supposed to quite literally double the face cost of the listing. It’s rude and feels very leechy. Also, there wasn’t any face that I saw during my stay, which I thought was weird. My room was also unlocked when I first arrived which was creepy as fuck. I’m not super upset but I probably won’t stay here again. Great blackout curtains, though.

Pros: This apartment was in a very convenient location for those working or touring the Upper East Side and Midtown. The neighborhood is fun to be in and fairly peaceful for Manhattan. It had a decently stocked kitchen in terms of flatware, bowls, etc. with a toaster, coffee maker, air fryer, and blender. The living room had an adjustable wall-mounted smart TV with access to Netflix, Disney+, Amazon, etc. The sink and shower had decent water pressure, and checking in was easy with the key available in a lockbox and the apartment being a second floor walkup. The host also reimbursed us for additional cleaning and toiletry products that were needed throughout our stay.  Cons: If you look closely at the pictures, you can see that the apartment is very small. Each part of the apartment is big enough for one person to occupy, but it gets cramped with  more than one person. The kitchen is difficult to cook in as the only countertop space is located in a corner between the stove and sink, so not easy for those looking to eat at home. The bed (full size?) is in a pseudo-loft at a height from the floor, and initially was dangerous and uncomfortable to sleep in as part of the mattress was hanging over the edge, but the building attendant kindly brought a wooden board to support the edge. Those who roll often could potentially still roll off, though. It was a little difficult to load and unload the apartment (for a month's stay) because the building is on a busy corner and the stairs are sort of narrow. While the neighborhood itself isn't very loud, there is a pizza restaurant underneath that has live music throughout the day that reverberates through the apartment, and you can smell the pizza they're making. Lastly, the host is usually very quick to respond, but since she does not reside on site she relies on other cohosts who are less responsive to help address any problems you might have. As a result, it often takes time for problems to get resolved.

Definitely recommend for NY first timers or anyone staying longer than a week. Great location and pretty affordable 👍🏾. The environment is great during the day and night compared to other areas in the city, you don’t have to deal with too many drunk night walkers or anything sketchy.

This property is in Queens Elmhurst and conveniently close to LaGuardia airport (about 6  miles away) and the Metro station.  It is located in a multi-ethnic working-class neighborhood with plenty of American, Asian, Indian and Spanish restaurants, and a Foodtown supermarket nearby so you won't be suffering in a food desert.  It also felt safe walking around at 10pm: no panhandlers and no shady characters lurking in the shadows.  As to the rental facility, the room and the bathroom are almost exactly like in the posted pictures: clean and spacious enough.  Toilet paper, soap, shampoos, and towels are provided.  There is also an efficient and nearly silent wall-mounted ductless mini-split A/C system with remote to cool the room.  The room also has what looks like functional but untested floorboard heaters.  At night, the faint rumbling of the nearby Metro trains shouldn't disturb your sleep in the comfortable memory foam bed.  If the urge strikes, you can cook a good meal in the shared kitchen which is equipped with a gas range, a fridge, basic utensils and condiments, and enjoy it in the shared dining area.  Our hostess was very nice and responsive; she even cooked us some tasty noodle soup once.  It is hard to find fault with the facility and the service, as long as you aren't expecting luxury hotel accommodations.  We can't speak to the parking space availability since we were here for a quick jaunt to visit New York city and mostly stuck to a combination of trains, bus, and Uber rides.  All in all, this is highly recommended for the casual tourist or even for extended stays.

Very dirty house! Check-in takes place 5 hours after the appointment A hot August day in a neighborhood where there is not even a bar to wait. The host offers to return the first day's payment for the inconvenience. He pays me 41 dollars, even if my mental and physical health from the stress of 5 hours on the sidewalk is worth much more. I enter the house, a macabre stench assails me. I walk into my room, it's smelly and dirty, not ready. I help him make the bed and I notice that the mattress cover is full of stains. I ask him to change it but he replies that he doesn't have another one. The next day, I still feel a stench in the room. I move the bed and find dog droppings under the bed at the height of my pillow. At my call, the host sweeps away the excrement and makes no mention of washing the floor. I go to the bathroom first and find the first cockroach. So in the kitchen, it's full of cockroaches! For this reason I don't use the kitchen for the whole stay! The dog present in the house meanwhile continues to make his excrement around the house and several times I find poop in the bathroom on the carpet around the W.C. At my call, the host just removes the poop with a handkerchief and leaves the carpet dirty. For the rest, noisy phone calls at all hours and TV turned on at high volume even at night! Leaving home for the whole day made me resist for a week, I did not choose to leave because the airbnb proposal was too far away or in the dormitory. The result was leg dermatitis!

The location was the best part of this stay. When we arrived it took us an hour to check in. There was a mix up and apparently two reservations were assigned to the same room. So we had to wait and receive the code for the room next door. The shower head was stuck on the highest setting of vibration so showering was pretty unpleasant as water pressure was insanely strong and sprayed water everywhere, it was hard to keep the floor dry because of this. It would have been nice to have more than one towel per person as well. The bed was also pretty bad. My partner and I I woke up each day extremely stiff and in pain. I def need a massage or chiro visit after staying here.  Request for a 12pm check out instead of 11 was denied for cleaning reasons. Cleaning fee was 60% of the reservation price.  Not sure if that’s standard but I was surprised we essentially paid for an additional night without the additional night. Unfortunately I would not stay here again.

Decent place in a safe location. However, there is very limited communication with hosts. Inquiries take hours for a response. The door code didn’t work upon arrival and there was NO HOT WATER during the last day of the stay … all of which was handled without any urgency from the host or AirBnB. If you want a stress free, drama free stay, choose someplace else.

I had a wonderful stay at Shoreham. IN the heart of the city, blocks away from Central Park and steps away from all the 5th Avenue shopping, you cannot find a better location. Check in was super easy and stress free, polite staff and very clean rooms. Highly recommend it!  Only the internet could have been better.

It’s a little awkward staying in a room in a hotel, when you’re not a guest of the hotel. When things go wrong, the front desk can’t help you, although the text/chat from Jurny was pretty quick. They still rely on hotel staff to do all the things you ask for, but you have to ask them, and wait for them to ask the hotel. On the first day, the towel rack fell off, and onto my foot. They couldn’t fix it because a part was missing. We asked to rent a fridge, which was available through the hotel, but I had to get Jurny to ask the hotel, who had to bill me through the app, which took a day, and then I paid and then they brought the fridge. A couple days in, the batteries on the door lock kept saying “critically low”. They did this for two days despite my requests to fix it, and I was very afraid I wouldn’t be able to get into my room. Then, after the batteries were changed, I could no longer open my door from the Jurny app. Later, one of the maids from the hotel came by at like 8 am and we were still asleep, she said she needed to clean, and we told her she could clean if she wanted or come back, and she said “NOOO! It’s hotel policy, you have to leave when I clean!” And when my mom and I looked at each other in our pajamas, then looked back at her, we were like “ummm no, we aren’t leaving”. Honestly, I just got tired of having to call about things, so I just decided to deal with it.   I did like not having to check in or out in person. The shower has good pressure and got decently hot. There is not enough counter space, and a real lack of plugs. Like, the second side of the bed just doesn’t have anything on the whole wall to plug something in. We all have phones and watches that need charge everyday, so it just wasn’t practical. If you sleep next to someone wiggly, you are going to feel their every wiggle on this mattress. The AC works very very well.   There are a few good places to eat nearby, and a pub that’s open late about 30 seconds away. It’s an easy walk to a ton of places, and a great location. Several points of access to the subway too. Overall it was decent, but I’ll probably spring for a hotel next time

Hotel Shoreham is wonderful, impeccable daily cleaning, unbeatable location, the only problem is the communication through the Jurny application which does not have an immediate response, we had problems entering at the agreed time (not only us but several guests from other rooms) due to problems with the electronic locks, finally after 1.30 of waiting they solved the problem, but it was not possible to contact anyone by phone, but to wait for the resolution, the The uncertainty experienced at that moment was very stressful, not being able to know whether or not I could access the room.

Small room very well placed for visiting New York. A more than fair price!  However, there is no possibility of ventilating the room which can be unpleasant after several days and the cleanliness of the carpet on the floor leaves something to be desired. I still recommend it for a short stay.

Wonderful experience! It’s through the Jurny app and it was so easy. We just walked right in and we could open the door with my phone. We had a flight cancellation due to weather and had to miss one day of the trip and then extend it and they accommodated so easily. The location was great. It was only me and my daughter and My biggest worry was making sure we were in safe area and this was great. We never felt unsafe or “sketchy”. The room was great, the bathroom was huge! The service came everyday and cleaned and restocked with fresh towels. And the door men were so sweet!

This is a quaint and cute space for young travelers. If you are traveling alone, this is great. With more than one person though, I’d say the futon is not super comfortable to fit two people and that the bunk bed can be squeaky and a bit painful to climb up to (the ladder had skinny steps that would hurt your foot a bit when you put your full weight on it - for reference, I am 125 pounds). The rest of the private space is excellent and totally functional!   Please be aware of the shared toilet. You are 1/6 tenants on the floor and the building is old so the bathroom and shower are not super ideal but they work totally fine.   The area of this place is not the best, to be honest. The listing says Chelsea, but it is much closer to Hudson Yards and Penn Station. Although you can easily walk to nicer parts, the place itself is on a street with some homeless people and sketchy people at night. You may get asked for change or see some people who do not look well (passed out on the street in half their clothing). The 7/11 nearby (I’d go to get water) also has a lot of lurkers waiting by the door to ask you for something. You will certainly need to use your street smarts!

If you’re looking for a host with hospitality Koichi is not it. He was rude on both times I communicated with him, even shouted at me. Tried to take MY belongings from me, other guests where checking in at the time of him being nasty, so he’s not shy to be a terrible host in front of anyone. Shared bathrooms were disgusting, trash and mud on the floors each time I used it. He left me scared to be around him because of how he was talking to me. So women staying alone, I do not recommend.
This is a steal!! Super cozy and welcoming place. Love the fact that it has a private bathroom and all amenities to make you feel at home! Amazing place! Would definitely recommend to anyone!

This is a great location for our visit to NYC to see SNL. The room was comparable to other hotels I've stayed at in NYC at this price point — small, but that's to be expected in NYC. Bed and bathroom were clean, though might need new curtains as I did notice some weird stains. The TV in the room said it had no service, although it wasn't needed at all. Since it's in a hotel, the room did have regular room service which was nice. The only issue we had was that the lock code on the door changed sometime between us being there at 2am and returning at 4am the early morning of our check out date. Despite the email from the host saying the front desk wouldn't be able to help us, they did confirm with me that the host company can be reached 24/7 and sent an email to them about our issue. I went back up and called the number I was provided through Airbnb and was put on hold. During that hold, someone from the company texted me to ask what the issue was, when I told them the code had been changed on our door and we were not able to access our room, we heard the door unlock and quickly opened it. I heard via text a minute later that they were able to remotely unlock it. All that to say, not sure why our key code was changed in the middle of the night, but we were able to get back in fairly easily after our initial heart attack.

Do not stay at this AirBNB, I left after one night and did NOT get a refund, even though it was my birthday and Christmas and the place was terrible!!  The lock fell off the door and they accused me of breaking it.  This place is far from the subway, my friend who is a New Yorker got lost trying to find it.  They leave the keys outside the house under the mat, extremely unsafe in this neighborhood.  There are no restaurants other than being right in China Town.  They have no amenities, just one small towel.  There are no towels in the bathroom or kitchen.  There is one blanket on the bed and if you ask for more, there are none.  They tell you to lug out the heater in the closet and turn it on.  You will share a tiny bathroom and if anyone uses it before you, the entire floor is wet.  Do not stay at this AirBNB, even if the price is low.  They will take your money with no refund even if the stay is terrible.  I asked them nicely for a refund prior to this review and they said no.

Josh and Victoria’s place is just as cozy as advertised; a lovely comfy place to relax after hours of walking and sight seeing! The J train is very convenient as is the food market. We cooked several meals in the well equipped kitchen!   Josh and Victoria are excellent, responsive hosts and super easy to communicate with.   Two small negatives. The neighborhood definitely felt a little sketchier than we expected from previous reviews. I wouldn’t recommend this  apartment for a woman traveling alone. There were also not many restaurants in walking distance as we had hoped, but we did enjoy cooking so that was no big deal.   We’ve travelled the world and always stay in neighborhood AirBnbs and this one definitely stretched our comfort level regarding safety.   Overall, though, a positive experience once we were safely tucked into that cozy apartment each evening.

Justina's apartment was clean, comfortable and really spacious.  We really enjoyed our time there. Justina was very responsive and easy to communicate with.  At first I thought the area was a bit sketchy, but we stayed a week and never really felt unsafe. The neighbourhood seemed ok, and we had teenagers with us.

We had a really nice stay! The location was just right and the room was very comfortable and clean. The hotel employees were also very friendly. Communication between the host was quick, informative and helpful. Our stay was safe and stress free.

The shoreham and airbnb have severed ties so upon check in I had to rebook my hotel room through the shoreham hotel directly which was definitely an unexpected expense to say the least. Then once I attempted to contact them about the host they suddenly did not have nearly as fast of a response time as previous. I called their support number and the host tried to get me to cancel the airbnb myself which would make me have to pay for the first night! Thankfully I knew that sounded sketchy and called Airbnb support and they finally got me a refund after a few days. Such an unfortunate headache on what was supposed to be a carefree weekend.

The description was accurate, and the place itself was very clean. During the day, everything was fine, aside from the piles of trash that lined the streets (but I guess that can't be helped), but at night it was a bit sketchy. Overall, enjoyed my stay and liked that there were extra blankets and a space heater because it got pretty cold at night.

Room is ok and in a good location but unfortunately we had an unpleasant situation concerning the check-in. The address while using the “Get directions” option was not the correct one which forced us to walk more than an hour under heavy rain to find the good one. The host was not very reactive when we called her and no support was really provided (considering that we just landed in NY without a local sim and not familiar at all with the city). Hopefully it was just an unfortunate series of events.
Martin was a gracious host, communicated quickly, and and promptly addressed questions/concerns. The stay was comfortable and stress free, in a great location. Recommend this stay.

My friend and I really enjoyed staying in this master bedroom with an ensuite bathroom. The location was safe, didn’t feel unsafe even when coming home late at night. The area is residential, but there is a grocery store and restaurants, and the subway is right there with quick connections to Manhattan.  The bed was very comfortable and the apartment was quiet, but since there are other rooms in the apartment, we did hear people coming in late at night, while others woke up early and since the bedroom is right next to the kitchen, our sleep was interrupted when people microwaved food at 1am, and the kitchen/hallway is very echoey. Some people struggled to use the door code and we woke up to their struggles and beeping. We also talked to other guests and realized none of us were told how to lock the door once you’re inside, so sometimes the apartment door was unlocked. You can lock your room door, but maybe a good idea to tell guests to lock the door once they leave the apartment.  The bathroom has a tub/shower combo, lots of counter space and a mirror cabinet where you can store things. There was no hand soap in the bathroom or hand towels, so we got our own soap and used the bath towels provided, but especially during a pandemic it would’ve been nice to have soap and separate little towels. The kitchen also had no hand soap. The bathroom was however nice and clean, so convenient to have our own bathroom.  Karen was a good host, responded quickly and fulfilled our requests. We would definitely recommend staying here. No bed bugs, roaches or rats were seen and it was clean in the apartment, although there was some hair on our bedroom floor. This place is good for families too!

TAKE NOTICE 2/5 stars. Poor. It was the false advertising that was it for me.   Location was amazingly 1 minute away from Times Square and across the street from a parking garage, plus the on site staff was curteous. But other than that, everything else was disappointing and mediocre. Wouldn't stay again.   -1 point: Raised price. I had inquired about the "King bed overlooking Times Square/ No cleaning fee" for 1 night originally for $532 (this is in Sept 2022). A couple hours later, I went back to book only to find that the price had raised to $592 ($60 extra). But, it was my birthday and was willing to splurge to get "the best veiw to overlook the times square area", as described by them, so I went ahead and booked.   -1 point: Musty bedroom and bathroom. I was told while checking had been upgraded to a suit on the highest floor. I was really excited only to be severely unimpressed upon entering. Everything was dated and cheap, it wasnt giving the luxury as advertised on the pictures. In addition, I made the mistake of turning up the room temperature only for it to smell like the room was going to burn down. Like being locked in a room full of cigarette smokers. I was so scared, I turned it off immediately.   -1 point. NO VEIW OF TIMES SQUARE. I was willing to deal with the price increase and outdated room, but when I saw the "times square veiw", I had to call front desk. The veiw that I got was facing the H&M building, AWAY FROM TIMES SQUARE, this is the one thing I wanted. When I spoke to the receptionist, he claimed that what I booked was the "ball drop room", like I didn't read the title of "overlooking Times Square" in the listing title. I was so upset. I had saved and hoped for this for months, and I was ready to leave but it was late and I was tired, so I bit my tongue, said thank you and hung up the phone.   If you want a veiw of Times Square, this isn't it. Might as well get a cheap room in a box somewhere else if it's the location you really want. Highly disappointed and a great waste of money. My only regret was that I didnt heed the bad reviews and giving the place the benefit of the doubt.

Nice quiet area away from the city and best part it is right across the street you have an awesome view of the Brooklyn bridge and there is a Starbucks walking distance.  Room was a little small but everything was great. Rob at the front desk was great! Thanks again

Exceptional Host, Good spacious rooms, Good location, We happened to stay for 4 nights and the stay was made comfortable and good. Host is very professional and friendly and she makes sure to keep your stay very comfortable. She offer me their own parking spot so we don't stress out trying to find street parking which it will be nightmare for tourist. Rooms were clean. All basic necessities were provided. Highly recommended ! Thanks again!
this is scam

It was a nice apartment, everyone that worked there was very friendly.  It is close to the subway and if you like Latin food, it's the place to be.  Only 15 minutes from downtown on the train and really close to LaGuardia.   My only knocks- The mattress is rock hard and the neighborhood is not the best.  Taking the subway uptown was sometimes a little scary and the streets are a bit dirty and didn't seem very safe.   I never had any issues, but the subway and East Harlem did make me nervous.

Dusean saved my family & I weekend trip this past weekend! Due to our previous air bnb booking being a scam and we traveled all the way from Boston, Massachusetts, Dusean was able to answer our last minute request and have his location ready for us in less than 2 hours. The home was beautiful, the location was so convenient, & he even took time out of his day to check in with us personally. We truly appreciate all of his efforts that were put in. We’re looking forward to coming back to NY and booking with him again!

Pat's apartment is very comfortable and clean. It's not far from two subway stops, so it's very convenient for public transportation. However, the area wasn't great to walk through late at night. I never felt in danger, but also wouldn't be surprised. The air in the bedroom helps to cool own the room and apartment quickly. The bed and couch are both comfortable. (The pillows felt too flat, but turned out great for both my boyfriend and I.)

I stayed at Pet’s listing for about a week while I was taking classes at Columbia.   Overall the apartment itself is well appointed, nicely decorated, and most importantly incredibly clean. The Wi-Fi and TV also worked great. It was nice to have an smart TV to login to easily. Pet was kind enough to ensure the apartment was cool before I arrived by running the AC for a bit the day I was checking in given there was a heat wave going on. The apartment felt secure due to multiple keyed entries - you have to enter the building gate, then the side of the building has its own key, then the hallway section has its own locked door, and then the unit itself has a locked door. So once you are through all 4 doors you feel pretty safe.   The area itself is not the best - I ended up going to either Lenox or Frederick Douglas for food because these streets were more populated and had better restaurant options. Members in my program who live in NY would not let me walk home by myself given the location of Pet’s listing, so they either walked me home at night or I took a Lyft. When it rained homeless people would gather under the scaffolding from the park across the street to stay dry. I never had any safety issues during my stay.  While the apartment is nice and modern, the building itself is clearly in disrepair and in need of fixes. There was scaffolding up on the entire outside of the building and inside of the courtyard, so it seems they are working on this. It felt pretty standard though for a NY building.  The unit itself is on the corner of Adam Clayton and a two-lane street, so while you are not directly on Adam Clayton, it is quite loud at night. I came up with a system of running two rain sound apps on different devices - one close to the bedroom window and one close to the bed, wearing earplugs, and I purchased a sleep aid medication. This in combination with the AC noise made it possible to sleep. If I hadn’t had earplugs though I would have had a pretty rough time sleeping. If I was at the Airbnb and not immediately going to bed (which I mostly did) I would just wear noise cancelling headphones and listen to music to block out the noise.  Pet was very helpful in the beginning of my stay - making sure I had his friend’s number to let me in and as mentioned running the AC due to the heat wave. I did hear from Pet more than a typical Airbnb host. Most of it was fine, asking me to water his plants, providing trash instructions he forgot to tell me, reminding me to lower the curtains to keep the heat out, etc. Pet did ask me to lie to neighbors and tell them I was his friend if anyone talked to me in the building. This annoyed me - I get it I’m sure the building doesn’t allow short-term rentals, but to get this message after I checked in didn’t make me feel great about staying there.  Lastly, and maybe this is more normal and I’ve just never experienced it, but Pet or someone clearly lives in the Airbnb. The closets and dresser were full of clothes. I used the dining room table for my clothes. Again maybe this is normal and I just typically stay in Airbnbs that are exclusively setup for rental only.  I would not stay at this Airbnb listing again, and I will be in Harlem many more times throughout my program. Overall the unit was great, and it just comes down to there being better areas to stay in Harlem and I got a little bit of a weird vibe from Pet.

Great location, easy walking to coffee shops, restaurants, drug store, subway.  Lovely street.  Parking is tricky, but it's New York, so it is what it is.  Stairway to apartment is tall and narrow, typical for a brownstone, but this was made very clear in advance.  Fun and cute decor, comfortable bed.  Appreciated the plentiful plugs and USB ports in the bedroom.  Kitchen is very small, but usable enough - there's so many restaurants around, you won't really need it.  We arrived several hours before official check-in time, but Nina was nice enough to let us drop our luggage in the apartment's closet, so as to not leave it exposed in the car.  Fun visit to Brooklyn!

Takanori's place is so cute! I loved the decor, the little design touches, the bed linen, mirrors in the room - the lot! Lots of brightness in the room, which I suspect might get hot as a result in summer - but in January was perfect! Can see the Manhattan downtown skyline from the window (at an angle), there's a large wardrobe for storage and although the bed could be better I found the room a real delight to stay at. Bathroom is adequate, and my favourite here was the location - the coolest part of Bushwick, with graffiti / street art galleries, cute cafés, bars etc.  Would stay again in an instant next winter.

I traveled alone  The apartment is located in Brooklyn not too far of a walk from Subway. Host was extremely nice and tried to make the stay pleasant with a mini fridge and access to the kitchen and also some tea and tea kettle. The room was nice and clean, it was in the basement so it was a little cool which was perfect for the hot day I spent there. I was able to come and go as I pleased​. The bed was not a super soft bed but for me it was perfect. Slept well and felt comfortable. During the day the area felt safe, late night it was ok but felt it someone could feel unsafe. I did walk from Subway late night alone, made it ok, but just a heads up. Other than that, the place seemed good. The roommates were nice when I did meet them. I also received a text my first day out asking if I was ok and getting around and if there was ant problems. Super nice that he checked in on me.

Great place. Every clean and comfortable.  Pet is a excellent host and very accommodating.   The apartment was well secured, however, we felt unsafe at night in the neighborhood when walking from the subway to the apartment.

R.J is the best host I never had. He is very thoughtful, friendly and available. The apartment is wonderful, cozy and lovely. The place is nice, in front of a park and with the police station across the street. The G subway is at 5 min by walk. You can cross the park anytime even by night. I didn't feel unsafe there. I really really recommend R.J apartment

We appreciated that Marc was able to accommodate us on short notice.  He only had a couple days heads up.  The location is great.  I love that neighborhood.  There’s great food, drinks and art nearby.  Marc’s place didn’t have A/C.  NYC summers are pretty brutal and we had an incredibly hard time with the heat.  It was especially tough to sleep.  I think a window unit would be very helpful.  Also, the apartment is not as clean as I would’ve liked, especially the bathroom.  The edges had dark black and red mold and the shower curtain was also turning red-ish.  It was really unpleasant to try to get clean in this shower.  The fridge was dirty.  The couch was really worn and uncomfortable.  Check in was a breeze and Marc was really easy to get in touch with.  This location is awesome but the apartment could use improvement.

Spacious, comfortable, well-equipped and functional apartment. R.J. was very available during our stay, regularly asking us if everything was okay. He even held our luggage for us on our last day so we could enjoy our last day before our late flight. Very practical code system. A little noisy at night though, but that's probably due to the hustle and bustle of NY!

R,J's place was awesome. Extremely comfortable, newly renovated space, not too far from Manhattan. We were able to save some money on our trip using some of the nearby bodegas, and also really enjoyed our time relaxing in the apartment. Neighborhood was a bit sketchy to walk around at night in, but other than that, highly recommend this place.

The apartment has been recently renovated and everything is new.  R, J is a very responsive host and quick to help out in any way.  Close to subway, about 3 blocks, but time to get into Manhattan a bit long, about 45 - 60 minutes to midtown as a bus as well as the subway is needed (buses are close also).  The neighborhood, however, is not what I expected as that it is mostly a black population.  It did not, however, make me feel unsafe at all.  Overall, apartment a good value for New York City and a couple or small family.

Great little space, perfect for a night to stay if you are out in Brooklyn/Manhattan. My stay didn’t go as I had planned it to be, due to changes in my own schedule. So I didn’t get to experience the room as much as I wanted to. But I would recommend to anyone. My only concern was the neighborhood, a little bit sketchy.

Located conveniently in Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn. The subway is a half-mile walk. Convenient store on the corner! If you want to stay in Brooklyn, this place is a good value. Not bad value for the price. Walls are a bit thin but that's New York lol! RJ was super responsive, which was great. Good area, not unsafe- police station across the street.

In my experience of AirBnb, more often times than not, the pictures are much better than the actual room.  That was the case for this apartment. All in all, it was not the worst place to spend a night in Brooklyn. The location is not the best. Apparently, it’s kind of dangerous in Bed-Stuy. But this place is right next to the police station, so there’s some measure of safety.  Here are the cons of this place:  -The bedsheets and towel smelled pretty bad.  -There was a ton of short hair on the bed.. -The sink is obnoxiously small. Like, you can’t comfortably wash your hands without spilling a puddle on the floor. Maybe not a deal breaker for one person, but for four girls staying two nights, it got really annoying. We started using the bathroom sink for ease.  Despite that, the room was okay. If you don’t want to spend a ton of money and are okay with some amenities being uncomfortable, go for this room. I, on the other hand, would probably skip out on this place. RJ, the host, is quick to communicate. Check in was a breeze.

We loved our stay in the very roomy (even bigger than expected) very nice, very light Appartment with good beds.   We suspect it could become hot in summer as it is a topfloor appartment. But there is airco (not in small bedroom) so should be okay.  The neighbourhood was great as were Monica’s suggestions. Subway just steps from the house, straight to Union Square.  Just beware of the fact that it is a very lively neighbourhood: first two nights during weekend we had trouble sleeping (only frontrooms). Also, the curtains are very light, think of bringing an eyecover if you do not want to be waken up by the morning light.  Monica was very helpfull throughout, even receiving missed luggage from the airport for us.

Don’t go there if you want to sleep well  Bad host, uncomfortable place, dumpy/noisy area Monica is NOT a super host: we were forced in a delayed arrival : 7 PM vs 3 PM, advised less than 48h prior, even coming from overseas / lying about "safety emergency works" while it was painting of the main room ceiling: so we had to sleep in the room, with the smell, and headache! Cabinet used for painting tools so we could not put our stuff NO window blinds / No microwave / No TV / No bedside table Water flow is a joke Old windows + very loud area (restaurant just in front + planes!) = permanent noise One room has an AC unit from last century and nobody can sleep in there Listed in the beginning of “The 20 NYC Neighborhoods with Highest Violent Crime Rates”: indeed a desolated area Good points: Clean Good beds Right on subway But it I would have known the above, I would NEVER have choosen this place!

Rachel is very hospitable and helpful. We loved her place, it was updated, modern and very clean. The main bed is firm just the way we like it. We used the subway and it was an easy walk. The neighborhood is transitional but we never felt unsafe. The street is quiet... no problem with noise sleeping. It was a nice refuge to come to after busy sightseeing days!

Rachel is an adorable person who welcomes you into her lovely home with a warm smile and obvious kindness. What could be more pleasant after a long flight from Europe? Her house is very well appointed, very comfortable, everything is new and very clean. The pieces are much larger than in the photos. The apartment measures 100 m2 with two very beautiful, impeccably clean bathrooms. The little extra: contemplating the squirrels in the trees that border the house while opening your eyes at daybreak... happiness :-) The only downside would be the area served by the Ralph Avenue subway station, Brooklyn downtown, has unappealing nighttime security. For the rest, everything was more than perfect. Rachel is a great air bnb host and plays the game by welcoming you with fresh fruit, snacks and fresh, soft sheets. Thank you Rachel ☀️

This apartment blew us away! It was much bigger than we expected, and totally new/renovated.  Rachel was super responsive, and left helpful information on a laminated sheet.  This place is an absolute steal.

I had a very pleasant stay at Mariama's place. Location is great, especially if you want to escape all the stress of Manhattan but still to be close to all important sights. I strongly recommend this place and would love to come back if I happen to return to NYC. Mariama is very helpful and sweet.

Wow, such a bomb spot. There’s a lot of food places and it’s right next to the train. There’s a lot of picture worthy spots. The Airbnb was clean, just like the photos. The bed was so comfortable, just like the ones in those fancy hotels. The only cons I have was the fact that there was no microwave, no tv and the WiFi is sketchy. But I would definitely book there again.

This is a good spot if you want to explore Brooklyn or anything on the L line in Manhattan. Centrally located to a lot of popular restaurants. As other reviews said, the bars on the street can be a bit loud, but the back bedroom is relatively quiet. Lots of natural sunlight, and we enjoyed the amount of full length mirrors. Feels homey, has cool art, and has a lot of rooms - we were three people and had tons of space. The AC was strong which was good because it was 90 Degrees F on the first day we came. We did have a little bit of a fly issue in the bathroom, but they didn’t bite, so I suspect it could be just because it’s a New York humid summer and there are a few plants around.

First, I thought the location was sketchy but neighborhood and people are super nice! I and my boyfriend made a couple friends over there and hangout with them. The host was quick response, always care about us, and kind!!  Akir helped us a lot. I will definitely come back to the place!! The all restaurants and delies are so cheap and there are bars.  Thank you so much for having us! We had an amazing time with you guys! I highly recommend to stay with them!!

When you first arrive to Jeanette’s place it looks sketchy, but everyone in the neighborhood is super nice and helpful with questions. The apartment is close to the train which is only about 30 minutes to Manhattan which is where we spent most our time. It was a nice place to stay when we were out walking around all day and would come back to sleep.

Jeannette's place was located in a super convenient area, near everything you might need. This spot is super cozy and personal. She was very nice and quick to response to our questions/ suggestions. The place may seem a bit sketchy from the outside but it's completely safe and secure. Recommend this spot if you're in town from work or would like to explore uptown Manhattan. Thanks Jeanette!

This location is a steal! It offered a very great location with quick access to the city for reasonable fares using the subway. Plenty of markets and food options within walking distance. The host was very kind and would communicate with us to coordinate our arrival. I would highly recommend staying here if you are looking for somewhere to stay while wanting to visit New York City!

John was very kind upon our arrival. We have been in contact with him since the day before to let him know about our arrival time and communication has been very easy and fast. If you cannot reach John on WhatsApp, I recommend calling directly.  At first while we were arriving from the airport, my girlfriend was afraid of the area. But you really don't have to worry about anything at all. In this neighborhood all the people are friendly and calm. It is a different culture but believe me, you should not be afraid to go to Brooklyn, John has been very warm at all times and has explained to us that it is a very safe area. Also, if you go sightseeing you will be in Manhattan all the time and you will only go to the apartment very tired to sleep.  The closest subway is Nostrand AV and it has Lines A and C Uptown Express and local to go to Manhattan and arrive in approximately 22 minutes, it is really fast. To get to Times Square, you can take both Lines (A and C) and I recommend getting off at the Porth Authority stop.   The apartment was clean and had an amazing, giant bed.   Remember women: Don't be afraid!! You have to know how to live with cultures, and you will have a wonderful trip!   We have stayed 13 days and it has truly been wonderful.   As an additional note: Be careful not to leave the keys outside the apartment door. One day we did it by mistake when we arrived very tired and we got stuck, but John immediately helped us. Thanks John!    Private transportation to and from JFK Airport (Use the Lyft APP): To go from JFK airport to the apartment during rush hour it cost us 45 USD on Lyft, it is the same as Uber, but much cheaper and better. During off-peak hours, the Lyft to the airport has cost us 35 USD.   In the early morning one day we took a Lyft to go to JFK for our trip to Las Vegas and it charged us $29 at 4:50 AM, really cheap. Lyft accepts prepaid cards, in my case I recommend the Revolut card to travel.   The first day we went to Manhattan on Lyft and it cost us $38 to Times Square during off-peak hours.   Our experience has been incredible, and my girlfriend, after being scared the first day, had a perfect vacation!   Thank you very much John and Trilla! I hope one day to return to your apartment.   Thank you!

Really great place to stay in Crown Heights. Clean and spacious apartment that is well represented in the pictures. Fast internet, good water pressure, AC that worked perfectly, cable TV and a comfortable bed, kitchen utensils and cooking gear, and an in unit washer/dryer (huge bonus).
