We did not wind up staying the whole time, but went to stay with friends. Also, the windows (filthy) are on a fire escape with no real way to lock them, and no real way to open them. Top floor, no smoke detector in sight-some wires dangling from the wall where it may have been. The bathroom seemed to have been cleaned, but there were only two sad thin towels and the shower curtains smelled…unpleasant.  Check in was easy and Tom’s communication was cursory but fine.  All in all a very depressing and prideless place.

Was very disappointed in this stay. I arrived to Tom's for a single night stay as I was eloping nearby the next morning. I messaged Tom a few times in the days prior asking about a mirror. He never responded. I notified him we would be headed over shortly and also no response. When I arrived it was as if someone had just hopped out of bed and left. There was an unmade bed, wet towels on floor, urine in toilet, food in fridge and rose petals all over. I was with my 10 year old son to make matters worse. I sent photos to Tom letting him know that I think someone had been there. He responded instantly saying he was sorry and the cleaner must not have come. Which didn't make sense to me because why would the towels still be wet if someone checked out earlier that day. Anyway, he offered to a full refund and said I could change the sheets and towels. He then offered for his babysitter to come over and clean if we could leave for 45 minutes at 9pm at night. Someone came and switched sheets. It was still dirty but the sheets were clean and the floor towels and trash gone. To be honest I am surprised by all the positive reviews. Aside from this experience the apartment is very dark, dingy, and the hallway it shares has a fake wall at the end. What should feel quaint by the pictures actually feels creepy. The lamp knobs were broken and so lighting was an issue as well. Anyway, we stayed because we had no place else to go and a wedding at 10am and my 10 year old in tow. The next day I checked out and messaged Tom about the refund. He ignored that message until I looped in Air BNB and then only sent a refund for $100 saying his "cleaner" came and therefore the full refund was not possible. I went back and forth with him via email asking him to do the right thing which he did in the end. After the hassle I got my money back. But I wanted to be clear that communication, cleanliness, and condition of apartment as well as agreements with Tom were all not ideal. Would not recommend.

Positive: very good and comfortable bed. We slept very well. WiFi and television worked very well. Negative: The carpet on the steps was covered with plastic sheeting that wasn't attached everywhere. As a result, I slipped and fell while going down. Extremely dangerous.  The loose carpet on the common room carpet had bunched up at the corners. Great risk of tripping. Beds were only for 2 people. prepared even though there were 3 of us. But it was quickly remedied by the host. Electricity very dangerous. Sockets were not fixed to the wall, which meant that the fuses regularly blew out.  In our opinion it should be completely renovated. Ventilations and fans were completely dirty. Cockroaches spotted again and again. The host has sprinkled a white powder on the kitchen counter. When we asked, we were told it was not dangerous and against bugs. But a bitter aftertaste remained. Conclusion: Unfortunately, we didn't feel very comfortable and can't recommend the accommodation.

We arrived at Lee and Teri’s home mid-morning after a red-eye flight from San Francisco. We were in Brooklyn for our niece’s wedding. As it turned out, Lee and Teri’s place was two blocks from our niece’s apartment and a few blocks the other direction was the AirBnB my sisters and their families had rented. It was perfect for our family of 5 and easy walking to each other’s places. Lee met us with a friendly welcome and although our apartment wasn’t ready yet, he graciously offered to let us use their bathroom to freshen up. Storing our bags was no problem. Their was a secure separate entrance to the apartment. So we could easily come and go as needed. In addition, the property was very quiet. We loved the Ditmas neighborhood. Very diverse, very family oriented. There was a Co-Op market, a bagel shop, restaurants, wine shop, drug store, mini-mart, delis, and bodegas (small corner store) all within a few blocks walking distance. The Q train metro station was just a short walk and made it easy to commute into Manhattan for site seeing, etc. We found everyone to be friendly and welcoming. If you choose to stay at Lee and Teri’s place you will not be sorry. Our stay was nothing short of lovely and we would definitely stay at Lee and Teri’s apartment again if the opportunity arises. Just as a side note and this is definitely in the description, the apartment is on the third level which requires ascending many steep stairs to get to. Although my fitness level is somewhat compromised, I just took it slowly and it was no problem.

As folks have written before me, Lakshmee's place is very convenient to JFK. I booked the ensuite bedroom (double bed and private bathroom). Everything was extremely clean. There were a few aspects I might suggest changing. 1. The wording, in my opinion, does not make it clear that there the kitchen space and the living room have two single beds--it is a studio basically. I was scared to death by a young woman who was sleeping in one of the beds and jumped up when I turned on the light. I would have felt better knowing she was there so I could tread more quietly upon my entrance. 2. Street parking was not easy, probably due to the fact that it was a holiday weekend. Lakshmee did offer a parking place in her driveway for $10 more. It was 11 pm and there were very few street lights. It would have been nice to have the space offered. In the end, I did find a space around the corner. 3. When I came out of my room this morning, there were three teenagers in the living room. Again, not a problem but kind of weird. The other teenager whom I had scared the night before was not one of the morning teenagers. So, in sum, I think Lakshmee could communicate slightly more clearly who her guests will be living with when they stay and two, offer a parking place if needed by the guest. These are easily solvable issues.

A difficult review. Layla was a good communicator prior to our arrival and also helpful when we had a phone issue, loaning is an iPad. However the apartment was well below standard and the following areas need urgent attention- Bathroom- Shower tray was not clean, ingrained dirt not just superficial. Shower curtain greasy, grimy and hair on some rings which were rusted. Shower control fell off when used once. Grouting in the shower area was really dirty. No stopper in the washbasin. Kitchen/living area- Stove top rings were greasy and dirty. Oven was worse making this facility totally unsafe from a health prospective. TV aerial was an indoor box top one with foil attached. 2 stations which cut out every time a car went by. Bedroom- Needs a good clean and my wife woke up on the first day with lots of bites on her abdomen. We did raise these issues during the stay but as Layla had gone away (not ideal) on vacation we did not receive a response and could not discuss them face to face. I/we are regular Airbnb users and never had to write a negative review before, unfortunately on this occasion, the description of “clean and cosy” does not match the apartment.

This neighbourhood is extremely unsafe. The host is invasive, even though he doesn’t claim to live there, he comes anytime he wants. He is controlling and watches the cameras like it’s his full time job. He sent screenshots of me entering or leaving the house. Walked in on me using the bathroom  when I thought I was alone. Can’t drink in the house. Can’t have people over without permission, sometimes even after asking. Randomly blames you for “damages”. Has been extremely aggressive numerous times. You can’t cook in the house. This is def not good for long-term stay. I stayed here for a month, and it was very uncomfortable stay. Provides 4 hangers. No rod in the closet. The upside is that is newly renovated. Be prepared to sleep on a futon. If you just want a place to sleep at night, this place is good for you. Also- the place is 1 min away from the train station which is convenient! Pizza shop, bodega and Jamaican food right outside the house. Lastly, he’s selling the property, so expect random open houses. No privacy!
Not a clean hotel. Its only use is their shower. Very shady and #sketch.
The street is a little sketchy, but check-in is quick.  Also the elevator is really slow.

The hotel was a good, safe location that was relatively convenient to major locations. We never felt unsafe in or around the hotel. We would have loved to have an extra sheet between the comforter and bed to make us feel a bit more clean, but the front desk staff was kind and personable, and overall the stay was good!

Check in is very simple and you get a detailed breakdown of just about everything you need to know. Surprisingly enough i found parking twice in front of and near the residence so don't be too afraid to drive here! The place was very clean and spacious as expected. No one will bother you at all 🙂

Had a 24 hour delay at JFK. All hotels nearby are over 100 which I am willing to pay, but not just for overnight when I will head right back to the airport in the morning. This location allowed me to do that. Just a quick 13$ Lyft over, Lakshmee was very friendly and accommodating, her quick response and communication is what made my stressful situation calm. I got the door code fast, and was told to head on over. Thank you! Next time I’m stuck at JFK this is where I’ll be staying!!  Nice calming sounds of the highway, very comfy bed, soft sheets with a plush fluffy comforter. Comfy couch as well. Wi-Fi included. No tv but you can connect your devices to Wi-Fi and watch your shows. Not a dealbreaker at all. Room comes with body wash and shampoo, towels and washcloths. Other guests were very friendly and polite as well. Highly recommend this place. Remember to keep your shoes off! Thank you!

The place had an overall tidy appearance and nice decor as seen in the pictures and the host was very responsive. However there were roaches and centipedes crawling along the walls in the living room and bathroom and in the rooms.  We walked to a local store and bought roach spray and bleach and sprayed around the apartment in hopes that it would stop the roaches. The shower curtain liner was also very grimey and not clean but inside of the tub was clean.The price was affordable for a 3 bedroom and in a good location  and a nice neighborhood. We took pictures of the roaches and centipedes.We really wish we had known there was a roach infestation because it made the stay unpleasant.  When we returned home from vacation we didnt even bring suitcases inside our homes and went straight to the laundry mat in fear that the roaches from the air bnb could have traveled back in our suitcases. This part of the experience was very disappointing. We genuinely were excited about the trip and just want to make people aware of the pesticide issue as we wish a previous guest would have indicated in a review because for us this was a deal breaker. Some people may not mind if they are accustomed to roaches but this was very appalling and since it was the weekend of a huge festival it was impossible to find a reasonable last minute place to stay once we became aware of the roaches.

Overall, my friends and I did not enjoy our stay here, and we actually left a day early to instead stay at a friends place because we found this apartment very unpleasant.   First, the beds advertised to us a queen sized were actually only full sized. We were expecting queen sized beds, so this was a disappointment. Secondly, the apartment smelled overwhelmingly strong of artificial air freshener. There were multiple plug-in air fresheners and about 2 dozen artificially scented candles in the apartment. The smell was so unpleasant that when we arrived, we left the bathroom fan on to try to get rid of it. Airing out the apartment did help a little bit, but the strong smell never fully went away and ultimately made the apartment an unpleasant place to be. Third, the internet connection was unreliable and we could not use it to stream videos on our phones or the TVs in the apartment. And a final point - the lighting in the apartment is not very good, and the shower has an opaque black-out curtain that makes it very dark in the shower and difficult to see.   Some positives: the location of the apartment is conveniently located to nearby subway stations (8 min walk to F and ACE lines). The apartment also felt very safe and was generally quiet at night. Alfredo was communicative before and during the trip, as well as pleasant/friendly in our text conversations.

Quiet area, metro nearby. We felt at home, nothing was missing!! Alfredo and Noel are very responsive and pleasant. Our return flight was canceled and they immediately agreed to an extra night and took care of all the arrangements. Top stay!! Thanks again

This place looks great upon first glance. The layout is exactly as it appears in the photos. However, buyer beware. The dishwasher was NOT installed and nearly crushed my foot when I attempted to load dirty dishes. It was merely slid into place with no anchoring at all which is extremely unsafe, and not as advertised. The windows were not insulated at all and we were cold most of the evening. There was residual dust along the base of all the furniture. There was barely any bath tissue, the blankets did not smell clean, half the beds were missing flat sheets, and the mattresses were very uncomfortable. We asked if there were pots and pans available for   cooking in advance of arriving and were told yes; we found literally one pot and one pan. There was no first aid kit. The smoke/carbon monoxide detectors were still wrapped in bright red factory/installation plastic so could not possibly be functional. We had obtained permission from our host to have six guests, the Airbnb advertises it can house six guests, however we were only provided with four sets of towels and washcloths. Upon arrival, we were greeted with the stench of hot grease as one of the unit’s doors were opened. The Airbnb host emerged from the unit, greeted us, and helped us open the door as it was stuck. She then scolded my friend who had arms laden with heavy luggage for leaving the main door open while he walked the three feet from our parked rental to the front door. “Please keep the door closed, this is still our home” she said to him as he blatantly struggled through the door and up the stairs to our death trap of an Airbnb (uninstalled dishwasher, drafty windows in winter,  and smoke detectors wrapped in bright red plastic). We were so appalled we nearly sought out a hotel. We really wanted to support a new Airbnb however this listing needs more time to get up to snuff. Beautiful facade, sparse amenities

When we arrived to stay at Nick and D.‘s place we were completely caught off guard when we saw that it was cancelled. We messaged the hosts hoping that it was just a mistake, however they contacted AirBnb about a week before our arrival to tell us that their roof would be repaired when we were supposed to be staying. Because they did not contact me personally a week before (which still would not have been ideal) they relied on Airbnb. And although our hosts tried to help us find a new place, Airbnb had blocked me from being able to find a home because this was my first experience using it and I didn’t have enough reviews. We had to use by friends moms account to just book a new place, and it was in a very unsafe area. Once again, Airbnb left us stranded because we then found out that there were people staying in the new place and we were not able to even get in until the next day. We ended up having to book the hotel for 2/3 of the price we had allocated for our entire hotel funds on only the first day. AirBnb did not help us in the slightest and is definitely at fault for not contacting us at all, however the hosts should have contacted me directly instead of relying on a third party to do so.

The location of David's place was fantastic for easy access to city sites and public transit. Check-in and communication were very smooth, which always reduces travel stress. I was traveling by myself, and the apartment provided a cozy, quiet place to recoup and relax after walking around all day.

The place was a steal. Everything was accessible with a nice stroll in the city. It’s a pretty quiet  and comfortable area. Also, the 4 flights of stairs are not a problem at all even with my bad left knee.  David’s check in was simple and easy. He made sure we were settled. He had left us with refreshments which was a nice touch. The place can get toasty but he will let you know how to cool it down. Overall, his place was perfect for a place for me and my friends for a quick stay in NYC.

In my honest opinion and this review is for people to understand what my experience was like at Sonya’s place. My hope is she will take this constructive criticism and use it to make others stay more enjoyable and A little  less stressful. First, if you’re looking for an entire place to yourself this is not it. Yes there is a separate entrance, but the owner controls your temperature( you are not in control), yes she asks that you let her know how you need your temperature adjusted, but during my stay I was asked if I wish sure I needed the A/C(option leave the windows open). The one day we did leave it open because the temperature cooled down ants were all over the window seal and crawling down the wall in the small bedroom. I was also asked if I could let her know when I would be gone for the day(I assume all these requests were for her to save money on her electric bill) so she can adjust the temperature. I felt very uncomfortable in letting her know that I needed the temperature adjusted and as a paying customer you shouldn’t have to feel that way. We talked about parking before our arrival and the way I understood it to be is, we would work parking out if there was no where to park. The very first night she left for the evening to go out. There was no other parking and the gate was open when we arrived after an evening out and we thought we seen her car parked across the street( big mistake for us thinking she left the parking open for us). Instead of her parking at the gate behind us, she called and woke me up at 2am to move our vehicle( we felt she could’ve park at the gate behind us and waited till daylight hours to communicate with us what she meant by “working out the parking situation.” Also, we had to deal with all the different smells coming from her apartment thru the vents where we stayed upstairs (not because we live in Colorado are we comfortable with the use and smell of cannabis). I was highly offended that someone doing this for a business would think this was okay to do while we were staying there. Lastly, if you’re looking for peace and quite count this place out. Sonya’s place is right in the flight path of arrivals and departures at jfk airport. It was loud and noisy all day and all throughout the night. On a good note Sonya’s place was very clean and looks just as the pictures are posted on the website.  Sincerely,  The customer
Expect all the rooms to be the way it was described. Do not be afraid to ask for what you might need such as soap, toilet paper.

Deon and Monique are wonderful hosts; super-fast communicators and attentive to all of our needs.  Their property is relatively new to Airbnb so there are a few amenities and details they are still working out - like stocking the kitchen with all the necessary tools, etc - but overall the unit is great.  Lots of room for our family of five to spread out and relax after a busy day in the city.  The location is a short five minute walk to the C train into Manhattan.  The neighbourhood is great with some tasty restaurants nearby.  It was very quiet and we always felt safe.  Monique went above-and-beyond to ensure my parents were able to check in late at night alone as my flight was cancelled and I wasn’t able to arrive until the following morning.  She waited up in the unit until they arrived and let me know they were safely inside as they did not have a phone that worked in the US and could not communicate with me.  I was so relieved to have this stressful situation so thoughtfully dealt with.  It’s not very often in life you meet people as lovely and kind as Deon and Monique!

Possibly, the location of the house is the best and there are good comments from other people who have stayed there. But, unfortunately, my experience with him was INTIMIDATION and not feeling safe.  If he plans to continue offering his accommodation like Airbnb, it must be clear and not hide anything in all the information he gives to his guests (clients). His hospitality was not pleasant and not at all friendly.  Before our arrival, the host had sent us a text message confirming that the room where we were going to sleep was the one next to the bathroom.  Because before that, he hadn't mentioned anything in which room we should sleep.   On the penultimate day of our stay, he knocked on the door early to tell us that we had to change rooms as soon as possible. We remained perplexed and a little confused and asked him for an explanation. When he became AGGRESSIVE, he was talking to us and INTIMIDING us, we felt in DANGER and our reaction was to immediately lock ourselves in the room. An hour later, when we didn't hear anyone in the house, we decided to leave the room and change to the one he told us to spend the last night. We didn't know what to do and where to go. We still stayed knowing that our return ticket was at 8 a.m. the day after the strong discussion. We couldn't sleep. We had a sleepless night, all we wanted was to leave the house as quickly as possible until we left around 6am.   From now on, I hope that the host will be clear in all the information that he will transmit to his other guests and to offer them a warm stay.

*Get Ready to Read*  So I stayed in this Airbnb for about 2 1/2 months or so, and here are some things I had gone through and would look out for in the event one is considering this Airbnb.   - Host does not have an issue yelling at guests and/or verbally coming off aggressive to prove a point. During my time there, he had made several ridiculous accusations and statements about me and other guests who had lived there.  - Restricted use of Oven, ice maker in the Freezer, and turned off Central Air in the home. There ARE AC units in the rooms, however, there’s a skylight in the hall area so as you can imagine the rest of the home felt like you were baking in an oven.  - The “bed” shown in the listing is not an actual mattress, rather it’s an AIR mattress. He informed me that he has his reasons why he has that instead of an actual bed, however, for the price presented you would hope for a real bed that would not deflate every other night. After expressing several times that there was an issue with the mattress, the issue was never fixed. They were “looked at” but never fixed. Don’t even think the other room is better, you’ll get a hard futon.  - I was informed upon arrival that he would provide new sheets and blankets every two weeks. He did provide new sheets after FOUR weeks and only after I asked more than once. Then I asked if he could wash my sheets and he wanted to charge me an EXTRA $20 when the local laundromat charges much less.  - False advertisement about the neighbourhood. This neighborhood is not for your average tourist. It’s in a tough neighborhood, and the average Joe may not be able to handle the environment. I’m personally use to the environment based on my background but others be wary. Many New Yorkers I met during my time there referred to it as “Probably the worst neighborhood in New York”. Granted, to each his own, however if several people are saying the same thing about the area I’d be a bit cautious.  - Provides VERY minimal things for guest.  - Has very particular rules for guests THAT WERE NOT INITIALLY OUTLINED IN THE LISTING. - There are cameras outside the property and inside of the stairwell of the property and he creepily watches the camera minute by minute and knows when we are home. He will take screenshots of you coming in and out in the event he wants to talk about something. Personally, I find that super creepy.  - Comes in home unannounced. Just creeps in on us without knocking. Unfortunately saw one of the other guests in an indecent state due to his inability to respect boundaries. Luckily, I was not that guest. - Lies when reporting to Airbnb about his guests. If he has an issue with you, he will fabricate things to Airbnb and you will look bad. I personally did not go through that misfortune, however, my roommate did.  - Lied to my roommate saying that I filed a complaint against her when in reality it was HE who had the issue with someone she had over for a few minutes. This of course could have caused tension between roommates and is not something I’d recommend for anyone. - Used offensive language during conversation with me saying he “Grew up with hood n*ggas” putting me in quite an uncomfortable position. Like, seriously? - Charging my roommate for a toilet situation for a value of $1,500 when he has no proof that she nor I did anything to his property. Putting me in an uncomfortable position when speaking to him as I am afraid that he will charge me for one false move. My roommate and I lived in fear. Literally.  - Told me that “the blacks in NY have not earned their blackness”. Also saying that black people in New York are not “True Blacks”, AGAIN, putting me in an uncomfortable position - Having open house events for the apartment and not informing guests every time that they will occur. Even when he did, it would be like maybe the hour before.  - Saying that I did not inform him of a guest I had arriving when in our Airbnb messages it CLEARLY states that I have messaged him about it.  - Then he claims that the guests that my roommate and I would bring over were “random people” compromising our integrity by assuming we are having relations with these guests when they are simply GUESTS (who we have known for years and who we have had confirmation that there would be no issue with from the other roommate).  - Overcharged for the location provided. All New Yorkers I spoke with about the Airbnb, what it looks like, what it offers, where it’s located and what it costs monthly, ALL agreed that it was overpriced and informed me that there are better options for a lower costs or equal cost with less restrictions.
If I could give Rob 10 stars I would. He was an amazing host, very hospitable, great communication, and a great place in an awesome Manhattan neighborhood. Highly recommend!

That was my second stay at Rob’s apartment and I’ll be returning for a third stay in November! Apartment is super clean and comfortable, location is perfect, host is quiet and friendly. Highly recommend!

Rob is an amazing host. Very kind and helpful and we had some good talks. Room is as the pictures and I enjoyed the art on the walls in the apartment. Apartment is 15 steps up and very close to subway and buses. The bed is super comfortable and the room is spacious for Manhattan standard. I will definetely come back 😊
Modupe and Snowball were the absolute best! I will miss them. She made having to be a "roommate" for the first time in my life less stressful.

The room was nice. The location is very far. Thankfully I drove my car but I wanted to leave it and take the subway. I would have been upset as the home is on the other side of Queens, very close to the border of Long Island which is less than a 10 minute drive. There is no mention of a dog anywhere in the listing. I didn't know there was a dog until I arrived. It was too late to cancel so I had to deal with itchy and watery eyes all weekend. I received a text on Friday from the host saying she left the key in the mailbox but when I arrived, no key. The host came home to let me in and said she told the last guest to leave the key but they didn't. I feel as the host that should have been her responsibility to make sure this was done. I am just glad I drove as it was cold and rainy on Friday. The bathroom was not the cleanest but there was another guest in the home so I suspect it was them. The room was nice but it was really cold Friday night. There is a heater but it didn't put out any heat. It wasn't a bad stay, just needed some improvements. I don't think I would stay again though. The host is a nice lady though.
The place is clean and a bit small than I expected from the pictures. That said , the price for the neighborhood ( food/ bars/ activities) is a steal. Would love to visit NY again. Super stoked!!

We had a fantastic stay. We were looking for a place that we could explore NYC from (and to rest at), and their apartment had a good location near several subway lines. The AC's great, we had full access to their kitchen, and could use some space in their fridge and freezer. Perfect!  We also had a fantastic time playing with their dog! Keep in mind that he's very energetic and persistent. If you're a dog person like us, that's amazing, but if you're afraid of or uncomfortable around dogs, you should consider looking elsewhere.  We'll certainly stay again if we happen to be in the area.

Thatcher is a lovely person and host, always personable, polite and quick to respond. I unfortunately had to cancel my reservation on very short notice due to some travel restrictions and he was incredibly accomodating during that stressful time. He had also agreed earlier on to buy an extra bed to accomodate us, which we really appreciated. I would definitely recommend Thatcher’s apartments, and hope to have the opportunity to stay in his beautiful home in the future.

If you’re a cool person with good vibes this is the ONLY Airbnb you should stay at. Soft is truly the best host we’ve ever had, it was like staying with a friend for a long time ago, not a host from Airbnb. I trust soft with my life and you will too. Pizza is the best dog you’ve ever met - I say that confidently as a lifelong dog owner myself, and Soft goes above and beyond to make sure Pizza doesn’t steal the show by offering advice on things to do and see, where to go, we really had the best experience in NYC and it’s all because of Soft and Pizza providing a safe environment that really felt like a safe home to go home to. If you’re looking for an easy place to connect to the city this is it- we never even had trouble getting to and from Randall’s island for gov ball.  We came back from a cancelled strokes concert and Pizza was there to cuddle with me and dry my tears. A hotel could NEVER! On top of that, location, It’s a really accessible place that comes with an amazing host with an amazing dog. It’s easy to get places and then you get to come home to the sweetest most well behaved Lil pup I’ve ever met. If you’re even thinking for a SECOND “should I book this?” I’m telling you, me Francesca, that yes, book with Soft and Pizza. You won’t be disappointed. You will be at home.

Our tour guide had told us that it was a dangerous area. Adrián explained to us that no, in addition to explaining perfectly how to get there. Everything was fabulous, the thing is that the sofa is not so comfortable but for Lisa Nuñez it is fine. The accommodation is well worth it. Thanks Dona

Beds are comfortable and the place is clean enough. The walls are thin so you might hear a bit noise coming from upstairs depending on whether the ones there are moving around a lot. It was also scary to see a spider and a fly at this place.

Xavier's place was a great last minute stay. The neighborhood is going through it's phases it seems a little sketchy but this is Bushwick. What drove me a little nuts was the fact there was a bar close by and you could hear the music and the conversation from the apartment. People out and a little loud possibly due to the bar close by. Welcome to BK. Be ready for a little scavenger hunt when it comes to the keys but at least it's a option. Not  many late night host offer. If your looking for a quick place in Bushwick and want to be in the middle of this neighborhood then i would recommend Xavier's place. The apartment is pretty new but in an older building. Again looks a little  intimidating But once inside the apartment has hardwood floors newer kitchen and spacious room to lay in. Thank Xavier for opening your doors

Great place except for check-in and check-out. Uses this weird key system which means you have to leave your luggage unprotected in the street while you go and get the keys from a supermarket, which is a huge risk of it getting stolen . Do not stay here if you have a lot of luggage.

Great apartment, the room is just like the photo, I was a little scared because at the last minute my husband didn't travel, alone in a shared apartment scared me, but I felt very comfortable, nothing to talk about, the apartment has everything and with the cold it was warm and comfortable. The only thing that was a problem for me was getting around since I arrived at night and walking from the subway to the apartment was quite lonely on the streets, but other than that, great.

I had a wonderful time at Max's amazing apartment! The room was extremely cozy and has everything you could possibly need! The apartment is in a great location- close to everything you could need in Harlem. Max is an excellent host and a great communicator and his home is beautifully decorated! Also want to say, that Max was great and responded immediately when Airbnb arranged for me to be re-housed after an unfortunate incident with a racist Airbnb host. Max responded immediately and accepted the booking without delay- thus alleviating a great deal of stress. I'm so grateful. Would highly recommending booking with Max!

Definitely a great place!  Apartment in general was so nice and extra clean!  Room was big, and just as described! It was perfect for me and my daughter.   Max explained everything as soon as we got there and was very clear.   I just wish the area around it was better. We had to walk several blocks to and from the subway. It was dark, and a bit scary at night.   Other than that, everything was perfect.   PS Subway line 3 was closer than 1 and A and got us to Times Square faster.

Room was beautiful and well-thought out! Bathroom was great; I was worried about sharing a bathroom, but with 2 other airbnbers in residence at my stay time, I only had an interaction once! Only thing that was concerning for me about this place was location/outside. I knew I was going to be staying in Harlem,  but I had a couple of shady interactions that will now lead me to never stay in Harlem again. As a young woman going solo, I understand the dangers, especially in NYC; however, I have never been as harassed as I have in Harlem. Made me really scared to come back to or leave the apartment sometimes. Outside exterior of this place is well….fine, but there were bugs flying all over the place. I get that’s something Max can’t help. Just something to be aware.

property doesn’t have a tv as the advertisement states, when I contacted the host she said that she would provide a projector which took a whole day for her to give to me when she lived right downstairs.. then I had two female friends & Gma of 84yrs old over and we were playing picture people and her husband came knocking like a crazy man scaring my daughter to the point that she use the bathroom on her self.. They were very inappropriate and threaten to call the police on me because we have music on which was not loud at all. Then her dog always barked loudly and had her child up around 8-9am making all types of noise waking me and my kids up.. home was ok location was ok

If your happy to stay in Harlem which might be a bit scary and off putting to some , Miltons place is fantastic. We had no trouble from anyone at all and the apartment was perfect . Ten minutes walk to subway and then about ten fifteen minutes to Times Square. Apartment was spotless with everything we needed and Milton was the perfect host . As I said of your happy to stay in Harlem I would well recommend.

This Airbnb is probably the best value you can get in NYC. Kyoko was a very nice host and the apartment had a nice atmosphere in general. There's a subway and buses close by and it was very easy to commute around Manhattan/Brooklyn (probably more, but those are the places I mostly hung out at). The area itself feels safe enough, I came home a few times during 1-4am and never felt unsafe. Don't really have any complaints, especially for the price.
Lakshmee is a real life angel sent from the heavens. Eye swear to y’all! She made me feel like she was a relative. It was kinda creepy how nice she was. Didn’t know people could be that great!

Jeannie is very kind. The AirBnB is a great place when you want to visit NYC for a weekend trip. You can easily take the bus or the ferry to go to downtown Manhattan. However, you should not be afraid of a dog when you would like to stay here.
Someone picked my rooms door lock while I was sleeping, felt unsafe, did not communicate to resolve.

Jason was perfect host, good communication . Place itself was as it was advertised. Metrostation is very close. Nr 2 and 5 takes to Manhattan fast ( in case there is no traffic jam) . As weather turned cold the days we stayed in Jasons place, from outdoor cold came. There was possible to turn on heater, that made loud noise, so we preffed to put on one more layer of cloth on. So everything was fine. There was enough room for 3 people and and all luggage. For us the surrounding street life was a bit scary but it didn't seem dangerous as we were keeping inside at nighttime. I definitely suggest this place as it is totally relevant to the value.

My boyfriend and I loved Jason's place. He communicated so well and answered any questions we had. I went for work and just to have a new space to get things done. We usually stay in the city but it was really nice to stay in a neighborhood and not have to worry about parking in an expensive garage! At first the neighborhood can seem sketchy, but everyone really minded their own business. The only time we struggled to find parking was at night, but even then we weren't too far from the apartment. There was soooo many food places around and scenery that we never really see in the city. I highly recommend this place if you don't feel like dealing with the city. The bed was super comfortable and we loved the smart tv..The only downside was that it was very hot, even with the air conditioner and fan on. I figured it was because we were in a basement level, but Jason allowed us to keep the door open when we were inside the apartment to get some air. I would recommend dressing cool.

We booked this place more than 6 months in advance, and this Host canceled our reservation on the check in day without explanation. We came from Seattle after a long flight on Christmas Eve and we realized the host canceled our reservation, we arrived in New York with 15 degrees outside and we had to find a place to stay on Christmas which meant more money than we budgeted and all the stress of being in New York on a freezing Christmas night without place to stay. She never called or text us.  This Host offered an apology the day after at 5 pm. We don’t recommend this Host due to she is an irresponsible person.  She could have at least sent us a notification no matter what happened. Then to send us a message a day later, her sincerity is gone at this point.
enjoyed the room alot, close to the metro line. Neighborhood was a little sketchy, but had no issue's. Recommend if your on a budget and want a quality place to stay.

If you are solely concerned with saving money, perhaps this site is a good fit. Otherwise, the location is dead square in a minority neighborhood. Well located apartment, 3 or 4 blocks from the subway that takes you anywhere in NY. A store a few steps away that is always open and has all the basics. It is also a quiet place to sleep and without complications or fear to arrive at night. Communication with administrators is very fast and cordial. For very hot months, like August, you need a little more air conditioning since it only has it in the bedrooms, you can sleep very well but not stay in the living room. You also need some blackout curtains in the rooms so you don't wake up with the sun. In any case, it is a very good price/quality equation. As a plus, we asked to leave our suitcases at the house until 2 pm and we were able to do it without a problem, thank you ☺️.
This is a steal for the price, and great for a large group looking for a NYC stay. Bodega next door has everything, and great eats around!

This is what is described, neither more nor less ideal for a few hours before a trip or after a late flight. You have to add 20 dollars for Uber because there is no public transport nearby to go to the airport.

We loved the privacy of this apartment! The bed and pillows are insanely comfortable and the air conditioning units were a Godsend. Not only did they cool the apartment down, but the white noise made the perfect environment for snoozing. I was also glad for all the security. There are 3 locked doors/locks to get into the place which offset the neighborhood. During the day walking around is okay, but at night I would Uber/Lyft back. The train is about a 10-minute walk but the neighborhood was a little sketchy at night. Regarding Joseph & Teresa, FANTASTIC hosts. Our plane got in super early and they accommodated us for early check-in. They made things super easy and have appointed the apartment very well. It's really cute on the inside. All in all a good place to stay for your own space in NYC.

Very good location of the apartment, located 3 blocks from the direct subway to Manhattan. The neighborhood is quiet, no insecurity.  The arrival time is not flexible as indicated in the announcement, (or finally flexible for the host and not the visitors). Kalid warned us at the last minute that we could not have the room before 7 p.m. which is very late for a check-in. However, he let us access the common areas and finally arranged to vacate the room a little earlier.  The toilets are rather dirty.  The rooms are not soundproofed, because it is an old house.  But overall it’s a good plan when you want to visit Manhattan and only come back to sleep.

Renee was truly an amazing host. She went above and beyond in ever aspect, she made sure we had everything we need and more, gave great recommendations for food and activity spots and was great with communication! We also found parking super easy and stress free, the road itself has a lot of street parking and Renee was also kind enough to offer her driveway if we needed. Apartment itself was super clean and the TV already had Netflix connected which was super convenient. Overall we had an amazing stay and would definitely recommend!

Ana and her husband were fantastic hosts. My daughter and I came to Brooklyn to live like locals for a week, and we checked that box! The apartment was clean, cozy, and had many amenities that made it feel like a home away from home. The local grocery store is literally around the corner, making it easy to grab what we needed for the week.   Some notes: The closest subway stops are a good 13-15 minute walk away. We didn't use the local bus but probably should've explored that option. Be aware after dark. We decided it was best to Uber back if we knew we would be arriving back later at night. My daughter and I had a handful of scary experiences walking back from the station, which had nothing to due with Ana's incredible apartment.   We sincerely appreciate Ana opening up her home to us! It was so cool to stay in that gorgeous, lovingly renovated brownstone!

My girlfriends and I chose those Airbnb for our girls weekend in New York and it exceeded our every need. It’s a very spacious, clean, and cozy place, which worked so well for three people. We each were able to have our own bed and the bathroom situation was so easy for us because there is a main one upstairs and another bathroom with a toilet downstairs. The subway stations do require a little bit of walk to access them, but we never felt unsafe in the area and we enjoyed being able to explore Bedstuy whenever we would venture out to other places. Anytime we had a question or concern, Ana was very quick to respond and always very kind. If you’re looking for a place to stay with a few friends and plenty of room for everyone, I cannot recommend this Airbnb enough!

We stayed at the accommodation for a week and we would like to express our clear and honest opinion. First I would like to talk about the positive points, which the accommodation has. We really liked the comfort of the bed, very soft and comfortable. Plus we don't get cold and that's important, the heating works well. And finally the price, it is clear that it is also important and was the reason we selected that apartment. Now let's go with the negative. Basic areas such as the bed and bathroom are clean. The rest honestly aren't. The floor, countertops, windows... All of this really needs a thorough cleaning. Also the drawers, kitchen message storage area... this was quite messy. Another important point is the neighborhood. I can't say it's unsafe, but it's not quiet. The accommodation indicates that parties and smoking are prohibited, which I think is great because it is not the goal of our trip. When I reserve an accommodation that indicates this, I understand that those conditions are met in the area but that was not the case. We stayed on New Year's Eve and I'm not saying anything about that night, but there were two or three more that a neighbor went out to the patio with music at full volume and with a large speaker until 3am. In addition, cars pass by at full speed all night long, police cars... by this I mean that it is not quiet. But if you are a super deep sleeper this may not be a problem for you. For us it was. I repeat that it was not something occasional, we were there for a week and we only slept well one night.

Famous for being infamous, Harlem unfortunately continues to be in the collective imagination an dangerous ghetto but today Harlem is a vibrant, safe, hospitable, multi-ethnic neighborhood, full of shops and clubs and with a more glorious than infamous past. From our experience we can say that we have always felt safe walking around the streets of Harlem at any time of day or night.   To reach the apartment, if you arrive at JFK like us, we recommend to take the Airtrain to Howard Beach from there take train A to Manhattan and get off at the 125th. In 50 minutes with the cost of 8 $ you will be at home.  The apartment is located in West Harlem, in a quiet street near to nice restaurants, bars, markets and well served by public transport. The 125th subway station with  A-B-C-D lines is 2 blocks from the apartment (3 minutes walking) with the A and D express lines you’ll be inTimes Square in 10 minutes. If you like traveling by bus, the line 3 stops just in front of the apartment.  The apartment is well furnished, clean and tidy with a large well equipped kitchen.  The room is spacious and comfortable with a large closet, comfortable bed with cozy pillows and scented sheets. Wi-fi free and also Apple TV for those who have nothing better to do 😊. The large private bathroom is next to the room, you’ll find soft and fragrant towels of various sizes, shower soap and hairdryer.  The check-in was perfect. Stephen is such a friendly, kind and cheerful boy and we can say to have a new good friend in NYC. He has made us felt welcomed every moment and really enjoyed the conversations with him. Non-intrusive and respectful of our privacy.   We have not met Amy personally, she was out of New York during our stay, but by messages she has always been ready to answer, helpful and kind.  We really enjoyed our stay and we would definitely recommend this place. Thank you for the pleasant experience and best regards!!!  We wait for you in Italy 😉

Good and valuable place to stay. Earlene's cosy place helps you feel home. Yes, the surrounding neighborhood can get a bit rough sometimes - the entire time that we stayed in the house, there were a police car more or less 24/7 right in front of our house 192 Madison St. No complaints about that, since we all felt quite safe. The short stroll from or to the subway station (C line) via Nostrand Ave. has never left us feel somehow unsafe.  Just wave a smile or short greeting to someone when you feel like it. He will greet back and everything's gonna be fine.

Kimesha is a great host . She went above and beyond . Place is exactly like the pictures. Location is a little sketchy but she reassured us it was safe. Very spotless  and beautiful  place .Kitchen had snacks, water and some food which was nice . We were welcomed with champagne and chocolate because I told her we were in NYC celebrating our anniversary. She also provides a very detailed binder with subway and bus routes and local areas to check out. Only thing is transportation was kind of a hassle for us and we wish we would've just rented a car because of your not from NYC its confusing. Kimesha also provided us a free lyft ride to the local subway which was sweet . I would recommend it.

Definitely a steal and a must recommend. The place was cozy and Kimesha was very quick on her responses. She made me feel like family and I had a wonderful couples getaway for my girlfriends birthday. Thank you so much for being a wonderful host.

A cozy Place with an excellent host - very communicative, excellent service. For example, offering to install another air condition because of weather forecast (hot!) was super nice.   It’s a clean(!) apartment with a small backyard, which could need some helping hand in terms of gardening 👨‍🌾😉 The BedStuy neighborhood is definitely not 5th Avenue (luckily), but never felt unsafe or uncomfortable. Actually, people are pretty relaxed and friendly. The nearby football (aka soccer) playground is a nice spot on weekends when several different ethnicities playing tournaments.  Subway stations to Downtown Manhattan or Queens are a 10-15 minutes walk away - I personally preferred J-Train as it goes overground and crosses Manhattan Bridge providing some nice views.  There are some Delis around. Didn’t try out some nearby restaurants but there are also some fast food spots.   Thank you Vika & Joshua for the enjoying time!

Nice little apartment. We haven't met Joshua but he always responded very quickly and kindly to our messages and questions. Plus we arrived late and really appreciated finding something to eat in the fridge and cupboards.  On the other hand, we would have liked the apartment to be a little cleaner, closer to Manhattan because in fact it takes almost an hour to be in the center and less noisy (street with frequent sirens, people on the floor above who you can hear a lot, very noisy air conditioning so impossible at night). Without a car there isn't much in the area but we had no feeling of insecurity.
Elen was wonderful and so was her place . Everything we needed was right there . Easy check in made our stay non stressful . Loved the backyard courtyard area .

My boyfriend and I just spent a week at Dorina's.  It was our first time using Airbnb as well as visiting New York.  Dorina's place was exactly as shown in the photos.  It was clean, beautiful, spacious, and very comfortable.  She had provided toilet paper, soap, shampoo, eggs, milk, juice, coffee, cereal, house slippers, robes, blankets, etc.  It was a delightful surprise, and it definitely added a special touch.  I can see why she is a super host.  Dorina was very friendly and gave us our space, but was always readily available to answer any questions we had.  She responded promptly to all of my texts.  She gave suggestions on food, markets, and transportation.  Everything we needed to know was printed out in the room as well.  The area felt extremely safe and was quiet.  Metropolitan Ave. was about an 8 minute walk, and there was a CVS, 7-eleven, shops, and a really delicious pizza place called Carlos that we tried.  The bus stop was right on the same street where we were able to catch the Q-54 bus to the subway.  The subway ride was only about a 30-45 minute ride, depending on where you want to go in Manhattan.  It was not a problem for us since we enjoyed the subway ride.  Just be aware that if you stay out late, there may be delays on the subway.  One night it took us about 2 hours to get back to our room because our subway got delayed and we had to catch 3 different subways to get back.  However, it was part of the experience and it never felt unsafe when we stayed out late.  There are so many people around even when it's super late.  If you don't mind putting in a little work to get to Manhattan, then this is a perfect location for you.  Dorina's place was also a lot more affordable and bigger than most places in the city.  And we were able to explore Williamsburg as well since we were close by.  Dorina even allowed us a later checkout since our flight was later.  The whole experience was great, and we would love to stay here again.  Thank you, Dorina!

Dorina's place was not only exactly as advertised but even lovelier in person. Everything felt/looked brand new and was very clean and comfortable. Dorina was super kind and hospitable and accessible through text and phone if we needed anything or had questions. It was awesome to be able to return to her space after a long tiring day of exploring Manhattan. We slept very well in the comfy new king sized bed and enjoyed having the ability to watch some tv or eat takeout if we wished. The walk to the train station was very easy and never took us more than 8-10 min, though there was a bus option that was even closer that we didn't use. Even when coming back even as late as 2 am we never felt unsafe. Dorina's neighborhood is very clean, quiet, and well lit. I would recommend considering Uber or a cab though if you want to get somewhere quick, as there were delays at night that made things take longer and some construction that slowed things. We didn't mind a whole lot but could see how that would inconvenience some. All in all, at a normal time of day it took about 35-50 min to get where we wanted to go in Manhattan depending on which area we were traveling to. We would stay definitely stay here again if we come back to NYC in the future!

Jackie's place is very conveniently located- right in the bustling LES, close walking distance to other amazing parts of the city, and also the subway is super close for those times when you don't feel like walking or want to travel further. The room was very spacious for me as a solo traveler but I'd suspect it'd be pretty decent for two people as well. Jackie provided incredibly thorough and clear instructions for checking in so I had no issues at all. I met him just briefly in the beginning and he was very kind and non intrusive which I appreciated. I was visiting the city for the weekend so I just needed a place to take a warm shower and sleep comfortably at night and for that purpose it was perfect. Cute friendly cat was a bonus!

Our experience with Dorina was exceptional. It was beyond expectations. The place was clean, modern, and spacious yet cozy. We had no concern for our safety staying there, the outside is well-lit, gated, and there's a private entrance as well.   Transportation was made very easy as it is only a 10-minute walk to the subway station. There are plenty of shops like nail salons, restaurants, grocery stores, and drug stores within a 15-minute walk as well.  Her communication skills were excellent. Her replies were instantaneous, and she has answers to all of your questions.   Dorina was very welcoming, it really made us feel at home. It was actually very sad to leave the place on our last day. Highly, highly, highly recommend staying with Dorina! Definitely looking forward to book with her again on our next visit to NY.

Please read this review till the end with Pros and “CONS”. It took me 1 week to write this review, and be fair to Jackie and to the upcoming TRAVELERS. Pros: Friendly Jackie, Central located, checking in easy peasy.  Cons: Mice Droppings, Cockroaches smell, Steam heater’s noise at midnight (or morning around 03:00AM) like someone is hitting with a hammer on the piece of metal. Pillows were dark yellow to brown (after taking off the cover), luckily I brought my own pillows. Even towel had a yellow stain in the middle, my good I had my own. And all this for $90 per night. There was a hotel 2 blocks away for $105 per night including taxes. Kitchen: I was afraid to step in. I don’t understand how he has positive reviews.  Details: Jackie is very friendly, nice, and communicative. He did his best for the ambience of the apartment, i.e. designer look.  Location: Lower East Side, in the center of everything. I booked this accommodation because my business activities were 10-12 minutes walk from this place. I wanted to extend for 2 more months. But sleepless nights and all other cons prevented me from.  Room: Exactly as shown in pictures (room#1).  At the entrance of the building there was mice droppings all over the street (even by freezing temperatures 8•F / -13•C) and on the floor behind the fence toward the entrance of the building. Trash cans (not trash containers, but plastic buckets) were to blame for this and obviously mice. Mice were coming at night to eat out of those plastic trash buckets and left their droppings (shit) behind. My entry into the building looked like I was walking on the minefield. After entering the building’s door, there was a notice with legal articles and sections from building’s management that it is illegal to use this place for Airbnb guests, walking one flight up another notice from PEST CONTROL, once in a month (every first Saturday) there will be an exterminator coming for free. I was thinking would it get worse..?? 2nd floor entering into the apartment smell of cockroaches’ eggs. In the apartment I didn’t find any mouse or cockroach but that smell didn’t let me sleep until midnight, and then the SHOW began with the hardest metallic Techno(lol). The building is very old (pre war) old steam heaters are built in, at night when heaters were popping up, they were making a noise as someone is hitting a metallic bars with a metallic hammer (not a rubber hammer). I spent 6 sleepless nights there. I was sleeping in the daytime in the basement of my office…. horrible. Check out time was 11:00 AM, a very friendly cleaning lady showed up at 10:35 AM and informed me that she’s here to clean. Anyhow I made it to check out at sharp 11:07 AM while she was cleaning other area of the apartment.  I’ll definitely NOT book this accommodation again, no matter how friendly and communicative Jackie was. I’ll better walk 2 blocks to the hotel and pay $15 more per night, and have clean pillows and towels and no noise and no smell of anything. I ended up renting a room for next 2 months in a high-rise building on Wall St. with amenities i.e. Gym, Swimming Pool, Bar on 10th floor, Coffee & Bakery at the entrance, every 2nd floor Cinema Lounge with Cuddling Corners, Terrace with East River View on 23rd floor, Laundry room with Ping Pong, Billard, and Arcade, Banquet Hall and Grand Kitchen where you can cook for your friends with all the kitchen appliances. All this for $67 per night ! ! ! A LIGHT after DARKNESS.

Jackie’s place was perfect for solo travelers visiting NYC on a budget! It’s definitely tight quarters but if that doesn’t bother you you’ll be just fine. The area can look sketchy at certain points in the night but is perfectly safe, and nearby plenty of grocery stores and shops. You will share the common areas with others, but I never ran into Jackie or his other guest. Would stay again if I needed to!

Melissa was very easy to communicate with and responded promptly to messages. The exchange of keys was also very simple and stress free. The neighborhood was decent, with the C train only a block away. The building in which the listing is located is not the greatest in terms of appearance and upkeep.  The apartment itself was clean and well kept with plenty of room for guests to store personal items.  She had fresh towels ready for us on arrival, and the bed linens smelled freshly washed as well.  Our only complaint was that the bed was actually more of a futon than an actual bed and was a bit of a tight fit for my 6' 3" husband and myself. That being said the mattress itself was very comfortable and we were so exhausted that we slept fine despite that.  Overall this place was sufficient for what we needed it for - a place to crash for the night.  I wouldn't necessarily have wanted to stay there for any longer than that.

The room is great and private. Not in as good condition as the photos would indicate but still perfectly fine. There is no air con so I can see it getting a little uncomfortable if it were very warm outside, however Shae does provide a cooling fan. The area looks a little sketchy on first impression but it is honestly fine. My girlfriend and I walked through the streets at all sorts of hours with no problem. Its 8 mins from the J line and is quick to get in the city, which is what we did every day. Shae was a most helpful host who made sure we had everything we needed. Parking is a ball ache, as you have to move the car every few days for the sweepers, but it is like this EVERYWHERE in NY so nothing on Shae, just a warning.   Overall, you get what you pay for in terms of quality and definitely worth the money we saved from not staying in the city.

It was very unpleasant.   On my last night, when I arrived from Manhattan tired late at night, a night club was installed above my basement apartment, literally! I called her as soon as I saw the house full people (between 20 and 30) drinking and dancing over my ceiling and blocking the front door. One person came to me and aggressively asked who and why I was making the phone call in front of his party and  warned me to be cool. At 3:30AM She said she would ask the guest to lower the music and when I got more upset she said would prepare the room upstairs for me as if it would change a thing. Of course, it didn’t work. It was just too much to handle. I left her place at 4:00 AM without anywhere else to stay.   I strongly believe her attitude was unprofessional and unethical. Now I understand why she mentioned she was having problems with airbnb.  In the end, AIRBNB returned all my money because of her terrible service! It is worth mentioning that I tried talking to her twice trough the AIRBNB page but she  only responded once and refused to repair me for all the inconvenient. Hope this review can be of good help for future possible guests.

Would not currently recommend staying here to anyone else unless the host makes some changes.   We were not greeted in person. Felt unsafe. Host acted very bizarre in general. I paid for this unit for my mother. She was locked out at 10:00PM when returning to her room after dinner. I called the host to let her in. I was sent to voicemail but the door was unlocked in person. No follow up via phone.   This place isn’t worth more than $50/night. We paid $116 (including fees). Overall disappointed with the experience.   The unit is in a great location however. And the host made a real effort in making the space hospitable.

Thank you, Shae! The listing and regular communication were wonderful and helpful. I really appreciated being able to drop my luggage in advance in the hallway (so that I didn't have to lug it around all afternoon) and even check-in slightly earlier. Location is great. Plenty of hand sanitizer. Keurig coffee maker. Easy to use the code lock. The bed was super clean and comfortable. Pretty quiet. It was a great place to be out and about busy all day and lay your head at night. Short walk to public transit. Wonderful cafe/bar nearby just a couple minutes walk called Sunrise/Sunset.   However, there were a few cockroaches in and around the bathroom on the first day, but the man (sorry, I can't remember his name) took care of this immediately by spraying and no more cockroaches. Maybe they came because of the heavy rain that day? Not surprised because it's NYC, but nonetheless the cockroaches were unpleasant. Also, the shower temperature does not seem to have been fixed. It was still a cold temperature, as some had noted in previous reviews. The bathroom sink water got nice and hot, but the shower never got hot. Lastly, it was a bit dirty/dusty in some spots (e.g. bathroom, floor, near refrigerator, etc.). I would recommend a deep clean and fixing the shower again, or decreasing the price.

The Good: "Host" is very friendly and accommodating.  Great location.  Safe and clean.  The bad: Cheap furniture, cheap toilet paper, cheap everything. Bed broke on me halfway through my stay.  Shower needs to be fixed.  If you're a traveler looking for low frills accommodations in the heart of West Village, this is a good spot.  I do not recommend this place for people looking for something comfortable or stress free.

Airbnb owes me ‼️‼️‼️ I’m taking this host to court ‼️‼️ I’m also suing Airbnb . This man pressured me . Asked for my id . Accused me of stealing keys (then found them ) then says he found a clip joint ......duhh your a crappy  488$ piece of stress . I️ felt intimidated , I️ felt watched .... I️ will get justice

I had a pretty good stay here. The room is comfortable, but much smaller than it looks in the picture. Also, I didn't realize the windows face the side of a neighboring building, so little sunlight gets in. It gave the room a bit of cave-like feeling. However, the bed is very comfy, there was ample storage space, and Alejandro was nice enough to give me access to sheets, towels, and an iron. And there is a big tv with cable which was great. But, unfortunately, the wifi was horrendous!  Alejandro is a sweet guy, although strict about his cleanliness policies, and he does keep watch. Made the place a little less comfortable because I was afraid I would forget to follow one of his rules.  Biggest plus is the location. I was able to walk to work in Midtown which was ideal. All in all, however, I don't personally think the room is worth the high booking price. For a younger person who is looking for a lively place with affordable restaurants and bars, Midtown is not that place. Even if you work in the area, you're better offer getting a much cheaper place a dozen blocks away and just hopping on the subway for a few minutes to get to work.

Amy is a great host! Her apartment is tastefully decorated and everything you need is provided for. We noted a special attention toward detail. Amy checks on you regularly and she is readily available to give you suggestions and answer your questions. Steven was also helpful. He gave us clear instructions on how to use the alarm system. The neighbourhood can seem sketchy at first. Before you ask Amy if the neighbourhood is safe, be aware that the apartment is a short 2 blocks away from the subway station and that I walked back to the apartment late at night without any problem. I do suggest you do your groceries/errands in another area for a better experience.   The apartment is nice and quiet, the bathroom is amazing! The kitchen is very practical and clean. There were some issues with the heating system while we were here, and unfortunately we were not warned or kept in the loop as to what was happening. Otherwise, everything was simply perfect. We would definitely recommend Amy's apartment and book it again when we come back to NYC.   Thank you Amy and Steven. Your house is a lovely and peaceful haven in a wonderful and bustling city.

David was an excellent host. Was great about asking if we needed anything and offering to help us with figuring out how to get places. Never felt unsafe in the neighborhood, but as with anywhere, be cautious. Not a far walk from several subway and bus stops. I would stay here again if I came back to NYC!

We stayed in Studio Sweet for the first two weeks in June and we were absolutely delighted with our choice. We did a lot of due diligence to find a place that met our strict criteria, which included avoiding exorbitant Midtown rates so we could spend our hard earned money on things other than accommodation. It may seem peculiar, but we also didn't want to stand in a bath tub to have a shower after a busy day of sightseeing, nor did we want a noisy air-conditioner to be immediately above the bed, which are both things that seem to be prevalent in NYC apartments. Amy's apartment delivers on all these fronts. It is also clean, comfortable and tastefully furnished. This was our first NYC experience and we found the area surrounding the apartment to be perfectly safe and very well positioned in respect of proximity to supermarkets etc. In addition, Amy is a genuine, lovely person who endeavours to help her guests have the best possible NYC experience, with the cold beers and snacks on arrival being an immediate indication to us that Amy puts a level of thought into her hosting responsibilities beyond that which you would normally expect from an Airbnb host. What we want to stress the most about Studio Sweet though is that for us, the location was non-comparable. Central Park is only minutes away, as is the Museum Mile and Harlem. If you have the time, the best way to explore NYC is on foot and we enjoyed all the sights the East Side has to offer by using the avenues between First and Fifth as corridors to walk to important landmarks. If time is short, the 110th St subway station is ridiculously close and catching the 6 train is a simple process that will give you access to absolutely everywhere. With our preference for walking though, we often walked to Grand Central Terminal to catch the subway to destinations such as Coney Island. On one occasion we walked to the Staten Island Ferry Terminal and we also walked to The High Line, before walking back to the apartment via Chelsea, Times Square, Midtown and Central Park. An evening in Harlem is an experience and we were comfortable about walking back to the apartment at night after dinner at Red Rooster and a show at the Apollo Theatre. Thank you to Amy and her brother Steven for playing an important part in our dream NYC holiday!

Amy's apartment is simply perfect! Decorated with great taste, equipped with everything necessary. We slept very well there. The neighborhood is very typical and very pleasant. Not once did we feel unsafe or uncomfortable. In the evening, the streets are very lively. The metro is just a stone's throw away and Central Park is also very close.  The welcome was perfect and we felt very comfortable.

The living/sleeping apartment on the 3rd floor is modern, the bathroom is unusually furnished with a mosaic shower and an antique wooden washbasin. The bed was a bit too narrow for us (1.40 m) and only had a large duvet, but there is another sleeping option available, which is otherwise used as a sofa. Of the 3 windows you can only open one (the other 2 are secured with an alarm system). Fridge huge, but unfortunately a bit loud, which bothered me at night. It's very quiet in the house itself, otherwise the noise is typical New York, but not as bad as in downtown.  The kitchenette (gas stove) is large, but sparingly equipped for German requirements (e.g. no breakfast plates, no egg cups, no coffee/egg spoons, no toaster, only 4 juice glasses..), i.e. you have to wash up after every meal. Nevertheless, you can get along well with a little improvisation.  The building is secured with an alarm system, the use of the access code is well explained, but it takes some getting used to.  The subway station can be easily reached in 4 minutes on foot. The area is not posh, but there is no need to be afraid. Supermarket 50 m from the subway station is completely sufficient (Amy also recommends a supermarket 3 subway stops away, but we found it to be very expensive). The metro runs from 110th Street every 4 minutes during the day, to 42nd Street about 15 minutes. Overall we found the location very good. We were welcomed very nicely by Steven (Amy's brother), there were chips and 2 bottles of beer as a welcome, coffee powder and pads, sugar, salt and pepper were also available.  Steven was very helpful when we had problems with the TV and got everything sorted the same day.

I had a bad experience in this house. Me personally, I couldn't feel comfortable here because the house was really dirty . Here is what get me to that sensation : Strong smell of dirt, mustiness and urine (dog) all over the common area. Diapers of their son on the floor of the guest bathroom Pee and poop of the floor of the guest bathroom and PEE on the living room of their dog Cockroachs all over the kitchen sink from the trash can to the floor Dirt all over the kitchen ventilation and the AC in my room + Bathroom About the atmosphere : Polite at first, then Kinda tense as I heard an argument with some new guests who was asked to leave the house while I was in my room. It was really disturbing as they just arrived. I called Airbnb regarding the cleaning situation to ask for a solutions regarding the cleaning issue. They told me they did not have any solutions, because the 24h delay was already gone. Telling me I have to speak with the host first or the 2nd option would have been to end my reservation and look for another place. When I heard this, I asked Airbnb to give me some time to figure it out with the family but because I had the feeling that the atmosphere was kinda heavy, I didn't want Airbnb to be the middle man and talk to them.So I asked this company to let me discuss this with the family and if I couldn't find any solution then we will see. That's not what they did, despite the fact that the guy on the phone told me and promise me, he won't contact them behind my back. Airbnb called anyway this is what happened : When I came back at the house around 11pm, the family put me on blast and explained to me I was fired and to pack my bags. The husband cursed me out and was aggressive towards me with harsh words such as "fuck you". The family forced me to call AirBnb in front of them to lie and tell the company it was a mistake Forced me to apologise Called me a princess because I wanted a place without dog poop in the bathroom and gave me a sermon about loyalty and friendship when not once I shared any personal moments or eat with them, because i didn't know them. So what loyalty are we talking about ? I also received mails after I left accused me of stealing their personal key, which is of course totally false. You can imagine that I don't want to come back at this house, so why would I put myself in a position where I have to come back again and return the key ? and I don't steal point blank period. After getting humiliated, insulted with a man using his position of power to be aggressive, and left alone with this couple,...

I gonna give an honest review despite the fact i hate spoiling any one's business/ hustle. This was a horrible place. The room was so tiny and messy with dirty linens. The room is located at the basement of their apartment (narrowest and dangerous staircase even seen - normally Airbnb shouldn't advertise that as i heard per NYC regulations that's unacceptable), no window, no AC- trust me during summer you don't wanna have to deal with that in NY. It's a shared bathroom and you have to come all the way to the main parlor where everyone/guest present can see you-so uncomfortable for me and my wife. Another thing was the smell of tobacco everywhere. If you are not a cigarette person it's a nightmare, you can't breathe. We paid for two nights and couldn't even spend 2hrs in that room. We left and finally took a hotel at 27th street, way more expensive but worth the price. We couldn't get a refund as per their policy with Airbnb. This place also ruin our vacation if not of the mood we were in , not to let anything spoil our time in NY. I sincerely hope Airbnb could actually visit locations before approving them on the website. So if you're a tourist as we were, wanting to have a good night rest after spending the day out in NYC, this is definitely not where you wanna spend the night!  Enoh

The studio is really comfortable, has all the things you can imagine for a good experience (coffee machine, oven, microvawe, pans, laundry... and a good bed!). The metro station is really close, just two streets. The neighborhood sometimes (at night) seems to be dangerous but we really hadn´t any problem at all, so think that´s a sensation more than a reallity. Amy and Steven were really helpfull.

We spent a week in Suzanna's apartment and I must say that we were delighted. Very spacious, well decorated, very well equipped, really quiet (we slept very well) and the Williamsburg district is really very practical and well served. Suzanna couldn't be there when we arrived but everything was planned. The keys in a code box outside, the written instructions so that everything goes smoothly in the apartment, a whole list of advice and good addresses in the area and tourist guides. Our host was very helpful and offered to leave our suitcases at the apartment for a few hours on the last day after checking out in order to enjoy one last walk before our flight. I highly recommend this beautiful address. Thank you Suzanna.

Unfortunately I cannot be only positive about our stay in Brooklyn. The neighborhood felt far from safe upon arrival at 9:00 PM, luckily the walk from the subway to the apartment was rather short and there was police on the streets during the night. Rez was not in her apartment at that time as been told to us beforehand, but neither was her friend to open up for us. With the help of her awesome neighbour, we finally made it in which took some time. This all was not very welcoming, neither was the following: we were surprised by the amount of stuff lying around and the weird things everywhere, some were kind of scary. Even the kitchen and bathroom were full of this stuff, although the sanitary was clean. After a short introduction with Rez after coming home, we could go to bed. The room was private as promised in the description and tidy as well. The bed itself could only fit one person! Therefore one of us needed to sleep on an air mattress. Both were comfortable though. Rez was a friendly social person, busy working during the day, so we didn't talk too much. She gave us good directions to places throughout Brooklyn and was determined to help us out on that part. I would recommend this apartment to others, on the condition that Rez is at home on arrival and makes the house/room more ready for guests to feel welcome immediately.

Staying w/ Rez was the best experience I've had during my Airbnb adventures in NYC this fall.
