I already thanked her, but will do so again, for keeping her rates at the lower end of the Airbnb scale and not charging ridiculous prices like so many other hosts are doing right now.   Rez does a good job detailing her apartment's ambiance for prospective guests, and anyone who ends up feeling uncomfortable with the "artsy & funky" vibe obviously didn't look over the listing before booking. For me, what matters most is that the host is a good person and the space is clean (especially the bathroom). Rez is very easy to be around and keeps her apartment above par as far as hygiene is concerned.  Location-wise, the subway is right around the corner. Once you're on the train, Manhattan and many parts of Brooklyn are only 10-30 min away. A realtor might describe the area as "in transition" and, as a result, some people may be a bit uncomfortable in this neighborhood. The block seems sketchier than it actually is. I came back to the apt at 11/11:30pm every night without any issues. There may be some street noise outside at night, but in NYC that's to be expected.  All in all, for the price, the location, and the awesome hostess, this is a great option. Airbnb is a crapshoot, and oftentimes one never knows what they're gonna find till they arrive. With Rez, you'll feel right at home.

It was our first time to book an apartment and we were little bit anxious about it. Of course lots of scams, and all kind of problems associated with apartment rentals. But, am I happy to book this apartment,             Oh Yeah... I was a great experience from booking to check out. Michelle was very responsive and helped us in every detail, including nearby restaurants, cafe, and bakeries.  Apartment is located very quiet and nice neighborhood of Brooklyn, and we did not get any trouble with anyone at all. Parking in the back of the apartment is a big plus, no need to drive around to find a spot. Handing keys to us and initial check of the house was so quick and easy. We texted with manager and he greeted us at the apartment and gave us a quick tour. It was so good to enter the apartment and found everything exactly same as photos on the web site, actually better than that. It was clean, well maintained and lots of daylight. All three bedrooms were in good size, with lots of closet space, I mean lots. Fridge, range, dishwasher, microwave,  coffee maker and other appliances were very good, and all clean. More than enough plates, cutlery, and all other things that you in the kitchen. All good quality stuff, not cheap ones. We did not get a chance to try washer and dryer but they were ready to operate. WiFi worked perfectly, did not have any problems. We did not watch TV, but there was a nice big screen TV. Check out just like check in, was smooth and easy. We asked for few our late check out, and Michelle replied "It is not a problem at all".  She was really nice from check in to check out. It was little bit far from Manhattan but who wants to stay in the middle of a crazy crowd. We enjoyed quiet evenings and mornings. don't get me wrong you can still find some good places around if you like to party, but at least not next to your apartment. Cherry Hill Bakery, Liman restaurant and Rocca, were our favorites, if you stay you should try them. I strongly recommend this apartment for people looking safe, quiet and clean place to stay and don't mind to drive or take trains to Manhattan. No need to look for a hotel in NYC anymore, we know where we gonna stay next time.

Lucas and Maria are accommodating, caring, respectful, friendly and communicative hosts. The apartment is quiet, private, clean, spacious and right next to a train stop. The Casper bed was very comfortable - and overall, a great value. No unpleasant surprises.

Amy's studio was comfortable and provided everything we could have needed--nice hot showers and a comfy bed for us at the end of long days roaming the city.  Don't let the 3 flights of stairs scare you! My husband and I are in our late sixties and managed just fine--:) Having the subway just right around the corner was also a big plus; as well as the East Harlem Bottling Co. and a grocery that has everything your little heart would desire within a short walking distance.

Please, put your prejudices aside! We live in a world where we seem to believe that living amongst diversity is dangerous! This is rubbish. Amy’s home is a in a great community where people are kind and there is so much life. It’s a great spot near public transport and a nice way to escape the city at the end of a big day. Amy is so kind and so willing to help. She was so generous with our check in when we arrived very early. Book this space

Stayed here for a week in March and Amy's studio apartment is fantastic!  First let's start with the location.  It is in Harlem and is a short two block walk to the 6 line.  I loved how quiet the neighborhood is and enjoyed hearing the birds chirping from the open window in the mornings. It's definitely a relaxing and cozy retreat from the hustle and bustle of the louder and busier neighborhoods in Manhattan. Everything you could possibly need is provided.  There were cold beverages in the refrigerator and small oatmeal packets and chips as well.  The bed was very comfortable and I slept very well.  The bathroom is HUGE by NYC standards! The shower was amazing and toiletries, towels and hair dryer were provided.  There is a lot of information in the apartment about neighborhood restaurants, bars, things to do around the city, etc.  Found some new favorites that I hope to revisit on my next trip.  Check-in was super easy (Amy's brother provided the keys and alarm code info) and Amy was always available by phone for any and all questions.  I loved how attentive she was to my needs and I felt comfortable knowing she lived on site and was a quick call away if needed. I was so grateful that she was very flexible about a later check-out due to evening flights and it eliminated a lot of travel stress having that extra time. The decor is very cozy and bohemian and the studio is very spacious. Keep in mind that this place is a walk-up with 4 flight of stairs but Amy is very upfront about that before approving the booking. I have stayed at various hotels in the city and this apartment blows them out of the water! I'm so thrilled my first AirBnb booking in NYC experience was top-notch! I can't wait to come back and stay at Amy's wonderful place again! Don't hesitate to stay here! 4 stars!

Perfect Place for a stay in New York City.  We (m, 24 & f, 21) are originally from Cologne, Germany and stayed in Amy's place for five weeks in August 2022 to study in (Midtown) Manhattan and live in the city.   The apartment is ideally located to commute via Subway/Bus, both stations are two streets (3 min. walk) away. The neighbourhood (East Harlem) is a typical urban, residential area. For anyone concerned about security: We were never afraid to walk outside, even late at night.  The  Supermarket is also only two streets away. You can find restaurants, fast food chains, barbers and whatever else you need usually within in a five minute walk very close by. The next Whole Foods is reached on foot within 25 - 30 minutes, with the train it's 10 to 15. The northeast of Central Park is reached within a few minutes as well, you don't need public transport to get here.  Our daily door-to-door commute to Bryant Park (42nd Street) via subway usually took between 19 and 26 minutes.  A few others (all door-to-door): Empire State Building ~ 20 minutes The Vessel, Hudson Yards ~ 35 minutes Wall Street ~ 40 Minutes DUMBO ~ 45 Minutes  The apartment is bigger in reality than it looks on the pictures - I would estimate it at around 45 square metres (~485 square foot). It is beautifully designed and furnished.  All appliances (AC, Fan, Washer, Dryer) work perfectly. It was an incredibly hot summer, so we we're glad to have the AC since the city get's very hot.  Amy is the best host ever, answers quickly and helps out instantly if needed. (For example if somebody should forget their keys. Twice. 😉) It was an amazing time and and we would absolutely recommend staying at Amy's place!

The place was everything you see in the pictures! Extremely clean and uniquely decorated. The subway was maybe 4 blocks away, and it was an easy ride into the city. We always came home in the night time and we never felt unsafe, the neighborhood was absolutely lovely. We tried some of Blake's recommendations in Williamsburg and they were sooo delicious. All in all, Blake's place was the best! Though we didn't meet him because he was away, it was easy to get the keys from his friend Julia. She was very helpful when we needed her assistance and also so sweet. We hope to come back some time!

Hugo and his family are great! I had some delay arriving in the apartment but Hugo's brother waited for me with a smile on his face. They are very sweet and kind, and the room was clean, organized and as perfect as I could possibly wish. They even gave me they keys for the room and the apartment even before I asked for them. The location was even better than I thought, with the subway system being really close to the house and I could easily get to the center of Manhattan, and within 30 minutes or less.  I recommend this place, it was my first Airbnb experience, I was really scared about it, but everything went great.

Hugo and his mother were very friendly the entire time and made me feel very relaxed about the accommodation. The room is small and humble, but quite decent, with a TV and great for resting after a long day of walking in NYC. Close to the subway and with plenty of shops nearby. I felt a little unsafe walking alone so late, but I actually didn't see anything wrong happening.

As a small-city boy, traveling to New York City seemed like it would be scary or stressful. Having a wonderful host such as Hugo and his wonderful mother made the short weekend I spent in the big city quite a welcoming experience. The room was nice and well-dressed. It was very clean and they had helpful guides to the city left in there for the guest's use. I was only there very late in the evening and left very early each morning. Even though I was only there for a few hours each night, I felt very welcome. The turtles made great friends as well. :)

The airbnb was a dream come true! The location was convenient, as it was close to a subway station that would take us directly into Manhattan, but was in a relatively quiet area in Brooklyn. We never felt unsafe or uneasy in our surroundings and our week-long vacation was made even better knowing that we had such a lovely home to stay in.

When I first arrived to Hugo's I was a bit worried.   After settling in I have to say the room is quite charming .  Actually the whole area is .  Little cafe tables on the outside walk of the Airbnb( to bad it rained the whole time).  I fell in love with the place .  The whole apartment is going through a full renovation and many upgrades .   The place is super clean .   There is a collection can for extra change to feed homeless cats!     My Uber ride to LGA was only 19.00.    Hugo's mother is super sweet and very accommodating .    I will be back !  Next time I have a long layover  Thank you Hugo  !!!!!

We loved staying at Abigail's apartment! The space was actually a lot bigger than expected, very spacious. Also super clean space with lots of great reading! The neighborhood around her apartment is awesome as well- within walking distance to Robertas, juice bar, coffee shops, subway stop  and lovely street art all around. Abigail made it super easy to stay at her place, just had to pick up keys at a key cafe only a couple blocks away and there was no specific check-in or check-out time which made it a lot less stressful getting in and out of the city. I would DEFINITELY return again!

WOW!  This was our first time in the big city, and we were apprehensive about what it would be like.  But no worries here. The house is spacious and very well kept, in a nice neighborhood.  The house was very clean and had everything we needed.  The beds were extremely comfortable, even the "cube" foldout bed (what a clever item...I need one!) The bathrooms provided great water pressure (I didn't expect this for some reason).  Be aware that the bedrooms are at ground level, but this was not an issue.  It felt safe and there wasn't much road noise. Tim was extremely good with communication and so helpful with advice on subway, etc.  The house is less than one block from a subway station that makes most any connection you would need.   The decor is fun, midcentury and artsy.  Lots of interesting things to look at, games to play, and a projector instead of TV.  The kitchen is gorgeous, only things I would say about that are 1)  there's no microwave, which is fine, but be aware if you're used to having one and 2) there isn't a regular coffee maker, but a very nice espresso machine that I was afraid to touch, although he provided excellent detailed instructions. We loved walking and riding the subways everywhere, didn't touch our car while we were staying.  It was pretty easy to find parking within one block of the house (we arrived on a Wednesday night).  If you are lucky enough to be finding Tim's place available for your dates, BOOK NOW!!  It is an amazing value.

For nyc, this was a steal of a deal.  It's about 3 blocks to the subway which isn't bad, but with the kids and luggage I would opt for a lyft or uber instead of a subway.   Laura and Matt are so friend and accommodating.  They're quick to respond back when you have questions and helpful with suggestions and tips about the city.

It is an super affordable place in an area relatively close to midtown. There are a few cats, both in and outside of the apartment. If you like cats, you’ll be in heaven. I didn’t meet anyone in the apartment while I was there, but there were definitely other people which made it a bit unpleasant because I had to constantly be cleaning for them both the kitchen and the bathroom. If you don’t mind cleaning for such an affordable price close to the city, this really is a great place.

We had a great time as a family in Josandra's apartment. Spacious, very nicely furnished and everything you need is there. Subway station around the corner. The Key Food supermarket is about 5 minutes away. The neighbors were always very friendly!!! Josanandra and John always responded quickly to inquiries and helped wherever they could. The price/performance ratio is definitely right if you are happy to make the journey to Manhattan. Here you can really get away from the stress of the big city, an oasis of peace!!! We'll be back :)

This was our first experience with Airbnb. My goal was to find a place in NY that allowed us to be close to the cultural side of NY (at a great price) while having quick access to the surrounding metropolitan areas. With our four children (ages 13, 12, 9 and 4), we arrived at Ed's place in the early evening. While my family was a little suspect of the urban Brooklyn setting, Ed quickly brought us to ease by having the house in great shape and breakfast in the frig for the next morning. He topped it off by ordering a delicious pizza which hit the spot after a long drive!   The house was less than .5 mile from the subway and the onsite parking space was extremely convenient. We didn't spend a lot of time inside the house, but it was comfortable for all six of us with two bathrooms and three bedrooms. Ed was available for any questions throughout the trip and he gave us recommendations for nearby sites such as the downtown Brooklyn promenade and the up and coming Williamsburg area (the Lodge is a wonderful restaurant, btw). Ed was also very generous in printing out the Yankees tickets which we had purchased and delivering them to the house.  Any hesitation we had with the area was quickly gone by the next day as we settled in. It was a wonderful experience with Airbnb and Ed was a big reason for that. Thanks, Ed.

The perfect place to stay if you want to live like a local or be a tourist. Having the convenience of subway transport at your fingers tips was fantastic as it made our journeys in to Manhattan so easy and we never felt unsafe. We also had plenty of local shops that we could either dine in at home with local food stores or eat out with handy restaurants or fast food places close by.  We thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

This place was the perfect place to stay. I was afraid we wouldn’t be able to sleep with all the honking they do in NY but this place was so quiet and peaceful! It was so close to the train station as well. The host were very helpful and friendly! Would definitely recommend staying here! Its also a very cute place!

The space is stylish and pretty much as shown in the photos. The only down side is no wardrobe in one of the bedrooms, not enough towels, and a fairly basic kitchen, no dishwasher or microwave. The location is handy for Manhattan, and the subway is super easy, but I did feel that 5 white Scots stood out like a soar thumb, walking in the neighbourhood. We took a walk to a local Italian restaurant, which was lovely, but there are groups of guys hanging about on the street, with a strong smell of weed wherever you go! In saying that, we never really felt unsafe and it gave us a real taste of Brooklyn, which really added to our trip. Josandra was very accommodating and getting access to the flat was very easy. For a family of 5 it was a good option.

yes i was welcomed. Neighborhood was scary although it was my first time in New York so i was a bit afraid of the neighborhood, of course it  is down town. the building is great and easy to locate with a parking space.

Loved the place! Location was a little sketchy at night but regardless we enjoyed our stay.   It’s pretty close to the trains and the host of this home is super responsive and accommodating to your needs :-)

We really had a great time at Ed’s place. As a group of five, the space is enough and the rooms are comfortable.  Just like the pictures, not surprises there, and with the subway in a walking distance (3 blocks). The path from the subway station late at night can be a little scary, especially the first block, but we find cops everyday and a bunch of people in the zone even at 2-3 am. As an option, there is a bus that drops you a block from the apartment (works with the metrocard as the subway).  I would really recommend it for groups that are looking for a cheaper option and willing to wake up a little earlier, since the whole trip, walking included, to Middletown Manhattan could take up to 45 minutes by subway.  Ed was always a message away, a quick responder, and a couple of days when he wasn’t at town had people looking for us checking constantly that everything were okay.  Thanks again Ed for your support!

The home is located in a great spot in Park Slope, Brooklyn. There are lots of places to eat and shop. It's very close to Prospect Park, the Brooklyn Museum and library. We rented a car and finding a parking spot was easier during the day in the weekend, a bit more challenging in the evenings, especially on Sunday night. The subway is somewhat close. There were lots of kids books that our kids enjoyed and they loved the bunk bed, which I found a little nerve wracking at first (safety), but it ended up being fine. The antelope head above the master bed was a little creepy...  The home didn't seem like it had been cleaned thoroughly - the floors weren't mopped. The host was very accessible and friendly.

The host (Emilie's mother Victoria) was very welcoming... The place was very clean, tidy and very spacious. There was no personal stuff of the owner so it was practically like staying in a apart hotel. We were only 2 people and used the place basically to sleep only but it can accommodate up to 2 or even 3 couples or large families. Despite that we arrived so late (past 11pm) Victoria was so kind to wait for us and give us the keys. She also let us leave the luggage after check in until late afternoon.   The Harlem area may seem slightly unsafe at first (specially at nights) but we didn’t have any issues except for a couple of (drunk or homeless looking) people approaching for cigarette/coins late night, though they seemed harmless. There is some garden work right next to the building so you might wake up after 8am (weekdays only)  if you are a light sleeper like myself.. The subway is round the corner with frequent access to lower Manhattan. Otherwise the cab rates are very reasonable (20-25USD) to lower Manhattan.  Overall it was a very pleasant stay.. I definitely recommend it.

My friends and I enjoyed staying in the apartment. It was very convenient for us to use the public transportation. Since we were not from the region, we didn't want sketchy places for this break, but it was not sketchy at all, even at night. The host was nice, and she would answer our questions immediately as possible. I appreciated all the food and things that she provided to us! If I come back to the city and Brooklyn, I would love to stay at her place once more!

The entire experience with Amy went smoothly from the first to final day of our trip. Not only was the apartment perfect, very clean and well kept being exactly as described/photoed, Amy herself was a great hostess as well, responsive to all questions and concerns and very accommodating. Booking the place and enjoying our stay was easy and stress-free, and Amy provided very helpful information and suggestions for our trip. We will definitely be looking to stay here again.

I stayed one week with two friends in New York. Natasha's apartment was really beautiful, cozy and clean (such as on the pictures). We felt at home because of the sweet decoration and the nice facility. The flat is well equipped (towels, dishes, washing stuff etc.) The location is perfect. You are still in Manhatten and just need about 20 minutes with the subway to Times Square.  At the fist evening we sat on the terrace for just 10 minutes because many mosquitos attacked us. I don't know if this is a general problem or if just we were unlucky. We went in August and the flat was very hot because of the missing windows. The sofa is unforunately no third bed, as it's very hard. Therefore I would prefer the flat just for two persons. The neighbour in the apartment above is quite loud in the morning and in the evening.  Natasha is very very nice. I wrote with her before and during the trip and she was always well accessible. Every time  I had a question she apparently answered me and gave me good advices. We get to know her in person and our first impression was affirmed. All in all we always would go to the apartment again during our stay in New York.  Thank you very much for letting us live in your aparmtent, Natasha!

A stylish apartment from which to explore Brooklyn & Manhattan with good subway & bus links, handy convenience stores & some great cafes & restaurants within walking distance. Be prepared for an ethnically diverse neighbourhood - our teenagers thought it was a bit “gritty” - but we didn’t feel unsafe & found people to be friendly & helpful. Good communication & recommendations from our host.

Natasha’s place is in a fantastic location! We were able to take the subway there and back. Lyft/Ubers take literally 2-5 mins to get there. I cannot stress the ease of this location! If you’re a solo traveler or a couple this is the perfect destination for you while you’re in NYC. It is quiet and cozy and Natasha gives you lots of great information about what is nearby and what to do in the city!

Super cute apartment in a great location in a beautiful, historic neighborhood. Check out the Schomberg Center before heading downtown to visit the other museums!  Natasha was quick to respond to questions, check in and check out were completely stress free, and the apartment was spotless.   It is a basement apartment, there was a full sized bed, and there was no air conditioning. These are to be expected in the city and none of these were a problem, but I wouldn't want anyone to be surprised.

This place is awesome.  It’s bigger than we expected and the walk to metro train is very close.  The Atlantic station by the Barclays center is about 7 minutes walk and Bergen street is less than 5.   We never felt unsafe walking at any hour.  There’s a secure lock, washer and dryer.  Large large towels.  Comfortable mattress and soft pillows.   There’s local coffee, breakfast, drinks, bagels close by.  Would recommend this place to anyone.  Michael was also extremely reachable - he got back to me quickly and checked in with me regularly to make sure we had everything we needed.

The apartment can easily sleep two people and has everything you could need. In fact, the photos of the apartment match reality, but I believe there are some things that are not under the host's control that can surprise. 1- When we arrived there was a lot (a lot) of rubbish piled up right outside the gate with a very unpleasant smell. I believe that the trash is due to the fact that access to the apartment is collective, so I believe that everyone deposits trash there. But it scared me a lot. 2- Access to the apartment is collective, which was not very clear in the advertisement. This access area is a kind of laundry room for the other apartments and, when we arrived, there were a lot of clothes spread out there. 3- although the apartment is close to the subway, the neighborhood does not inspire much security, especially at night. I found a lot of beggars and drug users around the place. 4- The heater only worked in the bedroom, and not that well, the kitchen was very cold especially at night.  In addition to these points, the stay was peaceful and without any setbacks, the house was clean and had everything we needed, and Natasha was always available.

Jonathon is a very kind and gentle person, always ready to make you feel at home.  The neighborhood is not the best in the world, but it is not as bad as it seems. I mean, it's not pretty, but it's not dangerous. The other kids who live in the apartment are also very kind and friendly.

We stayed at Kendall's for approx. a week and our experience was great. When we got there we had a bit of a cultural shock, it's a very black neighborhood and coming from Iceland which is a very white community we felt weird for a moment but there's  nothing to be afraid of. It's a lot of family people. The people in the building were friendly and told us good morning when we'd leave for Manhattan and there's a lot of kids playing outside in the evening. It's very vibrant so there's a lot of eyes on the street. The apartment is very spacious and clean. The bed was really comfortable. Since Kendall just recently moved there there isn't much of kitchen stuff in there, there weren't any bowls so we just bought two bowls in goodwill for us and then took them with us when we left. The curtains tend to fall off if you pull the string too hard so be careful with that. The fridge is new and HUGE so it's great for those who want to cook at home. The subway is really close which was great, we bought a seven day pass to the subway for 30 dollars and using it was very convenient. Overall we were really happy about staying there, Kendall is so nice and I'd definitely stay there again.

The place is huge which is a big plus and really atmospheric. The check-in and communication were fine. However, the photo of the bathroom you see on Airbnb is misleading, and there is a garbage bag taped to the ceiling :/ The A/C which is mentioned here is just 2 fans, one of which is kinda dirty and makes the noises that can scare you at night.   Also, Kendall allowed other guests to leave their stuff in the apartment until their flight without checking with me first. Everything ended up okay, but those guests came back for their stuff when we weren't in the apartment but all of our stuff was there.

A very good place, with a great host! Nice roomates. The place is very comfortable to cook and sleep. Maybe the neighbourhood it's not the best, and it can be a little dangerous to walk on the nights, so bear that in mind if you want to party at nights in Manhattan and come back home late. Besides that, the place is good, and its close to lines D and 4 which can be very helpful to reach every corner of NYC.

This property was an absolute delight to have made my "home away from home" for two weeks. My arrival went very smoothly and everything in the home was perfectly as described and as I had hoped for. More than just a home, this was the complete Brooklyn experience ... an idyllic neighborhood, super friendly neighbor, very convenient to Prospect Park, a bicycle at my disposal, backyard with an awesome old and venerable shade tree, picture-perfect covered front porch for hanging out. It had the feel of a great family home, which was exactly what I had wanted since I was visiting and hosting my own daughters who live nearby. To boot, the master bed was super comfortable ... I slept better than in my own bed!

This place is absolutely massive. Huge rooms, high ceilings, nice neighbors, and lots of privacy - which is surprising considering it is located in the heart of Ridgewood. The kitchen is nice and has everything you would need, and the work space was lovely to have separate from the living and sleeping area. This apartment is doors away from the gym, 24/7 rite aid, and countless countless varieties of food options. Directly next to the front door there’s a 24/7 shop with fresh fruits, food, etc. The Myrtle-Wyckoff subway with the L train is two blocks down and it takes no time at all to get to the heart of the city or the LIRR. Even at 3 or 4am it’s completely safe to walk from the subway as it’s a very commercial area near a Police Station. The roof deck was also an amazing surprise - it’s almost the same square footage as the apartment itself! Had a great time sharing memories with friends there while the weather permitted. There’s a lovely friendly homeless cat that lives there and is a pleasure to have around too (please, please feed him.) I stayed here for three months alone studying since my Uni went remote and loved every single second of it. I was able to focus on studies, have fun, feel comfortable, and have anything I needed at my convenience. If I could do it again I 10000% would - especially when you realize how grimy some (most) of the other options in or around the city are for a comparable price. Suzy was a great host too - highly responsive and friendly. If this place is available for the days you’re looking to visit NY - BOOK IT! You won’t regret it. Highly undervalued.

The listing description was, pretty much, what we found once we got there. Mario and his roommates were very polite, kind and respectful. Everything was very neat and clean and the bed was really comfortable. Great listing, but the neighborhood was rough and packed with homeless people.

Great room, very close to the subway (about 3 blockes and 5 minutes walk) and to central park. The neightbare hood has a quiet a few homeless people, but at night they clear out and safe.  The room itlself is alittle small, but very cozy. The apartment is quiet big, very nice, clean and welcoming. Unfortunetly i didn't spend much time talking to Mario and his roomate, but they were both very nice on the ocations we did meet. Flet right at home and comfortable, could come and go any time of the day without being bothered about it  GREAT PLACE! highly recommended!!

The room and restroom is very clean, and just walking through three blocks then you can see the subway, don’t be scared to live in Harlem, it’s really safe, I’m highly recommending this for you guys :)

Me and my girlfriend stayed in the apartment which is on 4th floor and Subway (Utica Ave) is just 5 minutest walk away. We booked this place based on all the positive reviews but our personal experience was totally different. On our arrival we were greeted by the couple and they are such a lovely people. Apartment is great and same as in pictures. The area is called Crown Heights. However on our first day out we decided to explore the area but it ended soon when we were followed by a group of men who tried to talk to us and when we didn't respond they stated following us and shouting. We turned on busy road  and then they stopped. Anyway we didn't let them ruin our moment. We came back to apartment in the night around 9ish and there was a house party going on with loud music and some guy on microphone. We were tired and fell asleep even with rumbling of sound in the whole apartment but only to wake up in the morning to find out some one was shot dead right outside our apartment. Area was secured by police barriers. We were really scared and wanted to move out but could not due to limited funds. Around 500 people attended the house party and it was all over the news. We decided to leave early in the morning and return before dark and it really impacted our very first holidays in NYC. Then every evening some guy parks a car outside apartment with all doors wide open and plays really load music with massive speakers and of course a microphone. I thought I might ask them politely to turn down the music but how do you speak to 40-50 people who are drunk and abusive to each other. Few days later another guy was shot dead on the same street. Anyway there is a fire station opposite apartment which is very busy and goes on all night with very loud sirens and also police sirens because of police station being on the same street. We did not feel safe at all in this area and if I return to NYC I will not stay in Crown heights or even in Brooklyn. We found queens to better area for stay and shopping. It feels safer and shops are cheaper with large variety. For travel I would recommend getting subway weekly metro card which covers whole New York including ferry and trams. Airport entry costs $5 which is easily accessible by subway to both airports in the city. I would suggest to get subway map and also download offline maps (I use HERE Maps) to make life easier.

We stayed with Ayodele's apartment for 11 nights. Simone, his girlfriend, greeted us at the house - she was very welcoming and gave us helpful info about the closest station/supermarkets etc. She also warned us that it can feel unsafe for women especially to walk alone around the area at night, but I was with my boyfriend so it wouldn't be so bad. Ayodele was away on business for the first four days. He was nice, friendly and mostly stayed in his work room in the house. We felt comfortable in the house. Overall we really liked the apartment - it was clean, well kept, with good facilities like washing, drying, good kitchen and air conditioning, and is just as it was shown in the pictures. Also the room is sound proofed quite well - so even when the tv was on, we were never disturbed. A few negatives are: it's about 50 mins - 1h to get to central places like times square and central park, which got quite tiring to do everyday. The neighbourhood, Crown heights, is a little run down - and at night times it felt unsafe to us to walk to the apartment from the station. On a couple of occasions at night, a few strangers talked at us, (whom we ignored) and it felt quite intimidating. Also the neighbourhood can be loud - there were many people playing music out loud on the streets at night - but if you sleep with ear plugs, thus shouldn't be a problem. Overall we had a good stay here, but if I were to go to New York again, I'd choose to stay somewhere closer to central Manhattan and in a better area.

Ayodele did everything so we felt like home. We had all the kitchen appliances one could wish for, we had our own bathroom and the place was clean and tidy, air conditioning, etc. Couldn't have been better, especially when talking to others about their NYC airbnb experiences. The place is pretty huge by the way and the bed room down the hallway so we didn't hear any street noise. It's located across the street from a fire department but as said, the bedroom is not facing the street and even during the day I didn't notice any loud sirens or anything like that. Even though this is one of the parts of Brooklyn that are not gentrified yet, we didn't feel unsafe at any point in time and walked home during day and night without any fear. The next subway station is within 5 minutes walking distance, same goes for a bus, there are super markets and diners, a bank close by, and some delis are open 24hrs. We got very lucky, I guess, and I'd stay at Ayodele's place any time again.

Francesco's place fully matches to the pictures and description provided. There is not much space there, but it's enough for one person and probably would be fine for two as well. Wi-fi was quick, the bed was comfortable and the water was hot - these are the things I mostly used during my stay. Due to the weather it was very hot and stuffy in the apartment so I had to leave the air conditioner switched on during the night and it made lots of noise. Also when I payed 90$ cleaning fee I expected the apartment to be ideally clean however it is pretty dusty in some areas like windows and shelfs and towels definitely require to be changed - they look very used and stained.  Regarding the location: line 6 is very close and lines 2,3 are not so far and it's quite easy to reach any places you want. I'd recommend to use subway if you're back late because the surrounding doesn't look friendly and actually I felt uncomfortable and sometimes scared walking from downtown about 9pm.

The pictures are a true representation of the Airbnb. Francesco was quick to reply to my messages and the check in process was very easy. The place was relatively clean. The only really negative experience that I had from this Airbnb is that the neighboured felt really dangerous. The closest metro was about a block and a half away, but I felt really scared walking back as soon as it got dark (I rarely ever get scared). There were a lot of homeless looking people that looked drunk or on drugs walking the streets, and a few were saying/screaming stuff to me as I was walking by (I avoided eye contact). With this in consideration, during the mornings when I left the Airbnb I didn't feel as worried. With everything is consideration, I did take the metro everyday. If you are planning on taking an Uber directly to your door step every night, then this should not be as much of a worry for you.

Apartment is exactly as depicted on listing. Very clean and well organized. Lightning fast, reliable WiFi. Plenty of hot water. Fully equipped kitchen. Large dining/work table set up in front of the windows is a nice touch.  Some previous guests have complained about the size, but for a NYC apartment in this location and for this price I would actually consider the unit quite spacious. Easily big enough for 2 people unless you plan on breakdancing inside.  Communication with host Francesco was excellent with very fast turnaround. Check in instructions and house instructions are very easy, clear, and concise. Francesco certainly deserves the title of Superhost.  As an added bonus there is a nice view out the window of St. Paul’s Catholic Church (1908) across the street, especially beautiful at night.   You can walk to one subway station in less than 5 minutes. Can walk to a second in about 10-12 minutes.  I will check to see if Francesco’s apartment is available each time I plan to stay in NYC because pound for pound it’s the best place for me and I really like the neighborhood, especially the food. But, to be fair to potential guests who don’t think like me and who may not be familiar with New York City, East Harlem isn’t necessarily the best option for every traveller. What one person considers a semi-gentrified, diverse, culturally rich, vibrant gem of a neighborhood, another person might consider gritty, unsafe, and unappealing. While it’s home to some of the hardest working people in NYC, there’s no denying that East Harlem also struggles with a disproportionate amount of social problems such as poverty, crime, homelessness, drug/ alcohol abuse, and mental health disorders - It’s borne out in the statistics and is on display in the streets. While this should be a non-issue to a street-smart experienced traveller, just be aware of where you’re booking in case this isn’t what you’re looking for.

Francesco’s place super cozy! Right next to the subway and we were able to get to anywhere in the city pretty easily.  Francesco’s place had everything we needed and the stay was a steal for the price!  Would definitely stay again if I were in New York!

We gave Tom’s apartment a “BAD” review. It is difficult to know where to begin. Dirty. I touched nothing in the kitchen as there were almost no dishes etc. and everything was grimy. Drawers full of random stuff, plastic forks etc. The bathroom was no better! Random clothes and shoes on the closet floor, smoke detector detached from ceiling and sitting on table, a piece of cardboard taped by air conditioner (instead of proper covering for open window)…(Tom did cover opening after we asked). An open window at street level was   Dangerous! Outdoor space was horrible. I take no pleasure in giving this review but feel I need to. I am actually itchy just recounting our stay.

Steven was very kind to us and the hospitality was nice. The apartments is a bit old but well preserved. Though, it had an unpleasant smell during our time which really bothered. It was probably an effect of fresh painting as Steven explained.  The location is great and the proximity to the subway station was awesome.

Michael made us feel very comfortable and responded in a timely manner to our texts and emails.The apt was very clean and very close to the 2&3 and a short distance from the 4,5,6 trains. The studio apt actually feels larger than it is because of the interesting configuration that Michael has assembled. There were clean towels and linens at our disposal as well as other toiletries that we were able to use. (i.e.) mouthwash, soap, dishsoap,cleaning supplies, bandaids, blowdryer, iron. This all made it so much easier to stay in an apt. Lastly but probably the best thing about Michael and the apt is that he gave us small snacks for the duration of our trip. top ramen, apples, cheez- its, a big jug of apple and orange juice and there were even fresh cut flowers! Man this help our appetites and wallets out tremendously! There was a great deck that we would hang out on at night and take in the nice weather. The neighborhood is an urban area and those that are faint of heart should not be expecting the upper west side. That being said, we never felt unsafe walking late at night or in the building. We will contact Michael upon our return to NY to stay at his awesome place again! Thank you!!

I had a great stay here! Justa is the sweetest person, and she is a fantastic host. She responds quickly to messages and is very good about making sure you are comfortable during your stay. She is awesome to hang out and chat with!  The apartment is always kept nice and tidy, and she is very generous with her space. The kitchen is open for us guests to use, and she keeps cereal and other small snacks stocked for guests as well. The guest bedroom is very comfy (if you have a lot of luggage it might be a squeeze), and the living room has awesome decorations from Tanzania all over. There is wi-fi and cable t.v. Brooklyn has a certain reputation, but I never felt unsafe while I was staying there. If you are a light sleeper, bring earplugs, the neighborhood is noisy at times. Luckily I sleep like a rock. The subway is only a few blocks away, and there is a nice laundromat and grocery store nearby as well. If work brings me back to NYC, I'll certainly stay here again!

Michael is one of the most positive and welcoming hosts that I have encountered through Airbnb. He was very flexible with our needs (check-in/out) and made us feel happy and relaxed throughout our stay. The apartment was very clean and beautifully organized, with food stocked when we wanted to eat in, clean towels, awesome hair dryer, q-tips, shampoo, soap, extra blankets for warmth etc., etc., etc.  His apartment and his personality as our host made our short trip to NYC stress-free and set a bright tone to our trip from beginning to end!

Saint gave us a very warm and humorous welcome. Fruits and chocolate were there.  He is very available for suggestions for activities or tours and even signed me up for the morning session at the Central Park outdoor pool!  Her apartment is a stone's throw from the northeast corner of Central Park, in a neighborhood where, despite palpable social difficulties, we did not feel unsafe.

I traveled with a friend and Saint was our first AirBnb host ever and he made our experience a great one! His place is very clean, welcoming, and in a great location. My friend and I were very hesitant about driving into the city and not being able to find parking, but there was plenty of parking and Saint helped ease our stress as soon as we arrived after a long trip from Ohio. He was always available if we needed assistance to navigate the city and was very pleasant to talk to. I definitely recommend for future travelers to stay with him!

This was a very cute apartment, I was very pleased when we first arrived and the first night that we stayed there. The hot and cold water was a little sketchy and it was a little dusty  but could overlook these as "quirks" or "charm" of an old apartment. On our 4th night out of 6 nights the only A/C unit, which is in the bedroom stopped working. Thankfully, there was a fan, but that was not enough to keep an apartment even slightly cool in July, basically just blew the warm air around. When I communicated this issue to the host that morning, she quickly responded, but we were questioned about how we were using it when we hadn't even touched it and told it "just needed a break" (even though that's not how air conditioning works...) we gave it a chance and kept it off during that day and it of course didn't work and when I told the host it didn't work she responded that she would have someone look at it after our stay. Therefore, we had two more nights of a very hot apartment and uncomfortable sleeping. Location was also a little far from a lot of the attractions of NYC, it is close to the subway but was quite a few stops from a lot of places. Overall, ok but wouldn't stay there again.

Michael and his place are amazing. This is THE hotspot of Manhattan!   After a very warm welcome, you can relax from your journey on your own wooden deck with a drink and a bite (waiting for you in the fridge), while the squirls run around you. Who would have thought that in the middle of Harlem!  The apartment gives you the right home feeling. We stayed here for 4 nights with our 2 teens, who loved to sleep in the high bed. Michael managed to decorate the space in a very efficient way; room enough for the 4 of us (there was even 1 bed left).  The neighbourhood is fibrant and never gave us an unsave feeling, day & night!  Practical things like the subway and supermarket are within a few minutes. Less than a minute away you can get the best coffee on Manahattan at Lennox cafe and eat fingerlicking SoulFood at Jackob's Resaurant for a steal.  If you send Michael a message, my experience is that he will reply instantly. The foto's shown in the add give a good impression of what to expect. Looking for the best value for your money? Want to feel like a New Yorker for a few days and bring some soul into your life; look no further!  Micheal thank you for your good care and the chance you gave us to enjoy New York for such a fair price in your wonderfull apartment in a beautifull neighbourhood.
Great place. It is Harlem but the subway is a short walk and I never felt unsafe.  It's a great little studio with three places to sleep and well stocked.

We loved staying in Michael's place. Convenient location (only a couple blocks from the Subway) in a cool neighborhood. I always felt safe walking between the subway and the apartment. The apartment is  very small, but had everything we needed. He even stocked the fridge with some snacks, water bottles, and frozen waffles which was amazing! Came in very handy for breakfast, and it was great not to have to buy water bottles from the expensive street vendors! The bed is hanging from the ceiling and accessible via ladder, which was fine for us, but I could see how it could be a problem for some people if they were afraid of heights or something. Michael was great to work with, he was awesome to coordinate our check in/check out times with. He also took the time to explain the area and subway stations to us when we checked in. If we ever come back to New York and his place is available we will definitely stay there again!

Our stay at Michael's place was perfect. It was very comfortable for 4 people and had a nice shady patio outside. Michael provided lots of food for us and communicated well. It was about a 25 min ride into central manhattan by subway or car, the nearest stop was a 5 minute walk. We would definitely stay there again.

I cannot say enough good things about Tony and his apartment.  Tony is friendly and very helpful, and really does know how to be a great host. The apartment is lovely, clean and anytime we needed anything we found it! He took the time when we arrived to show us how everything worked and introduce us to the area. He has some great recommendations of places to go, and I am certain that should you need anything whilst being there he would respond brilliantly. He even sent a message in the middle of our stay just to check that we had everything we needed.  The location is fantastic - so easy to explore both Brooklyn and Manhattan from here. The train will take you over to Manhattan in no time at all, and all of Williamsburg is on your doorstep. We frequently walked up into the busy areas of Williamsburg, because it has so much and is on the doorstep!  The area also feels safe, at no time during the week that we stayed did I feel at all unsafe.   Yes, the road is busy and loud, but this never caused us a problem. The only time we were ever woken up was if drivers started beeping really loudly, and hey, it's New York, so that would happen anywhere :D Tony even provides a white noise machine to help if you are a light sleeper.   Overall, an absolutely wonderful stay in a wonderful apartment with a wonderful host. I myself would not hesitate to return, and I would highly recommend this apartment for your New York trip.  Thank you so much for everything, Tony!!

Michael's place is wonderful. Let me tell how many ways: Location-spectacular! easy access to M60 for LaGuardia, and the 2-3 for downtown. Too many amazing restaurants within walking distance. Lenox Cafe is a must. Every morning! Space-high ceilings allow raised bed in the center of the room  to create a spacious living/sleeping area. We had 6 people in for a visit, never felt crowded. Patio is also a major plus (when it's not raining). Amenities-plentiful snacks and coffee. Don't be afraid to make coffee with Cuban grind in the French Press. Four tablespoons makes a full pot. Breaks all the rules, but it is GOOD. Michael-Absolutely the most charming and enthusiastic host we've every met.

Anthony's apartment is clean, comfortable, a good size and brilliantly located in the fab area of Williamsburg. I was staying alone for my first night but felt safe and secure in the apartment. Anthony is a friendly, perfect host who is on hand to help at all times and  made check in/out easy and stress free. The location is absolutely brilliant. Whether you're wanting to experience the great vibe of Williamsburg and fab things Brooklyn has to offer or looking for a base to visit all the tourist attractions in Manhatten, the apartment location is ideal. I highly recommend Anthony's apartment as a place to stay.

Honestly, unless you're planning on two hours of poor sleep or never really spending time here — unless you love the sound of traffic, tractor trailers honking, jackhammers, essentially the sound of thousands of people angrily driving into manhattan — oh and you don't like windows or views of anything then dont spend your time here.  I honestly don't believe five people let alone over one hundred people gave this a positive review and I suspect it's actually a scam .  Bottom line: this place was awful and I'd not recommend it at all.

Had a very good time there, the location is ideal with the subway so close and one stop from Manhattan. I was afraid about the noise from the highway before arriving (I’m not the heaviest sleeper), but in the end it didn’t bother me one bit and I didn’t need earplugs either. Cool neighbourhood as well! Tony’s friendly and he left a booklet with many, many places in the neighbourhood to try out for food or drinks. Also, we arrived in the evening and he was there to welcome us. He was always easy to contact from beginning to end and was very understanding for the check-out, as our plane was in the evening again and he let us leave our luggage in the studio and keep the keys until evening. Highly recommend the place!

Great space to stay in for a trip to New York! It was my first time using Airbnb and our host made the trip stress free and flawless. Apartment is cozy and has everything you need to make your stay comfortable. Everything was clean and he even left us little extras like water and donuts. I had never been to New York so when we checked in Michael stuck around and showed me how to use the subways and gave us some pointers on food places. Would recommend staying here for sure!

Superb little apartment in the heart of Harlem, full of nice and practical little touches to improve our stay.  Mickael explains the apartment and the things to visit well. Very pleasant. He waited for us late despite our flight being delayed.  Very easy to find. Line 1/2/3 towards uptown then continue to 129th street, turn right number 28, right into the street. He is waiting for you...

This is a super stylish apartment located in the great neighborhood. Everything you need is right there: the bed is comfy, internet is good, AC is chilly (especially useful during NY heat in August). I didn’t use kitchen/laundry at all - lazy lazy - but they are right there in the apartment as well. And that leopard bedding in the pink bedroom is just awesome. I’m painting my walls pink too. Bedroom windows overlook buzzing Allen street with hip crowd, nice coffee shops and red brick apartment buildings with exterior stairways - so New Yorkey! Small window in the living room has pigeons cooing on the window ledge outside and a tiny piece of blue sky in between two adjacent brick buildings! Very cool. Kinda like in a movie. Then you run down the stairs, open the porch door and step our right in the busy street. I mean how much more of the New York vibe can you get just from the place you stay at?!   There’s Starbucks, huge Whole Foods, Fedex, trains to Upper Manhattan and Brooklyn - everything is a 5-min walk. Few short stops and you are in all the touristy places like Times Square, Bryant Park, Upper Manhattan. There’s a J-train at Delancey/Essex (5-min walk) that goes straight to/from JFK - watch out for the cool Manhattan view while you ride. Chinatown, Little Italy, Brooklyn Bridge, Freedom Tower, these are close too. Sometimes I’d just walk, watch people and accidentally stumble on the places of interest from the guidebook.  Communication is great. When I arrived at the address I was greeted by Shannon, Elisa’s friend. They are both really friendly and professional (really no any difference from the hotel, just a better way to experience New York in my opinion). Big thanks to Elisa and Shannon for making my first Airbnb experience perfect. It was easy, cool and absolutely zero stress.

I had an absolute amazing stay at Tonys place in Williamsburg when i visited New York for 10 days.   Communication with Tony was great and he made check in and check out really easy and always answered really quick! It was nice to feel safe knowing he was there if you needed any help.   The place itself is really cozy, I would say the only thing that would make it even better is if it was one level up instead of ground floor but mostly to be able to look out more. I however did never feel unsafe!   Comfy bed and air condition in bedroom, there’s also a big fan in the other room! I mostly only ate breakfast at home and the kitchen worked really well. Also the bathroom was clean and worked great! For me who’s used to living in the city the sound was no problem accept for an ambulance one early morning ;)  The location is EVERYTHING! so close to so many nice spots, restaurants, bars and shopping in Williamsburg that you can walk to. And so easy to get to manhattan as well ! Be sure to check Tony’s recommendations, a lot of them are really nice! And be sure to take at least one morning to buy a coffee and walk down to domino park ✨

This was my first true AirBnB experience, and it couldn't have been better. First, Danielle was very fast to respond to all communication, and was very accommodating with check in times. I didn't get into the city until 8pm and she had zero problem. I also needed to check out late and she was super cool with it too!  Next up, the neighborhood is great. It's quiet, safe, lots of shops and drugstores nearby for whatever you need. Lots of folks walking their dogs, etc :)  The unit itself is great!  Fantastic furniture and lights, amazing big windows with tons of light. Great TV, etc.  The bedroom is nice and quiet with a window shade, which is awesome for us non-morning people. Very comfortable bed as well.   Overall I loved my experience and will definitely stay again. Danielle was an amazing host (even left snacks for me!)

I'm afraid to say how GREAT my stay at Danielle and John's apt was for fear it will go up in price, or not be available the next time I am in town. :) My flight got in VERY late and yet Danielle and a sick John greeted me and like other posts mentioned, Danielle grabbed a bag and took it up the 5 flights of stairs for me! So kind and accommodating. The apartment was quiet, spacious and clean. Centrally located near everything. Really great!

The appartment was nice. The nieghborhood is dangerous. The appartment was warm, the place never cooled lower then 76 degrees.... However Justa is very kind, helpfull and is easy to work with. The appartment is also close to the subway.

The apartment is a perfectly adequate place to stay for a couple of nights.  It looks exactly as it is shown on the airbnb website with all the Tanzanian furnishings and paintings.  It has two bedrooms (which is great) and one bathroom and kitchen (as described).   Justa wasn't around but Gladys welcomed us (she had to wait a little longer than we had hoped - NYC traffic) and passed us the keys.  She included a fruit basket as a welcome gift, which was a very nice gesture.  The neighborhood might seem dangerous but its actually nice, albeit a little far from amenities such as good cafes etc.  It was perfectly safe for us - but its worth not being too complacent.    The apartment has some major deficiencies.   First, we didn't have Wifi during the entire duration of our stay.  Gladys and Justa used Optimum wifi, which simply did not work.  This means we had to hotspot the entire time and couldn't use the TV.  They were responsive and tried to fix the problem by providing us with the neighborhood's wifi password but that did not work either.  While its not entirely their fault that this happened, it was certainly a major problem.    Second, the house, while being fairly clean superficially, was definitely not spotless.  There were very dusty areas.  The towels were a little damp.  The kitchen counters were a little stained. The couch did not seem super pleasant. I would recommend the hosts to do a very thorough deep cleaning and decluttering, especially behind or under the furniture as well as within the cupboards. Another solution could be to decrease the price per night. Others gave similar reviews, so might be time to reflect.  Third, some lights did not work making the house feel a little dark, damp and claustrophic.   Overall, the experience was good  but I can't say its value for money.  We travelled directly from NYC to Copenhagen and spent a little more money for an absolute gem of an apartment in a very good neighborhood.  This might just be the "New York" factor but its difficult not to take this into account when reviewing the apartment.    Regardless, we thank Gladys and Justa for letting us stay in their apartment and for their excellent communication. Good luck with all of your plans and dreams -you seem to be very kind people!

Tomer has been very helpful all the time but the apartment needs to be updated. The bed is uncomfortable for two, the lights are badly situated and few, the bathtub gets stuck, the rats aré dangerous, the towels and sheets rather old and shabby. Kitchen tools are poor and is not nice to find food in the refrigerador or clothes in the chest of drawers. Aldo the door is old and does not work properly. The price is too high for the product offered.

The place is just like what the pictures showed. It is clean and conveniently located to get to public transportation.  The kitchen and bathroom are well stock.  Everything else (ex: towels, bed sheets, paper goods, etc.) is provided.  The neighborhood is mixed, but we never felt unsafe walking around late at night.  Erin and her family was on vacation when we were there, but Erin responded to my text right away when I had any questions.  We would definitely stay here again!

rental conforms to its description. Quiet neighborhood despite external appearances. We were only 40 minutes from JFK, which we liked after an 8-hour plane ride to get to Central New York. We appreciated the grocery stores for our shopping, always close to our accommodation. Finally, we appreciated the availability of our hosts and especially their discretion. they allowed us to leave our luggage there safely which allowed us to enjoy our last day before taking a night flight. All 4 of us agree to recommend this accommodation! 😎😎😎😎

Juliana and her roommates were very nice and accommodating throughout my trip. They were available to answer all of my questions that I had including always having good ideas for me regarding restaurants and close-by grocery stores.  However, the kitchen in the home had food + dirty pots and pans laying out several days throughout the night. Despite it being cleaned up first thing the next morning, it never gave me the ability to use the kitchen myself because it was a bit dirty.   The room that I stayed in was the smallest room that I have ever stayed in, but it still got the job done since I was literally only in the home each night to sleep. The room also did NOT have a window-shade, so the sun would blast into the room each morning very early and the room would get very, very warm.  The towel that I received on my first day was quite dirty, and since nobody was home for two (2) days, I did not know where to find another towel.  Lastly, the WiFi did not work for the entire trip. The hosts boyfriend told me that he would stop by to fix the WiFi for me on my computer starting on Day Two, but he never arrived as promised. It was a big inconvenience because of this and I needed to go to my local office hours before I needed to be there in order to get work done on my computer.

Juliana and her friend are very nice persons. They are helpful. The flat is well located. The room is well fitted despite there's no curtain. The only point that was unpleasant for me was the lacks in the cleaning of the flat.

We (2 adults, 2 children aged 12 and 15 years old) stayed at Assiati’s place for 4 nights.  Positives - The apartment is spacious, sunny and quiet and there is  lovely art work displayed in various rooms. There are a number of small supermarkets close by and  a number of very good restaurants. Assiati is friendly and helpful and her communication was excellent.  Negatives - The apartment is looking a little ‘tired.’ One of the bedroom blinds was broken, a mirror in the lounge was cracked, the  toilet roll holder was hanging off the wall , part of the stairwell bannister was missing and the overall cleanliness was ok but not excellent. Although this is subjective - we did not feel safe in the local area (especially with the children) and kept our time outside the apartment to a minimum.  There was a police crime scene in an adjacent road on one day involving a vehicle that had been used in a robbery in the Bronx. Other guests who arrive and utilise a vehicle may not experience this issue.

First of all I love AirBnB and the people who trustingly rent their homes at a fraction of hotel prices!  It provides cost-conscious families like mine an opportunity to expand our world experiences.  Thank you Chaim and family!  Chaim’s loft is an outstanding place to stay in NYC…period!  The place is exactly as portrayed in the photos and is set in a gritty, industrial warehouse district with great access to Manhattan and other parts of Brooklyn.   While my first impression was how sketchy the neighborhood looked, I quickly began to see the eclectic mix of young urban artists that live and work in the area.  We also discovered the urbane gems like the Grapeshot, a hip wine store, Brooklyn Roasting Company for a great coffee experience and other neighborhood charms.  The mixed Asian/Jewish influence is so America…so NYC.  I was impressed by the extensive bike culture (lots of fixies) and proximity to Steiner Studios that lent to the artsy feel of the neighborhood.  We felt quite comfortable walking around the neighborhood and had easy access to free on-street parking.  Chaim and family were great hosts leaving a carefully curated list of recommended Brooklyn restaurants.  They communicated regularly and in a timely manner (more than me).  I highly recommend this stay and hope you like your Brooklyn adventure as much as my family of five did!

Andrew’s quiet apartment was the perfect landing pad for our family’s Christmas holiday in NYC! The location near Columbus Circle is convenient to EVERYTHING and is exactly as advertised. We would have given 5-stars, except Andrew did not respond to our requests for the exact address and check-in instructions until the day before we arrived, which was incredibly stressful. Thankfully, it all worked out & we had a great time!

This review is written about the experience the parents of one of my friends had. They were staying there because their son sustained a serious brain injury and was in the hospital nearby.  I set them up with this rental and they had such a great experience.  Joaquin was an amazing host. From the moment they walked in, Joaquin made them feel so at home. He gave them a wonderful tour of the entire house, offered to make then coffee and breakfast every morning (for a small extra cost), and seemed truly interested in getting to know them. He also offered to walk the mom to the hospital to get her comfortable with the area. He helped her figure out the subway (which she was afraid of using because she was from Alabama!) and gave her great recommendations for places to eat.   The listing of this space doesn't even do it justice. The house is so beautiful- Joaquin and John have AMAZING taste in art and decor. Their dogs (Maggie and Bodi!) are also so adorable and lovely. Their stay felt like a true home and is somewhere anyone would be lucky to stay.  At a really scary point in this family's life, Joaquin was a tremendous comfort and ally. He listened to their story and took care of them when they needed it most. Not only a beautiful place to stay, but beautiful people to stay with.

I rented the room for my parents, who were visiting my wife and I, and our new newborn daughter for two weeks. Joaquin was a gracious host and he has a charming home that is well taken care of. The whole house is very tastefully decorated and you can tell Joaquin has put a lot of his loving attention into it. My parents had a private bedroom on the 3rd floor with a nice view of the street and a small private bathroom. The floor is shared with the host's master bedroom, bathroom, and office. Joaquin was extremely patient in showing my parents all the details of how to use everything in his home.  The house is well situated near all the Sunset Park attractions.  It is very close to the subway and public buses, and the park itself is only half a block away. You also have easy access to Latin American restaurants on 5th Ave and Chinese and Southeast Asian places on 8th Ave. Any way you go, you're sure to have plentiful choices for affordable and tasty cuisine.   Lastly, Joaquin's two dogs were sweet and gentle. My mom is VERY afraid of dogs, so this was a concern for me. Somehow, by the end of her visit even she was OK with them. That was unprecedented!

Joaquin is a wonderful host.  He and Jon have a beautifully remodeled brownstone just half a block from Sunset Park. The guest room is large, sunny, and air conditioned, its huge windows overlooking  a tree lined street; it features a flat screen TV with NetFlix, plenty of storage space, and, of course, a comfortable double bed. The guest bathroom is modern and immaculate.  The house features a shady, restful back garden.   The park, which is famous for its views of NY harbor, itself is being refurbished. There is a subway stop just a block away from Joaquin's as well as several nearby bus routes.  The house is half a block from a grocery store and close to coffee shops and small restaurants.  Joaquin is friendly and extremely hospitable.  He will do his utmost to make your stay comfortable.

Super convenient location, great apartment, we had everything we needed.  Meghan was a GREAT host.  If you are looking for an affordable alternative to hotels and the crazy that is Manhattan, we recommend staying with Meghan.  It is only a 5-10 min walk to the Ferry which provided a relaxing, stress-free commute in the morning and evening.  We hope when we return in a few years that Meghab will still welcome Airbnb guests!

This apartment was spacious and was perfect for our group of 5 adults and our 3 young grandchildren, and a great value compared to other places that size. Short walk to the subway and then about a 30 min ride into the heart of Manhattan. We have never stayed in Brooklyn before. Apparently the city is being revitalized and there are a number of hip restaurants, etc in the area. We spent the bulk of our time in NYC but did really enjoy Saraghina bakery and restaurant (short walk) and Dough has amazing doughnuts! Some of the nearby streets/houses seemed a bit rough but we NEVER felt unsafe walking about. Hosts were very sweet and willing to help.

It was my wife and I who stayed here. The host Michael is friendly and helped us with whatever we needed throughout our stay. The shower was a nightmare with the temperature changing constantly on its own. But Michael fixed it immediately for us. The apartment is facing the back of the building so it is quite. The internet and TV work fine. It is a fifth floor walk which we did not expect. The building is very old and reeked constantly of smoke on the 2nd and 3rd floor. A lot of the times we could even smell it in our apartment. We also had roach issues on a daily basis which made cooking or preparing any food next to impossible. The sheets and towels were dirty so we decided to use our own. The bathroom is really small too. The bed is also not the most comfortable and creeks with the slightest movement. On occasions we saw rats outside the building. Though it is centrally located and close to Penn station, the block itself at night can get sketchy with some homeless people around the block at all times. Overall, not the best experience. I also think we over paid for the kind of place it is and since the cancellation policy is strict we could not do anything about it. We had to stay there for the month we paid for.

I’m going to get this out of the way first - we booked this apartment based on the glowing reviews of the apartment, hosts, and value. I was nervous about staying in Bed Stuy and although many of the reviews discuss the food nearby, very few address the area. As a family traveling with children and not familiar with the area except for vague warnings from local family members - this did make me nervous. So I will address that: While we were cautious, we never for a moment felt unsafe. There were many families + individuals  walking dogs, jogging, and trying to stay cool at the park across the street. The block is quiet and sunny as described in other reviews. Everywhere you go you should be cautious, but we found the area very warm and inviting. The walk to the Fulton St. station via Stuyvesant Ave was quiet and full of the old architecture Brooklyn is known for. It was a pleasure to take the short walk to and from the train. Which by the way are a direct route to Manhattan.   The apartment is exactly as described. We visited during a 3 day heat wave, and the 3 air conditioners + ceiling fans provided plenty of comfort. The bedding was clean and fresh smelling. All the utensils and plates/bowls we used were clean. The coffee maker had been reported to Tonderai as malfunctioning before our arrival so he replaced it the day we arrived which we very much appreciated. The natural light in this apt was insane! You literally don’t need the lights on until the evening. TV service and WiFi was also great.   Tonderai was our host for our stay and he was great. Very warm and welcoming. Answered all of my questions via text and when I reached out for a couple of needs (charging cable, fan remotes) he was more than accommodating. Check in instructions and house rules were very clear and concise.   I wouldn’t change a thing about this stay. We wanted to stay in Brooklyn to be outside the Manhattan bubble and see and eat all the things Brooklyn has to offer and this apartment was the perfect home base. My family will definitely refer others as well as come back to this apartment in the future!

Location was awesome but couldn’t say the same for the stay. She advertised a smart lock entry and AC but had neither. Sleeping with windows open was LOUD and unsafe on the 1st floor. Was also very impatient  with check-in  as I encountered traffic during a long drive.  House had odd smell as well. Now I’m aware why it was so cheap.

The room is OK. Bathroom is shared with a couple of roommates. We did not have the chance to meet personally Jillian but she let us to leave the baggage after the check out time which was very nice. 10 minutes walking distance to L-train station. At night time the area looks a bit sketchy.

Natalia was SUPER AH-MAZING!! We had to check in late and she responded right away that it wasn’t an issue and provided detailed instructions for the check in process.  We unexpectedly met her checking in and she was extremely nice. She made my first experience in NY comfortable, stress free and was always available if I needed anything. Especially when it came to directing me how to navigate through the city train system, she is the ultimate pro lol.  She provided great instructions to the train station prior to my visit which was very helpful and she was quick to reply when we got lost. On top of that her space is exactly as pictured and very clean and I could tell that the neighborhood is family oriented which made me feel safe. Overall, Natalia was the best host I could ask for and I will definitely book again plus recommend her place. Thanks so much Natalia!!

Sofia's place was perfect. Great location, clear communication, and incredibly clean. We came in facing a forecast of rain while toting a tired baby, but the hydrant out front made unloading easy. So often the city can be stressful to get around, but Sofia's place made our stay simple and fun. Would definitely consider staying there again.

This was a great apartment for our family of 4 adult-ish people.  It has recently been renovated and looks great on the inside. All the appliances and furniture seem to be new. The kitchen has a full-size fridge/freezer, toaster, coffee maker, oven and stove and microwave.  The Wi-Fi worked fine and there are TVs in every room with cable. The pictures supplied about the  apartment are accurate and the apartment was very clean.   It was hot in the apartment when we arrived but the three window mounted air conditioners cooled it down very quickly.  Elito met us late at night to provide access to the apartment and give us information. He was both friendly and informative.  There are several groceries within a block or two if you want to cook food.  Likewise there are several coffee shops, bars and restaurants. Generally, it doesn’t seem that much is open early in the morning so if you are an early bird, you may want to hit the grocery store. Coffee shops seem to open at 7 AM.  The neighborhood is in transition or gentrification. Some streets are quite nice and others are somewhat sketchy. We felt safe although we took an Uber  back rather than the subway when returning from a very late night. The building itself is quite safe with 2 external ground floor  deadbolts and a very secure door Otherwise, we walked everywhere and use the subway without any concerns for our safety  It’s on the second floor with only stairs available so keep that in mind if you have heavy bags or physically find that difficult  Loved our stay and would recommend it to good friends

The first thing we noticed was how CLEAN the apartment was! The floors were shiny, there were ample towels, and the refrigerator was stocked with bottled water for us. The apartment looked just liked the pics. The neighborhood was really nice and safe. We walked around several nights to different restaurants and bars and NEVER felt unsafe. Any emails we sent were responded to promptly. I would definitely recommend this host and property!

It was very easy to communicate with Marco during the booking period, I got answers right away and he was very accommodating of some special requests like late check-out. He was there to welcome us, helped with the bags and very friendly and helpful at all times (even his family who live 10 meters away in a separate flat). He made sure all things that might be needed in the room were available. We stayed for eight nights so he changed all sheets and towels and cleaned in the middle of the week, at date and time that was convenient for us.   The room is perfect for two persons, with own toilet and shower, sink, we did not even use the TV and VCR but nice to have in case needed, wifi, small ref and microwave, hot and cold water. There is aircon, which is very much needed during summer. It is in a basement so easier to bring large luggage, which was also reason why I chose it since I would not have energy to go up and down with bags.   The neighbourhood is safe. We did not feel afraid at all even if we were walking from subway or theatre at midnight. Lots of delis, restaurants (esp in 8th and 9th Avenues), 24 hour pharmacies and just walking distance from Times Square. The daily price of this bnb is very good for such a central location.   Will I stay here again when I go back to NYC? Yes, definitely! No second thoughts.
