First experience with AirBnB and could not have asked for a better host! Lola was accommodating and helped make my trip to NYC so convenient! She gave me a little tour of the area and shared her local NYC knowledge. The room was so cute and the apartment was great! I had such a great 2 days and attending my conference was stress-free! I highly recommend booking this room if available:-)

Studio meets our expectations. We were not received personally but Tom remained contactable if necessary. The key box is extremely practical, we took advantage of it every day to leave the key there. Quiet accommodation with nice glasses of wine that just need to be filled 😁. The green area is pleasant for breakfast. And finally Tom offered to keep our luggage because our flight was late. THANKS
Excellent place to stay in New York. It has everything you need (even suitcase scales). Very comfortable room, just like the photo. Everything excellent. You can be without fear.

This little  apartment was just as advertised, it fit our needs well, and it was VERY quiet. No street noise, no neighbor noise, no barking dogs, etc. Although the bed is a fold out couch, it’s firm and comfortable, although the memory foam mattress was a bit hot. The wooden blinds darkened the room nicely, and I slept very well each night!   We didn’t use the fancy spa bathtub other than for showers, so I can’t speak to its luxury, but it looked a bit intimidating with all the nozzles and knobs. It was simpler and faster to just take a shower! I’m sure for hot tub fans it would be delightful.  My only reason for 4 stars rather than 5 was the kitchen. It was mostly adequate, with a microwave, toaster, coffee pot, etc. but the coffee pot was tiny and the fridge was a problem. As others have mentioned, it is a wine fridge, and only cools to 46 degrees. A little scary for leftovers or half and half. Since one can’t cook in this apartment, leftovers and carry out foods are important - and it was spooky to keep leftover soup or pizza in a warmish fridge.  Aside from the fridge, the apartment is very nice. It feels secure, it’s quiet, and has easy access to corner markets, restaurants and subway stations. I highly recommend this sweet place!

Located in a basement, it was warm, the shower worked and was warm, they had a microwave and fridge and even plastic plates/silverware, toilet and shower are in the same room with no privacy (just a shower curtain), the owners are really respectful and sweet people who were very responsive to us. It was cozy and the bed was comfortable. It’s located in Hell’s Kitchen about a 15 minute walk to Times Square, we didn’t feel unsafe walking home at all. Overall, I really enjoyed it and felt like it was reasonably priced!

My stay with Gabrielle was wonderful. She and her partner Rich are really nice, and their home is wheelchair accessible with an elevator connected to the condo (which is really important to me.) They were really friendly and accommodating, offering to help with me whatever I needed, from making tea in the morning to helping me get dressed with a costume in the city (thanks for your help, Rich! :P) They were also very flexible with their schedules, and I never felt like I had to wait for anything, since we had constant communication from beginning to end. I would love to stay with them anytime I was in back in NYC. In terms of the area, I have to mention that for me, that was a stressful situation considering that A) they live on the 3rd steepest hill in Manhattan and in my wheelchair, this was a problem (I thought that was exaggeration, it's NOT.) B) It's not particularly close to downtown, so if you're there for attractions, be prepared for some high taxi costs (about $40 between them and the Theatre District) or for a particularly long commute via the subway.

I felt at home. Lola was more than a host to me, she became a friend that I will carry with me forever. The apartment is cozy, as described in the photos and close to everything. Close to the Empire State Building, close to the subway, close to restaurants and bars. Perfect for those traveling alone, quiet neighborhood and easy to find. I didn't feel insecure. When I return to NYC I want to spend time with Lola again.  I highly recommend it.

Unexpectedly, I slept amazing well the first night at Ms. Yvonne's. The location is quiet and neighborly, just blocks from grocery, coffee, drug stores. Terribly convenient. Ms. Yvonne made me feel welcome in her home, and takes time to ensure I am acquainted with her home and the area. I really appreciate Ms. Yvonne. She has a home away from home. To add, I thought Ms. Yvonne's space is perfect for working in between meetings and social affairs.

Positives: Clean place, comfortable bed, relatively quiet, great A.C. and ceiling fan, mini fridge in room, close to subway station and bus stops. Negatives: She has a LOT of rules, which makes it stressful.  (Don't sit on the bed, sit in the recliner.  Take your own bathmat to/from restroom every time, etc.) She expects guests to take household trash / recycling out of the building. All dryers in the building were broken, which I didn't find out until after I had washed my clothes.  It's close to Columbia in  distance (0.5 mi) but you have to climb about ten flights of stairs to cross Morningside Park.  It's not a quick walk as I was told.  Overall, I was disappointed for several reasons.  I never felt comfortable using the kitchen because I was afraid to make a mess. I was very upset that all of the dryers were broken during my two week stay, as laundry is one of my deal breakers, and that I wasn't told about it or reimbursed for going elsewhere.  I wouldn't stay here again.

There is just so much to say about my experience here - I am not sure where to begin. So, I decided to make a Pros and Cons list to help readers understand where I'm coming from:  PROS: - Literally the best AirBnB experience I've ever had.  - Rich made banana bread and cookies for me (He needs to open his own bakery!)  - Rich also treated me to delicious home-cooked meals while I was his guest. - The apartment is beautiful. The neighborhood is well connected. - Traveling in the city is a piece of cake thanks to Rich's excellent advice.  - Did I mention the cookies? - KITTENS! Stella is so much fun to hang with.   CONS: - The other kitten, Neil, was very suspicious of me.  - You may not want to leave after your visit.

My boyfriend and I spent two nights in this beautiful apartment. Gabrielle was away during our stay so we were hosted by Rich. He was superb in every way, welcoming us from the first moment we walked in the door. He had advice on where to eat, the best parts of The Metropolitan to see during our short visit and even where to quickly get a toothbrush. We especially enjoyed the restaurant he recommended, Hand Pulled Noodle, which was just steps away from the apartment and so delicious we ate there twice. His experience in the city was invaluable and made our trip much less stressful.   Rich was very responsive to any questions we had, and is simply a great person to converse with. We loved listening to the presidential debate with him while we ate our dinner one night. We really appreciated him contacting us before our arrival to help plan our trip and get directions to the apartment.  The location is ideal, close to the 1-line of the subway and just up the block from Riverbank Park with views of the Hudson bridge. Inside everything was clean and comfortable and each room is brimming with cool artifacts and artworks, each of which had its own story. Stella and Neil are very personable cats that are nice to come back to after a long day of exploring the city.   All together our stay exceeded our expectations. Even compared to New York City hotels I’ve stayed at in the past this was by far the my most relaxing and luxurious stay.  Rich and Gabrielle have a really ideal place in the city and we’re thankful they decided to share it. Hopefully we will be back for longer next time!

Gabrielle is very quick with communicating with her guests. She is very helpful especially with the subway which is daunting for a first timer in New York. Her instructions are spot on and we didn't get lost once🤗. And the towels are so very soft. She made our stay with her very stress free. Thanks Gabrielle

Long story short, stay here. We had an amazing stay and would go back again.  Now for the details. The first big pro of staying here was its close proximity to Utica Station. From there you can take either the C or A train straight to midtown Manhattan (about 30 minutes to Penn Station). The neighborhood can feel a bit sketchy, but all in all we felt safe walking to and fro from the station at all hours of the day/night.   OD is extremely flexible with check in times, which was another plus. I met him around 10:30am and he gave me the grand tour of the place. It’s spacious. More room than we expected, with an ample sized living room and a perfect sized bed.   The refrigerator was stocked with various breakfasty things like bagels, jam, milk, orange juice and eggs. (There wasn’t any basic cooking ingredients like oil, butter, or spices for the first day of our stay. OD was quick to supply us with everything promptly though.) He had also purchased a bouquet of flowers and a bottle of sparkling cider for us as well.   Everything about the stay was smooth and pleasant. The best place to stay for a romantic getaway on the cheap. Excellent service and supreme facilities. OD has our thanks.

The place is excellent and exceeded our expectations the apartment is much better to see it personally than in the pictures the photos are as is the place It is two blocks from the subway and you are 20 minutes from downtown Manhattan and all attractions. OD is very friendly and an excellent host. Not only leaves the sheets and towels but is concerned with leaving you food and drinks and the milk you drink. The refrigerator and cupboard is provided with everything you need. The bed is very comfortable and the shower is excellent and you have all the hygiene items Shampo soaps etc. If you need a transfer to the airport, OD solves it at a very good price. I do not doubt in voler.

This was definitely a great place to stay. I was a bit afraid that my boyfriend would have said that he didn't want to stay again because the bathroom was not very big. His description was, it's only for a few nights so a small bathroom wasn't really a problem. We have the benefit of a great host and a quiet neighborhood with great food. He wants to come back and stay at Sylvia's again. She was very accommodating and made sure that we were happy with everything.  And although we did not get to see much of the neighborhood, we ate at the Brazilian resteraunt around the corner and had Ecuadorian food twice. Both very very good places to eat before heading off on the subway which is only a few blocks away. The only thing I would say to beware of on your stay, is not this apartment, the neighborhood or the local food, it would be the subway schedule change for the weekends. You don't know where the train is going until you get on and you wait for trains that aren't coming. So, either ask someone around that knows or hop on the first one that comes by and only then, you can see the weekend schedule. Other than that, you can't beat it. I slept awesome. I read so many stories about people staying in other noisy neighborhoods so I was nervous and there was no need to be. Thank you Sylvia.

This private room and bathroom were perfect for our NYC stay. We had never been to the city but Gabrielle & Rich were helpful with any questions we had. Also the apartment is close enough to walk to and from the subway. Never felt unsafe and the private bathroom was a HUGE bonus for us as I couldn’t find many other listings with that in NYC. Would stay again and recommend it to others.
Excellent welcome with a pretty house with almost everything you need. The area can be a little scary at night but we were never bothered. Amy is very helpful and available.

HAD A VERY GREAT AND PEACEFUL STAY WITH MARRISA AND HER HUSBAND THEY WE'RE BEYOND ACCOMMODATING FROM RECOMMENDING THE BEST RESTAURANTS AND LANDMARKS TO MARISSA ACTUALLY MAKING ME AND MY FRIEND SOME BLT SANDWICHES (WHICH WERE AMAZING BTW). THE ROOM'S LOCATION WAS PERFECT HAD A VIEW OF BROADWAY STREET AND THE LIGHTING IN THE MORNING MADE WAKING UP A PLEASURE EVERY DAY OF OUR STAY.  THE SUBWAY IS LITERALLY 2 BLOCKS FROM THE APARTMENT WITH VARIOUS RESTAURANT OPTIONS TO CHOOSE FROM (MAILY DOMINICAN SPOTS) VERY YUMMY. THERE WAS ALSO A STARBUCKS AT THE CORNER OFF BROADWAY FOR YOU COFFEE DRINKERS LIKE ME:).  AT NIGHT IT IS ALSO A GREAT PLACE TO GO OUT AND GRAB SOME COCKTAILS, RELAX ENJOY A LITTLE MUSIC OR DANCING. NEVER FELT UNSAFE WALKING BACK LATE FROM THE SUBWAY IN THAT NEIGHBORHOOD I REALLY FELT LIKE I WAS BACK HOME. I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS PLACE TO ANYONE COMING TO NEW YORK FOR ANY OCCASION.

This place was nothing like the pictures at all yes the furniture and location was accurate but that’s about it. Brad needs to include that his place is infested with water bugs the big flying cock roach tht I normally see in the train station or by a bunch of trash. During our stay my boyfriend killed 5 of them. The place is dusty & dirty if your afraid of those flying bugs & want a clean place to stay I would not recommend this one!

Donna provided lots of info before our arrival.   The apartment is in a great neighborhood location with coffee shops, restaurants, groceries nearby. The subway is very close also.Getting the key was easy. was stress free,had plenty of space to stay for 2 persons.. We would definitely recommend staying here for anyone wanting something more genuine than a Times Square tourist hotel :)

The  place was just the right size for us, bed could’ve been a lil bigger, location was in the perfect area to walk to most anything you need. The room had everything you need for vacation. I knew the street noise would be loud and was prepared with earplugs, but I didn’t expect everyone who lived/work there to be talking outside my door or window starting at 6:30-7am. And the last 2-3 days we had to hear furniture being drug upstairs because they were moving!!!

Checkin and other aspects were clear. Room was clean. The staff is unresponsive to guest requests and did nothing to fix their overheating problem, even when we asked 4 different times. When we asked for water, they said they don’t supply it although they did provide it at check in. Shady.

Daniela was an excellent excellent host. On my first night since it was really cold outside when I entered the room the heater was on and room was warm so I could be comfortable. I don’t have a pet so I was a bit uncomfortable with Jazz (the dog). Daniela made sure that it doesn’t bother me but Jazz was very loving and nice dog. I stayed five days and never have I heard one single bark from him. The room is quite no disturbance at all. Neither from outside or any other people living in the apartment. The room was exactly as it was shown in the pictures. It has a small lamp, a window, a kallax and wardrobe with hangers for clothes to hang.  Apartment was nicely set up too although I didn’t use the kitchen much as I was out the whole day. Kitchen seemed fully equipped too.   The location of the place was very very nice just. There was a bus stop 2 mins away that can take you anywhere around queens. Subway was 8 mins walk to reach Manhattan and all the touristy places in 15-20 mins minimum. The location is very safe and near to the LaGuardia airport. I used sometimes to come to the room around 2-3 AM. And I didn’t feel unsafe at all. Overall it was one of the nicest Airbnb experience. Would love to stay her again.

Daniela is a very available hostess, she answered all my questions very quickly. Her dog is very cute and didn't make a single noise during my entire stay. Daniela's room is comfortable for the price paid.   Daniela's apartment is very well located 10 minutes walk from the N metro towards Timesquare/Manhattan. There are a lot of shops around her place to do small errands.   However, I would have preferred that several sheets and duvets were made available because you can never know if they have been washed or not before. It’s a shame, it’s a small investment that makes the difference. If you book, remember to take sheets and blankets with you.   Second negative point: there is no lock on the bedroom door... it's a shame because Daniela was absent during my entire stay and you never know who the other guests are. A handle with locks costs almost nothing to install and would allow passports and important documents to be left at the apartment. Don't be afraid to sleep with strangers without a way to lock the door.

Could not check in to hotel until 11pm because some other people were late, they had a don’t care attitude and when we finally were able to check in and asked for water they told us off. We ordered food and water from Uber eats it came in 10 minutes by the time we went down they had already stolen it and staff did not know who it was. Stay away. You will regret booking this stay. Worst airbnb experience ever.

This is a great place to stow your stuff and get out and explore.  It's clean, the bed is comfortable and the water pressure is perfect.  Eddy was an attentive host and check in was very easy.  You can't go wrong staying here.  Ps don't be afraid to walk over the Washington Bridge.  :)

Due to an unresponsive host at another NYC location, we had to book Eddy's place VERY last minute - we are so grateful for the flexibility and communication in a stressful situation!  Eddy was immediately accommodating and had the place ready for us within a few hours of the request.  He was continually communicative with us, which was so helpful!  The apartment itself is very simple, but very clean - if you're out and about in the city (as you should be!), the simple accommodations are exactly what you'll need. The building is secure and a quick walk from the 1 (subway).  The area is pretty quiet and easy to navigate - a quick ride from LGA, too.  The price is great for the location/accommodations.   Thank you again, Eddy, for all the communication and help in the last minute re-book.

When I first arrived in NYC, I will admit I was a bit scared. However, when I checked in, I felt so much better after meeting Rachel. She was very friendly and welcoming! The check-in process was easy. The shared bathrooms and showers were clean. Everything I wanted to do was very close to the BNB.  I enjoyed my stay so much and would definitely come back again :)

My plans changed and still within my timeframe to cancel my reservations. But instead decided to just remove 1 day off and keep the reservation. Host never responded. Had Airbnb try with the same results. Arrived at Hotel to tell me I was a no show and my reservations were cancelled.     I was told if I wanted to stay they would have to use my original booking info and charge me for the whole stay since they are book up. (How are you booked up but can give me a room if i pay an extra night,scam) Had no choice but to pay for extra day and still no call or response from host.

READ THIS BEFORE BOOKING!!! The hotel gave us someone else’s room number and card access to there room. We entered it as she told us it was our room but when we entered it we knew immediately that this was someone else’s room. There belongings and luggage was everywhere. We went back down and told them they gave us the wrong keys and she apologized and said this was her worst nightmare. She gave us new keys to a new room. I told her I was nervous other people would be able to access our room since she just did that with us. I didn’t want to say anything until after our stay in fear of repercussions.  We placed do not disturb signs in hopes that no one would enter the room. And they disregarded the sign and still entered our room to clean it. THIS IS NOT A SAFE HOTEL. People easily could get access to our room without permission and steal our belongings. Also it was disgusting not clean at all. The sink would not drain. DO NOT STAY HERE.
The shower wasn’t working and there was an unpleasant smell in the kitchen/bathroom area.

Danielle’s place was just as listed down to the tee. Check in was smooth with Danielle providing pictures of the property and how to get inside. Place was perfect and looked just like the pictures although There were a few minor imperfections that concerned me:  1. Upon arrival we noticed baby roaches coming out from behind the bathroom mirror  2. The light in the little dining area didn’t work or come on  3. The socket near the double sliding door is very dangerous. It comes out of the wall every time u try to unplug something.  If these issues were to be maintained; this would be a 10/10. Walking distance to a couple different food spots was cool and a rite aid was a couple blocks down. Nice quiet area and a first floor apt is a plus.
Lovely spot right near the Myrtle Broadway M/J. It’s a first floor unit with a sliding door out to the street but I didn’t feel unsafe. Well appointed and modern. Very comfy! Would stay again.

Nothing to say, I confirm Danielle is a great host, nice clean apartment, Danielle is responsive and even allowed us to return the apartment 3 hours later because our flight to JFK was in the evening. Perfect for a family of 4.

Do not rent this room, the ad is a lie. The photos taken are not of the room they rent. This image of the Empire States does not exist. The room is from a hotel and must be around 15 square meters. That's why there are no large photos in the ad. I will report this thief on Airbnb and I want my money back at least.
This place looks amazing but the host didn't steal the money along with arbnb and page for something he didn't use thanks for stealing my money

AT's home was an amazing stay for my family and I. Not only was the space modern, clean and we'll designed... AT was an exceptional host that helped  make our stay stress-free and enjoyable. highly recommend!!!!!

Pros: very comfortable double bed, location to explore Manhattan and communication with the host.  Con: to improve the kitchen utensils and some table and chairs to eat at.   Good value for money for New York. A multicultural neighborhood and environment, we have not felt danger at any time, neither on the street nor with the neighbors (despite having a sign that says that Airbnbs are prohibited in that building)
Really great stay! Christina is super friendly and communicative and the place is a steal considering the privacy and how easy it is to get around the city from there.

Staff were ok, except our kids found a gun under the pillow. I’m assuming nobody change the sheets and didn’t check the room before we checked in. I found it very neglectful and that would have been very dangerous for my kids!! Contacted the property and the manager retrieved the gun.

You're getting what you'd expect. A pretty cheap closet in the middle of NYC-- its even smaller than it looks in the pictures. Air conditioning works great, thank goodness. Biggest complaint is the extremely strong smell of weed and old cigarettes in the apartment. You get nose blind to it after a bit, but it hits you again every time you walk in the place and is quite unpleasant. Not the end of the world by any means, but if you are sensitive to that sort of smell this might not be the place to you. Also be aware that although there is wifi, you have to pay $5 a day for it.

Great location, hosts are amazing and very kind. They do their best to keep everything clean. Lots of amenities made my stay stress-free (laundry, good wifi, dishwasher, etc.). I stayed their for a long stay and it felt like home by the time I left.

The location was great and the neighborhood felt very safe to walk around at night. The price was also very reasonable which is why we chose it. The cons are that it is just not very comfortable especially for two people. The room is very small which was not an issue at all because I was expecting that but it was more that we each got one pillow that was very flat. The bathroom trash also stayed full the whole 6 days I was there with peoples waste tissues which made it pretty unpleasant to use the restroom. All in all i definitely don’t think it’s a bad stay as long as you go into it expecting the bare minimum and are not a particular sleeper. The area around it is great so I would recommend it for people who really don’t care about that stuff because it’s super convenient and Karen was a great host!

Location is fantastic. Staff were friendly and helpful. The elevators were a bit scary--made thumping sounds and we were never quite sure if we'd make it up to our floor. The room was kind of dirty; not in a housekeeping way but in a "needs upkeep" kind of way. Walls were stained, particularly grimy around the switch in the bathroom. Tub drain was completely pulled out. But worth it for the location and ease of going to theaters, etc.

Functional accommodation for 2, less functional for 4. Well renovated, cute and clean. However, some equipment is missing. Be careful, old renovated house, you can hear the neighbors upstairs clearly. Owner easily and quickly reachable. Accommodation super well placed to take the ferry, in 10 minutes. The neighborhood can be scary at first, but ultimately no problem.

meh... I mean if you need cheap  NYC. Store at building entrance is very sketchy. Homelesss panhandlers all over. Room is small. Toilet room is very small.  Would not recommend for anyone tall. there is an additional 62$ fee when you get there that is not mentioned.

great space, Perfect location, very friendly host, and a steal at the price ! Will hook again :)  Amir had a Keurig machine as well as some snacks and such in the cabinets as well which made everything feel a bit more home-like as well.  My friend and I loved coming back from the city to this quiet little spot on the north shore of the island !

We loved everything about this place. It's proximity to an accessible subway station was great for us!   It was clean and convenient. Everything you could need is nearby as far as grocery stores and pharmacies go.   The area is a bit sketchy but overall we felt safe inside the house and walking to the subway station.

honestly it's a amazing location and a good price  staff is cool we did find a cockroach in the space and the guy wanted  to change us extra for towels which Airbnb does not allow there is a store downstairs which was very convenient but there are crackheads that hangout outside the entrance to this airbnb  because of the store so it can be a little sketchy walking in and out especially at night my wife did not feel safe walking out of the airbnb by her self the the shower and toilet are shared the toilet is not tall person friendly it a very small room

From the day we got there to the day we left it was sketchy situation.We are artists, photographers, and musicians that travel. We had worked with some other creatives from New York before that we had never met. They stopped by to meet us before we flew out the next day. The owner said he has a policy that we couldn’t have any visitors, I asked what we needed to do he said 25 dollars for each so I sent him 50. They left and a lady we met at a label meeting wanting to be apart of our podcast so we told her she could be apart of it. He called and said we needed to pay for her being there as well. I guess I thought if we spoke maybe he would work with us. She was there 2 mins and I received a call. Also in one of the bathrooms a soap dispenser broke and he wanted 80 dollars for it. My friend said it fell on its own. He has no reason to lie we are grown. Now I admit when we found the place we didn’t know the rules because we just needed a place for a few days to crash in New York and we didn’t look over anything. Enjoyed New York but the owner could have been more understanding, money wasn’t the problem. The problem was feeling like someone is watching your every move. Kinda creepy to be honest.

The instruction to getting in was unclear. I had troubles with the door into the building. There were some homeless people sitting near the entrance, and I didn't feel safe. The bedroom (though it is small), the toilet and the shower were clean, and the place is convenient as it is close to a lot of tourist places and train station. The price is relatively fair given the location. Overall, I think this place is good for the people who travel on budget and just need a short stay in NYC.
Nice and clean rooms, quick response during communication. Having a 7/11 close-by is helpful but also means a lot of homeless people are always near the entrance of the building.

This was a great stay! Everything went so well, and I couldn’t recommend staying here more for the value. One note - it is located next to a 7/11 and I found it to be a bit unsafe at night. If you are traveling solo, just be aware!

This place was exactly as depicted! The room is HUGE! And, yes, it does include a couch. It is located in Parkchester, (got this from a sign at the train station)-"the oldest housing development in the city". The area is actually really nice (in spite all of these rumors and stereotypes you hear about The Bronx), there is greenway that runs parallel to the developments with a fountain in the middle-which has a 24 hour guard posted. If anything this area might be a bit too safe, with some cameras on the block, police patrolling the area. I spoke to the guy at the deli right outside and he told me that everything closes around midnight or 1 to prevent the likelihood of criminal activity occurring, which is a downside because I like 24 hour deli's, but at the same time, good, I guess, for the community? But seriously everything you need is right at your finger tips, with two grocery stores within blocks, one of which is right across the street. The area is super quiet at night, as the people that live in Parkchester are for the most part 9 to 5ers. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a place to stay for a month, as that is what I did. There is a bus that runs right outside to the train station if you don't feel like walking. Tori was also super willing to make this stay great for me in any way. Being as this was my first ever time using Air BNB I didn't know what to expect, so everything I experienced was new. I'm not sure if other Air BNB's are like this, but essentially this was just a place to stay at, during my stay there wasn't a host living in the place. I was fine with this as I was just looking for a place to stay-AKA a room to rent. From what I understood, when Tori isn't around her friend Kenya addresses any issues that are had. She was the one I met to get my keys from. Tori was even so kind as to be willing to negotiate the price of another month when I told her that I was having money troubles. Unfortunately due to said money difficulties I decided not to stay a month, but if I had the opportunity to return I would definitely! Thanks again Tori for opening your place up to me! :)

We enjoyed our stay, the location is amazing and the front desk workers are friendly. However there were a couple issues with this place- the room is very small for the price, and the curtains had a lot of stains which was unpleasant to look at, also the WiFi was really slow. This company just uses Airbnb to list their properties and they made me download a separate app to finish booking and for check in which was a little annoying. Not sure if I would stay at this location again, it’s probably not worth the price.

Ok so first the positive , the room is spacious and just like on the photography, the bed was very comfy , the bathtub had some drainage problems and there is not much space next to the sink to put stuff but it’s fine ,  it’s also very quite which I liked  Ok now the negative, an early check in cost around 100 dollars , bag deposit around 50 dollars , the elevator was not working and believe me it’s creepy to walk down a fire exit stair at 01 am and getting the luggage up without any help 4 flats of stairs was not nice either .

Place was ok. The owner has a dog which is not mentioned in the comments or description but a very polite and calm big dog. Since I am afraid of dogs it was a big shock when I see it lol, but place was very really clean and on a good close and loud location near to Time Square. Host is really nice. He made a gift for us when we was leaving.

Be careful for a potential scam: This Airbnb was “double booked.” I arrived, was given a key, and left my stuff there, and went out in Brooklyn. Shortly thereafter I got a call saying that the place was also rented to another person, and she tried to get me to accept a lower cost, lower quality rental as an alternative (listed at a third of the price — she wanted me to continue to pay the cost of this rental which was about $375 a night). The other people were in the apartment, but my stuff was in there as well. I wouldn’t have had anywhere to stay that night if friends hadn’t helped me. It felt to me like a scam to get me to accept a lower quality, further out, cheaper rental for the same price.

Basement apartment consistent with the photos, and above all very spacious, with plenty of storage: ideal for 4 people. Comfortable beds, air conditioning in all rooms, 2 TVs, no noise, we slept very well. Only downside: the cleanliness of the bathroom. Moldy shower curtain, toilets cleaned quickly and floor not clean. Apart from that the apartment is 3 minutes from the Utica subway which takes you to Manhattan in 30-40 minutes. The neighborhood can be scary but in 10 days we were never bothered, even when we returned late. Very practical small supermarket on the corner of the street. Chaim was very attentive, accommodating and easily reachable. On the last day, he kept our suitcases at his place because new tenants were arriving and our flight was late in the evening. I recommend this apartment for its value for money.
Great Space. Hosts were amazing! Location feels dangerous at night as a young women.

booked in the morning and checked in later around 3, the experience was great. stress free and found a spot to stay so that we could explore on our time whenever. would definitely return in the future if a opportunity arises.

Key wasn't where it was supposed to be (In a little bowl by a bush outside? No lockbox?). The host didn't answer calls from myself or Airbnb support, so we canceled and received a full refund. I was traveling with a toddler and mostly for business, so this situation added unnecessary stress for all of us. I do not recommend booking with BlockStreet.
Be careful with the driving in bad weather in this area of Queens New York very unsafe.

Beth is an amazing host! The apartment is everything she described it to be. Location is perfect. My 13-year-old daughter and I walked around well after dark and never felt unsafe. We were only about a block and a half away from the ferry that took us straight to Wall St., Manhattan in right around 10 minutes.  We enjoyed ourselves so much that we have already booked our next stay so that we can see the area in the summer!

Beth is an amazing host, the communication is clear and easy. Her appartement is located in a beautiful area really well connected to Manhattan in just 10min. The flat itself is well-furnished, clean and has all appliances to feel comfortable and stress-free. I would highly recommend !

Please save yourself money. This company is extremely unprofessional. I was given an unclean apartment which I paid $14000 for 2 months. The rug was dirty, so much so that you could feel it when you take off your shoes.   The toilet seat was cracked in half and they wouldn’t replace it. They tried to get the building maintenance to do it and they refused as they said the company never pays them back. I purchased a new toilet seat. The building maintenance said of all the corporate tenants this company is the worse.   The vents have so much dust around them. The shower curtain was mildewed so bad.   This was by far the worst Airbnb experience in all the years of being a guest and host on this platform. I’d be embarrassed. But they won’t because there is simply no where to stay in nyc.   They literally forced me to rent the space early or they wouldn’t rent to me. Scam.   I’ve heard about experiences such as this but I never had one until this one. This was a company BTW!!! WTF.  RUN!

Everyone drops the ball sometimes, but this situation bordered on dangerous. Navid confirmed my reservation quickly but did not provide information to actually access the apartment. I was in transit and he knew that i would be arriving late at night. I needed to find another place to spend the night at midnight because of this.   I'm thankful that he refunded me a portion of the night I was unable to stay with him, but the amount refunded was roughly 1/5th of the total cost.
The apartment is clean and the owner is welcoming, however the location of the apartment leaves something to be desired. We were afraid to walk the streets...

DO NOT STAY AT THIS PLACE! We made the mistake of booking this apartment after reading the positive reviews and it ruined our family vacation.  First of all the check-in process was a mess. I had to contact the host, who then in turn contacted a friend of her (who did not speak a single word of english). She met us at a different address than the one provided in the ad and then just gave us the keys and left. We had some questions but as she did not speak english those could not be solved.  After our first night we noticed that:  1. The apartment was VERY cold during the night, there was no working heating system 2. There are extremely loud noises coming from the pipes at random times. Sleeping was basically impossible here.  I contacted Kamilla straight away and she wanted to ask her husband how we can turn on the heating unit in the back of the apartment. She wanted to follow up with me which never happened. After the next night (again it was extremely cold and the loud noises made it impossible to sleep more than 2 hours) I once again contacted Kamilla. She said she is trying to solve the problems and I should wait a little. At this point she also lied to us for the first time as she said that the noises are normal because the city of New York changed their heating system. I asked 6 people who I know who live in NYC and all of them said that this is bs and not true. Extreme loud noises from pipes at random times are not normal.   After our 3 and 4 night I kept messaging Kamilla that this really needs to be solved as my mum is feeling extremely unwell because of the lack of sleep and the freezing temperatures. She then claimed to have sent in a technician. When I asked her if he fixed anything she said that she needs to wait for his report and it will take time again. The problems were not fixed as we found out in the next night and she again never followed up with the report of the technician. I kept messaging her and told her that this needs to be solved but she managed to tell me to wait and wait until after stay was over. Our whole family vacation was ruined because of her knowing about these problems, lying to us and then not doing anything to fix it.   After I mentioned to her that we are demanding a refund another very suspicious thing happened. All communication was done through Airbnb up until I asked for a refund. She then sent me a phone number and asked me to call. There I was talking to a guy who told me that he is Kamillas assitant. He told me that we will get a 35% refund and will get it at the 15. of January and that I shall write a positive review. I at first thought that this was legit but as I asked a friend of mine who is more expierenced with Airbnb and also researched on the Internet I found out that this is a common scam. We can't write a review anymore after 14 days so they wanted us to wait just enough so that they can get away with this. After telling Kamilla to process the refund through Airbnb in an official manner she once again told me that it will take time because she has to file her taxes (???).  I am very very sad that I fell for such a scam and that it ruined our family vacation but I at least hope that nobody else will...

Really great value for your money! Clean rooms and shared bathrooms. Location was a 3 minute walk away from MSG. Area is a little sketchy at night especially if you are a woman, but besides that everything was lovely!

Do not go under any circumstances, the worst apartment I have ever been in in my life. The area is far from Manhattan, it is quite dangerous, the streets are very dirty, full of rats and there was a lot of insecurity when returning at night. In the portal there was a homeless man sleeping inside for 3 nights, in addition to the dirt and bad smell of the portal. The photos in the advertisement do not reflect the truth of the apartment, they are taken from angles so that it looks better than it is. The apartment was very dirty, old, full of flies and had an unpleasant smell. The bathroom is very old, the bed is very high and the mattress sinks towards the center. But, if this were not enough, there is a nightclub on the opposite sidewalk with reggaeton music all night at a very high volume that has not let us rest. I have photographs and video of all this and I am going to complain to Airbnb as soon as I arrive in Spain since we wrote to Airbnb via private chat and they did not give us any solution. The only good thing about the site was that the WI-FI connection worked well.

Apartment was very simplistic yet clean. Easy check in. Well equipped kitchen, nice appliances. ( Only 2 individual serving packets of instant coffee) No dressers or night side tables. Hide -a-bed was a rock to sit on & no pillows. It was 90 degrees inside ( no AC) to sleep on mattresses covered in the manufactures plastic! #puddle   Had to sleep With windows open to try to circulate some air and it was noisy and a well traveled street at night.  This neighborhood did NOT feel safe. A Rite Aid was close enough for necessities.  Sketchy people on the street partying, and the smell of pot wifted into our windows from below which was very unpleasant. ( men getting high out in front of the building in the courtyard not a good look to have to expose my daughter to!)

This is a perfect spot! Raymond was incredibly responsive whenever we needed help with anything, and we had a completely stress free stay. Cute little apartment in a great location with lots of restaurants in walking distance and just 5 minutes walk from the A and C subway lines. Highly recommend.

Check in and check out was easy. The freeze, stove and microwave was nice to have. The location was in a good area. Great information how to get there and checking in.  The staff was nice at the front desk.  The down side was there was a lot of cockroaches even with no food left out or garbage was taken out. We made sure it was clean all the time but still a lot in the bathroom and kitchen counter and stove top.  We saw mice multiple times running from under the fridge. When we called to see what they can do for the problem with the mice. They said “if you feel unsafe go ahead and leave”  they did NOT follow up or even come and check. they where rude on the call.    The AC to small for the room. Was really hot with only 5 people in the room. If we did have 7, like it stated  it could accommodate, it would be unbearable.

I loved my stay! It was in a sleepy part of Brooklyn which I had never been to but my local friends told me was a steal. Akino was a wonderful host that was extremely responsive (even when my challenged self couldn’t figure out the locks). Was a little slice of heaven in the city. ❤️
The place is nice. Beautiful !  The host was really nice and helpful. !They helped us to check in early. The neighbourhood is a bit scary in night.

We came for a quiet stay so jimmy did an excellent job  down the street from presumably the only 24 hour bodega in the area  “The super fantastic deli” is truly epic  fantastic staff and made our stay feel welcomed we had such a fun and stress free time really close to LIRR it was easy to get in and out of the area via train and close to a JFK INT. AIRPORT thanks jimmy!

Hasem was very easy to communicate with and always answered questions promptly. The room is the same as in pictures and nice but the building itself was a bit dirty and sketchy- not to the fault of Hasem but the location itself. It was literally right next to ktown which made it easy to travel around.

This place is good to stay at if you want to find a place in NYC to put you luggage in and sleep at the end of a long day of exploring. If you want a luxury experience this isn’t it. Room was very clean but small— good for 1-2 people. It was warm. Had utensils that were clean/newish. Bunk bed is comfortable. Sleeper isn’t.   Things to consider: the elevator has a strong mold smell that worsened my asthma (I think the whole building has mold — the bathroom vent has some mold coming out of it), the halls smell funky, the neighbors are loud and walls are thin (the guy next to me keep on coughing), the halls are sketchy (if you’re not used to NYC apartments), lots of tourists, the host is slow to respond, you only get 2 towels.

For the affordable price this was great place to spend our short trip to NYC. Nice appliances, and I can tell how they keep the place clean. Everything you need for cleaning it is there. Very good quality big bath towels, and all the necessary complementaries are there with extras. Nice balcony with Brooklyn view, bedrooms are comfortable, each room has own AC, TV with wifi connected. Check in was very easy and very good documented with pictures. So you won’t get confuse. The only problem we had was parking, street parkings not much available, and creepy to park nearby streets. Would appreciate if owner had one for an additional fee. Definitely recommend this place to my friends.

This is a lovely condominium in a lively area of Flatbush with good access to public transportation.  For older people or single women, the neighborhood may feel slightly unsafe at night, but we were able to negotiate it all easily and used Lyft and Uber after dark.  The condo is centrally located for people visiting Brooklyn.  There are great TV's with ready access to Hulu, Netflix, Amazon Prime, and YouTube in both bedrooms. The living room and the kitchen is very up to date.  The neighbors in the building were very nice and friendly by NYC standards.  The beds were comfortable.  On the whole, it was a positive experience at a relatively reasonable price.

We definitely recommend this place, our stay here was excellent due to multiple reasons! 1.- Mehmet is such a nice guy! He was really kind during all our stay, treated me and my wife warmly and respectfully. Knowing this was our first time visiting the city he even explain us the basics about how to move using the subway and gave us recommendations about some nearby restaurants and places to the apartment. Most importantly, we experienced a flight cancellation by the airline in the day of our return and Mehmet was really understanding and flexible with us, helping us to make the necessary arrangements to stay one more night. 2.- The apartment was exceptionally clean. The entire place was always clean, our room was spacious enough for two people, the bed and bedsheets were very comfy and it is really safe to leave your stuff there. You can use the kitchen and Mehmet even give you some space on the fridge that you can use to store your groceries (there are grocery stores within a walking distance). A TV with all the channels and streaming services is available at the living room. The bathroom was very clean all the time. 3.- Location. The apartment is about 10 to 15 minutes away from LaGuardia Airport, so it is very convenient if you are flying to this one. Furthermore, Astoria Blvd subway station is really close to the apartment (~10 to 12 minutes walk) and from here, you can go everywhere! Plus, there are multiple deli and coffee shops in the way from the apartment to the station, so is not bad at all. The neighborhood was pretty safe, we walk at late nights and never feel scared or something.

I found this place was a perfect spot away from noisy Manhattan and in a very lively neighborhood with everything at hand. Even if it's your first time in NYC, don't be afraid to book this place as it is close to Dekalb and Knickerbocker subway station and you'll be able to navigate all boroughs. The bedroom is very quiet at night which is a big plus when you play tourist all day long. Finally you'll get to visit Bushwick, which you would maybe not do if you were staying closer to the city.

The place was not at all what I expected.  Sure it was a cheaper Airbnb but the place smelled like cigarettes and alcohol.  There was so much trash lying around in the entrance area that it reminded me of a college dorm. The horrible smell crept into the bedroom at night and it was really hard to fall asleep.  The bathroom is located in a different house with no handsoap or body soap. Walking downstairs into that basement for the bathroom feels scary.  Towels were provided. Travis was very responsive to texts even at night.  I wouldn't pay anything more than $30 a night for this place.  For the amount I paid,  I expected basic cleanliness.

Hi, Since you've insisted so much I must say the Appartement does exactly what it says on the tin, except for the missing massage chair, that was announced on the house description. If you don't have it, don't mention it. As you certainly agree, it's a matter of honesty. About the proximity to the subway, laundromat, and grocery store, it couldn't be better. The area can be a little scary for easily impressed people, considering the activity around, especially at night. With daylight, it's fine and pittoresque, in spite of the almost constant police presence. I've to confess I don't like much being pounded with emails about the same, especially when on holiday. After all, it is my prerogative whether to rate the house or not. Considering the amount paid, 4 start is certainly fair. PS: As you've said this is a family business, hence the name "Opulence Oasis" is not only very impersonal but a bit Las Vegish too. Just a thought.

Overall great stay and definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a good valued room in nyc! The room was clean. The check-in process was super easy. The location is very central to Manhattan, however, the block itself where the building is located is a little sketchy, especially at night. Also, just be aware that this is a hostel-style accommodation, so you'll be sharing bathrooms with other guests.

Room was very clean and comfortable. The toilet and shower are shared but were always clean and accessible, we never had to wait for other guests. If you are local, or driving from nearby, the free parking is very hard to find, so plan to pay for parking. The room was a minutes walk to the NYC metro, so you can access any and all locations with ease. So many amenities are next to this location, so don't stress if you forget a toothbrush or need late night snacks! Great value in NYC which is usually VERY expensive to stay.

Great location! Pack light because it is the size of what you would expect in New York City. Extremely clean especially for sharing bathrooms and showers with other guests. No one comes to New York to stay in their rooms, so it was exactly what we needed. Bring a sound machine because the City noises are no joke! We also never felt unsafe. And it was very convenient to have the seven eleven right next door!

Steven at the front desk was extremely helpful and welcoming that was the best part of my stay. Rooms are small but they are enough if you're planning spending your time in the city. The bathrooms also pretty small but they were always well maintained and clean.  The City noises are no joke! If you can’t sleep with noise I should recommend you to find other place, the room has earplugs but they are not enough! Great location, it was very convenient to have the seven eleven right next door and the subway so close, we never felt unsafe.  If you are driving, the free parking is very hard to find, so keep that in mind you have to pay for parking. Also be prepared to pay more when you arrived for NY city taxes I pay 55 dollars extra. Even with that I would 100% recommend this rooms to anyone looking for a cheap place to stay in the city.   Also communication was absolutely perfect, I forgot a hoodie and they sent it back to me, thank you so much!

The management of this place is extremely unprofessional. When we checked in, they demanded us to pay an arbitrary amount for taxes and fees, which is quite standard for NYC hotels. However, they did not mention this on their listing or informed us prior to check-in. When we tried to explain that any taxes to be paid at check in should be clearly stated in the listing prior to booking, they started to argue and curse us out lol super unprofessional. They immediately modified the listing to avoid facing consequences with Airbnb and even tried to kick us out of the building on a winter day. The place is located on a sketchy block. There is only one tiny bathroom shared with a bunch of other people, which is not clearly described in the listing either. There are better places. Avoid this!

Good rooms in a good area for a good price.  The room I got looked exactly like the photo, though my room did not have a safe. Make sure you look closely and are fine with things like no television, no place to sit in the room aside from the bed, and a shared bathroom&shower.  The Pros: The Location - This place is a short walk away from some great locations. There is a 7-11 directly next door and this can both a gift and a curse as I will explain under the “cons” list below.  The Staff - I didn’t get to meet the owner but the staff were very warm and friendly. Everyone from the guy at the desk to the cleaning woman were top notch and always available.  The Value - if you’re just looking for a place to hang your hat at the end of the night while traveling this is a great place at a great price. It’s right next to penn station, you can’t beat it.  The Cons: Location - like I mentioned, this place is next door to a 7-11. If you plan on leaving anytime after dark, you will have to go in and out next to a group of… homeless? I don’t know their specific living situations, and in my experience they were all actually really nice — though I wouldn’t have let my wife go downstairs alone after dark if she’d come on this trip. The folks I met when going downstairs for a cigarette were polite, not pushy, and mostly minded their business - though I don’t know who you might meet, how drunk they might be, or how they might react when you tell them you don’t have any change.  I don’t fault the owners for this, there is little they can do as this is a free country and there is a store directly next door/under you — but it is what it is, and I would accompany anyone that wanted to leave after dark.  The Meat Clause - In truly bizarre eccentric NYC fashion there is a clause in the rental agreement asking you not to bring meat onto the premises. They are a vegetarian establishment, and think it’s important enough to maybe throw you out over — but not important enough to put in the listing so customers can make an informed decision before being surprised with this during check-in.  I like to play devils advocate, so I thought deeply on this one for a few days. I can definitely understand a vegetarian owners position of discovering rooms smelling like BBQ or steaks on checkout and feeling sick to your stomach over it — but at the same time, that’s what the customer is paying you for. They’re paying for use of the room, so it isn’t yours anymore, it’s why you’re being compensated. Where is the limit on this? If the owner only likes a certain ethnicity of women would that be the only kind I could bring to my room? Why should the owners preferences matter to me one bit? They absolutely don’t and it’s a totally bizarre request. Of course you aren’t going to like the smells people leave, but it’s why you’re compensated for crying out loud. This situation reeks of “I inherited a hotel and I’ll do whatever I please”, regardless of if it makes sense for any sort of business, let alone hospitality.  I’ve had a fairly good experience with Airbnb as far as “what the listing says is exactly what you get” until now. This room has me wondering if I should message the next host I book and ask if there is anything bizarre they leave out of the listing.  The owner was on vacation when so visited so I didn’t get to ask him about this — which is probably good as a few other reviewers mentioned he sometimes gets into shouting matches with customers and as a native New Yorker I likely would have shouted back and likely gotten kicked out.  Never in all my days have I had a hospitality owner tell me what I could eat on premise, totally bizarre and I can’t believe no other reviewer had mentioned it. I didn’t deduct many stars for this but I just can’t get over how strange it is.

Lisa and James were the perfect hosts, and this apartment more than exceeded our expectations! It’s incredibly clean and cozy, smells wonderful and has all the amenities that we needed. They provide cookware, dishes, silverware, salt & pepper, a coffee station with various sweeteners and creamer, soap, shampoo, toothpaste, mouthwash, bottled water and more. We did a small Instacart order for groceries and we had everything we needed for our 6 day stay in NYC!   It’s about a 0.3 mile (8 minute) walk to the subway and very close to 2 bus stops. It does take about 30-45 min or so to get into Manhattan using public transportation, but it was worth it for us to have a home to go back to, rather than a hotel or one room apartment. We never felt unsafe walking to and from the subway, even though it was just my teenage daughter and myself. It’s a lovely neighborhood. We will absolutely be staying here on our next trip!

we really loved Lisa’s apartment and all the amenities she kept for us. It was overall a great stay.   Lisa surprised us with a very thoughtful welcome gift. The apartment had everything for a family traveling across the country. It was clean and looks lovely just like in the pictures.   The area around the apartment is perfect during day time but we felt a bit shady when we walked from the Rockaway Ave subway station back home after 10 when we finished our sightseeing.
It's a scam

This location is not in a safe area whatsoever to begin with, people right outside of the house dealing and doing drugs. This place can fit 4 guest max comfortably, otherwise its an couch in the living room that is super crammed up, Host will watch cameras and follow up the entire time you’re there, they live right below the apartment, you can hear the host singing and moving around the house in the morning In Case you’re looking to get some rest In the morning. All the canners In the house are zip-tied, do not touch anything in the refrigerator (vendor machine) because everything is for sale. No proper trash cans in the house just utility buckets under the sink. Worst place rented on this app so far. Do not recommend!

Easy check in and check out. Joseph is there if you need him for anything. The bed is firm and comfy. The AC keeps you cool.  In the kitchen theres pans, plates, everything you need to make a meal, even oil, salt and pepper. CVS and grocery a block away. The train to Broad Channel Station, A line, that leads you into NYC, is just a few steps away! The beach is very close  location itself felt a little unsafe at night, but isn't actually (checked crime reports).  I'm new to New York so maybe it's like that everywhere. what I really liked were the chairs right outside the apartment, it's great to sit there, drink some tea, read, hear the wind and and the birds. Thanks for the stay Joseph.

Be very careful if you decide to stay here.  There are no pictures of the outside for a reason.   The neighborhood is unsafe and you will constantly hear sirens and gunshots.  For your safety, stay away from this place.

I read that the neighborhood was sketchy but we actually had no problems at all and everyone around was nice. Very short walk to the closest train station so we didn't have to move our cars at all. The house was very clean and spacious.

This Airbnb served its purpose of a family reunion (meeting in NYC with international travelers).   It was convenient for public transit, grocery shopping, and basic restaurants in the area. It fit our budget in comparison to other places as well.   The property has the essentials- beds, furniture, bathroom, etc. Nothing over-the-top, however nonetheless a decent/clean place for the area.   The area does leave much to be desired, as were a bit guarded in walking around and also leaving my vehicle unattended parked on the street.   Aside from the sketchy area, overall it was a nice time. You get what you pay for, and I feel this fit our budget and needs for our trip.

The apartment is very clean. modern and up to date.  The bedrooms are roomy.  We had 10 people in the apartment and we never felt crowded.  It was also very nice to have two full bathrooms.  The neighborhood appeared very sketchy at first sight and yet once we were there, walking home from the subways from the city, we never felt unsafe or threatened.  Subway entrances were only a block or two away.  It can be a long commute from Manhattan, but as with everything else in New York, that can change depending on the time of the day.  Price is very reasonable.

Let me start by saying, the host was amazing with checking us in and etc. However, the pictures don’t even match up to the entire experience. When you walk you walk up to the place, you’re kinda thrown off because it’s located on top of a day care. We weren’t able to check in at 3 because of our busy schedules so we came in that night and it felt unsafe. When we finally came in, it was like “decent” if you’re wanting that Brooklyn type stay. However, we stuck it through because it was the 9th hour. I was very upset to find multiple bugs crawling around and roaches. I felt like an expensive stay like that, the place should be “immaculate”

Pros: *close to JFK airport *spacious (as advertised)  *very responsive host  *neighborhood was accessible to subway, bus to JFK, wasn’t far from shopping, etc. the street offered a Bodega and some good food!  we arrived late to check in and as others noted, it can be pretty disconcerting to be in that neighborhood but I’ll note once we got inside, I felt safe. Also we stood outside for more than 5 minutes trying to figure out which gate and such and no one bothered us or even paid attention. It was high traffic area but folk were minding their own business. All of that to say, it’s New York and I think most of what you experience on the outside of the apartment is culturally true for Brooklyn and not that you are in a dangerous place.   With that said, as everyone has noted and in the description, the street noise is LOUD. If you’re a light sleeper or feeling scared, you’ll likely not sleep well. Interestingly the first night felt like full activity with sirens every hour and car horns and big vehicles zooming next to us, but the second night the street was quieter.   Things to note: these were cons for us but may not be for you.   *access to apartment is up a very narrow steep flight of stairs.  We were on a quick layover in NY from a week in Northern Europe and heading back to Caribbean so we had a million bags because of clothes needed for our prior vacation.  We also had a senior citizen with us who can walk but has significant knee challenges. Had I know about the flight of stairs, for both these reasons, I wouldn’t have booked so I thought to share because I don’t recall seeing it anywhere in the description.   *window units for cooling the apartment. The first of our group got in the apartment at 9:15 and proceeded to turn on all a/c because it was steaming hot in there. The general area didn’t get “cool” until 1am. Rooms cooled by 11. Some of the ceiling fans work, some don’t. I reached out to the hosts whose main point to me was that “no one else complained” and their a/cs are "working". I had to concede that this is true, they do turn on and blow air but the reality is that they are not strong enough to cool the spaces even within an 1-1.5 hour timeframe of cooling. It's pretty warm this time of year, heat rises and this is upstairs and window units are the least effective for cooling. For example, the temp  setting on the  a/c  in the sitting area says 60 degrees and if I stand directly in the front of it, I feel 60 degrees. If I sit at the table right next to it, not with the air blowing directly on me, at 9.30am (literally 12 hours since it was first turned on), I felt about 70ish degrees…not warm but not 60 degrees as would be the case for ductless or central air. The fan isn't working in main sitting area (maintenance guy checked it) so that adds to the limited circulation of the cold air.   *the wifi is pretty crappy and as non-Americans, we rely heavily on wifi for communicating. Even in room 2, the person has to come outside the door for a strong signal. Room 4, there is no wifi signal at all.   When we arrived our bed was broken but maintenance fixed it quickly and the sofa bed is broken and an air mattress was offered. Two members from our booking ended up leaving to stay in a hotel because the air mattress was not going to work and after an extremely loooong travel day, having to lay in a hot room was not up to their standard. There was no option for even a partial refund so the rest of the group remained and all in all it was okay for the quick 2 night, maybe 36 hours layover we had in New York.  Would I come back?  Ehhh I’m not sure. I think most of our issues were specific to our group not that it was a bad place so given that, even as a 100% proponent of the airbnb market (I’m a host myself), I’d likely opt for a hotel, even with a large group and split up in rooms which would likely double the cost.

Hady’s place was even better then the pictures the place so clean which was great. Few issues before arriving the host notified us that the city was working on a gas leak that will cause us not to have hot water. He said it should be fixed that same day turns out we were without hot water the entire trip we were there for four days. The host refunded us for two nights I understand that was out of his control but this made our stay a bit stressful as it was cold out. We were told to boil water which we did but still wasn’t enough. We also had an issue with the stove could not get it to work at all the owner had to come take a look turns out the stove plates don’t take metal pans. We were provided with a few cast iron pans. One last thing not that big of a deal because no one lived downstairs or they just weren’t home for our stay.   The way they have the living room was odd the whole upstairs was open no door separating the downstairs so if someone did in fact live downstairs they can easily come up to our space with all our belongings there. Since no one appeared to be downstairs it’s was fine. Perhaps putting a door in the kitchen will make guests feel more safe.  I do believe the house was converted to make two separate spaces when it’s supposed to be one.  All that being said my family and I had everything we needed and the host was very responsive I would stay there again if the hot water issue was to never happen again and no one is home downstairs.

Radeisha was hands down the best host I've ever interacted with. Visited NY to host a surprise birthday dinner for my boyfriend with all of his friends so my stress levels were high. She was very accommodating, had a fast response time, and was very informative of the general inquiries that I had. I love the entire vibe of Queens, so this will definitely be a go to Air BnB when I return🤍🌸🙏🏽   Thanks again Radeisha for helping our trip be an overall success and contributing to another great memory for my friends and I!

Located right in the hustle and bustle of Manhattan. Walking distance to many things including Madison Square Garden 😊 rooms are small but it is New York…sometimes sketchy people were outside the main door but that was noted all over Manhattan. Overall enjoyed the stay 😊

I was unable to actually attend my reservation due to a COVID-19 scare. Chris was very polite in our communication before booking and after I found out about the potential exposure.  Unfortunately, I was not refunded for my booking seeing as it was less than 24-hour notice. However, that was not something I could control -- I received the call notifying me of the exposure at 6 am on the morning I was meant to check in. :(  Chris has offered me a future stay at this location with a discount which is nice but I wish I could get refunded.

I tried to ignore the things that were not up to my expectations when I arrived, like the confusion over the parking space (the driveway is apparently not open to guests?) and the general lack of clean space (though there was no cleaning fee, I expected they'd at least wipe down the space because of covid; I was prepared with my own cleaning supplies because I'm paranoid about getting sick). But then confusion over the parking space lead to an altercation with one of the neighbors who blocked me into the driveway and tried to argue with me about my face as if I was trying to start a fight with him. When I tried to discuss the incident with the host, she dismissed my side of the story and said I needed to control my emotions after I admitted that I was having an awful day due to a suicide of a close friend. Basically, seemed like a nice place that I could tolerate because I'm from the BX and don't mind sharing space with people, but that was the last straw of a shitty stay that left me feeling unsafe and caused me to leave my reservation a day early.

We stayed at Pettrina's for 12 nights. The accommodation was exactly as described. It was clean, tidy and there were new towels and fresh bed linen every week. Communication with Pettrina was very good. There was always someone in the house who you could talk to if you had any questions. The room is quite small for two people, but completely sufficient for overnight stays. The price-performance ratio is definitely great! We had our own key and could therefore come and go at any time. The neighborhood in which the accommodation is located is less attractive than the accommodation itself. However, we never felt unsafe there. The immediate proximity to the subway is great. Pettrina and her family are warm, lovely people who really made us feel very comfortable.

Manuel's place was perfect for us. We were three adults and a 4 1/2 year old child and we all had plenty of room and space. What we liked most was the dining room table that can easily seat 6. The kitchen was very well furnished - had everything! The place was ultra-clean and comfortable. There was even an area for the child to play (Manuel supplied the books, toys, etc) The location is very cose to everything in the neighborhood - especially Prospect Park West which has all the restaurants, bars, pizza, coffee and bakeries one could ask for. Very close walk to Prospect Park, subway and the Nitehawk Theater - if you have never been to the Nitehawk it is awesome. Right across the street from Manuel's is the most unbelieveable, small market. It is privately run, and looks small from the outside but is actually quite big and has everything under the sun including an amazing meat deli department.  Also a drug store. The neighborhood is very residential and friendly. We will return!
Very responsive host, nice clean modern interior. Noisy neighbors. Kind of scary neighborhood. No decent restaurants within walking distance.

The room is small but comfortable, the heating works well, it just makes a noise all night. I never felt unsafe on the streets (I only went from the Airbnb to the subway) but in the early mornings you could hear people arguing and ambulances or the police on the street. I had understood that the bathroom was private since that is what the advertisement mentioned, but it was shared. In general, the cleanliness was good, the room was comfortable, Lidia was a very good person, she made me feel at ease.
This is a clean and stress free place to stay in Brooklyn. With a parking spot and enough space for a family.

Is it rust? I was concerned about the sink being dirty. The rest is very clean. The response time is also very fast. However, I couldn't sleep because of the loud music coming from other houses until midnight. I used the subway, but it was very scary and I felt unsafe. However, it may not be a problem for people who are used to traveling.

What we liked: - Communication with Brandyce which was quite easy. - Quality of bed and bedsheets : going to bed was a real pleasure especially after a long walk in NY😊 - There are plenty of cleaned towels and bedsheets which we appreciated.  What we disliked: - Check in conditions : key box not located in the building was a bit confusing.  - Strict instructions : found it stressful  - Lack of ustensiles : only one glass, one knife and one fock except plastic ones.  - Cofee machine did not work 😔

Living at this residence was just great! The room was sizeable and the walk-in wardrobe was massive! Sofia and her mum were lovely, and her mum was really friendly, sharing with me good places in the area and sites in the city for my first visit to NYC! If you're worried about safety (as I was), I am happy to share that the neighbourhood is rather safe and I did return past midnight for a couple of days and it was perfectly safe (as a matter of fact, I had a few unpleasant encounters in Manhattan - Times Square area towards the night, and it was all okay in The Bronx). The apartment is a short train ride to Manhattan.

Crystal was super nice and her place was incredibly clean however we did have a scare our first night with an unknown additional guest in the apartment we weren’t told about the other guest. Also should be noted sometimes bathroom is not available for 2 hours at a time due to massage clients coming in which we weren’t aware would be a rule. All in all not a bad stay a very sweet host.

Aubrey is super responsive. The property is delightfully designed with a wonderful fully equipped kitchen, a small but workable bathroom, and comfortable bedroom-sitting room combination. Security quite good with keyed gate and electronic interior door lock. Location great in hip Bed-Stey neighborhood with cool bars, cafes, coffee shops. The only blemish was dirty dishes in dishwasher and full recycled can receptacle upon our arrival. Suspect these are rare oversights for these hosts.  There is access to back garden that could  be a fabulous amenity. We already have plans to stay here again.
a wonderful host. perfect, low stress stay.

Loren and Ronald are a lovely couple who do actually live in the home.The room isn't particularly large, but larger than some and is nicely set up with a desk and plenty of hooks and a coat stand. Since they only host the one bedroom and have their own bathroom you have a wonderfully clean bathroom all to yourself, plus use of a kitchen, it's a steal for the price. Ronald also helped me carry my luggage up the stairs and even ran down the block to save a parking spot for me. College  Point isn't one of the prettiest spots in Queens, but I grew up in neighboring Flushing, and it has always been considered a safe area. There are also buses that run in front of the house, fairly frequently, 24/7. The house itself is quite peaceful, painted in soothing colors and tastefully decorated, in an uncluttered way. Loren even offered to extend my checkout time when I got a call from my doctor's office trying to set up a teleconference about test results. I'd definitely stay there again!

The place is very clean, and the neighborhood is safe , I was  afraid to parking my car , but they are plenty parking  around ,but thank God we found parking front the house ever 🙏🏼 . I recommend it property ever 100%   Ernesto Morales Miami, Florida

A wonderful and memorable stay with my son, memories that will last a lifetime. The room was so clean and perfect for our quick stay in NYC. The location and check-in were perfect, with access to everything! Chris was readily available prior to our stay to ask questions and made the whole process stress free. Highly recommend it and would definitely come back to stay! Thank you Chris!

Host had very good communication. Check in was very easy. Street parking was convenient. There were plenty of extra things in the house we appreciated. The only reason I can give any bad review is the upstairs neighbors. We were woke up both nights around 3 am to screaming, banging, loud music, running up and down the steps. At one point they were banging on our door which scared my daughter who was sleeping on the couch. We had to just leave about 4 hours early on our check out date because it was just to uncomfortable. I did contact the host and he was understanding but at that point we were exhausted and just wanted away from the party.

Eufemia was very kind, very communicative and easy to reach.   This room is upstairs, behind a curtain at the top of a slim set of metal stairs. My assumption is that this part of the house was built with the intention of being some sort of storage area, based on the layout.   As stated in the listing - it’s a crash spot. For clarification, it’s a twin bed behind a curtain covering where a door would be had the room been built with the intention of being an actual bedroom.   Pros :   Affordable, off of the bus line, not too far from a train line. Neighborhood seems to be safe and I never had any issues over two days in which I felt unsafe.   Cons : I couldn’t figure out how many people actually lived there full time, but there seemed to be a somewhat present buzz about the place of 1 - 3 people on their phones during the day (the 2nd morning consisted of someone on speaker phone for a few hours) and some kind of dancehall/reggaeton music playing on the living room tv most of the time. Neither of these things were loud by any means, but again - you’re in a “room” behind a curtain. Translation - you hear everything.   Did this bother me? No. Could it bother more uptight types? Possibly. But if this is a point of complaint for you, suck it up and pay more for something else.   Be aware of how the MTA functions before booking this room. This is off of a bus line, which you need to take a little ways to get on a train. I’m pretty low-maintenance so I don’t care, but someone may be bothered by having to stand outside, etc etc.   OVERALL, I would book again. I got exactly what I paid for and I don’t have complaints.

The apartment is on the fourth floor, the building is old and dirty, the neighborhood is dangerous but it is close to a metro stop, at night there is a lot of noise and the adjacent buildings are under construction.

The neighborhood was a little sketchy.   Several residents sit on there front steps smoking marijuana and playing loud music in the evening.   Room is on the 4th floor and no elevator.
