If you have lots of luggage or traveling with someone who has a hard time climbing stairs, this is not the place do you.  The room was clean, the owner was very nice and responded right away to all my messages.

I contacted the host to make sure a later check-in time was okay & she was sweet to accommodate. However, when I got there, there were no keys in the lock box so I had to wait outside. Once I was let inside, my actual room door was locked and couldn’t get inside that. I was definitely annoyed, but other than that, I had no problems. Location isn’t too bad, emphasis on the too (we had a scary situation our first night in which my boyfriend was chased) It was farther from a working subway station than I anticipated so going to & from Manhattan took over an hour. At night, we felt safest to just Uber which made me spend extra $$. The house itself was great! All things considered, i think I’ll pay more to find a convenient place tho :)

04/01/04.We got there after 6 pm someone was there to give us the keys home is very tidy clean very welcoming our room was big enough space we had no problems with location because we had our suv but you definitely needs your own transportation.We did had some issues which i didn't address with them because i didn't really see a number for the host it could be over look on my part but i didn't see a actual number okay the curtain on the front windows where i stayed in you can see through to the sky cars road everything through the curtain that was not too private secondly the temperature that room was freezing no heat Friday night was not too bad Saturday and Sunday night when the temperature drop we where freezing in that room make it uncomfortable  for us to sleep sheets on bed spred we where covering with was cold and kind of silky no heat to turn on or off,  the man next to our room speaks a different language very loud early in the morning smh our experience was a very unpleasant and uncomfortable you gets whats you paid for i guess cheap comes with a price wouldn't want to experience that situation again.

This is the information I just left for Xie in my message to them. If I could attach pictures, you’d be able to see for yourself.   You advertised your place as clean and it was no where near clean. The bed had hair on it before I ever sat on it. I have sister alocs so there’s no way that was from me or my fiancé. The dresser and tv had dirt on them and the inside of the dresser had items. There were mice/bug traps everywhere, the A/C in the window was filled with dirt, the baseboards were filthy in the room and bathroom and the decorative pillows had someone’s make up stains on the back, but you had them on the bed that had the hair on it… I was disgusted and I tried to find another place to stay, but due to Fashion Week and the anniversary of 9/11 everyone was booked. My fiancé and I changed the bed, sprayed with Lysol before putting on new sheets and cleaned your bedroom 1 as best we could which was not our job.   The rug in room 1 looks very old and like it needed to be cleaned and/or thrown out.   Your other tenants also didn’t make sure the front door was closed several times and I felt that was unsafe for times when I was there alone.  I have never seen such carelessness in Air BnBs I’ve stayed in and there’s no way we’d ever attempt to stay there again… there are too many viruses running around for that and even if there weren’t you should have more pride in cleaning your unit better. Room 1 was unacceptable and I’m still frustrated by the experience.
Room was clean and bed was made. Shared space was small but adequate. Sketchy neighborhood but to be expected

Host wasn’t clear stating someone else actually lives in the house. When phone was answered it was picked up in a rude obnoxious way. When host was asked if he was “there” he said yes but never announced someone actually fully LIVED there. Host also opened the room door after closing room door which is very unsafe! No privacy here super unsafe especially for couple to have alone time.

My husband and I visited for a weekend. The apartment was exactly as pictured. Very clean, full kitchen, everything you need.  Alex and Shaila were super helpful and even made our last day stress free by allowing us to keep our bags there after checkout due to our late flight out. Would definitely recommend.

We went to NYC for the first time and this was a great place to stay. I would say if you are wanting to spend the majority of your time in Manhattan you’ll want to get familiar with the subway because Ubers really start to add up from this location to Manhattan. The hosts were very accommodating and communicated well. Checkin/out was easy, she had everything clearly written out so it was easy to follow. For not being familiar with New York everything can be a bit scary but we felt safe and secure in this air bnb. It also was really spacious so that was nice too!

The great thing about the apartment is the location, which is perfect if you are in NY for work or leisure. But it is a 4 floor walk up with 17 steps for each floor. You have to travel light.  On the other hand, I was unhappy with the hosting. After an 8 hour flight from London I arrived at JFK with a message from Marina that she was in Miami...When I got to Marina's apartment, having to discover where the keys were hidden, I was faced with an impaired key lock. I could not get in as the lock's cylinder tilted. After a while, with Marina on the phone, the door finally opened but I was unable to lock the door again. So, I was afraid to leave the door unlocked and leave the apartment unprotected. After two hours of my arrival the super showed up and fixed the problem. However, it was a stressful start. The other problem was that the apartment was not cleaned up before my arrival. Not even the bed sheets were changed, with the usual marks out there to my astonishment. I had to look for clean sheets in Marina's apartment...Probably Marina left to Miami and did not check if her house-cleaner had done the work before my arrival. I have checked the reviews of Marina as a host and they seemed good.  Unfortunately, I did not have the same experience and it makes all the difference. For a guest, being able to get the keys, be introduced to the apartment, move into a clean room with clean sheets is a host's most basic responsibility. So Marina was not nice to me...and the price I paid definitely did not match what I have got.

Margo and her husband Vipin are always very attentive and concerned.  We had heating problems with the main room, we think it could become a major problem closer to winter, they gave us a heater to solve it. The location is very good, just two blocks from the subway and it connects to the main stations. The house is very well equipped, which is a great saving since you can cook and wash there. I think the neighborhood is somewhat dark, it gives the feeling of danger although we did not experience any situation that would cause us problems, but it is to be protected at least. Given that, I think the price is overvalued, just because of the sector.

Carlos is a gentleman, discreet, very polite and silent. Your suggestions and directions were excellent. Harlem still has a certain mystery and appearance as a dangerous place. But, in fact, we didn't have any problems of the kind, the metro is very close and is covered by express lines, which is a relief at the end of several long days of walks/tours. The duck is clean and tasteful. Ideal for 4 days/1 week.

Carlos wonderful person! Very friendly and always explained everything to us. We also liked the room, very nice and comfortable. Apartment located near the metro, but nightfall we were a little scared to go back to room, maybe district did not cause us confidence for some reason. And probably the only negative - it's noise. Windows are not soundproof, and hard to open. But everything else was great! Clean, comfortable, nice room and pleasant host :)

Carlos' place is easy to find and it's conveniently close to the subway. For someone who had never travelled in the States  the Harlem neighbourhood looked a bit sketchy at first. But it was actually fine.  Carlos himself is a relaxed and very friendly guy, so for me the perfect host.

My wife and I stayed at Carlos place for 4 days, we had a wonderful stay here. His apartment is very nice and our room made us feel right at home. The AC unit worked great, the bed was comfy, and it proved a very comfortable sleep each night.  Carlos was fantastic. We got in late (3am) and didn't manage to get to the apartment to nearer 4am, I communiated with Carlos and he was still willing and happy to let us in at such an early hour!  The area - fine in the morning, we would walk to the subway which was just a 2 minute walk around the corner. Very convenient! However in the evening time we would always taxi it back as there was always a few sketchy looking people that were around hanging around outside.  The location is great though, a short 10 minute subway to Times Square, and just a 15-20 minute cab right.  Would highly recommend staying here, especially for the price!  Will stay here again no problem if we return to New York in the future.

We had a very good experience. It was the first time we traveled through Airbnb, we were a little reluctant, but we ended up surprised. Carlos is super friendly, very discreet and attentive. The house is very cozy and warm. He always made us feel at ease. He gave us some good advice on where to go for a walk and recommended some restaurants. Harlem is a neighborhood that, at first impression, brings some respect, but in the end we realize that it is super quiet. We didn't have any unpleasant adventures, quite the opposite, the people we talked to were always very attentive and it was even cool to see how people live in a typical New York neighborhood. The subway line two streets down also makes your stay much easier. We spoke to Carlos about delaying Check Out, and he was super available. We left the house at 4pm, which allowed us to make the most of the last day of the trip. We recommend.

Everything great. The room is just as in the photo, metro stop 5 minutes away and very well connected to places of interest and Carlos was great with us at all times. We found the neighborhood at night a little unsafe, but perhaps it's just an impression, we didn't have any problems and we were delighted with our stay. We would repeat.

We found the apartment as described on the site, simple but sufficient. Located in Harlem certainly, but no feeling of insecurity, even at night.  Carlos' welcome is sober but friendly. We really appreciated the fact that he was very discreet and was not stingy in giving us information on visits, places to walk as well as places to eat or have a drink. The geographical location is a little far from the center of Manhattan but that did not bother us because it is only a few steps to reach the subway and about twenty minutes later we are there. We had a great stay and would be willing to come back. Many thanks to Carlos. Pascale.

This is the second time we have stayed with Carlos and it will certainly not be the last.  He is a great host and was very helpfull, giving us various Restaurant and Bar suggestions. We tried some of them and the were really good: Kitchenette (for Breakfast/Brunch) and Dinosaur (BBQ southern style cuisine).  I was on a visit to NY as I had a concert with a local band in the Lower East side of the city, I invited Carlos to the gig after a long conversation about music and the current scene in NY. To my surprise, he turned up to the show!  This just shows how nice and cool Carlos is.  With regards to the appartment, it is immaculate. The room is spacious enough for 2 people, with a big double chest of drawers, a wardrobe and with plenty of space in the room and under the bed to store your luggage during the stay so it is not in the way. TV, wifi and plenty of light on tap if needed.  The appartment is only a 3 minute walk to the Subway station, it is 125th street but there is a very convenient entrance on 127th that you will get to know. The "A" train is an express one that takes around 10 minutes to get to central NY (59th, 42nd, 34th streets) and it is a time saver compared to the Local trains. But note that from 125th street it does not stop until 59th, so if you have plans on the West Side of Central Park, just grab a local train.  I have read some reviews stating that the neighbourhood seemed dangerous and unsafe. My thoughts are that if you have not lived in a cosmopolitan city and/or you are not used to sharing your space with other racial profiles you may be uncorfortable in New York itself.  On the other side, I live in London (UK) and I was completely fine, love NY!. We meet lovely people on our street, next to the park were a lot of children play basketball (St. Nicholas Terrace); the guys at the Deli were friendly; I had to go to the laundrette on Carlos's street and the lady was super sweet and very helpfull too.  All in all, a great experience and I would not hesitate to stay again and/or suggest to my friends Carlos' appartment.  Great host, lovely flat and extremely well connected transport wise.

Can't say enough about Liza's great responsiveness. We had a flight delay and she provided amended check-in instructions so there was no stress upon our arrival. She also replied quickly to questions and inquiries. And the location can't be beat! The apartment is one block to the subway and there are also terrific neighborhood amenities within several blocks -- restaurants, coffee shops, bakeries, book shops, shopping, bars, and more!

A wonderful experience I had to look for a place to stay in one of the most expensive cities in the world, NYC. It had several requirements: economical, central, safe and above all clean. Finding a hotel was impossible, nor a complete apartment, you had to stay in a room and share with the owner of the place. It was my 15 year old niece and I, 2 women. The first ones searched on Airbnb in areas I knew of in Lower and Middle Manhattan were not available. Then Harlem appeared, which sounded dangerous to me, where blacks, Hispanics and many others live (I had no problem with that part, I'm Hispanic and Puerto Rican). In addition to all this, I was going to share the apartment with a man I didn't know, but after several messages with him, I rented it for a week and it was an excellent decision. The neighborhood is mixed, meaning you see people from all over, black, Hispanic, American and many other places, 2 universities nearby. Some may seem intimidating, you don't mess with them, they don't mess with you. I carried it several times in the middle of the night, always alert, but without any problems. The 125 station is excellent, it is a main stop. There is Express Line A and in 2 stops you are in Times Square or you can use the B/C location. It is important to look for the exit and entrance of the station on 127th St, which is the closest to the apartment 3 blocks away. At night when you get off the train try to get on with other people, otherwise it's lonely. But nothing happens as soon as you leave there is a French bistro in front, very busy. Deli and Super nearby, laundry 1 min. The apt was in perfect condition, clean, kitchen, bathroom and bedroom, excellent bed, air conditioning. We use facilities without problem. Carlos was an excellent host, a polite, familiar, respectful man with excellent conversation. We come back and we have a new friend. Thank you Carlos, we are waiting for you in Puerto Rico. Wonderfull Experience I had to find a cheap place in NYC to stay, which would have several requirements: economic, central, safe and above all clean. She was an adult ME and my youngest niece for whom I had to care. I started my search on Airbnb and there were multiple options, some not very reliable but in well-known areas of the city by me like Lower and Middle Manhattan. The 3 that you selected were not available and others did not seem to have the requirements you wanted. Until this room appeared in Harlem. If Harlem where it sounds dangerous, where blacks, Hispanics and many others live (I had no problem with that part I am Hispanic and Puerto Rican) but I did not stop worrying, it would also be the first time I shared an apartment and besides being 2 women with A man we did not know, there was something in reserve. After clarifying the doubts I decided to take the room for 1 week. The neighborhood is mixed means you see people from all over Black, Hispanic, American and many...

Very helpful and genuine host- checked in with us frequently to ensure everything was going well. Met us at the apartment on the first day to run through everything. Gave us some good tips on where to find things in the area (grocery stores, drug stores etc).  Apartment well appointed for cooking at home (kitchen utensils etc). Well stocked with towels/sheets/toilet paper etc. Bed very comfortable!!  LOCATION ABSOLUTELY PERFECT!  Would stay here again for sure!!

Mark's duplex on the Upper East Side was in the perfect location for us and we so enjoyed having the opportunity to stay here.  The apartment is clean and well-equipped and has an endless supply of hot water, which was truly a delight.  The duvet cover and sheets were so comfortable, I was searching for a manufacturer's tag so I could steal his good ideas for my own AirBnB place!

Our stay was great. This cozy one bedroom basement apartment was thoughtfully laid out, well decorated and perfect for our short over night stay in Brooklyn. A large comfortable bed, big screen TV, comfy couch, and modern bathroom made the place feel like a steal for the price. Sharon was a gracious host and very accommodating. Allowing us to check on a couple hours early. She responses to airbnb messages quickly and was excellent with directions and helping us find the best diners and restaurants in the area. The apartment is located on a quiet street in a residential neighborhood and parking wasn't that difficult to find even at 1 o'clock in the morning.  I would definitely recommend Sharon's place if your ever visiting Brooklyn New York.

I can use only one word: perfect!!! Faster answer ever (I was in JFK airport without a reservation). Nice welcome in the early morning with a the. The apartment is few blocks near subway, that work all night. The area is very quite (I never felt sensation of danger), few cars on the road in front of the apartment. Sharon is very friendly and helpful, she often was looking for the right way for my journey around New York area. There is tv. Wifi. Cable channel... So, I missed nothing, all is perfect!

I enjoyed my stay here. Sharon has everything you can think of available for you to use. Available to me was a closet full of fresh clean white towels, a million different types of soaps, lotions and candles, a mini fridge, a TV that I am convinced had every channel, beautiful dishes, pots and pans, I mean everything. All of the furniture is clean and comfortable. I fell asleep on the couch sometimes because I was so comfy that I did not want to get up. I didn't see Sharon at all, which was great for me because I don't like to socialize in my "home environment." Oh! The shower. The shower is just lovely with nice pressure and hot water every time.  Considering that the weather was cold during my stay, a downside was that I could not control the heat from inside the apartment. Only Sharon could control the heat and every time I was cold I was expected to text her. I was afraid to trouble her every 5 minutes so I just wore more clothes or just walked around in a blanket. A portable heater would've been great.  Sharon respected my privacy and managed to ask every now and then if I was comfortable without being overly attentive. She let me know that if I needed anything to just let her know.  I would not stay here again unless I have a car. The L train was such a long walk away and the 105th street station does not look safe enough to travel at night. Also, the fast food stores I love like chinese food, pizza, and golden krust were about a 30 minute walk away. There are buses but I didn't want to pay for them every time I wanted to buy food. Clearly, I need to stay in an area with food and the train close by unless I have a car.  However, I would recommend this place to you. I loved it here :)

Nice place, close to the 8 express which brings you fast into Manhattan. Make sure you take that one. On the other side on 125 station at night there some shady persons 🥲. I would recommend not to go there.   Furthermore. Carlos is a very nice host. Helps with everything and want you to have a good stay.   Thanks Carlos!

I was very pleased with the Sharon's beautiful suite. Getting there was easy. She provided refreshments for my arrival including milk, bread, eggs and juice. The suite was very clean, inviting with a wonderfully inspiring atmosphere. Soaps and lotions were available in a lovely bathroom.  I was able to access the Internet and many TV channels were available. My stay was stress-free and I will definitely stay at Sharon's again.

Sharon was a wonderful host, welcoming and very helpful. The place was spacious and comfortable, decorated with beautiful art from her world travels. Everything - kitchen, bath, living room, and bedroom - was super clean and well-equipped. Sharon offered to pick me up at the airport -- very much appreciated.  She waited for me while I dealt with my luggage not showing up, and injected humor and support into that stressful situation. Unfortunately my stay was short and I did not have time to explore the neighborhood. I think hosts like Sharon are the best possible advertisement for Airbnb.

We reached in the afternoon and found the keys exactly where Sharon had kindly mentioned they were at. Sharon had shared the address and other details with us via text the day before, which was very kind and proactive of her. The apartment is one of three in the same house - each apartment has a different door to enter and separate amenities. This one's in the basement - with four 23kg suitcases each, it would have been nice to have been mentally prepared for the staircases. Impeccable apartment undoubtedly. Only one ~2x3 foot window looking out ground level. There was milk, bread, eggs in the refrigerator that Sharon had kindly provided! Pleasant surprise that. Neighbourhood is quiet, friendly neighbours, takes about a 17min walk to the train station ( ~60min to get to Central Park ), lots of buses around, closest 7/11 is a 10min walk. The toilet backed up a couple of times, and resolved itself automatically. Really appreciated the access to a washer & dryer since I'd been in NYC for three weeks already and had laundry to do. It rained the last day I was there at Canarsie and some weird looking insects crawled out into the apt on my clothes. Luckily the insects were more scared of us than we were of them so we didn't have to call for help! We met Sharon once during our stay and she's a lovely, inspiring person. We watched a lot of TV when we weren't travelling to Manhattan. We cooked breakfast in the kitchenette most days. The apartment looks like a hotel room - it's quite fabulously well done. I couldn't sleep on the mattress though - it really moved each time my sister turned over - I slept on the couch for three nights. Sister slept on the mattress. Had I been staying alone, I'd have slept like a baby on that mattress.

Our stay at Amy's apartment was absolutely wonderful. As soon as I booked, Amy was in contact to ask if we had any questions about New York and during our stay she checked in many times to make sure everything was going smoothly and there was nothing we needed. It was so lovely to end our trip in a home away from home, and so close to everything you would want to see in New York. Central Park is only three blocks away, the subway two blocks away that will have you downtown in 15 minutes max.  The neighborhood is really cool too - perfectly safe and more of an authentic New York atmosphere. We came home very late at night by subway on a few occasions and never once felt unsafe.  Amy was super flexible with check in/check out and even let us hang around after we had checked out to wait for our shuttle to the airport.  Oh! And you can't go past the kuerig coffee machine and all the goodies Amy leaves for her guests. It was so great to arrive to beer in the fridge and chips on the table after a long day traveling.  Amy's apartment is an oasis in a big city, which can be very hard to find. Amy goes above and beyond to make sure your stay is as enjoyable as can be and our trip was definitely made by ending in such a fantastic place - thank you Amy!!

We stayed for a week in Amy and her brother Steven's apartment and everything was perfect from start to finish.  Whether it was booking, preparing for our arrival and departure, Amy, as well as Steven, were available every time. Impossible to find nicer people.  Imagine arriving in a new place after hours of flying, and having cold drinks and snacks waiting for you... The dream!  The apartment is perfect, clean, consistent with the photos in the ad. The neighborhood may seem "hostile" at first, but you will quickly feel at home.  Two metro lines serve the neighborhood, the 6 (green) but also the 2 and 3 (red) north of Central Park, ideal when the first is under construction, which was the case for us the weekend of our arrival.  In short, it's impossible not to recommend this apartment if you go to New York, excellent value for money!

The primary host was unavailable but her brother lived on site . They are excellent in communicating and getting you situated. The neighborhood was a bit sketchy especially at nights but after a day got accustomed to it and it wasn't so bad. The apartment itself is nice and cozy with all the things one would need .

We were made very welcome by Amy's brother when we arrived. The apartment corresponds to the photographs. It is spacious and well maintained.  The decor is typical of New York.   It is well equipped (dishwasher, washing machine, sheet, towel, basic necessities, etc.). It is located 2 minutes walk from metro 6 (green). And about 10 minutes from Central Park. We did not feel unsafe despite a fairly popular neighborhood. Especially since the apartment is equipped with an alarm and the host stays in an apartment below.

Amy’s place was wonderful and I’d highly recommend. It faithfully represented the pictures and it was close to the subway and buses making getting into the city easy. We really enjoyed exploring the area and checking out local restaurants. Amy and her family were very helpful and made our stay stress free.

First time visitor from Illinois! Sharon’s home was lovely and very cozy. Spacious and clean. Easy street parking out front. Don’t stress about parking if you arrive later in the evening because more parking spots will open up in the morning. There are local bus option. There is also a subway station a mile from the home (for the L train, which ran at all times including nights and weekends), with easy Uber options to and from, if you prefer (also at all times of day). The subway ride was around 45 minutes - 75 minutes to main tourist attractions (Times Square, 9/11 memorial, Chelsea Market, the High Line, Battery Park, Chinatown). I will definitely stay here the next time I’m back and highly recommend for anyone!

Great place next to express station at 125th that make you Central Park 5 min away, MET 10, and Grand Central 15 minutes away. The surrounding is a little bit creepy at first look but when you used to its a kind of cute. There is a great park on 3 minutes walk and a variety of food deliveries around. All in all was very satisfied with my two months spent within Sergio's listing.

I had a wonderful stay with Charles, very welcoming and attentive. He is always ready to help and give advice on things to see in New York. No constraints in terms of schedules, Charles provides a set of keys and it is possible to return at any time. The apartment is located in Harlem, a stone's throw from two subway stations. Safe neighborhood with lots of activities and entertainment. There is a large laundromat nearby, shops and snack bars. I highly recommend the accommodation and its host for the welcome, the facilities, the proximity to the subway and the proximity to the heart of Manhattan. Many thanks again Charles and we look forward to coming back!

We had an excellent stay. Charles is very friendly and willing to help. Location is perfect, there's a metro station 2 blocks away which brings you all the way down to buzzing downtown. Neighbourhood not unsafe at all. I can surely recommend!
The room was very clean and good. The person was very kind. There was a police station nearby, so it was not dangerous at night.

I stayed at Sandra's sweet house for 2 weeks. I had to chang the departure day suddenly, Sandra and her family accepted with smile and totally understood my situation. I miss already Sandra's kindness, the sense of humor of Valleria, shouting of Donny for soccer game and such a lovely powerful baby Lucas. I and my son really enjoyed the NY life at Sandra's home. I used to take buses Q58 and Q59 and change to metro R and M. It takes about 50 min to the Time squre. We usually came home late over 10 pm and never felt dangerous or uncomfortable at all. Her house was clean and She is always ready to support her guests.  I highly recommend her house for travelers  looking for the room outside of Manhattan.

Charles is an amazing host. When I arrived he kindly welcomed me in the great room I was going to stay in for a few weeks. The room is spacious and has everything you need.   These had been some amazing two weeks, and that’s partly because I had an excellent host who showed me around, gave me some cool tips and told me exciting stories.  Charles’ apartment is super efficient and spacious for New York terms. Everything is extremely clean. The location is nice because the subway is close and it’s relatively close (20 mins to Times Square)  to the rest of Manhattan.   The area is really safe and made me, a solo female traveller, not feel scared/unsafe at all.  I totally recommend this Airbnb to everyone who wants to have a great, local experience of New York.   Thank you Charles for everything, I will be back soon!!!

We really enjoyed our stay at Jason's! Me and my partner stayed for 12 nights and it felt like home. Jason was a great host, he gave us advice and directions how to get to his from the airport which was handy and made himself available for our arrival. Everything was as pictured, very clean and there was Jason has stocked up basics in the fridge for us which was lovely and had clean towels and sheets ready. There is a super huge tv with a Netflix account and the kitchen comes with everything you would need to cook (we didn't use any but handy to have). The appartent is very easy to get to from the subway station (10-15 min walk), where you can the train in to the city (roughly took about 45-60 mins) or around Brooklyn. For us it was an ideal location as we were more interested in exploring Brooklyn but it was handy to have on your door step. On the way to the subway, there are a few streets filled with restaurants and grocery shops, pizzerias, coffee and bagel shops so if you don't fancy venturing out far for dinner there is lots of options nearby. The actual aprtement is very comfortable to live in, there is a big wardrobe for your things (very helpful for long stays) the place was very big and airy and there was a full AC system which kept us cool. We felt very safe and at home throughout our whole visit, the neighbours said hello (mostly young professionals and families in the building) and we had regular communication with Jason, it was so nice of him to check in on us to make sure everything was grand! Overall, we would definitely stay with Jason again if we come to NY on holiday again. The place is great value for money, as long as you are happy with traveling a little bit to get places, which was ideal for us and normal within NY. The whole experience was stress free and I knew if I did need a hand with something Jason was just at the other end of the phone. Thank you again for a wonderful stay Jason!

Enjoyed 5 nights at Jason's apartment in Brooklyn. Bay Ridge was a quaint area with close proximity to public transportation to Manhattan (25-50 minutes depending on final destination). Jason was very accommodating and went above and beyond to make sure we had a stress free trip to New York.

For the price and location, this apartment is a steal! Mike is a really nice and warm guy. And he was very patient with all of our questions. The bunk bed was quite comfortable and after a day of walking around in NY, we simply passed out. Overall, the apartment was clean and quiet. The only drawback is the steep 5 floor walk-up especially since we were carrying big bags. But then I can't say we weren't warned.

Where to start... If you want to spend more than 2 or 3 weeks in NY this is your place. Literally 40 minutes from the center if you make the right arrangements (one stop on the six, transfer and the express leaves you at Times). Everything very easy. Daniel is charming and just like Nino, his dog. Impossible to feel alone in this apartment. The Bronx is scary, we have all seen many movies. But really, nothing at all. There was never any problem, the people were very nice and everything was super close. There is only one bad thing. And very bad too... There comes a day when you have to leave.   Dani is the best host in the world!!

Daniel and his girlfriend helped us greatly when we found ourselves without a return flight (flight canceled due to snow storm). We thank them again enormously for their generosity, they really were at the top! We can really count on them.

well, I chose the Daniel loft based on the reviews left by travellers.   First time in New York before booking I exchanged with this one in order to avoid any inconvenience during my stay.  Communication was good. But the problem arose when I arrived.   After a flight of more than 7:30 a.m.  I just wanted to sleep, to rest well the first morning so that I could enjoy the rest of my stay and be in good shape. I received the day before a message from Daniel telling me that he would not be at the loft when I arrived and that we would see each other in the morning, I told him that I had a long trip and that I intended to rest this first morning and that we would see each other when I woke up. I arrived quite late in the evening I had warned him there is no problem for late arrivals knowing.   At 8 am Daniel arrived at the apartment with his dogs, and did not respect the fact that I was sleeping and made a lot of noise, coffee machine, blender etc... (kitchen facing  the door « partition room »  he received the call from his girlfriend who had a car problem, he put her on speakerphone!!! And spoke with her for several minutes.   The real bedroom is a partition, it's not a wall, it's planks, a rapid construction of what he calls a bedroom.  No isolation and no privacy you can hear everything. So I couldn't rest (4 hours of sleep) so I got up.  Ithought to myself he looks cool I'm not here to have any problems let it pass.   We got to know each other a little, the communication went well.   After spending the day outside I come home tired I go to bed but impossible to sleep because the upstairs neighbor was making a lot of noise from 1 a.m. until 3:30 a.m.,  you can hear when he sings when he whistles, when he walks when he goes to the toilet in short we live with the neighbour.  I send a message to Daniel asking him if the upstairs neighbor is aware that there is someone currently in his loft (because Daniel has another apartment where he lives there with his girlfriend next to this one) specifying  that if I can't sleep in the morning and also in the evening it's going to be complicated.   I saw him in the morning, we don't discuss it, he tells me that it's New York, that's how the person upstairs used to live from his loft, etc.  OK !  I don't want to epilogue let's move on.   2nd day I spend my day outside it snowed in it is very cold so happy to come back to be able to take a hot shower, and there Surprise !!!   the hot water only ran for two minutes,  I waited for it to come back of course still no hot water I turned off the water, I still turned on no hot water!!!  The water was freezing, I had to rinse with.  I send a message to this one unfortunately it was a little late around 11 p.m. but I had no choice.  He answers me by telling me that he had no problem with the water.  I dont think that Is it normal when it's over -5 degrees outside to take a cold shower ! So Too much for me,  I send a message to Airbnb because for me it was too much trouble. I could have overlooked a lot of things but not this.   Airbnb decides to inform him and there I discovered another personality of Daniel, he knocked very hard on the door spoke to me in an aggressive tone, and told me that I had one hour to leave the apartment (rather his place of work  ),  I did not intend to leave an opinion but following his change of personality I thought that people might need this feedback to know that:  Daniel is a person who will be cool with you, which is completely normal, it is thanks to us that he can pay his 2nd rent!   and yes it's not an artists loft it's his place of work he's not just a painter he works on computer and machine he starts very early so if you've been on a long trip and you need  of your first morning of rest in order to start your stay in shape you can forget!  you should also know that the cleaning leaves something to be desired, the room was full of dusted, I found the remains of chips on the floor, dust on the pillow (supporting evidence I took photos) Note also that dog come inside « the private room partition » when you open it. Know that this is the first negative opinion that I leave since I am registered on Airbnb (almost 9years)  I have traveled all over the world and it is one of my 1st bad experience in a country so far from mine.  I'm really amazed to see so many good feedbacks on Daniel I spent three really unpleasant days, I asked for a refund for the last 4 days that I will not spend in his apartment, which is totally legit, I could have ask for the full refund given the aggressive manner and the threatening tone of this one.   Know that I found in the heart of Manhattan a 4star hotel with all the comfort and cleanliness desired with the subway and restaurants right in front of this one, all for about the same price as "his freezing loft"  where it saves water heating and cleaning…  Don't get me wrong to think it's good value for money, in short I didn't come on holiday for that kind of thing.   I do not recommend Daniel's loft either for couples or for single travelers but rather for workers or students.  Daniel will only be nice to you if you don't

Shannon and Dahrehn's appartment is a great place to explore the city during the day and to get away from it at night and "hide" in Brooklyn. Public transport is easy to get to and close by. Stayed in the app. with my friend for 10nights and we have nothing negative to report. Everything as described and the beds are great to relax from a stressful day with lots of walking around. Shannon and Dahrehn are very friendly and very quick to respond to Q&A's. I only can highly recommend this place. Good value for money.

The stay with Roque was a pleasant first introduction to NYC. In special Roque's support through e-mail, in advance of my departure from Amsterdam, made my trip to the Bronx even more convenient than expected. Guiding me with suggestions on how to get from Newark to Grand central, and how to get a weekly MTA card (it does save you some $). And once there he informed me about the shops in the neighbourhood, tips on the New York City Pass and some must see things that aren't in the lonely planet.  The room felt cosy and welcome, the house was comfortable to use; when you like to cook your groceries from Chelsea market, the kitchen is big plus over having a hotel.  With a subway station one block full of friendly shop owners away, where the 6 line takes you without transfer directly to central park, grand central, soho or south manhattan, or if you want, with a single transfer to almost any other interesting point in manhattan, there is no need to use a taxi.  Sometimes there are those stories about the Bronx, the ones that make your friends ask whether you aren't afraid to get robbed. I think they belong in music clips or movies. Several times I walked a mile or some through the bronx because i took the wrong subway line uptown. I experienced no such thing at all. People were attentive and polite, give a smile and receive free suggestions and a compliment or two.   When I plan to revisit NYC I would definitely try to return to Tinton Av. The kindness and price are really competitive in my opinion :)  Feel free to ask me about my experience with Roque  (in English or Dutch)

We loved Doug's place. It was really big for New York, and bright with big windows. We never did meet Doug, our fault, I suspect, but he was on top of everything by phone. Doug's art was wonderful and whimsical. We enjoyed staying in a place that was very far from a drab Comfort Inn. I feel we should add, the bedroom is a private room with a fantastically great bed ands wonderful sheets. I felt like I had a really cool New York cousin, who let me stay in his industrial loft. We had a great time and admired the creativity all around us. I would  recommend it highly.  Because it's in an industrial area, Memorial day weekend was very quiet and peaceful. I'm sure the same would be true weekends

Doug's place is clean and comfortable with a lot of light, really cool art, and lots of house plants.  If I wasn't so excited to see the city I could have hung out there the whole time.  The area is kind of a warehouse district I take it, so on first glance (I arrived late at night) of his street I was a little unsure, but I never felt unsafe at any point.  If I had  a little more time I would have checked out some of the neighborhood watering holes.  It's a 30 min train ride to the middle of Manhattan, and the station is just a couple of blocks away.   I'd say my stay was pretty much perfect, and I would gladly stay again or recommend it to a friend.

This loft was great! It's in an industrial area so it's not going to look like much from the outside but I promise you it's so much better once your inside.  I was worried at first about the area especially being that I was going to be out late and I was here by myself, but the neighborhood is real quiet at night and safe! At no point was I scared or worried.  Also Doug and Tommy were wonderful. I would definitely stay here again.   Note: because this is an industrial area, it may get a little loud 7am and will last for an hour or 2. If you're a light sleeper like me, you may want to bring some ear plugs. The noise was not that bad during my stay.

We spent a very nice week in the apartment. Our arrival was very late due to our flight time but the keys were readily available. We lacked nothing during our stay. The metro located 400 m away allows you to reach Manhattan in 20 minutes.  New York is an obligatory stop for all travel lovers. I recommend this accommodation for this trip.

A gorgeous apartment, really large for ny standards, lots of cool art and an amazing coffee machine. Communication went smoothly, bed was comfortable and the wifi worked well for when i needed to work. The area feels a little sketchy at night, mainly if you're on your own,  but the express subway and plenty of great food and bar options are a 10-12 mins walk away. I highly recommend this spot and I'll definitely stay here again!

Excellent location, 2 minutes walk from the metro. Perfect for getting around Manhattan and Brooklyn. Very good places around (Choice Market, our favorite spot for breakfast, Mayflower for a drink in a speakeasy atmosphere etc...) The apartment is exactly as shown in the photos, easy to access and Darhren and Shannon are very available. Our flight was delayed, our hosts immediately agreed to a late check out which was a great help. Well equipped and clean apartment. The only downside is the sofa bed, suitable for children/teenagers, but not for a couple of adults.

Just okay, there was good and bad.  Having stayed in AirBnB’s I would have to say this is not the standard we have come to expect BUT it could be amazing. I’ll start with the good - The location is great and provides a real Brooklyn experience with local shops and restaurants starting almost next door. We walked to the Brooklyn Bridge and didn’t find it a problem and used the subway which is just a short walk around the corner. We interacted with many locals in the area and never felt unsafe or unwelcome in their neighbourhood.  Now the bad - I chose to stay here based on reviews and can see why people could have loved it. The space is great but it feels like the love and care of hosting has been lost along the way. Previous reviews have commented on the hospitality and even the guide book left inside the home states ‘there are fresh eggs in your refrigerator and treats from Mekelburg’s (The Best!) for your enjoyment’ and ‘The “Whirly POP” makes the best popcorn, help yourself. Sounds great but no eggs, no treats and no popcorn kernels. There was only a container of hand soap in the bathroom and no other toiletries. Dahrehn did contact me on the second day and I requested a tea towel or paper towel for the kitchen which was left outside our door later that night. I didn’t question the treats as this wasn’t something we needed but it did feel like our 3 nights were not enough to warrant this or that the love of hosting had gone.  My husband for the first time since using AirBnB in Australia and overseas commented on cleanliness issues within the apartment.  I do hope the space becomes as wonderful as the previous reviews make it sound and that future guests enjoy booth the location and the space.

Experience was overall very good. Host was amicable and place is centrally located. Walking alone at late night in that street is not suggested...which was the only drawback (it could be a myth due to predominant African American residents and homeless people on the street. However, place is quite good at much decent cost.  Host was very much helpful and informative...guided us throughout when needed. Really impressive.

Staying at Roque’s place was our first Airbnb experience for my friend and I and we both agree that we got everything we were hoping for and more! We felt at home right away and appreciated all the little details and attentions. Roque was always willing to answer any question we had and give us advice so we could make the most of our too short stay in NY. Also, when staying in the Bronx, we never felt unsafe or unsecure, and it was actually nice to escape the hustle and bustle of Manhattan while discovering another “borough” of the Big Apple. To anyone looking for a great host and place, we definitely recommend staying at Roque’s house!

Our experience was good and bad for many reasons. My bf and I booked the room several months out because we are planning to stay 3 months. Christine agreed to the allotted days and we paid the first installment. Two months after we had booked plane tickets Christine emailed us to say we had to come a week later bc she needed the room for someone else. We explained that we already booked flights and she told us to "figure it out" for a few days and offered for us to stay at her friends home. We spoke to Airbnb but the next day she said we could come when we agreed. So despite my concerns we did go through with it. The room was nice. The kitchen had the basics and probably the best toaster I've ever used. The fridge made a pretty awful noise (Christine's husband did all he could to fix it). We did see a few roaches, but expected it because it's NYC. Although we got great sunlight in our room, we were awoken every morning at 8 AM by construction going on literally 5 yards from our window (not saying she could do anything about it...but it was hella rough). The apt is located in an interesting area. Gentrification is taking hold because one block was super sketchy and the next was decent. Just be smart when walking at night. We didn't have issues with living with roommates or sharing space. We were rarely home and so that made things easier. Everyone cleaned up after themselves for the most part. The third week of September (1 month and three weeks into our stay) Christine approached my bf and told him that "someone" had rented our entire floor and needed us to move out a week early, or move into her apt for a week, or move out by Sept 30th and get prorated. When I asked for the details in a written email she said she never said she was "renting" it and that she just "needed" to change our agreement. We again found it frustrating and inconvenient that she was forcing us into changing our original rental agreement. We couldn't find a new place in such a short time so agreed to just leave completely a week early.  We just felt like there was a lack of communication and respect for our rental agreement. SO I wouldn't recommend staying long-term unless you're flexible with possible changes. But if you're popping in for a week  and mostly will be in the city traveling then definitely go for it.

Roque was very friendly, the room is spacious and clean in a nice apartment. The building and neighborhood never felt unsafe, and I was able to find street parking for several days right outside with no difficulty.  A fantastic location by the 6 train, very easy to get into Manhattan. I'd gladly stay again next time I visit the city!
I booked the room for 3 nights, but ended up staying just one. The room was cold, with no heat and the windows did not close. I ended up losing my voice and with an asthma attack.

It was the first time that my daughter and I booked on the Airbnb platform; we were delighted by the welcome that Christine and her family gave us; Although we arrived after midnight (Air France delays), we were greeted with a smile;  The description of the accommodation corresponds perfectly to reality: independent bedroom with air conditioning, TV, storage space and refrigerator..., kitchen, bathroom; the accommodation is located approximately 10 minutes on foot from a metro station and 5 minutes from the bus stops; this makes it very easy to reach Manhattan. Christine's accommodation is located in a safe neighborhood and although we came home late, my daughter and I never felt unsafe; Chritine speaks French very well and gives good advice for visits. In conclusion, we had a great stay; The welcome is really warm but Chritine and her family still know how to remain very discreet; we felt a bit like at home... In short, I highly recommend....

This was my first time using Airbnb and the experience was more than perfect for me and my girlfriend's 5 day stay.  MarQuerite's hospitality was very helpful and welcoming. She was also very professional and showcased the home in the same way. There was a booklet waiting for you full of laminated sheets that provided you with everything you needed to know as a tourist there.  There was also fresh fruit waiting for us, accompanied by a fully stocked kitchen with everything needed to prepare meal. The home looked identical to the pictures and is located right underneath the host's home, with its own separate entrance. My favorite part was how VERY CLEAN and nicely decorated the entire place was. The bed and couch were also very comfortable. MarQuerite also had a great personality and amazing communication, as she was available via phone, email, and text and had immediate response time.  I couldn't have asked for a better host. Also, although the subway was several blocks down Church Ave it never posed as an issue. We would  usually walk there, which only took 10 minutes or take a gypsie cab for $2 per person, or hop on the M-35 bus. Once on the subway it only took about 20 mins to reach tourist areas, like Time Square. My girlfriend and I never felt unsafe in the neighborhood. It is in a very friendly/lively Caribbean area of Flatbush. There are also plenty of local markets (including a Family Dollar and RiteAid)  all on Church Ave so "you will never go hungry" as MarQuerite promised.  Taking the chance on this place made our trip to NY a billion times more enjoyable.Thanks MarQuerite and family! Until next time. :)

We had a really good stay with Roque in the Bronx. The room was clean and very well stocked with amenities and thoughtful touches, even a bottle of wine for our special occasion! Roque is a really kind person and I am sure we would have enjoyed chatting more if we had had more downtime. The building is older and as Roque warned us at the beginning of our stay, the heater was quite loud for about an hour in the early morning when it warmed up. It didn't seem quite so loud the next three nights so this may be variable. Also, the area didn't feel quite as safe to me as I would have expected given previous reviews, which may be related to some stores in the area having permanently shut down since the pandemic and causing the streets to feel more empty of the usual city activity - however, this is just speculation. We tried to avoid coming home late at night for this reason. Otherwise - the location was very convenient and very near the subway. The value for this place was awesome relative to other similar options, even just for two people (if you have four people - incredible steal!). Thanks again Roque!

This was my first Airbnb experience. I don't know how it could have been any better. Angus' was a great host. There was clear and timely communication. The home is clean and comfortable. The neighborhood was safe and had restaurants, groceries, drug stores, and subway access within walking distance.  I would highly recommend this home to anyone.

I stayed at MarQuerite’s place with my boyfriend for 5 days. This is a fairly nice place to stay in Brooklyn, and the neighborhood is alright. I didn’t feel unsafe while walking around and you can find some really good jerk chicken in the area. MarQuerite is great and very responsive. She even left some chocolate, fresh fruit, and flowers in the place for us which was a nice touch. The kitchen is fairly well stocked with utensils and spices etc. but unfortunately we did not have a chance take advantage of it since we were out most of the time. There were only two things that were less than ideal about this place for us. The first one was that the unit is not exactly soundproof so you can pretty much hear everything going on above. MarQuerite lives with her family (incl. 3 kids) and we could hear them running/walking and even talking. This wasn’t really a huge issue for us since we were out most of the time but it’s something to consider for those who are sensitive to noise. The other thing is that the place is a little bit further than the train than I’d like, but it’s not hard to get to, there is a bus not too far from the place that can take to right to the train but if you were to walk it’s about 17 min. Overall I’d say MarQuerite’s place is a good place to stay in Brooklyn and I’d recommend it for those who anticipate spending most of their time out and about.

Firstly, Rose was fantastic as a host.  Before we even arrived there was a lot of communication not just about the apartment, but about the neighbourhood, things to do, places to go, popular restaurants (all of which were great suggestions).  Throughout our stay whenever we had questions she was always very quick to respond with helpful suggestions.  The listing description is very accurate.  The apartment is a short walk from basically anywhere - Central Park, Time square, Moma, even Grand Central is only a 25 minute walk.  There are all the subway lines you could need only a few blocks away - we mostly used the E\C line to get downtown, but the NQR lines are also very handy and Columbus Circle is close as well.  Anywhere you want to go, you can go without any problems.  Easy to get to from the airport (JFK) as well - we just took the airtrain than the E line and we were within 5 minutes walk!  The apartment itself was very clean, well organised and comfortable.  There was enough room for 2 with luggage, and the bed was comfortable.  The bathroom is standard size, and the kitchen was handy for storing drinks\food.  The wifi was fast, and Netflix was a great addition.  There is a little bit of street noise, but nothing that keeps you up at night.  We didn't use the building laundry, but having it there is a bonus.  The neighbourhood is great.  Minutes from a lot of nice restaurants, and at no stage did we feel unsafe at all, even walking back late at night.  I highly recommend Rose and her apartment if you are looking for a great place to stay in New York.

Ehren's apartment is a dream of a New York loft coming true. The view over the Manhattan skyline is amazing. Ehren is a cool guy and gave us lots of great tips for stuff to do in the neighbourhood. Bushwick is a fun and dynamic area and we really enjoyed living there. His partner in crime Cindy the cat made us feel even more at home!

This was not the best fit for us, perhaps we should have done more research. Ehren was very communicative and made arrangements for us to be let in by a friendly neighbour when our flight got in late. We never met Ehren because we seemed to be on very different schedules- perhaps a note from him with wifi password, check out instructions could have been helpful. We struggled to sleep as their were no curtains and a lot of light comes through the big windows, its extremely noisy at night in the neighbourhood. The neighbourhood is great if you want to enjoy Brooklyn's nightlife, however this was not the case for us. Neighbourhood also felt unsafe for us and we did not feel secure walking at night from the subway. Had to invest in bug repellent due getting bitten by mosquitos and the spiders in the bathroom meant that I tried to spend as little time in there as possible

I needed a quiet place for a couple nights for my parents to rest and recover from their 20-hour flight from Taipei a before they continued on with their travels.  They are a bit a afraid of NYC, so I wanted to find a place near me in Downtown Brooklyn, but in a neighborhood more green with a less big-city feel (my parents are not used to NYC).  Sarah's place was perfect!  The neighborhood is lovely with its little shops and restaurants; it made a nice impression on my parents whose opinions of the city improved.  The cottage is very homey and comfortable.  Definitely very quiet and my parents were able to rest.  Sarah was very prompt with answering any question or emails I had, and everything was very easy.  Sarah herself is very lovely and friendly and it was good to know that she was available in case my parents needed anything.

Triny's place is in a very convenient location close to the train and many restaurants, bars and stores, but on a quiet street.  The two bedrooms are spacious and the living room is very comfortable.   There is a full kitchen if you feel like cooking and a very clean and large fridge for storing supplies for your trip.  The keyless doors worked super well, you don't have to stress about remembering to bring keys or which key goes in which door.   If you are looking to make Williamsburg your home base for a trip, this is a great choice!

Jeffrey is the perfect host, charming and welcoming. The apartment stylish and very clean. Jeffrey made sure we were comfortable and always had what we needed. The location is excellent in a nice quiet upper west side neighborhood, very close to a subway getting you to midtown very quickly.  The apartment is quiet, clean and Jeffrey always had fruit sacks and drinks (hot and cold) available at all times.  Staying with Jeffrey made our stay in NYC hassle and stress free. Jeffrey is a great host with a great apartment and we unequivocally recommend him.  Thanks Jeffrey!

Staying with Jeffrey really was a huge pleasure. He picked us up from the subway, helped us carry our luggage and was just all around a nice person. Whenever we did see him during our stay at his place he was extremely nice and helpful. The location of his apartment is a huge plus as well. It’s close to public transport and downtown Manhattan and even when we got back a bit later at night we didn’t feel unsafe walking from the subway to his apartment. We really enjoyed our stay and strongly recommend Jeffrey as a host!

Charming and comfortable. Entry a little sketchy but room is clean and cozy. But it’s  above a very noisy bar so if you tend to stay out very late you’ll be fine. If you’re looking for a good nights sleep this is not the place.

When I arrived to Jackie’s place, she and her son were standing on the porch. Her appearance was gravely different than her profile photo. She looked unkempt, wearing a dirty long t-shirt, and she picked up a dog, which was not included in the listing. Jackie and her son seemed to stare right through us with little greeting. My cousin and I did not want to cast judgment, yet we felt afraid and driven to follow our gut. We walked to a nearby park and reached out to Jackie to discuss our concerns. She was defensive and felt judged. I brought up the dog and she insisted she did mention the dog in her listing and the dog would have been located downstairs and away from us. I told her I am allergic to dogs and would not have selected a place with a dog had I known. She replied that her dog did not have hair so it wouldn’t bother my allergy. Note we did see hair on the dog. Thankfully, AirBnB was attentive to our concern and we found another stay within a couple hours. I do not wish to offend, I just want to be honest and helpful by sharing my experience. It was very concerning and had I seen a review like this, it would have saved a lot of headache on this trip.

Sarah and Allon were great, we had such an AMAZING time at their cozy cottage. Sarah provide insight about things to do in Brooklyn and coffee! Both were incredibly appreciated and needed. Whilst their little black folder acted as our food bible for restaurants in the Forte Green area. We definitely wished we had a longer trip to explore and eat!  Easy to communicate with and incredibly accommodating- a last minute request to look after our suitcases was very gratefully met. Having previously stayed in Manhattan I can't stress enough how much more enjoyable this trip was and how much more of New York I saw! The transport links were great and were only a 15-20 minute walk away, this flew by as we walked past beautiful brown stones, restaurants and Forte Green Park. I would definitely recommend staying here! Although maybe it's best to keep this as a secret….. for my next trip

We stayed for 5 days there. The apt. was cozy and private  as if we stay in our own place. Laura was kind and informative and caring. Because of our busy schedule we left early and returned late. The area was safe. There is subway station within 2 blocks away and drug store and super market are nearby. We enjoyed our stay. I want to come back to Gadson Gallery whenever I have another chance to come to New York.

Where to start? Simply put, Paco & Pamela’s Loft was the highlight of our week long New York vacation. Not only is it wonderfully air-conditioned, gorgeously decorated, and welcoming, but it wound up feeling like a home of our own amidst the city—our little hideout.   We found ourselves being excited, not to see sights or go out, but to come back to what felt like “our place”—a place that has an incredible kitchen next to a spacious living room with a dining table that seats eight. In fact, we managed to save money because we were so drawn to cook at “home.” Not to mention, in addition to the fact that Paco & Pamela’s listing was nothing short of delightful, they were amazingly communicative—answering any questions we had with kindness and haste.   Lastly, we cannot stress enough how special of an experience this place was for us. For the duration of our short getaway in Williamsburg, the Loft wasn’t merely where we stayed, it was where we lived.   May you be blessed with the same beautiful feeling it left us with.  Thank you Paco & Pamela, it was a pleasure :)

Such a beautiful and cozy apartment! The location is incredible, filled with brooklyn charm. Close to the subway station and a quick walk to food, groceries, and drug stores.  Paco & Pamela communicated in a timely manner and are really nice people. I would stay again!

Beautiful, large loft. Loved this appartement and the way the owners decorated! Really spacious.  It’s on the third floor so make sure you can carry your bags up the stairs.  Kitchen didn’t have a microwave, but there was a toaster oven, a regular oven and a stovetop.  Hosts provided al necessary information a couple of weeks in advance so no stress for us! They were also really helpful with any questions we had.  Located near two metro stations (J line, 5 minute walk and L line, 10 minute walk), which was amazing.   Would definitely recommend staying here!

Great experience! Allon and Sarah attended us in every moment, they were kind and fast!. Very clean and completely equipped. Close to lots of Cafés and subway.  The neighborhood is quite safe and during the day is really nice to take a walk around. The problem came at night, Myrtle ave and Park ave are not the safest streets of Brooklyn. We had not any problem, but they are quite scary streets. Highly recommendable.

We had a great time in New York that was enhanced by staying at Laura's charming garden apartment. For anyone who's only experience of NYC is midtown, staying in Harlem gives a wonderfully new perspective. Transport links downtown are excellent and there was really never any time - even getting back late at night - when there was a feeling of any danger. There are jazz clubs and one or two top restaurants within easy walking distance from Laura's. Laura is great! She runs a busy house, along with her friendly little dogs, who will only stray into your space if you let them (we did!). The apartment was all we needed - very clean, nice bed, hot shower.  Give Harlem and Laura's place a go! I'm very happy to recommend it.

The cottage is nicely private and contained. Very quiet which was a delightful surprise.    It was 90 degrees and humid during my stay but because of how the place is situated in the shade I didn’t have to run the AC— and I’m usually an AC guy.   Would definitely book again

I am afraid to say how wonderful this rare and wonderful host and home is for fear of never being able to stay again!!! She will be booked up constantly!! Deborah is AMAZING and so is her home. As a host previously Debbie does everything right...everything!!!! I felt incredibly welcome and at home immediately. We laughed and chatted and my only regret is I could not stay longer. Debbie has a beautiful home and there are toiletries in the bathroom and when I had asked for peanut butter (after being offered everything:)) she went out and bought some so I would have for the morning:))) As I was leaving Debbie handed me a snack bag for my flight...it doesn't get any better than this. Thank you Deborah and I can't wait to catch up or stay again or both!!!

Pros: The bed was outstanding. Super comfy and quality linens. Location, location, location. Nice street in Bed Stuy and check out Chez Oskar for drinks, brunch or dinner if you get a chance. The shower was hot with plenty of pressure. Larger bathroom than most in the area. Private yet close to the owners. Kitchen space. (I did not use it much, however.) Cons: I did not see smoke detectors. That was a little stressful. There were no trash liners upon arrival though the situation was corrected after I texted. An extra blanket for the bed would have been nice. Coffee for the coffee maker would have also been nice. And instructions for the water filter. I felt it was a good value and would stay again. Hosts are attentive and will probably correct the missing amenities based on this review, but if you are concerned, ask!

Majar's home was affordable, clean and a friendly living experience for the duration of my stay. The door to our room had a lock, we had a big comfy bed with a couch, mini fridge and air conditioning. His brownstone was close to the bus stop and subway station and across the street from a nice coffee shop/bar! It took an element of stress out of our vacation because it was so easy. He provided shampoo, conditioner and coffee as well! I would stay there again.

I stayed at the gadson Gallery with my grandmother and brother.  We enjoyed our stay very much. The beds were excellent! The places Laura recommended were very good aswell. The metro was a 5 minute walk, super reachable! It took us only 15 minutes to reach times Square with the metro. We would recommend this place; quality is good for the price you pay! Harlem was a very nice place, full of life. We didnt feel unsafe during our stay.

Nice appartment in Brooklyn. The neighbourhood is nice, and never felt unsafe here. There are lot's of shops, supermarkets and restaurants nearby. Red-metro 3 brings you to lower Manhattan in 30min. A little further is the green 5 line, which only takes about 15 to lower Manhattan.   You can also catch a bus (stop around the corner) and tour around Brooklyn in search of that nice diner or restaurant nearby!   Would definitily recommend, as this stay gives you an excuse to leave Manhattan and see another part of New York City.  The accomodation is as described. Don't expect anything more or less. It's perfect for a good night sleep. The TV has no live tv, but you can use Michelle's Netflix, or just stream youtube or some newschannels. But hey, who comes to NYC for the TV? The bathroom is shared, but it won't give an issue as it is just with one other room.   The brownstone itself is old, and has a certain charm to it.  Michelle is the percfect host. She leaves you be. No strings, no questions. And if you need her, she is there to help!

Ingrid was very communicative and friendly... The cabin is soooo nice, excellent energy. We stayed there for one night and enjoy two days on the beach. The decoration is cute, plenty of plants and cool furnitures. The location of the boat is perfect because its at the end of the dock, it gives a lot of privacy and its opened on the water, nice view! Moreover, the inside is large, way more than you can imagine with the pictures.  Also, there is a huge deck on the top of the cabin with deckchair, table, plants... We brought our bikes there and ride to the beach during the day. The shared bathroom are modern and very clean. The area of the Marina is a little sketchy on this part of Rockaway but its safe inside and you can move very easily around! Very good time, thankkkyou :)
I didn't like the neighborhood that much, it's not downright dangerous, but I've seen better places in Brooklyn. The value for money is excellent however, and Kiriko is very flexible and welcoming.

Everything was fine at the house.  Everything was as described. Subway into Manhattan is a stones throw from the house. No frills, but spacious and accommodating. The immediate area isnt particularly desirable, but doesn't feel unsafe. A nice surprise is the cozy good vibed Gratitude Cafe, aprox 10 minutes walk from the house. They make a great egg bagel sandwich to get you started on your day!

Kiriko welcomed us very kindly and showed us the apartment, which is bright and large, just steps from the subway station on line 2 that takes you to Manhattan. The neighborhood is a little far from the center, getting to Central Park can be an easy 40 minutes by subway or more. The other thing is that the neighborhood feels a little dangerous, especially if you arrive at night.  The apartment has everything, you can cook, the only thing is that since there were 5 of us, two of us had to sleep on mattresses on the floor, it's a little hard if you stay for many days.  In relation to price quality I think it is very good, the only thing is the time you lose in transportation, but for us it was perfect.

Laura's place is FANTASTIC. A serious AirBNB golden star. I arrived during one of her shows and they all welcomed me so easily. Her place is VERY clean, super comfortable and is in such a great location. It's super close to the Metro but far enough away so it's not crazy. never felt unsafe walking at night and it was spacious. Laura was readily available with local suggestions and easy to get into contact with. Don't second guess staying here - do it!

So nice and peaceful to sleep under the stars and floating on water. We got to fish, meet cool people that lived there and cruise the boardwalk just a few blocks away. You can also walk 2 blocks to hop on the subway to NYC. The surrounding area seemed a little sketchy but we felt safe behind locked marina gate. The bathroom was a bit of a hike so go before bed! :) Ingrid was very helpful with things to do and how to get there. Enjoyed

Great place to stay and for the price incredibly economical. Got in right before the COVID scare so still got to do a lot. The place was very homy and confortable. The hosts were very helpful whenever we needed.

Andy, my host was really kind, and we could have nice talks together. Also, if i was in trouble with travelling directions he could always be there to help me. He cared to fix any issues, and the bathroom was tidy. Our bedroom was for 3 people, and it was fine. The surroundings of the house could be first scary for a european but in New York it is normal. Right now, they are building something on the next house, so it took me a while to find the right one :)

Teresa is a very responsive host who lives downstairs if you need her. Steps up are quite steep so this is definitely a problem for older travelers or those with heavy luggage. Also, the bathrm sink is so narrow most people will find it more comfortable to wash up in the kitchen. Be aware the 2nd bedrm is accessed by walking through the 1st. These are structural things Teresa cannot change. She said she'll replace the air conditioning units & kitchen screen to prevent the mosquito attack we weren't prepared for, probably left by previous guests trying to avoid Aug in NY...Still, we had a great time! The kitchen was well stocked for cooking with real olive oil, good coffee maker & spices beyond salt & pepper. Knives in the kitchen were sharp. I could name names, but you should explore the local shops within a 3 block radius. Fish market which also had good prices on organic eggs, great Italian butcher shop, natural foods stores, 2 bakeries (bread/desserts). Small shops featuring items like freshly made mozarellla, olives, pickles, meatballs, asparagus salad.  Hangout coffee shop, wine shop & of course, excellent pizza. You can even check out the Brooklyn Library. Access to subway lines is excellent. Take the G to see the Botanical Garden/Prospect Park. The L will take you to Manhatten. Our flight was delayed so late our rental car agreement wasn't honored at JFK. We were able to take the AirTrain to the Howard Beach A Line to Brooklyn before we finally used a cab late at night. This set us up for using the subways extensively the rest of our stay using a 7 day pass. NY is full of challenges & surprises. Teresa's deck would be delightful at  another time of year, so we can't regret booking our stay because we needed to attend a wedding. We had great access to every other part of the city from the World Trade Center to the Bronx without a rental car. Life is beautiful.

We stayed in Seth's home for one week and we met both him and his husband. They are very pleasant people and did their best to make us feel welcome, help us around, and recommended neighborhood restaurants. The property is on the second floor in a residential neighborhood. We never felt unsafe there and never had any problems returning home late night. There is a bus from LGA going there directly and using the metro you can be in Time Square in 20 minutes. A small supermarket is nearby.  During our stay we had access to the kitchen and the living room. So I would say this is an inexpensive and nice way to experience New York.

Seth and Paulo made me feel right at home. They were both extremely helpful from the moment I made my reservation up until my last encounter with them. The accommodation was as described and the pictures found on the listing were faithful to the actual physical appearance/layout. I can gladly say that my stay was pleasant, convenient, and completely stress-free. If I ever find myself in the Queens are of New York area, I will definitely book with Seth and Paulo once more.

Seth and Paulo's place its a very good choice if you are on a budget - NY is a very expensive city and here you'll get a cozy room where you can use the kitchen (and save some money if you have time to cook or make your own breakfast). You get what you pay, so in overall we were happy with our choice - not very expensive, with all that you need. (even with a shared bathroom)  You'll get a warm room, with a real bed (not a sofa or something), a good wireless signal and two very helpful hostess. Seth and Paulo always answer our questions since the first moment. In new year's eve they give us a bottle of champagne to celebrate and it shows their hospitality.  The room and bathroom were clean.   The only unpleasant thing was the tricky lockers from the house and apartment doors.

This is in a great spot and was mostly clean and is in a great location it is also just two blocks to the traían to take you to JFK.  The garbage was pretty full in my room when I arrived, the iron looked completely unsafe.  Under the bed was not completely clean.  The bed and pillows were NOT tempurpedic.  The pillows were old, flat and hard.   The laundry are was a mess.  I was really uncomfortable with the note I was left when I came in, in which I was asked to leave my door open so he knew I wasn’t home.  The door does not lock, in fact unless it’s closed very softly it won’t stay closed.  Ron was great at getting in touch.  I just kept to myself.  I did take photos, so if I can put them up I will.
Ron’s place is beautiful and uniquely decorated! He was friendly and responsive. Made our stay much less stressful would absolutely recommend and would definitely book with him again.:)

Shola's home was very clean and spacious and I had a wonderful stay. His apartment is located in a convenient location, just minutes away from the Church St stop, so it's an easy ride into Manhattan. It's also close to the Botanical Garden. Moreover, it's surrounded by small supermarkets so I was able too pick up fruit and groceries for dinner when I wanted. The neighborhood was busy and fun, and I didn't feel unsafe. Shola himself was incredibly nice. He always responded promptly to my texts and was very helpful. I highly recommend staying here!
Great Apartment with everything you need for a short stay. It seemed a sketchy area but in fact it is very safe once it becomes familiar.

London didn't get involved in anything.
