As always, she was very attentive to her cell phone in case we wrote something or had any questions, and her parents who received us at 11 at night (very late for them) were very pleasant.  The neighborhood is amazing, very happy and lively although they told me it was an unsafe neighborhood. I have lived in Madrid and there are neighborhoods much worse than Harlem. Also, people helped you with everything. The house is very, very good, it does not lack detail.  If I return to New York and this price continues, I will surely return to the London house.

Overall this is a great location for the cost. The apartment was spacious for NY, had a kitchen, bed space and bathroom. Definitely a studio. The apartment was really clean and had a "honey" feel. There were some items in the home I which you can tell someone lived there, like clothes, but really you feel safe like you have a place of our own. My only suggestions would be to be prepared to Uber back and forth from the train to the apartment. The walk is long, uphill, and a bit scary at night and to be cautious of the sofa as it seems like a leg is missing and was replaced with books- it was still very sturdy and can hold the weight of two, but something to be made aware of. Again, overall a great place that I would highly recommend. She was very nice and very responsive.

Denae's place was great. She was extremely communicative and checked in several times during my stay. The apartment was exactly as described and pictured. It was a bit further from the subway than I'd have preferred in the middle of winter, but not terrible (but be careful of late night or seasonal construction affecting the train schedules). It is just a short ride into manhattan depending on where youre going. I was in town for an event at the Javits Center, and I had to leave 1.5 hours early every morning to arrive on time. The neighbourhood was extremely friendly, and I never felt unsafe, even walking alone at night. The only downside to the neighbourhood was that it wasn't loaded with things to do, as I'm used it in almost any of area of NYC in which I've stayed, but for the price, I can't be upset. Overall, I had a great stay!

Nicole and I stayed to weeks in Martins apartment and we loved the charm and style of it and enjoyed our time there very much. First we were a little bit stressed because Martin didn´t answer our messages until one day before our journey started but then everything went quite well and easy. The room is very nice. The mattress was really comfortable but could have been a little bit bigger (think, it is a double-bed size 135x190). We haven´t  been up to the rooftop because the accsess is through the window over the fire-escape - unfortunately the two german girls were afraid! Bars, restaurants, supermarket are around the corner and it is easy to go to Manhatten by subway. Martin was a calm and polite host. Thank you very much!!!!!! Nicole and Katharina

Me and my boyfriend stayed at Martins for two weeks and it was amazing! The apartment was spotless and he was always friendly and gave us some of the best suggestions for places to eat including one restaurant that turned out to be the best meal we had our whole trip! (Traif) He recommended sunset drinks on his roof and that was lovely and very New York, climbing the fire escape out back. But don’t have too many up there because coming down is a bit scary. Martin also had some friends over a few nights for dinners and drinks and they were really friendly and left around midnight so we were able to still some rest and go siteseeing. Overall, I can’t say enough about how great this experience was! Our trip was one we’d never forget and staying here was a big part of it!

My stay here was quite an unpleasant experience. When I arrived, the apartment reeked of marijuana smoke. The second bedroom had no linens, no blanket, and no clean pillows or pillow cases. The tub did not have a clean shower curtain, and the tub had dirt marks. My guests and I had to clean it ourselves. There were dirty dishes stashed away in the cabinets that my guests and I also had to wash. We requested towels, shower curtain, and clean blankets/sheets which she delivered in a timely manner. She was apologetic.  Be advised, she expects you to clean the house before you leave although thats what the cleaning fee already includes. No where in her house rules or manual does it state that the guest should clean the house before departure. But she will request additional fees if you do not clean it.

London is a super host! She was reachable if needed and also cared about our pleasure with her flat. There were no problems with check-in & check-out, just be sure you use uber or cabs to get safe back to the apartment in the night ;)   The flat is totally  same as in the description, clean & have enough space for over four people and all the gadgets you use in your daily life! there is all you could need in the neighbourhood like drug store, laundry, restaurants and bars open the whole night. There is just one point we're sure London will improve asap: the speed of Wi-Fi

The room is really good, King is a great host, the neighborhood is safety and has a lot of markets, some restaurants and 3 drug stores close to the apartment, also the subway is very close too.  No complaints. I strongly recommend!

Gyas place is roomy as described. My family, two adults, two kids could easily fit in there. There was a minor problem with the lock, but Gya fixed it in a hurry. She was also helpful and available if we had any questions or doubts. The neighborhood is caribian/mixed and we didn't feel unsafe at any time, day or night. Pretty close to Subway A or 3. Plenty of restaurants and takeaways. Supermarkets etc.

Gyas place is roomy as described. My family, two adults, two kids could easily fit in there. There was a minor problem with the lock, but Gya fixed it in a hurry. She was also helpful and available if we had any questions or doubts. The neighborhood is caribian/mixed and we didn't feel unsafe at any time, day or night. Pretty close to Subway A or 3. Plenty of restaurants and takeaways. Supermarkets etc.

What a difference that extra room makes - it’s almost like your own apartment. Gya is a fantastic host and was super fast to respond to any and all questions. For anyone who may be concerned about the neighborhood (Crown Heights doesn’t get the best press) DON’T BE. I walked to work for months from this spot, often past the Albany housing projects, and never once did I sense or see malice or danger. In fact, I’ve been living all over Crown Heights for more than a year now and I’ve never had cause for concern. One always has to be smart in any urban environment, for sure, but this area isn’t even ‘shady’.

The apartment had the perfect size for 4 people. It was absolutely adequate for our stay in NYC. The next subway station was very close to the apartment, and in 15 to 20 minutes we were at the Times square. We also had a lot of options for buying groceries. London always responded very quick and nice and was always there when we needed help. In the night there was a lot of police presence in the area which made the way from the subway station to the apartment more comfortable for us despite the homeless and addicts in the streets. (You got this in whole NYC not only in this area)

The place is acceptable, it is spacious and although it is a little old everything is in order and works correctly. The neighborhood is very heavy, on Fridays and Saturdays there are parties in the street with a lot of noise and people drinking and smoking marijuana that do not allow you to rest and it is scary to walk at night in the neighborhood. The good thing is that the metro station is very close, a few steps away, but the neighborhood and the street around it is very ugly, if you want a quieter and safer stay, it is better to think twice.  Despite all of the above, London was an excellent host and always kept up with us, always with great kindness.

Overall we had a pleasant stay. Accommodation as advertised, clean and spacious. London and very responsive and attentive.  In terms of location, the accommodation is well located in Harlem with the subway 2 minutes away. Which makes it easy to reach southern Manhattan in around 25 minutes.   The neighborhood is very lively and a little noisy but with the fatigue of the days it didn't bother us. We didn't feel unsafe because no one came to bother us and the PDNY was really present but we felt that alcohol and drugs were present.

Great stay in New York. Close to the subway station and only 20min from Times Square. The neighbourhood is a bit shady at night times, but we never felt uncomfortable. The apartment was clean and had everything we needed.

The room and apartment were just as described.  The room worked well for my daughter and I.  We enjoyed having computer access in the room, as we were traveling without.  Jia Jia was helpful with figuring out parking.  There is free parking in the neighborhood and we were able to find a spot to leave our car in, but it was a little challenging to get the spot in the first place.  If I were staying again, I'd definitely try to do it without a car.  We were welcomed with cold bottles of water and a sheet of information about the neighborhood.  The hosts were very welcoming of having us in the main part of the apartment.  We were inclined to stay in our room, though, after long days of being out in the crowds of New York.  I suspect that the hosts would have enjoyed more interaction with us.  Great place if you're looking for a social experience.

Hello fellow travelers.  I learned that I have different standards then others. That said, the lower apartment was spacious.  It had alot of things you would not expect, like oil and spices that others guest may have left behind.  That was a plus. The back yard was a great escape from Harlem transits. Unfortunately, everything else may sound bad but it really depends what you like and what you are comfortable with.  Tip, walk on the side of street of whole foods the other side is a little sketchy.  I don't think is dangerous just alot of unwanted activity.  I think the house could have been cleaner, found 2 roaches.  The linen was all rough.  They have two very old TV's but the one in bedroom has dvd player so if that is something you like then good.  The apartment size is great but outdated with 2nd hand furniture and the Bed was ok.  The street Ray lives on seems safe its the outer street.  If you go south on his street there is a  nice park.  Overall, it was not at my comfort level but Harlem in that area has great culture and its close to alot of good food and Apollo.  It is just like any other neighborhood, one wrong turn and your experience in Harlem can go wrong.  I would definitly go back to area. Hope this was helpful.

Hi everyone! The apartment is a wonderful place to stay. First of all it DOES LOOK like the pictures on the website. It is tastefully decorated (with a lovely quirky touch!), very bright, roomy and airy. Lots of storage to keep one's things if you are staying long term. The kitchen is well-equipped and super clean. The space in general is very peaceful and the perfect place to relax and chill out. The bed and futon are comfortable (both are in the upper level of the apartment) I stayed in the flat with a friend while searching for a more long-term place to live so its location is ideal both to explore the Upper West Side, Central Park area, Columbia Univ. area, and to wander around mid/downtown. If you are not a walker, there is a subway station literally two minutes away from the flat and lots of convenience stores and restaurants around, so perfect to eat out or for a last minute buy.  The apartment was very clean. Sibylle, our hostess, was lovely and facilitated our stay from the minute we got in touch with her. She provides fresh linen, towels and other things for the guest use on a daily bases (there is a Nespresso machine for the coffee lover and a wonderful kettle and teas for the tea lover!) Bathroom was pristine, of a good size and the water pressure was excellent. It has lots of storage too and plenty of space to keep one's toiletries. The air conditioning works perfectly well, although we barely used it as windows can be opened and you get a lovely breeze. Although NY is a very noisy city, the apartment, being on a high floor and perfectly sound-proofed, doesn't feel noisy at all so we could rest well every night. Neighbours are lovely and quite, and doormans really look after security and made us feel at home too! Having the laundry room in the basement was very convenient and useful and it's not expensive to use it.   I'm a Spanish woman who travels around the world quite a lot so I'm familiarised with different standards of cleanliness and types of accommodation. This being said, the apartment was a lovely place to stay and we both felt very happy about making this choice, but the best thing was Sibylle, who made us feel at home way before we travelled and helped us in many ways, which took stress away from us. The apartment also keeps her personal touch which makes you feel really at ease and relaxed. It was the first time I used airbnb and was a bit anxious about renting someone's home however I don't regret it for a second. It was the perfect choice and it makes a big difference from staying in a hotel. You feel at home. So Sibylle's place was our home away from home for 15 days. Best choice we could have made! HIGHLY RECOMMEND IT!

Kimberly and her husband were excellent hosts and we felt absolutely welcome in their home. We loved have their lovely pets around. The fact that they have so many pets is the reason we chose them :). I was a little worried that it wouldn't be clean with so many animals in a small space but Kimberly keeps the rental room and bathroom spotlessly clean. The bathroom door was broken and wouldn't stay shut when we were there so hopefully that has been fixed. Was quite uncomfortable. Also, we couldn't sleep our second night because it was so hot it was like a sauna in our room even though it was very cold outside. We opened a window and it didn't help much. This room is a bit out of the way so be prepared for that as well. But we never felt at all unsafe even when walking at night.

Amazing Host ! Outstanding amenities and what A place to relax and forget that NY is a stressful city ! It's an oasis with a great vibe! But be mindful of the park at night , not suttible for young children .

The description of the bdroom was very accurate. Room and bathroon were very clean. Kimberly was absolutely helpful with my check-out. I just felt sort of unsafe in the neighborhood during the night. It is located in alphabet city and people adviced me not to walk around at night.

Martin's place was exactly what we needed. It's the perfect place to set your bags down and rest, which is exactly what we came to NY for. The living area and roof are definitely cozy, but we took more advantage of the roof. The view is really great. Just a heads up to anyone that's not fire escape savvy, it is kind of scary. Another thing to be aware of with this place is that it gets warm very easily with the space heaters. We actually had to turn ours off at night because it was so hot. It did seem that the building itself was fairly WARM!!!! I only mention this because I get hot easily and figure there are others out there just like me that may want to know this. All in all though it really was everything we needed for the weekend.

Very bad experience. It is not at all what the host promises. The area is dangerous and not pretty. The whole place is very dirty on the outside and inside, plus the photos posted in airbnb have nothing to do with reality. The place is not even in the building, the airbnb is at the bottom of the building (by the way even the entrance too dirty and unpleasant). The furniture with dirt marks, the sheets, the walls, the patio ... all dirty. In the ad it does not put the reality of things, and that is lying. In addition, the host has not responded to us to return our money, because it was a very bad experience, he uses the arrival time of the cleaning company as a pretext. Do not go.

Kay was a wonderful host. I had a weird stop over night inbetween air b n bs which was stressful with a big case and Kay very kindly let me drop it off early and leave it there to pick up later in the day. Hands down it is the nicest air b n b I’ve stayed in. I would love to stay for longer next time. A lovely experience!

Finding a place to stay in NYC is a challenging task, but Kim's place is incredible. I really felt at home during the days I was at NYC. It's very clean, cozy, has a great bed, good shower and great vibes. The bedroom is big - actually, I think bigger than some hotel rooms you find in midtown.  Kim was super helpful with all I needed. It is very clear that she really cares about her guests, answers are very quick and assertive. Not to mention the details of decoration of the bedroom, it inspired me and I'll probably steal some ideas for my own house, lol.  Stayed there for 10 days and felt like I was home. I was looking for a truly newyorker experience and nailed it.  There is no metro station close to the apartment (actually, there is and it is a walking distace), but for me, it wasn't a problem at all: first, there's a bus stop across the street and took me like 5-10 minutes to get to Union Square or, even better: there is a citibike by the corner, and it was the best feeling when riding a bike to wherever I wanted. If I wanted to go to the west village/soho/meatpacking, I did it walking, Manhattan is a very good place to walk any time of the day.  The neighborhood is great, there's a nice coffee by the corner, a park, drugstores, it is close to brooklyn (by williamsburg bridge) and a place to have breakfast that I fell in love: C&B.  If you're looking a nice place to stay in the villages, I strongly recommend Kim's AirBnb!

The home was lovely and a great value. The host communicated very well and was very responsive to needs. Lots of amenities in the house and spacious enough for our family of five. The downside was the surrounding neighborhood. A few very scary occurrences when walking in the neighborhood at day and at night. We didn’t feel safe utilizing the Metro in that area after our first two attempts due to harassment.

This was a good spot for our NYC vacation. It was close to the subway and there were several good local places: El Barrista for breakfast, Mess Hall for drinks, Harlem Hops for breweries, and Patsy's for pizza. The neighborhood has a lot of activity, some sketchy, but mostly friendly.

Stay here at your own risk. I was billed $150 for a professional painter to come out and repaint his entire "antique" table because of a single cup ring.   There are no coasters, no table cloth, and no protective covering on the table surface. No warning was given not to set drinks there. We drank no wine or juice or anything that would normally stain. This "damage" likley resulted from simply setting down my blue paper coffee cup on the only available surface in the room. This host needs to take responsibility for his failure to take any preventative action.  Secondly he suggested that we could climb out the window onto the fire escape to access the roof. When my wife attempted to climb out she recieved a laceration to her arm from sharp metal. She did not notice at first which resulted in blood stains and more damages I'm being billed for.   Besides that the fire escape presents an extreamly dangerous situation. It is there for emergency use only. The rooftop itself is even more dangerous with nothing to stop you from falling off the edge. I work in construction and I'm well versed in these dangers. I would lose my job if I ever climbed onto a roof like that without a fall protection harness. It's one thing to take that risk yourself but to suggest it to tourists many under the influence of alcohol is not cool. Thankfully I stopped my wife before she climbed all the way up and put herself as such risk of death.

Place was very bad, didn’t look anything like the pictures. False advertisement, the place smelled like urine, it was very dangerous for my friends and I to stay there, there were men approaching our door and windows. I sent the host a message and he deleted it. This place should not be rented out on Airbnb.

This apartment is so cute with its interior brick walls and courtyard out back. There was plenty of room for our large group. The tree lined street was so pretty and quiet, but still really close to the subway for easy access to NYC sites. We felt safe with the gate at the front and the iron door at the back, plus the windows were barred. We never felt unsafe in the neighborhood, but it still helped to sleep easier knowing my kids were safe. We will definitely stay here again when we visit NYC.

Accommodation well located in Harlem, close to metro, shops and restaurants. Manhattan in 20 minutes. Park nearby. Interesting when you want to discover Harlem but not recommended for a family (drug addicts, homeless people, syringes on the sidewalk).

Great Airbnb! For context, me and a roommate from California were here for two weeks while apartment hunting in NYC. Having never been to the area we didn’t know what to expect.  In terms of location, Alphabet City is definitely not as nice as other parts of the city - Avenue D which is just around the corner was a little uncomfortable for us girls to be around at night. We also had some interactions with creepy men at Tompkins Square Park which is close by, so would certainly avoid that.   In terms of the actual stay, Kim was great!! Super easy to reach and if we had any issues (need more towels, Netflix troubleshooting on the TV, etc) she was quick to respond and help! She was not at the place for the majority of our stay, so it felt like we had a whole Airbnb for the price of a private room. :) great amenities, well air conditioned room and a huge TV with streaming platforms on it! Would recommend if you are comfortable with the neighborhood!!

i don't even know where to start. this was my first time coming to NYC & Ty was a HUGE part of this amazing experience! to start, the place was PERFECT. absolutely clean, amenities were all available to us (even though we packed everything we needed, Ty even had little things like shampoo/conditioner/forks/knives/towels available to use). the room was adorable with its decor! fresh sheets, more than enough pillows, hangers for our jackets, with the cutest little balcony. this was the NY experience! what a steal. i would pay hundreds more per night for this place. the most amazing part was how welcoming & warm he was to us! definitely feel like we've made a life-long friend that you never want to lose touch with. everything we needed, Ty had or would give to us. this place was amazing, TY WAS AMAZING! WE LOVE YOU TY! <3

Other than the location, which me and my partner found to be ideal and a cheaper way to explore New York, the rest of the stay was unpleasant. We found Martin to be abrupt and rude. When arriving at the apartment you’re greeted with a hallway of tools and equipment outside of the apartment which was dusty and unsightly and not pictured on his profile.  The apartment was filled with boxes and clutter and the bathroom was very grubby. Throughout the stay we often found dirty dishes out in the kitchen. To top everything off Martin attempted to claim that my 2nd guest was never communicated to him and requested a reservation change and for more money. Whilst there was a booking error, the additional guest was communicated long before arriving at the property on a couple of occasions via message, of which Martin acknowledged yet he raised no change at this point and waited until we arrived before asking for more money. Clearly he wanted to avoid losing a reservation and so waited until we arrived at the property as put us both in a difficult and an uncomfortable position in a city we didn’t know. Thankfully we didn’t spend too much time at the apartment and we didn’t allow this to impact our trip.

This Guy scary .. he was Shouting at me & he said ( Send me your picture now or I will take picture for for you when you arrive !!! )  Imagine !!! That's his welcome call !   Then he asked me to cancel ..  Of course I will Do   I don't know how Airbnb allowed him to participate in this application  Horrible

The room is spacious and very pleasant, you have to climb a steep staircase but it can fit eight people comfortably, plus a sofa.  The location is perfect in a neighborhood that is not scary and well connected.  Full kitchen and adequate and comfortable bathroom.  It doesn't have television.  But there is wifi and the host responds quickly to messages.
Excellent location in Manhattan.  We had 8 people fly in for my daughters wedding.  Everything from check in to checkout was stress free. I would reccomend staying here. Pablo quickly communicates!
Perfect location! 1 block to train and next to Deli, plenty of food places around. Apartment is very spacious but the stairs to go up to 2nd floor are scary steep.
Booked around 10pm for same day. Kevin was on it within 5 minutes. No stress stay! Easier than a hotel.

The house is great. It feels safe and cozy. The roommates are very friendly. The surrounding area does seem as if it could be sketchy at night, just make sure not to walk alone/take an Uber home versus walk. During the day, the area has great restaurants that are walkable, you can tell the area is in the beginning stages of gentrification. All in all, great value for the price! I would come back!

Vadim is truly a phenomenal host and just a great person in general. Enjoyed chatting with him whenever we interacted. Always made sure to check-up on anything I might need and was very responsive when I had a question. The space is fantastic, you get your whole top floor in the duplex with your own bathroom. It's super clean and the bed is extremely comfortable with a nice nook to hang out and do some work in. Oh and washer/dryer available, huge bonus. Tons of subway options within walking distance, coffee shops everywhere, and great food all around. This Airbnb is a steal and I would book it again in a heartbeat.

Just know that I had asked Lola if there was a key to the bedroom that I was staying in.   I was told the same day by Lola that she did not have a key to the bedroom.  The lock acts up at times and she repeatedly mentioned that I should not lock the door from the inside while I sleeping because, the lock my stick when leaving and I might get locked out.  She said this has happened before and and has locked out people who stayed there previously. She mentioned that she was out of town and If I locked the door when sleeping and leave out of the bedroom the door sometimes doesn't unlock and there would be no way for me to get back into the bedroom.  I suggested to her that she should change the lock to make sure that it locks along with a key for safety reasons. I felt very uncomfortable knowing that I had to sleep in a room with couldn't lock and knowing that there was another person in the second bedroom.  I mentioned to Lola that I don't feel comfortable sleeping with the room door unlocked and that someone can walk in on me while I was sleeping.   I felt very nervous, uncomfortable and scared. When I left I have to leave the door unlocked.  Weird feeling.  She said well the person there is leaving tomorrow, however another person will be arriving the day after.  That did not make me feel safe.    I will never book there again.

So, I never actually stayed at this place. There was fault on both parties here. Communication began in an odd way with Sean. I never officially got check-in instructions though I asked for them. He texted vague things with unclear expectations and when I asked for clarification, I didn’t get it. He texted me rather than messaged through the app, which I thought was fine but I had to send screenshots to Airbnb. There was a picture of the lockbox code on Airbnb listing and I thought that might be the code. Sean just sent me a picture of the lockbox without a code that day, I believe in a way to communicate the place was ready. I asked to clarify the code before we got there and he didn’t respond. When getting there, the code in the picture didn’t work. He didn’t answer his phone and wasn’t texting me back. My friends felt incredibly unsafe in the area. We decided to leave and grab a hotel and thankfully had the means to do so. I texted him that I planned to cancel the reservation. He didn’t respond. Once I did cancel the reservation, he texted me the check-in code. Nevertheless, my friends were already uncomfortable and I got a funny feeling from the oddity of the texting conversation. I tried to get a refund but Airbnb said I broke their terms and conditions by not contacting them prior to cancelling. Okay, fine. Apparently the host must be given an hour to give check in instructions. We were cold and uncomfortable so we left, but rules are rules. They said they would reach out to him and ask for at least a partial refund, but he never got back to them, so I lost the entirety of the money. Also, heads up that finding out the safety of an area is the responsibility of the Airbnb user, and it’s not a good-enough reason to cancel and get a refund. Lesson learned. Like I said: mistakes on either side. I’m not bitter but I still feel uncomfortable about the situation.

The apartment was clean and the room was just like it looks and describes on the pictures! Cristine and Fabio were really nice, they were flexible with the check-in, they recommended places to visit and restaurants with good food!! They were always there to help and they also make a really good coffee!! The apartment is located within a few blocks from the 6 and Q subway lines so it is actually really easy to move around the city!! The neighborhood wasn't that pretty but we didn't really feel unsafe walking around neither so overall it was a good experience!! We definitely recommend this place!

Location was ok (not very far from subway station), whole building is very old so everyone hear each step, staircase is very narrow (apartment is on the first floor, so it's very hard to carry big suitcases there). Communication with Paul was very good and the big plus is that you are able to checkin/checkout by yourself. Unfortunately how the batchtub in bathroom and kitchen sink and oven in the kitchen looked like is just horrible (dirty and unpleasant to use it). Also sheets in the bedroom were dirty - there were stains all over it. The appartment looked like noone cleaned it after previous guests :( Beside that the place was spacious and generaly ok.

Perfect stay at Hind, better than at the hotel! She is very available and welcomed us very late on the day of our arrival due to a flight delay. The accommodation is impeccable and very cocooning. There is everything you need for a good vacation. A 10-minute walk from the subway, it is also well served by bus lines (4 or 5) which provide easy access to Manhattan.  Hind took great care of us on a daily basis and ensured that we had an excellent stay. I highly recommend and I will not hesitate to come back! ☺

Vadim's place was a great stay in Brooklyn. It was stylish, clean and brought in plenty of natural light. We had 4 people, so it was definitely a plus to have separate bedrooms and bathrooms. We weren't able to access the rooftop due to ongoing construction, but I imagine it would be an awesome hang out spot once construction is completed. There were very detailed step-by-step instructions provided, so I definitely appreciated the stress-free check-in!

Janu is a very nice and friendly guy. His appartment is very close to different subway stations and about 25 minutes to midtown Manhattan by subway trains. Only two streets to Central Park north. His air mattress was very comfortable after days full of impressions in NYC. We had really interesting conservations about modern life and meditation and Joga to take down of stress. For all German guys his favorite chocolate is Milka :-) Thanks a lot Janu to stay in your appartment

15mins metro away from main tourism spots and a supermarket located nearby. It is very convenient with a budget price that you probably could not find in other place in New York. But I suggest avoid taking metro line 2 or 3 as the station (central park north 110 st) has strong unpleasant smell as well as the train cabin. I thank for Janu hosting me as this is the very first time I use Airbnb. I asked him a lot of questions but he is very kind and patient, he took care all of the enquiries with quick response! That was a very great experience! :D

When I booked I thought I would not share with Janu more than the space.  How wrong I was!  Janu was an excellent human with me all the time, he cares for your well-being and for knowing if you are comfortable, he lets you know that you can call him if you need (he even helped me when I felt afraid of a homeless that scared me haha, he was my  salvation!) I RECOMMEND JANU AND ITS SPACE COMPLETELY, I SLEPT VERY WELL! It was a pleasure to have met you, Janu, and I hope to visit you again very soon!

Heavenly! The old mansion is lovely, with lots of period decor - parquet floor, lots of aged wood & stained glass.  The subway and all sorts of great neighborhood places (grocery stores, restaurants, nail salons) are within a few blocks. The Brooklyn Museum of Art and the Botanic Garden are no more than a 15-minute walk away. Checking in was very easy, and I was made to feel welcomed from the first moment. The kitchen is the only part of the house that is not of the time period - it's amazing: recently updated, spacious, light-filled, great surfaces for cooking and baking. The house is really lovely - a charming environment that feels safe, comfortable, and homey. There's even a yard in front with shade trees - a rarity in Brooklyn. Although there is a family upstairs and a housemate on the same floor, the house is so solid and everyone so thoughtful that it is serenely quiet. Melissa's place was perfect!

I planned to travel to NYC with my mom and was delighted to find Cannon's place, at a great location and offering everything we could need. The neighborhood is great, all the main subway lines are close by, there's a really handy convenience store  just a block away and Cannon gave us a lot of useful tips for dining out and ordering food.   We didn't have to interact much with Cannon, but I felt confident I could reach out to him at any time in case of need.   This was my first time in an AirBnB so the first day felt a little weird to just step into someone's home, a home they clearly do live in. By the second day the place felt already familiar and we loved every square inch of it after having walked up and down the city.   The apartment has a king-size (I guess, not really used to American bedding sizes) bed where my mom slept. There was also an inflatable mattress, very easy to pump up but way too big for just one person, and it too up a lot of room. I ended up sleeping in the couch, which I guess is comfortable enough but I'm afraid I cannot be a good judge since I like my mattress to be rock-solid (I tried the large bed which I found extremely soft for my taste buy my mom loved it, so there's that).  The place is indeed noisy being on a second (first for us, Europeans) floor, but I guess it's regular NYC-upstairs-a-bar noisy, and I was glad to bear the noise in exchange for just having to climb two flights of stairs to get to the apartment. I am a sound sleeper anyway and also I always travel with earplugs just in case. My mom complained a little at first but when I turned on the white-sound machines she was delighted. She has bought one for herself upon arrival back home.   I guess if there's one thing we missed it was a microwave. Cannon has a Nespresso machine (and coffee pods that were available for us to use!) but my mom has tea for breakfast. We weren't quite sure how we were supposed to heat up the water. Of course there were cooking tools available at the apartment, but we could only find iron-cast frying pans, and my mom didn't want her tea to taste like sausages or bacon. We ended up buying a saucepan at the hardware store downstairs and we brought it back home, so now we have a real New York saucepan that is our most cherished acquisition, since we didn't really go fashion-shopping crazy.   Our experience was really good and I really liked the place. Since it's a second floor the fire escape is like a balcony, and I spent a lot of time there just watching the lively street while I waited for my mom to wake up (those white-noise machines do wonders).   I feel I need to point out that, though I haven't personally met Cannon, I believe he has a dog. He states in his profile that he loves dogs and his apartment is full of French Bulldog memorabilia. I have dogs and I'm a dog lover myself, but sometimes I could get a whiff of dog smell that made me homesick and that for some people might be a problem.   My mom's only complaint is that she thinks the stairs and common zones in the building should be fixed and renovated. I don't think it's within Cannon's scope, nor did I expect the building to be in top-notch condition, just the apartment I had rented, and that did fill my expectations, but since it's the only thing she had to say and we were in this together I thought I should mention it.   All in all, I would recommend Cannon's place and if I travel to NYC  in the near future I will surely look up AirBnB to see if it's available. The place is probably better for a single person or a couple sleeping together, but my mom and I had a great time.   An insider tip: If you ever need anything at all, there are a few CVS nearby, there's the Greenwich Village Farm store I mentioned before, and a couple blocks away you can find Citarella, a cool gourmet market with lots of delicious prepared food.   If you want to be in the greatest location in Manhattan and enjoy your stay in NYC, by all means do rent Cannon's apartment.

Kim's place was absolutely perfect. The neighborhood is great, there are a variety of stores and restaurants nearby and a subway station less than 5 minutes walking distance. For an apartment in NYC it was super spacious, and has everything needed for a comfortable stay (we were even looking forward to possibly being rained in one of the days). Kim is a fantastic host, she was always reachable and the check in/out process was so stress-free. Kim's place made our weekend trip phenomenal, and we would definitely look to book again on future trips.

The place was very small, but good enough for the price for two people to stay. There was people yelling at night and in the morning, but I suspect there were kids staying near. The TV was nice, but the wifi was a little slow. Overall, I did enjoy the decor and theme of the listing, and place was good if you want somewhere in Flushing near a transit station, and Laguardia Airport. She provided several things others might need, like toothpaste, shampoo, conditioner, and body wash. We found a bug on the 3rd night we stayed though.

I absolutely loved my stay at Kathleen’s place. The place was spotless and felt like home to me. Kathleen was attentive and resourceful. She was the best to talk to about ANYTHING and had great advice in return. I would definitely recommend her... I cannot say how much I appreciate her and her hospitality. I couldn’t stress enough how great my stay was.

A++++ rating for Kathleen and she’s a very reliable and kind young woman and I’m glad that I had the opportunity to stay with her....Just a quick heads up if you need anything or want to do something don’t be scared to ask her anything......

The most keep and dangerous place to stay , the host it’s waiting for you inside of the unit even it’s 2am , all access doors open, none of the unit doors close properly,  dirty and unsafe, unfortunately the host isn’t an honest human been , when confronted about the lack of cleaning or safety he push me to leave , me and my 2 female companions at 2am in the morning at the check in night, he kept the whole payment of 2 nights and was offensive till the last moment, please if you want a safe place for you and your love ones Thea isn’t it , please don’t waste your money and place like these, for your own safety
Very nice apartment/apartment building  located in a great part of Brooklyn plus a total steal for the price it’s going for. Would definitely recommend. Host is also attentive and detail oriented.

My first time in the United States I was lucky enough to choose Carolyn. she received me in a kind and loving way that I could not have imagined. I came in very afraid and alone, but the first impression I had was the best. Super I recommend that you spend your stay in this piece of heaven.

Great place to stay, thank you, Mekkie! The apartment is in a strategic point, the subway is literally two passes from the entrance, we were able  to reach the center and museums in a short time without stress. The apartment is clean, stylish, found all we need for our vacancy trip and even more. Hope to be back one day!

Since my flight got canceled and I got scammed for another stay, I was having a tough day. Fortunately, Carolyn allowed me to stay in her place and she really saved my day. In her place, I felt safe and at home. I really appreciate her kindness🙂

Cosy,  comfortable, clean and well-equipped basement apartment near subway, buses and shops, ideal base for exploring Brooklyn and beyond. Sleeps up to 5 pax although access from main bedroom to bathroom  through second bedroom so recommended for a family or group of friends. Efficient AC unit and ceiling fans kept the place cool even on hot muggy days and nights. We welcomed the super size fridge, large stove, and kitchen table which gave us the option to stock up with fresh produce at the local stores and cook at night after a long day sightseeing, before relaxing in front of the  smart TV.  The host is super friendly and welcoming and very easy to communicate with ahead of  and during our stay (he lives on the top floor of the property) responding instantaneously to all our queries. He also very generously drove us to JFK airport on the morning of our departure  thereby alleviating the stress of a very long journey back home. Thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

If you’re expecting more than a bachelors pad, this is not the place for you. It is clean and conveniently located, however there are numerous, relatively minor issues with the functioning of the apartment because it’s an older building. After some incorrect information on this website about where to pick up the keys, I made it to the apartment and schlepped the fifth floor walk up.  For me, Emch’s place was really just a place to sleep because my week was filled with classes and activities.  For that purpose, it was okay. The bed is comfortable! Plus, there’s a lovely rooftop garden with flowers, chairs and a picnic table, an amazing view of One WTC, and a statue of Buddha to ease the stress of the city. But frankly, I wouldn’t stay here again.

It was a great place to stay! It’s in a quiet neighborhood. You can catch the bus around the corner to the subway. My family just Uber to the subway for under fifteen dollars a way. The pictures match the place. I would come back to the place again.. if I would have to say something negative about it. You park on a drive way on a forty-five degree angle so kinda scary getting out. Over all it was home away from home feeling!!

Myles is an exceptional host. Great human qualities, airport/home transport was carried out by Myles (Thank you +++ because less stress). The apartment is very well maintained, the linen is changed. If you have a question, Myles is very responsive in his response. In addition, the apartment is very well located (supermarket, metro and all amenities less than 5 minutes walk). As soon as you arrive, there is coffee, tea, cold drinks... Excellent stay. A big thank you to Myles and don't hesitate if you detour to Brittany.

Myles was a wonderful host! He did everything and more for us to enjoy our stay. I cannot stress enough how great of a host he was!   His place was clean, has great location and was sooo comfy and homey.  You are walking distance to an easy way into the city on the subway, and very very close by to a big target and a big grocery store.   Also, if you need to do laundry, there’s a very good laundromat around the corner. Myles recommend it and the lady that works there was very helpful.   Myles is so kind and helpful and his place was great.

We had a great stay- went in for a concert at the Ford theater, and it was an easy walk there and back. Meeting them before hand was so nice to put a face to the name, and to get a lay of the land. The off street parking was perfect and took a stress off the plate. Highly recommended, would stay there again!

Quiet, private, and easy to relax and get work done.  Super close to airport made my traveling expierence much less stressful. Super responsive and made sure i was good and settled in. Highly recommended.

This is a good space for some (probably younger folks not needing accessibility) looking for a little adventure in New York without paying Manhattan prices, but it's not right for everyone (such as probably older or people with disabilities.) This is in a fairly busy part of Brooklyn and the appliances at this space, like the space itself, are nice and modern like the sleek in-room air conditioners akin to the whole decor, however, this space is NOT right for some people. My family had a very, very hard time without a railing on the fairly steep stairs over the shops below. This is a Brooklyn experience- to be over a store and under train tracks (and the train is surprisingly almost silent inside the apartment, even while it roars outside) but the stairs, with no railing, were difficult for all of us- my wife and I, in our 30s (without any manifest physical disabilities), generally, did fine but would slow down a little at the top and bottom. My father, in his 70s, was a little more careful, but, again, was alright, given his ability to still hike with us. My mother, however, just a little slower than most and with bad knees and feet so she can't walk much, had a VERY hard time with the stairs. I'm not sure if it's legal in New York to have stairs without a railing but it seemed both uninviting at best and dangerous at worst. It was uncomfortable for some of us and terrifying for others. Other missing amenities in the space included towel bars, the back leg of the low couch in the kitchen (which many people, including my mother, couldn't sit in anyway), furniture other than stools, a baking sheet, drawer stoppers and an ideally functioning bathroom drain. For a few days, these things add up but Utrecht Avenue in Brooklyn is a nice location; the train, grocery and liquor stores are just a block or less away and Joseph and his family are friendly and  efficient, off-site hosts, so this is a great, stop-over space for some, but definitely not right for all.

I always struggle with writing critical reviews, especially when this platform and the ability to have guests supports this person’s livelihood. In this case, I’m writing because the other reviews just didn’t mention some of these things and that was challenging for me. Shiva was a very lovely guy. Very sweet. I enjoyed all of our encounters. But here are some of the things that I struggled with during my stay.   There was hair literally everywhere. Long hair, beard hair, pubes. Hair in the tub and on the floor of the bathroom. There was hair in the bed and on all the rugs. Hairs clinging to my socks and to my bare feet. With this lack of cleanliness it was a bit annoying that no shoes were allowed in the house.  Shiva worked from home daily and had loud, headphoneless Zoom calls all day long just outside my door. I was in and out a lot, but often when I wanted to sleep late, this disturbed me.  The woman upstairs stomped unrelentingly. The apartment was not quiet.   During my time there, Shiva would cough so aggressively I thought for sure he would produce a lung. During a pandemic this caused a constant stress and fear.  He would piss in the toilet and not flush it, which was gross. What was even more gross was that after having a lady friend over he left a used condom at the top of the trash can. After two days of seeing this, I expected him to empty the trash bin… instead he placed hair shavings on top of it from his beard.  Shiva was great…but I’d consider these things when booking.
Clean, hospitable and very friendly  No need to be concerned with it being shady - it’s a great spot near LGA

Expect an extra charge for extra people. The listing said room for two, but we were charged additional 25$ for two people staying in the room. I guess this is a normal practice on AirBnB, but this just feels borderline shady.  The place is okay. Relatively clean. The building is old and it is very noticeable on the inside. On the plus side, the neighborhood is quiet and looks safe. But it is not the nicest neighborhood in the area. You can find better.
Everything was good, the house is so clean and home is so cute but the street is a little bit scary but it is near the subway that’s good point

Xavier was very prompt in responding to texts. He made sure that he was attentive to anything I might have needed. The bed was really comfy, which was a huge bonus for me. Given the location, this is a steal for this price. I felt very safe and the place was clean. Highly recommended.

This is a very comfortable, spacious, and quiet place to stay. The rooms are big, the bathroom is probably the nicest i've ever seen in NYC, and I love the skylight in the master bedroom. The neighborhood is quiet and comfortable. There are great restaurants and bars a half a block away, and its about a 10min walk to the subway.    BUT we had some issues with the lock on the front door that were pretty inconvenient. The front door of the airbnb has a deadbolt and also a knob lock below it. To enter the airbnb, the instructions were to open a lockbox to get the key for the deadbolt, and then unlock the deadbolt. When I first checked in, I was able to get into the lockbox and get the key for the deadbolt and unlock the deadbolt, but the knob lock below it was locked and so I couldnt get in. I texted the host Barbara and rang the door bell, and Barbara opened the door and said that the door already *was* unlocked and open. I tried to explain that the deadbolt unlocked properly, but that the knob lock below it was also locked and there was no key for this. She didn't understand this because she was able to pull the door open (by the knob with the knob lock, because twisting it unlocks the knob lock). I decided not to push it. For the next 2 days of my stay the knob lock was unlocked, and I was able to come and go with the key to the deadlock.  But on Saturday night 11/12 / Sunday morning 11/13 we came back to the airbnb at 2am to find that the knob lock was accidentally locked again, and we were locked out. This was scary to be locked out in NYC in the middle of the night. I banged on the door, texted and called. Eventually after banging on the door for 20min Barbara woke up and came to the door and let us in. She was understandably distraught, and yelled at us for scaring her and waking her up. But what else were we going to do, being locked out? Barbara accused us of not knowing how to use the deadbolt. We explained that the knob lock was accidentally locked again, and tried to show her how even with the deadbolt unlocked, the knob lock prevented entry from the outside, but she refused to listen and kept yelling at us. We went to bed, very shaken, and left the next morning.   For the safety of future guests, the host should either include a key to the knob lock as well as the deadlock, or take care to NOT accidentally lock the knob lock on the door handle again.
Brett and rob is very easy to communicate with. The place is amazing!

If you like to stay outside the city then Staten Island is for you.   It is a 15 minute ferry ride to go back and forth between the city.   Staten Island Ferry station is very sketchy late at night with people hanging around there who I did not feel comfortable with.    Price was reasonable on this place for the time we were there.  We spent most of our  time in the city so basically only at the house to sleep and shower.   Unit is perfect for 2 people and David was very good at answering my text questions about the unit and the ferry.   I wouldn't stay here again as I just didn't like the travel time and the Staten Island Ferry station late at night was just not good.

I tried to find a reasonably priced place near JFK to spend the night and came across this! The walk from Jamaica station to the place is a little bit scary at night but during the day it's fine! Seeranie was very kind and hospitable, I thoroughly enjoyed my stay! :D

David’s place is a wonderful value—clean, stylish, modern and in a great location.   I absolutely love the way they’ve decorated and furnished the space. From the exposed brick to the New York-inspired artwork, it was nice to feel like you were truly in the city (instead of a bland hotel room). Amenities like the kitchen appliances and TV we’re all top notch, and I appreciate the effort that went into the guest manual...and I also appreciate the Harry Potter books.  My favorite part of the apartment was by far the bed, about which I can’t rave enough. I’ve traveled a lot, and this is easily the best bed I’ve ever slept in—huge and ridiculously comfortable. I never wanted to leave it, which is a problem when you’re in the greatest city in the world and have things to do!  David was a great host that was very kind and responsive. I arrived a bit late after attending a baseball game, and was unable to open the front gate at first. Afraid to set off an alarm if I kept trying, I called him; he answered immediately and stayed on the phone to ensure I got in okay.  The noise we heard above us was nothing out of the ordinary for a family home, and was never an issue. Besides, you shouldn’t be sitting around all day anyway—did I mention you’re in the greatest city in the world?  Manhattan (and the other boroughs) are VERY accessible. Buses stop right across the street that take you straight to the ferry, which is a beautiful and free ride to Manhattan. There’s no reason to pay crazy prices for a hotel in Manhattan when you can stay in a place like this. Save some money and have the experience of staying in a beautiful home in a lovely neighborhood!

I’m not usually one to leave bad reviews but I feel this place needs attention. This was my first time visiting New York and my first time in Brooklyn. If you are looking for a nice location, forget this place. It is close to the G train but not close enough that someone didn’t try to rob us on the way in from the airport.  The streets are not safe in this area and it looks run down and scary. I will give Pamela credit for allowing us to check in super late as our plane arrived late at night. However after that, the next day when I needed an iron i could not reach her to save my life. We finally had to go bang on her downstairs door and a man told us where to find a steam iron. The thing is she told us she would be available after 3pm yet I never could reach her. I never heard from her again until it was time for us to check out and all she did was leave a message reminding us to leave by 11am. My guests and i do not see the appeal at all with this place. Location sucks, WiFi was poor, the shared bathroom is between 4 bedrooms so if the place is full good luck getting into the bathroom. The floors are noisy as well as the AC in the room makes a ton of noise. The window to our room was held open with a piece of wood. The beds have plastic on them that make you feel are noisy and uncomfortable. I mean I could go on and on.. the price is way too expensive for this small room and I can’t believe that people leave good notes. I noticed most of the good reviews left are from foreign travelers who maybe don’t know any better but as an American that has travelled the world this was by far the only airbnb that I am leaving a bad review about. All of the others were great.  Too expensive and hardly cozy. Sorry Pamela, but with all the money you are making by charging people so much you should invest in making the place more comfortable and get some better WiFi. She did have water available but that’s about all I can say.. we couldn’t even get the TV to work...

Excellent! We loved the room, the kitchen and shared bathrooms were no problem. And it had everything we needed. The metro is a very short distance away. Easy access day and night. So much so that we left at 05:00 am for the airport and it was very quiet. The check-in process was easy, we accessed the compartment with the key through the password sent and we opened the door quietly. A detail, the key turns to the left to open the door, we are not used to it, since in Brazil it is on the right. We had a little scare when trying to open it for the first time. Once we learned it was easy. I highly recommend the space!

We loved our stay with Mark! His apt. is located steps from Columbus Circle, Central Park, Times Square and Broadway, so much going on so close - we walked everywhere! Luxurious towels, fresh flowers and fragrant soaps welcomed us to the spacious room - the center piece of which was the supremely comfortable bed.  Fresh, strong coffee awaited us in the morning - perfect.  Mark went above and beyond (and helped take the stress out of our travel schedule) by being flexible with our check in/out times.  Great host with outstanding communication in a central NYC location, would 100% recommend.

David was very helpful he went above the call of Duty. We arrived earlier than check in and he allowed us to leave our baggage early so we could leave for NYC using the Staten Island Ferry.  The place was very clean and nice.  He was extremely accommodating to our needs.  There even a kitchen, refrigerator and coffee machine. The Keurig coffee machine even had coffee for us to use which he provided. He gave us helpful tips to get around NYC which made our family trip less stressful.  I cannot say enough good things about our stay.  Thank You David.

This is a nice place. Parking was across the street from the house just like he said. It was a bit further from the ferry than I expected. Also make sure you know how to get there if you plan to walk. Find an app on your phone that is easy to use. There were only directions on how to get there using the bus and we were unprepared. We were uncomfortable walking back after dark so took a taxi from the ferry and it was $8. The bathroom was very small but fine for us. He wins the prize for the most comfortable bed we have had at one of these places. We didn't want to get up. Also the noise machine in the room is the best one I have used. You will hear some normal footfalls in the morning. There are great shades and an AC in the bedroom. I wish there was a shade or curtain or something for the bedroom door since it is see through and lets sunlight in. This is a nice house and suite. I wish we could have stayed longer than just the one night. It is a good value.

I didn't like finding myself in a house decorated strangely and really overloaded with unnecessary things. I stayed in this apartment for only one evening. and yes I lost a colossal amount of money with this apartment. I ask RBNB to check the photos of the apartments PLEASE If the accommodation was presented correctly I would never book it. It’s organized theft!  In addition, I had requested a modification which was also not taken into account.....this is not normal!!!

This lady is delusional. I stayed at her place with 3 of my boys and this lady drove me crazy.  After we checked out she claimed that I broke her chair. She accused me of stealing her steamer iron, now what am I going to do with that smh....She called me a thief and talking a whole lot of nonsense.   I stayed in many Airbnb’s all over the US but this one was the worst one.  Her add said that she had a two bedrooms but she only let us used one and locked the other room. So imagine 4 grown men sleeping in a one bedroom with only a regular couch in the living room.  It was a very uncomfortable stay for me and my friends and wouldn’t recommend this property to anyone.

The apartment is ideal for several travelers. My husband and I stayed in one bedroom with a very large closet and plenty of hangers and my brother used the second. There would have been even more sleeping options. You then have a large kitchen-living room together and can prepare a wonderful breakfast. The apartment is bright and tastefully furnished. Everything you need is there in the kitchen. There are enough fluffy towels in the bathroom, there is also a hairdryer and even shampoo and conditioner are available. Just around the corner, about a 5 minute walk, is a large supermarket. The location is ideal because after a strenuous day in Manhattan, after the scenic ferry crossing, you can get off on the S78 bus after 4 stops directly in front of the house. Things are generally much quieter and cheaper on Staten Island. We ate burgers near the arrivals terminal at Steiny’s Pub, which were very good, served with chips and cost around $10. The beer was $5.50. The 120 Bay Café was also good and cheap. We had the recommended 7-day ticket for $32 and were able to travel unlimited anywhere in the 5 New York boroughs. Even with the cable car to Roosevelt Island, which is really recommended because of the view. When we arrived at Newark Airport we wanted to take public transport, but that would have taken about 2 hours and we didn't know our way around at all. I contacted the host because there was WiFi at the airport and since we couldn't book UBER, Dine gave us the tip to take the official yellow cap. It was really great to get help straight away. Right out of the airport, there was a taxi station where you could indicate your destination. We just said Staten Island Ferry, paid $48. In the taxi we were told there would be an additional toll of $17. OK. We then discovered that the driver was taking us to Staten Island and then told him the exact address. We neglected to tell "MANHATTAN' Staten Island Ferry what Dine had written to us. So we would have taken the free ferry over. All in all we paid $70 and arrived happy. On the way home with more experience, we took the public transport. First with one of the numerous bus lines that all go from Bay Street in front of the gas station to the Staten Island Ferry, then ferry, then on line 1 to PENN STATION NEW YORK. We We always use elevators or escalators and were able to get there with the luggage. Then we got to NJ Transport. There we bought a ticket to Newark Airport for $13 Clock. We were way too early.

We absolutely felt at home in this little piece of Harlem! Everyone we came in contact with was friendly, we never felt unsafe. Theresa had fresh linens, soap, and even shampoo/conditioner waiting there for us. The apartment was sparkling clean, and very well decorated. Plenty of sleep space and room to spread out. The accessibility to public transit was pretty sweet, too! We downloaded the app ‘Citymapper’, which made it that much simpler. The smoothie shop and coffee shop on the block were amazing. We didn’t want to come home!! Thank you so much for your hospitality!

My family and I stayed at Mark’s place for a short visit with the purpose of visiting NYC. The apartment itself was very quiet and comfortable. The beds were great!!! The location was very convenient for travels to NYC. It was a short walk to the ferry. The ferry was a beautiful, quick, and free way to get to the city. The neighborhood itself felt a little sketchy at times, but overall it was perfect for our visit bc we spent little time in the neighborhood. We recommend driving to the ferry as to avoid walking late at night on your return to the house. It only costs 8 dollars to park all day and it is free on Sundays. I advise getting there early on week days bc the parking lot is small and fills up quickly.  Mark’s place was a quiet escape from the busy city we had been in all day. Overall, our trip was great and would recommend Mark’s place if you are looking for a quick and cheap way to visit New York.

Rachel is very available. On the day of our arrival we received precise information on how to pick up the keys and access the accommodation. 10 minutes away you have different Metro. Lively neighborhood but you don't feel unsafe. The accommodation is very clean, you feel good inside. It's just what you need for a short stay, the bed is comfortable.

The study is good. The neighborhood is not what I expected, it seems a little dangerous. I wouldn't recommend it to a woman who doesn't like walking alone on the street. The shower is in a part of the house with low height. My boyfriend who is 1.84 couldn't fit standing in the shower, which was quite uncomfortable for him. For everything else it was fine.

Lovely space in the heart of Harlem--away from the hustle and bustle of Times Square! Very close to all sorts of wonderful eateries, grocery stores,  delis and drug stores.   Very close to the subway --everything is walking distance. To top it off the accommodations are top notch. Very neat and clean --hardwood floors, private bath and entrance -- kitchen with all sort of appliances--including cable TV and Netflix.  Great place!  Excellent hostess -- Hope to return!

Rachel is a great host, always trying to solve any problems we had and helpful with dropping off the luggage after checking out. Unfortunately we didn't like the area, felt unsafe for us. There are not any good cafes around but Rachel left some coffee pods and oats for us, which was very convenient to have a morning coffee and quick bite before heading out. The apartment was very clean but the low ceilings, especially in the shower and the small windows make it feel claustrophobic. Overall a good price for 3 nights in NY.

This was a great place to crash after spending the day out in the city. The area surrounding the place is a bit sketchy but it was described well in the introduction so you get what you pay for. The studio itself was clean and nice. It has a small fridge, microwave and coffee maker. It’s easy to get into and it’s a 11 min walk to the C Train stop. Rachel was a great host, let us drop off our bags before check in and was super fast at replying back. Great stay overall!!

The space was very clean and Rachel was very sweet!  She always being very quick to answer my questions and help me. However we didin't feel safe walking on the streets.  Locals around us often talked nonsense to us and we got scared.

Don't be scared to stay here in Harlem! Felt very safe, great location, good restaurants, awesome breakfast cafe just around corner, loved the space, had everything we needed , easy subway access... We will be back and we highly recommend Will and Felicias place!

The Airbnb was cute and well-positioned, but the bathroom situation proved to be an absolute nightmare. Because the bathroom is very tiny, and because the shower floor wasn't divided by the rest of the bathroom floor, water would flow out from the shower and into the entire bathroom floor. We had to use multiple towels to try to block the water, which was really unpleasant and each towel would just get sopping wet. The bathroom also had very poor ventilation and had a slight moldy smell.  On top of that, there was no body wash or soap for us to use, and because we were in a rush to meet our reservations, we had to use the conditioner that was there in the meantime, until we could run out and buy our own.  The decoration of the living room is very cute, but functionally it wasn't an ideal space because of the bathroom, and because of the thin walls and noisy upstairs neighbors, as other reviewers have mentioned. I would not stay in this AirBnB again.

This place was the worst airbnb I've ever stayed in. We ended up leaving within 24 hours because the noise was unbearable. When they say paper thin walls they really mean a paper thin ceiling. The family above sounds like they will fall through the ceiling into your bedroom at 2 and 6 in the morning. Plus, Maria was completely unaccommodating when we decided we needed to go elsewhere. She refused to grant any refunds despite us not even staying more than 1 night (our reservation was 3). I am a deep sleeper and it was the worst sleep of my life even with earplugs. NEVER STAY HERE. It's an absolute scam.

Overall: This will work as a cheap Airbnb if you just need a place to sleep, but everything is cheap and low-quality, and there are lots of odd disappointments/inconveniences. Pros: Location is great, Maria communicated adequately and getting in was fine. Cons: Low-quality everything. Tile and metal brackets were broken or falling off in the shower and bathroom floor, making it pretty dangerous to get in and out of without cutting yourself. There were no bath towels, just a bunch of pretty raggedy bath mats. The sink was so narrow that trying to use it meant spilling water all over yourself and the bathroom. There was an iron but no ironing board. All the lights were those blue-hued harsh LEDs.  The upstairs neighbors had dogs and the ceiling was very thin, so maybe avoid if you're not used to living in thin-walled city apartments because that sound can get unexpectedly grating.

Excellent experience. I spent a month here. I was a lucky one cuz Lara was out this month so I have the apartment by myself. Very good location, with all the restaurants, cafe, grocery shops, metro station near around. Also, it is a very safe and nice place. I have never felt unsafe here. Lara is a very nice and helpful host. Although we haven't met each other face to face, she offered me so much help while I was here.

Although there are 3 bedrooms in the apartment, the living space is not designed to accommodate 5 or 6 people, in fact there are only 4 chairs around the table pressed against the wall and against the sofa in the living room. We were 5 adults and it was impossible for us to have our meals in the apartment. There is a big heating problem (2 overheated bedrooms, no heating in the 3rd bedroom or in the living room, burning heating pipe in the bathroom which could be dangerous with young children). Not much communication, no help from his assistant to bring up the luggage, old and dirty apartment, we were disappointed by this one however I would point out that the location is really excellent.

Absolute superb location with the subway right across the street. Right next to a drug store and great dining. Easy and quick access to Broadway, the Met, and major museums. We honestly could not have had a better time, even though one of our shows was canceled due to COVID.   We were a family with 2 adult kids (21 & 17) who each at their own space, but the space is very small—which is typical in NYC. We didn’t spend too much time in the apartment, so it wasn’t a problem to us.  A few details:  Furnishings are very low-quality. Some things were in disrepair—the ceiling had a leak just before we showed up (from the apt upstairs) so an unsightly duct-taped garbage bag covered it up. One set of blinds in a bedroom had no cord to raise/lower, the faucets are loose feel like they are falling apart.  None of that is really the point in staying here, so it is more of an FYI than a problem to me.  The owner was very responsive, (for example, the coffee maker died and it was replaced that same day), checkin/out was super easy.  I told the owner about the points in this review, so I’m sure these things will be taken care of soon if my experience with them is consistent.  If I was coming to NYC again on holiday, I would not hesitate to book it again, if it was available.  One tip—the main bedroom has a radiator that makes all kinds of random clicks and knocks. Bring earplugs if it might bother you! After the first night, I didn’t notice but my wife slept better with earplugs.

Rosemarie was responsive and kind, and her place made for a wonderful jumping off point to explore the city. You're a ten-minute walk from nearly any metro line in the city, and the apartment is located next to an endless number of incredible shops, cafes, and restaurants. I really can't stress enough how perfect the location was! In the span of a weekend, my friend and I already developed a quasi morning routine, featuring a morning pop into Happy Bones for hot chocolate and coffee. The space was perfectly clean and charming, and Rosemarie provided anything you could think of needing, i.e. towels, shampoo, conditioner, etc. Such a great value!

Beebe's place was awesome! She was easy to communicate with and so outgoing. The room was clean and the beds were comfy after a long day in NY. Little tight in the bathroom, but clean and had all the amenities one needs along with soft towels. The location is a couple blocks away from the train (about 35 minutes into the city) and had plenty of places to eat in walking distance. Don't be scared to try the Chinese food or the Deli & Grill up the street (Tried both) while Manny's was delicious as well. I definitely plan to stay with Beebe again and would recommend it to all my friends.   If you're planning to use rideshare, take Juno. Better prices than Uber or Lyft in NYC

Beebe's communication was great - she was always there to help if needed.   There was a flood in the apartment the day before we arrived and Beebe informed us of this. It did make the place smell a bit damp (inc. the sheets). But this was resolved on the second night.   The apartment is private and clean and quite spacious. It was great that we could use the washing machine and drier.  The area is quite far out from Manhantan. We enjoyed finding 'Manny's' for breakfast. At times the area felt a little unsafe (at night) and was noisy - something we didn't realise beforehand. However it was good to have public transport close by. All in all, Beebe was helpful and made us feel welcome.

Apartment is located  next to the subway station. Neighbourhood was ok during the day, a bit sketchy in the night time. We were provided clean bed sheets and towels. Apartment was clean. Only issue was that plates and cups had stains.

Airbnb location was very convenient, just a few steps from the subway entrances and with 3 grocery stores on walking distance.  Although the location could be tricky on nights, many homeless walking on the area, in addition there’s a construction on the road just in front of the Airbnb door. Expect noice, trash and be cautious during night.  WiFi was great, strong signal and speed, in addition the TV on the living room includes Netflix.  The bathroom have a lot of opportunity areas, the bath tub was dirty, full of moho, with hair stuck and with the steam came a  weird smell.   During nights the Airbnb is very hot, we were there in December and nights were very hot, expect sweating nights, Airbnb Manager mentioned that the only way to control the “heat” would be to open the window, which is try as is a very noise neighborhood (homeless, construction + subway/train). So, I do not recommend the Airbnb for summer.  I had an error in the arrival time, I said we’ll arrived at 12:00 pm on November 21st instead of 12:00 am, and she asked a friend for help to give us the keys, because she had a dinner family, her friend charged her $150 dollars, Kate paid $50 for toll booths and gasoline and we the rest for him to give us the keys.

Bad experience: Our experience was ruined by the fact that the apartment had mice. We've informed Jennifer but the thing was handled only after 6 DAYS (6 days of sleeping hearing mouse squeakings at night) and the solution was glue traps all over and rat foam to block all the holes the kitchen had. The foam created another problem because it gave a strong chemical smell which lasted for 3 days. We had trouble breathing and we had to sleep with our windows open (in winter). We had a dog too so it was even more scary. I've asked Jennifer for a partial refund but she rejected our request without even a word of apology. She just clicked "reject" without even replying with words. We felt unsafe and not welcome in this apartment so I wouldn't recommend.

Daniel's place is great. The location is the biggest factor. 1 block from 2 different subway stations that both go into main subway stations on Manhattan. We could get just about anywhere in the city in 20 minutes or less. The neighborhood felt safe and was pretty quiet, except for the construction in the area. Don't let that scare you away, though. The room was exactly what we needed: a clean place to sleep in between long days of exploring the city! Book it!

Accommodation very well located 2m from the subways (E-7-G) which takes us to the heart of Manhattan in 10 minutes. The room is very clean with comfortable bedding. The environment is a little noisy because of the skytrain (at night) but especially because of the construction going on in the area from 7 a.m.  We were warmly welcomed by Daniel despite our very late arrival due to a delayed flight.  Daniel is very responsive whether by phone or messaging. We recommend.

Alex was a good host.  He was there when I arrived with the keys.  He showed me the space and answered all my questions.  The picture of the room on the airbnb was different then the room I stayed in, however it was very similar. There are 3 rooms in his apartment, so i suspect the picture was one of the other 2 rooms.  The room and bathroom were clean.  There was a nice air conditioner and ceiling fan in the room. There was also a decent tv in the room, but i did not use it. This place is a very good value for the money.

Clean, comfortable, quiet, with everything you need for an enjoyable stay. Patricia is very attentive, kind and considerate. She even has a card for you to use in the building laundrymat if you need it. There is a nice grocery store downstairs and the kitchen is well equipped. The neighborhood is a bit sketchy at night but during the day it is fine. The D train is a 10 min walk and 4 train 15 min walk so you'll be to midtown Manhattan in about 30 min. Thank you Patricia for your hospitality!

I don't even know where to start, seriously. I stayed here for almost two months, which was a very long time. It became more than just an accommodation. It was a home. And, not only because I stayed here for so long, but also how welcomed Luz and her daughter made me feel. Luz was an AMAZING host and just, without a doubt, an AMAZING person. She was extremely kind, caring, considerate, and friendly. She would go out of her way to make you feel comfortable and welcomed. She provided everything you need, or wouldn't even hesitate for a moment to grant your wish if you needed anything else. To me, she was more than just an Airbnb host, but a friend who was always looking after me, the new kid in town. As for the place, the photos don't even do it justice. You think those photos look good? Wait 'til you see the real place. It's like 150%+ accuracy. The place was picture perfect--straight out of a magazine. Clean. Tidy. Organized.
